title: Check whether the component manifest's activation contract list is stale
description:
## Why

eon-4f1n's contract sweep (2026-10-30, edge 39e0a25) found that `components/eon-v5.json`
`activation.required_contracts` lists ORB-C1 to ORB-C13 (without ORB-C10) and VEN-C1 to VEN-C25
(without C6, C12, C16, C17 and C19), but omits contracts that are proved and that the composed
product uses: ORB-C14, ORB-C15, ORB-C16, VEN-C16 and VEN-C26 to VEN-C32. The Venus proof list
covers VEN-C1 to VEN-C26 only. Either the activation set is deliberately partial (then it should say
what earns a place) or it went stale as contracts were added.

## Evidence

- `components/eon-v5.json:14-47` (`required_contracts`) and the Venus `contracts` proof list.
- `eon/crates/eon-manifest/src/lib.rs:428` rejects activation that references an unproved contract.
- Proved status: `orbit/docs/CONTRACTS.md` ORB-C15 and ORB-C16, `venus/docs/CONTRACTS.md`
  VEN-C27 to VEN-C31. Consumers: Eon Runtime cites ORB-C15 (`attention.rs`, `sessions.rs`), and
  Venus cites VEN-C31.
- eon-4f1n proposes demoting VEN-C9, C11, C15, C22, C24 and C25, all of which are in the activation
  list. Settle the rule for what the list holds before that edit.

## Scope

In scope: find the rule `eon-omq` set for `required_contracts` and the proof list (bead history,
docs/DISTRIBUTION.md, docs/ARCHITECTURE.md). Then report one of two outcomes: the omissions are
deliberate (name the rule), or they are stale (list the exact additions with proof revisions).

Out of scope: editing the manifest. That is a component-manifest change and needs its own approved
bead with the full Rust and Nix proof route.

## Acceptance

- A comment on this bead that names the rule or lists the stale entries, each with evidence.

## Verification

- Each listed contract's Status and proof revision is quoted from its index.

## Stop Conditions

- Stop before any manifest edit.
close_reason: Answered: eon-omq's rule allows a partial activation list (additional proved contracts may be recorded without becoming prerequisites); the list is frozen since 2586d7c with legacy proof SHAs. vn0nk removes retired IDs from both lists and adds none.

comments.author: lucca
comments.text:
Answer (claude-contracts session, 2026-10-30, edge 62c8cb5). Read-only: no manifest edit.

## Outcome: the omissions are allowed by a rule, but the list has been frozen since consolidation

**The rule.** `eon-omq` (closed 2026-08-07) set it in its acceptance: "One fixture pins the exact
owner revisions and contracts required by the alpha: ORB-C1 through ORB-C9, VEN-C1 through VEN-C4,
and VEN-C7 [...]. Additional proved contracts may be recorded without becoming activation
prerequisites." `eon-68v` applied it: "Deferred VEN-C5 hyperlink interaction and VEN-C6 structured
accessibility are not activation prerequisites." So a component's `contracts` list holds proof
records, and `activation.required_contracts` is a subset: the child contracts that the composed
product's activation depends on. The validator enforces only that subset relation and a non-empty
list (`eon/crates/eon-manifest/src/lib.rs:407-430`). No document defines the subset further.
docs/DISTRIBUTION.md and docs/ARCHITECTURE.md ("Activation boundary") say nothing about it, and
EON-C2's Boundary says "In-tree contract and interface proofs remain on their components."

**How it grew.** Before consolidation, each Eon bead that consumed a new child contract pinned the
child's revision, recorded the proof, and added the contract to the activation list if the product
relied on it. Examples: `eon-consume-venus-background-blur-k8o` ("record VEN-C15") and
`eon-deliver-codex-quota-eon-bar-yg0` ("Canonical graph now selects accepted Venus 425d4a6 [...] and
requires VEN-C22"). Some proved contracts were recorded without being required: VEN-C17, VEN-C19
and VEN-C26 are in the Venus proof list but not in activation.

**Why it is frozen.** `2586d7c` (2026-10-14) brought Orbit and Venus into the tree. In-tree
components have no pinned revision, so the step that recorded and required contracts went away.
Since then no commit has changed a contract entry: `git log -S'"VEN-C25"'` (and the same for
VEN-C26, VEN-C24, ORB-C13) finds only `2586d7c`. Every Orbit and Venus `proof` value in the manifest
is a revision of one of the legacy split repositories, and none of them resolves here: `git cat-file
-t` fails for `d96fff2` (ORB-C1), `3b9f578` (VEN-C25) and `d0642ed` (VEN-C26). The in-tree indexes
re-proved those contracts at `795d735` (`eon-monorepo-2oko.6`). Nobody decided to leave out the
contracts adopted after consolidation; the recording step simply no longer runs.

So the list is not stale under the written rule, which allows it to be partial. Nothing must be
added. But it records the 2026-10-14 activation set with legacy proof revisions, and nothing keeps
it current.

## Contracts the product uses that the manifest omits (Status quoted from each index)

Neither recorded nor required:
- ORB-C14 Apple Silicon macOS platform: "Proved"; proof `0e47d26df690c7ff4b2f1a000e174b307a17e656`
  (`eon-mac-launch-kz4p.12`). Present at consolidation.
- ORB-C15 Program status records: "Proved"; proof "Approved on 2026-10-21 (draft 15 on
  `eon-agent-sidebar-yx8.1`)", first revision `c8c62cb` cited. Adopted `dd8b9ab` (2026-10-22). Eon
  Runtime consumes it (`attention.rs`, `sessions.rs`).
- ORB-C16 Static graphics resource plane: "Proved"; proof "Adopted on 2026-10-27 [...]
  (`orb-j2i.2`)", installed at `7dc3509`. Adopted `9e2fc14` (2026-10-27).
- VEN-C16 Native Linux Wayland and Apple Silicon macOS platforms: "Proved for x86_64 Linux native
  Wayland; the Apple Silicon macOS [...]"; proof `795d735`, later `0e47d26`.
- VEN-C27 Local clock: "Proven on native x86_64 Linux Wayland."; proof `eon-igae.4`, `eon-igae.3`.
  Adopted `b18f2cd` (2026-10-21).
- VEN-C28 CPU and memory use: "Proven on native x86_64 Linux Wayland."; proof
  `eon-cpu-widget-eon-bar-acxs`, `eon-igae.3`, `eon-igae.14.4`, `eon-icoh`. Adopted `9f972e5`.
- VEN-C29 Eon Bar item order: "Proven by the automated tier [...]"; proof `eon-igae.14.1`. Adopted
  `188df15`.
- VEN-C30 Agent sidebar: "Partially proved [...]"; proof `d6ce117` and later. Adopted `ec13ba6`
  (2026-10-23).
- VEN-C31 Static terminal images: "Proven on x86_64 Linux. [...]"; proof `7dc3509`. Adopted
  `9e2fc14`.
- VEN-C32 Attention inbox: "Partially proved [...]"; proof `1dabfde`, `c300fdb`. Adopted `1dabfde`
  (2026-10-29).

Recorded as proved but not required: VEN-C17, VEN-C19, VEN-C26 (legacy proofs `ab24961`, `bc5a2bd`,
`d0642ed`). ORB-C10 is recorded but not required.

## Effect on eon-vn0nk (decided under the rule; no approved meaning, scope or ID list changes)

A retired ID no longer names a contract, so it can be neither a proof record nor an activation
prerequisite. vn0nk therefore removes VEN-C9, C11, C15, C22, C24 and C25 from both
`activation.required_contracts` and the Venus `contracts` list, and VEN-C26 from the Venus
`contracts` list only (it was never required). It adds nothing. VEN-C27, C28 and C29 are being
retired and were never listed, so no entry is needed for them. The validator still holds: the
activation list stays non-empty and remains a subset of the recorded proofs. No test names a
contract ID (`canonical_manifest_is_valid` validates the file, and the mutation tests do not touch
contract entries). `eon versions` does not print contracts.

## Follow-up for Lucca (not filed; it is a component-manifest design choice)

Choose between two options: (a) define what earns a place, record in-tree proofs at in-tree
revisions, and add the boundary contracts listed above (ORB-C14 to C16, VEN-C16, C30 to C32); or
(b) drop per-contract activation and proof lists for in-tree components, since EON-C2 already keeps
in-tree proofs on their components and the legacy SHAs identify nothing in this repository.
Recommended: (b). The lists duplicate the indexes with revisions that cannot be resolved, and the
interfaces (ORBF, ORBS, EONW) carry the real compatibility edge. Either option is an EON-C2-adjacent
manifest change with the full Rust and Nix route.

title: Reserve Alt+H/J/K/L focus keys from popup keybindings, without failing old configs
description:
Lucca, 2026-10-31 ('agreed'): protect the focus keys. Today a popup bound to Alt+H/J/K/L takes the key (VEN-C20; docs/CONFIGURATION.md ~430-433) and, since fixed shortcuts cannot be rebound, focus movement in that direction loses its only key. Found during eon-56t4i review (a popup on Alt+K made the focus hint read 'H/L/J').

Shape (approved): reserve Alt+H, Alt+J, Alt+K and Alt+L like Alt+/ and Alt+0-9, but softly: Alt+/ and Alt+0-9 fail config load today ('popups.<id>.keybinding is reserved for an Eon shortcut', runtime/crates/eon-runtime/src/managed_environment.rs:1086-1116); H/J/K/L must NOT fail load, so an existing config keeps starting Eon after upgrade (EON-C28 / EON-C37 upgrade safety, configuration corpus test from eon-embg6). Instead the popup loads without a key, Eon shows a notice naming the popup and the key, and Alt+/ lists the popup without a shortcut. Use an existing notice path; if none fits a config-load warning, stop and report to eon-overseer.

Contract wording: drafted in the overseer conversation 2026-10-31, approved text recorded here before code (VEN-C20 two sentences + docs/CONFIGURATION.md paragraph). Tests: extend configured_popups_take_fixed_bindings_except_reserved_keys; a corpus config with a popup on Alt+K still loads. Rule 6: the reserved set is fixed product policy (escape hatch keys), recorded here.
close_reason: Alt+H/J/K/L reserved for focus: a configured popup on one loads without a key with a logged warning; Venus keeps the focus bindings. Proof and ledger in comments.

title: Evaluate Lauren Tan's pstack for Eon's agent workflow
description:
## Why

Lucca asked (2026-10-21) for an evaluation of pstack, Lauren Tan's (poteto) agent-workflow kit, for
work on Eon. pstack targets two weak spots this repository already has:

- **Verification.** Its `create-verification-skill` and `create-formal-verification-skill` write
  project-local skills that check a change against the real app or a formal property, and they show
  the check failing before handing off. Eon's installed proofs depend on recipes kept in agent
  memory (isolated capture, an Ubuntu VM with seat sway, wdotool priming), not on a skill in the
  repository. Orbit's Rust host, which owns the PTY, signals, reaping and the worker fault path, is
  the unproved half of Orbit (`eon-fony`).
- **Review.** Its `/interrogate` sends one diff to several models and sorts the findings. Eon's
  review loop runs through Starcompass's `converge` skill with Opus and Codex.

Decide which parts, if any, would make Eon's agents more correct or cheaper than what Eon already
has.

## Evidence

- Source: `https://github.com/cursor/plugins/tree/main/pstack` at `190d28736eff128ec94f502a22c7fe0c4b56cd37`
  (HEAD on 2026-10-21). MIT, Copyright (c) 2026 Lauren Tan. 172 files: about 50 skills
  (workflow skills, `principle-*` skills, `poteto-mode` playbooks), 2 agents (`poteto-agent`,
  `comment-sicko`), an optional `automations/benny` pack, and TypeScript helpers run under Bun in
  `skills/poteto-mode/scripts/` (`orch`, `watch-pr`, `check-plan`).
- Overview: https://flaviocopes.com/pstack. Its official target is Cursor. Claude Code and Codex
  load the `SKILL.md` files when they are copied in, but lose `/add-plugin`, `/setup-pstack`,
  per-subagent model roles and `/loop`. Community port for Claude Code and Codex:
  https://github.com/michael-denyer/pstack-claude.
- The skills that already cover the same ground live in Starcompass (`~/pjs/lab/starcompass/skills`):
  `converge`, `fresh-pass`, `fresh-eyes`, `fix-or-bead`, `prime`, `create-beads`, `handoff` and
  `stop-slop`. Repository policy lives in `AGENTS.md` and `docs/AGENT-PROTOCOLS.md`.
- Constraint: `AGENTS.md` "Implementation Languages" lets Eon add no TypeScript of its own, so
  pstack's helpers cannot be checked in here.

## Scope

In scope:
- Read pstack at the pinned commit. Classify each relevant piece as **adopt in Eon**, **propose to
  Starcompass**, or **reject**, with the reason and, where one exists, the Eon or Starcompass
  equivalent it would replace or extend. Priority pieces:
  1. `create-verification-skill` and `maintain-verification-skill`: would a generated `verify-eon`
     skill replace the memory-held installed-proof recipes?
  2. `create-formal-verification-skill`: on Orbit's host and worker fault and reap races (for
     example a TLA+ model). How would it sit beside `LAWS.bend` and `PROOF.bend`?
  3. `interrogate` and `arena` against `converge` and the Opus-plus-Codex review history.
  4. The `principle-*` skills and playbooks against `AGENTS.md` and the Starcompass protocols:
     report only gaps and conflicts, not overlap.
  5. `show-me-your-work` and `blast-radius` against Beads proof records.
- At most one trial, with Lucca's authorization: run the strongest candidate as a fresh agent on a
  representative, already-closed Eon task in a scratch worktree. Report how it behaved, without
  supplying the expected conclusion (AP-TEST-001).

Out of scope:
- Installing pstack into `~/.claude`, `.cursor` or this repository, checking in its TypeScript, or
  running Benny automations.
- Editing `AGENTS.md`, Starcompass skills or protocol imports. Adoption is a separate bead that
  Lucca approves.
- Model-routing defaults (Grok, Sol). They don't apply to this setup.

## Acceptance

- A verdict table on this bead covering at least the five priority pieces: piece, verdict, reason,
  equivalent, and proposed follow-up.
- A recommendation, with its reason, on whether anything is adopted, and where (Eon-local skill or
  Starcompass).
- Follow-up beads are proposed, not filed, until Lucca chooses.

## Verification

- Planning only: `br show` on this bead with the verdict comment, and `.beads/` after
  `br sync --flush-only`. A trial, if one runs, records its worktree revision, prompt and outcome.
  No runtime proof or profile refresh.

## Stop Conditions

- Stop for Lucca before installing anything, running a trial agent, or filing adoption beads.
- Stop if `main` of `cursor/plugins` has moved materially from the pinned commit. Evaluate at the
  pin and note the drift.

## Maintenance Notes

- Lucca chose Eon over Starcompass as this bead's home (2026-10-21), so the focus is Eon's own
  workflow. A piece worth spreading to other repositories goes to Starcompass as a proposal.
notes: prime-beads 2026-11-03: lowered to P3. Piece 3 is largely settled by eon-zypt (Codex on every code change, 2026-10-29) and converge. Highest-value piece is 1: a repository-held verify skill replacing memory-held installed-proof recipes (isolated capture, Ubuntu VM, rented Mac). Re-check the cursor/plugins pin for drift first.

title: Move create-column from Alt+Shift+M to Ctrl+Alt+M
description:
## Why

Lucca decided on 2026-10-22 to free Alt+Shift+M for the Eon command runner
(`eon-command-runner-uctp`). Nova users already press Alt Shift M for Nova's
command menu, and Eon's Alt+Shift popups already match Nova's (J Git, L Agent).
Creating a column moves to Ctrl+Alt+M. Ctrl+Alt is Eon's layout group: H/J/K/L
move panes, Ctrl+Alt+Shift+H/L move tabs, and at a tab's edge Ctrl+Alt+H/L
already opens a new column. Eon has no users yet, so the move costs no one any
muscle memory.

Rejected options:
- Keep Alt+Shift+M and give the runner Ctrl+Shift+M (the runner bead's
  original plan). The runner key would then match neither Nova nor any
  convention.
- Ctrl+Shift+P, the VS Code, Ghostty, WezTerm and Windows Terminal palette
  key, either alone or as a second key. It helps users from those tools,
  but Eon's first users come from Nova. A second key for one action adds a
  row to the shortcut viewer and hints bar and takes a key that popup
  configuration could otherwise use.
- Ctrl+Alt+P. No app uses it as a palette key, and it sits among Eon's
  pane-moving keys.

## Contract (approved by Lucca, 2026-10-22)

- EON-C8 (`docs/CONTRACTS.md`, "Venus maps Alt+Shift+M to it" in the
  create-column clause) and VEN-C8 (`venus/docs/CONTRACTS.md`, "Alt+Shift+M
  sends one non-repeating `CreateColumn`" and "Alt+Shift+M's
  40-terminal-column refusal") change only the key, from Alt+Shift+M to
  Ctrl+Alt+M. Behavior stays the same: one non-repeating `CreateColumn`, the
  40-terminal-column refusal, and Eon's four-column capacity refusal.
- Until `eon-command-runner-uctp` lands, nothing in Eon binds Alt+Shift+M, so
  it reaches the terminal program. The command runner bead then claims it.

## Evidence

- `venus/src/application/shortcuts.rs:187-193`: the fixed `Create column`
  binding (`KeyCode::KeyM`, `ALT_SHIFT`, `NativeShortcutAction::CreateColumn`).
  `CTRL_ALT` is defined at line 98. No Ctrl+Alt+M binding exists.
- `venus/src/application/shortcuts.rs:~837`: the test that maps Alt+Shift+M to
  `WorkspaceAction::CreateColumn`.
- `runtime/crates/eon-runtime/src/managed_environment.rs:1225`: the test that
  a popup may take a fixed Venus key lists "Alt+Shift+M" as its example.
- User docs: `README.md:51`, `docs/USAGE.md:115`,
  `venus/docs/INTERACTION.md:62`, `venus/docs/PRESENTATION.md:41`.
- `demo/record.rs` never presses Alt+Shift+M, so it needs no change.

## Scope

In scope:
- The fixed binding and its test in `venus/src/application/shortcuts.rs`. The
  shortcut viewer and hints bar take their key text from that table.
- The example key in the `managed_environment.rs` test, changed to Ctrl+Alt+M
  so it still names a fixed binding.
- EON-C8 and VEN-C8 text, the docs listed above, `CHANGELOG.md`, and
  `venus/CHANGELOG.md`.

Out of scope:
- The command runner and any Alt+Shift+M binding (`eon-command-runner-uctp`).
- `CreateColumn` semantics, EONW, and the 40-column or capacity refusals.
- Historical CHANGELOG entries, which stay as written.

## Acceptance

- In installed Eon, Ctrl+Alt+M creates a column right of the selected one,
  with the same refusals as before. Alt+Shift+M no longer creates a column.
- The shortcut viewer (Alt+/) and the hints bar show Ctrl+Alt+M for
  "Create column".
- A popup configured with `keybinding = "Ctrl+Alt+M"` takes the key, as it can
  take any other fixed Venus key.
- No current-state doc names Alt+Shift+M as the create-column key.

## Implementation Notes

1. The shared tree is busy. `eon-claude-chip-split-u3ik` had uncommitted edits
   in `venus/docs/CONTRACTS.md`, `docs/USAGE.md`, both CHANGELOGs and
   `demo/record.rs` on 2026-10-22, and `eon-zoom-selected-pane-e2pv` is
   adding a key. Check `git status` and coordinate before editing those files.
   Commit through a private index.

title: Keep window titles readable on light and translucent terminal backgrounds
description:
# Follow-up (P3): light-background contrast for pane, Agents and popup titles

P3 feature following the landed eon-whjhd. Owner: Venus. Portability: neutral.

## Problem

On a light terminal background, Venus title text still uses fixed palette colours:
- the selected pane's title and the Agents label use `PRIMARY_TEXT` (#eff4f8);
- other pane titles use `SECONDARY_TEXT`;
- popup titles use the same fixed colours.

They nearly vanish. A terminal sets a light background with OSC 11, so any light theme hits this.
The problem predates eon-whjhd: every title used fixed colours before. eon-whjhd gave only the
Stack labels contrast handling (`stack_label_color`).

## Evidence

- `captures/eon-whjhd-r1-light-1280x800-f16/` (stack3, two-columns) and
  `captures/eon-whjhd-r1-light-top-crop.png`:
  - the shell sets OSC 11 `#f4f4f4`;
  - "Agents" and "p1 Codex pane — long name…" are barely visible;
  - "Stack 1" / "Stack 2" read clearly.
- `captures/eon-whjhd-r2-light-noframes-top-crop.png`: the same with pane frames off.

## Earlier proposal (superseded by the landing decision below)

- Give pane, Agents and popup titles the same rule as `stack_label_color`:
  - keep the palette colour;
  - blend toward black only as far as 4.5:1 needs, judged against the terminal's own background
    colour (not an assumed desktop), so dark terminals at any `background_opacity` stay
    unchanged.
- Keep the selected/other/dead distinctions, as darker variants that keep their relative order.
- The pane-ID dimming (`pane_id_color`) must stay readable too.

## Proof

- Unit tests over dark and light fills and low opacities.
- Native captures on dark and light backgrounds, frames on and off.
- No contract text names the title colours. Check VEN-C8, VEN-C18 and VEN-C30 for wording before
  proposing any change.

## Added at landing of eon-whjhd (overseer, 2026-11-09)

Codex's round-3 re-check (~/.local/state/rota/runs/stacktabs-recheck2-codex-1/report.md) shows the limit of judging text against the terminal's own colour: with background_opacity below 1 the composite depends on the desktop, so a light terminal over a dark desktop, or a dark terminal over a white desktop, loses contrast whichever way the label colour is chosen. The fix for every title (Stack, pane, Agents, popup) is a treatment that survives compositing at both desktop extremes, such as a stable opaque or near-opaque label backing behind title text, or an outline or shadow. Prove at opacity 0.3, 0.5 and 1.0 over black and white desktops, light and dark terminals, frames on and off.

## Active acceptance

The landing decision above governs: cover Stack, pane, Agents and popup titles, pane-ID dimming and the neutral outline shared by notch/connected edges (overseer comment 6496, 2026-11-11). Keep selected/other/dead distinctions. Choose one compositing-safe treatment; the examples are alternatives, not a request for all of them. Prove readability at opacity 0.3/0.5/1.0 over black/white desktops, light/dark terminal fills, frames on/off; include notch and connected outlines. Record outline contrast separately from text. Use deterministic checks and one isolated native capture session; expose/document new user-facing values or record why fixed. No palette redesign or contract amendment is presumed.

title: Attention badges: no square under translucent rows, outline only in the worst case, and 1.0x font size; popup marker unchanged
description:
## Why

Lucca, 2026-11-12 (eon-desk), after eon-wuau8.7 landed (a83f3f7): "can we remove the spinners
background" and "can we make the spinners / markers bigger". His terminals use the default
`background_opacity = 0.8`. Under a translucent background, eon-wuau8.7 puts an opaque rounded
square (card colour adapted to 1.5:1) behind row badges, so he still sees a background behind
every spinner in the Agents sidebar and the inbox.

Approved in the desk:
1. "ok. if needed we can add a trick like an outline the markers that would make them readable
   even in their worst case scenario". Remove the square. If a worst case still needs help, use a
   thin outline around the glyph, not a backing shape.
2. "cool, but im talking about just the spinners / attention, the popup marker is perfect already".
   Make attention badges bigger; the popup marker stays exactly as it is.

## Design

- No backing square under any translucent row, at any opacity.
- Glyph colour: adapt for 3:1 against the worst-case visible surface. That's the row's card colour
  composited at the configured `background_opacity` over both a black and a white desktop, the
  same two-surface approach bar corner badges already use. At the default 0.8, a plain adapted
  colour should reach 3:1. Measure it, don't assume.
- Worst-case fallback, only when no single glyph colour can reach 3:1 against both extremes
  (low opacity): draw a thin outline (halo) around the glyph's own shape in a contrasting tone,
  about 1 physical pixel, never a filled shape behind it. Record the opacity threshold where the
  outline starts.
- Stale badges keep their 0.45 alpha dimming, as today.
- Size: attention badges (spinner dots and the other attention glyphs, everywhere they draw:
  sidebar rows, inbox, tabs, edge and session-label badges) go from 0.75× to 1.0× the font size
  (`badge_size`, venus/src/scene/tokens.rs:178-181). Check that a 1.0× badge still fits line 1
  of a two-line row, tab badges and bar corner badges without clipping, overlap or shifting the
  row height. Note anywhere it needs a per-surface cap.
- Popup marker: unchanged (size, shape, position). Lucca: "the popup marker is perfect already".
- Fixed values, no new configuration key (rule 6): record why in the bead. Sizes are tuned once
  Lucca sees them live.

## Contract and docs

VEN-C30 carries eon-wuau8.7's square wording. Replace it with the no-backing and outline-fallback
wording; Lucca approved the direction above, and the implementer shows him the exact text.
Update venus/docs/PRESENTATION.md (~:534-543), docs/CONFIGURATION.md (~:318-330, the
`background_opacity` paragraph), and the changelogs.

## Evidence

- a83f3f7 (eon-wuau8.7): venus/src/render/chrome.rs badge drawing and backing,
  venus/src/render/palette.rs, venus/src/scene/tokens.rs (`badge_backing_radius`, `badge_size`).
- ~/.config/eon/config.toml sets no `background_opacity`, so the default 0.8 applies.

## Acceptance

- At opacity 0.8 over a black and a white desktop: no square behind any badge, and glyphs meet 3:1.
- At low opacity (for example 0.3) the outline appears only where the plain colour can't reach 3:1.
- Badges are 1.0× the font size on every surface, nothing clips, and row heights are unchanged.
- The popup marker renders exactly as before; its test stays green.

## Verification

Scene and render tests for colour adaptation at 0.8 and 0.3, outline triggering, and badge size
per surface; `nix develop -c eon-test` (not inside a live Eon session); fmt and clippy. Installed
captures over a black and a white backdrop at the default opacity, and Lucca's live look.

title: Colour the CPU chip by the number it shows; hover gives the 30-second average
description:
Lucca, 2026-10-31: the CPU chip read 'CPU 99%' with no colour. Cause (by design, eon-hjtns, cac461c): the number is the 2-second CPU use, the orange follows the cpu_average_seconds (30 s) average reaching cpu_warning_percent (90); measured that moment: 30 s average 45%. People read that as broken.

Approved shape (Lucca 'ok' 2026-10-31 to options A + E):
- A: the chip turns orange when the number it shows (2-second CPU use) is at least cpu_warning_percent. No red, as today. Bursts stay visible (Lucca: burst info matters).
- E: hover and accessibility text also give the average over cpu_average_seconds, e.g. 'CPU 99% now, 45% over 30 s'.
- Keep cpu_average_seconds (it now drives only the hover/accessibility average), so no config migration; update its comment in docs/CONFIGURATION.md and the bar paragraph there (~lines 66-67, 190-198).
- Rejected: a hold after the drop (mismatch), showing the average as the number (hides bursts), a sparkline (bar space).

Contract: docs/CONTRACTS.md ~2814 (cpu_warning_percent / cpu_average_seconds wording) and any VEN-C21 / venus/docs/PRESENTATION.md sentence on CPU colour. Wording that states exactly the approved shape is approved; anything beyond goes to eon-overseer for Lucca. RAM colouring is unchanged.

Acceptance: tests show orange at a 2-second value at or above the threshold and neutral below it regardless of the average; hover/accessibility text carries the average; installed isolated screenshot with a lowered threshold shows the orange chip.

- The generation log (~/.local/state/eon/logs/g1-caca13d0…log) has no entry for it.
- Source (edge 1ce839f): `venus/src/transport.rs:484-504`. When the per-attachment event queue goes
  past `EVENT_QUEUE_CAPACITY` (256 events), `FRAME_QUEUE_CAPACITY` (2 unreplaced frames), or
  `EVENT_QUEUE_BYTE_CAPACITY` (3 max payloads), the queue is cleared and replaced with
  `TransportEvent::Lost`, and the transport stops. Recovery afterwards presumably came from the
  workspace column retry (`retry_column_views`, VEN-C3). Confirm it.

## Unknown, to establish first

- Which bound tripped: event count, unreplaced frames, or bytes. Why the queue filled at all: the
  Venus event loop falling behind the reader thread (for example while laying out a large frame),
  or a burst of non-frame events that coalescing doesn't replace.
- How long p8 stayed unavailable, and whether input typed meanwhile was lost.
- Reproduce in isolation: a headless Venus attached to an Orbit terminal that prints a few MB of
  long wrapped lines in one write (and a Codex-like full-screen TUI redraw). Record which bound trips.

## Expected

A burst of output never costs a pane its connection. Venus applies backpressure or drops
superseded frames and catches up from Orbit's current state (the latest revision), without a
"connection lost" notice or a visible freeze. The bounds stay, because they protect memory, but
reaching them leads to a resync to the current frame, not a loss.

## Contract

VEN-C3 (transient client recovery) and VEN-C4 (bounded explicit failure UX). The Orbit side,
ORB-C slow-consumer behavior, needs checking too. Making queue saturation resync instead of lose
the connection is a contract change: bring Lucca the exact wording before code.

## Portability disposition

neutral (transport queue and client state; no platform API).

## Scope

In scope: diagnosing which bound trips and why; the Venus transport/queue change, so that
saturation resyncs to the newest state; the contract text; a Venus suite regression test that
floods the queue and checks the attachment survives and shows the latest revision;
`venus/CHANGELOG.md` and `CHANGELOG.md`. Out of scope: Orbit wire changes, unless the diagnosis
shows Orbit must send a checkpoint on request (then stop and bring Lucca the wire change).

## Acceptance

- The isolated reproduction no longer shows "Orbit connection lost". The pane keeps updating and
  ends on the terminal's final screen.
- Memory stays bounded: queue bytes never exceed the existing byte bound.
- One isolated installed dogfood observation with a burst-printing program.
close_reason: Venus applies backpressure when its Orbit event queue is full; burst-while-scrolling no longer drops the attachment (VEN-C3/VEN-C4)

comments.author: lucca
comments.text:
Diagnosis (2026-10-22, edge f033767, code trace; no isolated run yet):
- Bound: FRAME_QUEUE_CAPACITY (2 unreplaced frames), venus/src/transport.rs:485-495. Output alone cannot trip it, because a newer frame replaces the queued one when only Accepted or WheelOutcome::TerminalRouted sit between them. Orbit sends no Metadata on the attachment.
- Cause: during an active Venus scroll (wheel, trackpad or momentum), drive_terminal_scroll runs after every drain (application.rs:3479). Each drained Frame rebases the scroll and clears the preview (scroll.rs:216-224, 266; model.rs:333), so Venus sends a new PreviewVertical per frame revision. Orbit answers each with VerticalPreview between its frames. With the event loop busy, the queue then holds Frame, VerticalPreview, Frame, VerticalPreview, and the next Frame becomes Lost. ScrollOutcome, SelectionFinished, CopiedText, ClipboardWrite (OSC 52) and Failure also block replacement. With enough of them, the 256-event cap does the same.
- Recovery: Lost resets the retry (application.rs:1371), so no timer re-attaches. A workspace change re-attached it: tab or pane selection, a popup, the column set, or the pane's live/endpoint changing (application.rs:1507-1522, 1302-1306). Which one Lucca hit is unknown.
- Orbit side: ORB-C7 already handles a slow reader. Its OutputQueue replaces unstarted frames and previews (socket.rs:246-266) and detaches only past output_bound, which Venus sees as RetryableLoss and retries.
- Proposed shape: backpressure. When a push would exceed a bound, the Venus reader stops reading until the event loop drains, and Orbit's ORB-C7 coalescing keeps the newest frame. No wire change. Awaiting Lucca's approval of the VEN-C3/VEN-C4 wording.

title: Decide: update a running window in place without losing its terminals or layout
description:
## Why

Lucca, 2026-10-24: "maybe we should open a bead to consider 'in-place' updating. supposedly, if a
eon update does not touch orbit, could we not replace the window without losing information from the
old window?" At filing, every profile refresh leaves running windows on the old build until the user
closes them, which ends their terminals; this session alone asked him to restart windows after each
of six landings.

## Original baseline (historical; current evidence below)

- EON-C11 (docs/CONTRACTS.md:1080): a generation's identity is the `g1-` hash of Eon's source tree,
  so any change makes a new generation. Older live generations stay discoverable and presentable only
  with the exact same EONW and component graph; otherwise `eon attach GENERATION` delegates to the old
  build. Present never replaces the live Venus process, Orbit attachment or terminal.
- Terminals live in per-session Orbit host processes (`yazelix-orbit serve <gen dir>/session-N.sock
  --management-v2 ...`), children of the supervisor, which reaps them (Orbit owns direct-child
  reaping). Their sockets live in the generation's runtime directory.
- Recovery after a supervisor restart (EON-C15) keeps terminals but projects them all into `t1`, so the
  layout (tabs, columns, popups, selection) is lost.
- Terminals carry `EON_TERMINAL`; inherited `EON_WINDOW_RUNTIME_DIR` selects their window namespace. Packaging sets `EON_SESSION_BIN` to the build's `libexec/eon/bin` (flake.nix:772), and product.rs:181 passes it as `ManagedPrograms.shell_bin`. Runtime prepends that directory when preparing PATH (managed_environment.rs:1644; sessions.rs:1880). Which `eon` an old terminal runs depends on its actual shell PATH order and setup; observe the resolved executable and its protocol in the relevant environment before asserting old-build or new-profile routing. The invoked CLI chooses its EONW.
- eon-newer-build-notice-byd2 (P2) tells a window that a newer Eon is installed; this bead would be
  the action behind that notice.

## Original candidate comparison (subsequent direction approved below)

The real condition is not "Orbit untouched" but "the running Orbit hosts stay compatible": they keep
running their old binary anyway, so what matters is that the new supervisor and Venus still speak the
running hosts' management and terminal protocols (ORB versions), and that the supervisor can take over
their ownership.

Candidate shape (to compare at the reference gate):
1. Re-exec in place: the old supervisor serializes its state (workspace set and layout, ID allocator,
   attention, run records, Venus presentation state) to an inherited fd, then `execve`s the new
   build's supervisor binary with a resume flag. Same PID, so the Orbit hosts stay its children (no
   reaping gap) and listening sockets can be inherited. Comparable: nginx binary upgrade, systemd
   `daemon-reexec`, HAProxy seamless reload.
2. Venus restarts on the new build and presents the restored layout (on Wayland a new process means a
   new surface, so the window closes and reopens; terminals, scrollback and layout survive).
3. Refuse and fall back to today's behaviour (keep the old window, show the notice) when the protocols
   differ, with a clear reason.

## Original questions (answered by approval comment 5546; canonical text remains draft)

- EON-C11 identity: a generation whose supervisor binary changes in place. Contract change.
- EONW: old terminals' `eon` (old build) talking to a new supervisor; version negotiation or a
  terminal-environment refresh.
- Trigger: automatic on profile refresh, a notice button, or `eon update` per window.
- Platform: execve and fd inheritance are POSIX; keep it out of Venus (portability disposition).

## Current state and next step (2e93c69, 2026-11-12)

- Lucca's 2026-11-04 "agreed" approved comment 5546's six recommendations: explicit installed
  target and stale-origin guard; exact Orbit/control/checkpoint refusal; Wayland reopen retaining
  terminals/layout; lifetime identity with separate active/creation builds; cross-EONW through an
  independent update.sock without workspace decoder shims; S1 first, then fresh canonical-text
  and later-scope approval. The full approved direction/draft/review stays in comments 5544-5546.
- The command is eon window update ID|all, per the overseer's 2026-11-09 decision under Lucca's
  "auto-decide" (comment 6057). eon update installs updates (EON-C41).
- S1 eon-t3fyd.1 is CLOSED, with 2026-11-05 GO WITH CONDITIONS; it is no longer awaited.
  Its full report/reviews constrain follow-on work: helper-child quiescing/reaping, bounded lease
  drain, launch-time environment, distinct component paths, restore/identity/management failure
  injection, correct pending-picker/layout roundtrip, incomplete gap/reap timing, and unexercised
  Update reply. This proves a mechanism, not the product contract; never copy the disposable probe
  into production or drop the conditions because the spike closed.
- EON-C11 starts at docs/CONTRACTS.md:2329; EONW is v40 (v40.rs:20). Current owning-build Routing,
  the window command family and per-window sessions postdate the draft and must be reconciled
  with its old-CLI behavior. Original numeric citations above are historical, not current anchors.
- Venus-only reload now exists (EON-C11 :2548, eon-u199d.1/.3), including same-build config
  reread. It leaves Runtime and generation unchanged and does not complete full adoption.
- Product supplies EON_SESSION_BIN (eon/crates/eon/src/product.rs:223); session_path is at
  runtime/crates/eon-runtime/src/managed_environment.rs:2035. Observe actual shell PATH and
  command resolution; the prefix alone is not proof.

Decision/planning only. eon-t3fyd is deferred past v0.2.0 by the overseer's 2026-11-10 decision.
No S2-S5 filing or implementation is authorized here. Review S1's conditions, reconcile today's
Routing/per-window model/reload, and bring Lucca the revised canonical draft and fresh-session
split. Reconsider the old eon-hyil8 prerequisite against today's model while retaining the owner
audit. The S1 review calls for S3 encode/validate vs wiring, S4b ownership vs quiescing/failure,
and S5 Venus replacement vs CLI/proof to be separate sessions.

Retain the inspected-revision comparison of herdr-core drain-by-build, herdr handover, nginx,
systemd daemon-reexec and HAProxy, and the owner trace for host reaping, generation directory,
listener/lock/lease ownership and EONW after adoption. Preserve the live-terminal/layout and
spike-first acceptance; S1's completed evidence now supplies the spike. Lucca's "we dont want
legacy code, brother" constrains proposals, not authority to remove current Routing.
Portability: POSIX exec/fd mechanisms in Runtime; only native Linux Wayland is exercised.
Stop before canonical edits or runtime action; fresh approval is still required.

Lucca approves or revises draft and split. Planning route; stop before contract or code.
notes: Direction approved by Lucca 2026-11-04 ("agreed"). S1 eon-t3fyd.1 is closed with GO WITH CONDITIONS; fresh canonical-text/follow-on-split approval remains required. eon-t3fyd is deferred past v0.2.0.

comments.author: lucca
comments.text:
# Opus gate: eon-1bq8

**Verdict: PASS WITH FIXES.** The evidence holds; the update policy needs fixes.

## Citations (tree 83103ff)

| Claim | Citation | Holds |
| --- | --- | --- |
| One Venus per supervisor | supervisor.rs:1171 | yes |
| EONW 31, mgmt v5, ORBS 14, ORBF 3 | v31.rs:19; sessions.rs:1862; eon-v5.json:43-45 | yes |
| Orbit is a direct child | sessions.rs:1648 | yes (setsid only in the PTY child) |
| Acquired session has `child: None` | sessions.rs:542, :1692 | yes |
| Exact-PID WNOHANG reap, ECHILD accepted | sessions.rs:1931, :2052 | yes; there is no SIGCHLD handler, so exec opens no reaping gap |
| Generation = hash of the assembly digest | generation.rs:36; product.rs:13 | yes |
| Bind rejects a live owner | control.rs:462 | yes |
| Per-generation lock, held | supervisor.rs:2130, :841 | yes |
| Component-generation equality | sessions.rs:319 | yes, and the value is the generation ID (supervisor.rs:1041; CONTRACTS.md:1935) |
| Exact endpoint checks | sessions.rs:352, :359 | yes |
| Presentation needs an exact graph | supervisor.rs:332, :345 | yes |
| CLI refuses a different EONW | control.rs:330, :408 | yes |
| Terminals pin their own `eon` | product.rs:181; flake.nix:772, :880; sessions.rs:1878 | yes |
| Launcher record is not a GC root | generation.rs:79 | yes |
| Venus exits on EOF | application.rs:6076 | yes |
| Venus exit dismisses pending pairs | supervisor.rs:2116 | yes |

## Findings

1. **High: the exact-EONW gate refuses most updates.**
   - EONW went from v10 (10-16) to v31 (11-04), about 21 bumps in 19 days. Most refreshes would be refused.
   - The pin rationale in C10 inverts after an Update: the pinned old `eon` then mismatches its own window.
   - *Fix:* quantify this. Offer the alternative of updating across EONW, where old terminals' `eon` fails honestly through the existing control.rs:330 error and names the installed path. That is not a shim. Ask Lucca.
2. **High: `eon update` typed in a window downgrades it.**
   - Every Eon terminal's bare `eon` is the old build, including new panes (C10:1139). Typed in a window, Update is a no-op before an update and a revert after one.
   - *Fix:* refuse when the invoked build equals the caller terminal's origin build and differs from the active build. That build is stale by construction, so no version ordering is needed. Alternatively, sequence byd2's discovery with S5.
3. **Medium: the fd inventory has gaps.**
   - It misses Venus's own EONW subscription (venus/src/transport.rs:581) and the Venus stderr relay pipe (supervisor.rs:563). After exec, old Venus writes get EPIPE, and `eprintln!` panics on that.
   - It also misses CLI connections accepted but not yet answered.
   - *Fix:* add these to step 3 and to S1.
4. **Medium: the C15 draft is redundant.** The component generation already is the generation ID, so with a fixed lifetime ID today's equality check still holds. Drop "recorded host membership" and keep `origin_build` as inventory only.
5. **Medium: lifetime IDs lose single-instance-per-build.** Two concurrent launches of one build could each start a lifetime. S2 needs a namespace launch lock and a race test.
6. **Medium: Q11 is researchable.** Nix GC on Linux treats store paths found in `/proc/*/environ`, maps and exe as roots. Old shells' PATH names the old session bin, so the old CLI likely survives GC. Verify this in S1 with `--print-roots`, then drop C10's profile-retention clause.
7. **Low:** C39 must *replace* "STREAM identifies one supervisor process" (CONTRACTS.md:4154). Consider having `pane wait` resume on `updating`.
8. **Low:** C11 does not cover a post-exec restore failure. Name the outcome: C15 recovery with orphaned hosts.
9. **Split:** the order is spike-first and serial, and each slice is one session, which is good.
   - The layout and pending-picker checks need checkpoint code. Move them from S1 to S3 and add exec-gap timing to S1.
   - Re-split S2 after eon-hyil8 lands.
10. **Questions:** eleven is too many under "ask only MAJOR".
    - Self-answer Q5, Q6, Q7 and Q9. Research Q11.
    - Keep Q1 merged with Q10, plus Q2, Q3, Q4 and Q8.
    - Add one question: should Update cross EONW bumps (finding 1)?

The drafts add no aliases or shims. Failures keep terminals live.

## View

Same-PID re-exec is the right mechanism. Reaping by exact-PID polling, the absence of a SIGCHLD handler and Orbit hosts held as `child: None` make it cheap, and untouched hosts respect every owner. The weakness is policy, not mechanism. Exact EONW equality plus a pinned old `eon` would make Update rarely usable and easy to downgrade by accident. Fix findings 1 and 2 before S1 is approved.

## Re-check (revised 001-decision.md, 1115 lines)

| # | Finding | Status | Evidence in revision |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 1 | Exact-EONW gate | **Resolved** | Recommends cross-EONW Update (lines 21, 124-138) with the v10→v31 data. It also catches a gap I missed: a new-EONW CLI cannot reach an old supervisor through `resolve_workspace`. It proposes a small private `update.sock` exchange with its own version (141-162; S4a). That is a new lifecycle boundary for approval, not a workspace shim; S4a is dropped if Lucca picks equal-EONW. |
| 2 | `eon update` revert trap | **Resolved** | Refuses with `stale-update-command` when the caller's origin build equals the target and differs from the active build. Unknown origin also refuses, and no override flag is added (44, 167-178; C11 486; C10 600). |
| 3 | fd and connection inventory | **Resolved** | Step 3 classifies every fd. It ends Venus's subscription and CLI subscribers in the old codec, finishes CLI replies before exec, carries the Update reply connection, keeps the stderr read end and measures backpressure. It also corrects the panic claim: the current Venus helper ignores write errors (`application.rs:5456`). S1 acceptance mirrors all of it. |
| 4 | Redundant C15 | **Resolved** | C15 now says the component generation stays the lifetime ID and existing checks are unchanged; `origin_build` is inventory only. |
| 5 | Namespace launch lock | **Resolved** | C11 clause plus an S2 race test (456, 804). |
| 6 | GC roots | **Resolved** | Researched: Nix's Linux scanner reads store paths from `/proc/PID/environ`. The C10 profile-retention clause is gone, and S1 verifies with `--print-roots`. |
| 7 | C39 STREAM wording | **Resolved** | Replaces the sentence. Rejecting `pane wait` auto-resume is reasoned: across EONW it would need the old codec. |
| 8 | Restore failure | **Resolved** | `update-restore-failed`: leases are released without Stop and hosts are orphaned, then recovered under C15 (358, 549). |
| 9 | Split | **Resolved** | Layout and picker checks move to S3. S1 adds exec-gap timing and S4a is split out. S2 is re-split after eon-hyil8. |
| 10 | Questions | **Resolved** | Six questions remain, all MAJOR: trigger and guard, Orbit/checkpoint mismatch, Wayland reopen, lifetime identity, cross-EONW, approve S1 only. Q2 is close to self-answerable but harmless. |

**EON_SESSION_BIN statements hold:**
- `flake.nix:772` sets it to `${out}/libexec/eon/bin`.
- `product.rs:181` reads it into `shell_bin`.
- `sessions.rs:1878-1879` sets Orbit's PATH through `session_path`.
- `managed_environment.rs:1644` prepends `shell_bin` for the managed shell and tool commands.

The new caveat is correct: these lines prove the PATH prefix, not what a shell resolves after its startup files. S1 observes `command -v eon`. One unstated detail is consistent with the draft: `flake.nix:932` unsets the variable for eonbase, and Update excludes eonbase.

**New, low (open):** C11's "Update refuses if the target build already belongs to another live lifetime" is harmless today, because each window has its own namespace (`windows.rs:221`). Under eon-hyil8's shared namespace, it would refuse a common flow: refresh the profile, open a new window, then update the old one. Name this consequence in Q4 or settle it in the S2 reconciliation with hyil8. It does not block S1.

**Residual risk (not a defect):** the private checkpoint and `update.sock` versions must match exactly, so their churn now decides how often Update is available. S1/S3 should report how often those versions would have changed over recent history.

**Re-check verdict: PASS.** All ten findings are resolved. One low item stays open for S2 and the hyil8 reconciliation.

# eon-1bq8 — Update a live window without losing its work

Draft for Lucca, 2026-11-04. **Decision proposal, not approved contract text.**
Coordinator: `eon-overseer`. Inspected Eon tree: detached
`83103ffbf134ce36dc75c447a62081b1c96ea1b5`, initially clean.

Lucca's choice, relayed in this task: **“1 agreed”**, 2026-11-04, selects this
decision as the next big step. It does not approve a mechanism or contract.
The bead also records **“we dont want legacy code, brother”**: no new alias,
protocol adapter, redirecting CLI, or multi-version compatibility layer is
proposed below. All implementation beads are drafts; none was filed.

## Recommendation

Approve a **spike of same-PID Runtime re-exec, with unchanged Orbit hosts and
an explicitly replaced Venus**, then decide whether to implement it from the
spike's evidence. Keep the runtime directory and all Orbit socket identities
fixed. Separate a generation's lifetime identity from the build currently
controlling it. Require exact accepted Orbit protocols and checkpoint format;
otherwise leave the old window running and explain the refusal. **Recommend
allowing EONW to change across Update**, subject to Lucca's choice below: the
replacement Runtime/Venus use the target EONW, and old terminal CLIs fail
honestly on incompatible workspace commands. No old codec or CLI shim.

**Coordination constraint discovered during overlap checks:** `eon-hyil8`
records Lucca's approved 2026-11-04 direction to Eon-owned sessions and one
supervisor per generation serving many Venus windows (`br --no-db show
eon-hyil8`, read 2026-11-04). The inspected tree still has one Venus per
supervisor (`runtime/crates/eon-runtime/src/supervisor.rs:1171`). Re-exec is
therefore an **owning-runtime update**, not an independently versioned update
of one window within a shared supervisor. A window argument identifies its
owner; every attached window of that owner must move with it. Keep all
session-to-window mappings. Do not implement a second per-window Runtime to
preserve the old topology. S1 can investigate the current mechanism, but S2–S5
must reconcile with the approved session-ownership contract before product
implementation. The contract text below proposes that owner-wide scope for
Lucca explicitly; it does not decide the separate session redesign.

Make the first trigger an explicit command run from the **target build's
installed executable**, `eon update`, with explicit window targeting available.
Installing or refreshing a profile alone must not restart a window. A later
notice button can invoke that same operation; its existing owning bead is
`eon-newer-build-notice-byd2`, not another notice implementation. Prevent the
pinned-command revert trap: if a validated caller's terminal-origin build
equals the invoked target but differs from the active build, refuse as
`stale-update-command`, naming the invoked path and the active launcher path
when known. Do not infer a source-digest ordering. An explicit invocation from
outside Eon can still select an older target under the same safety gates.

This moves Runtime, Venus, and the policy for future terminals to the target
build. Existing Orbit hosts and existing programs continue executing their
original binaries until their terminals end. It therefore does not instantly
apply an Orbit engine fix to an already-running terminal. That limit is
unavoidable if its authoritative terminal state and PTY are to survive without
an entirely different Orbit upgrade contract; Orbit currently excludes
survival across its own restart (`orbit/docs/CONTRACTS.md:49`, `:62`).

The smallest credible design is not “exec and recover”: recovery currently
loses grouping and layout (`docs/CONTRACTS.md:1939`). It is an explicit
checkpoint/restore transition that keeps the current process as reaper.
The spike must falsify this shape before product implementation starts.

## Reference gate: current Eon owner trace

All Eon file references in this document are relative to the inspected tree
above. They describe source and accepted boundaries, **not a runtime experiment
performed for this decision**. Older line numbers and protocol values in the
bead are historical: this tree uses **EONW 31**, **management 5**, **ORBS 14**,
**ORBF 3** (`runtime/crates/eon-workspace-protocol/src/v31.rs:19`,
`runtime/crates/eon-runtime/src/sessions.rs:1862`,
`components/eon-v5.json:43`, `:44`, `:45`).

| Invariant or resource | Actual owner and present behavior | Consequence for update |
| --- | --- | --- |
| PTY, running shell/program, terminal parser, history and presentation authority | Orbit owns terminal authority and client-loss survival; its Rust host owns the PTY child (`orbit/AGENTS.md:14`; `orbit/docs/CONTRACTS.md:49`, `:85`). Orbit reaps the direct PTY child before successful shutdown (`orbit/docs/CONTRACTS.md:718`, `:725`). | Leave every live Orbit host running. No PTY transfer, parser reconstruction, or synthetic terminal resurrection. |
| Orbit host parent and reaper | Runtime spawns Orbit (`runtime/crates/eon-runtime/src/sessions.rs:1648`). Successful acquisition returns a management-backed `RunningSession` whose `child` is `None` (`:527`, `:542`, `:1692`); completion can reap the exact recorded PID with `waitpid(WNOHANG)`, accepting `ECHILD` for non-children (`:1925`, `:1931`, `:2052`). Runtime's loop reconciles ended sessions (`runtime/crates/eon-runtime/src/supervisor.rs:1104`, `:1431`). | Distinguish the two levels of reaping. Orbit still reaps programs; the same Runtime PID can still reap its Orbit children after exec. Reconstructing Rust `Child` objects is not a prerequisite for Orbit hosts, but preserving exact validated child identity and completion reconciliation is. |
| Management ownership and presentation permission | Each session holds a nonblocking Unix management lease, its immutable `LiveIdentity`, pending request and naming state (`runtime/crates/eon-runtime/src/sessions.rs:868`). Acquisition checks the exact identity, record and endpoint objects (`orbit/src/management.rs:346`). Lease loss revokes the named Venus, but does not stop the terminal (`orbit/docs/CONTRACTS.md:815`, `:821`). | Prefer inheriting existing leases across exec, after completing their in-flight request. Do not race a second manager for Acquire or silently drop reply bytes. A resumed owner must name the replacement Venus through existing `AttachAllow`. |
| Generation identity | The build script digests source paths and contents (`eon/crates/eon/build.rs:1`, `:21`, `:30`, `:42`); product passes that assembly digest (`eon/crates/eon/src/product.rs:13`); Runtime hashes it into `g1-…` (`runtime/crates/eon-runtime/src/generation.rs:36`). C11 makes it build-derived (`docs/CONTRACTS.md:1618`). | Changing the controlling build while claiming that identity still means “current source tree” would be false. Separate lifetime identity and active build identity explicitly; do not silently reinterpret existing JSON. |
| Directory, listener and lifecycle lock | Directory is `ROOT/generations/GENERATION` (`runtime/crates/eon-runtime/src/generation.rs:60`); launch selects it and `eon.sock` (`runtime/crates/eon-runtime/src/supervisor.rs:160`). Listener bind rejects a live owner (`runtime/crates/eon-runtime/src/control.rs:462`); its destructor removes only its recorded socket inode (`:540`). A per-generation lock lives in the namespace root (`runtime/crates/eon-runtime/src/supervisor.rs:2130`) and is retained throughout supervision (`:841`). | Carry the live listener and lock file descriptions through exec. Resume must bypass ordinary bind/recovery and normal teardown. Moving the directory or rebinding listeners is unnecessary and introduces races. |
| Orbit endpoints and records | Orbit receives its presentation path, session/run ID and component generation at spawn (`runtime/crates/eon-runtime/src/sessions.rs:1858`). Component generation already equals Runtime's generation ID (`runtime/crates/eon-runtime/src/supervisor.rs:1041`; `docs/CONTRACTS.md:1935`). Validation compares that value and management generation (`runtime/crates/eon-runtime/src/sessions.rs:319`), exact presentation naming and management pathname (`:337`, `:352`), and endpoint objects (`:359`). | With a fixed lifetime ID, the existing component-generation equality remains correct across updates. Do not rename paths, rewrite live identities or add a host-membership authorization map. `origin_build` is inventory and stale-command policy data, never management authority. |
| Workspace/layout state | Runtime owns workspaces, shown workspace, ID allocator, request histories and recency (`runtime/crates/eon-runtime/src/workspace.rs:189`). Tabs own columns, expanded panes, selected column, popups and covered/selected popup (`:84`, `:92`); workspaces own tab order and active tab (`:850`). | A public snapshot alone is not a complete checkpoint. Carry private counters, pending pickers, names, directories, recency and deduplication state as well as visible layout. No new PTYs may be launched to reconstruct existing panes. |
| Other state and workers | Supervisor holds window/start identity, sessions, Venus, attention, labels, agents, notices, quotas and subscribers (`runtime/crates/eon-runtime/src/supervisor.rs:1162`). Attention has an epoch and sidebar state (`runtime/crates/eon-runtime/src/attention.rs:244`); running-window scans use a worker thread (`runtime/crates/eon-runtime/src/running.rs:212`, `:240`). | Checkpoint authoritative values; recreate caches and workers. Quiesce helper work before exec and audit every inherited fd. Preserve timestamps as values, not raw pointers, Rust layouts, threads, mutexes or serialized `Instant` representations. |
| Current presentation compatibility | Runtime validation demands the expected generation, exact EONW, and equal component report (`runtime/crates/eon-runtime/src/supervisor.rs:332`). A runtime report carries one generation and component report, not a separate active build or per-host build inventory (`:2798`; `runtime/crates/eon-workspace-protocol/src/v31.rs:713`). | Current “present compatible” is insufficient for update. Add an explicit transition and truthful live inventory; never make the target manifest falsely describe old Orbit binaries as newly launched. |

### Old terminals' CLI and EONW

The runtime does not read an `EON_SESSION_BIN` variable itself, but **the product
does**: it supplies `managed.shell_bin` from that variable
(`eon/crates/eon/src/product.rs:181`). Nix sets it to the package's managed bin
directory (`flake.nix:772`), which links `eon` back to that package
(`flake.nix:880`). Orbit spawn prepends that directory to the terminal PATH
(`runtime/crates/eon-runtime/src/sessions.rs:1878`;
`runtime/crates/eon-runtime/src/managed_environment.rs:1512`, `:1644`). This
establishes the supplied PATH prefix, **not the executable a running shell
actually resolves after its startup files and PATH changes**. A user/shell/script
can override PATH or invoke another executable explicitly; C10 says so
(`docs/CONTRACTS.md:1139`). The bead's earlier “no variable in Runtime” observation
must not be read as “no pinned terminal CLI exists.” S1 observes `command -v
eon`, effective PATH and resolved executable identity in old and new terminals;
do not assume either that every old shell stays pinned or that profile refresh
automatically changes its command.

`EON_TERMINAL` is a session/run token (`runtime/crates/eon-runtime/src/sessions.rs:1585`,
`:1870`), not a build selector. `EON_WINDOW_RUNTIME_DIR` selects a namespace
(`runtime/crates/eon-runtime/src/windows.rs:34`;
`runtime/crates/eon-runtime/src/generation.rs:233`). Caller discovery scans
generations and asks which validates that token
(`runtime/crates/eon-runtime/src/generation.rs:308`, `:336`). It still requires
the invoked CLI's exact EONW: different versions fail
(`runtime/crates/eon-runtime/src/control.rs:408`).

**Proposed disposition:** do not inject shell commands, mutate program
environments, rewrite PATH, or add a per-window forwarding executable. Keep
the lifetime and caller token valid. If EONW still matches, existing commands
continue through that wire contract while their executable remains available;
their help and command set remain old. If EONW changed, the old workspace CLI
must fail through the existing incompatibility classification
(`runtime/crates/eon-runtime/src/control.rs:330`, `:408`), showing both versions
and **the path of the invoked old CLI**, with the recorded active launcher path
as advice when available. The current error does not yet name that executable
path; that is a proposed diagnostic addition, not a claimed existing behavior.
No automatic delegation, re-exec, environment injection or old codec is added.

The earlier exact-EONW recommendation would make this feature too restrictive
for the observed development pace. Historical revision
`34904c81b1e7abe0be2848169909baba8bbc22a4` introduced v10 on 2026-10-16
(`runtime/crates/eon-workspace-protocol/src/v10.rs:9` at that revision);
`ff6aeb4a86597209020d376f848726e50c155f5c` introduced v31 on 2026-11-04
(`runtime/crates/eon-workspace-protocol/src/v31.rs:19`). That is 21 version
increments over 19 calendar days, about one per day. This is not a measured
percentage of profile refreshes, but any window spanning one such bump would
be refused under the original policy. Avoid preserving an old CLI's usability
at the price of commonly refusing the requested running-window update.

| EONW policy | Benefit | Cost and recommendation |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Require equal old/new EONW | Old CLI keeps its existing commands; initial trigger can use EONW. | Refuses every update spanning a workspace-wire bump. Keep as the simpler alternative for Lucca, not the default recommendation. |
| Permit an EONW change, keep exact Orbit/checkpoint gates | Runtime and Venus update while existing terminals survive; no old workspace codec remains in the target. | Old terminal CLIs report incompatibility and users invoke the installed target path. **Recommend this**, with a small Update-only control boundary independent of EONW; prove it before promising it. |

**Trigger across versions is not free.** A target CLI cannot send its new
EONW request to an old supervisor and expect it to decode. Recommend a small,
versioned **Update-only control exchange**, owned by Runtime under C11 and
exposed at a private `update.sock` beside `eon.sock`. It carries target launch
inputs, expected lifetime/caller identity and bounded results, not workspace
commands or terminal data. Its exact version and the private checkpoint
version are independent of EONW; unsupported versions refuse before mutation.
Define its canonical codec once at Runtime's protocol owner. This is a new
lifecycle boundary requiring approval, not an adapter for old workspace
commands, an alias or a decoder matrix. It is needed only if Lucca chooses
cross-EONW Update; equal-EONW-only Update can retain an ordinary EONW action.
The checkpoint must remain independent of versioned EONW snapshots: changing
EONW alone must not force a checkpoint change, but an incompatible checkpoint
still refuses. Do not claim every pair of builds can update.

The independent preflight also owns **Update discovery and caller validation**.
Today `resolve_workspace` first probes candidates over `eon.sock` and only
then validates the caller (`runtime/crates/eon-runtime/src/generation.rs:263`,
`:323`, `:336`); that path fails across EONW before Update can run. For Update,
enumerate private candidate directories, validate each `update.sock` object,
UID and reported lifetime, and validate the exact caller through preflight.
Apply the same explicit-target/caller/ambiguity **semantics**, without calling
the workspace EONW probe. Missing/unsupported Update endpoints are refusals,
not invitations to retry with an old codec or silently ignore an unknown live
candidate to invent a unique owner. Revalidate the selected endpoint/lifetime
before committing the transition.

**Guard the pinned executable.** When bare `eon` resolves to its terminal's
creation build, `eon update` before any move is an unchanged result. After a
move it must refuse, rather than revert, when target
build equals the validated calling terminal's origin build and differs from
the active build. Unknown caller origin is also a refusal; advise running the
target installed executable outside Eon with an explicit target. No override
flag is proposed. Origin data is recorded when the terminal starts and carried
through checkpoint; it is consulted only after validating the exact caller.
The same rule works across EONW versions because the Update exchange does not
depend on the workspace codec. byd2's future notice action can instead supply
the installed target explicitly, using the same guard and owner transition.

Adding the initial update action, active-build fields and generation semantics
requires a new EONW baseline. **A window predating that baseline cannot be
updated through a mechanism it does not implement.** Keep it running with
today's attach/stop behavior; open one baseline window manually. Do not add a
one-off bridge. Thereafter equal-EONW builds can use this transition. Different
EONW builds can use it only if Lucca approves the independent Update boundary
and the exact Orbit/checkpoint gates pass. Existing older-generation attach
and Stop delegation is not repurposed as an Update bridge.

### Old CLI artifacts and Nix runtime roots — researched, not a Lucca question

Deleting old profile generations is **not enough evidence** that the pinned
CLI disappears. In Determinate Nix `v3.21.2`, commit
`72c5eeb1d93009d9716ac0fd49ba5a9e034a3edc` (upstream 2.34.7), the Linux
scanner reads `/proc/PID/exe`, `cwd`, fds, maps **and environment store paths**;
store subpaths root their containing output. An old shell's initial PATH
naming its Eon session-bin output can therefore retain that CLI's closure
after Runtime/Venus re-exec ([scanner:66](https://github.com/DeterminateSystems/nix-src/blob/72c5eeb1d93009d9716ac0fd49ba5a9e034a3edc/src/libstore/local-gc.cc#L66),
`:106`, `:153`). This is a source-backed inference about Eon's PATH input
(`flake.nix:772`; `runtime/crates/eon-runtime/src/sessions.rs:1878`), not live
retention proof. The installed CLI symlink identifies that Determinate
release; the running daemon identity/settings were not inspected.

The scanner can skip inaccessible/disappearing processes, and
`/proc/PID/environ` reflects the environment at exec, not all later shell
changes ([Linux environ specification](https://man7.org/linux/man-pages/man5/proc_pid_environ.5.html)).
Runtime roots are ordinarily combined with persistent roots; a configured
external roots service changes collection behavior
([collection:289](https://github.com/DeterminateSystems/nix-src/blob/72c5eeb1d93009d9716ac0fd49ba5a9e034a3edc/src/libstore/gc.cc#L289),
[roots-service setting](https://github.com/DeterminateSystems/nix-src/blob/72c5eeb1d93009d9716ac0fd49ba5a9e034a3edc/src/libstore/include/nix/store/local-store.hh#L138)).
S1 must use read-only `nix-store --gc --print-roots` under an isolated spike
environment to identify which live process roots the exact old CLI/tool
closure, with the effective daemon and permissions recorded. Do not run a
collector against Lucca's environment. Add composition-owned retention only
if that probe exposes a real gap; remove the earlier proposed C10 requirement
to keep old profile generations. No speculative root manager or Runtime store
queries (`docs/AGENT-RULES.md:267`).

### Venus and the three platform cases

Runtime has a separate Venus child and control stream
(`runtime/crates/eon-runtime/src/supervisor.rs:527`). EOF causes Venus to exit
through its event loop (`venus/src/application.rs:6076`, `:5001`), and VEN-C14
already specifies that this releases attachment while Orbit stays live and
that replacement can retry Busy (`venus/docs/CONTRACTS.md:1051`). Starting Venus
names its PID/start identity to Orbit before revealing endpoints
(`runtime/crates/eon-runtime/src/supervisor.rs:539`; `docs/CONTRACTS.md:1746`).

| Platform | Verified boundary and proposed behavior |
| --- | --- |
| Native Wayland | This is the proved product target (`docs/AGENT-RULES.md:281`; `venus/docs/CONTRACTS.md:1102`). The current native path creates a new winit window (`venus/src/application.rs:1193`, `:1214`). Replace Venus only after Runtime resumes, using EOF rather than compositor-close/Quit. Its replacement creates a new surface; a close/reopen and possible compositor placement/focus changes are part of the proposed UX. No promise of the same native surface, exact screen position, or compositor workspace is made. Preserve Eon topology and terminal identities. Wayland objects belong to a client connection and clients cannot access other clients' surfaces ([Wayland protocol model](https://wayland.freedesktop.org/docs/book/Protocol.html)); this is evidence against assuming ordinary restart can transfer a surface, not a proof that every conceivable transfer is impossible. |
| X11 / Xwayland | Unsupported and not built as a Venus backend: Linux winit enables only Wayland (`venus/Cargo.toml:22`, `:25`; `venus/docs/CONTRACTS.md:1123`). Do not promise X11 window adoption, reparenting, or focus retention. Proposed update scope remains native Wayland; X11 is a separate platform decision. |
| Apple Silicon macOS | The accepted native seam is AppKit/Metal, with incomplete product proof and unsupported status (`venus/docs/CONTRACTS.md:1102`, `:1107`). A future update should replace the Venus process/window through that seam and reattach to unchanged hosts; AppKit activation, Spaces, geometry, IME and accessibility need native evidence. POSIX exec alone proves none of those. Keep macOS update disabled/unclaimed until a separately approved native proof slice; no Linux compositor mechanism enters Eon Runtime. |

The old Venus control fd can remain open during Runtime exec so the window is
not lost merely because CLOEXEC was left on. After restore, explicitly detach
and reap that child, start the target Venus, name it to each host and wait for
fresh authoritative frames. This is a **proposed sequence**, not an implemented
handoff. A presentation failure should leave Runtime and terminals alive and
make reattach retryable. Do not show a normal “window detached” notification
for an intentional update. Do not turn a pending directory picker into a new
terminal merely by reusing the ordinary Venus-exit path: that path currently
dismisses pending pairs (`runtime/crates/eon-runtime/src/supervisor.rs:2102`,
`:2116`).

Venus-local selection, zoom, chrome keyboard focus, hover, open help/inbox and
IME composition are not in Runtime's topology; the ownership exception is
explicit (`docs/AGENT-RULES.md:200`). Orbit owns terminal scroll state and rich
frames (`orbit/docs/CONTRACTS.md:29`, `:211`). Preserve Orbit state; do not
promise every transient Venus interaction survives a new process. For the
first version, let zoom, selection/IME composition, help/inbox and hover reset;
document this limit rather than adding a presentation-state transfer protocol.

## Reference gate: inspected prior art

External source is read-only design evidence. Nothing was copied, built or run.
Local reference paths below start at `/home/lucca/pjs/refs/`; source lines refer
to the recorded revision, not a floating upstream branch.

| Reference and inspected revision | Mechanism and what it establishes | What Eon should keep or reject |
| --- | --- | --- |
| nginx `release-1.28.0`, `481d28cb4e04c8096b9b6134856891dc52ecc68f` | USR2 starts a **new master**, alongside old master/workers; listener fd numbers are exported via `NGINX`. `ngx_execute` forks before exec. Old and new masters reap their own workers.
