## Proposed transition and the limits that must be proved

1. **Choose and preflight the target.** The explicitly invoked target executable
   supplies its immutable build/manifest/launch inputs. The approved independent
   Update exchange validates private socket/UID/lifetime/caller identity and
   the stale-origin guard before mutation; an EONW mismatch alone is not a
   refusal under the recommended policy. Discovery/selection uses those
   preflight exchanges over private candidate update sockets, not the existing
   EONW-dependent `resolve_workspace` probe. Unsupported candidates fail closed
   without an old-codec fallback. Validate platform, exact Update
   control/checkpoint versions and management/record/ORBS/ORBF support for
   every live host. Ask the target to validate the checkpoint in a separate
   read-only child; it must not consume live leases or bind sockets. Serialize
   active-build publication with namespace launch selection; refuse if another
   lifetime already uses the target build rather than merge owners. No Nix
   query, inferred “latest,” old workspace decoder or automatic CLI forwarding.
2. **Reach a safe boundary.** Serialize workspace mutation; complete current
   requests and pending host publication/cleanup, or refuse while busy. Drain
   management replies, including poll/name/read/send work. Reject an incomplete
   Stop or unreconciled run. Do not clone one lease into two active readers.
   Preserve request deduplication and checked ID allocation. User programs and
   Orbit continue running throughout.
3. **Checkpoint and exec.** Classify **every fd and connection**, not just the
   listeners. Preserve a bounded private checkpoint fd, the `eon.sock` listener
   and proposed `update.sock` listener, generation lifecycle and namespace
   launch locks, each management lease, each old Venus presentation-control
   socket, each Venus stderr-pipe **read end**, and the accepted Update reply
   connection. Record request ID and reply encoding/progress so the target
   does not lose or duplicate the initiating response. Checkpoint identifies
   exact run/process/start/endpoint/record objects; `origin_build` is not an
   additional management credential. Other worker/log/helper fds must be
   explicitly closed or reopened, with a complete inventory in S1, including
   standard input/output/error destinations and any startup-admission pipe.

   End EONW event subscriptions **before exec in the old codec**, including
   Venus's own subscription (`venus/src/transport.rs:581`) and CLI subscribers;
   bound final-frame draining and use `updating`, never `ended`. The replacement
   starts fresh streams; no old partial event buffer crosses EONW versions.
   Old Venus may attempt another old-version request until deliberately
   detached; reject incompatible messages without executing a mutation.

   Finish ordinary accepted CLI requests and flush their replies before exec;
   do not checkpoint an accepted-but-unanswered mutation, partial request or
   reply as if it were complete. The current handler accepts, dispatches and
   writes synchronously (`runtime/crates/eon-runtime/src/control.rs:553`,
   `:568`, `:586`); exec must occur after that turn unwinds, except for the
   explicitly retained Update response connection. Incomplete/slow clients
   receive a bounded refusal/disconnect. The inherited listeners retain their
   kernel backlog; queued connections are decoded normally after resume.

   Preserve and promptly recreate the stderr drainer before detaching old
   Venus: stderr is piped at `runtime/crates/eon-runtime/src/supervisor.rs:563`,
   and its reader is moved into the relay thread (`:581`, `:590`;
   `runtime/crates/eon-runtime/src/diagnostics.rs:113`). Closing the read end
   exposes the writer to EPIPE; `eprintln!` panics on write failure
   ([Rust documentation](https://doc.rust-lang.org/std/macro.eprintln.html)).
   The current Venus diagnostic helper ignores its write result
   (`venus/src/application.rs:5456`), so a literal current-helper panic is not
   established; older builds or dependencies must not be assumed safe. Keep
   the pipe reader until Venus exits, rather than provoking this risk, and
   measure backpressure while no relay thread exists. Raw pointers, Rust
   memory layout and thread handles are not a checkpoint format. Paths stay fixed.
4. **Restore ownership before replacing presentation.** Same PID resumes,
   validates all imported resources, reconstructs state and workers, and
   reconciles natural exits exactly once. Publish the new active build and
   launcher record truthfully. An exec failure returning to the old image must
   undo fd-flag changes and continue old state/window. Successful exec has no
   surviving old manager to roll back automatically. If restore fails after
   exec, do not pretend that owner/layout survived: report `update-restore-failed`
   when possible, close inherited leases non-destructively and exit without
   terminal Stop or ordinary destructive teardown. The hosts remain live but
   become unmanaged/orphaned; explicit C15 reacquisition from the target build
   restores today's synthetic layout, not the lost checkpoint layout. A crash
   before the reply gives the initiating CLI transport failure/unknown outcome.
5. **Replace Venus deliberately.** Preserve the old control fd across Runtime
   exec. Once the new Runtime owns restored state, use the existing detach
   mechanism, wait/reap the old Venus, launch target Venus with saved Eon
   topology, name it to the hosts and accept fresh frames. With the shared
   supervisor model, do this for every attached Venus while preserving the
   session/window mapping and keeping detached sessions detached. Do not use Quit or
   dismiss pending pickers. Reattachment can retry existing transient Busy.
6. **Report a truthful outcome.** Success identifies unchanged window/generation
   and old/new active builds, and confirms target Runtime and presentation.
   Before-commit refusal leaves the old window intact. After exec, a failed
   Venus start yields a **partial failure**, not success or terminal Stop: keep
   Runtime/hosts/layout available for `attach`. A lost reply is an unknown
   outcome; inspect active build before retrying. Abrupt Runtime death after
   successful exec remains a crash, not an atomic rollback guarantee.

Operational choices intentionally kept small: no durable cross-generation
workspace database, perpetual old checkpoint decoders, watchdog daemon,
automatic restart watcher, fd-transfer broker, per-build Runtime, CLI shim,
environment injection, dependency or generic portability framework. Inherited
checkpoint transport is ephemeral and distinct from the reboot-restore epic's
durable versioned files; reuse model validation where useful, not its process
resurrection policy (`br show eon-reboot-restore-im8y`, read 2026-11-04).

### Unverified and consequential limits

- No handoff, fd inheritance, child exit race, lock retention, native restart,
  performance, or rollback was exercised. Exact inherited fd flags and the
  complete shutdown behavior of helper workers still need the spike inventory.
- A normal POSIX exec is the hypothesis behind same-PID ownership; its use
  with this Runtime's threads, Nix wrappers, platform start identities and
  restored leases is unproved. Do not use systemd's success as Eon's proof.
- A checkpoint schema change is deliberately refused. Carrying prior schema
  decoders would be a compatibility choice for Lucca, not an implementation
  convenience. Frequent refusals would be evidence against this design.
- Exact protocol numbers are a necessary boundary, not a license to change
  semantics under the same number. The target must satisfy the accepted Orbit
  contracts for those versions. Live old hosts retain their original code;
  their exact origin must remain inspectable.
- If Runtime crashes after exec, Orbit's existing supervisor-loss survival
  boundary applies, but today's recovery does not preserve layout
  (`docs/CONTRACTS.md:1939`). This draft promises layout through a successful
  update and deliberate failure handling, not recovery from arbitrary process
  death. A crash-durable checkpoint would be a separate scope decision.
- Linux environment scanning supports old CLI retention even without old
  profile generations; exact artifact roots under the deployed daemon remain
  S1 evidence, not a reason to ask Lucca to choose GC mechanics in advance.
- No exact-position/focus/surface transfer was verified on Wayland, X11 or
  macOS. Preserving the person's currently active desktop surface remains a
  proof obligation, not permission to forcibly activate the replacement.

one-supervisor-per-window clause. This draft does not approve the latter.

### EON-C1: add retained-host composition clause

Add after the exact-component result (`docs/CONTRACTS.md:81`):

> EON-C11 Update validates the target's one component manifest for target
> launches and separately validates its use of each retained live Orbit host
> at the exact accepted protocol versions. The live inventory retains that
> host's origin build and immutable identity; it never reports the host as a
> target-build process. This inventory is observed running state, not a second
> component compatibility graph. Existing hosts are not restarted to satisfy
> target artifact identity.

EON-C2 stays the single manifest owner (`docs/CONTRACTS.md:183`, `:195`); no
second manifest, persisted Nix identity or dependency graph is proposed.

### EON-C15: add planned-update/recovery distinction

Add after the initial generation-identity result (`docs/CONTRACTS.md:1935`):

> For an Update-capable full-Eon lifetime, generation means its unchanged
> lifetime identity, not its active build. Orbit's component generation remains
> that lifetime identity before and after Update, so existing generation
> equality and complete live identity/record/UID/endpoint checks remain in
> force unchanged. A terminal's origin_build is inventory and Update-policy
> data, never a replacement or extra credential for management validation.
> Planned Update inherits ownership and restores its complete Runtime checkpoint
> under EON-C11; the synthetic-t1 behavior and lost-layout boundary here apply
> to supervisor-loss recovery, not a successful planned Update.

### EON-C39: replace stream identity wording and add Update interruption

Replace the sentence beginning “STREAM identifies one supervisor process” at
`docs/CONTRACTS.md:4154` and its restart continuation with:

> STREAM identifies one supervisor execution, not merely its PID or
> generation. Planned Update starts a new STREAM even when PID and generation
> are unchanged. Restart or EON-C15 recovery also starts a new STREAM.

Add to End (`docs/CONTRACTS.md:4157`):

> A planned Update ends current subscriptions with reason `updating` and EOF;
> their CLI exits 1, so a waiter does not report a predicate as satisfied. The
> replacement Runtime uses a new STREAM even though its PID and generation
> remain the same. Reconnecting with the old cursor returns a full snapshot
> with `resumed:false`. Update never emits `ended` for a still-live generation.
> A subscriber that cannot receive its final end frame observes transport
> failure instead. Update waits are bounded and never wait indefinitely for
> subscribers to drain.

Keep `pane wait`'s updating exit as a failure, not automatic resume. A
cross-EONW update can make that waiting executable incompatible; resuming it
would require the old codec/CLI adaptation this proposal rejects. Users may
restart the wait from the target CLI. This is a deliberate bounded first
version, not an overlooked reconnect promise.

This avoids inheriting bounded output buffers, partial subscription frames and
retained event history (`runtime/crates/eon-runtime/src/subscriptions.rs:32`,
`:58`; `runtime/crates/eon-runtime/src/events.rs:1039`). Preserve completed
workspace request deduplication; do not imply event cursors survive.

No Orbit contract amendment is proposed: hosts and their protocols stay intact.
No new Venus wire/platform contract is proposed: consume VEN-C14 EOF/detach,
Busy retry and native host boundaries. If the spike needs a new Orbit message,
cross-process window transfer or new Venus launch schema guarantee, return
for the corresponding ORB/VEN contract approval. EON-C28's existing promise
to list/stop older 1.x generations remains binding from 1.0
(`docs/CONTRACTS.md:2803`, `:2842`); “no new shims” does not repeal it. Existing
attach/stop delegation is retained, not expanded into cross-version Update.
Cross-EONW Update instead uses the newly proposed Update-only boundary; it
does not change the version contract of any existing workspace command.

## Proposed fresh-session split — drafts only

Sized using `/home/lucca/.claude/skills/create-beads/SKILL.md` and its body
template: one independently verifiable outcome, bounded files, one proof route
per child, comfortably below about 100k context tokens. Draft keys below are
not Beads IDs. After Lucca approves, the overseer should check for overlap and
file/refine the implementation epic; do not reopen duplicate `eon-0o5d`.
In the child bodies, abbreviated `*.rs` evidence names resolve under
`runtime/crates/eon-runtime/src/`; `v31.rs` resolves under
`runtime/crates/eon-workspace-protocol/src/`. Re-read exact lines after drift.

### Parent U — Update a running full-Eon window without moving its terminals

**Why:** profile changes currently leave existing windows on the old build;
Lucca has to move manually (`br show eon-1bq8`, read 2026-11-04).

**Acceptance:** an explicitly selected installed target build controls the same
window lifetime after one command, preserving every surviving terminal and
Runtime layout; hard-protocol/checkpoint refusal leaves old work untouched; installed
native Wayland evidence covers success and deliberate failures. The contract
draft and scope must be approved before product changes. Child slots are
S1–S3, S4a/S4b and S5 below, with S2 re-split after eon-hyil8 lands;
existing notice bead is related, not silently absorbed. No macOS/X11 feature,
automatic watcher, cross-version bridge or machine-restart restore.

### S1 — Spike inherited Runtime ownership across same-PID exec

**Why:** prove the proposed hardest boundary before building its product shape.

**Evidence:** `sessions.rs:1648`, `:1925`, `:2028`; `supervisor.rs:841`;
`control.rs:540`; systemd/HAProxy sources above.

**Scope:** disposable isolated spike and report only, using real Orbit hosts
and two explicit manager images in a private runtime/display; no public update
command, canonical contract edits, installed user profile, durable compatibility
code or new process owner. Portability disposition: POSIX mechanisms isolated
in Runtime; Linux native Wayland is the only exercised target.

**Acceptance:** record before/after manager PID, Orbit PID/start/run identities,
listener/lock/endpoint objects and management lease continuity; an Orbit exiting
during exec is reaped once; an explicit Stop after resume still confirms PTY
child and host cleanup. Prove old-Venus control **and stderr-pipe** continuity;
exercise diagnostics while the relay thread is absent, record backpressure
and establish whether the actual old build exits/panics if a reader closes.
Classify Venus's EONW subscription (`venus/src/transport.rs:581`), all CLI
subscriptions, accepted-but-unanswered CLI exchanges and the Update reply
connection exactly as transition step 3 requires. List carried, drained,
closed and recreated fds/workers, not just listeners. Inject target exec
failure and malformed transport/checkpoint header before mutation. A full
layout/pending-picker roundtrip belongs to S3, after checkpoint code exists.

Measure the **exec gap** from last old-image control/poll service to first
restored service: record timestamps, queued-client latency, host-exit reap
delay, stderr buffering and whether programs/Orbit continue progressing. Do
not claim zero pause from same-PID exec or invent a timing guarantee before
measuring. Inventory old CLI/tool closure roots after the old manager/client
images are gone using isolated `nix-store --gc --print-roots`; record the
effective daemon/procfs permissions and exact rooted output. Do not delete
roots or invoke collection against Lucca's environment. The Linux environment
scanner is the default hypothesis, not a reason to add retention machinery.
Observe effective shell PATH, `command -v eon` and resolved build before/after
the transition and in a newly created terminal; compare that to the environment
at exec seen by root discovery. EON_SESSION_BIN is present in product assembly;
shell overrides mean its presence alone does not prove command resolution.
Report success or a concrete no-go; a negative spike closes with evidence and
blocks later children for Lucca's decision.

**Implementation notes:** inventory first; use existing canonical protocols,
not a fake terminal or copied upstream code. Do not turn the probe into the
production implementation or add a generic handoff framework.

**Verification:** one isolated real-process spike through the repository's
sandbox/proof surface; retain exact image revisions, observations and failure
results. Commands/harness are selected and recorded by that session, after
reading `docs/DEVELOPMENT.md`; never exercise the person's live window.

**Stop conditions:** parentage/lease/lock invariants fail; full layout needs
terminal-state reconstruction; a new platform assumption, protocol or owner is
needed; source has drifted materially; the same check fails twice after a
reasonable fix. **Maintenance:** no new dependency; report minimum viable
handoff schema and estimated follow-on scope, then return for approval.

### S2 — Separate full-Eon lifetime identity from active build

**Why:** a fixed socket directory must not claim it always names the executing
source tree; lifecycle discovery/defaults must stay truthful after a move.

**Evidence:** `generation.rs:36`, `:60`, `:282`; `supervisor.rs:332`, `:2798`;
`docs/CONTRACTS.md:1618`, `:1139`; `v31.rs:713`.

**Prerequisites:** S1 supports the shape; Lucca approves the relevant exact
contract clauses and the identity allocation/uniqueness rule. Reserve the next
free EONW version with the coordinator; do not assume v32 is free.
Reconcile with `eon-hyil8` and its `eon-8mw1v` supervisor/session ownership
spikes before implementing this baseline; do not cement per-window namespaces.
**This is a provisional slot: after that owner change lands, re-prime and
re-split S2 before filing or implementing it.** Separate identity data/codec
from discovery/launch arbitration if their combined remaining scope exceeds
one fresh session; drop work the session redesign already delivered. Do not
blindly carry today's file list into the new owner shape.

**Scope:** `runtime/.../{generation,supervisor,windows,cli}.rs`, canonical EONW
lifecycle values/codecs, product manifest/assembly and existing CLI fixtures;
docs/help for new identity fields/default targeting. Choose an opaque unique
lifetime ID without aliases or directory moves; keep build digest separate.
Carry host origin identity from creation; retain existing non-Update legacy
attach/stop behavior and eonbase semantics. No exec or Venus replacement yet.

**Acceptance:** newly started full-Eon lifetimes have stable independent IDs;
CLI inspection distinguishes generation, created build and active build;
current selection, ambiguity, caller validation and stop/attach work against
that model, with old generations still discoverable/stoppable as previously
promised. Missing/corrupt identity metadata cannot authorize takeover. New
wire fixtures cover changed semantics and reject mismatched versions.
One namespace launch lock covers select/create/publication and Update's
active-build change, in addition to the per-generation lifecycle lock. A real
concurrent-launch race for the same build yields one lifetime/terminal set;
an update racing a target-build launch never creates two current owners or
merges terminals. Document lock order and inherited lock ownership.

**Implementation notes:** derive target compatibility only from the one
manifest; live host inventory is state. Update every current-generation caller
and fixture; keep this baseline usable without the future Update command.

**Verification:** shared lifecycle/wire route: full affected Rust and Nix
surfaces through `nix develop -c eon-test` and relevant flake checks, plus the
required fresh review loop. Focused selection/identity cases are the falsifier;
no extra desktop update claim. **Stop conditions:** unapproved JSON/CLI break,
old lifecycle regression, material source drift, out-of-scope owner needed, or
twice-failing check. **Maintenance:** records/bootstrap are versioned and local;
no adapter to make a pre-baseline supervisor implement Update.

### S3 — Checkpoint and restore complete Runtime state at a safe boundary

**Why:** EONW presentation snapshots and C15 synthetic recovery omit necessary
private state. A successful update must not restart hidden terminals or reuse
IDs.

**Evidence:** `workspace.rs:92`, `:120`, `:189`, `:850`;
`sessions.rs:868`; `supervisor.rs:1162`; `attention.rs:244`.

**Prerequisites:** S1's fd/state inventory and schema choice; S2 baseline;
approved C11/C15 checkpoint scope.

**Scope:** private checkpoint representation in Runtime's existing workspace,
session, attention and supervisor owners, canonical validation and focused
fixtures. No durable reboot restore, old-schema decoder, public Update CLI,
native window transfer or event-history serialization. Portability: neutral
state plus isolated Unix fd transport; no Linux-only data in durable formats.

**Acceptance:** a representative checkpoint roundtrips all C11 topology,
attention/sidebar, private allocator/deduplication and immutable run values;
cover multiple sessions/workspaces, columns, hidden/covered popups and pending
directory pickers here, including a move and completed mutation just before
checkpoint and a new creation just after restore. Layout and picker checks
are intentionally moved out of S1. Checkpoint encoding must remain independent
of EONW; two different workspace-wire versions can share one exact checkpoint
schema without retaining the old workspace codec in the target.
malformed/duplicate/wrong-identity/oversized/future-schema data is rejected
before becoming authority. In-flight lease bytes are completed or update is
refused; no second reader, duplicate send or fresh terminal appears. Recreated
caches cannot overwrite authoritative values. Account for measured exec-gap
elapsed time when rebasing monotonic deadlines: stale attention/status must
not become fresh merely because Runtime re-executed. Explain timer outcomes.

**Implementation notes:** encode logical values, never Rust memory. Keep the
checkpoint transient and exact-schema; reuse existing model validators. Close
the slice with an independently executable encode/restore boundary check.

**Verification:** shared lifecycle/format route, full affected sandboxed Rust
and Nix surfaces with focused roundtrip/rejection cases; fresh review required.
**Stop conditions:** state omitted from S1 changes the contract, migration or
Orbit/Venus protocol change is required, material drift, or repeated failed
proof. **Maintenance:** changing the private schema makes update unavailable
until both sides match; do not retain obsolete readers by default.

### S4a — Define and prove the Update-only control boundary across EONW

**Why:** a target CLI using a different EONW cannot ask an old workspace decoder
to replace itself. A separate lifecycle format avoids an old-codec matrix.

**Evidence:** `control.rs:330`, `:408`, `:553`; canonical EONW header at
`runtime/crates/eon-workspace-protocol/src/v31.rs:3`; gate/history above.

**Prerequisites:** S1, final S2 slices and S3; Lucca approves cross-EONW Update
and C11's independent control boundary, exact-version/refusal rules and guard.
If he chooses equal EONW only, omit S4a and use an ordinary EONW action in S4b.

**Scope:** one canonical bounded Update codec at Runtime's protocol owner,
private update listener/validation, candidate discovery/selection through its
preflight exchange and result framing; no
workspace command adapter, older-version decoder, public updater daemon or
automatic discovery. Portability: existing Unix/private-UID boundary.

**Acceptance:** different workspace EONW builds can exchange Update preflight
using the same Update format without decoding each other's workspace actions.
The target CLI finds the owning lifetime and validates its caller through that
exchange without entering `resolve_workspace`'s EONW probe. Explicit targets,
multiple owners and missing/unsupported pre-baseline endpoints fail safely;
no unsupported candidate is ignored to infer a sole target.
Wrong Update format, UID/lifetime/caller, oversized/partial data, unknown origin
and the stale-origin target are refused before mutation; target artifact and
checkpoint validation are explicit. Reply request/progress state is suitable
for S4b inheritance. No malformed request authorizes execution or signalling.
Prove the boundary independently with real bounded exchanges, without claiming
a completed runtime update yet.

**Implementation notes:** keep one codec and one owner; no generic routing
framework or caller-supplied compatibility claim. Refuse when target build is
already active in another lifetime under the namespace launch lock.

**Verification:** shared wire/trust route, focused real-exchange rejection cases
plus full affected sandboxed Rust/Nix checks and required fresh reviews.
**Stop conditions:** old workspace codecs become necessary, an unapproved trust
boundary is needed, scope exceeds one session, source drifts, or checks fail
twice. **Maintenance:** exact independent format version; unsupported formats
remain a reasoned refusal. No claim that it can update pre-baseline windows.

### S4b — Re-exec Runtime while retaining its resources and reaping

**Why:** implement the ownership transition independently of user-facing
discovery/presentation UX.

**Evidence:** `supervisor.rs:841`, `:1101`, `:1150`; `control.rs:462`, `:540`;
`sessions.rs:1925`; `running.rs:240`; S1 report and S3 checkpoint.

**Prerequisites:** final S2 slices, S3 and S4a when cross-EONW is chosen;
approved C11/C15 boundaries.

**Scope:** Runtime supervisor/control/platform lifecycle, existing executable
internal resume entry and product-supplied launch inputs. Validate target in
an isolated child; quiesce worker activity; allowlist inherited fds; restore
leases/listener/lock in the same PID. Preserve old Venus control until resumed.
Include namespace launch lock, accepted Update reply and stderr pipe readers;
end all old EONW subscriptions and finish ordinary CLI replies before exec.
No updater daemon, new signal permission, Nix evaluator, UI or automatic
profile trigger. Portability: POSIX process/fd seam in Runtime, Linux proof.

**Acceptance:** the actual internal resume entry replaces the manager image
while PID, host identities and locked socket ownership stay fixed; real host
exit before/during/after exec reconciles correctly. Failed exec returns to old
service; preflight rejection leaves it untouched. Post-exec restore failure
reports its distinct outcome when possible and releases failed-owner leases
without Stop: hosts survive unmanaged/orphaned for explicit C15 recovery,
which may lose layout. Do not invoke ordinary destructive teardown.
Helper fds do not leak to later children. Check the wrapped installed target's
environment/inputs rather than execing a stale unwrapped binary by accident.

**Implementation notes:** preserve existing management-only cleanup authority;
do not recover by scanning PIDs or deliberately orphan a host in a successful
handoff. The explicit failed-restore fallback above is the exception: release
the failed owner non-destructively and use C15, with its stated layout limit.
Use the internal entry
through a real-process integration case, not a separately implemented model.

**Verification:** lifecycle route, full affected Rust/Nix surfaces and one
isolated real-process observation of the transition using exact artifacts;
fresh review and Codex as repository rules require. **Stop conditions:** a
watchdog/old reaper becomes necessary, fd/worker safety is unproved, source
drifts, scope/contract changes, or proof fails twice. **Maintenance:** record
irreversible exec boundary and truthful failure outcomes; no automatic rollback
claim.

### S5 — Ship explicit target-build Update with Venus replacement

**Why:** turn the proved transition into the one-command workflow Lucca chose.

**Evidence:** `cli.rs` targeting; `supervisor.rs:539`, `:2102`;
`venus/src/application.rs:1193`, `:6076`; `docs/CONTRACTS.md:4148`.

**Prerequisites:** S4b; Lucca approves command targeting, Wayland close/reopen,
transient-view limit, refusal/partial-failure result and C39 stream behavior.
Owner-wide scope follows the shared-supervisor direction; preserve every mapping.

**Scope:** CLI/help/results, supervisor Update dispatch, deliberate Venus
replacement bypassing pending-pair dismissal/normal detach notice, C39
`updating` end and new stream, caller-visible build inventory, product docs and
changelog. Retain ordinary Present semantics. Affected surfaces include
`runtime/.../{cli,generation,supervisor,subscriptions,events}.rs`, canonical
workspace EONW diagnostics/events plus S4a's independent Update results,
`eon/crates/eon/tests/workspace_control.rs`,
`docs/{USAGE,CONFIGURATION,CONTRACTS}.md`; Venus launch/presentation owner only
if existing EOF/startup admission is insufficient. Keep fixed refusal rules as
protocol/safety bounds with rationale in this bead; no new arbitrary timing
settings. No notice watcher or macOS/X11 launch scope.

**Acceptance:** target installed `eon update` updates the selected lifetime;
caller/explicit target rules and external ambiguity are correct; equal target
is idempotent; a pinned stale-origin invocation refuses instead of reverting,
including after two updates and from a newly created pane. New Runtime/Venus
report the target identity, old hosts retain
exact identities and state, and a new pane launches target components. Prove
multiple workspaces, columns, hidden panes/popups, pending picker, attention,
selection and old-terminal commands. For a cross-EONW success, old commands
fail honestly with both versions and the invoked path; the installed target
CLI controls the same terminal without a shim. For equal EONW, old commands
continue to work. Orbit/control/checkpoint/unsupported-platform
refusal leaves old state and surface untouched. Presentation failure leaves
reattachable layout/terminals with a nonzero truthful result. Subscribers/waits
end as updating, and an old cursor reconnects with a full snapshot. Repeated
success and natural exits neither duplicate terminals nor leak zombies.
If the shared supervisor model has landed, include two attached windows plus a
detached session: update all attached clients, preserve assignments, open no
client for the detached session and stop no session merely for losing a view.

**Implementation notes:** target equals invoked executable; docs show invoking
that installed path from an old terminal whose bare `eon` is pinned. No
hard-coded personal profile path. Keep first-baseline/manual-window limitation
visible. The notice's action, when added, invokes this same operation.

**Verification:** lifecycle/wire plus installed-interaction route. Full affected
Rust/Nix checks, changed Orbit/Venus crate fmt/clippy only when applicable,
required reviews, then one isolated installed native Wayland upgrade/failure
scenario on exact artifacts, with no user's active profile/process touched.
Record PID/endpoint identities, layout and old/new executable identities in
proof. Runtime synchronization for eventual landing belongs to the coordinator
under then-current authorization; this draft authorizes none.

**Stop conditions:** focus theft cannot be avoided within approved UX, no
truthful target identity, unexpected protocol/scope change, material drift, or
proof fails twice. **Maintenance:** report old-host engine-code retention and
transient Venus limits; never call a failed restart a successful update.

### Existing work and dependency order

`S1 → approval of spike result → final S2 slices → S3 → S4a → S4b → S5`
is deliberately serial (omit S4a if Lucca chooses equal EONW only):
these slices share lifecycle/protocol owners. Re-split after S1 if its measured
scope exceeds one fresh session. S3/S4a/S4b's preparatory boundaries must be
independently exercised; do not land an unused framework or claim the parent
feature finished before S5. Re-split S2 after eon-hyil8 lands, before filing it.

`eon-newer-build-notice-byd2` remains a related existing feature. Its future
notice button can use S5 and must obtain the target executable as an opaque
composition input/validated announcement; the current code has no accepted
installed-build discovery mechanism (`br show eon-newer-build-notice-byd2`,
read 2026-11-04). Do not silently add a mutable dispatcher or profile watcher.
`eon-agent-parity-a9g0.7` may reuse deliberate Venus replacement after its own
configuration contract choice; `eon-reboot-restore-im8y` may reuse model
validation, not ephemeral exec-state semantics. Apple Silicon Update would be
a later separate native proof/scope bead, not a blocker disguised as support.

`eon-hyil8` / `eon-8mw1v` are material ownership prerequisites, not duplicate
update beads. EON-C38 already distinguishes durable host-owned workspace ID
from window-local handles (`docs/CONTRACTS.md:3945`, `:3956`, `:3980`); do not
conflate that identity with the proposed Runtime lifetime/build split. Its
remote plan also uses equality of the wire tuple
(`docs/REMOTE-WORKSPACES.md:90`). Coordinate shared C10/C11/C15 and EONW edits,
without importing remote transport or registry persistence into this spike.

## Planning verification record

- Route: planning only. Read `AGENTS.md`, `docs/AGENT-PROTOCOLS.md`, all of
  `docs/AGENT-RULES.md`, subsystem rules, named references, eon-1bq8 and the
  three related beads read-only. Checkouts/revisions and source locations are
  recorded above; source evidence is separated from recommendations/unknowns.
- No product source, canonical contract, Beads storage, branch, profile or
  process was changed. No build/test/dogfood, signal, GitHub action or outward
  message was performed. Only the assigned work directory contains the draft
  and progress record. No `br` write or sync was run per this pane's scope.
- Review ledger: 2 read-only planning passes. Initial pass found conflicting
  C23 launcher wording and an unqualified old-CLI availability promise; both
  corrected, with explicit backward-target and shared-supervisor consequences.
  Finder's narrow re-check reports no blocking findings. Citation existence
  and line-bound checks passed for Eon references; local competitor references
  use the separately recorded checkouts. Repository diff/status remained clean.
- Opus gate, 2026-11-04: **PASS WITH FIXES**, read in full from
  `../opus-gate.md` with the coordinator's `../INBOX.md`. Revised the EONW
  policy and stale-origin trigger; completed subscriptions/stderr/accepted-
  connection handling; removed redundant C15 host-membership authority;
  added namespace launch locking, researched GC roots, replaced C39's stream
  identity sentence, named failed-restore/C15 outcomes, moved layout proof
  to S3, added S1 exec-gap measurements and S2's post-hyil8 re-split gate.
  Kept the corrected `docs/AGENT-RULES.md:281` platform and `:200` view-state
  citations, and corrected Orbit authority to `orbit/AGENTS.md:14`.
  Questions reduced from eleven to six. Latest inbox correction about
  EON_SESSION_BIN is incorporated: S1 observes actual shell resolution instead
  of inferring it from assembly inputs. Revised-draft review: 2 read-only
  passes; initial pass found the EONW-dependent discovery gap and two wording
  ambiguities. Independent discovery, logical lifetime identity and explicit
  failed-restore exception fixed; the finder's narrow re-check is clean.
- Approval remains with Lucca. The overseer should replay this record onto
  eon-1bq8; the decision is not closed by producing this file.

## Numbered questions for Lucca

1. **Trigger and revert protection: explicit command, notice action, or automatic
   refresh?** Recommend **target-installed `eon update` plus the stale-origin
   guard**, and a notice action in byd2 later; no automatic refresh trigger.
   Refuse when the invoked target is the caller terminal's origin build but
   differs from active, rather than letting bare pinned `eon update` revert
   the runtime. Reason: target selection stays explicit and needs no version
   ordering or forwarding shim. Deliberate backward selection remains possible
   outside Eon with an explicit target; do not add an override flag.
2. **What happens when Orbit management/record, ORBS/ORBF, Update control or
   checkpoint formats differ?** Recommend **refuse the exact mismatch before
   mutation**, keeping the old window. Reason: unchanged live Orbit hosts must
   remain speakable, and an unsupported checkpoint cannot safely restore the
   owner. No adapters or old-schema decoder matrix. EONW alone is question 5;
   pre-feature supervisors still require one manual move to the baseline.
3. **Is a Wayland window closing and reopening acceptable?** Recommend **yes,
   explicitly**, with terminals and Runtime layout preserved, and compositor
   position/workspace/focus treated as unguaranteed. Reason: a new Venus uses a
   new native window in the current host path; preserving the actual surface
   requires a different, unproved lifecycle. If no, stop at the spike and
   reconsider the presentation boundary before implementation.
4. **May generation identity name the lifetime, with active build and creation
   build separate?** Recommend **yes**. Reason: fixed directories and host
   identities avoid socket aliases and dishonest source identity. This changes
   C11/C10 defaults and JSON meaning, so it needs an explicit baseline/protocol
   change and complete caller audit, not a silent metadata tweak.
5. **Should Update cross EONW bumps even though old terminals' CLIs then become
   incompatible?** Recommend **yes**, while exact Orbit/control/checkpoint
   gates pass, with the independent Update-only boundary and honest old-CLI
   errors naming the invoked path. Reason: v10→v31 in 19 days makes an equal-
   EONW-only update commonly unavailable for long-lived windows. Retaining
   live programs is more useful than keeping their old CLI operational; users
   can invoke the installed target explicitly. No workspace decoder shim.
   If old bare commands must keep working, choose equal-EONW refusal instead
   and accept that availability cost explicitly.
6. **Approve this contract direction and spike-first split?** Recommend **approve
   S1 only first**, then review evidence before later slices. Reason: fd and
   connection continuity, exec-gap timing, GC roots and failure outcomes still
   need real isolated evidence. Re-split S2 after eon-hyil8 lands; include S4a
   only if cross-EONW Update is chosen. Nothing here authorizes product code,
   live updates, Beads writes or the canonical contract edits.

## Approval (Lucca, 2026-11-04)

Lucca answered the six numbered questions in the revised decision (records 001-decision and opus-gate on this bead) with "agreed", accepting every recommendation:

1. **Trigger:** an explicit, target-installed `eon update`, plus a notice action later in eon-newer-build-notice-byd2. Never an automatic refresh. A stale-origin guard refuses when the invoked target is the calling terminal's origin build but differs from the active build. No override flag.
2. **Mismatch:** refuse before mutation when the Orbit management or record format, ORBS/ORBF, Update control or checkpoint formats differ, and keep the old window. No adapters, and no matrix of old-schema decoders.
3. **Wayland:** the native window closes and reopens. Terminals and the Runtime layout are preserved. Compositor position, workspace and focus are not guaranteed.
4. **Identity:** the generation identity names the lifetime, and the active build and creation build are reported separately. This is an explicit baseline and protocol change, with an audit of every caller.
5. **Cross-EONW:** Update crosses EONW bumps while the exact Orbit, control and checkpoint gates pass, through the independent Update-only boundary (`update.sock`, slice S4a). Old terminals' CLIs give honest incompatibility errors that name the invoked path. No workspace decoder shim.

## Evidence and remaining scope (6e63eb7)

After a profile refresh, reach a previous same-EONW build; preserve successful one-hop routing to another EONW when its recorded executable exists and refusal when it does not. Keep reserved Stop/attach and explicit --terminal semantics; no new compatibility codec.

Settle outside-caller command policy with eon-j9wyn during the contract round; do not add its exact-argv pane/tab launch implementation here. Read EON-C10/EON-C11/EON-C23 and applicable REFERENCES routes. Target resolution and validated caller identity each have one owner.

## Verification and integration

Focused real-binary routing/refusal checks plus one isolated installed two-window observation including a same-EONW profile refresh, under current affected-boundary proof rules. Never restart a live user supervisor.

With eon-j9wyn, eon-cglv2, eon-fv1j0, delivered eon-quick-search-parity-23y9.2 and eon-ciwn.5-.9, this retires agents2-eon.sh, quit-look*.sh, pane-run.sh and needs-input-watch.sh. title: Fix the intermittent quota worker isolation test
description:
## Defect

eon-runtime's quota::tests::workers_isolate_failure_and_bound_output_timeout_and_shutdown failed once in an 80-run loop of `nix develop -c eon-test -p eon-runtime --lib` (2026-10-21, x86_64 Linux, 1-minute load about 2-13, while working eon-p8cq on base 9e0bb86 with an earlier p8cq candidate). It panicked at quota.rs:447:37 on that revision (now quota.rs:448, after cbe397c added a line): `quotas.codex.snapshot().unwrap()` found None after the test's 2 s wait. It passed in the 110 other full-suite runs that session.

## Suspected cause (unproved)

Linux refuses to exec a file while any process holds it open for writing (ETXTBSY), and Rust's Command::spawn does not retry. The test writes its fake backend with fs::write and execs it right after. Other tests in the same process spawn children; a child forked during that fs::write inherits the write descriptor until it execs, so the backend is briefly "text file busy". The first fetch (claude, 50 ms timeout) expects an error anyway, so an ETXTBSY there fails instantly instead of after 50 ms, and Quotas::start then spawns the codex worker microseconds later, still inside the window. That fetch also fails, the worker waits its 60 s interval, and the snapshot is still None at 2 s. This is the same fork-inheritance class as eon-p8cq.

The later rewrite of the backend before the output-bound fetch (quota.rs:468) has the same race; there ETXTBSY yields the expected Err, so it cannot fail the test but can skip the output-bound check it means to exercise. claude_waits_300_units_after_a_failed_read_while_codex_reads_every_60 writes and execs its backend the same way (quota.rs:490).

Alternative to rule out: plain scheduling delay under load (sh startup plus printf exceeding 2 s).

## Contract

No contract change. The test protects EON-C27 quota worker isolation, the output bound, timeout and shutdown.

## Acceptance

- Name the cause from evidence: a reproduction under the full suite (or a focused one, e.g. a concurrent fork loop around the fs::write), showing the failing spawn's error kind.
- A test-only fix that makes the backend's spawn deterministic without weakening what the test checks, for example writing the script to a temporary name and renaming it into place, or writing it once before any other test can fork, rather than retrying the spawn in product code. The output-bound fetch must exercise the bound, not fail at spawn.
- Red/green from the reproduction; `nix develop -c eon-test -p eon-runtime --lib` looped under the full suite.
- cargo fmt --check and clippy -D warnings clean.

## Scope boundary

The quota tests that write and exec a backend script. No product change unless the reproduction shows a product defect; then stop and record it.
close_reason: Quota test script helper now has a child sh write each script, so no forked child inherits a write descriptor; ETXTBSY red/green 107-135/2000 to 0/2000, suite 30/30

comments.author: lucca
comments.text:
From eon-ven-new-window-test-flake-66gm (2026-10-27), which asked whether one shared test-helper pattern fixes both. What I found by reading the code at 6a3ee78; nothing here is proved in eon-runtime.

- The quota test helper `script` (runtime/crates/eon-runtime/src/quota.rs:522-530) still writes the backend with `fs::write` in the test process, then chmods it. Its callers exec it right away: lines 629 and 674 in workers_isolate_failure_and_bound_output_timeout_and_shutdown, and 687, 759 and 848 in other tests.
- bd7fa29 moved the callers to fresh paths ("callers use a fresh path for each one (eon-1fxc)"). A fresh path does not close the race. The descriptor that a concurrently forked child inherits refers to the new file and stays open until that child execs or exits.
- 66gm's standalone reproduction of exactly this pattern (~/.cache/eon-agents/66gm-work/repro/main.rs: four threads forking while the main thread writes, chmods and execs a fresh script) failed 162/2000 and 758/10000 rounds with "Text file busy (os error 26)".
- The pattern 66gm adopted had 0 failures in 20000 rounds: a child shell writes the file (`sh -c 'printf %s "$1" > "$0"' <path> <body>`) and the test process only chmods by path. The same pattern applies here, using the `sh` that the helper already finds on PATH.
- It cannot be one shared helper: Venus depends only on the protocol crates, and there is no shared test crate, so each crate keeps a local copy.
- eon-1fxc's acceptance still needs its own red/green in eon-runtime, including ruling out plain scheduling delay.

comments.author: lucca
comments.text:
Cause and red/green (eon-50, 2026-10-27, x86_64 Linux, base abdbfd0, `nix develop -c eon-test -p eon-runtime --lib zz_repro -- --test-threads=1 --nocapture`, 1-minute load 7-13). The reproduction is kept outside the repository at ~/.cache/eon-agents/1fxc-work/repro.rs, with logs red*.log and green.log next to it. It adds two temporary tests to quota.rs `mod tests`, both run while four threads fork and exec /bin/sh in a loop.

- Spawn error kind. In each of 2000 rounds the test writes a fresh script with the `script` helper and spawns it at once. Old helper: ETXTBSY in 107, 135, 44 and 49 of 2000 rounds across four runs (the last with fork-forcing pre_exec forkers), and no other spawn error. When the first spawn hit ETXTBSY, an immediate second spawn hit it again in 46/135, 20/44 and 24/49 of those rounds. Fixed helper: 0/2000.
- The failing test's prefix, 1500 rounds: script, the 50 ms claude fetch timed, then Quotas::start_every for codex and the test's 2 s wait. Old helper: the claude spawn failed (the read ended before its 50 ms timeout) in 12/1500 rounds; the codex snapshot was missing at 2 s in 0/1500. Fixed helper: 0/1500 failed claude spawns, 0/1500 missing snapshots, slowest snapshot 25 ms.
- Conclusion. The helper's own write makes an immediate exec fail with ETXTBSY under concurrent forks; that is the proved cause class. The full failure needs the codex worker's spawn to fail too (it then waits its 60 s interval), which happened once in 191 suite runs and 0/1500 times in this focused loop; it was not reproduced end to end. Plain scheduling delay is not supported: across 1500 rounds at load about 10 the slowest snapshot was 25 ms, against the 2 s budget.
- Fix (test-only, quota.rs `script`): a child `sh` writes the script (`printf '%s' "$1" > "$0"`), so the test process never holds a write descriptor that a forked child could inherit; it then only chmods by path. All five callers already use fresh paths, which the redirect needs. The output-bound fetch (flood) now spawns, so it exercises the bound.

title: Report the created pane and tab IDs in eon pane create and tab create JSON replies
description:
## Why

`eon pane create --json` and `eon tab create --json` reply with the whole workspace snapshot, but nothing in the reply says which pane or tab the command just created (checked 2026-11-06 on the installed 0.1.18: keys are generation, window, workspace, active_tab, geometry, entries, tabs, sidebar, quotas, attention_queue, running, busy). An agent that starts a pane must diff the pane IDs before and after, which races with any other agent or person adding a pane at the same moment. rota-pt9 (`rota launch --pane`, rota opens the agent's pane itself) needs the new pane's ID for its session registry, and the mac-proof driver already works around the gap with a before/after diff (eon/tools/mac-proof/src/scenario.rs `new_pane`).

## What

Add a top-level `created` object to the JSON reply of every action that creates a pane or tab: `{"tab": "t12", "pane": "p40"}` (`pane` null when no pane was started). Human output unchanged. Document it in the owning contract (EON-C for the CLI action replies) and docs/USAGE.md.

## Acceptance

- `pane create --json` (with and without `--no-focus`, with and without `-- COMMAND`) and `tab create --json --directory` report the created IDs; tests assert them.
- Contract text amended (minor; approval mode per Lucca 2026-11-04).

Filed by eon-overseer 2026-11-06; filed only, not started.
close_reason: Landed: pane create, tab create and edit JSON replies report created IDs

comments.author: lucca
comments.text:
# eon-1jeai plan: `created` in pane and tab create JSON replies

Base: edge aa970dc (EONW v34, Eon 0.1.18). Worktree /home/lucca/.cache/eon-agents/eon-1jeai.

## Finding: no EONW change needed

- The CLI prints every workspace action's reply in `control()`
  (runtime/crates/eon-runtime/src/cli.rs:1186), from the `Response::Snapshot`
  the supervisor builds right after `dispatch` in the same request step
  (supervisor.rs ~2890, `workspace_snapshot_in(reply_workspace)`), where
  `reply_workspace` is the caller's workspace (or the shown one), which is the
  workspace the action acted on (workspace.rs ~674).
- `IdAllocator` (workspace.rs:121) hands out `wN`, `tN` and `pN` window-wide,
  rising, never reused (recovery sets `next_pane` past every recovered pane,
  `next_tab = 2` past t1).
- `workspace new` already relies on exactly this: the CLI names the highest
  `wN` in the reply as `created` (cli.rs ~1330). So the CLI can name the new
  tab and pane the same way, with no wire change.

## Shape

Top-level `"created":{"tab":"tN","pane":"pN"|null}` in the JSON reply, placed
where `workspace new` puts its `created` (after `workspace`/`caller`).
Human output unchanged.

| CLI | EONW action | `created` |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `pane create [--no-focus]` | `CreatePane` | newest pane in the reply, and its tab |
| `pane create [--no-focus] -- CMD` | `CreateCommandPane` | same |
| `edit -- FILE` | `Edit` | same |
| `tab create` (pending, picker) | `CreateTab` | newest tab; `pane` null (no pane until the pick) |
| `tab create --directory D [--no-focus] [-- CMD]` | `LaunchTab` | newest tab and its one pane |

"Newest" = highest numeric suffix, the same rule as `workspace new`.
The pane rule spans all tabs, so a pane created from a caller in a background
tab names that tab.

## Scope decisions (deviations to confirm)

1. `workspace new` keeps its existing string `created: "wN"` (the bead: no
   other reply changes). Recommendation: keep; changing it to an object breaks
   its existing consumers.
2. `tab directory TAB` (a pick on a pending tab) and `popup hide` of a pending
   tab's pair also start a tab's first pane, but as a side effect of naming an
   existing tab. Recommendation: leave them out; their caller already names the
   tab, and the bead says no other reply changes. Recorded here for review.
3. `CreateColumn` has no CLI path (parity exception eon-agent-parity-a9g0.6);
   nothing to change.
4. mac-proof's `new_pane` before/after diff (eon/tools/mac-proof/src/scenario.rs)
   stays: it drives installed releases that predate `created`. Follow-up for
   the overseer to file if wanted.

## Code

cli.rs `control()`: classify the action (workspace / tab / pane creation),
one small helper for the numeric ordinal shared with the existing `wN`
rule, emit the JSON key only in JSON mode.

## Docs and contract

- EON-C10 (docs/CONTRACTS.md, near the `pane create` / `tab create --directory`
  bullets ~1212-1240): one sentence for `created`.
- docs/USAGE.md command table rows for `pane create`, `tab create`, `edit`.
- CHANGELOG.md: one entry (agent-visible CLI JSON).

## Tests (eon/crates/eon/tests/workspace_control.rs, real supervisor, via eon-test)

- `commands_from_a_terminal_target_its_column_and_stale_callers_change_nothing`:

title: Keep the directory picker's header and footer readable in narrow panes
description:
## Why

Found in eon-7cf0y.7's installed check (/home/lucca/.cache/eon-agents/eon-7cf0y/claude7-report.md, "Finding for the overseer"; screenshot /home/lucca/.cache/eon-agents/eon-7cf0y/dog/out7/default-attached.png, left half): in a narrow directory picker (a window tiled to about 60 columns) the header and footer lose their left end, because the picker's `--keep-right` (needed for long paths) also applies to fzf's header lines in fzf 0.73.1. The running-windows notice then reads `··on windows are still running: proj, another Eon build`: the count, the most important word, is gone. The footer is clipped the same way (`··se directory · …`). At full width both fit.

Overseer chose to accept this for eon-7cf0y.7 (it matches the footer's existing behavior) and file this follow-up.

## Do

Make the picker's header and footer readable at narrow widths without changing how long paths show. Options to weigh: put the most important part last (count at the end) or first with the header built to fit the picker width (Eon knows the pane width when it builds the argv), shorter narrow-width variants, or a newer fzf option if one exists. Text changes need the overseer's/Lucca's approval (product text). Prove with a narrow-pane installed capture.

## Acceptance

- At 60 columns the running-windows count and the footer's first action stay visible; long paths still keep their right end.

title: Keep the link hover steady while the terminal is printing output
description:
## Report

Lucca, 2026-10-22 ~16:30 -03, installed eon ckisr53k (EONW 15): "hovering on links while a program
or agent is outputing makes it flicker on and off a lot". The link highlight and its Open/Copy hint
blink while the terminal keeps receiving output (for example a Claude Code agent streaming), even
though the pointer stays still on the link.

## Contract

VEN-C5 (native hyperlinks), Failures: "Revision, attachment, geometry, presentation, focus,
occlusion, or scroll changes retire link actions." Scene re-detects plain-text targets on every
frame's visible rows.

## Hypothesis (inference, not yet evidence)

Each new terminal revision retires the hovered target, and the highlight only returns once hover is
re-derived (on the next pointer event or frame). Streaming output produces revisions many times a
second, so the highlight toggles at that rate. First check: confirm it in the Venus scene/input code
and reproduce it in isolation. Use a headless Venus with the pointer on a plain-text URL and an OSC 8
link, while the terminal prints a line every ~50 ms on rows away from the link. Count how often the
highlight changes state.

## Expected

While the pointer stays still and the same target (same URI, same visible cells) remains under it,
the highlight and hint stay steady across revisions. They change only when the target under the
pointer actually changes or goes away (scrolled, overwritten, rewrapped, retired by focus or
presentation). Activation safety stays as it is: Ctrl+click still opens only a target that is
current at both press and release.

## Contract change (needs Lucca's approval before code)

Keeping hover across revisions narrows VEN-C5's "revision changes retire link actions" for the
hover highlight. Proposal to bring him: a revision re-validates the hovered target instead of
retiring it. If the same URI still occupies the same cells, the hover is kept. Activation still
requires press and release on the same current target. Bring the exact wording first.

## Portability disposition

neutral (scene and hover state; no platform API).

## Scope

In scope: Venus hover persistence across revisions for OSC 8 and plain-text targets; the VEN-C5
text; a Venus suite regression test; `venus/CHANGELOG.md` if the contract changes; `CHANGELOG.md`
(user-visible).

Out of scope: link detection rules, open/copy behavior, the AccessKit target list (unless it
flickers for the same cause, then note it).

## Acceptance

- In the isolated reproduction, the highlight stays on for the whole streaming run while the
  pointer is still and the target is unchanged.
- When the line under the pointer is overwritten or scrolls away, the highlight follows within one
  frame.
- One isolated installed dogfood observation: hover a link while an agent streams output, with no
  flicker.

## Verification

A Venus suite regression test for hover across revisions, through `nix develop -c eon-test -p
venus` (or Venus's documented harness), plus `cargo fmt --check` and clippy for venus. One isolated
installed observation per venus/docs/DEVELOPMENT.md.
close_reason: Hover and hint stay steady under output, and Ctrl+click survives output that keeps its target. VEN-C5 updated with Lucca's approved wording. Proof is in the comments; the profile refresh is left to the coordinator.

comments.author: lucca
comments.text:
Cause, from code at edge 1ce839f (venus/src/application.rs). The bead's hypothesis was close but not exact.

- Every plain output frame bumps the presentation generation (`content_changed`, ~2052). Eon workspace focus changes and invalidations bump it too.
- `render()` (~2731) takes the highlight from `focused_link()`, and `status()` takes the hint from it through `link_status()`. Both go through `link_scene()`, which requires `presentation.is_current(candidate)`. The candidate being drawn is not yet published, so a frame that presents a new revision is drawn with no highlight, no hint, and a 1.5-row notice box instead of 3 rows.
- After `Presented`, `inspect_pointer_link()` re-derives focus against the newly published identity. The identity differs, so it calls `refresh_client_view()`, and the next frame draws the highlight again.
- Result: each revision gives one frame off, then one frame on. With output arriving every frame, the highlight stays off most of the time. The ignored live test (~4961) asserts the unpresented half: `handle_transport(linked_frame(7)); assert!(focused_link().is_none())`.
- Same mechanism for Ctrl+click: press at revision R and release at R+1 are different `LinkFocus` identities, so a Ctrl+click during streaming output is consumed without opening (test "a captured click cannot cross a frame replacement").
- AccessKit's link list is replaced per presented revision, not cleared in between, so it does not flicker from this cause.

Proposed shape (pending Lucca's approval of the VEN-C5 text): render derives the highlight and hint from the candidate scene it is drawing (the same pointer hit test, with `scroll_offset == 0` for unshifted). Actions keep requiring a published current target. When focus moves to a new identity at the same cells with the same URI, it updates without a second redraw.

Lucca approved the VEN-C5 change in this session on 2026-10-22, around 16:50 -03 ("1 ok, 2 ok"). Both items are in this bead's scope:

Change Failures to: "Attachment, geometry, presentation, focus, occlusion, or scroll changes retire link actions. A revision retires them too; the hovered target is re-derived in the new frame."
2. Ctrl+click: replace "Opening requires a press and release on the same current presented target" with "Opening requires a press and release on the same target: the same URI over the same cells, presented at both; output revisions between them keep the press, and every other change in Failures retires it."

The regression test covers both: the hover flicker, and Ctrl+click failing while output streams.

title: Add eon-test --under-load N to repeat a test under 2x-core synthetic load
description:
## Why

K5 of ~/.cache/eon-agents/eon-ideas-work/ideas.md (Lucca's idea request,
2026-11-09; filed by eon-overseer's "auto-decide" note).

On 2026-11-09, 10 flaky-test beads were open and 14 closed. Several repeat
the same acceptance by hand, for example eon-yz6ei: "passes 20 consecutive
runs under a synthetic load of 2x cores". Each author rebuilds that harness.
eon/crates/eon/tests/workspace_control.rs alone has 164 timeout literals and
its own `wait_for*` helpers.

## Scope

- `eon-test --under-load N[:FACTOR]`: start bounded CPU busy loops (FACTOR x
  cores, default 2) inside the sandbox from nix/test-sandbox.nix, run the
  named test N times, stop the loops, print pass count, slowest run and the
  first failure's output. Run through heavy.sh on shared machines.
- Not in this bead: a shared `wait_until(what, deadline, condition)` helper
  that reports what it waited for; adopt it per flaky bead as each is fixed.
- It must not weaken tests: product bounds (send_typing_quiet_ms, the 2 s
  Orbit answer limit) stay exact.

Contract: none (repository tooling, Rust/Nix). Codex review applies.

## Acceptance

Reproduce one open flake red with the new flag before its fix (for example
eon-flaky-focus-test-15g8o), and document the flag in docs/DEVELOPMENT.md.

## Completion boundary

Use nix/test-sandbox.nix's existing isolation/nextest delegation and preserve normal arguments/offline behavior. Durable orchestration belongs in Rust; Nix/shell supplies process glue only. Keep N[:FACTOR]; reject malformed, nonpositive or overflowing counts/factors before starting workers and require the selected test. Do not bypass Darwin's live-supervisor refusal; state any Linux-only support honestly.

Success reports N/N and slowest run. A failed selected test stops repetition, returns failure and prints that output. Interruption/timeout/failure clean up only exact child workers started by this invocation, with bounded lifetime. One small self-check covers argument rejection, failure propagation and cleanup. Retain the requested real-flake reproduction (choose an open example at implementation time), documentation and current required workspace/review checks; no new benchmark suite or shared wait helper.

title: Show the directory the shell used, not the resolved one, for a tab on macOS and symlinks
description:
## Why

On macOS `/tmp` is a symlink to `/private/tmp`. Eon reports a terminal's directory from the
process's physical cwd (getcwd), so a tab opened from `/tmp/x` shows `/private/tmp/x`, unlike the
path the person typed and the shell shows. Found by kz4p.25 (its workspace_control.rs test now
expects the physical path for 8 cwd-derived assertions). The same happens on Linux for any
symlinked directory.

Lucca, 2026-10-28, agreeing to the recommendation: show the path the shell used.

## Contract

The tab/pane directory Eon shows and reports (`eon workspace --json` `directory`, tab labels). Check
docs/CONTRACTS.md for the owning EON-C text before code; if a contract names "the working
directory" precisely, propose the wording change to Lucca first.

## Change

Prefer the logical directory: when Eon learns a directory and a logical `$PWD` is available (the
launching environment, or the shell's reported cwd such as OSC 7), use it only if it resolves to
the same physical directory (same device and inode); otherwise keep the physical path. One owner
for this choice in Eon Runtime.

## Acceptance

- Launching from a symlinked directory on Linux shows the symlink path; a stale or lying `$PWD`
  falls back to the physical path (tests for both).
- workspace_control.rs's 8 macOS-adjusted expectations go back to the raw path where they derive
  from such a launch.
- `nix develop -c eon-test -p eon-runtime -p eon`, fmt, clippy on Linux and darwin.

## Scope

Eon Runtime directory reporting only. Not part of the macOS CI blockers. Codex review per
AGENTS.md.

## Current evidence and boundary (6e63eb7)

supervisor.rs:1020-1023 chooses explicit directory or env::current_dir(); cli.rs:653 and :3080 use std::path::absolute for launch/tab-create --dir. EON-C17 is docs/CONTRACTS.md:3010; use eon session --json.

Include absolute/relative --dir in the approved logical-path outcome: preserve valid explicit spelling, resolving relative inputs against the validated logical cwd. Trust PWD only when absolute and device/inode matches actual cwd; absent, invalid or mismatched PWD falls back. Keep shell-reported OSC 7 distinct from the stable tab launch directory; do not infer current terminal cwd from the supervisor's old environment.

Audit the former eight macOS assertions individually; reverse only expectations deriving from a validated logical launch. Cover Linux symlinks, --dir and bad PWD; native Darwin evidence is required for macOS claims. Runtime owns the choice; portability neutral using native filesystem identity. Confirm EON-C17 permits this spelling, stop for approval if its meaning changes, and use current whole-workspace/boundary proof requirements.

title: Let the CLI act on the calling terminal's own workspace when another generation is current
description:
## Why

Found 2026-10-24 by the overseer (agent in Lucca's live Eon window, g1-712f) when Lucca asked to
run Codex workers "live on this stack" (pane stack of his window). The window's terminals carry
`EON_TERMINAL=session-1.338547-...` for generation g1-712f, but another live generation
(g1-7241..., started 16:44 in the default runtime root with no Venus window) had become the
"current" one. Then, from a terminal of Lucca's window:

    $ eon workspace --json
    {... "tabs":[{"id":"t1","directory":"/home/lucca/pjs/games/machines_vs_aliens", ...}]}
    # the other generation's workspace, silently, not the caller's

    $ eon pane create --json --no-focus -- tail -F <log>
    {"error":{"code":"unknown-caller","detail":"the calling terminal is not live in this Eon workspace"}}

So an agent in a perfectly live Eon terminal cannot act on its own window, and reads another
window's state without any sign that it is not its own. AGENTS.md "Humans and Agents": every
window action has a CLI path an agent in an Eon terminal can use, naming its target by ID.

## Goal

The CLI targets the calling terminal's own workspace when it runs inside an Eon terminal,
whatever generation is current, and otherwise has an explicit way to name the target
(generation or window ID). `workspace --json` says which generation/window it describes. Owner:
Eon's CLI target resolution (eon crate) over Eon Runtime's caller identity.

## Acceptance

- Reproduce first: two live generations, the caller's not current; `eon workspace --json` and
  `eon pane create --no-focus` from the caller's terminal act on the caller's workspace.
- Outside Eon, the current generation stays the default; an explicit target flag (name chosen in
  the contract) reaches a non-current one.
- Contract wording to Lucca before code (EON-C CLI clause).

Related: eon-agent-parity-a9g0, eon-89ho (pane create --tab), eon-agent-terminal-control-n8ic and
eon-pane-send-research-fo4p (sending input to a pane; the other limit hit the same day: an agent
cannot drive a TUI such as a live Codex session running in a pane).
close_reason: Landed: CLI targets the caller's own workspace

comments.author: lucca
comments.text:
Approval (Lucca, 2026-10-25 ~05:40 -03, direct to the overseer, answering its numbered list item 3): "approval to all". Approved: inside an Eon terminal the CLI resolves the terminal's own supervisor and workspace through EON_TERMINAL whichever generation the invoked build would pick, with no fallback to another workspace; outside Eon, explicit `--generation G` / `--window ID`; workspace JSON gains `generation` and `window`. The draft's choices stand as it recommends (separate flags; explicit targets constrain rather than override the caller; window-only selection follows `window attach`'s rule; bounded validated discovery; incompatible builds fail explicitly). Drafted wording (Codex draft reviewed by the overseer, 2026-10-25):

**3. eon-2gk7 — Resolve the caller’s supervisor and workspace**

**Current clauses → proposed replacements**

EON-C10, `docs/CONTRACTS.md`, caller-targeting sentence:
> When set, it makes `pane create`, `edit`, `pane close PANE`, `pane move` and `tab move` act on that terminal's tab instead of the active tab: `pane create` adds to the caller's column, the moves move the caller's own pane or tab, and `pane close` resolves PANE in the caller's tab.

Replace with:
> For workspace control, `EON_TERMINAL` selects the live supervisor and workspace that own that exact terminal, independently of the invoked CLI build’s current generation. Within that workspace, `pane create`, `edit`, `pane close PANE`, `pane move` and `tab move` retain their calling-tab, column and pane rules: creation uses the caller’s column, moves act on its pane or tab, and pane close resolves its target in the caller’s tab.

EON-C10, remaining-command sentence:
> Other commands, and commands run outside Eon terminals, ignore it.

Replace with:
> Other workspace-scoped commands use the caller’s workspace and retain their existing per-tab rules. Without a calling terminal or explicit target, workspace control uses the invoked build’s current generation in the selected runtime namespace and its shown workspace. Launch, lifecycle and local information commands retain their existing targeting.

EON-C10, build-mismatch failures:
> This includes a caller whose CLI build has no supervisor in that terminal's window, as when an `eon` from another build runs inside an Eon terminal: its detail names that build's generation and points to the terminal's own `eon`, never to running `eon` first. Other commands run inside an Eon terminal that find no supervisor of their build still exit 4, with the same detail.

Replace with:
> Absence of this CLI build’s supervisor does not prevent control of the caller’s compatible supervisor. Caller resolution uses the complete opaque terminal identity and never falls back to another workspace. A malformed or stale caller exits 3; failed or ambiguous resolution changes nothing. An unavailable or incompatible selected supervisor fails explicitly without starting, presenting or restarting it.

EON-C11, default-generation clause:
> Eon and eonbase use separate runtime namespaces and default to their exact current generation.

Replace with:
> Eon and eonbase use separate runtime namespaces. Launch and lifecycle defaults use their exact current generation; Eon workspace control follows EON-C10’s caller and explicit-target rules.

**Add to EON-C10 Result:**
> Workspace commands accept `--generation GENERATION` and `--window ID` before any `--` operand separator. `--window` selects an independent window’s runtime namespace; otherwise the existing runtime namespace applies. `--generation` selects an exact generation there. With only `--window`, selection follows `window attach`’s current-or-sole-live-generation rule. If `EON_TERMINAL` is set, the selected supervisor must validate that caller; explicit targeting does not waive caller validation. Workspace CLI results name the described `generation` and `window`, with `window` null for the default namespace, and identify the projected workspace through shn4.3’s workspace discriminator.

**Wire:** no additional EONW change is required for generation routing or the CLI’s `generation`/`window` fields. Existing `Request.caller: Option<String>` carries the opaque identity; the selected supervisor validates the exact live run. Generation IDs retain `g1-` plus 32 lowercase hex digits; independent window IDs retain eight lowercase hex digits. Caller-scoped snapshot projection needs shn4.3’s work, including distinguishing the described workspace from the shown one. Unknown explicit targets exit 3, unavailable supervisors exit 4, malformed flags/IDs exit 2, and ambiguous window selection exits 1.

**Open choices**
1. Flags: separate `--generation`/`--window`, one `--target`, or positional targets. **Recommend separate flags**, reusing the nouns and validation already used by `attach GENERATION` and `window attach ID`.
2. Explicit target precedence: constrain the caller or override it. **Recommend constraining it**; `env -u EON_TERMINAL eon ...` already expresses acting without caller context and preserves command-pane caller validation.
3. Window-only selection: current-or-sole-live, or require a generation. **Recommend the existing `window_generation` rule**, with `--generation` resolving ambiguity.
4. JSON: `generation`/`window` or `generation_id`/`window_id`. **Recommend `generation`/`window`**, matching lifecycle results and `window stop all --json`.
5. Discovery: validate candidate supervisors in the inherited namespace, or add an exported routing locator. **Recommend bounded validated discovery first**; the current identity is opaque, and `Runtime.sessions` contains local session IDs rather than complete caller identities. Never match only `session-N`.
6. Incompatible builds: fail explicitly or delegate workspace commands to the retained old executable. **Recommend explicit failure**, preserving the existing EONW boundary; delegation currently belongs to attach.

**Conflicts/splits:** “current” in the report is misleading: `current_generation()` hashes the invoked build’s immutable assembly; a newer live generation does not become a mutable global current. title: Notify the desktop when an agent finishes, fails or needs input
description:
## Why

Approved as "configurable later" (`eon-configurability-audit-twdr`, Lucca, 2026-10-23); undeferred
and raised to P2 by Lucca on 2026-10-27 ("update them make both p2", with eon-iwmz). Apart from the
one-time detach notice, nothing tells the desktop when an agent needs the person, so a person
working in another window misses finished, failed or waiting agents.

## Historical evidence (edge a4c0904)

- `runtime/crates/eon-runtime/src/notification.rs`: the only desktop notification today, the
  detach notice (EON-C8), sent through org.freedesktop.Notifications over the session bus from a
  worker thread; Linux only.
- EON-C31 (Agent attention, docs/CONTRACTS.md): raises, Seen rules and the `background` state
  (eon-agent-background-work-yte0.2, closed) that holds a raise while an agent's background work
  runs. Spans every workspace (EON-C33).
- The terminal bell (BEL) is ignored; handling it needs Orbit's ordered-effects channel (`orb-ll1`,
  deferred) and stays with eon-bell-accent-appearance-2t2z.

## Approved decisions (Lucca, 2026-11-06)

Lucca said "agree" to the overseer's recommendations on the Sol plan in
/home/lucca/.cache/eon-agents/eon-2kvr-plan-work/ (contract step bead/01-contract-step.md):

- N1 (planner D1) yes: a terminal counts as seen only in the shown workspace of an attached Venus
  whose window has native desktop focus; unknown focus counts as unfocused.
- N2 (D3) yes: [attention] notify = true by default, one switch to disable; sound stays eon-iwmz.
- N3 (D4) yes: once per raise or blocked episode, no delayed nagging, nothing while viewed.

## Scope

Out of scope: terminal BEL handling (2t2z, `orb-ll1`), the completion sound itself (eon-iwmz),
phone push (eon-sixj, which reuses this bead's trigger, quiet rule and setting family), macOS (a

## Stop Conditions

- Stop if the trigger needs a second attention owner outside EON-C31.

## Authority and sequencing

Read .1/.2 before implementation; do not redo closed slices on this epic. .2 records the short EON-C31 amendment approved by the overseer under Lucca's auto-decide mandate; verify its exact plan text before editing. The earlier N4 revision requirement must retain names by default and IDs-only when notify_names=false.

Athas/Rex per-state switches and a 60-second timer are research suggestions, not new approval. .1 explicitly records Lucca rejecting the timer; .2 rejects per-kind toggles. Keep N1-N4, one notify switch, no rate limiter. Linux first, Darwin/eonbase no-op.
