comments.text:
# eon-2kvr slice 1 — implementation notes (focus-aware Seen)

Implementer: eon-2kvr-1 (Claude Opus 5.5), worktree
`/home/lucca/.cache/eon-agents/eon-2kvr-1`, base edge `4168d66` (EONW v34,
Eon 0.1.18). Plan: `eon-2kvr-plan-work/PLAN.md` sections 1-6 and 8; contract
step `bead/01-contract-step.md` C1-C3. Approval: Lucca 2026-11-06, N1 (D1);
D2 by the overseer (bead comment of 2026-11-06 01:36 UTC).

## What changed

- **Runtime** (`runtime/crates/eon-runtime`):
  - `platform::read_available`: one `recv(MSG_DONTWAIT)`, per call; the
    socket's blocking mode is never changed (the Present writer and the
    child's stdin share the open file).
  - `supervisor::NativeFocus` on each `PresentationProcess`: complete
    8-byte `focus:0\n`/`focus:1\n` reports, latest wins; partial reports
    change nothing; a turn reads at most 512 report bytes and leaves the rest
    for the next turn; EOF, a malformed report or an I/O error end reports
    for that process, set focus unknown and record one diagnostic line
    (`Eon Desktop focus reports are invalid|ended|failed: ERROR; treating
    the window as unfocused`), except that EOF from a Venus that has already
    exited records nothing.
  - `PresentationProcess::start` always gives Venus stdout on the same
    private socket, with modes `stdin-ready-focus-v1` (admission) and
    `stdin-focus-v1`. Admission still reads exactly eight `ready-v1` bytes.
  - `SupervisorState::tend` drains the current Venus's reports first, in
    full Eon only (also while a Stop is incomplete). Every Seen gate passes
    `venus.as_ref().is_some_and(PresentationProcess::viewing)`:
    `workspace_snapshot_in` (Inspect and action replies), `projection`
    (EON-C39), `follow_attention`, and `attention.handled` in
    `dispatch_control_request`. The startup snapshot still passes `false`.
    Attachment-based uses (naming, busy, notices, lifecycle) are unchanged.
  - `attention.rs`: `attached` renamed to `viewing` (field, parameters,
    docs); logic unchanged.
- **Venus** (`venus/src`):
  - `launch.rs` recognizes only the two new modes; old names are not
    aliases.
  - `application.rs`: `FocusReporter` (Mutex/Condvar mailbox holding only
    the latest unsent focus, one `venus-window-focus` worker, write without
    the lock, no repeat of the last written focus, half-close of the write
    direction plus one stderr line `Cannot report Venus window focus:
    ERROR` on failure), and `admit_presentation`, which writes readiness
    when admission asks and then starts reports from the window's latest
    focus, only for a supervised workspace. `WindowEvent::Focused` also
    reports. Venus stays `forbid(unsafe_code)`; no manifest change.
- **Docs**: EON-C31 Seen and Window focus (C1, C2 verbatim) plus a status
  amendment line; VEN-C14 Result paragraph (C3 verbatim) plus a status
  amendment line; `docs/USAGE.md`; `eon/skills/eon/SKILL.md`;
  `venus/docs/LAUNCH.md#supervised-startup`; `CHANGELOG.md`;
  `venus/CHANGELOG.md`.

## Deviations from the plan

1. **VEN-C19 text** (`venus/docs/CONTRACTS.md`, Supervised startup
   admission) named the old mode `stdin-ready-v1`. Renaming the mode without
   an alias makes that sentence false, so its mode name changes to
   `stdin-ready-focus-v1`; nothing else in VEN-C19 changes. The plan did not
   list this contract. It is a mechanical consequence of approved D2.
2. **Test names kept for historical proof records.** EON-C31's proof cites
   `seen_needs_an_attached_venus_and_the_exact_focused_terminal` and VEN-C14's
   cites `startup_admission_keeps_presentation_control_enabled`. Both keep
   their names (the latter now parses `stdin-ready-focus-v1`), so the indexed
   proofs still resolve. The plan's `focus_reporting_modes_are_supervised` is
   added beside it; the old `stdin`/`STDIN` assertions in the typography test
   moved into it.
3. **No new attention.rs test** (`viewing_sees_only_the_selected_terminal`).
   Attention's logic is unchanged (a rename), and the existing semantic tests
   already cover viewing false/true, hidden workspaces and popups, newer work
   and Background. The one gate the unit tests never exercised with
   `viewing = false`, `handled(FocusAttention)` on an already-focused target,
   is covered at the boundary by
   `supervisor::tests::selected_raise_waits_for_native_window_focus`
   (CLI FocusAttention to the selected pane keeps the finish queued).
4. **Venus tests split.** The plan's `focus_writer_keeps_latest_...` row is
   three tests: `focus_writer_keeps_latest_without_blocking_native_reporting`
   (held write, latest-only mailbox, no repeated focus),
   `interrupted_and_short_focus_writes_still_send_complete_frames`, and
   `a_failed_focus_report_closes_only_its_direction` (a write that times out
   on a full socket; Eon then reads EOF while `present\n` still reaches
   Venus). The failure is induced by a full socket and a write timeout rather
   than by closing Eon's receiving half, because a reader-side shutdown also
   makes Eon's own reads return 0, which would not prove Venus's half-close.
5. **`focus_reporting_follows_admission`** exercises `admit_presentation`, the
   helper the readiness point calls, not an `Application` (constructing one
   needs a native display). "Before admission no frame" holds by
   construction: `focus_reporter` is `None` until that helper runs. The
   cached-true case (`ready-v1focus:1\n`) shows a focus that arrived before
   admission is reported after readiness.
6. **Field named `ended`**, not `disabled`, in `NativeFocus`.
7. **Size.** About 870 changed Rust lines against the plan's "rescope above
   ~600". Product code is about 315 lines; the rest is the plan's required
   tests. Flagged to the overseer in STATUS.md; not split, since Runtime and
   Venus must ship together.

8. **Installed observation differs from plan section 6 in mechanics**:
   built packages run from `--out-link` paths (no throwaway `nix profile`);
   Sway, wdotool, grim and jq come from existing store paths rather than
   `nix shell`; the driver's whole-run bound is 400 s, not 120 s (two windows,
   a reattach and eonbase took about 15 s in the passing run, but startup
   under load can be slower); Sway runs with `no_focus [all]` so no window
   takes focus by itself and the driver moves focus explicitly; the probe
   starts by closing the startup quick search with Escape; eonbase runs in
   its own `EON_RUNTIME_DIR`, since one runtime namespace refuses a second
   mode of the same generation. The plan's error and blocked steps, detach,
   reattach and eonbase are all covered.

9. **Installed eonbase step runs `sleep 2`**, not the plan's
   `read -r _` with a closed control stream: the driver checks only that
   eonbase starts and exits 0 with its command. Control EOF in a
   non-workspace launch is covered by the existing VEN-C14 tests, not by
   this run.

## Review round 1 (overseer INBOX 2026-11-06 ~03:40Z)

- **Rebase.** The change moved from `4168d66` to `b69b2cb`
  (`eon-agent-parity-a9g0.3`, close any tab by ID): `git diff --binary`
  saved as `slice1-r0.patch`, reversed, `git checkout --detach b69b2cb`,
  `git apply -3`. `CHANGELOG.md` and `venus/CHANGELOG.md` conflicted on
  adjacent Unreleased entries; both kept, this change's entry first. No
  other file conflicted, and `b69b2cb` added no Seen caller or presentation
  launch use in the Runtime.
- **Deviation 10 (approved by the overseer, nit 3).** Plan section 3.2 had
  more than 512 report bytes in one turn end reports for that Venus's life.
  Now a turn reads at most 512 bytes and defers the rest; only a malformed
  report, EOF or an I/O error ends reports. Test: the parser test writes 65
  reports (64 `focus:0`, then `focus:1`) and sees `false` after one turn and
  `true` after the next. Sensitivity R7 (bound raised to 4096) goes red at "read past one
  turn's bound", and R10 (round 0's exact read loop) goes red at the first
  poll after the burst (`supervisor.rs:4147`).
- **No "ended" line for an exited Venus** (nit 6): `read_native_focus`
  returns silently on EOF when `child.try_wait()` reports an exit.
  `replacement_venus_does_not_inherit_focus` now keeps each fake Venus alive
  until it is replaced and checks one "ended" line for a live Venus's EOF
  and none for an exited one's (R11 red).
- **Error text** (nit 7): `cannot create Eon Desktop presentation return
  channel`, since the channel now exists in every supervised launch.

## Fixed values (AGENTS.md rule 6)

No new configurable value. These stay fixed:

- Native-focus Seen semantics: an approved EON-C31 contract rule (N1/D1),
  not a preference.
- The 8-byte `focus:0\n`/`focus:1\n` reports and the mode names: a private
  launch interface between components shipped in one closure (VEN-C14,
  `venus/docs/LAUNCH.md`), a protocol bound.
- The 512-byte per-turn read budget: a work bound that keeps a burst of
  reports from holding the supervisor loop; the rest is read next turn.
- The `venus-window-focus` thread name and the diagnostic lines: support
  identities, not product values.

title: Investigate directory-scoped lookup of past agent conversations
description:
## Why

From the Atuin Threads research (eon-overseer, 2026-11-11; /home/lucca/pjs/refs/competitor-audit-2026-10/atuin-threads-strands-deciders.md, idea 1). Atuin 18.24 (MIT) captures Claude Code, Codex, OpenCode and other agent conversations, searches them with full-text search, and gives agents read-only lookup tools. Eon shows only live terminals, so someone starting an agent cannot see what earlier agents in the same directory already did.

## Scope

A first step that only investigates: could Eon offer opt-in, directory-scoped lookup of past conversations from the Agent popup and the CLI by reading Atuin's data or its read tools, instead of owning transcript adapters and sync itself? Note that Atuin's local search index holds readable conversation text. Report a recommendation with cost and trust boundary. Related: eon-agent-popup-resume-p681 (launch and empty history only).

## Acceptance

A written recommendation on this bead; no product change without approval.

## Research boundary

At a named Eon revision and inspected Atuin version, compare supported read-only tools/APIs with private database parsing; record directory attribution for symlinks/worktrees, permissions, retention and readable-text exposure. Do not assume stable schemas. Separate provider resume IDs from pane/process IDs and never mutate a live conversation.

The recommendation covers opt-in popup/CLI use, empty/unavailable history, consent, ownership/cost and no-adoption. Read applicable REFERENCES routes. Resume launch stays eon-agent-popup-resume-p681; fork identity stays eon-4l33f. No account access, transcript copy/index, sync, dependency or product/contract edit is authorized here; propose follow-ups only. Proof is the evidence-backed recommendation.

title: Stop Eon's Helix from running a repository's own Steel code (.helix/*.scm) without trust
description:
## Problem (security)
Eon's Helix (Yazelix/nova-helix at the pinned cd48907) loads a repository's own Steel code when it opens inside that repository. In helix-term/src/commands/engine/steel/mod.rs:2247-2259, with `HELIX_STEEL_CONFIG` unset, `preferred_config_path` returns `<workspace>/.helix/{helix,init}.scm` whenever both files exist, with no workspace-trust check (the trust gate at :1541 covers only reloads). Steel can `spawn-process`, so `git clone <untrusted repo>` and then opening Helix there from Eon (Alt+Shift+O Editor, `eon edit`, Files Enter) runs that repository's code as the user. Eon does not set `HELIX_STEEL_CONFIG` today (EON_HX at flake.nix:686 points straight at the package).

Found 2026-11-03 by the eon-bjov6 planner (/home/lucca/.cache/eon-agents/eon-bjov6/plan.md, "Eon already runs unsandboxed Steel today"); verified by the overseer at nova-helix cd489078.

## Fix (narrow, independent of eon-bjov6)
For every Helix that Eon launches, set `HELIX_STEEL_CONFIG` to Eon's own Helix config dir (`<eon config root>/helix`, the same dir Helix already reads `config.toml` from), so the user's own `helix.scm`/`init.scm` still load and a repository's `.helix/*.scm` never does. Find every Eon path that starts Helix (wrapper, Editor popup entry, `eon edit`, Yazi opener) and set it in one owner. Do not change the fork in this bead.

## Contract
Add the trust clause to the contract that owns Eon's Helix launch (EON-C9 or EON-C10, whichever names EON_HX): "Helix that Eon starts loads Steel only from Eon's Helix config directory, never from a repository's `.helix` directory." Applied under the overseer's obvious-text rule (Lucca 2026-11-03); reviewers check it.

## Acceptance
- A red-first test or Nix check: a scratch repo with `.helix/helix.scm` + `.helix/init.scm` whose init writes a marker file; Helix started through Eon's launch path in that repo writes no marker; a marker in `<config root>/helix/init.scm` still runs.
- Isolated installed check with real Helix (no live Eon).
- CHANGELOG.md bullet (security fix). Review loop with Codex (trust boundary).

## Follow-ups (not this bead)
- The fork itself should gate workspace Steel on workspace trust for standalone and Nova users: a nova-helix change, tracked separately.
- eon-bjov6 builds on this (its plan sets HELIX_STEEL_CONFIG to a packaged dir that loads the user's init last).
close_reason: Eon's Helix loads Steel configuration (helix.scm, init.scm) only from Eon's Helix config directory, never a repository's .helix; a non-UTF-8 config root refuses Helix launch. Proof, review ledger and gate PASS recorded above.

For each fork (hexal, mitos, github.com/gj1118/helix; find the canonical repos and say which you looked at):
1. Base: which upstream rev it tracks, how far behind master, rebase cadence, maintainers, activity, licence (MPL-2.0 like Helix?).

A report with a comparison table (stock 25.07.1, upstream master, nova-helix, each fork) and numbered decisions for Lucca with recommendations. No code or flake changes. Using a fork as Eon's editor would be a dependency decision for Lucca.

title: Rename workspaces to sessions in the CLI, IDs, JSON, config and product text
description:
## Why

Lucca, 2026-11-06: "we can just rename workspaces to sessions right now and not worry about the bigger change", "eon session ls is shorter to type", then "ok" to each of the overseer's five points. Lucca asked for the name on 2026-11-04 (eon-hyil8, item 4: "Session" replaces "workspace" in product text, the CLI and configuration, no aliases). This bead does only the rename; the ownership model in eon-hyil8 (sessions owned by Eon, shown by windows) stays undecided and out of scope.

## What (approved)

1. "Session" replaces "workspace" in product text, the CLI, configuration, docs, contracts' user-facing text and the embedded agent skill. No aliases, shims or compatibility paths (Lucca: no legacy code).
2. CLI: `eon session` (inspect), `eon session ls`, `eon session new|switch|rename|close`; `workspace` and `workspaces` are removed outright. The list verb is `ls` for every noun, no plural commands.
3. IDs: `w1`, `w2`, ... become `s1`, `s2`, ... everywhere a person or agent sees them.
4. CLI JSON keys rename too (e.g. `"workspace"` to `"session"`), superseding eon-hyil8's 2026-11-04 "JSON field names retain their spellings" (Lucca 2026-11-06: Eon is not announced, agents read docs and JSON side by side). Internal wire and code names may stay where no person or agent sees them; if EONW field or tag names are visible in CLI JSON they rename with it.
5. Configuration: old `workspace` key names are warned about once at startup and ignored; they never block startup and do nothing (not an alias). Defaults documented in CONFIGURATION.md.
6. The Workspaces picker and Alt+Shift+S's labels say Sessions; the key itself is unchanged.

## Contract

EON-C33 and every contract that names workspaces in user-facing text, EON-C10/EON-C11 CLI clauses, CONFIGURATION; exact text in the plan. Lucca approved the points above; the overseer approves wording that carries them out, Lucca anything beyond them.

## Acceptance

- Every CLI command and JSON key named in USAGE and the skill uses session/s1 forms; the old commands fail as invalid (exit 2); a test asserts no user-visible "workspace" remains in help, USAGE, the skill or CLI JSON (with an explicit allowlist for internal names).
- A config with old `workspace` keys starts, warns once, and the keys have no effect.
- The installed window shows Sessions in the picker and the Eon Bar.

## Order

After the window-family CLI change; before eon-ezeb7 (completion).

title: Show the Eon icon in the Eon Bar
description:
## Decision
Lucca, 2026-10-19: show the Eon icon in the Eon Bar.

## Contract (provisional; needs Lucca's approval before code)
- Consumer: a full-Eon user on native x86_64 Linux Wayland.
- Result: the Eon Bar shows the Eon icon (the shipped `assets/eon.png` mark, the same one the
  desktop entry uses) at a fixed size that fits the existing tab-strip height, at a fixed position.
- Failures: a missing or undecodable icon shows no icon and leaves no gap, hit target or accessible
  node; the icon never displaces required tabs, controls or drag space under width pressure
  (VEN-C21 priority); it stays sharp at integer scales.
- Contracts: an extension of EON-C21 (native workspace header) and VEN-C21 (native Eon Bar
  workspace header); stop for approval of the text first.

## Ownership
Eon owns product identity and the icon asset. Venus owns the bar's geometry, painting and AccessKit
projection. Venus must not hard-code Eon's brand, so the slice decides how the asset reaches Venus
(decision 1).

## Open decisions (recommendations)
1. Delivery: Eon's launch passes the icon to Venus as a launch input the way other product inputs
   travel (recommended, keeps Venus brand-neutral); or Venus embeds it at build time (cheaper, but
   puts Eon's brand inside Venus); or EONW carries it (a protocol revision for a static image; not
   recommended).
2. Position: at the bar's leading edge before the first tab (recommended, where app marks usually
   sit).
3. Behavior: decorative only, with no click or hover action (recommended); a click target such as
   an About or menu is a separate feature.
4. Accessibility: no accessible node, since it is decorative (recommended); or one static label
   "Eon".
5. Width pressure: drop the icon first, before quota chips (recommended).

## Reference gate
Consequential only if decision 1 adds a launch-input or protocol field: then record the existing
launch-input path in Eon and Venus, a comparable header (e.g. Ghostty's or WezTerm's tab bar), the
rejected delivery options, and the check before code.

## Prerequisites
None.

## Acceptance
Venus layout test: icon present, its size and position, and absent with no gap or node when the
asset is missing or under width pressure; affected Rust tests through `nix develop -c eon-test`;
fmt and clippy for the changed Venus crate; nix build; one isolated installed capture showing the
icon in the bar; review loop; profile refresh.

## Scope boundary
The static icon only: no animation, menu, click action, theming variants or new icon design. Linux
Wayland only; no macOS claim.
close_reason: The Eon icon shows at the left end of the Eon Bar with Lucca's approved geometry, the round (?) and right group order, narrow and overflow yielding, and a reservation that keeps live values and resets from moving the tabs. # For the bead

Gate tree **`370b0f65e982183098d5a1ff933763b294f87764`** on edge **`819fd51`** (private index; uncommitted worktree
`/home/lucca/.cache/eon-agents/eon-369s/wt`, HEAD detached at `819fd51`). Moved from `a012ead`
by applying the diff three-way; nothing conflicted (tree `49ca1de`, as the gate predicted), then
one docs-only change: PRESENTATION's round `?` spacing says "after a chip or reading" (the gate's
optional item). Earlier, moved from `0da39a8` to `a012ead`; edge's EONW v30 renamed the protocol
module, so the two test modules this change adds code to import `v30`. Edge's quit prompt, the Detach and Quit Shortcuts rows and the hints
(`eon-7cf0y.3`, `.16`) are untouched by this change and their tests pass in the suites below.
This section supersedes the round sections above.

## What changed (final behaviour)

- **Logo at the bar's left end.** The Eon Bar starts with `assets/eon.png`'s logo in its own
  colours, two logical pixels shorter than the tab pills (pill height − 2 × scale, rounded to
  whole pixels: 28, 36 and 56 px at scales 1, 1.25 and 2), centred on them. Its centre is as far
  from the window's left edge as the bar's centre line is below the top, and the workspace label
  (else the first tab) starts as far after it as it lies from the left edge (11, 13 and 22 px of
  ink). It is decorative: no click, hover or accessible node. It is not a `[bar] widgets` item and
  shows whatever the list holds.
- **When the logo shows.** Venus first lays the bar out with the logo and every listed live item
  at the widest it can be. For each provider that has a quota fact it reserves Codex's two chips,
  or Claude's two unscoped chips plus one per scoped window its latest read reported; each chip
  is as wide as `{scope }{last minute}/{duration} 100% old` over the canonical five-hour and
  seven-day windows and the provider's own, with every digit set to the font's widest digit.
  Every listed reading and the clock are reserved with or without data. The logo shows only if
  that bar shows everything (the workspace label, every tab at its full width, every chip,
  reading and version label) and the whole tab strip fits unscrolled; the bar is then laid out
  with what the items show now. Otherwise the bar is exactly the bar without a logo. So the
  logo hides before any other item and stays hidden at every narrower width, and it hides
  whenever the tabs would overflow, however wide the window.
- **Resets.** The runtime drops a window at its reset until the next read. Venus remembers the
  scoped windows of Claude's latest read (`ScopedWindows`, keyed by the read's `observed_at`) and
  keeps reserving them until a new read reports a different set or Claude's quota goes away, so
  no window's reset moves the tabs. The tab scroll and live values (quota numbers, readings, the
  clock) never do either. Lucca's approved exception: the logo can change once when a provider's
  quota first appears or goes away (as it does when all its windows reset before a read, the
  runtime then dropping the whole fact), or when a read finds a scoped window gained or lost. A
  window opened after a scoped reset and before the next read learns the scoped window only at
  that read, which is a read finding it.
- **Missing icon.** A missing or unreadable icon file shows no logo and leaves no gap, logs one
  stderr line, and never fails launch. Eon passes only an absolute `EON_ICON`, since Venus refuses
  a relative `--eon-icon`.
- **Delivery.** Nix derives `$out/share/eon/eon-icon-256.rgba` from `assets/eon.png` (trimmed,
  centred on a transparent square, Box-resized to 256×256, premultiplied 8-bit RGBA; the build
  fails unless it is 262144 bytes). The `eon` wrapper sets `EON_ICON`; Eon reads it as the
  product's icon; the supervisor passes `--eon-icon PATH` to every workspace window (never a
  terminal window). Venus reads the file once at startup (a square of 16–512 px a side,
  4 bytes per pixel), area-averages premultiplied RGBA to the drawn size and draws a colour glyph.
  No new dependency, no PNG decoder, no wire change.
- **Right end: `(?)  EON <version>  ×`.** Readings and quota chips keep Eon's order between the
  drag region and Shortcuts; then Shortcuts, the version label, Close. The version label always
  sits between `?` and `×`, whatever its place in `[bar] widgets`; it is plain text.
  Accessibility order follows the visual order.
- **Round `?`.** Shortcuts is a circle as tall as the tab pills, outlined like the bar's chips,
  with the existing hover, pressed and focus states; its target is the whole control column
  (larger than the circle). After a chip or reading it keeps the chips' own spacing (the target
  reaches back over the space, so it only grows). Its `?` is centred on its ink: Venus shapes
  the glyph, reads its ink box from the rasterized glyph as glyphon places it, and puts the ink's
  centre on the circle's centre in whole physical pixels.
- **Corner.** Close's target reaches the window's right edge. Its `×` is placed by its ink the
  same way: centred vertically on the bar's centre line, with as many whole pixels between its ink
  and the window's right edge as between its ink and the top. Where that would put ink outside
  Close's target (a window about 100–120 logical px wide), the ink centres on Close's glyph
  position instead, moved only as far as keeps it inside the target.
- **macOS.** Venus sets no macOS title-bar extensions, so a decorated window keeps its native
  title bar above the bar and `--no-decorations` has none; the bar never shares a row with the
  traffic lights (code reading, no macOS capture).

## Rule 5 (humans and agents)

No new window action: the logo is decorative (no click, hover or focus), and the round `?`, the
version label and Close keep their existing actions, keys (Alt+/, Alt+Shift+W) and CLI paths.
Nothing a person sees becomes unreadable to an agent: the logo carries product identity, not
workspace data, and needs no new CLI state or action; the running version stays in the
AccessKit tree and in `eon generations --json` (each record's `eon_version`).

## Rule 6 (configurability)

- The logo image, its colours and its being shown are product identity, fixed: Lucca chose that
  it shows whatever `[bar] widgets` lists; it yields only for room, and a missing icon file
  removes it.
- One new fixed value: the logo is 2 logical px shorter than the tab pills. Lucca chose it on
  the look ("the icon feels one or a couple pixels too large"); it scales with the display like
  every bar metric and stays fixed as part of the logo's proportions to the pills.
- Everything else derives from the existing bar metrics (font size, line height, padding,
  scale): the pill height, the insets and the gap after the logo, Close's corner inset, the `?`
  circle's size and its spacing after a chip.
- The version label's place between `?` and `×` is fixed layout chosen by Lucca; `[bar] widgets`
  still chooses whether it shows.
- The `?` circle's outline uses the existing chip outline colour and `border_width`.

title: Centralize Venus chrome colors in one role-named palette
description:
Contracts: Venus chrome presentation (VEN-C8, VEN-C18, VEN-C30 colors as drawn); no contract text change expected, since this is a behavior-preserving refactor.

Decision (Lucca, 2026-10-26): centralize Venus's colors in one palette and use it everywhere.

Problem: Venus has about 84 inline `SceneColor { r, g, b }` literals across venus/src/render/chrome.rs, render.rs and render/cells.rs, and only two named constants (`CARD_OUTLINE`, `DEFAULT_BACKGROUND` in render.rs). Shades repeat by hand (bright label 239,244,248; dim label 162,174,190; accent 126,231,185 defined locally inside `build_border_title`), so contrast drifts per call site; eon-furp's tab contrast bug came from that.

Change: one Venus palette module with role-named colors (for example surface, bar, pill idle/hover/selected, text primary/secondary, outline neutral/focus, accent, danger, attention states), each defined once; every draw site uses the role. Keep test-only literals (fixtures like 255,0,0) where they are test inputs. `focus_color` stays the configured value Runtime sends; the palette holds Venus's own fixed chrome colors.

Acceptance: identical rendering: no pixel changes (prove with the existing Venus render tests plus a before/after capture or golden comparison of the chrome at one size and scale). Record each role's contrast ratio against its background in the bead, flagging any below 4.5:1 for text or 3:1 for UI edges as follow-up candidates (do not change colors in this bead). Venus tests, fmt and clippy green.

Scope boundary: no user-configurable theme (Eon Runtime would own parsing; separate decision), no color changes, no Orbit terminal palette (cells.rs ANSI defaults stay unless they are chrome colors). Prerequisite: eon-furp landed (955df93).
close_reason: done

title: Make eonbase-closure absence checks fail on a match
description:
## Why

The eonbase-closure flake check asserts that the eonbase closure excludes Eon's managed tools
and the full eon package, and that the eonbase wrapper does not name libexec/eon/bin. Both
absence assertions are written as `! grep ...` (flake.nix:542, :546). Under the stdenv builder's
errexit, a command negated with `!` never stops the script, so the check passes even when grep
finds a forbidden path. Found during eon-zti4.2 review.

## Scope

In scope: the two absence assertions in eonbaseClosureCheck in flake.nix. Make each fail on a
match and on a grep error (status 2), using the pattern managed-command-path already uses.
Out of scope: other checks, eonbase composition, and the bundle.

## Acceptance

- eonbase-closure fails when a forbidden store path is in the eonbase closure or the wrapper names
  libexec/eon/bin, and when grep cannot read its input.
- It passes on the current tree.

## Verification

- Red/green: run the check's exact build script with a forbidden path that is in the closure.
  It exits 0 before the fix and non-zero after.
- `nix flake check` exits 0.
close_reason: Absence checks fail on a match or grep error; proof recorded

comments.author: lucca
comments.text:
Proof (revision = this commit; x86_64 Linux, native host, Nix):

Fix: each absence assertion in eonbaseClosureCheck is now

A match (status 0) and a grep error (status 2) both fail the check.

Red/green: I ran the check's exact buildCommand (from `nix derivation show`) under the stdenv
builder's `set -eu; set -o pipefail`, unchanged and with four mutations:
- orbit added to the forbidden list (orbit is in the closure);
- the wrapper grep pointed at a string the wrapper contains;
- the closure store-paths file made unreadable for the absence grep only;
- the wrapper file made unreadable for the absence grep only.

| Script | Unchanged | Each of the 4 mutations |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| HEAD | exit 0 | exit 0 (the bug) |
| This commit | exit 0 | exit 1 |

nix flake check: exit 0 (default, eonbase-closure, managed-command-path, helix-grammars).
This is a check-only change with no package behavior change, so the eon profile was not
refreshed.

Review ledger: 1 pass, using a fresh Claude subagent and Codex (gpt-6.1-sol, xhigh, read-only).
Nothing blocking. Nits not applied, both pre-existing and out of scope:
- forbidden packages are matched by their default output only, not other outputs;
- the wrapper grep reads bin/eonbase, not bin/.eonbase-wrapped.

title: Run lifecycle test suites outside the live Eon session

## Chosen outcome — Lucca, 2026-10-14

title: Show retained failed-start runs in the CLI and stop them blocking a terminal number
description:
From the Opus review of eon-g3vdz (2026-11-11): when a failed start's cleanup cannot be confirmed, terminal-N's launch record is retained. The next create picks the same N and fails at create_new (runtime sessions.rs:71) with 'resolve the launch record before retrying'; nothing retries the cleanup later and no CLI shows retained runs (rule 5). The error says not to retry until the retained run ends but gives no way to see when. Fix: pick a free terminal number past retained records, retry the retained cleanup when the child is reaped, and list retained runs in eon session --json (and the human-readable form) with what the person can do. Before code, read EON-C10/EON-C11 and snapshot/protocol ownership. Added session JSON is script-visible: propose fields, human output, lifecycle semantics and any EONW/contract amendment for exact-text approval. Distinguish still-running, exited-but-cleanup-pending and cleanup-failed retained starts, outside usable pane topology. Give an existing safe action or honest diagnostic, never record deletion/PID reuse advice.

Prove live terminal-N retention permits a different free number without overwrite; exact-child exit retries reconciliation and leaves other live/new terminals untouched. Include repeated cleanup failure and stale process/run identity. Human/JSON output agree without a second state owner. title: Investigate which EON, ORB and VEN contracts should be boundaries rather than features
description:
## Why

Lucca, 2026-10-30, after a project opinion pass: "create one bead to investigate each of those".
The finding: Eon has 89 indexed contracts (35 EON, 21 ORB, 33 VEN by `## ` heading count),
including chrome items such as "Local clock in the Eon Bar" (EON-C29) and "CPU and memory use in
the Eon Bar" (EON-C30). Contracts carry the most ceremony (user approval to add or change, proof
records, Codex review of text changes). Their weight pays off at boundaries (wire formats,
lifecycle, trust). On presentation features it may add approval gates with no safety benefit.

## Evidence

- `docs/CONTRACTS.md`: EON-C1 … EON-C33; `docs/CONTRACTS.md:2450` EON-C29;
  `docs/CONTRACTS.md:2470` EON-C30.
- `orbit/docs/CONTRACTS.md` and `venus/docs/CONTRACTS.md`: the ORB and VEN indexes.
- `AGENTS.md:168-175` "Contract-Driven Method": stop for user approval before adding, changing,
  replacing, or retiring a contract.
- `orbit/AGENTS.md` "Contracts, crates, and test doubles": index only user-visible behavior,
  correctness boundaries, ownership invariants and interfaces; never configuration literals or
  speculative features.
- `docs/AGENT-PROTOCOLS.md` AP-CONTRACT-001: give a stable ID only when later consumers need one.

## Scope

In scope (read-only investigation; report to Lucca):
- Classify every EON, ORB and VEN contract as boundary (wire/protocol, lifecycle,
  security/trust, ownership invariant, cross-component interface) or feature (presentation,
  chrome, one-component UI behavior).
- For each feature contract: does a later consumer rely on its ID (other contracts, EON-C28
  fixtures, tests, docs)? What did it cost (approval rounds, proof records, Codex reviews)?
- Propose a criterion for what earns a contract ID and, for feature contracts, a demotion path
  (for example a bead with acceptance checks plus a `docs/USAGE.md` or `docs/CONFIGURATION.md`
  entry) that keeps their proofs and history. Contract IDs are never renumbered or reused.

Out of scope:
- Retiring, merging or editing any contract: each is Lucca's decision.
- EON-C28 (1.x stability) fixtures and the 1.0 proof beads under `eon-igae`; note interactions
  only.

## Acceptance

- A comment on this bead with the classification table (ID, title, class, consumers of the ID,
  recommendation), the proposed criterion as draft rule text, and the list of demotion
  candidates.
- Everything is marked as needing Lucca's approval.

## Verification

- The table has one row per contract heading across the three CONTRACTS.md files.
- Each "no consumers" claim is backed by an `rg '<ID>\b'` over the repository.

## Stop Conditions

- Stop if demotion would weaken EON-C28's 1.x stability promise; report the conflict.
- Stop before any contract or rule edit.

## Maintenance Notes

- Delegate the classification sweep to a subagent; keep the criterion design in the main session.
close_reason: Investigation delivered; Lucca approved all recommendations 2026-10-30; follow-ups eon-vn0nk, eon-08w18, eon-946u

Each "0" in the rg column was rerun by hand: EON-C14, EON-C25, EON-C29 and EON-C30 return only their own heading. EON-C6 has rg 0 but DISTRIBUTION.md:92 cites it as "EON-C5/C6", and EON-C12 and EON-C16 have rg 0 but are product/interface boundaries, so all three stay. No test name or fixture uses a contract ID; every code hit is a comment. Hidden consumer: `components/eon-v5.json` lists VEN-C9, C11, C15, C22, C24 and C25 in `activation.required_contracts`, and `eon-manifest` rejects activation of an unproved contract, so demoting them needs a manifest edit.

## EON-C28 check (stop condition): no conflict

EON-C28 names only EON-C11 and EON-C20 by ID. Both stay, and so does VEN-C20. It binds everything else by document: commands in USAGE.md, keys in CONFIGURATION.md, and the shortcuts the Alt+/ viewer lists. Its Boundary excludes "how appearance and layout render". Demotion is therefore safe under three conditions: every demoted feature's keys stay in CONFIGURATION.md, its shortcuts stay in the viewer, and EON-C20/VEN-C20 keep the reserved-key and override rules. From 1.0, C28's "every other default changes only with a changelog entry and a restoring setting" still governs demoted features' defaults.

## Proposed criterion (draft rule text, for AGENTS.md "Contract-Driven Method" and the Rules of all three indexes)

> A behavior earns a contract ID only when something other than a person looking at the screen relies on it, or when breaking it would lose data, work or trust:
> 1. a wire, protocol, file or configuration format;
> 2. a lifecycle: starting, stopping, recovering, upgrading or shutting down processes, terminals, generations or windows;
> 3. a security or trust rule over untrusted input, credentials or authorization;
> 4. an ownership invariant between components;
> 5. a CLI, JSON, exit-status or configuration surface that scripts and agents rely on, including the CLI path the Humans and Agents rule requires;
> 6. platform and distribution scope.
>
> Presentation (layout, geometry, colour, glyphs, labels, chrome items and their order, animation) and UI behavior whose only consumer is a person looking at it are features. A feature lives in its bead (scope, acceptance checks, proof) and in user documentation (`docs/USAGE.md`, `docs/CONFIGURATION.md`, `venus/docs/PRESENTATION.md`). Its configuration keys, shortcuts and CLI paths stay under the boundary contracts that own those surfaces. A bound or trust rule a feature needs, such as a redraw-rate limit or plain-text-only agent text, becomes a clause of the boundary contract it touches or a test its bead names. Launch arguments between components built and shipped in one closure are internal interfaces documented in `venus/docs/LAUNCH.md`, not contracts. One behavior gets one contract: an owner does not mirror a contract that it only composes.

Under this rule a feature still needs an approved bead, its configurability entry, Codex on its code, and an installed dogfood observation. It no longer needs contract text approval, Codex review of contract text, a twin EON and VEN entry, or an index proof record.

## Demotion path (keeps proofs and history; IDs never reused)

One approved bead per batch:
1. **Check the docs.** Confirm the behavior's user-facing text is in USAGE.md, CONFIGURATION.md or PRESENTATION.md, and add anything missing.
2. **Move the proof.** Copy the Proof field's test names and proof beads into the bead.
3. **Retire the section.** Replace it with the heading, `Status: Retired <date> by Lucca: demoted to a feature; behavior in <doc#anchor>; proof in <beads>`, and a `Reason`. Git keeps the old text.
4. **Retarget citations.** Update citing contracts and code comments.
5. **Edit the manifest.** Remove the IDs from `components/eon-v5.json`. This is a manifest change, so it needs the full Rust and Nix proof route.

No changelog entry is needed, because no user-visible behavior changes.

## Demotion candidates

- **Wave 1 (16 IDs; no boundary contract's meaning changes):**
  - EON-C13 and VEN-C11: opacity.
  - EON-C14 and VEN-C15: blur. Keep the patched-winit rationale in venus/docs/CRATES.md.
  - EON-C24 and VEN-C24: hints.
  - EON-C25 and VEN-C25: version label.
  - EON-C29 and VEN-C27: clock. jiff stays in CRATES.md.
  - EON-C30 and VEN-C28: CPU and RAM. The macOS readings stay under EON-C7 and VEN-C16.
  - VEN-C22 and VEN-C26: quota chips. Their EON twins are already retired, and EON-C27 keeps collection and trust.
  - VEN-C9: decorations.
  - VEN-C29: bar order. EON-C32 keeps the setting and the quota-read gating that EON-C27 relies on.

  Pointers to retarget: EON-C19 (to VEN-C11), EON-C27 (to VEN-C22 and C26), EON-C32 (to C25, C29, C30 and VEN-C29), and VEN-C8, C20, C30 and C31 (to C11, C22, C24 and C26).
- **Wave 2 (needs boundary text first):**
  - EON-C21 and VEN-C21: header. EON-C33 and EON-C8 delegate to VEN-C21 by ID, and its ≤10 Hz badge bound must survive as a clause.
  - VEN-C32: attention inbox. Its plain-text trust clause duplicates VEN-C30's, so do VEN-C30's split first.
- **Split on next touch (11):** EON-C1, C8, C10, C18, C19 and VEN-C1, C5, C8, C18, C19, C30 keep their IDs, and their presentation text moves out when each is next amended. C8, C10, VEN-C8 and VEN-C30 alone are about 1,400 lines and the most-amended sections.

## Other findings

- VEN-C6 and VEN-C12 have no heading and no Retired entry. The index rules require one. Bead history shows C6 was a dropped accessibility plan and C12 an identity ID lost in consolidation.
- The manifest's `activation.required_contracts` omits proved contracts that the product uses (ORB-C14 to C16, VEN-C16, VEN-C26 to C32). It may be stale or deliberately partial. Filed as eon-08w18 (investigation only).
- EON-C10 contains a near-copy of EON-C33's workspace section.

## Decisions for Lucca

1. **Adopt the criterion above** in AGENTS.md and the three indexes' Rules. Recommended: yes. It matches AP-CONTRACT-001 ("stable ID only when later consumers need one") and Orbit's existing rule, and nothing in Orbit changes.
2. **Demotion means Retired with a pointer.** Extend each index's Status line to "Retired: explicitly replaced, removed, or demoted to a feature". Recommended over a separate feature index, because the user docs already hold the text and a fourth copy would repeat the duplication.
3. **Approve wave 1 (16 IDs) as one bead,** with the manifest edit. Recommended: yes. It touches no boundary meaning, and C28 is unaffected.
4. **Defer wave 2 and the 11 splits** until each contract is next amended, inside that amendment's approval. Recommended: no proactive split work.
5. **Mark VEN-C6 and VEN-C12 Retired** as part of the wave 1 bead. Recommended: yes. The index's own rules require it.
6. **Approval for new features moves to the bead.** Recommended: you approve a feature bead's scope as today, and contract-text approval rounds stop for features. Without this, the criterion saves little.

title: Split Venus stack_inset and inner_inset into role-named tokens
description:
## Why

Split the broad Venus chrome inset names into names for the roles they serve, so changing one role later does not silently couple unrelated surfaces. This is the P3 follow-up requested by Lucca during the eon-wuau8.1 landing replay on 2026-11-11.

Contract: no EON-C, ORB-C or VEN-C changes. Preserve all existing geometry and draw inputs. Owner: Venus. Portability: neutral.

## Evidence

- Fable review of eon-wuau8.1, finding 4, `/home/lucca/.local/state/rota/runs/review-chrome-tokens-ufable-1/log`: `stack_inset` combines the hints-row margin and frameless-header inset; `inner_inset` is similarly broad. The review requests a separate follow-up.
- `venus/src/scene/tokens.rs:75` at reviewed tree `2bd131b39a5fa04f59fa7122ead6b45aa1b26142` and rebased tree `7a42dc09008127e45e6d08196f584ede57c47476`: `inner_inset(metrics)` returns `metrics.padding / 2.0` for sidebar row content/list, pane and heading buttons, keycap legends and floating scrollback text.
- `venus/src/scene/tokens.rs:102` at those trees: `stack_inset(metrics)` returns `metrics.padding / 3.0` for the hints-row bottom margin and frameless pane-header inset.

## Prerequisites

eon-wuau8.1 must land first; it introduces `scene/tokens.rs` and the two names. Read root and Venus AGENTS.md, then inspect every caller of both functions before choosing role names.

## Scope

In scope:
- Split `stack_inset` and `inner_inset` into role-named tokens in `venus/src/scene/tokens.rs` and update all their callers in `venus/src/scene.rs`, `venus/src/render.rs` and `venus/src/render/chrome.rs`.
- Update the owning token table with each name, unchanged formula/default value and consumers.

Out of scope:
- Any visible change, arithmetic reorder, rounding change, layout or draw-order change.
- Other tokens, new configuration, colours, contracts and control-layer redesign.

## Acceptance

- Each formerly shared inset is named for its role; no generic `stack_inset` or `inner_inset` caller or definition remains.
- Every role preserves the original expression and default value: 4 px for former stack insets and 6 px for former inner insets at padding 12.
- Venus scene/render checks retain the same expected geometry, and no golden or expected value is changed.
- The bead records the final names and their consumers.

## Implementation Notes

1. Group callers by the role of the inset, using existing token conventions.
2. Rename/split definitions and update callers without changing expressions or introducing wrappers.
3. Verify the complete diff contains names and documentation changes only.

## Verification

- `nix develop -c eon-test -p yazelix-venus` passes through the project sandbox; existing scene/render assertions detect geometry drift.
- `nix develop -c cargo fmt --check` and `nix develop -c cargo clippy --locked -p yazelix-venus --all-targets -- -D warnings` exit 0. Schedule heavy commands through the overseer's heavy.sh and use this session's assigned target directory.
- Compare old/new expressions and call sites to confirm the token split changes no values. Reuse the retained eon-wuau8.1 chrome_dump harness if a value-preservation question remains.

## Stop Conditions

- Stop if keeping the same geometry needs a formula or expected-value change.
- Stop for user approval if a contract change becomes necessary.
- Stop if the cited callers have drifted beyond this naming-only scope, or the same verification failure repeats twice after a reasonable fix attempt.

## Maintenance Notes

Two roles may share today's formula and remain separate names. Keep this as one bounded naming change, not a broader token redesign. Fable findings 5 and 6 are resolved in eon-wuau8.1 and are outside this follow-up.

title: Prove Yazelix Eon as a thin orchestrator
description:
## Current planning disposition — 2026-09-08

This is an unclaimed, deferred product-horizon container. The user authorized reconciliation of the Eon backlog after benchmark/focus-policy commit `418c388`; no implementation child, runtime change, new issue, platform, consumer cutover or distribution channel is activated. EON-C7 and `eon-linux-wayland-product-wr0` govern Linux/native-Wayland-only scope with exact x86_64 alpha proof. The Nova transition below remains a separately gated consumer plan; its historical macOS path cannot block unrelated Eon Linux work. Organizational epic links use `related`; real outcome prerequisites retain `blocks`. Exact contract phases and defaults belong to `docs/CONTRACTS.md` and README.

## Goal and permanent product hierarchy

Keep Eon a thin orchestrator with one canonical exact component graph and one owner for each behavior.

- **Eon** is the full managed experience and permanent product name; command/package `eon`.
- **EonTerm** is the reusable terminal product in this repository; command/package `eonterm`.
- **Nova** remains an independent full Yazelix/Zellij product and currently uses its accepted minimal Rio surface. Any later adoption of exact EonTerm instead of Rio requires fresh Nova-owned acceptance; it is not an Eon alpha requirement.
- **Eonova** remains private transition dogfood and is retired after Nova acceptance.

Do not use `Eon Terminal`, `eon-term`, `terminal-host`, `bare`, `minimal`, or `Eon Workspace` as public product identities. This epic is a deferred planning container and must never be claimed for implementation.

The executable EonTerm transition issues are associated through this recorded sequence, labels, external references, and real `blocks` dependencies rather than parent-child edges. In this tracker parent-child edges are treated as prerequisites; retaining them would make children wait for an epic that may close only after those children. Closed historical relationships retain their proof history; uncompleted organizational relationships are non-blocking.

## Accepted current state

Eon has accepted activation, one canonical manifest, a Nix-only Linux alpha, Eon-owned workspace topology, managed environment, generation/lifecycle behavior, and proved EON-C12 exact-command terminal hosting, EON-C13 opacity, EON-C14 blur, EON-C16 application identity, and EON-C19 typography/initial geometry. EON-C8 workspace is Partially proved; EON-C11 generations and EON-C15 same-boot recovery are Proven on x86_64 Linux native Wayland, each only within its recorded proof and limitations. Private Eonova proved exact Eon plus Nova-no-Mars composition. `docs/CONTRACTS.md` remains authoritative for exact proof phases.

## Ownership boundary

Orbit owns generic terminal Sessions, PTYs, attachment, transport, authoritative terminal state, and any accepted graphics resource plane. Venus owns native graphical materialization, input, clipboard effects, presentation settings application, and native window identity. Eon owns product lifecycle policy, workspace topology, configuration schema, composition, diagnostics, updates, and distribution; Eon Runtime owns reusable runtime mechanisms and canonical EONW packages. EonTerm reuses the Eon lifecycle and Orbit/Venus boundary without Eon workspace or managed-tool policy. Nova owns `yzx`, branding, tools, Ratconfig integration, Zellij workspace/layout/keys, its current Rio surface, and any later migration to EonTerm. Eonova owns only temporary pins, wrapper, package, namespace, desktop metadata, and dogfood proof.

Cross-repository consumers pin exact proof commits and contract IDs. No repository copies child schemas or behavior, creates a second compatibility graph, or adds a generic terminal-provider abstraction.

## Deferred Nova transition sequence

1. `eon-4is.4` changes and proves EON-C12 under permanent `eonterm` identity while preserving full `eon`.
2. `eon-4is.5` advances temporary Eonova and proves exact EonTerm plus Nova on x86_64 Linux.
3. Venus `ven-native-clipboard-paste-uas`, `ven-lq4`, `ven-terminal-presentation-settings-5y7`, `ven-wayland-background-blur-e06`, and `ven-caller-application-identity-dcb` prove native paste, hyperlinks, presentation application, compositor blur, and caller identity at their owning boundaries.
4. Eon `eon-eonterm-presentation-e4f`, `eon-consume-venus-background-blur-k8o`, and `eon-eonterm-application-identity-xwi` publish EON-C13 opacity, EON-C14 blur and EON-C16 application identity without duplicating Venus policy.
5. Nova `yazelix-5vl-map-eonterm-presentation-0kd6` and `yazelix-5vl-eonterm-nova-identity-e8ra` consume those exact interfaces. `yazelix-5vl-eonterm-kitty-graphics-decision-totz` decides required Kitty/Yazi parity or an explicitly bounded regression.
6. Nova `yazelix-5vl-wmg` is the deferred EonTerm dogfood gate, but its pinned-Mars comparison is stale after Nova accepted minimal Rio. Before reactivation, Nova must refresh that bead against its exact current Rio surface under one predeclared functional/performance envelope and must recommend promotion.
7. `eon-4is.6` first requires a fresh user platform/consumer decision: Eon is Linux-only, and Nova's advertised systems cannot be silently narrowed. Only then can an approved target set receive exact package and native proof.
8. After successful dogfood, Nova must create and accept a Nova-owned EonTerm cutover issue. Closed `yazelix-5vl-eonterm-only-graphical-surface-q5w4` accepted Rio and is historical comparison evidence, not an EonTerm prerequisite.
9. `eon-4is.7` retires Eonova from active use after exact Nova cutover. Destructive repository disposition remains a fresh user choice.

Existing full-Eon workspace, direct/public distribution, Home Manager, editor, isolation, AgentRun, provider-attention, and extension work stays in its current owners. Public distribution is independent of a future private Nova cutover. Any consumer target mismatch remains an explicit decision, not implicit Eon portability work.

## Success Criteria

Eon stays the complete experience and EonTerm stays the small reusable terminal product. Nova may remain on Rio; any later exact-EonTerm adoption is Nova-owned and Eonova disappears from active products only after that cutover or another explicit retirement decision. The result retains one manifest, lifecycle owner, terminal authority, renderer owner, settings inventory, application identity policy per product, and no compatibility aliases or speculative provider framework.
notes: Repository-wide prime — 2026-09-17: reconciled the deferred consumer sequence with Nova's accepted Rio cutover. This is planning correction only; it does not reactivate Nova integration, retire Eonova, or change Eon's product frontier.

Every outcome child (.1, .2, .3, eon-ax4, eon-omq, eon-68v) and the sequence beads .4-.7 are closed; Eon ships as the thin orchestrator in this repository.

title: Expose an Eon single-surface terminal-host lifecycle
description:
## Why

Eon Desktop already has a native one-Orbit-socket mode in which Venus presents one terminal surface and forwards terminal input without EONW workspace shortcuts. Eon always launches Venus with the workspace socket, so an external composition cannot use that accepted child capability through an Eon-owned lifecycle. Nova inside the current workspace mode also loses its Zellij Alt navigation to Eon.

The smallest generally useful groundwork is one explicit Eon terminal-host mode. It belongs in Eon because Eon owns launch, generation, cleanup, and component selection. A private Eonova wrapper must not bypass Eon by starting Orbit and Venus itself.

## Contract routing

- Proposes additive EON-C12 because a separately released composition needs a stable Eon-owned contract. Stop before implementation until the user explicitly approves adding EON-C12 to docs/CONTRACTS.md.
- Changes and reproves EON-C1 through EON-C4 only where the canonical component graph and launch policy gain the accepted mode.
- Consumes and preserves EON-C9 managed command semantics, EON-C10 lifecycle actions and bounded unavailable-action failures, and EON-C11 generation identity, selection, attach, stop, and cleanup.
- Preserves EON-C8 workspace behavior unchanged. Terminal-host mode does not expose or mutate workspace topology.
- Current planning evidence: Eon f4303e2181ccc7ebf7a44bbe333a36e8e3d3eaaa; component manifest Orbit 64db581445bafca1a08a6530f8e44f9c1edbc169 with ORBF v1 and ORBS v2 proof 9d6d2bb37f20ab4ad9e186c7bc715eabef43e757; Venus 6ef19afddaedcbe2b9ed0996e31bc02df5d854ac with VEN-C1 proof e7bda96822274727faacb51731ae19181295e1cd and standalone-capable VEN-C3/VEN-C4 at that revision. Rebaseline all identities before implementation.

## Proposed EON-C12 observable contract

- Consumer: one local user or local composition that asks Eon to host exactly one command in one native terminal surface.
- Trigger: an explicit terminal-host invocation supplies a non-empty argv. The final CLI spelling is approved in the contract index before code; do not overload bare launch or the existing eon run meaning.
- Result: Eon selects the exact current component generation, starts or attaches one compatible terminal-host instance in the selected runtime namespace, owns exactly one Orbit Session for the supplied command, and launches Venus with the Orbit endpoint but no EONW workspace endpoint. Venus therefore sends terminal input, including Alt-h/j/k/l, Alt-m, and Ctrl-t, to Orbit rather than interpreting Eon workspace actions. Reopening the same compatible namespace attaches the existing instance instead of creating a second hidden Session. Command exit closes the terminal surface and supervisor through the existing bounded lifecycle.
- Important failures: an empty command, unsafe runtime namespace, incompatible or wrong-mode live supervisor, component mismatch, child startup failure, stale endpoint, or partial launch returns a bounded explicit error. It never attaches a workspace instance as a terminal host, mutates an EON-C8 topology, substitutes a different generation, or leaves an unsafe endpoint or newly orphaned child.
- Ownership: Eon owns mode selection, exact component set, process orchestration, generation policy, and cleanup. Orbit remains sole owner of the process, PTY, terminal state, attachment, and transport. Venus remains sole owner of native presentation and input collection. The caller owns only the command choice and runtime namespace.
- Boundary: no Nova or Zellij dependency, preset framework, configurable keymap, second workspace model, split layout, terminal parser, compatibility window, remote behavior, macOS proof, or Kitty graphics work.

## Evidence-first reference gate

Required before code:
1. Complete current AGENTS.md, docs/CONTRACTS.md, docs/ARCHITECTURE.md, components/eon-alpha-v1.json, the supervisor and launcher flow, and their focused tests.
2. Exact accepted Orbit contracts and proof named by the implementation baseline.
3. Exact accepted Venus contracts and the one-socket startup/input path at the selected revision. Confirm that direct Eon shortcuts are conditional on a valid EONW snapshot and that standalone mode sends the same keys to Orbit.
4. Nova at exact comparison revision 6c7174b4efca5f139a461d204186c5001d6457bd: yzx enter, yazelix-no-mars, and fixed Zellij keybindings. This is required comparison evidence only; copy no Nova code or schema.
5. Current runtime-generation and installed Nix proof paths.

Rejected surrounding reference scope: Nova package ownership, Mars, Nova shell/configuration policy, Zellij compatibility promises, and all terminal-emulator features unrelated to input pass-through.

Record the required Execution baseline and Reference gate comments before production, test, manifest, or generated-fixture edits. No new crate or direct dependency is expected; stop for the crate gate and user approval if evidence requires one.

## Implementation shape

1. Reuse the current supervisor, generation namespace, component manifest, child-spec helpers, and lifecycle cleanup.
2. Add one explicit mode value at the existing launch owner. Do not create a second orchestrator, adapter process, or generic preset system.
3. In terminal-host mode, start one Orbit Session and invoke Venus with only that Orbit endpoint. Keep workspace actions unavailable rather than allowing invisible tabs or panes.
4. Keep the supplied command as exact argv and preserve eon run as the existing escape hatch.
5. Update the contract index first after approval, then current help, README, architecture/component documentation, changelog if user-visible, focused tests, and the README LOC scorecard.
6. Classify the slice as isolated Linux platform integration; name any newly discovered macOS blocker and stop rather than building a platform framework.

## Acceptance criteria

1. The user explicitly approves EON-C12 and the exact CLI spelling before production edits.
2. One focused deterministic test proves the terminal-host child graph contains one Orbit Session and Venus receives the Orbit endpoint without an EONW endpoint; workspace mode remains unchanged.
3. Focused lifecycle tests prove same-namespace reopen attaches the compatible terminal host, wrong-mode or wrong-generation instances are rejected explicitly, command exit closes the last surface, and partial startup cleanup leaves no new child or unsafe endpoint.
4. A focused input proof at the exact Venus revision demonstrates Alt-h/j/k/l, Alt-m, and Ctrl-t reach the Orbit Session in terminal-host mode and do not invoke EON-C8 actions.
5. The canonical manifest, versions output, runtime identity, and Nix composition remain one exact component graph with no new dependency or duplicate schema.
6. Locked Rust format, check, tests, Clippy, exact Nix build/check, manifest validation, README LOC check, and git diff --check pass.
7. Installed x86_64 Linux dogfood launches Zellij or an equivalent key-reporting command, exercises the conflicting keys, closes and reopens the terminal host, and records the exact package, revisions, environment, and result.
8. docs/CONTRACTS.md records the exact proof-bearing commit only after all canonical checks and dogfood pass.

## Out of scope and stop conditions

Out of scope: creating Eonova, changing Nova, publishing a repository, remapping Zellij, a named preset or profile system, multiple simultaneous terminal-host Sessions, distinct application identity, desktop integration, Kitty graphics, general configuration, macOS implementation, and public compatibility promises.

Stop if standalone Venus requires an unproved Orbit or Venus contract, if lifecycle reuse would duplicate EON-C10/EON-C11 ownership, if invisible workspace mutation is required, if a new dependency or protocol change is needed without its gate and approval, or if the chosen CLI would change bare launch or eon run semantics.
close_reason: Proven and published: Eon owns optional terminal-host decorations, Eonova requests no decorations, installed native dogfood shows no title bar, and both profiles resolve the accepted artifacts.

title: Create the private Yazelix/eonova dogfood composition
description:
## Why

The user chose a pushed private repository under the Yazelix organization to dogfood Nova with Eon replacing Mars. A local-only Nova branch would be easy to leak or lose and would make Nova carry a secret product fork. An Eon preset alone cannot own the exact Nova pin, package, desktop entry, or private distribution boundary.

The smallest useful result is one separate private composition repository. It contains no terminal or workspace implementation: Eon owns the terminal-host lifecycle, Nova owns the Yazelix/Zellij environment, and Eonova owns only exact pins, one wrapper, one package, and one desktop entry.

## Prerequisite and contract routing

- Parent: eon-4is, the thin Eon orchestrator initiative. Nova remains independent.
- Blocked by eon-4is.1. Begin only after proposed EON-C12 is approved, proved, committed, pushed, and available at an exact revision.
- Consumes exact proved EON-C1 through EON-C4, EON-C9, EON-C11, and EON-C12 revisions. It does not change an Eon product contract.
- Consumes Nova only through an exact accepted revision exposing yzx enter and yazelix-no-mars. It creates no Nova contract or compatibility promise.
- Planning comparison identity: Nova 6c7174b4efca5f139a461d204186c5001d6457bd. Rebaseline before implementation.
- The new repository uses Apache-2.0, matching Nova, per the standing user direction.

## Observable integration contract

- Consumer: the authorized user on x86_64 Linux.
- Trigger: the user runs the Eonova package or selects the Eonova desktop entry.
- Result: one wrapper selects exact pinned Eon and Nova artifacts, uses an Eonova-private runtime namespace, and asks Eon's proved terminal-host mode to run Nova's yzx enter from yazelix-no-mars. Eon and Venus provide the native window and terminal surface; Nova and Zellij retain their normal workflow and keys. Alt-h/j/k/l, Alt-m, Ctrl-t, and other Zellij input reach the Orbit Session because EONW workspace materialization is not active.
- Important failures: unavailable private inputs, pin or component mismatch, unsafe runtime namespace, failed EON-C12 launch, or failed yzx startup is explicit. The wrapper never falls back to Mars, regular Eon workspace mode, an unpinned checkout, or a public repository.
- Ownership: Eonova owns only its pin set, Nix composition, runtime namespace choice, wrapper, desktop metadata, and dogfood documentation. Eon owns component orchestration and terminal-host lifecycle; Orbit owns the PTY and Session; Venus owns native presentation and input; Nova owns yzx, Yazelix defaults, Zellij layout and keys, and its shell/tool environment.

## Repository and secrecy boundary

1. Create exactly GitHub repository Yazelix/eonova with private visibility. Create the empty private remote first, verify its visibility through the authoritative GitHub API, then push source. Do not create or push a public remote even temporarily.
2. Keep the work directly on the repository's edge branch unless its generated AGENTS.md selects another branch. Do not change Nova or publish Eon/Nova integration material in Nova.
3. Store no credentials, access tokens, copied private source, machine-specific store paths, personal paths, or runtime state. Private dependency access uses the user's existing Git and Nix credential mechanisms.
4. Add the minimum self-contained AGENTS.md/import record, README, LICENSE, flake.nix, flake.lock, wrapper, and Linux desktop metadata needed by the vertical slice. Do not bootstrap a second issue tracker for this already-owned slice.
5. Use Nova's Apache-2.0 license text. Record the exact licenses and redistribution implications of both pinned inputs before the first push.
6. After the initial private push, all fixes use normal reviewed commits and pushes; never rewrite published history.

## Evidence-first reference and dependency gates

Required before repository or manifest edits:
1. Complete current Eon and Nova instructions, licenses, package outputs, flake locks, wrappers, and launch paths at exact revisions.
2. Eon's exact EON-C12 proof, CLI/help, component manifest, runtime namespace validation, and installed Nix package.
3. Nova's exact yzx enter implementation, yazelix-no-mars output, Mars boundary, Zellij configuration, desktop packaging patterns, and current local proof commands.
4. Nix primary documentation only for a concrete private-input or desktop-package question not answered by the two repositories.

Record in the owning Bead:
- an Execution baseline before the first durable or external write;
- a Reference gate classifying Eon and Nova as required and rejecting copied implementations, Mars, EONW workspace mode, and unrelated Nova packages;
- a dependency gate with exact revisions, licenses, direct and transitive closure cost, update burden, private-fetch behavior, replacement cost, and the user-approved choice before flake manifest edits.

No new Rust crate, service, daemon, plugin, shell framework, or non-Nix dependency is expected. Stop for approval if one is required.

## Minimum implementation

1. Create the private remote and local repository without forking Nova.
2. Define only the x86_64-linux default package and app needed for dogfood. Pin exact Eon and Nova sources; consume Nova's yazelix-no-mars rather than subtracting Mars locally.
3. Add one eonova wrapper. It selects a private runtime namespace below the valid per-user runtime root and invokes the proved EON-C12 surface with exact argv for yzx enter.
4. Install one Linux desktop entry named Eonova that executes the wrapper with Terminal=false. Reuse the current Eon icon and application identity initially; distinct WM grouping or art is deferred until observed confusion justifies it.
5. Document install, launch, update, inspect, and remove commands plus the exact ownership/keybinding model.
6. Keep updates explicit by advancing flake pins and recording the dogfood result. Do not add an updater or channel.
7. Install the package for the authorized user only after local proof, then verify the active artifact matches the built package.

## Acceptance criteria

1. GitHub reports Yazelix/eonova as PRIVATE before the first source push and after the final push; origin points only to that private repository.
2. The repository is independently cloneable by an authorized account and cannot be read without authorization.
3. flake.lock pins exact Eon and Nova revisions. The package consumes Eon's proved terminal-host artifact and Nova's yazelix-no-mars output; its closure contains no Mars artifact.
4. The wrapper uses one validated Eonova-private runtime namespace and exact argv. It contains no copied Eon lifecycle logic or Nova configuration.
5. The installed desktop entry launches Eonova in one native window. A second launch attaches the same compatible terminal host rather than creating a hidden duplicate.
6. In installed x86_64 Linux dogfood, Zellij receives Alt-h/j/k/l, Alt-m, and Ctrl-t; basic shell, Helix, and Yazi text workflows render and accept input; closing and reopening preserves only behavior promised by EON-C12.
7. Regular Eon and Eonova runtime namespaces do not attach to, stop, delete, or report each other's Sessions.
8. Build, flake check, package metadata, desktop-file validation when available, closure inspection, license inspection, repository visibility checks, git diff --check, and repository-specific AGENTS/README checks pass.
9. The proof records exact commits, package/store identity, NAR or closure size, commands, platform, keybinding observations, and known gaps. The private edge branch is committed and pushed, and the active local package matches it.

## Deliberate exclusions

- No Eon preset framework, keymap profiles, EONW tabs or panes, Nova branch, Mars fork, Home Manager module, macOS package, CI, release channel, updater, public announcement, remote access, distinct app ID/icon, or Kitty graphics support.
- Kitty graphics are not acceptance because the currently accepted Orbit contract declares them unsupported. Revisit only if Yazi image workflows materially block dogfood.
- The composition dogfoods Orbit, Venus, Eon lifecycle/input/rendering, and Nova's Zellij workflow. It does not dogfood Eon's EONW workspace tabs and panes.

## Stop conditions

Stop before any source push if the remote is not authoritatively private. Stop if EON-C12 is unproved, if Nova no longer exposes a Mars-free package and terminal-agnostic enter command, if the composition needs copied child code or changes to Nova, if private Nix input access would require embedding credentials, if regular Eon and Eonova namespaces can collide, or if a new public compatibility promise is required.
notes:
Accepted historical state: private Yazelix/eonova commit 61b786d81581207ca2a45ff355953b03491d9b8e composes exact proved Eon ece0f1bc151eeccd15b0172c5fbdbe8ab32c502c with Nova 6c7174b4efca5f139a461d204186c5001d6457bd#yazelix-no-mars. Its Nix-owned wrapper selects `$XDG_RUNTIME_DIR/eonova` and invokes exact `eon terminal -- yzx enter`; one desktop entry reuses Eon icon and WM class. The closure is Mars/Rio-free, namespaces are isolated, the pushed artifact was installed, and the user accepted native dogfood.

Current disposition approved 2026-08-11: Eonova is a temporary private bridge, not a permanent product or compatibility promise. `eon-4is.5` will advance it to exact `eonterm` after `eon-4is.4`; the old exact Eon pin remains valid during that sequence, so the new EonTerm product need not retain `eon terminal`. Nova cutover is `yazelix-5vl-eonterm-only-graphical-surface-q5w4`; `eon-4is.7` removes Eonova from active use afterward while preserving historical proof and requiring a fresh user choice for repository archival or deletion.
close_reason: Private Eonova edge composition is pinned, built, installed, pushed, isolated, Mars-free, and accepted in native dogfood.

title: Publish EonTerm as the reusable terminal product
description:
## Decision

The permanent product hierarchy is Eon for the full managed experience and EonTerm for the reusable terminal product. Their lowercase command and package identities are `eon` and `eonterm`. EonTerm stays in this repository and consumes the same canonical component graph; it is not a new repository, profile framework, or alternate provider architecture.

## Observable contract

- Consumer: a local user or an approved composition that needs one native terminal surface without Eon workspace or managed-tool policy.
- Trigger: `eonterm [--no-decorations] -- COMMAND...` with one non-empty exact argv.
- Result: the current EON-C12 lifecycle hosts that command in one Orbit Session and one Venus surface. Eon retains generation and lifecycle authority; Orbit owns the PTY, terminal state, Session, and transport; Venus owns native presentation and input.
- Failures: missing argv, incompatible components, partial startup, attachment conflicts, and unsupported workspace actions fail explicitly. There is no fallback to full Eon, Mars, another terminal, or a default shell.

This changes and reproves EON-C12, hardens and reproves EON-C1 through EON-C4, and preserves EON-C8 through EON-C11. EonTerm does not consume EON-C8 workspace topology or EON-C9 managed-environment policy.

## Breaking-name disposition

The permanent public spelling is only EonTerm / `eonterm`. Remove `eon terminal`; do not add aliases for `Eon Terminal`, `eon-term`, `terminal-host`, `bare`, or `minimal`. The only known external consumer is private Eonova. Its old exact Eon pin remains functional while this owner publishes the new proof, then a separate Eonova bead advances its pin and wrapper. No compatibility window or adapter is promised.

## Product and package boundary

- Full Eon remains `eon`, with its existing workspace, managed Helix, Yazi, Carapace, shells, configuration, and product identity unchanged.
- EonTerm includes only the Eon lifecycle and exact Orbit, Venus, terminfo, and native runtime needed for EON-C12. It neither exposes nor injects the EON-C9 managed environment and must not pull Eon-managed user tools into its closure.
- One canonical manifest remains the source of compatible component identity. If the selected product composition must be represented, extend that owner truthfully without duplicating the graph or introducing a generic profile/configuration system.
- The first accepted artifact is the existing x86_64-linux Nix proof surface. This bead makes no direct-distribution or macOS support claim.

## References before code

Required: current AGENTS.md; EON-C1 through EON-C4 and EON-C12 index entries and proofs; the canonical manifest/package/runtime owners; current CLI, generation, lifecycle, and terminal-mode tests; and the exact private Eonova consumer wrapper and pin.

Conditional: primary Nix evidence only if closure separation cannot be established from current package ownership; Orbit or Venus source only if an existing contract check exposes an owner gap.

Comparison only: Canario, Herd, Ghostty, Mars, and Zellij architecture research informs product positioning but does not define this implementation.

Rejected: copied child behavior, a second component graph, a generic surface provider, a compatibility alias, a new repository, managed-tool selection flags, a default shell, or broader platform/distribution work.

## Acceptance

1. Current docs and help consistently name Eon and EonTerm and expose only `eon` and `eonterm`.
2. An exact installed `eonterm -- COMMAND...` and no-decorations invocation preserve EON-C12 launch, attach, reconnect, input, resize, exit, and cleanup behavior.
3. Full `eon` still proves its workspace and managed environment unchanged.
4. The EonTerm closure and runtime environment contain no Eon-managed Helix, Yazi, Carapace, shell bundle, or EON-C9 PATH projection.
5. The canonical manifest reports exact component identity for both products without a duplicate graph.
6. Required Eon checks, package/closure inspection, fresh installed dogfood, and `git diff --check` pass at one proof-bearing commit.
7. Update `docs/CONTRACTS.md`, `CHANGELOG.md`, README current-state language, and the Rust LOC scorecard as required by the resulting implementation.

Stop if package separation requires a second compatibility graph, if EON-C12 cannot be preserved under the new identity, or if the implementation would silently narrow an existing Eon contract beyond this approved rename and package split.
close_reason: Simplified EonTerm real-process test setup by 13 lines at published revision bb9a7d3; exact Rust/Nix, installed profile, runtime identity, and live-process preservation proofs pass.

Smallest correction contract:
- Consumer: an installed EonTerm user with current or older live EonTerm generations.
- Trigger: `eonterm generations [--json]`, `eonterm attach [GENERATION]`, or `eonterm stop GENERATION [--json]`.
- Result: reuse the existing EON-C11 discovery, validation, presentation, confirmation/JSON stop, and cleanup behavior against only the EonTerm runtime namespace. Launch remains exact non-empty argv; workspace/config/managed-tool commands stay unavailable.
- Failures: malformed arguments retain EonTerm usage; unknown, incompatible, corrupt, replaced, or unconfirmed generations retain the existing explicit lifecycle failures.

- Confidence 95%; verification strength high through real-process generation, attach, stop, replacement, cleanup, and full flake checks; blast radius one Rust owner plus its focused test/docs.
