title: Advance the temporary Eonova bridge to EonTerm
description:
## Outcome

Advance the private Eonova dogfood composition from the historical `eon terminal` host to the exact accepted EonTerm product. Eonova remains a temporary bridge for proving EonTerm with Nova; it does not become a permanent product, brand, compatibility layer, or second implementation owner.

## Prerequisites and routing

- Blocked by eon-4is.4, including its exact proof-bearing Eon revision and changed EON-C12 spelling.
- Consumes EON-C1 through EON-C4, EON-C11, and EON-C12 at that exact revision and changes no Eon product contract.
- Consumes an exact Nova no-Mars package and `yzx enter`; Nova continues to own Zellij, workspace, tools, and key policy.
- The Nova defect `yazelix-5vl-eonova-shifted-punctuation-9g3h` must be resolved at its confirmed owner or explicitly shown not to reproduce on the accepted EonTerm path before this bead closes.

## Smallest change

Update only Eonova exact pins, lock data, wrapper argv, current-state docs, and proof metadata needed to invoke `eonterm -- yzx enter`. Preserve its private runtime namespace, one package/app, one desktop entry, exact Nova no-Mars input, and current Eon icon. Do not rename the repository, invent Eonova features, copy Eon/Nova code, or add a provider selector, updater, CI, release channel, or second tracker.

Eonova retains its name only while this bridge is needed. A separate retirement bead removes it after Nova itself accepts EonTerm.

## References before code

Required: current Eonova instructions, wrapper, package, lock, installed-profile workflow, and historical `eon-4is.2` proof; exact eon-4is.4 EonTerm package/help/contracts; exact Nova `yzx enter`, no-Mars package, and shifted-punctuation evidence.

Conditional: Eon, Orbit, Venus, or Nova owner source only when a fresh exact-pin failure cannot be routed from the published boundary.

Rejected: compatibility aliases in EonTerm, Eonova-owned keyboard translation, Eon workspace mode, Mars/Rio, a Nova fork, and any permanent Eonova identity.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. Eonova pins the exact accepted EonTerm and Nova revisions and its wrapper invokes exact `eonterm -- yzx enter` argv.
2. The installed x86_64-linux artifact remains private, Mars/Rio-free, namespace-isolated from full Eon, and traceable to the pushed edge commit.
3. Fresh dogfood proves launch, repeat attach, detach/reopen, resize, cleanup, Zellij keys, `?`, representative text/Unicode/paste/mouse, Helix, Yazi, and one long-running command; gaps are routed to their owner.
4. Package, closure, lock, license, private-visibility, desktop, runtime-namespace, and repository checks pass.
5. Current docs describe Eonova as temporary EonTerm-plus-Nova dogfood and point retirement to the accepted Nova cutover rather than promising a product future.

Stop instead of adding an EonTerm alias, Eonova workaround, hidden fallback, public compatibility promise, or broader product scope.

title: Prove EonTerm across Nova's supported systems
description:
## Outcome

If the user later resumes Nova integration, prove one exact EonTerm package and behavior set across Nova's then-advertised Nix systems without narrowing them silently. This is a Nova-consumer portability gate, not a prerequisite for full Eon.

## Current boundary

Deferred on 2026-09-11 when the user selected Eon as the primary focus. Eon's approved `aarch64-darwin` work may supply reusable Orbit, Venus, and EonTerm evidence, but it does not activate Nova integration, `x86_64-darwin`, another Linux architecture, or a multi-target package matrix.

## Prerequisites and ownership

- Reinspect Nova's current supported systems and exact consumer contract before activation.
- Consume exact accepted EON-C13 opacity, EON-C14 blur, EON-C16 application identity, and the final Orbit/Venus revisions selected for Nova.
- Require exact native Orbit and Venus platform proofs for every advertised interactive target; evaluation or compilation is not GUI runtime proof.
- Eon owns the EonTerm package identity and canonical component graph. Nova owns its supported-system promise and cutover choice. Child projects own their platform mechanics.
- A later component-pin change invalidates this evidence before Nova cutover.

Rejected: using Nova to drive Eon's platform order, silently dropping targets or features, hidden Rio or historical Mars fallback, duplicated manifests, per-target behavior under one identity, and folding signing or distribution into this gate.

## References before code

Required: current Nova supported systems and claims; exact EonTerm contracts; accepted Orbit and Venus platform proofs; Eon package instructions; native dependency support per target; and the Nova cutover issue. Any target, dependency, or scope mismatch returns for a user decision.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. Every Nova-advertised target has either an exact EonTerm package with honestly classified native evidence or a precise blocker naming its owner and affected contract.
2. Package identity, argv, presentation, blur request, application identity, component reporting, and failures do not vary silently by target.
3. Runtime checks exercise the exact relevant Eon, Orbit, and Venus contracts on each approved target; build/evaluation evidence is labeled and never widened.
4. Nova cutover cannot close over a blocker, stale component proof, or weaker platform claim without a separate user decision.
5. Canonical package and contract docs record exact revisions, systems, commands, artifacts, closure differences, and limitations.

Signing, notarization, installers, full-Eon macOS support, and public distribution remain outside this issue.

title: Finish retiring Eonova: remove its local profile element
description:
## Outcome

Retire Eonova as an active name and composition after Nova permanently adopts exact EonTerm. Eonova is historical private dogfood, not a third product. Eon and EonTerm remain the Eon repository products; Nova remains the full Yazelix/Zellij consumer.

## Preconditions

- `eon-4is.5` has completed its temporary EonTerm acceptance role.
- `eon-4is.6` has accepted the final EonTerm package/platform result consumed by Nova.
- Nova has separately accepted, committed, pushed, installed, and dogfooded a Nova-owned exact-EonTerm cutover issue. Current `yazelix-5vl-wmg` is only a deferred dogfood/comparison gate and does not authorize cutover; closed `yazelix-5vl-eonterm-only-graphical-surface-q5w4` accepted Rio.
- The user confirms whether the private GitHub repository should be archived, retained read-only, or deleted. Archival is the default proposal; deletion is destructive and is never inferred.
- Before uninstalling or removing runtime state, inspect for live Eonova supervisors, Venus clients, Orbit Sessions, and child work. Stop for the user if any live work exists; never kill or orphan it as cleanup.

This task changes no Eon product contract. It removes only the temporary consumer composition and active Eonova identity.

## Retirement boundary

- Remove Eonova from the active user profile, desktop launcher, application search, routine update instructions, and current product documentation.
- Remove stale Eonova runtime state only when ownership is exact, no process is live, and the state is safe to discard. Preserve unrelated or ambiguous user state.
- Leave Eon, EonTerm, Nova, and their runtime namespaces untouched.
- Preserve exact historical pins, commits, Beads proof, license record, and accepted dogfood evidence. A repository archive may carry that history without presenting Eonova as a supported product.
- Do not rename EonTerm, turn Eonova into an alias, redirect its command, add migration code, or create an Eon/Nova compatibility layer.

## References before action

Required: current Eonova instructions, repository visibility and branch state, installed-profile and desktop identity, runtime namespace, historical `eon-4is.2` and `eon-4is.5` proof, current `yazelix-5vl-wmg` evidence, and the exact accepted future Nova EonTerm-cutover revision.

Conditional: GitHub authoritative documentation only for the chosen archive/delete action; Nix profile documentation only if the exact installed entry cannot be established locally.

Rejected: deleting history by default, terminating live Sessions, removing ambiguous user files, Eon/Nova source edits, compatibility aliases, and a replacement Eonova brand.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. Exact accepted Nova plus EonTerm is installed and dogfooded before Eonova is removed.
2. No live Eonova work is terminated; after safe removal, no Eonova package, profile entry, desktop launcher, process, or owned runtime namespace remains active.
3. Eonova is absent from current product/install/update documentation except explicitly historical proof.
4. The private repository disposition matches a fresh explicit user choice and preserves required history unless the user explicitly selects deletion.
5. Eon, EonTerm, Nova, and unrelated user state are unchanged; exact inspection commands and resulting state are recorded.

Stop if Nova cutover is not accepted, any Eonova Session is live, ownership of state is ambiguous, or repository disposition lacks an explicit user choice.

title: Print the configuration defaults from the CLI
description:
## Why

Lucca, 2026-10-25, to the overseer: "we need a cli option that generates the config defaults, like
prints it". docs/CONFIGURATION.md keeps an example by hand, which drifts from the code's defaults.

## Goal

A CLI command prints Eon's configuration defaults, so a person or agent can start from a complete,
current config.toml. Proposed shape (wording to Lucca before code): `eon config defaults`
(TOML to stdout, comments naming each default; `--json` for the same values as JSON), grouped like
docs/CONFIGURATION.md. Exit 0, nothing on stderr but the unknown-key warnings from reading config.
The existing `eon config-path` stays; whether `eon config` also gains `path` is a contract choice.

## Ownership

One owner of the defaults (Eon Runtime's typed config). The printed values must come from the same
code the supervisor resolves, not a second hand-written table: either the structs serialize their
resolved defaults, or one derived printer asserts equality with the resolver in tests.
docs/CONFIGURATION.md's example is generated from (or checked against) that output.

## Acceptance

- Red/green: `eon config defaults` prints a complete config that parses with the build's resolver
  and resolves to the same defaults as an empty config; `--json` gives the same values; every
  documented default in docs/CONFIGURATION.md agrees with the output (one cheap check).
- Contract wording to Lucca before code (EON-C CLI/configuration clauses).

Portability: neutral.
close_reason: Landed: eon config defaults; proof in comments

comments.author: lucca
comments.text:
Approval (Lucca, 2026-10-25 ~05:40 -03, direct to the overseer, answering its numbered list item 2): "approval to all". Approved: `eon config defaults` prints this build's built-in defaults as TOML (`--json`: the same values as a nested object), without reading the user's configuration; unset defaults appear as comments; `eon config-path` stays as it is (no `config path` alias); the bead's "nothing on stderr but the unknown-key warnings" is dropped (a defaults command reads no config). Drafted wording (Codex draft reviewed by the overseer, 2026-10-25):

**2. eon-4j79 — Print configuration defaults**

**Current clauses → proposed replacements**

EON-C9, `docs/CONTRACTS.md`, Consumer:
> Eon terminals launched under Nushell or Bash.

Replace with:
> People and agents inspecting Eon configuration defaults, and Eon terminals launched under Nushell or Bash.

EON-C9, Trigger:
> Eon constructs a child launch environment.

Replace with:
> Eon prints configuration defaults or constructs a child launch environment.

**Add to EON-C9 Result; no existing defaults-printing clause:**
> `eon config defaults` prints a TOML configuration representing this build’s defaults, with comments explaining defaults that require omission or remain Eon-owned. `--json` prints the same configurable values as a nested JSON object using the configuration’s table and key names. Optional fields whose default is omission remain omitted in both formats. Loading the printed TOML produces the same configuration policy as an empty configuration. The command does not read the user’s configuration, prepare directories, contact a supervisor or start children. Successful output exits 0 with no stderr output; invalid syntax exits 2 and output failure exits 1. `eon config-path` retains its existing behaviour.

**Add to EON-C9 Owner:**
> Eon supplies product defaults; Runtime prints them through the configuration model used by its resolver. Documentation examples are generated from, or checked against, that output.

**Wire:** none. This is a local CLI command, so EON-C10’s live-supervisor control contract needs no amendment. EON-C28 already covers the command and JSON fields if present at 1.0; comment wording and TOML layout need no stability guarantee.

**Open choices**
1. Command: `eon config defaults` or `eon config-defaults`. **Recommend `config defaults`**, matching existing grouped `window`, `tab` and `pane` commands.
2. Path spelling: retain only `config-path`, or add `config path` as an alias. **Recommend retaining only `config-path` in this bead**; it already appears in help, usage and `RUNNER_COMMANDS`.
3. Meaning: built-in defaults or current effective configuration. **Recommend built-in defaults**, matching the request and allowing recovery even when the user’s config is invalid.
4. Unset values: omit them with explanatory comments, or materialize child defaults as explicit values. **Recommend omission**: `TerminalConfig` uses `Option` to preserve Venus selection and initial geometry.
5. JSON: nested configuration object or a metadata envelope containing `defaults`. **Recommend the nested object**, following the code’s configuration tables and avoiding another naming layer.
6. Comments: explain omissions and constraints, or explain every emitted setting. **Recommend explaining every setting briefly**, as the bead requests, while leaving exact prose outside the contract.

**Conflicts/splits:** the bead’s unknown-key stderr warnings imply reading user configuration; that conflicts with a pure defaults command. Recommend removing that exception. Defaults are supplied by `eon/crates/eon/src/product.rs`, using Runtime-owned types—not owned solely by Runtime. The documentation example is not an empty-config default: it explicitly selects Iosevka, a cursor preset and a 100×30 grid, whereas those defaults are unset. Project’s command and Anima’s command/lifetime cannot be emitted as editable overrides: the resolver rejects them. Custom popup templates, effective-config inspection, config writing and path aliases can be separate work.

EON-C28 also still says unknown configuration keys fail, contrary to EON-C9 and `read_config`; repair that contract inconsistency separately. The cheapest future falsifier is the bead’s parse-and-resolve equivalence check, including omitted fields and built-in popup restrictions, plus JSON/TOML value agreement.

title: Fork an agent, or start a reviewer from it, in a new isolated pane
description:
Delta's `/fork` and `/review` start a subthread that carries the parent's conversation, in its own copy of the worktree (https://delta.dev/docs/agents/review-and-sync). Eon can do this with the providers' own fork commands: `claude --resume <id> --fork-session` and `codex fork`. A sidebar action and `eon pane fork TARGET [--review]` open a new pane, in its own worktree once eon-el45 lands, running the forked session; `--review` adds a reviewer prompt that points at the parent's changes from bead 1. Blocker: OSC 7501 records hold `state`, `kind`, `progress`, `app`, `title` and `msg` but no provider session ID (orbit/docs/CONTRACTS.md, ORB-C15). The first step is deciding whether to add an ORB-C15 field or read the ID from the optional SessionStart hook. Needs an EON-C, and touches launch policy in eon-eon-agent-lr8sx. Depends on eon-el45.

From the Zed Delta threads research (report /home/lucca/.cache/eon-agents/eon-zed-delta-work/report.md, screenshots in shots/ there). Lucca, 2026-11-09, on the report's proposals: "i agree".

Decide precisely what a read-only fork may do while its source is live; never mutate a live conversation. The ambiguous "bead 1" means the design child's parent-change/reviewer prompt scope.

No OSC field/hook/dependency is chosen by this split. eon-el45 remains the worktree implementation prerequisite, eon-eon-agent-lr8sx the launch-policy owner, eon-k611q the nesting owner. title: Tab chips clip descenders (g, p, y cut at the chip's bottom edge)
description:
## Report

Lucca, 2026-11-06, relayed by the S3 agent (pane p47): tab chips clip descenders. In a tab reading "2  rota-gtp", the tails of g and p are cut along the chip's bottom edge. Not yet diagnosed.

## Pointers (from the relay)

- The label is drawn at venus/src/render/chrome.rs:1688 (`push_text_clipped`), with a text box of height `metrics.height` centred in the pill.
- It is clipped by `workspace.tab_label_clip` from venus/src/scene.rs:2392.

Likely the clip rect is the pill's inner height, or the text box's, rather than the line's full ascent plus descent. Or the centring puts the baseline too low for the pill height.

## Acceptance

- A tab label with descenders (g, p, y, j, q) draws its full glyphs inside the chip at scale 1 and 2, with the packaged fonts. Prove it with a test on the clip and text geometry that uses real font metrics (EON_VENUS_TEST_SANS_FONT or the terminal font, whichever the tab label uses), plus one isolated installed capture of a "rota-gtp"-style tab.
- The fix does not change the chip height or the header layout unless that is needed. If it is, say so in the bead first.
- Check other pills that use the same clip pattern (workspace pill, sidebar chips) for the same clipping, and fix or record each.
close_reason: Landed: chip and hint labels keep their descenders

comments.author: lucca
comments.text:
# eon-4x5tb notes

## Diagnosis

The clip rect (`workspace.tab_label_clip`) is not at fault: vertically it is the whole header
row. The text box is. `build_workspace` pushes the tab label with a box `metrics.height` tall
(the terminal's line height, 18 px at 16 px with the default `line_height = 1.125`) centred in
the pill, and `push_text_clipped` intersects the clip with that box. The label is shaped in the
sans header font (DejaVu Sans in the package) with line height `metrics.height`. cosmic-text
0.19 centres the font's full extent in the line (`line_y = line_top + (line_height -
(ascent + descent)) / 2 + ascent`), and DejaVu Sans' ascent + descent is 1.164 em, taller than
1.125 em. So the extent spills past both box edges, and with `line_y` rounded to whole pixels
the tails of g, p, y, j, q fall below the box bottom, where the box clips them. The pill itself
is taller (about 1.5 lines), so the glyphs fit the chip; only the clip box is short.

## Which face Lucca's tab labels use (deviation from the brief)

The brief and the bead assume the packaged DejaVu Sans. Lucca's running Venus (pid 4180165,
eon 0.1.18) maps DejaVu Sans, Noto Sans and Open Sans from /usr/share/fonts, despite the packaged
FONTCONFIG_FILE, and cosmic-text 0.19 names "Open Sans" as the SansSerif family
(`font/system.rs:206`). So his tab labels are in the host's Open Sans, whose ascent + descent is
1.362 em (hhea 1.069 + 0.293): 21.8 px against the 18 px box, about 1.9 px past each edge.
That is his clipping.

With the packaged DejaVu Sans (1.164 em) at the default line height 1.125, the drawn ink just
touches the old box's last row at scales 1, 1.5, 1.75, 2 and 3 (measured, all inside), so the
default packaged-font case does not clip today. It does clip at a configured `line_height` of
1.0 (allowed range 1..3): ink rows 17..32 against clip rows 15..31 at scale 1, and 34..64
against 30..62 at scale 2.

So the test sweeps line heights 1.0 and 1.125 at scales 1 and 2 with the packaged DejaVu Sans
(red today at 1.0). The installed capture runs with host fonts visible, so that it uses Open Sans
as Lucca's window does.

Separate finding, not fixed here: the packaged fonts.conf does not keep host fonts out of
Venus's font database, so the header face depends on the host (Open Sans when it is installed).
The overseer filed eon-l41xa for font selection.

## Plan (round 0, superseded by Round 1 below)

1. Add `DrawStyleKind::Chip`: one sans line whose line height is its box's height, so the
   glyphs centre where a `metrics.height` line centred in the box put them, and the box clips
   at the chip, not at the terminal line height.
2. Draw the tab, workspace and quota chip labels with a box equal to their pill (`visual`).
3. Extract the buffer shaping from `push_text` into one function the test shares.
4. Test with DejaVu Sans at scales 1 and 2: the "2  rota-gtp" ink lies inside the label's clip
   bounds and the chip, and its baseline did not move; red on today's box first.
5. Record the other pills below; CHANGELOG fix entry; installed capture.

No chip height or header layout change.

## Other pills with the same pattern (round 0, superseded by Round 1 below)

- Tab label, workspace label, quota labels: sans text in a `metrics.height` box. Fixed.
- Header control glyphs (+, ?, ×): same box, but no glyph reaches the descender. Recorded,
  unchanged.
- Scrollback pill (`↓ N rows`): the in-header pill is itself `metrics.height` tall, so a
  bigger box would need a taller pill; its text has no descenders. Recorded, unchanged.
- Sidebar rows, attention filter chips, border titles: boxes are `text_height` =
  max(line height, 1.25 em) with the line at their top; the ink bottom is at most
  line/2 + 0.554 em, inside that box for every line height. Not affected.
- CPU, RAM and disk chips: monospace cell font fitted to the cell. Digits and % only. Not
  affected.

## Round 1 (review: Codex and fresh Opus, LAND WITH FIXES)

Deviations and decisions:

- **Rebased** onto edge a55118d (EONW v35): the test imports `v35`; the CHANGELOG keeps both
  entries.
- **Placement kept exactly (Codex 2).** Round 0's `DrawStyleKind::Chip` made the line as tall
  as the pill. cosmic-text then centred it with a different rounding, so at scale 2 text moved
  down one row. Round 1 drops `Chip`. `push_chip_label` shapes the label exactly as before: a
  `Status(Wrap::None)` line `metrics.height` tall, at the old origin (centred in the pill).
  Only its clip bounds change, to the chip (`chip_label_bounds`). Old and new placement are
  therefore identical whenever no lift applies, and the test asserts the drawn ink at the chosen
  top equals the ink at the old origin.
- **Large font sizes (Codex 1).** `chip_label_top` lifts the line by whole pixels when the
  face's descent (cosmic-text's `max_descent`, at glyphon's baseline: truncated top plus
  rounded line offset) would pass the chip's bottom. This happens only when the face is taller
  than the chip: never with the packaged faces (tallest packaged ascent + descent is 1.200 em,
  Accelerando; the pill is at least about 1.21 em, at font_size 96, line_height 1), but with
  host Open Sans at 96 / 1.0 it lifts 8 px (scale 1) or 15 px (scale 2). The ascent side may then
  pass the chip's top for very tall accents; caps and ascenders stay inside (measured, below).
- **Test coverage of the lift without a new dependency.** Adding Open Sans to
  `venusTestEnvironment` would make it a build input of the Venus package (that set feeds its
  check phase): a build-dependency change with the full Nix proof. Instead the maintained test
  exercises the lift with the packaged DejaVu Sans in a chip 1 em tall (shorter than its
  1.164 em face), and the Open Sans 96 px case was proved by a scratch red/green run against
  /usr/share/fonts/truetype/open-sans/OpenSans-Regular.ttf (02-proof.md), not kept in the tree.
  If maintained Open Sans coverage is wanted, add `pkgs.open-sans` to the test environment in a
  follow-up with its Nix proof.
- **Workspace chip** shares `chip_label_box` with the tab chip, and the test asserts its ink
  (a workspace named "gpy-jq").

Other pills, measured with host Open Sans by the scratch survey (02-proof.md): ink of
"gpyjq Copy" against each box, at 16 px with line heights 1.0, 1.125, 1.25 and 1.3, scales 1,
1.25, 1.5 and 2, and at 6 px:

- Sidebar rows and border titles (box `text_height` from the line's top): inside in every case
  (at 1.25 the ink ends exactly at the box's last row).
- Attention filter chips (line centred in a 2-line chip, box `text_height`): inside in every case.
- Scrollback pill ("↓ 12 rows", box = the line): inside in every case; its text has no
  descenders. Unchanged.
- Bottom-bar hint pieces (bare keys and labels such as "Left/Right  tabs", box = the line):
  **clipped** by 1 to 2 rows at 16 px and line heights 1.0 and 1.125, at every scale. Fixed:
  `hint_label_box` gives them a box as tall as the hints bar, centred on their line, so the
  text keeps its exact place; the test covers it.
- Keycap legends (Alt, Ctrl+Alt, Alt+Shift, Ctrl+Alt+Shift and their short forms): drawn in the
  keycap fill, which is one line tall; they have no descenders. Unchanged.
- Clock and version: monospace cell font, fitted to the cell; digits, letters without
  descenders. Unchanged.
- Header control glyphs (+, ?, ×): no descenders. Unchanged.

Remaining host-font gap: the clipping boxes above are proven for DejaVu Sans (maintained test)
and Open Sans (scratch survey). A host face taller still could reach the edges of the
`text_height` boxes or the keycap fill. Font selection is eon-l41xa.

## Round 2 (Codex re-check of 7ff8018: LAND WITH FIXES, one item)

The large-font lift constrained only the descent, so with host Open Sans at 96 / 1.0 / scale 1
an accented capital (É) clipped at the chip's top. `chip_label_top` now handles it as follows:

- Default placement is unchanged: while the face's descent fits the chip, it returns the old
  origin.
- Otherwise it measures the label's own ink rows (glyph images from the renderer's swash
  cache, so only on this path), centres them in the chip's clip rows, and keeps the
  descenders inside first when that ink is taller than the chip.

A face too tall for its chip therefore keeps its descenders and may lose the top of a tall
accent. That is recorded, as the overseer asked.

title: Keep the pane background inside each column's outer edge
description:
## Why

eon-2x6h (4b3be05) fills each whole allocated column area, title rows and the space around the
curves included, with the translucent terminal background while the gaps stay the opaque frame, so
in Lucca's window the card background shows above the first top border and outside the outer
rounded corners. Lucca, 2026-10-24: "the pane backgroun can never leak". He also flagged the
stacked collapsed rows in his window as "obviously wrong" (dark bands and hooks between stacked
rows). After a mockup of four options he chose A: "in A, the mockup is wrong, the background should
be the same inside the whole main area ... lets go with A for now".

## Behaviour (option A as Lucca defined it)

- Each column's fill starts at its first pane's top edge and follows that pane's rounded top corners
  down to the column's rounded bottom. Inside it, title rows and the space between stacked pane cards
  share one background (the expanded terminal's colour and opacity), so a stack has no bands.
- Nothing above that top edge or outside the outer corners takes the terminal background; the gaps,
  the space above the first top edge and the footer band stay the opaque frame.

title: Draw the Agents sidebar popup marker as two overlapping rounded squares so it stops reading as a checkbox
description:
## Why

Lucca, 2026-11-11 (eon-desk): "the popup marker looks a lot like a big checkmark". A desk
screenshot shows the marker drawn as specified by eon-wpbjz (127a157): one thin rounded-square
outline at the row's right edge. A lone empty rounded square is the shape of an unticked checkbox,
so it reads as a to-do or a control instead of "this agent runs in a popup".

Lucca chose option 1 of four ("1 ok, do it"): two overlapping thin rounded squares, the common
"floating window" icon. Rejected: a dimmed "popup" text tag (takes width agent names need); the
popup's shortcut as a keycap (longer, busier); a rounded square with an up-right arrow (reads as
external link). The earlier "small window with a filled title bar" was rejected on 2026-11-10 as
too heavy (eon-wpbjz).

Contract: VEN-C30 Popup marker clause (venus/docs/CONTRACTS.md:2425-2433) describes "a thin
rounded-square outline". Presentation is a feature (docs/AGENT-RULES.md, Contract-Driven Method):
amend the wording and venus/docs/PRESENTATION.md to the new shape, citing this approval; no
behaviour clause changes.

## Evidence (line numbers at 481fe27; verify)

- `venus/src/render/chrome.rs:898` `push_popup_marker`: one `push_rounded_outline_width` with
  `tokens::popup_marker_radius` (size/4) and the card stroke.
- `venus/src/render/chrome.rs:1960`: call site for sidebar and attention inbox rows.
- `venus/src/scene.rs:2820`: marker rect, 1.25x font size, vertically centered at the padded
  right edge; text stops before it.
- `venus/src/render/chrome.rs:5274` test `popup_marker_is_a_crisp_rounded_card_outline`, plus
  uses at :5304, :5379, :6756.

## Scope

In scope:
- Marker drawing in `push_popup_marker` (and `tokens::popup_marker_radius` if the two squares need
  their own radius), its tests, VEN-C30 wording, PRESENTATION.md, CHANGELOG.md, venus/CHANGELOG.md.

Out of scope and unchanged:
- The marker's bounding rect, placement, colour (title colour, dimmed when stale), stroke width
  (`border_width`), and the text stopping before it.
- Accessible names ("popup"), attention badges, row fills (eon-wuau8.4 changes the current-row
  selection in parallel; touch only the marker to avoid conflicts).
- The hover tooltip (eon-k80py).

## Acceptance

- Within today's marker rect, two thin rounded-square outlines: a back square and a front square
  offset toward the top-right (or bottom-left; agent's call), overlapping by roughly a third to a
  half of each side. Where they overlap, the back square's lines do not show through the front one,
  so it reads as one window in front of another.
- Same stroke and colour as today; corners stay rounded at every supported scale; crisp at scale 1
  and 2 (no blurry half-pixel lines).
- Nothing about it reads as a checkbox: a reviewer looking at a capture of a popup row at scale 1
  agrees it reads as stacked windows.
- Still clearly distinct from every round attention badge and spinner.

## Verification

- Replace or update `popup_marker_is_a_crisp_rounded_card_outline` to assert two crisp outlines
  inside the marker rect and no back-square stroke inside the front square.
- `nix develop -c eon-test` over the workspace (not inside a live Eon session environment), plus
  `cargo fmt --check` and `cargo clippy --locked --all-targets -- -D warnings` for Venus.
- Installed: one dogfood observation after the overseer's profile refresh; Lucca judges it live.

## Stop Conditions

- Stop if at the smallest supported font size the two squares merge into a blob; record sizes and
  ask rather than enlarging the row.
- Stop if the cited marker code has drifted materially.

## Maintenance Notes

- Follow-up to eon-wpbjz. Runs alongside eon-wuau8.4 (same file, different function); land
  whichever is second with a rebase.
- Rule 6: the shape is a fixed product glyph like the attention badges; no setting.

title: Document Eon's release classes and changelog prefixes for upgrades
description:
## Why

Lucca accepted the eon-c8ytm release classes on 2026-10-31 (decision 7,
proposal table E). Before the announcement (the macOS launch or the first
public announcement), Eon may break things, but only through aliases and
warnings. From the announcement:
- 0.N.y patch releases break no config, CLI or JSON;
- 0.N.0 minor releases may break, with a deprecation;
- 1.x follows EON-C28;
- 2.0 removes the aliases.
Users and release agents need this written where they look, with the changelog
wording that goes with it.

## Evidence

- `CHANGELOG.md`: breaking changes today are prose bullets, such as the
  `show_version` entry and repeated EONW "stop with the old `eon`" notes.
- `eon/crates/eon/Cargo.toml:3`: version 0.1.9 is shared by every edge build
  between bumps, so a version cannot name a config shape.
- docs/AGENT-RULES.md Git Workflow, docs/DISTRIBUTION.md: where release steps
  live.

## Scope

In scope:
- A short "Upgrades and compatibility" section in user documentation
  (`docs/DISTRIBUTION.md` or README Status). It contains:
  - the release-class table from the eon-c8ytm proposal, section E;
  - the announcement milestone;
  - the 60-day migration floor;
  - what each class may break.
- `CHANGELOG.md` header note on entry prefixes: `Action needed:` with the
  exact edit, and `Deprecated:` naming the replacement and earliest removal.
- A release-step line: from the announcement, an edge change to the config or
  durable-state shape bumps at least the patch version, and each release
  states its migration floor.

Out of scope:
- The contract and rule text (the contract indexing bead), and code.

## Acceptance

- The docs state the classes and the milestone, and the changelog header states
  the prefixes. A release agent can apply both without reading eon-c8ytm.

## Verification

- docs route: changed Markdown reviewed, `git diff --check` clean, review loop
  per docs/AGENT-RULES.md Proof and Review.

## Stop Conditions

- Stop if the wording would change an approved contract.

## Maintenance Notes

- Policy: eon-c8ytm proposal, section E.
acceptance_criteria: - [ ] The section links EON-C37 (docs/CONTRACTS.md) as the promise and matches its wording, citing the 60-day floor from eon-c8ytm section E; README.md Status (lines 80-81, 'may still change between 0.x releases') is reworded to hold only until the announcement.
notes:
prime-beads 2026-11-03: EON-C37 indexed by 23bb774 (eon-z7kku). The 'stop ... with the old eon first' changelog guidance belongs to eon-v0b7y / eon-7cf0y.9, not here. The release-step line can go directly in docs/AGENT-RULES.md Git Workflow (not generated).

Approved eon-c8ytm section E's alias policy conflicts with current docs/AGENT-RULES.md Configurability (no aliases; tombstones/warnings). Ask the overseer which authority supersedes which before copying the release table; preserve the 60-day floor and patch/minor/announcement promises until resolved. No approved decision or contract text changed here.

title: Agents launched into a new folder hang silently on Claude Code's folder-trust prompt
description:
Reported by general-overseer for Lucca (2026-10-31): eon tab create --directory /home/lucca/pjs/apps/beadseer --no-focus --json -- claude "Read docs/KICKOFF.md and follow it." (EONW v25, generation g1) stopped at Claude Code's folder-trust prompt ("Do you trust the files in this folder?") because the folder was new. The pane stayed live with attention null, so Eon showed no sign it needed input; Lucca had to switch tabs and answer by hand, and the launcher could not tell. Likely cause: Claude Code reports status (hooks or OSC 7501) only after the trust step, so nothing reaches Eon's attention. Investigate and propose (numbered, with recommendation): (1) surface it: can Eon mark the pane as needing input while an agent sits at a startup prompt, without screen scraping as the primary signal (see the agent-sidebar research against heuristics)? (2) avoid it: a documented, supported launch path for agents in new folders; check what Claude Code actually supports for pre-trusting a directory (settings, CLI flag, managed config) and the same for Codex; --dangerously-skip-permissions is NOT acceptable (not a trust fix, widens permissions). (3) fallback: with eon pane read/send (EONW v26, landed acc29d2) a launching agent can detect and answer the prompt; check whether a bare Enter via eon pane send --enter works on that menu or needs named keys (eon-0um2b). Deliver: findings as a comment, follow-up beads proposed to eon-overseer; docs change for the supported path if one exists.

## Current remaining work

Comment 5574 already established that paste is not a menu key and bare Enter may select No/exit. Do not repeat that as unresolved. Document trusted project-folder launch, human acceptance for a new folder and --add-dir where appropriate; never hand-edit hasTrustDialogAccepted or use --dangerously-skip-permissions. Future named keys (eon-0um2b) do not authorize granting trust.

Examples use eon tab create --dir DIR --no-focus -- COMMAND...; --directory is historical. Record exact provider versions without copying credentials. Post-start OSC 7501 does not prove a pre-report prompt signal; screen/stall inference must not become semantic truth. Remaining acceptance: safe-path docs/skill, Codex prompt evidence and numbered EON-C31 proposal. Implementing another attention source needs separately approved text/slice. eon-ed9d.4 is closed related research, not an unfulfilled blocker.
acceptance_criteria: 1. docs/USAGE.md and the Eon skill say to start agents in an already-trusted project folder, and that a folder-trust prompt needs a person. 2. Codex behaviour at its equivalent prompt is recorded here. 3. A numbered proposal for marking a pane that waits at a startup prompt before its first OSC 7501 report (an EON-C31 change; eon-ed9d.4 covers only agents that never report) goes to Lucca. Related: eon-0um2b (agent keys could answer the menu).

comments.text:
## Finding: the home-folder case (eon-overseer, 2026-11-05)

Reported by general-overseer for Lucca. Running `eon tab create --directory /home/lucca --no-focus --json -- claude -n disk-overseer ...` (tab t6, pane p14) stopped at Claude Code's folder-trust prompt, while the popup-launched Claude sessions in /home/lucca did not.

**This is not an Eon launch difference.** The stuck process (pid 2880449, /home/lucca/.nix-profile/bin/claude) has:
- cwd /home/lucca, HOME=/home/lucca and PWD=/home/lucca;
- no CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR and no XDG_CONFIG_HOME;

which is the same as the popup-launched session (pid 2870391). Claude Code's own record, ~/.claude.json `projects["/home/lucca"].hasTrustDialogAccepted`, is `false`, while /home/lucca/pjs/eon/eon and /home/lucca/pjs/apps/beadseer are `true`. The popup session was started with `--continue`. Unverified: Claude Code may not persist trust for the home directory, or a resumed session may not re-check trust.

**Supported paths today:**
1. **Launch agents in a project folder, not $HOME.** Trust persists for a project folder once accepted. For a machine-wide job, start in a dedicated folder, and give it reach with `--add-dir` if it needs it.
2. **Do not hand-edit `hasTrustDialogAccepted` in ~/.claude.json.** It is an undocumented internal record, and editing it bypasses a safety prompt Lucca should answer.
3. **`--dangerously-skip-permissions` stays rejected,** as in this bead.

**Answering the prompt through `eon pane send` is unsafe today.** The menu reads "❯ No, exit / Yes, I trust this folder", with the cursor on "No, exit". A bare `eon pane send PANE --enter` would choose No and exit the agent. `pane send` has no named keys (Down, digits as keys) until eon-0um2b decides them, and pasted text is not a menu keypress. So a person answers by hand, or the agent is relaunched in a trusted folder.

**What is still Eon's to do:** the attention gap. The pane shows attention null while it waits on a startup prompt. That is the "surface it" part of this bead, together with eon-ed9d.4.

title: Investigate Shopify's Reflex agent-drivable architecture for Eon's agent CLI
description:
## Why

Lucca, 2026-11-05: "create a bead to investigate this: https://shopify.engineering/reflex".

Shopify's "Reflex: an architecture for building mobile apps with agents" (Thiago Magalhaes,
2026-11-05) makes every screen's state and actions machine-readable so agents can build, test and
drive the app without the UI. That is close to Eon's own aim (AGENTS.md rule 5: every window action
has an `eon` CLI path, and everything a person sees is readable as data). The article publishes no
code ("This article *is* the open source"), only the pattern.

Its four pillars:
- a core module with no UI imports;
- an Elm-shaped ViewModel contract: Action in, State out, and one reducer as "the only place state
  ever changes";
- per-node introspection as JSON (name, state, actions), arranged as a tree. The CLI targets the
  deepest focused node, and an action outside its scope is refused with the list of valid actions;
- a platform-neutral CLI (`ls`, `do Action [json]`) over newline-delimited JSON, headless in tests.
  Behaviour tests use fixtures and a network guard, and one shared test suite enforces parity
  across platforms. The article claims 1,700+ behaviour tests in about 4 minutes on CI, and
  hundreds of milliseconds per case versus about 2 s on a simulator.

## Questions to answer (investigation; no product code)

1. **Action discovery.** Can an agent list the actions available right now, on the workspace, a
   tab, a pane or a popup, with their arguments, as data? Compare with Reflex's per-node action
   list and its "refuse and list what's valid" error. Today's surface is EON-C10 (typed workspace
   control), EON-C35/C36 (reading and sending to a terminal), EON-C39 (workspace events) and
   `eon session --json`.
2. **One action path.** Do the human keybinding path and the `eon` CLI path for the same action go
   through one typed action and one state writer, so "the CLI can't do anything a View couldn't",
   and the reverse? Where do they still diverge? Use the parity epic eon-agent-parity-a9g0 and its
   audit eon-agent-parity-audit-t31r as the inventory; don't repeat them.
3. **Headless behaviour tests.** Could Venus/Runtime workspace behaviour be tested through the
   typed action and state layer, without a display, faster than the current real-display and
   real-PTY checks? What already exists (Runtime unit tests, the eon-test sandbox), and what would
   a fixture-driven reducer test layer cost?
4. **Skills for agents.** Reflex says "Teach your agents how to run the CLI." Compare with Eon's
   embedded agent skill, and say whether it covers discovery and errors well enough.
5. **What doesn't transfer.** Eon is a live multi-process terminal, not a mobile app (Orbit owns
   terminal state, PTYs, and humans need the GUI). Name the ideas that don't fit, and why.

## Deliverable

- A decision comment on this bead: for each question, the current state with file:line or contract
  evidence, the gap, and a recommendation (adopt / adapt / reject) with its cost.
- A ranked list of candidate follow-up beads, **not filed**. Lucca picks which become beads. Any
  that add or change an EON-C or VEN-C contract stop for his approval as usual.

## Scope boundary

- Read-only: no product code, contract, configuration or test changes.
- Not a redesign of Eon's architecture, and no new dependency.
- Not a re-audit of CLI parity: build on eon-agent-parity-audit-t31r.

## Verification

The decision comment cites the article sections it relies on and, for every claim about Eon,
contract IDs or file:line at a named edge revision. Reviewed by the overseer before the follow-ups
are proposed to Lucca.

Contract: none changed; reads EON-C10, EON-C31, EON-C35, EON-C36, EON-C39. Prerequisites: none.
Related: eon-agent-parity-a9g0.

title: Extract managed-environment ownership from Eon main
description:
## Contract routing

This is an isomorphic internal refactor. It changes no EON product contract, command, configuration surface, protocol, component revision, process lifecycle, error, or output. Preserve every current contract, with EON-C9 as the extracted owner and EON-C1, EON-C3, EON-C4, and EON-C12 as adjacent launch boundaries.

## Why

`crates/eon/src/main.rs` is 2,808 lines: 2,185 production lines followed by 623 unit-test lines. Size alone is not the finding. The concrete problem is that it contains two architecture-defined subsystem owners:

- `docs/ARCHITECTURE.md:98` assigns runtime and lifecycle to `main.rs`.
- `docs/ARCHITECTURE.md:102` separately assigns managed-environment dispatch to `main.rs`, `defaults/`, and `flake.nix`.
- `crates/eon/src/main.rs:937` begins managed configuration types.
- `crates/eon/src/main.rs:984` defines the managed program graph and `ManagedTool`.
- `crates/eon/src/main.rs:1035` through `:1164` owns managed invocation and environment construction.
- `crates/eon/src/main.rs:1479` through `:1548` resolves managed programs and shell configuration.
- `crates/eon/src/main.rs:2341` through `:2597` contains the focused managed-environment tests.

That boundary is independently reviewable and already has a dedicated prerequisite audit. Extracting it removes one owner from the supervisor file without pre-deciding speculative runtime, generation, or control modules.

Impact: MED — reduces cross-subsystem review context and makes later environment changes less likely to disturb lifecycle code.
Effort: M.
Implementation risk: MED because source movement changes Eon's generation digest and command-environment behavior is security- and compatibility-sensitive.
Confidence: HIGH.

## Prerequisite and reference gate

- Blocked by `eon-audit-eon-managed-environment-hay`; consume its exact-revision findings before choosing the final move boundary.
- Do not start while `eon-4is.1` or another issue is changing an in-scope surface.
- Required evidence: complete current `AGENTS.md`, this Bead and prerequisite audit record, `docs/ARCHITECTURE.md`, EON-C9 and adjacent contract proofs, all managed-environment code and tests in `crates/eon/src/main.rs`, `defaults/`, `flake.nix`, and the installed-runtime generation identity owner.
- External reference implementations are rejected for this isomorphic extraction: existing Eon ownership and tests define the behavior. Stop if the audit discovers a product, dependency, or cross-repository decision instead.
- No dependency or crate feature is expected. Stop for the dependency gate and user approval before any manifest change.

## Scope

In scope:

- Add one Rust module under `crates/eon/src/` for the existing managed-environment owner.
- Move the minimum coherent set of existing types and functions: managed invocation recognition, managed program inputs, shell configuration values and parsing, integration-mask projection, and managed command construction.
- Keep runtime-root selection, directory safety, generation discovery, CLI policy, supervisor state, EONW handling, child observation, and Orbit/Venus lifecycle in the runtime owner.
- Keep the module interface narrow by passing existing explicit paths/configuration; expose no new public API.
- Move focused unit tests with their owner when that reduces private visibility; preserve process integration tests unchanged.
- Add the new source file to `current_generation()`'s complete source digest.
- Reconcile current-state architecture wording and README LOC only if file ownership/counts change.

Out of scope:

- Splitting runtime/generation/control code further.
- Changing CLI parsing, managed command names, defaults, user configuration order, environment variables, PATH order, argv, filesystem permissions, errors, protocol bytes, process order, generation selection, or Nix composition.
- New traits, interfaces, generic frameworks, dependencies, crates, compatibility paths, shell features, or configuration.
- Changelog entries unless observable behavior changes, which is a stop condition rather than part of this Bead.

## Implementation notes

title: Dead keys type a stray character: us+intl Shift+6 then e gives 6ê instead of ê
description:
## Why

Lucca, 2026-11-12 ~16:55Z, typing in the Eon 0.1.24 window (EONW v42, profile at 1b1d4fb): "p1 bug: trying to type voce results in: voc6ê ... dead key issue". He meant "você". His layout is us with variant intl (X11 Layout us,jp; Variant intl,kana) on COSMIC (Wayland), where Shift+6 is dead circumflex. The terminal receives a stray "6" (the dead key's unshifted text) before the correctly composed "ê". Portuguese text is everyday input for him, so this is P1.

## Goal

A dead-key sequence (dead circumflex, acute, grave, tilde, diaeresis on us+intl, then a letter, or Space for the bare accent) delivers exactly the composed text to the focused terminal and nothing for the dead key press itself, in every pane program (shell, Helix, Claude Code and Codex, which may enable the kitty keyboard protocol). Find where the "6" comes from (Venus key translation in venus/src/input.rs, the semantic key event Venus sends, Orbit's encoding of it under legacy or kitty keyboard modes) and whether it is a regression (recent candidates: c37a6a8 shortcut table, 825dd62, and anything since the last release that touched input; check git log). Fix at the owner.

## Done when

- A test reproduces the stray character before the fix (red) and passes after, at the owning layer, covering at least dead circumflex + e, dead tilde + a, dead acute + e, and dead key + Space, under both legacy encoding and the kitty keyboard protocol if both are reachable.
- The installed-candidate check, or a recorded reason why the test layer already covers the real path: typing "você", "ação", "é" into a shell and into a Claude Code pane gives exactly those words.
- If an ORB-C/VEN-C/EON-C contract describes key or dead-key semantics and the fix changes it, stop for contract text (overseer).

## Evidence

- venus/src/input.rs: `ime()` near line 246; line ~819 "Space carries text that a dead key composes, so it has unshifted text too"; test near line 1141 "us+intl: Shift held from a dead key through Space composes text".
- eon-igae.7.5.4 (re-prove semantic input on the beta candidate) should pick up the new test.

title: Keep scrolling a drag selection while the pointer is above the pane's top row
description:
## Why
Lucca (2026-10-30): while drag-selecting in a pane and moving up, the selection scrolls into history only while
the pointer sits exactly on the top row (row 0). Moving the pointer above the pane's top edge, which is the
normal gesture, stops the scroll instead of continuing to extend the selection into scrollback.

Cause: `Input::selection_at_top` (venus/src/input.rs:461) calls `selection_position(cursor, size, false)`.
With `clamp = false` a pointer outside the terminal surface returns None, and `drive_selection_autoscroll`
(venus/src/application.rs:1126) treats None as "left the edge" and cancels the ticks
(`SelectionAutoscroll::edge`/`next = None`, venus/src/application/scroll.rs). So only
`padding_top <= y < padding_top + cell_height` ticks; y above the surface (pane above, tab bar, Eon Bar,
or outside the window under the pointer grab) does nothing.

VEN-C7 currently says "While a held host selection stays in the top visible row, Venus sends one upward
selection tick at a time", so today's behaviour matches the contract text literally. Per AGENTS.md
"Happy Users" this is a gap to close: every terminal users know (Ghostty, kitty, foot, WezTerm) keeps
scrolling while the pointer is held above the viewport.

## Change
1. Contract (stop for Lucca's approval of exact text): VEN-C7 bullet becomes
   "While a held host selection's pointer is in or above the top visible row, Venus sends one upward
   selection tick at a time, with the pointer's column clamped to the pane and its row clamped to the top
   row. ..." (rest unchanged). ORB-C9 needs no change: Orbit still receives a top-row surface position.
2. Venus: when selecting and the pointer y is at or above the top row, clamp the position to the top row
   (and x into the pane's columns) instead of returning None; keep None (cancel) only for pointer below the
   top row. Applies per pane in split layouts, measured against the selecting pane's surface, including
   pointer positions outside the window delivered under the compositor's implicit grab.
3. Out of scope: speed scaling with distance above the edge (cadence stays one row per accepted frame) and
   downward autoscroll (ORB-C9 excludes it); file separately if wanted.

## Acceptance
- Red/green unit test at the input owner: a selecting pointer one cell, several cells, and outside the
  window above the surface yields a top-row position; below the top row yields None.
- nix develop -c eon-test -p yazelix-venus; cargo fmt --check; cargo clippy --locked --all-targets -- -D warnings.
- One isolated installed observation (private headless Sway, wdotool): fill history, press in a lower row,
  drag above the pane's top edge and hold; the selection extends into scrollback until release or the
  oldest edge; same in the lower pane of a split.
- Codex and a fresh Claude reviewer per AGENTS.md.

## Scope
venus/src/input.rs (and callers in application.rs/scroll.rs only if needed), its tests, VEN-C7 text after
approval, venus/CHANGELOG.md. Portability: neutral (works the same under the macOS pointer drag).
close_reason: A held drag selection above the top row, over the Eon Bar, pane headers or the scrollback pill, keeps extending into history. Proof and ledger in the landing comment.

Coverage gap: no automated test drives `WindowEvent::CursorMoved`, which needs a native window and renderer (only the ignored tests in venus/src/application/tests/native.rs have one). Two regressions would therefore pass every suite:
- putting back a `WorkspaceHit::Terminal` gate on `selection_scroll.edge(..)` in the selecting branch;
- computing `was_scrollback`/`over_scrollback` without passing `self.input.is_selecting()` to `pill_takes_pointer`.
The unit tests cover only the two decisions. Reproducer:
- private headless Sway 1.12, pixman, 1280x720, `gaps outer 80`;
- wdotool 0.5.3 prime plus `mousemove`; `swaymsg seat seat0 cursor press|release button1`; `^seq 1 300`;
- press at (640,540), 8 steps up, then hold 20 s, either still or moving ±1 px every 0.3 s; check with `wl-paste`.
The base fails 7 of 8 gestures and the fix passes 8 of 8. Driver: ~/.cache/eon-agents/eon-5uw0/dog/observe-r2.sh.

Portability: neutral, which corrects the Scope's "works the same under the macOS pointer drag".
- The in-window cases (the pointer over the Eon Bar, a pane header, or the scrollback pill) do not depend on the platform.
- Outside the window is proved on Wayland only. Under the implicit grab, motion keeps arriving and no `CursorLeft` arrives until release.
- It is unproved on macOS. `CursorLeft` runs `cancel_pointer_sequence()`, so if winit on macOS sends it while the drag is held outside the window, the selection is cancelled there. That matches the behavior before this change, so it is not a regression.
- The check is queued on eon-mac-launch-kz4p.

Rule 6: no value is added or changed. The cadence, the per-tick row bound and the clamp are unchanged or structural.

title: Install fails: deleted tree-sitter-cylc GitHub repo breaks Helix grammar evaluation
description:
## Report (Lucca, 2026-11-02)

A friend ran `nix profile add --refresh github:Yazelix/eon/v0.1.2`; evaluation failed downloading
`https://github.com/elliotfontaine/tree-sitter-cylc/archive/6d1d81137112299324b526477ce1db989ab58fb8.tar.gz`
with HTTP404. One upstream grammar removal could break every fresh Eon install because Helix used
evaluator-time fetchTree for grammar sources. Local stores concealed the failure.

The original brief named `/nix/store/7fahsb7dmsddy184sp4m8m2hhkhcjzw7-helix-tree-sitter-cylc-6d1d81137112299324b526477ce1db989ab58fb8`;
that is the compiled grammar output. Its derivation identifies the actual original source as
`/nix/store/p6hlffdcdk4nppvapgpki7cjqa7scfmq-source`, NAR
`sha256-jgQCTM36S8UwSyT4LAfcX4DUIl2OYVMeQdDg3zRrw00=`. Both source and publication archives are preserved.

## Approved contract and owner

Eon's published pins evaluate without grammar-source network fetches and build all selected
Helix grammars without depending on third-party grammar hosts remaining available. Exact source
identity, archives, source selection/subpaths, compiler and export stay owned by nova-helix; Eon
consumes its exact revision and publishes/retains its source closure through the existing cache job.

Every pinned grammar source has a catalog entry with an original source NAR hash and immutable
Yazelix-owned archive URL. Fixed-output build-time fetchers try that owned URL first and the exact
upstream archive second. Missing catalog coverage fails clearly, including disabled grammars;
source tampering fails the hash check. Keep every existing language and source subpath. Standalone
`hx --grammar fetch` remains its existing upstream path; the approved change is Nix delivery.

Lucca's "we have to make this very robust.." expanded the original cylc unblock to the systemic
mechanism. The 2026-11-02 decision comment records approval of option1 under "every thing is auto
approved": immutable per-source release assets in the existing Yazelix/nova-helix repository,
fixed-output sources and retained Cachix publication, with upstream only a secondary URL. No new
repository, grammar removal, alternative product channel or platform expansion.

## Prerequisites and references

The narrow cylc repair is published as nova-helix cd4890783fd43a99097721422ec08ea05978b7fe and Eon
2b20975a165beed312aedd693c10948e11077579. The immutable source release
`grammar-sources-2026-11-02` (id431903578) is public with290 archives+SHA256SUMS; every archive's
published digest/size and extracted NAR match the preserved source. Assets must precede every
consuming child commit. Prior archival precedent is eon-adopt-offline-helix-grammars-boop; grammar
removal remains rejected as lost syntax support.

Reference gate: pinned languages.toml/grammars.nix/default.nix and existing check/README,
Nixpkgs567a49d fetchzip/fetchurl semantics, Nix local/chroot store isolation, Cachix source-vs-runtime
closure publication and retained pins, and GitHub immutable release behavior. Reuse Nixpkgs helpers
and the existing compiler; do not add a second grammar graph or move child policy into Eon.

## Scope and acceptance

- [x] Audit all295 grammar entries/290 sources; preserve all sources, retaining the existing293 enabled grammars.
- [x] Publish290 immutable owned archives before a consuming revision; verify all original NARs and published digests.
- [x] Empty-cache/hidden-host-source evaluation with all five grammar evaluator fetch builtins throwing.
- [x] Fresh tool-only store builds all293 selected grammars and all290 sources with substitutes, upstream URLs and hashed mirrors unavailable; preserve production output identities and record proof-recipe differences.
- [x] Verify293 native shared libraries,295 source/parser links,290 source NARs and290 actual owned-only fetch logs.
- [x] Explicitly export/retrieve290 sources through an offline local binary cache and build the production source-only aggregate, with no grammar products seeded.
- [x] Finish fresh independent child review, then commit/push the child and update Eon's exact flake/lock/component identity. (Helix af9acb1; Eon 22d9213, shipped in v0.1.16, d41f99e.)
- [x] Build the exact downstream Eon candidate, validate the source-retention workflow, and finish its independent review. (22d9213, in v0.1.16, d41f99e.)
- [x] Prove actual hosted Cachix source publication/retention/retrieval through the configured authenticated publisher. (CI run 41912131573; comment 2026-11-04 21:24.)
- [x] Refresh the active eon profile from the accepted working tree and check the exact installed artifact without interrupting any running supervisor or terminal. (Profile refresh comment 2026-11-04 21:39.)

The local-cache lane proves substitution mechanics, not hosted Cachix retention. Native Darwin
build/runtime remain unproved; Darwin evaluation is shape evidence only. The guarantee concerns
upstream grammar disappearance/outage, not an installation with every owned delivery service offline.

Git metadata is read-only in Codex's host. Claude performs commit/push/gh actions from exact commands
in `~/.cache/eon-agents/codex-cylc/claude-todo.sh`, signaled by `CLAUDE ACTION` in STATUS.md. Preserve
concurrent Eon work and use coordinator's current edge base (5f59cc1 after v0.1.12). No further
product release tag is included. Proof and review records stay in this issue; detailed evidence and
backups remain under `~/.cache/eon-agents/codex-cylc/`.

comments.author: lucca
comments.text:
Audit and systemic design ready for Lucca's choice (2026-11-02).

AUDIT

Audited every grammar in nova-helix 817dcbca8b99c3db35ea66ded7492673d1a397ad; the published cylc fix cd489078 retains byte-identical languages.toml (SHA-256 822d08634f44dcb616c5106d966c40d903ccd5761d105dce58806e4719a2347f). There are 295 grammar entries, 293 enabled, referring to 290 distinct upstream URL/revision sources (288 enabled). Wren and gemini are disabled by the existing selection, not removed by this work.

289/290 pinned upstream sources are available. Cylc alone returns HTTP 404 for both repository and exact-revision archive. 283 ordinary archive URLs returned 200. Six GitLab web archive URLs returned 403, but all six exact-revision API archives returned 200/application/octet-stream: blueprint, debian, lpf, nginx, rpmspec, t32. These are alive and must not be reported as deleted. No unresolved endpoint remains. Checks were bounded HEAD requests with redirects, three workers maximum, at least 0.4 seconds between starts, 5-second connect/20-second total limits; availability is a timestamped observation, not a future-availability/build guarantee.

Every source is now preserved under /home/lucca/.cache/eon-agents/codex-cylc/: 288 enabled raw source trees were identified through grammar derivations' src (not compiled grammar outputs), copied into sources/, and individually NAR-hashed against the originals with equality. The two disabled sources were absent locally, so their exact pinned SourceHut archives were downloaded into downloads/, safely extracted into recovered/, and hashed (no prior original NAR available for those two). Every one of 295 configured grammar/subpath roots contains src/parser.c. Enabled file payload is 1,732,280,844 bytes (1.61 GiB); gzip backup is 139,352,604 bytes (132.90 MiB), integrity-tested, SHA-256 6b6e80dba52e1e0a60bebfbb917911ffc2008ff806abaf75742a5efc8cdb309c. Excluded trees add 847,446 file bytes, retained separately. Use the measured source payload rather than the earlier ~248 MB estimate.

The complete 295-row alive/unavailable list is audit.md; exact upstream URLs/revisions/subpaths, backup locations and hashes are grammar-inventory-preserved.json, source-backups.json, recovered-backups.json. Raw timed HTTP evidence is audit-http-observations.jsonl and audit-gitlab-rechecks.jsonl, merged into audit-results-final.json. Archive/record identities are in audit-evidence-identity.json. Backups survive Nix GC but are still only on this machine; nothing has been published as a systemic source mirror.

DESIGN — RECOMMENDATION, NOT IMPLEMENTED

1. Recommended: immutable Yazelix-owned per-source release assets in the existing nova-helix repository, fetched with Nixpkgs fixed-output build-time fetchers, plus explicit retained source-cache publication. Extend Helix's existing hash catalog to every pinned source and include its immutable owned URL. languages.toml remains owner of upstream URL/revision/subpath. Missing catalog coverage must fail, never silently fetch upstream. Reuse existing grammar compilation, overlays, source subpaths and runtime packaging. Use fetchzip with the extracted source NAR hash, proving exact output equality first; retain exact extraction if normalization requires it. No new repository is needed.

This removes grammar networking from evaluation and upstream-owner dependence from installation: the configured binary cache can substitute the source; on a cache miss the owned archive reconstructs it. Preserve all licenses/files/modes. Publish archives before the consuming pin, reuse prior immutable URLs for unchanged trees, and upload only changed trees on grammar bumps. About 133 MiB compressed current source payload moves outside Helix git; normal source-code pins stay small. Source retention must be explicit: Eon's current .github/workflows/cachix.yml uploads runtime closures only. Publish source outputs as well and protect them with retained cache pins. Keep grammar policy wholly in nova-helix so Nova, standalone Helix and Eon share it, including Linux/Darwin source identities; Eon does not become Nova's compatibility layer.

2. Valid simpler alternative: bundle everything in nova-helix git using the current local-archive mechanism. This is maximally self-contained but adds roughly the measured 133 MiB compressed payload to fresh child flake downloads and grows history at later grammar changes (per-source compressed total not separately measured). Choose this if that ongoing transfer/history cost is preferable to source-asset publication.

3. Valid alternative: a dedicated owned grammar mirror repository with fixed-output consumers. Equivalent upstream independence, but a new repository adds lifecycle, access and publication upkeep with no present advantage over assets in the existing Helix repository. Requires Lucca's explicit repository choice.

Rejected as insufficient: switching only to hashed upstream fetchers (cold cache still needs the deleted host); retries (cannot recover deleted content); ordinary runtime-only/unretained Cachix publication (does not preserve source availability); patching the next dead source reactively (no systemic guarantee); removing grammars (lost syntax support); mirroring full Git histories (builds require exact source trees only).

Before accepting the later mechanism: prove evaluation in an empty grammar store/cache with evaluator grammar fetches made to throw; separately build all selected grammars from owned archives in a fresh store with upstream URLs and tested cache substitution blocked; separately prove explicit source-cache substitution with owned archive URLs blocked; verify hashes/subpaths/license retention and the exact downstream Eon delivery path. No grammar-source mechanism can promise an install with every owned delivery service offline; this guarantee concerns upstream grammar-owner disappearance/outage, not unrelated flake/toolchain availability. Standalone hx --grammar fetch remains its existing upstream path unless scope expands.

Full rationale and primary references are in design.md: https://nixos.org/manual/nixpkgs/stable/#sec-fetchers ; https://docs.cachix.org/pushing ; https://docs.cachix.org/pins ; https://docs.github.com/en/code-security/concepts/supply-chain-security/immutable-releases . No systemic implementation, repository, assets, cache uploads, jobs or install changes were made. Await Lucca's mechanism choice.

Planning/audit review ledger: one independent read-only evidence review, no blocking factual or goal-coverage findings. Reviewer checked original TOML counts/selection, source mappings, all 295 parser roots, archive SHA-256 and all 288 enabled backup roots plus embedded metadata, recorded byte totals, recovered archive hashes, availability classes, and evaluator/build/cache/ownership boundaries. No new builds or broader delivery proof is implied.

comments.text: Fresh final Claude review found a material portability risk after Linux proof: rpmspec and wikitext contain case-colliding Swift directories; generic fetchzip extraction can merge them on default case-insensitive Darwin volumes. Independent primary-source investigation confirms default upstream/Determinate macOS stores are case-insensitive, and current Nix build-dir normally shares that volume; merely extracting tar directly into out is insufficient. Native Mac failure is not reproduced (previous SSH host was deleted), but conflicting paths and extraction loss are established constraints. Adopt the already-approved fallback in the design: keep fixed-output build-time fetchurl with exact extraction, using Nix itself for Darwin case-aware tarball import and NAR restoration; Linux reuses prior exact tar extraction. Nix owns case escaping; do not hand-code it, drop files, change source hashes, require the cache on Darwin, or change asset formats. A local prototype imports each published tarball through build-time native fetchTree into a private scratch store and restores its NAR with case handling on/off; both reproduce both original catalog hashes. New build-only dependency capability: pinned Nixpkgs nix supplies that canonical archive/case implementation on Darwin, never ships in the runtime closure. It removes ownership of case escaping rather than creating it; no new toolchain/language or repo. Exit: remove Darwin glue when an upstream case-aware build-time fetcher covers these trees. Rejected direct-out tar (default store remains case-insensitive), source removal/renaming/hash changes (lose exact source identity), and NAR-only assets (extra publication/format branch and incompatible upstream tar fallback). Primary references/evidence: darwin-investigation/report.md, case-hack-roundtrip.json, local-tarball-nar/result.json. Revalidate changed acquisition path/source identities and review again; unchanged grammar compilation is not rerun without an identity change.

title: Make the popup margins fixed instead of configurable
description:
Contracts: EON-C10 (popup configuration clause), EON-C18 (picker uses popup margins). VEN-C18 unchanged (already "Eon-supplied logical margins").

Decision (Lucca, 2026-10-26, in session): popup dimensions are not configurable, to avoid edge cases. Approved, verbatim "agree. go ahead", on:
1. Contract edits: EON-C10 "`[popup]` owns finite side and vertical margins, defaulting to 8 and 4 logical pixels." becomes "Eon fixes popup margins at 8 side and 4 vertical logical pixels; a `[popup]` table is an unknown key and warns as described in EON-C9." EON-C18 "using Eon's shared configured popup margins" becomes "using Eon's fixed popup margins".
2. Keep EONW `PopupGeometry` on the wire (no v21 bump); Eon supplies fixed values.
3. One proof batch with eon-rpt9: one installed dogfood capture on the final revision of both, then profile refresh; the running Eon needs a restart to show it.

Configurability record (AGENTS.md "Configurability"): the margins stay fixed by the user's decision; the support cost of the margin/grid/short-window edge cases outweighs users differing.

Change: Runtime stops parsing `[popup]` (it becomes an unknown key with EON-C9's one warning) and always sends the product's `PopupGeometry` (eon/crates/eon/src/product.rs: 8, 4). `eon config defaults` (TOML and JSON) stops printing `[popup]`. Update docs/CONFIGURATION.md (defaults listing and Popups example), the two contract clauses, CHANGELOG.md, and every runtime test or fixture that configures `[popup]`. No wire, Venus or protocol change.

Acceptance: a config with `[popup]` loads with one unknown-key warning and the popup uses 8/4; `eon config defaults` has no `[popup]`; Runtime tests updated, not deleted where they still guard behaviour. Proof: affected Runtime/Eon tests through `nix develop -c eon-test`, then the batch's installed capture.

Prerequisite: eon-rpt9. Scope boundary: no change to popup entries (`[popups.<id>]`) or the wire format.

title: Decide whether Eon adds a command palette (scripting stays with eon-ix6)
description:
## Why
Rex offers Lua scripting with events and a command palette. Eon covers key rebinding
(eon-configurability-qkq8.12) and a Shortcuts viewer (EON-C20, VEN-C20) but no palette or scripting.
Source: competitor audit eon-r6yt (2026-10-29), reports in ~/pjs/refs/competitor-audit-2026-10/.
Lucca, 2026-10-29: "file the beads". Filing only; no work is approved yet beyond planning.

## Narrowed 2026-10-29 (prime-beads pass): palette here, scripting with eon-ix6
The scripting half is already owned by eon-ix6 ("Decide whether Eon needs an extension system",
deferred P4), which lists Lua and other embedded runtimes as discovery inputs and sets the
direction: configuration-first, actions through the `eon` CLI and external programs, plugins only
after two recurring unmet cases. Rex's Lua is recorded there as competitor evidence. An event stream
for external scripts is eon-ciwn.1. This bead decides only the palette, unless Lucca chooses to
reopen eon-ix6.

## Decision question
Should Eon add a command palette (a searchable list of every window action with its key)? Inputs:
eon-cli-action-discovery-ogzi's action registry (one list of actions, no second owner),
eon-configurability-qkq8.4 (`eon keys --json`, the effective keymap), EON-C20/VEN-C20 (Shortcuts
viewer: could the viewer become the palette?). A palette is a window action, so it needs a CLI path
or a named exception under the Humans and Agents rule, and a configurable key.

## Contracts
If yes: palette presentation lives as a feature in its bead and user docs. Changed key/configuration/CLI semantics amend the owning boundary contract; Lucca approves exact text. Do not create a contract solely for the palette's appearance.

## Acceptance
- Decision recorded with reasons. If yes: propose any needed boundary-contract draft and fresh-session implementation slices to Lucca, with prerequisites from the approved discovery/control-layer design; preserve the goal that every window action is reachable from the palette.

## Verification
Planning route: bead state only.

## Ordering and pending decision

Lucca's 2026-11-10 "ok:" puts the control layer before palette implementation (comment 6419). eon-uczzf.2 now exists: the future implementation must depend on it. This decision remains researchable now; ogzi's deferred action-discovery work informs it without blocking the decision on that implementation. If approved, propose fresh-session slices and their actual prerequisites instead of one oversized implementation bead. Retain every-window-action reachability and one action registry. Flow/Rex/Tern comments are evidence, not approval for remote/switcher/setup scope; scripting stays eon-ix6.

title: Picking a project in quick search flashes the Files Yazi before the pane
description:
## Why

Lucca, 2026-11-04: after picking a project in a new tab's quick search, the
Files Yazi shows for a moment, then the pane appears. A pick should go
straight from quick search to the pane. Regression from the directory pair
(`eon-quick-search-parity-23y9.2`, ff6aeb4).

## Evidence

Quick search is the Files Yazi's `quick-search` plugin (`flake.nix:550-642`),
which runs fzf under `ui.hide()`. After fzf accepts, `search()` calls
`permit:drop()` (`flake.nix:617`), so Yazi resumes and redraws its Files view,
and only then reports the pick with `require("tab-folder").set(target)`
(`flake.nix:631`). That runs two blocking `eon` calls (`eon workspace --json`,
then `eon tab directory`); the supervisor hides the pair as it starts the
pending tab's first pane (`workspace.rs:2253-2262`). Yazi stays visible for
that whole window. fzf also clears its frame on exit (no `--no-clear`).
Inference: Esc (fzf 130 → `tab-folder.close()`, after the drop) flashes the
same way.

## Scope

Feature fix inside the Files Yazi's quick-search plugin in `flake.nix`:

- Report the pick (`tab-folder.set`) and the Esc close (`tab-folder.close`)
  while Yazi is still hidden, then drop the permit.
- Keep fzf's last frame on screen until the pair hides (`--no-clear`), and
  check that Tab to Files, status 11 and refusals still redraw Yazi cleanly.

Out of scope: removing the `eon workspace --json` pre-check (it backs the
EON-C18 refusal text, `docs/CONTRACTS.md:2121`; changing it needs contract
approval); established-tab picks, which keep the pair shown by design.

No contract or configuration value changes. Portability: neutral.

## Acceptance

In installed Eon, on a fresh workspace and on Alt+Shift+T:

- a quick-search pick shows quick search, then the pane, with no Yazi frame;
- Esc on a pending tab goes to the pane with no Yazi frame;
- Tab still switches to Files at the highlighted entry, and Alt+Shift+Y from
  quick search still shows Files;
- an established tab's pick still retargets Files as before.

## Verification

`nix flake check` for the `quick-search-guard` and `default` checks, plus one
isolated installed dogfood observation of the pick and Esc paths, then the
profile refresh.
close_reason: Landed on edge as 533eb6e (plugin) and 47e5566 (eon-61efs.1, Venus subscription): a quick-search pick or Esc shows no Yazi frame.
