title: Venus learns workspace changes by subscription, so a hidden pair shows no stale frame
description:
## Why

After eon-61efs's plugin slice, a quick-search pick on a fresh workspace still
shows 2 Yazi frames before the pane, and Esc on a pending tab 3 (isolated
dogfood, 2026-11-04). Venus learns of workspace changes only by polling
`Inspect` every 250 ms (`venus/src/transport.rs` ~79, loop ~169-205), while
Orbit pushes terminal output at once. `eon tab directory` / `eon popup hide`
return after the supervisor has hidden the pair, Yazi resumes and redraws, and
Venus presents that redraw until its next poll. Whether a frame shows depends on
where the poll falls. This also serves VEN-C18 ("Hidden or replaced endpoints
retain no active presentation").

## Evidence

- The supervisor's EON-C39 subscriptions exist with no production client:
  `Action::Subscribe{filter, after}` (eon-workspace-protocol v31.rs:242-247),
  SUBSCRIBED/TABS/EVENT/GAP/END messages, `Subscribers` in
  runtime/crates/eon-runtime/src/subscriptions.rs (32 subscribers, 1 MiB
  pending, 30 s stall end).
- A pending-tab pick emits tab-directory, pane-created, pane-selected and
  popup-hidden (events.rs:490-727); Esc emits popup-hidden.
- Events are published in `tend` on the loop turn after the reply is written
  (control.rs:586, supervisor.rs:1092-1113, 1327), so today they follow the
  CLI's reply.

## Scope

- Venus (`venus/src/transport.rs`, self-contained, since eon-8wh7h will touch
  this file next): one unfiltered subscription per window on its own thread; on
  EVENT or GAP, wake the workspace worker to `Inspect` at once (coalesced, never
  filling the action channel); keep the 250 ms poll as a fallback; on END,
  Failure or I/O error, back off and resubscribe. When an event says the shown
  popup was hidden, stop presenting that popup at once. Shut the stream down
  when the transport drops, so the worker's disconnect exit still fires.
- Supervisor: write the events of a change made by an EONW action before that
  action's reply.
- Transport tests and the native.rs fake supervisor learn Subscribe.
- EON-C39 amendment, approved 2026-11-04 by eon-overseer under Lucca's
  standing approval for this fix (Lucca: "auto-agree with anything related to
  this"), text exactly as in eon-61efs's STATUS questions 1a-1d, with 1a
  reading "approved by eon-overseer under Lucca's standing approval for this
  fix". Venus prose: venus/docs INTERACTION.md:39-40, REFERENCES.md:591-593.

No EONW or ORB wire change. No configuration value (the 250 ms fallback stays
fixed, as today).

## Acceptance

In installed Eon, isolated: a quick-search pick on a fresh workspace and on
Alt+Shift+T, and Esc on a pending tab, each go from quick search to the pane
with no Yazi frame (frame bursts around the key). External `eon` CLI changes
still appear in Venus without waiting for a poll; with the subscription refused
or ended, Venus still updates within 250 ms.

## Verification

Full affected Rust and Nix surfaces (`nix develop -c eon-test` for the runtime
and Venus crates, Venus `cargo fmt --check` and clippy `-D warnings`), the
quick-search-guard and default checks, one isolated installed dogfood of the
pick and Esc paths, converge with Codex, then the profile refresh by the
overseer.
close_reason: Landed on edge as 47e5566: Venus learns workspace changes by EON-C39 subscription; the idle-CPU follow-up is eon-ozcsz.

comments.author: lucca
comments.text:
Approval (eon-61efs.1, 2026-11-04): Codex's full review found that subscriber
writes are nonblocking, so a subscriber whose socket is full gets an action's
events after the reply; the approved (c) Latency sentence was not true for it.
eon-overseer approved the qualified text, under Lucca's standing approval for
this fix ("auto-agree with anything related to this", 2026-11-04):

"**Latency.** An event is written within one supervisor loop turn of the
Runtime state change it reports. The events of a change made by an EONW action
are written before that action's reply to each subscriber with no earlier
events still pending; a subscriber that is behind receives them after its
pending output. An attention change reported by a program is a Runtime state
change when the poller receives it (at most 2 Hz, EON-C31)."

The overseer also rejected the timing-only rebuttal of the Venus cross-socket
race: the fix must make Venus apply a readable pending hide before it presents
an Orbit frame, shown from the code.

comments.text:
Dependency gate (eon-61efs.1, 2026-11-04): approved by eon-overseer under
Lucca's standing approval for this fix ("auto-agree with anything related to
this", 2026-11-04).

- Change: rustix's `event` feature enabled on the existing exact pin
  rustix =1.1.4 in venus/Cargo.toml (Linux and macOS target table). No new
  package or version; Cargo.lock unchanged. On Linux, other crates already
  build rustix with `event`, so nothing new compiles there.
- Capability: `rustix::event::poll` lets Venus's subscription thread wait until
  its EON-C39 subscription socket is readable without holding the lock under
  which it reads, so the window thread can read the same socket (catch_up)
  before it applies an Orbit frame. This is what makes "no hidden popup frame"
  hold from the code, not from timing.
- Why not the alternatives: a blocking read outside the lock can hold bytes the
  window cannot see; a short read timeout under the lock stalls the window;
  libc's `poll` is unsafe code and libc is pinned only for macOS; polling the
  socket on a timer reintroduces latency.
- Replacement cost: one call site in venus/src/transport.rs; drop the feature
  if the standard library gains a readiness wait or peek on UnixStream.
  Recorded in venus/docs/CRATES.md ("Subscription readiness").

title: Check how Claude Code prints long URLs for plain-text link detection
description:
## Why

`eon-nlcy` (commit c04632f) made Venus detect plain-text http/https URLs, joined only across
soft-wrapped rows. A URL that a program breaks onto a new line itself is detected only up to that
line end, and that first part can still pass the opener, so Ctrl+click opens a truncated address;
only the target preview shows it. Claude Code output was the case that motivated `eon-nlcy`, and
Ink-based TUIs such as Claude Code may lay out long lines themselves. Lucca asked for this check on
2026-10-21. Nobody has observed yet which rows Claude Code produces for a long URL in Eon.

## Evidence

- `venus/src/scene.rs:5319`: `Scene::logical_line` joins rows only when `wrapped`/`wrap_continuation`
  (Orbit's soft-wrap flags) link them; `Scene::detected_links` stops a target at a hard row end.
- `venus/src/scene/tests/links.rs:106` test `plain_text_links_join_soft_wrapped_rows_only`: a hard row end leaves
  `https://exa` detected on its own.
- `venus/docs/INTERACTION.md` (Hyperlinks) and VEN-C5 in `venus/docs/CONTRACTS.md` record the
  limit; the reference gate on `eon-nlcy` notes Ghostty and foot behave the same.
- `eon-nlcy` decision 5: setting `FORCE_HYPERLINK=1` for Orbit children would make
  supports-hyperlinks-based programs emit real OSC 8 links; recorded there, not decided.

## Scope

In scope:
- Observe, in an isolated Eon session, how Claude Code (and one other Ink-based TUI if cheap)
  prints a URL longer than the pane width: soft-wrapped
  rows (whole URL highlights on hover) or program-inserted line breaks (only the first row's part
  highlights). Also note whether it emits OSC 8 links under any environment it checks.
- Record results here, then propose the smallest fix with a recommendation if real output breaks,
  and stop for Lucca's decision before any contract or code change.

Out of scope:
- Any code, contract, or `FORCE_HYPERLINK` change in this bead.
- Other schemes, bare hosts, file paths (excluded by Lucca's scheme-only decision on `eon-nlcy`).

## Acceptance

- The bead records, for Claude Code at an exact version: the pane width used, whether a long URL
  arrives soft-wrapped or hard-broken, what hover and the target preview show, and whether OSC 8
  appears under default or `FORCE_HYPERLINK=1` environments.
- If real output breaks, a proposal (options, recommendation, affected contract VEN-C5 and owner)
  awaits Lucca; if it does not, the bead closes with a note on VEN-C5's limit staying as is.

## Implementation Notes

1. First use `eon pane history` on a pane where Claude printed a URL longer than its width: one joined logical line indicates soft wrapping, split lines indicate hard breaks. Record alternate-screen use; missing history is inconclusive. Only for hard-broken or inconclusive output, build or reuse the installed `eon` and run it on a private headless Sway as in the
   `eon-nlcy` proof comment (fresh HOME/XDG dirs, short `mktemp -d /tmp/claude-1000/sc.XXXX`
   root, `wdotool prime`, a fake `gio` first on PATH that records dispatches).
2. Claude Code needs sign-in; if the isolated HOME cannot use it, ask Lucca for a one-minute
   observation in his own Eon instead (have Claude print a 200-character https URL in a narrow
   pane, then hover it) rather than copying credentials.
3. Hover the URL's first and last rows and compare the preview with the printed URL; Ctrl+click
   and read the recorded dispatch.
4. Check OSC 8 emission by repeating with `FORCE_HYPERLINK=1` in the terminal's environment.

## Verification

- Planning/observation route: bead comments with the exact Claude Code version, Eon revision,
  environment and observations; no profile refresh, no runtime claims beyond what was observed.

## Stop Conditions

- Stop before editing any code, contract, or Orbit/Eon environment policy.
- Stop if observing Claude Code would require copying Lucca's credentials into a test HOME.

## Maintenance Notes

- Candidate fixes to weigh if it breaks: emitting OSC 8 from the program (`FORCE_HYPERLINK` or the
  program's own option), a narrowly gated join of a full-width row ending in URI bytes with the next
  row, or leaving the limit documented. A join heuristic risks false targets; weigh it against
  Ghostty/foot behavior recorded on `eon-nlcy`.

Record actual versus inferred hover/preview results; a clear history result may reuse the existing soft-wrap regression evidence rather than requiring another native capture. Keep default/FORCE_HYPERLINK=1 OSC 8 observation: text history cannot prove escape sequences. Record exact version/width/revision. Authentication unavailable leaves that observation unproved; never copy credentials or change a live user window without authorization. No code, contract or environment-policy change here.

title: Fix the crash-recovery test race that turned edge CI red
description:
## Why

Edge CI (Publish Linux binary cache, run 42155256949 on 7b59e45) failed in the Nix build: `a_recovery_adopts_the_snapshot_of_an_unconfirmed_scrollback_start` (added by eon-u5bvd.4) panicked at workspace_control.rs:1434, eon.sock did not become connectable.

## Cause (diagnosed 2026-11-06)

A race in the test harness, not a product bug: after killing the first supervisor the test waited for one fake Orbit to log its lease release, but the supervisor held two; the replacement supervisor (fast in release builds) met a fake Orbit still answering Busy for the dead lease and exited ("already managed"), and the test then waited 5 s on a socket that never came. Real Orbit sees the hangup at once (orbit/src/host.rs ~815-846). Five kill-then-recover tests shared the race.

## Fix

Test-only: the fake Orbit appends releases to its log; `PairWindow::crash()` waits until every terminal of the window logged its release; the five recovery tests use it.

## Noted, not filed

Theoretical gap: real Orbit could still answer Busy if a new lease request and the old hangup arrive in the same poll turn, and recovery does not retry Busy. No real crash path is known to reach it.
close_reason: Landed: crash tests wait for every lease release

title: Fall back to the foreground program name in pane labels
description:
## Why

Split from eon-8rdi (Lucca, 2026-10-24, chose pane labels without it): when a program sets no
terminal title, the label could fall back to the foreground executable's name (`hx`, `cargo`).
That needs Orbit to read the foreground process (procfs on Linux), which ORB-C12 forbids today
("Orbit scans no procfs"), and it is Linux-only until a macOS replacement is proved.

## Shape (from the research, ~/.cache/eon-agents/8rdi/research/recommendation.md)

A bounded, fallible foreground executable basename (no argv) in a read-only Orbit metadata reply
on the existing management lease; ORB-C12 narrowed to shutdown; ORB-C13 and ORB-C15 rules kept;
label precedence pin > title > executable > directory.

Deferred until Lucca asks for it.

title: Exit cleanly when a stdout consumer closes
description:
Contract:
- Consumer: a person or program piping output from an Eon CLI command.
- Trigger: the downstream reader closes stdout before Eon finishes writing.
- Result: Eon exits quietly without a panic or backtrace; complete stdout and existing exit codes remain unchanged when the sink stays open.
- Important failures: non-broken-pipe errors reported by the standard output writer remain explicit.

Evidence: `eon versions | head -n 1` previously left Eon with status 101 and printed a Rust panic because `print!` and `println!` unwrap stdout writes. The same output paths serve generations, stop, workspace, versions, config-path, and JSON failure output.

Scope: central Eon CLI stdout handling plus one regression test and required README LOC/proof bookkeeping. Preserve managed child processes, supervisor logging, stderr diagnostics, protocols, product contracts, dependencies, and command output bytes. This changes no EON product contract.
close_reason: Current wording matches the standard writer's detectable failure boundary; runtime behavior and proof remain sound.

title: Give the expanded pane's bottom edge the stack's row spacing to the row below
description:
## Why

Lucca, 2026-10-24, on the installed build (after eon-glp0), screenshot of two columns with rows
below the expanded pane: "these bottom gaps in the stack, between the 'open pane' and the stacked
pane just below ... the gap is like twice as small than the other stacked panes because the pane
name and cwd of the pane that is open goes to it's top ... so the bottom border without words
flushes with the pane name of the stacked pane below".

Collapsed rows' label lines sit one title row apart (20 px at scale 1), each through the middle of
its title band. The expanded pane's top edge also passes through the middle of its title band, but
its bottom edge sits on the boundary with the next row's band, only half a title row (10 px) above
that row's label line, so the bottom border crowds the label below it.

## Behaviour

- When collapsed rows follow the expanded pane, the expanded frame's bottom edge sits one title
  row above the next row's label line (the same pitch as between collapsed rows): half a title row
  higher than today, inside the expanded terminal's bottom padding, the same mechanism and bounds
  as eon-glp0's shared bottom (inset = min(text_height/2, padding - widest stroke), and never over
  the actual rounded grid; where it cannot fit, the edge stays as low as the bounds require).
- The rows' sides (eon-m5bv joints) continue up to the raised frame edge; fill, focus frame (painted
  once, no neutral under it), eon-54jv fill rule unchanged.
- Layout unchanged: terminal rects and grids, header rows, hit targets, AccessKit bounds (VEN-C8
  frame-mode parity). Frameless and popups unchanged. When the expanded pane is the column's last
  pane, eon-glp0's shared bottom applies as today.

## Contract

No wording change expected: VEN-C8 describes the expanded pane as a full rounded frame with its
label in the top edge and does not fix its bottom; guides and changelogs describe the new spacing.
If the implementer finds a sentence the change makes false, it stops and reports it.

## Acceptance

- Venus paint test (fails first): with rows below the expanded pane, the distance from the expanded
  frame's bottom line to the next row's label line equals the collapsed-row pitch (within
  snapping) at scales 1/1.3/2; no stroke over raw grid rows (reuse eon-glp0's sweep); joints
  continuous.
- Isolated capture: a 4-pane stack with p1 expanded (before/after).

Portability: neutral.
close_reason: Expanded bottom edge keeps the stack row pitch; proof in comments

title: Add a panel heading position setting: notch (default) or connected, a straight top edge at notch height
description:
## Why

Lucca chose two panel heading settings on 2026-11-10: where the title sits, and whether the heading
has a grey fill (eon-ve7dc holds his words and the drawings,
https://claude.ai/artifact/84vXbE9p889TT6RN7KJwDt; letters below are that page's). He then added a
third position: "oh. we did not consider rex like? interesting. it would be like the double notch,
but connecting them. this is a very good option", and, once shown it needs no extra setting, "we def
need this too".

| position      | no fill                 | fill                        |
| ------------- | ----------------------- | --------------------------- |
| **notch**     | B: today's double notch | C: notches plus a grey row  |
| **connected** | H: Rex-like heading     | H2: plain header bar        |
| **inline**    | G: title in the line    | F: pills on a straight edge |

eon-ve7dc delivers the fill setting on notches. This bead introduces the position setting with its
first new value, "connected", the simplest drawing of the three. eon-pdstn then adds "inline".

Contract: VEN-C8 and VEN-C18 describe the notched headings. Presentation is a feature
(docs/AGENT-RULES.md, Contract-Driven Method): extend their wording, docs/CONFIGURATION.md and
venus/docs/PRESENTATION.md, citing the approval above. The key follows EON-C19's rules.

## Evidence (line numbers at 040cb56; verify)

- Panel title layout venus/src/scene.rs:4101-4147; paint venus/src/render/chrome.rs:3056-3302; title
  types chrome.rs:1118-1544; outlines venus/src/render.rs:3035-3158 and scene.rs:73-185.
- The fill setting and its path through Eon Runtime to Venus come from eon-ve7dc; read its landed
  code first and carry the new value the same way.
- An expanded pane inside a Stack already draws "one continuous raised band" instead of notches;
  check whether the connected outline can share that code.

## Scope

In scope:
- A setting, suggested `[panels] heading = "notch" | "connected"`, default "notch" (final name in
  the plan, beside eon-ve7dc's fill key; leave room for "inline"). Eon Runtime parses it and sends
  the resolved value; Venus parses none. Live reload.
- "connected": the panel's top edge runs straight at the height of today's notch tops, with the
  card's usual corner radius, so the outline is a plain rounded rectangle. The title, the actions,
  their targets and their positions do not move; they now sit inside the panel's top row.
  - Fill off: nothing behind the title row (the Rex look).
  - Fill on: the title row is filled in the unselected-tab fill across the panel's full width, from
    the top edge to the bottom of the title row, with no separator line (a plain header bar).
- One setting covers Stacks, popups, the Agents sidebar and dialogs alike.
- Same actions, keyboard stops, focus feedback, accessible names and CLI paths in every
  combination; only the drawing changes.

Out of scope:
- The "inline" value (eon-pdstn). The notch looks (unchanged), the defaults, pane titles inside a
  Stack, colours.

## Acceptance

- With "notch" (either fill value), rendering is pixel-identical to before this change.
- With "connected", no panel draws a notch or a curve in its top edge, in every panel kind (lone
  Stack, collapsed rows, zoomed, popup, Agents sidebar, dialog) and both fill values, and no
  panel's terminal row count changes.
- The focus frame colour and width follow the straight edge.
- The bead records how a connected Stack heading reads directly above an expanded pane's own band
  (the panel and its first pane must stay distinguishable), with a capture for reviewers.
- With fill off, title text keeps at least 4.5:1 contrast on the translucent terminal background at
  `background_opacity` 0.8 over a light wallpaper; if not, stop (see eon-0kq2c and eon-jg86j).

## Configurability (rule 6)

The key is the setting, documented in docs/CONFIGURATION.md with its default.

## Verification

- Venus scene and render tests for both fill values in every panel kind at scale 1, 1.125 and 2; a
  config parse and reload test. Run through `nix develop -c eon-test` (docs/DEVELOPMENT.md).
- No capture gate: Lucca reviews in his own window after the profile refresh.

## Stop Conditions

- Stop if carrying the value to Venus changes the EONW codec without a version bump.
- Stop if joining the notches moves the title, the actions or the terminal rows.

## Maintenance Notes

- Lands after eon-ve7dc (it reuses the fill setting and its path). CHANGELOG.md: new key.
close_reason: Landed: connected pane heading (panels.heading), proof in comment

title: Bind Nix package versions to their Cargo owners
description:
## Contract

Consumer: the x86_64-linux Nix alpha packager and a local user inspecting Eon package/version diagnostics.

Trigger: Nix evaluates or builds the accepted Eon graph, including `default` or `eonterm`.

Result: Eon's Nix package version comes from the Eon Cargo package that is compiled. Orbit, Venus, and Helix canonical-manifest versions are checked against the exact selected child Cargo metadata before a package can be produced. The packaged binaries, Nix metadata, and `eon versions` agree.

Important failures: a manifest/source version mismatch fails during Nix evaluation before package construction and identifies the mismatched component. A malformed or relocated child Cargo manifest fails explicitly. Current accepted versions remain unchanged.

Ownership: each Cargo manifest owns the actual Rust package version; `components/eon-alpha-v3.json` selects child identities; `flake.nix` owns the narrow assertion/translation between them. This hardens EON-C1 and EON-C9 without adding a product contract.

## Prerequisites and Reference Gate

- Originating audit `eon-audit-eon-nix-composition-teq` is closed with exact evidence at Eon `f2c5f8dbf250672b2f7798c4ad19a98f9044c59c`.
- Before code, compare the manifest Orbit and Venus pins with their latest accepted child source revisions as required by repository policy.
- Reinspect the exact selected Orbit, Venus, and Helix Cargo manifests, pinned Nix `builtins.fromTOML` behavior, pinned Nixpkgs `buildRustPackage`, and Nova `124308bfa128203f843839346c88296cd266568a` only for its useful version-assertion precedent.
- Preserve one canonical component graph, exact revisions, opaque store-path injection, and child ownership. Add no dependency: Nix builtins and the already selected source trees are sufficient.

## Why

The current graph can successfully build and report trusted version labels that differ from the source actually compiled. That defeats exact-version diagnostics during the update path where those diagnostics matter most.

Impact: MEDIUM. Effort: S. Implementation risk: LOW. Confidence: HIGH.

## Evidence

- `flake.nix:105-113`: Orbit's derivation inherits `orbitIdentity.version` but does not compare it with the selected Orbit Cargo package.
- `flake.nix:168-174`: Venus has the same unbound manifest-derived version.
- `flake.nix:211-213`: Helix checks only the selected revision and ignores `helixIdentity.version`.
- `flake.nix:534-540` and `crates/eon/Cargo.toml:3`: Nix separately hardcodes Eon `0.1.0` while the compiled binary reads its Cargo version.
- Exact selected source manifests currently report Orbit `0.1.0`, Venus `0.1.0`, and Helix workspace `25.7.1`.
- Audit reproduction: a valid manifest mutation to `99.99.99` produced fake Orbit/Venus derivation labels and retained the unchanged Helix artifact; a complete Helix mutation built and reported `99.99.99` while wrapping the same `hx`. Changing only Eon's Cargo version to `0.1.1` built a Nix package advertised as `0.1.0` while `eon versions` reported `0.1.1`.

## Scope

In scope:
- `flake.nix` version ownership and assertions for Eon, Orbit, Venus, and Helix.
- Focused negative mutation proof for each mismatch class.
- README LOC scorecard and exact proof/current-state documentation only where the accepted tracked change makes them stale.
- Exact Nix package/profile verification required by repository policy.

Out of scope:
- Changing any current Cargo or component version, revision, source URL, manifest schema, component set, runtime command, wrapper variable, or child repository.
- Binding Ratconfig runtime behavior, changing already-bound managed-package/Yazi/Bash/Zsh versions, or generalizing a package metadata framework.
- New dependencies, generated version files, release tooling, direct distribution, macOS packaging, or compatibility paths.

## Implementation Notes

1. First reproduce the four mismatch classes in disposable clean archives: Eon Cargo version and Orbit, Venus, and Helix manifest versions. Require current Nix evaluation/build to accept them before the correction.
2. Read Eon's package version from `crates/eon/Cargo.toml` with Nix's existing TOML builtin and use that value for `eonPackage`; EonTerm should continue to inherit it.
3. Read the exact selected child Cargo metadata from the already pinned source inputs. Assert Orbit and Venus `package.version` and Helix `workspace.package.version` against their canonical manifest versions before their packages are consumed.
4. Prefer one tiny local helper only if it removes repeated TOML reading without hiding the different package/workspace paths. Add no parser or generated owner.
5. Update only required current-state proof/LOC records, build both outputs, and refresh the active `eon` Nix profile without restarting the supervisor or live Sessions.

## Acceptance

- Eon's Nix `version`, Cargo package version, compiled `eon versions` line, and EonTerm inherited version are identical.
- Orbit, Venus, and Helix selected Cargo versions equal their canonical-manifest versions.
- Each of the four disposable mismatches fails during Nix evaluation before a successful package derivation/build; the diagnostic identifies the relevant owner.
- The unchanged accepted graph still reports Eon `0.1.0`, Orbit `0.1.0`, Venus `0.1.0`, and Helix `25.7.1`.
- No new dependency, schema, generated artifact, child change, or compatibility surface exists.
- The active `eon` profile resolves to the exact verified current-tree artifact; running supervisors and Sessions remain untouched and restart requirements are reported.

## Verification

- `cargo fmt --all --check`
- `cargo check --locked --workspace`
- `cargo test --locked --workspace`
- `cargo clippy --locked --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings`
- `cargo run --locked -p eon-manifest -- components/eon-alpha-v3.json`
- `nix eval --raw --no-update-lock-file path:.#packages.x86_64-linux.default.version` should equal the Eon Cargo package version.
- `nix build --no-link --print-out-paths --no-update-lock-file path:.#default`
- `nix build --no-link --print-out-paths --no-update-lock-file path:.#eonterm`
- `nix flake check --no-update-lock-file path:.`
- Run the four disposable negative mutations and record their failing commands/errors.
- Verify `eon versions`, Nix profile/store equality, README LOC, and `git diff --check`.

## Stop Conditions

- Stop if any selected child pin is stale; refresh only through the normal accepted-revision gate.
- Stop if the exact child Cargo metadata shape has changed enough to require a child edit or new cross-repository contract.
- Stop if the fix requires a manifest schema change, generated version file, parser dependency, runtime lookup, or second component graph.
- Stop rather than weakening a mismatch to a warning or allowing package construction to continue.

## Maintenance Notes

This is the first remediation recommended by `eon-audit-eon-nix-composition-teq`. The cheapest sufficient shape is Nix TOML reads plus assertions at the existing package owners. Do not turn it into a generic metadata abstraction. The duplicate `protocol` input is an independent simplification and must not be bundled into this issue.

Inspect eon-b3i7g first: document Alt+R hide if present, otherwise use the existing keep-alive Files toggle/CLI owner, not another reveal transport. title: Make Venus's live output test pass on edge again (header hit-test at 100 px)
description:
## Report

eon-42 found this while proving eon-1u9e (2026-10-22). Venus's ignored live test fails on unmodified
edge, so it can't catch regressions in later Venus changes. Lucca approved filing it ("1 ok",
2026-10-22).

## Evidence (eon-42)

- Test: `application::tests::live_output_keeps_application_input_admitted_before_repaint`
  (`venus/src/application.rs`, ignored; run as venus/docs/DEVELOPMENT.md describes).
- On unmodified edge 587563d the failure is at venus/src/application.rs:5291. After
  `WindowEvent::Resized(PhysicalSize::new(100, 600))`, `presentation.invalidate()` and `render()`,
  the tab-strip loop moves the cursor to `PhysicalPosition::new(10.0, 1.0)` and asserts
  `workspace_scene().hit_test(10, 1) == None`. It gets `Some(Control(NewTab))`.
- Environment: private headless Sway 1.12 (`WLR_BACKENDS=headless`, output 1280x800, scale 1),
  with the installed Venus wrapper's LD_LIBRARY_PATH and FONTCONFIG_FILE. eon-42's script was
  /tmp/claude-1000/-home-lucca-pjs-eon-eon/cb8e8e25-ce64-4d82-82f8-9c0d45eb1ab8/scratchpad/live.sh
  (a scratch path, so it may be gone).

## Unknown, to establish first

- Is the test's assumption stale, or did the header regress? At 100 px width, recent Eon Bar
  changes (VEN-C21 header, VEN-C29 item order, the New Tab control, the quota and clock chips) may
  legitimately put the New Tab control at x=10. If so, the test is wrong. If the contract says
  that point should be empty, Venus is wrong.
- Find the commit where it started (bisect the live test on headless Sway), and whether fonts or
  the environment change the result.

## Contract

VEN-C21 (Eon Bar workspace header) and VEN-C29 (item order) decide what belongs at that point.
A contract change, if needed, goes to Lucca first.

## Portability disposition

neutral.

## Scope

In scope: diagnosis; fixing the test or the header layout, whichever is wrong; keeping the test's
original intent, which is checking live output vs. input admission, not header geometry.
Out of scope: other header redesign.

## Acceptance

- The live test passes on edge in the documented headless environment.
- The fix keeps a meaningful check: if the header assertion was incidental, it's replaced with one
  that checks the intended thing, not deleted.

## Verification

The live test on private headless Sway per venus/docs/DEVELOPMENT.md, `nix develop -c eon-test -p
yazelix-venus`, venus fmt and clippy.

comments.text:
Diagnosis (2026-10-22). Reproduced on private headless Sway 1.12 (pixman, 1280x800, scale 1) with the packaged Venus wrapper's whole environment (LD_LIBRARY_PATH, FONTCONFIG_FILE and XDG_DATA_DIRS pointing at Nix Mesa; without XDG_DATA_DIRS no Vulkan backend loads).
- Correction to the evidence: (10, 1) hits None. The failing probe is the loop's second one, (tabs[0].right + 1, viewport mid) = (46, 30.5). There the first pill spans x 8..45, the tab viewport ends at 45, and x 46 is New tab.
- Bisect of the live test over venus/ from 2586d7c (pass) to 43908c0 (fail): first bad commit 4910b81 'Inset the tab pills by the card gap'. That commit moved the first pill from one tab gap to one card gap (2*padding/3) from the left edge but left two widths sized for the old offset. (1) scene.rs tab_max_width caps a pill at viewport - 2*padding/3, which was a tab gap on each side and is now exactly the inset, so a capped pill ends on the viewport edge with no gap before New tab. (2) workspace_header_geometry's identity_width reserves pill + 2*tab_gap + 1, not inset + pill + gap + 1.
- Verdict: the header regressed; the test's assumption (a tab-strip gap right of the first tab) is still the intended layout. Contracts: VEN-C21 requires an active-tab region and controls without overlap, which holds either way; VEN-C8 keeps 'the gap between pills' as before. No contract change.
- Fix: tab_max_width subtracts card_gap + padding/3; identity_width = pill + card_gap + tab_gap + 1 (card_gap keeps header widths independent of the header's extra inset, per the tab_text_width comment). Both are needed: with only the cap fixed, the existing assertion that a narrow pill keeps one cell of label fails. eon_bar_keeps_tabs_controls_and_drag_hits_disjoint_under_pressure gains the display-free check that the narrow (100 px) scene's first pill keeps its trailing gap (hit None): red on unmodified edge, green with the fix. The live test passes with the fix.

comments.text: Width notes (review round 1): the fix narrows a capped pill by padding/3 (about 2.7 px at scale 1), so labels elide that much earlier. The cap applies when the tab viewport is under about 292 px, including medium windows whose quota chips take header space. In very narrow windows (under about minimum tabs + 3 pill rows, about 140 px), each header button is (card_gap - tab_gap)/count narrower, about 1.3 px with three controls. VEN-C8's 'header button width stay as before' was written about the header-height inset; here the buttons follow the same width-limited rule, giving up those pixels so the narrowest pill keeps one cell of label and its trailing gap. No CHANGELOG entry: the regression (4910b81) and this fix are both unreleased, so nothing changes against v0.1.1.

title: Warn once per unknown configuration key, as EON-C9 says
description:
Contract: EON-C9 ("An Eon build ignores a configuration key it does not know, with one warning naming the key and file"). No contract text change.

Observed (batch proof for eon-rpt9/eon-5z6y/eon-furp, 2026-10-26, edge 955df93, isolated headless Sway): a config with one unknown key (`[popup]`) logged "eon: ignoring unknown setting popup in .../config.toml" six times in the same millisecond at supervisor start, once more per directory-picker start, and once in each new terminal's scrollback. Artifacts: ~/.cache/eon-agents/eon-overseer/batch/run1/logs/.

Cause: `read_config` (runtime/crates/eon-runtime/src/managed_environment.rs, around line 1040) emits the warning on every read, and about ten callers read the file independently (shell command, shell config, terminal presentation, startup animation, popup catalog, ...). With no DiagnosticLog it writes to stderr, which a terminal launch path puts into the new terminal's scrollback. Predates the batch; any unknown key does it.

Decision (Lucca, 2026-10-26): fix it to match EON-C9.

Change: one warning per unknown key per supervisor start (and once per standalone CLI invocation that reads the config), in the supervisor log; nothing in terminal scrollback. Pick the owner deliberately: warn where the configuration is loaded once for a launch, or deduplicate per (file contents, key) in one place; do not scatter suppression across callers. Each new terminal still rereads settings (EON-C9 "each new terminal rereads them"); a reread of an unchanged file must not warn again, while an edited file with a new unknown key may warn once for that key.

Acceptance: with one unknown key, a supervisor start plus picker plus two new terminals yields exactly one warning line in the supervisor log and none in terminal scrollback; a test pins the count across repeated reads; `unknown_configuration_keys_preserve_known_settings` keeps its per-key check; Runtime tests, fmt and clippy green; one installed observation of the log and a new terminal's scrollback.

Scope boundary: warning emission only; no change to which keys are known, to error handling for known keys with bad values, or to the log format.
close_reason: done

comments.author: lucca
comments.text: Causes: supervisor reread config ~6x at start (supervisor.rs:238-244, 383, 765-771) plus per new terminal via sessions.rs shell_command; the 'per-picker' line was the terminal started after the picker; scrollback copy came from the eon-nu/eon-bash launcher (cli.rs launch_managed -> managed_environment::command, no log -> stderr). Fix: DiagnosticLog::note_once is the single dedupe owner; parse_config/read_config split; supervisor sets a Runtime-private one-shot marker EON_CONFIG_WARNED only when it launches the default shell and argv[0] is a bare Eon launcher name with the session bin dir set; the launcher parses silently only with the marker and always removes it before exec; explicit children and non-Eon shells get it removed. Implementer deviation accepted: eon-nu/eon-bash outside Eon must still warn (existing test). Review ledger: round 1 Claude clean, Codex 2 blocking (explicit children lost the warning; inherited EON_TERMINAL silenced tmux descendants) -> marker design; implementer then closed the non-Eon-shell marker leak; converge round 1 changed CHANGELOG text only; round 2 clean; narrow Codex re-check a79bfe4..ed06f8e: 1 finding accepted as a gap: an absolute path to Eon's launcher in [shell].command gets no marker, so that terminal prints a redundant warning (undocumented config; never loses a warning). Accepted behaviours: anything started inside a terminal (tmux, typed eon-bash) warns on stderr; a key added mid-session warns at the next supervisor reread. Proof on this commit's tree (ed06f8e plus bead records): nix develop -c eon-test -p eon-runtime -p eon: workspace_control 46 passed, eon_runtime 117 passed 1 ignored; fmt --check and clippy --all-targets -D warnings green; new tests red without their part of the fix; x86_64 Linux.

title: Show quota pace as soon as 1% of a window is used
description:
## Why

Lucca 2026-11-10, looking at the Claude 7d chip 5 hours after its weekly reset (85% left): "why is it not telling me about my pace". The pace colour and hover line wait until a tenth of the window has elapsed (venus/src/scene.rs quota_shortfall: `elapsed < 0.1` with quota left returns None; venus/docs/PRESENTATION.md, the pace bullet). For a 7-day window that is 16.8 hours with no warning, even when the start is fast: 15% used in 5 hours runs the week out in about a day and a half. Lucca chose to show pace earlier ("yeah") and put it inside the v0.2.0 release ("inside the gate").

## Change

Lucca, same day, after the 10%-used proposal: "why so careful? lets just show it with no restrictions". Then: "after 1% was used, start calulating". A fresh window with a reset shows its pace (label colour and the hover/accessibility pace line) as soon as at least 1% of its quota is used (remaining_percent <= 99), with no elapsed-time threshold. Under 1% used it stays neutral with no pace line, as a young window does today. Everything else in the pace rule stays: the linear projection, the colour scale and thresholds, used-up windows always coloured, stale/blocked/unknown/reset-less windows neutral (they have no basis), contrast. 

- Replace the `elapsed < 0.1` branch of quota_shortfall with a used-share check (under 1% used and not used up: None) and update its doc comment.
- Update the pace bullet in venus/docs/PRESENTATION.md ("past its first tenth" becomes "with at least 1% used"; "younger windows" becomes windows under 1% used), and venus/docs/CONTRACTS.md if a VEN-C clause states the tenth (the overseer approves the narrowed wording under Lucca's standing rule).
- The 1% threshold is Lucca's chosen fixed value; record that here rather than adding a setting, unless an existing quota setting makes one natural.
- venus/CHANGELOG.md and CHANGELOG.md entries (user-visible).

## Proof

Venus unit tests for quota_shortfall and the chip text/tooltip: a window minutes old with some quota used shows pace in the right colour band; a window minutes old with under 1% used shows no pace; past a tenth unchanged; used-up, stale and reset-less unchanged. Venus focused suite via `nix develop -c eon-test -p yazelix-venus`, fmt, clippy. No visual capture needed beyond the existing bar tests unless the colour code path changes.

## Acceptance

The 5h-into-7d example above (15% used) shows a red/orange chip and a hover line saying it runs out about a stated time before the reset.
close_reason: Landed: pace shown from 1% used; Codex + Opus land; merged-tree checks green

title: Spike frame-arrival-to-present scheduling in Venus before choosing a present mode
description:
From the agreed performance plan /home/lucca/.cache/eon-agents/eon-perf-research-discussion-final.md (Codex and Opus researchers, both signed AGREED 2026-11-09; eon-bah29), accepted under Lucca's "auto-agree with the final plan". Read the plan's sections Numerical implementation goals, Ranked implementation beads and Pacing proof guards before planning; its goals are acceptance objectives measured with matched before/after artifacts, 10+2 launches, p50/p95 and the full frame/timing gate (eon-benchmarks-xl2bp.7).

Rank 6. Measure arrival to dispatch, rebuild, submit and present waits on both adapters before choosing frame latency 1, immediate-when-idle or Mailbox; no vsync or photon gain is established yet. Keep platform, configuration, IME, accessibility and presentation semantics.

## Acceptance and boundary

At 6e63eb7 render.rs:1274 selects Fifo; application.rs/render.rs own redraw requests. Both adapters means hardware Vulkan and software on the same Linux host. Portability neutral; native mechanics stay at their seam.

Produce a decision record comparing supported candidates with a matched baseline: arrival→dispatch, rebuild, submit/present-API waits, CPU, gaps, memory and correctness. Keep the approved plan's 10+2 launches, p50/p95, full frame/timing gate and input/held-output/effects guards. Goals from that plan: native ingress→submission p95 ≤30 ms (20 stretch), dense render-call p95 ≤4/10 ms hardware/software, submission-gap p99 ≤20/25 ms, clean memory ≤1.05x. State unavailable measurements; API return is not GPU completion or photons.

The spike recommends proceed/reject and ships no default/mode change. Any adoption is a separately approved one-session slice with config/fixed-value rationale. Keep IME/accessibility/platform semantics. Stop for any necessary contract/dependency change; gu13n.2 remains the measured pacing prerequisite.

title: Make a closed Eon window that keeps running visible and easy to quit
description:
## Why

Lucca, 2026-11-01: "create a p1 bead to decide if closing should kill. right now i dont know a good
way to kill the entire window".

Lucca, 2026-11-01, later: "we def have to fix this problem. i close the old window and it keeps
existing without me knowing about it".

The problem to fix, not optional: a window closed by habit keeps running (agents, servers, memory)
and nothing in Eon shows it afterwards. Its author could not find how to end a window for good.
Under AGENTS.md "Happy users", that is a gap whatever the contracts say. The decision must make a
backgrounded window both visible and easy to end.

## Current behavior (accepted child records own proof)

- Closing the window (title-bar X, compositor close) quits it, as Alt+Shift+Q does. It asks first
  only while a terminal runs something other than its idle shell, and names those terminals.
- Alt+Shift+D detaches without asking. Each time, on Linux, a desktop notice names the window and
  how many terminals still run.
- `eon quit` quits the calling terminal's window (`eon quit --all` quits every window).
- `eon window ls` lists every running window; `eon window stop ID|previous|all` stops one or more;
  `eon window attach [ID]` presents a detached window.
- `eon generations` and `eon stop GENERATION` are gone.

## Settled decisions and remaining work

The original questions below are historical. Comment 5149 records Lucca's 2026-11-03 change:
close follows Quit with the busy prompt; Alt+Shift+D detaches; crash/logout must preserve terminals.
This superseded the 2026-11-01 detach-on-close choice. No [window] close setting was approved.
The Window menu now opens from the leading Eon icon (EON-C32), not the old version badge.
Routine child text follows the approval mode in comment 5023; real trade-offs still go to Lucca.

Open children: .11 (notice click to attach), .14 (notice-Quit regression), .19 (dev-shell docs),
.20 (Plasma logout), .23 (released beta site text). Preserve each bounded follow-up. The site
child follows the tag; never make the beta cut wait on this whole epic and introduce a cycle.

## Original decision questions (historical)

1. **What the window close (X) does.** Options: (a) keep detach (Eon's pitch: "Close the window, keep
   the work"); (b) quit, like other desktop apps; (c) ask once with Quit / Keep running / Cancel,
   with "remember my choice"; (d) a setting `[window] close = "detach" | "quit" | "ask"` (AGENTS.md
   rule 6), choosing its default. Weigh: the README's lead promise, users who close by habit and
   lose agents or servers, users who expect X to end things and leak processes, and the compositor
   close path (a close request cannot always wait for a prompt; check Venus/winit behavior).
2. **A direct Quit action.** A shortcut for Quit this window (check EON-C20 and Venus for
   collisions, e.g. Alt+Shift+Q), its Alt+/ line, the bottom hints (EON-C24), and whether the Eon
   Bar gets a control. Quit keeps the live-terminal confirmation Stop already shows.
3. **A short CLI path from inside the window.** For example `eon window stop` with no ID (or
   `eon quit`) meaning the calling terminal's window, asking first from a terminal (EON-C10),
   so agents and people need no ID lookup (AGENTS.md rule 5).
4. **Showing what keeps running.** Lucca's idea, 2026-11-01: a session section in the agent sidebar.
   A compact footer (not a second list) showing this window (name, uptime, live terminal count, so
   what Quit stops), other generations or windows still running (a count that opens a list), and
   Detach and Quit actions (Quit keeps Stop's live-terminal confirmation). Its CLI twin already
   exists in `eon window ls` / `eon window stop`. Limit: the sidebar can be hidden or turned off
   (`[sidebar] enabled = false`), so it cannot be the only quit path.
   Alternative Lucca found interesting: the Eon Bar's `<icon> EON <version>` badge (EON-C25,
   eon-369s) becomes clickable and opens a session menu with the same contents; always visible,
   also with the sidebar off, closer to a desktop app menu, less discoverable as a click target.
   Decide one, or the sidebar footer with the badge menu as fallback when the sidebar is off.
5. **Discoverability.** Whether detach should say how to quit every time it would surprise
   someone, not only once per user; and whether `eon --help`, USAGE.md and the README name the
   quit path next to `eon window attach`.

## Contract

EON-C8 (final close and detach), EON-C10 (typed workspace control), EON-C11/C23 (stop, windows),
EON-C20 (shortcuts), EON-C24 (hints), EON-C25 (version badge, if it becomes a menu), VEN-C30 and EON-C31 (sidebar),
VEN-C8 if Venus gets a new launch argument, and EON-C28 (1.x
stability: default shortcuts and close behavior are promised from 1.0, so decide before 1.0).
Follow the recorded approval mode above; this planning refresh supplies no new approval.

## Reference pass (required before recommending)

Survey how comparable tools handle close versus keep running, how they show background sessions,
and where quit lives: Zellij (on_force_close, session manager), tmux, WezTerm mux, Kitty, Ghostty,
VS Code remote, close-to-tray apps, the macOS app model, and the watch list in
~/pjs/refs/WATCHLIST.md (Rex, Moshi, herdr, Moshline). Record the findings, with sources, as a
comment here before the recommendation goes to Lucca.

## Acceptance

- Reference pass comment recorded (done 2026-11-01).
- Lucca's decisions recorded (done 2026-11-01; no `[window] close` setting for now).
- Every child is closed, or moved out of the epic with a recorded reason.

## Scope

Not in scope: final-tab close (settled in eon-pg67), restoring after a reboot
(eon-reboot-restore-im8y), and a `[window] close` setting (rejected for now, see the decisions comment).

comments.author: lucca
comments.text:
Reference pass, 2026-11-01 (subagent; local clones under ~/pjs/refs plus docs). Sources are file:line in the clones unless a URL.

- Zellij: closing the terminal detaches by default ("on_force_close ... detach (Default)", zellij-v0.45.1/zellij-utils/src/kdl/mod.rs:3528-3540), prints "Session detached" (zellij-utils/src/ipc.rs:324). Background sessions show in `zellij ls` and the session-manager pane (Ctrl o w), live and exited (session-manager-alias.md:3-15). Quit is Ctrl q with no confirmation (assets/config/default.kdl:198). Sessions are saved and can be resurrected (session-resurrection.md:3-5). Setting: `on_force_close detach|quit` (input/options.rs:14-19,186-188).
- tmux: closing the terminal is SIGHUP; the session stays (client.c:533-540) and the client prints "detached (from session X)" (client.c:192-198). Background sessions show in `tmux ls` and prefix s (key-bindings.c:439). No default key for kill-session; kill-window and kill-pane ask y/n (key-bindings.c:396,444). Options: destroy-unattached (off), exit-empty, exit-unattached (options-table.c:401-412,813-827).
- WezTerm mux: close kills the window and its panes, asking first ("Really kill this window and all contained tabs and panes?", overlay/confirm_close_pane.rs:52-60; termwindow/mod.rs:485-520). Detach is a separate named action, DetachDomain. Quit is QuitApplication with a confirmation. Settings: window_close_confirmation, skip_close_confirmation_for_processes_named, quit_when_all_windows_are_closed.
- Kitty: no persistence. confirm_os_window_close defaults to -1, which with shell integration counts only windows running a command (kitty/options/definition.py:2013-2028).
- Ghostty: no persistence. confirm-close-surface asks only while a process runs (src/config/Config.zig:2620-2626). On macOS the app outlives its last window (:2628-2637). quit-after-last-window-closed (+ -delay, Linux only, :2678).
- herdr TUI: ctrl+b q detaches and panes keep running in a server (how-to-work.mdx:8-31). Quit is `herdr server stop` or `herdr session stop <name>` (troubleshooting.mdx:67-71).
- herdr-app (GUI, the closest analogue): on Linux, closing the window quits the app while herdr-core keeps the terminals, with no prompt or notice (herdr-app/src/window.rs:532-544; docs/commands.md:528-530). There is no in-app stop; only `hc server stop` (herdr-core/docs/commands.md:589). This is Eon's problem exactly. Inference: its users likely hit it too.
- Wave Terminal: closing a non-last window deletes its tabs, with an optional confirmation; the last window is saved (waveterm/emain/emain-window.ts:295-330). Settings: window:confirmclose, window:savelastwindow, app:confirmquit.
- VS Code: terminals reconnect on reload and are revived on restart, but do not keep running after the window closes (https://code.visualstudio.com/docs/terminal/advanced).
- Docker Desktop, Slack, Discord: close hides to the tray by default. Quit is in the tray menu. Each has a setting.
- macOS app model: closing a window does not quit the app. The Dock dot shows it is running, and the app menu holds Cmd+Q. (From general knowledge; the HIG page did not load.)

Lessons:
1. Every GUI that keeps running after close shows it all the time at OS level (tray icon, Dock dot). Multiplexers instead print a detach line, and the user started the server knowingly. Eon on Wayland has neither: GNOME has had no tray without an extension since about 3.26. So Eon must show background windows itself, both inside every window and as a notice on each close.
2. herdr-app shows the failure mode: silent close-keeps-running with a CLI-only stop.
3. Both camps keep detach and kill as two named actions, never one ambiguous gesture.
4. No tool checked (about ten) uses an ask-on-close dialog with "remember my choice". The pattern is a setting plus a confirmation only while something runs (Kitty -1, Ghostty, WezTerm skip list).
5. Quit lives in one fixed, discoverable place (app menu, tray menu, one key), and short CLIs need no ID (`herdr server stop`, `tmux kill-session`).
6. Resurrection lowers the cost of quitting (Zellij). Eon cannot restore after a quit yet (eon-reboot-restore-im8y), so Quit should confirm while terminals run a command.

comments.author: lucca
comments.text:
Decisions, Lucca 2026-11-01, his words: "i agree overall, lets create and update the beads. but number 5 is bad for now because it increases the UX we have to cover and make coherent. we have to pick one of the three options and make it feel great and then one day in the future we can carefully add this setting".

Read as decided (the five numbered recommendations from the reference pass):
1. Accepted. Closing the window keeps detaching by default, never silently: every close sends a notice naming the window and how many terminals still run, with a Quit action.
2. Accepted. Eon shows running windows itself: the sidebar session footer (this window, live terminal count, other running windows, Detach and Quit), plus the clickable `<icon> EON <version>` badge as the always-visible entry, which also covers the sidebar turned off.
3. Accepted. A new launch says when older windows still run.
4. Accepted. A Quit shortcut, `eon quit` (this window, no ID) and `eon quit --all`, confirming only while a terminal runs something other than an idle shell.
5. Rejected for now. No `[window] close` setting. Window close has one behavior, detach, and the work is to make it feel great. A setting may come later, added carefully. This is the AGENTS.md rule 6 record of why close behavior stays fixed.

The remaining decisions in the body (1 window close, 2 direct Quit, 3 short CLI path, 4 showing what runs, 5 discoverability) are answered by the above: 1 detach; 2 a shortcut; 3 `eon quit`; 4 footer plus badge; 5 a notice on every close plus the launch notice. Implementation is split into the child beads of this epic; each child's contract text still comes to Lucca before code.

title: Add eon quit and eon quit --all, needing no window ID
description:
## Why

eon-7cf0y decision 4 (Lucca, 2026-11-01): a short CLI path to end a window, no ID lookup. Today it needs `eon window stop ID` or `eon stop GENERATION`, and `eon stop` with no argument fails ("invalid Eon generation identity"). It is also the CLI path for the Quit shortcut and the notice's Quit action (AGENTS.md rule 5).

## Change

- `eon quit`: inside an Eon terminal, stops the calling terminal's window (from `EON_TERMINAL`, as EON-C10 targets the caller). Window names come with eon-7cf0y.4.
- `eon quit --all`: every running window of this user (what `eon window stop all` / `eon stop all` attempt today; state which, and why).

## Contract

EON-C10, EON-C11, EON-C23; EON-C28 (new command names join the 1.x promise). Show Lucca the exact text first. If the foreground query changes an Orbit or EONW message, that is a protocol change with its own approval and version bump.

## Acceptance

- Tests: caller targeting, one versus several windows outside Eon, `--json`, exit statuses.
- Installed check in an isolated root: `eon quit` from a pane ends its window; from outside with two windows it refuses and lists both.
- USAGE.md command table and `eon --help`; CHANGELOG entry.

## Scope

CLI only. The window's Quit shortcut and prompt are a sibling bead.

title: Reattach the closed window when its close notice is clicked
description:
## Why

Found by the eon-7cf0y.2 planner (2026-11-01, Q3): clicking the body of the detach notice on GNOME opens the default window, even when the detached window was independent. People expect the click to return to the window the notice names. Closing now quits; Alt+Shift+D is the deliberate detach path (eon-7cf0y.16).

## Scope and ownership

The notice's default action reattaches its named window through the existing window-attach/presentation owner. Runtime owns notification identity and lifecycle; Venus remains the view. Quit and Keep running keep their current behavior. No new agent command is needed: `eon window attach ID` already provides it. Portability: isolated Linux freedesktop-notification dependency; no macOS notification expansion.

## Evidence and prerequisites

At 6e63eb7, `runtime/crates/eon-runtime/src/notification.rs:46-65` has only Confirm/Quit events and no attach command. `supervisor.rs:2450` answers notice events. eon-7cf0y.2 is closed; its installed proof and Lucca's COSMIC confirmation are historical evidence, not proof of this action. Read EON-C8's current detach-notice paragraph in docs/CONTRACTS.md, not only the temporary .2 plan.

## Contract and reference gate

Before code, propose the exact EON-C8 amendment for Lucca's approval. Check the freedesktop default action, optional actions capability and sender/notice-ID filtering against .2's reference record and one current comparable client at recorded revisions. Reuse the existing window-attach route; stop if a new trust or lifecycle guarantee is needed. Default-action support is optional; an unsupported server keeps the text-only notice.

## Acceptance and verification

- On isolated installed Linux with default-action support, detach independent window B using Alt+Shift+D, invoke its notice's default action, and observe B return while window A and all terminals stay intact.
- Default-namespace windows return to their own generation too. A stale notice for an ended window must not create or target a different window; agree its failure behavior in the amendment.
- Missing default-action support does not delay detach or break the existing Quit confirmation/Keep running paths. Confirm the existing sender/ID checks still reject unrelated actions.
- Retain focused regression coverage of notice action dispatch, run the required workspace checks/review, and record the exact installed artifact and isolated observation. Update USAGE and CHANGELOG for the accepted behavior.

## Boundary

Default action only. No notification preference or new desktop support; .2's fixed safety-notice rationale remains. Desktop focus changes only when the person invokes the notice action.

description:
## Why

`~/.cache/eon-agents/eon-7cf0y/eon-7cf0y.8-plan.md`, section "Split?", recommendation applied under
the epic's approval mode, 2026-11-01). `eon-7cf0y.8` now carries Orbit management v5 (the
`foreground` fact) and the Runtime's adoption of it; this bead carries the busy rule that reads it.

## Change

- The idle/busy rule in Eon Runtime (EON-C11), as the plan's "The idle/busy rule" section states,
  with Lucca's Q1 decision (2026-11-01): the Agent popup counts as busy; the Files (Yazi) and Git
  (LazyGit) popups count as idle. Builtins and background jobs of an idle shell are not seen,
  documented beside that exception.
- EONW v29 (or the next free version) carrying `busy`; CLI `busy` in JSON (rule 5).
- `eon quit`: without a terminal, returns not-confirmed while something is busy; idle windows quit
  without asking. Prompt reworded to window language (see `eon-7cf0y.1`'s comment).

## Contract

EON-C10, EON-C11 and EON-C15 text exactly as the plan's "Contract text" section.

## Prerequisites

`eon-7cf0y.8` (Orbit management v5 landed and adopted).

## Acceptance

The plan's integration tests for the busy rule fail first and pass; full `eon-test`; package build;
one isolated installed check: an idle window quits without asking, a window running a foreground
command or an Agent popup asks first. Nushell external-command process groups are the go/no-go in
that check (plan, installed-check step 2).

## Scope boundary

No Orbit change. No Quit shortcut (that is `eon-7cf0y.3`).

title: Stop any window, the default one included, with one short command
description:
## Why

Found while landing eon-7cf0y.2 (2026-11-01). The close notice must name a command that stops exactly its window from a shell. `eon window stop ID` accepts only independent windows (window IDs are eight hex characters, windows.rs:36), and `eon quit` outside an Eon terminal only lists windows when several run. So the default window's notice has to say `eon stop GENERATION`, with a long generation ID, while independent windows get a short `eon window stop ID`. People should not need to know about namespaces or generations to stop a window.

## Change

One short, exact command stops any running window, the default one included, from any shell, e.g. `eon window stop` accepting the default window by a short ID or name shown in `eon windows` / EON-C23. Then the close notice (eon-7cf0y.2) and `eon quit`'s listing name that one command for every window.

## Contract

EON-C11 / EON-C23 CLI clause for the accepted target forms; exact text in the plan.

## Acceptance

From a plain shell with the default window and one independent window running, the same command form stops either one, and only that one; `--json` reports it (rule 5). The close notice's fallback and failure texts use it.

## Scope boundary

No change to Stop semantics or confirmation. Related: eon-7cf0y.9 (older EONW windows), eon-7cf0y.10 (one listing of every window).

title: Closing the window quits it like Alt+Shift+Q; Alt+Shift+D keeps it running
description:
Closing the window (Super+Q, the compositor's close, the macOS close button) quits it like Alt+Shift+Q, instead of detaching. Alt+Shift+D stays the deliberate way to keep terminals running.

Lucca, 2026-11-03: "what if closing the window (super q for instance) killed everything? we already have the detach command as an option" — then "agree" to the overseer's four guards below. Under eon-7cf0y's approval mode the overseer applies the contract text below; it reverses proved EON-C8/VEN-C14 text with his approval.

## Behaviour (approved)
1. A compositor close request takes the Alt+Shift+Q path from eon-7cf0y.3 exactly: an all-idle window quits at once; while a terminal is busy, the .3 quit prompt shows ("Enter Quit · Esc Cancel", hint "Alt+Shift+D keeps it running instead"). A close request while that prompt is open leaves it open.
2. Only a deliberate close quits. Venus crash, control loss, compositor exit and logout keep every terminal, as today (VEN-C14 control loss unchanged).
3. Alt+Shift+D still detaches without asking and still sends the "still running" notification; the Shortcuts row becomes "Detach: hide the window, keep terminals running".
4. Same on macOS: the close button is the same close request. Command+Q is eon-7cf0y.15.
eonbase, and any snapshot without a running-windows summary, has no Quit (EON-C8 via .3), so there a close request still detaches.

## Contract text (exact; applied on top of eon-7cf0y.3's landed text)
**EON-C8** Result: "Closing the window itself, or Alt+Shift+D, detaches every workspace together without asking; attach then shows the last shown workspace (EON-C11)." becomes "Alt+Shift+D detaches every workspace together without asking; attach then shows the last shown workspace (EON-C11). Closing the window itself quits it as Alt+Shift+Q does, prompt included, and a close request while the quit prompt is open leaves it open; where there is no Quit key (eonbase) closing the window detaches as Alt+Shift+D does." The detach-notification sentence "Each time a full-Eon window detaches this way" is unchanged (it now follows only Alt+Shift+D).
**EON-C20 / VEN-C20** Result: the row "Detach: close the window, keep terminals running" becomes "Detach: hide the window, keep terminals running".
**VEN-C8**: "…detaches by the same path as a compositor close request (VEN-C14)." becomes "…detaches (VEN-C14)."; after the Alt+Shift+Q clause add "A compositor close request acts as Alt+Shift+Q, and detaches without a running-windows summary."
**VEN-C14** Result: "Alt+Shift+D and the compositor close request both detach;" becomes "Alt+Shift+D detaches, and a compositor close request quits under VEN-C8;".
Unchanged: EON-C11, EON-C23, EONW (no wire change), ORB-*.

## Rule 6
Fixed, not configured: Alt+Shift+D is always the keep-running path and the busy prompt names it; a `close detaches` setting can follow if a user asks (Eon is not announced; Lucca is the only user).

## Scope
Venus only plus contract and user-docs text (docs that say closing keeps terminals running, Shortcuts wording, CHANGELOG bullet). No runtime or EONW change expected; if one is needed, stop and report.

## Proof route
Red first on edge+.3: Venus tests that a close request with an all-idle snapshot sends Stop for this generation, with a busy snapshot opens the quit prompt, a second close leaves it open, and without a running-windows summary still detaches. `nix develop -c eon-test -p venus`, clippy. Installed tier (isolated Sway, per the .3 recipe): `swaymsg kill` on an idle window ends its supervisor; on a busy one shows the prompt, Esc keeps it, Enter quits; Alt+Shift+D still detaches with one notification; Shortcuts shows the new Detach row. macOS: the mac-proof final run closes via the close button if the rental is up, else Yu checks at the end (memory: no slow VNC).
close_reason: Closing the window (desktop close key or close button) now quits it like Alt+Shift+Q, asking while a terminal is busy; Alt+Shift+D keeps terminals running; eonbase and an unavailable workspace still detach. Logout keeps terminals on desktops that end the session without closing windows (COSMIC, GNOME; KDE caveat documented). Proof, review ledger and gate PASS recorded above.

## For the bead

### What changed

- **Venus.** `WindowEvent::CloseRequested` goes through `close_request(snapshot, unavailable)`,
  the one place that chooses quit or detach. It detaches without a running-windows summary
  (eonbase), without a snapshot, while the workspace is unavailable, or after Eon refuses
  refreshes following a failed Stop. Otherwise it takes .3's Alt+Shift+Q path (`begin_quit`):
  - a busy window shows the prompt;
  - an idle window sends Stop once the next snapshot confirms it is idle;
  - a close while any close prompt is open does nothing, so the prompt keeps the answer.
- **Prompt opening.** The quit prompt replaces an open attention inbox or Shortcuts viewer in a
  single dialog change.
- **Workspace model.** `WorkspaceModel::unavailable()` is set by a lost connection or a
  `stop-incomplete` failure and cleared by a snapshot. `Destroyed` still exits.
- **Alt+Shift+D** is unchanged; its Shortcuts row reads "Detach: hide the window, keep terminals
  running".
- **Demo recorder.** `demo/record.rs` detaches the Eon window with Alt+Shift+D instead of
  closing it.
- **Docs.** README, CHANGELOG, venus/CHANGELOG, USAGE and INTERACTION follow these changes.
  `eon --help`, docs/ARCHITECTURE.md and the EON-C9 paragraph in USAGE no longer say a close

### Close wording sweep (gate B1)

Method: a whole-sentence scan across line breaks of every tracked file, `.beads` excluded
(`scan-close.py`, `scan-close2.py`; output in `scan-close-r3.txt` and `scan-close2-r3.txt`). The
first scan finds sentences where a close goes with detach, keeps, survives, still running or
hide. The second finds every "close the/a/its window", "window closed", "close request" and
"close button" phrase.

Fixed:
- `runtime/crates/eon-runtime/src/cli.rs:1112` (`eon --help`): "Closing a window detaches; eon
  quit ends it." → "Alt+Shift+D detaches a window; closing it or eon quit ends it."
- `docs/ARCHITECTURE.md:42`: "Closing its window detaches the view; explicitly stopping it ends
  the terminal." → "Detaching its window (Alt+Shift+D) keeps the terminal; closing the window or
  explicitly stopping it ends the terminal."
- `docs/USAGE.md:797` (EON-C9 paragraph, on edge's eon-yxo2y text): "closing and reopening a
  window, reattaching it, or recovering it keeps the old environment." → "detaching and
  reattaching a window, or recovering it, keeps the old environment."
- `eon/crates/eon/tests/workspace_control.rs:5463` (test comment): "Told to detach, it exits 0,
  as Venus does when its window closes." → "… as Venus does on Alt+Shift+D."

- Already updated by this bead, so they state the new rule: README:23 and :64; USAGE:57, 63-66,

    and `supervisor.rs:51` ("close its detach notice").

    keeps those detaching.
  - REFERENCES:119 describes Ghosthub's design ("detach-only close"), not Eon's.
  - Orbit's "a client that closes is detached" (ORB-C1, BEHAVIOR.md, LAWS.bend) is about an Orbit
    client's socket, not the window.
- `eon/skills/eon/SKILL.md`: only `eon tab close` and `eon pane close`. No window-close claim.

### Rule 5 and rule 6

- **Rule 5:** no new window action. Closing the window quits, and `eon quit` is that CLI path
  (the same Stop); what the prompt shows is readable from `eon workspace --json` `.busy` and
  `.running.this`. `eon --help` now tells an agent the same thing: "Alt+Shift+D detaches a
  window; closing it or eon quit ends it." There is no `eon detach` command. Detaching the person's window is a listed
  rule-5 exception (AGENT-RULES, Humans and Agents). It covers Alt+Shift+D and every close that
  detaches: eonbase, an unavailable workspace, after a failed Stop, and logout.
- **Rule 6:** fixed, not configured, as the bead records. Alt+Shift+D is always the keep-running
  path and the busy prompt names it; a `close detaches` setting can follow if a user asks. The
  Detach row and the logout and close wording are fixed product text.

### Logout: what desktops do (from source, read only, no runtime test)

- **KDE Plasma sends close before ending the session.** plasma-workspace@4f6a334
  `startkde/plasma-shutdown/shutdown.cpp`, `Shutdown::ksmServerComplete()`, calls
  `org.kde.KWin.Session.closeWaylandWindows` and cancels the logout on an invalid reply.
  `SessionManager::closeWaylandWindows()` calls `closeWindow()` (xdg_toplevel.close) on every
  `XdgToplevelWindow` and waits up to 10 s for them to close
  ([kwin@96546b8 src/sm.cpp#L367](https://invent.kde.org/plasma/kwin/-/blob/96546b84ddd6a6c3080b894da1773506f698f847/src/sm.cpp#L367)).
  So a busy Eon window's prompt probably holds a KDE logout until it is answered or that timer
  ends.
- **COSMIC sends none.** cosmic-osd's logout calls `com.system76.CosmicSession.Exit`
  ([cosmic-osd@4f96e98 src/components/app.rs#L150](https://github.com/pop-os/cosmic-osd/blob/4f96e98981712f02b98f704a6f19c4c6a58b378b/src/components/app.rs#L150)).
  cosmic-session aborts the compositor
  ([cosmic-session@4b0a0a2 src/main.rs#L466](https://github.com/pop-os/cosmic-session/blob/4b0a0a24e98b9e755b6a7146e4cb29539cacda0a/src/main.rs#L466)).
  cosmic-comp@6e29ee6 calls `send_close` only for user actions. Clients just lose the
  connection.
- **GNOME on Wayland sends none.** gnome-session's end-session phases talk only to registered
  D-Bus `GsmClient`s
  ([gnome-session@0cfee22 gsm-manager.c#L396](https://gitlab.gnome.org/GNOME/gnome-session/-/blob/0cfee2253b53f71343f2db6a4fc9a8cd2ad1e6c0/gnome-session/gsm-manager.c#L396)).
  mutter@432c167 reaches `xdg_toplevel_send_close` only from `meta_window_delete` (close
  keybinding, attached dialogs, X11 `_NET_CLOSE_WINDOW`). gnome-shell@7904014's
  `endSessionDialog.js` only confirms logout.
- **Docs.** USAGE and the CHANGELOG name GNOME and COSMIC as desktops that detach at logout, and
  KDE Plasma as one that closes windows. The contracts use KDE Plasma alone as the example.
  Whether terminals survive logout at all still depends on logind (EON-C15 boundary).

### Open items

- macOS close button: not proved here. Per the bead, the mac-proof final run covers it if the
  rental is up; otherwise Yu checks it at the end.
- Website text and clips: eon-7cf0y.21.
- Leftovers to delete at retirement, all under /home/lucca/.cache/eon-agents/eon-7cf0y16/:
  `target/`, `target-darwin/`, `pkg`, `pkg-r1`, `pkg-r2`, `pkg-r3`, `r1-recorded-features/`,
  `installed1/` to `installed4/`. Keep `installed3/s4-viewer.png` and `detach-row-ref.ppm`

title: Reserve a version-independent Stop in EONW before beta
description:
From the eon-7cf0y.9 plan: a newer eon stops an older-EONW window by running that window's recorded eon. If that file is gone (garbage-collected store path), the window cannot be stopped except by killing it. its predecessor to the previous-generation Stop test" (~:3177). Exact text needs approval before code.

delegator's "v34 or older gets the old form" choice (LAST_GENERATION_FORMS in

title: Notify on every window close that Eon still runs, with a Quit action
description:
## Why

eon-7cf0y decision 1 (Lucca, 2026-11-01): closing the window keeps detaching, but never silently. Today only the first detach per user sends a notice (runtime/crates/eon-runtime/src/notification.rs, `notify_first_detach`, marker `first-detach-notified`), so later closes leave windows running unseen, which is how Lucca lost track of an old window.

## Change

Every detach by window close or Alt+Shift+D sends one non-activating freedesktop notification: it names the window (EON-C23 name or ID), says how many terminals still run, says how to return, and offers a Quit action that stops that window (through `eon quit`'s path, the sibling bead) after the same confirmation rule. Drop the once-per-user marker (keep reading or ignoring an old marker file harmlessly). A Venus crash still sends none; a missing notification service still never delays detach.

## Reference gate

Before code, confirm notification actions on the supported desktops (COSMIC, GNOME, Sway with mako or similar): whether `ActionInvoked` arrives, who must stay subscribed (the supervisor is the live process after Venus exits), and what happens when a server lacks the `actions` capability (then the body names `eon quit` instead of a button). Record findings here.

## Contract

EON-C8 (the first-detach notice clauses, docs/CONTRACTS.md around "Eon is still running in the background"). Show Lucca the exact new text before code. Text is fixed product text; record in this bead why it is not configured (rule 6), or expose it.

## Acceptance

- Unit tests for the notice body (window name, terminal count, singular and plural) and for no marker gating.
- Installed check on the isolated Sway root: two consecutive closes each send a notice; Quit from the notice ends the window; with actions unsupported the body names `eon quit`.
- CHANGELOG entry.

## Scope

Notice only. Not the sidebar, badge or launch notice (sibling beads).
close_reason: Close notice with Quit landed; proof, installed check and review ledger in the closing comment

Under the epic's approval mode the overseer applies the planner's recommendations (2026-11-01): Q1 Quit swaps the notice for a 'Quit NAME?' notice with Quit / Keep running, until eon-7cf0y.8's busy fact lets idle windows skip it; Q2 the notice stays fixed for now (rule 6 reason: one notice per detach is the product's safety net against silently running windows; a [window] detach_notice setting is drafted in the plan if wanted later); Q3 clicking the notice body to reattach this window is a possible follow-up, not filed yet (Lucca asked for no new work this session). comments.text:
Landed (overseer, 2026-11-01). Every full-Eon detach on Linux sends one non-activating desktop notification naming the window, its live terminal count and how to return; Quit asks "Quit NAME?" and then stops that window with the in-process Stop; Keep running closes it. Reference gate (from the plan, edge 3988679): one owner, the window's supervisor (runtime/crates/eon-runtime/src/notification.rs `Notices`, one session-bus connection per supervisor from its first detach); Venus unchanged. Sources: freedesktop Notifications spec 1.2 (actions optional without the `actions` capability, replaces_id, NotificationClosed reasons, `resident`); COSMIC cosmic-notifications 1.11.0 measured on this machine (advertises actions, persistence, body-markup; a real click unobserved, left to dogfood); GNOME Shell js/ui/notificationDaemon.js and mako dbus/xdg.c read at their default branch heads on 2026-11-01 (revisions not recorded): GNOME sends ActionInvoked/NotificationClosed only to the sender's connection and drops a non-resident notice on action; mako broadcasts ActionInvoked, `actions=0` drops the capability. Comparable clients: agentaps src/system_notifications.rs at 66c7116 (zbus, one long-lived worker, subscribe before Notify, replaces_id, forget on owner change) and kitty glfw/linux_notify.c at b2cb871. Constraints kept: stay subscribed on the connection that sent Notify; believe signals only from the issuing unique name for its own IDs, and owner changes only from the bus; replace and close go to the issuer; without `actions` the body names the stop command. Rejected: notify-rust (second owner of the same D-Bus calls), zbus p2p for a test bus (adds uuid and getrandom), a dbus-daemon in nix/test-sandbox.nix (widens isolation), spawning `eon stop` (Quit runs the in-process Stop). No dependency added (zbus =5.19.0 already in use).

Text decision (overseer, approval mode, 2026-11-01; supersedes the acceptance line "with actions unsupported the body names `eon quit`"): the fallback and failure bodies name the window's own stop command, because outside Eon with several windows `eon quit` only lists them. Independent window: "Run `eon window stop ID` to stop it." / "Some terminals may still run; run `eon window stop ID` to try again." Default namespace: "Run `eon stop GENERATION` to stop it." and the matching failure text. The short default form assumes a shell outside Eon; in an independent window's terminal it fails harmlessly (EON_WINDOW_RUNTIME_DIR selects that namespace). One short command for every window is eon-7cf0y.13. Notices with actions carry `resident` so GNOME keeps them for the in-place confirmation.

Rule 5: no new CLI. Quit maps to `eon quit`, `eon window stop ID` or `eon stop GENERATION`; return to `eon attach` / `eon window attach ID`. What the notice shows (name, live terminal count, running) is data in `eon windows --json`, `eon generations --json` and `eon workspace --json` running.this. Whether a notice is on screen is notification-server state, not workspace state.

Rule 6: the notice and its text stay fixed. Lucca's decision 1 (2026-11-01) makes "never silently" the product rule for close; an off switch would recreate the unseen-window failure this epic fixes. One notice per window replaces itself and never takes focus. The 500 ms end-of-window close wait and the 25 s D-Bus method timeout are internal bounds. A `[window] detach_notice` key (drafted in the plan) can be added later, additively.

Performance: from its first detach, each full-Eon supervisor keeps one session-bus connection and four idle-blocked threads (eon-detach-notice, eon-detach-notice-signals, zbus's executor, async-io's reactor), no polling; the main loop adds one try_recv per 25 ms tick; detach does no D-Bus work on the supervisor thread; supervisor end waits at most 500 ms, only when a worker exists.

- Installed observation (Codex, isolated): candidate /nix/store/fqcwf9m6icpv4gb6ysvn3ld57pd2wm39-eon-0.1.11 built from the tree; private headless Sway 1.12 (pixman, 1280x720), private dbus-daemon, mako 1.11.0. (2) A failed Stop from the notice is covered only by its text test. (3) "A Venus crash sends none" has no test (unchanged). (4) COSMIC click delivery and `resident` handling unobserved: dogfood. (5) A server reusing an ID it reported closed would leave the confirmation's buttons inert; GNOME and mako do not. (6) After a supervisor crash a stale notice's Quit does nothing.
