title: Keep terminals at KDE Plasma logout instead of quitting on its close requests
description:
Follow-up to eon-7cf0y.16 (Lucca 2026-11-03, option A). KDE Plasma's shutdown (plasma-shutdown closeWaylandWindows -> KWin closeWindow) sends every Wayland window an ordinary xdg_toplevel close, which Venus cannot tell from a deliberate close, so an idle Eon window quits at logout and a busy one shows the quit prompt. Before treating a close request as Quit on KDE, ask the session manager whether it is logging out (ksmserver's D-Bus interface or plasma-shutdown's; verify which exists and is reliable), bounded and cancelled at its deadline (see eon-yxo2y's lessons), and detach instead when it is. Same check for any other desktop the .16 source survey finds closing windows at logout. Acceptance: on a KDE Plasma VM, logout with an idle Eon window keeps its terminals (eon session --json after re-login shows them); a deliberate close still quits; the docs' KDE caveat is removed for covered desktops.

## Contract, reference and scope gates

Before implementation, draft the exact EON-C8 logout-paragraph and VEN-C14 close-text amendments for Lucca. At 6e63eb7 the KDE caveat remains in docs/CONTRACTS.md:741-744. The selected desktop set is still a question: KDE is required, and any additional desktop from .16's survey needs an explicitly recorded disposition before code. Do not silently widen platform support.

Read the owning reference routes in docs/REFERENCES.md and venus/docs/REFERENCES.md (supervisor-owned native presentation), then record exact ksmserver/plasma-shutdown revisions and the reliable signal/property, one comparable logout detector, and adopted/rejected mechanisms. eon-yxo2y's deadline finding is a warning: stopping a wait did not cancel a zbus read; it used a bounded child process, killed and reaped at deadline. Do not presume that mechanism is necessary until the selected interface is understood.

Portability: isolated Linux/KDE D-Bus dependency at the native lifecycle owner. Unknown/unavailable session-manager state or deadline expiry keeps today's close-as-Quit behavior, as recorded in comment 5769; detach must not wait indefinitely. No systemd requirement and no running-supervisor restart.

## Additional acceptance and verification

- Record the deadline and configurability/fixed-safety-bound rationale; demonstrate timeout and unavailable-bus fallback without leaking work.
- Preserve busy prompting on a deliberate close, deliberate Alt+Shift+D, control-loss recovery, and ordinary non-KDE behavior.
- On a private KDE Plasma VM, record the installed artifact, logout/re-login observations and surviving terminal identities, plus idle and busy cases. Remove the caveat only for desktops actually proved.
- Use the lifecycle proof route and fresh review required by AGENTS.md; update user docs and changelogs for the accepted guarantee. Stop if the reference gate cannot establish a reliable logout signal; report the choice instead of guessing.

title: One window family in the CLI: window ls, short ID prefixes, default window, no generations
description:
## Why

Lucca, 2026-11-06: "eon generations is too long a command", then "that makes sense, i agree" and "also agree" to the overseer's proposal. Windows and generations are two names for the one thing a person cares about, a running Eon window, so the CLI has three overlapping families: `windows` / `generations` to list, `window attach ID` / `attach [GENERATION]` to reattach, `window stop ID` / `stop GENERATION` / `quit --all` / `window stop all` / `stop all` to stop. The default window can only be stopped with a 35-character generation ID. This bead supersedes eon-7cf0y.10 (one listing of every window) and eon-7cf0y.13 (stop any window, the default included, with one short command).

## What (approved shape)

```
Windows
  quit [--all] [--json]                 End this window (or every window)
  window ls [--json]                    Every running window: ID, name, version,
                                        started, terminals, compatible or not
  window new                            Open an independent window
  window attach [ID]                    Reopen a window (no ID: the default one)
  window stop ID|previous|all [--json]  End a window, the old-version ones, or all
```

1. One `window` family. Removed outright, with no aliases (Lucca: no legacy code): `windows`, `generations`, `attach [GENERATION]`, `stop GENERATION|previous|all`, and the `--generation` workspace flag (only `--window ID` remains).
2. The list verb is `ls` (Lucca 2026-11-06: "eon session ls is shorter to type"; `ls` for every noun, no plural commands).
3. The default window's ID is the literal `default` (this build's default-namespace window; an older build's is addressed by its generation's hex, 4+ character prefix). Generation IDs leave all human-facing text but stay as data: in JSON (including the Stop result older builds parse), in `eon versions` and in `eon workspace`'s key=value lines. Notices (the close notice, the Venus-exit log line) name a default-namespace window by its generation's short hex, never `default` (S2 decision, 2026-11-06).
4. Short IDs: wherever Eon takes a window ID, any unique prefix of at least 4 characters selects it; an ambiguous prefix fails with the candidates (exit 3). Human output shows the shortest unique prefix, at least 4 characters. Matching only selects among existing windows; the full ID is used internally.
5. `eon config-path` and `eon config-dir` become `eon config path` and `eon config dir`, next to `eon config defaults` (no old names).
6. `eon -V` and `eon --version` print one line, e.g. `eon 0.1.18`.
7. The close notice (eon-7cf0y.2), `eon quit`'s listing, USAGE, the embedded agent skill and `eon --help` name only the new forms.

## Contract

EON-C11 and EON-C23 (CLI target forms and the window listing), EON-C10 where it lists the CLI; exact text in the plan. Lucca approved the shape above; the plan's exact text follows it (the overseer approves wording that carries it out, Lucca anything beyond it).

## Acceptance

- From a plain shell with the default window and one independent window running, `eon window ls` lists both (text and JSON agree), and the same `window stop` form stops either one, and only that one.
- Prefix selection: unique, ambiguous and unknown prefixes, each tested.
- Every removed command fails as an invalid command (exit 2).
- `eon -V`, `eon --version`, `eon config path`, `eon config dir` tested.

## Order

After eon-agent-parity-a9g0.3 (close any tab); before the workspace-to-session rename and before eon-ezeb7 (completion).

# eon-7cf0y.22 S1 — implementation notes

Base: edge `7b59e45` (EONW v34, Eon 0.1.18, close-any-tab included). Plan:
`eon-7cf0y-22-plan-work/PLAN.md` S1, contract text from
`eon-7cf0y-22-plan-work/bead/01-contract-step.md` [S1] items. The plan was
written at `4168d66`. Line numbers were rebaselined; the close-any-tab work in
`cli.rs`, help, USAGE and CONTRACTS is unchanged.

## What changed

- `control.rs`: `ambiguous-window-id` exits 3. It is a separate match arm,
  because adding it to the existing arm made rustfmt lay out all twelve
  patterns vertically.
- `generation.rs`:
  - `Select { Current, Previous, All, Generation }` replaces
    `stop_generations`'s `include_current: bool`.
  - `attach_generation` takes `root`. Its delegated exec sets
    `EON_WINDOW_RUNTIME_DIR` to `root`, or removes it for the default namespace
    (product `eon` only).
  - `window_inventory` is deleted. `generations_command/_human/_json` stay for
    `eonbase generations` (D8).
  - New: `GenerationRecord::{current, label, compatible}`, `window_json`,
    `window_cells` and `local_minute`.
- `windows.rs`:
  - New: `DEFAULT_WINDOW`, `Window`, `Listed`, `running_windows`, `short_ids`,
    `window_id_argument`, `Match`/`match_id` and `select_window`.
  - Rewritten: `attach_window`, `stop_window` (in process) and `list_windows`
    (the table and `{"windows":[...]}`).
  - `run_in_window` is deleted. `stop_namespaces`'s human branch re-execs
    `stop all` for every namespace, so `window stop all` behaves as at base.
  - Three unit tests, as planned.
- `cli.rs`:
  - New arms: `window ls [--json]`, `window attach` with no ID, and the new
    `stop_window` signature.
  - Removed: both `windows` arms.
  - `generations` is gated to `eonbase`. `attach` passes
    `&runtime_directory(product)`.
  - The Commands popup has "List windows" → `window ls`; "List generations" is
    gone.
  - Help: the S1 Windows rows, the `generations` row removed, the example
    changed to `eon window ls --json`, and the two "Window IDs" note lines.
- `cli/parity.rs`: `InspectRuntime`/`InspectPresentation` →
  `Lifecycle("window ls")`.
- `running.rs`: the D10 hint.
- Docs: CONTRACTS (EON-C10, C11, C23 [S1] items and their Status notes),
  USAGE, README, the bug-report template, SKILL.md and CHANGELOG.

## Deviations from the plan

1. **`window_id_argument` takes `&OsStr`**, not `&str`. It returns the
   validated `&str`, so a non-UTF-8 argument becomes the "invalid Eon window
   ID" usage error in one place, as the plan specifies.
2. **Corrupt default-namespace entries stay in matching and are refused**
   (round 1; the round-0 version filtered them out, which let a prefix fall
   through to another window, Codex finding 1). `select_window` matches over
   the whole listing. A match that lands on a damaged entry, or on an ID that a
   damaged entry shares, fails with `unknown-window` (exit 3): "ID selects
   NAME, a damaged Eon generation directory that is not a window". No target
   is built and no Stop is sent. An ambiguity that includes a damaged entry is
   the usual `ambiguous-window-id`. `stop_window`'s `&generation[3..]`
   therefore only ever sees valid generations. `unknown-window` was chosen over
   a new code: a damaged entry is not a selectable window (plan), and EON-C23
   gives `unknown-window` to an ID that selects none.
3. **The human table escapes the ID cell** (`escape_debug`), in the rows and
   in the `cannot stop:` lines. A damaged directory keeps its raw name as its
   ID, so this stops it from driving the terminal. It has no effect on valid
   IDs. `generations_human` escaped IDs the same way.
4. **`window stop UNKNOWN --json` now prints a JSON failure on stdout.** Before,
   `selected_window` raised a usage/missing `Error` and printed to stderr. This
   follows the plan ("A selection `Failure` returns
   `Ok(report_failure(&f, json)?)`"). The existing test
   `…unknown window is missing…` asserted empty stdout for
   `window stop 0000abcd --json`. It now checks the human form for empty
   stdout and the JSON form for `error.code == "unknown-window"`. Exit 3 is
   unchanged.
5. **Migrated `"sessions":[…]` substring checks go through serde**
   (`listed["windows"][0]["terminals"] == [...]`), not
   `"terminals":[…]` substrings. Window JSON nests `busy.terminals`, so a
   substring could match the wrong key. A multi-terminal check tests
   membership, not order, as the base substring check did: the first full run
   failed `a_pick_commits_…` on order `["session-2","session-1"]`.
   `eonbase_reopens_without_workspace_or_a_second_session` keeps
   `generations --json`, because it runs `eonbase` (D8). The first full run
   failed after I migrated it by mistake.
6. **`window_attach_runs_the_build_that_started_its_generation`**: the human
   `executable` line has no equivalent in the table. Per the plan, the JSON
   `executable` assertion carries it, and I added `compatible == false` for
   the recorded window. The human check is now: the `0000abcd` row ends with
   `no (other EONW)`, and neither `0000dcba` nor the generation ID appears in
   the text.
7. **CHANGELOG** adds one sentence beyond the plan's text: the new
   quick-search hint, and that Commands drops "List generations". Both are
   user-visible S1 changes (rule 10).
8. **Contract Status notes put the bead ID in backticks**
   (`` `eon-7cf0y.22` (S1) ``), matching the existing amendment notes. EON-C23's
   Status was the bare word `Proven`; it now reads `Proven. Amended on …`.
9. **USAGE "Window IDs" paragraph**: written in user words. It explains an
   older build's default-namespace window as "one that another Eon build
   opened that way, such as the old build's window after an upgrade".

10. **`window stop ID --json` closes its array when listing fails.** If
    `stop_generations` fails before it writes its own array (for example an
    unsafe namespace directory), the command prints
    `[{"window":ID,"results":[{"error":{"code":"stop-failed",…}}]}]` and exits
    1. It does not leave a half-written object on stdout. This follows
    `stop_namespaces`, which already reports `stop-failed` inside `results`.
11. **In-process attach is environment-independent.** `present_at` only sends
    `Present` to the selected supervisor, and that supervisor starts Venus
    with its own environment. Running `window attach ID` in process instead of
    re-exec'ing with `EON_WINDOW_RUNTIME_DIR` therefore changes no Present.
    The delegated exec sets that variable explicitly (see `attach_generation`).

12. **Rebased** (round 1) from `7b59e45` onto edge `605cca5` (acd858a
    notification slice 1, 6a42d65 README, 605cca5 records). I committed the
    staged S1 as a temporary detached WIP commit, ran `git rebase 605cca5`,
    resolved the one conflict (CHANGELOG.md Unreleased: kept both bullets,
    S1's first), then ran `git reset --soft 605cca5`. HEAD is `605cca5` with
    S1 staged; no branch was created and no stash was used.
13. **`ambiguous-window-id` is built as a `Failure` directly** (round 1,
    Codex 2), as `quit`'s inventory is, so EONW's 1,024-byte detail limit never
    drops a candidate or the "type more of the ID" advice. It is a pure helper,
    `ambiguous_window`, with a unit test over 1,024 bytes.
14. **Help note** (round 1, Opus 4): "window attach and window stop take
    default, an independent window's ID, or a unique prefix of 4+ characters,
    as eon window ls shows them." It sits above the `Workspace flags` line,
    because `--window` takes only exact IDs until S3.
15. **bug_report.yml**: the field label is "Window" (round 1, Codex 4). The
    form field `id: generation` is kept, because the label is all the finding
    covers and the id keys existing issue-form data.

16. **One guard, ahead of every exact path** (round 2, Codex re-check 1).
    `select_window` first reads the default namespace's damaged entry names
    (`generation::damaged_generations`: the generation-directory entries that
    are not valid generations; a read, with no supervisor probe). An argument
    equal to one is refused before the `default` and exact-8-hex early
    returns, so an exact ID shared with a damaged entry never reaches a
    window. A prefix match still checks the listing's damaged entries, as in
    round 1. The refusal is `unknown-window` (exit 3, helper
    `damaged_window`). One path deliberately skips the guard: `eon window
    attach` without an ID names no ID, so it means `default` and a damaged
    directory cannot be what it names.
17. **A damaged entry's `short_id` is its whole raw name** (round 2, Codex
    re-check 2; PLAN.md "keeps its raw name as `id` and `short_id`"). Other
    IDs' short forms are still computed against it. Text output escapes it
    (`escape_debug`).
18. **Rebased again** (round 2) from `605cca5` onto edge `03f72d3`
    (`eon-6bfqs`, test-only), the same way as item 12. There was no conflict.
    HEAD is `03f72d3` with S1 staged.

## Rule 6 (configurability)

D12: nothing becomes configurable. The 4-character minimum, the 24-character
NAME cut and the column set are approved output shape (EON-C23), not
preferences.

## Untested claims

- `local_minute` returns `-` when `localtime_r` or `strftime` fails. No test
  forces that failure.
- A NAME longer than 24 characters is cut with `…`. No test produces one.

# eon-7cf0y.22 S2 — implementation notes

Base: edge `78e14de` (S1 = `2b776c5`). Plan: `00-plan.md`. Contract text:
`01-contract-step.md` [S2] items, applied as written.

## What changed

- `generation.rs`
  - `Ask<'a>` names its target: `Stop` (generation wording, kept for
    `eon stop GENERATION|previous|all` until S3 and for eonbase, D8),
    `StopWindow(ID)`, and `Quit { caller, this_window, window: ID }`.
    `Ask::subject` gives `generation G` or `window ID`; the Stop question,
    decline, `not-confirmed` detail, `stopped …:` result, delegated question
    and the `stop-unavailable`/`stop-failed` details use it.
  - `quit_question` falls back to the window ID, not the generation, when the
    window has no name. `GenerationRecord::name` is `pub(super)` (quit listing).
- `windows.rs`
  - `window_listing` lists every running window and, in its place, each
    independent window whose generations cannot be inspected
    (`Uninspectable`); `running_windows` keeps S1 behaviour (first such error
    fails). `default_namespace_id` is the one ID rule for the default namespace.
  - `stop_windows(previous, json, quit)` replaces `quit_all`,
    `stop_namespaces`, `stop_window_json`, `ordered_namespaces`, `namespaces`,
    `candidates` and `namespace_command` (no re-exec). One window = a run of
    listed entries with the same ID and root; each generation gets its own
    validated `stop_generation`. Uninspectable windows report `stop-failed` in
    their `results`. Damaged entries (`damaged_entry`: a record whose ID is not
    a valid generation) are never sent a Stop: `stop-unavailable`, raw name
    `escape_debug`ged in the detail, JSON `window` = full raw name.
  - Order: listing order, stably sorted so the caller's own window is last.
    The caller's window is `runtime_directory("eon")` when `EON_TERMINAL` is
    set, else the default namespace (base `quit --all` rule); in the default
    namespace only `default` counts as the caller's.
  - `quit`: lists `running_windows`; rows are
    `window SHORT name=NAME state=S terminals=N; eon window stop SHORT` (or
    `cannot stop: REASON`); a lone damaged entry is refused, not stopped; in
    Eon it names the window by its full ID.
  - `stop_window` (S1): human mode names the window by its listed short ID
    (one extra listing; JSON uses the full ID).
- `cli.rs`: `window stop previous|all [--json]` → `stop_windows`, `quit --all`
  → `stop_windows(.., quit)`. Commands: "Stop old-version windows" →
  `window stop previous`; label column 24 → 26. Help: `quit [--all] [--json]`
  and `window stop ID|previous|all [--json]` rows (D9 wording).
- `notification.rs`: `eon window stop default|ID`.
- `supervisor.rs`: ``Run `eon window attach default|ID` to reconnect.``
- Docs: CONTRACTS (EON-C8, C10, C11, C23 [S2] items + Status notes), USAGE,
  SKILL.md (window stop previous|all), CHANGELOG.

## Deviations and decisions

1. **Caller-last rule.** Base had two rules: `window stop all` put the
   `EON_WINDOW_RUNTIME_DIR` namespace last; `quit --all` put the default
   namespace last unless `EON_TERMINAL` was set. The contract makes them one
   ("outside Eon `default` counts as the caller's"), so the `quit --all` rule
   (outside Eon = no `EON_TERMINAL`) now governs both. The `window stop all`
   test ran without `EON_TERMINAL`; it now expects `default` last.
2. **Within the default namespace only `default` is the caller's.** Another
   build's default-namespace window keeps listing order. The recorded-`eon`
   test's `quit --all --json` order changed accordingly
   (`[00000…15, 0000abcd]`).
3. **Ended windows are absent from the JSON array.** Base re-exec'd every
   namespace and printed `{"window":ID,"results":[]}` for ended ones; the
   contract says "one object per window it attempted", and only running
   windows are attempted. Tests updated.
4. **Human headers removed** ("Stop Eon window ID:", "Quit the default Eon
   window:"): every question, decline and result now names its window.
5. **Several generations in one independent window**: one question per
   generation (each is its own validated Stop), all naming the same window ID.
6. **Commands label column 24 → 26**: "Stop old-version windows" is exactly 24
   characters and would touch `eon`. Presentation only; the runner test now
   asserts the gap.
7. **`window stop ID` human label lookup** re-lists windows once to show the
   short ID; on any listing error it falls back to the full ID.
8. **Running-windows hint fallback unchanged** (`window_label` still falls
   back to the generation for an unnamed entry with no window ID). Live
   windows always carry a name, and the hint is not in S2's list.
9. **`quit_outside_eon_…` now opens 14 extra windows** (was 8): short IDs make
   rows shorter, and the test must still pass the 1,024-byte detail limit.
10. **USAGE "Stop terminals" block** shows `eon window stop ID|previous|all`;
    the `eon stop …` table rows stay until S3. README unchanged (S3).

## Rule 6

No new configurable value (D12): wording, the popup label and its column width
are approved output and presentation.

## Review round 1 (INBOX 2026-11-06)

Reviews: `codex-review.md` (DO NOT LAND), `opus-review.md` (LAND WITH FIXES).

1. **Caller last by generation (Codex 1 = Opus 4).** `own_window` resolves
   the calling terminal with `resolve_workspace(.., caller)` in the caller's
   namespace: the generation whose supervisor validates `EON_TERMINAL` is the
   caller's window, whatever build started it. Outside Eon it is `default`.
   If resolution fails (e.g. a damaged entry in that namespace makes
   `resolve_workspace` refuse), it falls back to the round-0 namespace rule
   (in the default namespace only `default`). Order is only an ordering; no
   Stop depends on it. Supersedes notes 1–2.
2. **Inspection failure continues (Codex 2 = Opus 5).** `window_listing`
   turns an uninspectable default namespace into an `Uninspectable` named
   `default`, and `window_entries` checks each `w/` entry on its own (unsafe
   or invalid entries become per-entry `Uninspectable`s, named by their entry
   name, with `cannot inspect Eon window ID: …`). `existing_windows` (used by
   `window ls`, selection and `window_root`) stays all-or-nothing on top of
   it. A wholly unsafe `w/` directory or unsafe runtime root still aborts the
   command (unchanged: nothing in it can be identified). Short IDs are
   computed over every entry, inspectable or not.
3. **Stable window name (Opus 3).** `durable_window_id`: an independent
   window's ID, else `generation[3..11]`; used by the notice's stop command
   (detach and failed-Stop notices) and the Venus-exit log line.
   `select_window`/`match_id` give the listed `default` window an alias, its
   generation's 32 hex digits, matched by prefix; an alias never wins as an
   exact ID (an argument equal to an independent window's ID that also begins
   the alias is `ambiguous-window-id`), and the exact-8-hex fast path is
   skipped when the argument begins this build's generation hex. `short_ids`
   never yields a prefix of that hex. "Open Eon to return." in the default
   namespace is unchanged: it is not a command and not in item 3's list
   (overseer may want it to say `eon window attach HEX` too).
4. **Full escaped names (Codex 3).** `cli_failure` builds CLI-only
   `Failure`s without EONW's 1,024-byte detail cap; `ambiguous_window`,
   `damaged_entry` and `stop_windows`' uninspectable result use it.
5. **No-Stop sentinels (Codex 4).** `untouchable_endpoint` counts every
   connection (stronger than counting Stops) at: the damaged entry, an
   unsafe base `generations/`, a `w/` symlink to an outside-root live
   endpoint, and a `w/ID/generations` at 0o755.
6. **Stale target (Codex 5 = Opus 7)**: `"{subject} was not found"`.
7. **Opus 2** is covered by the uninspectable test (stop-failed for each
   refused namespace, stopped for the live one, exit 1).
8. **Docs**: USAGE popup paragraph ("stopping old-version windows", plus the
   note that from an older window it also stops newer builds' windows),
   `previous` vs `all`/`quit --all` coverage, reflowed lines, Window IDs alias
   sentence; CHANGELOG.
9. **Nits**: `quit` in Eon shortens its own ID with `short_ids(&[id], alias)`
   (no listing, Opus 8); `select_window` returns the shown ID, removing the
   second listing in `stop_window` (Opus 11); `Bulk { Previous, All, Quit }`
   replaces the bools (Opus 12).

Declined / unchanged:

- **Opus 6** (questions per generation where the contract says per window):
  kept. Each generation is its own validated Stop with its own terminals, and
  every question names the same window ID; an independent window runs two
  generations only briefly during an upgrade. Accepted reading of EON-C23.
- **Opus 10** (human `window stop previous` prints nothing when nothing
  matches): unchanged; base `eon stop previous` behaves the same and exits 0.

## Review round 2 (INBOX 2026-11-06, Codex re-check of `f6906de`)

1. **No exact shortcut (blocker).** `select_window` matches every argument
   other than `default` against every running window (`running_windows`):
   `match_id` selects only when exactly one distinct window's ID (or
   `default`'s generation alias) starts with it; a whole ID that also starts
   another window's ID is `ambiguous-window-id`. The exact-8-hex shortcut is
   gone; an independent window that is not running is still selected by its
   whole ID only after the listing finds no match (`Match::None`). Since
   other default-namespace windows' IDs are their full generation hex, the
   alias is needed only for `default`. Consequence: when listing fails (an
   uninspectable namespace), `window stop|attach ID` fails too instead of
   taking the shortcut; it cannot rule out a collision. Known limit: an
   independent window whose ID equals the first 8 digits of a running
   default-namespace generation (2^-32) can only be selected by
   `window stop all`/`quit` from inside it; its short ID is its whole ID.
2. **Caller identification (blocker).** `generation::caller_generation`
   searches the caller's namespace for the one supervisor that validates
   `EON_TERMINAL`, probing each valid generation (identity check, then the
   caller Inspect) and skipping entries that name no generation (the bulk
   command reports those itself). `own_window` refuses the bulk command with
   `unknown-caller` (exit 3, no Stop) when none or several validate it, or
   `EON_TERMINAL` is invalid; the round-1 namespace fallback is gone.
   `resolve_workspace` is unchanged for other commands.
3. **Shown IDs (should-fix).** `select_window` always returns the listing's
   short ID (also for a typed whole ID); `quit` in Eon looks its window up in
   `window_listing` and falls back to the full ID only if the listing fails.
   Notices print the durable ID (EON-C8: full independent ID, 8-digit
   generation hex), not a short ID, by contract: a short ID can become
   ambiguous later.

# eon-7cf0y.22 S2 — plan

Base: edge `78e14de` (S1 landed as `2b776c5`; EONW v34, Eon 0.1.18). Sources:
`eon-7cf0y-22-plan-work/PLAN.md` (S1 design, slice table),
`eon-7cf0y-22-plan-work/bead/01-contract-step.md` ([S2] items applied as
written), bead comments (decisions 1–3 as revised by the overseer; S1 notes,
proof and ledger). No EONW change, no package version bump.

## Scope (S2 only)

- `eon window stop previous|all [--json]` over every running window, default
  included; `eon quit --all [--json]` over the same windows with the same JSON.
- Window language (window ID as `eon window ls` shows it, never a generation)
  in Stop and Quit questions, declines and results of the window commands, in
  `eon quit`'s ambiguous listing and in the close notice; `eon window stop
  default` in the notice; the Venus-exit log line.
- Commands popup "Stop old-version windows" → `eon window stop previous`.
- Not S2: removing `eon attach|stop GENERATION|previous|all`, `--generation`,
  `--window` prefixes, delegation (S3); `config path|dir`, `-V` (S4). The
  legacy `eon stop …` forms and all of `eonbase` keep their generation wording
  (they are generation commands; S3 removes eon's, D8 keeps eonbase's).

## Behaviour per command

Window ID display (`short_id`) is the S1 rule, computed over one
`running_windows` listing. `--json` output always names the full ID.

| Command | Selects | Human | JSON |
|---|---|---|---|
| `window stop ID` | S1 selection, unchanged | asks `Stop window SHORT and N live terminal(s) [..]? [y/N]` per generation; decline `cancelled; no Stop sent for window SHORT`; result `stopped window SHORT: session-…` | `[{"window":ID,"results":[…]}]` (S1) |
| `window stop previous` | every listed window whose generation another build started (`!current`), any namespace | as above, per window, caller's own last | one `{"window":ID,"results":[…]}` per window attempted, `[]` when none |
| `window stop all` | every listed window | as above | as above |
| `quit --all` | as `window stop all` | `eon quit`'s busy-only question, always `Quit window NAME?` (name, else SHORT); results `stopped window SHORT: …` | identical to `window stop all --json` |
| `quit` (outside Eon, several) | unchanged | listing rows `window SHORT name=NAME state=S terminals=N; eon window stop SHORT` or `; cannot stop: REASON` | `ambiguous-window` failure with the same detail |
| `quit` (one / inside Eon) | unchanged | question unchanged except `window ID` instead of generation; result `stopped window ID: …` | unchanged Stop result |

- **Order** (D7): the listing's order, stably sorted so that the caller's own
  window goes last: windows in the caller's namespace
  (`runtime_directory("eon")`, the default namespace outside Eon, as base's
  `ordered_namespaces`) after the others, and within the default namespace
  `default` last.
- **Grouping:** one window = the consecutive listing entries with the same ID
  and root (an independent window can run several generations); each of its
  generations gets its own validated Stop and question, as base Stop does.
- **Namespace that cannot be inspected:** it does not abort the others. It is
  reported as its window ID with a `stop-failed` result
  (`cannot inspect Eon window ID: …`), as base `stop_namespaces` did.
- **Damaged entries** (a generation-directory entry that names no valid
  generation, any namespace): never sent a Stop. Reported as their own
  window, `window` = the full raw name (JSON-escaped), with
  `{"error":{"code":"stop-unavailable","detail":"RAW is a damaged Eon generation directory, not a window"}}`,
  human `error stop-unavailable: …` with the raw name `escape_debug`ged, exit 1.
  Included in `all`; included in `previous` (they are not this build's).
- **Status:** the highest status among the Stops; `not-confirmed` (1) per
  declined window without a terminal, later windows continue.
- **Delegated Stop question** (another EONW build): `Stop window SHORT? It runs
  another Eon build, so its terminals are unknown. [y/N]`, or `Quit window
  SHORT? …` / `Quit this window? …`.
- **Failure details** inside the window commands say `window SHORT` where they
  said `generation G` (stop-unavailable, stop-failed wrappers).
- **Close notice** (EON-C8): without actions the body ends ``Run `eon window
  stop ID` to stop it.``, ID `default` in the default namespace, the full ID in
  an independent one; the failure text likewise.
- **Venus-exit log line:** ``Eon Desktop exited; terminals remain active. Run
  `eon window attach ID` to reconnect.`` (ID as in the notice). eonbase's line
  is unchanged.
- **Commands popup:** "Stop older generations" (`stop previous`) becomes
  "Stop old-version windows" (`window stop previous`), Keep. The label column
  widens from 24 to 26 so the 24-character label keeps a gap before `eon`.
- **Help:** Windows rows become D9's `quit [--all] [--json]` and
  `window stop ID|previous|all [--json]` rows (the other rows stay; S3 does
  the rest).

## Code

- `generation.rs`
  - `Ask` gains a window name: `Ask::Stop` (generation wording, legacy `eon
    stop` and eonbase), `Ask::StopWindow(&str)`, and `Ask::Quit { caller,
    this_window, window: &str }`; `Ask::subject(generation)` gives
    `generation G` / `window ID`.
  - `stop_generation`, `delegated_stop`, `delegated_question`,
    `quit_question`, `report_stopped`, `stop_generations` use the subject.
  - `GenerationRecord` keeps every field.
- `windows.rs`
  - `window_id(root, generation, current)`: full window ID of a generation.
  - Listing split: `window_listing(inputs) -> (Vec<Listed>, Vec<(id, error)>)`;
    `running_windows` keeps S1 behaviour (first namespace error fails).
  - `stop_windows(inputs, which: Previous|All, json, quit: Option<caller>)`
    replaces `stop_namespaces`, `stop_window_json`, `ordered_namespaces`,
    `namespaces`, `candidates` and `quit_all`'s loop; no re-exec.
  - `stop_window` (S1) names the window via `StopWindow(SHORT)` in human mode.
  - `quit`: listing over `running_windows`; new row format; single-window
    and in-Eon paths pass the window ID.
- `cli.rs`: arms for `window stop previous [--json]` and `window stop all
  [--json]` → `stop_windows`; `quit --all` → `stop_windows`; popup entry and
  width; help rows.
- `notification.rs`: `stop_command` → `eon window stop default` / ID.
- `supervisor.rs`: Venus-exit log line.

## Tests

Unit (runtime): update `quit_asks_only_while_busy_in_window_language`,
`delegated_question_names_another_build`, the notice tests and the command
runner test as wording changes.

Integration (`workspace_control.rs`), migrate and extend:
1. Existing `window stop all` test (~9073): now covers the default window too;
   prompts `Stop window …`, caller last, JSON per window with `default`.
2. Existing `quit --all` tests (~8143, 8197, 8220, 8252, 8569, 9979, 10008):
   per-window JSON with `"window":"default"` instead of null; prompts and
   results in window language; headers gone.
3. Quit listing test (~7940): new row format, `eon window stop SHORT`.
4. Delegated question/result tests (~9964): window wording.
5. **New** `window_stop_previous_stops_only_other_builds_windows_and_refuses_damaged_entries`:
   default-namespace previous supervisors `a`, `b`, an independent window
   `w/abcd3000` with another build's generation, plus a damaged
   `generations/abcd` entry. `window stop previous --json`: one object per
   window in order (a, b, abcd3000, damaged raw name), the damaged one a
   `stop-unavailable` error, exit 1; every previous server got exactly its
   Stop; a damaged entry got none (its directory remains, nothing else
   stopped). Human `window stop previous` with piped `n`/no answers: each
   window asked by its short ID, `not-confirmed`, no Stop sent (servers still
   answer).
6. `window stop all` with the default window running stops it (in 1).

## Docs

- CONTRACTS: every [S2] item of `01-contract-step.md` (EON-C23 Result block,
  EON-C11 Trigger, older-generations bullet, new `window stop previous|all`
  bullet, `eon quit` bullet edits; EON-C8 notice; EON-C10 popup), Status notes
  `Amended on 2026-11-06 (approved by Lucca, relayed by eon-overseer) by
  `eon-7cf0y.22` (S2): window stop previous and all, window language.`
- USAGE: command table rows for `window stop ID|previous|all` and `quit
  --all`; the "Stop" paragraphs at ~117–143 and ~596–605; popup list.
- SKILL.md: window stop previous|all if it names `stop previous`.
- CHANGELOG Unreleased: one bullet (rule 10).

## Proof

fmt, clippy (eon-runtime, eon), `eon-test -p eon-runtime`, `eon-test -p eon
--test workspace_control` (window/quit first), full `eon-test`, the three Nix
checks + `.#default --out-link`, one isolated installed observation (default
+ one independent window: `window ls`, `window stop all` at a TTY, prompts in
window language, popup list text), all on the exact staged tree.

## Rule 6

No new configurable value: wording and the popup label are approved output
(D12); the popup label column width is presentation derived from the longest
label.

> … the exact ID or any prefix of at least 4 characters selects a window. An
> exact ID wins. Otherwise the prefix must begin the ID of exactly one running
> window. A prefix that begins several fails with `ambiguous-window-id` (exit
> 3) and names each match. One that begins none fails with `unknown-window`
> (exit 3).

New:

> … the exact ID or any prefix of at least 4 characters selects a window. It
> must begin the ID of exactly one running window: an independent window's ID
> and the hex digits of default-namespace generations share one space, so a
> whole ID that also begins another window's ID selects neither. One that
> begins several fails with `ambiguous-window-id` (exit 3) and names each
> match. One that begins none fails with `unknown-window` (exit 3).

Old: "That form never wins as an exact ID: an argument that begins both those
digits and another window's ID fails with `ambiguous-window-id`."
New: "An argument that begins both those digits and another window's ID fails
with `ambiguous-window-id`."

Old: "`default` and an independent window's exact ID select that window even
when it is not running: attaching it then exits 4, and stopping it stops
nothing."
New: "`default`, and an independent window's exact ID that no running window
answers to, select that window even when it is not running: attaching it then
exits 4, and stopping it stops nothing. Questions and results name the
selected window as `eon window ls` shows it, even when the whole ID was
typed."

## EON-C23 bulk Stop

Old: "Both stop the caller's own window last, and outside Eon `default`
counts as the caller's."
New: "Both stop the caller's own window last: the window whose supervisor
validates the calling terminal, whichever build started it. Outside Eon
`default` counts as the caller's. Inside Eon, when no single supervisor
validates the calling terminal, they refuse with `unknown-caller` (exit 3)
and send no Stop."

(EON-C11's `eon quit --all` follows `eon window stop all`'s order and so the
same rule; its text is unchanged.)

## Non-contract text

USAGE Window IDs paragraph ("which must start exactly one running window's
ID. One that starts several, even when it is one window's whole ID, exits 3")
and bulk-stop paragraph (`unknown-caller`); CHANGELOG bullet.

# eon-7cf0y.22 S3 — plan

Base: edge `987a0f6` (S1 `2b776c5`, S2 `99d7319`; EONW v34, Eon 0.1.18).
Sources: `eon-7cf0y-22-plan-work/PLAN.md` (S1 design, slice table),
`eon-7cf0y-22-plan-work/bead/01-contract-step.md` ([S3] items, adjusted for
decision 2), `br comments eon-7cf0y.22` (decisions 1–3 as revised, S1/S2
notes and review rounds), the overseer's S3 brief (decision 2 binding text).

## Scope (S3 only)

- Remove from `eon`: `attach`, `attach GENERATION`, `stop GENERATION
  [--json]`, `stop previous|all [--json]`, and the `--generation` workspace
  flag. All become invalid commands (exit 2), with no marker-gated form left.
  `eonbase attach [GENERATION]`, `eonbase generations [--json]` and
  `eonbase stop GENERATION [--json]` are unchanged (D8).
- `--window ID` takes every EON-C23 window ID and prefix, with S1/S2's
  selection (`select_window`).
- Cross-build delegation picks its argv by the recorded build's EONW
  (decision 2), and EONW goes from v34 to v35 so builds can be told apart.
- Stop advice prints the same command the delegator would run, marker
  included.
- Migrate the integration-test call sites, final help, README, USAGE, SKILL,
  CONTRACTS [S3] items, mac-proof harness, CHANGELOG.
- Not S3: `config path|dir`, `-V|--version` (S4).

## EONW v35: version-only bump

S3 needs **no codec change**. Decision 2 requires the bump as a marker only:
a v35 delegator knows that a v34-or-older build takes `stop GENERATION` /
`attach GENERATION`, and that v35 or newer takes `window stop ID` /
`window attach ID`. Mechanics (memory `eonw-codec-change-needs-bump`):

- `runtime/crates/eon-workspace-protocol/src/v34.rs` → `v35.rs`, `v34/` →
  `v35/` (`git mv`), `lib.rs` `pub mod v35;`, `VERSION: u16 = 35`.
- Hex goldens: the version byte `454f4e5722` → `454f4e5723` (32 in `v35.rs`,
  13 in `v35/subscription.rs`); any other literal-34 golden found by grep.
- Every importer `eon_workspace_protocol::v34` → `v35` (runtime, `eon`,
  Venus: import paths only, nothing else in Venus).
- `components/eon-v5.json`: `required_interfaces` EONW 35 and the three
  EONW interface entries `version: 35`, `proof` = the subtree hash
  `git rev-parse <staged tree>:runtime/crates/eon-workspace-protocol`.
- Eon 0.1.18 → 0.1.19 (`eon/crates/eon/Cargo.toml`, `Cargo.lock`).
- Docs that name the current EONW (ARCHITECTURE, CONTRACTS "Consumes"
  lines that say "current EONW v34", runtime/README, venus PRESENTATION and
  CRATES, venus/CHANGELOG one line: "Consume EONW v35, which changes only
  the version"). Proof/evidence records keep their text.
- CHANGELOG: windows started before this release keep running, but their
  terminals' `eon` (the profile's) cannot control them until they restart.

## Behaviour per command

| Command | After S3 |
|---|---|
| `eon attach`, `eon attach X` | exit 2, `invalid command or arguments` + usage; nothing presented |
| `eon stop X [--json]`, `eon stop previous\|all [--json]`, `eon stop --json X` | exit 2; no Stop sent; also with `EON_STOP_DELEGATED=X` set |
| `eon … --generation G …` (first word or inside a workspace command) | exit 2 |
| `eon … --window ID …` | ID syntax as `window_id_argument` (exit 2); selection as `select_window` (unknown/ambiguous exit 3, never a pick); see `--window` below |
| `eon window attach [ID]` | S1, plus the attach marker scope below |
| `eon window stop ID [--json]` | S1/S2, plus the stop marker scope below |
| `eonbase attach/generations/stop` | unchanged |

### `--window` (EON-C10 [S3] text)

`parse_workspace_target_arguments` keeps only `--window`; its value goes
through `windows::window_id_argument` (usage error, exit 2). `--generation`
is no longer a target flag: it stays an operand, and the control parser
rejects it (exit 2). It also leaves `control_command`'s first-word list, so
`eon --generation G …` is an invalid command.

`WorkspaceTarget` loses `generation`. `resolve_workspace`, when
`target.window` is set, calls `select_window(inputs, id)` (any `Failure`
returned as is: `unknown-window`, `ambiguous-window-id`,
`supervisor-unavailable`) and maps:

- `Window::Default` → default namespace, exact generation = this build's
  current. Not present → `missing-supervisor`: `the default Eon window is not
  running; run \`eon\` to open it` (as `window attach`).
- `Window::Other(g)` → default namespace, exact generation `g`. Not present
  (it ended after the listing) → `unknown-window`: `Eon window SHOWN was not
  found`.
- `Window::Independent { root, .. }` → that namespace, window-only rule
  (current, else the sole live generation), as today. Several live, none
  this build's: `ambiguous-window` with `Eon window ID runs generations of N
  Eon builds and none is this build's; run the command from a terminal of
  the one to target` (no `--generation`, no generation IDs).

The exact-generation path is today's `--generation` path (probe, then caller
validation when `EON_TERMINAL` is set). Results still name `generation` and
`window` (null for the default namespace).

### Delegation by EONW (decision 2)

One owner, `generation::delegation(eon, root, generation, protocol, kind)`
→ the `Command` words (env + argv), used by `delegated_stop`,
`attach_generation` and `stop_advice`:

- Environment, both forms: `EON_WINDOW_RUNTIME_DIR=ROOT` for an independent
  window, removed for the default namespace (as today); `EON_STOP_DELEGATED=G`
  (Stop) or `EON_ATTACH_DELEGATED=G` (attach); Stop also removes
  `EON_TERMINAL` and closes stdin (as today).
- `protocol` = the EONW version the generation's supervisor reports.
  `None` or `<= LAST_GENERATION_FORMS` (34): `stop G --json` /
  `attach G`, exactly today's argv. Otherwise: `window stop ID --json` /
  `window attach ID`, ID = `default` in the default namespace, else the
  independent window's ID.
- `const LAST_GENERATION_FORMS: u16 = 34` carries a comment that it goes with
  eon-7cf0y.17 (version-independent Stop).

The reported version: `EndpointFailure` gains `protocol: Option<u16>`, set by
`protocol_endpoint_failure` (`UnsupportedVersion { version }`) and
`validated_runtime` (`runtime.workspace_protocol`); `failed_generation`
copies it into `GenerationRecord::workspace_protocol`. A live record with a
launcher (same EONW, other component graph) already has it. Side effect:
`window ls --json` now shows `workspace_protocol` for an `incompatible`
window when its supervisor reported one (was null). That is the documented
field's meaning ("a value that is not known is null"); recorded as a
deviation.

`delegated_result` accepts, for the new form, `[{"window":ID,"results":[R]}]`
with exactly one window and one result `R` (a `stopped` for G with success,
or an `error` with an exit code), or a top-level `{"error":…}` (selection or
syntax failure); anything else is "no complete Stop result", as today. The
old form parses as today.

### Marker scope in the new build (needed for exactness)

`window stop ID` on an independent window stops every generation of its
namespace, so a delegated Stop through it would stop more than G, and two
builds sharing one window would delegate to each other without end. So:

- `window stop ID [--json]` run with `EON_STOP_DELEGATED` set: the value must
  be a valid generation (else exit 2, nothing sent). The selected window's
  namespace is used with `Select::Generation(G)`, so only G is stopped, and
  `stop_generation`'s existing guard keeps G from delegating again.
- `window attach [ID]` run with `EON_ATTACH_DELEGATED` set: likewise
  validated, and the selected window's namespace presents generation G (not
  `window_generation`'s pick); `attach_generation`'s existing guard keeps it
  from delegating again.

This is the public command plus the existing loop-guard marker, not a
second form: without a marker nothing changes, and `stop G` stays invalid
with the marker set. EON-C11 states it (below). **Overseer: this is the one
reading of decision 2 that I add; redirect through INBOX if you want
another (e.g. refusing delegated Stop into a multi-generation independent
window instead).**

Direction cost, stated in CHANGELOG/USAGE: a v34 build runs `stop G --json`
against a v35 window's `eon`, which refuses it (exit 2), so v34 builds cannot
stop or reattach windows of v35 builds; a v35 `eon` stops and reattaches v34
windows through their recorded `eon`.

### Stop advice

`stop_advice` (printed when the recorded `eon` is missing or not
executable) prints `delegation(...)`'s words for the record's reported
EONW, e.g. `then run env -u EON_WINDOW_RUNTIME_DIR EON_STOP_DELEGATED=g1-…
/nix/store/…/eon stop g1-…` for a v34 build, or `… EON_STOP_DELEGATED=g1-…
…/eon window stop default` for a newer one, quoted as today (shared word,
else sh and Nushell variants). The `--json` is dropped from the advice
(human run asks first, as today's advice).

### Other text

- `window_generation`'s several-builds error names each one's `eon` path
  and Eon version, not generation IDs (D3).
- Help (D9): delete "Attach & stop"; Windows rows already final (S2). Notes:
  `Window IDs, as eon window ls shows them: default, another build's or an` /
  `independent window's ID, or any unique prefix of 4+ characters.` and
  `Workspace flag: --window ID, before any --.`, replacing the S1 note and
  `Workspace flags: --generation GENERATION / --window ID, before any --.`
  Keep `Explicit targets still validate EON_TERMINAL; …` and the
  `Results name …` line.
- `EON_USAGE` loses any `attach`/`stop` mention if it has one.
- `cli/parity.rs`: `Present` → `Lifecycle("window attach")`, `Stop` →
  `Lifecycle("window stop")`.

## Code (files)

- `runtime/crates/eon-workspace-protocol/src/{lib.rs,v35.rs,v35/subscription.rs}`: rename + VERSION + goldens.
- `runtime/crates/eon-runtime/src/control.rs`: `EndpointFailure.protocol`.
- `runtime/crates/eon-runtime/src/generation.rs`: `WorkspaceTarget` without
  `generation`; `resolve_workspace` over `select_window`; `delegation`,
  `LAST_GENERATION_FORMS`; `delegated_stop`, `delegated_result`,
  `attach_generation`, `stop_advice`, `failed_generation`,
  `window_generation` text; `Select::Previous` deleted (no user left);
  pub(super) marker readers `delegated_target(var)`.
- `runtime/crates/eon-runtime/src/windows.rs`: marker scope in
  `attach_window` / `stop_window`; `select_window` reused by
  `resolve_workspace` (already pub).
- `runtime/crates/eon-runtime/src/cli.rs`: `lifecycle_command` arms only for
  `eonbase`; `stop_argument` loses previous/all; `--generation` removed from
  `control_command` and `parse_workspace_target_arguments`; help; unit tests
  of target parsing.
- `runtime/crates/eon-runtime/src/cli/parity.rs`: two Lifecycle names.
- Every `v34` importer (runtime, `eon/crates/eon/src/product.rs`, tests,
  Venus).
- `components/eon-v5.json`, `eon/crates/eon/Cargo.toml`, `Cargo.lock`.
- `eon/tools/mac-proof/src/scenario.rs` (`attach` → `window attach`,
  `stop all` → `window stop all`, the stop scenario's `proves` text) and
  `final_check.rs` (the `eon stop all` hint → `eon window stop all`).

## Tests

Unit (runtime):
1. `delegation_follows_the_recorded_builds_eonw` (new, generation.rs):
   protocol `None`, `Some(11)`, `Some(34)` → `stop G --json` / `attach G`;
   `Some(35)`, `Some(36)` → `window stop default --json` /
   `window attach default` in the default namespace and `window stop ID
   --json` in `w/ID`; env words carry the marker and the namespace. Catches
   the wrong argv for either side of v34/v35.
2. `stop_advice_runs_as_printed_in_sh_and_nushell`: updated for the marker
   word (old and new form).
3. `delegated_result_accepts_one_stop_result_only`: new-form cases (one
   window/one result accepted; two results, two windows, wrong generation,
   killed → none).
4. `cli.rs` target-parsing tests: `--generation` cases become exit-2 cases;
   `--window` accepts `default`, `defa`, `abcd`, 32 hex; refuses `abc`,
   `ABCD`.

Integration (`workspace_control.rs`):
5. **Migrate** every `stop G|previous|all`, `attach [G]` and `--generation`
   call (about 60): default-namespace generation → `window stop default` /
   the 32-hex ID / `window stop previous|all`; output assertions follow the
   `[{"window",…,"results":[…]}]` shape and `window …` wording. Keep each
   test's intent; record any assertion that cannot carry over.
6. **Extend** `removed_window_listings_are_invalid_commands` (renamed
   `removed_commands_are_invalid`): `attach`, `attach G`, `stop G`, `stop G
   --json`, `stop previous`, `stop all --json`, `--generation G workspace`,
   `workspace --generation G`, each exit 2, empty stdout, `invalid command`
   or the usage text. With a `previous_supervisor` G running, `stop G
   --json` and `stop G --json` with `EON_STOP_DELEGATED=G` send no Stop (the
   server still answers an inspection afterwards, then is stopped by
   `window stop`).
7. **New** `delegated_window_stop_and_attach_reach_only_the_marked_generation`:
   `w/abcd3000` runs two `previous_supervisor`s A and B. `window stop
   abcd3000 --json` with `EON_STOP_DELEGATED=B` → one window, one result,
   stopped B; A still answers inspection, then stop it normally.
   `EON_STOP_DELEGATED=bad` → exit 2, A untouched.
8. **New** in `older_eonw_generations_stop_through_their_recorded_eon` (or a
   sibling): a supervisor that reports EONW `VERSION + 1` gets the new form;
   the recorded-`eon` log shows `window stop default --json|unset|unset|G`
   (default namespace) and `window stop 0000abcd --json|ROOT|unset|G`; its
   array output is reported as the Stop result. The existing v11 case keeps
   proving the old form.
9. **Migrate** the `--window` tests to prefixes, and add: `--window abcd`
   ambiguous → exit 3 `ambiguous-window-id`, nothing sent; `--window
   default` reaches the default window; `--window <4+ of another build's
   hex>` reaches that generation.
10. Help test: no `attach [GENERATION]`, no `stop GENERATION`, no
    `--generation`, contains the new notes; every line ≤ 80 columns.

## Docs

- `docs/CONTRACTS.md`: every [S3] item of `01-contract-step.md`, with
  decision 2 in place of the "Delegation entry":
  - EON-C23 Window IDs paragraph: "(`eon window attach`, `eon window stop`
    and `--window`)".
  - EON-C11: the Stop-of-older-build bullet says "runs that `eon` as
    Delegation (below) describes, in the generation's namespace"; the
    missing-launcher clause "prints the command that stops it once that
    build is restored: the Delegation form for that build's EONW, run with
    `EON_STOP_DELEGATED` set to GENERATION, in the generation's namespace";
    the launcher bullet "`eon window attach` runs it, as Delegation
    describes, when this build cannot present that window"; delete the
    "`eon stop previous` attempts…" bullet; add:
    > - **Delegation.** To stop or present a generation that another build
    >   started, `eon` runs that build's recorded `eon` in the generation's
    >   namespace (`EON_WINDOW_RUNTIME_DIR` set to an independent window's
    >   root, else unset), with `EON_STOP_DELEGATED` or
    >   `EON_ATTACH_DELEGATED` set to the generation. The form follows the
    >   EONW version that the generation's supervisor reports: a build of
    >   EONW 34 or older, or one whose version is unknown, runs as
    >   `stop GENERATION --json` or `attach GENERATION`; a newer one as
    >   `window stop ID --json` or `window attach ID`, ID being `default` in

    >   that generation of the selected window; run with
    >   `EON_ATTACH_DELEGATED` set, `eon window attach ID` presents only that
    >   generation. A value that names no generation is invalid (exit 2).
    >   So a delegated Stop or attach reaches only its generation and never
    >   delegates it again. `eon stop` and `eon attach` are invalid commands
    >   (exit 2), with or without these variables.

Records under `bead/`: `01-notes.md` (deviations), `02-proof.md` (every

No new value a person sees or feels (D12): removed commands, flag syntax
and the delegation form are contract surfaces, not preferences.

# S3 notes: deviations and decisions taken while implementing

Each item departs from, or adds to, `00-plan.md` or the [S3] text of
`eon-7cf0y-22-plan-work/bead/01-contract-step.md`.

1. **Marker scope (added reading of decision 2).** Decision 2 replaced the
   contract step's "Delegation entry" (old forms accepted while a marker is
   set) with delegation by EONW. It did not say how `window stop ID` names one
   generation of an independent window that holds several, or how two builds
   avoid delegating to each other without end. In this build, `window stop ID`
   run with `EON_STOP_DELEGATED=G` stops only G in the selected window, and
   `window attach ID` with `EON_ATTACH_DELEGATED=G` presents only G. A value
   that names no generation, the empty value included, is a usage error
   (exit 2). Announced in STATUS.md at PLAN WRITTEN; no INBOX redirect came.
   CONTRACTS EON-C11 **Delegation** states it.
2. **Exact `default` path.** `window stop default` and `window attach default`
   inspect this build's generation directly and never enumerate generation
   directories, so the overfilled-directory tests (more than 256 entries)
   still stop and attach the current window. `select_window` checks
   `generations/default` with one lstat for the damaged case instead of the
   bounded enumeration.
3. **`workspace_protocol` for incompatible windows.** `EndpointFailure` now
   carries the EONW version a supervisor reported (`UnsupportedVersion`, or a
   validated `runtime.workspace_protocol` that does not match). `eon window ls
   --json` therefore reports `workspace_protocol` for an incompatible window
   where it printed null before. The delegation form needs that value; the
   field's meaning is unchanged.
4. **Help notes wording.** The help notes now say "Window IDs, as eon window
   ls shows them: default, another build's or an independent window's ID, or
   any unique prefix of 4+ characters. Workspace flag: --window ID, before any
   --." in place of the generation and window ID note.
5. **No exact generation in multi-generation independent windows.**
   `--generation` was the only way to pick one generation of an independent
   window with several live generations and no live current one. Without it,
   such a window fails as ambiguous; the message now says to run the command
   from a terminal of the one to target, and names no generation ID.
6. **`window_generation` several-builds message.** It lists each build as
   "Eon VERSION (its eon: PATH)" or "(its eon is not recorded)", without
   generation IDs, in line with human output naming windows by ID.
7. **Not in S3 scope, left for the overseer.** Some workspace-control failure
   details (`resolve_workspace`'s unavailable and missing-supervisor paths for
   a non-default namespace) still name generations. They are not attach or
   stop advice, so S3 leaves them.
8. **Known cost (documented in USAGE and CHANGELOG).** An Eon 0.1.18 or older
   `eon` runs `stop G --json` or `attach G` against a v35 window; this build
   rejects both (exit 2), so an old build cannot stop or attach a window of
   this release. The newer build stops and attaches old windows.
9. **CONTRACTS text not present.** The [S3] items "CLI confirmation list" and
   the `eon tab close`/`eon pane close` "as `eon stop` does" bullet do not
   exist in the current EON-C10 text (S1/S2 or earlier work reworded them);
   only the workspace **Close.** item carried "as `eon stop` does", and it now
   says `eon window stop`.
10. **USAGE.** The paragraph describing `eon stop previous|all` (previous and
    all over generations, per-generation confirmation, batch note) is removed;
    the window-stop paragraph under Workspace already covers `previous`, `all`,
    order, `--json` and the batch note.
11. **Historical records kept.** Proof, Evidence and Amendment-proof records
    in CONTRACTS and venus/docs/CONTRACTS.md that name `eon attach` or
    `eon stop` describe what ran and stay as written, as the contract step's
    "Unchanged" list says. EONW references that describe the current boundary
    move to v35, as the v33 to v34 bump did; references to when a message
    entered the wire stay.
12. **mac-proof.** The stop scenario now runs `eon window stop all --json` and
    reads the nested `[{"window", "results"}]` shape, flattening every
    window's results before checking that each one is `stopped`.

## Round 1 changes (after review)

13. **Marker narrowed (supersedes item 1's reading).** A marker is accepted
    only when it equals this build's own generation, and only for a window
    that runs it (`default`, or an independent window holding that
    generation's directory). Anything else exits 2 and sends nothing. Both
    markers are stripped from every child Eon starts. Approved by eon-overseer
    in round 1, item 5 (ledger row 5).
14. **Unsafe default namespace.** `window stop default --json` inspects before
    it opens the result array.
15. **Demo recorder** migrated to `window stop all --json` and `window attach`.
16. **Rebased** onto edge 960e515; `CHANGELOG.md` kept both entries.

title: Update eonterm.com's text for v0.2.0: window commands, sessions, eon update and the Nix-free install
description:
## Why

docs/AGENT-RULES.md#website: site text follows every release that changes what a person can do or
see, in that release. v0.2.0 (eon-igae.9) changes these things eonterm.com describes:

1. The window command family (eon-7cf0y.22): `eon window ls|attach|stop`, `eon quit`; the site
   still names the removed `eon attach`, `eon stop GENERATION`, `eon generations` and
   `eon windows`:
   - src/content/docs/docs/cli.md (~16-38), start.md (~76-86), troubleshoot.md (~15, 19, 35).
   - The window-family text is drafted on eon-site branch site-cli-window-family (51bb0cb),
     unmerged (eon-7cf0y.21's 2026-11-08 comment).
2. Workspaces renamed to sessions (eon-30skm): CLI, IDs, JSON keys, configuration and product
   text.
3. `eon update` and the update button (eon-update-button-f10d1): checking and installing updates
   from the CLI, the Commands popup and the session menu.
4. The Nix-free install (eon-igae.15) as the first install line, with its checksum, signature and
   attestation checks and its stated limits; Nix second. eon-igae.15 leaves eonterm.com to this
   bead.
5. The Nix no-Helix variant (eon-igae.17): name the #no-helix install line, as Lucca
   recorded here on 2026-11-10.

Widened on 2026-11-09 from the window family alone (prime-beads, overseer's OK; Lucca said
"auto-decide" for pending questions on 2026-11-09).

## Contract

None (website text). Product terms per docs/ARCHITECTURE.md#naming-boundary.

## Prerequisites

The v0.2.0 tag exists (eon-igae.9): nothing on the site describes unreleased behavior as current.
Drafting on a site branch may start earlier against the candidate.

## Scope

One site pass after the tag: the changes above across the docs pages, start and install
pages and src/site.ts (which reads the release tag). Text only: the demo clips are eon-igae.16,
which follows this bead. Out: benchmark numbers (not published, eon-benchmarks-xl2bp.8).

## Acceptance

- The site describes `eon window ls|attach|stop`, sessions, `eon update` and the Nix-free install
  and the Nix #no-helix variant as shipped in v0.2.0; src/site.ts reads tag v0.2.0.
- No page names a removed command (`eon attach`, `eon stop GENERATION`, `eon generations`,
  `eon windows`) as current commands, or calls the product concept session a workspace.
  Preserve technical identifiers and dated historical quotations per the naming boundary.
- The install page's Nix-free commands match README's (eon-igae.15.2) and name the v0.2.0 assets.
- The site's checks pass (typos, Astro check, build, browser smoke tests). Pushing or deploying
  only on Lucca's request.

## Verification

Site checks and one Codex review of the text (docs-only rule).

title: Give Quit this window a shortcut and a prompt
description:
## Why

eon-7cf0y decision 4 (Lucca, 2026-11-01): a direct Quit action in the window. Today "Quit this window" exists only inside the Commands popup (Alt+Shift+M) with no shortcut, no Alt+/ line and no hint, and Lucca could not find it.

## Change

- One default shortcut for Quit this window. Pick it against EON-C20 and Venus collisions; note Alt+Q already opens the attention inbox, so weigh a neighbor key against mistaken quits. It is rebindable like other Eon keys (rule 6).
- A Venus prompt in the final-close prompt's style (EON-C8): "Quit this window? This stops N terminals.", the busy terminals listed by title, "Enter Quit · Esc Cancel", and the hint "Alt+Shift+D keeps it running instead". Whether an all-idle window skips the prompt follows `eon quit`'s confirmation rule.
- Alt+/ line, Commands popup entry showing the key, and a bottom hint (EON-C24) if it fits.
- Runs through the same supervisor action as `eon quit` (sibling bead), which is its CLI path (rule 5).

## Contract

EON-C8, EON-C20, EON-C24, EON-C28 (default shortcuts are promised from 1.0), VEN-C8 if Venus needs a launch argument. Show Lucca the exact text and key first.

## Acceptance

- Venus and runtime tests for the key, prompt wording (singular and plural), cancel, and Alt+Shift+D during the prompt.
- Installed check on isolated Sway: the key quits after Enter, Esc keeps the window, the Alt+/ line shows.
- USAGE.md shortcut table, README shortcut table, CHANGELOG.

## Scope

Key and prompt only; the sidebar footer and badge menu reuse this prompt in their own beads.
close_reason: Alt+Shift+Q quits this window like eon quit, asking first (naming busy terminals) while one runs something; Enter quits, Esc cancels, Alt+Shift+D detaches. Proof, review and gate PASS recorded above.

title: Give each window a session summary of itself and the other running windows
description:
## Why

eon-7cf0y decisions 2 and 3 (Lucca, 2026-11-01): Eon itself must show what keeps running, because Wayland desktops give no tray or Dock dot (reference pass on eon-7cf0y). The sidebar footer, the badge menu and the launch notice all need the same facts, and an agent must read them from the CLI as data (AGENTS.md rule 5).

## Change

The supervisor gives each window a session summary: this window's name and ID, its start time, its live terminal count, and the user's other running windows (name, ID, live terminal count), refreshed when windows start or end. Venus receives it with the workspace snapshot; the CLI prints it (extend `eon window` or `eon generations` with `--json` fields, decide which).

## Reference gate

Find how `eon generations` and `eon window list` discover other windows today, and the cheapest correct refresh trigger (no polling loop that wakes an idle machine, AP-PERF-001). Decide whether the summary rides the EONW snapshot (a codec change: bump the EONW version, never amend in place) or a separate message.

## Contract

EON-C11, EON-C23, EON-C10 (CLI read). EONW change if any. Show Lucca the exact text first.

## Acceptance

- Tests: summary contents with zero and two other windows; refresh when another window starts and ends; CLI JSON fields.
- Installed check in an isolated root with two windows: each window's summary names the other.

## Scope

Data and CLI only; drawing is in the footer and badge beads.

Upgrade note: after the profile refresh, the profile's `eon` speaks EONW v28; windows started on v27 list as incompatible and need their own recorded `eon` (or a restart) to be controlled from outside them.

title: Add a session footer to the agent sidebar with Detach and Quit
description:
## Why

eon-7cf0y decision 2 (Lucca's idea, 2026-11-01): a session section in the agent sidebar so a running window and its siblings are always in sight, with Detach and Quit at hand.

## Change

A compact footer at the bottom of the agent sidebar (one or two lines, never a second list): this window (name, live terminal count), the count of other running windows when there are any, and Detach and Quit controls. Quit opens the Quit prompt (sibling bead); Detach is Alt+Shift+D's action. Activating the other-windows count opens a small list of those windows, each with Quit. Reachable by keyboard through F6 focus, with accessible names. Shown only while the sidebar is shown; with the sidebar hidden or off, the badge menu covers it.

## Contract

VEN-C30, EON-C31 (sidebar), EON-C8 (detach and quit). Show Lucca the exact text first. Visible sizes and text follow rule 6 (configure or record why fixed).

- Venus tests: footer layout at narrow and wide sidebar widths, zero and several other windows, keyboard reach, Quit opens the prompt, Detach detaches.

Footer only.


## CLI and proof parity

Keep the existing Detach/Quit CLI actions and Runtime-owned running summary as their authoritative paths. `eon window ls` (eon-7cf0y.22) is the all-window listing. eon-1exhj (cross-window targeting preserving caller identity) owns the remaining targeting gap for agents in another window. title: Report each terminal's foreground from Orbit (management v5)
description:
## Why

eon-7cf0y decision 4 (Lucca, 2026-11-01): quitting asks only while a terminal runs something other than an idle shell. eon-7cf0y.1 ships `eon quit` with Stop's always-ask prompt because the supervisor cannot learn this today (plan: ~/.cache/eon-agents/eon-7cf0y/eon-7cf0y.1-plan.md, finding 3).

## Facts (edge ab0e37f)

- Orbit samples the PTY foreground on every management `ProgramStatus` request (orbit/src/management.rs:255-266; host.rs:834; `Foreground::{Unknown, Child, Other}`, orbit/src/pty.rs:795-801) but the reply omits it (orbit/crates/protocol/src/management.rs:170-180).
- The attention poller already asks every pane and popup each 500 ms (runtime attention.rs:42-75, 241-262).

## Change

1. Orbit management v4 -> v5: a `foreground` byte in the `ProgramStatus` reply (ORB-C13, ORB-C15; run the ORBS/ORBF bump checklist: manifest subtree hash, version goldens, Bend output bound).
2. Runtime caches the fact per terminal. Idle only when started with the default shell, foreground `Child`, and the sample fresher than 3 s. Busy otherwise: explicit command (`pane create -- CMD`, popups, `run -- CMD`), recovered with unknown launch, `Unknown`, or stale. The caller's own terminal is excluded.
3. EONW next version (after eon-7cf0y.4's v28): the busy fact on `InspectRuntime` (CLI) and the snapshot (Venus, for .3's prompt).
4. `eon quit` asks only when some terminal is busy, naming them. Draft EON-C11 text in the .1 plan, "Draft only, for the foreground protocol bead".

## Contract

ORB-C13, ORB-C15, EON-C11, EONW revision. Approved under eon-7cf0y's approval mode; reviewers still check the text.

## Acceptance

- Orbit protocol tests and goldens for v5; runtime tests for the idle/busy rule (default shell idle, `claude` pane busy, stale busy); CLI test: idle window quits without a prompt, busy window asks and names the busy terminals.
- Orbit Nix checks with --keep-going; installed check in an isolated root.

## Prerequisites

eon-7cf0y.1 and eon-7cf0y.4 landed.

title: Let a newer eon stop and quit windows that run an older EONW
description:
## Why

Found by the eon-7cf0y.7 planner (2026-11-01, plan ~/.cache/eon-agents/eon-7cf0y/eon-7cf0y.7-plan.md, "Out-of-scope findings"). A newer build's `eon` cannot stop or quit a window whose supervisor speaks an older EONW: `eon quit --all` and `eon stop G` fail with `stop-unavailable` for incompatible generations, and `eon quit`'s ambiguity listing even suggests `eon stop G`, which fails the same way. This is the "old window I can't get rid of" case the close-and-quit epic exists to remove. It bites Lucca now: his live window is EONW v27 while the profile `eon` is v28.

## Change

Stop and quit hand an incompatible generation to the `eon` recorded for that generation, the way attach already does (EON-C11, docs/CONTRACTS.md "EON-C11 — Runtime generations and presentation"). Fix `eon quit`'s listing so every command it suggests works on the listed window.

## Contract

EON-C11 (and EON-C27/the `eon quit` clauses if they name stop-unavailable): exact text drafted in the plan and applied under eon-7cf0y's approval mode.

## Prerequisites

None (eon-7cf0y.1 `eon quit` landed in 7de7d87).

## Acceptance

- A test where a v(N-1) generation is stopped by `eon stop G` and by `eon quit --all` from a vN CLI (fails first today with `stop-unavailable`).
- If the recorded `eon` is missing (garbage-collected store path), the error says so and names the manual fallback.
- Isolated Sway installed check: the v27 build in ~/.cache/eon-agents/eon-7cf0y/pkg1 as the old window, the current build's CLI stops it.

## Scope boundary

Only stop/quit delegation and the listing text. No change to attach, no wire bump.
close_reason: A newer eon stops and quits windows started by an Eon with another EONW through the eon that build recorded, with paste-safe recovery advice (sh and Nushell). Proof, review ledger and gate PASS recorded above.

Approved: (1) this eon asks its own question, then runs the generation's recorded eon as '<recorded eon> stop G --json' with no stdin, in the right namespace, with a loop guard (EON_STOP_DELEGATED), and reports the result as its own (else stop-failed); all five stop/quit paths go through stop_generation (generation.rs:1050). Rejected: keeping old codecs, a version-independent stop frame now, signalling the supervisor, interactive delegation, exec like attach, stopping a whole namespace. (2) Always ask before quitting an older-build window (busy terminals are invisible to this build; EON-C11 already asks when it cannot inspect). (3) Missing-record fallback text is generic ('restore that build, then run PATH stop G'), no nix-store hint, no kill advice. (4) .9 takes all stop delegation; eon-v0b7y is rescoped after .9 lands (comment there). (5) No parent-side timeout on the delegated eon (the old build bounds its own I/O; a fixed limit would kill a slow but correct Stop). Open for Lucca: (6) file a pre-1.0 bead reserving a version-independent stop message in EONW for windows whose recorded eon file is gone.

  - Stop and quit are CLI commands. `--json` gives agents one result object per target, with
    the advice exact in `detail`.

    terminals, and EON-C11 already asks when it cannot inspect them.

    in them paste. This is a display fact, not a preference.

Once the profile `eon` is this build, these commands stop Lucca's live EONW 28 window **without
asking**, because `--json` never asks (EON-C11), and that window is now stoppable:
- `eon stop previous --json` and `eon stop all --json`;
- `eon stop <its generation> --json`;
- `eon window stop all --json`, and `eon window stop <its window ID> --json` when it is an
  independent window;
- `eon quit --all --json`;
- `eon quit --json` when that window is the only candidate.

Until now these returned `stop-unavailable` for it. In human mode every one of these commands
asks first (`It runs another Eon build, so its terminals are unknown.`). Rule 4 already forbids
agents from running them against the live runtime. The pane agents and Lucca should hear this
with the refresh. Human `eon quit --all` would also quit his current window.

title: Show machine load in eon session --json for agents
description:
## Why

Filed on Lucca's approval relayed by the Starcompass session (starcompass-8c, 2026-11-02, Lucca: "agreed."). Ownership decided by Lucca the same day: Starcompass owns coordination policy (AP-COORDINATOR-001 schedules heavy runs against machine load); Eon owns the mechanism. Today the Eon Bar shows CPU and RAM chips, but agents cannot read machine load from Eon (`eon session --json` has no load figures), which is also a rule-5 parity gap. Coordinators read `uptime`/`free` by hand; on 2026-11-02 six agents drove load to 30 on 16 cores.

## Change

Add a `load` object to `eon session --json` (and the human `eon session` output): load averages (1/5/15 min), logical core count, memory available and total, read the same way as the Eon Bar chips (Linux /proc, macOS native readers as venus/src/system.rs does). Read-only; no limits.

## Contract

A new or extended EON-C clause for the `load` fields; stop for Lucca's approval of exact text. An EONW field only if the figures travel through the snapshot; prefer computing them in the CLI if that is enough.

## Order

Independent of eon-eon-agent-lr8sx.21: the heavy-run queue reads no load figures (comment 6202). eon-agent-parity-a9g0.12 consumes this bead's sampler; do not duplicate its shown-chip/grade work.

## Acceptance

Tests for the JSON shape on Linux; macOS path compiled and covered by the mac harness; docs/USAGE.md; CHANGELOG.


## Evidence, ownership and boundary

At 6e63eb7, venus/src/system.rs owns CpuTimes::read (line 99), one-minute load formatting (278), and RamUse::read (563); runtime workspace.rs::json (3441) has no machine-load fields. The current chip exposes one-minute load, so 5/15-minute values are additional CLI readings, not already-displayed chip data.

One owner for raw sampling and memory formulas (commented decision, 2026-11-03). Do not make Runtime or Eon depend on Venus or add a second sampler. If sharing requires a new crate/cross-crate dependency, stop with a recommendation before implementation, per comment 6202 and Product Boundary. Record the reference gate and exact EON-C10 amendment, with units and unavailable-value semantics, for approval before code. An EONW amendment is needed only if the approved route transports the readings there.

Acceptance also covers finite nonnegative 1/5/15-minute values, logical cores and memory amounts with named units, a failed/unsupported read represented honestly rather than as zero, and identical raw-source formulas between chip and CLI where they overlap. Tests must exercise parser failures as well as the JSON shape. Keep scheduling policy and limits outside Eon; no new machine metrics beyond the approved set. macOS compilation/harness evidence does not establish a wider platform-support claim.
notes: Plan check 2026-11-03: contract is an EON-C10 amendment (eon session --json), whose JSON fields freeze at 1.0 (EON-C28). One owner for sampling: share the reader with Venus's chips (venus/src/system.rs) or move it to one crate both use, so memory figures use one formula. eon-agent-parity-a9g0.12 (chip values and shown state) now waits on this bead and reuses its sampler.
