title: Show one Codex quota chip per window, like Claude's
description:
## Why

Lucca, 2026-10-29: "codex widgets should be split like claude's" / "do it". Today Codex shows its
five-hour and seven-day windows in one chip that condenses to the lowest-remaining window under
pressure (VEN-C22), while Claude shows one chip per window (VEN-C26). One rule for both providers
is easier to read and to configure.

## Evidence (edge 127adde)

- venus/docs/CONTRACTS.md:1498 VEN-C22 Result: "one noninteractive fact chip ... such as
  `[mark] 3h/5h 74% · 6d4h/7d 42%`. Under pressure the chip keeps the mark and complete
  lowest-remaining window, then disappears".
- venus/docs/CONTRACTS.md:1707 VEN-C26: one chip per Claude window, five-hour then seven-day;
  compact, then chips disappear one by one, the one closest to the tabs first.
- docs/CONTRACTS.md:2251 (EON-C27): "Codex's in one chip and Claude's in one chip per window".
- docs/CONFIGURATION.md:286-290 and venus/docs/PRESENTATION.md:26-30 describe the one Codex chip.
- Runtime already supplies each Codex window separately over EONW; no wire change is expected.
- Code: Eon Bar chips are built in venus/src/render/chrome.rs (`build_workspace`, about :1053) and
  laid out in venus/src/scene.rs.

## Proposed contract text (needs Lucca's approval before code)

VEN-C22 Result, replacing its first three sentences:
"Venus projects one noninteractive fact chip per Codex window into the existing single-row Eon Bar,
five-hour then seven-day, as VEN-C26 does for Claude. Each fresh chip shows the exact monochrome
OpenAI Blossom, that window's elapsed/total position and remaining percentage, such as
`[mark] 3h/5h 74%`. Under pressure full labels become compact, then chips disappear one by one, the
one closest to the tabs first, before active-tab identity, fixed controls, or the bounded drag
region lose their accepted space. Stale labels include `old` on every chip; a blocked or unknown
observation shows one chip with the mark followed by `blocked` or `unknown`."
Hover and AccessKit: each chip names Codex and its window (unchanged otherwise).
EON-C27: "Codex's in one chip and Claude's in one chip per window" becomes "one chip per window for
each provider". VEN-C26's "Codex's mark, labels and provider policy remain unchanged" keeps its
meaning (the mark and policy are unchanged; only the chip split changes).

## Scope

In scope: the Venus chip split and compaction order; the contract texts above; CONFIGURATION.md
and PRESENTATION.md; the existing quota tests updated (`quota_chip_preserves_truth_layout_and_
static_accessibility` and neighbours) plus one test for per-window Codex chips and their
disappearance order.
Out of scope: EONW or Runtime changes, colours or pace gradient, Claude's chips, new providers
(Amp is eon-amp, filed separately), configuration of which windows show.

## Acceptance

- With both Codex windows reported, two Codex chips appear (five-hour then seven-day), each with
  the Blossom, position and percentage; under shrinking width they compact and then disappear one
  by one like Claude's; blocked/unknown show a single chip.
- Contract texts updated as approved; docs match.

## Verification

- `nix develop -c eon-test -p yazelix-venus` with the updated and new quota tests.
- Installed UI change: profile refresh plus one isolated installed dogfood observation of the bar
  with both providers (AGENTS.md Verification table).
- Review: contract change, so the full Codex path applies.

## Stop Conditions

- Stop for Lucca's approval of the exact contract text before code.
- Stop if the split needs an EONW change.

The rank-based IDs it planned (rank 0 keeps NodeId 9, rank 1 a new NodeId 21) moved the seven-day chip's node whenever the five-hour window expired or came back (review round 1, both reviewers). Adopted: a fresh or stale Codex chip's NodeId is `(1 << 40) + 2 * duration + occurrence` (`CODEX_QUOTA_NODE_START`, venus/src/accessibility.rs `quota_id`), where occurrence is 0, or 1 only for the second of two EONW-valid windows of equal duration (Runtime never sends those). title: Talk to Eon's agents from a phone chat app, both ways
description:
## Why

Lucca, 2026-11-01: "i wonder if we can do the same to eon". He shared a post with no author named. It recommends connecting T3 Code machines to "grok bot" to do more work from a phone. With Cursor cloud agents it works "two way": the bot and the agents message back and forth. The post says T3 Code's integration "isn't quite as seamless yet".

Competitors reach people away from the desk: T3 Code, Rex, Amp and herdr via Moshi (competitor audit eon-r6yt). Eon has no path from a phone to a running agent today. Related work:
- eon-sixj pushes attention out to the phone, one way;
- the mobile client and SSH beads are frozen (orb-native-mobile-access-bwg, orb-permanent-ssh-terminal-access-hd6);
- remote workspaces (eon-remote-workspaces-52i4) are for a person at another computer.

A chat bridge is the cheap middle ground: the person keeps using a chat app they already have.

## Goal (to shape, not decided)

From a chat app on the phone, a person can:
1. See which agents in the workspace are working, waiting or done (EON-C31 attention).
2. Read an agent's recent output or summary.
3. Send a message or answer to a specific agent pane.
4. Get a message when an agent needs them or finishes.

Point 4 overlaps eon-sixj; point 3 is new.

## Questions for the reference gate (research first)

- **Which bot or chat surface?** Read what the post's "grok bot" is and how its T3 Code and Cursor integrations work (API, MCP, webhooks). Compare chat platforms people already use: Telegram, Slack, Discord, Matrix, Signal, and the Grok bot itself. Also compare a generic "agent of agents" pattern, where any chat bot drives the `eon` CLI over MCP.
- **How does a message reach an agent?** Typing into its terminal through the authorized terminal-write path (Humans and Agents) differs from agent-specific inbox APIs. david-crespo/ah routes per harness: a Claude Code inbox socket, `codex queue`, OpenCode's HTTP API. Eon owns panes and terminals, so it needs no session registry.
- **Trust boundary.** Commands come from outside the machine and agent output leaves it. Cover authentication, which chats may act, the risk of prompt injection into agents, and approvals for destructive actions. Default off.
- **Where does it run?** Inside the Runtime, or as a separate opt-in process that uses only the `eon` CLI and JSON. The latter keeps Eon free of chat-platform dependencies. Rule 5 already gives agents every workspace action as CLI and data.
- **Comparables:** T3 Code's and Cursor's bot integrations, Rex, herdr and Moshi, and the Claude Code / Codex remote or mobile features.

## Contract

Not chosen. It is consequential: a new trust boundary, possibly a dependency, and possibly a CLI surface for "send a message to a pane's agent". Lucca approves the contract text before any code.

## Acceptance (this bead)

A research comment covering:
- the comparables, with sources;
- the recommended surface and architecture, and the rejected ones;
- the trust model;
- the smallest first slice (likely: an opt-in bridge process over the `eon` CLI, read-only status plus one "message this agent" action);
- proposed child beads.

Lucca picks before implementation.

## Scope boundary

Research and design only. No new client, no unfreezing of the mobile or SSH beads, no code.
notes: Split 2026-11-03 (prime-beads P2 pass): the 2026-11-02 scope addition (send a message to a pane's agent, routed per agent as in david-crespo/ah) moved to its own research bead, which this bead now waits on; this bead keeps the chat-platform, bridge and trust research and uses that CLI path.

title: Start the Agent popup's Codex with --no-daemon, so its eon commands act for its own terminal
description:
## Why

Lucca asked for an idea run on 2026-11-09; this is K1 of
~/.cache/eon-agents/eon-ideas-work/ideas.md, filed by eon-overseer's
"auto-decide" note the same day.

The Agent popup's `auto` command runs `["codex", "resume"]`
(eon/crates/eon/src/product.rs:176). Eon's own docs (docs/USAGE.md, "Codex's
shared daemon") and skill (eon/skills/eon/SKILL.md:171) say Codex in Eon needs
`--no-daemon`: by default the Codex TUI runs its commands through a shared
background server that keeps the environment of the terminal that started
it. A Codex in another pane then runs `eon` commands as the Agent popup's
terminal, they fail once that popup ends, and `eon quit --json` through the
daemon quits that window without asking. Eon's default creates the trap its
docs warn about. The argv predates the finding (2586d7c, 2026-10-14, versus
acc29d2, 2026-10-31): an oversight, not a choice.

Codex accepts `resume --no-daemon` (reference clone ~/pjs/refs/codex-0163 at
8308618: cli/tests/features.rs:414; main.rs `resume_and_fork_preserve_no_daemon`).
EON-C36's installed proof ran `codex --no-daemon` 0.166.0 in Eon panes.

## Scope

- `agent_commands` becomes `["codex", "resume", "--no-daemon"]`.
- docs/CONFIGURATION.md names the new argv; CHANGELOG.md entry (a default
  command changes).
- A test pins the `auto` argv list.
- Out of scope: Codex started by hand (USAGE and the skill keep their advice);
  any caller-identity guard (see the follow-up comment).

Contract: none (the `auto` list is configuration documented in
docs/CONFIGURATION.md). Owner: Eon product defaults.

## Acceptance

- The argv, doc line and changelog entry change together.
- A test fails if the Codex entry loses `--no-daemon`.
- fmt, clippy and the whole-workspace `eon-test` pass on the staged tree.
- After landing and a profile refresh: one isolated installed check that the
  popup's Codex starts and that `eon session --json`'s `caller` from inside it
  names the popup.

## Release gate

In the v0.2.0 gate (blocks eon-igae.9, eon-igae.7, eon-igae.8). Lucca, 2026-11-09: "you can add some or all to the release gate / we cant release without yu's ssh anyways".

title: Keep usage and cost history per agent provider
description:
## Why
T3 Code has a usage page with estimated cost across providers; Amp explains per-thread cost. Eon's
Eon Bar shows current quotas only, and EON-C27 keeps one stored reading per provider, expiring after
24 hours. Source: competitor audit eon-r6yt (2026-10-29), reports in
~/pjs/refs/competitor-audit-2026-10/. Lucca, 2026-10-29: "file the beads". Filing only; no work is
approved yet beyond planning.

## Contracts
- EON-C27 (CodexBar quota collection), currently partially proved; the pre-Bend baseline is candidate evidence and the installed quota observation remains pending: "each successful read replaces
  one stored reading per provider"; "Readings disappear after 24 hours"; "No credential, identity,
  raw output or billing data enters EONW, Eon logs or the stored readings." History and cost both
  change this contract (consequential: new local data format, privacy boundary).
- EON-C32 owns bar configuration/order. VEN-C22 and VEN-C26 are retired presentation contracts; if a bar view is chosen, use venus/docs/PRESENTATION.md#eon-bar for feature scope, and EON-C27/canonical EONW for the data boundary.
- EON-C22 and EON-C26 are retired (EON-C27 owns quota now); do not cite them.
- Humans and Agents rule: whatever history a person can see, an agent can read from the CLI as data.

## Phase 1 (this bead, before any code)
Reference gate and contract draft, recorded here:
1. Owner first (AP-DEPENDENCY-001, AP-OWNERSHIP-001): check whether pinned CodexBar already owns
   usage or cost history (for example a cost scan of local agent logs) so Eon consumes it instead of
   storing a second history. Compare with T3 Code's usage page and ccusage-style local log scans at
   recorded revisions.
2. If Eon stores history: format, location, retention bound, size bound, versioning (like EON-C27's
   stored reading), and what "estimated cost" means given EON-C27's no-billing-data rule.
3. Presentation: a CLI read (`--json`) first; a popup or bar view only if Lucca wants one.
4. Providers: whichever EON-C27 collects (Codex, Claude); OpenCode Go and Grok follow their quota
   beads (eon-opencode-go-quota-eon-bar-5tt9, eon-grok-quota-eon-bar-c2ni).
5. Propose a fresh-session implementation split. Implementation beads are filed after approval.

## Acceptance
- Phase 1: Lucca approves the owner, contract text and split.
- Outcome: after a day of use, the history shows per-provider usage over time from the CLI (and
  any approved view); nothing leaves the machine; no new credentials.

## Scope
Read only what providers or CodexBar already expose; no new credentials, no network beyond EON-C27's
existing collection.

## Verification
Phase 1: planning route (bead state). Implementation: per child.

This bead finishes Phase 1 only: the one-day history outcome describes the later implementation, whose session-sized children are proposed here and filed after approval. No storage, billing-data permission, new view, or implementation is approved by this planning bead.

title: Evaluate code sharing between Eon and Yazelix Nova
description:
## Why
Eon and Yazelix Nova are parallel product lines that solve several of the same problems in separate code. Lucca asked Eon to evaluate code sharing between them in general (2026-11-02, from the nova-overseer session). Both repos are Apache-2.0, so licensing does not block sharing.

They already share some pinned children:
- Anima (`Yazelix/anima`) and Nova Helix (`Yazelix/nova-helix`).
- Kinestra (`Yazelix/kinestra`), the private-display recorder and proof harness.
- Ratconfig (`luccahuguet/ratconfig`) is an Eon input.

The question is what else should move into shared crates or repos, and what must stay separate.

## Candidate overlaps (hypotheses to verify)
1. **AI quota core:**
   - Eon `runtime/crates/eon-runtime/src/quota.rs` (1,952 lines at 6e63eb7; compare behavior, not historical line counts) vs Nova Bar `src/agent_usage.rs` (1,466 lines), a rewrite of Eon's rules as of 2026-10-16.
   - Nova has since missed about ten Eon refinements: per-window chips, pace colours, a kept last reading, per-user reads with back-off, the stale-chip fix and scoped weekly windows.
   - Most concrete case. Nova's P1 port, yazelix-5vl-ai-quota-widgets-eon-q8wg, is on hold for this decision.
2. **Agent activity and hooks:** Eon's attention records and agent integration vs Nova Radar (`Yazelix/zj-radar`): Codex hook setup and trust (`yzx radar-setup`, `zj-radar setup codex`), and running and done detection.
3. **Bar system widgets:** Eon Bar's CPU, RAM and disk chips (coloured by load) vs Nova Bar's system widgets.
4. **Install and release:**
   - Eon `installer/` vs Nova `packaging/install.sh` with its portable release tooling: SHA256SUMS, attestations, SOURCE-DELIVERY, native-library notices and `publish_release.py`.
   - Both packages pin CodexBar (Nova `packaging/codexbar.nix`).
5. **Diagnostics and config:** doctor and status checks (for example PATH shadowing of an installed CLI), config loading with deprecated aliases and migration floors, and the config corpus tests.
6. **Test harnesses:** Nova's tmux-driven checks (`checks/tmux.rs`) vs Eon's proof harnesses. Both already use Kinestra for GUI proofs.

## Method
For each candidate:
- Compare the two implementations: size, behaviour differences, IO and runtime coupling (Orbit and Venus vs Zellij plugins and widget commands), and platform targets.
- Classify it: share now, share later, or keep separate, with the reason.
- For "share", name the boundary (types and functions), the home (a standalone `Yazelix/...` repo, or a dependency-free crate in one workspace), the owner whose behaviour is the reference, and the migration order.

The rule of thumb to test: share what something is (models, parsing, validation, rules, stores), and keep what it looks like and how it is wired per product.

## Acceptance
- A table on this bead: candidate, decision, reason, boundary, home, owner.
- Lucca's approval of the first slice. Quota is the expected first slice.
- Follow-up beads filed in Eon for approved extractions. Tell nova-overseer so the matching Nova beads are filed and q8wg switches from a port to adoption.

## Scope boundary
Evaluation only. No code moves until Lucca approves a slice. The two product architectures stay separate (site and docs keep separate owners). eon-iebt1 proceeds independently.

title: Make the macOS management-close fixture independent of inherited peer descriptors
description:
## Why

The Runtime management-close fixture assumes dropping its socket peer makes an Acquire request unsendable. A concurrent fork can inherit the descriptor and keep that socket connected, allowing the valid queued Lease to be accepted. eon-yooz3 fixes the Linux fixture using peer shutdown and retains a duplicate descriptor to make the race deterministic. On macOS, the reviewers predict that retaining the duplicate defeats the expected failure even after peer shutdown, so the regression clone is Linux-only and the original macOS inheritance gap remains.

## Evidence

- `runtime/crates/eon-runtime/src/sessions.rs:2424`, `management_close_cannot_grant_an_unvalidated_or_unsent_lease`, at base `8b5ee2dfad19c15f73754cd370e79164cf2881fa` and eon-yooz3 review tree `24bfde3d6530b0932a062045d2babbbada09fcae`.
- The old drop-only fixture with a retained `peer.try_clone()` deterministically fails on Linux: `unwrap_err()` receives `Ok(())` for a valid peer with a full Lease. Shutdown makes that case green on Linux. Historical intermittent workspace failure: eon-ipc6f's `workspace-final.log`, summarized on eon-yooz3.
- Opus implementation review: `/home/lucca/.local/state/rota/runs/flaky-tests-opus-1/log`. Concern is that Darwin peer credentials remain available while a clone is held, and writes to a peer whose read side is shut down can report success while discarding bytes.
- Codex independently raised the same concern from Apple's published XNU send/shutdown implementation: https://github.com/apple-oss-distributions/xnu/blob/xnu-11417.121.6/bsd/kern/uipc_usrreq.c#L565-L746 and buffer discard implementation: https://github.com/apple-oss-distributions/xnu/blob/main/bsd/kern/uipc_socket2.c#L847-L857 . Its report is `/home/lucca/.local/state/rota/runs/flaky-tests-codex-1/report.md`.
- These Darwin semantics are source-derived review findings, **not a native macOS reproduction**. The overseer explicitly requested the P2 follow-up at 2026-11-10T09:42:16Z; subsequent user direction authorizes acting on that INBOX entry.

## Scope

Make the management-close test fixture independent of concurrent descriptor inheritance on macOS while preserving its full/malformed/truncated/empty queued replies and valid/invalid peer cases. Keep the observable rejection of an unvalidated or unsent acquisition request. Ownership is Runtime; this is a test-fixture issue under existing acquisition behavior, not a product guarantee change.

Out of scope: changing production acquisition, widening time bounds, adding retries, changing contracts/protocols, changing Linux's deterministic clone/shutdown coverage, or unrelated timing tests.

## Acceptance

- Native macOS evidence establishes what peer shutdown, retained descriptors, queued replies and peer credential lookup actually do.
- The fixture reaches real peer disconnection before asserting an unsent request; no scheduler-dependent drop assumption remains.
- A deterministic regression demonstrates the unsafe drop-only fixture and a corrected fixture passes repeated loaded native runs without weakening existing error assertions.
- No hangup wait is introduced while the test itself still holds a peer clone: release owned peer references first, and wait without consuming the queued reply.

## Implementation Notes

Use a fresh session and inspect Runtime's platform credential and socket helpers. Consider a non-consuming hangup wait after releasing the controlled duplicate, or another small platform-correct fixture. Do not copy Linux shutdown assumptions into Darwin. Record a neutral/test-only portability disposition unless native investigation finds a production defect; that broader boundary needs a separate decision.

## Verification

Use isolated native macOS `nix develop -c eon-test` or the supported mac-proof route with the exact candidate revision. Include deterministic red/green, 20 loaded repetitions of the affected test and the eon-runtime suite. Linux focused regression stays green. Run fmt and all-target clippy for the touched crate on supported target routes. A Linux cross-target clippy pass does not prove Darwin socket behavior.

## Stop Conditions

Stop and report if current test or acquisition code has materially drifted, or a complete fix requires a production/contract change. Do not change acquisition simply to satisfy a closed-peer fixture.

## Maintenance Notes

P2 follow-up from eon-yooz3's first Opus and Codex reviews. The temporary Linux-only clone gating preserves the pre-existing Darwin close path but does not claim the macOS fork-inheritance race is fixed. It can be removed only after equivalent native Darwin regression evidence. No dependency on changing product behavior; native macOS execution is a prerequisite for closing this issue.

Five seconds later the pane was gone. The machine was at load ~16 on 16 threads with nix-store --gc running (heavy disk IO). Eon 0.1.22, edge 0dcc98c.

Problem: under load the CLI reports failure (exit non-zero) for a close that succeeds, so an agent or script retries or reports a false error. Diagnose the delayed stage, then apply the longer bounded wait selected by the overseer on 2026-11-10 under Lucca's standing auto-decide rule (comment 6314); preserve final success/failure and the exit-code contract (EON-C8/EON-C10, eon-8mnr.1).

## Decision already recorded

The overseer's 2026-11-10 decision under Lucca's standing auto-decide rule (comment 6314) selected a longer bounded wait after diagnosis, with the existing final success/failure and exit-status meanings. Do not re-open the accepted/pending-result alternative as if it were undecided. EON-C8 and EON-C10 own close completion; eon-8mnr.1 is closed and owns the existing exit-code decision.

## Current evidence and prerequisites

At 6e63eb7, runtime supervisor.rs::close_workspace_pane (2076) calls stop_closed_sessions (2388). sessions.rs::operation_timeout (368) now says "exceeded its deadline"; wait_and_finalize_tombstone is at 2235, with reconciliation checks at 2267/2276. Re-read the shared cleanup deadline and the CLI response-read bound before choosing the longer wait. The historical Orbit log was reported empty in comment 6221 and is not causal evidence. eon-etgwm is related Stop-reply timing work, not a prerequisite or proof of this bug's cause.

## Scope and reference gate

Runtime owns completion/reconciliation and the CLI owns its projection; preserve Orbit's Stop and terminal identity invariants. Diagnose the actual delayed stage first. Record the lifecycle reference route and one comparable bounded completion/reconciliation mechanism, then retain the smallest shared-owner change. Any contract-text/bound change still needs exact-text approval before code; no new result state or unbounded wait. Record why the internal safety timeout stays fixed or expose it under Configurability.

## Acceptance and verification

- A deterministic delayed-tombstone regression distinguishes confirmed completion within the accepted bound from genuinely incomplete/unreachable cleanup. A successful close exits 0 only after confirmation; a real failure keeps the existing nonzero status and honest remaining topology.
- The caller's read deadline accommodates the accepted server completion deadline; a longer server wait must not just move the false error to the CLI.
- Keep target identity/focus and other terminals intact. Record the delay attribution and the red/green evidence using the supported sandboxed harness.
- Run the required affected lifecycle/workspace proof, fresh review and an isolated installed close under controlled load; no stress or GC of the user's live terminals. Update USAGE/CHANGELOG if the accepted observable timing changes.

comments.text: prime-beads 2026-11-10: real and current. The bound is operation_timeout (runtime sessions.rs near :369), hit in wait_and_finalize_tombstone (near :2054 and :2063). The Orbit log the body cites is 0 bytes and holds no evidence. Contract: EON-C10 owns eon pane close; a new result state or exit status needs approval. Order of work: first find where the 5 s went (Orbit stop is SIGHUP, 500 ms, SIGKILL, reap; suspect tombstone publication under disk IO), then propose one option to Lucca (wait longer, or report accepted and still closing; the audit recommends a longer wait once the cause is known, because agents script on the exit status). Acceptance: a test with a delayed tombstone shows the CLI result matches the final state.

title: Split and modularize Venus application.rs and render.rs
description:
## Decision
Lucca, 2026-10-17: split, refactor and modularize `venus/src/application.rs` and `venus/src/render.rs` so humans and agents can read and change them cheaply. Structure only: no user-visible behavior, contract, wire, dependency or platform change. Follows `eon-venus-modules-oagt` (closed 2026-10-16), which moved shortcuts, scroll, fonts and the cursor trail out and left "further shrinking impl Application and impl Renderer" to its own design decision; this bead is that decision's home.

## Contract
- Consumer: maintainers and coding agents working in `venus/`.
- Result: each concern has one private module or type that can be read on its own; `application.rs` keeps native event dispatch and focus, `render.rs` keeps GPU frame submission. Behavior, public items and tests are unchanged; tests move with the code they cover.
- Important failures: behavior drift, a second owner for moved state or policy, a new framework or trait hierarchy introduced for modularity, lost test coverage.

## Evidence (edge 40b0982 plus the uncommitted slice 3b tree of eon-splits-opwv)
- `application.rs`: 6,847 lines (production 1-4236, tests 4237-6847); `impl Application` from 549, `impl ApplicationHandler` from 2793 (window_event about 500 lines, mostly pointer arms; handle_transport about 230).
- `render.rs`: 5,450 lines (production 1-3403, tests 3404-5450); `impl Renderer` from 380 (build_workspace about 340 lines, rebuild_if_needed about 330).
- Existing private modules: `application/{scroll,shortcuts}.rs`, `render/{cursor_trail,fonts}.rs`.
- Seams created by eon-splits-opwv: `TerminalView` (per-terminal attachment state, now one selected plus up to three column views) and `TerminalLayer`; carry-over (5) of slice 1a: methods that touch only one terminal's state can move onto `TerminalView`.

## Candidate slices (not chosen; the first step proposes slices with evidence and stops for Lucca's choice)
- Per-terminal methods onto `TerminalView` in their own module (attachment, retry, transport event handling shared by selected and column views, resize).
- Link handling and clipboard (kept in place by Lucca's 2026-10-16 decision; revisit only with new evidence).
- Pointer arms of `window_event` into focused handlers.
- `render.rs`: workspace chrome building (`build_workspace`, header tooltip, shortcut viewer) apart from terminal cell drawing.
Add a slice only on evidence that it makes the code easier to read and change; reject per-concern `impl` files that still touch the same fields.

## Prerequisites
After `eon-splits-opwv` (slices 3c and 4 still change these files; a parallel refactor would conflict and the column work decides the final per-terminal shape).

## Owners and boundary
Venus owns all of this. Keep modules private to the crate; keep one protocol validator, model, scene, draw-input, renderer, accessibility and semantic-action path (`venus/AGENTS.md`). A new Venus module is product scope: Lucca approves each slice's modules. Not consequential under the root `AGENTS.md`, so no reference gate. Portability: neutral.

## Acceptance
- Per slice: no behavior change; the Venus suites pass unchanged through `nix develop -c eon-test -p yazelix-venus`; `cargo fmt --check` and `cargo clippy --locked --all-targets -- -D warnings` green for Venus; `nix build --no-link .#default` builds. No new tests, since no behavior changes.
- Each slice gets the review loop; one ledger line per slice here.
close_reason: Chosen slices R2, R1 and A3 done: render.rs split into render/cells.rs and render/chrome.rs, application.rs sizing into application/geometry.rs; behavior unchanged. A1 and A2 not chosen.

Field use: build_workspace, build_shortcut_viewer and build_header_tooltip read only metrics, fonts, the text sink and the four header-interaction fields (hovered_header, quota_hovered, version_hovered, pressed_header); no GPU state. The cell and cursor drawing helpers (build_row/scene/preview_rectangles, push_cursor, cursor_bounds, cursor_outline, contrast, cell_text_*, block_span, fitted_cell_font, set_cell_layer) are free functions. handle_transport and handle_column_transport repeat the per-terminal Busy/apply/loss/retry handling; the selected handler also drives window-level input, presentation and renderer state, so only the per-terminal part can move. Proposed slices, each its own commit and review loop: (R1) render/chrome.rs: a HeaderInteraction struct owning the four hover/press fields plus the three chrome builders, push_quota_icon, rasterize_quota_icon, fit_header_text and their tests (about 750 production lines). (R2) render/cells.rs: the cell, cursor and text-segmentation free functions and their tests (about 600). (A1) application/terminal_view.rs: TerminalView, OrbitRetry and SelectionGate plus one shared per-terminal transport-event step (Busy, apply, loss, retry scheduling) used by both handlers, removing the duplicate; riskiest, since swap and reconcile are proved only live, so it adds one isolated dogfood observation. (A2) window_event's three pointer arms become named Application methods in application.rs (no new module; readability only). (A3) application/geometry.rs: initial_window_size, admits_column, surface_size, terminal_screen and rect_screen with their tests. Rejected: per-concern impl files for pointer, keyboard or workspace handling that touch the same Application fields; moving links and clipboard (kept by Lucca 2026-10-16, no new evidence). Recommended order: R2, R1, A3, A2, A1 (lowest risk and clearest seams first).

title: Release Eon v0.1.2 after the current UI batch, and bump the version on every EONW change
description:
## Why

Lucca, 2026-10-24, asked "are we stretching 0.1.1 too much? when 0.1.2 ?". v0.1.1 was tagged
2026-10-16; edge has since gained over 300 commits, 84 Unreleased changelog entries and two EONW
bumps (17 -> 19), so `EON 0.1.1` names builds that cannot talk to each other. The overseer
recommended cutting v0.1.2 right after the current UI batch and before the next EONW bump, and
bumping the version at least on every EONW change; Lucca: "ok".

## Scope

- When eon-6ros, eon-hg2v, eon-tfsg and eon-i6yf have landed (and before
  eon-workspace-switching-shn4.3 lands): bump `eon/crates/eon/Cargo.toml` (and lockfile) to
  0.1.2; turn CHANGELOG.md's Unreleased section into `## 0.1.2 - <date>` (Orbit/Venus changelogs
  keep their own version rules); tag `v0.1.2` on that commit and push the tag.
- docs/DISTRIBUTION.md "Versions and stages": add the rule that Eon's product version is bumped
  at least whenever EONW's protocol version changes, so the version identifies compatibility
  (Lucca's "ok", 2026-10-24).
- Delivery proof (AP-DELIVERY-001, AGENTS.md "Promotion or release"): exact-revision
  `nix build .#default`, profile refresh, `eon --help`/`eon versions` report 0.1.2, one
  fresh-session isolated dogfood observation; record it on this bead in the release commit.
- The overseer shows Lucca the 0.1.2 changelog section before tagging.

Out: main/stable promotion (no such branches exist yet), other channels.

title: Run eon-test through cargo-nextest with serialized supervisor suites
description:
From the fleet efficiency research /home/lucca/.cache/eon-agents/eon-efficiency-work/report.md (raw numbers in data.md beside it), Lucca 2026-11-09: "start a researcher on way to make our resource usage much more efficient ... these cpu queues and waiting times are hurting us". comments.author: lucca
comments.text:
Landing record (eon-overseer, 2026-11-10), part 1 of 3: plan review, implementation and review fixes. Author: eon-nextest pane agent. Records: ~/.cache/eon-agents/eon-nextest-work/bead/ (00-plan through 07-final-proof).

# Plan review disposition — eon-7tmc3

2026-11-10: overseer INBOX entry at 08:50:53Z directs implementation with the Opus
changes in `/home/lucca/.local/state/rota/runs/nextest-planreview-opus-1/log`.
All six findings are accepted; this record supersedes the corresponding parts of 00-plan.

1. Keep existing sandbox guarantees; audit cross-binary hazards. Use independent groups
   for Orbit's fork/socket lock, update's signal lock, and real_pty's serial lock. Add only
   groups justified by fixed shared paths, unscoped process scans or unowned signals.
   Normal workspace_control and supervisor tests remain parallel, as with libtest today.
2. Retain doctests separately and compare complete executable/ignored/doc inventories.
   Update Orbit's maintained ignored-suite invocation to native `--run-ignored only`.
3. Withdraw the 90-minute quiet request. Warm once, then measure five alternating old/new
   pairs through ordinary heavy.sh slots. Record wall/user/system CPU and uptime/loadavg
   per run, all failures and paired deltas. No retry or deadline widening.
4. Use cargo-nextest 0.9.137 from the existing nixpkgs pin with native flags.
5. No CHANGELOG entry or checkPhase bead. Change development docs and the Orbit invocation.
   The newest INBOX explicitly authorizes a br comment on eon-u5ooj with measured results
   and the shared `.config/nextest.toml` capability, superseding the general no-br-write
   instruction for that one comment only.
6. Add `--no-fail-fast`; nextest defaults plus the hazard/lock groups suffice. The sandbox
   function/environment/binds/guards must remain unchanged. Prove that by source diff;
   drop sentinel, namespace and overlap probes and deliberately unsafe configuration.

Worktree base stays 381e2e51b315ea7314b57c1f193b0061f517d46b. Edge has advanced to
bd7869bc4c6a35840609b2147ff1a3e70e441275; no rebase or branch change is authorized here.
No reviewers or package builds will be launched by this agent.

# Implementation and hazard audit

The accepted design changes only `nix/test-sandbox.nix`, `.config/nextest.toml`,
`docs/DEVELOPMENT.md` and the real-PTY command in `orbit/docs/BEHAVIOR.md`.

The shared Nix `tests` snippet has two actual callers (Linux/macOS) and owns command
dispatch once. The existing `sandbox` and `isolated` functions are unchanged. Lists
and explicit `--doc` requests use those same functions. Default Linux runs nextest
workspace, Cargo workspace doctests, then nextest installer; failures prevent later
steps. An explicit selection runs executable tests, with doctests selected explicitly.
`--no-fail-fast` finishes every selected executable test in the step. No retries,
default filters, test-source edits, timing bounds or ignored attributes are added.

Nextest discovers each workspace's own config. The root config governs all root
workspace package selections. Separate installer/relink workspaces use native defaults
because they have none of the three shared lock invariants.
The nextest default CPU-count concurrency remains configurable through native flags.
Group size one is fixed to preserve the three existing lock safety constraints.

## Hazard audit, at base 381e2e5

Raw discovery matches: `../hazard-matches.txt`. Matches that only construct protocol

## Why

Lucca, 2026-11-04, while reviewing eon-8r9a4, which kept `codex_quota` and `claude_quota` as aliases next to the new per-window widgets: "we dont want legacy code, brother". Then: "create a bead to audit the code for legacy stuff we can remove. lets not start it now."

Eon is not announced yet, and its users are few and close. Compatibility code (aliases, migration shims, fallbacks for retired formats or flags, dead paths kept "just in case") costs reading time and test surface, and protects almost no one.

## Scope

An audit only. Its output is a findings list and the removal beads it proposes. It removes nothing itself.

Look across the workspace (`eon/`, `runtime/`, `venus/`, `orbit/`, Nix and scripts) for:
- config aliases and old key names still accepted, renamed values, and deprecated CLI flags or subcommands;
- migration shims for config, state or on-disk formats that every current install has already passed;
- wire and protocol code kept for versions no supported pairing uses. Check the EONW, ORBS and ORBF version handling, and keep what contracts require for live terminals across an update (see eon-1bq8 and the bend-orbit swap);
- dead code: unused functions, feature flags that are always on or off, `#[allow(dead_code)]`, and TODOs promising a removal;
- tests and corpus cases that only pin retired behavior. The config-corpus versions under runtime/crates/eon-runtime/testdata/config-corpus are deliberate: report which old cases still earn their place, without deleting any;
- docs describing removed behavior.

Out of scope:
- Anything an `EON-C`, `ORB-C` or `VEN-C` contract requires. Report a candidate contract change instead of a removal, since contracts need approval.
- Live-terminal survival across updates (rule 4).
- Contract evidence records (eon-so8o owns those).

## Output

A findings comment on this bead. For each item: path:line, what it keeps alive, who or what still depends on it, what removing it costs (config warnings, user-visible change, contract text), and a recommendation. Group the items into proposed removal beads sized for one session each. File them only after Lucca picks.

## Verification

Read-only: `rg`, source/dependency metadata and contracts. No builds, tests or runtime probes are needed for this audit. Record uncertainty about reachability instead of deleting code or treating static suspicion as proof. A selected removal bead later proves its own affected boundary.

## Scope

The import render only. No change to Eon's local rules; any Eon-specific coordinator detail is a

title: Add the pane title notch (dual-notch layout, part 1)
description:
## Split (Lucca 2026-11-10)

Lucca: "if you want to split it in two / you can first add the notch / and in a second bead add close and zoom buttons / up to you". The overseer split it: this bead adds the pane title notch at the left of each pane header (the dual-notch geometry's title half) and lands first; the right action notch with zoom/restore and close buttons is the follow-up bead (blocked by this one). Everything below about the action notch, zoom/restore, close and their acceptance belongs to the follow-up; here, keep the title notch's truncation and geometry ready for an action area on the right but draw none.

## Why

Lucca chose dual notches first, then Rex-like as the second selectable style. He explicitly said on
2026-11-10: "we dont need to prototype / we can just add it", accepted the pair with "it's decided",
and requested one bead for dual-notch and another for Rex-like plus the setting. This bead
implements the first independently usable slice. No further speculative mockup round is requested.

## Evidence

- Exploration eon-ijyhk; Stack tabs landed in 0431ec5, following eon-whjhd. This session
investigated detached afc1907; rebaseline the fresh implementation on current edge.
- `venus/src/render/chrome.rs`: FrameTitleTab and workspace title/outline drawing.
- `venus/src/render.rs`: title-tab contours, fills and outline partitioning.
- `venus/src/scene.rs`: Stack/pane title geometry, bounds and hit geometry.
- `venus/src/application/`: existing zoom and close event/confirmation paths; identify exact current
owners before adding senders.
- `runtime/crates/eon-runtime/src/cli.rs` and `cli/parity.rs`: existing targeted ClosePane and `eon
pane close`; zoom is an existing Venus-local view state under Humans and Agents' explicit exception.
- Decision/reference record:
`/home/lucca/.cache/eon-agents/eon-notch-options-work/bead/06-decision-and-implementation-handoff.md`;
Rex reference images in `bead/references/`; Opus advice in `bead/05-opus-design-opinion.md`.

## Scope

In scope: pane title notch at the left; a second notch at the right grouping separate zoom/restore
and close buttons; shared layout for title and action slots; native pointer, keyboard and
accessibility activation; existing focus, close protections and terminal ownership; focused tests,
user/presentation docs and changelog. Preserve the Stack/pane hierarchy and existing
Stack/Agents/popup/dialog ownership; do not accidentally put pane-targeted close on a Stack heading.
Explicitly define applicability for collapsed panes, zoom and popup presentation using existing
semantics.

Out of scope: Rex-like renderer or a style selector (bead 2); original plain border-gap style; three
configurable styles; new outer wrapper borders; separator; popup-row redesign eon-x8d5x; unrelated
contrast cleanup eon-0kq2c; generic configurable notch counts.

## Acceptance

- Each applicable pane header has one title notch and one action notch containing independently
actionable zoom/restore and close controls. Controls target the pane whose header contains them.
- Zoom/restore reuses existing native zoom semantics. Close reuses the existing guarded close path,
including busy/final-pane confirmations; it does not directly kill an Orbit host or terminal.
- Title truncation reserves the action area; title ink, curves and controls never overlap.
Narrow/tiny windows degrade deliberately using existing layout bounds. Pointer, keyboard focus and
accessible names/state work for both buttons.
- A pane has a clear selected focus signal. No extra outline is added above the existing Stack/frame
contours; Lucca rejected that as "too many borders". Terminal translucency and
grid/input/accessibility ownership remain correct.
- The existing CLI close path is retained and documented; any genuinely new workspace action ships
its CLI path or names its owning open parity bead per rule 5. Do not claim an existing zoom CLI
without checking it; respect the documented local-view exception.
- Shape/action geometry reuses existing metrics/settings. Rule 6 is satisfied by documented
configuration or an explicit supported fixed-geometry rationale on this bead; the alternative-style
setting belongs to bead 2.

## Implementation Notes

1. Prime the current owners and references. State observable behavior and the cheapest falsifier
before code. Reconcile current VEN-C8/C18/C21/C30 presentation wording and any actual boundary/CLI
changes through the normal overseer approval path.
2. Build one title/action geometry and one action model that Rex-like can reuse. Reuse the existing
title shaping, input routing, focus treatment and error/confirmation paths.
3. Update maintained docs/help/accessibility and add meaningful geometry/action regression coverage.
An initial dual-notch-only implementation is the deliberate dependency boundary, not a compatibility
mode.

## Verification

Follow current repository proof rules: changed-crate fmt/clippy with all targets, affected Venus
tests (and Runtime/CLI tests only if changed), exact-tree whole-workspace eon-test before review,
then an isolated installed observation. Full-window captures: 1280x800 and narrow; one/three columns
and collapsed pane; dark/light and real opacity 0.8; focused/unfocused controls and
zoom/restore/guarded close. No package build as author proof except a candidate needed for installed
observation. Overseer runs fresh Claude/Codex review and lands; do not restart live supervisors.

## Stop Conditions

Stop for an actual undecided product/boundary choice, an action whose target cannot be identified
safely, or a required out-of-scope protocol/lifecycle change. Re-read current rules and code when
the cited base has drifted. Do not convert exploratory patches into production code wholesale.

## Maintenance Notes

This should fit one fresh agent session. Subsequent discussion asked for an opinion on a
triple-notch variant (title / zoom / close); the recommendation was dual-notch, keeping the two
actions grouped. That question did not itself change the approved pair. Record any later explicit
user choice before implementation. No new triple-notch option/setting is authorized by this bead.

  <- eon-2ibdd (blocks) - Add Rex-like pane headers and a dual-notch/Rex-like setting

comments.text:
Landing record (eon-overseer, 2026-11-10). Author: eon-title-notch pane agent. Records: ~/.cache/eon-agents/eon-title-notch-work/bead/ (00-plan through 07-bead-comment-draft). Reviews: Codex title-notch-codex-1, title-notch-recheck-codex-1 (land); Opus title-notch-opus-1 (land), title-notch-recheck-opus-1 (land).

## Chosen scope and Lucca's decision

Lucca chose dual notches first, with Rex-like as the second selectable style. His
words were “we dont need to prototype / we can just add it”, “it's decided”, and
“i dont want to see anything, the design is already decided, but i agree that these
are very important” (2026-11-10; decision/reference record and bead comments).
His split explicitly allowed “you can first add the notch” and put close/zoom in
a second bead. This change therefore ships only the left pane-title notch.
Right zoom/close controls remain eon-ipc6f; Rex-like/style selection is eon-2ibdd.
No captures were requested from Lucca for approval; author captures served proof
and the independent reviewers.

Framed first, lone and zoomed pane titles use the shared fitted notch/S return.
Interior collapsed lower edges mirror it; the final collapsed bottom title keeps
a compact gap. Insufficient clearance falls back safely. Keyboard focus colours
the existing contour; hover fills the whole notch. Fitting reserves scrollback's
right limit and is ready for the future action slot. Padding follows the contour;
terminal opacity, grids, hit targets and accessible full names keep their owners.
No new window action, CLI, wire, lifecycle, configuration key or dependency.
Portability disposition: neutral shared scene/render code; proved observation is
x86_64 Linux/native Wayland/Vulkan, not a Darwin GUI claim.

## Explicit VEN-C8/VEN-C18 approval

Approved by **eon-overseer under Lucca's standing auto-approval for minor items
through the overseer**, recorded in INBOX 2026-11-10T04:59:13Z and confirmed by
Opus's re-check. Lucca's design choice was already settled. Exact amendment scope:
pane titles share the fitted notch; interior lower/final-collapsed and clearance
exceptions; focus on the existing contour and hover inside it; decorative caps add
no hit/accessibility area, height or terminal rows. No boundary guarantees change.
VEN-C21 and VEN-C30 are unchanged. This approval and proof are to be imported into
eon-7xryp in the landing commit, not left only in the disposable work directory.

## Rule 6 — fixed geometry

The shape derives from configured font size/line height and existing title padding,
border/focus widths and colours. Terminal-backed fill retains background_opacity.
Separate rise, curve and padding controls would multiply combinations that must
simultaneously clear neighbouring ink, joined frames, tiny windows and the footer.
That support cost outweighs independently tuning each parameter; existing typography,
stroke/colour and opacity settings already govern its scale and appearance. The
alternate style setting belongs to eon-2ibdd. No independent notch-count/style knobs
or compatibility mode were added. Import this rationale into the bead at landing.

## Proof and identities

Base: 1d58067d087217b3d7d5e3a2988e08c70c835c1b.
Final source tree: dedc0adecbf471d9526051973e684384996f0e20.
Environment: x86_64 Linux, pinned Nix dev shell (Rust/Cargo 1.96.1); Rust suites in
eon-test isolation, heavy runs through heavy.sh at nice 19/CARGO_BUILD_JOBS=6.

- Final fmt --check and Venus `cargo clippy --locked -p yazelix-venus --all-targets
  -- -D warnings`: PASS.
- Narrow post-review `heavy.sh timeout 30m nix develop -c eon-test -p yazelix-venus`:
  PASS, 372 passed / 0 failed / 13 ignored, including lib/bin/canonical scene,
  production layout, scrollback-gap, cache-invalidation, ink/joins, hover and padding.
- Final exact-tree whole-workspace `heavy.sh timeout 60m nix develop -c eon-test`:
  **PASS, exit 0: 35 summaries, 1,165 passed / 0 failed / 68 ignored**, including
  final Venus lib/bin/canonical scene, all four notch/cache/padding regressions,
  downstream workspace suites and installer. Exact tree/base unchanged; authoritative
  result collected from job session 12407 and landing-workspace.exit. Log retained
  as landing-workspace.log. No unstaged/untracked source or staged whitespace errors.
  The earlier 1,164-pass workspace result was for original tree 46c62969 and is not
  reused as a whole-workspace proof of the corrected final tree.
- Native Cargo candidate composed with existing Eon 0.1.22/Orbit, no profile changes:
  27 original acceptance captures covered dark/light, 0.8 real opacity over non-black
  wallpaper, narrow, expanded/collapsed, focused/unfocused, hover, zoom and popup.
  Corrected-tree native scrollback/whole-notch hover/F6 full-window observations PASS;
  the stroke stays out of the capsule and the raised cap fills. Hashes and component
  identities are in captures/review-manifest.json. All private PIDs cleaned; user
  desktop focus and live supervisors were untouched.
- No Nix package build/profile refresh by this worker. The overseer's landing owns
  that delivery proof/synchronization. No Tier 2 gate or Darwin GUI proof claimed.
  Existing light-title/Agents contrast remains eon-0kq2c. An earlier private startup
  attempt hit EAGAIN before pane geometry in the unchanged transport owner; it is
  recorded separately, not fixed or attributed to this feature.

All attempted checks, including failures, were recorded in 02-proof.md. Source
changes stayed in this detached worktree; no author commit, branch, br write,
profile refresh, push or GitHub post.

## Independent review rounds

One full fresh review of 46c62969 by Codex and Opus, then each finder's re-check of
its own findings on dedc0ade. The author ran no independent reviews.

Round 1 Codex found the blocking scrollback-contour gap and stale Stack changelog
promise. Both fixed: the reflected replacement contour now subtracts physical
rule gaps before union; compact/notched regression reproduced red and passed green;
real scrollback/F6 captures confirm it. Superseded plain-title assertions removed.

Round 1 Opus requested durable contract approval/rule 6 records, real production
layout coverage instead of a test-supplied None, a shaping sanity number, and full
hover-cap fill. All addressed: records above, tests call the production layout
owner and check actual footer containment, complete contour hover, and one bounded
latest-input cache after measurement demonstrated repeated-layout cost. Cache key
includes complete workspace geometry/metadata, metrics, both physical strokes and
scrollback; resize clears it, colours/hover/focus remain drawn fresh.

Re-checks: title-notch-recheck-codex-1 says **land**, including supported cache-key
completeness/boundedness; title-notch-recheck-opus-1 says **land**, with approval and
rule 6 records to accompany landing. No code blocker remains. Reports built/ran
nothing and confirmed the candidate tree; author proof supplies checks.

## Cache sanity measurement (not a performance gate)

Overseer 2026-11-10T05:01:52Z explicitly waived a quiet slot for this focused sanity
number. Actual native rebuild_if_needed + queue submit/drain, debug profile,
1280x800, warm fonts; same-process A/B/A/B, eight blocks per path, 25 calls per
block, process CPU clock. A uses compact titles; B uses notches and contoured
padding. These are median block-mean CPU microseconds/call, not shipped frame latency.

| Case | Old | New | Ratio | Delta |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| 1 column ×4, before cache | 110,669.898 | 111,598.266 | 1.00839 | +0.839% |
| 3 columns ×4, before cache | 111,054.356 | 124,118.973 | 1.11764 | +11.764% |
| 1 column ×4, cached | 128,504.313 | 138,855.285 | 1.08055 | +8.055% |
| 3 columns ×4, cached | 150,089.940 | 150,871.390 | 1.00521 | +0.521% |

The three-column repeat cost justified bounded fitted-title reuse. The cached
one-column run was variable (old blocks 112.195–151.546 ms/call; new blocks
113.242–178.648), unlike the first +0.839%; it does not establish a repeatable
one-column cost or evidence of no regression. Both re-checkers accepted the bounded
cache and the honest measurement limit. No further speculative optimization or
broad speed claim. Temporary measurement hooks were removed before final checks.

For eon-ipc6f: reserve its action slot before fitting both title and scrollback;
keep those slots distinct. This bead draws no right action notch or controls.

comments.text:
Flow ideas for Eon (Lucca 2026-11-09: "extract ideas from https://getflowterm.app/, save relevant ones to a bead"). Read from every /docs page, the changelog index and the repo (getflowterm.app/docs/{getting-started,workspaces,agents,agents/claude-code,agents/codex,agents/opencode,settings,configuration,keyboard-shortcuts}, /changelog, github.com/thetinygoat/flow). Checked against Eon beads by keyword; "new" means no bead found. Ideas, not decisions.

Agents
1. Per-launch agent hooks with no user config written (new; compare eon-ed9d.1/.5/.6, which ship opt-in hook installers). Flow's shell shim starts Claude Code with `--settings` merging hooks for SessionStart, UserPromptSubmit, Pre/PostToolUse, Notification, Stop, StopFailure, SessionEnd; Codex with `-c hooks.<Event>=...` for SessionStart, UserPromptSubmit, Pre/PostToolUse, PermissionRequest, Stop, Interrupt, SessionEnd; OpenCode with a plugin through OPENCODE_CONFIG_CONTENT. Each hook calls a helper that reports status. `FLOW_AGENTS_DISABLED=1` opts out per launch. Eon could report exact agent state (working / needs permission / waiting for input / done) to the attention inbox this way, instead of inferring it, and keep the user's agent config untouched.
2. Use Codex's own alerts: Flow sets `tui.notifications`, `tui.notification_method = "osc9"`, `tui.notification_condition = "always"`, so Codex emits OSC 9 the terminal can read (new; cheap if Orbit/Venus already parse OSC 9).
3. Status priority and clearing: needs-you outranks working outranks done; done clears when the terminal is viewed; subagents do not change the dot; Reduce Motion stops the pulse (compare Eon's attention inbox and agent sidebar).
4. Agent jump order (Cmd+I): current, waiting, finished, idle, working; longest-waiting first within a group; across all windows (compare Alt+G / Alt+Shift+G and Alt+Q).
5. Paste an image: saves a PNG and pastes its path, so terminal agents get images (new).

Navigation
6. One palette over every tab and pane, most recently used first, filtering by workspace, folder, tab, pane or agent name (related: eon-5za8 command palette decision).
7. Hold the modifier and tap to step through the list, release to go; a quick double tap returns to the previous place (a "jump back" toggle; new).

Notifications
8. Notify only for terminals not in view; click focuses that terminal; title is the workspace; identical repeated asks do not re-notify; reason text ("Needs permission", "Waiting for your input"); per-event sound and notification toggles (compare eon-2kvr).
9. Command-finished notification: never / when not visible / always, with a minimum duration, success and duration in the text, optional bell (new).

Workspaces and restore
10. Sidebar entry shows git branch with `*` for uncommitted changes; the name comes from the git repo root, so it stays stable in subfolders (new for Eon's session and tab labels).
11. Lazy restore: restored terminals start their shell on first view, showing the target folder until then (relevant to reboot restore; Eon keeps live terminals through Orbit otherwise).
12. Tab bar appears only with two or more tabs; dim unfocused panes as an option (new, configurability).

Safety and input
13. Links in terminal output are checked before opening (Flow 0.4.0; compare VEN-C5 and eon-onvk0).
14. Secure keyboard entry at password prompts on macOS (new; macOS launch, eon-mac-launch-kz4p).
15. Kitty clipboard protocol (Flow 0.4.0; check Venus support).

Recommended first: 1 and 2 (exact agent state without touching user config), 9, 7, 10. Each would be its own small bead after Lucca picks.

title: Let eon pane create add a pane to another tab (--tab)
description:
## Why

On 2026-10-22 the coordinator agent, running in the eon tab's Agent popup, started a Starcompass
agent with `eon pane create --json -- env -C ~/pjs/lab/starcompass claude "..."`. The pane landed
in the eon tab (p7), because pane commands act on the calling terminal's tab (EON-C10). Lucca
asked: "can you move the starcompass agent to the starcompass tab?" No Eon command can do that.
`eon pane create` can't target another tab, and `eon pane move` only moves within the tab. Lucca
asked for this bead ("file it", 2026-10-22).

## Proposal (not approved; contract wording goes to Lucca first)

Recommended: `eon pane create --tab TAB [--no-focus] [--json] [-- COMMAND...]` adds the pane to tab
TAB (an ID from `eon session --json`) instead of the caller's tab. Without `--tab`, behavior is
unchanged. Whether `--tab` also switches the active tab follows the eon-zhjj focus rule: by
default the target tab and new pane are selected, and with `--no-focus` nothing changes.

Alternative: let `eon pane move` move a pane to another tab. Rejected as the first step. It needs
two commands for the launch case, and moving a live terminal between tabs is a larger change to
the session model. File it separately if users ask for it.

## Reference gate (to do before code shape)

This is consequential: an EONW wire change and an EON-C10 contract change. Record comparable
implementations at inspected revisions: tmux `split-window -t target-pane`, Zellij
`action new-pane` with its tab targeting, kitty `launch --match`/`--type`, WezTerm
`cli split-pane --pane-id`. Note how each names the target and whether targeting another tab
changes focus.

## Current evidence (2e93c69)

EONW v40 still has CreatePane { focus } at v40.rs:185 and CreateCommandPane { argv, focus }
at :257 without a tab target. The session rename and eon-zhjj are closed. Coordinate the next
free EONW with popup Show's reserved v41 and other in-flight bumps; never replace a landed schema.
Coordinate the same pane-create surface with eon-agent-parity-a9g0.21 (--dir, Lucca 2026-11-09),
without absorbing its scope. The overseer kept this bead separate and before eon-j9wyn on 2026-11-10.

At contract approval settle the recorded hidden-session question (EON-C33): may --tab name a tab
outside the addressed session, and what does default focus do then? --no-focus must preserve shown
session, selected pane and popup as well as active tab. Do not infer a new session switch from the
original proposal; record the choice before approving the exact amendment.

## Prerequisites

- eon-zhjj lands first. It changes the same two requests (`WorkspaceAction::CreatePane`,
  `Action::CreateCommandPane`) and defines the focus rule this bead reuses.

## Scope

In scope: the EON-C10 text (Lucca approves the exact wording before code); the next free EONW
version carrying an optional target tab on both pane-create requests; Runtime validation (an
unknown tab is a target-not-found error, exit 3); CLI parsing; `eon --help`; `docs/USAGE.md`;
`CHANGELOG.md`; the affected component graph/manifest in the same coherent change, per the current one-commit rule.

Out of scope: moving existing panes between tabs; `eon edit --tab`; creating panes in another
window.

## Acceptance

- From the eon tab's Agent popup, `eon pane create --tab t3 --no-focus -- sh -c 'sleep 30'` adds
  a pane in t3's selected column. In `eon session --json`, t3 lists the pane, and the caller's
  tab, popup, selected pane and shown session are unchanged.
- An unknown TAB exits 3 and changes nothing.
- Exercise default focus and --no-focus against the approved targeting rule.
- Without --tab, behavior is identical to before, including exact argv for command panes.

## Verification

Codec wire tests, a Runtime unit test for the cross-tab target and the unknown tab, and the CLI
end-to-end test in `eon/crates/eon/tests/workspace_control.rs`, through `nix develop -c eon-test`.
Full affected Rust and Nix surfaces for the wire change, plus one isolated installed observation.

title: Discovery fails when an Orbit host exits between the record read and the socket check
description: Found while diagnosing eon-j7zfg (plan: /home/lucca/.cache/eon-agents/eon-runtime-flakes-work/bead/j7zfg-00-plan.md). sessions::untracked_runs can read a Live run record and see its Orbit host still running; the host then publishes its tombstone and removes its presentation socket in host::exit before validate_management_identity(..., true) stats the socket, so discovery returns 'cannot inspect terminal endpoint ... terminal-N.sock' instead of treating the run as ending. EON-C8 makes column close fail safely when discovery cannot list untracked runs, but any discovery consumer (column close, session listing, attach, reconciliation) can fail transiently for one exiting terminal. Expected: a socket that vanishes while its host is exiting (tombstone present, or the host gone on re-check) is an ended run, reconciled by discovery, not an error; any other missing socket still fails closed. Acceptance: a deterministic test that removes the socket between the record read and the stat (no sleeps) and gets the ended-run result; existing fail-closed cases unchanged; EON-C8/EON-C15 text checked (amend only if behavior they promise changes, with overseer approval); fmt, clippy, eon-runtime suite, whole-workspace eon-test.
close_reason: Discovery rereads the record once after a failed endpoint check and reconciles only the same run if it ended; fmt, workspace clippy, eon-runtime suite and whole-workspace eon-test pass on the merged tree; Codex and Fable: land

Landing record (eon-overseer landing helper, 2026-11-11).

Change: sessions::untracked_runs, on a failed live-endpoint check of a Live record, rereads that record once and reconciles only the same run: a tombstone carrying the equal LiveIdentity goes through the existing tombstone reconciler (moved unchanged into reconcile_tombstone), and the same Live record at the same inode with a dead host is retired by retire_dead_run. Any other outcome (host still running, another run's record, no record) returns the first endpoint error; an unreadable record returns its read error. No retry, sleep or new timeout; ORB-C13's order (tombstone before socket removal) makes one read sufficient. A private discover_untracked_runs carries a test seam closure; the public signature and its four supervisor callers are unchanged. EON-C8, EON-C15 and ORB-C13 unchanged. title: Accept Claude quota readings whose weekly window CodexBar repeats
description:
Since 2026-10-31 17:13 UTC-3 every Claude quota read is rejected, so the Claude chip shows a stale reading marked old (21% left while the live value is 18%, the 5h chip gone at its 19:00 reset).

Cause (proven 2026-10-31 by running Eon's exact CodexBarCLI 0.74.1 command): CodexBar now returns primary and secondary both as windowMinutes 10080 with identical resetsAt and usedPercent, no 5h window, plus an extraRateWindows entry 'Fable only' (eon-wqkjc). runtime/crates/eon-runtime/src/quota.rs normalize rejects any reading with two windows of the same duration (quota.rs:83-87); a failed read keeps the old reading unsaved. Inference: Anthropic's usage API stopped returning the five-hour window and CodexBar copies the weekly one into primary.

Fix: when two windows have the same duration and are identical (reset and used percent), keep one; keep rejecting same-duration windows that differ. Fits EON-C27 as written ('every supplied supported window'), no contract change. Test with today's payload shape. Also check whether a newer CodexBar release changes the mapping (do not bump it here without a reason).

Acceptance: a reading with identical duplicate weekly windows yields one 7d window; differing duplicates still fail; installed: the Claude chip loses 'old' within one read cycle after the profile refresh.
close_reason: Installed observation passed on 0.1.10: Claude chip fresh, Fable scoped chip present, no failure

title: Propose Ratconfig to Ratty as its settings screen, after Eon's Config popup
description:
## Why

Lucca, 2026-11-11: "think if it would be nice to open a pr to the ratty terminal, made by ratatuis
creator, adding ratconfig support in ratty, and a key to call it", then "open the beads you think make
sense in ratconfig / i can improve it before opening the PR / and you can open a bead in eon to track
that". Ratty (github.com/orhun/ratty) is a Ratatui and Bevy terminal by Orhun Parmaksız, Ratatui's lead
maintainer (Ratatui's original creator is Florian Dehau, of tui-rs). A Ratconfig settings screen there
is the most visible showcase Ratconfig can get, and a host outside Lucca's own projects tests whether
its host API is general. Not an Eon product change: this bead only tracks the outward proposal.

## Findings (orhun/ratty main, 2026-11-11)

- 0.6.0 on crates.io, MIT, 3.3k stars; merges outside pull requests; CONTRIBUTING.md asks for an issue
  first for larger changes. No existing issue or pull request about a settings screen.
- `ratatui = "0.30"` (Ratconfig: 0.30.2), terminal surface is a Ratatui buffer through
  `bevy_terminal_ratatui`: Ratconfig can draw in-window as an overlay.
- `ratty.toml` from serde structs in `src/config.rs` (about 60 fields); key bindings are a list of
  `{ key, with, action }` mapped to `BindingAction`, so an `OpenConfig` action with a default key (for
  example Ctrl+Shift+comma, a common settings key) fits.
- Issue #111 "Config changes not applied": users struggle with the file; whether Ratty reloads config
  while running is unconfirmed.
- Ratty uses `toml` 0.8, Ratconfig `toml` 1.x: Ratty upgrades or carries both.

## Ratconfig work first (Ratconfig repository, epic ratconfig-5m2)

- ratconfig-5m2.1 publish on crates.io (a crates.io package cannot depend on git; publishing needs
  Lucca's go).
- ratconfig-5m2.2 render into a host-chosen area, with an overlay example for a non-crossterm host.
- ratconfig-5m2.3 read descriptions, defaults, bounds and enum variants from a `schemars` JSON Schema,
  so Ratty does not hand-write a second field list.
- Related control gaps Lucca may close first: ratconfig-0ly bounded numbers, ratconfig-wbj chord
  capture, ratconfig-dxs add/remove entries, ratconfig-oxk colour previews.

## Plan

1. After Eon's Config popup lands (eon-s0oj.4), so Ratconfig has a second shipped host, and after the
   Ratconfig work Lucca chooses.
2. Prototype on a personal fork of Ratty: overlay, `OpenConfig` binding, fields from a derived schema;
   capture a screenshot.
3. Draft the Ratty issue (proposal, screenshot, dependency and reload notes) and show Lucca the exact
   text before posting: it is public and outward.
4. Open the pull request only if Orhun welcomes it.

## Done when

The issue is posted with Lucca's approval, and either the pull request is merged or declined, or Lucca
drops the idea; record the outcome here.

## Notes

- Outward-facing: every post on GitHub stops for Lucca first. Never include personal details beyond his
  public GitHub identity.
- Rule 7 (outside contributions) is about code coming into Eon; this goes out, so it does not apply.

title: Refresh Eon and Eonova to accepted native paste
description:
Contract: new x86_64 Linux launches from the named Eon and Eonova Nix profiles consume accepted Venus source eb67dac509d0c6033e4373caf8c63eb6e4c88868 with partially proved VEN-C10. Ctrl+Shift+V and the native Paste key use the ordinary native clipboard and one canonical ORB-C5 semantic paste; Orbit alone owns normal and bracketed encoding. Existing live runtime generations and Sessions remain on immutable artifacts and are not stopped or restarted. A failed pin, manifest, lock, build, publication, profile refresh, artifact comparison, or installed paste check leaves the rollout incomplete.

title: Steer installs to the main and edge branches; advance main at every release
description:
## Why

Lucca, 2026-11-05, after Ronald switched to edge to get the `cd` fix: "this is more ergonomic.. we should steer users to use either edge or main. we could update main whenever we release ... like nova". Pinned tag installs (`github:Yazelix/eon/v0.1.12`) never follow fixes: `nix profile upgrade` keeps the tag, and moving needs remove and re-add. A branch install upgrades in place with `nix profile upgrade --refresh eon`.

AGENT-RULES Git Workflow already sets `stable ⊆ main ⊆ edge`, with `main` and `stable` created at the first promotion; until then releases are tags on edge. Nova runs that model today: docs/development.md "Edge, main, and stable" and docs/installation.md "Release channels" in Yazelix/nova.

## What

1. **Channels.** `main` is the release channel. Each release advances it to the exact released edge commit (fast-forward, no merges or cherry-picks), next to an immutable `vX.Y.Z` tag. `edge` is the dogfood channel. `stable` stays deferred until Lucca wants a slower channel.
2. **First promotion.** Create `main` at the next release's commit (v0.1.13; see the open release question on eon-5y25o). Pushing a branch is outward: do it only on Lucca's go for that release.
3. **Docs.**
   - README "Get started" and docs/USAGE.md install `github:Yazelix/eon/main`, with edge offered for people who want fixes first.
   - An Update section: `nix profile upgrade --refresh eon`, then a new window.
   - A one-time move for tag installs: `nix profile remove eon`, then add main.
   - Tags are named only as exact-release references.
4. **Rules.** AGENT-RULES Git Workflow says that main advances at every release, and how: the Nova promotion check sequence (`merge-base --is-ancestor` both ways, then review `log` and `diff` of the range, then `git push origin <sha>:main`). CHANGELOG notes the install change.
5. **Follow-ups (not here):** whether the Eon bar shows the channel (Nova shows `NOVA <ver> <CHANNEL>`), and whether CI or cache publishing keys on main.

## Acceptance

- `git ls-remote` shows main at the v0.1.13 commit, and `stable ⊆ main ⊆ edge` holds.
- `nix profile add --refresh github:Yazelix/eon/main` installs, and `nix profile upgrade --refresh eon` follows main.
- README, USAGE, CHANGELOG and AGENT-RULES are updated in the same change as the first promotion, so no doc points at a branch that does not exist yet.
close_reason: v0.1.16 released; main created at the release commit

title: Make the eon CLI scriptable by agents in their own pane
description:
## Why
"Made for coding agents" (README.md:21) needs a CLI an agent can script without guessing. Today an
agent running `eon` inside a pane cannot tell failure kinds apart by exit status, and workspace
commands act on whatever tab is active, not the agent's own. Superlogical Rex (Mitchell Hashimoto's
multiplexer; public macOS test since 2026-10-05) treats its `rex` CLI as the agent control surface:
`--json` on most commands, a fixed exit-code table (0 ok, 1 failed, 2 bad command line, 3 target
missing or ambiguous, 4 server unreachable, 130 interrupted), ambiguous targets that change nothing,
and `REX_SESSION`/`REX_BLOCK`/`REX_SERVER` in every Rex terminal so the CLI targets its caller.
Source: secondary write-up https://www.bitdoze.com/superlogical-rex/ (read 2026-10-19); Rex is not
open source, so it is a behavioral reference only.

## Decision
Lucca, 2026-10-19: plan a Rex-style scriptable CLI for agents (planning only; each child still needs
contract approval before code).

## Already owned elsewhere (do not duplicate)
- Discovery of valid actions, symbolic error codes in structured output, bounded `wait`:
  `eon-cli-action-discovery-ogzi` (deferred).
- Reading a terminal's screen: `orb-p92`. Sending input: `eon-agent-terminal-control-n8ic`.
- Native command runner UI: `eon-command-runner-uctp`. Agent attention: `eon-agent-sidebar-yx8`.
These consume this epic's exit codes and caller identity; none is a prerequisite.

## Acceptance
- An agent in any Eon pane can run workspace commands that act on its own tab/pane by default and
  branch on documented, stable exit codes, with `--json` output unchanged in meaning.
- EON-C10 records both behaviors, approved by Lucca, with proof per child.

## Children
1. Distinct, documented exit codes for every `eon` command (runtime-only, no EONW change).
2. Caller-relative targets: terminals carry their Eon identity; commands default to the caller's
   tab/pane (consequential: environment contract and likely an EONW change).

## Scope boundary
No event stream, MCP server, plugin API, remote control listener, authorization framework, Lua or
other config scripting, or second action schema (EON-C10 boundary, docs/CONTRACTS.md:647-651).
close_reason: All three children closed with proof (8mnr.1 exit codes, 8mnr.2 caller-relative targets, 8mnr.3 exit 3 for unknown window IDs); EON-C10 records both behaviors (exit 3 unknown-caller, EON_TERMINAL targeting)

title: Give eon commands distinct, documented exit codes
description:
## Why
Every structured workspace failure exits 2 (`report_failure`, runtime/crates/eon-runtime/src/control.rs:617-624),
so a script cannot tell a typo from a missing target from a stopped supervisor without parsing
output. Rex documents a fixed table (0 ok, 1 failed, 2 bad command line, 3 target missing or
ambiguous, 4 server unreachable, 130 interrupted; https://www.bitdoze.com/superlogical-rex/, read
2026-10-19). See the parent epic for context.

## Evidence (edge 38cb1ea)
- `runtime/crates/eon-runtime/src/control.rs:617`: `report_failure` returns `Ok(2)` for every
  `Failure`, JSON or human.
- `runtime/crates/eon-runtime/src/control.rs:595`: failures already carry a symbolic code, e.g.
  `failure("malformed-action", ...)`; `missing_supervisor_is_a_structured_workspace_failure` exists.
- `eon/crates/eon/src/main.rs:5-14`: `main` clamps the runtime's `i32` to the process exit code.
- `runtime/crates/eon-runtime/src/cli.rs:437-470`: help lists the `--json` commands; no exit-status
  documentation exists in `docs/USAGE.md` or `docs/CONTRACTS.md`.

## Contract (provisional, needs Lucca's approval before code)
- Consumer: a script or agent invoking `eon` (and `eonbase`) commands.
- Result: each failure class maps to one documented exit status, identical with and without
  `--json`; success stays 0; output content is unchanged.
- Important failures: usage errors, unknown or stale target, supervisor unreachable or not started,
  rejected or unavailable action, timeout or lost response, interrupt.
- Owner: Eon Runtime's CLI projection; the mapping derives from the existing `Failure` codes, not
  from parsing text. Add it to EON-C10.

## Scope
In: `runtime/crates/eon-runtime/src/{control,cli}.rs` exit mapping; `eon --help` footer;

title: Let eon commands target the calling pane by default
description:
## Why
Workspace commands act on the active tab or selected column (`eon pane create` "creates a pane in
the active tab's selected column", docs/USAGE.md:218; `pane close PANE` targets "a pane of the
active tab"). An agent running in a background tab therefore changes the tab the user is looking at.
tmux (`TMUX_PANE`), WezTerm (`WEZTERM_PANE`, `wezterm cli --pane-id`), kitty (`KITTY_WINDOW_ID`,
`--match`) and Rex (`REX_SESSION`/`REX_BLOCK`, ambiguous targets change nothing) let the CLI target
its caller. See the parent epic for context.

## Evidence (edge 38cb1ea)
- `runtime/crates/eon-runtime/src/managed_environment.rs:660-725`: the runtime builds each
  terminal's environment (`EON_CONFIG_HOME`, `EON_SHELL_*`) but exports no tab, pane or terminal
  identity.
- `runtime/crates/eon-runtime/src/cli.rs:646-660`: `pane create` maps to
  `WorkspaceAction::CreatePane` with no target; `tab move`, `pane move` act on the active selection.
- `runtime/crates/eon-workspace-protocol/src/{v2,v3,v11}.rs`: identity-naming actions include `ClosePane`, `CloseTab`,
  `FocusId` and `SetTabDirectory`; `CreatePane` and the moves name none.
- EON-C10 target safety (docs/CONTRACTS.md:674-681): the runtime validates targets against its
  current Snapshot; identities are not reused after recovery.

## Contract (provisional, needs Lucca's approval before code)
- Consumer: a command run inside an Eon terminal (agent, script, editor).
- Trigger: a workspace command without an explicit target, run from an Eon terminal.
- Result: it acts on the caller's own tab/pane (resolved from an immutable terminal identity the
  runtime exports at spawn), not the active one; an explicit target overrides; outside Eon,
  behavior is unchanged. Focus is not stolen unless the command is `focus`.
- Important failures: ended or older-generation caller identity, closed caller pane, or ambiguous
  target change nothing and return the "target missing" status from the sibling exit-code child.
- Owner: Eon Runtime (identity export, resolution, validation); EONW carries any new target field
  under its versioning rules; Orbit and Venus unchanged.

## Reference gate (consequential: environment contract, likely EONW change)
Read docs/REFERENCES.md routes and inspect at exact revisions: tmux `TMUX_PANE` and `-t` resolution,
WezTerm `WEZTERM_PANE`/`cli --pane-id`, kitty `KITTY_WINDOW_ID` and `--match`. Record adopted and
rejected shapes (e.g. exporting mutable tab IDs vs the immutable terminal identity), the EONW
classification, and the cheapest falsifying check before code.

## Scope
In: terminal environment export, CLI target resolution and an explicit target flag, EONW target
fields if required, EON-C10 text after approval, USAGE/help, CHANGELOG.md.
Out: sending input or reading screens (`eon-agent-terminal-control-n8ic`, `orb-p92`), discovery
and wait (`eon-cli-action-discovery-ogzi`), popups' own targeting rules, Venus.

## Acceptance
- From a pane in an inactive tab, `eon pane create --json` adds a pane to that tab and leaves the
  active tab and desktop focus unchanged; from outside Eon it behaves as today.
- A stale identity (closed pane, stopped generation) changes nothing and exits with the documented
  target-missing status.
- Full affected Rust and Nix surfaces plus one isolated installed dogfood observation; converge
  review loop; ledger line here.

## Stop conditions
- Stop for Lucca's design and contract approval before code.
- Stop if the change would require exporting mutable identities or a Nix store path.
