comments.text:
Reference gate (edge b18f2cd). Contract proposal follows; needs Lucca's approval before code.

Behavior owners: Eon Runtime owns the identity export (sessions.rs orbit_command), the caller resolution and its validation (workspace.rs dispatch, today hard-wired to `self.active` and the selected column/pane), and the CLI projection (cli.rs parse_control_arguments, control.rs failure_status). EONW owns the request field. Orbit and Venus are unchanged; Venus sends no caller.

Routes read: docs/REFERENCES.md has no CLI-targeting route; the "agent-readable actions" route (TUIOS 0047c409185f) applies only as "one registry, stable errors". Read EON-C10, EON-C28, docs/ARCHITECTURE.md EONW boundary, runtime/AGENTS.md.

Comparables (read at these revisions):
- tmux 6f655f487338c0a49a3ec2052e559f73f4419c8a: TMUX_PANE=%N from a never-reused counter (spawn.c:415, window.c:61,1474) that follows the pane through join/break-pane. With no -t, a command from inside a pane uses TMUX_PANE only to pick the session, then targets that session's current window and active pane (cmd-find.c:913-928); a gone pane falls back silently (932-935). TMUX_PANE is not checked against the server.
- WezTerm e2a98e1b8af156988ad0ac778658ac27b60a55fb: WEZTERM_PANE at spawn (mux/src/domain.rs:479-482), monotonic IDs (mux/src/pane.rs:24-28), the mux server strips it from its own environment (wezterm-mux-server/src/main.rs:190-201). resolve_pane_id: --pane-id, else WEZTERM_PANE, else the focused pane (wezterm-client/src/client.rs:1314-1339). split-pane splits the caller's pane; a gone pane is an error ("no such pane"). spawn quietly opens a new window when the caller is unknown (lib.rs:1334-1352).
- kitty cda133cd26a573474d7cf2eb3cf04dd9684aafb0: KITTY_WINDOW_ID (tabs.py:858). The default depends on the command: those with a --self option default to the active window, the rest to the caller (rc/base.py:366-410); a stale ID falls back to the active window.

Kept: a pane-level (terminal-level) identity that is never reused and follows its terminal, resolved to a tab at request time; the server strips the variable from its own environment; a present but stale caller is an error, never a fallback (WezTerm split-pane).
Rejected:
- Exporting tab or pane IDs. Tab membership is mutable, and pane IDs are renumbered on same-boot supervisor replacement (workspace.rs with_recovered_sessions: p{session number}), so a pane ID can name a different pane later.
- Kernel-attested identity (tmux tty match, kitty tty transport). The runtime does not know PTY devices: Orbit owns them. This would need an Orbit management field plus Linux /proc lookups (AP-PORTABILITY-001), for a same-user tool that has no trust boundary to defend.
- tmux's session-only use, kitty's per-command split, and every silent fallback.

Identity: Orbit session ID plus Orbit run ID (supervisor request_id(): pid-nanos-seq, sessions.rs:809), already in the management record. It is unique across generations, windows and fresh supervisors in the same generation, and it survives same-boot replacement, which keeps exact Orbit runs. So no generation or window field is needed: a foreign caller simply names no live terminal of the supervisor addressed. Windows already route through the inherited EON_WINDOW_RUNTIME_DIR.

EONW: every frame carries exactly v12 (v12.rs:1451-1453), with no negotiation. An optional caller on the request needs v13, and Venus moves with it in the same commit. Cost: the new eon cannot list or stop v12 generations, the same accepted cost as eon-igae.12.4. Only Lucca's own sessions run v12 (v0.1.1 ships an older version anyway), and EON-C28's lifecycle-codec promise binds only from 1.0.

Cheapest falsifiers: a Runtime unit test (caller in an inactive tab: pane create lands there and the active tab is unchanged; a stale caller changes nothing), an eon workspace_control integration test through the CLI with EON_TERMINAL set, and one isolated installed dogfood from a background tab.

title: Sessions owned by Eon, shown by windows (tmux model)
description:
## Why

Lucca, 2026-11-04, opened a second Eon window and could not find it in the Workspaces picker. Today each window is its own supervisor with its own workspaces, so what exists depends on which window you ask (evidence on eon-hyil8). Lucca thinks in tmux terms: a session is a persistent group of terminals, and a window is a view onto one. He approved that model, then deferred it: "we can create the beads for the new model, but lets defer it for now. i will try using the current system and learning from it". Revisit once he has used the current system and the decisions below are confirmed or revised.

## Decided (Lucca, 2026-11-04; details and evidence on eon-hyil8)

1. One supervisor per generation owns every session. Each window is a Venus process that this supervisor starts and that shows one session. This is tmux's model (one server, many clients), not Zellij's (one server per session).
2. Picking a session that another window shows moves it into the picking window. A session is never shown in two windows. Picking never raises another window.
3. The window that loses its session shows its most recent free session; if there is none, it closes quietly.
4. Closing a window ends only the session it shows.
5. "Session" replaces "workspace" in product text, the CLI and configuration. The former alias proposal is superseded by Lucca's 2026-11-04 "we dont want legacy code, brother": no aliases, shims or compatibility paths. People never see terminal IDs; JSON spells them `terminal-N`.

## Recommended, not yet confirmed

Lucca said "i mostly agree" without naming the part he disagreed with. Ask him before the contract is drafted.

- `eon attach` opens a window on the most recently shown session that no window shows; `eon attach NAME` picks one.
- Sessions on an older build's supervisor are listed as "older Eon", and picking one presents its own window instead of moving it.
- Implementation waits for a Claude quota window with room for a multi-agent epic.

## Accepted risk (explained to Lucca, 2026-11-04)

Shared fate. One supervisor serves every window, so a supervisor crash hits all of them. Terminals survive in Orbit, but recovery puts every terminal into w1/t1, so every window loses its layout, not just one. Restore-after-restart (eon-reboot-restore-im8y) softens this.

## Rejected before (eon-n77e, eon-new-eon-window-vkwl)

- Venus reconnecting to another supervisor (in-place switching). It needed about ten contract changes and a trust boundary where Venus picks a supervisor.
- Two windows viewing one terminal. Orbit allows one presentation client per terminal.

The chosen shape keeps one window per Venus (VEN-C23), and the supervisor launches every Venus as it does today.

## Acceptance

- In installed Eon, a second window's picker lists every session, marking the window that shows each.
- Picking moves the session without stopping a terminal.
- Closing a window ends only its session.
- `eon sessions` reports the same as the picker.
- All children are closed.

## Planned children (order)

1. Spike: one supervisor starts and owns two Venus windows.
2. Spike: move a live session between two Venus processes through Orbit's attach handover.
3. eon-hyil8: decide and draft the contract (blocked by both spikes).
4. Rename workspace to session, and hide terminal IDs.
5. `window new` joins the running supervisor; redefine `eon windows` and window stop/attach; assess shells that already carry EON_WINDOW_RUNTIME_DIR without adding compatibility paths; the approved transition/error policy is still a design question.
6. Cross-window session list, picking moves, fallback, and Alt+G across windows.
7. Close, detach and attach semantics, and older-build sessions.


## Pending transition question

Before eon-hyil8 (session ownership/naming decision) drafts contract text, Lucca must reconcile the clean rename with docs/AGENT-RULES.md Configurability's alias/tombstone requirement and choose how old config and inherited shell targeting are reported without shims or data loss. This pass changes neither rules nor contracts and does not activate the deferred epic. Current-workspace improvements stay ahead of it.

title: Spike: one supervisor starts and owns two Venus windows
description:
## Why

The sessions model (parent epic) needs one supervisor to start and own several Venus windows. Today a supervisor holds exactly one Venus, and each window is a separate supervisor in its own namespace. Prove the mechanism before anyone drafts contract text (small-beads rule: spike unproved mechanisms first).

## Evidence

- `runtime/crates/eon-runtime/src/supervisor.rs:1157`: `SupervisorState.venus: Option<PresentationProcess>`, one Venus.
- `supervisor.rs:2266-2269`: `Present` re-raises that one Venus.
- `supervisor.rs:402-454`: `venus_command` starts Venus.
- `runtime/crates/eon-runtime/src/windows.rs:221-295`: `eon window new` spawns a whole new supervisor under setsid with EON_WINDOW_RUNTIME_DIR.
- `venus/src/transport.rs:231-250`: Venus speaks EONW to its supervisor for snapshots and actions. `venus/src/transport.rs:507-518`: it attaches straight to Orbit sockets.
- EONW `Present` has no target (eon-n77e evidence). VEN-C23 keeps one window per Venus process; this spike keeps it.

## Scope

In scope: a throwaway branch or worktree proving that one supervisor can hold a list of Venus processes, each showing a different workspace from the same WorkspaceSet. It records what EONW needs: a per-Venus identity in snapshots and actions, and which workspace each Venus shows.

Out of scope: product CLI changes, contract text, merging the spike, and moving sessions between windows (the sibling spike).

## Acceptance

title: Spike: move a live session between two Venus windows through Orbit's attach handover
description:
## Why

Picking a session that another window shows moves it there (parent epic, decision 2). Orbit admits one interactive client per terminal, and only the PID named by AttachAllow; naming never ends an existing attachment. A move therefore needs a strict handover, and this spike proves it does not lose terminals or input.

## Evidence

- `orbit/docs/CONTRACTS.md:113-140, 819-825`: one presentation client, AttachAllow, and "naming never ends an existing attachment".
- ORB-C13: a lease moves only to a replacement after the supervisor is gone, so a move must stay within one supervisor.
- tmux `attach -d` detaches the other clients: /home/lucca/pjs/refs/tmux-3.8/cmd-attach-session.c:121-133.

## Scope

In scope: a throwaway proof, on top of the sibling spike's two-Venus supervisor, of this sequence for every terminal (panes and popups) of one session:

1. Venus A releases its Orbit attachments.
2. The supervisor names Venus B's PID.
3. Venus B attaches and resizes the terminals.

Include races: a key typed during the move, a terminal exiting mid-move, and Venus A dying mid-move.

Out of scope: product CLI, contract text, merging.

## Acceptance

A bead comment with:

- the handover order;
- each race and how it ends;
- whether Orbit needs any change (if so, name the ORB-C clause);
- a demonstration in isolated headless Sway that moves a session with a running program from window A to window B and back, with the program still running and its output intact.

## Verification

An isolated headless Sway observation. Never use Lucca's running Eon or its Orbit hosts.

## Stop Conditions

Stop if Orbit must allow two clients at once; that was rejected in eon-new-eon-window-vkwl.

title: Rename workspace to session in product text, CLI and config, and stop showing terminal IDs
description:
## Why

Lucca, 2026-11-04: "can we call it sessions instead of workspaces?" The sessions model makes the word accurate: tmux calls this a session. "Workspace" also means a virtual desktop on Wayland compositors such as COSMIC and Sway. Approved with the epic. Terminal IDs (`session-N`) would then give "session" two meanings, so people stop seeing them (Lucca, 2026-11-04, "agree").

## Evidence

- `eon --help`: the Workspaces section (`workspaces`, `workspace new/switch/rename/close`).
- `runtime/crates/eon-runtime/src/cli.rs:119`: the Commands entries (Rename workspace and others).
- Configuration keys under `[workspace]` (docs/CONFIGURATION.md).

## Scope

- Product text says "session" in the shortcut viewer, hints, picker title, Commands entries, Venus labels, docs (USAGE, CONFIGURATION, ARCHITECTURE naming boundary, AGENT-RULES Product Boundary), the packaged agent skill and CHANGELOG.
- The CLI adds `eon sessions` and `eon session new/switch/rename/close`, using only the approved current spellings; no `workspace` aliases or compatibility spellings are added (Lucca, 2026-11-04: "we dont want legacy code, brother").
- Configuration renames `[workspace]` keys only after Lucca resolves the conflicting alias/tombstone repository rule and approves old-key treatment. Retain corpus coverage of that approved transition; no aliases, shims or compatibility path are added.
- Human-facing output never shows terminal IDs; `eon windows` lists panes and popups (`p1`, `u1`).

## Acceptance

## Verification

- Converge plus Codex.

## Stop Conditions

description:
## Why

The losing window shows its most recently shown still-existing free session or closes quietly. Today the Sessions picker and `eon session ls` are per-window (docs/USAGE.md:733-737,864 at 6e63eb7).

## Scope and prerequisites

Runtime owns registry/session assignment and handover; Venus renders it and releases/acquires its Orbit attachments. Global picker rows and `eon session ls [--json]` mark the showing window. Use the eon-8mw1v.2 spike's handover for all pane and popup terminals: release A, authorize B, attach/resize B. Preserve the one-presentation-client rule. The window that loses the session falls back as decided, or only its view closes, without accidentally taking the user-close Stop path.

Wait for Lucca to resume deferred eon-8mw1v, approved exact contract text from eon-hyil8, and eon-8mw1v.4's multiple-window supervisor. Read both the two-Venus and handover spike records. EON-C8/C10/C23/C33 and any approved EONW changes belong to the eon-hyil8 contract decision; ORB-C3/C13 retain sole presentation/lease authority. Record the owning reference routes and the accepted tmux/session and Orbit handover evidence at exact revisions before code. Portability: neutral session policy; native handover proof is isolated Linux Wayland, with no new platform claim.

## Acceptance

- In two installed windows, both pickers and the CLI list the same sessions with showing-window identity; CLI targets a session/window by ID without moving the person's active window or selection unless the requested pick requires the move.
- Picking B's session into A keeps its running program/output and never lets two Venus clients present the terminal together. Include panes and popups.
- B falls back to the most recent existing free session, or closes its view quietly when none exists; neither case stops an unrelated terminal.
- The spike's mid-handover key, terminal-exit and old-Venus-death cases have the approved deterministic outcomes; stale picks fail honestly without losing topology.
- User docs, CLI JSON/help and CHANGELOG describe the same accepted behavior. No legacy `eon sessions` alias.

Cross-window listing/picking only; global Alt+G/attention is the sibling child, and close/detach/attach/older-build semantics stay in eon-8mw1v.6. title: Close, detach and attach per session, and list older builds' sessions
description:
## Why

The sessions model changes what closing, detaching and attaching mean (parent epic, decision 4, and two recommendations that still need confirming). Closing a window ends only the session it shows, which keeps eon-7cf0y's "closing the window quits it". Sessions that no window shows stay listed, so no work runs unseen.

## Evidence

- EON-C8 (docs/CONTRACTS.md:733-754 at 6e63eb7): closing a window quits every one of its sessions, and detach sends a desktop notice.
- EON-C11: `eon quit`, `eon stop GEN` and ambiguous-window.
- Runtime supervisor.rs::recover_sessions call (:1055 at 6e63eb7) still recovers terminals under a per-window supervisor; inspect the current recovery grouping rather than relying on the old w1/t1 line numbers.

## Scope

In scope:

- Closing a window, with its busy prompt, ends only its session.
- Detach (Alt+Shift+D) hides the window and leaves its session unshown.
- `eon attach` opens a window on the most recently shown unshown session; `eon attach NAME` opens a named one (confirm with Lucca first).
- Sessions on an older build's supervisor are listed as "older Eon", and picking one presents its own window (confirm first).
- `eon quit` and `eon stop` are redefined per the contract.

Out of scope: restore after a machine restart (eon-reboot-restore-im8y).

## Acceptance

In installed Eon:

- Closing one of two windows leaves the other window's session running.
- After a detach, `eon attach` brings back that session.
- After a profile refresh, an older build's session is listed and opens in its own window.

## Verification

- `nix develop -c eon-test` over the whole workspace before code review, plus one isolated installed observation.
- Converge plus Codex.

## Stop Conditions

## Planning split and gates

This is an epic with one child for current-generation close/detach/attach and another for discovery/presentation of older-build sessions. The original scope and three installed outcomes stay the parent acceptance; both children must finish. The older-build child follows the current-generation lifecycle child so its cross-generation exception is checked separately.

Neither this split nor the open status resumes the deferred eon-8mw1v model. Do not equate listing another generation with moving its terminals into this supervisor. No aliases, protocol-compatibility framework, live-supervisor restart or reboot persistence is added. title: Stop shipping Zsh and Fish as Eon managed shells
description:
## Why

User decision (Lucca, 2026-10-18): "we should not ship zsh and fish, makes no sense". Eon's managed environment (EON-C9) ships four shells. Zsh and Fish add maintenance, test and closure weight for little product value: Nushell is the default (`command = ["eon-nu"]`) and Bash covers the POSIX case. Users who want Zsh or Fish can still run their host shell as the direct argv command.

The bundle redesign (eon-zti4, decision record on eon-zti4.1) found a concrete cost. Fish pulls python3 (134 MB), coreutils, man-db, groff, gettext and util-linux into the closure, and Zsh links ncurses 6.6. Both raise the host glibc floor of the namespace-free bundle to GLIBC_2.42. Dropping them shrinks the payload and leaves ncurses 6.6 (libncursesw and tset, used by bash-interactive, readline and bc) as the only GLIBC_2.42 objects, so the later floor-2.39 work becomes an ncurses fix.

This decision authorizes removing Zsh and Fish from EON-C9's managed shell list. Any other EON-C9 change still needs separate approval.

## Evidence

- `components/eon-alpha-v3.json:10` lists `zsh` and `fish` in `tools`; their component entries start at :195 and :212.
- `flake.nix:130-131` (identities), `:317-321` (packages), `:336-344` (shell environment inputs), `:350-351` and `:479-480` (licences), `:456-463` (session command farm), `:500-510` (EON_ZSH, EON_FISH, EON_ZSH_CONFIG, EON_FISH_INIT wrapper env), `:562` (eonbase closure forbidden list) and `:572-579` (managed-command check).
- `nix/shell-environment.nix:3-54` (per-shell init generation), `:163-229` (zsh env/rc, ZDOTDIR config and its build check), plus the fish init.
- `eon/crates/eon/src/product.rs:115-124`: the `EON_ZSH`, `EON_FISH`, `EON_ZSH_CONFIG` and `EON_FISH_INIT` inputs.
- `runtime/crates/eon-runtime/src/managed_environment.rs` (38 matches), `sessions.rs` (2) and `fixtures.rs` (4): managed shell selection and its tests.
- `runtime/crates/eon-runtime/src/managed_environment.rs:214-215` maps bare `zsh`/`fish` to managed tools today; `managed_invocation_names_are_bounded` (:1315-1326) covers that mapping.
- `docs/REFERENCES.md:277-285` names Zsh and Fish as references.
- `docs/CONTRACTS.md:553-589` (EON-C9 consumer, result and proof mention Zsh and Fish); `docs/CONFIGURATION.md:134` (`eon-zsh`, `eon-fish`).

## Scope

In scope:
- Remove Zsh and Fish from the component manifest, the Nix composition (packages, licences, wrapper env, session commands `eon-zsh`, `eon-fish`, `zsh`, `fish`, the shell-init and config generation and their checks), the Eon product inputs, the runtime's managed-shell handling and its tests and fixtures.
- Bare `zsh`/`fish` stop mapping to managed tools (managed_environment.rs:214-215).
- Trim docs/REFERENCES.md:277-285 to what still applies to Nushell and Bash.
- Update EON-C9 to Nushell and Bash only, with the proof note that names the removed shells; also docs/CONFIGURATION.md and README if it lists them, and a CHANGELOG entry (user-visible: commands and packaged tools removed).

Out of scope:
- Nushell, Bash, Starship, Zoxide, Atuin, Carapace, Helix, Yazi and LazyGit behavior, and any other EON-C9 semantics.
- The bundle mechanism (eon-zti4 children), Orbit and Venus.
- A compatibility shim or migration for configs that name `eon-zsh` or `eon-fish`; they take EON-C9's existing explicit shell-launch failure path.

## Acceptance

- `eon versions` and the component manifest no longer list zsh or fish, and the eon closure contains no zsh or fish store paths (`nix path-info -r` of `.#default` has no `-zsh-` or `-fish-` entries).
- `eon-zsh`, `eon-fish` and the unprefixed `zsh`/`fish` managed commands no longer exist. A config with `command = ["eon-zsh"]` fails explicitly without a replacement terminal, as EON-C9 already specifies for a missing artifact; a host shell given as the direct command (for example `["zsh"]` from the host PATH) still launches as an unmanaged command.
- Nushell and Bash managed shells keep their EON-C9 behavior: Starship, Zoxide, Atuin and Carapace integration, and native user configuration loading.
- EON-C9 and docs describe exactly two managed shells.

## Implementation Notes

1. Start from the manifest and `flake.nix`; let manifest validation and the Nix build show every remaining consumer.
2. Remove the runtime and product handling, then the tests that only exercised Zsh or Fish; keep the Nushell and Bash coverage.
3. Edit EON-C9 (docs/CONTRACTS.md:550-600) to the two-shell set, plus CONFIGURATION, README and CHANGELOG.

## Verification

- `managed_invocation_names_are_bounded` asserts `None` for `zsh` and `fish`, so a host shell given as the direct command runs unmanaged.
- `nix develop -c eon-test` exits 0 (workspace and installer suites; never run inside a live Eon session's environment without that sandbox).
- `nix build .#default` and `nix flake check` exit 0; `nix path-info -r` of the result has no zsh or fish paths.
- Refresh the active `eon` profile element from the working tree and check that it resolves to the new store path. In one isolated installed dogfood observation, `eon versions` shows no zsh or fish, `eon-bash` and `eon-nu` start with their integrations, and a config naming `eon-zsh` fails explicitly. Do not restart the running supervisor; report that a restart is needed.

## Stop Conditions

- Stop if removal requires changing EON-C9 semantics beyond dropping the two shells.
- Stop if another component or contract depends on Zsh or Fish (for example a Carapace, Atuin or Helix integration that needs them).
- Stop if verification fails twice for the same reason after a reasonable fix attempt.

## Maintenance Notes

- Rejected: keeping Zsh and Fish as optional managed shells. The user decided they should not ship at all.
- Effect on eon-zti4: the namespace-free bundle's GLIBC_2.42 floor then comes only from Bash (ncurses 6.6), so the floor-2.39 work becomes an ncurses fix. Record this on eon-zti4.1 when this bead lands.
close_reason: Zsh and Fish removed from the managed shell set; proof and review ledger in comments

title: Let a person hide chosen quota windows, such as Claude's Fable chip
description:
## Why

Lucca, 2026-11-04: "start one to make the widget configurable (i personally never use fable for instance)".

`[bar] widgets` already chooses which providers' quota chips show (`codex_quota`, `claude_quota`). Inside a provider, though, every window the read reports gets a chip: Claude's 5-hour, its weekly, and each model-scoped weekly window such as `Fable 1d15h/7d 100%`. A person who never uses Fable cannot hide that chip, and it costs bar room. The Eon logo's room depends on the windows shown (eon-nfrbn).

## Scope

Configuration that hides chosen quota windows of a provider. Recommended shape, to settle in the contract draft:

```toml
[bar.quota]
hide = ["claude:Fable"]
```

Alternatives are `["claude:scoped"]` (all scoped windows) and duration keys (`"claude:5h"`).

- Default: hide nothing (today's behavior).
- An unknown entry is ignored with a warning, as other unknown keys are.
- The filter applies before Venus lays out the bar, so a hidden window takes no chip, no hover and no logo-room reservation. The read itself is unchanged.
- Decide where the filter lives: in Eon Runtime before the EONW quota fact (no Venus change), or as a Venus launch option.
- Rule 6: default and syntax in docs/CONFIGURATION.md, `eon config defaults`, and the configuration corpus fixture.
- Rule 5: `eon workspace --json` still reports every window (the data), so agents keep the full picture; only the chips are filtered. Say so in the docs.
- Related, not in scope: eon-iebt1, which makes a scoped chip show the lower of its own and the all-models remaining. Keep the two compatible.

## Contract

The configuration contract (EON-C9) and the bar contract (VEN-C21 or the EON-C quota section) likely need a sentence each. That is small contract text, approved by the overseer under Lucca's standing rule. A wire or EONW change would be major; avoid it.

## Acceptance

- With `hide = ["claude:Fable"]`, the bar shows no Fable chip, and the logo room counts only the shown windows.
- Without the key, the bar is unchanged.
- An unknown entry logs a warning and changes nothing.
- `eon workspace --json` still lists the Fable window.
- One isolated installed capture.

## Verification

- `nix develop -c eon-test -p eon-runtime -p eon` (plus `-p yazelix-venus` if Venus changes), fmt and clippy.
- The configuration corpus test.
- One isolated capture.
- Converge plus Codex.
close_reason: Landed on edge with its proof and review records

Example: `widgets = ["codex_quota", "claude_quota_5h", "claude_quota_7d", "cpu", ...]`, which leaves out Fable. Keep the provider-level names (`codex_quota`, `claude_quota`) meaning "all of that provider's windows", so existing configs keep working. Scoped windows such as Fable need a stable name; the contract draft settles the naming scheme. `eon workspace --json` still reports every window (rule 5). The rest of the bead (rule 6 docs, `eon config defaults`, corpus, the logo room counting only listed chips, the capture) stands.

title: Decide: pane labels that say what runs in the pane
description:
## Why

Lucca, 2026-10-24, asked the overseer "what do you think of our pane naming protocol", and on its
proposal: "your plan is good". Today each pane label is `pN`, two spaces, and a compact working
directory (EON-C8). In his screenshots every pane in a tab shows the same directory as the tab
(`~/pjs/games/machines_vs_aliens` four times), nothing says what runs in each pane, and workspace-
wide IDs grow (`p14 p15 p16` in a three-pane tab).

## Proposal to research (nothing decided)

- Keep `pN` (the ID agents use with `eon focus`, `eon pane close`) but dim it: the same label, the
  ID drawn in a lower-contrast colour than the rest, so the eye lands on the name.
- Then the terminal title the program sets (OSC 0/2; Claude Code sets its session name), falling
  back to the foreground command name.
- The working directory only when it differs from the tab's directory, written relative to it.
- `eon pane rename pN "<name>"` (and the matching window action) to pin a name; CLI parity per
  AGENTS.md "Humans and Agents".
- Examples: `p14  claude · eon-6ros review`, `p15  hx src/main.rs`, `p16  ../other-repo · cargo test`.

## Research path (overseer runs it, Lucca decides)

1. What Orbit already gives Eon for collapsed (unattached) panes: the metadata reply (working
   directory today), and whether the terminal title (ORB-C15, already on EONW v19 as
   attention.name) and the foreground command are available without attaching; contracts that
   would change (EON-C8 label clause, ORB-C metadata, EONW).
2. References at exact revisions: Zellij pane names and frames, tmux pane titles and
   automatic-rename, WezTerm/kitty tab and pane titles (local clones in ~/pjs/refs).
3. Mockups of 2-3 label styles over a real capture of a stacked tab.
4. Recommendation and contract wording for Lucca.

## Scope

Pane label content and the rename path. Out: tab labels, sidebar rows (they already use the
title), protocol work beyond what the chosen style needs.

Portability: neutral.
close_reason: Decided: PINNED labels without the process fallback; implemented by eon-a7xd

comments.text:
Landed: the compact shared list layout (option A, decided 2026-11-09T18:21Z under Lucca's delegation).

**What changed (Venus only, no contract change)**

- **One layout for every list dialog.** The Shortcuts viewer (Alt+/), the Window menu and the quit and close prompts share one layout. Each is sized to its content and kept between the Eon Bar and the hints bar.
- **Measured text.**
  - Label columns are as wide as their widest label, measured by the renderer.
  - Descriptions wrap at the width they draw in.
  - Each row is as tall as its renderer-shaped lines (`Renderer::dialog_text_lines`), cached per text and width at the current metrics.
- **Columns.**
  - Shortcuts flow into the fewest balanced columns, up to three, that show every row without scrolling. A section split across columns repeats its heading.
  - Columns are bounded by the dialog's width. A heading widens its column only into leftover width and is clipped beyond it.
- **Viewer rows and footer.**
  - Left / Right and Up / Down share one row each unless a popup takes either key.
  - The Shortcuts footer mentions scrolling only while rows overflow.
- **Attention inbox.** It keeps its rows and width and now sits between the bars too.
- **Unchanged.** Contract-quoted labels, dispatch descriptors, hints and AccessKit roles.

**Configurability (rule 6): why the new sizes stay fixed**

| Value | Fixed at |
| --- | --- |
| Row height | 1.3 lines, whole pixels |
| Each extra wrapped line | 1.25 lines |
| Section heading | 1.4 lines |
| Gap after a section | 0.5 lines |
| Gap between label and description | 1.5 paddings |
| Gap between columns | 2.5 paddings |
| Most columns, Shortcuts only | 3 |
| Narrowest description before giving up a column | 11 font sizes, or the widest description if narrower |
| Space kept clear at top and bottom | the Eon Bar's height plus one card gap, at most a twelfth of the window height |

- **Proportions of configured values.** Each is a proportion of the font size, line height, display scale and chrome padding, which people already configure. A denser or roomier dialog comes from the font size, like the rest of Eon's chrome.
- **No second owner.** A separate setting would give the dialog's density a second owner, and no user needs the dialog to differ from the chrome around it.
- **Layout limits.** The three-column cap and the description floor keep the reading order and line length readable; they are not a look people tune.

For the eon-8s8s7 bead record at landing.

The compact list layout adds these values for the Shortcuts viewer, the
Window menu, the quit and close prompts, and the attention inbox's frame:

| Value | What it is |
| --- | --- |
| Row height | 1.3 lines, rounded to whole pixels |

| Space kept clear at top and bottom | the Eon Bar's height plus one card gap, at most a twelfth of the window height |

They stay fixed, with no configuration key. Each is a proportion of values
people already configure:

- the font size and line height, through the terminal font settings;
- the display scale;
- the chrome padding, which derives from them.

A person who wants a denser or roomier dialog changes the font size, and every
one of these scales with it, the same as the rest of Eon's chrome. A separate
setting would give the dialog's density a second owner beside the font size,
and no user so far needs the dialog to differ from the chrome around it.

The three-column cap and the description floor keep the reading order (down

title: Print a redacted bug report with eon report
description:
## Why

K2 of ~/.cache/eon-agents/eon-ideas-work/ideas.md (Lucca's idea request,
2026-11-09; filed by eon-overseer's "auto-decide" note).

v0.2.0 brings outside users on unproved compositors and GPUs. The bug template
(.github/ISSUE_TEMPLATE/bug_report.yml) asks for versions, window, install
route, distribution, compositor and GPU, which users collect by hand
(docs/USAGE.md, Troubleshooting and reporting). The GPU field is optional and
usually blank, though it explains most rendering bugs.

## Scope

`eon report` prints one Markdown block with the template's fields filled in:
`eon versions`; the caller's window from `eon window ls --json`; install route
from the provenance `eon update --check` uses (EON-C41); distribution
(/etc/os-release PRETTY_NAME) or macOS version; compositor
(XDG_CURRENT_DESKTOP); configuration warnings once `eon config check` exists;
the last 40 lines of the newest supervisor log after redaction. Redaction:
`$HOME` becomes `~`, no environment values, never terminal content. It prints
and stops; the person reads it before sharing.

Later slices: `--url` printing a GitHub issue-form URL prefilled by field ID
(never opening a browser, desktop focus rule); the GPU adapter once
eon-venus-gpu-adapter-choice-qlgp logs it; `--json` only if wanted (it would
fall under EON-C28's stability rule).

Contract: none for human output (a feature). Owner: Eon Runtime/CLI. Docs:
USAGE Troubleshooting and the template's text point to it.

## Acceptance

- Output on a fixture matches the template's fields.
- A redaction test proves `$HOME` paths and environment values never appear.
- Rule 5: agents run the same command.

## Release gate

In the v0.2.0 gate (blocks eon-igae.9, eon-igae.7, eon-igae.8). Lucca, 2026-11-09: "you can add some or all to the release gate / we cant release without yu's ssh anyways".

title: Keep Eon windows answering under load, and say so plainly when one is slow
description: Lucca 2026-11-03 17:20Z: 'my laptop is slow, it was making eon irresponsive', with Venus showing 'Cannot read Eon workspace response header: Resource temporarily unavailable (os error 11)' (venus/src/transport.rs:291; WORKSPACE_EXCHANGE_TIMEOUT 6 s at :211, refresh every 250 ms at :79). Load was ~13 on 16 cores (three agents compiling Venus at -j4, reviews, CodexBarCLI near the top of the CPU list), 15 GiB RAM available: CPU alone should not delay a supervisor answer past 6 s. Approved 'agree' 2026-11-03. Scope: (1) find what blocks the single-threaded supervisor's request path under load (candidates: quota readings via CodexBar CLI, Orbit calls, attention polling, synchronous child waits) with timing evidence under a reproducible load (e.g. stress-ng on all cores in an isolated Eon); move the blocker off the request path so Inspect answers within a stated bound under that load. (2) Venus: a late or failed refresh shows a plain notice ('Eon is slow to answer' style, product text per rule 6) that clears itself on the next good answer, never raw OS error text; keep the last good frame. Contract text (EON-C/VEN-C for the answer bound or the notice) stops for approval. Proof: the isolated load reproduction before and after; installed proof.
close_reason: Both slices landed: d431fca (a close's terminal stops share one bound) and 1766afd (Venus says plainly when Eon is slow to answer or not answering; VEN-C8 amended). Follow-ups: eon-ih692, eon-u24pw, eon-pimct.

comments.text:
# eon-8wh7h record 01: investigation finding (comment)

Investigation result, 2026-11-04: a real blocker on the supervisor's request path, reproduced
with timing evidence in an isolated Eon. It was found under Lucca's condition ("only if we find
an actual bug to fix").

## Mechanism

The supervisor answers every control request on one loop thread (runtime supervisor.rs main
loop: reaps, tend, one accept per turn). Orbit lifecycle waits run on that same thread:

- the stops of a closed tab's terminals, one terminal after another;
- the wait for a new Orbit's record (25 ms polls, 5 s bound);
- end finalization.

While one of those waits runs, no request is accepted. Venus's Inspect waits behind it, and its
6 s read timeout (venus/src/transport.rs WORKSPACE_EXCHANGE_TIMEOUT) expires as EAGAIN:
"Cannot read Eon workspace response header: Resource temporarily unavailable (os error 11)".

## Reproduction

- Build: stock Eon 0.1.15 (installed profile, same runtime source as c5e922d).
- Setup: an isolated headless supervisor (stub Venus, private EON_RUNTIME_DIR, HOME and
  XDG_STATE_HOME), started by `~/.cache/eon-agents/eon-8wh7h-work/iso/start.sh`.
- Probe: `iso/probe.py` imitates Venus. It sends an EONW v31 Inspect with no caller, every
  250 ms, with a 6 s read timeout.

| Condition | Inspect latency |
| --- | --- |
| Idle | p50 2 ms, max 6.5 ms |
| CPU stress alone (stress-ng 16-24 cpu workers, load 18) with tab/pane churn (`iso/churn.sh`) | max 116 ms (not the cause) |
| IO+CPU stress (6 hdd writers + 16 cpu) with churn | max 1010 ms; `pane create` max 998 ms |

strace of the loop thread under IO+CPU stress: from 07:04:53.22 to 07:04:56.08 the thread
polled `session-29.sock.record` every 25 ms, waiting for a new Orbit. It made no accept4 call in
that time, and a probe Inspect waited 3758 ms. (strace slows the run; the untraced run peaked at
about 1 s.)

Closing a tab whose panes run a program that takes 1.5 s to exit on HUP/TERM (`iso/slowclose.sh`):
the stops run one by one, about 0.4-0.5 s each.

| Tab close | Close took | Inspect |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 6 terminals, no stress | 2751 ms | 2719 ms |
| 9 terminals, IO+CPU stress | 4410 ms | 4172 ms |
| 14 terminals, IO+CPU stress | 6992 ms | **TIMEOUT at 6011 ms** (Venus's exact failure) |
| 14 terminals, no stress-ng but system load 20 from other builds | 7079 ms | TIMEOUT |

## Ruled out

- CPU starvation alone.
- Quota readings: CodexBar runs on worker threads, and its fetch holds no lock the loop needs.
- Attention polling: nonblocking.
- No cgroup CPU limit on the Eon scopes.
- Lucca's supervisor logs around 2026-11-03 14:20 local show only short tab closes. They do not
  pin his incident to one action, so the evidence here is the isolated reproduction.

comments.text:
# eon-8wh7h record 02: reference gate (comment)

The change is consequential (AP-REFERENCE-001): it changes the EON-C8 contract text and a
lifecycle boundary, the stop of a closed tab's, pane's or workspace's terminals.

- **User-visible behavior and owners.**
  - Closing a tab, pane or workspace stops its terminals together under one shared five-second
    bound. The close then prunes each confirmed end, in close order.
  - If any stop fails, the close reports failure, and only the terminals whose end was not
    confirmed stay.
  - Owners:
    - Eon Runtime's supervisor owns the stop step (`stop_owned_sessions` in
      runtime/crates/eon-runtime/src/supervisor.rs) and the reconciliation bound
      (`session_finished_within` in sessions.rs).
    - The workspace owner (`WorkspaceSet::session_ended`) still owns pruning.
    - Orbit owns each terminal's own stop and its 500 ms grace (ORB-C12, unchanged).
- **Evidence read.**
  - EON-C8 and EON-C33 close text in docs/CONTRACTS.md.
  - ORB-C12 in orbit/docs/CONTRACTS.md, which sets the HUP, 500 ms, SIGKILL grace.
  - The supervisor loop and close path (supervisor.rs `stop_closed_sessions`, the old
    `stop_workspace_session`).
  - `stop_managed_sessions` (sessions.rs), with the existing tests on its silent-terminal and
    signal behavior.
  - docs/REFERENCES.md routes Orbit questions to Orbit's contracts. No external route applies
    to a supervisor-internal stop order.
- **Comparable implementation.** The in-repo comparison is generation Stop
  (`stop_generation_sessions`, supervisor.rs, as of c5e922d). It already passes every
  terminal to `stop_managed_sessions` in one call: Stop is written to every lease first, then
  the replies are read under one shared deadline. The new close step adopts that path rather
  than adding a mechanism (AP-MINIMAL-001).
- **Rejected approaches.**
  - **A pump that answers read-only requests during waits.** Medium size, with re-entrancy
    risk while state is mutably borrowed. It would also cover starts, which are out of scope.
  - **Deferred replies for terminal starts.** Filed as follow-up eon-pimct.
  - **Lifecycle waits on worker threads.** Largest option; it moves ownership of
    `RunningSession`.
  - **A contract latency bound.** Starts can still block, so no bound can be promised; Lucca's
    approval excludes one.
- **Decision.** Approach (a), batched stops. EON-C8 text approved by Lucca on 2026-11-04
  ("agree"). Reconciliation before and after the batch shares the same deadline, so a close
  never waits past one bound.
- **Checks.**
  - `a_close_stops_its_terminals_together_and_keeps_only_the_unended`
  - `a_close_waits_for_unreconciled_ends_within_one_shared_bound`
  - The isolated before/after load reproduction (record 03).

title: Slim AGENTS.md into a one-page hot path with linked detail
description:
## Why

Lucca, 2026-10-30, approving the overseer's recommendation "Slim AGENTS.md: a ~1-page hot path
(owners, commands, the five rules that bite), with everything else linked": "you can create a bead
for that". Every agent reads about 6,300 words of binding rules before it starts: root AGENTS.md,
docs/AGENT-PROTOCOLS.md, and the orbit/, venus/ and runtime/ AGENTS.md files (word count at edge
39e0a25). The rules are precise but dense and cross-reference each other, so each session spends
much of its context on orientation, and stale text (see eon-hgrq) binds every agent until fixed.

## Evidence

- `wc -w AGENTS.md docs/AGENT-PROTOCOLS.md orbit/AGENTS.md venus/AGENTS.md runtime/AGENTS.md`:
  6,325 words at 39e0a25.
- AGENTS.md says these files are generated: edit `.agent-protocols.local.md` (and per-directory
  sources) or `.agent-protocols.exceptions.json`, then render from the pinned Starcompass source
  (apply-agent-protocols skill). docs/AGENT-PROTOCOLS.md is the canonical import and stays as is.
- AGENTS.md sections most often needed per task: Product Boundary, Verification table, Proof and
  Review, Running Codex, Beads, Testing Discipline, Local Runtime Synchronization. Long-tail
  sections: Website, Composition and Distribution, Platform Discipline, Outside Contributions.

## Scope

In scope:
- Draft a restructured root AGENTS.md local section: a short hot path (one owner per subsystem,
  the commands, the rules that most often bite) and links to detail in owned docs (for example
  docs/DEVELOPMENT.md, docs/ARCHITECTURE.md, or a new docs/REVIEW.md if one owner is clearer).
  Every binding rule keeps exactly one home; nothing is dropped silently.
- A mapping table: each current rule → its new home, or "removed" with a reason.
- Move fast-changing status out of AGENTS.md if eon-hgrq recommends it.
- After Lucca approves the exact text: edit the sources, render, and run audit-agent-protocols.

Out of scope:
- docs/AGENT-PROTOCOLS.md and the Starcompass pin (canonical import).
- Changing what any rule requires; this restructures and links, it does not relax rules.
- Directory AGENTS.md files beyond moving duplicated root text out of them.

## Acceptance

- Lucca approved the hot path and mapping table before any edit.
- The rendered root AGENTS.md hot path is about one page, and the agent's total required reading
  drops measurably (report the new word count of what an agent must read before work).
- audit-agent-protocols reports no drift; every rule in the mapping table is findable at its new
  home.

## Verification

- Planning, docs and agent-policy route: render and import check, changed paths and diff; no
  runtime profile refresh.
- AP-TEST-001: this is a consequential agent-instruction change. With Lucca's authorization, run
  two or three isolated representative tasks (for example prime a small bead and state the
  required checks) on the new text without giving the expected answer, and compare with the old
  text; otherwise report agent behavior as unproven.

## Stop Conditions

- Stop for Lucca's approval of the text before editing sources.
- Stop if a rule has no clear single home; ask rather than drop or duplicate it.

## Maintenance Notes

- Waits for eon-hgrq's drift findings so stale claims are fixed or moved, not carried over.

title: Check whether OxiSH, a Rust SSH server library, matters for remote Eon
description:
## Why

Lucca, 2026-10-29: "create a bead to check on this https://github.com/djc/oxish". OxiSH is "A
modern, memory-safe SSH server" in Rust, usable as a server or a library with a sans-I/O protocol
crate. Eon's remote workspaces (eon-remote-workspaces-52i4) decided on OpenSSH-forwarded Unix
sockets with no new protocol in v1, while Rex acts as a full SSH replacement with system logins.
An embeddable Rust SSH implementation could matter later: a remote Eon that does not depend on the
host's sshd configuration, a Rex-style login path, or only a reference for SSH edge cases.

## Evidence (read 2026-10-29)

- github.com/djc/oxish at d81b20b (2026-10-25): MVP, README says "not yet ready for production use";
  Linux and macOS; public-key auth only; no SFTP; modern algorithms only (mlkem768x25519-sha256,
  curve25519-sha256, ed25519, ecdsa-sha2-nistp256, aes128-gcm@openssh.com), so clients need OpenSSH
  9.9+; optional FIPS crypto via aws-lc-fips; crates `oxish`, `oxish-proto`, `oxish-aws-lc`,
  `oxish-graviola`, plus `fuzz`; Apache-2.0 OR MIT; about 380 stars, 530 commits, started 2025-01.
- eon-remote-workspaces-52i4: Venus local, Runtime and Orbit remote, OpenSSH in v1.

## Scope

In scope (research only):
- Read the source at a recorded revision: what the library API offers (channels, PTY requests,
  Unix-socket or stream forwarding, auth hooks, async runtime), maturity signals (fuzzing, audits,
  releases, maintainers), and how it compares with OpenSSH and with russh for Eon's needs.
- A short recommendation: ignore, watch, reference only, or candidate for a post-v1 remote slice.

Out of scope:
- Adding any dependency, building or running OxiSH, changing the remote-workspaces decision.

## Acceptance

- A comment on this bead with the revision read, findings and the recommendation; if it is
  "candidate", a note on eon-remote-workspaces-52i4 naming the slice where it would apply.

## Verification

- Planning-only route: bead state and diff.

## Stop Conditions

- Stop before any code, dependency or contract change; those need Lucca's approval and the
  AP-DEPENDENCY-001 reference gate.

## Maintenance Notes

- Read the code on the web or in a fresh reference clone under ~/pjs/refs; do not build or run it
  on a maintainer machine.

title: Prove every EONW v2 request action
description:
## Contract Routing

This hardens the existing EON-C10 EONW v2 compatibility proof. It must not add an action, change a wire tag or field encoding, widen accepted input, or create a new protocol version.

Consumer: an EONW v2 client or legacy Eon supervisor.

Trigger: the client encodes or decodes any request action supported by EONW v2.

Result: every supported action has independently checked canonical bytes and decodes to the same typed request; incompatible versions, unknown tags, malformed presentation values, invalid identities/directories, and trailing payload remain rejected.

## Why

The 2026-08-28 coverage-aware audit found the largest actionable CRAP score in the repository here: `decode_request` has cyclomatic complexity 33, cognitive complexity 4, 37.21% line coverage, and CRAP 302.60. `encode_request` has cyclomatic complexity 19, cognitive complexity 1, 38.24% coverage, and CRAP 104.06. The low cognitive scores show exhaustive wire matching rather than a design problem; the missing proof is the issue.

Impact HIGH, effort S, implementation risk LOW, confidence HIGH.

## Evidence

- `crates/eon-workspace-protocol/src/v2.rs:169`: `encode_request` owns tags 0 through 12 for all v2 request actions.
- `crates/eon-workspace-protocol/src/v2.rs:208`: `decode_request` mirrors those tags and validates field-specific payloads.
- `crates/eon-workspace-protocol/src/v2.rs:811`: the only v2 request round-trip exercises `SetTabDirectory`; most action arms are uncovered.
- `crates/eon-workspace-protocol/src/v3.rs:306`: v3 already has a compact all-action corpus that demonstrates the repository pattern.
- `docs/CONTRACTS.md:311`: EON-C10 names EONW v2 codec/version rejection as accepted evidence.

## Scope

In scope:
- `crates/eon-workspace-protocol/src/v2.rs` tests.
- One compact golden request corpus covering every v2 action and both valid presentation values.
- Focused malformed-request cases needed to exercise v2-specific rejection branches.
- A before/after cargo-crap observation using cargo-crap 0.4.3 and the same LCOV workload.

Out of scope:
- Production codec refactoring merely to reduce a metric.
- EONW v3/v4 behavior, new actions, protocol negotiation, compatibility adapters, dependencies, CI thresholds, or contract-status changes.
- Tests that only mirror implementation trivia without independently constraining the wire contract.

## Implementation Notes

1. Re-read the v2 action enum, frame helpers, EON-C10, and the existing v3 corpus at the implementation revision.
2. Add one data-driven golden corpus that constrains canonical bytes as well as typed decode; paired round trips alone cannot detect matching encoder/decoder tag swaps.
3. Cover unknown action tag, invalid presentation byte, incompatible version, and trailing payload only where the current v2 suite does not already prove them.
4. Leave production code unchanged unless the golden contract exposes a real defect. If it does, stop and record the exact mismatch before changing accepted wire behavior.
5. Rerun the identical coverage-aware report and record the score change as diagnostic evidence, not a repository quality gate.

## Verification

- `cargo test --locked -p eon-workspace-protocol` should exit 0 and prove the complete v2 golden corpus and existing v3/v4 compatibility checks.
- `cargo clippy --locked -p eon-workspace-protocol --all-targets -- -D warnings` should exit 0.
- `cargo llvm-cov --workspace --all-features --lcov --output-path /tmp/eon-quality.lcov` should exit 0 and emit the shared LCOV workload.
- `cargo-crap --workspace --lcov /tmp/eon-quality.lcov --format json --output /tmp/eon-crap.json` with cargo-crap 0.4.3 should report materially higher v2 request coverage without source/LCOV mismatch diagnostics.
- `git diff --check` should exit 0.

## Stop Conditions

- Stop if current EON-C10 evidence or an accepted downstream v2 consumer disagrees with the encoded bytes.
- Stop before changing a production wire tag, accepted field, version, frame bound, or downstream consumer.
- Stop before adding a dependency, generated corpus, broad test abstraction, or CI threshold.

## Maintenance Notes

Prefer exhaustive data over helper layers. The CRAP result is a prioritization signal, not an architectural requirement; do not split the two wire matches solely to lower cyclomatic complexity.

## Acceptance Criteria

- One compact corpus independently constrains the canonical v2 request bytes and typed decode for every action tag 0 through 12, including every direction and both valid presentation values.
- Focused cases retain rejection of incompatible versions, unknown action tags, invalid presentation bytes, invalid bounded fields, and trailing payload without duplicating equivalent existing proof.
- The v2 codec package tests and Clippy pass. Production codec bytes and EON-C10 behavior remain unchanged unless a separately scoped confirmed defect is recorded.
- The repeated cargo-crap 0.4.3 report records higher coverage for both v2 request functions and no source/LCOV mismatch; it creates no threshold or CI policy.
- No dependency, generated fixture system, compatibility adapter, or EONW v3/v4 change is introduced.

title: Research AI agent messaging solutions against our hand-rolled INBOX/STATUS scheme
description:
## Why

Lucca, 2026-11-10: "we should create a bead to check for ai messaging solutions / we are kind of handrolling our solution but it may or not be the best for us".

Today agents and overseers talk through a hand-rolled mix: per-agent STATUS.md and INBOX.md files, a watch-agents.sh tail, nudge.sh typing a prompt into Codex panes (`eon pane send --stdin`, guarded so it never types over a person's unsent input), Claude Code's cross-session messages between overseers (tide-overseer, eon-overseer), and rota run reports. It works, but it costs overseer attention, Codex never wakes on file writes, pane sends risk interleaving with a person's typing (eon-2o85l), and nothing is queryable as data.

## Scope (research only)

Survey and compare existing agent-messaging solutions against what Eon needs, then recommend keep, adopt or build:

- MCP Agent Mail (Emanuel; the license rider is not a concern for Lucca), ntm, david-crespo/ah (already the basis of eon-gb5sr), Claude Code's own inbox/cross-session messaging and Agent SDK, Codex app-server/queue, OpenCode's HTTP API, Google's A2A protocol, ACP (Agent Client Protocol), and anything newer found on the web.
- For each: how a message reaches an agent that is idle or mid-turn (wakes it or not), delivery guarantees, local auth/trust, multi-backend support (Claude, Codex, OpenCode, others rota launches), human visibility in Eon, license and maintenance, and how it would fit Eon's rule 5 (every human action has an `eon` CLI path; agents read state as data).
- Measure today's cost: overseer tokens and missed or late wakeups from the current file+nudge scheme (the overseer's logs in ~/.cache/eon-agents/eon-overseer/ and agents' STATUS.md files).

## Output

A report with a recommendation: keep the files, adopt one tool, or build an `eon` messaging path (and if build, how it relates to eon-gb5sr's per-agent inbox CLI). Follow-up beads only on Lucca's or the overseer's approval. Reading only; clones go to ~/pjs/refs; never build or run outside code on this machine.
close_reason: done

title: Reopen Eon across last-Session exit
description:
## Contract

For a local Linux native-Wayland user, invoking Open Eon after the last Session exits converges on one fresh current-generation supervisor, Orbit Session, and Venus surface. A launch overlapping supervisor teardown waits for exact generation ownership. Before Eon forks any new Orbit process, Eon waits within the existing five-second Session-start deadline until Eon itself occupies a validated user-owned cgroup-v2 directory suitable for Orbit to inherit. Existing live Session recovery does not wait or restart anything.

The launch-readiness policy is independent of compositor, init, and service-manager APIs. Orbit remains the enforcement owner for Session containment. A system without systemd is supported by the implementation when its Linux environment provides Orbit’s existing documented delegated cgroup-v2 capability; non-systemd installed proof remains pending under EON-C7.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Close the Eon presentation, reopen the existing Session, and exit the last Session.
2. Invoke Open Eon through a launcher that starts Eon in a non-delegated login cgroup and relocates only Eon asynchronously.
3. Observe Eon fork Orbit before relocation; Orbit inherits the root-owned cgroup, fails ORB-C12 before Ready, and no surface opens.

## Prerequisites

EON-C11 runtime-generation and presentation ownership; EON-C15 exact same-boot Orbit recovery; ORB-C12 containment; current accepted Orbit and Venus pins.

## Acceptance Criteria

A focused red/green regression proves cgroup readiness is retried before the Orbit spawn boundary and fails boundedly if readiness never arrives. Existing generation-overlap regression remains green. Locked Eon Rust checks, governance, manifest validation, and affected Nix build pass. The refreshed installed profile preserves live Sessions and an ordinary Open Eon launch proves a fresh Orbit inherits Eon’s exact validated cgroup before creating its per-Session containment.

## Scope Boundary

Eon’s existing Orbit lifecycle adapter and current-generation supervisor lifecycle only. No systemd, D-Bus, compositor detection, launcher wrapper, daemon, new dependency, timeout expansion, relaxed Orbit checks, PID inference, automatic cleanup of unverified state, child-project edit, unrelated generation change, or claim that non-systemd dogfood has occurred.

Options compared: native application uniqueness; reconstruction-only app lifecycle; socket probe plus stale cleanup; root-wide startup lock; per-generation lifetime lock.
Decision: retain one stable per-generation lock for the supervisor lifetime, close/unlink its listener and finish runtime cleanup before releasing it, then let a waiting launch re-probe and start. Never unlink the lock file because replacing its inode defeats advisory-lock serialization.
Rejected: GTK/macOS native uniqueness does not own Eon's multi-generation process lifecycle; Canario restores fresh shells rather than process continuity; Herdr's socket-only check-then-spawn remains vulnerable to the demonstrated overlap; a root-wide lifetime lock blocks valid cross-generation use; intermittent startup/shutdown locking allowed queued connections to outlive the proof; sleeps, systemd scopes, and socket deletion without ownership are not lifecycle truth.

Reference gate (generic pre-fork cgroup readiness)
- Question: how can Eon prevent a new Orbit child from inheriting a transient non-delegated launcher cgroup without depending on COSMIC, systemd, or any other service manager?
- Contract and owner flow: Eon owns component launch ordering in crates/eon/src/sessions.rs; start_orbit is the sole new-Orbit spawn boundary used by initial Eon, EonTerm, and later workspace Session creation. - Linux kernel primary source: cgroup v2 documentation at https://www.kernel.org/doc/html/latest/admin-guide/cgroup-v2.html, inspected 2026-08-23. Children inherit the parent cgroup at fork; moving a parent later does not move an already-forked child. Process membership is observed via /proc/PID/cgroup. Migration across cgroups additionally requires write access at the common ancestor.
- Exact launcher reproducer: libcosmic 8cb10bf6e24b86a7d2a9cf8c662d3e0154db1b21 src/process.rs and src/desktop.rs spawn the desktop process and only afterward asynchronously request StartTransientUnit for that PID. This is evidence for the race, not a selected API or product dependency.

The common ancestor /sys/fs/cgroup/user.slice/user-1000.slice and its cgroup.procs are root-owned 0755/0644. Therefore an unprivileged already-forked Orbit cannot repair the race by migrating itself; the rejected Orbit issue orb-follow-validated-launcher-cgroup-x51 records this falsification.
- Adopt: immediately before orbit_command.spawn, retry inspection of Eon own cgroup-v2 membership within the already-shared five-second Session startup deadline. Readiness requires an absolute component-safe path, an exact user-owned directory not writable by group/others, and cgroup.procs membership for Eon own PID. Once ready, fork normally and let Orbit repeat/enforce ORB-C12. Recovery of existing Orbit runs bypasses this path.

A native-Wayland environment with an already-valid delegated parent proceeds immediately; a launcher that relocates Eon may converge; an environment that never supplies Orbit required delegation fails boundedly before Orbit spawn.

Shown in the tab label or sidebar heading and in eon session --json (rule 5), with a configuration switch (rule 6). Contracts: EON-C8, VEN-C8 or VEN-C30. Pairs with eon-el45 (worktree tabs).

## Planning and acceptance gate

Before code, record the selected display location, switch/default and directory source for Lucca, then draft exact EON-C10 JSON/configuration amendments for approval (EON-C17 owns the tab's launch directory; EON-C8/VEN-C8 own the tab view). A branch label is a feature in venus/docs/PRESENTATION.md, not a new presentation contract. Read docs/REFERENCES.md and one comparable branch/status reader at a recorded revision; explain any dependency.

Runtime owns a bounded background git read and canonical tab metadata; Venus renders the resolved result, without running git or parsing configuration. Resolve the repository from the approved tab directory, not the CLI caller's current directory. No dependency on eon-el45: ordinary tabs can be in repositories; worktree creation is separate.

Acceptance: a repository tab exposes its branch and dirty state through the selected window location and `eon session --json`; edits become visible and clearing them clears the mark. Cover a subdirectory, two tabs in different repositories, a linked worktree, detached HEAD, a non-repository and git failure/timeout. Define unavailable/detached representations in the approved shape instead of inventing a branch. Reads must stay off the request/UI path, be bounded and cancelled/reaped, and never modify the repository. Document units/timing/defaults or the justified fixed bound; no PR/ticket status or worktree-management scope.

Verification: focused parser/metadata regressions, final workspace checks and required review, and one isolated installed observation of live dirty-state change and disabled/unavailable behavior. Update USAGE, CONFIGURATION and CHANGELOG for the accepted feature. Portability: neutral git metadata; no new platform promise.

title: Retire Eon's dependency forks (accesskit, winit 0.30, libghostty-rs)
description:
## Why

Lucca asked on 2026-10-21 to get rid of Eon's dependency forks by whatever route fits each one: accept the upstream bug, land upstream PRs, or another way. Each fork is a second owner of upstream code, a Git pin outside crates.io, and extra work on every bump.

## Contract

No new contract. The consumer is Eon's build: every fork in `Cargo.toml` `[patch.crates-io]` or in a Git dependency has a recorded disposition, and is removed once its exit condition holds.

## Current dispositions (2e93c69; approvals stay in comments)

1. AccessKit fork retired: eon-9rtt.1 is closed. Cargo.toml's patch section (:17-18) has no
   AccessKit entry; venus/docs/CRATES.md:163-175 records the crates.io family/cache-signal fix.
2. winit fork remains: Cargo.toml:18 pins Yazelix/winit-0.30 at
   7c209ec5bebbd2963f75a39f79b320af6b03f72c. eon-9rtt.2 owns Lucca's accepted stable-0.31
   plus compatible accesskit_winit exit; its review date remains unchanged.
3. libghostty-rs fork retired: orbit/Cargo.toml:9 pins upstream Uzaaft/libghostty-rs
   9b598d6528c08c013407052767bb2e885ba869ba (eon-9rtt.4/.9 closed). The remaining upstream
   Git-to-crates.io swap is eon-9rtt.3, requiring callbacks/image iterator/Ghostty >= 1.0
   (orbit/docs/CRATES.md:17-50). Lucca removed that swap from the beta gate on 2026-11-08.
4. eon-9rtt.5 owns present-tense pin docs, retaining historical proof identities; rebaseline
   its 2026-10-27 example against today's actual pin.

These are repository/bead dispositions, not a fresh upstream-release check. Original fork identities,
Lucca's 2026-10-22 decisions and their evidence remain in comments and closed child records.

## Acceptance

- For each fork, Lucca chooses one disposition, recorded here with its evidence:
  - an upstream PR, with its link and status;
  - an accepted upstream bug, with the user-visible consequence named;
  - or keep the fork, with its exit condition and a date to look again.
- A fork whose fix has reached an upstream release is replaced by that exact release. The proof is the owning check: Venus's AT-SPI wire regression and an installed Orca observation for accesskit, an installed blur observation for winit, and the Orbit suites plus the real-PTY checks for libghostty-rs.
- Afterwards, `[patch.crates-io]` and the Git dependencies hold only forks that have a recorded reason.

## Scope boundary

- In scope: Eon's dependency forks.
- Out of scope:
  - Yazelix-owned inputs that are products rather than dependency patches: nova-helix, anima, kinestra and ratconfig. Include them only if Lucca adds them.
  - New forks.
  - Releases.
- Outward-facing steps need Lucca: opening PRs and creating or deleting fork repositories.

## Existing split and completion

This is an epic: the session-sized split already exists as .1-.9. Remaining children are .2
(winit), .3 (crates.io libghostty-vt) and .5 (docs); the rest are closed. Do not create a second
split or wait on closed eon-a9tr.2. Preserve exit conditions and external-release waits; independent
swaps need no ordering edge. Close only after every child closes or is explicitly moved with an
accepted disposition. Portability and affected proof remain with each owning child.

title: Replace the accesskit fork with the first release containing bffadac
description:
## Why

Eon patches accesskit, accesskit_consumer, accesskit_atspi_common and accesskit_unix to the fork
Yazelix/accesskit `0f9d186` (base upstream `c88605b`). The fork exists so the Linux AT-SPI cache
signals keep each AddAccessible/RemoveAccessible structure as one D-Bus argument
(`venus/docs/REFERENCES.md`, AccessKit; `venus/docs/CRATES.md`).

## Decision (Lucca, 2026-10-22, eon-9rtt)

Wait for an upstream release, then replace the fork with it. Rejected: pinning upstream Git
`bffadac` now (still a Git pin, plus an unreleased AccessKit bump and a fresh Orca proof).

## Evidence (checked 2026-10-22)

- Upstream issue AccessKit/accesskit#818 is closed. PR #819 merged as `bffadacde` on 2026-10-11 and
  makes the same code change as the fork in adapters/unix/src/atspi/bus.rs (`Type` bound and
  `&(body,)`). The fork also carries a wire-signature test.
- Latest releases: accesskit_unix 0.24.0, accesskit 0.25.1 and accesskit_winit 0.34.1, all
  2026-09-25. `bffadac` is 3 commits ahead of `accesskit_unix-v0.24.0`, so it's unreleased.
- Eon pins accesskit =0.24.1, accesskit_winit =0.33.2 and accesskit_unix 0.22.1 (Cargo.lock).
  accesskit_winit 0.34.1 still needs winit ^0.30.5, so this bump doesn't depend on the winit fork.

## Exit

When an accesskit_unix release contains `bffadac`: bump the AccessKit family to exact releases
(accesskit 0.25.x or later, accesskit_winit 0.34.x or later), delete the four `[patch.crates-io]`
lines, and update venus/docs/CRATES.md and REFERENCES.md.

## Acceptance

- `[patch.crates-io]` has no accesskit lines. Cargo.lock resolves the AccessKit crates from
  crates.io at exact versions.
- Proof: Venus's AT-SPI wire regression passes, and one installed Orca observation is made.

## Scope

In: the AccessKit bump and removing the fork. Out: winit (the eon-9rtt winit child) and new
accessibility behavior. Check for a release at the defer date; don't poll.
close_reason: Fork retired at 0e47d26: exact crates.io AccessKit releases, wire reproducer red/green, and the installed Orca return-to-live selection observation passed on /nix/store/x97lf54z...-eon-0.1.8.

So the eon-9rtt disposition is 'upstream PR merged, awaiting release'. The fork's wire test exists only in the fork, so the exit proof here is Venus's AT-SPI wire regression plus Orca.

The defer date (2026-11-30) can be pulled in; timing relative to the macOS final-revision proof (eon-mac-launch-kz4p.12) is Lucca's call, since the bump also changes the macOS AppKit adapter.

Sequencing: do not change the tree under an in-flight macOS proof run (eon-mac-launch-kz4p.12); the overseer schedules it so the macOS final-revision proof either includes the bump or precedes it.

comments.author: lucca
comments.text:
Plan (Opus planner, 2026-10-29, worktree at edge 6c0037b). Approval relayed by eon-overseer on 2026-10-29: Lucca's 'retire it' (session eon-8e), as recorded in the Decision comment above. Codex implements; Opus gates.

Approach. Use exact crates.io releases and drop the fork:
- venus/Cargo.toml: accesskit =0.25.2 and accesskit_winit =0.34.2 (both entries); the dev-dependency accesskit_consumer =0.39.2.
- Cargo.toml: delete the four accesskit [patch.crates-io] lines. The winit line stays.
- flake.nix: delete outputHashes."accesskit-0.24.1", since no Git source is left.
- Cargo.lock: the smallest re-resolve.
- Venus code changes only if the 0.25 API forces them (0.25.0 has one breaking change: "Reuse property buffers when cloning nodes").

Forced knock-on: eon-runtime's zbus moves from =5.18.0 to =5.19.0. accesskit_unix 0.24.1 needs zbus ^5.19, and one graph can't hold both. This is the policy eon-first-detach-notification-a0p3 recorded for that pin: follow the lock's single zbus. zbus 5.19.0 is the only release that satisfies the requirement. Other transitive bumps (zvariant >=5.15, phf 0.14, hashbrown 0.17 for accesskit_macos) come only from the new requirements.

Docs (current-state claims only; dated historical records stay as written):
- venus/docs/CRATES.md, Accessibility section: the selected shape, and the patch paragraph replaced by the release that carries the fix.
- venus/docs/REFERENCES.md: the AccessKit entry (:431-445), and the Click-only source link at :289-292, re-pointed to the accesskit_atspi_common 0.21.1 release.
- orbit/docs/CRATES.md:254: the selected Venus versions.
- No CHANGELOG entry: no Eon command, configuration or contract changes.

Reference gate (consequential: a dependency change). The user-visible behavior is Venus's native accessibility tree over AT-SPI (Linux) and AppKit (macOS). Venus owns the tree, derived from the accepted scene; AccessKit owns platform adaptation. Routes read: venus/docs/REFERENCES.md (AccessKit, AT-SPI 2.58.1 cache handlers) and venus/docs/CRATES.md (Accessibility). Comparable implementation: upstream AccessKit at its releases, with these sources inspected:
- accesskit_unix 0.24.1, src/atspi/bus.rs:465-474: the Type bound and `&(body,)`, which is the fork's change (bffadac, PR #819). 0.22.1 lacks it.
- accesskit_atspi_common 0.21.1, node.rs:525-537: still Click-only, so the Open/Copy Click-node design stands.

Constraints kept: one Rust type identity across the sibling crates (all from the registry now), and the libatspi rule that each cache structure is one signal argument. Rejected: keeping the fork (exit met), and a Git pin of bffadac (rejected 2026-10-22). Version policy: exact `=` pins, with the AccessKit family bumped together, and a later bump follows an upstream release. There is no Git pin, so there is no exit condition. Portability disposition: neutral (macOS gets accesskit_macos 0.27.2 through accesskit_winit, with no new platform assumption).

Red check:
- Acceptance: before the change, Cargo.lock resolves accesskit, accesskit_consumer, accesskit_atspi_common and accesskit_unix from the Yazelix Git fork. After it, all accesskit* packages come from the crates.io registry, and Cargo.toml has no accesskit patch.
- Cache wire: the repository has no in-tree AT-SPI wire harness. The fork's only wire test (bus.rs `cache_signals_preserve_struct_arguments`, private D-Bus) can't reach upstream's private Bus from Venus, and upstream declined the test until it has a Unix harness. Following AGENTS.md Testing Discipline, the proof is a disposable reproducer kept on this bead: the fork's test applied to the unpacked accesskit_unix crates, under dbus-run-session. Expected: red on 0.22.1 (signature not preserved) and green on 0.24.1. Maintained-coverage gap: upstream owns the wire, and nothing in this repository guards it.

Checks (Linux, worktree tree):
- `nix develop -c eon-test -p yazelix-venus` and `-p eon-runtime`.
- fmt --check, and `cargo clippy --locked --all-targets -- -D warnings` for yazelix-venus and eon-runtime.
- Darwin: kz4p.1's recipe, `cargo clippy --locked --target aarch64-apple-darwin -p yazelix-venus --all-targets -- -D warnings` (a compile check, not a Mac result), with a 6c0037b baseline.
- Nix: the workspace vendor derivation builds without the outputHash. `nix build .#default` runs at the final gate after eon-overseer's go.
- After landing, the coordinator makes the installed observation: real isolated Orca Return to live, which reports the actual combining/wide selection (ven-resolve-reader-focus-after-return-to-live-lmt acceptance 3). That closes this bead's Orca acceptance.

Scope: in scope are the AccessKit family bump, removing the fork, the forced zbus pin, and the docs above. Out of scope: winit (eon-9rtt.2), new accessibility behavior, and Venus test rewrites to absorb upstream behavior changes (if a test changes meaning, stop and report).

title: Replace the winit 0.30 fork once winit 0.31 is stable
description:
## Why

Eon patches winit to Yazelix/winit-0.30 `7c209ec`: v0.30.13 plus a backport of upstream
`c4afadbf` ("winit-wayland: use `ext-background-effect` if available"). Venus prefers
ext-background-effect-v1 for compositor blur and keeps the KDE fallback
(`venus/docs/REFERENCES.md`, "Required for compositor-owned background blur").

## Decision (Lucca, 2026-10-22, eon-9rtt)

Keep the fork until winit 0.31.0 is stable. Rejected: asking for a v0.30.x backport (a new
protocol feature, unlikely to be accepted on a maintenance branch) and dropping the fork (Venus
would lose ext-background-effect blur).

## Evidence (checked 2026-10-22)

- `c4afadbf` (2026-04-04) is on master and was cherry-picked to the v0.31.x branch, which is
  included in v0.31.0-beta.3 (2026-09-04, prerelease). v0.30.x has nothing after v0.30.13
  (2026-03-02).
- accesskit_winit 0.34.1 (at the 2026-10-22 check) needs winit ^0.30.5, so Venus can't move to winit 0.31 until
  an accesskit_winit release supports it.

## Exit

All three conditions must hold: winit 0.31.x stable is released, an accesskit_winit release supports that version, and the AppKit marked-text guard (or an equivalent fix) is merged and released in that winit version. eon-9rtt.6 found the bug still present in master ab2fe0cd / beta.4; it is closed research, not evidence of an upstream fix. Then port
Venus to winit 0.31 (an API break, so plan its own slice), delete the winit `[patch.crates-io]`
line, and update venus/docs/CRATES.md and REFERENCES.md.

## Acceptance

- `[patch.crates-io]` has no winit line. winit resolves from crates.io at an exact 0.31 version.
- Proof: Venus's suites pass, and one installed blur observation is made on a compositor with
  ext-background-effect-v1.

## Scope

In: tracking the exit and planning the 0.31 port. Out: an unrelated AccessKit update; a required compatible accesskit_winit migration must be scoped as its own approved session-sized prerequisite if it cannot fit this port. No defer date is set by this pass.

## Recorded upstream gate and current local evidence

Lucca opened winit issue 4807 and PR 4808 (https://github.com/rust-windowing/winit/pull/4808), prepared at Yazelix/winit-0.30:macos-ime-keep-composition-on-source-change 9bff271. This is recorded history; recheck actual upstream release/merge state when taking the bead. At 6e63eb7 Cargo.toml:18 still patches winit 7c209ec and venus/Cargo.toml pins winit 0.30.13 / accesskit_winit 0.34.2. Do not drop either the compositor-blur backport or IME guard before an accepted release owns it.

Portability: isolated Wayland blur and Darwin AppKit/IME host dependencies. Before replacing the accepted dependency, record the source/revision/API and platform comparison, version policy and exit condition under venus/docs/CRATES.md and REFERENCES.md. In addition to the existing blur acceptance, retain the Kotoeri marked-text input-source-change regression at the approved macOS proof boundary; compilation is not IME proof. Final workspace/affected package builds and required review apply, including isolated installed Linux proof. Public upstream posts remain Lucca's action.

That guard is not upstream: no winit issue or PR from luccahuguet exists, and the docs say upstream PR 4087's broader rewrite was rejected for Eon.
