title: Pin the first crates.io libghostty-vt release that carries Orbit's upstream callbacks and image iterator
description:
## Why

Orbit depends on libghostty-vt from upstream Uzaaft/libghostty-rs master, pinned by exact git rev
`9b598d6` (Ghostty vt-1.0.0 `0fa3d577`), since eon-9rtt.9. The fork is retired and nothing is
patched; what remains is the git source. A crates.io release lets Orbit's manifest name a normal
version, and would let Orbit itself be published to crates.io one day.

Lucca, 2026-11-08: "yeah, drop it from the gate". This bead no longer blocks v0.2.0 (eon-igae):
the git pin is exact and locked in Cargo.lock and flake.lock, so users get the same code either way,
and the release date is upstream's. It lands whenever a fitting release appears.

History: earlier text tracked the Yazelix fork and upstream issue #111 (OSC 7501 callbacks).
Upstream merged that work (Uzaaft's #125; our duplicate #126 was closed on 2026-11-08), and
eon-9rtt.9 moved Orbit onto upstream master.

## Exit

A libghostty-vt release on crates.io that contains everything Orbit uses at `9b598d6` or later:
the program-status and semantic-prompt callbacks, the Kitty image iterator, and Ghostty >= 1.0.

## Acceptance

- orbit/Cargo.toml depends on an exact crates.io libghostty-vt, with no git source; the flake's
  Ghostty input matches the release's embedded Ghostty.
- Proof: Orbit's suites, the orbit-* Nix checks including real-PTY and OSC 7501 record checks,
  whole-workspace eon-test, nix build .#default and the Nix-free bundle.

## Scope

In: the pin swap. Out: new Ghostty features. Agents do not open upstream PRs; Lucca does.

## Remaining accepted obligations and evidence freshness

At 6e63eb7 the current upstream git pin remains orbit/Cargo.toml:9 (9b598d6528c08c013407052767bb2e885ba869ba); orbit/docs/CRATES.md:18-19 records Ghostty vt-1.0.0 0fa3d577. Do not infer present crates.io availability from the dated comments: inspect the candidate release when taking this bead. eon-9rtt.9 already adopted the 1.0 port, so the older instruction to apply a temporary local port patch is historical; compare against current upstream instead of applying it blindly.

Carry forward comments 2026-10-27/29: confirm the candidate's embedded Ghostty includes bd647035 (Kitty releases do not fall back to inserted text), preserve the focused regression and physical-Space U+0020 metadata, and remove Orbit's release-text suppression only if the candidate proves it owns that invariant. If the swap also changes Ghostty/build fetching, apply Lucca's fetchAll-trimming instruction from eon-j0md's report in that proven slice; do not turn a same-core source swap into an unreviewed build-policy change. Record exact binding/core identities, dependency comparison and the owning reference routes before the change.

Keep live terminals and the shared standalone protocol boundary intact. Portability: neutral source/pin swap; preserve Orbit's isolated native seams. After source checks, record actual downstream Nix and Nix-free artifact identity/behavior and required review/installed synchronization; source resolution alone is not delivery proof. This remains outside the beta gate by Lucca's recorded decision.

title: Move Orbit's libghostty-vt pin to upstream libghostty-rs master and retire the fork
description:
## Why

Orbit depends on libghostty-vt from the Yazelix/libghostty-rs fork at `6313a9b` (upstream master `0ef8041` plus 4 commits: Ghostty 8c425a7 + Zig 0.17, enum prefix stripping, program-status and semantic-prompt callbacks, docs resync). Upstream master has since merged equivalents of all of it and more: as of `9ede35b8` (2026-10-24) it pins Ghostty `521cf2c` (18 commits ahead of 8c425a7bd, 0 behind), wraps program status (`c6878f53`, `a0e3dedd`) and the semantic-prompt callback (`9ede35b8`, `a48ad73a`), and adds the safe render-state image iterator orb-j2i needs (`660f10b6` ImageIterator, `7464fbe2` Kitty on the render-state image list, `b4d5a36c` animation_tick). No release contains these (last release v0.2.2, 2026-09-28; master still 0.2.1).

## Decision (Lucca, 2026-10-26, in the eon-overseer session)

Move Orbit's pin from the fork to an exact upstream Uzaaft/libghostty-rs master commit now and retire the fork, without waiting for a crates.io release. His words: "yeah, but i actually aprove this" (to: "File a bead to move Orbit's pin from our fork to upstream master and retire the fork ... the fork's exit condition says crates.io, so moving to an upstream git commit is a narrower step that needs your OK"). This extends the git-pin exception approved in eon-a9tr.1 (2026-10-21) from the fork to upstream for this dependency only. Returning to crates.io stays the later exit (eon-9rtt.3, orb-ze3). Asked whether to request a release on #111: "why not just wait?" — no upstream post; wait.

## Contract

No contract change intended: ORB-C15 (OSC 7501 program status records) and every Orbit terminal-semantics contract keep their behavior. If a breaking upstream change alters observable behavior, stop and ask Lucca.

## Reference gate (consequential: dependency change; record in a comment before code)

- Behavior: Orbit's terminal semantics unchanged; one owner (Orbit) of the libghostty dependency.
- Routes: orbit/docs/REFERENCES.md and orbit/docs/CRATES.md (current decision text, lines ~16-38); upstream commits from `0ef8041` to the chosen rev, read in full for every `!` (breaking) commit: `c5fc2d5b` (vt-sys to 521cf2c), `75228f9b`, `55e12782`, `ddb38f85`, `9d58ffa4`, `fb9378e3`, `8ea890ed`, `c7debec4`, `a122276d`, `83634421`, and others listed by `git log 0ef8041..<rev>`.
- Compare our fork's 4 commits with upstream's versions (API names and semantics of the two callbacks).
- Version policy: exact upstream commit, moved only by a bead. Exit: the first crates.io release whose GHOSTTY_COMMIT contains 8c425a7bd and whose API carries both callbacks and the image iterator (eon-9rtt.3).

## Scope

In scope:
- orbit/Cargo.toml and Cargo.lock: `libghostty-vt` from `https://github.com/Uzaaft/libghostty-rs.git` at one exact commit (prefer master `9ede35b8` or the newest master commit at start; record the choice).
- Orbit code adapted to the breaking changes, with no behavior change.
- Nix: whatever pins the Ghostty source or vendored build for libghostty-vt-sys (follow the existing derivation; Zig version per upstream).
- orbit/docs/CRATES.md decision text (upstream pin, no fork), orbit/CHANGELOG.md only if a wire/protocol/contract changes (none expected).

Out of scope:
- Any Orbit use of the image iterator (orb-j2i.6) or graphics behavior.
- Deleting or archiving the Yazelix/libghostty-rs repository (Lucca's call); opening PRs or posting on upstream.
- Other forks under eon-9rtt.

## Acceptance

- Cargo.lock has no Yazelix/libghostty-rs source; libghostty-vt resolves to the exact upstream commit.
- Orbit behavior unchanged, shown by Orbit's suites and real-PTY checks including the OSC 7501 record checks and semantic-prompt checks.
- orbit/docs/CRATES.md states the upstream pin, the approval, and the crates.io exit.

## Verification

- AGENTS.md route "runtime/build dependency": full affected Rust and Nix surfaces: `nix develop -c eon-test` (workspace), `cargo fmt --check` and `cargo clippy --locked --all-targets -- -D warnings` for yazelix-orbit, the Nix package build, and the installed outermost dogfood observation for the batch (a terminal with a shell prompt and an agent status record, in an isolated headless Sway per the capture recipe).
- Converge plus Codex per AGENTS.md (Cargo manifests and lockfiles included).

## Stop Conditions

- Stop and ask Lucca if an upstream change alters observable terminal behavior, drops a capability Orbit uses, or needs a Ghostty patch.
- Ask eon-overseer for a build slot before the full suites (shared machine).

----- ISSUE DRAFT (issue-draft.md) -----
Title: macOS: Kotoeri kanji conversion never commits because keyDown: disables IME on an input source change

### Description

With the built-in Japanese input method (Kotoeri, Romaji), converting a composition to kanji commits nothing. Typing `nihon` shows the preedit にほん as expected, but converting it to 日本 produces no `Ime::Commit`. The application receives `Ime::Disabled` instead and the text is lost.

Event trace from an application that logs winit's IME events (physical Apple M1, macOS 26.6.1, build 25G76):

1. `Ime::Preedit` for each step: `n`, `に`, `にh`, `にほ`, `にほn`, `にほん`.
2. During the conversion, `keyDown:` emits `Ime::Disabled` before it calls `interpretKeyEvents`.
3. No `Ime::Commit` follows. Enter closes the candidate panel and the にほん preedit stays on screen, but nothing is committed.

### Steps to reproduce

1. On macOS, add Japanese - Romaji (Kotoeri) in System Settings > Keyboard > Input Sources and select it.
2. Run a winit application that enables IME and logs `WindowEvent::Ime`.
3. Type `nihon`, convert it to the 日本 candidate, and press Enter.
4. Expected: `Ime::Commit("日本")`. Actual: `Ime::Disabled` during the conversion, and no `Ime::Commit` after the Enter.

Kotoeri takes one Enter to accept the highlighted candidate and a second one to commit it. The trace above is from a run with one Enter; we have not recorded an unpatched run with both.

### Cause

`keyDown:` in `winit-appkit/src/view.rs` compares `selectedKeyboardInputSource` with the last value it stored. When they differ, it sets `ImeState::Disabled` and queues `Ime::Disabled`, before calling `interpretKeyEvents`:

```rust
if *prev_input_source != current_input_source && self.is_ime_enabled() {
    *prev_input_source = current_input_source;
    drop(prev_input_source);
    self.ivars().ime_state.set(ImeState::Disabled);
    self.queue_event(WindowEvent::Ime(Ime::Disabled));
}
```

During the conversion, Kotoeri reports a different selected input source while the composition is still marked. During a key event, `insertText:` commits only when `is_ime_enabled()` is true, a requirement that #4651 kept. The state is already `Disabled`, so the commit is dropped.

This is present on `master` (ab2fe0cd) and `v0.31.0-beta.4` (d597ced7), and in 0.30.13. #4651 fixed commits lost after `unmarkText` (#3925), but it keeps this transition and the `ime_enabled` requirement, so this case is still broken. #4087 would have removed the transition, but as part of a larger rewrite that was closed.

### Proposed fix

Skip the transition while `hasMarkedText()` is true. The stored input source stays unchanged, so the transition still happens on the first key after the composition ends. Source changes without marked text behave as they do now. We tested this one-line guard on a fork based on winit 0.30.13 on a physical M1 on 2026-09-16. With it, the Kotoeri sequence above, with both Enters, committed 日本 exactly once. A PR against master follows.

### Platform

macOS

----- PR DRAFT (pr-draft.md) -----
Title: macOS: keep the IME composition across an input source change

Head: Yazelix/winit-0.30:macos-ime-keep-composition-on-source-change
Base: rust-windowing/winit:master

Body:

Fixes #<issue number>.

`keyDown:` disables IME as soon as the selected input source differs from the last one it saw, before `interpretKeyEvents` runs. Kotoeri (Japanese Romaji) changes the selected input source in the middle of a composition. Converting にほん to 日本 therefore disables IME first, and `insertText:` drops the commit because IME is no longer enabled.

This adds one condition to the existing transition: skip it while there is marked text.

- The stored input source is not updated while the transition is skipped. The transition therefore still runs on the first key after the composition ends, and it still emits `Ime::Disabled` then.
- Source changes without marked text behave exactly as before.
- `insertText:`, `setMarkedText:`, `unmarkText` and the `pending_commit` logic from #4651 are unchanged.

Testing: the same guard, applied to a fork based on winit 0.30.13, was tested on a physical Apple M1 (macOS 26.6.1, build 25G76) on 2026-09-16. Kotoeri converted `nihon` through the preedit にほん to 日本, and after the select and commit Enters the application received exactly one commit of 日本. Without the guard, in a run with a single Enter, the application received `Ime::Disabled` during the conversion and no commit. On master the condition goes in the same place; the only difference from the 0.30 patch is that `hasMarkedText` is a safe call there, so no `unsafe` block is needed.

This doesn't overlap #4744: that PR adds code after the transition and leaves the transition alone.

title: eon --dir says nothing when the launch recovers a window's terminals
description:
## Why

`eon --dir DIR` (and `eon run --dir DIR`) promise a fresh window whose t1 starts
its first pane in DIR (EON-C18). When the window's supervisor died but its
Orbit terminals live on, the next launch recovers them instead
(EON-C15, `recover_sessions` in `runtime/crates/eon-runtime/src/supervisor.rs`).
In that case `--dir` is dropped without a word: the recovered terminals show
in t1, t1's directory becomes DIR (the recovery fallback takes the launch
directory), no pane starts in DIR, and the command exits 0. The contract says
"a fresh window", so this is not a violation, but it is the silent drop that
eon-fv1j0's decision 2 avoided for a running window: a person or agent asks for
a terminal in DIR and gets their old terminals with no hint.

## What to decide (recommendation first)

1. Refuse as for a running window (recommended): when `recover_sessions`
   returns live terminals and the launch carried `--dir`, exit 1 before
   presenting, with the running-window message adapted ("this Eon window
   recovered its terminals, so --dir has no fresh first tab to start; use
   `eon tab create --dir DIR` ..."). Leaves the recovered window running and
   presentable with bare `eon`. Needs a one-line EON-C18 amendment (approval).
2. Or start the recovered window and add a tab at DIR (as `tab create --dir`
   would): friendlier, but a launch flag that sometimes means "new tab" is
   harder to describe.
3. Or document the drop in EON-C18 and USAGE only.

## Acceptance

- The chosen behaviour, covered by a workspace_control test that kills a
  supervisor with live terminals and relaunches with `--dir` (the existing
  same-boot recovery tests show the setup).
- EON-C18 text approved if it changes; USAGE `eon` row updated.
- `--no-anima` needs nothing: recovery never plays the startup Anima.

comments.author: lucca
comments.text: Decision (Lucca approved, 2026-11-12, "great, its all decided then. we converged", typed in eon-desk after reading the overseer/desk exchange; digest row D11): when a launch with --dir recovers live terminals, do not fail: recover them unchanged, then open a new tab at DIR in the recovered session; if that tab cannot be created, the recovered terminals stay alive and the launch reports the failure. Approved EON-C18 sentence: "When a launch with --dir recovers live terminals, Eon keeps them unchanged and opens a new tab whose working directory is DIR in the recovered session; if that tab cannot be created, the recovered terminals stay alive and the launch reports the failure." Reason: the user asked for a directory; an error that tells them to type another command fails rule 8.

title: Label panes with a pinned name, the program title or the directory, and rename them from the CLI
description:
## Why

eon-8rdi decision (Lucca, 2026-10-24: "ok, the pane labels are fine"): pane labels say what runs
in the pane. Research and mockups: ~/.cache/eon-agents/8rdi/research/ (frame PINNED,
mock/png/labels-zoom.png; recommendation.md has the ownership split, trust bounds and contrast
numbers).

## Behaviour

- Label = `pN` (drawn slightly dimmer than the name, contrast >= 4.5:1 over the resolved card
  fill at the configured opacity) + two spaces + name, where name = the pinned name if set, else
  the program's terminal title (sanitized as Orbit already sanitizes management titles, bounded),
  else the compact working directory, else nothing; plus ` · <directory>` context when the
  terminal's directory differs from the tab's launch directory (lexical, relative: `subdir`,
  `../other-repo`, or the compact path when shorter). States offline/connecting/unavailable stay.
- `eon pane rename pN NAME` sets the pin; `eon pane rename pN --clear` (exact flag in the
  contract) clears it; a matching window action. Pins live in the Runtime workspace state.
- Runtime composes the label (one owner) and sends it on EONW; Venus draws it (ID styled by the
  known `pN  ` prefix), fits it as today, and exposes the full label to AccessKit; `eon workspace
  --json` includes each pane's label and pin.
- Ships in the same next EONW version as eon-workspace-switching-shn4.3 (one bump, one window
  restart).

## Contract

EON-C8 pane-label bullet, EON-C10 (CLI), EON-C28 if fields freeze, VEN-C8, the EONW revision.
Exact wording to Lucca before code. Reference gate: consequential (wire change).

## Prerequisites

eon-workspace-switching-shn4.3 (same EONW revision; implement together or immediately after in
the same unreleased EONW version).

## Acceptance

- Runtime tests: precedence (pin > title > directory), context rules, sanitizing and bounds,
  rename set/clear over CLI and JSON.
- Venus test: dimmed ID colour and contrast, fitting keeps the ID, AccessKit name.
- Isolated capture: a 4-pane stack with claude, hx, a test in another repo and an idle shell.

Portability: neutral.
close_reason: Landed: pane labels and rename

comments.author: lucca
comments.text:
Approval (Lucca, 2026-10-25 ~05:40 -03, direct to the overseer, answering its numbered list item 1): "approval to all". Approved: the label shape and the drafted contract wording below, with the overseer's recommendations: (a) clearing by both `--clear` and an empty NAME; (b) JSON fields `label` + `pinned_name`; (c) order `NAME · DIRECTORY` as in this bead (the 8rdi mock's directory-first order is not used); (d) label policy fixed, no `terminal.pane_label_style`/`pane_id_dim` settings (Configurability reason: one more style setting costs more support than users differing would gain); (e) no executable/process-name fallback (eon-6heq stays deferred). The draft's remaining choices stand as it recommends: window action as Commands entries; metadata from the existing ORBS observers; contrast as a 4.5:1 target against the resolved fill. Ships on EONW v20 together with eon-workspace-switching-shn4.3. Drafted wording (Codex draft reviewed by the overseer, 2026-10-25):

**1. eon-a7xd — Pane labels and rename**

**Current clauses → proposed replacements**

EON-C8, `docs/CONTRACTS.md`, Trigger:
> Launch, create or close a tab, create or close a pane, create a column, traverse focus, reorder the active tab or selected pane, move the selected pane into a neighbouring column, zoom the selected pane, receive terminal exit, or recover accepted same-boot runs.

Replace with:
> Launch, create or close a tab, create, close or rename a pane, create a column, traverse focus, reorder the active tab or selected pane, move the selected pane into a neighbouring column, zoom the selected pane, receive terminal exit, or recover accepted same-boot runs.

EON-C8, pane-label result:
> Each pane is identified as `pN`, two ASCII spaces, and a compact working-directory label; home uses `~`, descendants use `~/`, and external paths remain absolute.

Replace with:
> Each pane retains its stable `pN` identity. Runtime supplies its label: the identity, two ASCII spaces, then the pinned name, otherwise the sanitized terminal title, otherwise the compact working directory, otherwise no name. The default style appends ` · DIRECTORY` when the terminal directory differs lexically from the tab’s launch directory, without repeating a directory already used as the name. Context uses a relative path, or the compact path when shorter; compact paths use `~` for home and `~/` for its descendants. Labels preserve explicit offline, connecting and unavailable states. Program metadata is untrusted display text, never identity or command input.

VEN-C8, `venus/docs/CONTRACTS.md`, metadata observer:
> Every visible live pane endpoint has one bounded read-only metadata observer.

Replace with:
> Runtime supplies labels for every workspace pane, including collapsed panes and panes in background tabs. Venus consumes those labels without reconstructing their naming policy.

VEN-C8, label clauses:
> Headers and AccessKit names show the opaque `pN` identity, two ASCII spaces, and one compact working-directory label.
>
> Home displays `~`; descendants use `~/`; paths outside home remain absolute; overlong paths elide from the left to preserve the leaf; an unset or empty `HOME` keeps absolute paths.
>
> Terminal title remains available to the selected window and is not repeated in pane chrome. Empty, offline, unavailable, or incompatible metadata falls back to pane identity without exposing mapped Session identity.

Replace those three bullets with:
> Headers show Runtime’s bounded pane label. Fitting retains the literal pane identity whenever it fits and middle-elides the remaining text at shaping-cluster boundaries; AccessKit and final-close pane listings retain the full bounded label. The ID may be dimmer than the name, with 4.5:1 contrast as the target against the resolved fill at the configured opacity; when dimming compromises readability, it uses the name’s colour. Terminal title remains available for selected-window compositor semantics. Labels never expose mapped Session identity.

VEN-C8, observation lifecycle:
> Hidden tabs have no observers, obsolete observations retire, and a 250 ms reinspection exposes accepted external workspace changes without native input.

Replace with:
> Venus opens no separate workspace-label metadata observers. Removed panes retire their label projections, and a 250 ms reinspection exposes accepted external workspace changes without native input.

VEN-C8, Owner:
> Venus workspace materialization, bounded metadata observation, clipping, and accessibility projection; Eon owns topology and Orbit owns terminal metadata and Session lifetime.

Replace with:
> Venus owns workspace materialization, label fitting, rendering and accessibility; Runtime owns semantic pane labels and pins; Orbit owns terminal metadata and Session lifetime.

VEN-C8, Consumes:
> Eon `EON-C10`, `EON-C17`, `EON-C18`, canonical EONW through the in-tree `eon-workspace-protocol` 0.1.0, and Orbit metadata observation in ORBS v13 through the in-tree `orbit-protocol` 0.1.0.

Replace with:
> Eon `EON-C10`, `EON-C17`, `EON-C18`, canonical EONW through the in-tree `eon-workspace-protocol` 0.1.0, and Orbit terminal presentation in ORBS v13 through the in-tree `orbit-protocol` 0.1.0.

VEN-C7, related fitting sentence:
> The selected pane header reserves space for the count and fits its directory label into the remaining width using the existing cluster-safe header fitter.

Replace “its directory label” with “its pane label”.

**Add to EON-C8 / EON-C10 Result; no existing rename clause:**
> `eon pane rename PANE NAME [--json]` pins a name; `eon pane rename PANE --clear [--json]` restores automatic naming. `--` permits an option-looking NAME. Names are trimmed; an empty result clears the pin. Invalid names fail without mutation. Rename addresses an explicit pane anywhere in the addressed workspace and changes no workspace, tab, pane or popup selection or desktop focus. Window rename and clear actions use the same mutation. Pins follow pane moves, survive presentation detach and reattach, and end with the pane or supervisor; recovery does not restore them. Workspace inspection and action replies expose each pane’s `label` and nullable `pinned_name`, independently of attention records.

**EONW proposal:** one v20 with shn4.3: `Pane.label: String` ≤450 UTF-8 bytes, containing the existing ≤128-byte ID and a name/context portion ≤80 Unicode scalars; `Pane.pinned_name: Option<String>` and `RenamePane { pane: String, name: Option<String> }`, with names ≤80 scalars/320 bytes, excluding controls and the format characters Orbit’s management-title cleaner removes. Reject oversized pins; visibly elide composed display text. Preserve the 2 MiB frame and existing aggregate limits. shn4.3 adds `workspaces: Vec<WorkspaceSummary>` of 1–32 entries, each `id: String` (canonical `wN`, ≤128 bytes), `name: Option<String>` (1–64 scalars/256 bytes), `tab_count: u16` (1–64), and `active_workspace: String`. Recommend also `workspace: String` identifying whose `tabs`/`active_tab` the reply projects; `active_workspace` continues to identify the shown workspace. These are proposed bounds and names, not fields already approved by shn4.3.

**Open choices**
1. Clear syntax: `--clear`; empty NAME only; both. **Recommend both**, with `--` handling like the existing command-pane parser; empty-name clearing also agrees with approved EON-C33 workspace rename.
2. JSON: `pinned_name`/`label` or `name`/`label`. **Recommend `pinned_name`/`label`**: existing attention `name` already means terminal title.
3. Context order: `NAME · DIRECTORY` or `DIRECTORY · NAME`. **Recommend the bead’s appended directory**; the mock uses the opposite order and needs reconciliation.
4. Configuration: fixed policy with a recorded rationale, or `terminal.pane_label_style = "title-directory"` (`directory`, `title`, `title-directory`) plus `terminal.pane_id_dim = true`. **Recommend the settings**, following existing terminal presentation settings; Runtime resolves them and Venus parses no config.
5. Window action: Commands entries or a pane-header menu. **Recommend Commands entries**, using the existing command surface without adding a shortcut.
6. Metadata: move existing ORBS observers to Runtime, or add management metadata. **Recommend existing observers for this slice**: they already carry title and CWD; `attention.record.name` alone cannot cover ordinary panes.
7. Contrast: a resolved-fill target or an opaque backing that guarantees contrast. **Recommend the target**; arbitrary translucent compositor backdrops cannot support the bead’s unconditional ≥4.5:1 guarantee.

**Conflicts/splits:** omit the research’s executable fallback, process lookup and ORB-C12/C13 management changes: the bead specifies title → directory, and those additions need separate approval. Preserve EON-C31 attention meanings. Pin persistence beyond supervisor life is separate. Label-only updates must preserve zoom, navigation, scroll and attachments. EON-C28 needs no field-specific amendment: its existing 1.0 fixture rule covers whichever fields ship. The shared bump also replaces the current EONW references: EON-C8’s “Current EONW v19 workspace/popup values, Orbit terminal identities/endpoints and Venus `VEN-C8`.” → the same clause with v20; EON-C10’s “Current EONW v19 and accepted Orbit management operations.” → v20; its package sentence’s “v19 bytes” → “v20 bytes”; Venus’s index preamble likewise moves canonical EONW v19 to v20. Historical proof/version references remain.

title: Find why keys right after window start miss the first terminal until it is clicked
description:
## Why

Seen by the eon-gl1xo agent, 2026-11-04, in its isolated installed dogfood (private headless Sway, keys from wdotool). After the window starts and the Files directory picker is dismissed, keys sent right away do not reach the first terminal (p1) until p1 is clicked once. The hints show terminal focus all the same. This happens without the shortcut viewer, and predates eon-gl1xo. Evidence: /home/lucca/.cache/eon-agents/eon-gl1xo-work/dog/focus/ (f1, f2).

It is either a headless or wdotool artifact, or a real startup-focus bug. If it is real, a person's first keystrokes after opening a window are lost, which would be bad (rule 8, happy users).

## What

Investigate and classify. Do not fix inside this bead unless the fix is small and obvious.
1. Reproduce in the isolated environment: docs/DEVELOPMENT.md, and the recipe in memory isolated-eon-capture-recipe.md.
2. Rule out the harness. Compare wdotool focus and seat state against a real key path. Check whether Venus's keyboard focus (the Wayland keyboard enter event) or Eon's selected pane is what is missing.
3. Check whether a real compositor shows it. A non-activating check on a private session is fine; never Lucca's live windows (rule 9).
4. Report the root cause, or a no-bug verdict with evidence. If it is a real bug and the fix is not small and obvious, file a separate fix bead linked as discovered-from this investigation. A small obvious fix may stay here only with the same required proof/review; do not silently expand this diagnostic session.

## Acceptance

A record that names the cause, with the evidence that proves it. Either the harness is at fault, with the recipe updated to prime focus, or there is a reproducible product bug with a linked fix bead (or the small verified fix is completed here).

## Evidence and proof boundary

Record exact artifact/compositor/input-tool revisions, seat and native keyboard-enter state, selected pane and a portable reproduction recipe on this bead; the temporary focus/f1,f2 captures and private memory recipe are discovery pointers, not the sole acceptance evidence. Distinguish keys sent before keyboard focus from keys delivered to Venus but dropped after the picker. A no-bug verdict needs a supported input path, not just a retry that happens to pass.

Owner: Venus's native input/focus boundary and Runtime's selected-pane state as found by diagnosis. Read venus/docs/REFERENCES.md for native lifecycle/input before choosing a fix. Portability: isolated Linux Wayland investigation; no X11 or other platform expansion. Any new lifecycle/contract behavior stops for approval. Never take focus from Lucca's live desktop or read/write his live terminal. A harness-only finding updates its owning reproducible recipe; a code fix retains a focused regression, required workspace proof/review and isolated installed observation.

title: Bump Orbit's Ghostty to a revision with OSC 7501 support
description:
## Why

Lucca decided on 2026-10-21 (eon-agent-sidebar-yx8.1) to bump Orbit's Ghostty now, at P1. This
replaces the alternative of adding an OSC 7501 pre-scanner to Orbit.

- **What the sidebar needs:** the agent attention sidebar (yx8) takes its state from OSC 7501,
  the Program Status Protocol
  (https://www.superlogical.com/rex/docs/build/program-status, rev 0.4). Claude Code >= 2.1.295
  and Codex >= 0.163 emit it natively.
- **What libghostty-vt provides:**
  - From Ghostty a4aacd91 (#14560) it parses OSC 7501 and answers the `OSC 7501;?` probe. Claude
    reports only after that answer arrives before DA1.
  - Rev 0.4 support lands in 9cd19b40d (#14630).
  - Malformed-id and length validation land in 8c425a7bd (#14793).
- **Where Eon is:** Eon pins Ghostty a887df42 (2026-07-11), about 1,700 commits older.
- **What else the bump brings:** the semantic-prompt (OSC 133) and reset options, and probably the
  key-release fix that the deferred bead orb-ze3 is waiting for (bd647035; ancestry not yet
  checked).

Rejected: an OSC 7501 pre-scanner in the Orbit host. It is smaller, but it would be a second OSC
parser beside libghostty. Lucca preferred the bump.

## Acceptance

- Orbit builds and ships through the flake against an exact Ghostty revision at or after
  8c425a7bd.
- Every ORB-C real-PTY and lifecycle check passes again on the new revision.
- Orbit's Rust host can reach the program-status callback, through a safe wrapper or a minimal
  binding, ready for the yx8 Orbit-records slice. Storing the records is not part of this epic.

## Children

1. Spike: measure the bump and choose the binding route. The output is a decision record;
   nothing merges.
2. Land the bump with full Orbit proof.

## Related

- orb-ze3 (the deferred adoption of a released crate) loses its purpose if this lands.
- Its stop conditions forbid unpublished Git dependencies and copied bindings. Whether to relax
  that is the policy question the spike must put to Lucca.
close_reason: Both children closed: the bump landed in 03afe53 with the full Orbit proof (eon-a9tr.2), after the eon-a9tr.1 spike.

title: Spike: measure the Ghostty bump to OSC 7501 and choose the binding route
description:
## Why

This is the first child of the Ghostty bump epic. Three unknowns decide how big the bump is: the
Zig toolchain, the Rust binding, and drift in the C ABI. Measure them before changing the
shipping tree.

## Evidence

**Current pins in this repository**

- `flake.nix:31` pins the Ghostty input at a887df42c56f6de86c0fe6da9c4eeca37931e083, and `:246`
  asserts that rev.
- `flake.nix:216`, `:271` and `:803` use `zig_0_15`.
- `orbit/Cargo.toml:9` pins `libghostty-vt = "=0.2.2"`.
- The sys crate's build.rs compiles the flake's Ghostty through `GHOSTTY_SOURCE_DIR`
  (`flake.nix:225-229`). Its checked-in bindings must match that source.
- Code that calls libghostty: `orbit/src/{cli,frame,input,pointer,pty}.rs`.

**Research from 2026-10-21**

The report is `~/pjs/refs/agent-sidebar-research/research-orbit-7501.md`; the clones are
`~/pjs/refs/ghostty-7501` and `~/pjs/refs/libghostty-rs-7501`.

- **Zig:** Ghostty 8c425a7bd needs Zig 0.17.0. Eon's nixpkgs (567a49d) has 0.16; nixpkgs master has
  0.17.
- **Rust binding:**
  - crates.io libghostty-vt 0.2.2 pins a887df42.
  - libghostty-rs master (0ef80413) pins 3425025e, which is older than #14560. It already
    carries the breaking PRs #84, #85 and #87.
  - It has no wrapper for program status, semantic prompt or reset.
- **C API at 8c425a7bd:**
  - `GHOSTTY_TERMINAL_OPT_PROGRAM_STATUS = 46`, with callback `GhosttyTerminalProgramStatusFn`.
  - The callback receives a sized struct with borrowed strings; progress is -1 when absent.
  - The probe is answered only when both that callback and WRITE_PTY are set
    (stream_terminal.zig:972).
- **ABI changes found so far:**
  - `GhosttyTerminalOptions` is removed, and `terminal_new` now takes `(cols, rows)`.
  - Scrollback is set through `OPT_SCROLLBACK_MAX_BYTES`. This touches Orbit's byte budget at
    `orbit/src/frame.rs:19` (ORB-C8).
  - The clipboard write callback now returns void and replies through a function (ORB-C11).
  - `mode_get/set` are removed.
  - The render-state colors call is removed.
- **Behaviour changes found so far:** CHA/VPA origin, DECRQM, DECXCPR, CSI 19 t, pulling
  scrollback on resize, and paste CR handling.

## Scope

In scope:
- A throwaway worktree or branch, never `edge`, that builds Orbit against Ghostty at or after
  8c425a7bd.
- Ways to get Zig 0.17: bump the nixpkgs input, or add a second pinned input used only for Zig.
- Ways to bind the new API:
  - (a) Send libghostty-rs an upstream PR that adds the wrapper and bumps Ghostty, and consume it
    as an exact git pin until it is released.

title: Accept a request ID on mutating eon commands so a retry never acts twice
description:
Problem: under load a close reported failed and then went through (eon-7nor8); an agent that retries can send text twice or open two panes.
Do: as with Pi Durable's requestId, a repeated ID returns the first result or reports it pending. Exit codes and how long IDs are kept need contract approval (EONW and the eon CLI contract). Owners: Runtime and Eon CLI.
Source: Alma/Pi research, /home/lucca/pjs/refs/alma-pi-research/REPORT.md idea 3.

## Epic boundary and first slice

The outcome spans different mutating command paths and is not one implementation session. Keep this bead as the overall outcome; its first child inventories the existing request-ID owner and drafts the retry contract. Implementation children are proposed there and created only after the approved boundary is known. This pass approves no new result/exit code or durable replay store.

At 6e63eb7, runtime control.rs:266 generates a fresh internal request ID; workspace.rs:1245 rejects duplicates, and :1262 retains separate bounded queues (MAX_RECENT_REQUESTS = 256 at :21). EON-C8 already protects the last 256 accepted mutations from repeating Stop; it does not promise that a new CLI invocation can provide that ID or recover the first result. Preserve this safety while defining stronger retry behavior.

Acceptance for the eventual epic: a caller can retry each approved mutating command with an explicit ID without duplicating its action, with specified behavior for pending/completed/failed work, payload/target mismatch, expiration and process/generation changes; docs and CLI/JSON/exit semantics match the approved guarantees. Every window action continues through the same owner. Never promise exactly-once behavior across a restart without an approved persistence design and proof.

Owners: Eon Runtime for request identity/admission/result lifetime, CLI for syntax/projection, existing authorization owners for terminal writes. EON-C10, EON-C8 and EON-C36 plus canonical EONW apply as touched; exact amendments need approval. eon-7nor8's longer wait remains independent and does not provide retry semantics.

title: Inventory mutating command retries and draft the caller-supplied request-ID contract
description:
## Why

Parent eon-aaxd7 asks for caller-supplied IDs so retries of mutating eon commands cannot act twice. A failed-looking close under load motivated it (eon-7nor8); the accepted longer-wait fix there remains separate. This is the first planning-only child, not authorization to implement a replay cache or change a protocol.

## Evidence and owner

At 6e63eb7, runtime/crates/eon-runtime/src/control.rs:266 generates an internal request ID; workspace.rs:21 bounds history to 256; reject_duplicate at :1245 answers duplicate-request, and remember at :1262 keeps mutation/inspection histories separate. EON-C8 already prevents repeated Stops among the last 256 accepted mutations. This is admission protection, not a caller retry/result-recovery contract.

Runtime owns admission, in-flight and result lifetime; CLI owns supplied-ID syntax/projection; terminal-read/write authorization stays with EON-C35/C36. Read runtime/AGENTS.md before judging the design and inventory the actual command paths, not only WorkspaceSet.

## Scope and deliverable

Research and exact contract proposal only. Inventory every mutating eon command and identify its current owner/transport: workspace actions, terminal send, lifecycle/window/config/update actions as applicable. Say explicitly which guarantees each would receive and any exclusions requiring Lucca's choice; never silently omit a command while calling the outcome all-mutations retry protection.

title: Venus panics in AccessKit on a pane-less tab with no visible terminal
description:
## Defect (found during eon-jqxr, read-only code hunt; confirmed by reading, not run)

`venus/src/accessibility.rs:325` always puts the terminal-content node (CONTENT) in the AccessKit
tree update. In workspace mode it gets a parent only at `:432-441`: under the pane panel when the
tab has no panes and a terminal is visible or the status is non-empty, or under the selected pane.
When the active tab has no panes, no visible terminal and an empty status, CONTENT is in the update
with no parent. accesskit_consumer 0.38.0 `tree.rs:306-310` then panics on the next update ("TreeUpdate
includes N nodes which are neither in the current tree nor a child"), or on the first tree if that
state is the initial one, and Venus exits.

Reachable state: EONW permits a popup-only tab with no selected popup (`validate_workspace`, and
`remove_empty_tab` keeps a tab that still has popups, `runtime/crates/eon-runtime/src/workspace.rs:1309`);
a kept-alive popup dismissed after the tab's last pane exited leaves `selected_popup = None`
(`workspace.rs:681`). Only fires while AccessKit's AT-SPI adapter is active (`update_if_active`,
`accessibility.rs:648`), e.g. with a screen reader running.

The existing unit test `accessibility.rs:2785-2790` asserts the node exists while the pane panel
has no children, but never feeds the update through AccessKit's tree, so it misses the panic.

## Contract

VEN-C18 (popup-only tabs with an empty body) and Venus accessibility: Venus must not exit in that state.

## Acceptance

Red/green: a Venus unit test that feeds successive tree updates for an empty popup-only tab through
accesskit_consumer's Tree (or an equivalent existing harness) panics before and passes after; fix
parents CONTENT (or omits it) consistently. Venus fmt/clippy green.

## Scope boundary

Only this orphan. A second, less likely AccessKit panic (focus on a header button dropped for width
<= 0, `accessibility.rs:380` vs `:519`) may share the fix only if trivially; otherwise file it.
close_reason: Venus omits CONTENT only when it holds no terminal and no status, and parents it otherwise; red/green through accesskit_consumer::Tree

Venus's accessibility snapshot (`Snapshot::tree`, venus/src/accessibility.rs) is the one owner of the AccessKit tree; it now omits the terminal-content node (CONTENT) whenever the pane panel does not parent it, and the panel stays labeled "Empty tab" with no children. Focus never named CONTENT in that state (it falls back to the selected tab without a visible terminal).
- References read: venus/docs/CRATES.md "Accessibility" (the shared Yazelix/accesskit pin); accesskit_consumer at that pin, rev 0f9d186ec6f5e66fe4ccc131ca318dc2725c12f5: consumer/src/tree.rs:306-317 (orphan node / dangling child panics), :546 (focus unwrap), and its own tests' no-op ChangeHandler pattern (tree.rs:751), which the Venus test mirrors as `IgnoreChanges`. docs/REFERENCES.md has no accessibility route.
- Dependency: `accesskit_consumer = "=0.38.0"` as a venus dev-dependency only. It is already in the graph through accesskit_winit's Unix adapter under the same [patch.crates-io] pin, so Cargo.lock gains only the venus edge; no new package, source, feature or build tool. title: Adopt continuous-output scrollback in Eon
description:
## Outcome and contract routing

Consumer: one installed Eon or EonTerm user on x86_64 Linux native Wayland.

Trigger: orb-keep-scrollback-usable-during-output-rgi publishes the accepted Orbit ORB-C8 producer proof and ven-accept-continuous-output-scrollback-a1s publishes the exact Venus VEN-C7 consumer proof.

Result: Eon selects that exact compatible Orbit/Venus pair in its one canonical component graph, refreshes the active Nix profile from the Eon working tree without interrupting live Sessions, and proves on a fresh installed surface that continuous Codex-like terminal output cannot starve entry into or movement within retained scrollback.

Important failures: incompatible identities or builds fail before profile activation; profile refresh never restarts a live supervisor; dogfood cannot be replaced by child documents or mock output; and Eon must not copy scrolling, revision, retry, or terminal policy from Orbit or Venus.

This refreshes EON-C1 through EON-C4 at the accepted child revisions and preserves EON-C5 onward, including EON-C8 workspace behavior. It adds no Eon-owned runtime behavior or new protocol.

## Ownership and order

Orbit owns authoritative terminal output, history, viewport, routing, revision coherence, and the fixed ORB-C8 behavior. Venus owns native input, fractional/kinetic scrolling, presentation, and notices. Eon owns only exact compatible selection, packaging, installed-profile synchronization, and composed acceptance.

Required order:
1. orb-keep-scrollback-usable-during-output-rgi
2. ven-accept-continuous-output-scrollback-a1s
3. this Eon rollout

Status remains deferred until both exact child proofs exist. If either child introduces a breaking ORBS version, second owner, dependency, or unaccepted limitation, stop and revise the rollout before Eon manifest edits.

## Scope boundary

In scope: canonical manifest and lock identities, exact Nix composition, component reporting, Eon/EonTerm packages, installed profile refresh, isolated outermost dogfood, current documentation/changelog, proof metadata, and README LOC.

Out of scope: Eon scroll logic, Venus retries, Orbit fixes, compatibility adapters, live supervisor restart, configuration, performance tuning, other terminal features, direct distribution, or platform expansion.

## Acceptance Criteria

The structured acceptance_criteria field is authoritative. Eon must pin the exact accepted Orbit/Venus pair, refresh the profile without interrupting live Sessions, and prove the installed continuous-output scrollback workflow on a fresh isolated surface.
design:
1. Begin from the exact accepted Orbit and Venus proof commits named by orb-keep-scrollback-usable-during-output-rgi and ven-accept-continuous-output-scrollback-a1s. Confirm the Eon manifest pins are stale before changing them and record old/new identities.
2. Update the single canonical component graph and existing Cargo/Nix inputs only. Preserve exact compatibility assertions and use no adapter.
3. Run the affected Rust, manifest, and Nix checks, build one immutable Eon candidate, and refresh the active eon profile from the working tree.
4. Preserve every running supervisor and Session. Report restart required unless the user explicitly authorizes interruption.
5. On one fresh isolated installed Eon or EonTerm surface, run a bounded continuous-output workload, enter and continue retained history, and verify the viewport remains pinned and neither stale-frame notice appears.
acceptance_criteria:
1. The canonical manifest, Cargo/lock identities, Nix graph, eon versions output, contracts, and package closure select the exact accepted Orbit orb-keep-scrollback-usable-during-output-rgi and Venus ven-accept-continuous-output-scrollback-a1s proof revisions with unchanged compatible ORBS identity.
2. Full affected Rust, manifest, and Nix checks pass; the active eon profile resolves to the just-built store artifact.
3. Profile refresh preserves every running Eon supervisor and Orbit Session. No process is stopped or restarted without explicit user authorization.
4. One fresh isolated installed Eon or EonTerm surface runs continuous Codex-like terminal updates while the user enters and continues retained scrollback. Movement completes, later output does not pull the viewport to live, and neither "preview frame revision is stale" nor "scroll frame revision is stale" is shown.
5. Existing fractional/kinetic behavior, history edges, terminal mouse routing, synchronized output, semantic-key return to live, selection, resize, pane/tab switching, detach/reconnect, and lifecycle remain intact at the composed boundary.
6. Eon contains no scrolling implementation, revision workaround, failure-string matching, compatibility adapter, new dependency, or second component graph.
7. EON-C1 through EON-C4 proofs, changelog, README identities/LOC, exact installed artifact, and Bead closure agree at one source candidate and one metadata follow-up.
notes:
Accepted Eon source proof 71e8f5a8cac938ed7f065890c83d9376551f6014 composes Orbit a65e199e16e97330175e314cacf791fa00f53069 and Venus bdd8b3628452b1dba8c4d4b2ad9bc2e802659d29 under unchanged ORBS v10, ORBF v1, and EONW v4.

Complete locked Rust and Nix checks pass, including 59 Eon workspace tests and 112 packaged Venus tests. Active profile outputs are /nix/store/4sxx1qwbphqrwnhlgz7f2f0ljb0hn6s5-eon-0.1.0 and /nix/store/n5bmygd82arnfhzlcgz6llydap8rr7lw-eonterm-0.1.0; installed generation is g1-d6c7ecee86b0ef8b6617526e8e708595.

The original supervisor and Sessions were preserved without restart. Isolated installed 30 ms continuous-output dogfood passed long, paused, and sub-row touchpad movement; the user accepted the result as super delicious. The isolated generation, scope, processes, and temporary root were removed.

title: Adopt live pane chrome and launch full Eon undecorated
description:
## Outcome

Adopt the exact Orbit/Venus live pane-metadata chain and make full Eon launch Venus without native window decorations by default, so Codex title animation and each pane's CWD live in pane chrome instead of an otherwise redundant desktop title bar.

Smallest observable contract:
- Consumer: a person launching full eon from the desktop entry or CLI.
- Trigger: a new full-Eon Venus surface starts against exact accepted Orbit orb-stream-live-pane-metadata-dz3 and Venus ven-render-live-pane-title-cwd-8c7 proofs.
- Result: Eon supplies --no-decorations to Venus, while every visible pane retains its live title/CWD header. The native window title continues to carry the selected terminal title for compositor/task-switcher semantics even though its decoration is hidden.
- Failures: incompatible child revisions, missing pane metadata, build/profile failure, or failed native proof leaves adoption incomplete and must not restart live Sessions.

Eon owns the default and exact component selection. Venus owns native decoration materialization and pane chrome. Orbit owns terminal title/CWD.

Impact: HIGH for daily dogfood. Effort: S/M after child proofs. Implementation risk: MED because the visible window control surface changes. Confidence: HIGH.

## Evidence

- Full Eon currently calls its launch owner with venus_decorations = true and supervisor::venus_command adds --no-decorations only when that policy is false.
- Existing tests already cover both Venus argv forms.
- Accepted Venus VEN-C9 at 90988f6ebcde68338e202a9c637c59398aafe93d proves the explicit --no-decorations capability while leaving the direct Venus default decorated.
- ven-render-live-pane-title-cwd-8c7 owns the replacement in-pane title/CWD presentation and depends on Orbit orb-stream-live-pane-metadata-dz3.
- The user reports the current native bar is ugly but values the Codex animated terminal title it displays; hiding it before pane chrome is accepted would lose useful state.

## Scope

In scope:
- Pin exact accepted Orbit and Venus proof revisions through Eon's canonical component manifest/lock.
- Rename only the installed desktop action to `Open Eon`, leaving the live window title, application ID, icon, and process identity unchanged.
- Change the full eon product launch default to decorations disabled using the existing boolean/argv seam.
- Preserve direct Venus and EonTerm decorated defaults and their explicit --no-decorations behavior.
- Preserve Window::set_title in Venus for compositor/task-switcher/accessibility and renderer diagnostics.
- Update Eon contract/current-state docs, changelog, manifest proof, README LOC, package tests, and active Nix profile.
- One isolated installed native Wayland dogfood proving pane title/CWD behavior before the decoration is removed.

Out of scope:
- A user setting, runtime toggle, custom titlebar, replacement close/drag/minimize/maximize controls, themes, pane rename, popup/sidebar, layout changes, EonTerm policy changes, stopping/restarting the active supervisor, or modifying Orbit/Venus code in this bead.

## Reference gate before code

Required:
- Exact accepted proofs and compatibility notes from Orbit orb-stream-live-pane-metadata-dz3, Venus ven-render-live-pane-title-cwd-8c7, and VEN-C9.
- Current Eon component graph, launch boolean, supervisor argv, tests, desktop entry, Nix package/profile, and lifecycle preservation checks.
- Current compositor behavior for undecorated winit windows on the supported native Wayland dogfood environment.

Use the existing Venus flag; reject a config schema, environment variable, runtime toggle, custom decoration implementation, or second window policy owner.

## Acceptance Criteria

- The installed launcher action is named `Open Eon`, while a running surface keeps its live terminal title, so launcher search distinguishes action from state.
- The canonical manifest selects exact accepted Orbit and Venus revisions containing live pane metadata and pane-header rendering.
- New full eon launches pass exactly one --no-decorations argument to Venus; no duplicate or conditional hidden source exists.
- EonTerm and direct Venus preserve their current defaults and explicit flag semantics.
- With at least two panes, each visible header shows its own live title/CWD and an inactive Codex-style title animation continues while the native title bar is absent.
- Pane focus, hit testing, accessibility, resize, IME, clipboard, selection, close, supervisor replacement, and Session persistence remain accepted.
- The selected terminal title still reaches Window::set_title and renderer failure still has higher diagnostic priority.
- Locked Rust/manifest checks, affected Nix checks/build, exact generated versions, LOC, docs/changelog, and git diff --check pass on one immutable candidate.
- The active eon profile resolves to the just-built artifact. Isolated outermost native Wayland dogfood passes without stopping or restarting the user's running supervisor or Sessions; handoff reports that a restart is required for an existing window.

## Stop conditions

- Stop until Orbit orb-stream-live-pane-metadata-dz3 and Venus ven-render-live-pane-title-cwd-8c7 have exact accepted proof commits and compatible update order.
- Stop if the pane header loses live inactive animation, CWD, accessibility, or honest failure state; do not hide the native bar as a partial substitute.
- Stop before adding settings, custom window controls, runtime mutation, EonTerm default changes, a dependency, or a compatibility window.
- Stop on package/profile failure or if exact pins drift. Preserve live processes and report the incomplete adoption.

## Maintenance notes

This issue removes only the redundant full-Eon decoration after pane chrome earns the job. Manual pane rename remains a separate user choice.
close_reason: Fresh-eyes corrections are implemented and mechanically verified: proof identity and legacy-decoration wording are exact, the regression is smaller, launcher behavior remains accepted, and live Sessions are untouched.

# eon-af2om — Darwin EINVAL in the transport drop test

Initial plan prepared 2026-11-10. Opus approved it with amendments recorded in `01-plan-review.md`, which supersedes this initial proposal's mechanism wording, proof scope and stop state. Implementation and all required proof are complete; results are in `02-proof.md`.

## Identity and scope

- Worktree: `/home/lucca/.cache/eon-agents/eon-venus-einval`.
- Clean detached HEAD and initial edge base: `01573431ed11ba7c60016cfab5d9d7b01102b1a6`.
- Owning bead: `eon-af2om`, already IN_PROGRESS. Read with `br show`; no Beads writes.
- Implementation scope: the existing `dropping_the_transport_stops_its_subscription_and_worker` test in `venus/src/transport.rs` only. Records stay in this work directory.
- Portability disposition: neutral test setup ordering motivated by Darwin's socket-option behavior.

## Observable behavior and owner

Dropping `WorkspaceTransport` must close its Eon event subscription, prevent resubscription, and stop its refresh worker after any already-started exchange finishes. Venus's `WorkspaceTransport::drop` and `Subscription::stop` own this cleanup. The fake Eon in the existing test observes EOF and the absence of later work. Setting a test read timeout must happen while the peer is still alive; its five-second bound must remain enforced.

No contract text, wire format, lifecycle policy, UI action, configuration, default, dependency, export, or changelog change is proposed. This repairs the fixture used to prove existing behavior. `VEN-C8` already specifies that connected workspace-request failures make the workspace unavailable and clear on a successful snapshot.

## Classification: production can encounter EINVAL, and already handles it

The classification at `/home/lucca/.cache/eon-agents/eon-events-macos-work/bead/eon-cud7o/07-mac-proof-42771289810.md` records an observed Darwin panic at the test's `set_read_timeout(...).unwrap()`, after `drop(transport)`. It passed elsewhere in that same mac-proof run. The ordering explanation was originally an inference; the kernel source supports the mechanism:

- Apple XNU revision `ac9718fb1af618d5ce8678d0dc6e8a58f252216f` (`xnu-12377.121.6`), [`bsd/kern/uipc_usrreq.c`, lines 1618–1631](https://github.com/apple-oss-distributions/xnu/blob/ac9718fb1af618d5ce8678d0dc6e8a58f252216f/bsd/kern/uipc_usrreq.c#L1618-L1631): disconnecting a Unix stream marks both endpoints unable to send or receive.
- The same revision's [`bsd/kern/uipc_socket.c`, lines 4502–4521](https://github.com/apple-oss-distributions/xnu/blob/ac9718fb1af618d5ce8678d0dc6e8a58f252216f/bsd/kern/uipc_socket.c#L4502-L4521): `sosetoptlock` rejects that state with EINVAL, before processing the requested socket option. This is inspection evidence, not a native reproduction on the mac-proof host.

I searched every `setsockopt`, `set_read_timeout`, and `set_write_timeout` occurrence under `venus/`. There are no explicit Venus `setsockopt` calls. The production timeout calls are all in `venus/src/transport.rs`:

| Path | Can peer close before option setup? | Existing handling |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `Subscription::open`, lines 620–627 | Yes, after `UnixStream::connect`, before `set_write_timeout`. | Any option/write/nonblocking error returns `None` through `.ok()?`, dropping the stream. `run_subscription` waits with bounded backoff and retries; ordinary workspace polling continues. EINVAL already takes this closed/failed-subscription path. |
| `workspace_exchange`, lines 927–938 | Yes, after connect, before read/write timeout setup. | Any timeout-setup error becomes `ExchangeError::NotAnswering`, drops the stream, and becomes `WorkspaceEvent::Unavailable` through `ExchangeError::into_event`. `exchange_until_dropped` continues with a fresh connection on the next request/refresh. EINVAL already takes the connected-request-loss path, like an early EOF. |
| Orbit `Transport::run` / `socket_loss` | No Venus timeout setup in this path. | No new EINVAL classification is needed in the Orbit error-kind matcher. |

Inspected callers: `exchange_until_dropped` is the production caller of `workspace_exchange`; `run_subscription` is the production caller of `Subscription::open`. Other direct callers are transport tests. `WorkspaceTransport::drop` synchronously invokes `Subscription::stop`, which takes the reader and calls `shutdown(Both)` before releasing it. In the failing test, the next socket-option call runs on the fake Eon's opposite endpoint.

Decision: the errno is reachable in production, but there is no missing production error handling to add. Only the test incorrectly requires option setup to succeed after peer closure. Preserve the existing production treatment of EINVAL as connection failure, and fix the fixture ordering. Adding a special errno branch would duplicate the current handling; broadly treating `InvalidInput` as retryable in Orbit would affect unrelated failures. Do not ignore a failed timeout and proceed with unbounded I/O.

Read the root instructions and protocols, required sections of `docs/AGENT-RULES.md`, `venus/AGENTS.md`, `VEN-C3` recovery and `VEN-C8` workspace-failure clauses, the workspace-provider/foundation routes in `venus/docs/REFERENCES.md`, both development guides, and the `eon-kz4p.1` cross-check recipe. The existing production paths are the comparable in-tree implementation: both already dispose of failed sockets rather than panicking. No lifecycle boundary or dependency shape changes, so no additional architectural reference gate is needed.

## Implementation after plan review

1. Fold in or explicitly rebut every Opus finding before editing implementation.
2. Move the existing `subscription.set_read_timeout(Some(Duration::from_secs(5))).unwrap()` immediately after `let mut subscription = eon.subscription()`, before writing the subscribed response, answering the refresh, and dropping the transport. Add one short comment explaining Darwin's rejection of socket options after peer close.
3. Keep the timeout value, its checked result, `read_to_end(...).unwrap()`, the empty-resubscription assertion, and all worker-quiescence assertions and timing bounds unchanged. No sleeps, retries, swallowed errors, platform skips, or relaxed assertions are added.
4. Inspect the diff to confirm the change reaches only this fixture. No callers, fixtures, configuration, exports, or user documents need adjustment. No live processes or user data are touched.

The existing test remains the meaningful regression check: a subscription left open fails its bounded EOF read; resubscription or continued refreshes fail the following assertions. Linux need not reproduce Darwin's errno to exercise these assertions. The requested deterministic Linux closed-peer test is conditional on a production-path change; none is planned. If review identifies missing production handling, revise this plan and add a deterministic closed-peer regression (including injected option failure if Linux does not emit EINVAL) before implementing that change.

## Proof after implementation

Stage the final source change before the acceptance checks, record `git write-tree`, and keep every attempt, environment, command, exit status, and nextest summary in numbered Markdown records here. Proof applies only to that staged tree. No tests have been run during planning.

Run focused checks first, with low priority and six Cargo jobs:

The stable rustup toolchain, Apple std, and clippy component are installed. Resolve the rustup cargo with `rustup which cargo`, then use that toolchain's bin directory on PATH and its `rustc` explicitly, so Nix's host-only compiler is not selected:

```sh
  "$task_rust_bin/cargo" clippy --locked --target aarch64-apple-darwin \
  -p yazelix-venus --all-targets -- -D warnings
```

Record both compiler versions and actual Linux host target. The kz4p.1 Bend/Zig environment exports are needed for Orbit's build script; Venus depends only on its protocol crate, so do not import that unrelated build environment. Darwin clippy establishes compilation only.

After clippy is clean, queue Venus's suite through the required machine-wide wrapper:

title: Project source-aware agent attention into the Eon Bar
description:
## Outcome and routed contract

After the source-aware agent sidebar and core Eon Bar are proved, add one compact bar projection of Eon-authored agent attention without turning the header into a generic status tray.

Consumer: one person supervising supported coding-agent work across an Eon workspace.

Trigger: the authoritative normalized attention owner reports a fresh actionable state, changes its count/priority/freshness, or the user activates the summary.

Result: the Eon Bar shows at most one bounded source-aware summary such as “1 needs input”, collapsing to an icon and count under width pressure. The summary uses the sidebar contract's exact normalized state, source, freshness, acknowledgement, and navigation owners. Activation opens or reveals the existing native sidebar without automatically changing desktop focus or jumping to an agent. Tabs and required bar controls keep priority.

Important failures: missing hooks, unsupported providers, stale/out-of-order events, provider restart, removed targets, unavailable sidebar, or narrow layout never become guessed working/done/input-needed state, never block terminal use, and never displace the active tab identity or core controls.

Impact: MEDIUM after provider-backed agent attention exists. Effort: M. Risk: HIGH before the prerequisite contract and LOW-to-MEDIUM after it. Confidence: HIGH in the projection boundary, deliberately LOW in any pre-provider schema.

## Evidence

- `eon-agent-sidebar-yx8` already owns provider selection, normalized working/needs-input/done/unknown-or-stale semantics, source precedence, freshness, acknowledgement, tab rollup, exact target navigation, and the native sidebar.
- `eon-deliver-native-eon-bar-w4d` owns the single-row bar, fixed controls, tab-first width priority, and installed full-product acceptance.
- EON-C8 currently excludes provider state. The attention contract must change that boundary explicitly rather than smuggling process or terminal inference into presentation.
- Nova and its Radar design deliberately keep agent activity out of tab labels and require source-driven state. Preserve that separation.
- VS Code status-bar and notification guidance inspected on 2026-09-17 supports brief contextual summaries and escalating higher-attention states outside a crowded permanent status area; it is comparison guidance only.

## Prerequisites and reference gate

Hard prerequisites:
- `eon-agent-sidebar-yx8` is closed with one real provider-backed workflow, exact normalized state/freshness/acknowledgement semantics, reliable sidebar navigation, and accepted Eon/Venus revisions.
- `eon-deliver-native-eon-bar-w4d` is closed with EON-C21 and exact accepted VEN-C21.
- No other Eon/Orbit/Venus implementation frontier is active unless the user explicitly authorizes a change.

Before implementation:
- Read the exact accepted sidebar and bar contracts/proofs plus their provider source, EONW, Eon action, Venus scene/accessibility, and narrow-layout owners.
- Decide whether the accepted existing snapshot/action surface can carry the projection. Add no protocol version or action unless the exact sidebar contract leaves a proven gap and the user accepts that scope.
- Reuse the normalized attention owner. Venus must not reinterpret provider events, terminal output, process names, elapsed silence, or pane activity.
- Record the smallest EON-C21/VEN-C21 extension and its first falsifier before code.

## Scope

In scope:
- One compact, optional, non-idle agent-attention summary in the existing Eon Bar.
- Deterministic priority, bounded count/text, narrow-width collapse/hide behavior, source/freshness accessible context, and activation of the existing sidebar.
- Exact Eon/Venus composition and installed native acceptance after prerequisites close.

Out of scope:
- Provider adapters or normalized-state design, sidebar implementation, agent launching/resume, chat, token/quota dashboards, terminal/output scraping, process inference, polling screens, notifications, or automatic focus.
- Per-tab dots, activity text in tab labels, multiple provider badges, user-configurable widgets, plugins, a second row, or a generic event/status framework.
- Nova/Radar compatibility, unsupported-provider claims, remote orchestration, Orbit terminal authority changes, or platform expansion.

## Implementation notes

1. Consume the accepted sidebar's normalized projection directly; do not create a second aggregate or freshness owner in Venus.
2. Give required bar interactions and active-tab identity priority. The summary yields text first, then count/icon, then the whole optional projection.
3. Use semantic text/icon plus color, never color alone. The accessible name carries the exact state, count, source, and freshness that the prerequisite contract authorizes.
4. Activation only reveals/toggles the existing sidebar. A separate explicit action remains responsible for jumping to a tab/pane.
5. Protect one deterministic state/width/accessibility boundary and one stale/out-of-order negative, then run the exact affected protocol/Rust/Nix/installed route.

## Acceptance criteria

- With no actionable supported-agent state, the core bar is visually and behaviorally identical to EON-C21.
- Fresh accepted attention produces at most one summary whose label/count/priority exactly matches Eon's normalized owner; Venus performs no provider-specific interpretation.
- “Needs input” and accepted completion/review attention outrank informational working state according to the prerequisite contract. Stale or unknown evidence is never displayed as live work or completion.
- At narrower widths, summary text yields before its count/icon, and the optional summary disappears before the active tab identity, New tab, Shortcuts, or active Close becomes unreachable.
- Pointer, keyboard, and AccessKit activation reveals the existing sidebar without terminal bytes, automatic target jump, desktop-focus theft, or Session mutation.
- Missing provider integration, sidebar unavailability, stale/out-of-order events, provider restart, and removed targets degrade to the prerequisite contract's explicit state without polling or inference.
- Existing tab labels, scrolling, bar controls, dragging, tooltips, notices, popup/picker behavior, terminal input, and accessibility remain unchanged outside the optional projection.
- Exact provider/Eon/Venus/EONW identities, focused state/width/accessibility checks, complete affected Rust/Nix checks, profile refresh, and isolated native Linux Wayland dogfood pass without restarting live Sessions.
- Documentation names only the proved provider workflow and preserves unknown state for unsupported providers.

## Stop conditions

- Stop if either prerequisite is incomplete, stale, or lacks one authoritative normalized attention/freshness owner.
- Stop if the projection requires terminal scraping, process-name inference, elapsed-silence inference, duplicate aggregation, a generic event bus, polling every terminal, or a widget/plugin framework.
- Stop if reliable activation requires automatic focus transfer, provider-specific UI logic in Venus, or a new protocol/action not explicitly selected.
- Stop before adding per-tab markers, quota widgets, another bar row, or platform/support claims.

## Maintenance notes

This bead records a gated future product outcome, not implementation activation. Its two dependency edges are intentional: the header supplies the presentation surface, and the sidebar supplies truthful semantics. The projection must remain removable without affecting agents, tabs, Sessions, or the sidebar.
notes: Quota reconciliation — 2026-09-17: `eon-deliver-codex-quota-eon-bar-yg0` is a sibling typed first-party fact, not a prerequisite and not plugin/widget-platform evidence. When both are proved, required bar controls and active-tab identity remain highest priority; source-aware actionable attention outranks informational quota; quota collapses/hides first. Reuse only VEN-C21's direct layout owner—do not introduce a shared widget trait, registry, command runner, provider aggregator, configuration surface, or event framework. Visibility/order configuration stays deferred until both chips are dogfooded and actual pressure exists.
close_reason: Superseded by eon-agent-sidebar-yx8.2 (Lucca, 2026-10-21, D11): per-tab attention badges show whenever the sidebar is not visible, replacing a single Eon Bar summary chip.

title: Show an agent that reported done while its background work still runs
description:
## Problem

Lucca, 2026-10-27: busy agents in the sidebar showed a green check (finished) until he clicked them.
eon-eon-attention-working-hides-finish-7df0's step 1 (pty harness, Claude Code 2.1.303; logs under
/home/lucca/.cache/eon-agents/attn-work/osc7501/) found the cause is not EON-C31's ranking:

- Claude Code reports its main record `done` whenever its turn ends, even while work it started
  keeps running: a background Bash task (run 2: done at 4.9 s while `sleep` ran until 24 s), or a
  background subagent waiting on its own background shell (run 5: main `done` and the subagent's
  `clear:id` in one write at 15.7 s, then 20 s of `done` with no record while the subagent and its
  shell were alive).
- Coordinator agents and their workers run long background builds, tests, Monitor and ScheduleWakeup
  waits all the time, so the sidebar shows a green check on agents that are still building.
- Eon receives only `done`; no ranking rule can see the background work.

## Expected

When an agent's record is done (or a raised idle) and processes it started are still running in
that terminal, the sidebar and tab badge show a distinct state, e.g. "waiting on background work",
not the finished check. When that work ends, the state returns to finished or idle per EON-C31
(including raising and seen rules: decide whether the finish is raised when the background work
ends).

## Approval

Lucca, 2026-10-27, relayed by eon-overseer. Asked: "5. 'Waiting on background work' badge: file it
as a P1 bead? I recommend yes." He replied "aprpove" to that message. This approves filing the bead
and investigating. The new EON-C31 state, its contract text, its badge glyph (VEN-C21) and any wire
change need his explicit approval before product code.

## Contract

EON-C31 (a new normalized state or a qualifier on Finished), VEN-C21 badge and sidebar row, ORB-C15
if Orbit must report the terminal's live descendant processes. A wire change is an EONW and possibly
ORBS version bump.

## Investigation first (reference gate, consequential: lifecycle and wire)

1. Where the signal comes from. Orbit owns the PTY and its process group: can it report "the
   foreground program has live descendants that are not the program itself" cheaply and portably
   (Linux /proc today; record the Darwin path per Platform Discipline), without polling cost beyond
   EON-C31's 2 Hz? Alternatives: Claude Code hooks or a status line Eon installs for Claude (does
   Eon already configure Claude's OSC 7501, or is it native?), which would cover only Claude.
2. What counts: child shells of a background Bash task, Codex `exec` runs, nix builds; exclude
   long-lived helpers (MCP servers, LSPs) that every Claude session keeps. Measure on a real Claude
   Code session which descendants are always present.
3. Comparables: how other agent-aware terminals (see ~/pjs/refs/WATCHLIST.md: Rex, Moshi, herdr)
   and Nova's radar show background work.
4. Propose the state, glyph, contract text and wire change to Lucca (numbered, with a
   recommendation) and stop.

## Prerequisites

eon-eon-attention-working-hides-finish-7df0 landed (same module).

## Acceptance

Defined after Lucca approves the design: at least a unit test on the presenter, an Orbit real-PTY
check if Orbit reports descendants, and one isolated installed observation with a real Claude Code
session running a background `sleep` showing the new badge, then finished when it ends.

## Scope boundary

Only "agent says done, its own background work still runs". Not: sounds or notifications, other
providers' quota, agent-parity CLI fields beyond what the new state needs.
close_reason: All slices landed: Orbit counts background processes (yte0.1, 2e7f6e6), Runtime attention reports background on EONW 23 (yte0.2, f495068), Venus draws it and the installed proof is recorded (yte0.3).
