comments.author: lucca
comments.text:
Reference gate (AP-REFERENCE-001; consequential: lifecycle, wire and contract). Recorded by bgwork, 2026-10-27, before code.

Evidence (no Eon or Orbit process involved; disposable PTY harness, Claude Code 2.1.303; logs under /home/lucca/.cache/eon-agents/bgwork-work/proc/, harness5.py, run1..run6 *.events.log/*.raw/*.screen.txt):
- Every Bash tool call, foreground or background, is `/bin/bash -c source ~/.claude/shell-snapshots/snapshot-bash-<id>.sh ...`, a direct child of claude in a new session (sid = pgid = its pid) with no controlling tty. Its command (`sleep`) is below it in its own group. The PTY foreground group stays claude's group throughout. So rules based on the tty, the PTY session or the foreground group (kitty's background-jobs rule) see none of the agent's work; only the parent-pid tree does.
- Run 2: background `sleep 25` started at 6.5 s, root `done` at 11.6 s while it ran, the sleep exited at 31.4 s, root `working` at 31.37 s (Claude wakes to report the task), `done` at 34.7 s. Run 4: a background subagent runs in the claude process (no new process); its background sleep is a direct child of claude, shaped like run 2; the subagent record clears before root `done`.
- Run 1 (baseline): nothing persists when idle. Claude's own helpers (`rg`, `git`, `gh auth token`) sit in claude's own group and live under 0.3 s; hooks and the status line are setsid but also live under 0.3 s. A read-only /proc scan of every claude process on this machine found no persistent child other than Bash calls (no stdio MCP server or LSP in Lucca's config). A stdio MCP server's group is unmeasured.
- Run 6: "Move to background and exit" spawns `claude daemon` on a new PTY; work reparents to pid 1 and leaves the tree.
- Claude Code exposes background work only to hooks (`Stop`/`SubagentStop` input `background_tasks` and `session_crons`, cc-changelog 2.1.145); its OSC 7501 has no background field and Eon installs nothing into Claude (OSC 7501 is native, cc-changelog 2.1.295).

User-visible behavior: a terminal whose agent record is `done` or `idle` while processes the agent started still run shows "waiting on background work" (new EON-C31 state), not finished or idle; when that work ends the state returns to EON-C31's rules.

One owner per behavior and data:
- Orbit (`orbit/src/platform.rs`, the platform seam, called from the `ProgramStatus` reply path in `orbit/src/host.rs:1414-1420` and `orbit/src/management.rs`) owns the neutral fact "background process count", sampled per `ProgramStatus` request. It already samples `tcgetpgrp` there (`platform.rs:217-221`) and knows its child, which is a session leader (`platform.rs:230-246`).
- Eon Runtime's attention presenter (`runtime/crates/eon-runtime/src/attention.rs`, `Record::normalized`) owns the attention meaning. EONW carries the normalized state.
- Venus owns the glyph only.

Routes read: docs/REFERENCES.md "How should Venus direct human attention across many agent-bearing workspaces..." (prefer structured events and exact identities). Comparables, inspected revisions:
- Codex 0.163 (`refs/codex-0163` 83086188ae): keeps OSC 7501 `working` while background exec processes exist (`codex-rs/tui/src/chatwidget/status_surfaces.rs:325-333`), and shows "1 background terminal running" (`status_indicator_widget.rs:502`). So background work = still busy, owned by the program.
- herdr (143bf5fd47): folds background agents and MCP tasks into `working` by screen regex (`src/detect/manifests/claude.toml:27-49`); no rule for background shells; its process walk uses `/proc/<pid>/task/<tid>/children` with bounded budgets and `starttime` against pid reuse (`src/platform/linux.rs:36-58, 540-559, 671-690`); macOS uses `proc_listpids(PROC_PGRP_ONLY)`, `proc_pidinfo(PROC_PIDTBSDINFO)` (`src/platform/macos.rs:186, 501-550`).
- Nova zj-radar (0b1672606c): hooks only; `Stop` maps to Done and ignores `background_tasks`, so it shows done until Claude's task notification flips it back (`crates/cli/src/agents/claude.rs:18-24`). Same defect as Eon today.
- Rex / OSC 7501 spec (ghostty-7501 8c425a7bd5): background work is a child record (`id=build/test`); no count field. Claude Code 2.1.303 sends no record for background Bash.
- kitty (b2cb871254): the only one that lists background processes, as other process groups of the PTY session (`kitty/child.py:571-590`); rejected below.
- tmux (7f2a35ad33) `osdep-linux.c:38-79`, `osdep-darwin.c:45-66`; wezterm `procinfo/src/{linux,macos}.rs`: foreground-process mechanisms only.

Constraints kept: OSC 7501 stays the sole source of records (ORB-C15); Orbit derives no attention meaning (the count is a neutral fact like the terminal title); no polling beyond EON-C31's 2 Hz (Orbit samples only on the existing request, and only while it holds a record); Venus normalizes nothing; platform mechanics stay in Orbit's one seam.

Rejected:
(a) Claude Code hooks (`Stop.background_tasks`): Claude-only, Eon does not launch the `claude` a person types in a pane so it would have to inject settings into a program it does not own, and it adds a second status source beside OSC 7501.
(b) kitty's rule (other process groups of the PTY session): Claude's Bash work is setsid with no tty, outside the session (measured), and the rule counts a shell's own jobs.
(c) The Runtime reading /proc: it holds no pids, and the PTY and process group belong to Orbit; a second owner and a distribution/platform leak into the Runtime.
(d) `PR_SET_CHILD_SUBREAPER` in Orbit to keep reparented work: changes Orbit's reaping and shutdown lifecycle for a case (work outliving its agent) the bead excludes.
(e) A full /proc scan per sample (kitty's pgid map): ~1000 processes per terminal per 0.5 s; a child-subtree walk costs the subtree only.

Version policy / exit: no new dependency (Linux `/proc` reads; Darwin `libproc` through the `libc` crate already used at `platform.rs:355-375`). ORBM 2 -> 3 and EONW 22 -> 23 if approved.

Checks (after approval): an Orbit real-PTY check of the count; a presenter unit test; one isolated installed observation with real Claude Code running a background `sleep`.

comments.text:

title: Count a terminal's background processes in Orbit's status reply
description:
## Goal

Orbit counts a terminal's background processes and reports the count in the ORBM `ProgramStatus` reply (ORBM 2 -> 3). First of three slices of eon-agent-background-work-yte0, whose comments hold the evidence, the reference gate and Lucca's approval (2026-10-27, relayed by eon-overseer) with the exact adopted text.

## Contract

title: Show waiting on background work in Eon Runtime attention
description:
## Goal

Eon Runtime maps a `done` or `idle` record to the new `background` attention state ("waiting on background work") while its terminal's ORBM reply counts background processes (EONW 22 -> 23). Second of three slices of eon-agent-background-work-yte0, whose comments hold the approval (2026-10-27, relayed by eon-overseer) and the exact adopted text.

## Contract

EON-C31: the Normalization table row, the sentence after the table, the Seen paragraph ("Background holds a raise..."), the caveat "Background work Orbit cannot count" and the Status amendment, exactly as adopted. EON-C28: v22 stays frozen; EONW 23 is a new version (see memory note: an EONW codec change needs a bump).

## Shape

- `runtime/crates/eon-runtime/src/attention.rs`: `Record::normalized` (or its caller) takes the terminal's background count; a record that would map to finished or idle maps to background while the count is above 0. Background neither sees nor clears a raise; focus sees it as usual; when the count returns to 0 normal rules apply.
- Priority: needs input > error > finished > working > background > idle > unavailable (`AttentionState` variant order is the priority order).
- `eon-workspace-protocol`: new version module v23 with `AttentionState::Background`; CLI JSON `attention.state`, tab `attention_rollup` and `sidebar` gain "background"; update parity and docs that list states (docs/USAGE.md or wherever states are listed).
- Venus must still build against EONW 23 (map Background to the working badge or no badge until slice (c), whichever needs no new glyph); say which on the bead.

## Prerequisites

eon-agent-background-work-yte0 slice (a) landed (ORBM 3 carries the count).

## Acceptance

- Presenter unit tests in attention.rs: background masks finished and idle; it ranks below working and above idle in a rollup; a held unseen raise shows finished when the count drops to 0; a `working` after the background work sees it (rule 1); errors and needs input are never masked.
- `nix develop -c eon-test -p eon-runtime -p eon-workspace-protocol` (note the known flake eon-prune-test-flake-sj0c), plus the crates touched by the EONW bump; Codex review per AGENTS.md; EON-C31 text edited exactly as adopted.

## Scope boundary

No Orbit change, no new glyph (slice (c)), no CLI fields beyond the new state value.

title: Count a terminal's background processes in Orbit's status reply
description:
## Goal

Orbit counts a terminal's background processes and reports the count in the ORBM `ProgramStatus` reply (ORBM 2 -> 3). First of three slices of eon-agent-background-work-yte0, whose comments hold the evidence, the reference gate and Lucca's approval (2026-10-27, relayed by eon-overseer) with the exact adopted text.

## Contract

ORB-C15: the "Background processes" bullet, the reply's field list and the Status amendment, exactly as adopted on eon-agent-background-work-yte0. Breaking ORBM change (approved, no adapter); consumer: Eon Runtime (`runtime/crates/eon-runtime/src/sessions.rs`, `attention.rs`), which this slice updates only so it builds and still reads the reply; it ignores the count until slice (b).

## Shape

- A background process descends, by parent process, from a member of the PTY foreground process group, is not in that group, is neither stopped nor a zombie, and started at least 1 s before the request. Walk only the child's subtree, at most 512 processes; count at most 255; a walk that reaches either bound reports the bound; 0 while Orbit holds no records.
- Mechanism in `orbit/src/platform.rs` only (the platform seam). Linux: `/proc/<pid>/task/<tid>/children` and `/proc/<pid>/stat` (pgid, state, starttime vs `/proc/uptime` or CLOCK_BOOTTIME). Darwin: `proc_listchildpids` and `proc_pidinfo(PROC_PIDTBSDINFO)` through `libc`, compile-only and unproved until ORB-C14 resumes.
- Sampled only on the `ProgramStatus` request path (`orbit/src/host.rs` ManageProgramStatus, `orbit/src/management.rs`). If the Bend worker must decide anything (for example "sample only while records exist"), follow orbit/AGENTS.md Host and worker and docs/HOST.md; the count itself is a host mechanism fact.
- `orbit-protocol` management: VERSION 2 -> 3, `ProgramStatus` gains `background: u8`; 4 KiB arithmetic gains one byte. Follow the ORBS/ORBF wire bump checklist (version goldens, manifest subtree hash).
- Portability disposition: isolated Linux and Darwin mechanisms behind the seam.

## Prerequisites

Lucca's approval (recorded on eon-agent-background-work-yte0). eon-overseer's go (Lucca asked to slow down).

## Acceptance

- An Orbit real-PTY check (`orbit/tests/real_pty/`): a child in the foreground group forks a grandchild into its own process group that sleeps about 3 s and the child reports `done`; the count is 0 before 1 s, 1 after, 0 after the grandchild exits; a stopped grandchild and an in-group grandchild do not count.
- The same harness or a disposable PTY measures a dummy stdio MCP server under Claude Code (`--mcp-config`) and records its process group on the bead; if it lands outside claude's group, stop and report to eon-overseer before landing.
- orbit-protocol management tests updated; `nix develop -c eon-test -p yazelix-orbit -p orbit-protocol` (and the Runtime crate it touches), `cargo fmt --check`, `cargo clippy --locked --all-targets -- -D warnings` for Orbit crates; orbit Nix checks per the wire bump checklist; Codex review per AGENTS.md.
- orbit/docs/BEHAVIOR.md and orbit/CHANGELOG.md record the wire change.

## Scope boundary

No attention meaning in Orbit, no EONW or Venus change, no subreaper, no polling beyond the existing request.

title: Share compiled dependencies across agent worktrees so first builds stop compiling everything from scratch
description:
## Why

Overseer, 2026-11-08, after Lucca asked why pane agents run 3-4 hours: each agent worktree compiles all of Eon and its dependencies from scratch into its own target directory (several GB of writes per agent, the IO storms seen on 2026-11-07), on top of queueing for two shared build slots. Lucca: "you decide"; the overseer chose to look at a shared compile cache.

## Scope (development tooling only; no product change)

- Measure a cold agent build today (time, bytes written) as the baseline.
- Evaluate sccache (RUSTC_WRAPPER) through `eon-test`: nix/test-sandbox.nix clears the environment and unshares the network, so SCCACHE_DIR, a writable cache bind and the server's socket need handling; keep the sandbox's isolation guarantees intact (docs/DEVELOPMENT.md). Compare with seeding a new worktree's target from a warm one (hard links), and with nothing.
- Pick one by measurement, document it in docs/DEVELOPMENT.md, and prove that tests still run isolated and that a second worktree's first build gets faster with fewer bytes written.
close_reason: done

comments.author: lucca
comments.text: Web research, 2026-11-08 (Lucca: 'also check the web for solutions'). Options found: (1) sccache as RUSTC_WRAPPER with one shared SCCACHE_DIR and per-worktree targets; set SCCACHE_BASEDIRS so absolute worktree paths hash the same, else cross-worktree reuse is limited (NVIDIA OpenShell PR https://github.com/NVIDIA/OpenShell/pull/2379; https://avihu-daft.pages.dev/recipes/sharing-caches). sccache does not cache workspace path crates well; one report found it neutral there. (2) Seeding from a warm target dir: one report 103 s -> 17 s rebuild (https://docs.rs/crate/trusty-mpm/1.8.2/source/src/core/build_env.rs); a shared live CARGO_TARGET_DIR serializes builds on Cargo's lock and risks overwrites across differing features/toolchains. (3) cargo-worktree puts output under a per-branch path (https://docs.rs/cargo-worktree/). (4) kache, another rustc cache (https://docs.rs/crate/kache/1.2.1/source/README.md), unevaluated. (5) Upstream: Cargo's 2026 cross-workspace cache goal (https://rust-lang.github.io/rust-project-goals/2026/cargo-cross-workspace-cache.html), nightly-first, needs the new build-dir layout, no build scripts or proc macros at first, so not usable yet. Start with sccache + SCCACHE_BASEDIRS through eon-test (registry deps like wgpu are most of the cold cost), measured against hard-link seeding.

title: Close the human-and-agent CLI parity gaps
description:
## Why

Lucca, 2026-10-23: "eon is the terminal for humans and agents to work together" and "agents should be able to do anything". The audit `eon-agent-parity-audit-t31r` mapped every action a person can take in an Eon window to the `eon` CLI path an agent in an Eon terminal can use (inventory recorded on t31r at edge 006e79a; children cite edge 8a25211). Lucca approved the gap ranking, the human-only exceptions and the "Humans and Agents" rule in AGENTS.md and docs/ARCHITECTURE.md. The rule names this epic as the home of the open gaps, so this epic stays open while any gap does.

## Approved gap ranking (original inventory; current status below)

1. Send input to a running pane or popup: eon-pane-send-research-fo4p, then eon-agent-terminal-control-n8ic (related).
2. Read a pane's visible text, title and cwd: orb-p92 phase 1 (related; phase 1 shipped through .15-.19; later reads remain in orb-p92).
3. Create a tab at a directory with an optional command, no picker, no focus change: eon-tab-create-launch-8tl4 (related).
4. Popups from the CLI: eon-agent-parity-a9g0.1.
5. Full attention detail and quotas in `eon session --json`: eon-agent-parity-a9g0.2. (Popup labels turned out to be available already: join `popups[].entry` to `entries[].label`.)
6. Close and act on any tab by ID without moving focus: eon-agent-parity-a9g0.3, plus eon-89ho (related).
7. A pane's command and exit status: eon-agent-parity-a9g0.4.
8. Discovery and `wait`: eon-cli-action-discovery-ogzi (related; un-defer at P2 after eon-agent-parity-a9g0.1 and .2).
9. Non-TTY confirmations that cancel silently with exit 0: eon-agent-parity-a9g0.5.
10. Thin wrappers for EONW actions only Venus sends: eon-agent-parity-a9g0.6.
11. Applying `[terminal]`/`[bar]` config without detaching: eon-agent-parity-a9g0.7.

Enforcement: eon-agent-parity-a9g0.8, a compile-time parity check over EONW `Action`. Docs: eon-agent-parity-a9g0.9 fixes doc/code mismatches the audit found.

## Approved human-only exceptions

Venus-local view state: zoom, keyboard focus in the chrome (F6, Tab, Escape, sidebar row stepping), the Shortcuts viewer, the attention inbox, the hints bar, hover and tooltips, scroll position and selection. Also pointer mechanics (mouse reporting to programs, window drag; links use the native opener; Linux uses gio), detaching the person's window, and desktop focus. Relative navigation (Alt+H/L/K/J) counts as covered when an equivalent that names its target exists (`eon focus ID`).

## Current completion map (2e93c69 / 2026-11-12 Beads snapshot)

- Closed original gaps: send/read phase 1 (.15-.19, EON-C35/C36), directory/command tab create,
  attention detail (.2), cross-tab close (.3), non-TTY cancellation (.5), parity enforcement (.8).

  (.20), pane --dir (.21). Cross-tab pane create remains eon-89ho.
- eon window reload implements Venus replacement/config reread (eon-u199d.1/.3); .7 records
  parity acceptance with remaining installed proof instead of adding a second mechanism.

  Linux opener evidence: venus/src/application.rs:382 (gio). Product workspace is now session;
  technical identities retain their spellings.

## Acceptance

- Every child is closed, and gaps 1, 2, 3, 6 (eon-89ho) and 8 are closed in their related beads, or Lucca records each remaining one as an accepted exception in the rule.
- `eon-cli-old-window-after-upgrade-mno4` (closed 2026-10-23) stays linked as a related CLI-reliability fix.

comments.text:
Decision (Lucca, 2026-10-30, "I agree" to all nine items eon-overseer merged from fo4p's and orb-p92's research; full research in the comments on eon-pane-send-research-fo4p and orb-p92, working copies in ~/.cache/eon-agents/claude-panesend-work/ and claude-paneread-work/, authorization notes in ~/.cache/eon-agents/agent-parity/).

Approved shape for pane read and pane send (parity gaps 1 and 2):
1. Callers: any same-user process; EON_TERMINAL validated when present as intent, not security. No tokens, grants or prompts. One setting `[agents] terminal_access = "window"|"none"`, default "window", governs read and send and is documented as not a security boundary.
2. Path: Eon Runtime is the only Orbit caller, over its existing management lease. Management v4, breaking, exact-version, no adapter; terminals on an older Orbit answer terminal-unavailable until restarted.
3. Read: visible area of the active screen as lossy plain text, alternate-screen flag and revision; no styles or history (phase 2). Ended terminal -> terminal-ended. No visible trace.
4. Send: paste, bracketed per the program's mode; `--enter` is a separate Enter key after a configurable 300 ms; 64 KiB limit; refuse text with a newline when the program lacks bracketed paste; refuse control bytes rather than rewrite them.
5. Docs: keep sends short and point at a file for long material (Claude Code treats long pastes as outside material); no typed mode now.
6. One merged split of five beads so each wire bumps once: (a) Orbit: management v4 with ReadVisible and lease input; (b) Runtime: EONW v26 with read, send and the setting; (c) CLI `eon pane read` + docs; (d) CLI `eon pane send` + docs; (e) one joint installed proof. Fallback if (a) cannot fit one session: read lands as v4, send as v5.
7. File an Orbit hardening bead (P2): close the ORBS attach slot on terminals no window shows (any same-user process can attach and type into them; Venus then gets Busy). Code inference, unconfirmed.
8. File a research bead (P2): can Codex's and Claude Code's sandboxes reach the Eon socket? Answer before send ships.
9. One agent writes the merged exact contract text for Lucca's final approval: new ORB-C17 (reads), EON-C35 (read), EON-C36 (send; EON-C34 is reserved by eon-remote-workspaces-52i4), amendments to ORB-C13, ORB-C5, ORB-C3.

title: Show, hide and focus popups from the CLI
description:
## Why

Parity gap 4 of eon-agent-parity-a9g0: create a catalog popup in a named tab and focus an exact
instance. Hide already ships as eon popup hide uN [--json] (eon-quick-search-parity-23y9.3),
not hide-by-entry.

## Approved scope (2026-11-06 Decisions comment; unchanged)

The overseer approved P1-P5/D6-D7 under Lucca's delegation, "i have already taken the important
decisions. the rest is up to you":
- P1: popup show ENTRY [--tab TAB] creates by entry, refusing with the existing ID if present;
  existing instances use popup hide uN / focus uN. No toggle command.
- P2: background creation in any tab of the addressed session preserves active tab/shown session.
- P3: refuse create/focus while the target tab shows a transient popup.
- P4: terminal_access governs Scrollback creation and popup focus, with or without a caller;
  hide stays allowed.
- P5: focus uN selects that exact tab/popup, never relaunches, retargets or sends keys.
- D6: one EONW bump with InvokeIntent::Show. D7: Runtime then CLI/parity/docs/installed proof.
  Session rename eon-30skm is closed. Exact text/plan remains at
  ~/pjs/refs/eon-a9g0-1-plan/bead/01-contract-step.md, PLAN.md and rebaseline-v40-00-plan.md.

This supersedes the old undecided show/hide/toggle ENTRY proposal. No canonical text is edited here.

## Current evidence (2e93c69)

EONW v40.rs:20 is current. Under runtime/crates/eon-runtime/src/, workspace.rs:1573 dispatch
still drops expected_instance; invoke_popup (:1861) refuses inactive tabs (:1876); focus_id
(:2549) handles tabs/panes. cli/parity.rs:107-110 still has InvokePopup's exception but maps
DismissPopup to shipped hide. The Show v41 checkpoint is reviewed but unlanded.

## Existing split and sequence

- .1.1 (in progress): reviewed protocol/preflight checkpoint, tree 084397779d0220a07dd1e20f6e1e5a258a53b887.
  Its handoff forbids standalone activation.
- .1.4 (in progress): popup-ID reuse after supervisor recovery. Preserve the live owner's scope.
- .1.3: remaining Runtime Show/exact focus/supervisor guards and approved EON-C8/C10 amendment;

- .1.2: CLI/parity/help/USAGE/skill/CHANGELOG and installed proof; waits on .1.1 and .1.3
  without a further wire bump.

No live child is edited here. Coordinate reserved v41 with eon-xvz5c/other in-flight bumps:
whichever lands second rebases and uses the next free version, never overwrites a landed schema.
Portability: neutral Runtime/protocol/CLI, native Linux Wayland installed proof.

## Acceptance

- All children close with their bounded proof. Background Show preserves shown session, active
  tab/pane/popup; exact focus selects the named instance without invoking another.
- JSON/refusals follow the approved matrix: pending tab/non-Project, unknown entry, existing ID,

- InvokePopup gains a CLI parity path without the exception naming this epic; DismissPopup keeps its path.
- One isolated installed end-to-end observation covers Show/focus after Runtime lands.

## Reference, proof and boundary

Retain the plan's owner trace CLI → EONW → Runtime → Orbit, inspected reference revisions and
kept/rejected mechanisms (original comparables: tmux display-popup, Zellij floating panes,
kitty overlays). Contract/lifecycle changes stay in their child with the approved amendment;

verification is Beads state/graph.

title: Popup IDs are reused after supervisor recovery, so a saved uN can name a different popup
description:
## Why

Found by the eon-agent-parity-a9g0.1.1 agent on 2026-11-12 (00:19Z) with a runnable failing test:
after supervisor recovery, popup IDs are reused. A popup ID saved before recovery (`u1`) is accepted
for a different, newer popup (a successor Git popup on terminal-2). EON-C10 Target safety says a
stale ID is refused, never silently retargeted. Today this mostly affects `eon popup hide uN`; it
blocks `eon focus uN` (eon-agent-parity-a9g0.1.3), which must select exactly the popup the ID named.

## Evidence

- Counterexample: ~/pjs/refs/eon-a9g0-1-plan/recovery-gate/recovery-gate.patch (a test in the
  existing Runtime harness, no real Eon instance) and recovery-gate.log: on edge 481fe27 plus the
  patch (tree 5f327b6e73ea139b2355970b82b70a387761b74e), `nix develop -c eon-test` exits 100 with
  that one test failing.
- Related: recovery epics eon-remote-workspaces-52i4.6 (checkpoint and restore of sessions and
  layout), which may already own popup ID allocation across recovery; check before fixing.

## Scope

In: popup IDs (and any other uN/pN/tN allocation the test shows reused) never name a different
object after recovery: either the allocator continues past every ID issued before recovery, or a
pre-recovery ID is refused as stale. Keep the counterexample as the red test, make it green, plus
the same check for pane and tab IDs if the allocator is shared. EON-C10 wording only if it is
silent on recovery.
Out: the popup show and focus features themselves (eon-agent-parity-a9g0.1.1 / .1.3).

## Acceptance

- The recovery-gate test passes; a pre-recovery uN is refused or still names the same popup.
- Whole-workspace `nix develop -c eon-test`, fmt and clippy for changed crates.

title: Name the shown session in the reply to eon session switch --json
description:
## Why

An agent that runs `eon session switch WS --json` from an Eon terminal cannot tell from the
reply which workspace the window now shows. The reply projects the caller's own workspace and
has no field for the shown one, so the agent must call `eon session ls` again to confirm the
switch. AGENTS.md "Humans and Agents": everything a person can see about the workspace, an agent
can read from the CLI as data, and the switch's result is what the person sees.

Source: eon-workspace-switching-shn4.9, comment 4351 (2026-10-27), "Out of scope, reported to
the coordinator, no bead filed", item 2 (the morning report's (b)). Approved by Lucca 2026-10-27
(morning report question 11): "11 ok", accepting the recommendation "one for (b) under agent
parity". Relayed by eon-overseer. Parent epic: eon-agent-parity-a9g0.

## Evidence

- ~/.cache/eon-agents/shn4.9-work/run4/inside/r5.json: the reply to a switch run from an Eon
  terminal has keys generation, window, workspace ("w1", the caller's), active_tab, geometry,
  entries, tabs, sidebar; no shown-workspace field and no `workspaces` list.
- runtime/crates/eon-runtime/src/cli.rs:1103-1135: the Snapshot reply prints
  `"session": snapshot.workspace` and then `json_output(&snapshot)` (or `list_json` for
  `eon session ls`); `created` is added only for `new`.
- runtime/crates/eon-workspace-protocol/src/v22.rs:459: the EONW v22 Snapshot already carries
  `active_workspace`, and cli.rs:292 already uses it for `eon session ls` rows. The fix probably
  needs no wire change.
- runtime/crates/eon-runtime/src/cli.rs:1496: `switch WS` sends `SwitchWorkspace`.

## Contract

EON-C10 (typed workspace control: the `eon session` replies) and EON-C33 (several workspaces in
one window); EON-C28 if it freezes `--json` fields (eon-igae.11 must then list the new field). A
new JSON field is a change to EON-C10 text: each contract-text change in this bead needs Lucca's
approval per AGENTS.md. Draft the exact wording and the field name, stop, and bring them to him
before editing docs/CONTRACTS.md. Contract text changes also need the Codex review AGENTS.md
requires.

## Prerequisites

None. Related: eon-agent-parity-a9g0.2 (full attention record in `eon session --json`) touches
the same JSON projection; coordinate if both are in flight.

## Scope

In scope:
- Add one field to the `--json` (and the human) reply of `eon session new/switch/rename/close`
  naming the workspace the window shows after the request, from the Snapshot's
  `active_workspace` (for example `"shown_session":"s2"`; name chosen with Lucca).

title: Let agents read the Eon Bar CPU, RAM and disk chip values from the CLI
description:
## Why

AGENTS.md "Humans and Agents" says everything a person can see about the workspace, an agent can read from the CLI as data. The Eon Bar shows CPU and RAM chips, but Venus samples them itself (venus/src/application.rs:4469), and neither `eon workspace --json` nor the EONW snapshot carries them (runtime/crates/eon-runtime/src/workspace.rs:2275; eon-workspace-protocol v23.rs:459). Found while researching eon-mac-launch-kz4p.9 (Codex report /home/lucca/.cache/eon-agents/eon-overseer/jxa/report.md). The macOS harness's scenario reads the chips through this CLI path once it exists, instead of the accessibility tree.

## Goal

An agent reads the values the window's CPU and RAM chips show (and their hidden or unavailable state) as data from the `eon` CLI.

## Open design (record the reference gate first)

Who owns the sample. Today Venus samples locally and shows it; the CLI is served by Runtime. Two options:
- Runtime samples, and sends the values to Venus and the CLI. Then there is one owner, but the chip moves out of Venus.
- Venus reports its displayed sample back to Runtime. Then the CLI shows exactly what is drawn, but Venus gains a report path.

Recommend one on the bead; it is a protocol/ownership question (EONW), so it stops for Lucca if it changes a contract.

## Acceptance

- `eon workspace --json` (or a named command) returns the chip values on Linux, with the hidden or unavailable state.
- The macOS harness scenario (kz4p.9's chips step) reads them on macOS.
- Review loop and Codex.

## Scope boundary

No change to what the chips show.

## Current plan and acceptance (8ebdd69; replaces stale v23/workspace evidence)

Use `eon session --json`. `venus/src/system.rs` is the sampler;
application.rs:6470-6526 selects CPU/RAM/disk reads. Current snapshot/projection:
eon-workspace-protocol/src/v40.rs:671; eon-runtime/src/workspace.rs:3484.
eon-7i3t9 owns the shared raw-sampler/one-memory-formula gate: reuse its accepted
owner, never a Runtime → Venus dependency or a second sampler. The two options above
cannot override that prerequisite. Settle displayed-sample transport at the reference
gate and obtain exact EON-C10/EONW approval before implementation.

Return CPU, RAM and disk figures/grades and each chip's shown/hidden/unavailable
state, RAM used and total GiB (comment 5830), and CPU information/temperature when
displayed (CONFIGURATION.md:260-301). Do not replace unavailable with zero.
Choose units, sample identity/age and JSON fields in the approval step so one can
compare the CLI data with the displayed sample. No chip behavior change.
Use focused projection/failure checks and one isolated installed comparison; the
current Rust mac-proof harness replaces the closed kz4p.9 scenario. Apply the full
affected wire/runtime route if needed. Portability: neutral projection with isolated
Linux/Darwin readers; name any unexercised native platform.
notes: Sequenced after eon-7i3t9 (2026-11-03 prime-beads P2 pass): 7i3t9 adds the load object (load averages, cores, memory) to eon workspace --json and settles who samples outside Venus (venus/src/system.rs is the only sampler today). This bead then adds the chips' own figures (CPU %, RAM %, disk) and whether each chip is shown, reusing that sampler so there is one RAM formula. eon-mac-launch-kz4p.9 is closed; the macOS acceptance means the current Rust mac harness.

title: Decide whether agents can capture the Eon window as an image
description:
## Why

The Humans and Agents rule (AGENTS.md) says everything a person can see about the workspace, an
agent can read from the CLI as data. Text state is covered by `eon session --json` and `eon pane read` (EON-C35);
what the window looks like is not, so an agent changing theme, fonts, bar or layout cannot check its
result. herdr-app (github.com/herdrdev/herdr-app at b41b5cb, 2026-10-29, defaults/AGENTS.md "Seeing
the window") ships `herdr-app shot [file.png]`: the last rendered frame as a PNG, captured by the
app itself (no screen-recording permission), even when covered or minimized. Lucca approved filing
this, 2026-10-29 (herdr-core/app review in session eon-8e). Parent: eon-agent-parity-a9g0.

## Evidence (edge 42a3f0e)

- AGENTS.md "Humans and Agents" and "Desktop Focus": capture must not take focus.
- eon-pxn.7 (deferred): warns against making pixels the primary state source and says a Venus
  capture contract needs separate approval.
- eon-eonjs-renderer-capture-wec (deferred, P4): renderer-owned capture for a future web client.

## Scope

In scope (decision only):
- Whether `eon` offers a window capture (PNG of Venus's last presented frame for a named window),
  who owns it (Venus renders, Eon Runtime routes, CLI projects), the privacy rule (terminal contents
  appear in pixels, so it follows the terminal-content authorization its owner defines), and a
  draft VEN-C/EON-C text for Lucca.

Out of scope:
- Implementation, screen recording, desktop capture through the compositor, pixels as a state API.

## Acceptance

- A recorded decision with Lucca's approval, and either filed implementation beads or a reason not
  to.

## Implementation Notes

1. Read eon-pxn.7 and herdr-app's `shot` docs; check how Venus could read back its own frame on
   wgpu/Vulkan without focus or compositor help.
2. Draft the contract text and stop for approval.

## Verification

- Planning-only route: bead state and diff.

## Stop Conditions

- Stop before any code or contract edit without Lucca's approval.

## Maintenance Notes

- Related: eon-pxn.7; capture must not become a second terminal-state authority.

## Current decision boundary (8ebdd69)

EON-C35/EON-C36 now define same-user terminal read/input and
`[agents] terminal_access`; orb-p92 is no longer a prerequisite to define base policy.
Recommend evaluating the same setting for pixels, as the existing 2026-11-03 note
says; text-read approval does not approve capture. Decide coverage of all visible
terminals, denied access, absent/stale last frame, hidden/minimized windows,
output-file permissions/overwrite and bounded cost. These are questions, not promises.
Inspect exact comparable/native-host revisions, including the approved Rune track
if relevant; do not assume the current wgpu path is the sole future renderer.
Keep focus and Orbit authority intact. No implementation or privacy/contract change
is approved by this audit. State portability with the recommended native-host route.
notes: 2026-11-03: terminal text is now readable through eon pane read (EON-C35, Proven). Recommend that a capture follows the same [agents] terminal_access setting as EON-C35/EON-C36, since the pixels contain terminal contents.

comments.author: lucca
comments.text:
Merged contract text for pane read and pane send (eon-agent-parity-a9g0.14, 2026-10-30, edge 39e0a25). For Lucca's final approval; nothing is indexed and no CONTRACTS.md, CONFIGURATION.md or code is changed. Sources merged: orb-p92's 2026-10-30 plan (~/.cache/eon-agents/claude-paneread-work/phase1-plan.md §4-6) and eon-pane-send-research-fo4p's draft §6 (~/.cache/eon-agents/claude-panesend-work/fo4p-draft.md), under Lucca's nine-item decision on eon-agent-parity-a9g0 (2026-10-30). Copy: ~/.cache/eon-agents/agent-parity/contracts-merged.md.

Wire summary: Orbit management v3 → v4, one breaking exact-version bump with no adapter that carries both `ReadVisible` and lease input. Consumers are Eon Runtime and Eon; Venus does not use management, and ORBS and ORBF are unchanged. EONW v25 → v26 carries read, send and the setting. Fallback (decision item 6): if the Orbit bead cannot fit one session, read lands as management v4 and send as v5. ORB-C5's and ORB-C13's texts then name v5 for lease input.

---

## 1. New: ORB-C17 — Bounded visible-text reads

- **Status:** Planned
- **Consumer:** The one validated management lease holder (ORB-C13); in Eon, Eon Runtime acting for `eon pane read`.
- **Trigger:** The lease holder sends one management `ReadVisible` request.
- **Result:**
  - Orbit answers with one snapshot of the terminal at one presentation revision N. It holds:
    - N;
    - the active screen, `primary` or `alternate`;
    - the terminal's rows and columns;
    - its title and raw working directory, as ORB-C3 reports them;
    - the active screen's live area as plain UTF-8 text.
  - **What the text covers.** The live area is the rows a client at live bottom would see, whatever any client's scroll position.
  - **How the text is laid out:**
    - one line per display row, top to bottom, separated by line feeds;
    - trailing blanks are trimmed;
    - a soft-wrapped row ends in a line break like a hard one;
    - wide-cell spacers are omitted.
  - **What the text drops.** Styles, colours, hyperlinks, images, cursor, selection and history are dropped, and the reply says the text is lossy. The text holds no control characters other than line feeds.
  - **Size bound.** The text is at most 1 MiB. When the live area exceeds that, Orbit keeps the last whole rows that fit and reports how many leading rows it omitted.
  - **No side effects.** Reading sends nothing to the PTY and changes no terminal, viewport, selection, presentation or lifecycle state.
  - **No partial updates.** While a synchronized update is held, the read waits for its release or the watchdog, as attachment does (ORB-C4), so it never sees a partial update.
- **Important failures:**
  - A malformed request, or one sent while another is in flight, fails with a typed failure and no text; the lease stays.
  - Extraction failure is a typed failure, never empty or partial text.
  - A lease holder that does not read its reply loses the lease under ORB-C13's slow-peer rule. That never blocks PTY processing, presentation, the interactive client or cleanup.
  - After the child exits the run ends (ORB-C13 tombstone), and there is no snapshot.
- **Owner:**
  - Orbit's Bend management policy, which admits the request and orders the reply;
  - its Rust host, which extracts the text with libghostty's plain-text formatter;
  - canonical `orbit-protocol` management v4.
- **Consumes:** ORB-C13 (lease, validation, slow-peer rule), ORB-C4 (held updates), ORB-C3 (title and directory values).
- **Boundary:**
  - No history, scrollback, semantic command regions, escapes, styles, raw PTY bytes or ORBF frames.
  - No input, resize, scroll or process authority; lease input is ORB-C5's.
  - No reader other than the lease holder, and no secret redaction.
  - The text cannot prove ORB-C6 fidelity.
  - Orbit identifies no agent; Eon owns agent policy.

---

## 2. Amendment: ORB-C13 — Same-boot management ownership (one merged change)

- In Result, the bullet "Management carries only bounded identity, live status, the ORB-C15 `ProgramStatus` request, and explicit Stop, with one request and response in flight." becomes:
  "Management carries only bounded identity, live status, the ORB-C15 `ProgramStatus` request, the ORB-C17 `ReadVisible` request, the ORB-C5 lease input request, and explicit Stop, with one request and response in flight."
- In Important failures, the bound "each management message and record: 4 KiB;" becomes:
  "each management message and record: 4 KiB, except one ORB-C17 `ReadVisible` reply, whose text is at most 1 MiB, and one ORB-C5 lease input request, whose pasted text is at most 64 KiB;".
- Consumes "Canonical management v3 and ORB-C12." becomes "Canonical management v4, ORB-C12, ORB-C5 and ORB-C17."

---

## 3. Amendment: ORB-C5 — Semantic terminal interaction

- **Consumer** "Attached clients sending key, mouse, focus, paste, or resize interaction." becomes:
  "Attached clients sending key, mouse, focus, paste, or resize interaction, and the management lease holder (ORB-C13) sending paste or Enter input."
- **Trigger** gains: "or Orbit accepts one management lease input request: a paste of up to 64 KiB, or one Enter key."
- **Result** gains these bullets:
  - Lease input is encoded exactly as an attached client's input would be:
    - a lease paste as an attached client's `Paste`, bracketed when the program enabled bracketed paste;
    - a lease Enter as an unmodified Enter press, plus its release when the terminal's keyboard mode reports releases.
  - Each lease paste is written whole, in owner-loop order with the attached client's input, never interleaved with it.
  - Lease input needs no attachment, works whether or not a client is attached, and changes no presentation, viewport, selection or attachment state.
  - The reply says whether a paste was bracketed.
- **Important failures** gains: "A lease paste containing a line feed or carriage return while the program has not enabled bracketed paste is refused (`unbracketed-newline`) and writes nothing. Lease input after child exit is impossible because the run has ended (ORB-C13)."
- **Consumes** gains: "management v4 lease input".
- **Boundary** gains: "Lease input carries no other keys, chords, mouse, focus or resize; raw bytes are never written."

---

## 4. Amendment: ORB-C3 — Bounded interactive and metadata attachment (Boundary only)

"Visible text observation, agent observation, multiple observers, multiple interactive clients, remote access, and process authority are excluded." becomes:

"Visible text over ORBS, agent observation, multiple observers, multiple interactive clients, remote access, and process authority are excluded. The management lease holder reads visible text through ORB-C17 and sends paste and Enter input through ORB-C5, without either ORBS role."

---

## 5. New: EON-C35 — Reading a terminal from the CLI

- **Status:** Planned
- **Consumer:** An agent or script running as the person's user, in an Eon terminal or outside one.
- **Trigger:** `eon pane read TARGET [--json]`, with:
  - TARGET a pane or popup ID as `eon workspace --json` names them;
  - EON-C10's `--window` and `--generation` selection.
- **Result:**
  - The supervisor that EON-C10 selects (validating `EON_TERMINAL` when set) resolves TARGET in any workspace of its window, shown or hidden, and reads the target's terminal through ORB-C17.
  - JSON carries:
    - the target: `workspace`, `tab`, `pane` or `popup`, and `terminal`;
    - `caller`, as `eon workspace` reports it (null outside Eon);
    - `generation` and `window`;
    - `revision`, `screen` (`primary` or `alternate`), `rows` and `columns`;
    - `title`;
    - `directory`: a string when valid UTF-8, else a byte array, as EON-C10;
    - `text`, `omitted_rows`, and `lossy: true`.
  - Human output prints the text alone.
  - Reading changes no workspace, tab, pane or popup selection, shown workspace or popup, or desktop focus, and never shows a hidden popup. It leaves no visible trace.
  - `[agents] terminal_access` (§7) governs it: `"window"` allows it; `"none"` refuses every read with `terminal-access-off` and no terminal content.
- **Important failures:**
  - Exit 1:
    - `terminal-access-off`;
    - `terminal-ended`: the target's terminal has exited; its exit status belongs to eon-agent-parity-a9g0.4;
    - `terminal-unavailable`: Orbit refused, or timed out after 2 s, or runs an older management version, until the terminal restarts.
  - Exit 3: a missing or stale target, generation or window.
  - Exit 4: a missing or unreachable supervisor.
  - Exit 2: invalid arguments.
  - No failure carries terminal content.
- **Owner:**
  - Eon Runtime: policy, target resolution, the EONW v26 request and the CLI projection;
  - Orbit: ORB-C17.
- **Boundary:** None of the following:
  - history, styles, streaming or waiting (eon-cli-action-discovery-ogzi);
  - per-agent tokens, grants, expiry or audit log;
  - remote or MCP exposure (eon-ciwn.3);
  - redaction;
  - protection against code running as the same user.

---

## 6. New: EON-C36 — Sending input to a terminal from the CLI

- **Status:** Planned
- **Consumer:** An agent or script running as the person's user, in an Eon terminal or outside one.
- **Trigger:** `eon pane send TARGET [--enter] [--stdin] [--json] [-- TEXT]`, where:
  - TARGET is a pane or popup ID as `eon workspace --json` names them;
  - TEXT is exactly one operand, or standard input with `--stdin`. TEXT is required unless `--enter` is given, and `--enter` alone sends only Enter;
  - EON-C10's `--window` and `--generation` selection applies.
- **Result:**
  - The supervisor that EON-C10 selects (validating `EON_TERMINAL` when set) resolves TARGET in any workspace of its window, shown or hidden, and pastes TEXT into the target's terminal through ORB-C5's lease input. Orbit brackets the paste when the program enabled bracketed paste.
  - With `--enter`, Eon then sends one Enter key after `[agents] send_enter_delay_ms` (§7). A line feed or carriage return in TEXT never submits.
  - Sending changes no workspace, tab, pane or popup selection, shown workspace or popup, scroll position or desktop focus. A hidden popup receives the input and stays hidden. The send leaves no trace beyond what the program shows.
  - On success the command exits 0. JSON carries:
    - the target: `workspace`, `tab`, `pane` or `popup`, and `terminal`;
    - `caller`, `generation` and `window`, as EON-C35;
    - `bytes`: TEXT's length, 0 for Enter only;
    - `bracketed`: a bool, null when only Enter was sent;
    - `enter`: true when the Enter was sent.
  - `[agents] terminal_access` (§7) governs it: `"window"` allows it; `"none"` refuses every send with `terminal-access-off` and sends nothing.
  - Documentation advises keeping a send short and pointing at a file for long material. Some agents treat long pastes as outside material: Claude Code marks pastes over 800 characters or 3 lines that way.
- **Important failures:**
  - Exit 2, with nothing sent:
    - `invalid-text`: TEXT is not UTF-8, or contains ESC, another C0 control except tab, line feed and carriage return, DEL, or a C1 control. Eon refuses rather than rewrites it;
    - `input-too-large`: TEXT exceeds 64 KiB;
    - no TEXT and no `--enter`, or other invalid arguments.
  - Exit 1:
    - `terminal-access-off`, with nothing sent;
    - `unbracketed-newline`: TEXT has a line feed or carriage return and the program has not enabled bracketed paste. Nothing is sent;
    - `terminal-ended`: the terminal has exited. The input is rejected, never queued;
    - `terminal-unavailable`: Orbit refused, or timed out after 2 s, or runs an older management version, until the terminal restarts.
  - Exit 1 also when the paste succeeds and the Enter then fails. The reply names the failure with `enter: false`, and the text stays in the program.
  - Exit 3: a missing or stale target, generation or window.
  - Exit 4: a missing or unreachable supervisor.
  - No failure changes focus or workspace state.
- **Owner:**
  - Eon Runtime: policy, TEXT validation, target resolution, the Enter delay, the EONW v26 request and the CLI projection;
  - Orbit: ORB-C5 lease input.
- **Boundary:** None of the following:
  - other keys, chords or raw bytes, or a typed (keystroke) mode;
  - waiting for the program to consume or answer the input; reading back is EON-C35;
  - per-agent tokens, grants, expiry or audit log;
  - remote or MCP exposure (eon-ciwn.3);
  - protection against code running as the same user.

---

## 7. Setting text (docs/CONFIGURATION.md)

Built-in defaults block gains:

```toml
[agents]
send_enter_delay_ms = 300 # Wait between `eon pane send` text and its --enter.
terminal_access = "window" # Let `eon pane read` and `eon pane send` reach this window's terminals; "none" refuses both.
```

Configuration behavior gains:

> `[agents] terminal_access` decides whether `eon pane read` and `eon pane send` may reach this window's terminals.
>
> - `"window"`, the default, lets any process running as you read or send to any pane or popup of the window, in any workspace, shown or hidden.
> - `"none"` refuses both with `terminal-access-off` and reveals no terminal content.
>
> The window reads the setting when it starts. It is a preference and a kill switch, not a security boundary: Eon's socket is private to your user, whose processes can already read and drive terminals.
>
> `[agents] send_enter_delay_ms`, 300 by default, is how long `eon pane send --enter` waits after the text before sending Enter, so agent prompts take the whole paste first. It must be 0 to 5000.

Fixed with reasons, recorded in the owning beads:
- the 1 MiB read and 64 KiB send bounds, as protocol bounds;
- the 2 s Orbit timeout, as a performance budget.

---

## 8. Approved items → clauses

1. Callers, no tokens or prompts, one setting: EON-C35 and EON-C36 Consumer, Result and Boundary; §7.
2. Runtime is the only Orbit caller, over the lease; management v4, breaking, older Orbits answer `terminal-unavailable`: ORB-C13 amendment; ORB-C17 and ORB-C5 Consumer; ORB-C3 Boundary; EON-C35 and EON-C36 failures.
3. Read: visible area, lossy, alternate flag, revision, no history, `terminal-ended`, no trace: ORB-C17; EON-C35.
4. Send: bracketed paste, separate Enter after a configurable 300 ms, 64 KiB, newline refusal, control-byte refusal: ORB-C5 amendment; EON-C36; §7.
5. Docs advice, no typed mode: EON-C36 Result and Boundary.
6. One bump per wire, with the v4/v5 fallback: the wire summary above.
7. and 8. Hardening and sandbox research beads: not contract text; filed separately.
9. This text. ORB-C13 is amended once.

Orbit records the name without checking that the process exists; ORB-C3 matches it at admission. A later `AttachAllow` replaces the name. The name belongs to the lease that set it: when that lease ends, no process is named until the next lease holder names one."

## 4. Amendment: ORB-C3 — Bounded interactive and metadata attachment

- **Consumer** "One local input-capable client and one local read-only metadata observer." becomes:
  "One local input-capable client, which in a run with management is the process the lease holder names (ORB-C13 `AttachAllow`), and one local read-only metadata observer."
- **Result** gains this bullet:
  "**Interactive admission.** A run with management admits the input-capable client only from the process its current lease holder last named, matching the peer's process ID and process start identity, read from the connecting socket's credentials, at the `Hello`. Any other peer is answered `Busy` and closed, as a second client is. While no lease is held, or before the holder names a process, no peer is admitted. A run without management admits the first peer, as before. Naming never ends an existing attachment, and metadata-observer admission is unchanged."
- **Important failures** gains:
  "A peer whose credentials or process start cannot be read, or differ from the named process, is refused with `Busy`, changes no state, and leaves the slot free for the named process. A recycled process ID cannot match, because its start identity differs."
- **Owner** "Orbit's Bend admission policy and Rust socket transport with canonical `orbit-protocol` ORBS v7." becomes:
  "Orbit's Bend admission policy and Rust socket transport with canonical `orbit-protocol` ORBS v7; the named process comes from management v4 (ORB-C13), and the peer process ID and start identity come from Orbit's isolated Linux and Darwin peer-credential and process-start mechanics."
- **Boundary** "Visible text observation, agent observation, multiple observers, multiple interactive clients, remote access, and process authority are excluded." becomes:
  "Visible text over ORBS, agent observation, multiple observers, multiple interactive clients, remote access, and process authority are excluded. The management lease holder reads visible text through ORB-C17 and sends paste and Enter input through ORB-C5, without either ORBS role. Admission tells processes apart, not people or agents: same-user code that controls the named process or the lease holder is out of scope, since no same-UID sandbox is promised (ORB-C13)."

---

## 4a. Amendment: EON-C11 — Runtime generations and presentation

- **Result** gains this bullet:
  "Only the Venus process a supervisor starts to present its window may attach to that window's terminals as their interactive client. The supervisor names that process, by process ID and process start identity, to each live terminal's Orbit through ORB-C13 `AttachAllow`:
    - when it starts that Venus, at launch and at every later presentation (`eon attach`, a window reattached after detach);
    - for each terminal it starts, or recovers under EON-C15, while that Venus runs.
  A terminal it cannot name stays unattached, and Venus reports it as it reports a refused attachment (`Busy`) and retries. No other process can attach to a terminal of a managed window, whether or not the window shows it."
- **Boundary** gains: "This keeps stray same-user processes from taking a terminal's interactive attachment. It is not a defence against same-user code that controls the supervisor or the named Venus."

title: Orbit: management v4 with visible-text reads and lease input
description:
## Why

Approved shape (eon-agent-parity-a9g0, 2026-10-30, items 2-4 and 6a): Orbit serves both reads and input to the management lease holder, so Eon Runtime can read and drive hidden panes and popups without a second interactive client. Also approved the same day (eon-ahzkt option 1): a managed Orbit admits the interactive client only from the process the lease holder names, closing the free attach slot on terminals no window shows (eon-ahzkt reproduced it on 2026-10-30; that bead is closed as carried by this one and a9g0.16).

## Contract

ORB-C17 (new) and the ORB-C13, ORB-C5 and ORB-C3 amendments as approved on eon-agent-parity-a9g0.14 (closed): the merged text in its 2026-10-30 22:14 UTC comment (approved 22:36 UTC) and the AttachAllow clauses in its 22:38 UTC comment (approved 22:40 UTC, with the stricter rule: a managed run with no lease or no name admits nobody), which replace that text's ORB-C13 and ORB-C3 sections. Working copy of the combined text: ~/.cache/eon-agents/agent-parity/contracts-merged.md. Index them as Planned when this bead starts.

## Scope

In scope: `orbit-protocol` management v4 (breaking, exact-version, no adapter; consumers Eon Runtime and Eon; Venus unaffected): a `ReadVisible` request (visible area of the active screen as lossy plain text, alternate-screen flag, revision; reply up to 1 MiB) and a lease input request (one paste up to 64 KiB, bracketed per the program's mode, or one Enter key; refuse an unbracketed newline, control bytes, and ended terminals), and an `AttachAllow` request (one process ID plus process start identity; the name belongs to the lease that set it). ORBS admission in a managed run: `Hello` only from the named process, matched by the connecting socket's peer PID and that process's start identity; anyone else gets the existing `Busy`; no lease or no name admits nobody; an unmanaged run stays first-come; naming never ends an attachment; the metadata observer is unchanged. Portability: the peer-PID and process-start lookup is an isolated Linux and Darwin mechanism behind Orbit's platform seam (Linux proved here; Darwin compile-only, a recorded gap under EON-C7). Bend policy and any changed management law shown to Lucca first (orbit/AGENTS.md). Follow the ORBS/ORBF wire bump checklist.

Out of scope: ORBS and ORBF changes (unnamed peers reuse `Busy`); Runtime naming of Venus (a9g0.16) and CLI; the Venus `Busy` text (its own bug bead); the metadata-observer slot (left first-come by decision).

## Acceptance

- Real-PTY checks: primary and alternate screens, wide and combining text, the 1 MiB cut, synchronized update held, PTY flood during reads, bracketed and unbracketed programs, an unattached terminal, a client typing during a lease paste (no interleaving), ended terminal, Stop around a request, over-size input. PROOF.bend checks.
- Admission (red test: eon-ahzkt's probe, ~/.cache/eon-agents/claude-paneread-work/ahzkt/orbs_attach.py, as a real-PTY check): in a managed run, an unnamed peer's `Hello` gets `Busy` and its paste reaches no shell (red on the current tree: it attaches and the marker appears); the named process attaches; a peer with the named PID but another start identity, and any peer before naming or after the lease ends, get `Busy`; renaming leaves an existing attachment alone; an unmanaged run still admits the first peer. Existing real-PTY and lifecycle checks that attach to a managed run name their client first. The admission law change is shown to Lucca before its proof is relied on, with a sensitivity check.

## Verification

- `nix develop -c eon-test` for Orbit suites, orbit-* Nix checks with --keep-going, cargo fmt and clippy for changed Orbit crates.

## Stop Conditions

- If this does not fit one session, land reads and `AttachAllow` as management v4 and input as v5 in a follow-up bead (approved fallback).

## Maintenance Notes

- References and traced code paths: comments on orb-p92 and eon-pane-send-research-fo4p (2026-10-30).

In scope now: the supervisor reads its Venus child's process ID and start identity and sends AttachAllow on each terminal's lease when it starts that Venus (launch and every later presentation: eon attach, reattach after detach) and for each terminal it starts or recovers (EON-C15) while that Venus runs; a failed naming leaves the terminal unattached and never stops it. comments.text:
Approved law text (copy of ~/.cache/eon-agents/claude-orbv4-work/laws-v4.md, approved by Lucca 2026-10-30, relayed by eon-overseer):
Proposed law changes for eon-agent-parity-a9g0.15 (Orbit management v4), for Lucca's approval before their proofs are relied on. Base: edge 9941580.

A. New laws in orbit/LAWS.bend

  # ORB-C17: a ReadVisible request gets the visible text exactly under the
  # lease while the child runs and no synchronized update is held.
  law management_read_needs_a_live_settled_lease:
    for slot: Management.Slot
    for live: Bool
    for held: Bool
    {Management.is_text(Management.answer(slot, Management.Read{live, held})) == Bool.and(Management.is_leased(slot), Bool.and(live, Bool.not(held))) : Bool}

  # ORB-C5: lease input is written exactly under the lease while the child
  # runs.
  law management_input_needs_a_live_lease:
    for slot: Management.Slot
    for live: Bool
    {Management.is_write(Management.answer(slot, Management.Input{live})) == Bool.and(Management.is_leased(slot), live) : Bool}

  # ORB-C13 and ORB-C3: only the lease holder names the process that may
  # attach.
  law management_allow_needs_the_lease:
    for slot: Management.Slot
    {Management.is_name(Management.answer(slot, Management.Allow{})) == Management.is_leased(slot) : Bool}

  # ORB-C3: a Hello from any process other than the one the lease holder
  # named is answered Busy, whatever the slots hold.
  law admission_strangers_are_busy:
    for slots: Admission.Slots
    {Admission.answer(slots, Admission.Stranger{}) == Admission.Busy{} : Admission.Answer}

B. Changed specifications the existing laws check (the audits, kept apart from the policy)

1. src/management.bend audit, used by management_answers_are_accounted and by the lease law management_follows_its_contract. New signals Read{live, held}, Input{live}, Allow{}, Invalid{}; new answers Text, Write, Name, Decline. Added cases:
   - Read: live, not held, Leased -> Text, stays Leased; held or not live, Leased -> Refuse (Busy), stays Leased.
   - Input: live, Leased -> Write, stays Leased; not live, Leased -> Refuse, stays Leased.
   - Allow: Leased -> Name, stays Leased.
   - Invalid (a whole request that does not decode, or a pipelined one): Leased -> Decline (typed refusal), stays Leased. This is the one behaviour change to existing answers: ORB-C17 says a malformed or in-flight request "fails with a typed failure and no text; the lease stays". A request that breaks framing (bad header, over its bound) stays Bad and still ends the lease.
   - For all four: Negotiating -> RejectRequest, then Closing; Free and Closing -> Quiet, as for the existing requests.
   Everything already in the audit is unchanged.

2. src/admission.bend audit, used by admission_answers_are_accounted and by the lifecycle law: new signal Stranger{} (a Hello whose peer is not the named process, or any Hello in a managed run with no lease or no name; Rust makes the identity check, as it does for Acquire). Added case: Stranger -> Busy, both slots unchanged. Everything else unchanged.

3. LAWS.bend lifecycle automaton: peer_signal maps the new first message FirstMessageStranger to Admission.Stranger{}. LAWS.bend lease automaton: management_signal maps the four new management events, Read taking live and held (the lease automaton is only in Leasing while the child runs, so live is true there, as it already assumes for ProgramStatus; held comes from the fact's flags, so lease_check gains the flags).

C. Host ordering (docs/HOST.md, not a law): the host reports a ReadVisible request only once no synchronized update is held, so the read waits for the release or the 1 s watchdog (ORB-C17, "as attachment does"); the law above makes Bend refuse a read reported while held, so a host that broke that order could never send partial text.

Each new or changed law gets a sensitivity check (policy broken in a scratch copy, proof fails on a concrete trace).

comments.author: lucca
comments.text:
Proof and review record (2026-10-31, x86_64 Linux, Wayland; this commit is the proof's revision; code tree 49ccc1516b7e on base edge 62c8cb5; the landed tree differs only in .beads/issues.jsonl).

Shape as built:
- Management v4: ReadVisible -> Visible (revision, screen, rows, columns, title, raw directory, omitted_rows, lossy, text at most 1 MiB); Input(Paste up to 64 KiB | Enter) -> Input{bracketed}; AttachAllow{pid, start} -> Allowed; typed Refused{InvalidRequest, UnbracketedNewline, InvalidInput, InputFull, ReadFailed, Closed} keeps the lease; Busy after the stop begins. Per-kind bounds; every other message stays at 4 KiB.
- Bend: the four approved laws (management_read_needs_a_live_settled_lease, management_input_needs_a_live_lease, management_allow_needs_the_lease, admission_strangers_are_busy) and the audit cases of laws-v4.md (approved by Lucca, "agree", relayed by eon-overseer 2026-10-30). The policy's text answer is named Visible because Text clashes with a Base constructor (BEND.md).
- Host: Rust makes every identity check. A Hello in a managed run is Stranger unless the leased connection names the peer's SO_PEERCRED pid plus its /proc start identity read at the Hello; the name lives on the leased connection and dies with it. A ReadVisible request is reported only once no synchronized update is held. A whole request that arrives while a read waits or while an answer is being written, or in the same read as an earlier one, is Invalid and declined; framing errors still end the lease. A queued reply must be fully written within one second, or the connection closes and the lease and name end. A stop finishes a partly written answer before Stopped.
- Runtime: one in-flight request slot per lease shared by ProgramStatus and AttachAllow; Venus's pid and start read at spawn; name_presentation after each Venus start (before the Present reply), after each new terminal's lease (before its control reply), and every loop tick as the backstop; failures logged, terminal left unattached and never stopped; supervised Venus retries Busy.
- Contracts: ORB-C17 indexed Planned; ORB-C3, ORB-C5 and ORB-C13 amended with the approved text and moved from Proved to Partially proved, with their new clauses an open proof until eon-agent-parity-a9g0.19; EON-C11 amended (section 4a) and awaiting its amendment proof; EON-C11, EON-C15 and EON-C31 consume management v4.

Configurability (values fixed, with reasons): the 1 MiB read and 64 KiB input bounds are protocol bounds (approved). The one-second reply bound is ORB-C13's existing management bound, applied to the slow-peer rule. AttachAllow's 1 s deadline and 500 ms retry are internal timings that no person sees or feels beyond a Venus retry, which Venus already shows.

title: Runtime: EONW v26 read and send with the terminal_access setting
description:
## Why

Approved shape (eon-agent-parity-a9g0, 2026-10-30, items 1-4 and 6b): Eon Runtime is the only Orbit caller for agent reads and sends, gated by one setting. Also approved the same day (eon-ahzkt option 1): the supervisor names its own Venus process to each terminal's Orbit, so no other process can take a terminal's interactive attachment (eon-ahzkt is closed as carried by a9g0.15 and this bead).

## Contract

EON-C35 and EON-C36 as approved in the contract-text bead (eon-agent-parity-a9g0.14); the EON-C11 amendment from its 2026-10-30 AttachAllow clauses (supervisor names its Venus); EON-C10 caller selection; EON-C15 recovery.

## Scope

In scope: EONW v26 (never an in-place amendment; next free version at landing) with read and send actions; target resolution for pane and popup IDs in any workspace of the window, shown or hidden; reads and sends over the Runtime's management lease, queued behind an in-flight ProgramStatus; `--enter` as a separate Enter after a configurable delay (default 300 ms); `[agents] terminal_access = "window"|"none"` (default "window") governing both, documented in docs/CONFIGURATION.md as not a security boundary; failure codes (unknown target, ended, older Orbit -> terminal-unavailable, access off). `AttachAllow`: the supervisor reads the process ID and start identity of the Venus child it spawns (supervisor.rs venus_command) and sends `AttachAllow` over each terminal's lease when it starts that Venus (launch and every later presentation, including `eon attach` and reattach after detach), and for every terminal it starts or recovers (EON-C15) while that Venus runs. A failed naming leaves the terminal unattached for Venus to retry; it never stops the terminal.

Out of scope: the CLI surface (sibling beads); Orbit; the Venus `Busy` text (its own bug bead).

## Acceptance

- Codec goldens for v26; unit tests for resolution, queueing, delay and every failure code.
- Naming: a test supervisor names its Venus child on launch, on re-presentation and for a terminal created afterwards, and a recovered terminal is named by the replacement supervisor. Venus attaches to every shown terminal as before (workspace suite). The installed red/green against eon-ahzkt's probe is in a9g0.19.

## Verification

- `nix develop -c eon-test`; EONW bump checklist (see memory note on EONW codec bumps).
close_reason: Landed EONW v26 terminal read and send; proof and review ledger in comments; installed joint proof is a9g0.19

comments.author: lucca

This bead keeps EONW v26 read and send, target resolution, the Enter delay, the terminal_access setting and the failure codes. Its naming acceptance item moves with it.

comments.author: lucca
comments.text: Note from a9g0.15 (2026-10-30): Orbit closes a management lease whose reply is not fully written within one second (ORB-C17's slow-peer clause, needed because a ReadVisible reply can be about 1 MiB, more than the socket buffer). When this bead sends ReadVisible, read the reply to completion promptly (for example a bounded blocking read right after the request), and never hold an unread Visible reply across a blocking supervisor step, or the Runtime loses that terminal's lease.

comments.author: lucca
comments.text:
Implementation and proof (2026-10-31, claude-eonw26; built on edge 9c90032, rebased onto 85894cf).

What landed:
- EONW v26: `Action::ReadTerminal{target}` and `Action::SendTerminal{target, input: Paste(text) | Enter}` (tags 38, 39), replies `Response::Text(TerminalText)` and `Response::Sent(Sent)` (kinds 134, 135). Paste and visible text use a u32 length prefix. Bounds equal Orbit's, pinned by const asserts in eon-runtime: text 1 MiB, paste 64 KiB, title plus directory 8 KiB. `validate_paste` is public for the CLI. Goldens for every new value; the version byte is 0x1a. Manifest EONW 26 with the protocol-tree proof; Eon 0.1.9.
- `[agents] terminal_access = "window" | "none"` and `[agents] send_enter_delay_ms = 300` (0..=5000), documented in docs/CONFIGURATION.md with the approved §7 text; `eon config defaults` prints both.
- Supervisor: resolves pane or popup IDs in any workspace (unknown-target, exit 3), with replay protection (reads are inspections, sends mutations); `"none"` refuses with terminal-access-off before resolving; eonbase answers workspace-unavailable. It reads or sends over the lease through ORB-C17 / ORB-C5 lease input and maps every Orbit answer: Stopped/Closed/EOF → terminal-ended; UnbracketedNewline → unbracketed-newline; InvalidInput → invalid-text; Busy, other refusals, wrong or undecodable replies, and the 2 s timeout → terminal-unavailable. No failure carries terminal content.
- Lease safety (the 2026-10-31 note): every read or send runs on a drainer thread over a clone of the lease, so a reply is read promptly even after the 2 s give-up while the supervisor blocks elsewhere (ORB-C13's one-second slow-peer rule). The request then holds the slot until drained, and a read or send behind it fails at once. An in-flight ProgramStatus reply is kept for the attention poller (`answered_status`), and an in-flight AttachAllow is completed as naming completes it. If the drainer cannot start, nothing is sent.
- EON-C35 and EON-C36 indexed as Planned with the approved text (§5, §6). EON-C10's consequential amendment names them as the exceptions to "no terminal content crosses EONW" (visible text, title and working directory, and input). Lucca approved it through eon-overseer: "approve the EON-C10 text" (2026-10-31).

Decisions (minor, mine):
- Enter delay: the window's `send_enter_delay_ms` comes back in `Sent.enter_delay_ms`. The CLI (a9g0.18) sleeps that long after a successful paste and then sends `SendTerminal{Enter}` as a second request, so the supervisor never sleeps up to 5 s. Recorded on a9g0.18.
- Fixed values (Configurability): `TERMINAL_DEADLINE` 2 s stays fixed as the approved performance budget and failure bound; the 1 MiB text and 64 KiB paste bounds are ORB-C17 / ORB-C5 protocol bounds; the drainer's 50 ms wake is internal.
- Accepted risks: an Orbit that never answers holds its terminal's slot until its lease ends, as a stuck ProgramStatus already does. A send that times out may still arrive; its failure detail says so. Several hung terminals each cost one 2 s wait per first request.

Proof (tree = this commit's tree):
- `nix develop -c eon-test` (workspace, isolated sandbox, CARGO_TARGET_DIR in ~/.cache/eon-agents/claude-eonw26-work/target): 625 passed, 0 failed on the rebased tree over edge 85894cf (624 on the converged tree over 9c90032).
- `nix develop -c cargo fmt --all --check`: clean. `nix develop -c cargo clippy --locked --all-targets -p eon-workspace-protocol -p eon-runtime -p eon -p yazelix-venus -- -D warnings`: clean.
- New tests: v26 goldens, `terminal_requests_bound_their_paste_on_both_sides`, `terminal_text_is_bounded_plain_text_on_both_sides`; sessions `terminal_requests_map_every_answer_and_queue_behind_the_request_in_flight` (includes a late reply larger than the socket buffer, read while the supervisor reads nothing; it fails with the drainer disabled or stopped at the deadline) and `a_real_orbit_shows_lease_input_in_its_visible_text`; managed environment `agent_settings_take_window_or_none_and_a_bounded_enter_delay`; workspace `terminal_targets_name_panes_and_popups_in_any_workspace_and_change_nothing`; supervisor `terminal_reads_and_sends_reach_a_hidden_workspace_and_change_nothing`, `terminal_access_none_refuses_every_read_and_send`.
- Not run: installed or display proof (a9g0.19 owns the installed joint proof). The profile is not refreshed: a v26 CLI cannot control Lucca's running v25 window; eon-overseer schedules that with Lucca.

Review ledger (converge, fresh Claude + Codex gpt-6.1-sol xhigh in parallel each round):
- R1 bc29a5d: Claude and Codex both blocking: a given-up read's large late reply was left unread across blocking supervisor steps → drainer + regression; removed an unapproved Consumes line from C35/C36.
- R2 745695c: Claude clean; Codex 2×P2: a read waiting behind ProgramStatus discarded the poller's reply → kept in `answered_status`; drainer start-up failure fallback → all reads and sends use the drainer, nothing sent when it cannot start; plus the drainer waits in poll(2).
- R3 ef6c87b: Codex: empty TEXT → CLI choice, recorded on a9g0.18; v26 header comment fixed. Claude: EON-C10 and ARCHITECTURE.md said no terminal content crosses EONW → consequential amendment proposed (approved by Lucca, see above); EON-C36 status reworded for the Enter delay; metadata bound pinned.
- R4 c9a319d: Claude clean, Codex clean. Text nit: EON-C10 wording widened to name title and working directory.
- Narrow Codex re-check of the text-only diff → 105e913: nothing blocking. Converged on 105e913.
- Rebase onto 85894cf (Ctrl+Tab, wave-1 contract retirement) → 7e038f1: conflicts in both changelogs, one Venus test import, and retired contract text (edge's kept). The full suite, fmt and clippy passed again; a narrow Codex re-check of the resolution found nothing blocking.

comments.author: lucca
comments.text:
Scope addition (eon-overseer decision, 2026-10-30, from eon-t85gf's research; within the approved
contracts' boundary "no protection against code running as the same user", decided under Lucca's
standing instruction on minor items): docs warning only, no refusal of sandboxed callers.

In scope for this bead: one warning paragraph in the docs for `eon pane create`, `eon pane read`
and `eon pane send` (docs/USAGE.md) and in eon/skills/eon/SKILL.md, saying in substance:

  A sandboxed agent that may connect to Unix sockets can drive Eon, and `eon pane create` and
  `eon pane send` then run commands outside its sandbox. Codex with
  `sandbox_workspace_write.network_access = true` and Claude Code with
  `sandbox.network.allowAllUnixSockets = true` allow this; both tools' default sandbox modes block
  it. `[agents] terminal_access` is not a security boundary.

Evidence: eon-t85gf comment (2026-10-30), logs in ~/.cache/eon-agents/claude-t85gf-work/.

comments.author: lucca
comments.text: Sandbox evidence from the eon-ng4bk audit (2026-10-31): herdr's agent skill says Codex must run with --no-daemon or its commands execute outside hc (herdr-core src/SKILL.md:182). eon-t85gf already decided the docs warning in this bead's scope; the send docs should say the same for Codex's daemon mode if it applies to Eon.

comments.author: lucca
comments.text:
Handoff from a9g0.16 (EONW v26, 2026-10-31), binding for `eon pane send`:
- Enter delay: the CLI implements it. Send `Action::SendTerminal{target, input: TerminalInput::Paste(text)}`; on `Response::Sent`, sleep `sent.enter_delay_ms` (the window's `[agents] send_enter_delay_ms`, ≤ 5000), then send `SendTerminal{target, input: Enter}` as a second request. The supervisor never sleeps. Add a test that Enter waits for the delay. Use `bracketed: null` for Enter alone. If the paste succeeds and the Enter fails, exit 1 with `enter: false`.
- Validate first with `eon_workspace_protocol::v26::validate_paste` and `MAX_PASTE_BYTES`: FieldTooLong → `input-too-large`, InvalidValue → `invalid-text` (exit 2). The encoder refuses both, and a raw client that sends them anyway gets `malformed-action`.
- Empty TEXT (`-- ''` or empty stdin) counts as no TEXT. EON-C36 requires TEXT unless `--enter` is given, and Orbit refuses an empty paste. Without `--enter` it is an invalid-argument usage error (exit 2, nothing sent). With `--enter` it sends Enter only (`bytes: 0`). `validate_paste("")` returns InvalidValue, so handle empty before calling it.
- A send that times out (`terminal-unavailable`) may still arrive; the docs should say so.
- Codes: terminal-access-off, terminal-ended, terminal-unavailable, unbracketed-newline exit 1; unknown-target exit 3 (already mapped in control.rs).

comments.author: lucca
comments.text:
Installed joint proof (2026-10-31, claude-parityproof). This commit is the proof's revision. The code proved is edge acc29d2 (a9g0.15 landed as 9c90032, a9g0.16 as ef82672, a9g0.17 as a2cb0a9, a9g0.18 as acc29d2); this commit changes only contract text, changelogs and bead records.

A foot 1.27.0 window ("person-foot") held the desktop focus during the read and send checks. Cleanup signalled only exact PIDs whose environment carried the run's HOME or runtime dir; none remained, and both directories were removed.
- The agent: bin/agent.sh, started by typing into t1's pane p1, ran each command it was handed in that pane, so every `eon` call carried p1's EON_TERMINAL (`caller` = t1/p1).
- Claude Code 2.1.303 (claude-haiku-5-5, API credits, isolated HOME) and Codex 0.166.0 on Lucca's personal account (codex-account-check.sh passed), started as `codex --no-daemon -c model_reasoning_effort=low -c features.hooks=false`. Codex is the one shared piece: it ran /home/lucca/.local/bin/codex with CODEX_HOME=/home/lucca/.codex (its session history landed there), as the account rule requires.
- Scripts, logs, screenshots and per-command outputs: ~/.cache/eon-agents/claude-parityproof-work/ (bin/, evidence/, agent/N.{cmd,out,rc,ms}, run1/).

Checks and results (all pass unless marked):
1. Hidden targets. Setup: t2 by `eon tab create --no-focus --directory`, workspace w2 "hidden" by `eon workspace new --no-focus` (its picker resolved once), a custom keep-alive bash popup u3 opened and hidden. From p1: `eon pane read` and `eon pane send --enter` on p2 (hidden tab), p3 (hidden workspace) and u3 (hidden popup). The JSON reads named the target, `caller` (t1/p1), revision, screen and size (agent/5 shows the whole reply for p2, with title, directory and `lossy: true`; agent/10 and 13 kept the first 400 bytes for p3 and u3); each send returned `bracketed: true, enter: true`, and the next read showed the command's output (HIDDEN-TAB-42, HIDDEN-WS-42, HIDDEN-POPUP-42). evidence/state-before.txt and state-after-all.txt (which workspace is shown, the active tab, the selected pane and popup of each tab in the shown workspace, Sway focus and urgency) are identical; hidden w2's own selection was not captured. Repeated with the Files popup shown in the active tab (state-before2/after2 identical; u3 stayed hidden, Files stayed shown).
