Also against t1's endpoint while the window was detached: Busy (probe-p1-detached.txt). Red: eon 0.1.8 attached and ran the marker command (eon-ahzkt out2, 2026-10-30), and edge 62c8cb5's Orbit failed the admission check (a9g0.15).
3. Venus attaches. At launch (00-start.png), to t2 (05), w2's t3 (06) and u3 (07) when shown; typing reached u3. After Alt+Shift+D detached the window (no Venus window in Sway) and `eon attach`, Venus showed t1 (09) and then t2, w2 and u3, and typed characters reached t2, t3 and u3 (pane read showed `~/w> y`, `~/w2> v`, `bash-5.3$ w`); in t1, keys typed after the reattach were echoed and drawn (the `q` before `[23]` in 13-flood-shown.png, and evidence/flood-*-keys.txt). Reads and sends worked while detached.
4. Flood. A `yes` pane in a second column of the shown tab. 20 reads of it: 73 to 109 ms (median about 76), each at a later revision (134405 to 140957). 20 reads of the quiet hidden p2: median 76 ms, max 100 (idle baseline: median 74, max 105). Keystroke to screen in the shown agent pane, measured by repeated region captures after the reads while the flood still ran: 82 to 86 ms (129 to 145 ms idle, where each capture covered a larger region). Venus kept drawing the flood (14-flood-column.png).
5. Claude Code and Codex. Each started in a hidden tab (t4/p5, t6/p7) by `eon tab create --no-focus --directory ... -- SCRIPT`. `eon pane send p5 --enter -- 'What is 17 times 23? Reply with only the number.'` -> Claude Code answered 391. `eon pane send p7 --enter -- 'What is 19 times 21? ...'` -> Codex answered 399. Both replies `bracketed: true, enter: true`; shown workspace and active tab unchanged.

A read -> terminal-unavailable "Orbit did not answer within 2 s" (exit 1); the next read and a send -> terminal-unavailable "its previous request was not answered in time" at once; a read of p3 meanwhile succeeded. After SIGCONT the same lease served a read and a send (AFTER-CONT-42).
9. terminal-ended: SIGSTOP of p8's Orbit, then `eon pane close p8` -> pane-close-failed after 5 s and the pane stayed; read and send -> terminal-ended exit 1 while the failed stop was still outstanding: that command finished at 08:58:51.666 (agent/51.rc), and the supervisor log records "terminal session-10 ended with status 1" at 08:58:51.787, after SIGCONT let Orbit finish the stop. p8 was then unknown-target.

title: Return the full attention record and quotas in eon workspace --json
description:
## Why

The agent sidebar shows each agent's title, needs-input message, kind, progress, age, stale flag and `+N`. The Eon Bar shows Codex and Claude quota chips. `eon workspace --json` returns only `attention{state, app, name}` and no quotas, so an overseer agent can't see that "Claude in t3 asks to run rm" without the person relaying it. Parity gap 5 of the epic eon-agent-parity-a9g0 (inventory on eon-agent-parity-audit-t31r).

## Evidence (edge 8a25211)

- `docs/CONTRACTS.md:2311-2323` (EON-C31 Q8): the JSON projection deliberately leaves out kind, progress, title, message, `changed_at`, stale and `others`.
- `runtime/crates/eon-workspace-protocol/src/v19.rs:204` (`AttentionRecord`) and `:399` (`Snapshot`): the snapshot already carries `AttentionRecord{kind, progress, app, title, message, changed_at, stale, others}` and `codex_quota`/`claude_quota`.
- `runtime/crates/eon-runtime/src/workspace.rs:1633` (`json`) and `:1707` (`json_attention`): the JSON projection that drops them.
- Popup labels are already available: `json` emits `entries[].label` (workspace.rs:1644-1648) and each popup's `entry` (:1690-1691). They were dropped from this gap after review; Lucca approved the gap with labels in it.

## Prerequisites

None blocking. eon-cli-action-discovery-ogzi waits on this bead and eon-agent-parity-a9g0.1.

## Scope

In scope: the EON-C31 Q8 and EON-C10 amendment, the JSON projection in `workspace.rs`, docs/USAGE.md, CHANGELOG.md and focused projection tests.

Out of scope: EONW wire changes (the data is already in the snapshot), Venus, new attention sources. The session `name` already landed (eon-agent-sidebar-yx8.11).

## Acceptance

- `eon workspace --json` carries the full attention record per pane and popup and the quota chips, with the field names in the approved contract.
- Contract text approved by Lucca before code.

## Implementation Notes

1. Draft the Q8 change: which fields, their JSON names and types (the contract text says `msg`, the Rust field is `message`; pick one), and whether the agent-authored message needs a length bound. EON-C28 freezes JSON fields from 1.0 (additions stay allowed), so this is cheaper before 1.0. Stop for approval.
2. Extend the projection and its tests.

## Verification

- `nix develop -c eon-test -p eon-runtime` exits 0 with a projection test showing every new field.

## Stop Conditions

- Stop if cited code has drifted materially, or if verification fails twice for the same reason.

## Maintenance Notes

- Unblocks eon-cli-action-discovery-ogzi's un-deferral together with eon-agent-parity-a9g0.1.

## Reference gate

Consequential (contract change). Before code, record on this bead: the owner of the projection (Runtime `workspace.rs`), the docs/REFERENCES.md routes read, and a comparable at an inspected revision, for example kitty `@ ls` and WezTerm `cli list --format json` field sets. Note what was kept and rejected, especially for agent-authored text in `message`.

comments.author: lucca
comments.text:
Plan and reference gate (Opus planner, 2026-10-29, worktree at edge 0842ddc).

Approval to start: Lucca, 2026-10-29, to eon-overseer: "we need to do more eon stuff / can we fire more agents?", then chose this bead from the overseer's list (relayed by the coordinator). The contract wording below still needs Lucca's approval before code.

Drift check: the cited code moved but did not change shape. `json` is now runtime/crates/eon-runtime/src/workspace.rs:2349, `json_attention` :2438, `attention_fields` :2262, `human_attention` :2282; the snapshot types are in runtime/crates/eon-workspace-protocol/src/v24.rs (`AttentionRecord` :240, `CodexQuota`/`ClaudeQuota` :419-453, `Snapshot` :467). The CLI wraps `json` in runtime/crates/eon-runtime/src/cli.rs:1120-1133, so every workspace action reply with `--json` carries the same projection.

## Approach

Projection only; no EONW change, no Venus change, no new dependency.

1. `json_attention` emits the full record: `state`, `app`, `name`, `kind`, `progress`, `title`, `message`, `changed_at`, `stale`, `others`, every key always present. Empty `app`/`name`/`title`/`message` are null, as `app` and `name` are today. `kind` is null unless needs input; `progress` null when unreported. For `unavailable` (no record) every key but `state` is null. `null` without attention stays.
2. `json` adds `codex_quota` and `claude_quota` on the snapshot after `sidebar`: null without a reading, else `{"state", "observed_at", "windows":[{"duration_minutes","remaining_percent","resets_at"}]}`. States `fresh|stale|blocked|unknown` (Claude `fresh|stale`). Runtime keeps quota times in Unix seconds (quota.rs `timestamp`); the projection multiplies by 1000 so every CLI JSON time is wall-clock Unix milliseconds, like `changed_at`.
3. `human` stays as it is (state, app and name only, no quotas) — see question 4.
4. `attention_fields` keeps serving `human`; its doc comment changes (the report text now leaves EONW through JSON).
5. Docs: EON-C10 and EON-C31 Q8 text (below), docs/USAGE.md (`eon workspace` row at :378 and a short JSON field note, including that `title`/`message` are program-authored untrusted text), CHANGELOG.md (user-visible CLI JSON change).

## Red check

Rework `cli_output_carries_attention_state_and_app_but_never_report_text` (workspace.rs:3783) into a projection test that asserts the exact attention object for a needs-input pane with every field set (kind, progress, title with a quote, message, changed_at, stale, others), the all-null object for an unavailable popup or pane, `null` for no attention, and the exact quota objects for a Codex reading (two windows, one without reset) and a Claude reading, plus `null` quotas. The human output keeps asserting that report text and quotas never appear there. It fails on 0842ddc because the JSON lacks every new key.

## Scope boundary

In: workspace.rs projection and its tests, CONTRACTS.md (EON-C10 bullet, EON-C31 Q8), USAGE.md, CHANGELOG.md, any eon/crates/eon/tests/workspace_control.rs assertion that pins the old attention JSON. Out: EONW/v24.rs, Venus, quota collection, `eon workspaces` list JSON, the attention queue order (eon-ngwf.1), the human projection.

## Checks

`nix develop -c eon-test -p eon-runtime` and `-p eon` (CARGO_BUILD_JOBS=4), `cargo fmt --check` and `cargo clippy --locked --all-targets -- -D warnings` for eon-runtime. Verification route: installed CLI output, so after landing the coordinator refreshes the profile and makes one isolated installed observation: `eon workspace --json` with a reporting agent pane (needs input or finished) and a plain pane, showing the new attention keys and the quota objects (or null when CodexBar has no reading).

## Reference gate (consequential: contract change)

- Owner: Eon Runtime's CLI projection (`workspace.rs` `json`/`json_attention`) is the one owner of the JSON. The record facts stay Orbit's (ORB-C15), normalization and `changed_at` stay Runtime attention.rs (EON-C31), quota readings stay Runtime quota.rs (EON-C27).
- Route read: docs/REFERENCES.md "How should Eon expose agent-readable actions and source-labeled attention without creating another terminal or action owner?" (TUIOS at 0047c409185f).
- Comparables (local clones under ~/pjs/refs):
  - TUIOS 0047c409185f37e568933a566e0253b2a6e96a96: `list-windows --json` carries each window's `agent_state`, the free-text `agent_message` and `agent_state_at` (internal/session/session.go:79-91, cmd/tuios/remote_commands.go:317-318, docs/AGENT_STATE.md:53-63), with `omitempty`.
  - kitty b2cb871254fbdac19a085188813c8dfb258b95cd: `kitten @ ls` returns the program-set `title` and `user_vars` raw (kitty/window.py:2343-2359).
  - WezTerm e2a98e1b8af156988ad0ac778658ac27b60a55fb: `wezterm cli list --format json` returns the program-set `title` raw (wezterm/src/cli/list.rs:119-139).
- Kept: one projection of owner state; program-authored text passed through unchanged and escaped, as all three do; an explicit change time; the record's freshness (`stale`) as data, as the TUIOS route asks.
- Rejected: TUIOS `omitempty` (absent keys) in favour of always-present keys with null, matching Eon's existing `pinned_name`/`app`/`name`; sanitizing or re-truncating `message` in the CLI (ORB-C15 already bounds it to 256 bytes and refuses control characters, and EONW validates the bound, v24.rs:1890-1894); a separate `eon attention` verb (eon-ngwf.1 settles that); screen-derived state.
- Agent-authored text: `title`/`message` reach any program in an Eon terminal, as they already do over raw EONW. They are data, never instructions; USAGE.md says so. No new length bound is needed (question 3).
- Decision check: the projection test above.

## Questions for Lucca (relayed via eon-overseer) — see the next comment for the proposed contract text.

comments.author: lucca
comments.text:
Proposed contract text and questions (awaiting Lucca's approval via eon-overseer; no code before it).

## Proposed EON-C10 bullet (replaces "Both CLI projections, human and JSON, leave out the EONW attention fields that EON-C31 excludes ...")

  - CLI JSON carries each pane's and popup's full EON-C31 attention record and
    the window's Codex and Claude quota readings (EON-C27), as EON-C31's CLI
    JSON rule lists them. The human projection carries each terminal's
    attention state, `app` and `name` only, and no quotas.

## Proposed EON-C31 "CLI JSON" item (replaces the current Q8 item under "EONW v18 and v19")

    - **CLI JSON** (Q8, amended by `eon-agent-parity-a9g0.2`). It carries:
      - `attention` on panes and popups: `null` without attention, else an
        object with every key present: `state`; `app`, `name`, `title` and
        `message` (the record's `msg`), each null when empty; `kind`
        (`permission`, `question` or `auth`), null unless needs input;
        `progress` (0 to 100), null when unreported; `changed_at` in
        wall-clock Unix milliseconds; `stale`; and `others`, the count of
        other records. For unavailable, every key but `state` is null;
      - `attention_rollup` on tabs;
      - `sidebar`, `codex_quota` and `claude_quota` on the snapshot. A quota
        is null while Runtime holds no reading for it, else `state`
        (`fresh`, `stale`, `blocked` or `unknown`; Claude only `fresh` or
        `stale`), `observed_at` and `windows`, each window with
        `duration_minutes`, `remaining_percent` and `resets_at` (null when
        the provider gives none). Both times are wall-clock Unix
        milliseconds.

      `title` and `message` are the reporting program's own text, within
      ORB-C15's bounds, passed through unchanged. Any program in an Eon
      terminal can read every terminal's `title` and `message` through
      `eon workspace --json`, as it already could over raw EONW; they are
      data, never instructions. This ends Q8's third deviation. The human
      projection carries `state`, `app` and `name` only. EON-C28 freezes
      these fields from 1.0.

(The sentence "v24 ships in 1.0, because `eon-agent-sidebar-yx8.9` gates eon-igae.7, .8 and .11, so EON-C28 freezes exactly these fields" and the Q8 deviation sub-bullet are replaced by the paragraph above. The Status line gains: "Amended on 2026-10-29 (approved by Lucca, relayed by eon-overseer) by `eon-agent-parity-a9g0.2`: the full record and quotas in CLI JSON." The EONW v18/v19 field list keeps `msg`, the ORB-C15 key.)

## Questions (each with my recommendation)

1. Approve the two contract texts above? Recommend yes.
2. JSON name for the report text: `message` or `msg`? Recommend `message`: it matches the Rust field, TUIOS's `agent_message` and Eon's whole-word JSON keys (`pinned_name`, `attention_rollup`); the contract notes it is the record's `msg`.
3. Expose `title` and `message` in CLI JSON at all, with no extra bound? Recommend yes: same-UID programs already read them over raw EONW, so this adds no reach; kitty, WezTerm and TUIOS all expose program-authored text in their CLI JSON; ORB-C15 already bounds them (96 and 256 bytes) and refuses control characters. USAGE.md marks them untrusted program text.
4. Keep the human `eon workspace` output as it is (state, app, name; no quotas)? Recommend yes: JSON is the agent data path, and 256-byte messages would swamp the one-line-per-pane text. A person sees the record in the sidebar and the quotas in the Bar.
5. Project quota times in Unix milliseconds (Runtime stores seconds) so every CLI JSON time shares one unit with `changed_at`? Recommend yes: these are the CLI's first time fields, so one unit now avoids a seconds/milliseconds trap for agents. Every key stays present, with null for unavailable's record fields rather than `false`/`0`, so "no record" differs from "fresh, no others".

title: Open a file in Helix without moving focus (eon edit --no-focus)
description:
## Why and approved outcome

Open a file without moving the person's view, and deliver the shared pane-directory
launch change without duplicating EONW. Parent: eon-agent-parity-a9g0.
The approved 2026-11-06 combined plan lives at
/home/lucca/.cache/eon-agents/eon-a9g0-2021-plan-work/PLAN.md and bead/01-contract-step.md.
Overseer comment 5662 quotes Lucca's delegation, "the rest is up to you", and approves
D1-D7/exact C8-A/C10-A/B/C text. Preserve those decisions, including D2 collapsed
editor pane, D3 plain edit unchanged, D4 no --tab, D5 one shared bump, D6 per-call
flags/no new setting, and D7 exactly two slices. Argon routing was superseded by
comment 5669; agent assignment is the overseer's, not this plan's requirement.

## Current evidence (8ebdd69)

cli.rs::parse_edit_arguments (:2975) accepts edit [--json] -- FILE;
parse_command_pane_arguments (:3002) lacks directory; tab create (:3037) uses --dir.
v40.rs:251-260 has Edit { file } and CreateCommandPane { argv, focus }.
Comment 6316 on .21 settles the directory flag as --dir, with no --directory alias.
The historical v29/v34 references in the plan must be rebaselined at the next free
version, carrying all intervening consumers. Portability: neutral.

## Approved split and ownership

This bead becomes the combined batch's implementation epic:
- .1: both wire fields and Runtime behaviors, explicit temporary parity gaps and
  raw-EONW installed proof; flags remain unavailable until the CLI slice.
- .2: both CLI flags, parity/help/docs and installed CLI proof, no additional bump.
The sibling eon-agent-parity-a9g0.21 tracks the directory outcome and depends on .2;
do not independently reimplement it. Both chosen features and their checks are retained.
The approved plan's focus/directory validation/failure matrix, reference evidence and
fixed-value rationale apply to each child; rebase evidence before implementation.

## Open decision requiring overseer/Lucca resolution

D2 appends a collapsed pane; newly approved eon-xodrj.5 makes plain eon edit default
to a reusable Editor popup ([editor] open_in = popup|pane). Neither approval decides
how --no-focus interacts with that popup route. Preserve both decisions as recorded;
stop before code and obtain reconciliation/exact amended text rather than silently
forcing a pane, showing a popup or changing defaults. .1 waits for S4's actual surface.
No accepted contract is edited by this planning pass.

## Acceptance and proof

Both approved slices complete after the interaction decision. No-focus preserves active
tab, selection, expanded panes, shown/covered popup, shown session and desktop focus;
plain edit preserves the then-accepted ordinary behavior. --dir changes only command
launch cwd with the tab-create validation, never tab root. Exact codec/failure/parity
checks and isolated observations in the approved matrix pass. Runtime/wire proof is
separate from installed CLI proof; current root verification/review applies.
No --tab/column choice, aliases or additional editor IPC in these slices. The later
Helix new-column recipe (comment 6448) belongs to .6's column-choice child after this

title: Close tabs and panes in any tab by ID without moving focus
description:
## Why

An overseer agent can't clean up a finished agent's tab or pane without moving the person's view. `eon tab close TAB` refuses any tab that isn't active, `eon pane close` resolves only in the caller's or the active tab. A person closes any tab from its `×` after selecting it. Parity gap 6 of the epic eon-agent-parity-a9g0 (inventory on eon-agent-parity-audit-t31r). Its sibling eon-89ho adds `pane create --tab`.

## Evidence (edge 8a25211)

- `runtime/crates/eon-runtime/src/workspace.rs:857-867`: closing a tab fails `not-active` unless the tab is active.
- `runtime/crates/eon-runtime/src/workspace.rs:890-941`: closing a pane resolves the pane in the caller's or active tab.
- `runtime/crates/eon-runtime/src/workspace.rs:383-397`: `Edit` always focuses; there is no `--no-focus`.
- `runtime/crates/eon-runtime/src/cli.rs:933` (`parse_control_arguments`) and `:1024` (`parse_edit_arguments`): the CLI parsing for these.

## Prerequisites

None blocking. Sibling of eon-89ho (`pane create --tab`); if both are open, settle their targeting rules together.

## Scope

In scope: the EON-C10/EON-C8 amendment, `tab close` on any tab by ID, `pane close` on any pane by ID, the final-close rules for each, docs/USAGE.md, CHANGELOG.md and tests.

Out of scope: `pane create --tab` (eon-89ho), Venus's own close path and prompt, and any change to which tab is active when the closed tab isn't the active one.

## Acceptance

- Closing a non-active tab or another tab's pane by ID works and leaves the active tab, the selection and the shown popup unchanged.
- Editor opening without focus is owned separately by eon-agent-parity-a9g0.20 (open Helix without moving focus); its acceptance remains there.
- The last-tab and last-pane rules still hold. Contract text approved by Lucca before code.

## Implementation Notes

1. Draft the contract text, including whether this needs an EONW change (the `CloseTab`/`ClosePane` payloads already name their targets). Stop for approval.
2. Implement, test, update docs.

## Verification

- `nix develop -c eon-test -p eon-runtime` exits 0 with cases for closing a background tab/pane, stale targets, last-pane and last-tab behavior, and preservation of the shown workspace, tab, selection and popup.

## Stop Conditions

- Stop if Venus relies on the `not-active` refusal, if cited code has drifted, or if verification fails twice.

## Maintenance Notes

- Why the active-tab rule exists may be recorded on the bead that added it; read it before removing the rule.
- Open question for Lucca at the contract step: the approved "Humans and Agents" rule says a CLI path leaves the active tab, selection and shown popup alone unless the agent asks. `eon pane create` focuses and dismisses the popup by default unless `--no-focus` is given, and `tab move`/`pane move` act on the caller rather than an ID. Propose whether those defaults change here.

## Reference gate

Consequential (contract change). Before code, record on this bead: the owner of each step (CLI → EONW → Runtime workspace → supervisor close), the docs/REFERENCES.md routes read, and comparables at inspected revisions: tmux `kill-window -t`/`kill-pane -t`, WezTerm `cli kill-pane --pane-id`, kitty `@ close-tab --match`. Note what was kept and rejected.


## Targeting decision before code

Confirm with Lucca whether explicit close IDs may name a hidden workspace as well as a background tab. Keep the shown workspace unchanged. Follow the recorded CLI → EONW → Runtime → supervisor owner trace, and choose the installed-runtime proof route if the consuming behavior changes. Portability disposition: neutral unless the implementation discovers an isolated platform dependency.


## Busy-close parity

Background tab/pane close uses the same approved busy-prompt/confirmation and final-close policy as the window path, preserving the requirement originally recorded by eon-cglv2 (tab control). Add a focused busy-background target case that verifies confirmation/refusal semantics and that cancellation leaves the active workspace/tab, selection and popup untouched. If current CLI and window policies differ, bring exact EON-C10/EON-C8 wording to Lucca before choosing a new policy; do not force-close busy work by default.

The field report's 'pane create --directory' gap is the sibling 'Start a pane in a named directory'. Rebaseline: tab close refuses at runtime/crates/eon-runtime/src/workspace.rs:1651, pane close at :1695. Contract step must say whether a target in a hidden workspace (EON-C33) can be closed and that the shown workspace stays as is.

comments.text:
# eon-agent-parity-a9g0.3 — contract step

Draft for Lucca's approval; no contract or implementation has been changed.
Baseline: detached edge `22f7d02c700e5b74c19dfd903cc6cc59950c3145`, clean repository on inspection, 2026-11-05.
The implementation plan is `../PLAN.md` and assumes all six recommendations below.
This document is a proposal, not a proof record or a Beads update.

## Reference gate and observed behavior

Read: root `AGENTS.md`, `docs/AGENT-PROTOCOLS.md`, the required sections of
`docs/AGENT-RULES.md` (also Platform Discipline, Product Boundary, Local Runtime
Synchronization and Git Workflow), `runtime/AGENTS.md`, `venus/AGENTS.md`, and the affected VEN-C8 close clause
in `venus/docs/CONTRACTS.md`.
Read the body and all comments of `eon-agent-parity-a9g0.3`, plus `eon-cglv2`,
`eon-89ho`, and `eon-agent-parity-a9g0`. Ordinary `br show`/`br comments` failed
on the shared store's read-only lock; `br --no-db show`/`comments` succeeded.
No Beads write or sync was performed. History inspected through `eon-pxn.8`,
`eon-close-pane-onwi`, `eon-8mnr.2`, and `eon-pg67`:

- Original tab close was deliberately scoped to active-tab keyboard actions.
- Original pane close explicitly excluded other tabs, confirmation, and the final pane.
- Caller targeting later deliberately limited pane close to the caller's tab.
- Final-close approval superseded the final-pane prohibition. The current C8/C10
  final-close policy differs from window Quit's subsequently added busy policy.
  No inspected history establishes a remaining terminal-safety reason for the
  active-tab requirement itself; removing it is nevertheless a contract change.

### Owner trace at this baseline

| Step | Owner and inspected implementation | Responsibility retained |
| --- | --- | --- |
| CLI | Runtime `cli.rs`: `execute`, `parse_workspace_target_arguments`, `parse_control_arguments` (~1767), `control` (~1127), `final_close_terminals`, `final_close_prompt`; `generation.rs::confirm` | Syntax, caller/supervisor discovery, human/JSON projection, CLI confirmation. No focus action to make close possible. |
| EONW | Runtime's canonical `eon-workspace-protocol/src/v32.rs`: `WorkspaceAction::CloseTab { tab: String }`, `Action::ClosePane { pane: String }`, `Request { id, caller, action }` | Bounded framing and exact target/caller syntax. No target inference, shutdown or UI policy. |
| Workspace | Runtime `workspace.rs`: `WorkspaceSet::prepare_close_tab/prepare_close_pane` (~716/729), `caller_workspace`; `Workspace::prepare_close_tab/prepare_close_pane` (~1773/1806) | Validate caller and workspace boundary, resolve exact ID, popup/last-pane rules, replay protection, terminal list. Tab/pane selection changes only through existing exit pruning. |
| Supervisor close | Runtime `supervisor.rs`: dispatch (~2477), `close_workspace_tab`, `close_workspace_pane`, `stop_closed_sessions`, `closed_response` (~1481–1638) | Reap exits, validate opaque caller, stop exact terminals with existing bounded concurrent stop, prune confirmed ends, retain failed stops, finish generation only when appropriate. |
| Terminal shutdown | Existing Orbit management, consumed through Runtime's session owner | Actual terminal/process-group shutdown; no new signaling path. |
| Window consumer | Venus `application.rs::request_workspace`, `send_close`, `final_close_tab`; `ClosePrompt::names_live_target` | Existing native confirmation and stable target. `send_close` (~1738) currently queues `FocusId(tab)` before close if a new tab became active during the prompt. |

**Stop condition discovered:** Venus does rely on the active-tab restriction:
its `send_close` comment says so and the function implements the workaround.
The proposed execution must wait for decision 4, as well as contract approval.
This planning pass does not remove it or treat the bead's Venus exclusion as waived.
Other `not-active` uses, especially popup invocation, are unrelated and remain.

### REFERENCES.md routes read

1. **“How should Eon organize and switch among durable terminals without absorbing
   terminal or rendering state?”** Keep Runtime topology and exact Orbit identities;
   reject moving terminal lifetime to Venus. Local Rio clone is
   `ec9ca5043e140c864cb9448eb27574c893132c33`; it lacks both
   `frontends/canario` and the routed `3e41b8b19a1cad9cd9bdfc8f7900cf61ce5a9098`
   object. Canario source was unavailable locally; no claims are inferred from it.
2. **“How should one Eon window let a user find and switch between several
   workspaces?”** Read C33 and local tmux `cmd-switch-client.c`/`window-switch.c`
   at `7f2a35ad3321f9ba57a1062ca73b1f3ff26aca53`. Explicitly showing a workspace
   is separate from addressing an object. The Zellij session-manager route exists
   locally at `efd8fd5a89a20c07a111d248ad7fce53848d2c18`; inspected its session
   identity/kill-warning state in `default-plugins/session-manager/src/main.rs`.
   Rex's pinned `llms-full.txt` snapshot was not located/read locally. No Rex
   behavior claim is made. Cross-OS-window reconciliation and restoration are out
   of scope; conditional kitty/WezTerm reconciliation sources are not needed.
3. **“How should Eon expose agent-readable actions and source-labeled attention
   without creating another terminal or action owner?”** Read local TUIOS
   `docs/protocol.md` and `docs/AGENT_STATE.md` at
   `0047c409185f37e568933a566e0253b2a6e96a96`. Keep explicit selectors, typed
   failures and one authoritative action owner. Reject protocol sniffing,
   negotiation, session-name targeting and semantic guesses from terminal text.
4. Read the shared-popup EONW route to check whether a new payload is necessary;
   inspected current v32 producer/consumers instead of restoring historical codecs.
   Keep exact framing and shared schema; no new schema/version is needed here.

### Required close comparables (read-only source inspection)

All three local clones were clean. No external code was copied or run.

| Comparable and inspected revision | Sources / observed mechanism | Kept / rejected |
| --- | --- | --- |
| tmux `kill-window -t` / `kill-pane -t`, `7f2a35ad3321f9ba57a1062ca73b1f3ff26aca53` | `/home/lucca/pjs/refs/tmux-3.8/{cmd-kill-window.c,cmd-kill-pane.c,server-fn.c}`: target resolved before `server_kill_window`/`server_kill_pane`; last pane delegates to window teardown. Single-target command has no preliminary select. | Keep exact target independent of focus, one teardown owner, last-pane lifecycle composition. Reject tmux target grammar, multi-target/filter/alias features and unconfirmed kill policy. Eon's bounded Stop and partial failure representation remain authoritative. |
| WezTerm `cli kill-pane --pane-id`, `e2a98e1b8af156988ad0ac778658ac27b60a55fb` | `/home/lucca/pjs/refs/wezterm/wezterm/src/cli/kill_pane.rs`, `wezterm-mux-server-impl/src/sessionhandler.rs`: explicit pane ID goes to mux lookup, `kill`, removal and response without an activation request. | Keep explicit ID and missing-target failure at owner. Reject implicit `WEZTERM_PANE` fallback for Eon's explicit close operand and direct unconditional kill semantics. |
| kitty `@ close-tab --match`, `b2cb871254fbdac19a085188813c8dfb258b95cd` | `/home/lucca/pjs/refs/kitty/kitty/rc/close_tab.py`, `kitty/boss.py::close_tab_no_confirm`: matcher yields tabs, remote close calls no-confirm close; default unmatched selector errors unless explicitly ignored. | Keep close independent of focus and stale-target errors. Reject match expressions, bulk close, ignore-no-match/no-response switches and bypassing confirmation by default. |

These sources demonstrate targeting mechanisms, not Eon's safety or focus proof.
No dependency is added; the version policy remains exact EONW v32. Exit condition:
the approved ID scope and safety behavior pass existing Runtime/CLI owners and an
isolated installed observation, with no new action owner or compatibility route.

## EONW decision

**No wire/schema/version change.** Both close payloads already carry the exact target;
`Request.caller` already identifies the caller's workspace. Snapshot already carries
that workspace's complete tabs and the window's bounded busy list. `--yes` is a CLI
confirmation decision, not a new wire flag: current native confirmed closes already
send the existing action directly. Update misleading Rust documentation on
`Action::ClosePane` and `Request.caller`; leave encoding, tags, bounds, VERSION,
component graph and lockfile unchanged. Direct EONW clients remain responsible for
obtaining consent, as Venus already is; this is not a new authorization boundary.

## Decisions for Lucca (all pending)

1. **Hidden workspaces — recommend retaining the addressed-workspace boundary.**
   IDs may name any tab/pane in the caller's workspace, even while that workspace
   is hidden. They may not name an object in another workspace. Outside Eon they
   resolve in the shown workspace. The shown workspace never changes to resolve
   a target. Reason: matches C33 and complete existing inspection without adding
   cross-workspace lookup/inspection scope. An arbitrary-hidden-workspace “yes”
   requires a revised plan and C33 amendment, not an executor's inference.
2. **Busy close — recommend target-scoped busy confirmation, explicit `--yes`
   for JSON callers.** Reuse C11's busy classification and `confirm`'s yes/no
   semantics for every CLI tab/pane close. Include a busy caller when it is itself
   a close target; Quit's caller exemption is specific to Quit. Human mode asks
   once; a TTY no cancels with exit 0, piped yes confirms, non-TTY no/EOF refuses
   with `not-confirmed`/1. JSON never reads stdin and refuses a busy or unknown
   target with `not-confirmed`/1 unless `--yes` was explicitly given. Preserve the
   separate existing idle final-close warning (TTY human mode only, governed by
   `warning_close_last_tab`, default true). Busy confirmation is independent of
   that setting. Reason: busy work is never implicitly confirmed by `--json` or
   lack of a TTY, while established idle final-close behavior is preserved.
3. **Other parity gaps — recommend no changes here.** `pane create` keeps its
   current focus/popup defaults and `--no-focus`; `tab move`/`pane move` keep
   caller-relative behavior. Reason: eon-89ho owns cross-tab creation, eon-cglv2
   owns the move decision, and editor focus belongs to a9g0.20; changing their
   defaults would expand this slice. Record this disposition in the owning bead
   after approval, without closing or claiming any sibling.
4. **Venus scope exception — recommend authorizing only removal of the
   focus-before-close workaround in `Application::send_close`, plus its proof.**
   Amend VEN-C8's explicit focus-before-close sentence to match. Native prompt
   wording, busy policy, shortcuts and popup guards stay as they are. Reason:
   after Runtime accepts exact background targets, focusing first
   is unnecessary and would undermine the focus guarantee when the prompt's
   named tab becomes background. Without this explicit scope approval, stop.
5. **Popup/final-pane rules — recommend preserving them, with the non-last
   caller exception applying to any validated caller in the addressed workspace.**
   With a selected popup/picker, a pane close without a caller still refuses;
   with a caller, only a non-last pane may close and the popup stays. The caller
   no longer has to inhabit the target tab. A last pane covered by a popup must
   still be closed by naming its tab instead. Hidden popups follow existing exit
   rules: a non-final tab may remain popup-only; final-workspace last-pane close
   includes all its tab's hidden popups. Reason: retain the existing protection
   against accidentally stopping a covering popup while removing tab-relative
   ID restrictions. No new popup action is needed.
6. **Confirmation consistency — recommend the existing snapshot-preflight
   model, with unknown/capped busy state treated conservatively.** Consent is
   decided from the latest successful CLI inspection; Runtime revalidates exact
   live targets before Stop. This is not an atomic “inspect and close”
   transaction. A missing busy list or nonzero `omitted` requires confirmation
   for any target, because the omitted entries cannot safely prove it idle.
   Reason: same observation model as the window path, no wire expansion or
   confirmation-token framework. If Lucca requires atomic busy revalidation,
   stop and redesign the contract/wire proposal before implementation.

## Exact proposed contract edits — NEED LUCCA'S APPROVAL

Apply only the identified replacements; retain all unrelated clauses and historical
proofs. Existing proof records do not prove this amendment. Record approval date
and bead in EON-C8/EON-C10/VEN-C8 status only once approval actually occurs.

### EON-C8

Replace the movement paragraph's ending beginning “Run from an Eon terminal” with:

> Run from an Eon terminal, `eon tab move`, `eon pane move` and
> `eon pane create` act on the calling terminal's tab and pane instead of
> the active tab and its selected pane (EON-C10). Explicit close targets
> follow the close rules below.

Replace the first two sentences of the close bullet, through “restores its prior tab”, with:

> Closing names an exact live `tN` in the addressed workspace (EON-C10),
> whether or not that tab is active. A close of a background tab preserves
> the active tab's identity, selected column and pane, shown and selected
> popup, and desktop focus. It does not show a hidden workspace. A
> non-final pending tab first stops its exact picker, then disappears;
> remaining selection follows the ended-terminal rules below.

Keep the rest of that bullet's bounded/partial Stop, final-tab, warning and detach
rules. Add this paragraph at its end:

> CLI closes also use EON-C10's target-scoped busy confirmation, independently
> of `warning_close_last_tab`. A native confirmed close sends its named
> close action without first selecting the named tab. If that tab became
> background while the prompt was open, the current active tab stays active.

Replace the entire “Closing a pane names” result bullet with:

> Closing a pane names an exact live `pN` in any tab of the addressed
> workspace (EON-C10), independently of the caller's tab and the active tab.
> Eon stops that pane's terminal and prunes its confirmed end through the
> normal terminal-exit owner, so its column, its tab and focus follow the
> ended-terminal rules below. Closing the final tab's last pane acts as
> final-tab close does, stopping that tab's popups with it. While a popup
> or picker covers the target tab, a close without a calling terminal is
> unavailable; a validated calling terminal of the addressed workspace may
> close a non-last pane in that tab, leaving its popup shown and selected,
> but may not close the tab's last pane. A close in a background tab
> preserves the active tab's selection and popup and never shows another
> workspace or moves desktop focus. A close in the active tab keeps every
> surviving selected identity when possible and otherwise follows the
> ended-terminal rules. A failed stop reports failure and keeps the pane;
> a terminal that ended naturally during the request is reconciled as an
> exit. Venus maps Alt+W directly to the selected pane without a mode;
> `eon pane close PANE` sends the same target-bearing EONW action.

Replace the Important failures opening through “invalid transition” with:

> **Important failures:** Unknown or stale identity, a close target outside
> the addressed workspace, pane close under a popup or picker without a
> calling terminal or naming the tab's last pane, creating a fifth column,
> durable close in the picker-bound tab, invalid transition

Retain the rest of that paragraph, including partial-stop exceptions and replay
protection. In Boundary, replace the exact phrase “closing panes outside the
active or calling tab” with “closing tabs or panes outside the addressed workspace”.

### EON-C10

Replace the entire result bullet beginning “A CLI confirmation” with:

> A CLI confirmation proceeds only on a yes answer (`y`, `Y`, `yes` or
> `YES`). Any other answer changes nothing. At a terminal it prints the
> cancel note and exits 0. When stdin is not a terminal, it exits 1 with
> `not-confirmed`, end of input included, and a piped yes still confirms.
> `--json` never asks or reads a confirmation from stdin. Stop, Quit,
> window-stop and workspace-close retain their existing JSON behavior.
> Tab and pane close use the separate busy and final-close rules below;
> `--json` alone never confirms a busy close.

In the entire EON_TERMINAL result bullet, replace the passage starting “Within
that workspace” through “the active tab and desktop focus never change” with:

> Within that workspace, `pane create`, `edit`, `pane move` and `tab move`
> retain their calling-tab, column and pane rules: creation uses the
> caller's column and moves act on its pane or tab. A popup terminal acts
> for its tab and that tab's selected column and pane. Within that tab each
> action behaves as it does for the active tab, so `pane create` selects
> the new pane and dismisses the tab's popup; the active tab and desktop
> focus never change. Explicit `tab close TAB` and `pane close PANE`
> resolve in any tab of that workspace by the close rules below.

Retain the bullet's supervisor selection, remaining workspace rules and EON_TAB.
Replace the entire result bullet beginning “eon tab close TAB and eon pane close
PANE may name the final tab” with these three bullets:

> - `eon tab close TAB [--yes] [--json]` and
>   `eon pane close PANE [--yes] [--json]` resolve their explicit live IDs
>   in any tab of the addressed workspace: the validated caller's workspace
>   inside Eon, otherwise the shown workspace of the selected supervisor.
>   The caller's workspace may be hidden; an ID in another workspace is
>   `unknown-tab` or `unknown-pane` (exit 3), with no fallback or workspace
>   switch. Caller validation and EON-C8's popup and final-pane rules still
>   apply. Closing a background target leaves the shown workspace, active
>   tab, surviving selected identities, shown popup and desktop focus alone.
>   Selection removed by an active-target close follows EON-C8's exit rules.
> - Before every tab or pane close, including with `--json` or `--yes`, the
>   CLI successfully inspects the addressed workspace and validates the
>   named target. It uses EON-C11's busy classification for the terminals
>   that this close will stop, including the caller when it is a target.
>   An unavailable busy list or a nonzero omitted count is unknown and
>   requires confirmation. A busy or unknown close in human mode lists its
>   affected terminals and asks for confirmation; cancellation stops
>   nothing. In JSON mode without `--yes` it stops nothing and returns
>   `not-confirmed` (exit 1), with detail `close of tab TAB requires
>   confirmation; rerun with --yes` or `close of pane PANE requires
>   confirmation; rerun with --yes`. `--yes` explicitly confirms this one
>   named close and never bypasses target, caller, popup or Stop validation.
>   Busy confirmation is independent of `warning_close_last_tab`. It uses
>   the latest successful inspection, not an atomic inspect-and-close
>   transaction; Runtime revalidates the exact live target before stopping.
> - Closing a workspace's final tab or that tab's last pane ends the window
>   when it is the last workspace (EON-C8), or removes that workspace while
>   others remain (EON-C33). With `warning_close_last_tab = true`, its
>   default, a human-mode CLI at a terminal asks first even when the target
>   is idle, unless `--yes` was given. An idle final close in JSON mode or
>   without a terminal retains its existing no-prompt behavior. A busy
>   final close requires the busy confirmation above, even in those modes
>   or with the warning setting false. When both warnings apply, ask once
>   with the final-close consequence and busy terminal list. The idle
>   final-close question and cancel note retain their existing wording,
>   naming the workspace while other workspaces remain. A close that
>   cannot inspect first fails without closing. Successful JSON and human
>   result shapes and exit statuses remain unchanged, including `Ended`
>   when the window ends. The caller's own terminal may end with it, as
>   with Stop. Eon rejects a non-boolean `warning_close_last_tab` with the
>   rest of `config.toml`.

In Important failures, replace the two sentences starting “While a popup covers
the caller's tab” and ending “including Alt+W” with:

> While a popup covers the target tab, `pane close` naming that tab's last
> pane changes nothing and exits 1. Without a calling terminal, a pane
> close under a popup also refuses a non-last pane, including Alt+W.

### EON-C33

**No amendment under recommendation 1.** Its addressed-workspace targeting,
foreign-ID exit 3, hidden-workspace continuity and emptying rules remain intact.
Do not use C35/C36's window-wide read/send lookup as authority to widen close.

### VEN-C8 — additional contract required by decision 4

The current clause at `venus/docs/CONTRACTS.md:731–736` explicitly requires the
focus workaround. **NEEDS LUCCA'S APPROVAL**, alongside the scope exception.
Replace this exact passage:

> shows the EON-C8 prompt, which Venus owns: Enter sends the held close,
> first focusing its tab if another tab became active, Escape dismisses it,
> Alt+Shift+D detaches, the wheel and the viewer's navigation keys scroll a
> long list, and other keys and pointer input reach nothing while it is
> open.

with:

> shows the EON-C8 prompt, which Venus owns: Enter sends the held close
> directly by its named target, without first focusing its tab. If another
> tab became active, that tab stays active. Escape dismisses the prompt,
> Alt+Shift+D detaches, the wheel and the viewer's navigation keys scroll a
> long list, and other keys and pointer input reach nothing while it is
> open.

Keep all other VEN-C8 clauses and historical proof records. Record this
amendment's approval and proof separately from old proof; add the accepted
contract change to `venus/CHANGELOG.md` under Unreleased.

## Approval boundary

Lucca must approve the verbatim EON-C8/EON-C10/VEN-C8 proposal and decisions
1–6 before code.
Decision 4 expressly expands the bead's Venus scope by one workaround removal.
If any decision changes, revise this document and the dependent plan first.
No runtime checks, profile refresh, installation, supervisor action, repository
edit, commit, review of an implementation, or behavior proof occurred here.

Planning review: one fresh read-only Codex pass found the omitted VEN-C8
amendment; the draft and implementation scope were corrected. The finder
narrowly rechecked that correction and reported the blocker resolved. Runtime
behavior remains untested. No repository contract has been changed.

comments.text:
# eon-agent-parity-a9g0.3 — implementation record (sclaude finish)

Implementer: Claude Opus 5.5 on Lucca's sclaude account, 2026-11-05, in the
detached worktree `/home/lucca/.cache/eon-agents/eon-a9g0-3b` at edge
`fe7c7b8` (EONW v34, Eon 0.1.18). Starting point: the overseer's `git apply -3`
of Argon's candidate (`argon-candidate-v34.patch`, written against `22f7d02`
and EONW v32). The plan is `eon-a9g0-3-work/PLAN.md` with the overseer's two
corrections (parity.rs and the command-runner test accept
`parse_close_arguments`; the exact help rows). The approved contract text is
the bead's contract-step comment. Nothing was written with `br`.

## 1. Rebase leftovers (B3)

- Resolved the three apply conflicts keeping both sides: `CHANGELOG.md` and
  `venus/CHANGELOG.md` put this bead's Unreleased entry above edge's EONW
  v33/v34 and scrollback entries; `docs/CONTRACTS.md` keeps edge's
  `eon-u5bvd.3/.4/.5` amendment provenance and scrollback proof records and
  appends this bead's provenance and proof record after them.
- Replaced the three leftover `eon_workspace_protocol::v32::` paths in
  `cli.rs` with `v34::`. The two protocol doc comments already sit in `v34.rs`.
  No wire field, tag, `VERSION`, encoding or graph changed; the protocol suite
  result is in the proof record.

## 2. What changed against the candidate

### CLI (`runtime/crates/eon-runtime/src/cli.rs`)

- **B1.** Every tab or pane close now inspects the addressed workspace and runs
  `close_question` first, with or without `--yes`. `--yes` skips only the
  question and the JSON refusal. An inspection failure or a target error from
  `close_question` is reported and nothing is sent.
- **S1.** `close_question` returns the final-close wording whenever the close
  is final and either its busy state needs confirmation or `warn_final` holds.
  A busy final close therefore names the window or workspace it ends with
  `warning_close_last_tab = false` too, at a terminal and through a pipe.
- **S2.** A missing busy list or any nonzero `omitted` is "busy state unknown"
  and lists every affected label. The candidate's "at least K still running"
  and partial-list branches are gone.
- **warn_final** is human mode, stdin a terminal, no `--yes`, and the setting.
  `control` computes the question without the warning, then with it, and reads
  `warning_close_last_tab` only when the two differ (N7: a non-final close no
  longer reads `config.toml`).
- **S3.** Help notes are the plan's exact lines:
  "Pane creation and moves, and tab moves, retain their calling-tab rules.",
  "Where shown, --json prints JSON and never asks.",
  "Busy tab/pane closes require --yes with --json; --yes confirms only that
  close.", "Tab/pane close IDs resolve in the caller's workspace, otherwise
  the shown one." The flags keep the existing `{command}…{reset}` colour
  markup that the replaced line used. Help rows are the overseer's exact rows.
- **N1.** `control(inputs, action, json, list, target, yes)` as planned.
- **N2.** `parse_close_arguments` is private.
- **N3.** One helper, `close_target_label`, names the target for the question,
  cancel note and refusal; `close_question` uses it. The `#[cfg(test)]`
  `final_close_prompt` shim and `final_close_prompt_with_busy` are replaced by
  one `final_close_prompt(terminals, workspace, busy)`; the existing
  `final_close_prompt_names_the_workspace_it_closes` test passes `None`.

### Runtime (`workspace.rs`)

Production code is the candidate's (both reviews: done as planned). Test
changes:

- `pane_close_targets_exact_ids_and_prunes_like_an_exit`: x6 is now the
  planned valid background close: a pane created in t1 before t2 opens is
  closed by ID, under t1's popup, by that popup's terminal, while the pending
  t2 is active; t2, t1's popup and selection stay; p1 is not consumed.
- `background_close_retains_popup_and_last_pane_guards`: rewritten. A pane
  caller and a popup caller of t2 each close a non-last pane under t1's popup
  (whole snapshot equal afterwards, exact popup ID kept); Alt+W without a
  caller refuses the same panes; both callers refuse t1's last covered pane;
  with Git hidden, t1's last pane closes and t1 survives with only its
  keep-alive popup; the sole tab's last pane with a hidden popup prepares both
  sessions and changes nothing.
- `workspace_set_refuses_foreign_targets`: adds stale local IDs (exact
  failures, with and without caller), a stale caller (`unknown-caller`), and
  shows a refused close does not consume its request ID.
- `hidden_callers_close_only_their_workspace_without_showing_it`: the shown
  w1 shows a selected popup and its whole topology is compared; the hidden w2
  gets a hidden popup; w2's final tab prepares the same terminals by tab and by
  last pane, and ending them removes only w2.
- N5: the stale comment ("Closing resolves the pane in the caller's tab") and
  the x5 comment now say ID/validated caller.

### Real-binary tests (`eon/crates/eon/tests/workspace_control.rs`)

- **Codex 6 / N4.** `run_with_pty` and the inline vanish PTY block are gone.
  `pseudo_terminal()` is lifted from the workspace-picker test (which now calls
  it), with its SAFETY comments and `FD_CLOEXEC`. `at_terminal()` bounds the
  wait for the question and for the exit by one 10 s deadline, kills and fails
  on timeout, kills its command if the meanwhile step panics, and keeps the
  controller open until the command exits. The meanwhile step itself is not
  under that deadline; its only blocking call, the concurrent close, runs
  through `bounded_output()` (10 s, killed and failed on timeout). Round 1
  (Codex 4).
- **Liveness (round 1, Codex 2).** `live_terminals()` reads each terminal's
  Orbit `LiveIdentity` before a close. `assert_only_ended()` then waits for
  each target's process to go with the existing bounded
  `wait_for_process_removal()`, and checks that each survivor's process still
  exists with the same start identity; it also keeps the record check (a
  target's record is no longer `Live`, a survivor's still is).
- `cli_closes_background_ids_and_preserves_the_presented_workspace`: the
  caller is t1's Agent popup; the active t2 shows its own Agent popup; t3 and
  t4 hold two panes. Pane and tab closes, each with that caller and with none,
  compare the whole presented workspace (only the target removed) and check
  that exactly the target's terminal processes ended (see Liveness). Stale tab
  (JSON, exact) and pane (human, exact) IDs exit 3 and change nothing. A raw
  replayed CloseTab returns `duplicate-request` and stops nothing.
- `cli_busy_background_close_confirms_refuses_and_cancels_without_focus`:
  t2 shows an Agent popup throughout; every comparison is the whole presented
  workspace; human pipe refusals assert the exact stderr; the vanishing target
  case runs the concurrent close inside the bounded wait and checks nothing
  else closed. The final matrix: busy × warning true/false × tab/pane ×
  terminal/pipe/JSON, all with the final-consequence wording; idle × warning
  true/false × terminal/terminal+`--yes`/pipe/JSON on fresh shown workspaces
  (their final close removes the workspace, so each case can succeed); then
  the idle window-ending close through a pipe.
- `cli_idle_background_close_ignores_other_busy_tabs`: rewritten (was
  vacuous). Default shells idle; a `sleep 300` command tab and t1's Agent
  popup stay busy, confirmed by the complete busy list. An idle pane closes
  through JSON without `--yes`, then its idle tab for a person with stdin
  null, neither asking; t1's popup stays; only the target's terminals end.
- `cli_close_preserves_workspace_scope_and_final_close_results`: adds
  caller-less and reverse (w2 caller → w1) foreign refusals with exact JSON,
  terminal liveness after each step, the hidden w2's removal through its last
  pane, a shown w3's removal through its tab, and the window's end through
  the last pane with the exact Ended JSON.
- New `a_confirmed_close_inspects_first_and_a_failed_inspection_closes_nothing`
  (Codex's B1 fix request): a fake supervisor answers lifecycle inspection and
  refuses workspace inspection; `tab close t1 --yes --json` and
  `pane close p1 --yes --json` exit 1 with its failure after exactly one
  Inspect and no close.

### Docs

- `docs/USAGE.md`: the two table rows point to the busy-close paragraphs; new
  paragraphs after the caller paragraph describe inspection before every
  close, the question, terminal/pipe/JSON outcomes, `--yes`, other tabs'
  busy terminals not counting, non-atomic inspection, busy final wording
  regardless of the setting, and (S6) that an eonbase window has no busy data
  so every close there is "busy state unknown".
- `docs/CONFIGURATION.md`: `false` turns off only the idle final warning; busy
  confirmation is independent, names the final consequence, and stays fixed
  because stopping busy work needs explicit consent (rule 6 reason).
- `eon/skills/eon/SKILL.md`: the refusal also covers "Eon cannot tell (always
  so in an eonbase window)" (S6).
- `docs/CONTRACTS.md`, `venus/docs/CONTRACTS.md` (B2): the proof records list
  the tests actually present. In round 1 the "pending" marks were replaced
  with the isolated installed observation: EON-C8's native confirmed close,
  EON-C10's closes and VEN-C8's amendment, with the code tree, store path and
  environment. The Venus test is not cited as proof. N6: changed contract
  lines are re-wrapped within the file's width, with no wording changed.

## 3. Deviations from the plan (all of them, mine and retained)

1. Test helpers beyond the plan's "no new harness": `at_terminal`,
   `wait_for_settled_workspace` (the candidate's, simplified), `show_agent`,
   `terminal_is_live`, `terminal_endpoints`, `assert_only_ended`, `presented`,
   `assert_closed_only`, all in the existing test file. `pseudo_terminal` is
   the planned lift of the picker test's PTY setup.
2. The real-binary tests use the Agent popup, not Commands: Commands needs
   `eon-commands` on the fixture's terminal PATH (`popup-command`); Agent's
   `auto` command finds the fixture's Codex stub. Agent is keep-alive and busy.
3. `presented()` drops `running`, `busy` and the four quota fields from
   comparisons: they change on their own (window-wide live counts, quota
   probe timestamps).
4. The idle final-warning success cases close fresh shown workspaces (removal)
   instead of the window, since a fixture window ends only once. The window's
   end is covered by: idle pipe (busy test), last pane `--yes --json` with
   exact Ended JSON (scope test), last tab `--yes --json`
   (`closing_the_final_tab_ends_the_window_and_its_terminals`, existing).
5. Extra test not in the plan:
   `a_confirmed_close_inspects_first_and_a_failed_inspection_closes_nothing`.
6. `final_close_prompt` takes a third `busy` argument (plan: keep it for the
   idle wording); its idle output is unchanged and still tested.
7. `close_target_label` is a helper the plan did not name (shared by
   `close_question` and `control`).
8. Retained from the candidate: `--yes` added to three existing real-binary
   tests whose fixture terminals are busy because no foreground is scripted
   (`commands_from_a_terminal_target_its_column_and_stale_callers_change_nothing`,
   `delayed_second_cli_receives_committed_workspace_and_controls_three_sessions`,
   `closing_the_final_tab_ends_the_window_and_its_terminals`).
9. Retained from the candidate: `hidden_callers_…` names the shown workspace
   w1 and the hidden one w2, the reverse of the plan's labels.
10. Retained from the candidate: the Venus chrome test as planned. It is
    tautological (Opus S7, a plan defect for Lucca) and is not cited as proof.
11. Profile refresh is not done here; it is the overseer's landing step. The
    isolated installed batch was first left pending (B2), then run in round 1
    against the exact candidate built with `--out-link`, not a refreshed
    profile (see `02-proof.md`).
12. Fixed in round 1: the first finish checked liveness only through Orbit
    management records (`terminal_is_live`), not processes. That was weaker
    than the plan's "exactly the intended terminal processes end". The process
    checks are now added (Liveness above).
13. The vanishing-target case removes the target with a concurrent
    `tab close --yes --json` from the real CLI, not the plan's direct-action
    fixture. The busy test's `pane` variant closes a background tab's only
    pane, so the tab goes with it. A busy pane closed beside a surviving
    sibling is covered only with `--yes` (`cli_closes_background_…`) and by
    the unit tests (Opus nit 2).
14. The replayed close in `cli_closes_background_…` sends a constructed raw
    `CloseTab` twice under one request ID rather than replaying a CLI
    request, because the CLI chooses its own request IDs (Codex round-1
    table).

## 4. Plan observation, not acted on

The plan says "a known idle pending tab's picker can close without a busy
prompt". By EON-C11's classification only Files and Git popups are never busy
(`attention.rs` `IDLE_ENTRIES`), so whether a pending tab's picker ever reads
as idle depends on which entry the pair uses. Not checked; no test claims it.

The busy confirmation and its question, cancel and refusal texts stay fixed:
stopping busy work needs explicit consent, and `--yes` is that consent. The
idle final warning stays governed by `warning_close_last_tab` (default true).

title: Show a pane's command and exit status to the CLI
description:
## Why

An agent can't tell what a pane is running or whether its command succeeded: the snapshot has no argv, and an ended pane is pruned with its exit status written only to the supervisor log. Use: did the build pane exit 0? Parity gap 7 of the epic eon-agent-parity-a9g0 (inventory on eon-agent-parity-audit-t31r). Title and cwd belong with orb-p92 phase 1, not here.

## Evidence (edge 8a25211)

- `runtime/crates/eon-workspace-protocol/src/v19.rs:241` (`Pane`): no command and no exit status.
- `runtime/crates/eon-runtime/src/sessions.rs:1376` computes the exit code; `runtime/crates/eon-runtime/src/supervisor.rs:1067-1070` logs "terminal … ended with status …" and prunes the session. The log lives in `$XDG_STATE_HOME/eon/logs` (docs/USAGE.md:422-427).

## Prerequisites

None blocking. Coordinate any EONW bump with eon-tab-create-launch-8tl4 and eon-agent-parity-a9g0.1.

## Scope

In scope: the contract amendment (EON-C8, EON-C10), exposing the Runtime-launched argv for command panes and a bounded record of recent pane exits (status and time) through `eon session --json` or a new read command, docs and tests.

Out of scope: reading a pane's output (orb-p92), inferring the foreground process of a shell, durable history across supervisor restarts.

## Acceptance

- `eon pane create -- CMD` panes show their argv, and after the command exits its status can be read by pane ID for a bounded time.
- Contract text approved by Lucca before code.

## Implementation Notes

1. Decide at the reference gate whether this needs an EONW change and bump. If so, coordinate the version with other changes in flight. Also decide where an ended pane's record lives and how long. Stop for approval.
2. Implement, test, document.

## Verification

- `nix develop -c eon-test -p eon-runtime` exits 0 with a test that runs `false` in a command pane and reads its non-zero status.

## Stop Conditions

- Stop if the exit status isn't available to Runtime without a new Orbit contract, or if verification fails twice.

## Reference gate

Consequential (contract change, possibly EONW). Before code, record on this bead: the owner of the argv and of the exit record (Runtime sessions and supervisor), the docs/REFERENCES.md routes read, and comparables at inspected revisions: tmux `#{pane_dead_status}` with `remain-on-exit`, WezTerm `cli list` fields, kitty `@ ls`. Note what was kept and rejected.

## Current evidence and completion boundary (8ebdd69)

v19 is historical; current SnapshotPane is in v40.rs and CLI json_pane is
workspace.rs:3424. Keep Runtime's launched argv distinct from foreground program/
OSC 133 facts owned by related eon-xjzr4.1 (which excludes argv by default).
Neither replaces the bounded by-pane-ID exit record. Related
eon-terminal-end-status-mapping-cxys owns signal/owner-loss mapping: reuse its
accepted mapping, never fabricate success or add a competing status policy.
No blocking dependency on foreground sampling is inferred.

At the reference gate choose bounds, eviction/expiry and query-after-prune behavior,
including unknown/live/exited/evicted IDs and unknown status; get exact EON-C8/C10
approval. Expose retention values or record their fixed-value rationale under
Configurability. Acceptance: launch argv remains byte-safe, completed status is
readable by the original pane ID before expiry, and expiry returns an explicit
unavailable result. Restart persistence remains excluded. Use a focused Runtime/CLI
regression and isolated installed completed-command query; full wire proof only if
the approved route needs it. Portability: neutral.

description:
## Why

Without `--json`, `eon stop` asks for confirmation on stdin. On EOF (for example `</dev/null`) or any answer but yes, it prints "cancelled" and exits 0; piped `y` confirms. A script or agent then believes the stop succeeded. Parity gap 9 of the epic eon-agent-parity-a9g0 (inventory on eon-agent-parity-audit-t31r).

## Evidence (edge 8a25211)

- `runtime/crates/eon-runtime/src/generation.rs:496-508` and `:562` (`read_stop_confirmation`): the prompt, the "cancelled" exit 0, and the stdin read.
- `runtime/crates/eon-runtime/src/cli.rs:745` (`control`, around `warning_close_last_tab` at :774): the final-close prompt for `tab close`/`pane close`, asked only on a TTY.
- `runtime/crates/eon-runtime/src/control.rs:477-491`: the exit-code map.

## Prerequisites

None blocking.

## Scope

In scope: the EON-C11/EON-C10 amendment and one consistent non-interactive rule for every CLI confirmation: either refuse with a defined non-zero exit and code when stdin isn't a TTY, or accept an explicit `--yes`. Docs and process tests.

Out of scope: changing what is confirmed, and the `--json` behavior (it already never prompts).

## Acceptance

- With non-TTY stdin and no `--json`, every confirming command either refuses with its documented non-zero exit or proceeds under the approved flag. None exits 0 without acting.
- Contract text approved by Lucca before code.

## Implementation Notes

1. List every confirmation site, draft the rule, and stop for approval.
2. Implement and add process tests on the real binary.

## Verification

- `nix develop -c eon-test` exits 0 with a test running `eon stop GEN </dev/null` that checks the new exit.

## Stop Conditions

- Stop if verification fails twice for the same reason.

## Maintenance Notes

- Overlaps eon-cli-action-discovery-ogzi's "structured mode never prompts". Keep the two rules consistent.

## Reference gate

Consequential (contract change). Before code, record on this bead: the owner (CLI projection in `cli.rs`/`generation.rs`), the docs/REFERENCES.md routes read, and comparables at inspected revisions for non-interactive confirmation: for example `apt-get -y` and its non-TTY refusal, `git clean` requiring `-f`, and `rm -i` on a closed stdin. Note what was kept and rejected.
close_reason: Rule shipped: CLI confirmations exit 1 with not-confirmed when stdin is not a terminal and no yes is read (EON-C10/C11, approved by Lucca 2026-10-29). Proof on the bead; installed observation by eon-overseer after the profile refresh.

comments.author: lucca
comments.text: Missing site, 2026-10-27 (prime-beads pass 2): 'eon workspace close WS' (5bc9970) has the same defect: runtime/crates/eon-runtime/src/cli.rs:1072-1075 reads read_stop_confirmation() and on EOF or any non-yes prints 'cancelled; workspace {id} stays open' and returns Ok(0). Cover it with the same rule. The generation.rs prompt cited above moved (prompt now around runtime/crates/eon-runtime/src/generation.rs:888-952).

comments.author: lucca
comments.text:
Plan (Opus planner, 2026-10-29; worktree ~/.cache/eon-agents/claude-confirm-loud at 0b6ef93). Approval to work this bead: Lucca, 2026-10-29, to eon-overseer: "we need to do more eon stuff / can we fire more agents?", then choosing this bead from the overseer's list (relayed by eon-overseer, 2026-10-29). Contract wording still needs Lucca's approval: Q1 below.

Confirmation sites (edge 0b6ef93), all in runtime/crates/eon-runtime/src:
1. `eon stop GEN`: generation.rs:886-897 (stop_generation). Asks whatever stdin is; non-yes or EOF prints `cancelled; no Stop sent ...` on stdout, exit 0.
2. `eon stop previous|all`: generation.rs stop_generations calls (1) per target; status is the max.
3. `eon window stop ID|all` (non-json): windows.rs stop_window runs the window's `eon stop all` with inherited stdin, so (2) per window.
4. `eon workspace close WS` (non-json): cli.rs:1048-1076 (control). Same defect as (1).
5. Final close of `eon tab close` / `eon pane close`: cli.rs:1014-1036. Asks only when stdin is a terminal; without one it closes. It never exits 0 without acting.
All three prompts share read_stop_confirmation (generation.rs:952) and repeat the `y|Y|yes|YES` match and cancel block.

Rule drafted (Q1, recommendation A): at a terminal nothing changes. When stdin is not a terminal, a yes line still confirms (EON-C23 keeps piped confirmations), and any other answer, end of input included, changes nothing and exits 1 with the new failure code `not-confirmed` on stderr (exit map unchanged: default arm, "refused"). No `--yes`: `--json` is already the non-interactive mode and a piped `y` covers human output. Site 5 is unchanged.

Approach (Codex implements):
- One owner: replace read_stop_confirmation with one helper in generation.rs that asks the question, reads the line and returns either "confirmed" or the exit to return (cancel note + 0 at a terminal; `not-confirmed` failure, exit 1, otherwise). Sites 1 and 4 call it; site 5 calls it too, for the same match and cancel note. The answer/terminal decision is a pure function with a unit test.
- cli.rs help line 874 and docs: EON-C10 (exit bullet ~819, workspace close ~933), EON-C11 (~1247 decline sentence), USAGE.md exit table row 0/1 (~463) and the stop paragraph (~100), CHANGELOG.md (user-visible exit change).
- Tests: eon/crates/eon/tests/workspace_control.rs. Red: a new real-binary check that `eon stop GEN` with stdin from /dev/null exits 1, reports `not-confirmed` and leaves the supervisor live (base: exit 0). Same check for `eon workspace close WS`. Update the existing piped cases: :3482 (workspace close cancel) and :6600 (`stop all` with `y\nn\n` now exits 1 with the first Stop done and the second not sent).
- Checks: nix develop -c eon-test -p eon (workspace_control) and -p eon-runtime; cargo fmt --check; cargo clippy --locked --all-targets -- -D warnings for eon-runtime and eon.

Scope boundary: no change to what is confirmed, to `--json`, to the exit-status map, to site 5's terminal gate, or to Venus. No new flag. eon-cli-action-discovery-ogzi's "structured mode never prompts" stays consistent (`--json` never asks).

Reference gate (consequential: contract change). Owner: the CLI projection (generation.rs stop_generation, cli.rs control). Route read: docs/REFERENCES.md "How should Eon expose agent-readable actions ..." (stable errors, typed failures; preserve). Comparables inspected on this machine, 2026-10-29:
- git 2.43.0 `git clean` without -f in a scratch repo: "fatal: clean.requireForce defaults to true ... refusing to clean", exit 128. Kept: refusal is loud and non-zero. Rejected: refusing even a piped answer.
- GNU coreutils 9.4 `rm -i f </dev/null` and `echo n | rm -i f`: both exit 0, file kept. This is the defect this bead removes; rejected.
- apt 2.8.3 apt-get(8) `-y, --assume-yes` (man page, not run: needs root): explicit assume-yes flag for non-interactive use. Rejected for Eon: `--json` already skips confirmation, so `--yes` would be a second owner of "skip confirmation".
- zellij v0.45.1 (~/pjs/refs/zellij-v0.45.1 at efd8fd5) src/commands.rs:49 kill_all_sessions: `--yes` skips; a decline prints "Abort." and exits 1. Kept: decline without a yes is exit 1. Rejected: exit 1 on a decline typed at a terminal (option B), because Eon's Commands popup keeps any non-zero result on screen until Enter (cli.rs:178), so "Quit this window" then n would need an extra Enter.
Decision: option A pending Q1. Its check: the red process test above.

comments.author: lucca
comments.text:
Q1 (contract wording; needs Lucca's approval before code). How should a CLI confirmation behave without a terminal?

A (recommended): only non-terminal stdin becomes loud. At a terminal nothing changes. Without one, a piped `y` still confirms, and anything else, end of input included, exits 1 with `not-confirmed`. Why: it fixes the defect (no exit 0 without acting for scripts or agents), keeps EON-C23's piped confirmations and the Commands popup's one-key decline, and adds no flag (`--json` already skips confirmation).
B: any decline exits 1, at a terminal too (apt-get, zellij). Simpler rule, but declining "Quit this window" in Commands then needs an extra Enter, because the popup holds any non-zero result.
C: without a terminal refuse outright unless `--yes`. Drops piped confirmations (EON-C23 amendment), adds a flag to four commands, and makes `--yes` a second way to skip what `--json` skips.

Proposed wording for A:
- EON-C10, new bullet after the exit-status bullet: "A CLI confirmation (`eon stop`, `eon window stop`, `eon workspace close`, and the final close of `eon tab close` and `eon pane close`) proceeds only on a yes answer (`y`, `Y`, `yes` or `YES`). Any other answer changes nothing. At a terminal it prints the cancel note and exits 0. When stdin is not a terminal, it exits 1 with `not-confirmed`, end of input included, and a piped yes still confirms. `--json` never asks. The final close asks only at a terminal and otherwise closes."
- EON-C11, after "Declining one target reports that no Stop was sent for that generation": "; without a terminal that target is `not-confirmed` (exit 1), and the command exits with the largest status."
- docs/USAGE.md exit table: row 0 "Success, including a Stop or close confirmation declined at a terminal"; row 1 "The command was understood but refused or failed, including a confirmation that got no yes when stdin is not a terminal".

comments.author: lucca
comments.text: Q1 decided: 1A, with the proposed wording for EON-C10 (new bullet after the exit-status bullet), EON-C11 (addition after "Declining one target reports that no Stop was sent for that generation") and docs/USAGE.md exit rows 0 and 1, exactly as in the Q1 comment. Lucca, 2026-10-29: "answer: all ok" (relayed by eon-overseer, 2026-10-29, who showed him Q1 with 1A recommended and the exact wording). The same relay gave the go for Codex and its checks at CARGO_BUILD_JOBS=4. eon-tab-create-launch-8tl4 also edits EON-C10, so this slice keeps its EON-C10 edit to its own bullet.

comments.author: lucca
comments.text:
Proof and review ledger (2026-10-29). Base edge 0b6ef93; final tree 612dac52aa71cf482be3e41745a94fff625e3f2b (this commit, plus this bead record). Implemented by Codex (gpt-6.1-sol, xhigh) from the plan; Opus first and final gate.

Change: generation.rs `confirm(question, cancelled)` owns every CLI confirmation (sites 1, 4 and 5 in the plan; 2 and 3 through 1). `confirmation_status(&[u8], terminal)` decides on the raw answer bytes, trimmed with trim_ascii: yes (`y`, `Y`, `yes`, `YES`) confirms; any other answer prints the cancel note and exits 0 at a terminal; without one it reports `error not-confirmed: <what stays>; no yes was read and stdin is not a terminal` on stderr and exits 1 (default arm of the exit map, unchanged). The final close keeps its terminal gate. Docs: EON-C10 bullet and EON-C11 addition as approved; docs/USAGE.md stop paragraph and exit rows 0/1; cli.rs help line; CHANGELOG.md Unreleased entry.

Red/green (Linux x86_64, `nix develop -c eon-test`, Determinate Nix 3.21.2 / nix 2.34.7, CARGO_BUILD_JOBS=4):
- Red on 0b6ef93 code (Codex run): `eon-test -p eon --test workspace_control stop_without_terminal_requires_yes` failed: status 0, stdout "cancelled; no Stop sent for generation g1-...". Green after the change.
- Final tree 612dac5, run by Opus: `eon-test -p eon --test workspace_control` 50 passed; `eon-test -p eon-runtime` 134 passed, 1 ignored; `cargo fmt --check` clean; `cargo clippy --locked --all-targets -p eon-runtime -p eon -- -D warnings` clean. The tree was unchanged after the checks.
- Tests: new `stop_without_terminal_requires_yes` (`eon stop GEN` with null stdin exits 1, `not-confirmed`, empty stdout, supervisor live); unit `confirmation_requires_yes_and_only_terminal_declines_succeed` (yes/no x terminal/not, invalid UTF-8 included); updated workspace close null-stdin case, `stop all` with piped `y\nn\n` (exit 1, first stopped, second `not-confirmed`), and window stop ID/all propagation.
- Note: one Codex run of eon-runtime saw `bound_io_accepts_einval_only_after_peer_hangup` fail once (EINVAL) and pass on retry; the test is untouched by this change and passed in both Opus runs.

Not proved here: installed behaviour. After landing and the profile refresh, the coordinator's one installed observation in an isolated Eon: `eon stop <gen> </dev/null` exits 1 with `not-confirmed` and the generation stays live; at a terminal, `eon stop <gen>` answered `n` prints the cancel note and exits 0 (so Commands > Quit this window, then n, closes the popup without "Press Enter").

Ledger: Codex reviews 2 (full review of candidate b77c69a: 1 blocking finding, an invalid-UTF-8 answer bypassed `not-confirmed`, fixed in fix round 1, which also simplified the decision to an enum and moved the USAGE sentences so "therefore" reads as before; narrow re-check b77c69a..612dac5: nothing blocking, 1 nit, ASCII-only trimming of the answer, kept because every yes answer is ASCII and a non-ASCII byte now refuses). Opus gate passes 2 (candidate: nits only, folded into fix round 1; final tree: clean).

comments.text: Installed observation (eon-overseer, 2026-10-29, x86_64 Linux, private headless Sway, profile build /nix/store/qjwbpjinqrx0fq4mziib01ddj627jcci-eon-0.1.7 at 459a7d1; evidence /home/lucca/.cache/eon-agents/eon-overseer/obs-0129/RESULT.md): PASS. `eon stop GEN </dev/null` exit 1, 'error not-confirmed: no Stop sent for generation ...; no yes was read and stdin is not a terminal', generation still live. At a TTY answered n: 'cancelled; no Stop sent ...', exit 0, still live.

title: Add CLI commands for columns, the sidebar and attention jumps
description:
## Why and approved scope

Parity gap 10 of eon-agent-parity-a9g0. Lucca raised this to P2 on 2026-11-02
(comment 5088). Preserve existing-action CLI coverage and the column-choice outcome
added by the overseer on 2026-11-11 (comment 6447): pane create/edit choose a column,
return new tab/pane identities and refuse clearly at four columns. Example
--column new is a proposal, not approved syntax.

## Current evidence and owner (8ebdd69)

v40.rs:233/276-282 carries the existing actions. cli/parity.rs:115-119 still
excepts CreateColumn/FocusAttention/NextAttention/PreviousAttention. ToggleSidebar
already maps to the shipped CLI at :111 and cli.rs:2356 (eon-5g0e5). Protect it;
do not implement it twice. Runtime workspace/attention owns selection and policy.

## Ordered children

- .1: wrappers for existing column/attention actions, parity/help/docs/proof;
  no new wire version or attention behavior. Keep the existing sidebar path.
- .2: column choice for pane/edit launch, after .1 and .20.2's shared directory/
  no-focus batch. This may require an EONW bump and EON-C8/EON-C10 amendment;
  the old no-wire promise applies only to .1.

## Approval, acceptance and boundaries

Get exact EON-C10/EON-C31/C33 command/focus text approved before code. Record owner
REFERENCES routes and comparable revisions. Specify pane/popup attention targeting
and hidden-session/shown-session effects explicitly. Column syntax/placement and
Editor-popup interaction remain decision questions, not silently chosen here.

Both children complete with full-value parity, approved failure matrix and their
own narrow checks/isolated installed interaction. Follow current root proof/review;
parent verification is Beads state/graph. No attention/sidebar redesign, arbitrary
split tree, ratio or more than four columns. Preserve desktop focus. Portability:
neutral Runtime/CLI policy with native evidence named explicitly.
acceptance_criteria:
- [ ] Child .1 maps CreateColumn, FocusAttention, NextAttention and PreviousAttention and preserves ToggleSidebar.
- [ ] Child .2 delivers the approved column option and requested Helix recipe.
