title: Decide the next proof-bearing Bend policy boundary in Venus or Runtime
description:
## Why

Lucca asked on 2026-11-07 to evaluate upgrading Bend and moving more responsibility into it, possibly Venus, then said "create and update the beads". Orbit already executes a proved pure policy; any expansion should protect consequential invariants while earning its adapter, proof-maintenance and failure-handling cost. This bead chooses whether and where to attempt one bounded follow-up. It approves no production migration, language-policy change, or new law.

## Evidence

- docs/AGENT-RULES.md, Implementation Languages approves Bend for Orbit session policy. Extending that ownership to Venus or Runtime needs an explicit subsystem advantage and user decision accepting the toolchain/ownership cost.
- venus/src/application.rs:977 onwards (`QuitProgress`, `QuitStep`, `QuitEffects`): QuitProgress coordinates busy confirmation, a pending refresh and a Stop ticket; repeated input and unrelated replies must not send or clear the wrong Stop.
- venus/src/input.rs:90-131: attachment retirement suppresses old key sequences. venus/src/application.rs:196-239 (`PresentationState`) and :481-501 (selection finish gate) bind interaction to current presentation and selection-finish revisions.
- venus/src/application/scroll.rs:245-320 and :355-469: request slots, matching outcomes, cancellation and authoritative-frame gating are discrete policies adjacent to floating-point scroll physics.
- venus/src/model.rs:762-927 (`apply`, `apply_resource`, `accept_scene`) validates message/resource order beside frame and pixel payload processing. A migration must retain the canonical protocol codec and avoid sending bulk frames/pixels through a policy worker.
- runtime/crates/eon-runtime/src/workspace.rs:882 onwards (`apply_action`) couples workspace actions to explicit preparation/operation callbacks. docs/ARCHITECTURE.md:103-116 keeps live topology/action policy in Runtime, serving both CLI and Venus.
- venus/AGENTS.md:40-49 preserves one shared model/renderer/input/accessibility path and native Wayland/Vulkan plus Apple Silicon/Metal. Upstream Bend v2.0.40 bend2/effs/window.c uses Xlib on Linux; Bend's native window stack is not an accepted replacement for Venus.
- Closed eon-pxn.9 proved a disposable AgentRun kernel but ended DEFER: no supported versioned native embedding target with generated typed C/Rust bindings. It rejected relying on generated private C entry points, Bun at runtime and a second handwritten schema. Read that decision itself; do not infer that a newer release removes its blocker.
- eon-fony owns Orbit worker-fault survival; eon-n2m7 owns evidence of proof value, maintenance cost and exit triggers. orb-reconsider-verus-eon-state-machine-kpw records the alternative verifier's high integration cost and remains deferred.
- Compiler baseline and compatibility work: eon-bend-2040-036p8, exact Bend 2.0.40 commit 624dd9f4607cd29b0871a9b96d413bfb11e92f52.
- Upstream references at that revision: https://github.com/bendlang/bend/blob/v2.0.40/guide/EFFECTS.md ; https://github.com/bendlang/bend/blob/v2.0.40/WONTFIX.txt ; https://github.com/bendlang/bend/blob/v2.0.40/bend2/effs/window.c . Recheck native library-target issue #813 without assuming it shipped.

## Contract and prerequisites

Evaluation/decision only. Candidate constraints route through VEN-C2, VEN-C8, VEN-C14/VEN-C16 and existing EON-C8/EON-C11 for quit/lifecycle, with exact clauses identified before proposing changes. Broader workspace policy stays Runtime-owned. Any eventual contract or law delta must be shown to Lucca for approval before implementation.

Use the accepted compiler/proof-cost evidence from eon-bend-2040-036p8 as the first evaluation baseline. Read the applicable root, Orbit, Venus and Runtime rules and owner reference maps, plus the complete prior eon-pxn.9 decision and the two open Bend risk beads.

## Scope

In scope: a source-backed comparison and concrete recommendation recorded here. Rank:
1. Extending proof coverage within Orbit's already-approved policy boundary.
2. Venus quit/close coordination: the recommended first Venus candidate, not an approved migration.
3. Venus input/attachment lifetime and selection/presentation gating.
4. Venus scroll-request sequencing, separately from physical input translation and numerical physics.
5. Runtime workspace transitions as a larger later candidate, retaining the same CLI/GUI owner.

For each, name a proposed invariant, the actual code/effect owner, what existing tests already cover, the smallest sufficient Rust/test alternative, the Bend integration boundary, expected proof value, and all unmeasured costs. Compare keeping Rust, a supported native library path if it exists, and a component-owned worker only if its lifecycle/IPC costs can be justified. Reuse recorded proof/cost evidence; no prototype, compiler fork or retained code is authorized by this research bead.

Out of scope: production source, contracts, laws, Nix/profile or dependency changes; adding a Venus/Runtime worker; a broad Venus rewrite; renderer/shaping/GPU/window/accessibility/IME replacement; duplicating EONW/ORBS/ORBF schemas or maintaining a second policy implementation; reviving AgentRun or Verus work without its own trigger/approval.

Portability disposition: neutral research. Every proposed integration must preserve native Linux Wayland/Vulkan and Apple Silicon Metal, input responsiveness and surviving Orbit terminals.

## Acceptance

- The comparison ranks the candidates by consequential invariants protected and total lifecycle cost, rather than migrated LOC. It distinguishes current code, historical experiment evidence, estimates and unresolved measurements.
- The current status of native embedding is established at an exact upstream revision. If unavailable, the earlier DEFER remains explicit; a sidecar is not treated as an already approved workaround.
- A proposed pilot, if justified, owns one complete production policy and removes its former Rust implementation. No proof-only duplicate may be described as proving the shipped Rust policy.
- The proposed boundary states bounded inputs/decisions, one state owner, canonical type/schema derivation, adapter responsibilities, timeout/crash/malformed-output behavior and the effect of stale/late replies. No UI-thread blocking, unintended input/Stop, terminal termination, or fallback policy duplication is accepted implicitly.
- Name the intended laws for Lucca's review and a property-targeted negative mutation plus an outer integration falsifier for a future pilot. Distinguish pure transition proof from unproved compiler, adapter, toolkit, compositor, GPU and OS behavior. These are proposals, not approved laws.
- Record one recommendation: retain Rust, defer until a named trigger, or propose one bounded pilot with expected cost, removal path and concrete acceptance. Lucca's response is recorded before language/contract changes or production implementation beads are created. Later candidates remain comparison context, without speculative implementation children.

## Implementation Notes

1. Use the upgrade's actual proof/tooling results; inspect existing quit/input/selection tests and the prior DEFER before designing a new boundary.
2. Produce the smallest candidate contract (consumer, trigger, result, failures) and compare complete integration shapes. Do not design a generic cross-product policy framework.
3. Present the recommendation and the exact outstanding user-owned decisions. If a new experiment is needed, propose its bounded scope and measurements for approval instead of running it under this bead.

## Verification

Planning-only route: source links, exact upstream revision/capability evidence, complete candidate matrix, clear decision/approval state, br show and dependency graph. No builds, tests, runtime/profile action or implementation change. A source-only recommendation cannot claim measured pilot latency, memory, robustness or end-to-end correctness.

## Stop Conditions

Stop before production/contract/law edits, an experiment, a new implementation child, or a new subsystem/language promise. Stop if a candidate requires duplicate policy/schema, generated private C as an API, or cannot isolate its failure from existing terminals. Record Defer or reject with the missing evidence rather than inventing a supported embedding surface.

## Maintenance Notes

Keep this separate from the compiler upgrade: a successful upgrade does not authorize expansion. eon-pxn.9 remains closed with its recorded DEFER. Existing Orbit host/worker ownership and eon-fony's unresolved recovery options remain unchanged. The earlier discussion's ranking is provisional and must be tested against integration cost.

Evidence relocated against detached 8ebdd69 on 2026-11-12; upstream capability claims still require the exact-revision research described above, not inference from this planning pass.

title: Bind stop confirmation to the observed supervisor
description:
## Contract routing

Harden EON-C11 without changing its command surface. The consumer is one local user or automation invoking `eon stop GENERATION [--json]`; the trigger is a stop attempt whose validated control-socket owner is replaced before mutation; the result is that Eon stops only the supervisor instance it validated or fails explicitly while preserving the replacement and every Session. Normal same-owner human and JSON stop behavior remains unchanged.

This correction adds no EONW field, command, compatibility window, persisted runtime identity, child contract, or distribution promise.

## Why

Human stop confirmation currently describes supervisor A, waits for input, then opens a fresh path and accepts a same-generation response from supervisor B. Session labels restart at `session-1`, so the displayed generation and Session names do not bind the destructive action to A.

The exact audit reproduction stopped A, started B under the same generation while the old prompt waited, then answered `y`; the old confirmation terminated B and exited successfully.

Impact: HIGH. Effort: S/M. Implementation risk: MEDIUM. Confidence: HIGH.

## Evidence

- `crates/eon/src/main.rs:840-879`: `stop_generation` inspects and displays one `GenerationRecord`, then waits without retaining the observed control-socket identity.
- `crates/eon/src/main.rs:881-905`: stop opens a new connection and accepts a `Stopped` response when only the generation string matches.
- `crates/eon/src/main.rs:315-357` and `:1439-1471`: presentation already captures and revalidates `SocketIdentity`, proving the repository has the needed owner mechanism.
- `eon-audit-eon-runtime-lifecycle-wqz` comment 271 records the exact 1b8836e reproduction, hashes, reference gate, and cleanup.
- EON-C11 in `docs/CONTRACTS.md` requires confirmed stop to name affected live Sessions and failure to preserve Sessions.

## Prerequisite and reference gate

- No implementation prerequisite. Fix this correctness defect before `eon-5rp` moves another owner out of `main.rs`; that refactor must preserve the corrected lifecycle behavior.
- Rebaseline the cited symbols after any intervening revision.
- Reuse the audit reference gate: Eon HEAD `1b8836e616222f29c57ac697916872010db14685`; Orbit source `64db581445bafca1a08a6530f8e44f9c1edbc169` with ORBS v2 proof `9d6d2bb37f20ab4ad9e186c7bc715eabef43e757`; Ghosthub lifecycle comparison `072cc83559bd590ed5d759af05ec0a1868dbf359`.
- Preserve fresh backend authority and exact destructive-target revalidation. Reject PID, process-name, pathname-only, or cached Session-name authority.
- No dependency or crate feature is expected. Stop for the crate gate and user approval before changing any manifest.

## Scope

In scope:
- `stop_generation` and the smallest existing runtime probe/connection helpers needed to retain and revalidate one `SocketIdentity`.
- One real-process regression in `crates/eon/tests/workspace_control.rs`.
- EON-C11 current-state proof metadata, `CHANGELOG.md`, and README LOC only as required after the accepted fix.

Out of scope:
- EONW schema or protocol changes, a supervisor nonce, PID files, process-tree inspection, persisted registries, daemonization, legacy stop support, compatibility windows, or child-repository changes.
- Changing confirmation policy, generation selection, Session naming, JSON structure beyond an existing bounded failure shape, attach behavior, or ordinary successful stop semantics.
- Refactoring unrelated runtime or managed-environment code.

## Implementation notes

1. Write the real-process regression first: pause a human stop after it displays A, stop A through its owner, start same-generation B, answer `y`, and require a bounded nonzero owner-changed failure while B and its child remain live.
2. Bind inspection and mutation to one validated socket identity. After confirmation, revalidate and send on the verified connection so replacement between check and use fails closed.
3. Route human and JSON stop through the same owner-bound helper where that removes duplicate policy; do not add a new protocol identity when the local socket identity is sufficient.
4. Preserve the current response-before-termination ordering and exact supervisor-owned cleanup.

## Acceptance

- The replacement regression fails on the audited implementation and passes after the fix.
- A prompt produced from supervisor A can never terminate same-generation supervisor B after path replacement.
- The failure is bounded, nonzero, and names that the validated supervisor changed; B, Venus state, and every B Session remain live.
- Human cancellation still changes nothing.
- Same-owner human and JSON stop still return the authoritative stopped Session list and terminate only that supervisor children.
- Existing presentation, attach, legacy, concurrent-launch, child-exit, workspace, and generation tests retain their observable results.
- No new product contract, EONW value, dependency, component identity, or public configuration surface is introduced.

## Verification

- `cargo test --locked -p eon --test workspace_control stop_confirmation_refuses_a_replacement_supervisor` should exit 0 and prove B remains live.
- `cargo test --locked -p eon --test workspace_control concurrent_launches_converge_and_generation_stop_is_owner_routed` should exit 0.
- `cargo fmt --all --check`
- `cargo check --locked --workspace`
- `cargo test --locked --workspace`
- `cargo clippy --locked --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings`
- `cargo run --locked -p eon-manifest -- components/eon-alpha-v1.json`
- `nix build --no-link --print-out-paths --no-update-lock-file path:.#default`
- `nix flake check --no-build --no-update-lock-file path:.`
- `git diff --check`
- After the proof-bearing commit, refresh the active `eon` profile without stopping running supervisors; verify the profile resolves the new artifact and report restart required for already-running generations.

## Stop conditions

- Stop if the current stop owner or EON-C11 contract has drifted materially.
- Stop if a correct fix requires a new protocol field, persisted instance identity, dependency, cross-repository change, or destructive process inference.
- Stop if the regression cannot distinguish A from B without relying on timing alone.
- Stop if the same verification failure repeats twice after a reasonable correction.

## Maintenance notes

The first sufficient fix reuses Eon existing socket identity and owner-bound connection pattern. Reject a general lifecycle token framework, manager daemon, or broad stop redesign. The final `eon-audit-eon-runtime-lifecycle-wqz` pass must rerun this regression after `eon-5rp`.
close_reason: Implemented dbffad4: stop inspection, confirmation, and mutation are bound to one SocketIdentity and verified stream. Replacement regression, 32-test suite, exact Nix artifact, installed dogfood, profile refresh, and final simplification pass all pass; proof indexed by cf329a7.

title: Make a missed Venus redraw invalidation fail a test instead of showing a stale frame
description:
## Why

Source: "A Critique of GPUI", https://blog.zortax.de/posts/a-critique-of-gpui (2026-11-08). Lucca asked for this review on 2026-11-09 ("get an agent on this"); analysis in ~/.cache/eon-agents/eon-ideas-work/gpui-critique.md (Venus read at edge 97bbd4c). Recommendation 4.

The post's lesson: when invalidation is hand-built, "a missed edge is silent". Venus's renderer skips
a rebuild when its `ContentKey` is equal (venus/src/render.rs:1820-1822), and the key holds
`generation` plus a hand-kept list of fields that "change without a new generation"
(render.rs:237-266). application.rs has 28 `presentation.invalidate()`, 6
`content_changed()`, 17 `request_redraw()` and 59 `refresh_client_view()` calls; a path that
forgets one shows a stale frame with no error. Existing tests check that the key separates
generations and viewer state (render/tests/device.rs:53-124), not that every drawn change alters it.
Planned work adds more edges (eon-venus-blink-no-rebuild-h222, eon-venus-row-text-cache-gxb4).

## Scope

Either a property test that every change to the renderer's drawn inputs (scene, snapshot fields,
dialog, chips, image bands) changes `ContentKey`, or derive the key from a hash of those inputs
instead of a hand-kept list; the bead picks one after reading render.rs. No behavior change, no
contract, no wire change. Owner: Venus. Portability: neutral.

## Acceptance

The test (or derived key) fails red when one field is dropped from the key, and passes on the
change; fmt, clippy and the whole-workspace eon-test pass.
## Current evidence and falsifier (8ebdd69)

The counts above describe 97bbd4c, not a current inventory. Production key construction is
`render.rs:1782-1819`; `render/tests/device.rs:53-125` also now checks quota-tooltip and other-column
revision changes. Reuse those tests instead of duplicating them. Changes represented by a new
generation need not add an independent key field; identify drawn changes that preserve generation
separately from those required to advance it. Do not require redraw for invisible/unconsumed data.

Exercise production key/invalidation/rebuild decisions with representative drawn-input transitions,
not only equality of manually constructed ContentKey values. A temporary omitted invalidation/key
input must make the check fail; unchanged drawn inputs must retain the cache hit. Cover both a
generation transition and a non-generation input, and preserve image/resource revision handling.
Avoid unconditional whole-frame hashing or rebuilds as an unmeasured fix: retain the existing
output/render verification route and compare the same workload if changing the key algorithm.
This one-session slice protects cache correctness; it does not implement blink/row caching or
promise exhaustive detection of all future fields. VEN-C8/VEN-C31 remain unchanged.

title: Open files in the running Helix instead of a new pane (eon edit, Files)
description:
## Why

Lucca, 2026-11-03: "eon cant open on running helix? this is a gap". `eon edit FILE` and Files' Enter (the Yazi opener calls `eon edit`) open a new editor pane even when Eon's Helix is already running in the target tab. The chosen outcome is to open the file as a buffer in that running Helix and select its pane, retaining today's new-pane path when no eligible Helix runs. The configured non-Helix editor retains its existing new-pane behavior from eon-ecupy (configured editor command, closed).

This is an epic: the existing plan at `/home/lucca/.cache/eon-agents/eon-bjov6/plan.md` estimates about 1,000 lines and separates an unproved real-Helix spike, bridge publication/registration, and reuse through edit/Files. These are provisional implementation slices until Lucca resolves the outstanding choices. This planning split approves no product behavior, contract wording or proposed implementation mechanism beyond the decision already recorded below.

## Historical mechanism decision (superseded 2026-11-10)

Lucca, 2026-11-03 (comment 5111, originating in the Helix ecosystem decision): "why not do it like nova does it in the meanwhile? to avoid depending on steel?", then "i agree. keeping it similar in eon and nova reduces maintenance costs".

Historical 2026-11-03 plan, superseded by the approved native listener below: reuse Nova's mechanism: nova-helix's existing Steel bridge (`bridge.scm`, `bridge-actions.scm`), authenticated Rust transport and registry shape, with Eon finding the Helix pane through Orbit. Keep Eon's side behind the small editor-IPC interface already approved so a later backend replacement does not spread through callers. Generate the token and register the instance like Nova, load the user's own `init.scm` last, and use the bridge already present in the pinned Helix; add no new Steel feature or nova-helix change. The code-sharing question remains with eon-7lny3 (Eon/Nova code-sharing evaluation); using Nova's mechanism does not itself approve a shared crate or a local reimplementation.

## Prerequisites and trust boundary

Build on eon-2yj90 (prevent Eon's Helix from running repository Steel without trust, closed). Preserve that launch fix throughout: enabling the packaged bridge must never load repository `.helix/*.scm`, restore implicit workspace-code loading or bypass workspace trust. The old plan's repository-Steel decision is resolved by that prerequisite, not reopened here. The evidence and line numbers in the 2026-11-03 plan are dated discovery and must be relocated against the current tree.

## Historical questions (current disposition below)

1. Approve exact EON-C10/EON-C9 amendments after reconciling the old draft with the configured editor and the closed Steel trust fix. This epic writes no contract text.
2. Choose the request owner: supervisor or CLI, including the cost of blocking the supervisor and any resulting EONW change. The old plan recommends the supervisor; that recommendation is unapproved.
3. Choose eligible Helix instances and candidate order (calling/selected/most-recent/layout order), multiple Helix panes, popup eligibility, target-tab boundaries and how focusing or background/no-focus calls compose. Preserve line/column and directory arguments on both paths.
4. Choose the configurable always-new/reuse policy, key name/default and whether a per-call flag is needed. The old plan proposes `[editor] reuse = true` and the existing `pane create -- hx FILE` escape hatch; those proposals are not decisions. Follow rule 6 and document approved defaults.
5. Choose refusal/unresponsive/transport-failure behavior, including whether an unanswered request fails or falls back and how duplicate opens are avoided. Preserve today's no-running-editor path.
6. Choose shared registry/client code versus an Eon implementation of Nova's wire/schema; record the dependency/ownership cost and the version/exit policy for anything adopted.
7. Approve or revise the S0/S1/S2 implementation split after the real-Helix spike. Creating provisional planning children does not approve their code.

## Acceptance

- Each child delivers one independently verifiable outcome; implementation starts only after S0 records Lucca's outstanding choices and relevant contract approvals.
- Through both `eon edit` and Files' Enter, an eligible running packaged Helix receives a file as a buffer and its pane is selected according to the approved focus/target rules; the new-pane and configured-non-Helix paths remain available as approved.
- Multiple editors, popup callers/eligibility, relative and line/column paths, stale registries, bridge refusal/unresponsiveness, user's init ordering, and terminal teardown follow the approved decisions and are covered by focused checks plus an isolated installed observation with real Helix.
- Rule 5 uses the same CLI path as Files and exposes the approved result as JSON. Rule 6 covers every changed value. User docs/configuration and changelog match accepted behavior.
- The closed repository-Steel trust fix stays intact. No aliases, shims or compatibility paths are introduced.

## Original children (superseded disposition below)

- S0: refresh evidence, spike the real bridge and resolve the remaining design/approval gate; no product commit.
- S1: publish/register the packaged Helix bridge, including private token/endpoint lifecycle and user's init ordering; provisional, blocked by S0.
- S2: reuse it through `eon edit` and Files, including configuration, target/focus rules, failures and installed proof; provisional, blocked by S1 and S0's approvals.

Related: eon-b3i7g (reveal the current editor file in Files, opposite direction); eon-agent-parity-a9g0.20 (open an editor without moving focus). The plan's first-selected-file versus documented multi-selection mismatch is a recorded adjacent finding, not permission to change Files' multi-selection behavior here.

## Current authoritative plan (2026-11-12)

Comment 6198 records Lucca's 2026-11-10 "cool. i agree" approving the Editor popup plan:
native nova-helix `--listen PATH`, Steel compiled out, supervisor client and Eon-owned request
format. That decision supersedes the historical Steel/token/bridge/registry/init-loading text,
old owner/shared-code questions and provisional split above; preserve those comments as history,
not implementation instructions. eon-bjov6.1 and .2 are closed as superseded, and no new bridge
spike or Steel activation is authorized here. Preserve the repository-Steel trust protection.

Only eon-bjov6.3 remains: ordinary Helix-pane reuse through the same native socket/client after
eon-xodrj.5. The 2026-11-10 overseer disposition (child comment 6303) waits for the popup to ship
before asking Lucca whether pane reuse is still wanted. Its five current decisions (need, target
ordering, eligible instances, setting, exact EON-C10 clause) replace the seven historical ones.
Do not infer those answers from the old plan. The child's no-duplicate-open/failure handling,
line/column/directory arguments, CLI/Files parity, docs/configuration, installed real-Helix proof
and approval gates remain the epic's completion criteria. No beta-gate expansion.

One existing implementation child is sufficient after the decisions; do not create replacement
children or close this epic merely because the popup may cover the need. Planning verification:
br show of this epic/.3 and graph against the existing eon-xodrj.5 prerequisite.

title: Open files in a running Helix pane through its listen socket (eon edit, Files)
description:
## Why

Lucca, 2026-11-03: "eon cant open on running helix? this is a gap". `eon edit FILE` and Files'
Enter open a new editor pane even when Eon's Helix already runs in a pane of the target tab.
Parent: eon-bjov6.

The Editor popup (eon-xodrj, in the v0.2.0 gate) closes that gap for the popup: Files' Enter and
`eon edit` open the file as a buffer in the running Editor popup. This bead is what remains: the
same for a packaged Helix that runs in an ordinary pane. It is not a gate member.

## Mechanism (changed 2026-11-10)

Lucca approved the Editor popup plan on 2026-11-10 ("cool. i agree"; option 1 of
~/.cache/eon-agents/eon-editor-plan-work/bead/report.md): a native `--listen PATH` Unix socket
in nova-helix (eon-xodrj.2, closed), Steel compiled out of Eon's Helix
(eon-xodrj.3), and the supervisor as the client (eon-xodrj.5). That replaces the Steel bridge,
token and registry this bead was written for on 2026-11-04 (parent comment 5111; previous body:
~/.cache/eon-agents/eon-prime-beads-work/bead/2026-11-10/eon-bjov6.3-desc-before.md). The plan
notes this bead "could later use the same socket for Helix panes". The siblings eon-bjov6.1
(Steel-bridge spike) and eon-bjov6.2 (publish and register the bridge) are closed as superseded.

## Decisions Lucca owns (bring them before any code)

1. Is pane reuse still wanted once the Editor popup ships, or does the popup settle the gap?
2. If wanted: which Helix receives the file when both the Editor popup and one or more Helix
   panes run in the target tab (popup first, calling or selected pane first, most recent)?
3. Whether a Helix pane started by hand (`hx` typed in a shell) is eligible, or only one Eon
   started through `eon edit`; only the second can be given `--listen` by the supervisor.
4. The setting: a third value of eon-xodrj.5's `[editor] open_in` (for example `"running"`), or
   none (rule 6).
5. The exact EON-C10 `eon edit` clause.

## Scope (after those answers)

In: the supervisor gives each packaged Helix it starts through `eon edit` a listen socket under
the window runtime directory, as eon-xodrj.4 does for the popup, and the one `eon edit` path
(Files' Enter uses it) sends `open` to the chosen live instance and selects its pane; with no
live instance it keeps today's new-pane path. A configured editor that is not the packaged Helix
keeps the new-pane path. Reuse eon-xodrj.5's client, bounds (connect 100 ms, answer 1 s) and
failure codes; add no second client.
Out: the Editor popup itself (eon-xodrj); other editors' remote protocols; revealing a file in
Files from Helix (eon-b3i7g); opening an editor without moving focus (eon-agent-parity-a9g0.20);
Files' multi-selection behaviour.

## Acceptance

- In an isolated installed Eon with the real packaged Helix: `eon edit a.txt` starts a Helix
  pane; `eon edit b.txt:12` and Files' Enter on c.txt open buffers in that pane with no new
  pane, and the pane is selected per the approved rule; after Helix exits, `eon edit` starts a
  fresh pane.
- Several Helix panes, the Editor popup also running, a background tab, relative and absolute
  paths, line and column forms and a directory argument follow Lucca's answers; Eon does not
  parse Helix path syntax beyond what eon-xodrj.5 already does.
- An unresponsive, unavailable or refusing editor fails as in eon-xodrj.5 and changes nothing: no
  duplicate open, no second instance.
- `eon edit --json` names the pane that shows FILE. docs/USAGE.md, docs/CONFIGURATION.md and
  CHANGELOG.md match; the EON-C10 clause is the approved text.

## Prerequisites

eon-xodrj.5 has landed (the listener is pinned, the client and failure codes exist). Lucca's
answers to the five decisions are recorded here.

## Verification

Focused Runtime tests with the fake listening editor from eon-xodrj.5 (several instances, stale
socket, refused, unresponsive), whole-workspace `nix develop -c eon-test`, and one isolated
installed observation as above on a `nix build --out-link` candidate. Fresh Claude and Codex
review (code and contract text).

## Stop Conditions

- Stop before code if any of the five decisions is open.
- Stop if it needs an EONW or Orbit change that eon-xodrj.5 did not already make.
- No aliases, shims or compatibility paths (no legacy code).

title: Re-prove the compositor background blur backdrop that VEN-C30 waits on
description:

One remaining contract depends on one of them: VEN-C30 (Agent sidebar) says its blur proof "waits on the native backdrop re-proof of background blur, whose open proof `eon-vn0nk` records" (venus/docs/CONTRACTS.md, VEN-C30 Status and Open proof). Nothing open tracks that re-proof.

## Scope

In scope: one installed observation of the compositor background blur behind a translucent Eon window on x86_64 Linux Wayland (COSMIC or another compositor that supports `ext-background-effect-v1`), recorded on this bead. Then update VEN-C30's blur pointer to cite this bead's observation in place of the eon-vn0nk record. The other open proofs in the eon-vn0nk record (installed chips, footer raster and AT-SPI, narrow version hiding, igae.14.2 placement) are features. (`venus/docs/CONTRACTS.md:2700-2703`), not translucency alone. Use a patterned backdrop and

title: Add a toggleable bottom shortcut hints bar
description:
## Contract

A full-Eon user can see a compact native shortcut-hints row at the bottom of the window and toggle it with physical Alt+Shift+B, like Nova. Start visible in a fresh window; retain that window's choice across tab switches, popup open/close and resize. Showing reserves one compact row; hiding returns its space to terminal content. The toggle also appears in the existing Alt+/ Shortcuts viewer so it remains discoverable when the row is hidden.

Show concise key/action pairs for real Eon workspace actions and enabled tool shortcuts, derived from the same descriptors and current popup catalog used by dispatch and the full viewer. Group shared modifiers once, following current native focus. Spread compact groups across the bar with outer groups at 12 logical-pixel side insets and equal inter-group gaps of at least 24 pixels at default typography; center a lone group. Keep 12-pixel within-group gaps. Give only each modifier header a rounded background, with 6-pixel inner side padding included in measured fitting. Keep the group bodies plain. Align the main region and footer sides using the existing pane inset (4 logical pixels at default typography). Use one continuous outer frame with the main region corner radius (12 logical pixels), a straight single-pixel separator at the join and the same bottom inset as the hidden-footer main frame (6 logical pixels at default typography). Reserve the bottom gap in addition to the compact hints row height, with a minimum row height equal to the existing corner radius; preserve hidden-footer rendering, input and pane-frame visibility. All spacing participates in whole-hint fitting. Use the inactive-tab background for the bar and the shared restrained outline, and coral red (#FF6B6B) modifier headers without braces separated from mint keys with gray labels. Omit F6, Project, Copy, Paste and Open link from compact hints while retaining their bindings and full-help entries. Compact group headers use C/A/S aliases and hyphens without braces, such as A-S; the tab range is shown as 1..9; concise labels include keys and hints. One move hint groups horizontal H/L and vertical K/J keys while full help and accessible labels retain the complete chords and distinct tab/pane actions. Creation labels retain their explicit tab, pane, or window target. Omit the header ? only when the visible bar fits every applicable hint, retaining it while keyboard-focused; retain Alt+/ and the full viewer. No minor mode exists yet; future real modes replace contents from their actual binding projection without a mode framework in this slice. Prioritize useful core actions and the hints/full-Shortcuts escape hatch; fit whole hints to the available width, dropping lower-priority entries rather than clipping a key into a misleading chord. Preserve keyboard focus, selected tab/pane, live processes and input. Normal terminal resizing is expected; a presentation toggle must not create/restart terminals or send its key bytes to them.

## Evidence and reference gate

Inspected 2026-10-11:
- Nova `38a5e29eb078e939d9729dfdbbdf3362292c20b9`: `docs/runtime-notes.md:224-259` describes Alt+Shift+B, visible-by-default startup, reclaiming the row and whole-hint fitting with workspace/action priorities. `defaults/zellij/layout.kdl:6-111` defines a one-row compact grouped-modifier display; `defaults/config.toml:41` supplies Nova's startup preference. Nova packages zjhints upstream `709d56292217920a5b7e2702302cd66b60ed6477` with `prototypes/zellij-distribution/zjhints-group-modifiers.patch` (`flake.nix:680-719`). These are comparison evidence, not an Eon dependency or copied implementation.
- Venus HEAD `14f6e7e32ff5dccf1f5f9b0b9c79faa2e11be18b` (current accepted runtime pin `58f2eaa8057627bdbf73262fdb10a1dc8b681ffc`): `src/application.rs:728` FIXED_SHORTCUTS and `shortcut_groups_for` already share native bindings with dispatch and project current popup entries; `workspace_scene:1639` and `initial_window_size:4539` feed native geometry/grid admission. `src/scene.rs:395,732` owns workspace/terminal rectangles. `src/render.rs`, `src/accessibility.rs` and `src/input.rs:402` own drawing, AccessKit and captured shortcut press/release sequences. VEN-C20/EON-C20 own the existing read-only full viewer.
- Eon Runtime `e30cf43b7ccc752d33edd4626aabbc4fd1cec579`, `crates/eon-runtime/src/managed_environment.rs:547`: popup collision validation reserves fixed workspace keys but currently does not reserve Alt+Shift+B. Reserve the chosen toggle there before delivery; do not silently steal an existing configured popup chord.
- Eon edge HEAD `d3b280870e046246f91c3c82f235c3ef9c6e90e5` has pre-existing working-tree changes. EON-C20/EON-C21 and each owner's reference routing remain the accepted baseline.

Before code, recheck exact sources, relevant native layout/input references and accepted child pins. Adopt Nova's compactness, toggle/reclaimed space and binding truth. Reject its Zellij modes, hint panes, plugin metadata and session-controller persistence: Eon has native window presentation and an existing canonical shortcut owner.

## Ownership, prerequisites and scope

Eon owns the chosen product outcome/default and exact composition. Venus owns one window-local visibility state, hint projection, responsive geometry, rendering, input precedence and accessibility. Eon Runtime keeps popup catalog validation/collision enforcement. Orbit owns terminal resizing and state; use its existing path. Existing EONW popup facts should suffice; no speculative schema or new dependency is planned.

The native viewer and Eon Bar prerequisites are accepted (`eon-deliver-native-shortcut-viewer-rif`, `eon-deliver-native-eon-bar-w4d`). This is independent of the version badge and Claude/Grok quota work; add no artificial blocking edge. Follow one active frontier, accept required owner changes, then pin accepted revisions in Eon and record the product contract before delivery.

Scope is one native, read-only bottom hints row, its toggle, the existing shortcut viewer entry, collision protection and affected geometry/grid/IME/hit/accessibility paths. Update affected documentation, changelog and LOC when implemented. Reuse current shaping and renderer; require no registry, second shortcut catalog, command polling or dependency.

No child-application key discovery, Zellij input modes, interactive hint buttons, new command palette, custom rebinding/settings UI, cross-window/session synchronization, durable visibility preference or platform expansion. Persistence beyond the current window is unspecified and requires a separate product choice.

## Acceptance and cheapest falsifiers

1. One isolated installed native x86_64 Linux Wayland workflow shows a readable single-row bar; Alt+Shift+B hides/restores it exactly once per press, captures repeats/releases, returns/reclaims the expected viewport space and retains the choice across tabs and popups. Full Shortcuts lists the toggle even when hints are hidden. The normal modal viewer's input-isolation contract remains intact.
2. Displayed hints agree with actual fixed dispatch and enabled/remapped tool entries; Project and F6 remain in full help; removed entries disappear and no child-application shortcuts are invented. A configured Alt+Shift+B popup collision fails clearly before workspace mutation. Use focused red/green checks for that boundary and shortcut capture, reusing existing harnesses rather than literal mirror tests.
3. Ordinary/narrow/tiny windows and scale changes fit whole hints, keep the top bar usable and preserve valid grid admission, terminal/popup geometry, IME placement, hit regions and accessible text. Repeated toggles preserve selected identities, focus, running processes and subsequent terminal input; normal resize is the only terminal effect.
4. Prove affected owner builds and the applicable Rust/Nix boundaries, then exact accepted manifest/lock composition. Refresh the active eon profile without restarting live supervisors and verify the installed behavior. Validate the approved Nix-free alpha artifact if its packaging changes. Record exact revisions, environment, commands/observations and proof phase; a mock or screenshot alone is insufficient.

Stop and resolve scope if sources have materially drifted or this needs a second shortcut/visibility owner, generic widget framework, new protocol contract or broader persistence. Existing live user work and desktop focus must remain intact.

title: Give a damaged session registry a CLI way out instead of blocking every new Eon window
description:
Found by the EON-C38 planning pass (eon-remote-workspaces-52i4.4; plan /home/lucca/.cache/eon-agents/eon-fable-c38-work/bead/00-plan.md section 2 item 5). One invalid file under ~/.local/state/eon/sessions (a truncated record, a record of a later format, or modes widened by a backup restore or chmod -R) refuses the whole registry: eon session new fails and no new Eon window starts for that user (runtime supervisor.rs:1073-1075, :1096-1103 at 84c20c8). Running terminals and recovery stay safe. The only fix today is editing files by hand, the same CLI-parity gap Lucca named in his PR #7 review for the checkpoint.

Change: the failure names the failing path; an explicit command (for example eon session registry repair, name chosen in the plan) moves the failing registry aside (kept, never deleted) and starts a fresh one, with the moved path printed. Rule 5: this is the CLI path. EON-C38 Boundary amendment if the behavior it states changes (overseer approves). Not a v0.2.0 gate; land before the announcement if it fits. Proof: tests for each damage kind (truncated, later format, widened modes) showing the named path, the repair result and that the old files are kept; fmt, clippy, eon-runtime suite.

## Current evidence and mandatory design gate (8ebdd69)

Current failure owners are `session_registry.rs:502-563` (whole-registry load/validation),
`:653-707` (private-file validation/read), and `supervisor.rs:1082-1117` (setup/worker submission,
fresh-start refusal; recovery remains diagnostic). `cli.rs:897` has registry read/lookup only.
Many failures already name a path via `Failure::at` (:94); retain that and cover remaining
validation branches, not only filesystem errors.

EON-C38 is explicit: `docs/CONTRACTS.md:5525` says Eon never repairs/replaces/removes failures,
and :5546 says no command repairs or sets aside an invalid registry. An amendment is therefore
required, not conditional. Lucca must approve its exact text and repair scope before code; the
overseer may relay that approval but cannot originate it. This pass proposes no contract text
and does not approve the example command name.

The plan must settle how an explicit move-aside operation serializes with all readers/writers
holding the stable registry lock: renaming a directory must not create two concurrently writable
registry/lock owners. Define live/recovered-session persistent-ID consequences and prevent any
old ID being silently retargeted. Preserve every original byte, private ownership/modes, and
reject unsafe/symlink/racing paths. If safe repair cannot be bounded to this slice, stop for a
separate approved design instead of weakening registry validation.

After approval, acceptance also covers concurrent/busy repair and rename/create, failed move or
fresh-registry creation with no data loss, unchanged running terminals/recovery, machine-readable
result/failure and documented CLI/help/config implications. Exercise the three original damage
kinds plus these safety failures in private roots. Follow full affected lifecycle/trust Rust/Nix
proof, whole-workspace eon-test before converge, and isolated installed CLI observation. No live
user registry is ever a test fixture, and no supervisor restart is authorized by this bead.

title: Find refactor candidates: long files and tangled modules
description:
## Why

Lucca, 2026-10-28: "create a bead to check long files or files that we should refactor in general,
so we can find candidates". Several files have grown large enough to slow review and agent work
(context cost, merge collisions between parallel slices). Line counts at 7888609, tracked sources:

    8514 venus/src/application.rs
    7048 venus/src/render.rs
    6685 venus/src/scene.rs
    6638 eon/crates/eon/tests/workspace_control.rs
    5930 runtime/crates/eon-runtime/src/workspace.rs
    3982 runtime/crates/eon-workspace-protocol/src/v23.rs
    3846 venus/src/accessibility.rs
    3478 runtime/crates/eon-runtime/src/supervisor.rs
    2815 runtime/crates/eon-runtime/src/sessions.rs
    2771 venus/src/render/chrome.rs
    2202 runtime/crates/eon-runtime/src/managed_environment.rs
    2186 orbit/tests/lifecycle.rs

(orbit/proof/{view,lease,step}.bend are 60-74k lines; check whether they are generated before
treating them as candidates.)

## Contract

None. An audit that produces candidates; it changes no code and no contract.

## Change

Survey the workspace (Rust, Nix, Bend, shell, mac-proof tooling) and rank refactor candidates.
Length is one signal, not the criterion. Also look for: modules with more than one owner of a
behaviour or data structure (AGENTS.md "one owner"), duplicated logic across crates, long
functions, test files that mix unrelated suites, files most often touched by parallel slices
(`git log --name-only` churn and co-change), and dead code. For each candidate record: file and
size, the problem in one line, the proposed split or simplification, the owner boundary it keeps,
risk (wire/protocol, lifecycle, proof checks it would touch), and rough cost.

## Acceptance

- A ranked candidate list in a comment on this bead, with the evidence above for each.
- One child bead per candidate Lucca picks (each small, per the small-beads rule), not before.
- Generated or proof-owned files are identified and excluded, with the reason.

## Scope

Read-only investigation; delegate the reading to subagents. No refactors in this bead. Not on the
macOS launch path (eon-mac-launch-kz4p); do not schedule it ahead of that work.
close_reason: Audit done (ranked list and picks in comments); children .1-.3 and .5 closed; bqxy.4 detached as standalone work (batch close approved by Lucca 2026-10-31 'i agree')

comments.author: lucca
comments.text: Approval, relayed by eon-overseer (2026-10-29): Lucca, 2026-10-28: "create a bead to check long files or files that we should refactor in general, so we can find candidates"; Lucca, 2026-10-29: "we need to do more eon stuff / can we fire more agents?", choosing this bead. Roles (Lucca, 2026-10-28, relayed): Opus plans and gates, Codex does the reading; read-only, no child beads until Lucca picks.

comments.author: lucca
comments.text: Lucca, 2026-10-29, agreeing with the recommendation: pick candidates 1, 2, 3, 5 and 10 (relayed by eon-overseer). Picking the Venus items approves their test modules (venus/AGENTS.md).

comments.author: lucca
comments.text:
Ranked refactor candidates at 0b6ef93 (survey: Codex gpt-6.1-sol xhigh, read-only; gate: Opus spot-checked the top items against the code). Full Codex report, with raw tables: /home/lucca/.cache/eon-agents/claude-refactor-audit-work/report-survey.md.

## Main finding

Most of the size in the largest files is inline `#[cfg(test)] mod tests`. Six files hold about 22,900 test lines, and they are also the highest-churn implementation files in the last 300 commits (2026-10-21..29). The cheapest large win is to move those tests out as pure moves, with no product code changed. Production-code splits come second and are smaller.

Gate corrections to the survey:
- Contract path links. Splitting a test file whose path a contract cites means editing contract text, which needs your approval plus a Codex pass. Path links: `orbit/tests/lifecycle.rs` 36x in orbit/docs/CONTRACTS.md (plus BEHAVIOR, DEVELOPMENT, LIFECYCLE); `runtime/.../workspace.rs` 4x, `workspace_control.rs` 2x and `accessibility.rs` 2x in docs/CONTRACTS.md. `venus/src/render.rs`, `application.rs` and `scene.rs` have none. Docs cite tests by bare function name, and a move keeps those names.
- Dropped the survey's note that source moves "affect assembly identity" (eon/crates/eon/build.rs). Every commit changes that digest, so a move costs nothing extra there.
- venus/AGENTS.md says "A new Venus module is product scope." A new test module counts, so picking a Venus item below is your approval for its new modules.
- Each item is a code change, so it goes through the Codex-on-every-change loop. Cost: S = under a session, M = one session, L = several.

## Candidates (pick by number)

1. **Split `venus/src/render.rs` tests.** 7,105 lines; 4,056 are tests (from :3050, 30 tests); 36 commits; co-changes with chrome.rs 26x. Problem: padding, outlines, clipping, opacity, GPU-failure and shaping suites all share one module next to the renderer. Split: `#[cfg(test)] mod tests;` -> `render/tests/{mod(support),padding,outlines,text_clip,device,shaping}.rs`, moving the existing helpers (`padding_scene`, `painted_rects`, `clipping_test_fonts`) into the support module. Owner kept: Venus renderer, unchanged. Risk: none (pure move, no contract path links); keep GPU/native gates. Cost: M. **Recommend: yes, first.** Best ratio of benefit to risk.

2. **Split `venus/src/application.rs` tests.** 8,514 lines; 3,210 are tests (from :5305, 44 tests); 42 commits. Problem: a 1,129-line native probe test (:5812) and the unrelated retry, selection, workspace, shortcut and zoom suites make every event-loop change load ~3k extra lines. Split: `application/tests/{mod,native,retry,selection,workspace,shortcuts}.rs`, beside the existing `application/{geometry,scroll,shortcuts}.rs`. Owner kept: Venus native event handling. Risk: none from the move; keep the ignored/isolated-display attributes and the documented test filters. Cost: M. **Recommend: yes.**

3. **Split `venus/src/scene.rs` tests.** 6,685 lines; 2,830 are tests (from :3856, 23 tests); 43 commits, the highest churn of any implementation file; co-changes with chrome.rs 32x and accessibility.rs 31x. Split: `scene/tests/{mod,workspace,sidebar,bar,links,terminal}.rs`. Owner kept: Venus scene composition. Risk: none; keep the geometry and hit-target assertions. Cost: M. **Recommend: yes.** Leave the 644-line `WorkspaceScene::from_snapshot_with_zoom` (:2103) for later; splitting it needs its own read.

4. **Split `eon/crates/eon/tests/workspace_control.rs`.** 6,638 lines, 49 tests; 38 commits; co-changes with supervisor.rs 24x, sessions.rs 20x, cli.rs 19x. Problem: configuration/help, startup, directory picker, targeting, eonbase, recovery and generations suites, with ~700 lines of inline process/mock/managed-Orbit scaffolding (:39-133, :609-735). Split: one test target, with `workspace_control/{support,configuration,picker,workspace,recovery,generations}.rs`, reusing `tests/process/mod.rs`. Trap: the managed-Orbit helper re-execs the test binary as `--exact managed_orbit_helper` (:679, :722). Keep that test at the crate root, or change the filter to its new module path. Owner kept: Eon composed-product proof. Risk: test discovery and subprocess cleanup; 2 path links in docs/CONTRACTS.md and 1 in docs/DEVELOPMENT.md need updating (contract text edit). Cost: M. **Recommend: yes.** It is the file most often touched alongside runtime slices.

5. **Move Runtime's CLI output projection into `workspace/output.rs`.** In `runtime/crates/eon-runtime/src/workspace.rs` (5,930 lines; 17 commits), :2163-2600 holds `human`, `json`, `list_*`, `failure_*`, attention and shortcut formatting, and `json_escape`. `json_escape` is also used by cli.rs, generation.rs and windows.rs, so it does not belong inside workspace state. Split: a pure move into a private `workspace/output.rs` (or a crate-level `output.rs` for `json_escape`) plus its tests (:3703). Owner kept: Runtime owns both state and its CLI projection; output only reads snapshots. Risk: none; keep the exact CLI bytes. Cost: S. **Recommend: yes. Cheap, and it makes item 6 smaller.**

6. **Split Runtime `workspace.rs` tests.** 3,328 test lines (from :2603, 37 tests): replay/targeting, set capacity, topology, popups/pickers, directory changes, output. Split: `workspace/tests/{mod,set,topology,popups,replay}.rs`, sharing `catalog`, `prepared`, `two_workspace_set`. Owner kept: Runtime workspace state. Risk: none to logic; 4 path links in docs/CONTRACTS.md (contract text edit). Cost: M. **Recommend: yes, after 5 (same file).**

7. **Split `venus/src/accessibility.rs` tests.** 3,846 lines; 2,873 are tests (from :974, 23 tests); 33 commits; co-changes with scene.rs 31x. Split: `accessibility/tests/{mod,bar,terminal,workspace,dialogs}.rs`. Owner kept: Venus accessibility projection. Risk: none to logic; 2 path links in docs/CONTRACTS.md. Cost: M. **Recommend: yes, lower priority than 1-4.**

8. **Extract the supervisor's presentation process.** `runtime/.../supervisor.rs`, 3,478 lines; 37 commits. `venus_command` (:389) and `PresentationProcess` with its `Drop` (:482-657) sit between config/runtime-dir helpers and the 297-line `supervise` loop (:745) and the 330-line `dispatch_control_request` (:1744). Split: `supervisor/presentation.rs` with those items and their command tests. Owner kept: Runtime owns the presentation lifecycle; `SupervisorState` stays put. Risk: lifecycle-adjacent (spawn, control-channel close, wait, cleanup must move together); no wire change. Cost: M. **Recommend: yes, but after 1-6. It is the top production split and needs a careful review.**

9. **Isolate managed-Orbit acquisition in `runtime/.../sessions.rs`.** 2,815 lines; 32 commits; co-changes with supervisor.rs 22x. Record reading (:222), identity/peer validation (:312, :451) and `acquire_management` (:466) are separable from launch/recovery orchestration (:637). Split: `sessions/management.rs`. Owner kept: Runtime manages Orbit through the management protocol. Risk: **security and lifecycle boundary** (no-follow opens, peer credentials, process-start checks, deadlines). Cost: M. **Recommend: later.** The value is real, but take it only when someone is already working in sessions.rs.

10. **Move the managed-shell checks out of `flake.nix`.** 1,113 lines; 17 commits. `managedCommandPathCheck` and `fakeMise` (:888-1086) interrupt the composition graph. Split: `nix/managed-command-checks.nix`, following the existing `orbitChecks` import (:341). Owner kept: Nix composition. Risk: none, if check names stay identical (verify with `nix flake show` before and after). Cost: S. **Recommend: yes, as a quick win.**

11. **Move link handling out of `impl Application`.** `impl Application` is 2,956 lines (:732). The hyperlink block (:2853-3105: `link_scene` through `handle_link_button`, ~250 lines) is cohesive. Split: `application/links.rs`, the same pattern as `scroll.rs` and `shortcuts.rs`. Owner kept: Venus local link focus. Risk: none (pure move). Cost: S. **Recommend: optional; pair it with item 2 if that slice has room.** (Gate addition: the survey proposed no production split of application.rs.)

## Considered and not recommended now

- 12. `runtime/crates/eon-workspace-protocol/src/v23.rs` tests (1,611 lines): only 1 commit in the window, so it causes little collision. Skip. (Correction: v23.rs is the live, hand-edited EONW codec, not frozen history; EON-C28 retention starts at 1.0.)
- 13. `orbit/tests/lifecycle.rs` (2,186): 2 commits, and 36 contract path links. A split means a large ORB-C text edit for little gain. Skip.
- 14. `eon/tools/mac-proof/src/scenario.rs` (2,009): defer behind eon-mac-launch-kz4p, as the bead's scope says.
- 15. `orbit/tools/step-proof.rs` repeats the boundary.schema fact list (:50) and enum table (:244) instead of reusing tools/boundary.rs's parser (:74). This is a real duplicate owner of structure, but a schema change without a table update should fail the proof check rather than drift silently, the fix touches proof generation, and the generator changed only 3 times. Cost: L. Skip unless the schema starts changing often.
- Dead code: none found that can be deleted with confidence. The only suppression is `venus/src/application.rs:651` `expect(dead_code)` on macOS for `application_id`, a recorded native-host gap.
- Duplication checked and left alone: Venus selected/background transport retry already shares `apply_retryable_loss`; Runtime attention rollup vs the EONW check is author vs trust-boundary validation; the nine-line decoder `finish` helpers are too small to share.

## Excluded (generated or proof-owned)

- `orbit/proof/view.bend` (75,638), `lease.bend` (69,076), `step.bend` (61,840): generated by `orbit/tools/step-proof.rs` (header line 15; writer :1228). They are 61.5% of all source lines.
- `orbit/src/boundary.rs` (752), `orbit/src/boundary.bend` (1,212): generated from `boundary.schema` by `orbit/tools/boundary.rs` (:823-824).
- `orbit/LAWS.bend` (1,812), `orbit/PROOF.bend` (980): hand-written but proof-owned; you own the laws (orbit/AGENTS.md).
- `Cargo.lock`, `installer/`, `launcher/`, `relink/` `Cargo.lock`, `flake.lock`: lock data.
- `AGENTS.md`, `orbit|venus|runtime/AGENTS.md`, `docs/AGENT-PROTOCOLS.md`: rendered from Starcompass.
- `.beads/`: br-owned.

## Recommendation

Take 1, 2, 3, 5 and 10 first. They are pure moves with no contract text, and they cut the Venus files that most often collide between parallel slices (scene/chrome/application/render). They touch different files, so they can run as parallel beads. Then take 4 and 6 (each edits contract path links), then 8. Leave 9 and 11-15 unless work already passes through them.

title: Move render.rs's tests into render/tests
description:

and ~/.cache/eon-agents/claude-refactor-audit-work/report-survey.md). Lucca, 2026-10-29, picked

tests): padding, outlines, clipping, opacity, GPU-failure and shaping suites in one module next to
the renderer.

## Contract
None changed: a pure move, no behaviour change. Picking this approves the new Venus test modules
(venus/AGENTS.md).

## Change
Replace the inline tests with `#[cfg(test)] mod tests;` and move them to
`venus/src/render/tests/{mod (shared support), padding, outlines, text_clip, device, shaping}.rs`,
moving the existing helpers (`padding_scene`, `painted_rects`, `clipping_test_fonts`) into the
support module. Keep every GPU and native gate (`cfg`, `ignore`) on the test it guards. The
existing import `use super::cells::tests::plain_style` (render.rs:3051) moves with the tests.

## Acceptance
- No behaviour change: the same test functions, same count, same `cfg`/`ignore` attributes (compare
  `cargo test -p yazelix-venus -- --list` and `-- --list --ignored` before and after; only the
  module path prefix may change), and the crate suite passes: `nix develop -c eon-test -p
  yazelix-venus`.
- Venus `cargo fmt --check` and `cargo clippy --locked --all-targets -- -D warnings` clean, plus
  aarch64-apple-darwin clippy (recipe on eon-mac-launch-kz4p.1), since Venus carries macOS code.
- No doc or contract citation goes stale. At filing, no doc or contract cites venus/src/render.rs
  by path, and docs cite tests by bare name, which a move keeps. If a citation would go stale, stop:
  editing a contract record needs Lucca's approval and a Codex round (AGENTS.md).

## Verification
Pure-refactor route: the crate suite, fmt and clippy above on the exact committed tree, and the
Codex-on-every-code-change loop (AGENTS.md). No runtime profile refresh: no product behaviour
changes.

## Scope
venus/src/render.rs and the new render/tests/ only. Read venus/AGENTS.md first. Approval: Lucca,
2026-10-29, "i agree with the recommended" (relayed by eon-overseer). Other refactor slices may run
in parallel on other files; whoever lands second rebases.
close_reason: Moved as a pure move (30 tests, 6 helpers into venus/src/render/tests/); Venus suite, fmt, Linux and darwin clippy pass; Opus gate and Codex review clean.

comments.author: lucca
comments.text:
## Plan (Opus, 2026-10-29, at 0842ddc)

Approval: Lucca, 2026-10-29, to eon-overseer: "we need to do more eon stuff / can we fire more agents?", then chose this bead from the overseer's list (relayed by eon-overseer, 2026-10-29). Roles: Opus plans and gates, Codex implements.

Evidence at 0842ddc: venus/src/render.rs is 7,105 lines; `#[cfg(test)] mod tests` runs from :3049 to EOF with 30 `#[test]` functions and six helpers. The module carries no `cfg`, `ignore`, `cfg_attr` or `should_panic` attribute on any test, so nothing gates them per platform. No doc or contract outside .beads cites venus/src/render.rs or `render::tests` by path. Not consequential (AGENTS.md): no dependency, protocol, contract or boundary change; no reference gate.

Approach: replace :3049-7105 with `#[cfg(test)]\nmod tests;` and move the bodies verbatim (dedented one level, then `cargo fmt`) into:
- `render/tests/mod.rs`: the module's imports (`super::cells::tests::plain_style`, `super::*`, `crate::{DrawCell, DrawCursor, DrawRow, SceneGraphics}`, `orbit_protocol::{CellWidth, CursorShape, Screen}`, trimmed to what the support code uses), the child `mod` lines, and every helper: `painted_rects`, `padding_scene`, `padding_pixel`, `clipping_test_fonts`, `retained_frame_text_clip`, `fractional_card_workspace`.
- `padding.rs`: the five `padding_color_*` tests.
- `device.rs`: `device_loss_blocks_surface_recovery_but_destroy_does_not`, `uncaptured_errors_remain_fatal_until_device_loss`, `content_cache_separates_generations_and_viewer_state`, `background_opacity_selects_only_proved_surface_modes`, `background_opacity_premultiplies_clear_colors` (renderer state: device loss, error fatality, content cache key, surface alpha mode and clear colour).
- `outlines.rs`: `tail_cursor_outlines_one_color_and_resets_when_hidden_or_blinking_off`, `trail_quad_is_two_clipped_finite_triangles_in_stable_order`, `rounded_outline_keeps_corners_and_interior_clear_when_clipped`, `selected_pane_outline_uses_scaled_widths_without_overlap_or_gaps`, `retained_resize_keeps_strokes_clear_of_displayed_rows`, `shared_bottom_preserves_grid_and_bounds_short_scene_paint`, `title_rules_leave_label_and_scrollback_gaps_inside_the_fixed_card`, `rectangle_encoding_is_row_major_and_bounded`, `column_backgrounds_cover_the_gaps_between_cards`, `frame_fills_everything_outside_the_cards`, `terminal_paint_stays_inside_rounded_fill_during_cursor_handoff`, `card_backdrop_keeps_cards_like_the_agent_sidebar_at_terminal_opacity`.
- `text_clip.rs`: `bounded_preview_rows_cover_multi_row_fractional_offsets`, `retained_frame_text_preserves_padding_after_resize`, `retained_frame_text_does_not_paint_in_an_empty_padded_interior`, `fractional_text_bounds_admit_only_pixel_centers_inside_the_clip`, `fractional_card_text_has_no_exterior_ink_with_hints_and_header_scroll`, `fractional_card_text_survives_glyphon_preparation_with_hints_and_header_scroll`.
- `shaping.rs`: `shaped_preedit_follows_emitted_glyphs_without_charging_combining_marks`, `ascii_uses_basic_shaping_without_weakening_unicode`.
Child files start with `use super::*;` plus only the imports they need. Comments above a test move with it. No test body, assertion or helper body changes; no visibility change outside the tests tree (`VERTICES_PER_QUAD` keeps its `#[cfg(test)]` in render.rs).

Red check: none possible for a pure move (no behaviour). The falsifier is the test inventory: `cargo test -p yazelix-venus -- --list` and `-- --list --ignored` before and after must match once the `render::tests::` prefix gains the child module name, and a line-multiset comparison of the old module body against the new files must differ only in `mod`/`use` lines and rustfmt reflow.

Then the Codex review loop (AGENTS.md). No profile refresh, no dogfood: no installed behaviour changes.

CLI output projection (`human` :3288, `json` :3484, `list_*`, `failure_*`, attention and shortcut
formatting, `json_escape` :3991 at 8ebdd69). `json_escape` (and `failure_json`) are also used by
cli.rs, cli/events.rs, control.rs, generation.rs and windows.rs, so they do not belong inside workspace state.

## Contract
None changed: a pure move, no behaviour change; the exact CLI bytes stay the same.

## Change
Pure move of the output projection, `json_escape`, and the output projection's own tests (the
output-only tests near :5742-6070, such as `json_paths_are_strings_unless_their_bytes_are_not_utf8` and
`cli_json_carries_the_full_attention_record_and_quotas_but_human_output_does_not`) into
`runtime/crates/eon-runtime/src/workspace/output.rs` (or a crate-level module for `json_escape` if
that reads better; one owner), updating the callers' imports.

Keep in workspace.rs every test that a contract cites by that path: docs/CONTRACTS.md (EON-C31,
EON-C33) cites `workspace_requests_keep_order_projection_names_and_bounds`,
`workspace_replay_windows_are_bounded_and_inspections_do_not_evict_mutations`,
`workspace_set_refuses_foreign_targets`, `only_a_queue_jump_crosses_workspaces_and_it_shows_its_target`
and `attention_focus_hides_keep_alive_popups_and_never_stops_a_transient_one` as "in
runtime/crates/eon-runtime/src/workspace.rs".

## Acceptance
- No behaviour change: the same test functions and count (compare `nix develop -c eon-test list -p eon-runtime` before and after; only the module path prefix of the moved tests may change), and the
  suites pass: `nix develop -c eon-test -p eon-runtime -p eon`.

  eon-runtime.

  state) gains the new file if the output module lives under workspace/.

## Verification
Pure-refactor route: the checks above on the exact committed tree, and the Codex-on-every-code-change
loop (AGENTS.md). No runtime profile refresh: no product behaviour changes.

## Scope
runtime/crates/eon-runtime only (plus the ARCHITECTURE.md line above). Approval: Lucca, 2026-10-29,

dependency and recheck current live workspace.rs editors before moving projection. Other refactor slices touch other files and may run in parallel.

At 8ebdd69 `only_a_queue_jump_crosses_workspaces_and_it_shows_its_target` is absent from

title: Add a GitHub bug report form before the public beta post
description:
## Why

Lucca plans a public-beta post to bring in users who run Eon and file bugs (Lucca, 2026-10-23: "1 public beta is good / 2 i will decide when to post / 3 file the bead"). The repository has no issue templates: `.github/` holds only `FUNDING.yml` and `workflows`, and the README's "Report a problem" link opens the issue list with no form. A bare issue rarely says which Eon build, compositor or steps hit the bug, so each report costs a round trip before anyone can act on it.

## Scope

In scope:
- `.github/ISSUE_TEMPLATE/bug_report.yml`: a GitHub issue form that asks for the Eon version (the `eon versions` output, which names every component), the install route (Nix profile, flake input or other), the distribution and compositor, the steps to reproduce, the expected and actual results, and optional logs or a screenshot. Mark the version, compositor and steps fields required.
- `.github/ISSUE_TEMPLATE/config.yml`: keep blank issues enabled, so the README's Apple Silicon tester link and other free-form reports still work.
- Point the README's "Report a problem" link at the bug form (`issues/new?template=bug_report.yml`).

Out of scope:
- The announcement itself (Lucca writes and posts it).
- A feature-request form, label automation and CI.
- Any diagnostics command in `eon`.

## Acceptance

- On github.com, New issue offers the bug form with every field above. Check the rendered form; a test submission is not needed.
- The form's version instruction matches the real CLI.

## Verification

Planning and docs route: the diff, plus one observation of the form on github.com after the push to edge. No runtime profile refresh.

title: eon pane send refuses while a person is typing in the target pane
description:
## Why

Lucca, 2026-11-04, approved ("agree") after the overseer's `eon pane send`
into the eon-61efs pane agent's pane landed in the middle of a reply he was
typing there, and was spliced into his prompt line (screenshot in that
session). The same happened on 2026-11-02 with Codex reporting into Claude's
pane. The current workaround (agents write to INBOX/STATUS files instead of
pane send) depends on every agent remembering it. Eon itself should not let
an agent type into an input a person is using (rule 8, happy users).

## Evidence

- Venus sends a person's keys straight to the terminal's Orbit host
  (venus/src/transport.rs input path); neither Venus, the runtime nor Orbit
  records when a person last typed in a terminal (no such field found).
- `eon pane send` is EON-C36 ("Sending input to a terminal from the CLI",
  docs/CONTRACTS.md:3696).

## Scope

1. Spike (first, small): find where "a person typed in terminal T at time X"
   can be known without a new wire message, if possible. Orbit sees both the
   attached client's input and the CLI's input, so it is the likely owner; the
   alternative is Venus reporting it to the supervisor. Record the mechanism,
   the owners it touches, and whether an ORB/EONW wire change is needed,
   before building. Stop for approval if a wire change or new contract is
   needed.
2. Build: `eon pane send` (and any other EON-C36 input path) refuses with a
   distinct status and message, e.g. `busy: a person typed in this pane in the
   last 2 s`, when a person typed in the target within the window; `--force`
   sends anyway. The window is configuration (default 2 s, documented in
   docs/CONFIGURATION.md, rule 6). Agents retry; the refusal is data in
   `--json`.

Out of scope: an agent-to-agent message channel (`eon message send`, an inbox
on the EON-C39 stream); possible later bead.

## Acceptance

- With a person typing (a real key into the pane via Venus in an isolated
  window), `eon pane send` exits with the busy status and sends nothing;
  after the window it sends; `--force` sends at once.
- Typing by the CLI itself never counts as a person typing.
- EON-C36 amended (text approved before building), `docs/USAGE.md` and
  `docs/CONFIGURATION.md` updated, CHANGELOG line.

## Verification

Spike: a written finding on the bead. Build: the affected Rust suites via
`nix develop -c eon-test`, fmt/clippy for touched Orbit/Venus crates, the
default Nix check, one isolated installed dogfood (typing in a pane while an
agent pane-sends to it), converge with Codex.


## Current plan and approval state

The spike above is complete (finding and approval in the 2026-11-04 comments). This bead is the acceptance container. eon-buys1.1 (Orbit quiet-window refusal, management v6) owns the active first slice and its scope is unchanged; eon-buys1.2 (CLI busy refusal, EONW v32) follows it. The existing dependency between children is the required order.

Lucca approved both wire bumps with "approve" (relayed by eon-overseer, 2026-11-04). The recorded smaller choices remain exit 5 for a refused paste, exit 1 with enter:false for Enter refused after a successful paste, `[agents] send_typing_quiet_ms = 2000` (0 disables, max 60000), and Rust-host enforcement. Exact contract wording still follows each child's approval requirement. No aliases, shims or compatibility paths are added (Lucca: "we dont want legacy code, brother").

The epic closes after both child outcomes and all original end-to-end acceptance are proved, including a real Venus key in an isolated window. Refreshing a profile never authorizes ending an old live window.
close_reason: Both children landed: Orbit management v6 (eon-buys1.1) and EONW v32 pane-send refusal (eon-buys1.2)
