title: Carry resolved shortcut bindings over EONW and dispatch Venus's fixed shortcuts from them
description:
## Why

The approved `[keys]` design (parent epic, Lucca 2026-10-23) has Eon Runtime resolve the keymap
and Venus dispatch from the result. Today Venus matches against its own `FIXED_SHORTCUTS` and only
popup keys come over EONW. This child moves the resolved bindings onto EONW and makes Venus
dispatch from them, still with default chords only, so that the sibling `[keys]` child adds only
parsing and resolution. It is split from that child so each fits one session.

## Evidence

- `venus/src/application.rs:3486-3530` (dispatch chain) and `:2087-2275` (workspace keys:
  Alt+digits, popup keys, fixed actions, focus-only keys).
- `venus/src/application/shortcuts.rs:826-838`: popup keys matched from `Snapshot.entries`.
- `runtime/crates/eon-workspace-protocol/src/v40.rs:425` (Shortcut), :503 (PopupEntry),
  :671 (Snapshot) at 8ebdd69; v19 is removed.
- EON-C20 (`docs/CONTRACTS.md:1689`): its boundary excludes "a second shortcut catalog" and an
  EONW change (`:1720`). VEN-C20 (`venus/docs/CONTRACTS.md:1125`).

## Scope

In scope:
- A new EONW version whose snapshot carries, per action, zero or more resolved chords and, for a default that lost its chord, the action or popup that took it (everything the `[keys]` child .12 needs, so .12 makes no EONW change), built from the
  shared key table of the sibling child. Follow the EONW codec rules: never amend a version in
  place.
- Runtime fills it from the defaults.
- Venus dispatches fixed actions from it.
- Build on the latest landed codec; .1's optional popup shortcut already shipped. Choose the
  next free version at implementation time, not the historical v19/v21/v23.
- EON-C20 and VEN-C20 boundary text, after Lucca approves the wording.

Out of scope:
- Parsing `[keys]`.
- Any user-visible key change.
- Non-rebindable keys (F6, Escape, Tab, Enter/Space, close-prompt keys, mouse), which stay in
  Venus.

## Acceptance

- Every fixed shortcut behaves as before.
- Venus matches fixed actions only from the bindings that EONW delivers.
- Standalone Venus (one Orbit session) still uses the shared table's defaults.

## Reference gate (consequential: wire format and contract)

Before code, record on this bead: the one owner of each behavior (Runtime resolves bindings, Venus dispatches), the `docs/REFERENCES.md` route "How should shared popups extend the workspace wire contract without breaking the installed client?", the comparable keymaps in the `eon-configurability-audit-twdr` audit (herdr `143bf5fd`, WezTerm `e2a98e1b`, whose one defaults table also drives its command palette), and the decision and its check.

## Portability

Neutral: key matching stays in the shared Venus path; native key capture at the host boundary is unchanged.

## Verification

- The full affected Rust and Nix surfaces (a shared wire-protocol change, per the AGENTS.md
  Verification table).
- One isolated installed dogfood check that the shortcuts are unchanged.
- Codex review.

## Stop Conditions

- Coordinate EONW writers and rebase onto the latest landed version before selecting the next
  free codec; never amend a landed codec or combine independent unverified changes just to save a version.

## Existing fold-in (comment 5816)

The overseer's 2026-11-07 eon-e3a1z.4 decision requires PopupEntry.custom: bool, set by Runtime for entries outside the built-in catalog. Venus shows a Custom Shortcuts section only when configured custom popups exist. Cover codec round-trip/validation, Runtime population and viewer grouping; retain current grouping until that lands. This is the recorded agreed feature, not new scope; exact contract wording still needs approval. No [keys] parsing here.

title: List the effective keymap with eon keys --json
description:
## Why

The Humans and Agents rule (AGENTS.md) says that everything a person can see about the workspace,
an agent can read from the CLI as data. Today `eon session --json` lists only popup keybindings,
so an agent can't learn which key does what or tell a person which key to press. Approved
2026-10-23 (parent epic).

## Scope

In scope:
- `eon keys [--json]`, initially from shared defaults plus resolved popup bindings (.2),
  per overseer decision 6306; .12 later adds user resolution: action ID,
  label, chords, whether it is a default, user-set, or overridden by another action, plus
  reserved chords and popup entries.
- `docs/USAGE.md`.

Out of scope:
- Changing bindings from the CLI.
- Live reload.

## Acceptance

- `eon keys --json` inside an Eon terminal matches what Alt+/ shows for that window, field for
  field.

## Verification

- A focused CLI test.
- One installed check that compares the output with Alt+/.
- Codex review.

## Maintenance Notes

- EON-C10 needs the new CLI/JSON clause approved before code. Coordinate the eventual
  EON-C28 JSON fixture with eon-igae.11.5; 1.0 is adjourned, not a deadline.

## Sequencing acceptance

Ship after .2 exposes descriptors to Runtime, without waiting on .12 or adding another catalog. Output matches Alt+/ for this window, including popup overrides, reserved chords and platform applicability. .12 then owns extending the same output to user-set/unbound/overridden bindings. Preserve the complete final feature and current desktop focus; update CLI help/USAGE and test real CLI projection/errors.

title: Let users set the 16 terminal colors with [terminal] palette
description:
## Why

Eon has no theme. The 16 ANSI colors are one hardcoded string, and users can't change them,
although Orbit already accepts any 16 colors. Approved as "configurable now" on 2026-10-23
(parent epic).

## Evidence

- `eon/crates/eon/src/product.rs:196`: `ansi_palette` default string.
- `runtime/crates/eon-runtime/src/sessions.rs:2129`: the palette is passed to every Orbit as
  `--ansi-palette-v1`.
- ORB-C2 (`orbit/docs/CONTRACTS.md`): Orbit accepts any 16 colors.
- EON-C19 (`docs/CONTRACTS.md`, EON-C19): terminal configuration.

## Scope

In scope:
- `[terminal] palette`, an array of exactly 16 `"#RRGGBB"` strings. Omitting it keeps today's
  default.
- Runtime parsing and validation.
- `docs/CONFIGURATION.md`.
- EON-C19 text: stop for Lucca's approval of the wording.

Out of scope:
- Default foreground, background and cursor colors, which need a new Orbit input (deferred
  chrome-theme bead).
- Venus chrome colors.
- Named themes.

## Acceptance

- A fresh terminal shows the configured colors.
- A malformed palette (wrong count or bad hex) fails the launch with a message naming the key.

## Verification

- A focused Runtime parse test.
- One isolated installed observation (for example, `printf` the 16 colors).
- Codex review.

## Current owner and acceptance

At 8ebdd69 TerminalSettings (`managed_environment.rs:684`) has no palette field; sessions.rs uses inputs.defaults.ansi_palette. Malformed count/hex must fail before children, preserving existing terminals. Keep the acceptance-field requirement for TOML/JSON printed defaults and a configuration-corpus fixture, and one product default so future theme work moves it. Comment 5178's contract wording is a draft awaiting approval, not authorization to edit EON-C19.

title: Let users turn the cursor trail off
description:
## Why

The cursor trail can't be turned off. Venus supports no trail, but Eon never asks for it. Motion
that can't be disabled is an accessibility gap. Approved on 2026-10-23 (parent epic).

## Evidence

- `venus/src/launch.rs:148-155`, `:234`: `--cursor-effect-v1 none|tail` is accepted.
- `runtime/crates/eon-runtime/src/supervisor.rs:413-426`: the supervisor never passes it.
- `docs/CONFIGURATION.md` `[terminal]`: `cursor_trail_color` and `cursor_trail_duration` exist,
  but there is no off switch.
- EON-C19 and VEN-C1.

## Scope

In scope (shape refined by the 2026-11-02 Codex brief):
- `[terminal] cursor_trail_duration = 0` (or `0.0`) disables motion while retaining the cursor
  colour and contrasting edge. The default stays `1.5`; existing finite `0.25..4.0` values keep
  their meaning. Forward zero through the existing duration argument to Venus for both products.
- Keep the existing colour setting and endpoint colour selection. Do not use the `none` profile,
  which changes the cursor fallback colour, or add another setting for the same value.
- `docs/CONFIGURATION.md`, `venus/docs/LAUNCH.md`, an Unreleased changelog entry and EON-C19 and VEN-C1 text.
  Lucca's session approval of the required contract/config text is recorded below.

Out of scope:
- A wider reduce-motion setting (deferred bead).

## Acceptance

- With `cursor_trail_duration = 0`, a fresh or reopened window draws the same cursor with no trail.
- The default is unchanged.

## Verification

- A focused Runtime test that the argument is passed.
- One isolated installed observation.
- Codex review.

title: Make copy on select and wheel scroll rows configurable
description:
## Why

Two selection and scroll behaviors are fixed, though users of other terminals differ on both.
Approved on 2026-10-23 (parent epic).

- **Copy on select.** Releasing a selection always writes both the clipboard and the primary
  selection.
- **Wheel scroll.** It is 3 rows per notch, written as a literal in three places.

## Evidence

- Copy on select:
  - `orbit/src/host.rs:1277`: the Orbit effect.
  - `venus/src/application.rs:7588` (native_clipboard_for): the Venus mapping.
  - VEN-C7 (`venus/docs/CONTRACTS.md:477-479`) and ORB-C9 pin it.
- Wheel scroll, 3 rows in three places:
  - `venus/src/application/scroll.rs:52`: terminal scroll.
  - `venus/src/application.rs:4294`: header and tab scroll.
  - `venus/src/application.rs:6155`: dialog scroll.
  - VEN-C7 (`:456`).

## Scope

In scope:
- `[terminal] copy_on_select = true|false`, default `true`. With `false`, a selection release
  writes nothing; explicit copy still works.
- `[terminal] scroll_lines`, bounded (for example 1–20), default `3`. One value governs all three
  sites.
- The value is a Venus startup input, because Venus parses no configuration.
- VEN-C7 and ORB-C9 text if needed, after Lucca approves the wording.
- `docs/CONFIGURATION.md`.

Out of scope:
- Kinetic-scroll tuning.
- Click interval and word separators (deferred bead).

## Acceptance

- Each setting changes behavior in a fresh window, and the defaults are unchanged.
- The three scroll sites read one value.

## Portability

Neutral, with one existing isolated Linux/Wayland dependency: the primary selection exists only there and stays behind the native host boundary.

## Verification

- Venus unit tests for the argument parse and scroll step.
- `cargo fmt --check` and `cargo clippy --locked --all-targets -- -D warnings` for Venus.
- One isolated installed observation.
- Codex review.

## Stop Conditions

- Stop if disabling copy on select needs an Orbit protocol change. Ask before touching ORB-C9.

## Fresh-session split

This epic retains both approved settings. One child owns default-true copy_on_select and preserves explicit copy/terminal clipboard writes; the other owns the bounded default-three scroll_lines value at all three wheel sites. Each includes Runtime validation/defaults/help/corpus, Venus launch consumers, docs and installed proof. They do not consume one another, so no ordering edge; coordinate shared-file edits. The proposed scroll bound is not approved by this split. Parent acceptance completes only after both children deliver the original behavior.

title: Make the agent sidebar's width and start state configurable
description:
## Why

The agent sidebar always starts open when it is enabled. It is always 28 cells wide and steps
aside below 80 cells of terminal space. Users with narrow screens or long agent names differ on
both. Approved on 2026-10-23 (parent epic): width and start state become configurable, and the
hide threshold stays derived.

## Evidence

- `runtime/crates/eon-runtime/src/attention.rs:277`: the sidebar starts Open.
- `venus/src/scene.rs:2608`: `SIDEBAR_CELLS = 28`.
- `venus/src/scene.rs:2610`: `SIDEBAR_MIN_CONTENT_CELLS = 80`.

title: Consume Orbit same-boot management in Eon
description:
## Outcome and contract routing

Implement Eon's consumer half of Orbit ORB-C13 as candidate EON-C15. This is the exact same-boot phase selected by eon-decide-eon-session-durability-qhf; it adds no reboot, logout, machine-loss, remote, or durable-topology promise.

Consumer: one local Eon or EonTerm user on the same boot and login.

Trigger: Eon starts a managed Orbit run, or a prior Eon supervisor disappears after Orbit published Ready and a later Eon targets that exact generation.

Result: Eon supplies one strict logical Session ID and fresh run ID, validates Orbit's complete Ready identity, acquires the sole management lease, and only then publishes the Session or launches Venus. Replacement Eon recovers each exact surviving Orbit without changing its PTY child or terminal state. EonTerm recovers one run. Full Eon projects recovered runs into one deterministic tab in numeric Session order; prior tab membership and focus are not reconstructed. Stop uses only validated leases and sends EONW Stopped only after every run has an ORB-C12-complete tombstone.

Important failures: partial startup, missing or malformed records, stale or replaced objects, wrong UID/mode/type, identity or generation mismatch, Busy, Orbit exit, and transport loss fail within one shared five-second operation. They never authorize PID, signal, pathname, process-name, cgroup, pidfd, or Child fallback after Ready; never launch a duplicate over unresolved live state; and never report clean stop from uncertain state.

Ownership: Eon owns exact generation selection, Session/run creation, a per-generation scan bounded by its existing MAX_PANES product limit, recovered-workspace projection, lease collection, deadline, EONW response ordering, the Eon-to-Venus control stream, and Eon-owned cleanup. Orbit owns ORBM/ORBR values, live identity, lease, PTY and terminal state, wait outcome, ORB-C12 cleanup, tombstone, and exact endpoint cleanup. Venus remains a transient ORBS client and owns managed presentation loss/retry behavior.

## Exact prerequisites

- User-approved same-boot decisions: eon-decide-eon-session-durability-qhf comment 511 and Orbit orb-define-orbit-session-management-contract-5p1 comments 611-613.
- Accepted and pushed Orbit source 86aa130629c09dce61d0f232150298656fa5cef4, metadata 68377ed9429e974b96757e48bea702150042689a, ORB-C13, ORB-C12, ORBF v1, and ORBS v4.
- Accepted and pushed Venus source a768e9a1bcb61eac5a21d25b7463c9dc44aa2df8, metadata 602e21ee224ad69e1bcd2959a02f3f66857ed55a, and VEN-C3/VEN-C4/VEN-C14; native owner-loss evidence remains scoped to predecessor 754eb057ea71ddee57b2f543d85d08d66edc953e because the accepted successor changes only the ordered control regression.
- Eon currently pins stale Orbit 6de95296d252c119d4fdba2d9b03cec1a09355ae, stale Venus 5d22b09e323212693a8e54c4c63089784b660cad, and ORBS v3. Refresh the one canonical graph only to the exact accepted compatible pair; changing only Orbit is invalid.
- Reconfirm exact remote accepted revisions and the sole active frontier before claim. Replace the provisional Venus starting identity in this Bead with the prerequisite's accepted identity before implementation.

## Scope boundary

In scope: EON-C15; exact manifest/Nix/lock/protocol substitution; canonical orbit-protocol consumption; Eon launch, strict ID handling, bounded discovery, lease acquisition, recovery projection, status/tombstone reconciliation, owner-routed Stop, stream-based Venus supervision, strong focused tests, current docs/LOC/changelog, package/profile refresh, and isolated installed dogfood.

Out of scope: Orbit or Venus source changes inside this issue; ORBM/ORBR/ORBS/ORBF/EONW vocabulary changes; prior topology restoration; persistent launch intent; logout/reboot recovery; cloud/sync/remote; service manager, broker, helper, async runtime, process scan, raw-signal fallback, compatibility adapter, or old-generation backport.

## Acceptance Criteria

The canonical completion criteria are stored in this Bead's acceptance_criteria field.
design:
## Reference and dependency gates

Before code, reread complete EON-C10/EON-C11/EON-C15 and ORB-C12/ORB-C13 boundaries; current launch, startup lock, generation, workspace, control-response, Venus, and Stop owners; Orbit's management codec/artifact rules; the accepted Venus prerequisite; and the recovery route in docs/REFERENCES.md. Reuse the exact Orbit owner reference record where its question and revisions still match.

Consume orbit-protocol from exact Orbit source 86aa1306, with Nix substituting that same pinned source path. Reuse existing eon-workspace-protocol MAX_PANES and the existing request_id entropy source. Add no copied codec, serializer, UUID/random crate, helper, async runtime, or second composition graph.

## Minimum vertical slice

1. Index EON-C15 before production code. Refresh the canonical graph to Orbit 86aa1306, ORBS v4, and the exact accepted Venus successor from ven-release-supervised-venus-on-owner-loss-np8; keep source, metadata, consumer, and runtime-generation identities distinct.
2. Accept only strict Eon-owned session-N identities. Require canonical positive decimal N without leading zeroes; parse numerically and reject zero, overflow, and duplicate live identities. MAX_PANES bounds live count, not the monotonic numeric ID. Reuse the existing bounded process/time/atomic request_id generator for fresh opaque run IDs. Pass the exact Orbit source revision from the manifest as component generation, never Eon's runtime generation.
3. Launch Orbit with --management-v1 SESSION_ID RUN_ID COMPONENT_GENERATION and no parent-death coupling. Derive .management and .record only from the existing presentation endpoint. Wait for owner-authored Ready and complete Acquire within the existing five-second startup budget before workspace publication or Venus launch.
4. Replace direct-child authority with one managed-session owner containing validated live identity, lease, endpoint, and optional local Child only for pre-Ready rollback and reaping. Child never authorizes attach or stop after Ready.
5. Recover only the selected exact generation. Count record candidates and fail closed if more than MAX_PANES exist; decode at most MAX_PANES. This newly reuses Eon's 256-live-pane workspace ceiling as the per-generation record count bound and is unrelated to MAX_GENERATIONS. Preserve the bound by validating and removing an ended run's tombstone before releasing its workspace slot or admitting a replacement Session; cleanup failure retains unavailable diagnostic state. Reject unsafe objects before decoding, sort valid session-N identities numerically, acquire every live lease under one shared deadline, and release all leases on partial failure. Tombstones reconcile ended runs and grant no authority.
6. EonTerm accepts exactly one live recovered run. Full Eon maps session-N to pane-N in one tab-1, selects the lowest surviving N, sets next_tab to 2 and next_pane with checked max(N)+1. If all MAX_PANES slots are live, the existing capacity owner rejects creation; numeric overflow fails recovery. A post-recovery create must never reuse a tab, pane, or Session identity. No prior grouping, focus, argv, request history, or configuration snapshot is claimed.
7. Concurrent replacements retain the startup-convergence owner: one supervisor acquires all leases; a Busy loser converges on that EONW owner or fails visibly without split ownership, partial publication, or duplicate launch.
8. Replace Eon's UnixDatagram presentation pair with UnixStream. The accepted managed Venus exits on stream EOF; its managed-only Busy retry absorbs the departing-client race. Launch presentation only after all leases are acquired. Venus never becomes a Session lifecycle owner.
9. Stop retains the accepted control stream and request until completion. Send canonical Stop to every validated lease before waiting, then reconcile Stopped or exact tombstones under one deadline. Write EONW Stopped only after all explicit-stop tombstones succeed; otherwise write bounded Failure and preserve diagnostic state. The existing six-second control transport bound contains the shared five-second operation.
10. Before Ready, the exact local Child remains rollback owner. After Ready, Orbit management is the sole Orbit stop path. After Orbit reconciliation, close the Venus control stream and reap the transient local client. Immutable old generations are not relabeled, adopted, signaled, deleted, or backported.

title: Consume Venus background blur in Eon
description:
## Contract

Consumer: one local Eon or EonTerm user and an approved composition using canonical Eon configuration.

Trigger: Eon creates or reopens a Venus surface while `$EON_CONFIG_HOME/config.toml` contains `[terminal] background_blur = true|false`, or contains no such field.

Result: new EON-C14 accepts one strict boolean, defaults absence to `true`, and when true passes exactly one `--background-blur` before Venus socket endpoints. Explicit false omits the flag. `terminal.background_opacity` remains independent; Eon never changes either value because of the other.

Important failures: invalid configuration names `terminal.background_blur` and creates no initial supervisor, Orbit, or Venus process. Invalid replacement configuration returns the existing bounded presentation failure while preserving Orbit and its child. Unsupported or policy-disabled native blur remains Venus VEN-C15 best effort and does not become an Eon failure.

Ownership: Eon owns the configuration schema, true default, apply timing, launch argument, exact Venus selection, and generation policy. Venus VEN-C15 owns the boolean native request through winit; the compositor owns availability, algorithm, strength, and policy. Orbit remains unaware.

## Prerequisites and exact inputs

- User approval: 2026-08-14 direction to create the Eon contract, advance Venus from `74ab5a0b661210f0afec94086f5358fe50b01f05` to exact accepted source `7fc7e4ba97aaf48b586002934a580ef2d1c31694`, and keep opacity independent; the user then superseded the initial false default with “blur on by default.”
- Consume proved Venus VEN-C15 at source `7fc7e4ba97aaf48b586002934a580ef2d1c31694`.
- Preserve Orbit `6de95296d252c119d4fdba2d9b03cec1a09355ae`, ORBF v1, ORBS v3, EONW v1, and all unrelated component identities and contracts.

## Reference gate

Required before code: current Eon instructions; this complete Bead; EON-C13 configuration, validation, launch/reopen, tests, docs, manifest, and Nix owners; Venus VEN-C15 contract, exact source implementation, CLI validation, tests, dependency identity, license, and COSMIC proof.

Comparison only: EON-C13 as the existing direct terminal-presentation configuration pattern.

title: Make concurrent supervisor startup converge
description:
## Contract routing

Harden EON-C11 and preserve EON-C12. The consumer is a local launcher; the trigger is two Eon processes starting the same current generation when no live control owner is reachable or an owned stale socket exists; the result is exactly one supervisor and Orbit Session owner while every competing attach-capable launcher converges on that owner. Unsafe or genuinely live endpoints still fail explicitly.

This correction adds no manager daemon, public lock, persisted topology, compatibility window, EONW value, child behavior, or distribution promise.

## Why

`create_control_listener` checks connectability, separately removes an owned socket path, and then binds. Two launchers can both observe absence or refusal before either owns the path; one can then unlink a newly bound peer. The existing concurrent-launch test passed seven stress iterations and failed on iteration eight because one launcher exited unsuccessfully instead of attaching.

Impact: MEDIUM. Effort: M. Implementation risk: MEDIUM. Confidence: HIGH.

## Evidence

- `crates/eon/src/main.rs:1830-1878`: connect, stale-path inspection/removal, bind, and listener identity capture are separate operations with no serialized or owner-bound acquisition.
- `crates/eon/src/main.rs:1811-1827`: `ControlListener::drop` protects a replacement after acquisition but does not protect acquisition itself.
- `crates/eon/tests/workspace_control.rs:570-629`: the accepted real-process test expects two launches to produce one supervisor, one successful attached launcher, and one Orbit start.
- Audit reproduction on exact HEAD `1b8836e616222f29c57ac697916872010db14685`: `for audit_run in $(seq 1 100); do cargo test --locked -p eon --test workspace_control concurrent_launches_converge_and_generation_stop_is_owner_routed --quiet || exit 1; done`; runs 1-7 passed and run 8 failed at line 615. The failed fixture recorded one Orbit launch and a dead mode-0600 `eon.sock` after process cleanup.
- `eon-audit-eon-runtime-lifecycle-wqz` comment 271 preserves the complete evidence and proof limits.

## Prerequisite and reference gate

- No implementation prerequisite. Correct this runtime invariant before `eon-5rp`; the later extraction must preserve it.
- Rebaseline the cited symbols after any intervening revision.
- Reuse the audit reference gate: exact Eon code and EON-C11/EON-C12 own the behavior; Ghosthub `072cc83559bd590ed5d759af05ec0a1868dbf359` is comparison-only for process-owned socket namespaces and dead-owner cleanup.
- Compare the standard-library bind/connect path, the already accepted `libc` dependency, and no new dependency. If advisory locking is considered, inspect the exact Linux and macOS primary semantics, crash release, path safety, and portability before choosing it.
- No new crate is expected. Stop for the dependency gate and user approval before a manifest change.

## Scope

In scope:
- `ControlListener`, `create_control_listener`, stale owned control-socket cleanup, and the minimum runtime helper needed to serialize or identity-bind acquisition.
- The focused concurrent-launch integration check and only the smallest deterministic lower-level check needed to prove the old interleaving.
- EON-C11/EON-C12 current-state proof metadata, `CHANGELOG.md`, and README LOC only as required after acceptance.

Out of scope:
- A long-running manager or lock service, persisted registry, PID file, public lock path, second socket namespace, compatibility window, EONW change, Orbit/Venus change, or broad supervisor abstraction.
- Weakening owned-mode-0600 validation, replacing unsafe non-socket paths, killing inferred processes, retry loops without a bound, or treating a stress test as the sole proof.
- Refactoring managed-environment, workspace, manifest, or Nix composition ownership.

## Implementation notes

1. Make the old stale-observation/removal/bind interleaving reproducible before the fix using the smallest deterministic seam that does not create a production framework.
2. Choose the first sufficient Unix-portable acquisition mechanism that ensures a newly bound live listener cannot be removed by a peer that observed earlier absence or refusal.
3. Validate that the path still names the acquired listener after bind and preserve replacement-safe Drop cleanup.
4. Keep one bounded competing-launch recovery path in `launch_current`; do not add another launcher coordinator.
5. Preserve stale owned-socket recovery and explicit refusal of symlinks, non-sockets, wrong owners, unsafe modes, incompatible supervisors, and wrong launch modes.

## Acceptance

- A deterministic regression exercises the former check/remove/bind interleaving and passes without timing luck.
- Two same-mode current-generation launches yield exactly one reachable mode-0600 control listener, one Orbit Session owner, and one launcher that attaches successfully; neither launcher reports a spurious failure.
- A competing wrong-mode launch still fails explicitly and starts no second Session.
- A dead owned socket is recoverable; a live listener, symlink, non-socket, wrong-owner path, or replacement socket is never removed.
- Listener shutdown removes only its own unchanged path and leaves a replacement intact.
- Crash or failed-start cleanup leaves no permanent acquisition blocker.
- The accepted mechanism works within the Linux alpha and has an explicit macOS proof plan; it depends on no mutable Nix/store identity.
- No new product contract, EONW field, dependency, public configuration, or child change is introduced.

## Verification

- `cargo test --locked -p eon --test workspace_control concurrent_launches_converge_and_generation_stop_is_owner_routed` should exit 0 and prove one reachable owner.
- The new deterministic acquisition regression should exit 0 and prove the exact former interleaving without repeated timing attempts.
- A supplementary bounded stress run should complete at least 100 iterations without one nonzero launcher, second Orbit start, unreachable control path, or leaked fixture.
- `cargo fmt --all --check`
- `cargo check --locked --workspace`
- `cargo test --locked --workspace`
- `cargo clippy --locked --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings`
- `cargo run --locked -p eon-manifest -- components/eon-alpha-v1.json`
- `nix build --no-link --print-out-paths --no-update-lock-file path:.#default`
- `nix flake check --no-build --no-update-lock-file path:.`
- `git diff --check`
- After the proof-bearing commit, refresh the active `eon` profile without stopping running supervisors; verify the selected artifact and report restart required for existing generations.

## Stop conditions

- Stop if listener ownership or EON-C11/EON-C12 has drifted materially.
- Stop if a correct mechanism requires a new dependency, Linux-only foundation, persistent manager, public lock path, protocol change, or process inference.
- Stop if the proposed deterministic check needs broad production-only hooks or cannot distinguish a live replacement from a stale socket.
- Stop if the same verification failure repeats twice after a reasonable correction.

## Maintenance notes

Prefer one local acquisition invariant over retries and cleanup patches at every caller. The stress reproduction is retained as negative evidence, but the regression must prove the race deterministically. The final `eon-audit-eon-runtime-lifecycle-wqz` pass must rerun it after `eon-5rp`.

title: Show the CPU's name, temperature, busiest CPU and load in the CPU chip's hover
description:
## Current completion state (8ebdd69) The approved design above is implemented. Comments 5839/5842 record landing/review/downstream fixes; 5852 records installed Linux name, temperature, busiest logical CPU, load and orange Running hot. Both Runtime threshold keys and Venus readers exist; do not reimplement them. Remaining original acceptance: macOS name/busiest CPU/load observation with no temperature. Closed eon-s412n records its event-test fixes passing in mac-proof 42688422839 on 032298c while other steps failed; that is not itself CPU-hover evidence. Find attributable later feature evidence or report the missing observation. Do not rerun proved Linux suites or require the obsolete failed 42386851894 run. Closure remains Lucca/overseer-owned; no hardware run in this planning pass. ## Historical scope and evidence (retained) ## Why Lucca, 2026-11-07, looking at the CPU chip's hover ("CPU · 16 logical CPUs / 5% on average over the last 30 s"): "and the cpu, can we put more info?" Lucca approved each piece below ("1 ok 2 ok 3 ok"). ## Goal The CPU hover and accessible description add the CPU's name, its temperature (Linux), the busiest logical CPU, and the 1-minute load average: ``` CPU · 13th Gen Intel Core i5-13450HX 16 logical CPUs · 59 °C 5% on average over the last 30 s CPU 3 at 97% Load 1.2 over 1 min Under high load (as today, only when high) ``` Decisions (Lucca, 2026-11-07): 1. Busiest CPU reads `CPU at

%`, not "Core": the readings are logical CPUs (this i5-13450HX has 10 cores and 16 logical CPUs), so "CPU" matches the line above. Numbered from 0, as the kernel, top and btop number them. Measured over the same 2-second interval as the chip. 2. Load average: only the 1-minute value, `Load 1.2 over 1 min` (one decimal). Linux `/proc/loadavg`; macOS `getloadavg`. 3. CPU name: Linux `/proc/cpuinfo` `model name`; macOS sysctl `machdep.cpu.brand_string`. Read once, not every sample. Strip `(R)`, `(TM)` and `(C)` marks and collapse spaces. No name: the first line stays `CPU`. 4. Temperature: Linux only, from hwmon: `coretemp` "Package id 0" on Intel, `k10temp` Tctl (or Tdie) on AMD; no other source (not acpitz, which is a board zone). macOS shows none: Apple Silicon temperatures need private IOKit calls. Whole degrees, `°C`. It colours like the other chips, orange from `cpu_temperature_warning_celsius` (default 85) and red from `cpu_temperature_critical_celsius` (default 95); both configurable under `[bar]` (rule 6: laptops run hot and users differ), validated like the RAM levels (critical not below warning; a sane range such as 30 through 120). Whether a hot CPU colours the whole CPU chip or only the hover line is the implementer's call to recommend; colour is never the only signal (say "running hot" in words, as RAM says "under pressure"). ## Contract and scope The hover text is a feature (venus/docs/PRESENTATION.md, Eon Bar). The two new `[bar]` keys extend the contract text in docs/CONTRACTS.md that lists the bar's threshold keys (~line 3865): a minor contract-text addition that Lucca's standing rule lets the overseer approve; Codex reviews it. Keys flow Runtime -> Venus as launch arguments (supervisor.rs ~489, venus/src/launch.rs), like the RAM levels: no EONW change. Document defaults in docs/CONFIGURATION.md and the managed config help (managed_environment.rs ~615). Owner: Venus samples (venus/src/system.rs), as the existing chips do; Runtime parses and validates the keys. Out of scope: GPU name (eon-gpu-widget-eon-bar-ri16), disk model and temperature (separate bead), top processes, the CLI read path (eon-agent-parity-a9g0.12). Portability: isolated Linux dependency for temperature (hwmon); the rest is neutral with a macOS reader each. New macOS FFI (getloadavg, sysctlbyname, host_processor_info for per-CPU ticks) goes in the existing `host` module and stays minimal (eon-b4vh plans to remove that module's unsafe code later). Depends on eon-ram-tooltip-used-u532r landing first (same file). ## Acceptance - Focused tests: per-CPU parsing and picking the busiest (a CPU going offline between readings gives no busiest line, never a wrong one), /proc/loadavg parsing, name cleanup, hwmon selection from a fixture directory (coretemp, k10temp, neither), the new keys' validation in Runtime. - `cargo fmt --check` and clippy `-D warnings` for yazelix-venus and eon-runtime; `nix develop -c eon-test` for the affected crates. - Installed proof: refresh the eon profile and observe the hover once on Linux. macOS readers through the next mac-proof run (busiest CPU, load and name present; no temperature).

title: Show a CPU widget in the Eon Bar
description:
## Decision
Lucca, 2026-10-17: add CPU, GPU and IO widgets to Eon. Lucca, 2026-10-20: CPU, RAM and clock are in
1.0 (`eon-igae`); GPU and IO are 1.x. This bead establishes the shared sampling and chip path that
RAM (`eon-igae.3`) reuses.

Lucca, 2026-10-21: accepted the design below. Venus samples locally, following the clock's
precedent (`b18f2cd`, VEN-C27/EON-C29), instead of Runtime sampling and sending facts over EONW.
Reasons: no EONW revision frozen for all of 1.x under EON-C28, and no complete EONW snapshot every
few seconds. Eon is local-only, so Venus runs on the machine it measures.

## Contract (direction approved 2026-10-21; exact wording needs Lucca's approval before commit)
- IDs: new `EON-C30` (product policy: always on, no configuration) and `VEN-C28` (the chip), the
  same pairing as the clock's EON-C29/VEN-C27.
- Consumer: a full-Eon user on native x86_64 Linux Wayland.
- Result: the Eon Bar shows a read-only `CPU 12%` chip with whole-machine CPU utilization, sampled
  every 2 s while the window is open and redrawn only when the shown whole percentage changes.
  Hover and a static accessible label name CPU, the value and its age.
- Failures: an unreadable or invalid sample shows no chip (never 0%); no chip, gap, hit target or
  accessible node while absent; refreshes do not replace attachments, scroll positions or
  navigation or send an Orbit resize; under width pressure the clock hides first, then CPU/RAM, then
  the quota chips, all before required tabs, controls or drag space (VEN-C21 priority).

## Decisions (Lucca, 2026-10-21)
1. Scope: whole machine, as htop and btop show. No per-Eon attribution (process-tree walks or
   cgroups, which Eon's Linux contracts avoid).
2. EONW: no revision. Venus owns sampling.
3. Cadence: 2 s (btop's default) while a window is open; redraw only on a change of the shown
   value. Measure idle wakeups in the installed check.
4. Source: owned `/proc/stat` delta parsing in one Linux-only Venus module (the platform seam;
   compiled out elsewhere). No `sysinfo`.
5. Visibility: shown by default, no toggle. A later toggle is additive under EON-C28; add one only
   if dogfood shows clutter. If added, Eon owns it and passes it to Venus as a startup input.

## Ownership
Venus owns sampling, chip text, geometry, hover and AccessKit. Runtime and EONW are unchanged. Eon
owns the product policy (always on) in EON-C30. This adds a Venus module, which is product scope
approved by Lucca on 2026-10-21.

## Reference gate (consequential: new Venus platform seam)
Before code record: btop and Waybar's cpu module at exact revisions (sampling, delta math, first
sample, counter wrap); constraints kept and approaches rejected; the chosen source and its check.
Read VEN-C21/C22/C26/C27 and EON-C27/C29 and reuse the existing optional-chip and clock paths rather
than adding a second chip owner or timer.

## Prerequisites
None. RAM (`eon-igae.3`), GPU and IO depend on this one.

## Acceptance
Focused sampler red/green (delta math, first sample, wrap and invalid input never becoming 0%);
Venus chip layout/absence/hiding-order/accessibility test; `nix develop -c eon-test -p
yazelix-venus`; fmt and clippy for Venus; nix build; isolated capture showing the chip, its hover
and narrow-width hiding; measured idle wakeups; review loop; profile refresh.

## Scope boundary
CPU utilization only: no per-core bars, graphs, history, temperatures, frequency, memory, process
list, alerts or click actions. Linux Wayland only; no macOS claim.
close_reason: CPU label shipped (VEN-C28/EON-C30 proven); RAM (eon-igae.3) can build on it

title: Add a consent-bound column close and SetSidebar to Runtime and the CLI (EONW v39)
description:
## Why

eon-t5boa (a Close button on Stack tabs) needs a way to close a whole column that cannot stop a
terminal nobody agreed to stop. Earlier plans asked only when a terminal was busy; three Codex plan
reviews (2026-11-10) found that work starting between the busy check and the Stop could still be
closed without consent, that a final close could stop runs it never listed, and that a consent made
of terminal numbers could match a different terminal that reused a number. Overseer decision,
2026-11-10: a Stack close ALWAYS asks, because it closes several terminals at once. The answer
lists every terminal the close stops and marks the ones known to be running; consent covers exactly
that list, by run; any change to it asks again; the CLI closes only with --yes and otherwise
refuses with the same list as data.

The same EONW bump carries `SetSidebar` (overseer, 2026-11-10T14:27Z): eon-5g0e5 ships
`eon sidebar show|hide` as inspect-then-toggle, which a concurrent keypress or command can reverse.

This bead is slice A, the Runtime and CLI half. eon-t5boa (the Venus button) depends on it.

Plan: /home/lucca/.cache/eon-agents/eon-stack-close-replan3-work/bead/t5boa-plan-v5.md, sections 2
(safety model), 3 (wire), 4 (this bead) and 9 (landing). SetSidebar design:
/home/lucca/.cache/eon-agents/eon-hide-buttons-work/bead/setsidebar-for-t5boa.md. Read both before
planning; the plan holds the exact contract text and the test list.

Codex re-checks of the plan, both "implement with these changes", both folded into plan v5:
/home/lucca/.local/state/rota/runs/stack-close-v3-recheck-codex-1/report.md and
/home/lucca/.local/state/rota/runs/stack-close-v4-recheck-codex-1/report.md.

Landing: this bead carries the EONW bump, so it lands only when Lucca can restart his window (see
Prerequisites and plan section 9).

## Scope

- EONW bump (v38 to v39, or the next free version when this starts; never amend in place):
  `Action::CloseColumn { pane, consent: Option<CloseConsent> }`, `Response::Confirm(CloseScope)` and
  `Action::SetSidebar { open }` (tag 45: the design's 43 is `InspectWorkspace`'s).
- Runtime, column close: without a consent it stops nothing and answers `Confirm` with its scope:
  the generation, every terminal it would stop with its unique run ID, name and EON-C11 busy mark,
  the end (column, session or window), and for a window end the generation's live runs that no tab
  tracks. It stops terminals only on a consent whose generation, run IDs and end equal the scope
  when the close runs; anything else answers `Confirm` again and stops nothing. No exception for an
  idle or one-pane column. Terminal numbers and busy marks never decide anything.
- A matching close stops exactly the consented runs. It does not reuse the generation cleanup behind
  `closed_response`: it leases only listed untracked runs, and a run that becomes ready during the
  close is left running, with the close failing into the existing incomplete-stop state.
- CLI: `eon column close PANE --yes [--json]`. It closes only with `--yes` and never reads standard
  input. Without `--yes` it prints what the close would stop (text, or the scope as JSON data) and
  fails `not-confirmed`. With `--yes`, a scope that changes before the close runs fails
  `close-changed` and stops nothing.
- SetSidebar end to end: codec and goldens; Runtime owns the value; in `Off`, `SetSidebar { open:
  true }` and `ToggleSidebar` fail `unavailable` and `SetSidebar { open: false }` changes nothing;
  `eon sidebar show|hide` send it directly with no inspection; Venus's Agents Hide button sends
  `SetSidebar { open: false }`.
- Contract text: EON-C8 (column close), EON-C10 (both commands), EON-C31 (sidebar visibility),
  VEN-C30 (Hide). Docs (USAGE, ARCHITECTURE, runtime README, the eon skill), CHANGELOG.
- For the column close, Venus gets only the version rename and the arms exhaustive matches require.

Out of scope: the Stack button and its prompt (eon-t5boa); consent for tab and pane closes, and
their final-close cleanup (eon-qi5nh); `eon column create` (eon-agent-parity-a9g0.6); any change to
EON-C11's busy classification or EON-C31's polling.

## Contract and reference gate

Changes EON-C8, EON-C10, EON-C31 and VEN-C30 and the EONW wire format, at a lifecycle boundary: a
consequential code shape. Before code, record in this bead the behaviour and its owners, the
`docs/REFERENCES.md` routes read, and at least one comparable close confirmation inspected at an
exact revision (candidates: WezTerm's close confirmation, tmux `confirm-before` with `kill-pane`,
kitty `confirm_os_window_close`), with what was kept and rejected. The SetSidebar design records its
own comparables. The overseer approves the contract text; Codex reviews code and contract text.

Fixed value (rule 6), to record with its reason: the confirmation has no setting and ignores
`warning_close_last_tab` (safety: the answer is the consent that binds the close to its runs).

## Prerequisites

eon-5g0e5 (it adds the `eon sidebar` command and the Hide button this bead changes). It does not
need eon-2ibdd beyond that. It renames the EONW module in every consumer, so land it while no other
EONW-changing bead is in flight, and only when Lucca can restart his window: after the profile
refresh, `eon` commands in a window still on the old version fail until it restarts (plan section
9).

## Size

One session, at the upper limit. If the implementer's plan shows it does not fit, split by action,
not by layer: first EONW v39 with SetSidebar end to end, then EONW v40 with the column close, both
landing in the same restart window (plan section 7).

## Acceptance

- A column close with no consent stops nothing and answers `Confirm`, for an idle column, a busy
  one, a one-pane one and a final one.
- A consent stops exactly its runs when it equals the scope, including when work started in a listed
  terminal after the answer (regression: the old busy race).
- A consent stops nothing when a pane joined or left the column, the anchor pane moved to another
  column, the close became or stopped being a final close, or an untracked run appeared; each
  answers `Confirm` with the new scope (regressions).
- A consent stops nothing when a listed run ended and a new terminal started under the same
  terminal number (regression: reusable terminal IDs).
- A window-end scope lists untracked runs; a close stops only listed runs; a run that appears after
  the stops is still live afterwards and the close fails `column-close-failed` naming it
  (regression: cleanup widening the consented set).
- `eon column close` without `--yes` prints the list and fails `not-confirmed`, also for an idle
  column and also with `y` on standard input (regression); `--json` gives the scope as data; `--yes`
  closes exactly the listed terminals; a change between the answer and the close fails
  `close-changed`.
- `eon sidebar hide` twice, and two started together, leave the sidebar closed; `show` and `toggle`
  with the sidebar off fail `unavailable`; the Agents Hide button never shows the sidebar.
- The person's active tab, selection, shown popup and desktop focus stay as they are for a
  background column.
- fmt and clippy clean for the changed crates; focused suites; whole-workspace `eon-test` once on
  the staged tree; one isolated installed observation of both commands from a candidate package.

title: Pick up popup changes in a running window without a new window
description:
Lucca, 2026-11-11: "do we have a bead for live config reload? would be nice to have eon picked this up now instead of needing a new eon". He had just added [popups.desk] to config.toml and wanted it in his running window.

## Now

The supervisor builds the popup catalog once, when the window's generation starts (runtime/crates/eon-runtime/src/supervisor.rs:286-288, `managed_environment::popup_catalog`), and hands clones to its tasks (:1140, :1165, :1258, :1295). Neither detach plus `eon attach` (which re-reads only `[terminal]`, `[bar]` and `warning_close_last_tab`; eon-agent-parity-a9g0.7) nor a Venus reload (eon-u199d) re-reads it. So an added, changed or removed popup needs a new window. Restarting the supervisor is never an option, since it kills live terminals.

## Do

Re-read `[popups.*]` in a running window and swap in the new catalog, keeping running popups' terminals:
- A hidden keep-alive popup whose command changed keeps its terminal until it ends.
- A removed popup that is running keeps running until dismissed.
- A malformed reload keeps the old catalog and logs a warning. Startup validation is separate;
  this does not claim startup accepts malformed configuration.

Trigger: an `eon config reload` CLI path (agent parity, rule 5), and possibly re-read on present/attach like `[terminal]`. A file watcher is optional.

Related: eon-agent-parity-a9g0.7 (terminal and bar re-read), eon-nhec3 (chrome and panel settings), eon-u199d (Venus reload). Check whether one reload path can serve all three.

## Contract

EON-C32 (docs/CONTRACTS.md) excludes live reload. This needs Lucca's approval of the contract change before implementation (AGENTS.md rule 1). The plan should propose the wording.

## Proof

Isolated window: add a popup, run the trigger, open it by its key. Change its command and remove another, checking that running popups survive. A malformed config keeps the old catalog. The live window's terminals survive throughout.

## Scope and approval gate

Runtime owns catalog validation/swap and CLI; Venus consumes canonical entries. Before code propose EON-C32/EON-C10 wording, any EONW change, and removed-running-popup identity/dismissal rules for exact approval. EON-C32 currently excludes live reload. Use the required explicit CLI trigger for the bounded slice; optional attach triggers/watchers need a recorded choice.

Acceptance includes real CLI/JSON reload results, keyboard/CLI discovery of an added popup, changed/removed running popup identity and dismissal, atomic retention of the old catalog on malformed input, and unchanged unrelated terminals/layout/desktop focus. Resolve how removed running popups stay targetable until dismissal; never orphan them. Align CONFIGURATION/USAGE/help/corpus and installed proof with approved semantics.

At 8ebdd69 eon window reload already replaces Venus and rereads terminal/bar configuration (eon-u199d.1/.3, consumed by a9g0.7). eon-nhec3 owns no-restart chrome/panel apply; its comment 6498 permits a popup sibling. This is that sibling, not a second full-window reload. Reuse existing config/control infrastructure. Never restart the supervisor.

title: Make the Nix alpha installable without repository credentials
description:
## Why

The proved Nix alpha cannot be tried by the public because its locked Orbit and Venus inputs require GitHub credentials. Public alpha needs one credential-free path to the same exact component graph; it does not need a second installer or bundle.

Contract: an unauthenticated user clones Eon, resolves the locked flake, builds or installs `.#default`, and obtains the exact reviewed Eon, Orbit, and Venus revisions. Missing or private inputs fail before release, and making source public never exposes secrets or content the user has not approved.

## Evidence

- Baseline `18f1874`: `README.md:93-103` says the alpha uses private Eon child inputs and requires GitHub credentials.
- `README.md:40-44` identifies the canonical Eon, Eon Desktop, and Eon Sessions repositories.
- `docs/DISTRIBUTION.md:35-45` requires one versioned component manifest, opaque Nix launch inputs, and no direct installer or package matrix during alpha.
- `docs/DISTRIBUTION.md:203-215` defines the Nix alpha candidate around exact manifest identity, isolated install, clean native Wayland behavior, lifecycle checks, and closure inspection.
- `flake.lock`, `flake.nix`, and `components/eon-alpha-v3.json` own the exact source and compatibility graph.

Impact: CRITICAL public-alpha access blocker. Effort: M. Risk: HIGH because repository visibility and full history are external user-owned state. Confidence: HIGH.

## Scope

In scope:
- Make the exact Eon, Eon Sessions, and Eon Desktop source revisions needed by the locked Nix graph readable without credentials.
- Audit each repository full reachable history, current issues/releases as relevant, licenses, submodules, LFS objects, CI references, and dependency URLs for secrets or private material before visibility changes.
- Refresh only exact source identities and public installation wording needed to prove the credential-free graph.
- Record the user approval and exact repositories/revisions immediately before any visibility change.

Out of scope:
- Direct bundles, Home Manager, signing, notarization, release automation, mirrors, vendored child source, a second component graph, macOS distribution, or publishing unrelated Yazelix repositories.
- Rewriting published history, removing security checks, or making any repository public by implication.
- Product behavior changes.

## Implementation Notes

1. Reconcile `flake.lock`, `flake.nix`, the component manifest, and each accepted child proof revision.
2. Perform and record a full-history secret/private-content/license review without reproducing secret values in Beads or logs.
3. Present the exact visibility changes and residual findings to the user. Stop until the user explicitly approves changing each repository visibility.
4. Prefer public read access to the canonical repositories. If a repository cannot be public, stop and create a separately approved distribution decision; do not add source mirrors or archives here.
5. After approval, change only the named visibility surfaces, then test from an unauthenticated clean environment and update the installation claim.

## Verification

- In an environment with no GitHub credentials, `git clone https://github.com/Yazelix/eon.git` succeeds and the checked-out release candidate resolves every locked input.
- From that clean clone, `nix build .#default` exits 0 and `./result/bin/eon versions` reports the exact manifest identities without a Nix store path.
- `cargo run --locked -p eon-manifest -- components/eon-alpha-v3.json` exits 0 for the published graph.
- The recorded full-history review finds no unremediated credential, private material, inaccessible submodule/LFS object, or license blocker in any repository made public.
- `git diff --check` exits 0 and README installation/support text plus the LOC scorecard match the public state.

## Stop Conditions

- Stop before changing repository visibility without fresh explicit user approval naming every target.
- Stop and report only credential type and location if a secret or private artifact is found; rotate or remediate under separately authorized scope before publication.
- Stop if credential-free access would require a mirror, copied child implementation, second manifest, history rewrite, or new distribution channel.
- Stop if any exact accepted revision differs from the locked graph; reconcile proof identity before publication.

## Maintenance Notes

The simplest accepted shape is public read access to the canonical three repositories. Alpha remains Nix-only. This issue owns source availability, not the public-alpha acceptance decision or later direct distribution.
close_reason: Public canonical sources and credential-free locked Nix install proved

title: Select the next and previous tab with Ctrl+Tab and Ctrl+Shift+Tab
description:
## Why

Eon has no single key that moves one tab over. Alt+H/L walk columns first and only then spill into the next tab, which is slow in a tab with four columns. Alt+1…0 needs the tab's position. Browsers, VS Code, kitty, WezTerm and Windows Terminal all use Ctrl+Tab for this. Today Ctrl+Tab is unbound and reaches the terminal; in legacy encoding it arrives as a plain Tab, so few programs rely on it.

## Decision (Lucca, 2026-10-23, to the overseer eon-a8)

The overseer proposed: (1) Ctrl+Tab and Ctrl+Shift+Tab select the next and previous tab, wrapping around; (2) in tab order, not most-recently-used. Lucca: "ok, i accept you idea for tabs / indeed. if the tab has 4 columns, it can be expensive to go through each of them". F6 is unchanged: it cycles focus regions, which is a different job.

## Contract

Amend the Venus contract that owns fixed workspace shortcuts and tab selection (find it: likely VEN-C8 Eon workspace presentation, with the shortcut viewer VEN-C20 and hints VEN-C24), plus any EON-C text that lists the fixed shortcuts. Consumer: a user with several tabs. Trigger: Ctrl+Tab / Ctrl+Shift+Tab with terminal or chrome focus. Result: the next or previous tab is selected, wrapping from last to first; selection works as Alt+1…0 does (pane, popup and focus behavior unchanged). With one tab, nothing happens and nothing reaches the terminal. Behavior while the shortcut viewer, a picker or a popup is shown follows the existing Alt+1…0 rule.

## Scope

In scope: a `FIXED_SHORTCUTS` entry in `venus/src/application/shortcuts.rs` reusing the existing tab-selection action (no new EONW request unless the reference gate shows one is needed); shortcut viewer and hints listing; docs/USAGE.md shortcut table, venus/docs/INTERACTION.md, CHANGELOG. Check that a configured popup key cannot take Ctrl+Tab silently.

Out of scope: MRU order, workspace switching (EON-C33 owns Alt+Shift+S), F6, macOS bindings.

## Prerequisites

Lands after the agent sidebar chain (eon-agent-sidebar-yx8.13, yx8.8), which edits the same shortcuts file. Contract text is approved under Lucca's 2026-10-23 approvals while the overseer runs. Record the exact text as relayed.

## Acceptance

- A Venus test: Ctrl+Tab and Ctrl+Shift+Tab select next and previous with wrap, and a single tab is a no-op with no terminal input.
- One installed dogfood observation in isolated Sway with three tabs.

## Verification

`nix develop -c eon-test -p yazelix-venus`, Venus fmt and clippy, converge plus Codex, and one isolated installed observation.

Portability disposition: neutral (Linux binding; macOS out of scope).
close_reason: Ctrl+Tab and Ctrl+Shift+Tab select the next and previous tab with wrap; Venus test and isolated installed observation recorded (proof comment)

comments.author: lucca
comments.text:
## Implementation notes (claude-ctrltab, 2026-10-30)

Approach: two `FIXED_SHORTCUTS` entries (`Ctrl+Tab` "Focus next tab", `Ctrl+Shift+Tab` "Focus previous tab", group Navigate) with new `NextTab`/`PreviousTab` native actions. `tab_shortcut_index` became `tab_shortcut_target(code, modifiers, snapshot)`, which resolves both Alt+1…0 and Ctrl+Tab to a tab of the accepted snapshot and sends the existing `FocusId(tN)`, so dispatch, consumption, repeat (none, as for Alt+1…0) and popup/picker/viewer precedence are the Alt+1…0 path's. No EONW change: `FocusId` already selects a tab.

Decisions (minor, taken while Lucca was away):
- One tab: the key is consumed and nothing is sent (not a `FocusId` of the active tab), so nothing happens and nothing reaches the terminal.
- Footer hints: none for Ctrl+Tab / Ctrl+Shift+Tab. They would add two new modifier groups (C and C-S) to the width-constrained footer for one concept; they stay in full help (Alt+/), like F6. Alt+H/L already holds the footer's "tabs" hint.
- Popup override: Ctrl+Tab is not reserved (EON-C20's reserved set never grows in 1.x), so a configured popup on Ctrl+Tab takes it the way it takes any other fixed key; the viewer then lists "Focus next tab (overridden by <popup>)" and the footer has nothing to drop. Runtime accepts `Ctrl+Tab` as a popup key (`Shortcut::validate`). Not silent: covered in `configured_popups_take_fixed_bindings_except_reserved_keys`.
- Configurability: the key stays fixed in this bead, as every fixed Venus shortcut does today; making fixed shortcut keys configurable is `eon-configurability-qkq8` (dependent `qkq8.2` moves this table). Ctrl+Tab is the key browsers, VS Code, kitty, WezTerm and Windows Terminal use.
- Humans and Agents: the CLI path already exists. `eon workspace --json` lists tabs in order with the active tab, and `eon focus tN` selects one (the same `FocusId`).

Amended contract text (approved direction: Lucca 2026-10-23, relayed by eon-a8, quoted above):

VEN-C8, new bullet after the Alt+1…0 bullet:
> - Physical Ctrl+Tab and Ctrl+Shift+Tab, with terminal or chrome focus, focus
>   the tab after or before the active one in the accepted snapshot's order,
>   wrapping from the last tab to the first and from the first to the last.
>   Venus sends that tab's stable `tN` through `FocusId`, as Alt+1 through
>   Alt+0 do, so pane, popup and focus behavior is the same. With one tab the
>   key is consumed without an action or terminal input. A configured popup on
>   either key takes it (VEN-C20).

VEN-C20 Result, Alt+Q sentence extended:
> The fixed bindings also include Alt+Q, listed as "Show the attention inbox" (VEN-C32) under
> every `sidebar`, and Ctrl+Tab and Ctrl+Shift+Tab, listed as "Focus next tab" and "Focus
> previous tab" (VEN-C8).

VEN-C24 Result, after the F6 sentence; EON-C24 Result, after its F6 sentence:
> Ctrl+Tab and Ctrl+Shift+Tab stay in full help and dispatch, without footer hints.

EON-C20 Result, fixed-bindings list extended:
> ... (EON-C31, VEN-C30) under every `sidebar`,
> and Ctrl+Tab and Ctrl+Shift+Tab, listed as "Focus next tab" and "Focus
> previous tab" (VEN-C8).

title: Join emoji modifier and flag sequences into one glyph
description:
## Why
Evidence: rented Mac (kz4p.12; Mac14,3 M2, macOS 27.2 26B123) `mac-proof final` dry run on c9174bd, archive /home/lucca/.cache/eon-agents/claude-rental-work/final1/eon-mac-final-c9174bdc9204-2026-10-29.tar.gz (sha256 6bc7fdfa...7034f0). Manual item 4 (Fonts) FAILED (capture manual/04-fonts.png): Han, kana, é and ä render fine, but 👍🏽 shows as a thumbs-up next to a separate skin-tone swatch and 🇯🇵 as two dashed-box regional-indicator letters J and P. Emoji modifier sequences and flag (regional-indicator pair) sequences are not shaped into one glyph. People see flags and skin tones constantly (agents' output, chat text, git logs); this looks broken.

## Change
First establish whether Linux does the same (installed Eon, `printf '👍🏽 🇯🇵 👨‍👩‍👧\n'`), so the owner is clear: Orbit's cell/grapheme segmentation (libghostty-vt width and grapheme clustering, Unicode mode 2027) or Venus shaping and font fallback (emoji font selection, cluster shaping). Then fix at that owner. Check the contract that covers text shaping/fallback (VEN-C16 for macOS native presentation, and the Venus text contracts) and whether a fixture already covers emoji sequences.

## Acceptance
Red/green on a scene or shaping test with 👍🏽, 🇯🇵 and a ZWJ family sequence; Venus or Orbit checks per their AGENTS.md; installed dogfood on Linux; the next macOS run's Fonts item passes (Yu or the rental).

## Scope
Venus (or Orbit, if segmentation is the cause). Portability disposition recorded. Codex review per AGENTS.md.
close_reason: Orbit part shipped at 5abc671: grapheme clustering on by default, widths verified installed on Linux. Rendering of colour emoji and flags moves to eon-wy1r (Venus).

comments.author: lucca
comments.text:
Plan (Opus, 2026-10-29). Approval as relayed by eon-overseer: Lucca, 2026-10-29, "we need to do more eon stuff / can we fire more agents?", then chose this bead from the overseer's list. Codex implements; Opus plans and gates.

Owner: Orbit, not Venus. Evidence:
- Orbit::spawn (orbit/src/pty.rs) builds the libghostty Terminal without DEC mode 2027 (grapheme clustering). In libghostty-vt mode 2027 defaults off (ghostty src/terminal/modes.zig, `grapheme_cluster` has no `.default = true`). Ghostty the app turns it on in Termio.init's default_modes because its `grapheme-width-method` config defaults to `.unicode` (src/termio/Termio.zig, src/config/Config.zig; inspected at ghostty a887df42, the source already on this machine; Orbit's pin is libghostty-rs 9ede35b -> ghostty 521cf2c5, and the red check confirms it there).
- With 2027 off, each codepoint is printed alone: 👍🏽 becomes a thumbs-up cell plus a wide skin-tone cell, 🇯🇵 two regional-indicator cells, a ZWJ family three emoji. That matches the macOS capture exactly (Apple Color Emoji draws a lone regional indicator as a dashed-box letter), so this is the same on Linux.
- orb-vt-unicode-baselines-i32 already measured it on Linux through Orbit and Venus: legacy mode RI flags 0/20 and ZWJ 2/22; with mode 2027 forced, RI flags, Fitzpatrick and ZWJ all 100%, and Venus placed the clusters correctly. Venus already shapes each cell's whole grapheme string (scene glyph_runs, render/cells.rs), so it needs no change.

Approach: in Orbit::spawn call `terminal.set_default_mode(Mode::GRAPHEME_CLUSTER, true)` (libghostty-vt's MODE_DEFAULT option), so clusters are on from the start and a full reset (RIS, `reset`) keeps them on. A program can still turn them off with DECRST 2027 and query them with DECRQM, which libghostty answers. No wire, protocol, Bend, schema or contract change: frames already carry each cell's full grapheme (frame.rs handles CodepointGrapheme).

Files:
- orbit/src/pty.rs: Orbit::spawn, one call plus a one-line comment.
- orbit/tests/held-attach-shell.sh and orbit/tests/real_pty/held_attach.rs: the rich alternate-screen line also prints 👍🏽, 🇯🇵 and 👨‍👩‍👧 (man, ZWJ, woman, ZWJ, girl); assert each is one Wide cell whose text is the whole sequence. One more gated step prints ESC c (RIS) and the same three sequences and asserts the same, so the reset default is covered.
- orbit/docs/BEHAVIOR.md: present-tense claim (Terminal identity or near it) naming orbit-held-attach and the red evidence; update the held-attach paragraph.
- CHANGELOG.md Unreleased: one entry (flags, skin tones and ZWJ sequences show as one emoji).

Red check: the extended orbit-held-attach fails on the unchanged pty.rs (cluster split across cells). Sensitivity: with `set_mode` in place of `set_default_mode`, the post-RIS assertion fails. Both reported, not shipped.

Checks: `nix build .#checks.x86_64-linux.orbit-held-attach -L` (builds the Orbit package, which runs its unit tests); `cargo fmt --check -p yazelix-orbit`; `nix develop -c cargo clippy --locked -p yazelix-orbit --all-targets -- -D warnings`. Then the full Orbit real-PTY set once on the final tree (`nix flake check` scoped to orbit-* with --keep-going), since a terminal-wide width default could move other checks.

Scope boundary: Orbit only. No Venus, runtime, protocol, contract or configuration change. Out: Venus emoji font selection on macOS (the next macOS run's Fonts item will show whether Apple Color Emoji fallback is enough), any width-method setting.

Configurability: the grapheme width method stays fixed. Mode 2027 is itself the per-program control (DECSET/DECRST 2027, DECRQM), so a program that lays text out per codepoint can turn it off. A user setting would add an Eon config key, a runtime value and an Orbit launch flag for the legacy layout that Ghostty keeps only as a non-default option; that support cost outweighs users differing until someone asks.

Reference gate: not consequential under AGENTS.md (no dependency, wire format, contract, lifecycle, security or trust boundary). Comparable: Ghostty Termio.init default_modes, as above.

Portability: neutral (libghostty mode, same on Linux and Darwin).

Acceptance after landing: installed dogfood on Linux (coordinator): in an Eon terminal, `printf '👍🏽 🇯🇵 👨‍👩‍👧\n'` shows three single emoji; then `reset` and the same. The macOS Fonts item stays for Yu or the rental.

comments.text:
Contract check and live effects (Opus, 2026-10-29, on eon-overseer's condition for the go).

Contract text: no ORB-C or EON-C text promises a width method, wcwidth, legacy per-codepoint widths or mode 2027. ORB-C6 promises only that each cell's grapheme and width reach the client. orb-vt-unicode-baselines-i32 states it makes no terminal-compatibility promise. The only text that states the current behaviour is VEN-C16's Open proof (venus/docs/CONTRACTS.md:1084-1088): "With stock macOS fonts at that revision, ... emoji modifier and flag sequences don't compose, ...; the cause is not diagnosed." A wording change has gone to Lucca through eon-overseer. It is not applied until he approves.

Venus: append_glyph_runs (venus/src/scene.rs) emits one run per authoritative cell at that cell's column. So a clustered emoji is shaped alone in its two cells and cannot shift later cells. That fixes the delimiter drift recorded in orb-vt-unicode-baselines-i32 (Venus cell placement 9953916), and the baseline's mode-2027 delimiter pages passed afterwards.

Running programs and reattach:
- Mode 2027 is terminal state in each Orbit host, set when that host spawns its terminal. Terminals already running keep the host binary they started with and keep clustering off until they are stopped. A program in one of them that queried DECRQM 2027 got "reset" and keeps getting "reset", so what it measured stays true.
- Only a terminal spawned by an Orbit built from this change starts with clustering on. A program started there that queries the mode gets "set" (permanently settable: DECRQM answers from libghostty's mode state).
- A program can still turn clustering off with DECRST 2027. A full reset (RIS, `reset`) puts it back on, since it is the reset default.
- Reattach changes nothing. The mode lives in the Orbit host, not in Venus. A Venus restart or a new attachment shows the same cells, and a reattached old terminal keeps its legacy widths.
- Mixed state after a profile refresh is expected: old terminals split emoji sequences and new ones join them.

comments.text:
Landed tree 0bf246e7 on edge c76610f. One file, eon/crates/eon/tests/workspace_control.rs:
test fixture only, no product, contract or changelog change.

Cause (mac-proof 42688422839 on 032298c, test:eon): the update-check test answered its
prompt through a PTY master and then waited for exit without reading that master again.
The echoed answer stayed in the terminal's output queue, and XNU drains a session
leader's controlling terminal before the leader can exit (proc_exit calls ttywait,
bsd/kern/kern_exit.c; ttywait in bsd/kern/tty.c sleeps with no timeout while the master
is connected). The helper had answered and was stuck in exit, so the test failed with
"decline: helper did not finish". Its ManagedChild guard then asserted while unwinding,
because XNU killpg1 answers EPERM, not ESRCH, when the group has no member left to signal
(bsd/kern/kern_sig.c). That second panic aborted the test binary, no other test's guard
ran, an `eon run` supervisor was left behind, and eon-test then refused to start
eon-manifest, mac-proof and eon-bench. Linux does not drain on exit, so it never showed.
The errno is inferred from the XNU source; the old assertion did not print it, and the new
one does.

Fix:
- `exit_reading_terminals`: waits for a child while reading its terminals' masters, as a
  terminal emulator does. A terminal that ends, fails or reports anything but input is
  retired from the poll set, so the loop never spins. Used by the update-check prompt
  endings (with the different-terminal master as well), its popup block, and
  `at_terminal`. Deadlines and assertions are unchanged.
- `TerminalChild { terminals, guard }`: owns the PTY masters and the ManagedChild. Fields
  drop in order, so a failing test closes the masters before the guard kills and reaps;
  closing a master ends the macOS drain. Both update-test blocks use it.
- `ManagedChild::drop`:
  - while the thread is panicking it never panics again: a best-effort group kill, then
    a bounded 5 s wait that reaps;
  - a failed status check never signals, since the PID may no longer be the child's;
  - outside unwinding the kill must succeed or fail with ESRCH, or with EPERM on Apple,
    and the assertion prints the error;
  - children it reaps while unwinding are recorded (`UNWOUND`) for the regression.
- New regression `a_failing_test_closes_its_terminals_before_reaping_their_child`:
  - runs `sleep 30` as session leader on a fresh PTY under a TerminalChild, with unread
    echo queued, and panics inside catch_unwind;
  - kills and reaps its child itself before any assertion;
  - asserts that the original panic came back (no abort) and that the guard reaped the
    child;
  - on Linux the last master close hangs the session up synchronously, so the child must
    end by that SIGHUP, not by the guard's SIGKILL.

Suite-concurrency finding: the first whole-workspace run on ffffaf4a failed once in the
regression (SIGKILL, not SIGHUP). Under the full suite, another thread's Command::spawn
holds a copy of every descriptor, our master included, between its fork and its exec.
Our close is then not the last, and the hangup lands only when that child execs, after
the guard's kill. The swapped order can never yield SIGHUP, so the regression repeats
the scenario up to 20 times (each try reaped before asserting) and needs one SIGHUP on
Linux; elsewhere one try that the guard reaps suffices.

title: Keep the cursor color across eon attach
description:
## Defect
After `eon attach`, every terminal's cursor draws red instead of its color before detach (blue in the default theme), in single- and multi-column tabs alike. Typing still works and the window is focused. Seen in the `eon-splits-opwv` slice 4 isolated dogfood (2026-10-17) on installed /nix/store/86755wd8yc9b63j6lwvic6grpslyg6kk-eon-0.1.1 and on 4wm3a2j2…-eon-0.1.1, private headless Sway 1.12 (pixman), Nushell prompt. Not caused by the splits work: no splits commit touches cursor color.

## Contract
A reattached presentation shows each terminal's cursor in the same color it had before detach (ORB-C6 rich presentation fidelity; VEN-C1 authoritative presentation). Venus draws `frame.colors.cursor`, falling back to the foreground (venus/src/scene.rs, `Color::from(frame.colors.cursor.unwrap_or(frame.colors.foreground))`), so the first suspect is the cursor color Orbit authors in the fresh attachment frame. The owner is decided by the first finding: Orbit if its attach frame carries the wrong color, Venus if it maps a correct color wrongly.

## Prerequisites
None. Reproduce first: launch Eon in an isolated session, note the cursor color, close the window, run `eon attach`, compare. Check whether a build from before `eon-splits-opwv` (for example 0f8462b) reproduces it, and whether the shell or Starship sets OSC 12.

## Acceptance
- A recorded red/green reproduction naming the owning component and mechanism.
- After the fix, the cursor color before detach equals the color after `eon attach` in installed isolated dogfood, and the owner's existing harness covers the regression where one exists.

## Scope boundary
Cursor color across reattach only. No cursor shape, blink, trail, or theme changes. An `orbit-protocol` change needs its own compatibility classification and user decision.
close_reason: Venus seeds an omitted or random cursor preset from the attached endpoint's identity, so reattaching to one live supervisor keeps the color; a new supervisor picks afresh. Not an Orbit defect. Proof, dogfood and 2-pass ledger in comments. Residual: EonTerm's first window predates its Orbit socket and uses the fallback pick (documented in EON-C1/CONFIGURATION).

comments.author: lucca
comments.text: Root cause found; stopped before a contract change (worktree agent, 2026-10-17). Not Orbit and not ORB-C6: the attach frame carries no explicit cursor color, so Venus draws the cursor body in its cursor-trail color (render/cursor_trail.rs: explicit_color false -> trail_color). With [terminal] cursor_trail_color omitted, Eon passes no --cursor-trail-color (runtime supervisor.rs venus_command), and each Venus process picks a fresh random preset (venus/src/launch.rs random_cursor_color, RandomState per process). eon attach only asks the supervisor to Present, which launches a new Venus, so every reattach rerolls the color for all terminals in the window. This is today's contracted behavior: VEN-C1 says an omitted choice 'selects one of eight Venus presets once per launch and uses it for that process'; EON-C1 says 'Omission emits no override; Venus chooses one random preset per surface' on new or reopened surfaces; docs/CONFIGURATION.md matches. Red, reproduced on edge c6e1f7d, installed /nix/store/scq38y49ba6i1in59mf48k46h17cff2y-eon-0.1.1, private headless Sway 1.12 (pixman, 1280x720), isolated HOME and XDG_RUNTIME_DIR under one mktemp root (cleaned), grim captures, Venus argv read from /proc, no config: cursor pixels launch (61,85,196) = ocean, attach1 (129,84,196) = nebula, attach2 nebula, attach3 ocean (presets at the surface's ~0.77 alpha); all four Venus argv identical, without --cursor-trail-color. Control, same build, cursor_trail_color = 'preset:ice': launch, attach1 and attach2 each show one 128-px cursor block of (94,168,196) = ice. The two red observations in eon-splits-opwv were magma (#ff3b30) rolled by chance. Keeping the color across attach therefore needs a VEN-C1 and EON-C1 change (user decision). No code changed, no commit.

comments.author: lucca
comments.text: Decision, Lucca 2026-10-17 (delegated: 'i will trust your judgement'): option (a). Venus seeds its omitted or 'random' cursor preset from the identity of the endpoint it attaches to (device, inode and ctime of the supervisor's eon.sock, or the Orbit socket for EonTerm), so every Venus launch against one live supervisor keeps one preset and a new supervisor picks afresh. VEN-C1 'once per launch' becomes 'once per live endpoint'; EON-C1 and docs/CONFIGURATION.md follow. title: Investigate showing the cursor tail in the pane being left on a focus change
description:
## Question (Lucca, 2026-10-20)
When focus moves to another pane, the cursor tail is visible only inside the incoming pane. Lucca
wants it to show in the pane being left too, so the trail visibly starts at the old cursor and
travels into the new pane. This bead decides whether that is reasonably doable; it does not ship it.

## Today
Venus draws the tail in `Renderer` cursor drawing (venus/src/render.rs, the block that calls
`build_tail_cursor`): `Renderer::rebuild_dynamic_cursor` (`venus/src/render.rs:2121`) obtains
terminal_paint_clip for the selected terminal and sets RectangleBatch.clip and card_clip;
the old workspace.visible_terminal() reference is stale. The trail's corners start at the
previous cursor rectangle (venus/src/render/cursor_trail.rs `start_jump`), so every part outside
the incoming pane is clipped away, including all of the old pane.

## What to find out
- Which switches leave the old pane on screen: column to column (yes), up/down in a stack (the old
pane collapses to a header), tab switches and tab-crossing traversal (old pane gone). The change
only means anything for the first case, and possibly the header case.
- Clip candidates: the union of the old and new pane terminals, the bounding box of both, or the
whole pane viewport. Check what each lets the trail cross: card gaps, headers, a third column
between them, the scrollback pill, popups (a popup-covered tab has no trail target today).
- Whether `RectangleBatch` supports more than one clip rectangle or a non-rectangular clip, or
whether the trail must be drawn in two passes.
- Where the old pane's rectangle comes from at the frame of the switch (the previous scene's
selected terminal) and what happens when the layout also changes in that frame (sideways move,
column created or removed, resize).
- Whether the old pane's last frame still shows its cursor, so the trail does not appear to leave
from a place without one.

## Contract
VEN-C1 ("A bounded four-corner trail approaches Orbit's exact cursor destination"; healthy pane
switches keep window-local cosmetic motion). Shipping the change would need a VEN-C1 text change
and Lucca's approval; this investigation does not.

## Acceptance
A comment on this bead with: the cases where it applies, the chosen clip shape with its trade-offs,
rough size (files, new state), the risks, and a recommendation (do it, do a narrower version, or
drop it). If doable, a follow-up implementation bead with its contract change for approval. A
throwaway prototype is allowed in a scratch branch or worktree, not on edge.

## Scope boundary
Investigation only. No change to the trail's shape, colours, duration, reset rules, or Orbit.
Portability: neutral (Venus rendering).

## Current investigation entry points (8ebdd69)

RectangleBatch (`venus/src/render.rs:3019`) has one rectangular clip and a card contour; inspect both for union/two-pass candidates. `cursor_trail.rs:104` owns start_jump; render/tests/outlines.rs holds shared trail regressions. Preserve original trade-offs/reset safety and VEN-C1 approval stop. This audit performs no prototype or live-window experiment.
