title: Show the drive's model and temperature in the disk chip's hover
description:
## Why

Lucca, 2026-11-07: "i kinda like the idea of showing cpu names, gpu names, disk names", and temperature. The CPU part is its own bead; this is the disk part, split off because mapping a mount to its drive is the fiddliest piece.

## Goal

The disk hover names the physical drive holding `disk_path`'s filesystem and, when the drive reports one, its temperature:

```
Disk · /home
Samsung SSD 990 PRO 1TB · 38 °C
15.0 GiB free of 100.0 GiB
```

## Shape (record the reference gate before code)

Linux: from the filesystem's device number, follow /sys/dev/block/<maj:min> to the whole disk, through partitions and device-mapper layers (LUKS, LVM: `slaves/`). Several underlying drives (RAID, multi-device btrfs): show none rather than guess. Model from `device/model`; temperature from the drive's hwmon (NVMe "Composite"). Read the model once per path; temperature each sample. macOS: decide whether IOKit/DiskArbitration is worth it; none is acceptable.

## Contract and scope

Feature (venus/docs/PRESENTATION.md). No new keys unless the temperature colours; if it does, its thresholds are configurable (rule 6) and the bar key list in docs/CONTRACTS.md grows (minor). Portability: isolated Linux dependency. Out of scope: GPU and CPU.

## Acceptance

Fixture-directory tests for the sysfs walk (plain partition, LUKS on a partition, LVM, multi-device gives none); one installed observation on Lucca's machine (/home on /dev/nvme1n1p3).

## Evidence, ownership and failure checks (dcaef1c)
Venus already owns filesystem sampling and hover/accessibility text in
`venus/src/system.rs:650` (`DiskUse`) and `:664` (`DiskUse::read`); the sampling
thread is `venus/src/application.rs:3980` (`read_disk`). Extend that owner rather
than introducing Runtime metric state or a second sampler. Reuse the existing
CPU sensor-reading pattern only where it applies to drive sensors.

Missing, unreadable, malformed or ambiguous drive metadata must omit that optional
fact while retaining the filesystem-use chip. Include missing sysfs nodes,
unsupported/network filesystems and cyclic/ambiguous slave links in the fixture
checks; never select an arbitrary member of a multi-drive filesystem. The sysfs
walk must terminate. Hover facts also appear in the accessible description.

## Verification and boundary
One bounded Venus sampling/formatting slice: focused fixture checks plus the
required workspace proof/review, Venus fmt/clippy, and one isolated installed
hover observation. Keep the existing nonblocking sampling path. Record any
unavailable hardware case as a gap. Portability: isolated Linux/sysfs dependency;
macOS may omit model/temperature as the original scope permits. Before any new
configuration or boundary-contract wording, obtain the required contract approval;
a contract's key list is not an automatic minor edit.

title: Say why Venus is retrying when Orbit answers Busy
description:
## Why

When Orbit answers a Venus attachment with `Busy`, Venus shows "Orbit connection lost: Orbit already has a departing presentation client; retrying" over a blank pane. eon-ahzkt's reproduction on 2026-10-30 hit this while another program held the terminal's interactive slot. The text named the wrong cause: no client was departing, another program was attached. Lucca approved fixing the text (eon-ahzkt option 4, 2026-10-30, relayed by eon-overseer: 'yess to all').

eon-agent-parity-a9g0.15 and .16 are closed. In a managed run, retryable `Busy` means an earlier presentation client is still attached or the supervisor has not yet admitted this Venus (ORB-C3). An arbitrary probe cannot take the managed slot.

## Evidence

- venus/src/application.rs:3408 and :4338 map a retryable `Busy` to the text above (edge dcaef1c).
- Screenshot of the blank pane with the banner: ~/.cache/eon-agents/claude-paneread-work/ahzkt/out2/2-t1-while-held.png (installed eon 0.1.8, isolated headless Sway).
- Reproduction record: eon-ahzkt comment, 2026-10-30.

## Contract

Presentation text only, no contract change. The banner text stays fixed rather than configurable: it is diagnostic text with no reason for users to differ. Retry behaviour is unchanged.

## Scope

In scope: one accurate message for a retryable `Busy` in both places, for example "An earlier client still holds this terminal, or this window is not admitted yet; retrying". One owner: a single shared string or helper, not two copies.

Out of scope: retry timing; Orbit admission (a9g0.15); naming Venus (a9g0.16); reporting which process holds the slot (Orbit does not say).

## Acceptance

- Both managed retryable-Busy paths use one accurate diagnostic covering an earlier
  client and pending admission. No retry timing, admission or attachment policy changes.
- A focused existing transport/retry-path test exercises Busy-to-notice mapping and
  preserved retry behavior; avoid a test that only compares a string constant to itself.
- Try one isolated installed observation only if a supported cheap Busy trigger exists
  (for example replacement of the admitted Venus). The old ahzkt probe gets Busy itself
  under ORB-C3 and cannot hold a hidden tab. If no cheap trigger exists, record why the
  focused check is the available proof and the installed banner remains unobserved.

## Verification

Presentation-text route with the consuming retry-path check, required whole-workspace
`nix develop -c eon-test` before code review, Venus fmt/clippy, and the observation
above where feasible. Update CHANGELOG.md for the user-visible text. Portability:
neutral. `managed_busy_is_retryable` is at `venus/src/application.rs:6738` on dcaef1c;
it returns true only for supervised Busy events. No runtime claim is made by planning.

comments.author: lucca
comments.text:
Plan check (prime-beads P2 pass, 2026-11-03, edge a4c0904): the text is still wrong (venus/src/application.rs:2233 and :2927 still say "Orbit already has a departing presentation client; retrying"), but the reproduction path in Acceptance no longer works.

- Since eon-agent-parity-a9g0.15 landed, ORB-C3 interactive admission (orbit/docs/CONTRACTS.md:126-133, 141-144) admits only the process the lease holder names; any other peer gets `Busy` itself. The ORB-C3 proof records that the eon-ahzkt ORBS probe's `Hello` now gets `Busy` (orbit/docs/CONTRACTS.md:192). So "another program holds the terminal" cannot happen in a managed run any more, and the probe cannot hold a hidden tab's terminal for the installed observation.
- The causes of a retryable `Busy` for Venus that remain in a managed run: this Venus is not yet the named process (startup, or a replaced Venus), or an earlier client of the same window is still attached. In an unmanaged run, the first peer wins, so another program can still hold it.

Recommended rescope before starting: one shared string that covers "an earlier client still holds this terminal, or this window is not admitted yet; retrying" (check against the remaining causes), the existing Venus unit test as proof, and an installed observation only if a cheap trigger exists (e.g. a second Venus for the same window); otherwise record why the unit test suffices.

title: Give each Agent popup a stable session ID and resume it by ID
description:

Source: Alma/Pi research, /home/lucca/pjs/refs/alma-pi-research/REPORT.md idea 1 (Pi 1.0's --session-id).

## Bounded delivery plan
This is an epic; each child is one bounded fresh-session slice, with approval
before consequential implementation. All original outcomes remain required.

title: Attached Orbit clients miss frame revisions on macOS (eon-bench gate fails)
description:
## Why

mac-proof 42809718166 on 0c3eee3 (macOS 15.8.2, Apple M1 virtual, 3 CPUs), the first run where eon-bench's gate got past the trace failures fixed by eon-it2ye, shows attached Orbit clients receiving fewer frame revisions than Orbit emitted:

- `eon-bench::gate attached_quick_corpora_obey_frame_invariants` (tests/gate.rs:25): ascii corpus, 96 emitted revisions (3..98) against 67 delivered; 29 missing; no repeats.
- `eon-bench::orbit orbit_runs_a_vtebench_sample_detached_and_attached` (tests/orbit.rs:78): revision_gaps 19 (21 attached frames, revisions 3..75); also frames_after_reply 2, above the later bound of 1.

The trace was complete with zero loss, so this isn't the trace transport. The same tests pass on Linux. Classification: /home/lucca/.cache/eon-agents/eon-mac-bench-work/bead/05-macproof-42809718166.md; artifacts in ../ci-42809718166 beside it.

## Scope

Diagnose where revisions disappear on macOS: frame replacement or coalescing in Orbit's attached send path under a slow client, a Darwin socket-buffer difference, or the gate's expectation being stricter than Orbit's contract (ORB-C) allows. Then either fix Orbit or correct the gate to the contract, without weakening a real guarantee. Related: eon-orbit-coalesce-gu13n (coalescing frames while attached). Read orbit/AGENTS.md.

## Acceptance

Root cause named with evidence; the fix or the gate change approved through plan review; Linux unchanged; the two tests pass on the next mac-proof run.

- `eon/tools/eon-bench/src/orbit/invariants.rs`: `check_revisions(first,
  emitted, delivered)` replaces the equality check: published revisions

- `eon/tools/eon-bench/src/orbit.rs`:

  - `Client` remembers the revision of the frame that completed `attach`;

title: Show what an agent changed during each turn, from the sidebar and the CLI
description:
Users cannot answer "what did this agent just touch?" without leaving their flow for LazyGit. Zed's Delta keeps per-thread edit history between commits (https://delta.dev/deltadb). Eon can get most of the value without parsing transcripts. When a pane's OSC 7501 state enters `working`, the Runtime records `git stash create` in that pane's checkout. That command writes an unreferenced commit of the working tree and leaves the index, refs and files alone. It records a second snapshot when the state leaves `working`. `eon pane changes TARGET [--turn N] [--json]` returns the files and the diff between the two snapshots for the last few turns. A sidebar key opens the same diff read-only in a popup, and a file can open in Helix via `eon edit`. In a checkout that several agents share, the view is labeled "changed here during this turn", not "changed by this agent". This bead settles the per-turn diff half of the eon-el45.5 decision and leaves restore for a separate bead. It needs a new EON-C (snapshot lifetime, bounds, which non-git directories are skipped, how snapshots are garbage-collected) and approval before implementation. Each new value (key, number of turns kept) goes into configuration. First step: a spike that times `git stash create` on a large repository and checks that it never touches the index.

From the Zed Delta threads research (report /home/lucca/.cache/eon-agents/eon-zed-delta-work/report.md, screenshots in shots/ there). Lucca, 2026-11-09, on the report's proposals: "i agree".

## Bounded delivery plan
This is an epic; each child is one bounded fresh-session slice, with approval
before consequential implementation. All original outcomes remain required.

- eon-duebo.1: Prove per-turn Git snapshots preserve work and fit the latency budget.
- eon-duebo.2: Draft and approve the per-turn changes contract.
- eon-duebo.3: Record bounded turn snapshots and expose eon pane changes.
- eon-duebo.4: Open the canonical turn diff from the agent sidebar.

Preserve Lucca's 2026-11-09 approval, the read-only sidebar/CLI diff and eon edit
handoff, configurable key/retention and truthful shared-checkout attribution.
The review-ready status suggestion remains unapproved. Destructive restore stays
with eon-el45.5. Snapshot safety includes untracked edits and Git-GC retention.

## Acceptance and verification
All four children satisfy their acceptance. A completed turn has one canonical
bounded file/diff result for people and agents, with no mutation of user work/index/
refs. Reference gate: the named Zed research plus docs/REFERENCES.md at recorded
revisions. The spike proves cost/safety; exact contract approval precedes delivery.
No spike, build or test is performed by this planning pass.

title: Prove per-turn Git snapshots preserve work and fit the latency budget
description:
## Why and contract
Parent eon-duebo's approved per-turn diff goal needs cheap snapshots that preserve
the user's index, refs and files. The proposed `git stash create` route is not yet
proved, particularly for untracked files. This child is a disposable spike only.

## Scope and reference gate
Read `/home/lucca/.cache/eon-agents/eon-zed-delta-work/report.md` and the owning
docs/REFERENCES.md agent-integration/Superset routes at recorded revisions. Use
private scratch repositories. Compare `git stash create` first and a temporary
index only if needed for the accepted outcome. Identify which Git binary Runtime
could invoke; do not add a distribution requirement. No product code or contracts.

## Acceptance
- Record before/after index bytes/entries, refs and files for staged, unstaged,
  untracked, ignored, deleted and renamed paths, no-op/non-Git paths, linked
  worktrees, in-progress Git operations, concurrent writers and command failures.
- Determine untracked-file coverage and any filter/hook/index-lock effects; record
  truthful limitations and safe failure behavior instead of claiming atomicity.
- Time the mechanism on a named large-repository workload with baseline, exact
  identities, environment and latency distribution. Record object/storage growth,
  ignored/secret-file policy and the protection retention needs against Git GC.
- Recommend the smallest sufficient mechanism or report a blocker. Do not silently
  omit untracked edits or change the parent's user outcome.

## Verification and stop conditions
One bounded scratch spike, recorded commands/results and AP-PERF-001 evidence on
this bead. No runtime profile refresh or shipped behavior claim. Stop if user
work/index/refs cannot be preserved. No destructive restore or real user checkout.

title: Type double quotes and other dead keys under us+intl
description:
## Why

Lucca, 2026-10-21: typing double quotes in Eon is a struggle. A programmer
types quotes constantly, so this blocks daily use.

## Evidence

- Lucca's layouts (COSMIC `xkb_config`): `us,jp` with variants `intl,kana`.
  Under `us+intl`, the quote key is a dead key: Shift+' is dead_diaeresis and '
  is dead_acute. A quote is typed as the dead key followed by Space, and the
  dead key followed by a letter composes (" then a gives ä).
- VEN-C2 (Native semantic interaction): punctuation keys "stay physical", and
  its Boundary accepts no dead keys on macOS; it says nothing about dead keys
  or compose on Linux. Its proof covers only the plain US layout and
  `caps:swapescape`.
- The exact symptom is not recorded yet: nothing appears, the wrong character
  appears, or Space is needed twice. Reproduce it first.

Owner: Venus native input (VEN-C2) resolves native keys and text; Orbit
encodes terminal input (ORB-C5).

## Scope

In scope: reproduce under `us+intl` in an isolated Eon (wdotool with that
keymap); record the symptom and how Venus handles the compositor's dead-key
and compose state; make dead keys compose as they do in other Wayland apps:
dead key then Space gives the plain character, dead key then a letter gives the
composed letter, and a dead key twice gives the character. Keep shortcuts
layout-independent as VEN-C2 requires.

Out of scope: Japanese kana input and other IMEs; macOS dead keys (VEN-C16).

## Acceptance

- Lucca approved the VEN-C2 text change for Linux dead keys and compose.
- Under `us+intl`, ", ', ` and ~ can be typed in an Eon terminal, as can ä, é
  and ã, as in another Wayland terminal; Alt and Ctrl shortcuts still work.

## Verification

- A Venus test for dead-key composition at the input owner.
- One isolated installed observation under `us+intl`.

## Stop Conditions

- Stop for Lucca's approval before changing VEN-C2 text.
- Stop if composition requires a new Wayland protocol or a dependency.
close_reason: Shift held through a dead key and Space now types the composed character in kitty-protocol programs (Claude Code); VEN-C2 updated with Lucca's approval; proved by test and isolated installed observation; profile refreshed.

comments.author: lucca
comments.text: Reproduced 2026-10-21 on installed eon-0.1.1 (/nix/store/spcr8z0m452r8v727895yniflra1dsq9) in isolated headless Sway 1.12, wdotool 0.5.3 keymap us+intl. Symptom (Lucca narrowed it): only with Shift still held at the Space press, and only where the app enables the kitty keyboard protocol (Claude Code; not legacy nushell). A raw reader with CSI >1u got a, ESC[32;2u, b ' c ¨ d for: Shift+dead then Shift+Space, dead then Space, Shift+dead twice. Dead then Space, dead then letter and dead twice already compose (winit's xkb compose); foot agrees. Cause: venus/src/input.rs layout_metadata infers consumed Shift only for Key::Character, so Space carrying composed text kept Shift as a binding mod and Ghostty's kitty encoder sent Shift+Space instead of the text. Fix: Space counts " " as its unshifted text, so Shift is consumed when the text differs. Red/green: derives_layout_metadata_without_a_keyboard_map fails without the arm (left (None, 0), right (Some(' '), SHIFT)) and passes with it. Note for later proof: wdotool runs each call on its own virtual keyboard, so a held modifier must be inside each chord (shift+dead_acute, shift+space); physical keysym names (apostrophe, grave) don't reach dead keys, keysym names (dead_acute) do.

comments.text: Lucca approved 2026-10-21 the VEN-C2 change: Result gains the Shift-consumed rule with Space's unshifted text a space (dead-key text on Space arrives as text with Shift held); Boundary gains acceptance of Linux dead keys and compose sequences from the keymap's compose table.

Claude Code 2.1.303 pushes only CSI >1u or >5u.

comments.author: lucca
comments.text: Reference gate (consequential: VEN-C2 contract change). Behavior: a character a dead key composes on Space with Shift still held reaches kitty-protocol programs as text. Owners: winit's xkb host path composes; Venus input (layout_metadata) owns the consumed-modifier report; Orbit/Ghostty's encoder owns the bytes (ORB-C5). Routes read: venus/docs/REFERENCES.md (winit 0.30.13 native-event boundary; Ghostling/libghostty-rs ownership), the eon-venus-keysym-named-keys-chnh Ghostty precedent. Comparable: Ghostty 8c425a7bd57de848aa83cb9b003b1ecd6037c56a (~/pjs/refs/ghostty-7501/repo), src/apprt/gtk/class/surface.zig:1396-1404 takes consumed_mods from GDK's per-key xkb consumed modifiers; its kitty encoder (src/input/key_encode.zig:126-214) sends text only when binding mods (mods minus consumed) are empty and report-all is off. Rejected: deriving consumed mods from xkb's per-key consumed modifiers (Ghostty GTK's approach): xkeyboard-config 2.47 pc symbols give <SPCE> one level ({[ space ]}), also under us(intl), so xkb consumes nothing on Space and Shift would stay a binding mod, the same CSI 32;2u; winit 0.30.13 also exposes no consumed-mods API. Rejected: changing Orbit's encoder input (Orbit already passes Venus's consumed mods through). Decision: extend Venus's existing text-vs-unshifted-text inference to Space (unshifted text " "). Check: derives_layout_metadata_without_a_keyboard_map red/green plus an isolated installed raw-byte observation under CSI >1u. Symptom as Lucca reported it, 2026-10-21: 'if i hold shift and the double quote key, and then space, while still holding shift, nothing happens. i have to release shift first' and 'this does not happen in nushell, only in claude'. The Venus test covers the Shift-consumed rule; composition itself is winit's and is covered by the installed observation.

title: Explore bolder hints bar designs: islands, hold-to-reveal, live state
description:
## Why

Lucca, 2026-11-06, after the 13-inch text cuts (eon-yvhke): "there are bolder ideas we can explore in the future for the hints bar ... like islands can toggle open and close, and only one island can be open at a time; it could be so that (?) would fit entirely and would incentivize users to learn the keys by heart. Help me brainstorm hints bar ideas." Then: "you decide" (on filing them). Originally filed as ideas only. The approved hover-popup and related layout slices subsequently shipped as eon-e3a1z.1-.4; the other ideas below remain candidates, with no design chosen.

## Ideas (overseer's brainstorm, with the overseer's picks marked)

Show less, only when wanted
1. **Accordion islands** (Lucca): each modifier group collapses to its keycap (`[A] [C-A] [A-S]`); opening one closes the others; the last-used group may default open. Also a graceful-narrowing step: collapse groups to keycaps before dropping hints. (pick, with 2)
2. **Hold a modifier to reveal its group** (which-key style): holding Alt ~300 ms opens the Alt island, releasing closes it; Alt+Shift opens that group. Teaches by reaching. Must never consume or delay Alt for terminal apps (Helix). (pick)
3. **Context hints everywhere**: extend the inbox's own-keys swap to every popup and state (Files shows Yazi keys, zoomed shows unzoom, moving shows move keys).

Learn, then get out of the way
4. **Fade what you know**: count key use locally; hints used often fade or drop and free space for unlearned keys. Needs a local usage-tracking design. (later)
5. **Teach on mouse use**: after a mouse action that has a key, flash that hint briefly.
6. **Tip slot**: one slot rotates lesser-known keys (Alt+Z quick search, Ctrl+Tab, Alt+G) per new tab.

Make the bar earn its space
7. **Clickable hints**: clicking a hint runs its action (needs the matching CLI path per AGENTS.md rule 5 already exists for each action).
8. **Live state instead of static labels**: e.g. `2 waiting` (Alt+Q on hover) only when agents wait, instead of a fixed inbox hint; the bar as the workspace status line, fitting an ADE. (pick)
9. **User pins**: `[hints] pin`/`hide` in configuration.
10. **Glyph mode**: icons instead of words with word tooltips; compact but harder to learn.

## Risks to settle in any design

- Accessibility: hints are read-only text today; collapsing islands changes what a screen reader announces.
- Alt handling: reveal-on-hold must not change key delivery to terminals.
- Configurability (AGENTS.md rule 6) for any new delay, threshold or default.

## Current planning state and acceptance
The four recorded children are closed. The remaining ideas are a research backlog,
not approval to implement all ten. Preserve Lucca's hover-popup choice (comment
2026-11-06) and the accepted child designs. Before another implementation slice,
record the selected user outcome, keyboard/accessibility behavior, configuration
choices, CLI parity for any new workspace action and its cheapest installed check.
Any chosen consequential boundary change still needs contract approval.

Planning acceptance: the overseer records whether to keep the remaining candidates
for later selection or finish this idea container after the shipped children; no
candidate is silently treated as selected. This pass leaves status and priority as-is.

title: Collapse hint groups to keycaps with a hover keys popup
description:
## Why

Lucca, 2026-11-06, choosing the first step from eon-e3a1z's ideas: "the island may never need to open, if you hover and see a keys popup instead"; then "1 is nice, but idk what we'd do with so much space. eon's version number could be moved there. maybe the session pill too. yeah, go on 1, it could open doors".

## Scope (slice 1)

- Each modifier group in the bottom hints bar collapses to its keycap (`[A]`, `[CA]`, `[AS]`); hovering a keycap shows a small popup listing that group's keys and descriptions (the same hints the expanded group shows today, including the popup hints that no longer fit). Nothing expands in the bar itself.
- Keyboard and screen-reader access stay at least as good as today: the full list remains in Alt+/ behind the always-visible `?`, and each collapsed keycap has an accessible name that says what it holds. Hold-to-reveal (eon-e3a1z idea 2) is a later slice, not this one.
- Built after eon-yvhke (the 13-inch cuts) lands, on top of its hint strings and legend.

## Before any build: mockups for Lucca

A planner first renders mockups at 1280 logical px (PNG, real system sans metrics, today's colours) for: (A) collapsed keycaps with one popup open; (B) A plus the Eon version moved from the header to the bottom bar; (C) B plus the session (workspace) pill moved to the bottom bar. Lucca picks which of B and C, if any, join this slice; the rest stays in eon-e3a1z.

## Acceptance (slice 1)

- Collapsed keycaps at every width; hover popup lists the group's keys; popup never takes keyboard focus or changes the terminal's focus.
- Accessible names for the keycaps; Alt+/ unchanged.
- Docs (docs/USAGE.md hints paragraph, venus/docs/INTERACTION.md) and any contract sentence that describes the expanded footer; CHANGELOG; tests; isolated installed screenshots with a popup open.

# eon-e3a1z.1 implementation notes (slice B)

Base: edge 5faac62 (includes eon-yvhke and eon-y22fl). Plan:
/home/lucca/.cache/eon-agents/eon-e3a1z-1-plan-work/PLAN.md. Overseer decisions
taken as recommended: version hides with the bar; short-legend fallback; popup
keeps its title row.

## What changed

- `venus/src/scene.rs`
  - `ShortcutHint` gains `modifier_names` (full names, e.g. `Alt+Shift`) and
    `description` (full-help text).
  - New `ShortcutHintGroup` (name, legend, keycap rect, hover rect, rows,
    accessible_label). `ShortcutHintPiece` loses `modifiers`/`key_offset`.
  - `ShortcutHintsScene::new(hints, size, metrics, version: Option<f32>, measure)`
    partitions hints into groups (first-appearance order) and modifier-less
    pieces, lays out one cluster (keycaps then pieces, one padding apart)
    centred on the window centre, and applies the narrow steps in order:
    centred-and-clear, shifted before the version, version hidden and
    re-centred, pieces dropped by (priority, index), short legends. The old
    group-spreading code is gone. `complete` = every piece shown, no short
    legends, version shown when requested.
  - `WorkspaceScene` drops the version from header label fitting and placement;
    `version` is built from `hints.version` + `bar.version` (same label,
    tooltip and description text). No hints -> no version.
  - `WorkspaceHit::HintGroup(usize)`; `hit_test` checks group hover rects after
    the header items/drag region and before sidebar rows, panes, columns and the
    terminal.
- `venus/src/application.rs`: passes the version text width
  (`"EON <v>".len() * metrics.width`) when `version` is listed; maps
  `HintGroup` to `set_hint_group_hovered`; adds `HintGroup` to the CursorMoved
  redraw set and to the press arm that does nothing (no focus change, no drag;
  `button_reaches_terminal` is false off the terminal).
- `venus/src/application/shortcuts.rs`: fills `modifier_names` (non-compact
  `physical_modifiers_label_for`) and `description` (fixed shortcut: its full-help
  label; popup: its configured label; merged `focus`/`mv pane`/`mv tab` get fixed
  phrases; merged arrow pairs keep their first line, unused since pieces show no
  description). Restores `Action::Move(Left | Right) => ("mv tab", 3)`.
- `venus/src/render/chrome.rs`: `hint_group_hovered` in `HeaderInteraction`
  (part of the content cache key) with setter; footer draws keycaps (hovered =
  `CHROME_HIGHLIGHT`), pieces, and the version (plain `VERSION_TEXT`, cell font)
  at the hints' right end; the header loop no longer draws the version. Tooltip
  placement extracted into pure `tooltip_edge` / `tooltip_room` /
  `tooltip_rect` / `hint_popup_rows` plus `place_tooltip` (fill, radius,
  padding, 40-em cap, `text_overlay`, scrollback-pill yield kept). Header items
  open Below; the version tooltip and the keycap popup open Above
  (`hints.rect.top - padding/3`).
- `venus/src/accessibility.rs`: HINTS is a `Role::Group` labelled "Eon shortcut
  hints"; one `Role::Label` per keycap (NodeId 23+index, label `<full names>
  shortcuts`, value the group's chords `Alt+Shift+T — Create tab; ...`, keycap
  bounds), one Label (NodeId 22) for expanded pieces. VERSION moves after HINTS
  in the root child order with footer bounds; name/value unchanged; no actions.
- Docs: USAGE, CONFIGURATION, venus INTERACTION and PRESENTATION; CHANGELOG
  entry; contract step in 01-contract-step.md.

## Deviations from the plan (each with the reason)

1. `ShortcutHint` carries the full names as a new field `modifier_names`
   instead of a separate "helper giving each group's full name": the scene
   needs the full name per group and only `shortcuts.rs` knows the platform;
   the helper is `physical_modifiers_label_for(platform, mods, false)` called
   where the hint is built.
2. The group struct names: plan's `modifiers`/`name`/`short: bool` became
   `name` (full) + `legend` (what the keycap shows); same information.
3. The footer's Scrollback shortening (`Scroll` unless configured) is removed:
   popup entries always sit in a keycap group now, so their bar label is never
   drawn, and the popup row uses the configured name as planned. No legacy
   code. The yvhke fit test's `Scroll`/`History` assertions went with it.
4. Cluster gaps: one padding between every cluster item (keycaps and expanded
   pieces), replacing the old 0.75-padding hint gap; the plan specified one
   padding between keycaps and was silent on pieces.
5. `hint_keycap_hover_hits_its_group` is its own test as planned; the shared
   one-pane snapshot moved into a helper `one_pane_snapshot()` in
   `scene/tests/bar.rs`.
6. `render/tests::hint_popup_sits_above_its_keycap_inside_the_window` lives in
   `render/chrome.rs` tests and checks the pure placement functions, because
   building the popup itself needs a Renderer, which only exists in the
   ignored live-display tests. "No hover, no popup" is structural
   (`build_header_tooltip` builds the popup only for `hint_group_hovered`) and
   is left to the installed observation.
7. `application/tests::hovering_a_hint_keycap_keeps_focus` is not added: the
   application's pointer handlers run only in the ignored native-display
   harness, and Testing Discipline says not to ship ignored tests merely to
   accompany a patch. Focus safety rests on code (HintGroup maps to no
   `hovered_header`, the press arm returns `None`, and the terminal never sees
   the press) and on the installed observation (hover and press on a keycap
   leave the selected pane and terminal focus unchanged).
8. The popup's "more" row is the fixed `Alt+/ lists all`, as the plan says; on
   macOS the viewer key is still written `Alt+/`, as the header's Shortcuts
   tooltip already writes it ("Keyboard shortcuts — Alt+/").

## Humans and Agents

Hover, the hints bar and its popup are Venus-local view state, a listed
exception in docs/AGENT-RULES.md Humans and Agents. The version stays readable
by agents through `eon versions` / `eon window ls`. No window action added.

## Configurability (rule 6)

Rule 6 covers presentation values too. These are new things a person sees or
feels, and each stays fixed:

- Keycap names and the short legends `A`, `CA`, `AS`, `CAS`. They come from the
  platform's existing modifier names (`physical_modifiers_label_for`) and the
  existing short labels, so they follow the bindings with no knob of their own.
- The popup's last row, `Alt+/ lists all`. It names the existing Shortcuts
  binding and the existing viewer. A separate text setting could drift from
  that binding, and nobody needs to reword it.
- Popup geometry: left edge at the keycap's, bottom padding/3 above the bar,
  kept inside the window, never taller than the space between header and
  bar. Also the narrow-window step order and its thresholds. All of it derives
  from the existing `CellMetrics` (padding, line height) and from measured text
  widths; there are no pixel constants. Knobs would add support cost: more
  layouts to test across fonts and scales, for no user need.
- Colours: the hover fill is the existing `CHROME_HIGHLIGHT`, the keycap
  `HINT_KEYCAP`, the version `VERSION_TEXT`, and the popup reuses the tooltip
  fill and text colours. The palette already sets all of them.
- Dismissal (round 1): Escape or a pointer press hides the popup until the
  pointer leaves the keycap. This is standard tooltip behaviour, not a tunable.

Not adding a setting to keep the old expanded bar was accepted (Lucca, top of
the plan). `[bar] widgets`' `version` still decides whether the version shows.

## Round 1 changes (review fixes)

- Rebased onto edge 95a1da0. The CHANGELOG conflict with `eon-i3th2` and
  `eon-7cf0y.22` was resolved by keeping both entries. The chrome.rs spinner
  hunks merged cleanly.
- Popup dismissal: `HintPopupLatch` (application/shortcuts.rs).
  - `popup(hovered)` shows the hovered keycap's popup unless it was dismissed.
    A dismissal ends once the hovered keycap changes, including to none.
  - `dismiss()` hides the popup that is open.
  - The application calls `dismiss()` on any Escape press (`KeyboardInput`,
    before key resolution) and on any pointer press (`MouseInput`, before the
    viewer and the hit handling). It only requests a redraw. The key or press
    then flows on unchanged, so focus and key delivery don't change.
  - The renderer keeps the keycap's hover fill while the popup is dismissed
    (`set_hint_group_hovered(group, popup)`).
  - A resize recomputes the scene; a keycap still under the pointer keeps its
    dismissal.
- Alt popup row: "Focus by direction, or a tab by position" replaces the plan's
  "Focus a column, pane or tab by position". This is a deviation from the plan
  text: HJKL focus by direction.
- Docs: `Escape terminal`, not `Esc terminal`, matching what the bar draws.
  USAGE, INTERACTION and CHANGELOG describe the dismissal.
- `ShortcutHintsScene::complete` also requires the bar to be tall enough.
- The expanded-keys accessible label is named "Other shortcuts".
- Keycap legends are chosen once, at placement, from the full name or the
  short legend.
- `scene::tests::bar::one_pane_snapshot()` is shared, as
  `pub(crate) mod tests` under `cfg(test)`. The render popup test uses it.
- The width sweep is now `sweep_footer`, which also reports which steps
  showed. It runs with the character-count measure and with
  EON_VENUS_TEST_SANS_FONT (DejaVu Sans), at scales 1 and 2. Both must show
  all five steps: centred, shifted, version hidden, pieces dropped, short
  legends. The DejaVu run also checks that the cluster at 1280 is complete
  and centred.
- venus/CHANGELOG.md has the VEN-C21 entry. The EON-C32 proof sentence is
  appended, and its Result line is rewrapped.
- Recorded deviation, not done (Opus 7): on macOS the popup's last row still
  reads `Alt+/` while its title uses `Option` names. Same as the header
  tooltip; passing the viewer chord through the scene is left for later.

comments.text:
# eon-e3a1z.2 plan (rescoped): move the clock to the bottom bar's left end

Base: edge 0aa82f2 (slice B, eon-e3a1z.1, landed as 787feb8).

## Rescope

The first plan moved the session (workspace) pill to the bottom bar. Mid-way, Lucca
reconsidered, because that made the bar unhideable. He weighed four options: give up on
the pill in the bottom bar so the bar can hide again; pill and version on either side;
the pill under the sidebar only; and moving the clock widget to the bar's left edge. His
decision, relayed by eon-overseer on 2026-11-06, was option 1 plus the clock. In
Lucca's words: **"lets do it"**.

- The session pill stays where it is today, in the header next to the Eon logo, and the
  focus order stays as today. The earlier tab-order and "bar stays for the label alone"
  approvals are void. The pill-move diff was reverted. It is kept for reference in
  `../pill-move-abandoned.patch`.
- The clock widget moves from the header to the bottom bar's left edge: clock at the
  left, keycaps centred, version at the right. Alt+Shift+B hides the whole bar again,
  clock included.
- The pill-to-sidebar-footer idea is decided later, with eon-7cf0y.5. It is not touched
  here.

## Behaviour

- **Bottom bar.** While the hints show and `clock` is in `[bar] widgets` with a known
  local time, the clock sits at the bar's left end, one padding from the window's left
  edge. It keeps its look and format:
  - a rounded outline at the cards' border width with no fill;
  - `HH:MM` in the cell font;
  - its width is five cells plus padding on each side, so it never shifts as minutes
    change.

  It is as tall as the tab pills, clamped to the bar, and centres on the hint line. Its
  hover (the date and UTC offset) opens above it, as the version's does. Hiding the
  hints hides it. It has no action.
- **Header.** The clock leaves the widget group, so the quota chips, CPU, RAM and disk
  get its room. The header's drop order becomes: the Eon logo first, then disk, RAM and
  CPU, then quota chips one by one. The logo's "everything shows" rule no longer counts
  the clock, so the logo needs less room to show.
- **Narrow windows (bottom bar).** The cluster centres on the window, clamped to stay one
  padding clear of the clock and the version. When it does not fit, things give way in
  this order:
  1. the version hides;
  2. the clock hides;
  3. hints without modifiers drop whole;
  4. the keycaps switch to short legends.

  Keycaps never drop. This is the overseer's suggestion, with the existing modifier-less
  drop placed after the clock. Those hints (`Escape terminal`, the arrows) are needed
  while the chrome has focus, and the clock is information `date` also gives.

  Approximate thresholds, at default typography with Noto Sans 16 (cell 10 px, padding
  12, clock 74 px, full keycaps 323 px, short legends 163 px, version 100 px):

  | Window | Clock | Keycaps | Version |
  | --- | --- | --- | --- |
  | 1280 | 12-86 | full, centred 479-801 | 1168-1268 |
  | 800 | 12-86 | full, centred 239-561 | 688-788 |
  | 545-571 | shown | full, shifted left to clear the version | shown |
  | 433-545 | shown | full, centred or shifted right to clear the clock | hidden |
  | 400 | hidden | full, centred | hidden |
  | 330 | hidden | short, centred | hidden |

  The packaged-font sweep (DejaVu Sans, the test sandbox's `EON_VENUS_TEST_SANS_FONT`)
  records the measured thresholds in the proof.

## Code (Venus only; no Runtime, EONW or configuration change)

1. `venus/src/scene.rs`
   - `ShortcutHintsScene::new(hints, size, metrics, version, clock, measure)`. The new
     `clock: Option<f32>` is its width. A new field, `clock: Option<SceneRect>`, holds the
     drawn outline. One loop over the steps above replaces the version-then-loop
     placement, and `complete` also needs the clock shown when it was requested.
   - `WorkspaceScene`:
     - the header readings lose the clock and its widest-layout placeholder;
     - `clock` comes from `hints.clock` together with `bar.clock`'s text, tooltip and
       description, as `version` does;
     - `hit_test` keeps `WorkspaceHit::Clock` on the new rect.
   - A nominal tab-pill height helper, shared with `bar_pill_band`.
2. `venus/src/application.rs` (`rebuild_workspace_measurements`): pass the clock's width
   while `clock` is listed and `self.clock` is `Some`.
3. `venus/src/render/chrome.rs`: draw the clock in the footer pass, as an outlined
   widget with its text centred, and remove it from the header readings loop. The
   tooltip's placement above the bar follows from `tooltip_edge`.
4. `venus/src/accessibility.rs`: `CLOCK` leaves the header's sorted items and goes
   before `HINTS` (drawn order: the bar left to right), with the footer bounds. Its
   name, value and lack of actions do not change.
5. The other `ShortcutHintsScene::new` callers pass `None`.

## Tests (each names the failure it catches)

- `scene/tests/bar.rs::footer_centres_full_name_keycaps_and_keeps_the_version_clear`:
  the sweep (200..2400, scales 1 and 2, both measured and packaged-font widths) runs
  with and without a clock. It checks:
  - the clock sits at the start, centred on the line, inside the bar, at its requested
    width;
  - the cluster stays one padding clear of the clock and the version, and is off centre
    only to clear one of them;
  - the step order: the version hides before the clock, the clock before pieces drop,
    and pieces before short legends;
  - widening never hides anything;
  - `complete`;
  - the step-sweep shows every step;
  - at 1280 the bar is complete and centred with the clock.

  Catches overlap, a wrong drop order, and a no-clock regression.
- Header: `local_clock_yields_first_and_has_no_actions` and
  `readings_yield_after_the_clock_and_have_no_actions` (wherever they live) become the
  footer clock test plus the header order disk, RAM, CPU. The clock never shows in the
  header, and the Eon icon no longer needs the clock's room. Catches the clock
  reappearing in the header, or the header order regressing.
- Accessibility: `CLOCK` sits before `HINTS` with footer bounds and no actions, and is
  absent while the hints are hidden.
- Hover and dismissal: hit-testing the clock gives `Clock`; one pixel outside it, and
  the band above, do not. The tooltip anchor lies in the bar, so it opens above it.
- Run `nix develop -c eon-test -p yazelix-venus`, then venus `cargo fmt --check` and
  clippy `-D warnings`.

## Contract text (minor; overseer approves)

- **EON-C32 Result.** Add `clock` beside the `version` exception: "except `clock` and
  `version`, which sit at the left and right ends of the bottom shortcut hints while
  they show". Add a Status amendment line.
- **VEN-C21 Result.**
  - "Tab pills and the quota, CPU, RAM and clock widgets share one height" drops the
    clock.
  - The icon's room drops "and the clock" and "the clock" from the live values.
  - The a11y order sentence is unchanged; it does not name the clock.
  - Add a Status amendment line.
- **EON-C33** does not mention the clock, so it is unchanged.
- `01-contract.md` records the exact old and new text.

## Docs

- `docs/USAGE.md` ~257-270: the clock sentence and the header drop order. The hints
  paragraph covers the clock at the left and the narrow-window order.
- `docs/CONFIGURATION.md` ~191-203: the `clock` exception and the drop order.
- `venus/docs/PRESENTATION.md` and `venus/docs/INTERACTION.md`: grep `clock`.
- `CHANGELOG.md`: one entry.
- `venus/CHANGELOG.md`: a VEN-C21 entry.

## Configuration, Rule 6, Humans and Agents

- The `clock` widget name does not name the header. `[bar] widgets` stays the one key,
  so nothing is renamed. The list order no longer affects where the clock sits, as with
  `version` (documented).
- There are no new values. The clock's height (the tab pills'), its gaps (one padding)
  and the drop order are presentation, derived from existing typography and bar
  spacing. A setting would only re-skin geometry that font size and `padding` already
  control, and the drop order is a layout rule, not a preference.
- Humans and Agents: hover and the hints bar are Venus-local view state. Agents already
  read the time from the system clock (`date`). There is no new action.

## Proof route

Installed UI, plus contract text. Unit tests, fmt and clippy, then an isolated
installed observation on the final tree. The candidate is built with
`nix build --out-link`, with an isolated root and display, never the profile, and never
taking desktop focus. Captures:

- 1280, with the clock bottom-left and a keycap popup;
- 800;
- 400 (clock hidden);
- 330;
- the clock's hover tooltip above it;
- Alt+Shift+B hiding the whole bar, clock included;
- the header without the clock;
- the focus in effect named in each capture, and typing from terminal focus;
- an AccessKit dump.

## Decisions (each with a recommendation; proceeding with them)

1. **The clock's look.** Recommend keeping its outlined chip, so the widget moves
   unchanged ("keep the clock's existing ... format"). The alternative is plain text
   like the version.
2. **Drop order.** Recommend version, clock, modifier-less hints, then short legends, as
   above.

comments.text:
# eon-e3a1z.2 implementation notes

## History

1. **First plan (session pill to the bottom bar).**
   - I implemented it.
   - The overseer approved its Tab-order change and the "bar stays for the label alone"
     rule (Lucca: "ok").
   - Then a HOLD, then a RESCOPE: option 1 plus the clock (Lucca: "lets do it").
   - I reverted the pill-move diff with `git apply -R` from the saved
     `../pill-move-abandoned.patch`. That kept it recoverable; dcg blocks
     `git checkout --`.
   - Nothing about the pill or the focus order is in the candidate.
2. **Rescoped work.** It reuses the bottom-bar layout loop written for the pill, with the
   clock as the left-end item and the drop order the overseer suggested.

## What changed (candidate tree 0187a74a)

- `venus/src/scene.rs`
  - `ShortcutHintsScene::new` takes `clock: Option<f32>` (its width) and records
    `clock: Option<SceneRect>`.
  - One loop replaces slice B's two-phase placement. The cluster centres, clamped to
    stay one padding clear of the clock and the version. It gives way in this order:
    version, clock, modifier-less hints by (priority, index), short legends. When even
    the short legends overflow, it clips from the start, as before.
  - `complete` also needs the clock shown when it was requested.
  - The clock is as tall as the tab pills (`nominal_pill_height`, now shared with
    `bar_pill_band`), clamped to the bar, and centred on the hint line.
  - `WorkspaceScene`:
    - the header readings lose the clock and its widest-layout placeholder, so the
      header's drop order is disk, RAM, CPU, then quota chips;
    - the Eon icon's widest layout no longer reserves the clock;
    - `clock` comes from `hints.clock` plus `bar.clock`'s text, like `version`.
- `venus/src/application.rs`
  - Passes the clock's width (five cells plus padding on each side) while `clock` is
    listed and Venus has a clock reading.
  - **Deviation from the plan:** when the clock's presence changes (the first reading,
    or the time zone going away), the bar's layout is rebuilt
    (`rebuild_workspace_measurements` plus `content_changed`). The hints scene is built
    only on measurement rebuilds. Without this, the first clock reading after the
    window's first rebuild would not show until some other rebuild. Minute-to-minute
    changes only repaint, as before.
  - No unit harness covers this application path: the application tests that build a
    real `Application` need a native display. The installed observation's `startup.png`
    (taken before any key press) covers it. Recorded as such in the proof.
- `venus/src/render/chrome.rs`: the clock is drawn in the footer pass with
  `push_bar_widget` (same outline) and centred `HH:MM` in cell monospace, in
  `SECONDARY_TEXT` as before. It is removed from the header readings loop. Its tooltip
  goes through the existing `tooltip_edge`, which opens it above anything in the bar.
- `venus/src/accessibility.rs`: `CLOCK` leaves the header's sorted items and is pushed
  after `PANE_PANEL`, before `HINTS`. Its role, value and lack of actions are unchanged.
- Tests:
  - `local_clock_yields_first_and_has_no_actions` is renamed
    `local_clock_leads_the_bottom_bar_and_has_no_actions` and rewritten;
  - `readings_yield_after_the_clock_and_have_no_actions` is renamed
    `readings_yield_disk_first_and_have_no_actions`;
  - `eon_orders_and_omits_bar_items` and `local_clock_names_minute_date_and_offset` are
    updated;
  - the footer sweep is extended (clock and no clock; the four widths with the
    packaged font);
  - the header widget-height test in `scene/tests/workspace.rs` no longer expects a
    header clock.

## Decisions taken (each recommended in 00-plan.md)

1. **The clock keeps its outlined chip.** In the footer its outline is the full
   five-cell-plus-padding rect. In the header the outline was inset by padding/3 on
   each side, so the footer chip is 2*padding/3 wider (8 px at default). The footer has
   no neighbouring chips to keep apart.
2. **Drop order:** version, clock, modifier-less hints, short legends.

## Not changed, with reasons

- **No configuration key renamed.** `clock` does not name the header, and
  `[bar] widgets` stays the one list. The list position no longer moves the clock,
  which is documented in CONFIGURATION, PRESENTATION and EON-C32.
- **Runtime's generated config comment** ("Eon Bar widgets, in display order",
  `runtime/crates/eon-runtime/src/managed_environment.rs:617`) is untouched. It was
  already loose for `version` after slice B. Changing it is a Runtime and
  configuration-corpus change outside this Venus-only slice.
- **Rule 6.** There are no new user-visible values. The clock's height (the tab pills')
  and gaps (one padding) derive from existing typography and spacing. The drop order
  is a layout rule, not a preference: a setting would only re-skin geometry that font
  size and `padding` already control.
- **Humans and Agents.** Hover and the hints bar are Venus-local view state. Agents
  read the time with `date`. There is no new action.

title: Group the keys popup into Actions, Popups and Custom sections with short labels
description:
## Why

Lucca, 2026-11-06, on the keys popup that hovering a hints-bar keycap shows (eon-e3a1z.1, .3),
with a capture of the Alt+Shift group: "it's a bit too much information / like a wall of text / i
was thinking we could have sections like: actions, popups, custom popups (shown only if the user
configured any)". He agreed ("i agree") to the overseer's variation below.

The wall comes from mixing two kinds of entries in one list: actions with sentence-long labels
("Detach: hide the window, keep terminals running") and one-word popup names. The Alt+Shift group
is 16 rows.

## Design (agreed)

- **Sections side by side.** "Actions" in the left column; "Popups" in the right column, with a
  "Custom" section under it holding user-configured popups, shown only when there are any.
  Section headers are dim and small.
- **Short labels in the popup.** Actions use short verbs ("New tab", "Close tab", "Zoom pane",
  "New window", "Detach", "Hints", "Sidebar"). The full sentence stays in the Alt+/ shortcut
  viewer, and shows as the tooltip when the pointer rests on an entry in the keys popup.
- **Order actions by what they act on:** tab, pane, window, then chrome toggles.
- **Overflow:** when a group has too many entries for the window height (Ctrl+Alt+Shift, or many
  custom popups), columns wrap rather than the popup growing past the window.
- The same layout applies to every modifier group's keys popup.

Target for the Alt+Shift group: about 9 rows instead of 16.

## Contract

None: presentation feature (docs/AGENT-RULES.md Contract-Driven Method). Behavior is documented
in venus/docs/PRESENTATION.md (hints bar / keys popup) and docs/USAGE.md. The short labels must
come from the one owner of each action's labels (runtime entries, sent to Venus as resolved
values); Venus parses no configuration and must not hard-code its own copy of action names.

## Configurability (rule 6)

Record a disposition before code: the short labels and section names are product text. The
planner recommends whether they stay fixed (with a reason allowed by docs/AGENT-RULES.md
#configurability) or are configurable, and the overseer decides or asks Lucca.

## Prerequisites

eon-igae.14.5 (chip icons, also Venus chrome) lands first, to avoid conflicting edits.

## Acceptance

- Installed keys popup for Alt+Shift shows Actions and Popups side by side, with Custom only when
  custom popups are configured; about 9 rows with the default configuration.
- Action entries show short labels; resting the pointer on an entry shows its full sentence; the
  Alt+/ viewer still shows full sentences.
- A group too tall for a small window wraps into more columns and stays inside the window.
- AccessKit announces each section and entry, with the full sentence available to screen readers.

## Scope

In: Venus keys popup layout and rendering, the short-label field and its single owner, docs
(PRESENTATION.md, USAGE.md, CONFIGURATION.md if anything becomes configurable), CHANGELOG.
Out: the hints bar itself, the Alt+/ viewer layout, the Commands popup, hold-to-reveal and other
eon-e3a1z ideas.

## Verification

Venus suite through `nix develop -c eon-test -p yazelix-venus` plus fmt and clippy for changed
crates; one isolated installed capture of the Alt+Shift popup with and without custom popups, and
at a small window height. Portability disposition: neutral.
close_reason: Keys popup grouped into Actions and Popups with short labels; Custom follows qkq8.3

title: Align Agents sidebar line 2 in columns: tag or label, age, ID, marker lane
description:
## Why

Pinned names such as `row-outline wuau8.4` put work identifiers at different x positions. Proportional sans text means padding or reversing the name order cannot align the fields. Lucca approved separate tag/label, age, ID and marker columns on line 2, in both Agents sidebar and attention inbox rows.

Source of truth: `/home/lucca/.cache/eon-agents/eon-desk/bead-sidebar-tag-columns.md` (Lucca, 2026-11-11: "i like it", popup option 1), with `/home/lucca/.local/state/rota/runs/desk-popup-rows-sol-1/report.md`. Popup labels and markers both stay; `Claude` is never conditionally hidden. eon-xvz5c owns the tag field/CLI/JSON and blocks this presentation bead.

## Evidence

Checked at edge `2e93c69b2250cb30346c2306502116ebfaebcd87`, after eon-wuau8.4's current-row outline and eon-5bft1's marker. Replace the spec's ~481fe27 pointers with these:

- `venus/src/scene.rs:353` SidebarRow; `:2679` shared attention_row; `:2717` pinned title fallback; `:2730` flat age/heading/source/+N/stale detail; `:2737` RTL boundary; `:2763` accessible label; `:2820` marker rect. Popup target IDs are omitted from accessible labels today.
- `venus/src/scene.rs:2148` resolves shown-session inbox pin; `:2913` popup source is catalog label while target is uN; `:2924` shares pane/popup row construction. Other sessions' queue entries lack pane pin/tag and popup catalog metadata.
- `venus/src/render/chrome.rs:898` draws the landed two-window marker; `:939` paints row surfaces; `:991` still promotes current detail to PRIMARY_TEXT; `:1964` paints both surfaces' rows; `:2061` clips a sidebar line. `:5327` protects marker geometry.
- `venus/src/render.rs:2768` Status text uses sans shaping with no monospace width. `venus/src/scene.rs:411` ages are now/minutes/hours/days; days are not capped at 9.
- `venus/src/scene/tests/sidebar.rs:263`, `:535`, `:838`, `:907`: row ordering, pin/inbox projection, marker lane/clipping and shaped RTL metadata regressions.
- `venus/docs/CONTRACTS.md:2306` VEN-C30, row content `:2404`, marker `:2429`, current text `:2452`; `:2873` VEN-C32 consumes VEN-C30 row presentation and preserves inbox context. `venus/docs/PRESENTATION.md:483`; `docs/USAGE.md:747`, `:808`; fixed palette policy `docs/CONFIGURATION.md:345`.

## Scope

In scope:
- One shared Venus row presentation for sidebar and attention inbox, with separate line-2 fields measured in rendered pixels, not spaces or character counts. Consume xvz5c's canonical tag without reconstructing it from pin/name.
- Left: pane tag (blank when absent), or popup entry label. +N and status stale follow on the left; that side yields/truncates first. Preserve existing inbox tab/session context and accessible location rather than losing it when replacing the flat detail string.
- Right: fixed-width right-aligned age slot, then a left-aligned source ID column (`pN` or `uN`) sized to the widest ID shown in that list, then a marker lane reserved on every row. Pane lanes are empty; popup rows use the landed marker. Column positions are shared across mixed rows/tabs in each sidebar or inbox list, not recalculated independently for each row.
- Popup entry labels stay on the left, including Claude; popup uN becomes visible in the ID column. Explicit LTR boundaries isolate age and ID from RTL labels/tags. Full accessible names carry name, full tag/label, ID, state and location regardless of clipping.
- All of line 2 uses the existing dim text hierarchy on every row, including current, with existing stale treatment and 4.5:1 contrast adaptation. No current-row primary-detail promotion. Line 1 and needs-input line 3 keep their existing behavior and roles.
- Lucca-approved VEN-C30 row/marker/current-text wording; `venus/docs/PRESENTATION.md`, `docs/USAGE.md`, fixed-look explanation in `docs/CONFIGURATION.md`, `CHANGELOG.md`, and `venus/CHANGELOG.md` for the accepted contract amendment. VEN-C32 already delegates row presentation to VEN-C30: preserve that reference and its inbox context, without duplicating the row contract.

Out of scope:
- Runtime storage, CLI parsing, JSON/protocol changes and their tests (eon-xvz5c); popup tags/pins or remote queue metadata (eon-inbox-pinned-name-yiogr).
- Line 1, badges/backings, selection/hover/focus treatments, row ordering/navigation/hit targets, marker shape/size/stroke/vertical centering, or row geometry beyond line 2. Build on the landed outline and two-window marker.
- New style families, per-tag colours, pills, separators, configurable colours/layout, or future command/background row content.

## Acceptance

- In both sidebar and inbox, mixed pane/popup rows with unequal names/tags/labels, ages now/59m/23h/9d and IDs p9/p10/u10 have identical tag/label left x, age right x, ID left x and marker-lane x within each list. Include multiple tabs and scroll/filter/resize transitions; no character-padding alignment.
- At the narrowest supported visible sidebar and a narrow inbox, long tags/labels and left-side +N/stale/context content truncate before age or ID; those right fields remain whole and disjoint. Untagged panes have no invented placeholder or duplicate name. Larger supported IDs and multi-digit day ages also fit; do not cap or abbreviate the existing age formatter to the examples. Tiny surfaces retain existing safe clipping/dismissal without changing the sidebar width policy or enlarging rows.
- Popup rows retain full label semantics (including Claude), show uN and the existing overlapping-window marker in the shared lane; pane lanes remain empty. Marker shape and vertical placement stay as landed; lines 1/3, badges, row heights and current/hover/focus outlines remain unchanged.
- Current, non-current, hovered and stale rows all keep line 2 in the existing dim roles with at least 4.5:1 contrast; no new text palette. Line 1 retains primary hierarchy and line 3 remains the existing plain-text needs-input message.
- Accessible names include the full name, tag or popup label, target ID, state and tab/session location despite truncation; retain popup/current, age, +N, stale and needs-input information. RTL labels/tags cannot reorder or join the LTR age and ID. The same canonical identity and available tag/label are readable through CLI/JSON.
- A changed tag updates both shown-session row surfaces without changing selection, filter, scroll or attachment. Cross-session inbox entries preserve current name/session fallbacks and full target ID; this bead does not invent missing pin/tag or popup label metadata. If yiogr has landed, consume its available metadata under the same columns.

## Implementation Notes

1. Await accepted eon-xvz5c and rebase to its canonical protocol. Before implementing, show Lucca the exact VEN-C30 row, popup-marker lane and current-detail wording. Design approval is not the requested contract-text approval. If preserving VEN-C32's context needs an actual text amendment rather than its existing VEN-C30 reference, include that exact delta in the same Lucca approval; do not change its behavior implicitly.
2. Keep ownership at the existing shared SidebarRow/attention_row and row painter; use existing text shaping/measurement and chrome tokens. Read `venus/docs/REFERENCES.md` "Read-only pane metadata: historical Venus observer and Runtime ownership" and "Canonical workspace protocol provider"; local comparables are shared row composition, Status shaping, explicit RTL metadata and the landed marker at the evidence revision. Keep the Runtime data owner and single row path; reject name parsing, padded spaces, a second sidebar renderer, a font switch or a general table framework. Record the mechanism/reference gate before contract/code edits.
3. Allocate the right-side fields before fitting the left text; use actual proportional-font widths at the current font/scale. Keep the existing age formatter (including multi-digit days) and unknown-age behavior. Do not replace it with a three-character assumption. Preserve the full untruncated source data for accessibility.
4. Use the same fields/measurement in both surfaces, update their existing geometry/render/a11y tests, and remove obsolete flat-detail expectations. Keep Runtime/CLI tag tests solely in xvz5c.

## Verification

Future implementation proof, not run by this planning pass:
- Extend `venus/src/scene/tests/sidebar.rs` and the existing chrome render tests: mixed-ID column positions, left-first clipping with real proportional-font measurements, no-tag/unknown-age/stale/+N/needs-input cases, popup label+uN+marker, full accessible names, RTL shaping, and dim current detail. Retain marker, outline, row-height and navigation regressions; scene strings alone cannot prove measured column placement or text colour.
- Before code review, whole-workspace `nix develop -c eon-test` via its isolation harness, Venus fmt and `cargo clippy --locked --all-targets -- -D warnings`. Apply the output/render route's Tier 1 frame invariants and machine-local eon-bench gate, or record the exact missing Tier 2 evidence per `docs/AGENT-RULES.md`; overseer runs the affected package build before landing.
- After accepted batch/profile refresh, one isolated installed observation on native Wayland covers narrow and normal lists, proportional text, RTL, mixed panes/popups, selection/stale states and inbox. Lucca judges the all-dim tag live. Preserve desktop focus/live terminals; record exact revision/artifact, environment and observations. No visual-quality claim from headless tests alone.

## Stop Conditions

- Stop for Lucca's approval of the exact VEN-C30 contract text before implementation (and any necessary VEN-C32 delta); no contract edits in this planning pass. EON data/contract approval and EONW allocation belong to xvz5c, not a second approval here.
- Stop if xvz5c is unaccepted or current data cannot supply its approved tag. Do not add a wire bump or queue-enrichment feature under this bead.
- Stop if complete age/ID cannot fit at supported visible widths without changing approved line-1/line-3 behavior, marker geometry or row sizing; report measured constraints for Lucca instead of silently changing the design. Stop for material evidence drift or out-of-scope requirements.
- Stop if the existing dim roles cannot meet contrast, if a new setting/style family is needed, if work no longer fits one fresh session, or if verification fails twice for the same reason after a reasonable fix attempt. Raising tag text to primary is only a later Lucca decision after live viewing.

## Maintenance Notes

- Size: one shared row-presentation outcome, bounded to scene/measurement, row rendering, accessibility, their tests and owning docs, with one render/installed proof route. Keep it one fresh session; no independently useful smaller child is needed now.
- Dependency: eon-e5qjv is blocked by eon-xvz5c. yiogr is not a blocker: whichever lands second extends the other's shown-session pin/tag projection when adding cross-session metadata; don't duplicate that work here.
- eon-wuau8.1-.3 are closed foundations; .4 and eon-5bft1 are landed. eon-wuau8.5/.6 change bar chips only; .7 changes badge backings in the shared row painter. Rebase/serialize overlapping landings, preserve .7 if it lands first, and do not add a semantic dependency for shared-file edits alone.
- eon-xjzr4.3 owns future running-command rows/toggle/CLI; eon-qczl0 owns background-work content/data. Neither blocks these generic columns and neither's content belongs here. eon-guqrt only renames panel terminology/internal identifiers: rebase shared docs/scene names in whichever lands second. No dependencies on these unneeded features.
- Rule 5: no new window action; row jumps keep their existing CLI parity, tags are written/read through xvz5c, and popup label/catalog and pN/uN identity already exist in session JSON. Inbox view state remains the documented Venus-local exception.
- Rule 6: Lucca chose fixed layout and existing dim palette roles. Shared column order/lanes preserve a consistent scan pattern; independent styling knobs multiply geometry/contrast combinations and support cost without adding a distinct capability. Reuse the existing fixed-look policy and font/scale/contrast mechanisms; no tag colours, pills, separators or settings. If readability requires a policy change, return to Lucca.
- Not a release blocker and not added to eon-igae (existing overseer call, 2026-11-12, relayed via eon-desk). Portability: neutral, shared scene/text/render/a11y only; prove native Wayland, make no unproved Darwin claim. After both beads land, the overseer may switch from `slug bead` pins to short slugs plus --tag.
