title: Spike and draft: remove a worktree when its tab closes
description:
## Why
The epic's original on-close cleanup idea is explicitly outside its current accepted
create/list/explicit-remove scope. EON-C42 leaves it out: two review rounds showed
it needs mechanisms nobody has proved. This
bead proves or rejects them and drafts the amendment. Parent: eon-el45.

## Deliverable (planning and a throwaway spike only; no product code lands)
An EON-C42 amendment draft for Lucca, with the beads that would implement it, answering:
1. Who runs Git on a close made from the window, and from which PATH (the supervisor
   runs no Git today, and Eon does not package Git).
2. How a second window, or a tab bound between the check and the removal, is kept from
   losing its directory; what an old-build window means.
3. How an agent reads the result after the tab is gone: EON-C39 ends a tab-filtered
   stream with its tab, rebuilds from snapshots after overflow, and lets Venus act on one
   event only.
4. What happens when the close ends the window, and on same-boot recovery.
5. Whether ignored files and reflog-only commits block an automatic removal (a close is
   not a request to delete them).
6. Whether a simpler rule meets the need: for example the close reply naming the
   worktree and the exact remove command, with no automatic removal.
Record each answer with its evidence, and a recommendation.

## Scope boundary
No contract text, EONW, supervisor or Venus change lands from this bead. Experiments stay
in a scratch repository and an isolated Eon. Stop for Lucca with the draft.

## Prerequisites
Blocked by eon-el45.4 (the explicit remove and its outcome object exist). Input:
`/home/lucca/pjs/refs/eon-worktrees-el45/report.md` sections 6 and 7, which hold
the review findings on the earlier on-close drafts.

## Acceptance
- The six questions are answered with evidence; Lucca approves, revises or drops the
  amendment; follow-up beads are proposed, not filed before approval.

## Verification
Planning route: bead state and recorded research; no runtime profile refresh.

title: Seed the configuration corpus test and declare the migration floor
description:
## Why

Lucca accepted the eon-c8ytm upgrade policy on 2026-10-31. Under it, migration
code (config aliases, state migrators) is deleted only when a release's declared
migration floor passes it, never one release later. Skip-version Nix upgrades,
rollbacks and older live windows make "delete after the next release" unsafe;
the full reasoning is the proposal comment on eon-c8ytm. That rule needs a
mechanical check: a corpus of past configurations that every build must load.
This bead seeds the corpus first, so later alias and value changes (the alias
table bead, the forward-compatible values bead) add fixtures to it.

## Evidence

- `runtime/crates/eon-runtime/src/managed_environment.rs:1293` `parse_config`:
  the one parser of `config.toml`; `:1274` `read_config` warns on unknown keys.
- `runtime/crates/eon-runtime/src/managed_environment.rs:134-142`: the
  `[bar] show_version` tombstone, a hard error since ddc6c44 (2026-10-21).
- `docs/CONTRACTS.md` EON-C28 Open proof: the 1.0 configuration fixture
  (`eon-igae.11`) becomes this corpus's first permanent entry when it lands.
- Tags: `v0.1.2`, `v0.1.1`; edge is 0.1.9 (`eon/crates/eon/Cargo.toml:3`).

## Scope

In scope:
- A corpus directory of `config.toml` fixtures under eon-runtime test data,
  one per release (start with `v0.1.1`, `v0.1.2` and current edge: the
  documented example in `docs/CONFIGURATION.md` at each tag, plus every key that
  release accepted set to a non-default value), each with its expected resolved
  values (`eon config defaults --json` shape) and expected warnings.
- A Rust test that loads every fixture through `parse_config` and compares the
  resolved values and the warning list.
- The floor declaration: one constant in Eon Runtime naming the oldest release
  the build upgrades from without loss, and a one-line note in `CHANGELOG.md`
  Unreleased stating the floor. The initial floor is `v0.1.1`.
- A short `docs/DEVELOPMENT.md` paragraph: a release that adds or changes a key
  adds its fixture; fixtures below the floor are deleted with their migrators.

Out of scope:
- Changing parsing behavior. A fixture that fails today (for example
  `show_version`) is recorded as an expected failure with a pointer to the alias
  table bead, which flips it.
- State-file fixtures (none of today's persisted files is durable state; see
  eon-reboot-restore-im8y).

## Acceptance

- `nix develop -c eon-test -p eon-runtime` runs the corpus test over at least
  three releases' fixtures and passes, with the `show_version` fixture marked
  as an expected failure.

## Implementation Notes

1. Recover each tag's documented example and accepted keys with
   `git show v0.1.2:docs/CONFIGURATION.md` and that tag's `managed_environment.rs`.
2. Keep fixtures data-only (TOML plus an expected JSON); one test iterates them.

## Verification

- `nix develop -c eon-test -p eon-runtime` exits 0.
- converge plus Codex (test and code change).

## Stop Conditions

- Stop if the floor needs to be anything other than `v0.1.1`: that is Lucca's
  call.
- Stop if a fixture shows a past key that now fails silently with a changed
  meaning: report it on eon-c8ytm.

## Maintenance Notes

- Policy: eon-c8ytm proposal, section D. The floor moves only at a breaking
  release boundary and no sooner than 60 days after the change it drops.
- Rejected: deleting each migrator one release later (eon-c8ytm, failure
  cases 1-5).
close_reason: Corpus test over v0.1.1, v0.1.2 and v0.1.9 fixtures and migration floor v0.1.1 landed; proof and review ledger in comments

comments.author: lucca
comments.text:
Proof (eon-embg6, on edge dd0ef12 plus this change; x86_64 Linux, Nix dev shell, CARGO_TARGET_DIR outside the repo):
- `nix develop -c eon-test -p eon-runtime`: 150 passed, 0 failed, 1 ignored.
  - `configuration_corpus_loads_from_the_migration_floor` passes over seven fixtures from three releases (v0.1.1, v0.1.2, v0.1.9).
  - Each release has a verbatim documented example and a non-default case; v0.1.1 also has `v0.1.1-show-version`.
  - `v0.1.1-example` and `v0.1.1-show-version` are expected failures pointing at eon-wc119.
- The floor check can fail: with the floor at v0.1.2 the test fails on "v0.1.1-example is below the migration floor" (reviewer run, then reverted).
- `cargo fmt -p eon-runtime --check`, `cargo clippy --locked -p eon-runtime --all-targets -- -D warnings` and `git diff --check`: clean.

Shape:
- Fixtures live in runtime/crates/eon-runtime/testdata/config-corpus/<release>-<case>/, each with `config.toml` and `expected.json`.
- `expected.json` holds either the resolved values in `eon config defaults --json` shape plus the warnings, or an `error` plus an `expected_failure`.
- The floor is `MIGRATION_FLOOR = "v0.1.1"`, placed beside the test. It is test-only: nothing in the build reads it yet, and a crate-level constant would be dead code.

  - Claude found 2 blocking issues (the changelog overclaim, and v0.1.1 untested beyond show_version) plus 1 should-fix: fixture vs product defaults, recorded above as a gap.
  - All were fixed: per-release example, non-default and show-version fixtures, plus comments and wording.
- Claude converge rounds, 3 in all:
  1. Moved the floor constant out of the public API and fixed the docs.
  2. Fixed a docs clause.
  3. Wrapped text. This was the second text-only restart, so its fixes were accepted at the cap.
- The narrow Codex re-check of f36de749..deea8913 was clean.
- Codex passes: 2. Findings: 3, then 0.

title: Say so when Alt+G or Alt+Shift+G finds no agent needing attention
description:
## Why

Lucca pressed Alt+G and Alt+Shift+G in his window on 2026-10-23 and reported "alt g and alt shift g are doing nothing in this window". Every agent there was working, so the attention queue was empty. EON-C31 says "An empty queue is EON-C10's unchanged-snapshot no-op" (docs/CONTRACTS.md:2353), and the yx8.9 proof recorded "On an empty queue, Alt+G and Alt+Shift+G changed nothing." That is correct to the contract, but a key that silently does nothing looks broken. Lucca approved the fix the same day ("1 do it", answering the overseer's item: "on an empty queue, Alt+G and Alt+Shift+G show a short notice, 'No agent needs attention', in the existing Venus notice style, without stealing focus"). He did not take the alternative of falling back to working agents.

## Contract (bring exact text to the overseer before code)

- EON-C31 NextAttention and PreviousAttention: replace the empty-queue no-op with a result the person can see, for example "On an empty queue, the window shows the notice 'No agent needs attention'; focus, selection and the cursor are unchanged."
- Pick the owner at the reference gate. Either the Runtime answers an empty-queue NextAttention or PreviousAttention with a typed, non-error outcome (which may be an EONW change and a version bump) and Venus renders it as a VEN-C8 notice, or Venus decides locally from the snapshot. Venus deciding locally is only acceptable if the snapshot carries enough to reproduce the queue exactly, including seen raises; otherwise it creates a second owner of the queue (AP-OWNERSHIP-001). Prefer the Runtime owning the answer.
- The notice never takes desktop or keyboard focus and never changes Orbit state.

## Scope

In scope: the contract text, the mechanism, the Venus notice, tests, and VEN-C30 and USAGE lines if they describe Alt+G.

Out of scope: changing what the queue holds, and falling back to working agents.

## Acceptance

- A test shows that an empty queue yields the notice and leaves focus, selection and the cursor unchanged.
- One installed observation: with only working agents, Alt+G shows the notice.

## Verification

The affected Rust surfaces (and Nix, if EONW changes), converge plus Codex, the profile refresh, and one isolated installed observation.

title: Remove an ended window's runtime directory without racing window new
description:
## Why

eon-reattach-after-upgrade-n5qv lists ended windows as ended (Lucca approved choice 4(a) on 2026-10-23, "agree to everything") and leaves their runtime directories in place. Over time, ended window directories pile up in the runtime dir. Current `eon window ls` (EON-C23) omits windows with no live supervisor, so the old listing-noise rationale is historical. eon-90 found that removing a window root races `eon window new`'s reservation of a window ID, so removal needs its own lock design.

## Scope

In scope: when a window's last supervisor exits, or on an explicit cleanup, remove that window's runtime directory safely against a concurrent `window new` reservation and a concurrent attach. Contract text (EON-C23 or EON-C11) goes to the overseer or Lucca before code.

Out of scope: n5qv's attach delegation and listing.

## Acceptance

- A test shows an ended window's directory is removed, and a concurrent `window new` never gets a half-removed or reused root.

## Verification

`nix develop -c eon-test -p eon -p eon-runtime`, converge plus Codex.
## Current evidence and approval gate (dcaef1c)
`runtime/crates/eon-runtime/src/windows.rs:591` (`new_window`) reserves a private
root by atomic directory creation before `launch.log` (:617) and before a
supervisor/socket exists. `running.rs:70` documents non-mutating lifecycle-lock
inspection; generation cleanup already exists in `generation.rs`. Do not equate
an absent socket or a listing omission with permission to delete that namespace.

Before code, record the one cleanup owner and proposed EON-C23/EON-C11/EON-C15
wording for approval. Decide whether automatic cleanup or an explicit cleanup
trigger is the selected surface; if explicit, give its CLI/JSON/exit contract.
Account for recoverable Orbit terminals, attach delegation/build records and
persistent session registry state: no live or recoverable work may be removed
merely because its supervisor is temporarily absent. An uncertain liveness result
keeps the directory. This is a lifecycle/trust reference gate, not permission to
choose a grace-period value without a recorded safety/configurability rationale.

## Additional acceptance and verification
- A deterministic scratch-root race covers reservation before launch.log, startup
  before the socket, concurrent attach and two cleanup attempts; no starting/live
  root is deleted or replaced, and no cleanup follows a symlink outside its root.
- An ended, non-recoverable private root is removed only under the approved rule;
  failures leave an inspectable result and preserve other windows/generations.
- Test the shared mechanism using the supported harness; full affected Rust/Nix
  lifecycle proof, required review, profile refresh and one isolated installed
  cleanup observation follow implementation. Never stop/restart Lucca's supervisor
  or terminals as part of this task. Planning here runs no tests or runtime actions.

Scope remains ended-window cleanup only, not a redesign of session recovery,
window listing or attach. If the proposed rule changes recovery/identity promises,
stop for that decision before implementation.

comments.author: lucca
comments.text: Constraint from eon-90 (n5qv, 2026-10-23): `eon windows` briefly lists a window as ended while its supervisor is still starting, because the window dir exists before the socket. Removal must never treat a starting window as ended: guard it with launch.log plus the lifecycle lock, or a start grace period.

Lucca may overturn this in his morning review.

title: Keep a slow-starting Eon window from being killed at startup admission under load
description:
## Why

An Eon window can fail to open when the machine is busy. Lucca approved filing this on 2026-10-22.

## Evidence

- eon-c1, during eon-0ka6's isolated installed proof on 2026-10-22, on private headless Sway 1.12 with pixman: the first
  launch at load 16 failed with `cannot admit Eon Desktop presentation: EAGAIN`, and Venus was
  SIGKILLed after 5 s. A relaunch at load 5 worked. The record is on eon-0ka6.
- Cause, from reading the code at 3afd58a:
  - `runtime/crates/eon-runtime/src/supervisor.rs` `PresentationProcess::start` waits for Venus's
    `ready-v1` reply with a read timeout bounded by a deadline of `SESSION_START_TIMEOUT` (5 s,
    supervisor.rs:43).
  - When that read times out, the `WouldBlock` error prints as EAGAIN, and the supervisor stops
    Venus (`stop(&mut process.child)`).
  - So under load, native startup (Wayland connection, Vulkan device, fonts, first frame) can take
    longer than 5 s, and Eon kills a healthy but slow window.
- Not yet established: whether the 5 s also bounds a user's real launch on COSMIC, and how long
  Venus startup takes at idle and under load.

## Owner and contracts

- Runtime owns the presentation admission deadline and its error. Venus owns how fast it reaches
  readiness.
- Read the contracts that own startup admission before choosing a fix:
  - EON-C19 in docs/CONTRACTS.md, which consumes Venus startup admission. Its proof includes
    `startup_snapshot_transfer_uses_the_admission_deadline`.
  - VEN-C19 in venus/docs/CONTRACTS.md.
  - venus/docs/LAUNCH.md.
- A changed deadline or new startup behavior is a contract change that needs Lucca's approval
  first.

## Scope

- Measure Venus startup-to-ready at idle and under a reproducible load (e.g. `stress-ng` or a
  parallel cargo build) in an isolated headless Sway.
- Choose the fix at its owner:
  - a deadline that tolerates a slow but progressing Venus;
  - faster readiness;
  - or a clearer error that names the timeout.

Out of scope: other workspace-exchange timeouts (eon-workspace-action-timeout-287o is closed).

## Acceptance

- A red/green reproduction at the cheapest harness, the existing presentation admission tests in
  `eon/crates/eon/tests/workspace_control.rs` if a slow fake Venus can express it.
- One isolated installed observation under load where the window opens.
- Review loop per AGENTS.md; profile refresh.
close_reason: Landed as f033767 (proof and ledger in the 2026-10-22 20:04 Proof comment). Installed: profile eon -> /nix/store/zfycqrmc4sgrgv4n5an8kw54pda9aksa-eon-0.1.1, built from 6bda1f5, which contains f033767. Observation (2026-10-22): Lucca's launch of that profile opened the new window g1-934c7cca (EONW 17). Running supervisors were not restarted.

comments.author: lucca
comments.text:
Measurement (2026-10-22, installed eon ckisr53k / Venus k2fg2dbk, private headless Sway 1.12 pixman, standalone stdin-ready-v1, spawn to ready-v1): idle 84 ms warm, ~160 ms cold cache; 16 CPU spinners 0.49-0.65 s; 32 spinners 0.55-0.93 s. Full isolated eon launch at idle: window in ~0.2 s. CPU contention alone does not reach 5 s; the eon-0ka6 miss needs more (cold page cache of a fresh store path, I/O or memory pressure from builds, GPU contention), not reproduced. A Venus crash or rejection closes stdout and fails at once on EOF, so the deadline only bounds a hung or very slow Venus.
Decision (Lucca, 2026-10-22): change EON-C19 so Venus startup admission has its own 30 s deadline, separate from the 5 s session-start timeout; reopen clients wait just past it; a timeout reports that Venus was not ready within 30 s instead of EAGAIN. Rejected: clear error only (still kills a healthy slow window); reproducing with real build load first (heavy and may not reproduce).

comments.author: lucca
comments.text: Decision (Lucca, 2026-10-22): all control clients wait 31 s (CONTROL_TIMEOUT = admission deadline + 1 s), keeping the rule that a client outlasts one in-flight supervisor operation; a second launch during a slow startup attaches instead of failing. EON-C15's Stop read timeout text becomes one preceding thirty-second operation plus five-second cleanup and a one-second margin (36 s). Accepted cost: a client facing a hung supervisor waits 31 s instead of 6 s. Rejected: only Present waits 31 s (second launch, CLI commands and Stop fail during a slow admission).

comments.author: lucca
comments.text: Review round 1 finding (Claude + Codex): in eonbase and full Eon with a recovered picker the first terminal started after admission with the pre-admission 5 s deadline, so a slow Venus still failed the launch. Decision (Lucca, 2026-10-22): that terminal gets its own fresh 5 s deadline, and control clients wait 36 s (30 s admission + 5 s first terminal + 1 s), Stop 41 s; EON-C15 text follows. Supersedes the 31 s / 36 s numbers above; the rule (a client outlasts one in-flight operation, a second launch attaches) is unchanged.

Proof (source tree c38e9e5c4d145c32022c3a5f7bfa21270fcf2690 on 1ce839f, identical outside .beads to the commit carrying this note; x86_64 Linux, 2026-10-22):

- Isolated installed launch of that artifact on a private headless Sway 1.12 (pixman) under 24 busy-loop CPU spinners (loadavg 10.6 -> 12.2): Venus up in 378 ms, the picker's Orbit in 1559 ms, and the window showed the Quick search picker with CPU 100%. title: Bake rota into Eon as eon agent, and share the overseer workflow with users
description:
## Decision

Lucca, 2026-11-07: "the goal here is empowering eon users. if we create our tiny universe of scripts without sharing it with eon users, that's not great". On rota he weighed leaving it separate, an optional `eon rota` addon, or baking it in, and agreed to the overseer's recommendations ("i agree"):

1. Bake rota into Eon, named for what it does: `eon agent ...`, not `eon rota ...`; the Agent popup (Alt+Shift+L) uses the same picker instead of "the first installed agent".
2. Timing: write the decision and the contract draft now; build after v0.2.0 (the announcement is not held for it).
3. The overseer's private scripts (~/.cache/eon-agents/eon-overseer/*.sh, audited in scripts-audit/report.md) become an epic of small beads in three groups: generic agent orchestration becomes eon features; the review and landing workflow ships as an Eon skill (eon/skills/); Eon-repo-only chores become repository tooling (Rust, per Implementation Languages).

## Why

rota (Yazelix/rota, ~4k lines of Rust, light dependencies) picks which coding-agent subscription runs the next agent session by remaining quota, caps and guards, and launches it in an Eon pane. It already reads quota from `eon session --json`, and Eon already shows Codex and Claude quota and starts an agent in the Agent popup, so two owners hold agent launching and quota today; the `eon workspace` -> `eon session` rename broke rota's quota checks (fixed in its config 2026-11-07). One owner in Eon gives users the picker, and the overseer workflow, without a private toolchain. Per the no-legacy rule, the rota repository retires once Eon has parity.

## Scope

This epic holds the decision, the contract, the port of rota's picker, launch and status into Eon Runtime as `eon agent`, the Agent popup's use of it, and the children filed from the scripts audit. Children are small (one session each). Contract work stops for Lucca's approval of exact text.

## Effective planning state (2026-11-12)

Comment 6556 relays Lucca's "i agree": internal slices may precede v0.2.0 only without public keys/CLI/popup/docs promises or unfinished public prerequisites; new features go into Eon, rota gets fixes only. The public-picker suggestion is not beta approval. The durable approved design is /home/lucca/pjs/refs/eon-agent-lr8sx/00-references.md through 05-children.md. .22 indexing remains open and its proposed amendments are not decisions.

Completion needs each delivered child at its actual proof scope, .19's exact-artifact batch, .20's real-account/caller/final-retirement acceptance and separately gated .21 queue decisions. The approved generic orchestration, shipped Eon workflow skill and Rust repository-tooling scope is reconciled in eon-eon-agent-lr8sx.23; it is not silently dropped when the base picker lands.

title: Share a fair machine-wide queue for heavy agent runs in eon agent: FIFO slots, quiet windows, wait alerts
description:
## Effective decision state (2026-11-12)

Epic comment 6556 relays Lucca's "i agree": remaining new features go into Eon; rota gets fixes only. Earlier rota-first feature work below is superseded for remaining work; current rota slot code is reference. Standalone eon slot is the recorded 2026-11-10 delegated naming direction. Scope, quota-ticket separation, model-checker choice, configuration and exact contract text still need reconciliation/approval. Preserve historical decisions and do not promote incompatible later proposals into approvals.

Lucca, 2026-11-09, after a pane agent's package build waited 2h46m unnoticed behind newer builds: "make it so this problem does not happen in the future" / "and dont forget adding it to rota and/or eon agent".

Today this lives in the overseer's private script /home/lucca/.cache/eon-agents/eon-overseer/heavy.sh (shared by the Eon, Tide and Clinica overseers): every agent runs builds, tests and benchmarks through it to get one of 2-3 machine-wide slots (flock on build.lock/build2.lock/build3.lock) at nice 19 with 6 Cargo jobs. Policy files re-read each pass: extra-slot-until (third slot), one-slot-until and slot2-stalled (narrow), quiet-until (hold new runs for a timing benchmark; HEAVY_QUIET_EXEMPT=1 for the granted one), HEAVY_ANY_SLOT=1 (priority). Until 2026-11-09 waiters raced every 5 s, so an old waiter could starve; FIFO tickets (queue/<start-ns>.<pid>.<class>, per class nix/run, dead tickets removed) fixed it that day, and queue-watch.sh reports any run waiting over 45 minutes.

Goal: users running several agents get the same thing as an Eon feature, not a private script: e.g. eon agent run-heavy -- COMMAND (or an eon agent queue family) with first-come-first-served slots, configurable slot count and priorities, quiet windows for timing runs, and a CLI view of the queue with each waiter's age and owner (rule 5: agents can read and act on it). Decide whether rota hosts it first (rota already routes agent launches) or it waits for eon agent; either way one owner. Configuration and defaults in docs/CONFIGURATION.md (rule 6). Implementation in Rust per Implementation Languages; the shell script is the reference behaviour and its comment history the requirements.

(9) mbx (Mr. Boxington, jdx, MIT; Cargo wrapper with a hardlinked/reflinked output store and a machine-wide CPU and memory scheduler) is the strongest candidate for a shared cache plus scheduler; spike on two agents before adopting (needs Lucca's OK to install). (10) after parallel checkPhase and nextest, replace fixed slots with systemd-run --user scopes at low CPUWeight admitted by memory pressure (PSI), allowing two package builds at once. Not recommended now: sccache inside Nix (impure), cachix on one machine, tmpfs (RAM short), mold/wild (linker is not the bottleneck), ovnfs for target dirs, Tide or lust (do not apply to Eon), remote builders (cost decision).

comments.text:
From the subscription-pool research (/home/lucca/.cache/eon-agents/eon-pool-research-work/report.md, 2026-11-09): quota slots beside build slots. 
The bead currently covers machine-wide build slots: FIFO tickets, quiet windows and wait alerts. Pooling research shows that agent capacity needs the same queue. A review or implementer that finds no backend with room should wait in first-in-first-out order for the next window reset, not be refused.

Design the `eon agent` queue so a ticket waits on a slot of a given kind:
- `build`: today's `heavy.sh` slots.
- `quota:<role>`: free when some backend for that role has headroom, or at the earliest known reset.

Both kinds share the same CLI view of each waiter's age, owner and reason (rule 5), and the same configuration in docs/CONFIGURATION.md (rule 6).

The queue never moves a running session between accounts. rota's `--wait` (bead 2) is the reference behaviour.

is no scheduler and no unbounded admission wait, so say whether the queue stays outside

## Evidence to read

- The reference behaviour: ~/.cache/eon-agents/eon-overseer/heavy.sh (FIFO tickets, 2-3 flock

## Scope

In: a numbered recommendation for Lucca on (1) owner and name: standalone `eon slot ...` or an

title: Persist slot tickets and grant leases with private, versioned, locked state
description:
## Why

On 2026-11-12 the machine hit load 44 with 77% I/O pressure when unqueued Tide tests ran on top of four Eon builds, and one rustc reached about 16 GB inside a single heavy.sh slot. ## Scope

Persist the queue: atomic sequenced enqueue, grant and cancel under one short admission lock; one flock-compatible lock per slot and per ticket; private versioned state (0700 dirs, 0600 files, bounded reads, owner/type/symlink checks) with boot and process identity. - Never replace a live lock inode or discard state because its version differs.

title: eon agent: record 'waiting for the orchestrator' as a durable state until input or ack
description:
## Why

On 2026-11-12, four agent panes (p8 eon-5si0a, p9 eon-jbr1w, p12 eon-t1rtk.2, p17 eon-0ntg1) wrote
"PLAN READY" at 16:54-17:15Z and then sat idle for about an hour. The overseer's status watcher
reported only new log lines and was started just after they finished. Eon itself knew: the
sidebar showed each one as finished. Lucca: "how can we improve eon agent so that [it doesn't]
happen again", then "yeah" to desk's proposal (this bead plus its sibling for stale escalation).

A handoff point is a state, not an event. It must not depend on someone watching at the moment it
happens.

## Goal

eon agent records "waiting for the orchestrator" as a durable state of an agent attempt. Examples:
plan ready, candidate ready, blocked, a question. The state persists until the orchestrator acts
on it, by sending the agent input or explicitly acknowledging it.

## Design sketch (the plan settles the exact shape and contract text)

- How the agent reports a handoff, to settle in the plan: (a) an explicit CLI call from the agent
  (`eon agent report --state plan-ready [--file PATH] [--note TEXT]`), (b) the existing attention
  state finished, with tag and attempt identity, or both. Reusing OSC 7501 and the attention model
  is preferred over a new channel.
- Persistence: stored with the attempt record (eon-eon-agent-lr8sx.9) and survives watcher
  restarts and window moves.
- Cleared by: input sent to the agent's pane (`eon pane send`), or `eon agent ack ATTEMPT`.
- Visible in: `eon agent ls --waiting` (or the lr8sx.11 status listing), the `eon events` snapshot
  (so any watcher sees it at startup), and the `eon session --json` attention queue.
- Ordering: oldest waiting first.

## Contract

EON-C40 (eon agent, Planned; see eon-eon-agent-lr8sx.22) gains the waiting state and its
clear/ack rules. Lucca approves the text before code (rule 1).

## Scope and order

Child of eon-eon-agent-lr8sx. Builds after lr8sx.9 (attempt storage) and lr8sx.11 (status listing). Out of scope: escalation
to the user (sibling bead), and orchestrator policy (what to do with a handoff).

## Acceptance

- An agent that reaches a handoff before any watcher starts is listed as waiting when the watcher
  starts.
- Waiting stays set across watcher restarts and Runtime reconnects, and clears on input or ack.
- `eon events` snapshot and `eon agent ls --waiting` agree.

## Verification

Runtime unit and integration tests for set, persist and clear; `nix develop -c eon-test` (not
inside a live Eon session); an installed proof with a fake agent that reports plan-ready before
the watcher starts.

title: Escalate agents left waiting for the orchestrator past a threshold to the sidebar and inbox
description:
## Why

Same incident as its sibling (the "waiting for the orchestrator" state): on 2026-11-12, four agents
waited about an hour unnoticed because the orchestrator missed their handoffs. Lucca approved
("yeah") escalating unanswered handoffs to the user, so a stuck or blind orchestrator becomes
visible to the human, not only to agents that sit idle.

## Goal

When an agent has been waiting for the orchestrator longer than a threshold, its Agents sidebar
row and the attention inbox mark it as stale-waiting, so Lucca sees "p9 has waited 40m for the
overseer".

## Design sketch

- Threshold: default 15 minutes. One configuration key (rule 6), e.g. `[agents]
  waiting_alert_minutes = 15`, with 0 meaning off. Name and placement follow
  docs/CONFIGURATION.md.
- Presentation: reuse existing attention styles; no new style family (eon-wuau8). The row shows
  the waiting age on line 2 (the age slot already exists, eon-e5qjv). The inbox lists it, with
  oldest first.
- It clears when the waiting state clears (input or ack).
- Agents only: plain terminals that finished a command are unaffected.

## Contract

VEN-C30 (sidebar and inbox presentation) and EON-C40 (the threshold and the event). Lucca approves
the text before code.

## Scope and order

Child of eon-eon-agent-lr8sx. Blocked by the sibling bead (the waiting state).

## Acceptance

- An agent that has waited past the threshold shows as stale in the sidebar and the inbox, and
  clears on input or ack.
- The threshold is configurable, and 0 disables the alert.
- No change for non-agent terminals.

## Verification

Scene tests for row and inbox presentation; Runtime tests for threshold timing using the existing
clock seam; `nix develop -c eon-test`; an installed observation.

title: Show a busy agent as working when an older unseen finish sits on the same terminal
description:
## Problem

Lucca, 2026-10-27, in his live Eon (build 11905dd, EONW v20): "in the sidebar, both other agents
were showing green [checkmark]. only for them to update their state in the sidebar after i clicked
them." Both agents (Claude Code in panes p54 and p55) were busy at the time. Edge b8533b6 behaves the
same; delivery is not the cause (the supervisor polls every terminal at 2 Hz and Venus inspects every
250 ms, with no focus filter).

Cause, from a coordinator investigation (paths relative to the repo):
- A terminal can hold several OSC 7501 program-status records (Orbit keeps one per id,
  orbit/src/status.rs). The sidebar's "+N" counts the others; p55 showed "+1".
- EON-C31's normalization (docs/CONTRACTS.md, "Agent attention", around lines 2446-2494;
  runtime/crates/eon-runtime/src/attention.rs:108-146) ranks Finished above Working, and
  `most_urgent` takes `min_by_key((state, Reverse(changed)))`.
- A finished raise becomes seen only by focus while a Venus is attached (attention.rs:336-399).
- So an older unseen `done` record (Finished, green check) hides a newer `working` record (blue
  spinner) on the same terminal until the user focuses or clicks it. For a single record, done then
  working already gives Working with no raise (attention.rs:298-306).
- Unknown: what Claude Code's second record on p55 is (a subagent or background task under its own
  id, or an earlier program). The CLI JSON omits record ids and count (eon-agent-parity-a9g0.2).

## Expected

A busy agent always shows as working. When a terminal has a Working record that changed more
recently than its unseen Finished raise, the terminal shows Working, and that older raise counts as
seen (so it does not reappear when the work stops). A real finish after the work still raises the
green check as today. Needs input and Error keep their current priority and are not cleared this way.

## Approval

Approved by Lucca 2026-10-27, relayed by eon-overseer. Asked: "1. When a terminal reports
'working' more recently than its unseen 'finished', show working and treat the older finish as
seen. 2. Find out what Claude's second record is (dump the raw records from Orbit) as part of the
same bead. 3. One small bead, started after the two image beads land." Lucca: "yes". This covers the
EON-C31 normalization and seen wording that rule 1 needs. Record the exact adopted contract text on
this bead; any further contract change beyond rule 1 needs Lucca's approval.

## Contract

EON-C31 (Agent attention): Normalization and Seen paragraphs. No wire change expected (the rule
lives in eon-runtime's attention presenter); if one turns out to be needed, stop and ask.

## Prerequisites

- Start after orb-j2i.8 and orb-j2i.11 land (proof-slot scheduling, not a code dependency).
- Read EON-C31 in full and runtime/crates/eon-runtime/src/attention.rs.

## Steps

1. Diagnose: in an isolated Eon (headless Sway recipe, never Lucca's running Eon), run Claude Code
   with a subagent or background task and dump the raw ORB-C15 ProgramStatus records of its
   terminal, to name the second record. Record the finding on this bead.
2. Implement rule 1 in eon-runtime's attention (the supervisor-side normalization/seen bookkeeping),
   one owner, no Venus logic.
3. Adopt the EON-C31 wording; update docs/CONTRACTS.md and CHANGELOG.md (user-visible).

## Acceptance

- A unit test in eon-runtime's attention module: terminal with an unseen done record and a newer
  working record presents Working; after the working record goes idle/done again, a new raise shows
  Finished; an older working record does not hide a newer unseen finish.
- The existing attention tests stay green (`nix develop -c eon-test -p eon-runtime`).
- One isolated installed observation: two status records on one terminal (e.g. printf OSC 7501 from
  two ids, or the Claude case from step 1) show the spinner without a click.
- Review per AGENTS.md (converge plus Codex).

## Scope boundary

Only the Finished-versus-Working rule across records of one terminal. Not: sounds or notifications
(eon-iwmz, eon-2kvr), exposing record ids in the CLI (eon-agent-parity-a9g0.2), staleness timing.
close_reason: Rule 1 implemented in eon-runtime attention with EON-C31/C33 wording approved by Lucca (relayed); tests, isolated installed before/after proof and review recorded in comments.

comments.author: lucca
comments.text:
Reference gate (AP-REFERENCE-001; consequential because it changes the EON-C31 contract). Recorded by eon-54, 2026-10-27, before landing.

- User-visible behavior: when a `working` record of a terminal changed later, by ORB-C15 change sequence, than the raise of a finished record (`done` or raised `idle`) of the same terminal, the terminal shows working and that raise is seen, so it does not return when the work stops. A finish raised after the work's last change still shows. Error and needs input are untouched.
- One owner: Eon Runtime's attention presenter (`runtime/crates/eon-runtime/src/attention.rs`, `Terminal::see_finishes_before_work`, run on every applied reply). Each `Raise` now records the change sequence it raised at, so an `idle` that inherits its `done`'s raise compares at the `done`'s sequence. Orbit's records and Venus are unchanged. No wire change: EONW still carries the normalized state.
- Routes read: docs/REFERENCES.md "How should Venus direct human attention across many agent-bearing workspaces..." (owner: Eon attention semantics; prefer structured events and exact identities). Comparable implementation: herdr at `143bf5fd4781`, `src/client/shell/endpoint_agent_state.rs:81-84`: a pane reporting Working removes its pending completion, and only a later Idle/Done raises again. That is the same rule (new work supersedes an unseen completion). herdr has one status per pane; Eon applies it across a terminal's records by change sequence.
- Constraints kept: seen stays keyed by (run, id, raise); errors and needs input are never cleared by work; ORB-C15 change sequences are terminal-wide (`orbit/src/status.rs:153-160`), so they order records exactly; fixed `Instant`s are not used for the ordering, because they come from ms ages taken at different receipts.
- Rejected: (a) a Venus-side rule (it would add a second owner; Venus never normalizes); (b) only reordering Working above Finished in normalization (a raise would come back unseen when the work stops, which the approval excludes); (c) comparing the finished record's current change rather than its raise (an `idle` that inherits a `done` raise would compare too late).
- Check: `attention::tests::newer_work_sees_an_older_finish_but_never_an_error`, plus one isolated installed observation of two records on one terminal.

comments.author: lucca
comments.text:
Approval, relayed by eon-overseer on 2026-10-27, quoting Lucca. eon-overseer sent him two numbered items:
6. "Approve the EON-C33 wording, 'Focus sees a raise only while its terminal's workspace is shown, under EON-C31's rules.' (replacing 'A raise becomes seen only while its terminal's workspace is shown, under EON-C31's rules.')."
7. "Accept the 1.0 limit that a working→done→idle cycle between two 2 Hz polls may not show its finish, recorded as an EON-C31 caveat ('A cycle between two polls'); exact handling would need an ORB-C15 wire change."
Lucca: "ok". This answers both open questions above.

Exact adopted contract text (docs/CONTRACTS.md):

EON-C31 Status, appended:
"Amended on 2026-10-27 (approved by Lucca, relayed by eon-overseer) by `eon-eon-attention-working-hides-finish-7df0`: newer work sees a finish."

EON-C31 Seen, last sentence of the focus paragraph (was "...so its raises stay unseen until its workspace is shown and that exact terminal has focus."):
"A terminal in a hidden workspace is never the focused target, so focus never sees its raises until its workspace is shown and that exact terminal has focus."

EON-C31 Seen, new paragraph (rule 1):
"Newer work also sees a finish, with or without a Venus attached and in any workspace. When a `working` record in a terminal's reply changed later, by ORB-C15 change sequence, than the raise of a finished record of the same terminal, that raise is seen: it no longer shows, and it does not return when the work stops. An `idle` that keeps its `done`'s raise compares at that `done`. A finish raised after the work's last change still shows finished. An error and needs input are never seen this way."

EON-C31 caveat, new (item 7):
"A cycle between two polls. A record that goes `working`, `done` and `idle` between two polls arrives as an `idle` from `done` and keeps the cached `done`'s raise. So the finish of that cycle does not show when the cached raise was already seen, or when a `working` record changed after the cached `done`. Polls at 2 Hz make this rare. This is accepted for 1.0."

EON-C31 caveat "Detached windows" (was "While no Venus is attached, nothing becomes seen."):
"While no Venus is attached, only newer work makes a raise seen. The supervisor knows this because it holds the control stream (VEN-C14)."

EON-C33 Attention (item 6):
"Focus sees a raise only while its terminal's workspace is shown, under EON-C31's rules."

The EON-C31 proof record for this amendment is added after the final proof.

comments.author: lucca
comments.text:
Open questions for Lucca (eon-54, 2026-10-27; sent to eon-overseer for relay). Landing waits on both.

1. EON-C33 wording. Rule 1 makes the EON-C33 Attention sentence "A raise becomes seen only while its terminal's workspace is shown, under EON-C31's rules" false: newer work also sees a finish in a hidden workspace. Proposed text: "Focus sees a raise only while its terminal's workspace is shown, under EON-C31's rules." Recommendation: approve. It only restates what the approved rule 1 already implies, but it is a second contract, so the rule 1 approval may not cover it.
2. Accept a 1.0 limit (Codex round 1). A record that goes working→done→idle between two 2 Hz polls arrives as an `idle` from `done` and keeps the cached `done`'s raise. A full cycle inside 500 ms is rare, and the common case (an idle first seen beside newer work) is tested.

Step 1 finding: Claude Code's OSC 7501 records (eon-54, 2026-10-27).

Method: Claude Code 2.1.303 ran in a disposable Python PTY harness that answers the 7501 probe before DA1 and logs every report. The child got a cleaned environment and ran in the trusted repository directory. No Eon or Orbit process was involved, and no permission prompt appeared. It goes `working`, then `state=clear:id=<agent>`. It never goes `done` or `idle`. Foreground and background subagents behave alike. A background Bash task gets no record.
- Run 1 (foreground subagent): main working → subagent working → subagent clear → main done.
- Run 2 (background Bash `sleep 20`): main went `done` at 4.9 s while the sleep ran, and `working` at 24.0 s when the completion notification arrived.
- Run 3 (background subagent): main stayed `working` ("Waiting for 1 background agent to finish") until the subagent cleared.
- Run 4 (a turn started by a cross-session SendMessage, not typed input): main emitted `working` 3 s before the subagent record appeared. Same sequence as run 1.
- Run 5 (a background subagent asked to outlive main's turn): main stayed working. Then the subagent moved its `sleep 30` into a background shell, and Claude wrote main `done` and `clear:id` in one write. From 21 s to 40.9 s main showed `done` with no subagent record, though the subagent and its shell were alive. Then main went `working` and the same agent id came back `working`, cleared, and main went `done`.
- On exit, three bare `state=clear`.

Conclusion: in none of these flows were main `done` and a newer subagent `working` in effect together. That is rule 1's case. It stays the approved fix for that state, which the isolated before-case observation reproduces with Claude's record shapes. A gap these runs did show is on Claude Code's side: work Claude runs in the background (its Bash, or a subagent waiting on its own background shell) leaves main at `done` with no record, so Eon shows a finish while the agent is busy. No Eon rule can see that work. Reported to eon-overseer, who is asking Lucca about a separate bead for it.

title: Accept native terminal text selection in Eon
description:
## Outcome and contract

Accept one exact Orbit and Venus pair that makes terminal text selection usable in installed Eon:

- Drag selects cells.
- Double-click and double-drag select words.
- Triple-click and triple-drag select logical lines.
- Terminal-owned mouse input remains unchanged; Shift forces host selection.
- Release copies to the Wayland primary selection.
- `Ctrl+Shift+C` copies to the ordinary clipboard.

Eon owns only exact component selection, launch integration, update policy, installed proof, and product defaults. Orbit Bead `orb-orbit-native-selection-gestures-qf3` owns terminal semantics. Venus Bead `ven-venus-native-selection-gestures-d3x` owns native input and clipboard effects.

This behavior refreshes the exact installed proofs for the existing EON-C1 through EON-C4 product contracts; it does not create an Eon-owned selection contract.

## Prerequisites and references

Required accepted children:

1. Eon Sessions `orb-orbit-native-selection-gestures-qf3`: exact ORBS and ORB-C9 selection proof.
2. Eon Desktop `ven-venus-native-selection-gestures-d3x`: exact VEN-C7 native input and Wayland clipboard proof.

Before implementation, compare the component manifest pins with both latest accepted child revisions and record the exact identities. Reuse the references and decisions recorded by the child owners. Inspect Eon's manifest, lock, Nix composition, launcher surfaces, profile update path, current EON-C1 through EON-C4 proof, and every packaged Eon, EonTerm, and Eonova entry point.

Impact: HIGH for daily terminal use. Effort: S after both children are accepted. Risk: LOW because Eon adds no selection mechanism. Confidence: HIGH.

## Implementation

1. Wait for both child Beads to close with immutable accepted revisions.
2. Update the canonical component graph and exact lock identities together; add no patch, adapter, fallback, feature flag, or duplicated schema.
3. Build and refresh the active Eon profile from the working tree without stopping live Sessions.
4. Verify each installed launcher consumes the just-built profile artifact.
5. Refresh EON-C1 through EON-C4 proof records, changelog, and LOC only for the accepted exact composition.

## Acceptance

- Manifest, lock, Cargo, and Nix identities resolve to the accepted Orbit and Venus revisions.
- Installed Eon and EonTerm demonstrate cell, word, and logical-line press-drag selection.
- A mouse-reporting application receives ordinary pointer input; Shift performs host selection.
- Release provides the exact frozen text through Wayland primary paste in another application.
- `Ctrl+Shift+C` updates the ordinary clipboard without conflating it with primary selection.
- Eonova launches against the same accepted Eon profile and demonstrates the same boundary.
- Closing and reopening launch surfaces preserves normal lifecycle behavior and does not disturb existing Sessions.
- The full affected Rust and Nix route, profile identity check, installed Wayland dogfood, governance checks, and `git diff --check` pass on one immutable candidate.
- Closure records exact Eon, Orbit, Venus, ORBS, package, profile, compositor, and platform identities plus user acceptance and remaining limits.

## Scope and stop conditions

In scope: exact child pins, canonical component graph and lock, Nix composition, installed launch surfaces, EON-C1 through EON-C4 proof refresh, changelog, LOC, and one accepted Wayland dogfood pass.

Out of scope: Eon-owned selection code, protocol translation, compatibility support, configuration, custom boundaries or timing, middle-click paste, right-click extension, block selection, drag autoscroll, OSC 133 command-output selection, other display systems, and other operating systems.

Stop if either child proof is incomplete or stale; if composition needs an Eon-side behavior patch, adapter, or second schema; if the profile cannot resolve exactly to the candidate; or if another active frontier owns the component graph.

title: Show the last quota reading in a new Eon session until a fresh read succeeds
description:
## Why

Lucca, 2026-10-22: after starting a new Eon session the Claude chips were missing (screenshot: only
Codex, CPU, RAM and clock). Decision, Lucca 2026-10-22: "just show the old value while it doesn't
[get] the new value".

## Evidence (eon-78, 2026-10-22)

- The new supervisor g1-a8951bc5... started 12:09:43 -03 with the default `[bar] widgets`.
- At 12:12 the same CodexBar call Eon makes (`CodexBarCLI usage --provider claude --source oauth
  --format json --json-only --web-timeout 8`, codexbar 0.74.1) answered once with both windows, then
  twice with `{"error":{"message":"Claude OAuth usage endpoint is rate limited by Anthropic right
  now...","code":3}}` (exit 3).
- The Claude reading is held only in the supervisor's memory (`runtime/crates/eon-runtime/src/quota.rs`,
  `Provider.quota`), so a new supervisor starts with none. A failed first read leaves the bar
  without Claude chips until a read succeeds, at least 300 s later (EON-C27 cadence).
- Several live generations and isolated test sessions read with the same login, which makes the
  rate limit more likely.

## Contract (change needs Lucca's approval of the exact text before code)

EON-C27 failure policy: "A failed read keeps retained data unchanged" extends across a supervisor
restart. A new supervisor shows the last good reading for each listed provider until a read
succeeds, under the same rules as today: `old` after one hour, gone after 24 hours, a window gone at
its reset. Recommendation: both providers (one mechanism; Codex has the same gap), and the readings
are shared by all generations of one user, so a new window never shows less than an older one.
Recommended owner: Runtime, a small file per provider under `$XDG_STATE_HOME/eon/` holding only the
typed facts EONW already carries (windows, remaining percentage, resets, observation time). No
credential, identity, raw CodexBar output or billing data is stored (EON-C27 boundary).

## Reference gate (consequential: new persisted state)

Before code record in this bead: the one owner of the stored reading; the EON-C27 and EON-C32
routes read; how an unreadable, malformed, future-dated or other-version file is treated (ignored,
never zero usage); concurrent writers from two supervisors (atomic replace); and that a provider
left out of `[bar] widgets` is still neither read nor shown.

## Acceptance

- A Runtime test: a stored reading is shown by a new quota owner before any read, ages and expires
  as today, and a malformed or future file is ignored. `nix develop -c eon-test -p eon-runtime`.
- Isolated installed observation: a reading recorded by one supervisor appears in a newly started
  one whose first Claude read fails (e.g. a fake CodexBar returning the rate-limit error).
- Review loop per AGENTS.md; profile refresh.

## Scope boundary

No new chip state or wording, no change to read cadence, CodexBar, EONW or Venus.

Reference gate (consequential: new persisted state).
- Behavior and owner: a quota chip shows the last good reading in a new supervisor (or a chip shown again) until that provider's own read succeeds. Runtime's quota worker (runtime/crates/eon-runtime/src/quota.rs, Provider) is the one owner of the stored reading: it loads it when it starts and replaces it after each successful read. Venus, EONW and CodexBar are unchanged.
- Routes read: EON-C27 (cadence, failure policy, boundary) and EON-C32 via its use in EON-C27 ([bar] widgets selects providers). docs/REFERENCES.md has no quota or state-file route. Comparable implementation: Runtime's own state handling at edge c76a8a5. diagnostics.rs resolves $XDG_STATE_HOME/eon (falling back to $HOME/.local/state), and sessions.rs publishes records with create_new, mode 0600 and rename. Both kept.
- Format: $XDG_STATE_HOME/eon/quota/{codex,claude}.json, {version:1, observed_at, windows:[{duration_minutes, remaining_percent, resets_at}]}, with unknown fields denied. It holds only the typed facts EONW carries. Not EONW's codec: EONW is wire, not storage.
- Ignored, never zero usage: unreadable, malformed or unknown fields, a version other than 1, observed_at of 0 or in the future, empty windows, a percentage over 100, a zero or duplicate duration, a Claude duration other than 300 or 10080. Aging then runs through the existing present_at (old after 1 h, gone after 24 h, a window gone at its reset).
- Concurrent writers: each worker writes a private temporary file in the same directory (create_new, 0600, named for its pid and provider) and renames it over the reading, so a reader sees one whole reading. Last successful read wins. A successful read with no quota removes the stored reading.
- Hidden chips: a provider left out of [bar] widgets has no worker, so it neither reads, loads nor writes.
- Rejected: one file per generation (a new window could show less than an older one); polling the file while running (not needed for the approved behavior); storing EONW state (fresh or stale is derived from age, not stored).
- Dependencies: none new; serde, serde_json and libc are already pinned.

title: Eon themes, including light mode
description:
## Why

Lucca, 2026-10-23: "create a eon-themes epic bead including light-mode". Eon has one selectable dark look. Semantic chrome colors are already centralized in venus/src/render/palette.rs (eon-3bhr/eon-ffjr); product.rs:196 owns the ANSI default. eon-jjix owns the default fg/bg gap; current cursor contrast/trail policy means not every terminal color is untouched libghostty state. Users in bright rooms, users with light desktops, and users who need higher contrast have no option. The configurability audit (eon-configurability-audit-twdr) recorded a chrome theme as "configurable later" in eon-bepr; this epic owns that work now.

## Goal

Built-in dark and light themes, a user [theme] section, and Eon following the desktop's light or dark preference, with every state glyph (needs input, error, finished, working braille dots, idle) and every chrome surface legible in both.

## Children (file each when started; one fresh session each)

1. Delivered foundation (eon-3bhr/eon-ffjr): centralize chrome colors into one Venus palette with one meaning per color, splitting the shared green (focused vs Finished) and red (Error vs hint modifiers). No visible change. Contracts VEN-C1, VEN-C21. This is eon-bepr's step 1.
2. Carry the terminal default foreground, background, cursor and selection colors as an Orbit input (ORB-C2), so a theme sets the terminal too, not just the chrome.
3. A [theme] config section with built-in "dark" (today) and "light", plus overrides; Eon Runtime parses it and sends resolved values (Configurability rule). Contracts EON-C19 and VEN-C21. Integrates eon-configurability-qkq8.5 ([terminal] palette).
4. Follow the system preference: theme = "auto" reads the freedesktop color-scheme setting (xdg-desktop-portal) and switches live, with no restart. Reference gate: how Ghostty, kitty, WezTerm and GTK apps do it.
5. A contrast check: a scene test that renders every state glyph and chrome surface in both themes and fails below a contrast threshold (WCAG-style), so a later color change can't make light mode unreadable.

Reference: docs/VISUAL-REFERENCES.md names Ramps (perceptual OKLCH ramps, semantic light and dark tokens, enforced contrast) as the starting point for an Eon palette.

## Related

eon-bepr (closed, superseded by this epic's children 1-3), eon-configurability-qkq8.5 (palette), eon-jrz0 (chrome font size), working badge (braille-dot colors must hold in light mode).

## Acceptance

- Installed observation in both themes and in auto mode switching live, with the contrast test green.
## Current owners and remaining scope

Light work is split under eon-eon-themes-or3q.1. Consume eon-jjix's fg/bg owner, eon-dmbbf's scheme planning and eon-configurability-qkq8.5's ANSI input. The parent's [theme] direction and dmbbf's [terminal] theme proposal need explicit reconciliation before keys ship; neither silently overrides the other. System-auto live switching and cursor/selection input remainders stay required parent scope, filed after settings/lifetime decisions. Explicit dark/light delivery does not close this outer epic. Presentation colors follow the feature route; actual config/wire/lifecycle text needs approval.

title: Show the running Eon version in the Eon Bar
description:
## Contract

A full-Eon user sees a compact read-only version badge in the existing Eon Bar, like Nova's version badge. Show the version of the Eon runtime serving that window, for example `EON 0.1.0`, with the complete version available to accessibility and hover if visually shortened. Updating a profile or bundle must not make an already-running window report the newer installation's version. Missing, invalid or disconnected identity must never become an invented version or the Venus version.

## Evidence and reference gate

Inspected on 2026-10-11:
- Nova `38a5e29eb078e939d9729dfdbbdf3362292c20b9`, `flake.nix:779` and `packaging/bar-render-request.nix`: packaging supplies runtime_identity.json and passes its runtime directory to the bar. Nova Bar `7295e9976803de8d912f766f1b00ad12652e3e9b`, `src/bin/nova_bar_widget.rs:74-147`: the version command reads that identity and formats a compact NOVA version/channel badge. Adopt the visible runtime-owned identity principle; do not copy its command polling, Zellij machinery, beta formatting or channel assumptions.
- Eon edge HEAD `d3b280870e046246f91c3c82f235c3ef9c6e90e5`, with existing working-tree changes: `crates/eon/src/product.rs:23` supplies Inputs.version from Cargo. There is already a version owner; no second version literal or generated identity file is needed merely for this widget.
- Eon Runtime `e30cf43b7ccc752d33edd4626aabbc4fd1cec579`, `crates/eon-runtime/src/supervisor.rs:1479-1483`: live Runtime facts already contain eon_version and generation. `cli.rs:400` reports the invoked executable's version, which is not sufficient evidence for another running window. Canonical EONW `v7.rs` reexports Runtime/LifecycleResponse; its Snapshot inherited from `v6.rs:42` does not contain the version.
- Venus inspected HEAD `14f6e7e32ff5dccf1f5f9b0b9c79faa2e11be18b` (Eon currently pins accepted runtime source `58f2eaa8057627bdbf73262fdb10a1dc8b681ffc`): `src/scene.rs:234,690` owns the existing read-only quota projection and responsive header, `src/render.rs` draws it and its tooltip, and `src/accessibility.rs:321` exposes static facts. EON-C21/EON-C22 and `docs/REFERENCES.md`'s canonical workspace-protocol route provide the established boundary.

Before implementation, reread these owners and compare accepted Orbit/Venus revisions with Eon's manifest pins. First evaluate reusing the existing live presentation/lifecycle identity boundary; extend the canonical typed snapshot only if that is the smallest correct route. Record that choice and any required exact protocol revision before consumer work. Never parse CLI stdout, inspect Nix store paths, query Git, or guess from the current installation to identify a live window.

## Ownership, prerequisites and scope

Eon owns the requested display policy, product version input, exact composition and delivery. Eon Runtime owns authoritative live identity; canonical EONW owns cross-process facts; Venus owns native layout, rendering, hover and AccessKit. Orbit remains unchanged terminal authority.

The native bar prerequisite is already accepted (`eon-deliver-native-eon-bar-w4d`, EON-C21); the accepted Codex chip is a presentation reference. No Claude/Grok quota bead blocks this work. Keep one active frontier: prove any necessary Runtime/EONW change, then Venus, then consume exact accepted child revisions in Eon.

Deliver one version badge in the current single row, visible at ordinary widths. When shortcut help is visible, place the version badge immediately before `?`, with close remaining last. The user approved restoring this order on 2026-10-13. On constrained widths preserve active-tab identity and required controls ahead of informational chips, without overlap or terminal-grid loss. Keep the badge read-only and preserve keyboard/terminal focus. Index the chosen product contract before implementation and update only affected documentation, changelog and LOC on delivery.

The user approved one startup preference: `[bar] show_version = false` hides the complete label; omission inherits true. No generic widget framework, polling service, new dependency, settings UI, update button, release/channel inference, generation hash display, component inventory panel, second row or platform expansion. The current semver may be identical across development builds; this bead does not promise distinct build identification or change versioning policy.

## Acceptance and cheapest falsifiers

1. An isolated installed native Linux Wayland window shows its supervising Eon's version, with a clear accessible name such as `Eon version 0.1.0`. A controlled old-runtime/new-installation mismatch proves the badge stays bound to the live owner, not PATH, profile, bundle selector or Venus's Cargo version.
2. The same observation covers ordinary/narrow layout, hover, accessibility and preserved tab/control/terminal input behavior. Missing or rejected identity cannot display a fabricated valid version or block workspace use. Reuse existing native scene/accessibility checks; add only focused regression/boundary checks needed for the selected transport, not literal mirror tests.
3. Exact manifest/lock identities and affected builds pass. A shared EONW/runtime boundary change requires the full affected Rust/Nix route; a consumer-only implementation uses the narrower applicable route. Refresh the active eon profile and verify the installed artifact, preserving live supervisors and desktop focus. Check the changed artifact in the approved Nix-free alpha delivery too if its packaging is affected.
4. Record exact revisions, environment, commands/observations and proof phase. Stop and resolve the owner/transport choice if delivery requires a second version source, speculative child API or wider feature scope; do not close on a static mock or source-tree screenshot.
notes: User selected implementation on 2026-10-12: native built-in read-only Eon <version>, visible by default, [bar] show_version = false hides both identity and version. This explicitly supersedes the original no-settings boundary only for this one boolean. Apply at window open/reopen; no widget framework, extra shortcut, polling, live configuration reload, channel inference or build-ID promise.
close_reason: Restored EON version before shortcut help, close last; native and exact installed accessibility/pointer/visibility checks pass. Current combined profile refreshed without restarting live terminals. Concurrent quota work preserved.

title: Decide EonJS renderer-owned capture boundary
description:
## Contract Routing

- This is a planning and architecture decision. It changes no current `EON-C*`, `ORB-C*`, or `VEN-C*` contract and creates no runtime behavior, repository, module, dependency, protocol, language, or compatibility promise.
- `EonJS` is a working label for a possible future **Eon for the web** renderer. The accepted public/repository naming remains `Eon for the web` / `eon-web`; closure must decide the durable technical name and owner before implementation.
- Orbit remains the sole process, PTY, terminal-emulation, terminal-state, attachment, terminal-query, and semantic-input-encoding owner.
- Eon remains the workspace, lifecycle, composition, compatibility, and product-policy owner. Venus remains the native rendering owner. A future web client may own its own pixels but must not become another terminal authority.
- Implementation requires a separately activated owner-specific Bead after exact contract, language/toolchain, reference, dependency, portability, and active-frontier approval.

## Why

A future Eon web renderer could make deterministic screenshots and recordings a nearly free output target of the actual product renderer. If capture is added later as a separate renderer, it would duplicate font/layout/compositing policy and could disagree with the displayed Eon surface. If it is treated as a terminal emulator, it would also violate Orbit authority. The decision is cheap before a web renderer exists and expensive after its rendering boundary hardens.

Effort: S for the decision. Implementation effort is intentionally unestimated until the renderer and protocol boundary exist. Risk: MED because this crosses a future repository, language/toolchain, rendering, and Orbit-client boundary. Confidence: HIGH in the ownership constraint; MED in the future implementation shape.

## Evidence

- `docs/ARCHITECTURE.md:11-20,65-93` assigns PTY and terminal state to Orbit, native rendering to Venus, workspace policy to Eon, and forbids Eon from implementing terminal parsing or rendering.
- `docs/ARCHITECTURE.md:38-41` reserves `Eon for the web` / `eon-web` for a separately implemented future client.
- `docs/CONTRACTS.md:18` proves `EON-C4`: Eon adds no duplicate terminal or rendering state.
- `AGENTS.md:252-259` requires explicit user approval before durable TypeScript or another implementation language is added.
- `AGENTS.md:286-302` permits research and Beads to prepare a later frontier but forbids implementation against speculative child APIs.
- Joshka Betamax at exact main revision `7fbaa1598e3601ccb60f244a8c669d60a6d780db` demonstrates an efficient PTY → `libghostty-vt` → persistent renderer → in-process PNG/GIF/state pipeline without tmux, a browser, or termshot. It is a comparison, not a dependency or source-reuse choice.
- Ghostty discussion `#12610`, answered 2026-05-12, records the material limitation: `libghostty-vt` exposes render state but no single canonical Ghostty pixel output; consumers own rendering.
- Related decision `eon-pxn.7` asks whether Eon owns agent-driven terminal-testing behavior. It may later consume a capture surface, but neither decision blocks or implies the other.

## Decision Question

If the user activates Eon for the web, should its actual product renderer be the sole terminal-to-pixel owner for both interactive presentation and deterministic capture, exposing an offscreen RGBA/PNG target from the same render path, or should Eon rely on external capture tooling?

## Smallest Candidate Contract

- Consumer: a future Eon for the web client and an explicitly authorized local capture caller.
- Trigger: the renderer has accepted one exact source-labeled Orbit presentation revision plus fixed render configuration, and the caller requests a bounded capture.
- Result: the same renderer path used for interactive presentation renders an offscreen surface and returns bounded RGBA or PNG with renderer, frame, font, theme, scale, dimensions, and clock identity sufficient to reproduce or reject the artifact.
- Important failures: incompatible or stale presentation revision, incomplete state, missing or mismatched font/resource, unsupported graphic, invalid dimensions, surface/readback failure, cancellation, timeout, and encoder failure are explicit and produce no falsely authoritative artifact.
- Authority: the artifact proves the selected web renderer's pixels only. It does not prove native Venus pixels or a universal Ghostty/Eon appearance.

## Scope

In scope:
- Decide whether built-in renderer-owned capture is part of a future Eon for the web boundary.
- Compare no built-in capture, external Betamax-like tooling, actual-renderer offscreen capture, native Venus offscreen capture, and compositor/window capture.
- Decide the owner and minimum boundary for presentation-state consumption, deterministic rendering inputs, offscreen pixels, artifact metadata, encoding, cancellation, cleanup, and failure reporting.
- Decide whether TypeScript/JavaScript and a browser, Node, Deno, WASM, Canvas, WebGPU, or another runtime removes enough complete responsibility to justify its toolchain and portability cost.
- Select at most one disposable proof, or record that external tooling is sufficient.

Out of scope:
- Implementing EonJS, `eon-web`, a renderer, capture API, tape language, recorder CLI, GIF/video encoder, browser server, agent harness, MCP/plugin surface, CI job, or remote service.
- Creating another PTY owner, VT parser, terminal emulator, Orbit schema mirror, raw-PTY consumer, OCR authority, or concurrent input-capable Orbit client.
- Claiming pixel identity with Venus, Ghostty, arbitrary terminals, operating-system compositors, or different font/platform stacks.
- Choosing arbitrary split trees, broader web access, authentication, collaboration, persistence, streaming, or distribution.

## Reference And Tool Gates

At activation, inspect exact accepted Orbit and Eon protocol revisions, the selected web-renderer candidates, Joshka Betamax `7fbaa1598e3601ccb60f244a8c669d60a6d780db`, and Ghostty discussion `#12610`. Resolve any named `RioTermJS` reference to an exact repository and revision before using it; an unresolved project name is not evidence. title: Expose caller-owned application identity through EonTerm
description:
## Outcome and contract

Fix the observed native-Wayland launcher collision by giving each Eon surface the application identity owned by its caller before Venus creates the window. This implementation creates `VEN-C17` and `EON-C16`; the user's 2026-08-24 instruction “fix it” approves this exact Eonova-driven contract.

- Consumer: full Eon, standalone EonTerm, or one approved EonTerm composition.
- Trigger: launch a new native terminal surface through Eon/EonTerm; an approved composition may supply one validated desktop application ID.
- Result: full Eon uses `eon`, standalone EonTerm uses `eonterm`, and Eonova supplies `eonova`. Eon passes the selected value unchanged to Venus before window creation; Venus maps it through exact winit `WindowAttributesExtWayland::with_name`, whose general name is the Wayland app ID. Each value matches the corresponding desktop-file basename where one exists, so launchers can distinguish Eonova from an already-running Eon window.
- Failures: an absent consumer override uses the mode-owned default; a non-UTF-8, empty, oversized, or non-token identity fails before Orbit or Venus starts. A profile refresh never mutates an already-running surface; that supervisor keeps its original identity until the user closes or stops it.

Eon owns defaults, validation, the EonTerm invocation surface, and the one-way launch value. Venus owns only native mapping and retains `eon` as its direct-invocation default. Eonova owns only its fixed `eonova` choice and matching desktop metadata. Orbit titles, PTY state, child argv/environment, and Session lifetime remain unchanged.

## Minimum shape

1. Add one optional `--application-id ID` argument to Venus and project it through the existing launch structure into `with_name`; keep the direct default `eon`.
2. Add one optional `--application-id ID` before EonTerm's `-- COMMAND...`; full Eon supplies `eon`, bare EonTerm supplies `eonterm`, and Eon passes exactly one value to Venus for initial and replacement presentation processes.
3. Update Eonova's existing wrapper to pass `--application-id eonova` and change its desktop `StartupWMClass` to `eonova` so metadata is honest on systems that consult it.
4. Update contract/help/current-state docs and exact pins in owner order: Venus, Eon, Eonova.

Reuse the existing parser, launch struct, `venus_command`, winit native seam, wrapper, and desktop item. Add no dependency, protocol version, registry, branding object, mutable identity, title coupling, environment inference, command inspection, desktop-file loading, or second launcher path.

## References and evidence

Required and inspected before code:

- Exact winit source at patched 0.30.13 commit `fb45fbf901fbe70cc9a877b5d651d0b60c206b08`: Wayland `with_name(general, instance)` maps `general` to xdg-toplevel app ID and ignores `instance`.
- Freedesktop Desktop Entry specification: application names/desktop IDs use an ASCII desktop-file-compatible identity and window app IDs should match the desktop-file basename.
- Venus `cd2c63363d670e27f09c26d3c8889d2849eabaec`: `application.rs` hardcodes `with_name("eon", "yazelix-venus")`; `launch.rs` already owns bounded CLI parsing before window creation.
- Eon `4a89960c17877e072cd23fa5ceab1e2cfd285da9`: `cli.rs` owns EonTerm invocation and `supervisor.rs::venus_command` owns every initial/replacement Venus argv. Current accepted Venus source pin is `ee3defea55c77f7acc4559606965d93d39bba8b5`.
- Eonova `d8a8729f442f3d535b30fd22ac8dc7b6da4626dd`: wrapper selects a private runtime namespace but passes no application identity; both Eon and Eonova desktop entries advertise `StartupWMClass=yazelix-venus`. Reproduced on COSMIC Wayland: the desktop entry's exact executable is valid and direct launch starts EonTerm, Orbit, Venus, and Nova, while shared native identity prevents reliable launcher distinction.

Rejected: changing only `StartupWMClass` while Venus still publishes app ID `eon`; deriving identity from child argv, executable name, environment, title, icon, or runtime path; adding product knowledge to Venus; changing Orbit/EONW protocols; a general branding framework; supporting X11/Xwayland or other platforms.

Portability disposition: neutral bounded identity value with one isolated native Wayland mapping. This creates no additional platform promise.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. Venus deterministically accepts its direct `eon` default and one valid caller ID, rejects invalid values before window creation, and applies the accepted ID to the native Wayland attributes while title updates remain independent.
2. Full Eon launches Venus with `eon`; bare EonTerm launches it with `eonterm`; `eonterm --application-id eonova -- COMMAND...` launches initial and replacement Venus processes with `eonova` without exposing the value to the PTY child.
3. Existing decoration, opacity, blur, cursor, socket, presentation, repeat-launch, recovery, and Session-lifecycle behavior remains exact. No wire contract changes.
4. Eonova's wrapper supplies `eonova`, its desktop metadata matches, and package/runtime namespaces remain unchanged and isolated.
5. Focused parser/argv checks, full affected locked Rust checks, Eon and Eonova Nix checks/builds, desktop validation, closure/license checks, LOC scorecards, and `git diff --check` pass.
6. After exact owner commits/pins and profile refreshes, native Wayland dogfood shows Open Eon and Eonova as distinct launcher/running-window identities. Repeated Eonova launch presents the existing Eonova surface rather than focusing Eon or creating a second Session.

## Scope boundary and stop conditions

In scope: one bounded ID string, Eon/EonTerm defaults, the existing Venus Wayland window-attribute seam, Eonova's fixed wrapper/desktop metadata, exact pins, docs, tests, and installed proof.

Out of scope: mutable identity, per-generation identity negotiation, branding/icons, a provider registry, desktop-entry discovery, X11/Xwayland/macOS, new distribution channels, or changes to Orbit, EONW, Nova, Zellij, or live Session ownership.

Stop and return to the user if the existing one-way launch value cannot fix COSMIC without a runtime/wire protocol, a second identity/branding structure, a new dependency, or changes outside Venus, Eon, and Eonova composition metadata.
close_reason: Installed distinct Eonova identity and crash-residue recovery accepted by user on native COSMIC Wayland.
