title: Draw columns and popups as one flush workspace sheet
description:
## Decision
Lucca, 2026-10-17: replace the per-column rounded frames, which have side margins and a gap of about
12 logical pixels between columns, with one flush workspace sheet:
- The sheet spans the window's full width; its side edges sit on the window edges (no side margin).
- Adjacent columns share one 1-pixel seam instead of two parallel edges.
- Seams meet the sheet's top line and the footer (or the sheet's bottom line when hints are hidden)
  in straight T-junctions, not rounded notches.
- The sheet's outer corners stay rounded. Rule: objects are round (tabs, chips, the sheet's outer
  corners); dividing lines inside the sheet are straight.
- Popups use the same sheet. VEN-C18 already makes a popup reuse the pane stack's outer frame (one
  full-width frame over several columns), so popups follow the sheet. `popup.side_margin` and
  `popup.vertical_margin` inset popup terminal content inside that frame and stay unchanged.
- Zoom (`eon-zoom-selected-pane-e2pv`) shows the zoomed pane in the same sheet with no seam.

Why: two 1-pixel edges about 12 px apart, each 6-8 px from its own text, read as one double rule;
the gap shows the terminal background (#040507 in the 2026-10-17 dogfood capture) and carries no
information. A clearly wider gap (about 36 px) reads as separate cards but costs about four
terminal cells per seam against Venus's 40-cell column floor. Rounded seam ends pinch into a wedge
at 1 px and an 8 px radius and dent the header fills.

## Contract (to approve before code)
- Consumer: a full-Eon user with `[terminal] pane_frames = true` (the default).
- Result: as in Decision, for one to four columns, with hints shown or hidden, and with a popup
  open. Selection and hover keep their current header fills; the pane-focus outline draws over the
  shared seam where it touches it. `pane_frames = false` keeps removing lines and separators while
  keeping headers.
- Contract edits: EON-C8's frame bullet ("one rounded border around each column's visible pane
  stack", side margins), VEN-C8 frame geometry, VEN-C18 geometry wording if needed, and
  `docs/USAGE.md`'s frame paragraph. No configuration default, EONW or Orbit change.
- Important failures: a double edge left at a seam or window edge; a seam that misses its
  T-junction; a terminal grid that changes size other than by the reclaimed margins; a popup toggle
  that moves any outer edge.

## References (read 2026-10-17)
- Zed `crates/workspace/src/pane_group.rs` @ 62507a19: one 1 px divider (`DIVIDER_SIZE`) with a 4 px
  drag hitbox (`HANDLE_HITBOX_SIZE`).
- Ghostty `src/config/Config.zig` @ 45db2c255: one divider (`split-divider-color`); focus shown by
  dimming unfocused splits (`unfocused-split-opacity` 0.7), not by frames.
- tmux shared pane borders with T junctions; macOS split views (thin divider); Hyprland and niri
  use wide gaps because their windows are separate objects.
- Grouping by shared boundary (NN/g common region), Refactoring UI "use fewer borders", and the
  concentric-radius rule (inner = outer minus the gap; it applies only to nested shapes, never to
  sibling seams).
- Rejected: wider gap (width cost, busy at four columns); rounded seam ends (wedge, mixed signal);
  square outer corners (loses Eon's soft language where the sheet really has a corner).
- Cheapest falsifier: one isolated installed capture at two and four columns, hints shown and
  hidden, with a popup toggled, enlarged at a seam end and at a window edge.

## Owners
Venus owns scene geometry, rendering, hit testing and accessibility. Eon owns EON-C8's product
text. Eon Runtime, EONW and Orbit are unchanged. Portability: neutral.

## Prerequisites
After `eon-7rk3` (closed 2026-10-17; it moved this drawing into `venus/src/render/chrome.rs`).
`eon-zoom-selected-pane-e2pv` follows this bead so zoom is designed on the sheet.

## Acceptance
- Lucca approves the contract edits.
- Installed Eon shows the sheet as decided at one, two and four columns, hints shown and hidden,
  popup open and closed, and `pane_frames = false`; terminal grids gain only the reclaimed width.
- Venus suites pass through `nix develop -c eon-test -p yazelix-venus`, with any changed geometry
  goldens updated deliberately; Venus fmt and clippy green; `nix build --no-link .#default`; one
  isolated installed dogfood observation; refresh the active Nix profile without interrupting live
  workspaces. Changelog entry for the visible change.

## Scope boundary
No column resizing, focus dimming, theme or color change, popup margin change or new configuration.
Standalone EonTerm keeps receiving no workspace frame.
close_reason: Flush workspace sheet shipped: window-edge sides, shared 1-px seams with straight T-junctions, rounded outer corners only, popups and footer on the same frame; frameless mode unchanged. Proof and 3-pass ledger in comments.

title: Adopt Starcompass 2720d5e (AP-MINIMAL-001 v7, AP-SCOPE-001 v5, AP-CONTRACT-001 v5)
description:
## Why

Eon pins Starcompass 2af5afb, whose AP-SESSION-001 v2 has agents delegate from 100k, add no steps from 180k, and start each issue fresh unless under 100k. On a 1M window, agents suggest a new session at about 15%. Since 2026-10-19 a user-level Claude Code hook (~/.claude/hooks/context-usage.py) reports context usage to the model at each 100k step, so the v2 marks now trigger every time.

Starcompass a37e2b1 (on origin/edge) carries:
- AP-SESSION-001 v3: from 400k add no scope or new steps, close the issue if it can close by 600k, else bring work to a verified state and hand off. Hand off before the host would compact or after any compaction. The 100k, 180k and 250k marks and the fresh-start rule are gone. Evidence and trials are on Starcompass ap-56s.
- AP-MINIMAL-001 v5: the Ponytail paragraph is gone. Starcompass README gives overlay text for repositories that use Ponytail.
- AP-PROOF-001 v10, with performance claims moved to AP-PERF-001, which Eon gets through terminal-engine. AP-REFERENCE-001 v4, with license interpretation moved to AP-LICENSE-001 (fork profile only).

## Scope

1. Re-render from a clean Starcompass checkout at a37e2b1 with Eon's existing inputs: the three nested directories and `--protocol-file docs/AGENT-PROTOCOLS.md`, following Eon's documented import steps.
2. Ponytail: Eon's code carries `// ponytail:` comments, but its overlay doesn't mention Ponytail. Ask the owner whether to paste the Starcompass README's Ponytail overlay snippet into `.agent-protocols.local.md`, and add it if yes.
3. Run `starcompass check` from the checkout at a37e2b1 and `check-consumer`, plus Eon's checks for the changed files.

Out of scope: other overlay changes. A second bump follows Starcompass ap-jo9.7, which lowers the byte caps and reruns the full behavior-trial suite.

## Acceptance

- `.agent-protocols.json` pins a37e2b1, and `AGENTS.md`, `docs/AGENT-PROTOCOLS.md` and the nested files match it. `starcompass check` and `check-consumer` pass.
- The owner's Ponytail decision is recorded on this bead.

## Stop Conditions

- Stop and ask if `check` fails for a reason other than the pin change.

title: Decide whether Orbit survives a Bend worker fault
description:
## Why

Every Orbit decision comes from the Bend worker, so a worker fault ends the user's terminal. When the
worker dies (a Bend `runtime fail-stop`, a crash, the OOM killer) or stalls past the host's 2 s
answer deadline, the host contains the session: it hangs up and reaps the PTY child, removes the
socket and exits (`orbit/docs/BEHAVIOR.md`, "Fatal-exit boundary"). The single-process Rust Orbit
(tag `orbit-rust-final`) had no such failure mode. Orbit's core promise is that the terminal
outlives everything else, so a defect in the policy layer, the part that is meant to be the
safest, now costs the user their live processes.

Decide whether Orbit should survive a worker fault and, if it should, how, without giving Rust a
second copy of the session policy.

## Evidence

- `orbit/docs/BEHAVIOR.md:1744`: Fatal-exit boundary. A dead or stalled worker is contained like a
  termination: SIGHUP, 500 ms, SIGKILL, reap, socket unlink, exit 1 for a stall
  (`orbit: worker stalled: no answer within 2 s`).
- `orbit/docs/HOST.md`, "What Rust holds": the host keeps no session state that Bend decides from,
  so today nothing can rebuild Bend's state after a fault.
- `orbit/src/host.rs:296` `decisions()` collects a whole answer before `carry_out`
  (`host.rs:1500`) runs, so a worker that dies mid-answer leaves none of that fact's decisions
  applied.
- `orbit/src/session.bend:38-53`: State includes session, shown and Status.Tracker.
  Re-measure checkpoint size/codec/proof cost; the small-state estimate predates status.
- Some facts are applied by the host before Bend answers, such as PTY output fed to libghostty or a
  resize (`HOST.md`, Decisions). Any retry must not apply them twice.
- How often it happens: answers took at most 7 ms in vtebench and at a load average near 10
  (lj8.80, quoted in BEHAVIOR.md). No dogfood signal beads were open at promotion (`eon-awmq.5`
  comment, 2026-10-20). The risk is untested, not observed.

## Options

A. **Keep containment (today).** Fail closed. No new code paths, and a Bend defect is loud.
   Cost: any worker fault ends the terminal.

B. **Restart the worker from a checkpoint Bend owns.** After each answer the worker also writes its
   encoded `State`. The host stores those bytes opaque and never decodes them. On death or stall the
   host starts a new worker, checks the schema handshake, hands it the last checkpoint and resends
   the fact in flight, which is safe because no decision of it was applied. Restarts are bounded,
   for example one per fact. A second fault on the same fact falls back to A.
   - Variant B2: on the repeated fault, instead of A, restore the checkpoint and send a recovery
     fact, such as dropping the client, for Bend to decide. The terminal survives a deterministic
     policy bug, and the client reattaches.
   - Cost: a boundary schema change, a `State` codec on both sides, a round-trip law
     (`decode(encode(s)) == s`) for you to approve, and more bytes per answer, which throughput
     would need to re-measure. B without B2 only helps faults that don't repeat (OOM kill,
     SIGSTOP, a runtime fault that depends on timing). A deterministic `step` bug would crash the
     restarted worker again.

C. **Rejected: a Rust fallback policy.** Rust keeps the child alive and runs its own minimal
   attach and stop rules while Bend is gone. That creates a second owner of session policy
   (AP-OWNERSHIP-001, `orbit/AGENTS.md` "Host and worker"), and a session nobody can attach to just
   leaves processes running unseen.

Recommendation: B with B2, if the reference read and a test of the recovery fact show it fits.
Policy stays in Bend. The checkpoint round trip can be proved. And B2 covers the failure that is
actually plausible: a deterministic bug in `step`. Otherwise keep A and record why.

## Scope

In scope (planning only):
- The reference gate below, recorded here.
- The chosen option, with a proposed contract delta. Survival changes the Fatal-exit boundary and
  probably needs ORB-C12 wording or a new ORB-C ID. Show that proposal and any new law to Lucca
  and stop for approval.
- If B is chosen, the implementation beads (schema and codec, the round-trip law and proof, host
  restart, B2 recovery fact, throughput re-measure), filed after approval.

Out of scope:
- Code, schema, `LAWS.bend` or contract edits in this bead.
- Moving Bend in-process, or a different host/worker split.
- Changing the 2 s stall deadline or the SIGHUP/SIGKILL timings.

## Reference gate

Consequential: lifecycle and failure boundary, host/worker wire format, Orbit contract.
- Required by `orbit/docs/REFERENCES.md` "PTY and session lifetime": FrankenTerm (lifecycle
  states, protocol recovery, crash and reconnect checks) before changing failure semantics. zmx,
  shpool and abduco for how session survival is owned.
- `orbit/docs/REFERENCES.md` "Session policy in Bend": Bend at `234cb9b9` and bend-orbit at
  `e03926274203`, for whether `State` can be encoded and the round-trip law proved within
  BEND.md's proof costs.
- Record sources and inspected revisions, constraints kept, rejected approaches, and the decision
  and its check.

## Acceptance

- One option is chosen, with the reasons for it and for each rejected option recorded here, plus
  Lucca's approval of any contract or law change.
- If B: the implementation beads exist with dependencies. The first one has a check that fails
  first: a fixture worker killed mid-session, after which the terminal survives and a client
  reattaches. Orbit already has the `Fault` containment fixture.

## Verification

- Planning only: `br show` on this bead and on any children, and the diff of `.beads/` after
  `br sync --flush-only`. No runtime proof or profile refresh.

## Stop Conditions

- Stop for Lucca before any contract text, ORB-C status or `LAWS.bend` change.
- Stop if the host has moved enough since `e1d7a7c` that the evidence above is wrong. Note that
  `eon-awmq.8` may move host platform calls.

## Maintenance Notes

- Order the implementation after `eon-awmq.8` (host platform seam) so the two don't edit
  `host.rs` at once.
- Rejected alternatives and their reasons stay in Options above.
- Weigh Bend's native library target (bendlang/bend #813, "planned, not scheduled" at `234cb9b9`).
  It would let Orbit link the worker in process with no C of its own (`orbit/build.rs` already
  compiles Bend's generated C). That removes the pipe/process boundary but moves faults into the host; it does not prove
  session survival, so
  B's checkpoint and restart work would be partly wasted if #813 lands soon.
- The architecture stays as it is (Lucca, 2026-10-21): Rust host plus Bend worker, kept for its
  proofs over the shipped policy, its marketing value, and Bend's trajectory. Fallbacks, should a
  trigger fire; neither is a revert to `orbit-rust-final`:
  - **Bend itself becomes the cost** (an upgrade breaks code or proofs, or Bend work makes
    boundary epics such as `orb-ll1` or `orb-p92` clearly slower than in Rust). Move `step` into
    in-process Rust behind the same fact/decision boundary, with `LAWS.bend` restated as Kani
    bounded proofs and property tests over fact traces (`orb-reconsider-verus-eon-state-machine-kpw`
    covers the Verus alternative).
  - **Only Bend at runtime becomes the cost** (a measured throughput regression on the shipped
    Orbit, or worker faults this bead cannot contain). Keep Bend's `step` and laws as the proved
    specification, ship a Rust `step` in process, and gate them in CI with a differential check over
    the same fact lines. Cost: every policy change is written twice.


## Current baseline superseding older preflight notes

At dcaef1c eon-awmq.8 and eon-bend-2040-036p8 are closed; the platform seam and Bend
2.0.40 are already baseline, not future blockers. host.rs:93 still sets a two-second
deadline. Re-locate future drift from this baseline rather than stopping solely because
the original e1d7a7c moved. Preserve Lucca's host/worker architecture and unresolved
A/B/B2 choice; neither the upgrade nor this refresh approves recovery. Portability:
neutral decision, native process mechanics remain in Orbit's seam.

Ask Lucca first whether to take A-with-triggers now or spend the reference gate on B/B2.

Current source: host.rs:80-85 retains a 2 s incomplete-answer deadline; :285 collects a complete answer, :297-301 sends one fact then waits; :1395 carries decisions out; session.bend:38-53 holds Session, Shown and Status.Tracker; HOST.md:96-104 makes whole-step proof coverage conditional on host fact ordering. title: Keep a terminal alive when its hyperlinks overflow the frame budget
description:
## Why

Found by eon-69 while fixing eon-osc8-invalid-utf8-ymts (2026-10-23); an inference from the code, not yet reproduced. An Orbit frame has a 4 MiB budget (`MAX_FRAME_BYTES`), and `FrameSize::add_cell` returns EOVERFLOW past it. The pinned Ghostty (8c425a7) stores an OSC 8 URI of up to about 2046 bytes per link. A 100x24 screen whose 2400 cells each carry a different ~2 KB URI makes about 4.9 MB, over the budget. Every frame error propagates to `host.rs` `run` → `contain()`, which HUPs the child, so the terminal ends. Valid output, from a program or a `cat`ed file, could therefore end a terminal. Larger screens need shorter URIs to get there.

## Scope

In scope:
- First, a unit test that builds a frame over the budget from valid hyperlinks, red, to confirm the inference. If it's not reachable (for example Ghostty dedups or caps links per page), record why and close the bead.
- If confirmed: bring the behavior choice to the overseer or Lucca before code. Candidates: (a) send each distinct URI once per frame and have cells reference it, which is an ORBF wire change consumed by Venus and bend-orbit; (b) past the budget, drop links (cells keep text) for the rest of the frame; (c) cap per-frame link bytes. The recommendation goes with the choice. In every case the terminal never ends because of its own output.
- The ORB-C6 (and ORBF, if (a)) wording, the fix, a real-PTY or unit check, and the changelogs.

Out of scope: invalid-UTF-8 URIs (ymts), and link opening in Venus.

## Acceptance

- The red unit test, then green: a frame whose links exceed the budget does not end the terminal, and its cells keep their text.

## Verification

`nix develop -c eon-test -p yazelix-orbit`, Orbit fmt and clippy, the relevant nix orbit-* check, and converge plus Codex. If ORBF changes, add the full affected Rust and Nix surfaces.

Portability disposition: neutral.
close_reason: A frame whose links exceed the budget keeps every cell's text and a reading-order prefix of the links; the terminal no longer ends. ORB-C6 updated as approved. Proof on the landing commit.

comments.text: Confirmed 2026-10-23 by eon-9b with a frame.rs unit test. 100x24 with 2399 distinct 2 KB URIs does not overflow: pinned Ghostty keeps at most 1663 distinct links per page (u16 hyperlink capacity), 3.37 MB, and drops the rest itself. 400x240 (3 pages), ten 2 KB links per row: FrameExtractor::frame fails EOVERFLOW. Any viewport spanning >=2 pages can overflow; small screens straddling a page boundary inferred, not reproduced. Option (a) dedup does not fix distinct URIs. Plain greedy (b) can still overflow on later text. Proposed (b'): text first, links in reading order while they fit, plus compatible FrameSize::add_hyperlink. Choice and ORB-C6 wording sent to the overseer; no code yet.

title: Keep a terminal alive when its cell text alone overflows the frame budget
description:
## Why

Today's beads found three ways a program's own output ended its terminal: an invalid UTF-8 title or directory (atq2, landed 4900b7f), an invalid OSC 8 URI (ymts, landed ad64d81), and links overflowing the 4 MiB frame budget (m62b). eon-9b found a fourth while on m62b (2026-10-23), by reading the code, not yet reproduced. Cell text alone can pass the budget. Pinned Ghostty 8c425a7 `page.zig` keeps up to `grapheme_max_len = 64` extra codepoints per cell, and a page's `grapheme_bytes` grows without a practical cap. One cell then encodes to about 284 bytes, so about 14.8k such cells (about 19k with 3-byte marks such as U+20D0, e.g. 200x97) exceed 4 MiB. `frame()` gets EOVERFLOW from `size.add_cell(&text, "")`, and `host.rs` `run` → `contain()` HUPs the child. Zalgo text `cat`ed on a large screen would end the terminal.

The shared cause: any frame error ends the terminal. Fixing each overflow source one at a time leaves the next one live.

## Scope

In scope:
- Reproduce first, with a release-mode unit test or real-PTY zalgo output on a large screen. Red.
- Bring the behavior choice, with a recommendation, to the overseer or Lucca before code:
  (a) cap combining marks per cell in the frame so a full screen fits the budget by construction (cell text truncated past the cap);
  (b) when text alone exceeds the budget, send a degraded frame (for example the cell base codepoints only) instead of failing;
  (c) the general rule: a frame-size error fails or degrades that frame and never ends the terminal, which would also cover any future overflow source. This may combine with (a) or (b).
- The ORB-C6 wording, the fix, the check, and the changelogs.

Out of scope: hyperlink budgeting (m62b) and invalid UTF-8 (atq2, ymts).

## Acceptance

- The red test, then green: a frame whose cell text alone exceeds the budget does not end the terminal, and the client gets a frame whose degraded content is defined by the approved wording.

## Verification

`nix develop -c eon-test -p yazelix-orbit`, Orbit fmt and clippy, the relevant nix orbit-* check, and converge plus Codex.

Portability disposition: neutral.
close_reason: A frame whose cell text exceeds the budget keeps every cell's first codepoint, then full text and links in reading order while they fit; the terminal no longer ends. ORB-C6 updated as approved. Proof on the landing commit.

comments.text: Approval relayed by the overseer, 2026-10-23, under Lucca's approval that day ("i give you auto-approval to everything, until 700k / but the focus is landing the sidebar / our mission is: happy users", recorded on eon-agent-sidebar-yx8). Approved: (2) behavior (b'): every cell's first codepoint is budgeted first (at most 28 bytes a cell, 2.8 MB at MAX_CELLS), then full cell text and then links are kept in reading order while they fit; the rest degrade to their first codepoint and no link. Previews unchanged; no host-level change (option c not taken: the remaining frame errors are libghostty EIO/EPROTO internals). Option (a), a fixed per-cell cap, rejected: it would cut real emoji ZWJ and flag sequences. (3) Replace m62b's ORB-C6 bullet with exactly: "When a frame would pass the frame budget, every cell keeps its first codepoint; full cell text and then hyperlinks are kept in reading order while they fit; the rest reach the client as their first codepoint and as no link, and the terminal keeps running." Plus changelogs and BEHAVIOR.md.

title: eon-bench orbit vtebench sample flakes: attached client connect gets ConnectionRefused right after the socket exists
description:
## Why

Seen by the eon-igae.18 agent on 2026-11-12 18:13Z: whole-workspace eon-test on staged tree 41385328 (edge 1390bc2 plus release prep that does not touch Orbit or eon-bench) failed once: eon-bench::orbit orbit_runs_a_vtebench_sample_detached_and_attached, vtebench-light_cells orbit-attached connect: Connection refused (os error 111), right after the socket file exists (log: /home/lucca/.cache/eon-agents/eon-beta-prep-work/05-workspace-41385328.log lines 1143-1146). The exact focused rerun passed (07-vtebench-recheck-41385328.log). A green rerun does not prove a test-only defect: the harness may connect before Orbit listens (test race), or Orbit may expose the socket path before it accepts (product race that a real client could hit).

## Goal

Find which. If Orbit binds or creates the socket path before listen(), fix Orbit so a visible socket always accepts (and add a regression test). If it is the harness, make the harness wait on Orbit's own readiness signal instead of the socket file. Related: eon-5wu6m (runtime editor ConnectionRefused flake) may share the cause; check it.

## Done when

Root cause named with evidence; a stress loop (e.g. 200 runs through heavy.sh) shows no refusal after the fix; no new sleep-based wait.

title: Prove the eon CLI from a fresh SSH login: session, pane read and send, and events
description:
## Why
Every SSH-based phone option (plain SSH apps, Moshi's moshi-hook, later live attach) rests on the `eon` CLI working from a fresh SSH login into the desktop. The research verified this only from a shell with `EON_TERMINAL` unset, and assumed `XDG_RUNTIME_DIR=/run/user/1000` and PATH (mobile-report.md §1C, marked inference). Filed on Lucca's "yeah", 2026-11-12.

## Goal
From a real `ssh localhost` login (non-interactive and interactive; bash and nushell), prove these against a live window:
- `eon session --json`;
- `eon pane read`;
- `eon pane send --stdin --enter`, into a disposable pane;
- `eon events --json`.

Record which environment is needed: XDG_RUNTIME_DIR, PATH to the profile's eon, and the window namespace. If something fails, fix the smallest thing: a documented env line, or a CLI fallback that finds the runtime dir from the UID.

## Acceptance
A recorded transcript of the four commands passing from an SSH login, plus any needed fix. SO_PEERCRED same-UID behaviour is confirmed (runtime/crates/eon-runtime/src/platform.rs:182). Nothing listens on TCP.

## Verification
The manual proof against the installed build, plus `nix develop -c eon-test` if code changes.

title: Stop spawned Sessions whose Ready identity is rejected
description:
## Contract routing

Hardens EON-C1 launch failure and EON-C15 pre-lease rollback by consuming accepted ORB-C13 owner proof `2518512758c7848bbd87f907b105c8bcf0fc4e1b`. Before Ready, only a launcher-held exact empty record claim authorizes local Child rollback. After Orbit marks that retained inode, Eon uses only canonical management Stop on a matching spawned-child Live identity and never Child/PID fallback. Changes no Orbit, Venus, EONW, or workspace topology contract.

## Why

The original `eon-g3k` work fixed rejected Live identity cleanup but inferred the Ready boundary from record observations. Orbit can publish between the final absent-record observation and local Child stop. Accepted `orb-h1f` supplies the exact-inode lock-and-marker owner boundary needed to remove that race.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Start Orbit while Eon retains local-child rollback authority.
2. Let Orbit mark or publish Ready after Eon observes no canonical record but before Eon acts on a startup failure.
3. Observe that an inferred `published` flag can authorize Child SIGKILL after Orbit owns the run, bypassing management cleanup.

## Scope

In scope:
- exact Orbit pin `2518512758c7848bbd87f907b105c8bcf0fc4e1b` in the canonical component graph and derived Cargo/Nix locks
- `crates/eon/src/main.rs` retained Ready claim and `start_orbit` rollback
- `crates/eon/tests/workspace_control.rs` managed helper and regression coverage
- CHANGELOG, EON-C1/EON-C15 proof state, README LOC, Nix profiles

Out of scope:
- Child/PID/signal fallback after Ready
- recovering or killing foreign Live records
- Orbit or Venus source changes, Venus pin changes, EONW, workspace topology
- module-splitting Beads or implementation

## Acceptance Criteria

- Eon creates and retains the exact empty owned 0600 record claim before spawning Orbit.
- A launcher-held empty claim is the sole pre-Ready Child rollback authority and is held through local stop.
- A marked claim permanently forbids Child/PID fallback even if Live later disappears; a matching spawned-child Live record may be stopped only through management.
- Rejected Ready identity leaves no live helper or record, and retry reaches the existing Venus-launch failure path.
- Exact Orbit pin/locks, full Rust/Nix surfaces, refreshed `eon` and `eonterm` profiles, and the cheapest installed behavior check pass without interrupting live Sessions.

## Reference Gate

Consume the accepted ORB-C13 exact-inode claim contract and proof. Preserve EON-C15 one-owner rollback, Orbit ORB-C12 shutdown, FrankenTerm lifecycle-boundary evidence, and Process Triage observe/act serialization. Reject a directory lock, inferred boolean Ready state, Child kill after a marker, record deletion without an Orbit tombstone, a second lifecycle owner, or a new dependency.

## Stop Conditions

Stop if exact claim arbitration cannot remain inside the existing local filesystem/process seam, if Orbit/Venus source must change, or if completion would interrupt live Sessions.

title: Make eon pane create start reliably on a loaded machine instead of failing its first try
description:
## Why

`eon pane create --json --no-focus -- bash SCRIPT` sometimes fails on the first try with
`terminal-start: terminal did not publish Ready within five seconds`, and an immediate retry
succeeds. Seen 2026-11-10 (overseer log: a create right after another create failed silently)
and 2026-11-11 04:5xZ: load about 16 on 16 cores, the first create named terminal-88 and
failed with an empty Orbit log (~/.local/state/eon/logs/orbit/g1-c280...-terminal-88-...-169.log),
and no pane appeared; the retry got terminal-88 again as p79 and worked. Agents depend on this path
to start other agents (AGENTS.md rule 5), so a one-shot failure under load breaks automation.

## Scope

Reproduce under load, find whether the five-second Ready bound is too tight for a loaded machine
or a start step races, and fix or make the bound a documented, configurable value (rule 6).
A failed start must leave no half-made pane and must say whether a retry is safe.

## Acceptance

A loaded reproduction (repeated creates while builds run) no longer fails, or fails with a clear
retryable error; the proof is recorded here.
close_reason: Landed: wider start bound with cleanup ownership and stage timings; natural cause unproved, follow-up eon-vq1r3

comments.author: lucca
comments.text:
Landing proof: eon-g3vdz and eon-l4e7s (fixed together)

Cause story. The first-try failure of `eon pane create` under load is mitigated by the wider start bound. A timed-out or failed start now keeps ownership of its retained children on every path: the cleanup owner keeps them until they are reaped, and a bootstrap-failed supervisor exits on its own once they are reaped (failed Stop keeps the explicit retry policy). The timeout error now carries per-stage timings. The natural cause is unproved: 20/20 creates passed at load 17 on the baseline.

title: Draw panes as gapped rounded cards
description:
## Decision
Lucca, 2026-10-18: the flush, fully square workspace sheet (eon-sheet-square-top-corners-e8pp) works
but is not the look he wants. Of two options (two frame styles like Zellij, or only a gaps-and-rounded
style like Superlogical's Rex), he chose to plan the single gapped, rounded style. Recommendation
accepted for planning: one framed look, no style setting; the existing `false` pane-frames setting
stays the frameless option.

## Contract (provisional; wording needs Lucca's approval before code)
- Consumer: a full-Eon user with pane frames enabled (the default).
- Result: each column's pane stack draws as its own rounded card inset from the window by one even
  gap, with the same gap between side-by-side columns. Cards have a 1 px border, rounded corners
  and the terminal background fill; the expanded pane's header sits inside its card. No card corner
  touches a window edge, tab pill or the footer.
- Frameless (`false`) keeps today's meaning: no borders, seams or separators.
- Popups use the same card treatment.
- Terminal grid sizing still follows from the space inside the card; gaps never change terminal
  geometry rules beyond the space they take.
- Edits: EON-C8, VEN-C8, VEN-C24 (footer placement against cards), PRESENTATION.md, LAUNCH.md if it
  mentions the sheet, changelogs. The flush-sheet and square-corner clauses are replaced.

## Open decisions (recommendations)
1. Gap and radius: one gap value (about 8-10 logical px at default typography) and a radius that
   fits inside the smallest card; record exact values from captures, not as configuration.
2. Stacked panes in one column: one card per column with the collapsed headers inside it
   (recommended, keeps the accordion compact), versus one card per pane.
3. Footer hints: sit in the bottom margin below the cards, or inside the window's bottom gap.
4. Tab strip: unchanged in this slice; Rex-style pill tabs are a separate question.

## References (discovery only; no source reuse)
- Superlogical Rex macOS screenshot (Bitdoze article, https://www.bitdoze.com/superlogical-rex/,
  checked 2026-10-18): per-pane rounded cards, even gaps to window edges and between panes, title
  and pane controls inside each card, pill tabs in the title bar.
- Zellij `pane_frames` and `ui.pane_frames.rounded_corners`: record the exact release inspected.
- History to avoid repeating: eon-sheet rounded corners (86ccad7, ba92d0d) failed because curves on
  one flush sheet collided with window corners, the first tab pill, footer and label clearance.

## Prerequisites
None. Presentation only; no EONW, Orbit or runtime change expected.

## Acceptance
Venus suites, fmt, clippy for yazelix-venus; nix build; isolated captures at one, two and four
columns, a stacked column, hints shown and hidden, a popup, and frameless; review loop; profile
refresh. Lucca's installed look is the final acceptance.

## Scope boundary
Pane, column, popup and footer framing only. No new configuration key, second frame style, tab-strip
redesign, color or typography change, animation, or terminal-geometry policy change.
close_reason: Each column draws as its own rounded card with an even 8 px gap; popups as one card; hints bare below. Proof and ledger in comments.

title: Spike provider-native pane-agent message delivery and draft its CLI boundary
description:
## Why

Split out of eon-7jw6p (phone chat bridge) to keep each research bead to one session. Lucca,
2026-11-02 ('ok', recorded on eon-7jw6p): include "send a message to a pane's agent" as one CLI path
routed per agent, studied from david-crespo/ah (Claude Code inbox socket, `codex queue`, OpenCode
HTTP API), with an explicit trust rule (ah has no local auth). The phone bridge would use the same
CLI path, so this research comes first.

It also bears on eon-2o85l (agent sends interleaving with a person's typing) and eon-0um2b (keys
and interrupt): a message delivered through an agent's own inbox API does not type into the
terminal at all, so it cannot interleave with the person's typing or need named keys.

## Questions

1. For each launchable agent (Claude Code, Codex, OpenCode, Pi, Grok), which supported message or
   queue API exists, at what version, and how a caller finds the instance running in a given Eon
   terminal (ah's per-harness routing; read ah's source at a recorded revision from ~/pjs/refs).
2. Trust: who may call (compare EON-C36's same-user rule and `[agents] terminal_access`), how the
   path avoids reading another tool's private files, failure when the agent has no API.
3. Shape: one `eon` command (e.g. `eon agent message TARGET -- TEXT`) that routes per agent and
   falls back to EON-C36 `pane send`, or no fallback; how it relates to EON-C36 and eon-2o85l.

## Acceptance

- A research comment with sources and revisions, a recommended shape with rejected options, the
  trust rule, and a contract draft for Lucca; proposed implementation beads, not filed before
  approval.

## Scope boundary

Research only. No code, contract or EONW change. Phone and chat-platform questions stay on
eon-7jw6p.

## Remaining research and acceptance

eon-9cv9s is closed; its survey answers Questions 1-3 on paper. The remaining bounded
experiment is the reported Codex queue, Claude socket and OpenCode queue paths on exact
versions, using disposable rota-launched agents only when separately authorized. For
each record idle/busy/waiting-on-command delivery, latency, model-turn count, one wake
per message or the observed limit, and correct subsequent eon targeting. A background
file watcher alone does not prove a model wakeup. Do not repeat the survey as the outcome.

Draft eon agent message / eon agent messages --json with explicit targets, same-user
trust, registration ownership under eon-eon-agent-lr8sx, bounded unsupported behavior
and rejected options. Preserve the approved busy-queue-without-typing rule. Comment 6484
also suggests steer/queue/reject and idle typing for API-less agents: that fallback is
an unresolved approval question, not permission to inject terminal input. Read the
provider-native handoff/fallback routes in docs/REFERENCES.md; revalidate Pi's dated API
finding. No private provider-file discovery, live-agent interruption or new daemon.

Acceptance is a per-backend results table and exact proposed contract text for approval;
implementation slices are proposed, not filed before approval. Stop with an observed
limit when an API is unavailable. If experiments consume the session, hand off contract
drafting as a bounded follow-up instead of starting implementation. Research only.

title: Keep the launching agent's session variables out of Eon terminals
description:
## Why

Seen 2026-11-01: the live Eon supervisor (PID 826284, started 10:28 UTC-3) was launched from inside a
Claude Code session's shell, so its environment carries `CLAUDECODE`, `CLAUDE_CODE_CHILD_SESSION`,
`CLAUDE_CODE_SESSION_ID`, `CLAUDE_CODE_ENTRYPOINT`, `CLAUDE_CODE_EXECPATH`,
`CLAUDE_CODE_SESSION_ATTENDED`, `CLAUDE_CODE_MESSAGING_SOCKET`, `CLAUDE_CODE_MESSAGING_TOKEN` and
`CLAUDE_PID`. The Orbit host and every terminal inherit them (checked through /proc/<pid>/environ
up the parent chain: claude -> sh -> yazelix-orbit -> .eon-wrapped, all carry the marker).

Two harms:
1. Every Claude Code started in any Eon terminal of that generation reads
   `CLAUDE_CODE_CHILD_SESSION` as "child session" and turns transcript saving off. The only sign is
   one status-line warning; `--continue` and `/resume` later find nothing. Agents launched with
   `eon pane create -- claude ...` are hit too.
2. `CLAUDE_CODE_MESSAGING_TOKEN` and the messaging socket path, a credential of the launching
   session, reach every process in every terminal.

This recurs whenever the supervisor starts from an agent's shell: an agent running `eon` or
restarting Eon, or a person launching Eon from a Claude pane. Eon is the terminal for humans and
agents, so an agent starting Eon must not break the next agent.

## Change

Eon Runtime's private launch environment (runtime/crates/eon-runtime/src/managed_environment.rs,
which already removes variables such as `HELIX_RUNTIME` and `CARGO_MANIFEST_DIR`) removes the
launching agent's session variables before it starts a terminal's child: `CLAUDECODE`,
`CLAUDE_PID`, and every `CLAUDE_CODE_*` name. Check the same for Codex (`CODEX_*` session or
sandbox variables, e.g. `CODEX_SANDBOX`, `CODEX_THREAD_ID` if present) and the other agents the
Agent popup starts (Grok, OpenCode, Pi); remove only session-identity, nesting-marker and
credential variables, never user configuration such as `CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR` or API keys the user
set on purpose. Record the chosen list and the reason for each name in this bead.

generation start with `CLAUDE_CODE_FORCE_SESSION_PERSISTENCE=1`.

title: Include generated managed behavior in Eon runtime generation identity
description:
## Contract routing

Harden the accepted EON-C11 runtime-generation contract and preserve EON-C9. The local launcher is the consumer; a build changes generated managed-shell adapters or the private Session command projection; the resulting Eon build must have a different stable generation identity so a bare launch cannot attach a supervisor with older managed behavior. This is a defect correction, not a new command, configuration field, protocol value, compatibility window, or distribution promise.

## Why

The generation digest covers Rust, Cargo, EONW, and component-manifest inputs but omits the Nix-owned generated shell adapters and private command projection. A flake-only runtime behavior fix can therefore retain the previous identity, attach the old supervisor, and give new panes its captured old Session environment.

Impact: HIGH. Effort: M. Implementation risk: MEDIUM. Confidence: HIGH.

## Evidence

- `crates/eon/src/main.rs:35-47`: `current_generation()` does not cover `flake.nix` or an equivalent managed-runtime projection identity.
- `flake.nix:228-479`: Nix generates runtime-visible native shell adapters.
- `flake.nix:537-585`: Nix constructs the private Session command projection and injects it into Session PATH.
- `crates/eon/src/main.rs:1220-1245`: a same-generation launch attaches the existing supervisor.
- `crates/eon/src/main.rs:2019-2025`: new panes use the existing supervisor's captured managed-program inputs.
- `eon-audit-eon-managed-environment-hay` records the exact 1b8836e audit and reproduction analysis.

## Prerequisite and reference gate

- No implementation prerequisite. This Bead is the prerequisite for the two EON-C9 managed-environment corrections found by the audit.
- Before code, record the repository execution baseline and classify the EON-C11 and EON-C9 proof records plus the managed-environment and runtime-generation entries in `docs/REFERENCES.md`.
- Required evidence is current EON-C11 generation selection, the exact Nix-generated adapters/private-bin owner, `eon-pxn.4` acceptance evidence, and the closed managed-environment audit.
- Existing Eon sources define the mechanism. External terminal or shell references are comparison-only unless an observed failure requires them.
- No dependency or crate feature is expected. Stop for the crate gate and user approval before any manifest change.

## Scope

In scope:
- The stable input set owned by `current_generation()` and the minimum Nix/build wiring needed to cover generated managed-runtime behavior.
- Focused unit/build/process proof that a managed-projection-only change selects a new generation while the old one remains live.
- Current-state EON-C11 proof metadata, CHANGELOG, architecture wording, and README LOC only where required by the accepted fix.

Out of scope:
- Hashing profile paths, store paths, PIDs, socket names, package channels, mutable user configuration, or runtime state.
- A Nix evaluator at runtime, a second runtime manifest, a manager daemon, live handoff, automatic old-generation eviction, or wider compatibility.
- Changing EONW, Orbit, Venus, shell behavior, managed command names, defaults, or user configuration.
- Adding a new dependency or speculative distribution framework.

Platform classification: neutral contract with an isolated current Nix build input; no new macOS blocker. A future distributor must be able to provide an equivalent stable behavior identity without Nix-specific runtime state.

## Implementation notes

1. Add the smallest existing build/source input that completely covers the generated adapter and private-bin behavior. Prefer conservative source hashing over a second schema or runtime mechanism.
2. Keep one generation owner in `current_generation()`; build tooling may supply immutable inputs but must not reinterpret launch policy.
3. Preserve old live generations and exact attach/stop behavior. Only the identity of builds with materially different managed projections should need to change.
4. Add one A/B regression whose only observable input difference is generated managed behavior.
5. Advance the EON-C11 proof revision after the proof-bearing commit and refresh the installed runtime without stopping old supervisors or Sessions.

## Acceptance

- Two builds with unchanged Rust, protocol, and component manifest but different observable generated managed behavior report different generation identities.
- A live build A remains discoverable and usable; bare launch of build B selects a fresh B supervisor; a pane created under B observes the B marker rather than A's projection.
- Rebuilding the same accepted inputs yields the same generation identity.
- Identity and persistent records expose no Nix store/profile path or mutable user state.
- Existing exact attach, listing, stop, cleanup, workspace, and managed-environment tests retain their observable results.
- No new contract, dependency, protocol, component identity, or compatibility window is introduced.

## Verification

- One focused A/B build/process check should exit 0 and prove distinct generations plus old-work preservation and B-pane behavior.
- `cargo fmt --check`
- `cargo check --locked`
- `cargo test --locked`
- `cargo clippy --locked --all-targets -- -D warnings`
- `cargo run --locked -p eon-manifest -- components/eon-alpha-v1.json`
- `nix build --no-link --print-out-paths --no-update-lock-file path:.#default`
- `nix flake check --no-update-lock-file path:.`
- `git diff --check`
- Installed `eon versions` and active profile/store-path checks after the accepted proof commit.

## Stop conditions

- Stop if the cited code or EON-C11 ownership has drifted materially.
- Stop if complete coverage requires a new public manifest, protocol field, dependency, distribution promise, or duplicate generation owner.
- Stop if the candidate identity depends on a mutable path/state value or requires evaluating Nix at runtime.
- Stop if the A/B proof cannot distinguish the corrected build from an ambient PATH or already-running supervisor.
- Stop if the same verification failure repeats twice after a reasonable correction.

## Maintenance notes

The first sufficient shape is one additional immutable generation input consumed by the existing owner. Do not create a general build-fingerprint framework. `eon-5rp` remains responsible only for keeping extracted Rust production sources in the digest.

comments.text:
Reference gate

Question:
- How can the existing EON-C11 generation owner cover Nix-generated managed-shell adapters and the private Session command projection without making Nix/store identity, a second runtime manifest, or another hash owner part of runtime policy?

Contract:
- Harden EON-C11 and preserve EON-C9. A build whose generated managed runtime behavior changes must select a different opaque generation; identical accepted inputs remain stable; older live supervisors remain untouched.

Sources and revisions:
- Eon exact baseline `57d7acc22f9f01c7f15d9d381845318b67f760e1`: `current_generation()`/`generation_id()`, all callers, focused generation tests, `flake.nix` generated adapter and private-bin owners, Nix source fileset and wrapper injection, EON-C9/EON-C11, architecture ownership, and runtime-generation proof records.
- Closed managed-environment audit `eon-audit-eon-managed-environment-hay` at subject `1b8836e616222f29c57ac697916872010db14685`, especially finding 3 and its exact flake-only stale-generation reproduction analysis.
- Closed `eon-pxn.4` EON-C11 evidence: stable source-and-graph identity, separate private generations, exact attach, owner-routed stop, and live A-to-B preservation.
- Exact accepted child sources remain Orbit `64db581445bafca1a08a6530f8e44f9c1edbc169` and Venus `90988f6ebcde68338e202a9c637c59398aafe93d`; this change consumes no new child behavior.
- The managed-shell upstream route and Nova are comparison-only and not triggered: this Bead does not change shell initialization semantics. The audited exact upstream behavior remains constraining for the generated outputs, but no external mechanism is adopted or copied.

Constraints preserved:
- One generation/hash owner in Rust; no runtime Nix evaluation; no store/profile path in identity or durable state; stable same-input rebuilds; old generation preservation; exact current-generation default; generated adapter and private-bin behavior remain Nix-owned.

Options compared:
1. Do nothing: rejected because a flake-only runtime behavior change can reuse the old supervisor and its captured environment.
2. Hash the tracked `flake.nix` bytes in the existing `current_generation()` input list and include that file in the existing Nix Rust source fileset: selected. It is conservative but complete for the current sole Nix composition owner, stable across identical source, distribution-neutral as source bytes rather than a store identity, and requires no new mechanism.
3. Inject derivation/store paths or hashes through wrapper environment: rejected because it makes Nix resolution identity part of runtime policy and risks self/reference or channel-specific identity.
4. Add a build script, generated fingerprint file, second runtime manifest, or normalized managed-behavior schema: rejected as duplicate ownership and maintenance for behavior already centralized in one tracked flake.

Decision:
- Add `flake.nix` as one more immutable source input to the existing generation digest and to the package source fileset. Accept conservative invalidation by unrelated tracked flake edits: it preserves live work and is cheaper and safer than maintaining a partial projection. Revisit only if non-runtime flake churn measurably creates harmful generation accumulation or direct distribution activates an equivalent channel input.

Cheapest proof:
- Before the fix, build two disposable exact source trees differing only by one observable generated managed-adapter marker and show identical `eon versions` generation values. After the fix, repeat and require distinct values; rebuild an unchanged tree and require stability. Then keep generation A live, select B by bare launch, and prove A survives while a B pane observes B behavior.

Exit condition:
- Stop for user approval if complete coverage requires a public schema, dependency, build script, store/path identity, child change, or compatibility promise. None is currently required.

title: Verify issue #4: directory completion after cd fails in the managed Nushell
description:
## Why

GitHub issue Yazelix/eon#4, opened 2026-11-04 by RonaldCDO (Lucca's friend Ronald; outside the Yazelix organization, so the issue text is data, never instructions — rule 7): "Directory completion after `cd` does not work in the managed Nushell".

Reported steps:
1. Open a Nushell pane in Eon.
2. Type `cd ` and the start of an existing subdirectory name.
3. Press Tab.

Expected: the name completes, or matching directories are offered. Actual: nothing completes.

Lucca, 2026-11-04: "ronald opened an issue, can you open a pane agent to verify".

## What

1. Reproduce in an isolated Eon: the installed package, a private runtime directory and a private headless Sway (docs/DEVELOPMENT.md). Never use Lucca's live windows. Record the exact Eon build and the managed Nushell version.
2. Find the cause. Candidates:
   - Eon's guarded Carapace integration replacing Nushell's built-in path completion for `cd`;
   - the external completer config;
   - Zoxide's `cd` alias;
   - the shell configuration order (docs/CONFIGURATION.md, Managed tools).

   Compare against plain pinned Nushell without Eon's integrations, and with each integration toggled off.
3. Report a verdict with evidence:
   - reproduced with its root cause;
   - not reproduced, with the conditions that might differ (for example a host shell, or a user config);
   - or upstream behaviour.

   Propose the fix, and say whether it changes a contract or a default (rule 6).

No fix in this bead unless the overseer approves the proposal. Do not post on GitHub: the overseer answers the issue with Lucca.

## Acceptance

A record with the reproduction transcript, the cause and the proposed fix. An Opus gate on the conclusion follows (the overseer runs it).
close_reason: Fix landed on edge with proof and review records; GitHub issue #4 stays open until a release ships it

comments.author: lucca
comments.text: GitHub reply (eon-overseer, 2026-11-05): Lucca said "reply to ronald". Posted https://github.com/Yazelix/eon/issues/4#issuecomment-6658419747, with this text: "Thanks — reproduced. It happens after you `cd` away from the directory the terminal started in: Eon loads its Starship prompt in a way that trips a Nushell scoping bug, and completion stays stuck on the startup directory. A fix is on the way. Until then, `[shell] starship = false` in `~/.config/eon/config.toml` and a new pane restores completion." The issue stays open until the fix lands and ships.

# eon-gkeae — reproduction

Verdict: **REPRODUCED** on installed Eon 0.1.15 and the overseer's packaged edge 0.1.16. No repository implementation, commits, Beads writes, profile changes or GitHub writes were made.

Current 0.1.16 private fixture:

```text

  complete-directory/
  other-directory/
    nested-directory/

=> cd complete-directory/                       # works at startup CWD
<Enter>
```

The overseer suspects the reporter uses v0.1.12; this is not confirmed. Read-only `git show v0.1.12:flake.lock` showed no per-tool lock nodes. The shell adapter also has the same SHA-256 as HEAD: `7807324dcb1dfeae1a491e6fdc754605011e3e96bf0a36e92ec59ae792921a4b`.

| Configuration | At startup CWD | After changing CWD |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Plain pinned Nu, `--no-config-file` | completes | completes |
| Managed defaults | completes | **empty menu** |
| Managed, `carapace = false` | completes | **empty menu** |

| Managed, `starship = false` | completes | completes |
| Managed, `mise = false` (mise absent) | completes | **empty menu** |

Startup transcripts are `../evidence/pty-plain.*`, `pty-managed-default.*`, `pty-without-{integration}.*`, and `pty-managed-none.*`. They were recorded on November 4. The expanded matrix and its retained runnable harness are [final-matrix.json](../evidence/final-matrix.json), [final-matrix.py](../pty/final-matrix.py), and [PTY helper](../pty/probe.py). Each final result asserts exactly one of an observed completed command or `NO RECORDS FOUND`, and asserts the expected split above. Earlier `pty-*-new-cwd` / `pty-new-cwd-without-*` discovery transcripts sent Enter after the empty menu and then a diagnostic command, which concatenated the two commands and produced an extra-positional error. The failure was visible before that error; the final matrix cancels with Ctrl+C instead and avoids this artifact.

## Activation mechanism controls

Separate private config files load the exact packaged Starship initializer, without Eon's other integrations. A second fixture command `cd comp<Tab>` after changing CWD detects stale lookup: `complete-directory` exists only under the startup CWD.

| Initializer activation | `cd nest<Tab>` in changed CWD | `cd comp<Tab>` in changed CWD |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Top-level `overlay use` Starship | completes | not tested |
| `if true { try { overlay use STARSHIP_INIT } }` | **empty menu** | **completes startup-only directory** |
| `if true { try { source STARSHIP_INIT } }` | completes | empty menu, as expected |
| `if true { try { use STARSHIP_INIT } }` | completes | empty menu, as expected |
| Top-level overlay, minimal `export-env` module | completes | not tested |
| Scoped overlay, minimal `export-env` module, no Starship | **empty menu** | **completes startup-only directory** |

The prompt remained Starship-rendered in the `source` and `use` cases. Controls: [activation-methods.py](../pty/activation-methods.py), [scoped-activation.py](../pty/scoped-activation.py). Their disposable `.nu` configs and fixtures live under `../pty/{starship-*,minimal-overlay,scoped-*}/`. Evidence: `../evidence/pty-starship-*.{raw,txt}`, `pty-minimal-overlay.*`, `pty-scoped-starship-*.{raw,txt}`, and `pty-scoped-minimal-overlay.*`.

This isolates scoped overlay activation, rather than the Starship executable, Carapace, a Zoxide `cd` alias, a wrong physical Tab byte, or Eon's renderer. Generated Zoxide setup defines `z` and `zi`; `cd` remained the built-in. Scope and diagnosis limits are in record 03.

title: Close the shortcut viewer when the person clicks outside it
description:
## Why

Lucca, 2026-11-04: "the shortcuts popup should vanish when i click outside of it".

Today the native shortcut viewer (Alt+/, VEN-C20) closes only on Alt+/ or Escape. While it is open, pointer input is captured: VEN-C20 says "While open, keyboard, pointer, IME, clipboard, link, and workspace actions do not reach their normal targets". So a click outside the dialog does nothing, and the person must find a key to close it.

## What

A primary-button press outside the viewer's dialog closes it, as Escape does. Prior terminal or chrome focus is restored.
- The click itself is consumed. It does not also focus, select, paste into, or open a link in whatever lies under it. The viewer keeps its rule that pointer input does not reach normal targets while open, and a dismissing click is part of "while open".
- A click inside the dialog keeps it open, as today. Scrolling stays as today.
- Other buttons outside the dialog (middle, right) also close it and are consumed, so a middle-click never pastes into a terminal hidden behind the viewer. Confirm this choice in the review.

## Contract

title: Close a stack with one line: the last collapsed row's label sits in the column's bottom edge
description:
## Why

Lucca, 2026-10-24, on the installed m5bv build (screenshot of a stack whose last pane, p3, is
collapsed): "shouldnt the bottomost pane of a stack share the same bottom border of the 'project
area'? insteaed of double bordering". Today the column's last collapsed row draws its own label
line (corners curling up, eon-m5bv), and the column's rounded bottom edge closes the stack about
one title row below it, so the stack ends in two parallel lines. At the top the first pane's label
already sits in the column's top line, which shares one snapped line with the agent sidebar card's
top.

## Behaviour

- When a column's last pane is collapsed, its label sits in the column's bottom edge: one line,
  through the middle of that row's title row, with the column's rounded bottom corners curling up
  and the stack's sides continuing up to the expanded pane's frame (eon-m5bv joints). No second
  line below it.
- At the unscrolled bottom that line and the agent sidebar card's bottom line are one snapped line
  (mirror of the top-line rule). The space that frees goes to the column above it (expanded
  terminal), as whole cells where Scene's existing sizing allows; nothing else moves.
- When the last pane is the expanded one, nothing changes (its full frame is the bottom).
- Neutral lines at border_width; the selected pane's focus frame stays its own rounded frame,
  painted once, no neutral paint under it (eon-e8hh/eon-f5pg rule). A selected last collapsed row
  keeps the focus colour on its edge as today.
- Labels, fill (eon-54jv: nothing outside the column's outer edge), hit targets (the last row stays
  clickable over its label) and AccessKit unchanged. Frameless mode unchanged.

## Contract

VEN-C8 collapsed-row sentence (venus/docs/CONTRACTS.md:590-595). Approved addition (see the
Approval comment): after "...its sides continue to the next card in that direction;" add "when the
column's last pane is collapsed, its label sits in the column's bottom edge instead, so the stack
closes with one line; at the unscrolled bottom that line shares one snapped line with the agent
sidebar card's bottom."

## Acceptance

- Venus paint/scene test (fails first): a stack whose last pane is collapsed draws exactly one
  horizontal line at the column's bottom, carrying the last row's label, on the same snapped y as
  the agent sidebar card's bottom; sides continuous from that line to the expanded frame; no paint
  outside the column's outer edge; no neutral paint under focus; scales 1 and 1.3; widths 1/1, 1/2,
  2/2; last row selected and not selected; last pane expanded unchanged.
- Isolated capture with Lucca's opacity: a 4-pane stack with the first pane expanded (before and
  after).

Portability: neutral.

title: Prove Orbit gives no reply to Glyph Protocol APCs, so a libghostty pin can't start answering before Venus draws them
description:
Prove that Orbit stays silent to Glyph Protocol APCs (`ESC _ 25a1 ; … ESC \`), so a libghostty pin bump can't start answering apps before Venus draws registered glyphs.

## Why

The pinned libghostty-vt (Ghostty 0fa3d577, vt-1.0.0, via libghostty-rs 9b598d6528c0) parses the Glyph Protocol, keeps a per-terminal glossary and answers `s`/`q`/`r`, but the feature is off by default (`GHOSTTY_TERMINAL_OPT_GLYPH_PROTOCOL`, `c/terminal.zig:890-892`). Orbit never calls `Terminal::set_glyph_protocol_enabled` (libghostty-rs `terminal.rs:1490`), so these APCs are dropped today (`apc.zig:84-96`).

The trap: if a future pin turns the feature on by default, Orbit would tell apps `r` succeeded while Venus still draws the Nerd Font glyph or tofu, and apps would drop their fallbacks. Ghostty 1.4.0 ships exactly that (answers, doesn't render). Nothing in Eon's checks would notice.

Source: desk research report 2026-11-12 (`~/.cache/eon-agents/eon-desk/glyph-protocol-report.md`). Adoption itself is tracked on eon-glyph-protocol-watch-gofox (deferred to 2026-12-12); this bead does not adopt the protocol.

## Do

- Extend Orbit's real-PTY reply check (`orbit/tests/real_pty/terminal_replies.rs` with `orbit/tests/terminal-replies-shell.sh`), or add a sibling check registered in `orbit/tests/real_pty/main.rs` and `nix/orbit-checks.nix`, whose child writes:
  - `ESC _ 25a1 ; s ESC \` (support / detection ping),
  - `ESC _ 25a1 ; q ; cp=e0a0 ESC \` (coverage query),
  - a minimal `r` registration with `reply=2` for a PUA codepoint,
  then a known-answered query (e.g. the cursor-position request the check already uses) as a fence.
- Assert the child receives the fence reply and no `ESC _ 25a1` reply bytes before it.
- A short comment on the check names this bead and says: enabling the Glyph Protocol requires Venus rendering first (see the watch bead), so a failure here means the pin turned it on.

## Done when

- The check fails if Orbit (or a libghostty pin) answers any `25a1` APC, and passes on current edge.
- It runs in `nix/orbit-checks.nix` like the other real-PTY checks.
- No contract change, no visible change, no Venus change.

## Out of scope

Enabling, parsing or rendering the protocol; upstream requests; ORBS changes.

title: Re-check Glyph Protocol adoption on 2026-12-12 and decide whether Eon adopts it
description:
Watch the Glyph Protocol (Raphael Amorim's terminal protocol, APC `ESC _ 25a1 ; …`). It lets apps register vector glyphs for Private Use Area codepoints at runtime and ask which codepoints the terminal can draw. Re-check it on 2026-12-12 and decide whether Eon adopts it. Lucca chose on 2026-11-12 to wait about a month rather than draft upstream requests now.

## Why wait

- The spec is a single-author draft in raphamorim/rio `specs/glyph-protocol.md`. It reached v1.12 on 2026-11-08 after twelve revisions since April, several of them breaking. It has no wire version.
- Rio is the only terminal that draws registered glyphs. Ghostty 1.4.0 parses and answers but doesn't draw them. Mitchell Hashimoto's renderer PR, ghostty-org/ghostty#12938, is open (last updated 2026-10-29).
- Eon gains little today. Venus already routes the PUA to the bundled Symbols Nerd Font Mono (`venus/src/render/cells.rs:125-132`). No major app sends the protocol yet (inference, 2026-11-12).

## What we know about Eon's fit (Eon 1390bc25d35c, Ghostty pin 0fa3d577 vt-1.0.0, libghostty-rs 9b598d6528c0)

- **Parsing:** libghostty-vt already parses the protocol, stores registrations per terminal and replies, but it is off by default. The binding has `Terminal::set_glyph_protocol_enabled`, and Orbit never calls it, so these APCs are dropped today.
- **Upstream gaps:** there is no C API to read registered outlines back. The `q` reply reports registered glyphs only and goes straight to the PTY, so Orbit can't add installed-font coverage (`apc/glyph/execute.zig:27-29`). Snapshots skip the registrations.
- **Eon's own work:**
  1. Orbit enables the feature and reads the outlines.
  2. An ORBS resource-plane change modeled on ORB-C16 sends them to Venus.
  3. Venus rasterizes them through the glyphon custom-glyph hook (`venus/src/render.rs:1996-2020`, today used only for Eon Bar icons).
  4. `q` comes last. A truthful `system` answer needs font coverage that only Venus knows (ORB-C2, `venus/AGENTS.md:14-16`).
- **Trap:** never enable replies before Venus draws the glyphs. Apps would drop their fallbacks.
- **Multiplexers (spec gap):** the spec requires per-pane isolation but gives multiplexers no mechanism, because they draw every pane into one outer glossary. Zellij ignores non-Kitty APCs today (zellij `9e7be20f`, `vt_parser_tests.rs:930`). Eon doesn't have this problem, since each pane is its own Orbit terminal.

## Triggers (any one starts adoption planning)

- ghostty-org/ghostty#12938 merges.
- The spec goes a month without a breaking change.
- A major app (Helix, Yazi, Starship, or an agent CLI) starts sending the protocol.

## On the check date

Re-read the spec changelog, #12938 and the libghostty-vt headers for a glossary accessor. Then either:

- report to Lucca with a recommendation (draft the libghostty-vt accessor and query-hook issue; a Venus trial drawing one `glyf` outline in a cell; an Orbit test that `25a1` APCs get no reply; a rio issue about the multiplexer gap); or
- defer another month with the reasons recorded here.

## Scope

This bead is research and a decision only: no code, no contract text, no outward posts. Any adoption gets its own beads and the reference gate (`docs/AGENT-RULES.md` Contract-Driven Method).

## Acceptance

A comment on this bead records the check, what changed upstream, and Lucca's decision. Then this bead closes or its defer date moves.

The full research report from 2026-11-12, which may be cleared, is at `/home/lucca/.cache/eon-agents/eon-desk/glyph-protocol-report.md`.

title: Gate workspace Steel files on workspace trust in the nova-helix fork
description:

In Yazelix/nova-helix (cd489078) helix-term/src/commands/engine/steel/mod.rs:2247-2259 loads <workspace>/.helix/{helix,init}.scm whenever both exist and HELIX_STEEL_CONFIG is unset, with no workspace-trust check, so standalone nova-helix (and any launcher that does not set HELIX_STEEL_CONFIG) runs a cloned repository's Steel code. Check with Nova's overseer whether Nova's launch always sets HELIX_STEEL_CONFIG. nova-helix has no Beads tracker, so this lives in Eon's backlog.

## Current baseline and acceptance

The cd489078 finding is historical. At dcaef1c flake.nix:24 / flake.lock:131 pin
nova-helix 6ee75ad3b7b2f2ed82daae0f9bf1663c168f48ea; flake.nix:683-692 builds Eon's
Helix with Steel disabled. Do not claim today's Eon runs workspace Steel or re-enable it.
The remaining outcome is the standalone/Steel-enabled fork trust rule. Re-read the
fork's rules and re-locate startup/reload at its exact revision before implementation;
stop/report if already fixed. No Nova compatibility or release work is authorized.

Acceptance: in the fork's supported test/reproducer, untrusted workspace Steel writes
no marker at startup or reload; trusted workspace follows the existing trust rule and
explicit user configuration keeps its behavior. One owner governs startup/reload trust.
Record exact revision, reference/trust gate and fork proof; bump Eon's pin only if needed,
preserving Steel-disabled packaging and affected downstream security/delivery proof.
Any EON-C9 text change needs approval. Check Nova's launch claim with its owner rather
than assuming it. The external current fork was not inspected in this planning pass.

title: Show a GPU widget in the Eon Bar
description:
## Decision

Lucca, 2026-10-17: add a GPU widget to Eon, alongside CPU and IO. Lucca, 2026-10-27 (question 17 of
the prime-beads passes, "agree with everything"): Venus samples the GPU like the CPU/RAM chips,
reading kernel sources (sysfs, fdinfo, /proc) itself with no EONW change, as the landed CPU/RAM
chips do (venus/src/system.rs); any NVIDIA NVML or nvidia-smi path is its own decision before code.

## Goal

The Eon Bar shows a read-only GPU label with GPU utilization as a percentage, through `[bar]
widgets` (EON-C32), on native x86_64 Linux Wayland.

## Rules for every child

- Failures: an unsupported, sleeping, permission-denied or failed GPU shows no label (never 0%),
  and Eon never wakes a powered-down discrete GPU just to sample it (check the PCI device's
  `power/runtime_status` first); failures are per GPU and independent.
- One label showing the busiest GPU, with every GPU in hover and accessibility text (open decision
  4's recommendation).
- Presentation is a feature (EON-C30/VEN-C28 were retired as features on 2026-10-30); the only
  contract text is EON-C32's widget name `gpu` and its Boundary clause, which needs Lucca's approval
  (filed with child 1). Hiding order goes in venus/docs/PRESENTATION.md.
- Configurability: the label shows only when `gpu` is listed in `[bar] widgets`.

## Platform evidence

There is no single Linux source. AMD exposes `gpu_busy_percent` in sysfs. Intel i915/xe whole-GPU
busy needs the perf PMU (CAP_PERFMON or perf_event_paranoid <= 0, which Eon must not require); DRM
fdinfo gives per-client engine time for processes the user owns. NVIDIA proprietary needs NVML
(`libnvidia-ml`) or `nvidia-smi`. Lucca's machine is hybrid Intel i915 + NVIDIA proprietary, and
neither has `gpu_busy_percent` (checked 2026-10-17); README lists proprietary NVIDIA as unproved.

## Reference gate (each child records its part)

nvtop, btop's GPU support and Mission Center at exact revisions: how each reads AMD, Intel and
NVIDIA without privilege, and how each avoids waking a suspended GPU.

## Children

1. Show NVIDIA GPU use in the Eon Bar without waking a sleeping GPU (needs Lucca's NVIDIA source
   decision; adds the `gpu` widget name).
2. Show AMD GPU use in the Eon Bar from sysfs (after 1).
Intel stays unsupported and documented as such unless child 1's gate finds an unprivileged
whole-GPU source; a DRM-fdinfo approach would be its own child.

## Acceptance

Every child closed; installed capture on Lucca's hybrid machine with the NVIDIA GPU awake and
asleep; each unsupported GPU kind recorded honestly in docs.

## Scope boundary

Utilization only: no VRAM, temperature, clocks, power, per-process GPU use, graphs or actions. No
privileged helper, setuid, udev rule or CAP_PERFMON requirement. Linux only (macOS would need its own
reader, see eon-mac-launch-kz4p.3).

## Accepted presentation details

Lucca 2026-11-06 (comment 5789): nf-md-expansion_card U+F08AE, using the packaged
Symbols Nerd Font Mono six-cell centered chip path. Lucca 2026-11-07 (comment 5832):
hover names the GPU actually measured, which may differ from Venus's rendering adapter.
Carry source/device identity through aggregation; never label a sampled NVIDIA value
with the renderer's Intel name. Unavailable data is absent; valid measured 0% is real.
Portability: isolated Linux GPU reader. NVIDIA source and gpu default remain child 1
approval gates, not choices made by this pass.

So 'No GPU vendor logic in Venus' conflicts with the established path: the sampling owner (Venus vs Runtime, especially for NVML/nvidia-smi) must be re-decided with Lucca. title: Show NVIDIA GPU use in the Eon Bar without waking a sleeping GPU
description:
## Why

Lucca's machine has an NVIDIA proprietary GPU (plus Intel i915) and asked for a GPU widget
(parent epic). NVIDIA exposes no sysfs utilization; the source is NVML or `nvidia-smi`, and Lucca
reserved that choice (comment of 2026-10-27 on the parent).

## Decision needed before code (Lucca)

NVIDIA source. Recommendation: a bounded `nvidia-smi --query-gpu=utilization.gpu --format=csv,noheader,nounits`
subprocess run by Venus at the CPU label's cadence or slower, only when the GPU's PCI
`power/runtime_status` is `active` (running nvidia-smi wakes a suspended GPU), with a timeout and no
retry storm. It uses the host driver's own tool (which must match the kernel module, so Nix cannot
pin it), adds no crate and no dlopen. Alternative: dlopen `libnvidia-ml` (faster, no process per
sample; more unsafe code). Any crate passes AP-DEPENDENCY-001.

## Contract

EON-C32: add `gpu` to the `[bar] widgets` names (the current Boundary no longer has the old "No ... new widget" phrase);
decide whether `gpu` joins the default list (recommend yes, low in the hiding order). Stop for
Lucca's approval of the exact text. The label itself is a feature (venus/docs/PRESENTATION.md).

## Scope

In scope:
- Venus GPU sampler for NVIDIA (sleep check, bounded read, parse, per-GPU failure), the label,
  hover and accessibility text (busiest GPU, every GPU in hover), hiding order.
- Runtime: accept `gpu` in `[bar] widgets` and pass it in `--bar-items`.
- docs/CONFIGURATION.md, docs/USAGE.md Eon Bar section, venus/docs/PRESENTATION.md, CHANGELOG.md.
- Reference gate: nvtop, btop and Mission Center NVIDIA paths at exact revisions.

Out of scope: AMD (child 2), Intel, VRAM/temperature/clocks, any EONW change.

## Acceptance

- Sampler red/green: asleep, missing tool, timeout, malformed output and permission failures show
  no label, never 0%.
- Installed capture on Lucca's hybrid machine: with the NVIDIA GPU awake, the label shows its
  utilization under a GPU load; with it asleep, no label and the GPU stays asleep (runtime_status
  unchanged across a minute).

## Verification

- `nix develop -c eon-test -p yazelix-venus -p eon-runtime`; fmt and clippy for both.
- Isolated installed capture; review loop with Codex; profile refresh.

## Stop Conditions

- Stop before code until Lucca has chosen the NVIDIA source and approved the EON-C32 text.
- Stop if sampling can wake the GPU and no check prevents it.


## Identity and power falsifiers

The mechanism above is unapproved. The reference gate must establish whether discovery
or query itself wakes any adapter: checking one active GPU before querying all devices
is insufficient. Scope queries to the measured device; unknown power state must not
trigger risky probing. Stop if no-wake cannot be guaranteed. Cover multiple adapters,
partial failure and out-of-range values; a real idle 0% is valid, missing data is not.
Carry the parent's approved GPU name/identity and U+F08AE glyph into hover/accessibility.
Record configuration or a performance-budget reason for cadence/timeout values.
Portability: isolated Linux/NVIDIA dependency. Use current affected dependency/config
proof, whole-workspace eon-test before review, converge/Codex and accepted profile
refresh; the older focused-suite list above does not replace that route.

title: Show AMD GPU use in the Eon Bar from sysfs
description:
## Why

AMD GPUs expose `gpu_busy_percent` in sysfs, so the GPU label (parent epic) can cover them with no
tool or library. Lucca's 2026-10-17 decision 1 recommendation: AMD sysfs "since it is free".

## Prerequisites

- Child 1 (NVIDIA) has landed the `gpu` widget name, label and hover; this child adds a source.

## Scope

In scope:
- Venus reads `/sys/class/drm/card*/device/gpu_busy_percent` for AMD devices whose
  `power/runtime_status` is `active`; per-GPU failures; the busiest-GPU rule from the parent.
- docs/CONFIGURATION.md and venus/docs/PRESENTATION.md lines naming AMD support.

Out of scope: Intel, NVIDIA changes, VRAM, any EONW or contract change.

## Acceptance

- Sampler red/green over fixture sysfs trees: valid percent, missing file, suspended device,
  invalid content and out-of-range values (no label, never 0%), mixed AMD + NVIDIA picks the
  busiest.
- No AMD hardware is available to Lucca: record the installed-observation gap honestly, or run it
  on a machine with an AMD GPU if one is reachable.

## Verification

- `nix develop -c eon-test -p yazelix-venus`; fmt and clippy; review loop with Codex.

## Stop Conditions

- Stop if a contract change appears necessary.

## Shared presentation and proof boundary

Keep child 1's single sampler/label owner and the parent's accepted glyph/name behavior:
hover names the AMD device actually measured. A real 0% remains valid; unavailable data
is absent. Cover independent mixed-device failure and unknown/unreadable power status.
Portability: isolated Linux/sysfs dependency. Current whole-workspace eon-test before
review and output-path proof apply if render code changes. Fixtures prove parsing and
selection, not AMD hardware collection: retain the installed AMD observation gap and
do not label support hardware-proven. On an assigned AMD host use one isolated installed
observation after accepted profile refresh. No contract text change is approved.
