title: Deliver trustworthy Grok quota in the Eon Bar
description:
## Contract

A full-Eon user who uses authenticated Grok Build can see a compact Grok quota chip beside the existing provider chips when a verified read-only source supplies authoritative subscription usage. Show the provider-reported remaining percentage and the actual supplied quota period, with reset details on hover and in the accessible description. Do not relabel a shared subscription pool as a Build-only allowance. Missing or unsupported usage stays absent or explicitly unavailable; local tokens, context usage and dollar balances cannot substitute for quota.

Important failures include missing or incompatible CLI, unsupported billing method/account type, auth change or expiry, malformed/oversized response, absent percentage/period, timeout or network/provider loss. They never block Eon or produce fresh-looking guessed quota.

## Ownership and prerequisites

Eon owns the product outcome and exact composition; Eon Runtime owns the provider source, lifecycle, normalization and freshness; canonical EONW owns the typed facts; Venus owns native layout, icon, hover and accessibility. Grok owns auth and billing semantics; Orbit remains terminal authority.

The accepted Codex delivery and EON-C21/EON-C22 supply the baseline. EONW v7 is Codex-specific, not a general quota schema. Before implementation, index the selected Grok contract and choose the smallest canonical typed extension, reusing an accepted Claude change only if it already exists and fits. Claude-first is scheduling preference, not a hard semantic dependency. Follow one active frontier and consume accepted Runtime/EONW and Venus revisions before Eon delivery.

## Evidence and reference gate

Reviewed on 2026-10-11:
- Official usage semantics: https://docs.x.ai/grok/faq. The documented paid weekly pool can span several Grok products; the percentage shown in Grok settings is subscription usage, not a fixed Build token budget.
- Official CLI and status-line docs: https://docs.x.ai/build/cli/reference and https://docs.x.ai/build/features/status-line. The documented status-line fields include session/model/context facts; this is not proof of an externally available subscription quota query.
- PATH discovery found grok-1.0.41-linux-x86_64. No live authenticated quota read was performed.
- Comparable implementation: CodexBar 444821be54e2571dd115ca07b2ce3d1e0a71a45c, https://github.com/steipete/CodexBar/blob/444821be54e2571dd115ca07b2ce3d1e0a71a45c/docs/grok.md. It describes a candidate ACP x.ai/billing method, historical method-not-found failures and read-only billing fallbacks using existing login credentials. This demonstrates a possible source, not compatibility of our installed Grok.
- Grok Build source discovery: xai-org/grok-build 2bdd1d6a6369de0e8c68132ea4539e9abd9e14a8. Reinspect exact CLI/billing ownership and license before adopting a mechanism.
- Nova e7d8d6ffe9994413944bac388620b9f9f61669d7 consumes Nova Bar 7295e9976803de8d912f766f1b00ad12652e3e9b and tokenusage. Compare quota labels/failure behavior; do not copy its widget, cache or multiplexer architecture.

First falsifier: establish whether the exact installed Grok can return quota through a supported read-only machine boundary without starting an agent turn. Prefer provider-owned auth and a documented CLI route when sufficient. If unavailable, compare a bounded authenticated billing read with leaving the chip unavailable; record endpoint stability, credential ownership, permissions, cost, license and maintenance. Direct HTTP or credential access is unresolved and must be explicitly selected before implementation, not silently inherited from CodexBar. Do not adopt its fallback chain or browser-cookie import wholesale.

## Scope and stop boundary

One read-only native quota chip for one verified Grok auth/account class on the accepted Linux Wayland alpha. Define period, remaining percentage, reset, source/account binding, age/expiry and honest stale/unavailable behavior. Bound retries and I/O, keep authentication out of Venus, and preserve existing provider chips and the bar's tab/control priority.

No billing/credit purchase, reset redemption, login UI, token refresh owner, browser-cookie scraping, transcript/history scanner, token/cost-to-quota inference, generic provider/widget framework, new row, provider bundling or platform/distribution expansion. Do not expose raw billing payloads, credentials or account identity through EONW or logs.

If no acceptable authoritative source exists, record the exact blocker and leave delivery incomplete rather than substitute local usage or close on an unavailable-only chip. Source selection must precede UI implementation.

## Validation

Record exact provider, Eon Runtime/EONW, Venus, Orbit, manifest, package and environment identities. Use focused parser/source red-green checks for meaningful malformed/missing/stale cases, then the full affected Rust/Nix route for shared protocol or dependency changes. Refresh the installed eon profile and observe one isolated native x86_64 Linux Wayland workflow with real provider facts plus bounded failure substitutes, preserving live terminals and desktop focus. Inspect responsive width, hover and AccessKit labels together; do not treat accessibility structure alone as screen-reader qualification.
acceptance_criteria:
1. The exact supported Grok version/auth class supplies a real authoritative quota observation through an explicitly selected read-only source. Source/API stability and any credential-access decision are recorded; no inference turn or provider mutation is needed.
2. Remaining percentage, actual supplied period and reset agree with that observation. Shared subscription usage is labelled honestly, absent facts remain unavailable, and local tokens/context/cost are never used as quota.
3. Bounded parsing/I/O/retry/cleanup, source/account invalidation and explicit freshness/expiry handle missing methods, auth failures, missing fields, malformed responses and provider/network loss without blocking product use or republishing obsolete facts.
4. Canonical EONW carries only bounded normalized facts. The native Grok icon/name, quota, hover/reset details and accessible stale/unavailable labels fit the existing single-row bar beside accepted chips; optional chips yield before tabs and required controls.
5. Exact accepted owner revisions, meaningful focused source/failure checks, affected Rust/Nix proof, profile refresh and one isolated installed real-source observation pass. Current docs/changelog/LOC state the supported scope and limitations; live terminals, desktop focus and user provider configuration are preserved.
notes: User authorized creation of this Claude/Grok planning-only batch on 2026-10-11. Open and unclaimed; no implementation, auth read or provider-configuration write in this run. Recommended after Claude, with no false blocking edge. The first implementation step is the unresolved authoritative-source gate.

Pinned CodexBar 0.74.1 (/nix/store/3m477g4r…-codexbar-0.74.1, the binary Eon launches as EON_CODEXBAR) lists grok as a provider. Read-only probes with Lucca's existing Grok 1.0.41 (4220f3b224a6) login, same flags as runtime quota.rs: `usage --provider grok --source cli --format json --json-only --web-timeout 8` -> error 'Grok request failed: Method not found' (the installed Grok does not answer CodexBar's billing request; matches CodexBar's documented historical failure); `--source oauth` -> 'No available fetch strategy for grok.' title: Name Stacks, popups and the Agents sidebar panels across docs, contracts and Venus
description:
## Why

Lucca, 2026-11-10: "we need a name for these structures that are notched: stacks, popups and sidebar, are share this notched ui, and have a bevahior different than panes". He chose **panel** (from region, surface, frame, panel; earlier rejected: tray, binder, pod, nest, bay). Reasons: frame (render frames, frame revisions), surface (Wayland surfaces) and region (selection regions) already carry meanings in Eon; panel had about 10 doc uses, all small collisions.

## Term

A **panel** is a notched container: a Stack, a popup, or the Agents sidebar. Its heading has notches (title notch left, action notch right with Hide or Close). A **pane** is a terminal card with a header band (eon-2ibdd). Panes have bands; panels have notches.

## Scope

- Define the term once (venus/docs/PRESENTATION.md, and docs/USAGE.md at first use) and use it where docs and contracts now list "Stacks, popups and the Agents sidebar" or describe notched headings: venus/docs/PRESENTATION.md, docs/USAGE.md, venus/docs/CONTRACTS.md VEN-C8 and VEN-C18, docs/CONTRACTS.md where relevant, CHANGELOG Unreleased if it names these.
- Reword the existing collisions so "panel" means only the notched container: AccessKit "tab panel" role mentions and the "pane panel" accessible name (venus/docs/CONTRACTS.md:723, :1432-1434, :1513; venus/docs/PRESENTATION.md:376); "Retina panel" (README.md:126, docs/CONTRACTS.md:528) becomes "Retina display".
- Code: rename internal identifiers only where they describe this concept (Venus scene and render names for notched headings); no behavior change, no compatibility aliases. Accessible names users hear change only where they say "panel" for something else.
- Contract edits are wording only (term substitution); Lucca chose the term, the overseer approves the substitution under auto-decision mode.
- Coordinate with in-flight work that edits the same text: eon-u5uv2 (band gaps), eon-cq38r and eon-t5boa (Stack close). Land after them or rebase onto them.

## Acceptance

A whole-word, case-insensitive search for "panel" and "panels" over docs, venus/docs, README.md and venus/src shows only the new meaning; Venus suite, fmt and clippy pass; no rendering change (no captures needed).

comments.author: lucca
comments.text: Decision (approved by eon-overseer under Lucca's standing rule, 2026-11-12; Codex second opinion agreed; digest row D34): May "panel" cover the Stack/popup/Agents container whatever the heading style, and allow technical AccessKit "tab panel"? Answer: Yes. Reason: Connected is now default; notch-only wording would conflict. Lucca may overturn this in his morning review.

title: Inset the tab pills by the card gap
description:
## Decision
Lucca, 2026-10-18: after the bar-colored frame (eon-tubj), the tab pill sat 4 px from the window's
top and left edges while every other visible gap was 8 px. Of two options (shrink the gap below the
pills to 4 px, or inset the pills by the 8 px card gap), the recommendation to inset the pills by
one card gap was accepted with "do it". The first pill then lines up with the first card.

## Contract
- Consumer: a full-Eon user (both frame modes share the tab bar).
- Result: tab pills keep one card gap (8 logical px at default typography) from the window's top
  and left edges and above the cards; pill size and the 4 px gap between pills stay unchanged, so
  the header grows by 8 px and terminals lose 4 px of height. Header buttons keep their width.
  On a window too short for it, the inset yields (at most a quarter of the header height).
- Edits (approved by "do it"): one clause in EON-C8 and VEN-C8 next to the card-gap text; both
  changelogs' unreleased card entries.

## Prerequisites
eon-tubj (closed).

## Acceptance
Scene assertion that the first pill sits one gap from the top and left edges and one gap above the
cards; tiny-window tests keep proving that card gaps yield before the terminal; yazelix-venus fmt
and clippy; Venus suites via `nix develop -c eon-test`; nix build; isolated captures framed and
frameless; review loop; profile refresh.

## Scope boundary
Tab-pill inset and header height only. No pill size, inter-pill gap, button width, color or
configuration change. Portability: neutral.
close_reason: Tab pills sit one card gap from the window's top and left edges and above the cards; pill row geometry unchanged; inset yields first on tiny windows. Proof and ledger in comments.

comments.author: lucca

title: Make eon config-path print config.toml's path and add eon config-dir for the root
description:
## Why

Follow-up to eon-wt5v8 (landed 6ee820d, unreleased). Lucca, 2026-11-03: "evaluate replacing eon
config-path --file with just eon config-path (it prints the entire path with file)", then "we could
also have eon config-dir", then "agreed" to the overseer's five recommendations below.

"Config path" reads as the path of the settings file, so `hx $(eon config-path)` should just work.
The configuration root still matters (it holds `helix`, `nushell`, `lazygit`, `yazi`, `yazelix`
tool directories), so it gets its own command, as Nushell splits `$nu.config-path` (file) from
`$nu.default-config-dir` (directory).

## Approved (Lucca, 2026-11-03, "agreed")

1. `eon config-path` prints the absolute path of `config.toml`; new `eon config-dir` prints the
   root (what `config-path` printed before). `--file` is removed with no alias: it never shipped in
   a release.
2. EON-C9 text, replacing the two sentences about `config-path` and `config-path --file`:
   > `eon config-path` creates the configuration root if it is missing and prints the absolute
   > path of the settings file `config.toml` inside it, without creating or reading that file.
   > `eon config-dir` creates the root the same way and prints its absolute path. On success both
   > exit 0 with one line on stdout and no stderr output; other arguments exit 2. A root that
   > cannot be resolved or created, or a stdout write that fails for any reason but a closed pipe,
   > exits 1 with the reason on stderr; a closed stdout pipe still exits 0 with no stderr output.
   > `eon --help` names `config.toml` beside `config-path` and `config defaults`.
   Update EON-C9's proof/evidence lines that name `config-path --file` to match.
3. Help lines: `config-path  Create the config root and print its config.toml path` and
   `config-dir   Create and print the config root` (keep the 80-column help test green).
4. Commands popup keeps one entry, "Show config path" (now the file); no `config-dir` entry.
5. Land before the next release so `--file` never ships.

## Contract

EON-C9 (text approved above). EON-C28 is not engaged (pre-1.0).

## Scope

- runtime/crates/eon-runtime/src/cli.rs: dispatch, help lines, `print_config_path`.
- eon/crates/eon/tests/workspace_control.rs: replace the `--file` cases with `config-path` (file)
  and `config-dir` (root) cases; keep the closed-stdout-pipe test covering both commands; help test
  asserts both lines per line.
- eon/tools/mac-proof/src/scenario.rs:1670: the identity check moves to `config-dir` (same
  meaning: the private configuration root).
- docs/CONTRACTS.md (EON-C9), docs/USAGE.md (command table), docs/CONFIGURATION.md (opening
  paragraph: `config-path` prints the settings file, `config-dir` the root that also holds tool
  directories), CHANGELOG.md: rewrite the unreleased eon-wt5v8 bullet in place rather than adding a
  second one.
- Grep the repo for any other `config-path` user (docs/ARCHITECTURE.md:374, CONTRACTS.md:1194,
  2502) and keep them true.

Not in scope: creating or templating `config.toml`; changing `config defaults`.

## Acceptance

- `eon config-path` prints `<root>/config.toml` (root created, file not created); `eon config-dir`
  prints `<root>`; `eon config-path --file` exits 2. Covered by workspace_control tests, red before
  the change.
- Closed stdout pipe: both commands exit 0 with empty stderr (test fails if the BrokenPipe arm is
  removed).
- `eon --help` shows both lines; help test green.
- mac-proof compiles (`cargo clippy` for its crate, plus the Darwin target clippy if available).
- fmt, clippy, `eon-test -p eon`, `eon-test -p eon-runtime`, `nix build .#default`.

## Rule 6

The command names and help text are CLI surface under EON-C9, which scripts and agents rely on; the
file name `config.toml` is fixed by EON-C28. Nothing here is a value a person tunes.
close_reason: Landed: config-path prints config.toml, config-dir prints the root, --file removed; reviews 0 blocking, Opus gate PASS

title: Alt+Shift+1..9 jumps to workspace N
description:
## Why

Lucca, 2026-11-04 (with its sibling, Alt+Shift+S twice): "lets do both". Faster workspace switching without the picker, mirroring Alt+1..9 for panes.

## Scope

- Alt+Shift+1..9 switches to the Nth workspace, in the strip and picker order.
  - A missing N does nothing, or shows the same short notice the pane keys give, if they give one.
  - Decide whether Alt+Shift+0 mirrors what Alt+0 does for panes.
- Bindings are physical keys, so layouts where Shift+digit gives a symbol behave the same.
- Alt+Shift+1..9 are free today (checked at 4272591).
- Rule 5: `eon workspace switch` accepts a 1-based index, or the bead names the CLI form that addresses workspace N. Check what the CLI accepts today.
- Rule 6: the binding is configurable, with its default in docs/CONFIGURATION.md.
- Contract: EON-C33 gets a sentence for the keys. That is small contract text, approved by the overseer under Lucca's standing rule.

## Acceptance

- A test shows Alt+Shift+2 switching to the second workspace and a missing N changing nothing. It fails on the current edge and passes with the change.
- The CLI form addresses workspace N.
- An isolated installed run.

## Verification

- `nix develop -c eon-test -p eon-runtime -p eon` plus the Venus tests if Venus binds the keys, fmt and clippy.
- One isolated installed run.
- Converge plus Codex.

title: Investigate Headscale and Tailscale for reaching Eon on remote machines
description:
## Why

Lucca, 2026-11-07: "create a bead to investigate Headscale / tailscale is all the rage right now in our competitors midst". Tern names Tailscale for `tern remote serve` (WATCHLIST.md); phone clients (Moshi, Moshline) and other agent terminals reach remote machines the same way. Eon's own remote work runs over SSH (eon-remote-ssh-x7dr, the remote workspaces epic eon-remote-workspaces-52i4, with Yu).

## Research (no product code)

1. What Tailscale and Headscale (the self-hosted, open-source control server) give a terminal: reaching a home or work machine from a laptop or phone without port forwarding, MagicDNS names, Tailscale SSH, ACLs, Funnel/Serve. Licences, who runs the control plane, cost, and platforms.
2. How competitors use them (Tern, Rex, herdr, Moshi, Moshline, Orca, Warp, Zed remote, VS Code tunnels, mosh/Eternal Terminal), with sources.
3. Fit for Eon: does Eon need anything beyond working well over an SSH connection that happens to run on a tailnet (host names, `eon window attach --host`, reconnects across network changes, phone attach)? Is there a case for first-class support (discovering Eon hosts on the tailnet, a `tailscale serve` recipe, Headscale for users who want no third-party control plane), and what it would cost to maintain.
4. Recommendation with small follow-up beads, if any. Nothing here enters the v0.2.0 gate without Lucca.

## Acceptance and boundaries

One dated primary-source record answers items 1-4, distinguishing capability, competitor
claims and anything actually tried. Include setup friction, control-plane/trust and
maintenance costs; compare OpenSSH over a tailnet with first-class integration. The
2026-11-09 recommendation stays the default to evaluate, not a Tailscale dependency
approval. Reuse docs/REFERENCES.md's remote SSH route and current remote-workspaces
epic; eon-remote-ssh-x7dr is a closed predecessor. attach --host here is planned work.

Research only: no account/ACL/service/host installation, listener, product dependency
or contract edit. Do not broaden Yu's assignment or add a release-gate blocker. Report
follow-up proposals for Lucca, plus unverified vendor/pricing facts, rather than filing
implementation. Verification is the research/Beads record; no runtime/profile proof.

comments.author: lucca
comments.text: Evidence for item 3, 2026-11-09: a Rex beta user found the Tailscale-first setup (each host a Tailscale machine, certificates, several service-start methods) the one clunky part of Rex, and contrasted it with herdr's plain SSH. Suggest the research weigh setup friction explicitly. The default answer stays "Eon works over SSH that happens to run on a tailnet" unless a concrete user need appears.

title: Stop evaluation-time GitLab grammar fetches from failing the cache CI
description:
## Problem
Cache workflow run 38929342825 (edge 32bb4ad, 2026-10-16) failed at evaluation: Nix could not fetch git+https://gitlab.com/gabmus/tree-sitter-blueprint (rev 355ef84ef8a958ac822117b652cf4d49bac16c79). Pinned github:Yazelix/nova-helix/817dcbca8b99c3db35ea66ded7492673d1a397ad grammars.nix:36 calls builtins.fetchTree (type git) for grammar sources, so a transient GitLab error fails the whole run before any cached build is used. The same pins passed on a14a90c two hours earlier; GitLab answered again minutes later, and nothing in Eon's Nix inputs changed.

## Contract
Evaluating and building Eon's packages never depends on a git host at evaluation time. Grammar sources resolve through fixed-output fetchers (hash-pinned), so a cached build needs no git host, and an uncached build fails only at build time for that grammar.

## Owner
nova-helix's grammars.nix owns the fetch; Eon consumes it via flake.lock. Fix it in nova-helix (fixed-output fetchers, as already done for Codeberg and SourceHut), then bump Eon's lock. The Eon helix-grammars check already rejects evaluation-time Codeberg and SourceHut fetches; extend it to every evaluation-time git fetch.

## Acceptance
nix eval of Eon's packages succeeds with gitlab.com unreachable (e.g. blocked in a sandbox); the extended helix-grammars check fails on any evaluation-time git fetch; cache CI passes. Full affected Nix surfaces.

## Note
Run 38929342825 was rerun with --failed on 2026-10-16 to restore this edge build's cache; that does not fix this bead.
close_reason: Transient GitLab 503 (run 38929342825 attempt 1); the rerun passed and nothing in Eon changed. Not worth fixing now: nova-helix grammars.nix still fetches ~283 GitHub and GitLab grammar sources during evaluation without hashes, so a host outage can fail evaluation. Reopen if that recurs or slows installs.

title: Investigate stale claims in the AGENTS.md files and how to stop the drift
description:
## Why

Lucca, 2026-10-30, after a project opinion pass: "create one bead to investigate each of those".
The finding: AGENTS.md is the most-read file and binds every agent, yet its "Status" section is
already stale. It says the Apple Silicon macOS expansion "stays deferred because the user has no
Mac", while P0/P1 beads (`eon-mac-launch-kz4p.*`) are running macOS proof on a rented Mac and
with Yu. Stale binding text misleads every fresh agent. This bead looks for other drift and for a
cheap way to stop it recurring.

## Evidence

- `AGENTS.md:55-67` "Status": macOS "stays deferred because the user has no Mac for native proof
  (`eon-next-expansion-0wfb`, 2026-10-16)".
- `br list --status in_progress` on 2026-10-30: `eon-mac-launch-kz4p.12` (rented-Mac harness
  run), `.38`, `.39`, `.41`–`.43` (Yu's final check).
- `eon-mac-launch-kz4p.14` already owns rewriting the macOS Status text; this bead does not
  duplicate it.
- AGENTS.md and the directory AGENTS.md files are rendered from `.agent-protocols.local.md`
  sources; direct edits are forbidden.

## Scope

In scope (read-only investigation; report to Lucca):
- Check every factual or dated claim in `AGENTS.md`, `orbit/AGENTS.md`, `venus/AGENTS.md` and
  `runtime/AGENTS.md` (status, sequencing, bead IDs, open-gap pointers, platform claims, tool
  versions, model names) against the tracker and the tree. List each stale claim with evidence.
- Find why they drift: which kinds of change (status, plans, platform scope) update beads but
  not the rules.
- Propose a fix, preferring structure over instruction text. For example: move fast-changing
  status out of AGENTS.md into a pointer to beads; add a cheap check that bead IDs named in
  AGENTS.md exist and are open; review AGENTS.md at release time.
- Note whether AGENTS.md could split into a short hot path plus linked detail to cut agent entry
  cost (about 6,300 words across the four AGENTS.md files and AGENT-PROTOCOLS.md at 39e0a25), as
  an option for Lucca.

Out of scope:
- The macOS Status rewrite itself (`eon-mac-launch-kz4p.14`).
- Editing any AGENTS.md source or render, or the imported protocols.

## Acceptance

- A comment on this bead listing each stale claim (file:line, what it says, what is true,
  evidence), the drift causes, and ranked proposals marked as needing Lucca's approval.

## Verification

- Each stale claim cites a `br show` or tree command that shows the current truth.
- Each bead ID named in the four AGENTS.md files was checked with `br --no-db show <id>`.

## Stop Conditions

- Stop before any rule edit: AGENTS.md text is Lucca's to approve.

## Maintenance Notes

- Coordinate with `eon-mac-launch-kz4p.14` so the Status rewrite and any structural proposal do
  not collide.
close_reason: Findings in the 2026-10-30 comment (stale claims, drift causes, ranked proposals). Fixes and the Status removal go to eon-946u (scope comment); the bead-ID check is eon-wxlad; macOS text coordination noted on kz4p.14 and .46.

"Codex cannot reach the Nix daemon" holds only for the prescribed `-s read-only` review; `~/.cache/eon-agents/eon-overseer/codex-run.sh` runs implementation with network access "needed to reach the Nix daemon".
9. Minor:
   - `AGENTS.md:198` "Do not mark a contract `Proven`". Orbit's index uses `Proved` (13 to 0) and Venus mixes both (13 Proven, 15 Proved), from `grep -c 'Status:\*\* Prov'`.

### Why the text drifts (from drift-causes.md)

- Only three commits ever touched Status (0955a7c, 4d1edb1, e1852b5). The first version was already stale the day it was written. The one fix that held (e1852b5, 2026-10-16) worked because 0wfb's acceptance required it.
- Timeline:
  - 2026-10-18: Lucca resumed Apple Silicon work, recorded in a t8o comment. That day 9bf1604 edited orbit's source but not the root Status.
  - 2026-10-21: lm9p closed.
  - 2026-10-27: kz4p was created, with the Status edit scheduled last (kz4p.14).
  - Status is now 14 days old. Since 10-16, 151 platform, release or distribution beads changed and the Status text did not.

Causes:
1. Status is a copy of bead state in a rules file. Nothing owns the copy.
2. Decisions arrive as bead comments or new epics, and nothing ties a decision to the rule text it invalidates.
3. Friction: fixing a fact in AGENTS.md is a rule change (Lucca's approval, a render, check-consumer), while a bead edit is free. So the bead gets updated and the rule waits.
4. No upkeep rule exists: not in AP-PLAN-001's "keep fields current", AP-DELIVERY-001 or AP-PROMOTION-001, nor in the create-beads, handoff or converge skills, nor in any release checklist.
5. No content check exists. `starcompass check-consumer` checks hashes and a byte-exact render, not meaning, and no CI or flake check runs it. `orbit/tools/governance` already parses `.beads/issues.jsonl` for Orbit's docs, but it runs by hand.
6. Inventories drift as well as status: the Venus feature list and the Orbit client count. Lists of what exists change with every feature; rules and owners do not.

### Ranked proposals (each needs Lucca's approval; none applied)

- P1. Remove the Status section from AGENTS.md. Keep only facts that carry a rule (Platform Discipline already holds the platform scope), and replace the rest with one pointer: "Current plan: `bv --robot-triage`; release epic `eon-igae`." This ends the class of drift instead of patching it. kz4p.14 and kz4p.46 would then delete the macOS sentence rather than rewrite it, so they need to agree. Cost: one approved edit plus a render.
- P2. Add a cheap reference check: a small Rust check, run as a flake check, that reads the four AGENTS.md files and `.beads/issues.jsonl`. Every cited bead ID must exist; IDs on "Open gaps:" lines must be open. It could optionally also check that named repo paths exist. It reuses orbit-governance's bead-reading pattern, but lives in a root Eon tool, since that tool is Orbit's. Since nothing runs flake checks per commit, list it in the Verification table's planning/docs row so policy edits and handoffs run it. Cost: about one session. It cannot tell present-tense prose ("owns", "comes next") from history, so it does not replace P1.
- P3. Rule of style for eon-946u: AGENTS.md names rules and owners, not inventories or state. The Venus feature list, the Orbit client count and present-tense status become pointers to the owning contract or doc (VEN-C*, ORB-C3, `bv`).
- P4. Same-commit upkeep: a decision bead whose outcome contradicts AGENTS.md text carries an "AGENTS.md text" acceptance item, as 0wfb did. This is one line in create-beads' template. It is text only, so it is weaker than P1 and P2.
- Not recommended: making factual Status edits approval-free (it is moot once P1 lands), and a session-end grep sweep (weaker than P2).

Coordination: the macOS text (A and B) stays with kz4p.14 and kz4p.46. Fixing items 1-9 belongs in eon-946u's restructure, so Lucca approves one AGENTS.md diff, not several. The Git Workflow item (3) needs his decision first.

title: Colour the CPU and RAM bar chips when the machine is under load
description:
## Why

Lucca, 2026-10-31: "should we color code cpu and ram too? like the ai quota widgets", then "yeah" to
the overseer's shape. Many agents and builds share one machine; memory pressure is what kills work,
and the bar shows CPU and RAM only as neutral numbers today. Quota chips colour by pace (a forecast);
CPU and RAM have no pace, so a continuous scale would flicker with every build.

## Decision (Lucca, 2026-10-31, "yeah")

- RAM: neutral below 80%, orange from 80%, red from 90%.
- CPU: colours only sustained load: the average over the last 30 seconds at 90% or more is orange
  (red at a higher sustained level only if the implementer finds a clear default; otherwise orange
  only), and short spikes stay neutral.
- No green: a healthy machine looks quiet.
- Hover and accessibility say why in words (for example `RAM use 91% of 31.3 GiB: under pressure`),
  so colour is never the only signal; every colour keeps at least 4.5:1 contrast on the bar, reusing
  the quota chips' orange and red where they qualify.
- Thresholds and the CPU averaging window are configurable under `[bar]`, defaults documented in
  docs/CONFIGURATION.md (AGENTS.md rule 6).

## Contract

Amends EON-C32 (Eon Bar items and order): the CPU and RAM load-level keys, their failures, the
Runtime-to-Venus levels, and the Boundary's per-widget option. Approved by Lucca on 2026-10-31,
quote "1 ok", relayed by eon-overseer; amendment text as drafted in
~/.cache/eon-agents/claude-hjtns-work/eon-c32-amendment.md. The CPU and RAM colouring itself is a
feature (bar items are features since eon-vn0nk retired VEN-C29). Behaviour home:
venus/docs/PRESENTATION.md (Eon Bar), docs/CONFIGURATION.md.

## Scope

In scope: venus/src/system.rs (readings and the 30 s CPU average), the bar scene and chrome render
(venus/src/scene.rs, venus/src/render/chrome.rs), accessibility text (venus/src/accessibility.rs),
the `[bar]` configuration keys and their validation, PRESENTATION.md, CONFIGURATION.md, CHANGELOG.md.
macOS readings use the same thresholds. Out of scope: per-process views, notifications, the quota
chips' pace scale, swap.

## Acceptance

- Scene tests (venus/src/scene/tests/bar.rs): RAM neutral at 79%, orange at 80%, red at 90%; CPU
  neutral for a short spike, orange after a sustained 30 s average at or above 90%; configured
  thresholds respected; invalid configuration rejected as other `[bar]` keys are.
- Accessibility and hover text name the state.
- One isolated installed screenshot showing an orange or red chip (isolated headless Sway, never
  Lucca's running Eon).

## Verification

`nix develop -c eon-test -p yazelix-venus` (and the config crate's tests if keys live there), fmt,
clippy, `nix build .#default --no-link`, converge with Codex, one isolated installed observation.

title: Decide: sessions owned by Eon, shown by windows, and draft the contract
description:
## Why

Lucca, 2026-11-04: opened a second Eon window and it did not appear in the Workspaces picker (Alt+Shift+S lists only this window's workspaces, EON-C33). He also asked "can we call it sessions instead of workspaces?" Thinking from first principles, the picker is a symptom: today a window owns its workspaces, so the answer to "what work exists" depends on which window you ask. Lucca thinks in tmux terms: a session is a persistent group of terminals, and a window is a view onto one.

Approved direction (Lucca, 2026-11-04, "i agree with the things you said", answering the overseer's numbered list):

1. Sessions are owned by Eon as a whole, not by a window. A window shows one session at a time. The picker and `eon sessions` list every session, marking which window shows each.
2. Picking a session that another window shows moves it into the picking window. The losing window shows its most recent still-existing session that no other window shows, or closes quietly if none exists (Lucca's later 2026-11-04 "agree", recorded in comments). A session is never shown in two windows at once (a terminal has one size), and picking never raises another window (rule 9).
3. Closing a window ends only the session it shows. Other sessions keep running and stay listed (the "closing the window quits it" decision, eon-7cf0y, still holds).
4. "Session" replaces "workspace" in product text, the CLI and configuration. The earlier alias proposal is superseded by Lucca's 2026-11-04 direction, "we dont want legacy code, brother": add no aliases, shims or compatibility paths. Human-facing output uses pane/popup IDs (p1/u1); terminal IDs appear only in JSON as `terminal-N`, per his later "agree" in the comments. JSON field names retain their spellings. Config/old-shell transition treatment and the conflicting repository alias/tombstone rule must be resolved with Lucca before drafting the contract; do not silently choose a data-loss or startup-failure policy.
5. This bead decides first: it confirms how supervisors and windows relate today, compares tmux's and Zellij's session models (~/pjs/refs), drafts the contract text for approval, and splits the implementation into small child beads. eon-remote-workspaces-52i4.4 (host registry contract) waits for this decision so it builds on sessions.

## Scope

In scope: the reference gate, the supervisor/window evidence, the exact contract text (EON-C33 and every contract that names workspaces or windows as owners, EON-C10 CLI and the configuration boundary), the approved terminal-ID naming change, retirement/transition impact and corpus coverage (without adding aliases, shims or compatibility paths), and the child-bead split with order and dependencies.

Out of scope: implementation; Nova.

## Acceptance

- The supervisor/window structure is recorded with file:line evidence.
- Reference notes: tmux and Zellij session/client models, with what is kept and what is rejected.
- Contract text is drafted, and Lucca has approved it.
- Child beads exist, each small enough for one session, with their dependencies.

comments.author: lucca
comments.text: Terminal IDs, Lucca, 2026-11-04: "agree", answering the overseer's recommendation. People never see terminal IDs. Human-facing output (for example `eon windows`) names panes and popups (p1, u1) instead. Terminal IDs remain only in JSON for tools, spelled `terminal-N` instead of `session-N`, so "session" means only the session. Lucca had asked "why terminal-N instead of pane-N?". Pane IDs (p1, p3) already exist; popups (u1, u2) run terminals but are not panes; and a terminal keeps its identity when its pane moves.

comments.author: lucca
comments.text:
Evidence (read-only investigation, 2026-11-04, at c5e922d).

Today:
- Each window is its own supervisor in its own namespace. `eon window new` (runtime/crates/eon-runtime/src/windows.rs:221-295) reserves $XDG_RUNTIME_DIR/eon/w/<ID> and spawns `eon run` under setsid with EON_WINDOW_RUNTIME_DIR. Bare `eon` uses the default namespace (supervisor.rs:735-750). A supervisor holds exactly one Venus (supervisor.rs:1157).
- One IdAllocator per supervisor (workspace.rs:119-184) hands out wN, tN, pN, uN and session-N, so every window has its own w1, t1 and session-1.
- EON_TERMINAL is session-N.<run_id> (sessions.rs:1587-1589). Shells inherit EON_WINDOW_RUNTIME_DIR, so CLI calls resolve in the terminal's namespace.

Contracts that encode window ownership: EON-C33 (1-32 workspaces per window; no showing another window's workspace; no zero-workspace window), EON-C23 (independent windows, own supervisor each), EON-C10 (--window namespaces), EON-C8 (close/detach per window, picker lists the window's workspaces), EON-C11 (quit/stop per window), EON-C31 (Alt+G per window), EON-C35/C36/C39 (targeting via EON-C10), EON-C38 planned.

Consequences:
- The direction needs one supervisor (per generation) serving many Venus windows, which is tmux's model (one server, many clients; global IDs; `attach -d` detaches other clients), not Zellij's (one server per session, clients reconnect). The per-window namespaces, --window, `eon windows`, window stop/attach, the `others` summary and the detach notice all need redefinition, plus adapters for shells that already carry EON_WINDOW_RUNTIME_DIR.
- Hardest part: moving a live session between windows. Orbit admits one interactive client, and only the PID named by AttachAllow; naming never ends an existing attachment (orbit/docs/CONTRACTS.md:113-140, 819-825). The handover order must be: the old Venus detaches from the session's terminals, the supervisor names the new Venus, then the new Venus attaches.
- Generations split the pool. Sessions on an older build's supervisor cannot move; they are listed as attach-only or not at all.
- References: tmux-3.8 (tmux.1:47-92, cmd-attach-session.c:121-133, options-table.c:401-412) and zellij-v0.45.1 (zellij-utils/src/sessions.rs:150-177, zellij-client/src/lib.rs:186,214) under ~/pjs/refs.

comments.author: lucca
comments.text: Losing window, Lucca, 2026-11-04: "agree". When a session moves out of window A, A shows the session it showed most recently that still exists and is not shown by another window. If there is none, A closes quietly. No terminal stops, because the moved session keeps running in the other window, and no window is ever left with zero sessions (EON-C33's rule carries over).

title: Design and prove native macOS Eon distribution
description:
## Outcome

Design and prove a native macOS delivery channel for an already accepted full-Eon Apple Silicon runtime. This issue owns delivery only; it does not implement Orbit, Venus, EonTerm, or Eon platform behavior.

## Current activation boundary

Deferred. On 2026-09-11 the user approved Nix-only `aarch64-darwin` runtime work and explicitly left signing, notarization, installers, Homebrew, and public distribution outside that slice. Reopen only after native `EON-C7` dogfood and a fresh distribution-graduation decision.

## Prerequisites and order

1. `eon-p93` approves graduation from Nix-only dogfood and selects the delivery target and maintenance envelope.
2. `eon-ohh` proves the shared direct-release verification, upgrade, rollback, and removal foundation.
3. `eon-prove-full-eon-apple-silicon-macos-t8o` proves the canonical full-Eon composition on Apple Silicon macOS.
4. This issue packages the exact accepted manifest and child proofs without another component graph.

## Reference and tool gate

Required before code: current Apple signing, hardened runtime, entitlements, notarization, stapling, Gatekeeper, quarantine, application bundle and disk-image behavior; Homebrew Cask requirements if selected; architecture-specific versus universal artifacts; exact runtime child proofs; canonical component manifest; active-work-safe upgrade policy; and credible release tooling. Record credentials, secrets boundary, hosted/local cost, dependency footprint, owned LOC, replacement cost, and recovery. Stop for user approval before selecting or adding a release tool.

Keep signing and notarization credentials outside repository state. Direct download and any package-manager entry consume the same immutable artifact, checksums, signatures, manifest, and version diagnostics. A website or package manager is not artifact authority.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. The selected architecture set has one immutable Eon application artifact or disk image, checksum, signature, notarization ticket, and exact component manifest.
2. Gatekeeper, quarantine, first/repeat launch, diagnostics, active-work-safe upgrade, rollback where supported, and removal pass on a clean macOS user account.
3. Any selected package-manager entry installs and removes the exact immutable artifact without rebuilding or changing the component graph.
4. Bundle identity, entitlements, privacy prompts, filesystem locations, logs, user data, and cleanup ownership are explicit. Uninstall preserves user data unless the user separately requests exact removal.
5. Exact credentials/tool boundaries, artifact sizes, closure contents, commands, environments, costs, limitations, and recovery results are recorded at an immutable candidate.

No runtime feature, child fix, second manifest, Nova package change, hidden Nix dependency, Intel/universal promise, App Store distribution, or auto-updater is implicit.
notes: Planning refinement — 2026-09-11: native macOS distribution is a deferred epic, not a claimable task. It stays inactive during the Nix-only EON-C7 frontier. If the user later activates distribution graduation, split notarized bundle/signing, delivery/update metadata, and install/upgrade/removal dogfood into owner-sized children after the runtime contract is Proven.

title: Decide: give Eon Bar widgets the tab pills' height and another way to tell them apart
description:
## Why

Lucca, 2026-10-24, looking at his installed Eon Bar after the pane chrome work (eon-mur2, eon-e8hh,
eon-f5pg, eon-2x6h, eon-54jv, eon-m5bv): "before i was happy with widgets being thicker than the tab
pills, but now im not so sure. i think it's worth creating a bead make them equaly thick. and maybe
change something to differentiate them, example: 'widgets get a sort of outline' or whatever. with a
research path before decision".

In his screenshot the bar's widget chips (Codex and Claude quota, CPU, RAM, clock, `EON 0.1.1`) are
taller than the tab pills (`1 machines_vs_aliens`, `+`).

## Contracts and code to read first

- VEN-C21 (venus/docs/CONTRACTS.md:1228, Native Eon Bar workspace header): pill size, the quota chip
  slot, control geometry.
- EON-C32 (docs/CONTRACTS.md:2529, Eon Bar items and order): the widgets.
- The Venus scene and chrome code that sizes tab pills and widget chips, and the beads that set their
  heights (find them with `br search` for the chip and pill work; record which bead chose the taller
  chips and why).

## Research path (before any decision; overseer runs it, Lucca decides)

1. Measure today: tab pill and widget chip heights, paddings, radii, fills and text sizes at scale 1

comments.text:
# eon-i3th2 implementation notes

Base: edge 2e8d519. Worktree /home/lucca/.cache/eon-agents/eon-i3th2.

## What changed

- `venus/src/render/chrome.rs`: `Spinners` holds the window's focus colour
  (`Spinners::new(turning, focus_color)`, from the renderer's already-resolved
  `focus_color`: Eon's `[terminal] focus_color`, else Venus's default
  `#b207fb` from `--focus-color`'s default in launch.rs). `push_badge` resolves
  the dots' colour per badge with `working_color(focus, surface)`, where
  surface is the disc the badge sits on (`ring`), or `BAR_BACKGROUND` when it
  has none (a sidebar row that is not hovered or focused sits on the sidebar
  card, whose fallback background is the bar's colour). Each `SpinnerSlot`
  records that colour, so `turn_spinners` rewrites a tick in the same colour.
  `push_badge_glyph` and `push_dots` take the colour as a parameter.
- `palette::ATTENTION_WORKING` is removed (no legacy constant); the palette's
  attention comment says working and background dots take the focus colour.
- Docs: `docs/CONFIGURATION.md` (`focus_color` paragraph), `docs/USAGE.md`
  (agent sidebar state list), `venus/docs/LAUNCH.md` (`--focus-color`).
  `venus/docs/PRESENTATION.md` names no badge colour; unchanged.
- `CHANGELOG.md` Unreleased entry (rule 10: user-visible presentation and the
  meaning of an existing configuration key change).

## Contrast handling

`working_color(focus, surface)` keeps `focus` when it already reads at 3:1
(WCAG non-text contrast; the same 3:1 bound `cells::cursor_outline` uses for
the cursor edge) against `surface`; otherwise it blends `focus` toward white in
1/255 steps and takes the first blend that reaches 3:1. All chrome surfaces a
badge sits on are dark (bar disc rgb(10,13,20), sidebar hover/focus highlight
rgb(40,54,70)), so a blend toward white always gets there (white is 12:1 on the
highlight). The focus frame itself has no contrast handling to share; the
cursor outline's blend-to-contrast is the precedent followed.

Per surface, not one colour for all: the default `#b207fb` reads 4.0:1 on the
bar disc but 2.5:1 on the sidebar highlight. One shared colour would lighten
every tab badge to rgb(192,51,252); per surface, tab badges and plain sidebar
rows draw the exact focus colour and only a hovered or focused sidebar row's
badge lightens (to that same rgb(192,51,252)).

## Deviations and decisions

1. **Background badges follow too.** The three still dots (agent waiting on
   background work) shared `ATTENTION_WORKING` with the working spinner
   through `push_dots`. The bead names needs input, failed and finished as the
   states that keep their colours and does not mention background; I kept
   background sharing the working colour, so both "still busy" badges stay one
   family in the focus colour, rather than keep the old blue as a new
   `ATTENTION_BACKGROUND` constant. Overseer: flag if background should keep
   the blue.
2. **No contract step.** No `EON-C`/`ORB-C`/`VEN-C` contract text names the
   working colour. `venus/docs/CONTRACTS.md:1732` says "the working blue" but
   inside a past proof record, which stays valid as written (Proof and Review:
   existing indexed proofs stay valid). `docs/CONTRACTS.md:486` says the
   selected pane's outline uses `focus_color`; it does not claim to be the
   key's only use, and presentation colour is a feature, not contract text.
   No bead/01-contract-step.md.
3. **Rule 6 (configurability).** No new setting: the working colour follows
   the existing `[terminal] focus_color` key, whose default is already
   documented in `docs/CONFIGURATION.md`. The 3:1 bound stays fixed as a
   readability (accessibility) floor, matching the cursor outline's fixed 3:1.
4. **Untested claim: the translucent sidebar card.** A badge on a plain
   sidebar row has no disc; it sits on the sidebar card, whose fill is the
   terminal's default background at `background_opacity` over the desktop. The
   colour is checked against the bar colour (the card's fallback background),
   not the live terminal theme or desktop behind it, the same assumption every
   other attention colour already makes there.
5. **Dimmed (stale) badges** keep drawing at 0.45 alpha as before; contrast at
   that alpha is not checked, as for every other state.

## Round 1 (review by Codex and Opus; overseer INBOX 2026-11-06)

Rebased onto edge ce09d2a (hints bar landing). CHANGELOG conflict: both
Unreleased entries kept, this one first.

1. **Contrast against the real surface (Codex 1, Opus 1): fixed.** Item 4
   above was wrong in practice: the sidebar card is the neighbouring
   terminal's background, not the bar colour (navy read 2.72:1 on the
   (25,25,25) card), and unfocused inbox rows sit on `DIALOG_BACKGROUND`
   (2.69:1). `Spinners::push_badge` now takes a `Backing`:
   - `Disc(color)`: tabs, edge and workspace-label badges (bar disc) and
     hovered or focused sidebar and inbox rows (highlight disc);
   - `Surface(color)`: an opaque painted surface: the inbox dialog, and the
     sidebar card when `background_opacity` is 1 (its fill is the last entry
     of `card_backdrops`, which now says so, with an assertion in
     `card_backdrop_keeps_cards_like_the_agent_sidebar_at_terminal_opacity`);
   - `Translucent`: the sidebar card below opacity 1, whose painted colour
     depends on the desktop behind the window. Working and background dots
     there get the bar's disc, as on a tab; other glyphs stay bare.
   The dots blend toward black or white (whichever contrasts more with the
   surface), so a light surface darkens them: white on an opaque white
   terminal becomes a mid grey at 3:1. Default `background_opacity` is 0.8, so
   by default sidebar working and background rows show the dark disc.
   Docs (CONFIGURATION.md, LAUNCH.md, USAGE.md, CHANGELOG.md) say exactly
   this; they do not name the Alt+Q inbox (item 6).
2. **Preset collisions (Opus 2): accepted trade-off, no code.** With
   `preset:magma` (#ff3b30) working reads like error (#ff6b6b), with
   `preset:solar` (#ffd23f) like needs input (#ffc457), with `preset:forest`
   (#35c978) like finished (#60c460). Glyph shape (braille cell or three dots
   vs ◆, ✕, ✓) and, on GPU, motion still tell them apart; no hue logic.
3. **Background badges follow the focus colour (Opus 6): confirmed** by the
   overseer.
4. **Nits.** Opus 4: one `cells::blend_to_contrast(color, against, ratio)`
   now serves both the dots and `cursor_outline` (which is
   `blend_to_contrast(fill, fill, 3.0)`, same results: amount 0 never passes
   since a colour has 1:1 with itself). Opus 5: the blend runs only for working
   and background badges. Opus 7: kept; the sweep's comment now says the
   search over increasing blends is what guarantees the least blend.
5. **Not covered by a unit test:** the two `push_attention_row` call sites
   passing the dialog surface and the sidebar card (Renderer methods; the
   renderer-building tests are ignored, needing a native display). Covered by
   the installed captures instead.
6. **The Alt+Q inbox shows no working or background dots (deviation from the
   INBOX request to name it).** The inbox lists only the attention queue:
   needs input, error and finished (docs/USAGE.md, Attention inbox); the
   installed capture with a working agent shows "All 0, No agent needs
   attention". So no doc or CHANGELOG line names the inbox. The code still
   passes the inbox rows' real surface (`Backing::Surface(DIALOG_BACKGROUND)`),
   since `push_attention_row` now needs one; it only affects dots if the
   inbox ever lists those states.
7. **Light terminal background is not reachable installed.** Orbit does not
   publish an OSC 11 default-background change in its frames (both `#ffffff`
   and `rgb:ffff/ffff/ffff` forms left the terminal black), and Eon has no
   terminal theme setting. The light opaque case is proved by the unit test
   (white focus on a white card darkens to 3:1); installed, the light case
   shown is a white desktop behind the translucent card.

## Round 2 (Codex re-check of 5c0d7ec6; overseer INBOX)

Docs and records only. CONFIGURATION.md, LAUNCH.md and CHANGELOG.md now say
the 3:1 holds for a current agent's badge: a stale badge draws at 0.45 alpha
on purpose (unchanged behaviour, `push_badge_glyph`) and reads below 3:1
(navy on the bar disc: about 1.9:1). Item 1's line about the inbox corrected.

title: Keep older running windows working when config.toml gains a newer setting
description:
## Why

Found 2026-10-24 by the overseer. After eon-f5pg landed, the overseer added `focus_border_width = 1`
to Lucca's `~/.config/eon/config.toml` at his request. An `eon` from an older build that was still on
PATH (the build Lucca's running window started from, cdnmbxk3, before eon-e8hh) then failed on every
read of that file:

    eon: invalid Eon configuration /home/lucca/.config/eon/config.toml: TOML parse error at line 4
    unknown field `focus_border_width`, expected one of `background_opacity`, ... `rows`

The failure aborted an unrelated command in the overseer's shell. The overseer removed the line again
at once. Lucca's live windows run their own build's `eon` (EON_SESSION_BIN), so any old window that
reads the shared config after a newer build's key appears in it rejects the whole file, until the user
restarts that window. Every new setting therefore breaks every running older window the moment the
user adopts it.

## Goal

A newer key in config.toml never breaks an older running build; an older build still refuses real
mistakes (typos, wrong types) for keys it knows. Options for the contract (wording to Lucca): keep
strict parsing but tolerate unknown keys when the file declares a newer config schema; or warn and
ignore unknown keys in running windows while `eon config check` stays strict; or version the
configuration. Name the owner (Eon Runtime parses configuration).

## Acceptance

- A Runtime test: a config with a key the build does not know loads in a running supervisor and its
  CLI without failing (behaviour per the approved contract), while a misspelled known key still fails
  where the contract says it must.
- Reproduce first with an older build and a newer key, as above.

Related: eon-1bq8 (in-place update), eon-newer-build-notice-byd2.
close_reason: Unknown config keys are ignored with a warning; proof in comments

comments.text: Approval (Lucca, 2026-10-24, direct to the overseer, "do it"): the contract is "An Eon build ignores a configuration key it does not know, with one warning naming the key and file, so a newer setting never breaks an older running window. A known key with a wrong type or value still fails." The popup clause "Eon rejects unknown fields" changes to match. Rejected: tolerating unknown keys only under a declared newer config version.

title: Name the core count in the CPU tooltip
description:
Contract: the Eon Bar CPU widget's tooltip (find the owning clause, likely VEN-C8 bar widgets / EON-C bar widget text; check whether the tooltip wording is contract text before changing it).

Decision (Lucca, 2026-10-26): show the number of cores in the CPU tooltip. Today it reads "CPU use 6%, all cores, over the last 2 seconds"; for example "CPU use 6% across 16 cores, over the last 2 seconds". The chip itself stays "CPU 6%" (the bar is short on space).

Find first: who measures CPU and who writes the tooltip text (Runtime sends resolved values, Venus parses no configuration; the core count should come from the same owner that computes the percentage, not be recomputed in Venus), and whether the count is logical CPUs (what the percentage averages over) — say "cores" only if that is what it counts, else pick the accurate word.

Configurability: the count is a measured fact, not a user value; no setting.

Acceptance: the tooltip names the core count used for the percentage; a test pins the tooltip text with a given count; affected crate tests, fmt, clippy green; one installed observation of the tooltip (hover cannot be driven in headless Sway per the capture recipe, so use whatever check the owning code allows and say what was observed). Scope boundary: tooltip text only; no chip, layout or per-core display.

Approved VEN-C28 change: tooltip reads "CPU use 12% across 16 logical CPUs, over the last 2 seconds"; the count is the cpuN lines of the later reading; a /proc/stat with no per-CPU lines is malformed and shows no CPU label. comments.text: Reference gate (contract change, VEN-C28). Behavior: the CPU chip's hover and static AccessKit label read 'CPU use N% across C logical CPUs, over the last 2 seconds' (singular 'logical CPU' for 1); chip text unchanged. One owner: the Venus system module (venus/src/system.rs) reads /proc/stat once per wake and derives both the percentage and the count from that one reading; Scene shows the text as before. No Runtime/EONW/config change. Routes read: venus/docs/REFERENCES.md 'CPU and memory use'. Sources: Linux v7.3 fs/proc/stat.c:64 (aggregate sums for_each_possible_cpu), :103 (cpuN lines for_each_online_cpu), kernel/sched/cputime.c:533 + kernel/sched/idle.c:283-288 + tick-sched.c:1098 (an offline CPU's idle and tick counters do not advance), so the aggregate delta holds only the CPUs the cpuN lines list; btop v1.4.7 6e39144 src/linux/btop_collect.cpp:321 (coreCount = sysconf(_SC_NPROCESSORS_ONLN)) and :1197-1200 (raised to the cpuN lines seen) = online logical CPUs; Waybar 0.15.0 90b209a src/modules/cpu_usage/linux.cpp:7-62 pads to every present CPU with zeros. Kept: count the cpuN lines contiguous after the aggregate in the same reading as the later sample (btop-equivalent, no second source like sysconf or /sys). Rejected: Waybar's present-CPU padding (counts CPUs that add no time); recomputing in Runtime (a second owner of the reading); 'cores' (16 logical CPUs on 10 physical cores on the i5-13450HX). Hotplug between two readings: counted as the later reading lists it. A reading with no cpuN lines is malformed and shows no label. Check: cpu_use_counts_iowait_idle_and_guest_once pins the text for 16 and 1 CPUs; cpu_use_rejects_bad_readings_instead_of_showing_zero pins the no-cpuN/non-contiguous/cpux cases. title: Stop the Fable chip from reading as a separate budget when it shares Claude's weekly
description:
## Why

2026-11-01: the Eon Bar showed Claude's weekly at 9% and a `Fable` chip at 100%. The overseer read the Fable chip as a separate full budget and proposed moving implementing to Fable subagents to spare the 9%. Lucca asked "fable will spend from the same 9% no?", and he was right.

Anthropic (https://support.claude.com/en/articles/15424964-claude-fable-models-on-your-plan): Fable models "draw from your plan's regular weekly usage limits and use them faster than other Claude models"; "You can use up to 50% of your weekly usage limits on Fable models"; other models "draw from the same usage limits and you can never use more than your weekly limit". The general article (https://support.claude.com/en/articles/11647753-understanding-usage-and-length-limits) calls it "a separate weekly limit for Fable", which invites the same misreading.

So a scoped chip at 100% beside an all-models chip at 9% tells a person they have Fable to spare when they have at most 9% of the weekly left. AGENTS.md rule 8: a reasonable expectation the display gets wrong is a gap to close.

## Change (recommendation; needs Lucca's approval)

A model-scoped weekly chip shows what is actually usable: the lower of its own remaining percentage and the unscoped seven-day window's remaining percentage, when both are known. Hover and the accessible label say both numbers and why, for example "Fable: 9% usable (Fable share 100% left; shares Claude's weekly, 9% left)". JSON keeps both raw readings unchanged (EON-C10 data stays the provider's numbers); the derived value is presentation. Alternatives: keep the raw number and only add the hover note (cheaper, still misleading at a glance); or hide a scoped chip whose remaining is above the all-models one (loses the Fable cap when it is the binding limit).

## Contract

EON-C27 alone owns these quota windows; EON-C26 is retired. Its Result says chips show
each supplied window remaining percentage: the recommended usable value requires exact
amendment approval before code. Presentation belongs in PRESENTATION.md, USAGE.md and
CONFIGURATION.md, without a new VEN chip contract.

## Acceptance

- Tests: scoped 100% with weekly 9% shows 9% with the explanation; scoped 20% with weekly 60% shows 20%; missing weekly shows the scoped value with "weekly unknown".
- Isolated capture of the bar with both chips; hover text checked.

## Scope

Display only; no change to how CodexBar readings are collected or stored.


## Current evidence and approval boundary

At dcaef1c quota.rs:29-48,154-185 parses scoped windows; scene.rs:3657-3684 presents
them. The provider articles are dated research: recheck their meaning/denominators before
asking Lucca to approve the min recommendation. Do not silently settle min, hiding or
hover-only. Preserve raw JSON and unknown/stale behavior. Verify number and hover/a11y
for the examples plus unchanged raw session JSON; use the current affected code/boundary
proof and isolated installed observation. Portability: neutral display.

title: Enter beta: ready Eon for its public announcement
description:
## Why

Lucca, 2026-11-06: "i think we made it beta too fast / we could make it alpha again and after
all's good we finally enter beta properly / and forget 1.0 / there's not a bead today that can
gate it, it only needs people using eon and filing issues". To the plan he said "agreed!".

Eon is alpha until v0.2.0 is cut (eon-igae.9), then enters beta. This announcement epic closes
after the released-version site text and demos are ready, before Lucca announces it publicly
(a video). 1.0 is unscheduled: no bead gates it; user reports will. The
Nix-free install ships as GitHub release assets on Yazelix/eon, with SHA-256 checksums and GitHub
artifact attestations, and becomes README's first install line. No v0.2.0 tag, release,
promotion or announcement without Lucca's explicit OK (2026-11-08), even with every gate bead
closed.

Earlier 1.0 scope and decisions: see this bead's history and comments.

## Gate membership

A gate member is a bead that blocks the cut, eon-igae.9, or a child of this epic; work that must
follow the tag blocks eon-igae.16 (the last step before the announcement). Members that
change shipped code also block the re-proofs eon-igae.7 and eon-igae.8, so the re-proofs run last.
Add new members the same way (blocks eon-igae.9), never as blockers of this epic: br treats a
blocked epic as blocking all its children, which hid ready children until 2026-11-09. Closed
members from before 2026-11-09 stay recorded as blockers of this epic.

## Historical gate snapshot (2026-11-10, edge d0d5b5f)

The dated list below is retained as history, not a current readiness claim. Use the cut's
live blockers, this epic's children and the current-state notes below for scheduling.

- Pane headers (Lucca, 2026-11-10: "the need rex-mode on the panes asap"): eon-2ibdd (one
  Rex-like header band per pane), in progress. It changes shipped chrome, so it blocks the

title: Write the 1.x stability contract
description:
## Why

1.0 leaves beta (`eon-versioning-beta-bfyf`). README "Status and limits" says commands,
configuration and behavior may still change between 0.x releases; 1.0 must say what no longer
changes. Without a written promise, "1.0" means nothing to users or to later agents deciding
whether a change is breaking.

## Draft discussed with Lucca (2026-10-20)

- Commands: every documented `eon` command, flag and exit code keeps working through 1.x.
  Machine-readable output is stable only where the docs say so.
- Config: a config file that loads in 1.0 loads in every 1.x. Old keys produce a warning, never
  a failure; nothing is removed before 2.0.
- Upgrades: installing a newer 1.x never ends live terminals; older generations stay listable and
  stoppable (builds on EON-C11 and the preserved EONW revisions).
- Default shortcuts: existing ones keep their meaning; new ones may be added.
- Not covered: appearance, the ORBS/ORBF and EONW wire protocols (own versions), macOS preview,
  anything outside x86_64 Linux on native Wayland.
Lucca said "ok, let's talk" to the promise; refine the draft with him before writing it.

## Evidence

- `README.md:74`: beta wording to replace at release.
- `docs/CONTRACTS.md`: EON-C1..C27; the next free ID is assigned when written (the CPU widget
  bead also proposes one, so check the index first).
- `docs/DISTRIBUTION.md:38`: 1.0.0 meaning.

## Scope

In: the contract text in `docs/CONTRACTS.md`, its check(s), and the user-facing summary in
`docs/USAGE.md` or `README.md`. Out: implementing exit codes (`eon-8mnr.1`) or other behavior.

## Acceptance

- Lucca approves the final contract text (stop for approval before editing the index).
- The contract names its consumer, trigger, result, failures and the cheapest falsifying check
  for each guarantee (e.g. a config-compatibility fixture, an upgrade-with-live-terminals proof).
- Docs link to it.

## Verification

Planning/docs route: changed Markdown paths, contract ID and diff reviewed; no runtime claim.

## Stop Conditions

- Stop if a guarantee needs behavior that does not exist yet; file or link the bead instead.

title: Let configured shortcuts take precedence over default shortcuts
description:
## Why

EON-C28 (1.x stability, `eon-igae.1`) promises that a later default shortcut never makes a 1.0
configuration fail. Today Eon rejects a configured popup shortcut that collides with a workspace
shortcut, and a configuration can bind almost any modified key. So any default shortcut added
during 1.x would break some 1.0 configuration, which would freeze default shortcuts until 2.0.
One gap already exists: Venus binds Alt+Shift+N (new window), but Eon's reserved list does not
include it, so a configuration can bind it today. This must change before 1.0, while breaking
changes are still allowed.

## Evidence

- `runtime/crates/eon-runtime/src/managed_environment.rs:538-542`: a popup shortcut that
  `workspace_shortcut` matches is rejected with "conflicts with an Eon workspace shortcut".
- `runtime/crates/eon-runtime/src/managed_environment.rs:554-581`: `workspace_shortcut`, the
  reserved list; Alt+Shift+N is absent.
- `venus/src/application/shortcuts.rs:96-280`: Venus's fixed bindings, including Alt+Shift+N
  near line 261.
- `docs/CONTRACTS.md` EON-C20: rejects popup shortcuts colliding with Alt+Slash or Alt+0..9.

## Decision to propose (recommendation)

A shortcut the user configures takes precedence over a default on the same key: the default
becomes unbound (and the Alt+/ viewer shows that), instead of the configuration failing.
Keep a small fixed set that can never be overridden (Alt+Slash, so the viewer stays reachable,
and perhaps Alt+0..9), stated in EON-C20. Rejected: freezing default shortcuts for all of 1.x
(blocks features such as the command runner); reserving whole modifier families for Eon
(restricts users and still needs a list).

## Scope

In: the EON-C20 change (approve with Lucca first), Runtime validation, the EONW popup catalog
or a new field telling Venus which fixed bindings are overridden, Venus dispatch and the
shortcut viewer, and one source for the reserved list so Runtime and Venus agree.
Out: user-configurable workspace shortcuts beyond popups; key remapping.

## Acceptance

- A configuration binding a popup to any non-reserved default key loads; the popup wins and the
  viewer shows the default as overridden.
- Alt+Shift+N and every other Venus fixed binding follow the same rule.
- EON-C20 and EON-C28 text agree; the EON-C28 shortcut fixture covers one override.

## Verification

Focused tests for validation and override (red/green), the affected Runtime and Venus builds,
`cargo fmt --check` and clippy for Venus, and one isolated installed dogfood observation.

title: Add the EON-C28 stability fixtures on the 1.0 candidate
description:
## Why

EON-C28 (1.x stability, `docs/CONTRACTS.md`) promises that commands, exit statuses, JSON fields,
configuration, default shortcuts, managed command names and older-generation Stop keep working
through 1.x. Each guarantee needs a check that every 1.x build runs, so a breaking change fails
the suite instead of reaching users. These fixtures record the 1.0 surface and must land on the
final 1.0 candidate, after the other 1.0 changes.

## Scope

In, as tests in the workspace suite (`nix develop -c eon-test`) unless noted:
- a configuration setting every documented 1.0 key, loaded with `EON_CONFIG_HOME` and
  `EON_RUNTIME_DIR` set;
- a parse corpus of every `eon` command and flag listed at 1.0;
- the 1.0 JSON fixture: the fields of each listed command's `--json` output (EON-C28 names this
  fixture as the documented JSON schema);
- the documented exit status of each failure class (after `eon-8mnr.1`);
- the 1.0 default shortcut actions, with one configured override (after `eon-igae.10`);
- the `managed-command-path` flake check extended to every documented `eon-` managed command
  name (eon-igae.11.3).
Out: the per-release upgrade observation and defaults review (release proof, `eon-igae.9`).
Older-window Stop (the 1.0 reserved-Stop golden fixture and the delegated test): eon-igae.11.3.

## Acceptance

Each fixture fails when its guarantee is broken (show one red/green per fixture class) and passes
on the 1.0 candidate.

## Verification

`nix develop -c eon-test` and `nix build --no-link .#checks.x86_64-linux.managed-command-path`
on the candidate revision.

title: Check every managed eon- command name and add the 1.0 older-window Stop test
description:
## Why

Split from eon-igae.11 on 2026-10-27 (prime-beads pass 2, Bead Size rule): EON-C28 promises that
managed command names and older-window Stop keep working through 1.x.

## Evidence

- nix/managed-command-checks.nix (imported as `managedCommandPathCheck` at flake.nix:981, check
  `managed-command-path` at :1116) checks only eon-nu and eon-bash.
- The delegated older-window Stop test already exists:
  `older_eonw_generations_stop_through_their_recorded_eon`
  (eon/crates/eon/tests/workspace_control.rs ~:10903, 6a0d8f4, eon-7cf0y.9). It stops an
  older-EONW window by running that window's recorded `eon`.
- eon-7cf0y.17 reserves a Stop message whose bytes never change across EONW versions, so any eon
  can stop any window even when the recorded `eon` is gone.
- Lucca, 2026-10-21 (on eon-igae.11): from 1.0 on a newer eon must be able to list and stop an
  older generation.

## Scope

In: extend `managed-command-path` to every documented `eon-` managed command name. After
eon-7cf0y.17, freeze the 1.0 reserved-Stop bytes as a golden fixture and test that a 1.0
supervisor answers it. Keep the delegated test. Out: the other fixtures (sibling slices); any
EONW change.

## Acceptance

The flake check fails when a documented managed name is missing and passes on the candidate; the
golden 1.0 reserved-Stop fixture fails on any byte change, and a 1.0 supervisor answers it; the
delegated test still passes.

## Verification

`nix build --no-link .#checks.x86_64-linux.managed-command-path` and `nix develop -c eon-test`
on the candidate revision; one red/green each. Codex review per AGENTS.md (Nix and test code).

## Contract

EON-C28 Open proof. Its sentence "Each later EONW revision adds its predecessor to the
previous-generation Stop test" (docs/CONTRACTS.md ~:3176-3178) no longer fits a fixed-bytes Stop.
This bead's change carries a minor amendment of that sentence (the overseer may approve it). If
the test needs any other shape EON-C28 does not describe, stop and bring the wording to Lucca.

title: Remove legacy compatibility before 1.0
description:
## Why

Lucca, 2026-10-20: "we should remove every legacy stuff from the repo. this is very important.
no one is using eon yet." Compatibility with earlier Eon builds, earlier EONW revisions, earlier
names and the pre-consolidation repositories costs code, tests, docs and agent context and
protects no user. It must go before EON-C28 (1.x stability) starts binding at v1.0.0.

## Inventory (edge bca350f, read-only survey)

1. EONW v2-v11 (`runtime/crates/eon-workspace-protocol/src/v2.rs`..`v11.rs`, ~4,800 lines) and
   their callers in Runtime `control.rs`/`generation.rs` and `eon/crates/eon/tests/workspace_control.rs`
   (~6,000 lines total). v12 re-exports v11 down to v2, so v12 must first become standalone.
2. Fixed-namespace "legacy" generation (`generation.rs` `inspect_legacy`, `control.rs`
   `send_legacy_inspect`, the `legacy` CLI target), which keeps `v4.rs` alive.
3. Old-Orbit differential check from the Bend swap (`flake.nix` input `old-orbit`,
   `nix/orbit-checks.nix`, `orbit/tests/real_pty/differential.rs`, `frame_after_vt`).
4. `eon claude-statusline` (remnant of retired EON-C26) and the retired `eonterm` name refusal.
5. Older-supervisor presentation fallback in `probe_presentable_runtime` (`control.rs:426-443`).
6. Pre-consolidation residue: Runtime source self-hash and provenance (`eon-runtime-residue-9475`),
   packaged notices (`eon-packaged-notices-wording-f6go`), "private pre-consolidation archive"
   preambles, ORBS version history table, ARCHITECTURE cutover acceptance.
7. `eon-alpha` naming: already `eon-igae.2`.

## Kept on purpose (recommended to Lucca; revisit only on his word)

- Retired contract stubs (EON-C22, EON-C26): the index rule keeps them so IDs are never reused.
- CHANGELOG.md and the component changelogs `orbit/CHANGELOG.md`, `venus/CHANGELOG.md`, which
  AGENTS.md assigns to wire/protocol changes.
- Dated benchmark records (`docs/benchmarks/`, `venus/docs/benchmarks/`): measurement evidence
  under AP-PERF-001, not compatibility code.
- "Pending re-proof" markers: they close through `eon-igae.7`/`.8`, not by deletion.

title: Make EONW v12 a standalone module with unchanged wire bytes
description:
## Why

Part of the legacy removal epic (Lucca, 2026-10-20). EONW v12 is built by re-export:
`runtime/crates/eon-workspace-protocol/src/v12.rs:7` does `pub use super::v11::*`, v11 re-exports
v10, and so on to v2; the shared Encoder, Decoder, `frame_version` and `identity` live in `v2.rs`,
and `v6::set_version`/`reframe` are reused. v2-v11 cannot be deleted until v12 stands alone.

## Scope

In: make v12 one standalone module (or v12 plus a small shared codec module) with byte-identical
wire output and decoding; move the shared codec pieces out of `v2.rs`; keep v2-v11 compiling
against the moved pieces for now. Out: deleting v2-v11 or their callers (next bead).
EONW is a wire format: this is a consequential shape (AGENTS.md); record in this bead the owner,
the decision and its check before code.

## Acceptance

Every v12 message encodes and decodes byte-identically before and after (golden bytes or a
round-trip corpus over every v12 message kind); Venus, Runtime and Eon build unchanged.

## Verification

`nix develop -c eon-test` (workspace suites), `cargo fmt --check` and clippy for touched crates;
converge review.
close_reason: done

comments.author: lucca
comments.text:
Reference gate (edge a80a6c6, before code).

Behavior and owner: EONW v12 wire bytes, decode results and errors stay unchanged; Eon Runtime's
`eon-workspace-protocol` crate stays the one owner. No consumer-visible v12 name changes.

Read: v2-v12 sources in full; consumers in Runtime (`control.rs` older-revision dispatch,
`workspace.rs`, `generation.rs`), Venus and Eon via v12 imports. No external comparable: this is an
internal flattening of an owned format.

Constraint found: Runtime `control.rs:294-379` passes a v12 `WorkspaceAction` into v3-v11 requests
and returns v2-v11 `LifecycleResponse`s as v12 values, and `eon/tests/workspace_control.rs` builds
v3-v11 failures from `v2::Failure`. Type identity across revisions is relied on.

Decision: v12.rs defines every v12 type, the framing and primitive codec (Encoder, Decoder, Error,
frame/unframe, identity checks) and flattened message codecs with no reference to v2-v11. The
dependency inverts for the interim: v2-v11 re-export the shared types and primitives from v12 and keep
their own message codecs, so `v2::Failure`, `v3::Action` etc. stay the same types as v12's. No
separate codec module: once v2-v11 go (eon-igae.12.4), v12.rs alone remains. Rejected: a v12 with
distinct types plus conversions in Runtime (adds code that the next bead must delete); a shared
`codec.rs` (a second module with one caller after .12.4).

Check: a temporary corpus test run before and after over the public v12 API (every request kind,
snapshots with columns/popups/quotas, failures, lifecycle results, plus truncations and single-byte
mutations of each encoding), diffing encoded bytes and decode results including errors; one
permanent golden-bytes test in v12.rs; then `nix develop -c eon-test`, fmt and clippy.

primitives, crate-private) from v12, keeping type identity; their own message codecs stay. Public
v12 names are unchanged. v12's two tests became: the malformed sideways-move test (ported) and a
new golden-bytes test over request, snapshot, failure and lifecycle forms. The v11-relative test
went: golden bytes cover it.

- Differential corpus (temporary integration test over the public v12 API, deleted before commit):

  after outputs identical (218,515 lines, 27,207,167 bytes, cmp equal). Two reviewers independently

title: Accept --json on eon window stop all
description:
## Why

Lucca, 2026-10-20, after `eon window stop all --json` failed with `invalid Eon window ID "all"`.
`eon stop all --json`, `eon stop previous --json` and `eon window stop ID --json` all exist, so the
`--json` form of `eon window stop all` is a reasonable expectation; today the parser
(`runtime/crates/eon-runtime/src/cli.rs:358-368`) only matches the three-word form and reads `all`
as a window ID. EON-C28 freezes the 1.0 command surface, so the gap should close before 1.0.

## Contract

EON-C23 (Independent Eon windows): add that `eon window stop all --json` returns one result array
per window without confirmation, matching `eon stop all --json` under EON-C11, with the caller's own
window still last. Changing EON-C23 needs Lucca's approval before code.

## Scope

In: the `window stop all --json` form in the CLI parser and `windows::stop_all_windows`
(`runtime/crates/eon-runtime/src/windows.rs:188`), its JSON output shape (follow `eon stop all
--json`), help text (`cli.rs:436`), `docs/USAGE.md` command table, EON-C23. Out: other window
commands; whether stopped windows should drop out of `eon windows` (observed 2026-10-20: a stopped
window still lists with only its unstarted current generation; report separately if it matters).

## Acceptance

`eon window stop all --json` stops every independent window's generations without prompting,
caller's window last, prints machine-readable results, and exits nonzero if any Stop fails; the
human form is unchanged; help, USAGE and EON-C23 list the form.

## Verification

A test next to `new_windows_keep_independent_supervisors_and_stop_by_window_id` through
`nix develop -c eon-test`; installed observation of the command after profile refresh; converge
review.
