title: Configure the Eon Bar widgets' order and visibility
description:
## Why

Lucca, 2026-10-21: for 1.0 the Eon Bar widgets need configuration, both their order and turning
each one on or off. Today the CPU, RAM and clock labels are always on with no configuration
(EON-C29, EON-C30), the version label has a single boolean (`[bar] show_version`, EON-C25), and
quota chips have no switch. Under EON-C28 (the 1.x stability promise) the configuration keys
and their names are frozen at 1.0, so the shape must land before 1.0 (rule (a) of `eon-igae`:
anything that would break users if it landed later).

## Design (proposed by eon-52 and accepted as recommended when Lucca said "create the beads",
2026-10-21; exact contract wording still needs Lucca's approval in each child)

```toml
[bar]
widgets = ["codex_quota", "claude_quota", "cpu", "ram", "clock", "version"]
```

- One ordered string list, the shape Nova uses for `bar.widgets`
  (`~/pjs/nova/nova-upstream-theme/crates/yzx-config/src/catalog.rs:54`, ordered string array,
  `ARCHITECTURE.md:158`), so Ratconfig's ordered string-list picker fits it.
- List order is the left-to-right order between the drag region and Shortcuts/Close.
- A name left out is off; `widgets = []` shows only tabs and controls.
- Omitting the key gives the default above, which is today's bar (`0d27a46`, `eon-igae.3`).
- An unknown or duplicate name is a startup configuration error through the existing
  invalid-configuration handling, which keeps live terminals.
- Applies when a window opens or reopens, like `show_version` today.
- Width pressure keeps a fixed hiding priority by kind (clock, RAM, CPU, version, then quota
  compaction) whatever the order: the list sets placement only, so narrow bars stay predictable.
- `show_version` is removed before 1.0, and a config that still sets it fails with an error
  that names `widgets`. Rejected: keeping both, because two settings for one fact would become a
  permanent 1.x promise.
- A quota chip turned off also stops Runtime polling that provider. Rejected: hiding the chip
  only, because Eon would keep calling CodexBar for data nobody sees.

Ownership: Eon owns the setting, its names and the default; Runtime parses and validates it
(`runtime/crates/eon-runtime/src/managed_environment.rs`) and passes it to Venus as a launch
input, the way `--eon-version` goes today (`runtime/crates/eon-runtime/src/supervisor.rs:407`);
Venus owns placement, fitting, hover and AccessKit.

## Children (in order)

1. Venus: an ordered bar-item launch input that sets placement and on/off.
2. Eon and Runtime: `[bar] widgets`, replacing `show_version`.
3. Runtime: stop polling a provider whose quota chip is off.

## Acceptance

- Every child is closed, and the contracts they change (a new EON-C ID for the setting,
  EON-C25, EON-C29, EON-C30, and the Venus launch-input contracts) are approved and proven.
- `docs/CONFIGURATION.md` describes `[bar] widgets` and no longer mentions `show_version`.

## Out of scope

New widgets (GPU `eon-gpu-widget-eon-bar-ri16`, IO `eon-io-widget-eon-bar-baie`, cursor color
`eon-rf4c`): they join the list later as new names, which is additive under EON-C28. Per-widget
options (formats, intervals), configurable hiding priority, a settings UI, and live reload
without reopening the window.
close_reason: All children closed: bar items, order and visibility configurable via [bar] widgets; polling follows shown chips. eon-igae.14.5 keeps its dot-notation ID but is reparented to eon-igae.

title: Place Eon Bar items from an ordered Venus launch input
description:
## Why

The parent epic's `[bar] widgets` setting needs Venus to place bar items in a given order and to
leave out the ones that are off. Today the order is fixed in Venus: quota chips, then CPU, RAM,
clock, then the version label at the edge (VEN-C25/C27/C28, commit `0d27a46`). The version label
is the only one with a switch: absence of `--eon-version`.

## Evidence

- `venus/src/scene.rs` `WorkspaceScene::from_snapshot_with_metadata`: the label array
  `[version, cpu, ram, clock]` fits in that priority order, then the code reorders it to
  `[cpu, ram, clock, version]` for placement. Quota chips are measured and compacted
  separately (`measure_quotas`, the `compact` loop).
- `venus/src/accessibility.rs`: AccessKit children follow the same fixed order (CPU, RAM, CLOCK,
  VERSION after the quota nodes).
- `venus/src/application.rs`: startup inputs such as `--eon-version` and `--pane-frames` are
  parsed before window creation. `venus/docs/LAUNCH.md` documents them.
- `venus/src/application.rs` wake loop: `READING_INTERVAL` drives `CpuTimes::read` and
  `RamUse::read` every 2 s while a workspace snapshot exists.

## Scope

In scope:
- One Venus workspace-only launch input naming the shown bar items in order, for example
  `--bar-items codex_quota,claude_quota,cpu,ram,clock,version`. The exact flag name and syntax
  are part of the contract wording for Lucca to approve.
- Its absence keeps today's default order, so standalone runs and existing launches don't change.
- Placement in the given order (quota chips may sit anywhere in it); items left out get no chip,
  hit target, hover or AccessKit node. Turning CPU or RAM off also skips its `/proc` read.
- A fixed hiding priority under width pressure, independent of order: clock, RAM, CPU, version,
  then quota compaction (current VEN-C28 rule).
- Contract changes: VEN-C25, VEN-C27 and VEN-C28 (placement follows the input), plus
  `venus/docs/LAUNCH.md`, and `venus/CHANGELOG.md`.

Out of scope:
- Eon or Runtime configuration (child 2), quota polling (child 3), EONW changes.
- New widgets, per-widget options, configurable hiding priority.
- Changing how quota chips compact.

## Acceptance

- With the input absent, the bar is pixel-identical in layout to `0d27a46`.
- With an input, items appear in that order, and absent items have no chip, hit target or
  AccessKit node. Hiding under width pressure still follows the fixed priority.
- Missing, duplicate, unknown or empty-element input fails before window creation, like the other
  startup inputs. Whether `--bar-items ''` (all off) is allowed is part of the wording: recommend
  allowing it, since the Eon setting accepts `widgets = []`.
- Contract wording approved by Lucca before commit.

## Implementation Notes

1. Parse the input next to `--eon-version`. Hold it as an ordered list of a small Venus enum,
   and pass it to the scene instead of growing more `Option` parameters.
2. In the scene, fit by fixed priority and then place in input order, reusing today's two-step
   fit-then-place shape.
3. Extend `readings_yield_after_the_clock_and_have_no_actions` and the version and clock tests
   rather than adding parallel ones. Add one test that reorders items, including a quota chip
   after a reading.

## Verification

- `nix develop -c eon-test -p yazelix-venus` passes, including the new ordering test. It should go
  red when the input order is ignored.
- `cargo fmt --check` and `cargo clippy --locked -p yazelix-venus --all-targets -- -D warnings`
  are clean (run inside `nix develop`).
- Portability disposition: neutral (no platform API).

## Stop Conditions

- Stop and ask Lucca if placing a quota chip between readings needs a change to quota
  compaction.
- Stop if the cited scene code has drifted materially since `0d27a46`.
- Stop before adding any EONW field.

## Maintenance Notes

- Item names are shared with Eon's `[bar] widgets` names (child 2). Keep one spelling and let
  Runtime pass the list through unchanged, with no translation table.

title: Replace [bar] show_version with an ordered [bar] widgets list
description:
## Why

The parent epic's design: one `[bar] widgets` ordered list sets the Eon Bar's order and which
items show, and replaces `[bar] show_version` before 1.0, so 1.x promises one setting.

## Evidence

- `runtime/crates/eon-runtime/src/managed_environment.rs:52-63`: `BarSettings { show_version }`
  with `deny_unknown_fields`, `show_version(root, defaults)`, and `Defaults::show_version`.
- `runtime/crates/eon-runtime/src/supervisor.rs:407-408`: passes `--eon-version` only when
  `show_version` holds, read per window launch. Tests at `supervisor.rs:1712-1746` and `:1968`.
- `eon/crates/eon/src/product.rs:14` and `runtime/crates/eon-runtime/src/fixtures.rs:16`: the
  `show_version: true` default.
- `eon/crates/eon/tests/workspace_control.rs:2140`: invalid `show_version` value case.
- `docs/CONFIGURATION.md:7-8,37-40`, `docs/CONTRACTS.md` EON-C25 (`show_version`), EON-C29 and
  EON-C30 ("always on, with no Eon configuration"), `runtime/README.md:25`,
  `venus/docs/LAUNCH.md:73`.

## Scope

In scope:
- `[bar] widgets`: an array of unique names from `codex_quota`, `claude_quota`, `cpu`, `ram`,
  `clock` and `version`. Eon owns the default, today's order, in `product.rs`. Runtime parses and
  validates it in `managed_environment.rs` when a window opens, and passes it to Venus through
  child 1's launch input. `--eon-version` is passed only when `version` is listed.
- Remove `show_version`. A config that still sets it fails with an error naming `[bar] widgets`.
  This is a breaking change before 1.0, so it gets a CHANGELOG line.
- New EON-C contract for the setting (next free ID), plus edits to EON-C25, EON-C29 and EON-C30.
  Also `docs/CONFIGURATION.md`, `runtime/README.md`, `venus/docs/LAUNCH.md` and `CHANGELOG.md`.

Out of scope:
- Stopping quota polling (child 3). In this bead a quota chip that is off is only left out of
  the launch input.
- New widget names, per-widget options, live reload without reopening the window, Ratconfig
  schema work (report it if Ratconfig needs a schema update to edit the list).

## Acceptance

- Omitting `widgets` gives today's bar. A reordered list reorders the installed bar on the next
  window open. `widgets = []` shows only tabs and controls.
- An unknown or duplicate name, a non-string, or a leftover `show_version` fails through the
  existing startup or replacement handling, and live terminals survive.
- Contract wording approved by Lucca before commit.

## Implementation Notes

1. Replace `BarSettings::show_version` and `Defaults::show_version` with the list. Keep
   `deny_unknown_fields`, but give `show_version` its own error instead of the generic
   unknown-field one.
2. Rework the supervisor tests at `supervisor.rs:1712-1746` and `:1968` for the list, keeping
   their invalid-input cases.
3. Update `workspace_control.rs:2140`'s case.

## Verification

- `nix develop -c eon-test` (the workspace and installer suites) passes. A focused red/green for
  the parser: unknown name, duplicate, `show_version` present.
- Installed (AGENTS.md "Installed runtime, UI, or product-configuration interaction"): profile
  refresh plus one isolated installed observation. A reordered list with `cpu` left out shows
  that order on window open, and a leftover `show_version` shows the error without killing live
  terminals.

## Stop Conditions

- Stop if child 1's launch input is not merged.
- Stop and ask Lucca if EON-C28's stability wording lists `show_version` by name, since removing
  it would then change the stability contract text.
- Stop if Ratconfig validation of Eon's config needs a schema file that this repository doesn't
  own.

## Maintenance Notes

- Runtime passes the names through to Venus unchanged. Don't add a second mapping.

title: Stop polling a provider whose quota chip is off
description:
## Why

The parent epic's decision is that a quota chip turned off in `[bar] widgets` also stops Runtime
polling that provider, so Eon doesn't call CodexBar, and through it the provider, for data nobody
sees.

## Evidence

- `runtime/crates/eon-runtime/src/supervisor.rs:783`: the workspace supervisor starts
  `quota::Quotas::start(&inputs.codexbar)` once, at supervisor start, for both providers.
- `runtime/crates/eon-runtime/src/quota.rs:189-223`: `Quotas::start` and `start_every` spawn one
  worker per provider (Codex every 60 units, Claude every 300 after a failure), and
  `Quotas::apply` fills the snapshot's `codex_quota` and `claude_quota`.
- `quota.rs` tests `workers_isolate_failure_and_bound_output_timeout_and_shutdown` and
  `claude_waits_300_units_after_a_failed_read_while_codex_reads_every_60`.
- `docs/CONFIGURATION.md` "Agent quota", and the EON quota contracts in `docs/CONTRACTS.md`.

## Scope

In scope:
- Start only the workers for providers whose chip `[bar] widgets` (child 2) lists, and leave a
  disabled provider's snapshot field empty.
- The timing rule: the setting is read when a window opens (child 2), but workers start with the
  supervisor. Recommended rule for Lucca to approve: re-evaluate on each window open, starting a
  newly enabled provider's worker and stopping a newly disabled one, so polling always matches
  what the bar shows. The alternative, which is simpler but stale until restart, is to read it
  once at supervisor start.
- Contract text in the quota contracts and `docs/CONFIGURATION.md` "Agent quota".

Out of scope:
- New providers, CodexBar changes, refresh intervals, how chips render.

## Acceptance

- With `claude_quota` left out, no Claude CodexBar process runs, and the snapshot carries no Claude
  quota. With both left out, no quota worker runs.
- Re-enabling takes effect under the approved timing rule, without restarting live terminals.
- Contract wording approved by Lucca before commit.

## Implementation Notes

1. Give `Quotas::start` the enabled set, and keep one worker per enabled provider.
2. Add a fake-CodexBar case that proves a disabled provider is never invoked. Extend the existing
   worker test rather than adding scaffolding.

## Verification

- `nix develop -c eon-test -p eon-runtime` passes, including a red/green check that a disabled
  provider is never spawned.
- Installed: one isolated observation with one provider off, showing no chip and no CodexBar
  process for it.

## Stop Conditions

- Stop if child 2 is not merged.
- Stop and ask Lucca for the timing rule before coding if it isn't recorded on this bead.
- Stop if stopping a worker mid-read can leave a CodexBar child unreaped (AP-FAILURE-001): report
  the shutdown path first.

## Maintenance Notes

- Runtime owns collection and freshness. Venus only renders what the snapshot carries, so this
  bead makes no Venus change.

title: Close the gap inside the CPU and RAM chips
description:
## Why

Lucca, 2026-10-21 (screenshot of the installed bar): the CPU and RAM chips show a visible gap,
`CPU  10%` and `RAM  34%`, and "we also have to fix this gap". VEN-C28 requires it today: each
label is "padded to the width of `CPU 100%` with the value right-aligned"
(`venus/src/system.rs:62,106`, `format!("CPU {:>4}", ...)`), so any value under 100% opens a hole
between the name and the value.

## Decision (Lucca, 2026-10-21, chosen as recommended)

One space between name and value (`CPU 10%`, `RAM 5%`), centered in a chip that keeps the width
of `CPU 100%`, so neighbouring items never shift as values change and the slack splits evenly on
both sides. Rejected: natural width (the clock and version shift one cell when CPU crosses 10% or
100%); trailing pad (lopsided chip).

## Scope

In scope: VEN-C28's label text and geometry sentence (contract change approved in substance
above; show the exact wording to Lucca before commit), the label text in `venus/src/system.rs`,
the scene/chrome geometry that sizes and places the CPU and RAM text in their chips, their tests
(`system.rs:130-187`, `accessibility.rs:1371-1373`), and `venus/CHANGELOG.md`.

Out of scope: hover and AccessKit descriptions (already single-spaced), quota chips, the clock,
the version label, width-fitting priority, item order (VEN-C29).

## Acceptance

- Installed bar shows `CPU 10%` and `RAM 34%` with one space, each centered in a chip as wide as
  `CPU 100%`; at 5% and 100% the chip width is unchanged and neighbours don't move.
- Width fitting still hides clock, RAM, CPU, version in that order.

## Verification

- `nix develop -c eon-test -p yazelix-venus`, `cargo fmt --check`, `cargo clippy --locked -p
  yazelix-venus --all-targets -- -D warnings`.
- One isolated installed observation of the bar (see the eon-igae.14.1 proof for the headless
  Sway recipe). Portability disposition: neutral.

## Stop Conditions

- Stop and ask Lucca if centering needs a half-cell offset that the chrome renderer can't place
  (monospace grid only); propose rounding the slack to the leading side instead.

title: Show icons in the Eon Bar's CPU, RAM and disk chips
description:
## Why

Lucca, 2026-10-21: use icons for the Eon Bar's CPU and RAM chips, and for the GPU chip too
("yeah / gpu too", on the eon-52 agent's recommendation). The quota chips already lead with a
provider logo, so the readings become the same family, and an icon is narrower than the
`CPU ` / `RAM ` text, so the readings survive narrower windows before width fitting hides them.
The clock gets no icon: `20:12` already says what it is (the eon-52 agent's recommendation,
not contested).

## Design (recommended, glyphs to confirm with Lucca from the capture below)

- Each reading chip shows an icon, a space and the value (`<icon> 12%`), with the icon drawn from
  Symbols Nerd Font Mono, which Eon already ships as the first `font_fallbacks` entry and which
  Venus's font tests already require. No new asset or dependency.
- The chip keeps a fixed width, that of `<icon> 100%`, with its text centered (the rule
  `eon-igae.14.4`, one-space centered reading labels, sets), so neighbours never shift.
- Hover and AccessKit text is unchanged ("CPU use 12%, all cores, over the last 2 seconds",
  "RAM use 43% of 31.3 GiB"), so no meaning is lost.
- Candidate glyphs: CPU `nf-oct-cpu` (U+F4BC) or `nf-md-cpu_64_bit` (U+F0EE0); RAM `nf-md-memory`
  (U+F035B); GPU `nf-md-expansion_card` (U+F02AE) or `nf-md-gpu`-style alternatives. The three
  must be told apart at bar size.

## First step (spike, before choosing implementation)

One isolated installed capture showing the candidate glyphs side by side at the default font
size and at the minimum (6 px) and at scale 1.25, so Lucca can pick. If CPU and RAM glyphs blur
together at bar size, stop and ask Lucca whether to keep the text labels.

## Scope

In scope: `venus/src/system.rs` labels, the scene width rule (`venus/src/scene.rs`, the
`"CPU 100%"` floor), centering in `venus/src/render/chrome.rs`, tests in `system.rs` and
`accessibility.rs`, `docs/USAGE.md`, `venus/docs/PRESENTATION.md#eon-bar`, `CHANGELOG.md`,
`venus/CHANGELOG.md`. Width-fitting checks must still pass with the new widths. Record the
chosen GPU glyph on `eon-gpu-widget-eon-bar-ri16` (GPU reading widget epic) so that chip uses it
from the start.

VEN-C28's label/width presentation was retired/demoted to a feature on 2026-10-30. Preserve the
same glyph, chip-width, centering and accessibility outcomes in this bead/current presentation
docs rather than changing the retired contract. Current configuration/CLI boundary contracts
are touched only if needed and after Lucca approves exact wording; this update supplies none.

Out of scope: a clock icon, the GPU chip itself (`eon-gpu-widget-eon-bar-ri16`, GPU reading
widget epic), quota logos, and item order (the presentation feature formerly indexed as
VEN-C29, with configuration owned by EON-C32).

The original chosen scope excluded configurable icons or a text/icon setting. That remains an
unresolved rule-6 gate: before implementation, either record a valid fixed-value reason allowed
by Configurability or obtain Lucca's choice about configuration and update scope accordingly.
This planning pass neither invents a fixed-glyph reason nor chooses a new setting or default.
If configuration is chosen, document its default in `docs/CONFIGURATION.md` in the same slice.

## Prerequisites

`eon-igae.14.4` (one-space centered reading labels) is committed first; this bead reuses its
fixed-width centering. Resolve the glyph choice and the configuration gate above before
implementing the final change.

## Acceptance

- Installed bar shows `<cpu icon> 12%`, `<ram icon> 43%` and the disk chip with its icon,
  centered in fixed-width chips; values from 0% to 100% never move a neighbouring chip. The clock
  and version now live in the hints bar (787feb8, 987a0f6), not in the Eon Bar.

title: Publish the signed Nix-free Linux install with the beta release
description:
## Why

Lucca, 2026-11-06: "i think nix free is important before public announcement / beta".
eon-igae.15 gates v0.2.0. He chose GitHub release assets on Yazelix/eon, SHA-256 checksums
plus GitHub attestations, and the Nix-free install as README's first install line.

## Contract and settled decisions

EON-C5 (direct bundle lifecycle), EON-C6 (shared graph) and EON-C7 (x86_64 Linux native
Wayland), docs/CONTRACTS.md. The two approved channels are already in docs/AGENT-RULES.md.

Lucca, 2026-11-06, "agreed" on eon-igae.15.1: retain independently trusted OpenSSH-signed
SHA256SUMS.sig, with Lucca holding the signing key, and add attestations. The installer verifies
offline; the attestation is additional evidence and EON-C5's trust anchor is unchanged.

## Historical GO evidence and limits

Read eon-qualify-nix-free-linux-public-beta-lm9p's comments and close reason. Its archive
eon-0.1.1-x86_64-linux.tar.zst, SHA-256
6379a43cfd779582534c97c564712a30057e906942e5251a710056c6b31e4a9b, came from edge 2e4a914
(new Orbit, ax8y fix). It is superseded for publication: v0.2.0 comes from the tagged revision.
Changed payloads need lm9p.3's Venus window/terminal checks and lm9p.4's Orbit steps when Orbit
changed. Both changed since that GO; .15.3 and eon-igae.7.3 carry the candidate evidence.

Historical limits to reassess and state accurately for the shipped asset: QEMU virtio-gpu and
lavapipe only (no physical GPU or NVIDIA); bundle desktop only Sway (no GNOME/KDE/COSMIC);
Ubuntu 26.04.1 and Fedora 44, x86_64 only; Orca and agent providers not exercised; no eonbase
in the archive; interrupted installs can leave .eon-stage-*; restarting ends live terminals;
the old installer reported the wrong error for an unmarked 0700 prefix. These are retained
GO observations, not fresh claims about the candidate. Host prerequisites and glibc floor:
docs/MANUAL-BUNDLE.md#execution-and-host-boundary and docs/INSTALLER.md.

## Children and order

- .15.1 (release route) and .15.2 (README/distribution docs) are closed.
- .15.7 supplies corresponding source from .15.6's landed inventory/table; .15.8 hardens
  audited-crate coverage without reopening recorded license decisions.
- .15.6 retains final notice/source publication acceptance, including the source mechanism's
  draft-release exercise and release checks for the approved grant-or-no-Accelerando variant.
- .15.4 is Lucca's own immutable-releases setting, before publishing the candidate pre-release.
- .15.3 proves the candidate's own pre-release on the fresh Fedora host, rather than a separate
  rehearsal tag (overseer decision 2026-11-10). Release actions remain with Lucca/the overseer
  under Lucca's explicit authority.
- .15.5 proves EON-C41 on that same host after .15.3, subject to its two-published-release
  prerequisite and recorded fallback. Prereleases are not updater targets.

The source/notice implementation must not wait for this whole publication epic to close.
Its output feeds the host proof. This epic closes only when its remaining children meet
acceptance or Lucca explicitly narrows the gate.

## Acceptance and scope boundary

- The route builds and verifies v0.2.0's Nix-free assets from the accepted revision.
- README/distribution docs describe the install and actual limits truthfully.
- The fresh host installs the exact downloaded candidate after trusted signature, checksum
  and attestation verification, then runs Eon. Notice/source and update ownership acceptance
  are resolved under their children.

In: Linux x86_64 assets, notices/source, signatures, attestations, docs and proof.
Out: the v0.2.0 tag/publish decision (eon-igae.9, Lucca), other architectures/macOS bundles,
auto-update, package formats and eonterm.com install pages (eon-h8rze).

title: Build and attach the Nix-free bundle, checksums and attestations to a GitHub release
description:
## Why

The beta (eon-igae) ships the Nix-free install as GitHub release assets on Yazelix/eon, with
SHA-256 checksums and GitHub artifact attestations (Lucca, 2026-11-06). No route builds and
attaches them today. Read the parent epic first.

## Contract

EON-C5 (direct bundle lifecycle) and EON-C6 (shared graph across channels), docs/CONTRACTS.md.
AP-CI-001 (bounded CI, docs/AGENT-PROTOCOLS.md) if the route is a hosted workflow.

## Reference gate

Consequential: a release tool and a trust boundary. Before code, record in this bead per
docs/AGENT-RULES.md "Contract-Driven Method" and the routes in
docs/DISTRIBUTION.md#reference-routing: sources and revisions read, options compared, decision,
version policy and exit condition. Compare at least one comparable signed release workflow.

Decide first, with Lucca's approval of the EON-C5 text: how `eon-install` trusts a download.
Today it needs `SHA256SUMS` plus an OpenSSH `SHA256SUMS.sig` from an independently trusted
signer (docs/INSTALLER.md). Lucca chose checksums plus attestations. State whether the installer
keeps a signer, checks the attestation, or relies on the user running `gh attestation verify`.

## Scope

In: a workflow or script that builds the bundle and installer from the tagged revision
(`nix build .#manual-bundle` and the installer), writes SHA256SUMS, creates GitHub artifact
attestations, and attaches all of them to a GitHub release. If hosted, name the contract and why
local proof is not enough; bound triggers (tag or manual dispatch only), jobs, timeouts,
permissions (`contents: write`, `id-token: write`, `attestations: write` only where needed),
secrets, fork behavior, cache and concurrency; record when to expand or remove it.
Any EON-C5 text change and docs/INSTALLER.md trust steps that follow from the decision.
Out: README and install docs (sibling b); the fresh-host proof (sibling c); tagging v0.2.0.

## Acceptance

- On a rehearsal pre-release or draft release (not v0.2.0), the route attaches the archive,
  installer, SHA256SUMS and attestations built from one exact revision.
- `sha256sum -c SHA256SUMS` passes on the downloads, and `gh attestation verify <asset> -R
  Yazelix/eon` passes for each asset.
- Cheapest falsifier: change one byte of a downloaded asset; both checks must fail.
- The archive's `eon versions` matches the Nix product of the same revision (EON-C6).

## Verification

The rehearsal release run, its URL and asset digests recorded here. Codex reviews the workflow
or script.

title: Prove the published Nix-free install from its GitHub release on a fresh Fedora host
description:
## Why and contract

The beta publishes the Nix-free install. AP-DELIVERY-001 requires delivery proof of what ships;
lm9p's GO archive 6379a43c is not that asset. Read eon-igae.15 and lm9p's 2026-10-21 harness
comment. Contracts: EON-C5 and EON-C6, docs/CONTRACTS.md.

## Prerequisites

eon-igae.15.1 is closed. .15.6's notice/source gate is closed and Lucca has enabled immutable
releases (.15.4). The overseer/Lucca have authorized and published the candidate's own
pre-release with its exact archive, installer, SHA256SUMS, OpenSSH SHA256SUMS.sig and
attestations. The 2026-11-10 decision below selects this candidate pre-release, rather than
a separate rehearsal tag. No agent publishes it here.

## Scope

On a fresh Fedora host without Nix (lm9p.3's Fedora 44 cloud-image harness is acceptable),
download those release assets. Verify the OpenSSH signature with the independently provisioned
release key, then sha256sum and gh attestation verify. Install with eon-install, launch Eon,
open a Venus window and run lm9p.3's terminal checks (NoNewPrivs, id, sudo -n true). Add
lm9p.4's Orbit steps when Orbit changed since 2e4a914. Record the exact artifact, environment,
commands and results; preserve this VM for .15.5 immediately afterwards.

Out: Ubuntu reruns; unrelated failure-path reruns (lm9p.1) when the installer and relevant
boundaries are unchanged; desktop qualification (eon-igae.8). Changed installer or lifecycle
boundaries require their affected checks rather than relying on the old exclusion.

## Acceptance

- The downloaded candidate installs only after signature, checksum and attestation checks
  pass, and Eon runs. An adjacent downloaded key cannot establish the trust anchor.
- Record the published candidate's immutable flag and exact release/asset digests.
- env -i eon versions from this install matches the same-revision Nix product.
- A tampered asset is rejected before installation; record the verification failure.
- Supply exact evidence to eon-igae.7.3 for its EON-C5/C6 assessment.

## Verification and stop conditions

Use an isolated VM with transcripts and digests here. If final v0.2.0 assets differ,
eon-igae.9 records which affected checks repeat; evidence never silently transfers to changed
bytes. Stop before paid-host allocation, publish, tag, upload or signing without the required
overseer/Lucca authority. The published-release pair needed for .15.5 is its separate explicit
precondition; this pre-release proof cannot make it eligible for the updater.

description:
## Why

Parent: eon-igae.15 (publish the signed Nix-free Linux install with the beta). EON-C41
(installation update ownership and provenance) ships in v0.2.0: the update button and
`eon update --check` and `--install` all landed (eon-update-button-f10d1.1 to .7). Its record
still reads Planned and says "Prefix and native macOS Install/HTTPS proof remain open", and no
re-proof bead owned it. Lucca, 2026-11-10 (relayed by eon-overseer): yes to one small re-proof
child, run with the fresh-host install proof (eon-igae.15.3).

## Contract

EON-C41 (docs/CONTRACTS.md, heading "EON-C41"). No text change beyond its Status and Proof
record; show the changed lines in the READY note for the overseer's approval.

## Scope

In: on the same fresh Fedora host and published release that eon-igae.15.3 uses, prove the
managed-prefix path over real HTTPS: `eon update --check [--json] --prefix PREFIX` names the
installed and the available release and their provenance, and `eon update --install` moves the
prefix to the newer signed release and leaves a running window's terminals alone.

  terminals unchanged.

Installed-observation route on the fresh host; evidence as files, no VNC. No build.

- Stop if the proof needs a code change; file it and report.

title: Ship an Eon variant without Helix for people who use another editor
description:
## Why and approved decisions

Lucca, 2026-11-10: "also, before the gate, we need a version without helix, for users that use
other editors"; and "it will build much faster". This is a v0.2.0 gate item and an epic of
session-sized implementation and measurement slices.

The overseer's decisions on plan.md section 9 (2026-11-10, Lucca: "we are in auto-decision
mode") stay verbatim in the comment below. Accepted: one Rust build, two compositions;
v0.2.0's no-helix variant is Nix-only. The archive and direct updater follow the release
(eon-no-helix-archive-033na and eon-no-helix-direct-update-elg9r, related follow-ups).

- Name: `#no-helix`, package `eon-no-helix-VERSION`.
- Without Helix, unset [editor] command resolves $VISUAL, then $EDITOR, else clearly refuses;
  no vi/nano fallback. Full-product behavior stays under its existing contract.
- Manifest unchanged; no substitute component. Artifacts and `eon versions` state the omission.
- Offered through Nix on macOS; v0.2.0 claims proof on Linux only.
- Approved contract text: EON-C6, C9, C10, C28, C41, with review in the owning slice.

## Children and current evidence

eon-igae.17.1-.17.5 are closed: runtime/editor behavior; one Rust build and composition;
no-helix package, closure, receipt/cache route and installed Linux proof; Nix update retains
the variant; the closure check gates the package itself. Their landing records own the proof
and limitations; do not reopen them to repeat unchanged checks.

eon-igae.17.6 retains Lucca's requested cold/warm build-time comparison (with/without Helix
and grammars) and recommendation about agent proofs and landing routes. The .17.3 landing
records 276.15 MiB less NAR closure on its measured tree; this alone proves no time saving.

## Acceptance and boundary

- The five implementation children remain accepted with their named artifacts and proof of
  Linux install, editor/refusal behavior, omission/closure, receipt and Nix variant retention.
- The measurement child records cold/warm timing, cache limits and which existing checks can
  use the variant when Helix is not under test. It cannot weaken required full-product,
  artifact-specific or release proof.
- Docs describe Nix-only availability and accepted editor resolution; existing final-candidate
  proof carries the relevant contract amendments.

Out: no-helix Nix-free delivery/updater, a manifest change, default-editor redesign and native
macOS proof of this variant. No unmeasured speed claim or additional channel is approved here.

title: Run Eon without a packaged Helix: editor from VISUAL or EDITOR, no hx names, no Helix in eon versions
description:
Plan: /home/lucca/.cache/eon-agents/eon-no-helix-plan-work/bead/plan.md (sections 4.3, 4.4, 5).
Lucca's approval of the plan's questions is quoted on eon-igae.17.

## Why

The no-Helix variant (eon-igae.17) is the same `eon` executable composed without Helix. The
runtime must behave correctly when the composition supplies no Helix. This bead is Rust only;
no package exists yet, so nothing user-visible ships until eon-igae.17.3.

## Contract

EON-C9, EON-C10 (Configuration clause) and EON-C28, with the text in plan section 5. EON-C10's
`edit-command` code and exit status do not change, so EONW stays v38; check that first and
stop if a result shape would cross the wire.

## Scope

- The composition supplies Helix through `EON_HX` (`eon/crates/eon/src/product.rs:193`). Make
  its absence mean "this build has no Helix" instead of falling back to a bare `hx`:
  `ManagedPrograms.helix` becomes optional (`runtime/crates/eon-runtime/src/managed_environment.rs:886`).
- Without Helix: the names `hx` and `eon-hx` refuse with one line and exit 1 (never exec
  `hx` from PATH: with the links present that would loop); `eon versions` prints no Helix
  line; `eon config defaults` shows `[editor] command` as unset with the rule below.
- `[editor] command` without Helix has no default. When unset, each edit resolves `$VISUAL`,
  then `$EDITOR`, from the supervisor's environment, split on ASCII whitespace. Nothing
  resolved: `edit-command` (and `popup-command` for Scrollback) with a message that names
  `[editor] command`. With Helix the default stays `["hx"]`.
- Tests: the harness supplies the Helix launch input where a test means the full product
  (`workspace_control.rs:8154` asserts the `hx` default). New tests: unset command with
  `VISUAL`, with only `EDITOR`, with an `EDITOR` that has arguments, with neither; `hx` name
  refused; `eon versions` without the Helix line.
- Docs: `docs/CONFIGURATION.md` `[editor]` (the default per package), `docs/USAGE.md:589,767`.
  No CHANGELOG entry: the behavior is unreachable until the package exists (eon-igae.17.3
  writes it).

## Acceptance

- With `EON_HX` supplied, every existing test passes unchanged in meaning.
- Without it, the cases above pass, and no code path execs a bare `hx`.
- Whole-workspace `nix develop -c eon-test`, fmt and clippy for the changed crates.

## Out of scope

Nix packaging, the updater, the Editor popup (eon-xodrj.4, .5), exporting `EDITOR` into
terminals, and any change to the full product's default.

## Prerequisite

eon-xodrj.3 (Helix without Steel): it edits the same `Tool::Helix` code and tests.

## Decisions

Recorded on eon-igae.17 (2026-11-10, auto-decision mode): `$VISUAL`, then `$EDITOR`, else a
clear refusal, with no `vi` or `nano` fallback; contract text approved.
close_reason: Landed on edge with merged-tree proof (fmt, clippy, crate and whole-workspace eon-test, nix build .#default): every acceptance item met on x86_64 Linux.

# Plan: run Eon without a packaged Helix (eon-igae.17.1)

Planned 2026-11-10 by the eon-no-helix-a-plan agent (Fable 5.2) at edge `624bfff` (Eon 0.1.22,
EONW v38), read against the staged tree of eon-xodrj.3 (Helix without Steel) in
`/home/lucca/.cache/eon-agents/eon-helix-no-steel` (`git diff --cached 1d9350d`). Read only: no
code edit, build, test run or `br` write. Line numbers are at `624bfff`; eon-xodrj.3 removes
10 lines from the `Tool::Helix` arm of `managed_environment.rs` and 20 from its tests, so later
lines in that file shift up. Functions are named so the lines are only a guide.

## 1. Summary

- One read of `EON_HX` in `eon/crates/eon/src/product.rs` decides three inputs: the managed
  Helix program, the default `[editor] command`, and the component lines `eon versions` prints.
  Unset or empty means "this build has no Helix".
- The runtime change is small: two `Inputs` fields become optional, one is added, the editor
  resolver gains the `$VISUAL`, `$EDITOR` step, and `hx`/`eon-hx` refuse.
- EONW stays v38 (checked, section 3).
- The code contradicts the parent plan in five places (section 2). The first changes how
  "no Helix in `eon versions`" must be built, so read it before the rest.
- Seven small choices for the overseer are numbered in section 9, each with a recommendation.
  None blocks.

## 2. Where the code contradicts the parent plan or the bead

1. **The component report is also the supervisor's identity.** The parent plan (2, 4.1) treats
   `eon versions` as a printout of the manifest. In the code, `Inputs.component_report`
   (`product.rs:12`) is printed by `versions()` (`cli.rs:856`) and is also compared by every
   launch and attach: `validate_runtime` (`supervisor.rs:374-390`, "supervisor reports a
   different component graph"), `inspect_generation` (`generation.rs:903`, "other build") and
   the generations table (`generation.rs:1254`). Generation identity is the source digest alone
   (`generation.rs:41-44`), so both variants of one Rust build share a generation directory.
   Dropping the Helix line from `component_report` itself would therefore make a `no-helix`
   `eon` refuse a full-product window of the same build, and the other way round.
   It would also break `eonbase`: it is the same executable, its wrapper sets no `EON_HX`
   (`flake.nix:1185-1189`), and `EON_HX` leaks into every Eon terminal (item 2), so an `eonbase`
   started from the desktop and one started in an Eon terminal would report different graphs
   and refuse each other.
   **Plan:** keep `component_report` as the build's whole graph (as `eonbase` already reports
   tools it does not compose) and give `versions()` a second, Eon-supplied string without the
   Helix line. This matches the approved EON-C6 text ("changes no other identity … states the
   omission … in `eon versions`").
2. **`EON_HX` is inherited by terminals.** The parent plan (4.3) says the runtime learns that
   Helix is absent the way `eonbase` learns from an absent `EON_SESSION_BIN`. Observed in this
   session's own Eon terminal: `EON_HX`, `EON_NU`, `EON_SESSION_BIN` and the other wrapper
   variables are all set in the shell. That is why the `eonbase` wrapper has
   `--unset EON_SESSION_BIN` and the test harness has `.env_remove("EON_SESSION_BIN")`
   (`workspace_control.rs:5025`). Consequences: the harness must set or remove `EON_HX`
   explicitly (section 6), and the `no-helix` wrapper in eon-igae.17.3 must `--unset EON_HX`,
   or a `no-helix` `eon` run inside a full-product terminal believes it has Helix (section 9,
   item 6).
3. **The default editor does not go through `ManagedPrograms.helix`.** The bead says to make
   `ManagedPrograms.helix` optional. That alone changes nothing for `eon edit`: the default is
   the static `Defaults.editor = &["hx"]` (`product.rs:175`), a bare name found on the terminal
   PATH (`popup_executable`, `managed_environment.rs:1496`). `EON_HX` is used only when the
   multi-call name `hx` or `eon-hx` runs (`command()`, `managed_environment.rs:1788`). So
   `Defaults.editor` must become optional too. The test at `workspace_control.rs:8154` passes
   today with no `EON_HX` at all, only a stub `hx` on PATH.
4. **A second test means "full product".**
   `config_defaults_ignore_user_configuration_and_have_documented_values`
   (`workspace_control.rs:199-262`) requires `eon config defaults` to equal the defaults block in
   `docs/CONFIGURATION.md`, which shows `command = ["hx"]`. The bead names only the test at
   line 8154.
5. **The supervisor validates `[editor]` at start.** `supervisor.rs:1009-1012` calls
   `editor_command` so a malformed `[editor]` fails the start. Without Helix and with no
   `$VISUAL` or `$EDITOR` that call would fail every window start. The check must cover only
   the configured value.

Smaller drift: `docs/USAGE.md:589,767` in the bead are lines 609 and 789 at `624bfff`. The
parent plan's "`hx` execs itself forever" (section 8, marked inferred) is confirmed by reading:
`configured_program("EON_HX", "hx")` makes `Command::new("hx")`, which finds the `hx` link on the
terminal PATH again. Not checked: the parent plan's "Files shows the message until Enter" (4.4).

## 3. Wire check (the bead's first step)

Nothing crosses EONW differently:

- The editor's argv "is runtime policy and does not cross EONW" (EON-C10). `Action::Edit`
  carries only the file (`workspace.rs:1586`).
- `edit-command` and `popup-command` are existing failure codes with free-text detail
  (`workspace.rs:1592`, `:2028`); only the detail text gains a new value.
- `Runtime.component_report` keeps its content (section 2, item 1).

No codec file under `runtime/crates/eon-workspace-protocol` changes. If the overseer picks
option (a) in section 9 item 1 instead, the report's content changes but its shape does not;
EONW still stays v38.

## 4. Contract (smallest observable statement)

- **Consumer:** a person or agent using an Eon composed without Helix.
- **Trigger:** `eon edit`, Enter in Files, the Scrollback popup, `eon pane history --edit`; the
  names `hx` and `eon-hx`; `eon versions`; `eon config defaults`.
- **Result:** with `[editor] command` unset, each edit runs `$VISUAL`, else `$EDITOR`, from the
  supervisor's environment, split on ASCII whitespace, with the file appended.
  `eon versions` has no Helix line. `eon config defaults` shows `command` as unset.
- **Failures:** nothing resolved gives `edit-command` (`popup-command` for Scrollback), exit 1,
  nothing changed, with a message naming `[editor] command`. `hx` and `eon-hx` print one line
  and exit 1. There is no `vi` or `nano` fallback.
- **Unchanged:** every behavior of a build that is given `EON_HX`.

## 5. Changes, file by file

### 5.1 `eon/crates/eon-manifest/src/lib.rs`

- `version_report(input)` (`:137`) becomes `version_report(input, omitted: &[&str])`, and

  ID to be in `manifest.composition.tools` (error: "an omitted component is not a composed
  tool"), then skip those components' lines. Eon's manifest crate stays the only reader of the
  graph; Runtime parses nothing (`runtime/AGENTS.md`).
- Test: extend `version_report_contains_identity_without_resolved_paths` (`:531`): the report
  with `["helix"]` is the full report minus exactly the `helix` line, and `["orbit"]` (a
  service) and `["nope"]` fail. It detects a wrong or silently ignored omission.

- `component_report` (`:12`): `eon_manifest::version_report(MANIFEST, &[])`, unchanged content.

- No new unit test here: `inputs()` reads the process environment, and the integration tests

### 5.3 `runtime/crates/eon-runtime/src/cli.rs`

- `Inputs` (`:48-61`): add `pub composed_components: Result<String, String>` with a doc
  comment ("the components this composition includes, which `eon versions` prints:
  `component_report` without the tools the package leaves out") and an accessor beside
  `component_report()` (`:65`).
- `versions()` (`:856-864`): print the new field in place of `component_report()`.
  `report.rs:55` reuses `versions()` and needs no change.
- `launch_managed` (`:585-624`): before `configuration_directory()` and
  `prepare_configuration`, resolve the program through the helper in 5.4, so a refused `hx`

### 5.4 `runtime/crates/eon-runtime/src/managed_environment.rs`

- `Defaults.editor` (`:163-164`): `Option<&'static [&'static str]>`; doc comment: "The editor's
  argv, before the file, while `[editor] command` is unset; none in a build without Helix,
  where an unset command resolves from the environment".
- `ManagedPrograms.helix` (`:886`): `Option<PathBuf>`.
- New `pub(crate) fn program(tool, programs) -> Result<&Path, String>` holding the `match` now
  at `:1785-1792`. `Tool::Helix` with no program returns
  `this Eon package includes no Helix, so it provides no hx or eon-hx`. `command()` (`:1767`)
  and `launch_managed` both call it; `command()` never builds a `Command` for a bare `hx`.
  `tool()` (`:907`) still maps `hx` and `eon-hx` to `Tool::Helix`, so those names refuse
  instead of running as `eon` with stray arguments. `main.rs` prints `eon: <message>`, exit 1.
- Split `editor_command` (`:929-950`):
  - `pub(crate) fn editor_setting(root, defaults, log) -> Result<Option<Vec<String>>, String>`:
    the configured argv, else `defaults.editor`, validated with `validate_argv`; `None` when
    both are absent. The `Named` error stays.
  - `fn environment_editor(visual: Option<OsString>, editor: Option<OsString>) ->
    Option<(&'static str, Vec<OsString>)>`: pure. The first of `$VISUAL`, `$EDITOR` that holds
    a word, split on ASCII whitespace by bytes (so a non-UTF-8 path survives), with its
    variable's name for messages. A blank value falls through to the next.
  - `editor_command`: `editor_setting`, else `environment_editor(env::var_os("VISUAL"),
    env::var_os("EDITOR"))` with the argv bounds applied under the variable's name, else

    It runs in the supervisor (the closures at `supervisor.rs:1252`, `:3245`, `:3408`), so the

  - `validate_argv` (`:1282`) becomes generic over `AsRef<OsStr>` so the same bounds (128
    arguments, 64 KiB, no NUL) cover the environment's argv.
- `prepare_popup_command` (`:1468`): only the comment changes ("an unavailable or unresolved
  editor fails the edit; nothing falls back to Helix"). The existing availability check on
  `argv[0]` then covers a `$EDITOR` that is not on the terminal PATH.
- `print_defaults` (`:744`): `defaults.editor` now serializes as null when absent. In the JSON
  branch (`:748-757`) drop null values from `editor` as is done for `terminal`. In
  `defaults_table` (`:831`) add an arm for a null editor command: "Direct argv that `eon edit`
  and Files run with the file appended. Unset, each edit runs $VISUAL, then $EDITOR." The
  full product's line stays byte-identical (the docs test pins it).

### 5.5 `runtime/crates/eon-runtime/src/supervisor.rs`

- `:1009-1012`: call `editor_setting` instead of `editor_command`, and reword the comment: a
  malformed `[editor]` still fails the start; an unresolved editor fails only the edit.

### 5.6 `runtime/crates/eon-runtime/src/fixtures.rs`

- `:13` add `composed_components: Ok("fixture-components".into())`; `:135`
  `editor: Some(&["fixture-editor"])`; `:145` `helix: Some("fixture-editor".into())`.

### 5.7 Not changed, and why

- Files and its Yazi opener (`flake.nix`, `Tool::Files`): the opener runs `eon edit`; it has no
  Helix code.
- The Editor popup (eon-xodrj.4, .5): not landed and out of scope. The Scrollback popup is the

  Helix.

## 6. Tests

### 6.1 Runtime unit tests (`managed_environment.rs`)

Mechanical updates: `Some(…)` for `helix` in the three `ManagedPrograms` literals (`:4020`,
`:4132`, and the fixture), and `resolved_config` (`:2529`) builds `editor` from
`editor_setting`. eon-xodrj.3 already removes the Steel assertions and the UTF-8 test.

New or extended, each with the failure it detects:

| Test | Detects |
| --- | --- |
| `environment_editor` cases in one test: `VISUAL` and `EDITOR` both set (VISUAL wins), only `EDITOR`, `EDITOR="my-editor  --wait\t-x"` (three words), blank `VISUAL` with `EDITOR` set, neither, and an `EDITOR` holding non-UTF-8 bytes (`/opt/\xffed --wait` gives those exact bytes and `--wait`) | Wrong order, a shell-style or single-space split, a blank value stopping the search, a lossy conversion of the path |
| In `managed_commands_use_exact_programs_and_private_configuration`: with `helix: None`, `Tool::Helix` is an error naming Helix and `Tool::Yazi` still builds | A fallback to a bare `hx`, which would loop through the `hx` link |
| In the defaults round-trip test (`:2449-2488`): one arm sets `defaults.editor = None`; the TOML has `# command: unset.` with the `$VISUAL` rule, the JSON has no `editor.command`, and the printed TOML loads to the same policy. `policy` compares `editor_setting`, which reads no environment | `eon config defaults` printing `command = null`, or printed defaults that do not reload (EON-C9) |

`editor_command`'s use of the process environment is not unit-tested: a unit test must not
set process variables. The integration tests below prove it with a real supervisor.

### 6.2 Integration tests (`eon/crates/eon/tests/workspace_control.rs`)

Harness: `eon_command` (`:5005`) gains `.env("EON_HX", <an absolute path nothing runs>)`,
`.env_remove("VISUAL")` and `.env_remove("EDITOR")`. Every one of its 129 callers then means
the full product whatever the developer's shell holds, which keeps the two tests of section 2
(items 3 and 4) and every other test unchanged in meaning. Tests that bypass it
(`env_clear()` at `:927`, `:1116`, `:1185`; bare `versions` at `:4021`, `:17421`) read only the
`eon VERSION g1-…` line, which does not change.

New tests, each removing `EON_HX` on the supervisor and on every CLI call:

1. **Names, versions and defaults without Helix** (no supervisor).
   The harness default's `eon versions` has exactly one line starting `helix `. Without
   `EON_HX` it has none, and equals the default's output minus that one line, so the first line
   (`eon VERSION g1-…`) is the same generation in both. `eon config defaults` has the unset comment under `[editor]`, and `--json` has
   no `editor.command`. Symlinks named `hx` and `eon-hx` to the test executable each exit 1
   with empty stdout and one `eon: …no Helix…` line on stderr, and the `EON_CONFIG_HOME` they
   were given is not created.
2. **`$VISUAL` first, with arguments, and what overrides it.** Supervisor started with
   `VISUAL="vis-editor --flag"` and `EDITOR=other-editor`; only `other-editor` is on its PATH
   at first. In order:
   - `eon edit --json -- notes.txt` exits 1 with `edit-command` naming `vis-editor` as
     unavailable, and changes nothing: an unavailable `$VISUAL` refuses and does not fall
     through to a valid `$EDITOR`. This reaches the availability check in
     `prepare_popup_command` (`managed_environment.rs:1487`).
   - The `vis-editor` stub is created; the next edit succeeds and the pane's Orbit argv ends
     `vis-editor\0--flag\0<file>\0` (the assertion style of `:8346-8353`).
   - `[editor] command = ["my-editor", "--wait"]` is written; the next edit's argv ends
     `my-editor\0--wait\0<file>\0`: the configured argv wins over a populated `$VISUAL` and
     `$EDITOR`.
   - **Cross-composition, full client on a window without Helix:** a client with the harness
     default (`EON_HX` set) reports the same generation in `eon versions`, lists the window in
     `eon window ls --json` as attachable with the same `component_report` the other client
     sees (never "other build"), and presents it (a bare `eon`, or `eon window attach`, as the
     existing attach tests do), exit 0. The presentation is what reaches `validate_runtime`
     (`supervisor.rs:374`).
3. **Only `$EDITOR`, with arguments.** Supervisor with `EDITOR="my-editor --wait"` and no
   `VISUAL`: argv ends `my-editor\0--wait\0<file>\0`.
4. **Neither.** `eon edit --json` exits 1 with `edit-command`, the detail names
   `[editor] command`, and the workspace snapshot is unchanged. Then `[editor] command =
   ["my-editor"]` is written and the next `eon edit` succeeds without a restart, which proves
   the message's advice.

5. **Cross-composition, client without Helix on a full-product window.** In the existing
   test at `:8154` (its supervisor has the harness default), one client with `EON_HX` removed
   gets the same checks as the last step of test 2: same generation, attachable in
   `eon window ls --json` with an unchanged `component_report` that still holds the Helix
   line, and a presentation that exits 0. Together with test 2 this fails if the Helix line
   is ever dropped from `component_report` itself, which tests that remove `EON_HX` on both
   sides cannot see.

Cases 2 to 4 need three short-lived supervisors because the environment is fixed at start;
share one helper for the setup. Test 5 adds calls to a supervisor that already exists. No separate Scrollback test: Scrollback builds its command
through the same `prepare_popup_command(PopupCommand::Edit)`, and its `popup-command` mapping
for a failed command is already covered at `:15338`.

Contract text is the approved text of the parent plan's section 5; it gets a Codex review at

- **EON-C9** (`docs/CONTRACTS.md`): after "Eon selects exact Nushell, Bash, … LazyGit

## 8. Proof route

- **Route:** Verification's "one owned parser or logic" and "one owned default" rows plus the
  contract text: focused red/green checks, then the whole workspace once. No wire, manifest
  file, dependency or lifecycle change.
- **Iterate** (no slot, `nice -n 19`, `CARGO_BUILD_JOBS=6`): `cargo fmt --check`; clippy with

  `managed-command-path` check runs the real `hx` and so proves the full product's Helix

- **No installed observation in this bead:** the installed full product behaves as before, and
  no package without Helix exists. The claim is narrowed to the source tier; eon-igae.17.3
  proves the installed `no-helix` package (`eon versions`, `hx` absent, `eon edit` with

## 9. Choices for the overseer

1. **How `eon versions` drops Helix.** (b) a second Eon-supplied string for `versions()`,
   identity unchanged; or (a) drop the line from `component_report` itself.
   *Recommended: (b).* (a) makes the two variants of one build refuse each other's windows
   and makes `eonbase` report two graphs depending on where it was started (section 2).
2. **"ASCII whitespace" in EON-C10.** The approved text says "split on whitespace"; the bead
   says ASCII. *Recommended: write "ASCII whitespace" in the contract*, so the text states
   what the code does.
3. **A blank `$VISUAL`.** *Recommended: fall through to `$EDITOR`*, as a blank value names no
   editor.
4. **Harness default.** *Recommended: `eon_command` supplies `EON_HX`*, so tests mean the full
   product unless they remove it; the alternative edits two tests now and breaks silently in a
   developer's shell that exports `EDITOR`.
5. **Docs name `no-helix` before the package exists.** The bead puts the docs here and the
   CHANGELOG in eon-igae.17.3. *Recommended: follow the bead*; both land before v0.2.0.
6. **Note for eon-igae.17.3** (I cannot write to Beads): its wrapper must `--unset EON_HX`
   and drop the `hx` and `eon-hx` links (`flake.nix:1087-1092`), because `EON_HX` is inherited

   eon-xodrj.4 and .5: "this build has a packaged Helix" is `inputs.managed.helix.is_some()`.
7. **Message texts** (5.4): the `hx` refusal and the no-editor refusal. *Recommended: as

title: Build Eon's Rust once and compose the product from it, keeping the installed tree unchanged
description:
Plan: /home/lucca/.cache/eon-agents/eon-no-helix-plan-work/bead/plan.md (section 4.1).

## Why

Today `eonPackage` compiles and tests the `eon` crate and, in the same derivation, writes the
wrapper that names every tool (`flake.nix:906-1058`, wrapper in `postFixup`). Any variant made
by overriding it compiles `eon` again, and on macOS every dependency again. Splitting the Rust
build from the composition lets the no-Helix package (eon-igae.17.3) cost seconds and never
instantiate Helix.

## Contract

None changes. EON-C3 and Composition and Distribution (docs/AGENT-RULES.md) already make store
paths opaque launch inputs supplied by the composition. This is a packaging refactor with no
behavior change.

## Scope

- A Rust derivation that builds and tests `eon` exactly as today (same `cargoTestFlags`,
  `preCheck`, `postCheck`, `ORBIT_BIN`) and installs only what names no tool: the executable.
- A composition function that takes the tools to include and produces today's installed tree:
  it copies the executable to `bin/eon`, then does what `postInstall` and `postFixup` do today
  (icons, desktop item, tool links, licenses, shell files, Eon.app on macOS, `wrapProgram`).
  Copy, not link, so the layout stays `bin/eon` beside `bin/.eon-wrapped`.
- `eonPackage` keeps its name and becomes the composition with every tool, so `eonProduct`,
  `eonbase`, the bundle relink, the demo recorder, the checks and the apps need no change.
  `checks.default` must still run the test suite.
- The Helix asserts (`flake.nix:913-915`) move to the place that includes Helix.

## Acceptance

- Oracle: for the full product, the file list (`find`, with link targets) and the wrapper's
  environment are the same as the parent revision's, apart from store hashes. Record the diff.

comments.text:
# eon-igae.17.2 — Build Eon's Rust once, compose the existing product

Plan date: 2026-11-10. Owning bead: eon-igae.17.2; beta epic: eon-igae.
Worktree: `/home/lucca/.cache/eon-agents/eon-rust-once`, detached at
`c7da9c8` (tree `7338dc1639bbb74b0d008bbd22fd248c4ce39da7`), Eon 0.1.22,
EONW v39. Initial index and working tree are clean. Records, logs, candidates
and disposable proof tooling stay in `eon-rust-once-work/`, outside source.

## Observable boundary and scope

Consumers are the full Nix product, eonbase, the apps/checks/demo/bundle
consumers of `eonPackage`, and later the no-Helix composition. Building the
existing outputs must retain the installed files, permissions, relative links,
wrapper environment and component selection. A composition copies one built
`eon` executable; it does not compile or test another copy. Missing components
and existing manifest/pin mismatches must still fail at the same owning
boundary. EON-C3, C6, C7 and C9 remain unchanged. There is no new runtime,
configuration, window action, CLI default, dependency or component graph.

This slice prepares a shared Rust artifact and composition function. It does
**not** add `#no-helix`, a no-Helix wrapper, conditional runtime fallback,
variant receipt, archive, cache job, updater change or contract amendment.
Those belong to 17.3/17.4 and the later archive beads. No branch, commit, Beads
write, profile change or interaction with live Eon is performed by this agent.

## Evidence and constraints read

- Root AGENTS.md and docs/AGENT-PROTOCOLS.md; AGENT-RULES sections Beads,
  Contract-Driven Method, Verification, Proof and Review, Testing Discipline,
  Humans and Agents, Configurability, Implementation Languages, Composition
  and Distribution, Platform Discipline and Git Workflow. Directory rules
  will be read if scope unexpectedly reaches orbit/, runtime/ or venus/;
  none of those directories is planned to change.
- `br show` and comments for 17.2, parent 17, 17.1 and 17.3, read from the
  main checkout using JSONL-only/no-auto-import/no-auto-flush mode. No issue
  records are edited. Parent section 4.1 and the recorded 2026-11-10 decisions
  approve one Rust build with two compositions, Nix first, no manifest change.
- 17.1 landing `c6989c1` and its landing record: absent EON_HX selects the
  build without Helix; component graph/generation stays shared between the
  two compositions. 17.3's wrapper comments require unsetting inherited
  EON_HX and removing hx/eon-hx links. These remain explicitly **17.3 work**.
- Current flake.nix: packageSource/workspaceSource, buildWorkspacePackage,
  wrapperArgs/eonEnvironment, all eonPackage hooks, cached eonTests,
  eonProduct/eonbase, checks/apps/demo and bundle-relink consumers. Also
  nix/macos-app.nix, nix/managed-command-checks.nix, nix/bundle-relink.nix,
  eon/crates/eon/build.rs, docs/DEVELOPMENT.md, DISTRIBUTION.md,
  ARCHITECTURE.md#in-tree-package-selection and REFERENCES.md's runtime
  package-composition route. Existing copied-executable eonbase and existing
  stdenv composition/install hooks are the comparable in-tree mechanisms.
- `624bfff` (eon-o5tyo): preserve Linux packageSource filtering, dummy
  workspace members and omitted-path-dependency assertion. Eon retains its
  complete source for the generation digest; Darwin source selection stays.
- `02177bb` (eon-psque): Linux release build has doCheck=false; one cached
  dev-profile eon/eon-runtime Nextest check gates default/eonbase/checks.default.
  Its regular, ignored and doc-test routes stay intact. Darwin's Rust build
  retains its current release tests, cargoTestFlags, ORBIT_BIN, native check
  inputs, short-TMPDIR/failure cleanup and postCheck.
- Landing GC roots use checks.x86_64-linux.default.cargoArtifacts and
  checks.x86_64-linux.eon-tests.cargoArtifacts. Preserve both attribute paths,
  their release/dev cache separation and derivation identities.

## Implementation

1. Before editing flake.nix, build/root the exact parent full product,
   eonbase and build-only test/cache outputs in this work directory. Capture
   derivation identities, file/link manifests, bytes/modes, wrapper text,
   versions/config-defaults output and recursive closure path sizes.
2. Extract `eonRust` inside the existing per-system let. Keep
   buildWorkspacePackage, workspaceSource, cargoLock, Cargo build flags,
   Linux release artifact reuse and platform test behavior. Its installed
   output is only `bin/eon`, with no wrapper, icons, tool links, licenses,
   shell resources or app bundle. Assembly assertions stay with their
   owners; specifically Helix pin/version assertions leave this derivation.
   Name it eon-rust, distinct from eonPackage/eonProduct. Its .drv requisites
   must contain no Helix derivation on either Linux or Darwin (hard gate).
3. Put the current composition into a small function in flake.nix, using
   the existing Nix install/fixup mechanisms. It copies eonRust/bin/eon into
   its own bin/eon, then performs today's asset/license/link/shell/desktop
   and Darwin Eon.app steps and the same wrapProgram call. The included-tool
   boundary belongs here (only Helix varies in the approved design), together
   with Helix's assertions. Preserve composition pname/version/meta and
   ensure desktop hooks still execute. Expose version for linux-bundle.nix.
   Set dontStrip=true and dontPatchELF=true explicitly to preserve bytes and
   the Darwin Mach-O signature. Gather EON_HX, hx links, Helix license and
   Helix assertions at a single composition seam with no null/variant branch.
4. `eonPackage` is the full-tool call of that function. All existing consumers
   keep that identity and layout: bin/eon next to bin/.eon-wrapped. Thread
   the release cargoArtifacts passthrough from eonRust through eonPackage
   to eonProduct/checks.default. Do not change eonTests or its GC-root path.
   The shared wrapper environment remains the one source used by Nix and
   bundle-relink; adjust its call sites only if the composition input requires it.
5. **Both products use the same build:** full eonPackage and 17.3's future
   no-Helix call both copy the same lexical eonRust derivation. Tool selection
   enters only the composition, never eonRust arguments or source selection.
   17.3 adds the omission branches/wrapper and second exported output; this
   slice does not add an unused partial no-Helix wrapper. Darwin similarly
   builds/tests Rust once and composes twice, without introducing crane there.
   eonbase continues copying the already built executable through its existing
   route; it does not gain a full-product runtime reference.
6. Update only the development documentation that describes this build shape.
   No CHANGELOG entry: no user-visible behavior, command, configuration,
   selected packaged tool, installation layout or contract changes.

Expected source changes: flake.nix and a short docs/DEVELOPMENT.md paragraph.
No Rust callers, fixtures, exports or tests need edits. Existing Nix checks
exercise managed commands, closure isolation, receipt and bundle delivery.
The principal risks are accidentally retaining Helix in the Rust build graph,
losing the test gate or cargoArtifacts passthrough, skipping desktop hooks,
double-fixing the copied binary, or adding the raw package to runtime closure.

## Proof and measurements

Every attempt, including failures, will be recorded in numbered bead records
with exact source/staged tree, command, environment, exit status and result.
All Nix builds, including direct .drv rebuilds, dry runs and cache roots, go
through `bash /home/lucca/.cache/eon-agents/eon-overseer/heavy.sh` and pass
`--max-jobs 2 --cores 6`. Queue immediately; do not pre-wait for load. Every
long run closes unused stdin, has a timeout, and is checked for progress;
stop/report a granted slot with no progress for ten minutes. Keep all out-links
in the work directory, never the profile or main checkout.

1. **Evaluation/graph checks:** nix-instantiate parse (or the installed Nix
   formatter if available), then evaluate Linux product/checks and
   `nix eval --raw .#packages.aarch64-darwin.default.drvPath`. Compare before/
   after Orbit, Venus, bench/mac-proof and both crane cache derivations. They
   must retain source-filtering/cache identity when this packaging-only edit
   does not alter their inputs. Both crane dependency drvPaths unchanged is
   a hard pass/fail gate. Inspect the derivation graph to show one real
   release `eon` compilation, no composition Cargo/test phase, no Helix
   derivation anywhere in eonRust's build requisites on Linux and Darwin,
   no tool locators/wrappers in eonRust, and the cached Linux
   eon-tests dependency on both default and eonbase. Tests must not leak into
   either runtime closure. Inspect Darwin's extracted test attributes too.
2. **Package acceptance:** candidate `nix build --out-link ... .#default
   .#eonbase` plus Linux checks bundle-relink, bundle-launch, eonbase-closure,
   managed-command-path and source-receipt. Retain and evaluate/build the
   landing's release and test cargoArtifacts attribute paths with local roots.
   Nix packaging is the explicit exception requiring the agent's build.
3. **Installed-tree oracle:** traverse both the underlying composition and
   outer product without following arbitrary symlinks, recording every relative
   entry, kind, mode, link target and regular-file SHA-256. Compare relative
   links exactly and external component targets by exact artifact identity.
   Compare wrapper environment/exec target and desktop entries with only
   their identified parent/candidate self store paths normalized. Require
   exact bytes for icons, RGBA, shell files, skill and licenses. Verify the
   copied candidate bin/.eon-wrapped is byte-identical to eonRust/bin/eon;
   compare ELF/auditable metadata as needed to explain any binary difference.
   Record every differing path and reason, including any mode or closure delta.
   Do not call a broad normalization byte identity.
4. **Expected differences to report, not waive silently:** build.rs digests
   flake.nix, so the raw eon executable and `eon versions` generation must
   change. Wrapper, desktop entry and outer symlinks contain new self store
   paths. The source receipt records the candidate build/revision (dirty-tree
   revision is null); its schema/repository/platform/attribute stay identical.
   Any other changed file must be individually explained or fixed before
   review. Compare actual before/after closure bytes/path count using
   `nix path-info --json --recursive --closure-size` and retain the path diff.
5. **Installed observation:** exercise candidate versions, config defaults,
   eonbase help and the existing managed-command check from private temporary
   HOME/config/runtime roots, with explicit candidate paths. Bundle-launch
   covers the relinked installed path. No live desktop, supervisor or profile
   is touched. If graph/tree proof reveals a launch-sensitive change, use
   the supplied isolated display recipe and heavy.sh for one candidate-only
   observation; never broaden an evaluation claim into Mac runtime proof.
6. **Whole workspace:** once on the final staged source, run
   `nix develop -c eon-test` through heavy.sh, with a separate task Cargo target
   directory. No Rust changed: no crate-specific clippy loop is needed; a
   cheap fmt check may verify source cleanliness. Run the same whole-workspace
   suite again only when required by the final READY FOR LANDING rule or a
   material review fix; text-only records reuse proof.

No timing benchmark or quiet slot in this bead: the 2026-11-10T20:54:42Z
overseer plan review explicitly defers timing to 17.3 with the variant.
Cancel the original 40-minute slot request. Ordinary build logs may retain
start/end duration and caching state, but support no performance comparison.

## Baseline observations already made

2026-11-10, Linux 7.2.6, Determinate Nix 3.21.2 / Nix 2.34.7, clean c7da9c8:
three `nix eval --no-write-lock-file --raw` commands exited 0 (no builds).

- packages.aarch64-darwin.default.drvPath:
  `/nix/store/82cishlws3yhr64h2cd9w5kwkl7x2m6v-eon-0.1.22.drv`.
- checks.x86_64-linux.default.cargoArtifacts.drvPath:
  `/nix/store/xag5cn1kkd7cclkkgvdxzdg2g9ay093z-eon-workspace-deps-0.drv`.
- checks.x86_64-linux.eon-tests.cargoArtifacts.drvPath:
  `/nix/store/r2zp73vw4fwqlm5sqzxi603siq377iwa-eon-tests-deps-0.1.22.drv`.

Nix warned that the flake's cache settings are untrusted; the evaluations
succeeded. These observations do not prove a build or Darwin runtime.

## Review and completion

After this plan, write PLAN READY and stop for overseer plan review. Fold in
or rebut each finding before implementing. During implementation record
deviations in 01-notes, all attempts in 02-proof, and the overseer's findings
and resolutions in 03-review-ledger. No self-run review. Stage only task
source changes, confirm their exact tree and proof, then write
`READY FOR REVIEW <staged tree hash>` to STATUS.md. The overseer runs fresh
Claude/Codex review and handles landing/Beads/profile work. Do not commit.
No unresolved product decision is currently needed.

Plan review ledger (2026-11-10T20:54:42Z, Fable, via INBOX): all seven
findings accepted. (1) full Linux/Darwin .drv requisites exclude Helix;
(2) distinct eon-rust name and composition version; (3) dontStrip and
dontPatchELF explicit; (4) both cache drvPaths must stay identical;
(5) timing/quiet slot removed; (6) one Helix seam, no null branch;
(7) eonbase unchanged. Implement after this amendment. The overseer will
dispatch native mac-proof after landing; agent proves evaluation only.

Unproved here: no-Helix delivery, actual Darwin build/tests/Finder behavior,
whole-store cold-build performance and live-profile activation.

title: Keep eon update on a no-helix Nix profile entry
description:
Plan: /home/lucca/.cache/eon-agents/eon-no-helix-plan-work/bead/plan.md (sections 4.5, 5).
Decisions are recorded on eon-igae.17 (2026-11-10): v0.2.0 ships the variant on Nix only, so
this bead is the Nix half of the update work. The Nix-free half is a separate bead after the
release.

## Why

`eon update` refuses a profile entry whose attribute is not `packages.<platform>.default`
(`eon/crates/eon/src/update.rs:1660-1705`, and `check_remote` at `:1484-1490`). A person who
installed `github:Yazelix/eon/main#no-helix` could not check for or install updates.

## Contract

EON-C41, the approved text in plan section 5 for Imperative Nix and Provenance only. The
Installer-owned Linux sentence stays as it is until the Nix-free bead. This is a
trust-boundary change: read the C41 sections first and record the reference gate (owner of
each rule, constraints kept, rejected approaches).

## Scope

- The accepted product attributes are `default` and `no-helix` for the receipt's platform.
  The profile entry's attribute must equal the receipt's. Install upgrades that same entry on
  its original ref and attribute; an entry of one variant is never moved to the other.
  Everything else that refuses today still refuses.
- `--json` output: say whether any field changes. If the result shape crosses EONW, bump it
  (v38 to v39); never amend in place.
- Tests beside the existing update tests: a `no-helix` profile entry is followed and upgraded
  on its own attribute; a receipt and entry that disagree (either way) refuse
  `source-unverified`; any other attribute still refuses.
- Docs: `docs/USAGE.md` update section if it names the attribute; CHANGELOG.

## Acceptance

The tests above; whole-workspace `nix develop -c eon-test`; fmt and clippy for the changed
crate. No hosted or network proof here.

## Out of scope

Switching variants from `eon update`, anything in `update/direct.rs` or the installer (the
post-release Nix-free bead), and building an archive.

## Prerequisite

eon-igae.17.3 (the package and its receipt attribute).

title: Record cold and warm Nix build times for full Eon and no-helix
description:
## Why

Lucca's 2026-11-10 comment on eon-igae.17 explicitly asks to measure cold and warm build time,
with and without Helix and its grammars, and say when agent proofs and landing checks may use
the variant. The five implementation children are closed. eon-igae.17.3 records closure size
(full 1,996,841,456 NAR bytes, no-helix 1,707,271,960; 276.15 MiB less on its measured tree),
but those figures and the shared Rust derivation do not establish a time saving.

## Scope

One bounded measurement session for the approved Nix compositions, default and no-helix, on
x86_64 Linux. Compare the same revision, inputs, machine and resource limits. Define cold and
warm precisely, including local store availability and substitutes; distinguish a first build,
cache retrieval and a no-op. Include Helix and grammar work in the full-product result. State
what is measured versus inferred. No archive or updater changes, cache architecture, CI job,
macOS proof or runtime feature.

## Acceptance

- Record a four-cell cold/warm by full/no-helix table with elapsed time, exact commands,
  revision, inputs, artifacts, hardware/load, build limits and cache/substitution state.
- Reuse the existing size/closure evidence when it applies; identify any changed revision.
  Record the resulting size and time differences without assuming the variant is faster.
- State which existing proof routes can use no-helix when Helix is not under test, and which
  still require the full product or a specific distribution artifact. This is evidence and a
  recommendation, not authority to weaken AGENT-RULES verification or release requirements.

## Prerequisites and verification

Read eon-igae.17's approved Nix-only decisions, closed children .17.2/.17.3/.17.5 and their
records, plus AP-PERF-001 and docs/DEVELOPMENT.md. Use existing Nix outputs and timing tools;
the table, derivation/artifact identities and retained timing logs are the proof. Coordinate
one bounded quiet slot with the overseer before heavy work. Do not clear shared caches, run
global garbage collection, rebuild unrelated packages, change profiles or touch live Eon.

## Stop conditions

If a genuinely cold comparison needs a separate paid host or destructive cache eviction,
report the limitation and obtain the overseer's scheduling/scope choice; label any substitute
measurement accurately. Stop if inputs differ materially or load invalidates the comparison.
No build/test/tooling implementation is part of this measurement bead.

comments.text: prime-beads 2026-11-12: new child owns the cold/warm full versus no-helix measurements explicitly requested on .17; timing evidence cannot weaken required checks or authorize shared-cache eviction.

No tag, push, hosted dispatch, paid host, signing, upload, publish, promotion, profile change

title: Rename the component graph's eon-alpha product ID before 1.0
description:
## Why

The component manifest's product graph ID is still `eon-alpha` (`components/eon-alpha-v3.json:4`).
`eon-versioning-beta-bfyf` kept it "until the next graph version, because renaming them changes
the component report that live generations compare". 1.0 should not ship with "alpha" in its
version report, and renaming after the stability promise would be a breaking change.

## Evidence

- `components/eon-alpha-v3.json:4`: `"id": "eon-alpha"`.
- `flake.nix:68`, `flake.nix:727`, `eon/crates/eon/src/product.rs:8`,
  `eon/crates/eon-manifest/src/lib.rs:424`, `demo/record.rs:75`: file path consumers.
- `docs/DEVELOPMENT.md:43`, `docs/ARCHITECTURE.md:10,239`, `docs/CONTRACTS.md:21`: doc links.
- `runtime/crates/eon-workspace-protocol/src/v2.rs..v6.rs`: historical `"eon-alpha x86_64-linux"`
  fixtures. Leave historical EONW fixtures alone (runtime/AGENTS.md: preserve history).

## Scope

In: a new graph version with a non-stage product ID (propose the name to Lucca, e.g. `eon`),
the manifest file name, its consumers and docs. Out: changing EONW historical revisions.

## Acceptance

- `eon versions` reports the new ID; no current product text or report says alpha.
- A live generation started before the rename stays discoverable, attachable as before, and
  stoppable from the new build (the comparison the versioning bead warned about).

## Verification

Component manifest route (AGENTS.md "Verification"): full affected Rust and Nix surfaces:
`nix develop -c eon-test`, `nix build --no-link .#default .#eonbase`, plus one installed
observation of an old live generation being listed and stopped by the new build.

## Stop Conditions

- Stop if the rename forces an EONW revision or breaks old-generation discovery; ask Lucca.

title: Show a RAM widget in the Eon Bar
description:
## Why

(`~/pjs/nova/nova-upstream-theme/crates/yzx-config/src/catalog.rs:54` lists `cpu`, `ram`).
`eon-cpu-widget-eon-bar-acxs` builds the shared sampling and chip path; RAM rides on it.

Lucca, 2026-10-21: Venus samples locally (no Runtime sampling, no EONW revision), and the chip
format is `RAM 43%`, matching `CPU 12%`. See the CPU bead for the full design and reasons.

## Scope

In: whole-machine memory use as a read-only `RAM 43%` Eon Bar chip, parsed from `/proc/meminfo`
(used = MemTotal - MemAvailable) in the CPU bead's Linux-only Venus sampling module, on its 2 s
cadence, with hover and an accessible label. Contract: extend the CPU bead's `EON-C30`/`VEN-C28`
rather than adding new IDs; the wording needs Lucca's approval before commit.
Out: per-process or per-Eon attribution; GPU and IO (1.x).

## Acceptance

- The chip follows every failure rule of the CPU bead's contract: no chip on an invalid sample
  (never 0), no layout or resize churn on refresh, and the width-pressure order (clock, then
  CPU/RAM, then quota chips).
- The contract extension is approved before code.

## Verification

Focused parser test for `/proc/meminfo` parsing (red/green) plus the Venus build, and one isolated
installed dogfood observation of the chip.

## Stop Conditions

- Stop and ask Lucca if `/proc/meminfo` lacks `MemAvailable` on a supported kernel, since the used
  figure would then need a different formula.
