title: Start a command pane from outside an Eon terminal by naming the window and tab, so no shell language is ever typed
description:
Lucca 2026-11-03: 'we have to figure a way to never use the wrong shell language...' -> 'do it'. The overseer, running in a terminal of Lucca's main window, could not start agents in a second Eon window with 'eon pane create -- claude ...' (exact argv, no shell): EON-C10 accepts a command over EONW only from a caller naming a live terminal of the addressed supervisor (caller-required). So it typed commands into the new window's shells, and Nushell rejected bash '&&'. EON-C10 itself says that check 'states intent, not security: the socket is private to the user'. Proposal: an explicit target states the same intent, so 'eon --window ID pane create --tab TAB [--no-focus] -- COMMAND...' and 'eon --window ID tab create --dir DIR -- COMMAND...' accept a command without a calling terminal when --window  and the destination tab are named explicitly; the argv limits, PATH resolution against the terminal PATH and tab directory, and ended-pane behaviour stay as for a calling terminal. A calling terminal's validation is never waived. Contract text (EON-C10 command-pane clause, docs/USAGE.md rows) stops for Lucca's approval. Rule 5: also makes agents outside Eon (scripts, cron, a second window's overseer) launch agents the way a person does. Acceptance: from a non-Eon process, the command starts in the named tab of the named window with an exact argv; tests cover missing --tab, stale window/tab, and the unchanged caller path; installed proof launching claude --name X in an isolated window. title: eon runs window commands with the window's own build when the protocol differs, so profile refreshes never strand live windows
description:
## Why

Lucca, 2026-11-12 (eon-desk), after the third forced window move in two days: "cant we make this
easier? i'd like the agents to be able to update in place or migrate more easily", then "lets try
to do 1, and eventually 2". Here 1 is this bead and 2 is eon-1bq8 (in-place update).

Each EONW protocol bump (v40 → v41 → v42 on 2026-11-11/12) plus a profile refresh means the
installed `eon` can no longer control windows started from the older build ("the 2026-11-10 gap",
overseer decision 33). Every agent, overseer and desk session uses `eon` all the time, so each bump
forces everyone into a new window and holds profile refreshes (`land-commit.sh --no-refresh`)
until then.

## Goal

When `eon` addresses a window (or session, pane, popup) whose generation speaks a different EONW
version than the running CLI, it runs the command with that generation's own `eon` build, not
failing. A profile refresh then never breaks control of live windows. Moving to a new window becomes
optional, only for the new features.

## Prior art to reuse

EON-C11 already delegates `eon attach GENERATION` to the old build when EONW or the component graph
differ (docs/CONTRACTS.md, EON-C11). Reuse that mechanism and its build lookup; don't build a second
one. Terminals also carry `EON_SESSION_BIN` (the build's libexec/eon/bin, flake.nix ~:772), so a
generation's build path is already known.

## Scope

- Version-mismatch detection for every window-addressing command (`--window`, implicit
  current-window from `EON_TERMINAL`/`EON_WINDOW_RUNTIME_DIR`, explicit generation).
- Delegation: exec the generation's recorded `eon`, passing argv, stdin, stdout and the exit status
  through unchanged, including `--json`.
- A clear error only when the older build is gone (store path collected) or no build path is recorded.
- Contract text: EON-C11 (and EON-C10 if CLI addressing wording changes) needs Lucca's approval
  before code (rule 1).
- Docs: USAGE.md, the CLI reference, CHANGELOG.

Out of scope: in-place window update (eon-1bq8), moving panes between windows (eon-8mw1v.5.1),
forward delegation (an old CLI driving a newer window), and garbage-collection policy beyond a
clear error.

## Acceptance

- With a window started on build N and the profile refreshed to N+1 with a new EONW version,
  `eon session --json`, `eon pane read/send/rename`, `eon pane create` and `eon window reload` from
  a terminal in the old window work, through N's build. The same commands addressed to the old
  window from a terminal in a new-build window work too.
- Output and exit codes are identical to running build N's `eon` directly.
- No delegation loop: a delegated build never delegates again.
- A collected or missing old build gives one actionable error naming the generation and suggesting
  a new window.

## Verification

Integration test with two packaged builds of differing EONW versions (or a fixture generation
reporting an older version plus a stub build); `nix develop -c eon-test` (not inside a live Eon
session); fmt and clippy. Installed proof: refresh the profile across a protocol bump while an
isolated window from the previous build runs, and drive it with the new `eon`.

## Stop Conditions

Stop for EON-C11 contract approval. Stop if a generation does not record a reachable build path
and adding one requires an EONW bump. Then that bump is the first slice, and it must land one
window move before delegation can help.

title: Honour OSC 10/11 default colours and answer their queries
description:
## Why

Found by eon-mac-launch-kz4p.36 (2026-10-29): Eon ignores OSC 10/11 on every platform. A program
that sets the terminal's default background or foreground (`printf '\e]11;#808080\e\\'`), as some
themes, editors and tools do, changes nothing, and OSC 110/111 have nothing to reset. A program
that queries the background (`\e]11;?\e\\`) to choose a light or dark theme gets no reply, so it
falls back to guessing. Users reasonably expect both (AGENTS.md "Happy Users").

Historical cause hypothesis (not revalidated on today's engine): Orbit only sets libghostty's default
palette (orbit/src/pty.rs:200-206), never a default foreground or background. libghostty (ghostty
521cf2c5) stores OSC 10/11 as overrides, but its render state (src/terminal/render.zig:1052-1066)
copies fg/bg only when both are set, so with no default foreground an OSC 11 never reaches
Orbit's frame colours, and Venus keeps its background. The OSC 11 query goes unanswered
(Terminal.zig:189).

## Contract

Likely a new or changed ORB-C (Orbit owns terminal state and replies, ORB-C2), and possibly an
EON-C for a configurable default fg/bg. Needs Lucca's approval of the contract text before code.

## Change (shape, to plan)

Orbit gives the libghostty terminal a default fg/bg (from product config or Venus's theme
colours, one owner), so OSC 10/11 set and 110/111 reset reach frames and Venus, and queries
answer. Decide the source of the defaults (Configurability rule), reattachment behaviour, and
how Venus renders a changed default background with background_opacity.

## Acceptance

- Real-PTY Orbit check: OSC 11 set, query reply, OSC 111 reset; survives reattach.
- Installed dogfood: a program's OSC 11 changes Eon's background; OSC 111 restores it.
- Afterwards the macOS scenario's translucency step can go back to a grey probe
  (eon-mac-launch-kz4p.36's accepted gap).

## Scope

Orbit (and Venus/Runtime only if the defaults' source needs them). Not on the macOS launch path.


## Rebaseline and complete acceptance

At dcaef1c flake.lock:109 pins Ghostty 0fa3d577a5614150ff8e2c152de5fb9d5c6d2dec;
orbit/Cargo.toml:9 pins bindings 9b598d6528c08c013407052767bb2e885ba869ba. The old
521cf2c5 diagnosis is historical. pty.rs:211-217 explicitly installs only the ANSI
palette. Reproduce before assuming old RenderState behavior; inspect exact pinned
capabilities under Orbit's REFERENCES gate, never a second parser in Venus.

Keep comment 5182's single Eon product-default fg/bg owner passed at spawn, without
treating that recommendation as contract approval. Preserve Lucca's after-Yu-testing
sequencing (eon-mac-launch-kz4p); coordinate themes/eon-dmbbf to avoid duplicate inputs.
Acceptance covers OSC10 AND 11 set/query, OSC110 AND 111 reset, pre-override defaults,
reattach/resize retention and Orbit query replies. Settle padding/opacity scope in the
approved plan, not silently here. Real-PTY authoritative-state/reply regression and
isolated installed color/reset observation use current shared-boundary/output proof
after approval and profile refresh. Portability: neutral terminal state; native Linux/
Darwin proof remain separate. No probes in live user terminals.

title: Correct handwritten policy LOC scorecard
description:
## Observable contract

Consumer: a reader using README's LOC scorecard. Trigger: inspect the Agent policy row and total. Result: count the tracked handwritten policy sources, .agent-protocols.local.md and .agent-protocols.exceptions.json, exactly once while excluding generated AGENTS.md as the scorecard promises; report the exact aggregate total. Failure: a generated artifact is counted, a handwritten policy source is omitted, or row values do not sum to the total.

## Prerequisites and reference gate

No product or runtime prerequisite. Evidence is the generated-file warning in AGENTS.md, the two named editable source files, their exact line counts, and repository history: protocol import 7185ea8 counted those sources, while 2b8fef1 accidentally switched the row to rendered AGENTS.md. No external reference is needed for this repository-owned bookkeeping rule.

## Acceptance

1. Agent policy equals the exact line sum of the two handwritten policy sources.
2. Generated AGENTS.md remains excluded.
3. Every scorecard row sums to the displayed total.
4. Markdown and git diff checks pass.

## Scope boundary

README scorecard and this bead only. No policy text, generated file, runtime source, package, contract, dependency, child revision, or changelog behavior changes.

title: Closing tab 1 closed the whole window, tab 2 included
description:
## Report

Lucca, 2026-10-21 ~20:29 -03: "i close tab 1 in an older eon, and the entire window closed,
including tab 2".

## Evidence (eon-52, 2026-10-21 20:37 -03)

- The window belonged to supervisor `g1-62066c6e2a8666d073e678c90a66bb3d` (PID 2021541,
  started 17:58:05, EONW 13, `/nix/store/l5ss1z32rbzzk13qgl4aqqaiv6m2jn35-eon-0.1.1`).
- After the close, that supervisor and tab 2's terminal stayed alive: Orbit `orbit.sock`
  (PID 2022048) still runs nu -> Claude Code (PID 2022912). No Venus child remains, so the
  window, not the workspace, ended. Tab 1's terminal is gone.
- The supervisor's stdout/stderr go to /dev/null, so it left no log of why Venus exited.
- Lucca then opened a new Eon window at 20:29:17 (COSMIC scope `app-cosmic-eon-2642696`).

## Unknown, to establish first

- How tab 1 was closed: tab close control, Alt+W on its last pane, `exit` in its last shell, or
  `eon tab close`. Ask Lucca if not recorded here.
- Whether edge (EONW 14) still does it. Reproduce on edge in an isolated headless Sway
  (two tabs, close tab 1 the same way), and check whether Venus exits, crashes, or the
  supervisor drops the presentation.

## Expected

Closing a non-final tab removes only that tab; the window and the other tabs stay (EON-C contract
for tab close; `eon tab close` says "Close the active non-final tab").

## Scope

Find and fix the cause at its owner (Venus or Runtime) with a red/green regression check at the
cheapest harness that reproduces it. Out of scope: logging Venus stderr (file separately if the
missing log blocked diagnosis).

## Recovery for the affected window

`/nix/store/l5ss1z32rbzzk13qgl4aqqaiv6m2jn35-eon-0.1.1/bin/eon attach g1-62066c6e2a8666d073e678c90a66bb3d`
(the installed EONW 14 `eon` cannot attach a v13 generation).

Reproduce with Alt+Shift+W on tab 1 of a two-tab window, first on edge; if edge doesn't reproduce, on the l5ss1z32 eon-0.1.1 build.

comments.author: lucca
comments.text:
Investigation (eon-43, 2026-10-21 22:10-22:50 -03). Not reproduced; blocked on a diagnostic log.

Lucca's answers: Alt+Shift+W on tab 1; the window vanished "after a few seconds"; tab 1 had several
panes/columns and an open popup; tab 2 layout unknown, probably a popup. Lucca's config runs the
Agent popup as `claude` with `keep_alive = true`.

Isolated headless-Sway runs (installed edge qp01mka6 / EONW 14, and the incident's l5ss1z32 / EONW 13),
each pressing Alt+Shift+W on the active tab 1 of a multi-tab window; Venus survived and the next tab
became active every time:
- two plain-shell tabs (both builds); a tab moved to position 1 (l5ss);
- tab with 2 columns / 3 panes (l5ss); tab with an open Git popup (l5ss);
- edge: tab 1 with 2 columns, 3 panes and a Git popup, tab 2 with a Git popup;
- edge: supervisor SIGSTOPped 8 s right after the keypress, so Venus's 6 s workspace exchange timed
  out (Venus only marks the workspace unavailable, then recovers);
- edge with Lucca's config: real Claude Code in tab 1's panes and kept-alive Agent popup (shown, and
  hidden), Claude Code plus Agent popup in tab 2.

Ruled out by reading: the supervisor never stops Venus outside its own shutdown (reap/present paths);
a workspace-exchange timeout is not fatal in Venus; Venus is always the supervisor's child, so no
terminal inside tab 1 owned it; the presentation-control stdin EOF fires only after the supervisor
drops the process. A read-only code hunt (column views, scene, render, transports) found no panic on
this path. It found one real AccessKit crash (orphaned terminal-content node when the active tab has
no panes, no visible terminal and an empty status), but it needs AT-SPI active (IsEnabled=false on
this desktop) and a pane-less tab, which tab 2 was not (its nu -> Claude Code pane survived); filed
separately.

Remaining hypothesis: Venus exited on its own (a panic, e.g. any wgpu validation error asserts in
venus/src/render.rs:2230) with the message lost: the COSMIC launch sends the supervisor's and
Venus's stderr to /dev/null, and the journal has no Venus entry. Next: the persistent diagnostic
log bead (Lucca, 2026-10-21: "improve our logging and wait for it to happen again"), then reproduce
or read the log after the next occurrence.

Windows started after their supervisor restarts write ~/.local/state/eon/logs/<generation>-<secs>-<pid>.log. On the next occurrence, read that window's log: the 'closing tab'/'closed tab' or 'close failed' lines, then 'Eon Desktop exited: <status or signal>' and any Venus panic text and backtrace just before it. Reproduce from there.

comments.author: lucca
comments.text:
Check (claude, 2026-10-22 01:10 -03). No recurrence captured yet, and Lucca's working window can't capture one:
- ~/.local/state/eon/logs holds one log: g1-e52499… (current build, EONW 14), where Venus exited 0 at 00:46 with its terminal kept.

title: A Close or Stop right after a failed column stop can refuse as Busy before Orbit sees the old lease end
description: Found by the runtime-flakes agent while fixing the test flake eon-lease-reacquire-flake-yk1oc (2026-11-11). After a failed consented column stop drops an untracked survivor, an immediately queued Close or Stop can reach Orbit before Orbit processes the old lease's EOF. Current contracts allow the Busy refusal and it fails safely, so nothing breaks, but the person sees a refused Close they did not cause. Scope: decide whether the runtime should wait for the old lease's release (bounded) before sending the next lease request for the same run, or retry once on Busy; keep contracts unchanged unless the fix needs one. Proof: a deterministic runtime test that queues Close right after a failed column stop and expects success.
close_reason: Landed: Close or Stop right after a failed column stop retries once instead of refusing as Busy

comments.author: lucca
comments.text:
Landing proof: eon-k0okt (a Close or Stop right after a failed column stop can refuse as Busy before Orbit sees the old lease end)

The fix: Runtime (sessions.rs) keeps Busy as a typed acquisition outcome and makes one retry only on that Busy, before any lease exists, inside the existing operation deadline. Each attempt re-reads the exact expected Live record and revalidates endpoint, peer and Lease identity. A real second Busy refuses with today's "already managed" message and opens no third connection. Non-Busy errors are never retried and the deadline is never refreshed. Supervisor changes are test-only. No contract change.

Orbit host-loop argument (copied from bead/00-plan.md, Opus plan finding 1; source evidence at 283bf76, not an Orbit guarantee): host::next_ready scans ready sources round-robin; the held management connection precedes the management listener. After accepting and answering the first competing connection Busy, the turn advances beyond that listener. The old connection's EOF was already pending before this connect (Runtime had dropped its lease), so the scan reaches the EOF before wrapping to accept the retry, and Bend processes Gone before the next host fact. One immediate retry therefore covers this ordering; a second Busy remains a safe refusal.

Red/green: deterministic injected regression (a_close_after_a_failed_column_stop_retries_the_old_leases_busy, plus the lease_retry negative fixture) failed on the old code: exit 100, 2 failed, with "terminal run lease-race-9 is already managed". After the fix: focused 7 passed (the two new tests plus the existing Busy, wrong-peer, unvalidated-lease, real Orbit contender and rollback-deadline tests), eon-runtime 379 passed / 1 skipped, whole workspace 1282 passed / 69 skipped, installer 11 passed, fmt and locked all-target eon-runtime clippy clean (tree f1f8a0b9; final tree 47205cc differs by one comment and changelog prose, fmt checked). title: Follow an agent: show the file it is working on in the Editor popup
description:
## Why
From the Athas audit (~/pjs/refs/competitor-audit-2026-10/athas.md, "What Eon should learn" idea 6; evidence under "Output into the editor and terminal"). Athas has a per-session "Follow agent" toggle: the file the agent's current tool call names opens in a preview tab of another pane, at most once every 300 ms, without taking keyboard focus; input in another pane stops following (athas: src/features/ai/lib/agent-follow.ts:3-80, src/features/ai/services/agent-follow-service.ts:75-78). A person watching an agent sees the code it is touching without asking.

## Idea
A per-agent toggle in Eon makes the tab's Editor popup (or a Helix pane) show the file the agent is working on, read-only in effect: the agent's terminal keeps the keyboard, and any key the person types in the editor stops following.

## Prerequisites
- A location signal. Eon does not parse agent output (docs/REFERENCES.md rejects screen inference), so the file and line must come from the agent: ACP tool-call locations (eon-ikny, undecided), a Claude Code /ide bridge (noted on eon-xodrj), or an agent hook.
- The Editor popup and opening a file in a running editor: eon-xodrj, eon-xodrj.5, eon-bjov6.3.

## Contract
None yet. The location signal is a wire format and needs an EON-C clause or a new contract, with approval, before implementation. The toggle, its key and the rate limit are configuration (docs/CONFIGURATION.md).

## Acceptance checks
- With following on, a file the agent reports opens in the editor within the rate limit and keyboard focus stays where it was.
- Typing in the editor, or turning the toggle off, stops following; a hidden Editor popup is not forced open.
- The CLI can set and read the toggle (Humans and Agents rule), and session JSON shows which agent is followed.

## Scope boundary
No diff review, no keep or reject of edits, no parsing of terminal output. One followed agent per tab.

## Reference gate
Athas (above) and Zed's follow mode, which Athas cites. Effort: high. Confidence: low until a location signal exists; do not start before eon-ikny or the /ide question is settled.

## Bounded planning and delivery
This is an epic, not one implementation session. Keep the original follow outcome and all acceptance above. First complete a design/approval child: establish an explicit location signal, editor target and path trust rules, reference revisions, exact changed boundary text, CLI/config grammar and a bounded delivery split. ACP remains undecided; a relation to eon-ikny is not approval to use it or to parse output. The existing popup route consumes eon-xodrj.5; ordinary Helix-pane reuse is optional and remains governed by eon-bjov6.3's separate decision, not a mandatory dependency of popup follow.

Do not implement following until the signal, file/line authorization and contract text are approved. Preserve focus, dirty editor buffers and edits when switching preview files; define missing/deleted/outside-project paths, stale signals and agent exit in the proposal. Keep 300 ms as the reference's value, not an approved Eon default. After approval, file one bounded signal/transport slice if needed and one editor-follow/CLI/config integration slice, reusing the one approved signal owner. title: Deliver long, pixel-smooth kinetic Eon scrollback
description:
## Chosen product contract

Deliver useful retained terminal history and responsive native-Wayland scrolling without moving terminal authority out of Orbit or adding a second scheduling/rendering architecture.

Consumer: one installed Eon/EonTerm user on supported x86_64 Linux native Wayland.
Trigger: primary-screen history owns scrolling and the user moves a precision/continuous surface or discrete wheel.
Result: Orbit retains a measured useful byte budget and applies bounded signed whole-row movement atomically; Venus presents direct fractional pixels, bounded release momentum only when the native phase supports it, three rows per discrete logical step, and compositor-paced FIFO redraw; Eon composes exact accepted child revisions and records installed dogfood.
Important failures: terminal-owned input keeps its canonical physical routing and receives no synthetic momentum; all motion is interruptible; history edges stop firmly; background output never produces stale/invented rows; profile refresh preserves live Sessions.

When measured safe choices are otherwise equivalent, prefer the more responsive/lively behavior while preserving 1:1 low-speed precision, exact distance, bounded stopping, routing, and authority.

## Owner beads and sequence

This epic is a planning container and is never claimed for implementation.

1. Finish the existing active Eon Sessions lifecycle frontier.
2. Eon Sessions `orb-orbit-history-byte-budget-ykn`: measure and set the Orbit-owned history byte budget.
3. Eon Sessions `orb-orbit-signed-scroll-batch-x12`: extend `ORB-C8` and the next canonical ORBS version with one atomic bounded signed history commit.
4. Eon Desktop `ven-venus-kinetic-touchpad-scroll-5sl`: revise `VEN-C7` for fractional presentation, native input interpretation, minimal elapsed-time physics, batching, pacing, and honest metrics.
5. Eon `eon-kinetic-scrollback-bjs.1`: pin exact accepted children, refresh the active Nix profile without restarting live Sessions, and dogfood the installed candidate.
6. After that first installed dogfood, Eon Desktop `ven-decide-winit-scroll-gestures-mfz` records the explicit choice to keep pinned winit, backport narrowly, adopt a stable release, or—only with user approval—use an exact unreleased revision. It does not block owner implementation or the first candidate, but it precedes final epic closure.

Cross-repository relationships are recorded by exact IDs rather than duplicated Beads. The two Orbit beads share a workflow prerequisite but no false technical dependency; Eon Sessions still implements only one active frontier at a time.

## Reference decision

Inspected 2026-08-24:

- Orbit `bad068a775140a1a4c4a157a0b9b64fba46f8202` and pinned Ghostty `a887df42c56f6de86c0fe6da9c4eeca37931e083`: current `max_scrollback: 1_000` is bytes, not rows; existing `ORB-C8` already owns authoritative adjacent preview, routing, viewport movement, and frames.
- Venus `082ecb7e9e2a8dde009db28e481a68bee2d3ace6`: current path truncates native movement to rows and may amplify one event into repeated requests/frames; existing winit, wgpu FIFO, glyphon, and event loop remain the chosen owners.
- Pinned winit 0.30.13 fork `fb45fbf901fbe70cc9a877b5d651d0b60c206b08`: Wayland exposes line versus pixel deltas and phases but discards axis source, native event time, and useful device identity. Core policy is therefore based only on observable delta/phase.
- Winit master `874a1e31f194d11313c1ac133b28037b99db3e19` has unreleased hold gestures and newer high-resolution wheel support but still lacks source/time/device guarantees. Defer selection until hardware dogfood identifies whether those capabilities matter.
- Wayland pointer semantics: https://wayland.app/protocols/wayland
- GTK's current frame-clock and elapsed-time kinetic model, Kitty's pixel/momentum behavior, winit redraw/presentation notification, WGPU FIFO latency, libinput scrolling, Ghostty history semantics, and Alacritty's useful-history/wheel defaults are routed in the owner beads.

Adopt: 16 MiB as a measured starting hypothesis; one-row authoritative preview as the architecture ceiling; one signed batch in flight; fractional rendering; phase-complete precision momentum; direct discrete wheels; actual elapsed-time decay; compositor callbacks; existing glyphon first; honest event-delivery-to-submit metrics.

Reject for the first slice: rows as the history unit, nominal fixed 60 Hz timers, fixed per-frame decay, device/source guesses, synthetic discrete-wheel inertia, velocity stacking, bounce, one frame per row, multi-row overscan, custom renderer/shader, refresh discovery, actual-presentation protocols, public tuning, new mouse bindings, worker threads, physics dependencies, or unreleased-winit adoption before dogfood.

## Epic acceptance

1. Both Orbit beads and the Venus bead close with exact accepted revisions, contract/docs alignment, focused owner proof, and full affected shared-protocol surfaces.
2. `eon-kinetic-scrollback-bjs.1` proves the exact installed component graph and profile artifact, retains live Sessions during refresh, and records real supported-Wayland hardware behavior across the agreed gesture, wheel, edge, live-output, routing, cancellation, resize, reconnect, and lifecycle cases.
3. The accepted metrics demonstrate control and identify the actual bottleneck: no lost distance, stale/invented rows, runaway tail, bounce, unbounded queue, terminal-routing regression, or misleading physical-input/visible-presentation claim.
4. Available 60 Hz and 120+ Hz surfaces are observed without promising a fixed cadence. If required hardware is unavailable, the proof records that gap rather than inferring it.
5. After first installed dogfood, `ven-decide-winit-scroll-gestures-mfz` records the user's explicit source decision. Any selected dependency change receives its own authorization and proof; “keep pinned” is a valid complete decision.
6. The user accepts the installed scroll length, sensitivity, smoothness, acceleration, stopping distance, and interruption behavior.

## Scope and stop conditions

In scope: the four owner slices above, exact composition, installed proof, and the post-dogfood winit decision.

Out of scope: scrollbar/search UI, persistent history, compression lifecycle, multi-row overscan, terminal cells owned by Venus, renderer replacement, public tuning/configuration, new mouse-button gestures, momentum inside terminal applications, display-refresh guarantees, X11/Xwayland/macOS, additional architectures, or init/service-manager work.

Stop and return to the user if the one-row preview is insufficient; a new dependency/thread/timer/renderer/public configuration appears necessary; protocol work expands beyond one bounded commit and atomic response; real hardware cannot be handled from existing observable events; per-device policy becomes necessary; or measurement cannot identify a bounded existing-owner fix.
close_reason: All Orbit, Venus, installed-composition, hardware-dogfood, and post-dogfood winit decisions are accepted; kinetic scrollback is complete.

title: Accept installed Eon kinetic scrollback
description:
## Outcome and contract routing

Compose the exact accepted Orbit and Venus kinetic-scrollback revisions into Eon and record one installed native-Wayland acceptance. This refreshes the proofs for `EON-C1` through `EON-C4`; it adds no Eon-owned scrolling, input, rendering, or terminal state.

Consumer: one installed Eon/EonTerm user on supported x86_64 Linux native Wayland.
Trigger: the accepted child revisions are available and Eon selects them in its canonical component graph.
Result: the Nix profile resolves to the just-built exact component set, existing live Sessions are preserved until the user restarts them, and a fresh installed surface exposes Orbit-owned useful history plus Venus-owned direct pixel scrolling, bounded kinetic release, discrete-wheel behavior, and compositor-paced presentation.
Important failures: incompatible pins/builds fail before profile activation; profile refresh does not restart a live supervisor; dogfood must not claim physical-input-to-screen timing or guaranteed display cadence unavailable from the accepted APIs.

## Prerequisites and references

Accepted child work:

- Eon Sessions `orb-orbit-history-byte-budget-ykn`: measured retained-history byte budget.
- Eon Sessions `orb-orbit-signed-scroll-batch-x12`: accepted canonical ORBS v7 bounded signed history commit.
- Eon Desktop `ven-venus-kinetic-touchpad-scroll-5sl`: exact protocol consumer, fractional renderer, input policy, physics, pacing, and instrumentation.

Accepted rollout source `b44d968e38474fc5b75a41bcde2ad750da0d1e3e` pins Orbit `baf8aa28dcaa50484cd221aa7730defedc2356bb` with ORBS v7 and Venus `f13dc7ac2e9a24c5cff5bb7e618436783ec76dbf`.

The post-dogfood winit decision `ven-decide-winit-scroll-gestures-mfz` is deliberately non-blocking. Run it after this installed runtime is dogfooded; do not expand the first slice to an unreleased dependency beforehand.

## Acceptance

1. The canonical manifest, lock identities, Venus protocol import, and Nix composition name the exact accepted Orbit and Venus revisions with no compatibility probe, adapter, duplicate schema, or copied child mechanism.
2. Full affected Rust and Nix surfaces pass because the work crosses the shared ORBS protocol and installed UI. Refresh the active `eon` profile from the working tree and verify it resolves to the resulting store artifact.
3. Preserve running supervisors and Sessions during profile refresh. With explicit user authorization to stop/restart or after natural closure, launch one fresh installed Eon/EonTerm surface for outermost proof.
4. Installed dogfood covers: retained-history usefulness; slow sub-row precision; weak and strong releases; detented and rapid wheels; history edges; background PTY output; semantic-key live return; selection and mouse buttons; cursor/focus/occlusion loss; resize; pane/session changes; reconnect; terminal mouse tracking; and repeated launch/close lifecycle.
5. On available 60 Hz and 120+ Hz displays, retain the child metrics for event-delivery-to-redraw/present-submit, redraw cadence/missed callbacks, requested/applied distance, Orbit batch/frame time, renderer preparation/submission, coalescing, fling duration, and stopping distance. Report unavailable hardware honestly and make no refresh-rate guarantee.
6. The user accepts that movement is exact, responsive, controllable, and sufficiently long-lived, with no lost distance, stale/invented rows, runaway tail, bounce, queue-pressure notice, terminal-routing regression, or lifecycle regression.
7. `docs/CONTRACTS.md`, component records, changelog, README LOC scorecard, exact installed artifact, and Beads proof all agree at the same revisions.

## Scope boundary and stop conditions

In scope: exact child pinning, canonical composition, Eon and EonTerm profile refresh, exact Eonova downstream pin/profile refresh, installed proof, and user acceptance.

Out of scope: Eon-owned scroll policy or state, winit selection, renderer/protocol redesign, public tuning, new platform support, init/service-manager work, or any child fix copied into Eon.

Stop and return to the user if a child contract is not accepted, the profile cannot resolve the exact built artifact, installed behavior contradicts child proof, live Sessions would need automatic interruption, or dogfood reaches a recorded child stop condition.

title: Switching workspaces from the picker loses the Agent popup the picker covered
description:
## Why

Lucca, 2026-11-04: "if im on the agent popup, and switch workspaces, when i swap back, it opens in a vanilla pane instead of the popup". EON-C33's Switch bullet says each workspace keeps its active tab, selected pane and popups across switches, so this is a defect against an accepted contract.

## Evidence

A read-only code diagnosis on 2026-11-04 at c5e922d; nothing was run.

- `eon/crates/eon/src/product.rs` ~95-133: `agent` is keep_alive; `commands` and `workspaces` (the `eon-workspaces` picker) are transient.
- `runtime/crates/eon-runtime/src/workspace.rs:1489` `open_popup`: `displaced_transient` (:1518-1535) keeps a keep-alive popup alive, then `commit_popup` (:1596-1597) overwrites the tab's single `selected_popup` with the picker. Nothing records the popup it covered.
- `workspace.rs:648-652` / `show` :483-488: a switch touches no tab or popup.
- `workspace.rs:1642-1659` `session_ended` → `remove_popup` (:2331-2335): when the picker exits, `selected_popup == removed.id` sets `selected_popup = None`. The Agent popup stays in `tab.popups` but is no longer shown.
- Commands > Switch workspace (`runtime/crates/eon-runtime/src/cli.rs:117`, :209-210) runs the same picker inside the transient `commands` popup, so it loses the popup the same way.
- Inference: Esc in the picker, and any transient popup (Commands, Anima) opened over a keep-alive popup, lose it too. `eon workspace switch` from the CLI does not.

## Scope

In scope, in workspace.rs:

- The tab remembers the keep-alive popup that a transient popup covered (for example `covered_popup: Option<String>` on `Tab`).
- When the transient popup ends, the covered popup is shown again if it still exists.
- Every other direct change of `selected_popup` or `selected_pane` clears the memory: focus_attention (:2050/2054), the re-select at :1472, dismissing a keep-alive popup (:1626), retarget (:2294-2296) and pending commit (:2262).
- One runtime test: Agent shown, picker opened, picker ends (switch and Esc), Agent selected again.
- docs/USAGE.md says that closing Commands, Workspaces or Anima returns to the popup it covered.

Out of scope: the picker's own keys (eon-p7omw), the sessions model (eon-8mw1v), and Venus.

Feature-level fix within EON-C33's existing text, so no contract change is expected. Stop and ask if EON-C10/C18 text turns out to say otherwise.

## Acceptance

In installed Eon:

- With the Agent popup shown, Alt+Shift+S to another workspace and back shows the Agent popup.
- Commands > Switch workspace does the same.
- Esc in the picker returns to the Agent popup.
- A transient popup opened over a pane still returns to the pane.

## Verification

- A red/green runtime test in `nix develop -c eon-test -p eon-runtime`.
- fmt and clippy.
- One isolated installed observation.
- Converge plus Codex.

Portability: neutral.
close_reason: Landed on edge with its proof and review records: when a transient popup ends, its tab shows again the popup it covered (EON-C10 amended, approved by Lucca).

title: Let eon pane close close a named pane from a popup
description:
## Why

On 2026-10-22 the overseer, running in Lucca's Agent popup on t1, tried to close two finished agent
panes with `eon pane close p5 --json`. The Runtime refused: `{"error":{"code":"unavailable",
"detail":"close the popup before closing a pane"}}`. So an orchestrating agent can open panes from
its popup (`pane create --no-focus`, eon-zhjj) but cannot close them, and every finished agent
costs Lucca a manual close. Lucca: "i dont think this rule is good ... the oveerseer should have
powers to do stuff", then "create a p1 bead".

## Decision (Lucca, 2026-10-22, approving the overseer's proposal)

- An explicit `eon pane close PANE` from a popup terminal closes that pane in the calling tab, and
  the popup stays shown.
- Alt+W under a popup stays refused: the selected pane is hidden, so the user can't see what it
  would close. That is the rule's sound purpose.
- Still refused from a popup: a close that would end the calling tab (its last pane), because that
  also stops the calling popup and ends the caller's own session.

**Contract:** amend EON-C10 ("Closing is unavailable while a popup or picker covers the tab", and
"pane close under a popup or picker" in its Important failures). This is a contract change: bring
Lucca the exact EON-C10 wording, in your own session, before code. Decide and record whether the
EONW request shape changes (it should not need to; the same v11 close action is accepted from a
new caller state). Keep the picker case as it is unless the wording says otherwise.

## Evidence (edge 4b150d5)

- `runtime/crates/eon-runtime/src/workspace.rs`: the close validation returns `unavailable`
  "close the popup before closing a pane" whenever `tab.selected_popup.is_some()`, for every
  caller (around line 917; also around line 2533).
- The rule came in with Alt+W, cfeb8b8 "Close the selected pane with Alt+W over EONW v11".
- `docs/CONTRACTS.md` EON-C10, around lines 505 and 524.
- Precedent: eon-zhjj made `pane create --no-focus` keep the caller's popup shown.

## Reference gate

This is a consequential shape (contract and lifecycle boundary). Record on this bead before code:
how comparable tools close a pane by id while another surface has focus, at pinned revisions from
docs/REFERENCES.md routes. tmux `kill-pane -t` (with a `display-popup` open), Zellij
`close-pane`/`--pane-id`, kitty `close-window --match`, and WezTerm `cli kill-pane --pane-id` are
the obvious candidates. eon-n6ga already pins four of them.

## Scope

In scope: the Runtime acceptance rule, the EON-C10 text, CLI help/USAGE if they mention the
refusal, CHANGELOG, and tests: a popup caller closes a named non-final pane and its popup stays
shown and selected; a popup caller naming its tab's last pane is refused with topology unchanged;
Alt+W under a popup is still refused.

Out of scope: closing panes in other tabs (the calling-tab rule stays), pane move under a popup
(the same refusal exists there; report whether it should follow, as a separate decision), and
reading pane text.

## Acceptance

- The three test cases above, red first where the behavior is new.
- An isolated installed observation: from an Agent popup, `eon pane close pN` closes pN and the
  popup stays shown with its conversation.

## Verification

Workspace/runtime route: focused `nix develop -c eon-test -p eon-runtime -p eon`, fmt and clippy,
the converge loop with Codex, and the installed observation after the profile refresh.
close_reason: Popup and pane callers close a named non-last pane under a popup; Alt+W and the last pane stay refused (EON-C8/EON-C10). Proof on the bead.

title: Initialize Orbit with the Eon vivid ANSI palette
description:
## Outcome and contract

Consumer: a local user opening a new full Eon or EonTerm Session.

Trigger: Eon starts a new Orbit process for that Session.

Result: Eon supplies one exact approved 16-color sRGB ANSI table through a bounded versioned component launch input. Orbit validates it, applies it as the authoritative default palette before processing PTY output, and emits the resulting exact values through existing ORBS frames. Full Eon and EonTerm use the same table. Terminal programs may still override colors through normal OSC semantics.

Important failures: malformed or missing required Eon input fails before the PTY child starts; partial tables are rejected; an Orbit process started outside Eon keeps its existing libghostty defaults; current live Sessions are not recolored or restarted. Direct RGB and palette indices 16 through 255 remain unchanged. OSC 4 overrides remain program-owned, and OSC 104 resets to the Eon-supplied defaults rather than bare libghostty values.

Ownership: Eon is the sole owner of the product default table and component launch policy. Orbit remains the sole terminal-state owner and applies the accepted default through libghostty. Venus remains an exact ORBS consumer and gains no palette setting, rewrite, saturation transform, or renderer change.

Contract routing: harden EON-C1, EON-C3, EON-C4, and EON-C12; change or add an Eon user-visible default contract only after explicit user approval. The producer work must preserve ORB-C1, harden ORB-C2 and ORB-C6, and define the new Orbit launch input before code. Existing ORBS values already carry the complete palette, so no ORBS version or VEN contract change is proposed.

## Why

The P1 Venus issue ven-render-vivid-terminal-colors-2ap proved that YZX Anima indexed colors are muted before Venus: bright indices 10, 14, 12, and 13 arrive as #b9ca4a, #70c0b1, #7aa6da, and #c397d8, while generic direct RGB #00ff88 remains exact. The Venus renderer is not the owner, but the user-visible product defect remains. Without a correct-owner Eon issue, closing the Venus investigation loses the chosen vivid-color outcome.

Impact: HIGH. Common Zellij and Anima indexed output uses the default palette.
Effort: M across one producer-first Orbit slice and one Eon integration slice.
Risk: MED because startup validation and terminal palette reset semantics cross the component boundary.
Confidence: HIGH in ownership and mechanism; the exact 16-color table still requires explicit user acceptance.

## Evidence

- Eon crates/eon/src/main.rs:1596-1635 has one Orbit process and argv owner. It currently sends only serve, socket, separator, and child argv.
- Eon docs/ARCHITECTURE.md:101 assigns component launch policy to the Eon runtime and excludes terminal state.
- Orbit src/main.rs:180-228 accepts only socket and child command, then constructs libghostty with columns, rows, and scrollback.
- libghostty-vt 0.2.1 terminal.rs:158-224 and :710-725 exposes default_color_palette and set_default_color_palette for embedder-owned defaults. It preserves OSC overrides and makes later resets return to the supplied default.
- libghostty-vt 0.2.1 style.rs:225-330 provides the existing 256-entry Palette, base-index setters, and built-in defaults. No new parser crate or palette type is needed.
- Orbit src/presentation.rs:147-153 already emits the effective complete 256-color palette through ORBS.
- eon-eonterm-presentation-e4f is not a duplicate: it routes fonts, geometry, line height, and opacity to Venus and explicitly excludes terminal palette authority.
- No existing Eon or Orbit Bead mentions palette initialization.

Exact inspected identities: Eon a701d55beaf4127c9ff4d1341214b1ebd82221ba; Orbit e60554623d2ad1e238fac84d0f8f49be0e81e522; Venus investigation at eon-desktop b18d5c34f794fd4e3c34beb64952a767c588db41; Ghostty a887df42c56f6de86c0fe6da9c4eeca37931e083 through libghostty-vt 0.2.1; Nova Bar d659fdf5ae0b4013aacaf31399e2bab064654320; packaged Anima d22d091d427af0be307056c65e475802b602d386.

## Minimum shape

1. Before implementation, capture the clean Ghostty palette and the user-approved vivid candidate beside Nova direct colors and the Anima/Zellij indexed corpus. Obtain explicit approval for all 16 RGB entries and whether foreground/background remain unchanged.
2. Create and prove a separate Orbit producer issue first. Define one bounded versioned launch value for exactly 16 RGB entries; reject partial or trailing input before PTY creation. Add no config framework or compatibility window.
3. In Orbit, start from the existing libghostty 256-color default, replace indices 0 through 15 with the supplied table, and call set_default_color_palette before the owner loop processes PTY bytes. Do not synthesize OSC, inject shell output, or change ORBS.
4. Prove initial frames, detach and reattach, OSC 4 override, per-index and full OSC 104 reset, direct RGB, and default standalone Orbit behavior.
5. After the exact Orbit proof is accepted, add the fixed approved table to the existing Eon Orbit-command owner and pass the exact child input for workspace and EonTerm launches. Add no user setting in this first slice.
6. Prove the composed installed artifact, update accepted contract metadata after proof-bearing commits, and refresh the Eon profile without stopping live supervisors or Sessions.

## Scope

In scope:
- One fixed Eon product-default ANSI 16-color table.
- Existing Eon Orbit launch composition and focused argv/process tests.
- A producer-first Orbit launch-input parser and direct existing libghostty palette setter.
- Contract, component-identity, current-state documentation, changelog, and LOC updates required by accepted runtime behavior.
- Native Linux dogfood in full Eon and EonTerm/Eonova with Zellij and YZX Anima Game of Life.

Out of scope:
- Venus source, renderer color transforms, saturation boosting, shaders, color management, or a Venus palette setting.
- A user-editable palette, theme registry, dark/light switching, live reload, per-pane colors, foreground/background changes without explicit approval, or Nova theme ownership.
- Replacing or forking libghostty, adding a dependency, changing ORBS, changing terminal direct RGB, or regenerating indices 16 through 255.
- Recoloring an existing Orbit process or restarting live Sessions.

## Reference classification

Required before code: this complete Bead; closed Venus issue ven-render-vivid-terminal-colors-2ap and its exact capture comments; current Eon launch owner and EON-C1/C3/C4/C12; current Orbit CLI, ORB-C1/C2/C6, palette extraction, lifecycle tests, and libghostty-vt 0.2.1 palette API; Ghostty a887df42c56f6de86c0fe6da9c4eeca37931e083; Nova Bar d659fdf5ae0b4013aacaf31399e2bab064654320; packaged Anima d22d091d427af0be307056c65e475802b602d386.

Comparison only: a clean standalone Ghostty native capture and the users configured Ghostty capture. They inform exact palette choice but do not transfer Ghostty configuration or renderer ownership.

Rejected: Venus palette replacement, global saturation curves, synthetic OSC prelude, shell startup escapes, environment-variable-per-color, a general theme schema, Mars configuration import, source copying, and a new dependency.

## Acceptance

1. The user approves one exact complete 16-color sRGB table before contract or source edits. The proof records the compared clean Ghostty, configured Ghostty, Nova, and current libghostty values without claiming they are identical.
2. Eon owns one fixed table and passes one bounded versioned value to every newly started full Eon and EonTerm Orbit process. No second table or consumer reconstruction exists.
3. Orbit rejects malformed, incomplete, duplicate, or trailing palette input before PTY spawn and reports one bounded launch failure. Omitting the option outside Eon preserves the built-in default.
4. The first ORBS frame contains the exact approved table. Detach and reattach preserve it without changing terminal or process identity.
5. OSC 4 overrides only named indices; OSC 104 for one or all indices returns to the Eon table. Direct RGB and indices 16 through 255 remain exact.
6. Venus receives and renders the resulting existing ORBS values without source or contract changes.
7. Native full Eon and EonTerm/Eonova dogfood shows accepted vivid Zellij and YZX Anima colors beside unchanged Nova direct RGB. Existing live generations remain untouched and report restart as required.
8. Orbit is proved and published first; Eon then pins that exact accepted revision, updates component identity and contract proof, builds the package, refreshes the profile, and runs the locked checks.

## Verification

Orbit producer:
- cargo fmt --all --check
- cargo check --locked --workspace
- cargo test --locked --workspace
- cargo run --locked --quiet -p orbit-governance -- .
- cargo clippy --locked --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings
- git diff --check

Eon consumer:
- cargo test --locked -p eon orbit_uses_configured_argv_only_for_default_sessions
- cargo fmt --all --check
- cargo check --locked --workspace
- cargo test --locked --workspace
- cargo clippy --locked --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings
- cargo run --locked -p eon-manifest -- components/eon-alpha-v3.json
- nix build --no-link --print-out-paths --no-update-lock-file path:.#default
- nix flake check --no-build --no-update-lock-file path:.
- git diff --check

Record exact ORBS captures before and after OSC override/reset plus the installed native comparison. Success means exact bytes and accepted visual output, not merely compilation.

## Stop conditions

- Stop for explicit user approval before assigning or changing EON or ORB contract IDs and before fixing the 16-color table.
- Stop before Eon code until a separate Orbit producer issue is created, approved, proved, committed, and published at an exact revision.
- Stop if another active frontier owns the Eon launch path or Orbit CLI/terminal owner.
- Stop if the existing libghostty setter does not preserve OSC override and reset semantics under focused proof.
- Stop if the change requires an ORBS revision, libghostty fork, dependency, theme framework, public configuration, live Session mutation, or Venus workaround.

## Maintenance notes

Keep this separate from eon-eonterm-presentation-e4f so palette authority does not block independent Venus font and window settings. Reconcile it before activating the Eonova bridge acceptance or Nova cutover. The removal path is one Eon table, one component launch field, and one Orbit application path.

title: Startup rollback reuses an expired deadline and can leave Orbit running after a start timeout
description:
## Why

Found by the Codex re-check of eon-flaky-focus-test-15g8o (2026-11-11; report /home/lucca/.local/state/rota/runs/recheck-15g8o-codex-1/report.md). In runtime/crates/eon-runtime/src/sessions.rs (around :1976-1988 at edge 2ac11f4), the rollback after a failed terminal start calls acquire_management(..., deadline) with the start's own deadline. When the start failed because that deadline ran out (Orbit published Ready near the five-second bound, then the lease timed out), acquire_management fails at once on the expired deadline and the ? returns before session.child = Some(orbit) and stop_managed_sessions run. The Orbit host (and its child program) is left running with no owner; its record may be cleaned up, so nothing reaps it later.

## Scope

Give the rollback its own bounded deadline (a lifecycle bound, documented like the existing ones), and make sure every early return in the rollback still stops or kills the Orbit child it started (kill by its own PID if the lease cannot be acquired). Test: a start whose lease times out leaves no Orbit process and no record. Relates to eon-k0okt and the lease waits of eon-lease-reacquire-flake-yk1oc. Lifecycle change: check EON-C contracts that state start or rollback guarantees; contract text needs approval if it changes.

## Acceptance

The test above passes under load; Runtime suite green; proof recorded here.
close_reason: Landed: a failed start's leftover Orbit always keeps an owner until it is reaped

title: Color the Eon Bar's quota windows by how sustainable the current pace is
description:
## Why

Lucca, 2026-10-21: "color code the AI quotas according to how sustainable the pace you are going
is. if it should last with confort or barely, or if it will lack, or if it will lack so hard you'd
spend days without usage ... we can tune this positively a bit, optimistic, green, but then it
starts yellowing, then oranging, then red-ing".

Today Codex's chip shows each window's position and remaining percentage (`3h/5h 74% · 6d4h/7d 42%`), and each Claude window has its own chip (`3h/5h 74%`), and the
reader has to work out whether that pace lasts until the reset. A color per window answers that
at a glance.

## Evidence

- `runtime/crates/eon-workspace-protocol/src/v14.rs:267-280`: each quota window carries
  `duration_minutes`, `remaining_percent` and `resets_at: Option<u64>`, and the quota carries
  `observed_at` and a state (fresh, stale, blocked, unknown). That is enough to compute pace in
  Venus with no EONW or Runtime change.
- `venus/docs/CONTRACTS.md` VEN-C22 (Codex chip) Boundary lists "threshold color" as excluded.
  VEN-C26 (Claude beside Codex) follows VEN-C22. Both need contract edits, and Lucca must approve
  them before the code.
- `docs/CONTRACTS.md` EON-C22 and EON-C26 describe the product-side quota chips. Check whether
  they also need a line.
- Related: `eon-claude-chip-split-u3ik` landed (3aa682b): Claude shows one chip per window, Codex
  keeps one chip with both windows. Pace is per window, so color each window's text inside Codex's
  chip and each Claude chip as a whole.

## Scope

In scope:
- One pure Venus function per quota window: from elapsed share and used share, project whether
  usage at the current pace runs out before `resets_at`, and by how long. Return one of four
  levels: green (lasts comfortably), yellow (barely lasts), orange (runs out before the reset),
  red (runs out so early you'd go a long stretch, e.g. days on the 7-day window, without usage).
- Color each window's text (or segment) in the chip by its level. Hover text and the AccessKit
  label say the same thing in words (e.g. "at this pace, runs out about 2 days before reset"),
  so color is never the only signal.
- Edits to VEN-C22 and VEN-C26 (and EON-C22/C26 if they need it), proposed for Lucca's approval
  first.

Out of scope:
- EONW, Runtime polling or CodexBar changes; a configurable threshold setting; alerts,
  notifications, charts or history; other providers.

## Acceptance

- Optimistic tuning, as Lucca asked: green covers "on pace or a little over", and the
  thresholds lean toward green. The exact cut points are proposed with the contract text and
  approved by Lucca. A starting proposal is to compare the projected run-out time with the
  reset: at or after the reset, or less than ~10% of the window early, is green; up to ~25% early
  is yellow; up to ~50% early is orange; more than that is red.
- No color without a basis: a window with no `resets_at`, a stale, blocked or unknown quota, or
  a window too young to judge (proposal: under ~10% elapsed) keeps today's neutral color.
- Hover and AccessKit name the level in words for every colored window.
- Narrow-width hiding, layout and the chip text are unchanged; only color changes.

## Implementation Notes

1. Read VEN-C22, VEN-C26 and the Venus quota chip code (`venus/src/scene.rs` and the chrome
   renderer) for where window text and color are produced.
2. Draft the contract edits and the cut points, then stop for Lucca's approval.
3. Add the pure pace function with unit tests at each boundary (exact pace, each cut point,
   missing reset, young window, the 100%-used window).
4. Wire the color into the chip, then hover and AccessKit text.

## Verification

- `nix develop -c bash -c 'cargo fmt --check -p yazelix-venus && eon-test -p yazelix-venus &&
  cargo clippy --locked -p yazelix-venus --all-targets -- -D warnings'` exits 0.
- Installed: one isolated headless-Sway observation with fixture quota data (check whether a
  fixture route exists; otherwise record the gap) showing at least green and red windows, plus the
  hover text.

## Stop Conditions

- Stop for Lucca's approval of the contract edits and cut points before code.
- Stop if pace needs data the snapshot does not carry (that would make it an EONW change).
- Stop if the theme has no accessible yellow/orange/red on the chip's fill in both themes.

## Maintenance Notes

- Owner: Venus Scene, as a projection of snapshot facts. If Lucca later wants the cut points
  configurable, the policy moves to Eon and travels as a launch input; not in this bead.
- Linear projection (used share over elapsed share) is the simplest model. A smarter model
  (recent rate, time of day) is a later idea, not this bead.
close_reason: Pace gradient on quota windows shipped with hover/AccessKit wording; automated and isolated installed proof recorded

comments.author: lucca
comments.text: Lucca, 2026-10-21: use a gradient. Decision: the window's color is a continuous blend along green -> yellow -> orange -> red, driven by the projected shortfall (how early, as a share of the window, the current linear pace runs out before resets_at), not four discrete levels. Kept from the body: optimistic tuning (pure green through on-pace and a small overshoot, then the blend starts), neutral color when there is no basis (no reset, stale/blocked/unknown, window too young), and hover/AccessKit wording so color is never the only signal (words may stay coarse, e.g. 'lasts until reset' / 'runs out about 2 days early'). The gradient's anchor points (where it turns yellow, orange and full red) are part of the contract proposal Lucca approves. Extra acceptance: every point on the gradient keeps readable contrast for the chip text on its fill; boundary tests cover the anchors and monotonicity (more shortfall is never greener).

comments.author: lucca
comments.text: Lucca, 2026-10-21, correcting the tuning: pure green only for 'on pace or slightly over' is too optimistic. Exactly on pace (projected to run out right at the reset) is a light green just starting toward yellow; full green is reserved for usage comfortably under pace, and any overshoot moves further along the gradient. Lucca floated today's neutral chip color for on-pace; recommendation (eon-c5): don't, since neutral already means 'no basis to judge' and on-pace should read as a judgement. Final on-pace shade is set with the anchor proposal Lucca approves. This supersedes the 'optimistic' anchor in the earlier gradient comment and the body.

comments.author: lucca
comments.text:
PROPOSAL for Lucca's approval (pace agent, 2026-10-27). No product code is written until approval is relayed.

## Reference gate (consequential: contract change)

- User-visible behavior: each fresh quota window's text in the Eon Bar (Codex's per-window segment, each Claude chip's label) takes a color on a continuous green -> yellow -> orange -> red gradient by how sustainable its current pace is; hover and AccessKit say the same in words. One owner: Venus Scene computes the pace from the current EONW snapshot facts (duration_minutes, remaining_percent, resets_at, observed_at, state); the chrome renderer colors the glyphs; hover/AccessKit reuse the chip description. No EONW, Runtime, CodexBar, config or dependency change.
- Routes read: venus/docs/REFERENCES.md "Codex quota fact chip" (Venus derives labels only from normalized duration, reset and observation facts; Nova Bar styled strings rejected as source).
- Comparable implementation: CodexBar `7c08c0ae783b72040b728757eb85a6cfe4fc2443` (MIT, the pinned quota backend), Sources/CodexBarCore/UsagePace.swift, UsagePaceText.swift, MenuBarLayoutRenderer.swift:687-701. Kept: linear pace (used share against elapsed share), run-out ETA = remaining / rate, "Lasts until reset" / "Runs out in X" wording, no pace without a reset, no pace when the window is not yet measurable. Rejected: its seven stages by percentage-point delta (Lucca asked for a shortfall-driven gradient), its binary green/red tint and half-alpha stale tint (stale stays neutral here), its optional setting `menuBarColorPace`, workday and historical models, and any copied source.
- Decision and check: pure Scene function with boundary and monotonicity unit tests; rich-text glyph color check in the renderer; contrast >= 4.5:1 for every gradient point on BAR_BACKGROUND; one isolated headless-Sway observation with a fake CodexBar (EON_CODEXBAR in a copied wrapper) showing green and red windows and the hover text.

## Model

For one window with a reset, at the snapshot's observed_at (the same instant the position label uses; Venus adds no timer):
- elapsed share e = elapsed / duration; used share u = (100 - remaining) / 100.
- Shortfall s = 1 - e/u: how early, as a share of the window, the current linear pace runs out before the reset (negative = lasts with that much to spare). u = 0 never runs out (full green). u = 1 gives s = 1 - e, the share of the window left without quota.

## Cut points (gradient anchors) -- Q1

Colors blend linearly between these anchors (s, color):

| s (shortfall) | pace (u/e) | 5h window | 7d window | color |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| <= -0.25 | <= 0.80 | lasts with 1h15m+ spare | lasts with 1d18h+ spare | full green |
| 0 | 1.00 (on pace) | runs out at reset | runs out at reset | light green, 30% toward yellow |
| +0.10 | 1.11 | 30m early | ~17h early | yellow |
| +0.25 | 1.33 | 1h15m early | ~1d18h early | orange |
| >= +0.50 | >= 2.00 | 2h30m+ early | 3d12h+ early | full red |

Colors (dark bar only; Venus has one theme): green rgb(96,196,96), yellow rgb(255,196,87), orange rgb(255,150,70), red rgb(255,107,107); each, and every blend between them, is >= 4.5:1 on BAR_BACKGROUND rgb(10,13,20) (computed minimum over the whole gradient 7.0:1, endpoints 7.0:1 to 12.3:1; today's neutral text is 8.6:1). New palette constants named for this role.

## No basis -> today's neutral text color

Stale, blocked or unknown quota; a window without resets_at; a window younger than 10% of its duration (first 30m of 5h, first ~17h of 7d) -- except a used-up window (0% remaining), which is always judged.

## Proposed contract text

New subsection after "VEN-C22/VEN-C26 -- Optional-reset consumer refinement":

### VEN-C22/VEN-C26 -- Pace color

- **Status:** Proposed.
- **Contract:** Each fresh quota window with a reset, past its first tenth, colors
  its text (one segment of Codex's chip, the label of a Claude chip) on a
  continuous green, yellow, orange, red gradient by how early its current pace
  runs out before the reset, projected linearly from the snapshot's used and
  elapsed shares at the observation time. Full green is comfortably under pace;
  exactly on pace is a light green turning toward yellow; full red runs out at
  least half a window early. A used-up window is always colored. Stale, blocked,
  unknown, reset-less and younger windows keep the neutral text color. Hover and
  the static accessible label say, for each colored window, that at this pace it
  lasts until reset, runs out about a stated time before reset, or is used up, so
  color is never the only signal. Separators, `old`, the marks, text, compact
  choice, widths and hiding order are unchanged; every gradient color keeps at
  least 4.5:1 contrast on the Eon Bar.
- **Owner:** Venus Scene projects the color and wording from snapshot facts;
  the existing glyphon renderer, hover and AccessKit owners present them. No
  EONW, Runtime, provider, configuration, timer, dependency or module change.
- **Proof:** pending (`eon-l8lt`).

Edit in VEN-C22 **Boundary**: "alert, threshold color, chart" -> "alert, threshold
color other than the pace gradient (VEN-C22/VEN-C26 -- Pace color), chart".

EON-C22 and EON-C26 are retired; EON-C27 describes collection, not color. No EON contract edit.

## Numbered questions (recommendation first)

1. Cut points: approve the table above? Recommended as is. Alternative: full red at +0.40 (about 2d19h early on 7d) if "days without usage" should go red sooner.
2. Young-window guard at 10% of the window, with the used-up exception? Recommended as is.
3. Configurability: keep the anchors and colors fixed in this bead and record why (bead scope excludes a setting; a setting needs Runtime to parse and send it over EONW, which this bead excludes; the words carry the meaning for anyone who cannot use the colors), with a follow-up bead for a `[bar]` toggle only if you want one? Recommended: fixed, no follow-up bead unless you ask.
4. Contract text above: approve as written?

title: Replace the attention poll test wall-clock bound with a withheld-response fixture
description:
## Why

The attention integration-test helper requires every poll to complete within 50 ms, which can fail when the scheduler pauses its thread under workspace load. eon-vhbmp's 2026-11-10 landing comment identified this as the likeliest remaining timing flake; eon-yooz3's Opus plan review confirmed that simply removing the assertion would lose the explicit no-wait check.

## Evidence

- `runtime/crates/eon-runtime/src/attention.rs:2772` at dcaef1c: `poll_until` already waits for the supplied state predicate with a 10 s liveness guard, but :2785 asserts each call takes less than 50 ms.
- Its callers are `the_poller_reads_real_orbit_terminals_without_waiting_on_a_silent_one` and `the_poller_reads_a_real_foreground` (six calls total at eon-yooz3's base `8b5ee2dfad19c15f73754cd370e79164cf2881fa`).
- `Attention::poll` at :290 must send/read without blocking; `POLL_DEADLINE` is 250 ms. EON-C31 keeps the last good state on a missed reply and marks it stale after 3 s.
- Review: `/home/lucca/.local/state/rota/runs/flaky-tests-planreview-opus-1/log`; disposition: `/home/lucca/.cache/eon-agents/eon-flaky-tests-work/bead/01-plan-review.md`.

## Scope

Replace the 50 ms per-poll assertion with deterministic test evidence that a poll returns while a peer's response remains withheld. Reuse existing Runtime test fixtures if sufficient; keep the current state-transition, fairness, stale-result and real-foreground checks. This is a separate test-design slice from eon-yooz3's management-close/update fixture fixes.

Out of scope: widening bounds, retries, production changes, changing the 250 ms poll deadline, ORB-C15's ignored latency measurement, contract amendments, packaging or installed observations.

## Acceptance

- No assertion fails merely because the scheduler deschedules a poll thread for over 50 ms.
- A poll that waits on its peer instead of returning pending is detected by a condition-based fixture; retaining state-transition checks alone is insufficient.
- Existing helper callers retain meaningful coverage, with bounded hang safeguards and cleanup of isolated test-owned processes.

## Implementation Notes

Inspect all helper callers and choose a small withheld-response/handshake fixture before editing. Keep response release causally after poll completion. Do not trade the 50 ms assertion for a larger correctness deadline. Product behavior and contracts remain unchanged; seek approval separately if the investigation needs a product decision.

## Verification

Use only the supported `nix develop -c eon-test` isolation. Show the replacement detects waiting on the peer, then show the fixed affected tests survive 20 loaded reruns through the coordinating heavy.sh wrapper and pass the eon-runtime suite. Run fmt and all-target clippy for the touched crate; choose any broader proof under the repository rules in force for that session.

## Stop Conditions

Stop if current-state code has materially drifted or a correct test needs a product/contract change. Record that boundary rather than weakening the tested guarantee.

## Maintenance Notes

title: Tighten the icon-to-value gap inside the CPU, RAM and disk bar chips
description:
## Why

## Goal

Bring the icon and the value visibly closer inside each CPU, RAM and disk chip, for the common one- and two-digit readings, while keeping what eon-wuau8.5 and its predecessor protect: the chip does not change width as the reading changes, and the icon does not jump. The implementer chooses the mechanism (for example a tighter reserved slot, a smaller icon gap or padding, or tabular digit widths), measuring where the space actually goes first (icon gap token, padding, the "100%" reservation, font advance widths).

## Done when

- A rendered capture of the three chips at 8%, 61% and 100% shows the icon-to-value gap visibly smaller than at be4469d, with no chip width change between readings.
- A Venus test pins the new geometry (chip width independent of the value; icon-to-value gap within the chosen bound).
- Configurability (AGENTS.md rule 6): any changed size is either exposed in configuration with its default in docs/CONFIGURATION.md, or this bead records why it stays fixed. venus/docs/PRESENTATION.md chip wording updated if it describes the layout.

Contract: none (presentation). Lucca judges it live after the profile refresh.

## Evidence

- eon-wuau8.5 body: `venus/src/scene.rs` `reading_width` = icon + `tokens::icon_gap` + width of "100%" + 2 x padding; `venus/src/render/chrome.rs` `chip_label_box`, `push_chip_label`.

title: Stop rebuilding Venus accessibility inputs while no assistive tool is active, and send only changed nodes
description:
## Why

Source: "A Critique of GPUI", https://blog.zortax.de/posts/a-critique-of-gpui (2026-11-08). Lucca asked for this review on 2026-11-09 ("get an agent on this"); analysis in ~/.cache/eon-agents/eon-ideas-work/gpui-critique.md (Venus read at edge 97bbd4c). Recommendation 5.

Each `refresh_client_view` (after every Orbit event, venus/src/application.rs:3953, 4305-4318)
refreshes the accessibility inputs: `accessible_content()` walks every cell and the workspace and
dialog are cloned (venus/src/accessibility.rs:1006, 204, 161), even when no assistive tool is
active; the tree itself is built only by `update_if_active` (accessibility.rs:1015). When one is
active, every update sends the full tree with `tree: Some(..)` and one TextRun per row
(accessibility.rs:257-846, 815-818), although node ids are stable (164-205).

## Scope

Measure first (AP-PERF-001): idle and busy-output cost of the refresh with and without an active
assistive tool. Then, if material: skip the input walk while no tool is active and rebuild on
activation; send only changed nodes while one is. VEN-C6 and EON-C8's bounded Orca qualification
must keep passing. Owner: Venus. Portability: neutral (AccessKit on both platforms).

## Acceptance

Recorded before/after measurements; Orca line review still works in one installed check.

## Current evidence, scope and correctness acceptance
At dcaef1c the unconditional scene walk remains in `venus/src/accessibility.rs:1082-1121` (`Accessibility::update`, `accessible_content` at :1112); `Activation::request_initial_tree` at :1047 returns the shared snapshot. `refresh_client_view` is now `application.rs:4840`, with the update at :4913. Refresh line references before implementation.

Measure the two costs separately on an exact build: inactive input extraction, and active full-tree emission. Keep the original measure-first/materiality gate; a no-change result is valid only with the measurements and reason. Do not skip state needed by activation: enabling an assistive tool after idle or busy output must immediately expose the latest text, focus and dialog, without waiting for another terminal event. An incremental update must describe changed nodes, deletions, reparenting and focus consistently; initial/re-activation still supplies a complete valid tree. Existing link accessibility and selection/action routing remain covered.

Use the current AccessKit activation/deactivation owner, not a second accessibility registry. Keep both optimizations if justified; if investigation shows they exceed one fresh session, split inactive extraction from active diff emission before code. Deterministic activation/tree-transition checks and the recorded installed Orca line-review observation are the correctness falsifiers; report both inactive and active before/after CPU costs. Any new dependency or actual VEN-C6/EON-C8 change needs its reference/approval gate. No broader screen-reader/platform qualification is claimed.

title: Start a pane whose agent cannot reach the live window
description:
## Why

Lucca, 2026-11-01, on the overseer's private ~/.cache/eon-agents/eon-overseer/codex-run.sh: "should eon have this ability built-in?" The overseer recommended that Eon own the part that is Eon's problem, and Lucca said "ok".

Today every pane inherits its window's control environment: `EON_TERMINAL`, `EON_TAB`, `EON_WINDOW_RUNTIME_DIR`, `EON_SESSION_BIN` and the rest (supervisor.rs, managed_environment.rs), plus `WAYLAND_DISPLAY`. Usually that is right: AGENTS.md rule 5 wants agents to drive Eon from their terminal. But an agent that builds and tests Eon-like software, starts supervisors, or should not touch the person's live window must not see the live window. The overseer works around it with a script that unsets `EON_*`, `WAYLAND_DISPLAY` and `DISPLAY` before starting Codex headless, which also means the run is invisible (no pane, no attention state).

## Change

An opt-in way to start a pane, tab or `eon run` command whose child does not inherit the window's control environment, for example `eon pane create --isolated -- CMD`:
- Removed: every `EON_*` control variable the window sets, so the `eon` CLI in that pane acts as outside Eon (no caller targeting, no live window). Decide whether `WAYLAND_DISPLAY`/`DISPLAY` go too (a separate `--no-display`, or part of `--isolated`), and whether the session marker variables eon-geigu strips are already gone by then.
- Kept: the managed shell environment (EON-C9 PATH, tools), so the pane still works as an Eon terminal for the person.
- The pane still shows in the window and still reports attention, so a person can watch the agent; it is only the child's control link that is cut.
- Window action and CLI path together (rule 5); the Commands popup entry if any.

## Reference gate

Check how herdr, Rex, Zellij and tmux scope what a pane inherits (e.g. tmux `update-environment`, `-e`), and whether Eon terminals' own features (pane labels, attention via OSC 7501, `eon pane read/send`) depend on `EON_TERMINAL` inside the child. Record findings here.

## Contract

EON-C9 (launch environment), EON-C10 (caller targeting: an isolated pane's CLI is not a caller). Show the exact text first unless an approval mode covers it.

## Acceptance

- Unit test: an isolated launch environment omits the listed variables and keeps PATH and managed tools.
- Integration test: `eon workspace --json` run in an isolated pane behaves as outside Eon.
- Installed check in an isolated root: a Codex or shell run in `--isolated` pane cannot reach the window (`eon pane list` fails as outside), while its pane shows attention.
- USAGE.md, CHANGELOG.

## Prerequisites

Related: eon-geigu (what a terminal inherits from the agent that launched Eon), eon-ciwn.1 (event subscription; the other half of retiring codex-run.sh and wait_pane_done.sh), eon-el45 (agent worktrees).

## Scope

No Codex-specific flags, models or account checks: those stay the user's Codex configuration.

## Corrected mechanism and bounded delivery
This is an epic. The 2026-11-03 and 2026-11-10 comments correct the older "remove variables" mechanism above: unsetting EON_* alone falls back to the live namespace (`supervisor.rs:921`, `base_runtime_directory`, at dcaef1c). Use a fresh private EON_RUNTIME_DIR and the one managed-environment scrub owner, shared with the approved headless design in eon-eon-agent-lr8sx.15. This is accident prevention, not a same-user security boundary (EON-C36); do not claim it makes the live socket inaccessible.

Current command acceptance supersedes the stale names above: from the isolated child, `eon session --json` exits 4 with missing-supervisor before it starts its own supervisor. A child-started supervisor belongs to the private namespace; the visible source pane and its attention remain in the real window. Do not remove managed tools or PATH in pursuit of scrubbing.

First child: reference gate, display-environment choice, shared helper ownership and exact EON-C9/C10 proposal for approval. After that approval, file one bounded launch/CLI implementation child preserving pane, tab and eon run entry points, environment tests, attention, cleanup and installed acceptance. No implementation is authorized by this planning split. The optional window affordance and Commands entry must be settled in that design, with CLI parity; provider flags/models/accounts stay out.

comments.text:

title: Deliver a terminal key's release when another key on the same resolved key starts a capture
description:
## Why

eon-venus-keysym-named-keys-chnh (VEN-C2 named-key resolution) records an accepted gap. Venus pins each native key's resolved key and coalesces two physical keys that resolve to one key. When a terminal press is held and a second physical key on the same resolved key starts a shortcut capture that does not retire the attachment, the terminal press's release is never delivered.

## Repro (reasoned, from Codex review of tree 1acfa397)

caps:backspace plus a configured Alt+Backspace popup. Hold physical Backspace (reaches Orbit), hold Alt, press CapsLock (resolves to Backspace, captured by the popup shortcut). If the popup request fails (for example at workspace capacity) the attachment stays. The first native release is consumed as shared by pin_key; the last is consumed by consumes_shortcut. Orbit never sees Backspace's release and pressed_keys keeps it until the next retirement or native focus loss.

## Scope

venus/src/input.rs InputState pin_key / consumes_shortcut only. Preserve release delivery for an admitted terminal sequence when another native key starts a capture. Out of scope: VEN-C2 text (unchanged), Orbit.

## Acceptance

A focused InputState test covering both release orders through capture and terminal bookkeeping (red before, green after); existing Venus suite, fmt and clippy green.
close_reason: Capture release hands the resolved key's one release to the terminal when it holds that key; red/green test, Venus suite, fmt, clippy green; Claude+Codex clean

comments.text:
Implemented. Not consequential (no dependency, protocol, contract or boundary change; VEN-C2 text unchanged), so no reference gate.

Fix: InputState::consumes_shortcut (venus/src/input.rs). When a captured key's release arrives while the terminal still holds the same resolved key in pressed_keys, the capture ends and the release passes on to the terminal. This happens only when two native keys coalesce on one resolved key (VEN-C2). Each handler in the KeyboardInput chain acts only on Pressed, so the release reaches InputState::key and commit_key. Retiring paths are unchanged: retirement empties pressed_keys. The pin_key doc now names the hand-off.
