title: Dismiss the link-opened notice on its own and never let a notice block links
description:
## Report

Lucca, 2026-10-23: "'link sent to desktop handler' stays forever until you click eon / might not be ideal". He approved the shape the same day ("file", answering the overseer's item: auto-dismiss the success notice after about 2 seconds, keep failure notices until acknowledged, and never let any notice block links).

## Why it matters

After a link opens, the browser takes focus, so the VEN-C8 notice waits for the next input in Eon and lingers. eon-empty-attention-notice-opy3 (landed 8f375fb) found that every VEN-C8 workspace notice outranks the link status and disables link highlight and open while it shows (venus/src/application.rs around 2564 and 3125 at that time). So a lingering link notice silently blocks the next link click.

## Change (VEN-C8 wording to Lucca before code)

- The link-opened success notice dismisses itself after about 2 s, and on the next input as today. It schedules one timed redraw and no repeating ticks.
- Link open failures keep today's lifetime: they persist until the user acts.
- No notice disables link highlight or open. Link hover and click work while any notice shows.
- Configurability rule: record whether the 2 s value is configurable or fixed, and why. The overseer leans toward fixed, a UX timing with no reason for users to differ, unless the audit epic (eon-configurability-qkq8) already plans a notice-duration setting.

## Acceptance

- A Venus model or scene test: the success notice is gone after its timeout with no input, a failure notice persists, and a link is clickable while a notice shows. The test fails on today's code.
- One installed observation: open a link, return to Eon after a few seconds, and the notice is gone.

## Verification

`nix develop -c eon-test -p yazelix-venus`, Venus fmt and clippy, converge plus Codex, and the profile refresh plus the observation.

title: Define Eon as a Linux Wayland product
description:
Contract: revise EON-C7. Consumer: Eon users, release work, and child repositories. Trigger: platform, desktop-backend, or distribution decisions. Result: Eon supports Linux on native Wayland; each channel names the Linux architectures it actually proves. X11, Xwayland, and macOS are outside the product contract. Preserve platform-neutral wire formats and state where they remain the natural owner, without preserving a portability promise or parallel backend. Important failures: public docs, policy, and release design must not claim macOS or X11 support; child implementations must not be changed from this owner-only slice. Prerequisite: user selected Linux/Wayland-only on 2026-08-21. Scope boundary: Eon policy, contracts, distribution design, references, generated agent instructions, and LOC only. Venus backend removal and child policy cleanup require ordered follow-up beads.

## Acceptance Criteria

EON-C7 states the Linux/Wayland-only product contract, distinguishes platform support from each channel exact architecture proof, and claims no runtime proof beyond the accepted x86_64 alpha. README and distribution docs describe macOS, X11, and Xwayland as unsupported rather than deferred targets. Repository-local policy names Linux/Wayland as the sole platform and generated AGENTS.md matches it. The reference route records the adopted foot/Monstar mechanism and rejected cross-platform scope. README LOC is exact. No runtime, component manifest, child repository, or live Session changes occur.

title: List every Eon window, including the default workspace, as open or detached (optional)
description:
## Why

The unified window inventory needs trustworthy open/detached state and attachability. Earlier switcher/naming scope was reduced by Lucca's "do it" on eon-n77e (window/workspace-switching decision, closed); the retained work is optional window-level enrichment. This remains distinct from eon-7cf0y.10 (list every running window across namespaces), which supplies the complete inventory first.

## Evidence and prerequisites

- runtime/crates/eon-runtime/src/windows.rs: default/named namespace listing and window attach.
- runtime/crates/eon-runtime/src/supervisor.rs: canonical presentation attachment state; derive from its owner rather than guess from process names.
- eon-reattach-after-upgrade-n5qv (older-build window reattach, delivered at e3682d5) already presents older-generation windows. The former claim that another generation is always unattachable is obsolete.
- EON-C23/EON-C11/EON-C10 own listing/targeting/attach; inspect current headings and codecs, not the retired v17/v22 line numbers.

## Scope

In: enrich the one inventory from eon-7cf0y.10 (all-window CLI listing) with open/detached state, the default window entry, honest attachability and a reason when unavailable; preserve the existing proposal for `eon window attach ID --json`. Listing data and JSON agree and listing has no side effects. Exact EON-C23 or other boundary wording is proposed to Lucca before code.

Out: names, a picker, workspace/session switching, another inventory owner, compatibility adapters or new cross-generation attach implementation. The broader tab-summary/name proposal was already dropped by the recorded decision, not by this pass. An older generation is not automatically incompatible: report the existing delegated attach path honestly.

## Acceptance

- With a default window, an open named window and a detached named window, the CLI/JSON inventory includes all three with correct state; "default" refers to a window namespace, not one of EON-C33's several workspaces.
- Demonstrate attachability for an older generation through its recorded executable; cover a genuinely unavailable/missing-executable target with the approved reason. Do not infer attachability from generation equality alone.
- Attach JSON describes the approved existing attach outcome; list/inspection never starts, attaches or focuses a window.
- Preserve all generation/start-time/terminal-count/compatibility fields owned by eon-7cf0y.10 (all-window CLI listing).

## Reference gate

Read docs/REFERENCES.md and the recorded comparisons on eon-n77e (window/workspace-switching decision): tmux 3.8, Zellij v0.45.1, WezTerm e2a98e1b, kitty v0.49.2, Superlogical Rex, herdr and TUIOS. Retain detached markers and JSON; reject name-as-identity, guessed merged state and an in-window supervisor swap. If presentation state crosses EONW, name its one owner and obtain contract/wire approval before code.

## Verification

Focused supported process checks via `nix develop -c eon-test` and one isolated installed default/open/detached/older-generation observation. Full affected Rust/Nix route only if the actual EONW/lifecycle boundary changes. Fresh reviews and exact proof records per repository rules.

## Stop Conditions

Stop until complete inventory exists and contract text is approved; stop if targeting/attach semantics need a new user decision, or the same verification failure repeats twice. Preserve live windows and desktop focus.

title: Poll Inspect only while Venus's workspace subscription is down
description:
## Why

Source: "A Critique of GPUI", https://blog.zortax.de/posts/a-critique-of-gpui (2026-11-08). Lucca asked for this review on 2026-11-09 ("get an agent on this"); analysis in ~/.cache/eon-agents/eon-ideas-work/gpui-critique.md (Venus read at edge 97bbd4c). Recommendation 6.

Venus sends a full `Inspect` every 250 ms (venus/src/transport.rs:106-107, 394-406) although it
holds an EON-C39 subscription whose events already trigger an immediate `Inspect`
(transport.rs:479-481, 692-730). eon-61efs.1 kept the poll as a fallback for a refused or ended
subscription. While the subscription is healthy the poll costs four full snapshot builds a second in
the supervisor (supervisor.rs:1594-1639, no equality check on the reply at 3284-3291) and a
snapshot comparison in Venus. eon-ciwn.12 covers the separate event projection, not this poll.

## Scope

Poll `Inspect` at 250 ms only while the subscription is down; while it is up, rely on its events
(optionally a slow heartbeat). Measure idle supervisor and Venus CPU before and after, together
with eon-ciwn.12's measurement. Owner: Venus transport. No wire or contract change expected; check
VEN-C8 and VEN-C18 wording on refresh bounds first.

## Acceptance

Idle CPU recorded before and after; with the subscription refused or ended, Venus still updates
within 250 ms (the eon-61efs.1 acceptance); whole-workspace eon-test passes.

## State-transition acceptance and current evidence
At dcaef1c, `venus/src/transport.rs:395-406` still schedules Inspect unconditionally after recv_timeout; subscription acceptance/follow and refresh coalescing are owned by Subscription. Reuse the existing fake-Eon cases `a_subscription_event_refreshes_the_workspace_at_once` (:2326) and `a_refused_or_ended_subscription_falls_back_to_polling` (:2815).

Acceptance: a healthy accepted subscription produces no periodic full Inspect, while its relevant event still refreshes immediately; initial acceptance/reconnection refreshes state missed before subscription; refusal, EOF, malformed input or reconnect failure restores fallback polling without losing an outstanding action. Return to event-driven refresh after resubscription, without queued duplicate refreshes or busy loops. Measure the configured 250 ms fallback cadence using causal fixtures rather than making scheduler delay a new correctness failure. No optional slow heartbeat is selected; if evidence requires one, propose its need/default/configuration before adding it. Retain docs' current refresh promises and EON-C39/VEN-C8/VEN-C18 approval stop if they actually need amendment. Owner: Venus transport; portability disposition: neutral. Focused transport checks plus one installed idle/subscription-loss observation accompany the before/after CPU record.

title: Return an agent pane's recent turns from its own transcript (eon pane turns --json)
description:
Problem: a phone bridge (eon-7jw6p), the sidebar, or another agent needs what an agent just said or asked without scraping a full-screen TUI; Alma shows people want this. Related: eon-2va3d, eon-duebo.
Do: use the stable session ID (eon-dol0n) to find the Pi, Claude or Codex transcript and return the last N messages and any pending question. Read-only and same-user; unknown agents fall back to pane read. Check Atuin Threads' read APIs first. Owners: Runtime and Eon CLI.
Source: Alma/Pi research, /home/lucca/pjs/refs/alma-pi-research/REPORT.md idea 4.

## Bounded design and delivery
This is an epic. The three providers' transcripts are independent, versioned sources, not one uniform API. First child: inspect Atuin Threads and exact Pi/Claude/Codex sources, map provider conversation identities from eon-dol0n, propose the bounded turns/pending-question JSON schema and authorization/failure behavior, then obtain exact EON-C approval before code. Reading same-user files still needs an explicit authorization and data exposure policy; define whether/how terminal_access gates this path and any pane-read fallback.

After approval, file bounded Runtime reader slices by provider (combine only when one fresh session truly covers them) and one shared CLI integration/proof slice. Keep all three named providers and unknown-agent fallback in the overall outcome. No screen/TUI inference of turns or questions. Keep IDs separate from Eon session/tab/pane identity, do not guess transcript paths or execute a transcript, and define missing/truncated/malformed/oversize/live-changing files, unsupported versions and unknown pending-question state without fabricated messages. The approved schema must bound N/output size and preserve source ordering. No writes to provider transcripts, cloud transmission or second conversation registry.

Overall acceptance: with isolated fixtures for each provider, the CLI returns that pane's last requested turns and only evidenced pending questions, changes no provider data or UI focus, refuses unauthorized paths, and behaves as approved for unknown agents. Record exact format versions, focused reader/CLI checks, docs/config defaults and one isolated installed observation; a fixture alone does not prove the installed provider association.

## Dependency placement
br propagates an epic's blockers to its design children. Keep eon-dol0n.2 related here so eon-m33i1.1 can research first; when the approved transcript delivery child is filed, add its blocking dependency on eon-dol0n.2 (the stable provider association), not on eon-dol0n.3's reboot restoration. title: Turn stacked rows' corners toward the expanded pane and join their sides
description:
## Why

Lucca, 2026-10-24, on eon-2x6h's stacked collapsed rows (installed, after eon-54jv): "can we extend the
borders from the rounded edges into the edges of the visible pane of the stack? tiny nit", then, on the
rows below the expanded pane: "lol. these guys are pointing down instead of up". Today every collapsed
row draws its card's rounded top edge with short corner hooks that curl down, also below the expanded
pane, and the hooks stop after one corner radius, so the stack's sides are broken curls.

## Behaviour

- A collapsed row's corner hooks turn toward the column's expanded pane: rows above it curl down, rows
  below it curl up.
- Its sides continue in that direction to the next card, so each side of the stack is one continuous
  line with rounded joints that meets the expanded pane's frame.
- Neutral rows use the border width; the selected pane's focus frame stays its own rounded frame, and
  no neutral paint lies under it (eon-e8hh/eon-f5pg rule).
- Labels, fill (eon-54jv), rows (33/31/30), hit targets and AccessKit unchanged.

## Contract

VEN-C8 collapsed-row sentence; wording to Lucca before code.

## Acceptance

- Venus paint test (fails first): hooks above the expanded pane point down and below it point up;
  continuous sides from the top row to the expanded frame and from it to the bottom row; no neutral
  paint under the focus frame; scales 1 and 1.3; widths 1/1, 1/2, 2/2; first/middle/last selected.
- Isolated capture with Lucca's opacity: a stack with rows above and below the expanded pane.

Portability: neutral.

title: Report created IDs exactly for every creating request, pending-tab picks and dismissals included (EONW)
description:
## Why

eon-1jeai adds `created: {tab, pane}` to the JSON replies of `pane create`, `tab create` and `edit`, inferred in the CLI from the reply snapshot: the supervisor serializes requests and IDs only grow, so the highest new ID is this request's. Two other requests can also start a pane: a directory pick on a pending tab (`tab directory`) and a pending pair's `popup hide`. They do not report `created`. The CLI cannot tell exactly whether this request started the pane: two racing picks get identical replies, and a retarget (workspace.rs ~2431, which parks a live Agent popup as an ordinary pane) can allocate a pane on a tab that already has panes. Found by Codex in eon-1jeai's review; scope split by eon-overseer 2026-11-06 (option C). The full analysis is in eon-1jeai's review ledger.

## What

The runtime records what each request created (tab and/or pane, set inside dispatch: create_tab, launch_tab, start_pane_in, retarget parking, finish_pending_tab), and the snapshot reply carries it. The CLI prints it as-is for every action, `workspace new` included, and drops eon-1jeai's max-ID inference. This is an EONW codec change, so it needs an EONW bump (codec, goldens, version, Venus rebuild). Never amend EONW in place. It could ride the EONW bump planned in eon-7cf0y.22 S3, if the timing fits.

## Acceptance

- Every request that creates a tab or pane reports exactly what it created, including the two pending-tab cases and retarget parking. Racing picks report correctly (one gets the pane, the other none).
- The contract sentence from eon-1jeai is widened to every creating request.

Filed by eon-overseer 2026-11-06; filed only, not started.

## Current owners and acceptance detail
At dcaef1c, CLI inference remains in `runtime/crates/eon-runtime/src/cli.rs:1707-1768` and helper :1937. Runtime creation owners are `workspace.rs` create_tab :1792, launch_tab :1839, start_pane_in :2453, finish_pending_tab :2503 and retarget :2878. Extend the one dispatch result, not a second ID allocator or CLI snapshot heuristic. Read current EONW v40 and its known consumers before proposing the next version; eon-7cf0y.22 S3 is historical timing advice, not an available future bump to amend.

The public command is now `session new` (formerly workspace new); preserve created_persistent_id as well as created local IDs and existing human output. Test each creating path, a no-create pending dismissal/pick, racing picks, retarget parking in a nonempty tab, and failed/refused requests. Replies identify only IDs created by that request in the approved result shape, including multiple effects if the design permits them; do not silently guess a scalar when one request can allocate several. Versioned codec/goldens, Runtime, CLI and Venus consumer all ship together. Exact widened EON-C10/request-result wording and schema require approval before code; this pass approves neither. Use focused causal Runtime/CLI checks, the required shared-wire Rust/Nix route and one isolated installed creating-request observation; document JSON/help/changelog. Portability disposition: neutral.

title: Launch Eon on Apple Silicon macOS: agents port and prove it, Yu checks last
description:
## Why

Lucca wants Eon to launch with Apple Silicon macOS support, with agents doing nearly all of the
port and proof on Linux plus automated Mac runs, and Yu doing only a short final check. Historical starting point (2026-10-27; superseded by the completed port):
Eon could not build for `aarch64-darwin`: `flake.nix:62` hardcodes `x86_64-linux`, every
component in `components/eon-v4.json` targets `x86_64-linux`, and Eon Runtime reads Linux
peer credentials and `/proc` unguarded (`runtime/crates/eon-runtime/src/sessions.rs:424-458`,
`:572-593`), so on macOS it would fail to compile, and if it compiled it would treat every live
terminal as dead (`:767`, `:1386`).

Native history: ORB-C14 passed on the old Rust Orbit at `4910b81` (`eon-orb-c14-mac-reproof-l8rz`)
and is "Not proved for this tree" after the Bend swap (`orbit/docs/CONTRACTS.md:809-841`). VEN-C16
has a partial native proof at `e0aa47e` on one scale-1 VNC display (`eon-z4n6`;
`venus/docs/CONTRACTS.md:1053-1090`: Retina, Kotoeri IME, renderer recovery not observed; Han
blank and some emoji uncomposed with stock fonts). Full Eon (EON-C7,
`eon-prove-full-eon-apple-silicon-macos-t8o`) never ran on a Mac. The Scaleway Mac was deleted
on 2026-10-20.

## Lucca's direction (relayed by eon-overseer, 2026-10-27; his words)

> "Yu is time constrained and already has ssh on his plate. i'd rather test everything possible
> and fix myself, letting to Yu only final testing and final fixes that i missed. we can even give
> him a list of tests to run (without overwhelmiing him). so the more automated, the better."

On launching: "it would be nice to launch with mac support, and we already have yu and his
friends". He also approved: "Yu's friends start only after full Eon builds and launches on Yu's
Mac with the Orbit and Venus suites passing; the README lists the macOS gaps; their patches
count as outside contributions."

Standing constraints: no slow manual VNC proof; everything on a remote Mac is driven over SSH,
GUI captures included (memory `no-slow-manual-vnc-proof`, decision on
`ven-prove-venus-apple-silicon-macos-nm7` 2026-10-18). Hosted macOS stays within R$100/month
(`eon-prove-full-eon-apple-silicon-macos-t8o`, 2026-09-11). Nix-only, Apple Silicon only; no
signing, notarization, DMG, Homebrew or Intel macOS (`eon-hzq` owns distribution).

## Original rollout, in order (historical; .1 through .44 are closed)

1. Map compile errors and Linux-only assumptions from Linux (gate + sweep).
2. Port Runtime peer identity and liveness to macOS.
3. Venus CPU/RAM chips on macOS.
4. Remaining Linux-only runtime assumptions (runtime dir, socket path bound, notification).
5. Runtime and Eon test suites runnable on macOS (Darwin `eon-test`).
6. Admit `aarch64-darwin` in the one component manifest.
7. `aarch64-darwin` flake outputs, evaluated from Linux.
8. macOS proof harness, part 1: build and suites.
9. macOS proof harness, part 2: GUI scenario, Retina probe, Yu's evidence command.
10. Decision: GitHub Actions macOS job (not scope until Lucca decides; blocks nothing).
11. Yu's guided final check: one command, at most ten items, one evidence bundle.
12. Remote batch: one rented Mac for 24 h (needs Lucca's go), fix loop, record proofs, dry-run
    Yu's check.
13. Yu runs the check; his findings are fixed or accepted as gaps.
14. Friends' gate: README gaps, preview wording (`eon-igae.5`), AGENTS.md Status.

Children 2-4 and 6 can run in parallel after 1 (2 and 4 both touch Runtime: land 2 first).
Each child is one session; 12 and 13 wait on a Mac and on Yu.

Existing beads this epic feeds, not duplicates: `eon-prove-full-eon-apple-silicon-macos-t8o`
(EON-C7; blocked by the batch), `ven-prove-venus-apple-silicon-macos-nm7` and its children
`c3b`, `yzw`, `piy` (VEN-C16; the harness gathers their automatable evidence),
`eon-igae.6` (Retina for the 1.0 preview; blocked by Yu's run), `eon-igae.5` (tier wording;
blocks the friends' gate), `eon-agent-background-work-yte0.1` (its Darwin path is compiled by
the gate and run natively by the harness), and the recipes in closed `eon-orb-c14-mac-reproof-l8rz`
and `eon-z4n6`.

## Acceptance

- Full Eon builds from this repository's flake on `aarch64-darwin` and launches natively from the
  harness, with ORB-C14's Orbit suite, Venus's suite and Runtime's suite passing natively;
  ORB-C14, VEN-C16 and EON-C7 proof records name the exact revision, Mac, macOS and artifacts.
- Yu has run a checklist of at most ten items on his Mac and reported through one evidence
  command; what he found is fixed or listed as a README gap.
- README lists the macOS gaps and the preview tier text approved on `eon-igae.5`; only then do
  Yu's friends start.
- Linux proofs stay green: `x86_64-linux` derivations unchanged unless a child says why.

## Stop conditions (all children)

- Any contract add/change (EON-C, ORB-C, VEN-C wording or status beyond a proof record) stops for
  Lucca's approval.
- Renting a Mac stops for Lucca's explicit go on the cost.
- A new dependency, toolchain input, language or CI workflow stops for Lucca's decision.
- A platform blocker (AGENTS.md "Platform Discipline") stops for Lucca's choice.

    
## Current state (source 2e93c69; Beads snapshot 2026-11-12)
The old compile-failure and never-ran paragraphs above are historical. components/eon-v5.json:5
admits both targets; docs/CONTRACTS.md:425 (EON-C7) records a partial full-Eon native proof at
0e47d26; orbit/docs/CONTRACTS.md:941 marks ORB-C14 Proved; venus/docs/CONTRACTS.md:1401 keeps
VEN-C16 partial. These records do not prove a later candidate.
Open children are .45, .46, .50, .51, .59, .60 and .61. Read their own titles/acceptance;
.54 is now closed, superseding the 2026-11-10 follow-up list. The epic remains their container.
The above-window selection-drag check requested on 2026-11-03 is tracked in .61; no recorded
native result is inferred and no duplicate is needed. Preserve all approved preview and cost constraints.

title: Map Eon's macOS compile errors and Linux-only assumptions from Linux
description:
## Why

Agents on Linux cannot build or run `aarch64-darwin`, so the cheapest early signal is a Rust
compile check for the Apple target plus a sweep for Linux-only assumptions. This bead produces
the exact list the port beads fix, so no Mac time is spent finding compile errors.

Lucca (2026-10-27, relayed by eon-overseer): "i'd rather test everything possible and fix myself,
letting to Yu only final testing and final fixes that i missed ... so the more automated, the
better."

## Evidence

- `rustup target list --installed` on this machine includes `aarch64-apple-darwin` (outside the
  Nix dev shell; nixpkgs `rustc` ships only the host std).
- Preliminary sweep at `4ae8a21` (verify and extend):
  - `runtime/crates/eon-runtime/src/sessions.rs:424-458` `validate_management_peer`:
    `libc::ucred`/`SO_PEERCRED` (absent on Apple targets, so a compile error) and
    `/proc/<pid>/stat` start time. Owner: Runtime port bead.
  - `sessions.rs:572-593` `recorded_process_is_dead`: `/proc` NotFound means dead; callers `:767`,
    `:1386` would retire every live terminal on macOS. Owner: Runtime port bead.
  - `runtime/crates/eon-runtime/src/supervisor.rs:681-692` `base_runtime_directory`: macOS has no
    `XDG_RUNTIME_DIR`, so every launch warns and falls back to `$TMPDIR/eon-<uid>`
    (`/var/folders/...`, long). macOS `sun_path` is 104 bytes. Owner: remaining-assumptions bead.
  - `runtime/crates/eon-runtime/src/notification.rs:10,44-51`: first-detach notification is
    Linux-only (zbus); macOS is a silent no-op. Owner: remaining-assumptions bead.
  - `venus/src/system.rs:13-19,93-99`: CPU/RAM from `/proc`; `None` elsewhere. Owner: Venus chips bead.
  - Tests: `sessions.rs:1676,1819,1938`, `supervisor.rs:2156-2161,2290`, and about 25 `/proc`
    reads in `eon/crates/eon/tests/workspace_control.rs`; `nix/test-sandbox.nix` needs bubblewrap.
    Owner: tests bead.
  - Already split: `orbit/src/platform.rs` (Linux/macOS seams), `orbit/build.rs:46-48`,
    `orbit/tests/lifecycle.rs` (3 Linux-only tests), `venus/src/launch.rs:424-427`,
    `venus/src/application.rs`, Venus render tests (`#[cfg(target_os = "linux")]`, ignored).
  - Nix: `flake.nix:62`, `:202` (CodexBar linux-musl asset), `:320-348` (X11/Wayland libs, Mesa,
    fontconfig), `:875` (kinestra recorder, `x86_64-linux` only), `:888-919` bundle relink
    (`relink/src/main.rs:20` ld-linux), `:919-934` br/bv Linux assets, `:652` manifest target
    assert; `components/eon-v4.json` targets. Owners: manifest and flake beads.

## Scope

In scope: run the check; extend the sweep (also `std::os::linux`, `/sys`, `/dev/shm`, `pidfd`,
`epoll`, `inotify`, `prctl`, `MSG_NOSIGNAL`, `SOCK_CLOEXEC`, `accept4`, `pipe2`, `O_PATH`,
`getrandom`, Wayland-only env, shell scripts under `nix/` and `eon/`); record results as a comment
on this bead and on each owning sibling bead; fix nothing except trivially mis-scoped `cfg`s that
block the check for other crates (if any, one commit, Codex per AGENTS.md).

Out of scope: the fixes owned by sibling beads; Nix changes; a permanent Nix route for the check.

## Acceptance

- One exact command per crate (`cargo check --locked --target aarch64-apple-darwin -p <crate>
  --all-targets` where possible) with its result for: `orbit-protocol`, `eon-workspace-protocol`,
  `eon-manifest`, `eon-runtime`, `eon`, `yazelix-venus`, `yazelix-orbit`. Crates whose build
  scripts cannot run for the Apple target on Linux (likely `libghostty-vt-sys` via Zig and the
  Apple SDK, and Orbit's Bun/clang worker) are named with the failing step.
- The sweep list above, confirmed or corrected with `file:line`, each item assigned to a sibling
  bead or recorded as already handled.
- `yte0.1`'s Darwin `proc_listchildpids` path is included if it has landed.

## Verification

- The commands and outputs summarized on the bead (first error per crate). No proof claim: a
  compile check is not native proof (EON-C7 rejects compile-only claims).

## Stop Conditions

- Stop if making the check permanent needs a new flake input (rust-overlay, fenix) or a CI job:
  that is a dependency/CI decision for Lucca.
- Stop if a finding needs a contract change or a platform blocker.

## Maintenance Notes

- Rejected: adding the Apple std to the Nix dev shell in this bead (dependency gate).
- This list is the input to beads 2-7 of the epic; keep it on this bead so they can cite it.
close_reason: Map recorded at 66b32d5: per-crate aarch64-apple-darwin cargo check results and the Linux-only sweep, on this bead and on kz4p.2-.9, .16 and yte0.1; open questions 1-4 for Lucca via eon-overseer. No code change.

title: Decide whether a GitHub Actions macOS job builds and tests Eon for aarch64-darwin
description:
## Decision needed (Lucca)

Should a GitHub Actions job on GitHub's Apple Silicon macOS runners build Eon for
`aarch64-darwin` and run the harness's headless parts (and optionally its GUI scenario)?
This is a decision, not scope: it adds a workflow (AP-CI-001), needs pushes to `edge` to run,
and costs runner minutes. Nothing is implemented until Lucca answers.

Lucca (2026-10-27, relayed by eon-overseer): "i'd rather test everything possible and fix myself,
letting to Yu only final testing and final fixes that i missed ... so the more automated, the
better."

## Evidence

- `gh repo view` on 2026-10-27: `Yazelix/eon` is PUBLIC. GitHub's standard hosted runners,
  including the Apple Silicon macOS ones, are free for public repositories (verify current
  terms when deciding).
- `.github/workflows/cachix.yml` already builds `x86_64-linux` on push to `edge` and publishes the
  runtime closure to the `eon-yazelix` Cachix cache; a Darwin job could push the Darwin closure
  too, so Yu and his friends install without compiling Rust, Ghostty and Helix on their Macs.
- `ven-qualify-venus-stack-apple-silicon-macos-ili` closed Conditional-Go from GitHub Actions run
  34809546212 on a standard M1: wgpu Metal, glyphon, AccessKit, AppKit window creation and
  visible presentation initialized there (per `ven-prove-venus-apple-silicon-macos-nm7`). So a
  runner can likely run Venus and the GUI scenario, at a virtual display without Retina.
- `eon-prove-full-eon-apple-silicon-macos-t8o` already planned "bounded standard Apple Silicon
  GitHub-hosted jobs first" for automated child and composition checks.

## Options

1. Workflow-dispatch and push-to-`edge` job on `macos-15` (arm64): `nix build` of the Darwin
   package, Darwin checks, `eon-test`, harness `run` (and `scenario` if the runner's GUI session
   allows), evidence uploaded as an artifact with short retention, Darwin closure pushed to
   Cachix. Bounded: one job, timeout, concurrency cancel, no fork secrets, repository guard as in
   `cachix.yml`.
2. Workflow-dispatch only (agents trigger it for a candidate), no push trigger.
3. No CI; rely on the rental and Yu.

## Recommendation

Option 2 first, then option 1 once green. Reason: on a public repository it gives agents a free
native Darwin build-and-test loop from Linux sessions, so the fix loop happens before any paid
rental; it can shrink or remove the rental, and the Cachix push makes Yu's install fast. Retina,
IME, VoiceOver and real-GPU behavior still need a physical Mac (Yu).

## Open sub-questions for Lucca

- Is a GitHub VM run (Apple Virtualization on Apple Silicon) acceptable as native proof for
  ORB-C14 and the suite parts of VEN-C16/EON-C7, or only as candidate evidence before the
  bare-metal batch? Recommendation: candidate evidence only, plus suite proof for ORB-C14 if he
  agrees; GUI proof stays on bare metal or Yu's Mac.

## Acceptance (if approved)

Lucca's answer is quoted on this bead with date; if he approves, a separate implementation bead
(or this bead retyped to a task) names the workflow file, triggers, permissions, timeout,
artifacts, cache behavior and its removal condition per AP-CI-001, and is proved by one green
workflow run on the candidate revision.
close_reason: Decided 2026-10-27 (Lucca, relayed by eon-overseer, comments on this bead): '1 ok' = a GitHub Actions macOS job, run by hand at first (option 2, then option 1 once green); '2 ok' = a runner VM is candidate evidence plus ORB-C14 suite proof, never GUI proof. Implementation: eon-mac-launch-kz4p.15, which now blocks the rental kz4p.12 ('only after the harness passes on CI', kz4p.12's '3 ok').

title: Build Yu's guided macOS final check: one command, ten items, one bundle
description:
## Why

Yu has little time ("Yu is time constrained and already has ssh on his plate"). His check must
be short, guided and self-reporting: one command that walks him through at most ten items,
captures evidence for each, and produces one bundle he sends back. This bead builds that guided
mode and the list; the next sibling is Yu actually running it.

Lucca (2026-10-27, relayed by eon-overseer): "i'd rather test everything possible and fix myself,
letting to Yu only final testing and final fixes that i missed. we can even give him a list of
tests to run (without overwhelmiing him). so the more automated, the better."

## Evidence

- Yu has a Mac mini; Retina needs a HiDPI monitor (scale 2), which no remote Mac we used had
  (`venus/docs/CONTRACTS.md:1053`, 1920x1080 scale 1).
- Items no remote run has observed: Retina redraw, Kotoeri IME (`venus/docs/CONTRACTS.md:1081`),
  Han/emoji with stock fonts (`:1085-1086`), a real Claude agent in the sidebar (EON-C31), Yazi
  images on the installed Eon on macOS, detach/attach by hand.
- Harness tool and evidence layout: the two harness siblings.

## Scope

In scope: a `final` subcommand of the harness tool, run by Yu as one command (e.g.
`nix run github:Yazelix/eon/<tag-or-rev>#mac-proof -- final`), which installs or runs the exact
build, then for each item prints one or two lines of what to do, waits for Enter, takes a
`screencapture` (asks for Screen Recording permission once, explaining why), asks pass/fail plus
an optional note, and finally writes `eon-mac-final-<rev>-<date>.tar.gz` with versions, hardware
and display info, logs, captures and answers. A short `docs/DEVELOPMENT.md` (or README "Mac
preview" link) section with the same list for reading ahead.

Proposed list (at most ten; final wording on this bead before code):
1. Install and launch: the command above opens Eon; `eon versions` shows `aarch64-darwin`.
2. Retina: on the HiDPI monitor, text is crisp; the tool records backing scale 2.
3. Resize and move the window between the HiDPI and another display, if he has one (skip
   otherwise).
4. Typing and IME: type in a shell; switch to a Japanese or Chinese input source and compose one
   word.
5. Fonts: `cat` a prepared file with Han, emoji (modifier and flag), combining marks.
6. Tabs, panes and popups by keyboard: new tab, split, Alt+Z zoom, Helix and Yazi popups.
7. Yazi image preview of a prepared PNG.
8. Agent sidebar: start `claude` in a pane, ask one short question, see working then done.
9. Copy and paste with Command+C/Command+V to and from another app.
10. Detach and attach: quit the window, run `eon attach`, the shell history is still there.
Plus automatic, no action: the harness suites summary from his Mac (`run`), since the friends'
gate requires "the Orbit and Venus suites passing" on Yu's Mac.

How to report: send the tarball to Lucca (channel Lucca names); failures become beads.

Out of scope: VoiceOver and blur (unless Lucca adds them), fixes (next sibling), anything that
needs ssh access to Yu's Mac.

## Acceptance

- `final --dry-run` walks the list without capturing; the full `final` was run once on the rented
  Mac in the batch bead (sibling) and its bundle reviewed.
- The list has at most ten manual items, each with expected result in one sentence.
- Deterministic parts (bundle manifest, answer recording) have a few tests; fmt, clippy, Codex.

## Verification

- `nix develop -c eon-test -p <harness crate>` exits 0.
- One dry-run bundle attached to this bead's notes (path outside the repository).

## Stop Conditions

- Stop for Lucca's approval of the final list wording before building (one comment, numbered).
- Stop if any item needs Yu to install extra software beyond Nix and `claude`.
close_reason: final built and dry-run proved on Linux (fmt, clippy Linux and darwin, eon-test -p mac-proof, nix run .#mac-proof -- final --help, dry-run bundle); Opus gates plus Codex review clean. The one native final run and its bundle review are kz4p.12's acceptance.

Plan (yufinal, Opus planner; Codex implements, Opus gates), 2026-10-28, on edge a36f243.

Approval relayed by eon-overseer (AP-COORDINATOR-001): Lucca, 2026-10-27, "do these two too, then ... i want to move closer to the 'yu testing' gate", standing for the macOS launch path. It covers this bead's build; it does not cover push, promotion, GitHub posts, workflow dispatch or a rented Mac.

## Q1 for Lucca: the revised list (stop condition; code waits for his answer)

The 2026-10-27 approval ("9 okay") was for the drafted ten. kz4p.9 and kz4p.17 now automate four of them, so the list shrinks to eight. Each item below is what `final` prints, then the expected result.

Done automatically first, with no action from Yu: the whole `run` on his Mac. That covers the package build, terminfo, the flake checks, the Orbit, Venus and Runtime suites, and the GUI scenario. The scenario covers launch, `eon versions` naming aarch64-darwin, Retina scale 2, panes, tabs, Files, zoom, Shortcuts, Kitty images, Command+V paste, detach/attach, crash, adoption and leftovers. That retires drafted items 1 (install and launch) and 10 (detach and attach). It also halves item 9: only Command+C on a pointer selection is still manual, as the scenario's help says.

1. Look. On a Retina screen (HiDPI monitor or a MacBook's display), look at Eon's window.
   Expected: text and the Eon Bar are sharp, not blurry, and the bar's CPU and RAM chips show numbers that change.
2. Second display (answer s to skip if you have only one). Drag the window to the other display and back, then resize it.
   Expected: text stays sharp on each display and the panes refit with no gaps or garbage.
3. Typing and input methods. Type `echo hello` and press Return. Then switch to a Japanese or Chinese input source, compose one word and commit it.
   Expected: the composition shows at the cursor and the committed word lands in the shell.
4. Fonts. Run `cat glyphs.txt`.
   Expected: Han characters, emoji (one with a skin tone, one flag) and accented letters each show as one glyph, with no empty boxes or overlaps.
5. Keyboard. Open Shortcuts with Option+/. Then use the keys it lists to open a tab, split a pane, move between panes and open the Helix popup.
   Expected: each key does what Shortcuts says.
6. Yazi images. Open Files with Option+Shift+Y and select `eon.png`.
   Expected: the picture shows in Yazi's preview.
7. Agent. In a pane, run `claude` (Claude Code 2.1.295 or later) and ask one short question.
   Expected: the sidebar marks the agent working, then done when it answers.
8. Copy out. Select text in Eon with the pointer, press Command+C and paste into another app (for example Notes).
   Expected: the same text arrives.

Out of scope, as drafted: VoiceOver and blur. Recommendation: approve these eight. Each is something no automated step observes, and each costs Yu about a minute.

## Implementation plan

All of it lives in `eon/tools/mac-proof`, plus the flake app and docs. No new crate dependency, protocol, contract or trust boundary is added, so this is not a consequential shape and needs no reference gate. Yu's Mac is driven only by the tool he runs himself, with no ssh.

What Yu types is one command: `nix run github:Yazelix/eon/<rev>#mac-proof -- final`. The flow:

1. **Preflight.** Require Apple Silicon macOS (dry runs excepted). Check both grants with `mac::grants()`. If either is missing, explain why it is needed: Screen Recording for the captures, Accessibility for the scenario's keys. Then open the matching System Settings pane and exit 2 before any long work, telling Yu to grant his terminal app, reopen it and rerun.
2. **Source.** The flake app's wrapper sets `MAC_PROOF_SOURCE=${self}` and `MAC_PROOF_REV=${self.rev or "dirty"}`. This goes in a small app wrapper, not in the cargo derivation, so the crate does not rebuild per commit. `final` copies that tree into a fresh temp directory and makes it writable. `run`'s source step already commits an archive extraction, so the copy can feed it. Without `MAC_PROOF_SOURCE`, `final` uses the current directory, as `run` does.
3. **Automatic part.** `final` calls the same steps `run` does, with evidence in `<out>/run`, under `caffeinate -d -i -s -w <own pid>` so the Mac stays awake. It first prints that the run takes hours, that Yu must leave the Mac awake and untouched until it rings, and that the GUI scenario types into Eon. It rings (BEL plus `osascript display notification`) when the manual part starts.
4. **Manual part.** If the package step passed, `final` launches Eon from the built package. Yu's real HOME and environment stay, so his shell setup and logged-in `claude` work. Eon's own state is private: `EON_CONFIG_HOME`, `XDG_STATE_HOME` and `EON_RUNTIME_DIR` go under a private root. The launch directory holds `glyphs.txt` and `eon.png`, copied from `assets/eon.png`. For each item, `final`:
   - prints the item and waits for Enter;
   - re-attaches Eon if Venus is gone;
   - captures only Eon's window, with `screencapture -x -R` on its bounds from `mac::windows`;
   - asks `p`, `f` or `s` and an optional note.

   After the last item it runs `eon stop all` and copies Eon's logs.
5. **Bundle.** `final` writes the evidence folder and the archive in HOME:
   - folder `<out>` (default `~/eon-mac-final-<rev12>-<YYYY-MM-DD>`, then `-2` and up if it exists), holding `summary.txt`, `final.json` (schema 1: rev, tree, date, run result, items with answer, note, capture and seconds), `run/`, `manual/`, `versions.txt` and `displays.json`;
   - archive `<out>.tar.gz`, beside the folder.

   It prints the archive's path and that Yu can look inside before sending it to Lucca.

Reuse, not parallel code:
- **Scenario.** Its environment becomes a parameter: private HOME, or Yu's own with private Eon roots. `final` reuses `start`, `wait_for_workspace`, `wait_for_venus`, `reattach`, `act`, `stop` and `clean` through a narrow pub surface.
- **retina.rs.** `report` writes `displays.json`, and `mac::displays` supplies the display list.
- **run.rs.** `run`'s step list is shared between `run` and `final`.
- **Privacy fix in a shared owner.** A new pure function strips serial numbers and hardware UUIDs from `system_profiler` JSON. Both run's host step and the scenario's retina report use it. `uname -a` becomes `uname -srm` (no hostname). Only Yu's bundle goes to a person, but one owner fixes both.

Pure and tested on Linux, run with `nix develop -c eon-test -p mac-proof`:
- the item table: eight or fewer items, each with a one-sentence expected result;
- answer parsing: p/f/s, a re-ask on anything else, and EOF making the rest "unanswered";
- `final.json` and `summary.txt`;
- the bundle name and the civil date computed from Unix time (no new dependency);
- the redaction;
- an integration test: `final --dry-run` with scripted stdin writes a `.tar.gz` whose listing and `final.json` match. The dry run walks the list without launching or capturing.

Mac-only, proved only in kz4p.12's rented-Mac batch: grants, caffeinate, the manual launch, the window capture and the full flow.

Scope boundary: the `final` subcommand, the shared refactors above, the redaction, the flake app wrapper, and a short "Yu's final check" subsection in `docs/DEVELOPMENT.md` (command, item titles, where the bundle goes). The README is left alone. Out of scope: running the list on a Mac (kz4p.12, kz4p.13), fixes to what it finds, VoiceOver and blur, and any change to the scenario's steps or run's step order.

Checks:
- `nix develop -c eon-test -p mac-proof`;
- `cargo fmt --check`;
- clippy `-D warnings` for mac-proof on Linux and `--target aarch64-apple-darwin`;
- `nix build .#mac-proof` on Linux and an eval of the aarch64-darwin app;
- one dry-run bundle, kept outside the repository and named on this bead;
- the Codex review AGENTS.md requires.

title: Run the macOS harness on one rented Mac and record ORB-C14, VEN-C16 and EON-C7 proof
description:
## Why

The ported code, Darwin flake outputs and harness are proved only by running them on a Mac. One
bounded rental, driven entirely over SSH by the harness, should turn the candidate into recorded
native proofs for ORB-C14, the suite and launch parts of VEN-C16, and EON-C7, and fix what
breaks while the Mac is still rented. Yu then only checks what a remote Mac cannot show.

Lucca (2026-10-27, relayed by eon-overseer): "i'd rather test everything possible and fix myself,
letting to Yu only final testing and final fixes that i missed. we can even give him a list of
tests to run (without overwhelmiing him). so the more automated, the better."

## Evidence

- Previous rental: Scaleway M2-M, fr-par-1, macOS 26.7.1, 24 h minimum; ORB-C14 (old Rust Orbit)
  and the VEN-C16 baseline were run from it (`eon-orb-c14-mac-reproof-l8rz`, `eon-z4n6`).
  Deleted 2026-10-20 (`ven-prove-venus-apple-silicon-macos-nm7` comment). Hosted macOS ceiling
  R$100/month (`eon-prove-full-eon-apple-silicon-macos-t8o`, 2026-09-11).
- Proof records to write: ORB-C14 "Open proof" (`orbit/docs/CONTRACTS.md:835-841`); VEN-C16
  native environment and gaps (`venus/docs/CONTRACTS.md:1053-1090`); EON-C7 "Open proof"
  (`docs/CONTRACTS.md:345-355`). AGENTS.md: "Do not mark a contract `Proven` from a document or
  mock"; proof records cite check, exact revisions, platform and artifact.

## Scope

In scope:
1. Ask Lucca for the go on one 24 h rental (Scaleway M2 or a cheaper equivalent he names), with
   the expected cost against the R$100/month ceiling. If the CI decision bead approved a runner
   route, first run the harness there and rent only for what remains.
2. Prepare the Mac over SSH only: Nix install, GUI auto-login if needed, the TCC items the
   harness probe reports (any click goes to Lucca as one short request, with "defer to Yu" as the
   alternative).
3. `mac-proof remote` on the frozen candidate (coordinate a branch freeze with eon-overseer per
   AP-COORDINATOR-001); fix failures on Linux in their owning code with focused commits (each
   through its normal review), re-run the harness on the new candidate; stop new fixes with
   enough rental left for one final full run on the final revision (AGENTS.md "Batch proof").
4. Dry-run Yu's guided check (sibling) on the Mac so Yu's first run is not its first run.
5. Record proofs from the final run only: ORB-C14 (Orbit suite natively), VEN-C16 native
   environment and observations updated (still partial unless piy's acceptance is met), EON-C7
   evidence (full Eon on `aarch64-darwin`); status changes beyond proof records need Lucca's
   approval. Record the evidence folder location and keep it outside the repository.
6. Cleanup: Lucca deletes the server; record the deletion.

Out of scope: VoiceOver, Kotoeri IME and blur acceptance (`c3b`, `yzw`), Retina proof unless the
remote display offers scale 2 (harness reports it), distribution (`eon-hzq`).

## Acceptance

- The harness's final `summary.txt` on the final revision shows every suite and scenario step
  passing or `skipped` with a reason that is on Yu's list.
- ORB-C14, VEN-C16 and EON-C7 proof text updated from that run (exact revision, Mac model,
  macOS build, Nix and toolchain versions, display scale, commands, artifacts, limits), through
  the Codex re-check AGENTS.md requires for contract proof records.
- A gaps list (what failed or could not be shown) is posted on the friends'-gate bead for README.
- The Mac is deleted and the cost recorded.

## Verification

- Harness `summary.json` exit status 0 on the final revision; Linux suites still green on the
  same revision (`nix develop -c eon-test`, Linux package build).

## Stop Conditions

- Do not rent without Lucca's explicit go (quote it with date on this bead).
- Stop if a fix needs a contract change, new dependency or platform blocker; record it and ask.
- Stop if the rental would end before a final full run: record the best candidate evidence as
  candidate, not proof.
- Never stop or restart a live Eon supervisor on Lucca's machine; Linux profile refresh only per
  AGENTS.md "Local Runtime Synchronization" after accepted runtime changes.

Both rows hold auth_value 2.
- macOS 27 then shows a UserNotificationCenter dialog: "com.apple.sshd-session is requesting to bypass the system private window picker and directly access your screen and audio" (Allow / Open System Settings). title: Add a hand-dispatched GitHub Actions job that runs the macOS harness on Apple Silicon
description:
## Why

Lucca decided on 2026-10-27 (relayed by eon-overseer, recorded on the closed decision bead
`eon-mac-launch-kz4p.10`) that a GitHub Actions job on GitHub's Apple Silicon macOS runners
builds and tests Eon for `aarch64-darwin`, "run by hand at first" ("1 ok"), and that a runner
VM counts only as candidate evidence plus ORB-C14 suite proof, never GUI proof ("2 ok"). The
rental decision on `eon-mac-launch-kz4p.12` says: "one 24 h Scaleway M2, only after the harness
passes on CI" ("3 ok"). So this job is the free native fix loop that runs before any paid Mac
time, and its green run gates the rental.

## Evidence

- `Yazelix/eon` is public (`gh repo view`, 2026-10-27); standard hosted runners, Apple Silicon
  macOS included, are free for public repositories (re-check current terms before landing).
- `.github/workflows/cachix.yml`: the existing `x86_64-linux` push-to-`edge` workflow and its
  repository guard; reuse its shape (permissions, concurrency, guard).
- `ven-qualify-venus-stack-apple-silicon-macos-ili` (closed Conditional-Go, run 34809546212 on a
  standard M1): wgpu Metal, AppKit window creation and presentation initialized on a runner.
- Harness: `eon-mac-launch-kz4p.8` (`mac-proof run`: build, Darwin checks, Darwin `eon-test`,
  `summary.json`).

## Scope

In scope:
- One workflow file (name it in the bead before code) with `workflow_dispatch` only (option 2 of
  `kz4p.10`): input `rev`; one job on an arm64 macOS runner (`macos-15` or the current arm64
  label); installs Nix; runs `nix run .#mac-proof -- run` on the checked-out revision; uploads
  the evidence folder as an artifact with short retention; job timeout, concurrency cancel, no
  secrets for forks, repository guard as in `cachix.yml`; least permissions (`contents: read`).
- `docs/DEVELOPMENT.md` harness section: how an agent dispatches the job for a candidate
  (`gh workflow run ... -f rev=...`) and fetches the artifact. Dispatching needs the revision on
  GitHub, which needs a push; pushes stay on Lucca's explicit request.
- The AP-CI-001 record on this bead: trigger, permissions, timeout, artifacts, cache behaviour,

title: Give eon-test a macOS branch with honest isolation
description:
## Why

`eon-test` is the only supported route for the Rust suites (AGENTS.md "Testing Discipline"), and
it refuses to run without bubblewrap, which macOS lacks. The macOS harness (`kz4p.8`) and the CI
job (`kz4p.15`) call `nix develop -c eon-test` on the Mac, so `eon-test` needs a macOS branch
with honest isolation. Split on 2026-10-27 from `eon-mac-launch-kz4p.5` (which keeps the tests'
process-read port) so each fits one session.

Lucca (2026-10-27, relayed by eon-overseer): "i'd rather test everything possible and fix myself,
letting to Yu only final testing and final fixes that i missed ... so the more automated, the
better."

## Evidence

- `nix/test-sandbox.nix:1-50`: `eon-test` refuses to run without `bwrap --unshare-all`; it hides
  live Wayland, D-Bus and Eon sockets and gives private PID/network.
- Yu's Mac may run Eon (memory `isolate-eon-test-suites`: never run Eon tests against a live Eon
  without isolation).

## Scope

In scope:
- A macOS branch of `eon-test` in `nix/test-sandbox.nix`: private `HOME`, `TMPDIR`,
  `EON_RUNTIME_DIR` and config roots under a fresh temp directory; a refusal when an Eon
  supervisor of the same user is running; the help text names what it does not isolate (no PID
  or network namespace). Arguments pass to `cargo test` as on Linux.
- The Linux branch unchanged.

Out of scope: the tests' own `/proc` reads (`kz4p.5`), the flake's Darwin outputs (`kz4p.7`),
CI, Orbit's and Venus's tests.

## Acceptance

- `nix develop -c eon-test` on Linux behaves exactly as before (same tests, same isolation).
- `nix eval .#devShells.aarch64-darwin.default.drvPath` evaluates with the macOS branch in it.
- The script's macOS branch is shellcheck-clean and refuses clearly when a same-user supervisor
  runs or the toolchain is missing.
- Native pass/fail is the harness's job; this bead claims none.

## Verification

- `nix develop -c eon-test` exits 0 on Linux.
- The `nix eval` above exits 0 on Linux.
- Codex review per AGENTS.md (Nix and script change).

## Stop Conditions

- Stop if honest macOS isolation needs a new tool (sandbox-exec profiles, a VM): ask Lucca.
- Stop if the Darwin dev shell from `kz4p.7` is not in place.
close_reason: macOS eon-test branch in place; Linux unchanged; native proof is kz4p.8's

Note for the macOS root: a private TMPDIR keeps Eon's socket paths under macOS's 104-byte sun_path only if it is short (see kz4p.4's windows.rs:113-119 item).

comments.text:
From eon-mac-launch-kz4p.7 (landed flake Darwin outputs): the Darwin dev shell leaves `eon-test` out (flake.nix devShells: `lib.optional pkgs.stdenv.isLinux (import ./nix/test-sandbox.nix { inherit pkgs; })`), because test-sandbox.nix's runtimeInputs include bubblewrap, which does not evaluate for aarch64-darwin. This bead's macOS branch must make test-sandbox.nix evaluate on Darwin and add it to the Darwin shell. Two more Darwin facts for that branch:
- The Darwin dev shell sets EON_VENUS_FONT_DIRS instead of FONTCONFIG_FILE, so eon-test's precondition `-z "${FONTCONFIG_FILE:-}"` (test-sandbox.nix:17) fails there as written.
- Venus's font-dependent library tests build their font database without EON_VENUS_FONT_DIRS, and fontdb on macOS reads only the system folders and $HOME/Library/Fonts. venusPackage's Darwin preCheck gives them HOME=$TMPDIR/home with Library/Fonts symlinks to Eon's font packages; eon-test's private HOME needs the same links.
- eonPackage's Darwin preCheck takes a private 7-byte TMPDIR (`mkdir -m 700 /tmp/e<c>`) for the socket bounds kz4p.4/kz4p.5 recorded; eon-test's macOS root has the same bound.

comments.author: lucca
comments.text:
Approval (relayed by eon-overseer, 2026-10-27): Lucca to eon-overseer: "do these two too, then ... i want to move closer to the 'yu testing' gate", which starts this bead.

Reference gate (test isolation boundary, recorded before code):
- Behavior: on macOS, `nix develop -c eon-test [args]` runs the workspace suites (args pass to `cargo test`) with a cleared environment (Linux's allowlist plus the Darwin SDK and font variables), a fresh short private root `/tmp/e<c>` as TMPDIR, HOME `<root>/home` (with `Library/Fonts` links to the dev shell's EON_VENUS_FONT_DIRS) and XDG_RUNTIME_DIR `<root>/r`, so config, state and runtime roots resolve inside it; it removes the root on exit. It refuses when the dev shell toolchain is missing or a same-user Eon supervisor (process name eon, eonbase or their `.…-wrapped` makeWrapper names) is running, prints what it does not isolate (no PID, network or /dev namespace; the suites see the host's processes and network), and skips the installer suite, which is Linux-only. Owner: nix/test-sandbox.nix alone; the dev shell only includes it.
- Read: nix/test-sandbox.nix (Linux branch), flake.nix eonPackage Darwin preCheck (`/tmp/e<c>` loop, kz4p.7) and venusPackage Darwin preCheck (HOME/Library/Fonts), runtime platform.rs:15-36 (macOS fallback root `/tmp/<product>-<euid>` is outside TMPDIR, so XDG_RUNTIME_DIR must be set), supervisor.rs:654-686 (config/runtime root order), diagnostics.rs:170 (state root), nixpkgs apple-sdk sdk-hook.sh (SDKROOT/DEVELOPER_DIR exports the cleared environment must keep).
- Comparable: eonPackage's Darwin preCheck (same 7-byte TMPDIR bound and per-run directory); tmux's `/tmp/tmux-<uid>` short root.
- Rejected: sandbox-exec profiles or a VM (new tool; bead stop condition); a runtime `uname` switch inside one script (would change the Linux eon-test derivation); a supervisor check from lock/socket files (they outlive the process and a custom EON_RUNTIME_DIR moves them; the process table covers both); pkgs.procps (Linux-only), so the check calls macOS's own /usr/bin/pgrep.
- Decision: test-sandbox.nix picks its text and runtimeInputs by platform, so every x86_64-linux derivation, eon-test and the dev shell included, keeps its drvPath; the flake includes eon-test in every dev shell. Checks: x86_64-linux drvPaths identical before/after; Linux eon-test wrapper builds and `nix develop -c eon-test` passes; `nix eval .#devShells.aarch64-darwin.default.drvPath`; shellcheck of the Darwin script text (writeShellApplication also runs it at build time on the Mac). Portability: Darwin-isolated.
- Help text: the script has no help of its own, since arguments go to `cargo test`; the macOS branch prints its non-isolation notice on every run instead.

comments.text:
Proof (tree e9fd69df27d54d2e51e7da7c0adca694b68432e3 on c24d4ab; the commit carrying this comment is the proof's revision; x86_64 Linux, Nix daemon; macOS evaluation-only):

Each changes only its `src`, because workspaceSource carries flake.nix, which had to change to put eon-test in the Darwin shell. Every other package and check drvPath is unchanged.

title: Add the Retina probe to the macOS harness
description:
## Why

The macOS preview's minimum bar includes Retina-scale rendering (`eon-igae.5`, `eon-igae.6`), and
no Mac run has ever observed it. The harness must record each display's backing scale and the
scale Venus actually uses, so a remote run claims Retina only when it really ran at scale 2, and
Yu's item 2 ("Retina: ... the tool records backing scale 2", `kz4p.11`) has a recorded value.
Split on 2026-10-27 from `eon-mac-launch-kz4p.9` (which keeps the GUI scenario) so each fits one
session and the one Venus change is reviewed on its own.

Lucca (2026-10-27, relayed by eon-overseer), on Retina: the harness records the display scale and
claims Retina only at scale 2 or more; no private-API virtual display; Yu's HiDPI monitor is the
proof: "7 ok, we can check with him" (comment on `kz4p.9`).

## Evidence

- The only native Venus run used one 1920x1080 scale-1 VNC display
  (`venus/docs/CONTRACTS.md:1053`), and Retina-scale redraw was never observed (`:1081-1082`).
- Venus reads `window.scale_factor()` (`venus/src/application.rs:849-854`, edge 01f5e3c) and
  logs no scale line today (check before adding one).

## Scope

In scope:
- A `retina` step of the harness tool (after `kz4p.9`'s scenario launch, or standalone): records
  each display's backing scale factor and available modes (`osascript -l JavaScript` with AppKit,
  `system_profiler SPDisplaysDataType -json`) into the evidence folder, and the scale Venus
  reports in its log; if a display offers a HiDPI mode, records it; switches modes only if that
  is possible without a new dependency. Reports "Retina proved remotely" only for scale >= 2 with
  a capture; otherwise `skipped: no HiDPI display`, which lands on Yu's list.
- One Venus `venus:` log line at window creation and on scale change naming the scale factor, if
  none exists (presentation diagnostics only; no behaviour change).

Out of scope: a CGVirtualDisplay or any private-API virtual display (rejected by Lucca), the
scenario steps (`kz4p.9`), Yu's guided mode (`kz4p.11`).

## Acceptance

- `retina --help` states what it records and when it claims Retina.
- The parse of the display report into scale and modes is a pure function with a test on Linux
  from a recorded `system_profiler` JSON sample.
- Venus logs its scale at window creation (seen in a Linux isolated run's log at scale 1).

## Verification

- `nix develop -c eon-test -p <harness crate> -p yazelix-venus` exits 0; `cargo fmt --check` and
  `cargo clippy --locked --all-targets -- -D warnings` for both crates.
- Codex review per AGENTS.md. Read `venus/AGENTS.md` before the Venus change.

## Stop Conditions

- Stop for Lucca if switching to a HiDPI mode needs a new tool (displayplacer, a CoreGraphics
  crate).
- Stop if the Venus change needs more than a diagnostic log line.
close_reason: Retina step landed in mac-proof's scenario (CoreGraphics display scale and modes, reversible HiDPI switch, passes only at Venus scale >= 2 with a capture) plus Venus's scale log line. Linux acceptance proved (tests, fmt, clippy on Linux and darwin, headless Sway live run logging scale 1); converge plus Codex clean. Mac observation belongs to kz4p.11 or the rented-Mac run (kz4p.12).

title: Make Orbit's and Venus's tests compile and run on macOS
description:
## Why

eon-mac-launch-kz4p.1 (map at 66b32d5, open question 1 as amended) found that Orbit's and Venus's own test targets have no macOS owner. `cargo check --target aarch64-apple-darwin -p yazelix-orbit --all-targets` fails only in the real_pty test target: orbit/tests/real_pty/unreaped_stop.rs uses ptrace. eon-agent-background-work-yte0.1 adds another Linux-only site there: the `age()` helper in real_pty/program_status.rs uses CLOCK_BOOTTIME and /proc. The flake's package builds run these suites (`orbitPackage` tests `--lib --test real_pty` at flake.nix:276-282, and postInstall requires exactly one real_pty binary at :295-299; `venusPackage` runs Venus's tests at :361-364), so the Darwin `packages.default` cannot build until they compile and pass. The Nix checks `unreaped-stop` (nix/orbit-checks.nix:188) and `program-status` (:219) are Linux-only as written, and real_pty/detached_exit.rs:8 needs `lsof` on macOS while the checks supply only procps (:77).

## Decision

Lucca, 2026-10-27, to eon-overseer: "agree to all that". That answered question 1 with its recommendation: create this bead, blocking kz4p.7 and kz4p.8, and gate unreaped_stop (ptrace) to Linux. This narrows ORB-C14's macOS check set from "every real-PTY check" (orbit/docs/CONTRACTS.md:837-839) to every real-PTY check except the Linux-only ones. Record the exact ORB-C14 wording change on this bead and in orbit/CHANGELOG.md.

## Scope

In:
- Make Orbit's lib and real_pty targets, and Venus's tests, compile for aarch64-apple-darwin.
- Gate unreaped_stop.rs and the Linux-only parts of program_status.rs with `#[cfg(target_os = "linux")]`, or give them Darwin equivalents where cheap.
- Keep exactly one real_pty binary.
- Amend ORB-C14's macOS check-set sentence.

Out:
- Flake changes (kz4p.7, which wires `lsof` and the Darwin check policy).
- Venus fonts (sibling bead "Give Venus Eon's fonts on macOS").
- Native runs (kz4p.8).

## Acceptance

- `cargo check --locked --target aarch64-apple-darwin -p yazelix-orbit -p yazelix-venus --all-targets` passes on Linux.
- Linux behaviour unchanged: `nix develop -c eon-test -p yazelix-orbit -p yazelix-venus`, fmt and clippy -D warnings for both crates.
- Codex review per AGENTS.md.

## Portability disposition

Isolated Linux test mechanisms behind cfg gates.
close_reason: Orbit's lib and real_pty targets and Venus's tests compile and clippy clean for aarch64-apple-darwin from Linux; unreaped_stop is Linux-only, program_status reads macOS process state through libproc; ORB-C14's macOS check set narrowed. Linux suites unchanged and passing. macOS runs are kz4p.8's.

comments.author: lucca
comments.text: Approval relayed by eon-overseer (coordinator), 2026-10-27. Lucca to eon-overseer: "continue with these 3, if possible in paraller". This starts this bead's implementation under the decision recorded in its body (gate unreaped_stop to Linux; narrow ORB-C14's macOS check set). Worked in a detached worktree at 2e7f6e6.

comments.author: lucca
comments.text:
Reference gate (consequential only because ORB-C14's text changes; no dependency, wire, lifecycle or trust change).

Behavior and owners: Orbit's and Venus's test targets compile for aarch64-apple-darwin and, where cheap, read macOS process state through the same libproc calls Orbit's own macOS seam uses. Orbit (orbit/docs/CONTRACTS.md, ORB-C14) owns the macOS check set; the real-PTY harness (orbit/tests/real_pty) owns which checks build per OS; Venus owns its unit tests. Product code is unchanged on every OS.

Routes read: orbit/docs/REFERENCES.md "Platform portability" (inspect the exact libc release's Apple definitions). libc 0.2.189 (Cargo.lock), src/unix/bsd/apple/mod.rs: proc_bsdinfo has pbi_status (:608), e_tpgid (:625), pbi_start_tvsec/usec (:627-628); PROC_PIDTBSDINFO (:3745), SSTOP (:4219), proc_pidinfo (:4992); PTRACE_SEIZE, __WALL and CLOCK_BOOTTIME are absent for Apple. Comparable implementations in this tree: orbit/src/platform.rs macOS bsd_info/started/process (the background-count walk, which reads pbi_status SSTOP and wall-clock pbi_start), and orbit/tests/lifecycle.rs:658 process_start_identity (proc_pidinfo, PROC_PIDTBSDINFO).

Decision:
- unreaped_stop stays Linux-only (approved): the real_pty checks! macro takes optional attributes per check and applies them to both the module and the test, so `#[cfg(target_os = "linux")] unreaped_stop` keeps one real_pty binary. Rejected: a Darwin ptrace equivalent (PT_ATTACHEXC stops the child and needs debugger privilege on macOS; not cheap).
- program_status gets macOS equivalents rather than a gate, so ORB-C15's foreground-drop and background-count checks (whose Orbit macOS path yte0.1 left compile-only) run natively under kz4p.8: foreground_group = e_tpgid, is_stopped = pbi_status == SSTOP, age = wall clock minus pbi_start. The Linux helpers are unchanged and now cfg-gated. Only the non-UTF-8 rename (/proc/$$/comm) and its assertion stay Linux-only; the Linux child script is byte-identical.
- Venus: the unused-on-macOS `crate::EonBar` import moves into the Linux-only test that uses it; stalled_link_dispatcher_is_bounded_and_reaped, whose /proc assertion was vacuous on macOS, checks `/bin/ps -p` there (both still see a zombie), keeping /proc on Linux. Rejected: a libc dev-dependency for Venus (dependency gate cost for one assertion).
Check: `cargo check --locked --target aarch64-apple-darwin -p yazelix-orbit -p yazelix-venus --all-targets` plus darwin clippy, and Linux eon-test, clippy and the orbit-program-status Nix check. The macOS paths stay unproved until kz4p.8 runs them natively.

ORB-C14 wording adopted under the relayed approval (orbit/docs/CONTRACTS.md, Open proof), replacing "Native re-proof runs `orbit-laws`, the unit tests, every real-PTY check and `tests/lifecycle.rs` on Apple Silicon.":

> Native re-proof runs `orbit-laws`, the unit tests, every real-PTY check except [`orbit-unreaped-stop`](../tests/real_pty/unreaped_stop.rs), and `tests/lifecycle.rs` on Apple Silicon. That check holds the child unreaped with Linux's `PTRACE_SEIZE`, which macOS lacks, so a Stop whose child cannot be reaped is checked on Linux only. Tests and assertions that read Linux-only process state are compiled out on macOS.

orbit/CHANGELOG.md (Unreleased) and orbit/docs/BEHAVIOR.md (unreaped-stop runs on Linux only; the program-status rename is Linux-only) say the same.

Sweep findings left for their owners (not fixed here):
1. Venus font-dependent unit tests panic on macOS without DejaVu Sans Mono and Symbols Nerd Font Mono (fontdb ignores FONTCONFIG_FILE there): render/fonts.rs:324, render/cells.rs:614-628, render.rs:5822 clipping_test_fonts (used at :5915, :6123, :6247), render.rs:6999, accessibility.rs:2645. Owner: the sibling bead "Give Venus Eon's fonts on macOS".
2. Socket paths near macOS's 103-byte bound under a /var/folders TMPDIR: orbit/tests/lifecycle.rs:41 TestDir (about 99 bytes for management-deny's orbit.sock.management with a 47-byte TMPDIR and a 5-digit pid), venus/src/transport.rs:1439 (about 99, or about 101 under a Darwin nix-build TMPDIR). The old server and bend-orbit passed lifecycle natively with the same naming, so no change now; kz4p.8's native run decides.
3. /bin/true (orbit/src/pty.rs:857, real_pty/management_record.rs:215, :250, :266) does not exist on macOS; each use expects the run to fail before exec, so nothing breaks; fragile only.
4. orbit/tests/real_pty/kitty.rs:82 skips its wmem_default tuning silently on macOS (harmless).

comments.author: lucca
comments.text:
Correction to the ORB-C14 wording quoted in the reference-gate comment above. Review found its last sentence untrue: the program-status rename and the older /proc reads sit behind runtime `cfg!` branches, which compile on macOS and only skip there. The adopted text in orbit/docs/CONTRACTS.md (ORB-C14, Open proof) is:

> Native re-proof runs `orbit-laws`, the unit tests, every real-PTY check except [`orbit-unreaped-stop`](../tests/real_pty/unreaped_stop.rs), and `tests/lifecycle.rs` on Apple Silicon. That check holds the child unreaped with Linux's `PTRACE_SEIZE`, which macOS lacks, so a Stop whose child cannot be reaped is checked on Linux only. Tests and assertions that read Linux-only process state do not run on macOS.

orbit/CHANGELOG.md records the ORB-C14 narrowing; the Linux-only non-UTF-8 rename in the program-status check is stated in orbit/docs/BEHAVIOR.md only.

comments.text:
Proof (x86_64 Linux host; worktree at base 2e7f6e6; code identical in every tree below, which differ only in ORB-C14 text and bead data):
- Darwin compile: `cargo check --locked -j 4 --target aarch64-apple-darwin -p yazelix-orbit -p yazelix-venus --all-targets` (rustup stable 1.96.0 with the aarch64-apple-darwin std, dev-shell build inputs exported from `nix eval .#devShells.x86_64-linux.default.<VAR>`, dev-shell zig 0.17.0 and bun 1.3.13): pass, no warnings. title: Give Venus Eon's fonts on macOS
description:
## Why

eon-mac-launch-kz4p.1 (map at 66b32d5, open question 2) found that Eon gives Venus its fonts only through fontconfig, which Venus ignores on macOS.
- Venus builds its font database with cosmic-text `FontSystem::new()` (venus/src/render/fonts.rs:90).
- On macOS, fontdb 0.23 reads only the system font directories. It also scans /System/Library/AssetsV2 and /Network/Library/Fonts. FONTCONFIG_FILE is read only off macOS (fontdb-0.23.0/src/lib.rs:424-428, :461, :509).
- Eon supplies its fonts only as `venusFontsConf`, set as FONTCONFIG_FILE (flake.nix:329-345, :370, :987). That file writes `<dir prefix="relative">` on purpose.
- The default fallbacks "Symbols Nerd Font Mono" and "Accelerando Terminal" (eon/crates/eon/src/product.rs:41-44) are always passed as `--font-fallback` (runtime/crates/eon-runtime/src/supervisor.rs:424-426).
- `FontSetup::resolve` errors when a family is unavailable (fonts.rs:104-111).

So on a stock Mac the default configuration most likely cannot open a window. That is inferred from code, not run. VEN-C16's record (venus/docs/CONTRACTS.md:1063-1066) already shows six Venus library tests failing on stock macOS without those fonts.

## Decision

Lucca, 2026-10-27, to eon-overseer: "agree to all that". That answered question 2 with its recommendation: create this bead, blocking kz4p.7, kz4p.8 and kz4p.9.

## Shape (decide under the reference gate)

Venus loads Eon's packaged font directories explicitly on macOS. Two candidate mechanisms:
- a font-directory startup input that Runtime passes from launch inputs Eon already owns (recommended starting point: it keeps Venus parsing no configuration);
- Venus reading the same fonts.conf's `<dir>` entries, including the relative prefix.

kz4p.7 wires the Darwin font package. A new Runtime-to-Venus startup input is an interface change, so record the reference gate on this bead before code. Stop for Lucca if it changes VEN-C16's text.

## Acceptance

- With the default configuration and Eon's fonts but no system copies, `FontSetup::resolve` succeeds for a macOS-shaped font environment.
- A Venus unit or integration check that runs on Linux exercises the explicit-directory path.
- Linux behaviour unchanged: `nix develop -c eon-test -p yazelix-venus -p eon-runtime`, fmt and clippy.
- Codex review per AGENTS.md.
- Native proof comes in kz4p.8 and kz4p.9.

## Portability disposition

Isolated Darwin font loading behind Venus's platform code.
close_reason: Venus loads EON_VENUS_FONT_DIRS before resolving fonts; Linux unchanged; Darwin wiring in kz4p.7, native proof in kz4p.8/9

comments.author: lucca
comments.text:
## Approval (relayed)

Relayed by eon-overseer (coordinator), 2026-10-27. Lucca, 2026-10-27, to eon-overseer: "do these two too, then ... i want to move closer to the 'yu testing' gate". It names this bead (Venus fonts on macOS) for implementation now. Contract text already adopted on this bead or its parent stands.

## Reference gate

**Behavior.** On macOS, Venus resolves the default fallbacks ("Symbols Nerd Font Mono", "Accelerando Terminal") and DejaVu from Eon's packaged font directories, not from system copies. Linux is unchanged. Owners: Eon's Nix composition chooses the font set, which is today's `venusFontsConf` list (flake.nix:328-343). Venus's package wrapper delivers it, as it already sets `FONTCONFIG_FILE` (flake.nix:345). Venus's `FontSetup` owns loading it into the font database.

**Evidence read.**
- fontdb 0.23.0 `Database::load_system_fonts` (src/lib.rs:400-475). On macOS it scans only /Library/Fonts, /System/Library/Fonts, AssetsV2, /Network/Library/Fonts and ~/Library/Fonts. It reads `FONTCONFIG_FILE` only on non-macOS unix (:461, :509). `fontconfig-parser` is a dependency only for that cfg (Cargo.toml:80), so the macOS build does not compile it. `Database::load_fonts_dir` is public and recursive.
- cosmic-text 0.19.0 `FontSystem` (src/font/system.rs:191-299). `new()` loads system fonts and sets the generic families. The constructor computes the monospace ID lists once, so faces added later through `db_mut()` are missing from them. `into_locale_and_db` plus `new_with_locale_and_db` rebuilds the font system with those lists computed.
- Venus: `FontSetup::new`/`resolve` (venus/src/render/fonts.rs:89-111), the single app caller `create_window` (venus/src/application.rs:832), existing env inputs `EON_VENUS_PRESENTATION_CONTROL` (main.rs:16) and `EON_NEW_WINDOW_EXECUTABLE` (application.rs:768); VEN-C16 text (venus/docs/CONTRACTS.md:1018-1090), VEN-C19 fallback decision (venus/docs/CRATES.md:122-141).
- Runtime: `venus_command` (runtime/crates/eon-runtime/src/supervisor.rs:388-460) and `Inputs` (runtime/crates/eon-runtime/src/cli.rs:42-52). Eon launches the wrapped `${venusPackage}/bin/yazelix-venus` (flake.nix:631, :764), so the Venus wrapper's environment reaches every Eon-launched Venus.
- Comparable implementation: WezTerm `e2a98e1b8af156988ad0ac778658ac27b60a55fb`, `wezterm-font/src/db.rs:36-60` (`font_dirs`). It walks the listed directories on every platform and adds them beside system fonts. Kept: extra directories are additive and platform-neutral. Rejected: making it user configuration. Here it is a packaging input, not a value a person sees.

**Adopted.** Venus reads `EON_VENUS_FONT_DIRS`, an OS path list (`std::env::split_paths`, colon-separated). It loads each directory into the platform font database before resolving typography. Empty entries are skipped. A relative or missing directory fails startup with a bounded "font directory is unavailable" error before the window opens. When the variable is unset, Venus follows today's path exactly. The Darwin Venus wrapper (kz4p.7) sets it from the same list as `venusFontsConf`. Linux sets nothing, so Linux behavior and derivations do not change.

**Rejected.**
1. Runtime passes `--font-dir` (the bead's suggested starting point). That needs a new Eon launch input, a new field in Runtime's public `Inputs`, Eon product code and a supervisor.rs change, which collides with kz4p.4. Runtime would become a second carrier of a font set the Venus package already owns. Standalone `yazelix-venus` and Venus's own test environment would still lack the fonts.
2. Venus reads `FONTCONFIG_FILE`'s `<dir>` entries on macOS. Doing it properly means adding `fontconfig-parser` to the macOS build, a new dependency that fontdb deliberately leaves out there. A hand-rolled `<dir>`/`prefix="relative"` reader would reinterpret fontconfig's format partially.
3. A `--font-dir` flag added by the wrapper (`--add-flags`). It works, but it is a second argv surface for a packaging input, and it is prepended to every invocation. The env var follows the existing `FONTCONFIG_FILE` channel.

**Contracts.** No contract text changes: VEN-C16's Result already confines variation to native host mechanics, and VEN-C19's typography is unchanged. No new dependency. Interface: one new Venus environment input, documented in the code. Its producer is the Darwin wrapper (kz4p.7).

**Portability disposition.** `neutral`: the mechanism is platform-neutral and runs on Linux in tests. Only the Darwin package sets the variable. This replaces the bead's "isolated Darwin font loading", because no cfg-gated code is needed.

**Check.** A Venus unit test on Linux builds a "macOS-shaped" font system. Its platform fonts are DejaVu only, with no Eon fallback families. Default Eon fallbacks fail to resolve without the directory list and resolve with it. A missing directory is rejected. Linux: `nix develop -c eon-test -p yazelix-venus`, fmt, clippy (host and `--target aarch64-apple-darwin`).

**Handoff.** kz4p.7: set `EON_VENUS_FONT_DIRS` on the Darwin Venus wrapper from the font package list used for `venusFontsConf`. Rejected option 1's test advantage does not apply to this design either. Venus's library tests build font systems directly (`FontSystem::new()`), so the variable does not reach them. kz4p.8's harness still has to make the fixture fonts visible to those six tests, as `eon-z4n6` did by installing them for the user.

Option 1 is rejected only for its extra Eon/Runtime plumbing, its second carrier of the font set, and its supervisor.rs collision.

## Review round 1 and a corrected gate claim

**Correction.** The gate's Behavior line says macOS resolves "DejaVu from Eon's packaged font directories, not from system copies". That overstates the change. What holds is narrower:
- The default fallbacks, "Symbols Nerd Font Mono" and "Accelerando Terminal", resolve from the packaged directories. That is the bead's acceptance.

This is inferred from source and not run on a Mac. VEN-C19's typography contract is unchanged; only which face macOS's platform default yields is in question.

## Question for Lucca

1. Which default terminal face should Eon use on macOS when `font-family` is unset?
