title: Port Eon Runtime's terminal peer and liveness checks to macOS
description:
## Why

Eon Runtime validates each Orbit run's management peer and process identity with Linux-only
calls. On macOS it does not compile, and the liveness check would read a missing `/proc` as "the
run is dead" and retire every live terminal. This is the one Runtime change full Eon needs on
macOS before anything launches.

Lucca (2026-10-27, relayed by eon-overseer): "i'd rather test everything possible and fix myself,
letting to Yu only final testing and final fixes that i missed ... so the more automated, the
better."

## Evidence

- `runtime/crates/eon-runtime/src/sessions.rs:424-458` `validate_management_peer`: `SO_PEERCRED`
  pid/uid, then `/proc/<pid>/stat` field 22 compared with the Ready `process_start`.
- `sessions.rs:572-593` `recorded_process_is_dead`: NotFound means dead; state `Z`/`X` means dead;
  start mismatch is an error. Callers `:767` (adoption) and `:1386` (owner loss).
- Orbit already publishes the macOS identity: `orbit/src/platform.rs:333-341` `getpeereid`,
  `:353-376` `process_start_identity` = `pbi_start_tvsec * 1_000_000 + pbi_start_tvusec` from
  `proc_pidinfo(PROC_PIDTBSDINFO)`. `orbit/tests/lifecycle.rs:658-678` reads it independently.
- `orbit/crates/protocol/src/management.rs:48,433` carries `process_start` as an opaque nonzero
  `u64`; its unit is the platform's.
- Contract: EON-C15 (`docs/CONTRACTS.md:1436`): "stale or mismatched process identity ... fails
  closed without PID/process-name fallback". ORB-C13/ORB-C14 own Orbit's side.

## Scope

In scope: a narrow Runtime-local platform seam (one module, Linux and macOS functions) for: peer
pid and uid of a Unix stream (macOS: `getsockopt(SOL_LOCAL, LOCAL_PEERPID)` plus `getpeereid`),
process start identity of a pid in Orbit's unit (macOS: `proc_pidinfo` as Orbit does), and
process state (macOS: `ESRCH` from `proc_pidinfo` is dead, `pbi_status == SZOMB` is dead).
`validate_management_peer` and `recorded_process_is_dead` call it; Linux behavior unchanged.

Out of scope: Orbit, `orbit-protocol`, EONW, Venus; the Runtime test files' own `/proc` reads
(tests bead); runtime directory and notification (remaining-assumptions bead).

## Acceptance

- `cargo check --target aarch64-apple-darwin -p eon-runtime` (gate command from the mapping bead)
  passes this item: no `ucred`/`SO_PEERCRED`/`/proc` on the macOS path.
- On Linux, existing Runtime identity tests pass unchanged through `nix develop -c eon-test -p
  eon-runtime`; one focused test covers the seam's "missing process is dead, mismatched start is
  an error" rule if no existing test does (name the failure it catches).
- Native macOS proof is deferred to the harness (Runtime suite plus full-Eon launch, where an
  identity mismatch fails closed and is visible).
- Portability disposition recorded: isolated Linux and Darwin mechanisms behind one seam.

## Implementation Notes

1. Read EON-C15, ORB-C13/C14, `orbit/src/platform.rs` seam and the mapping bead's list.
2. Add the seam; keep Linux code byte-for-byte equivalent in behavior.
3. Run the gate check, `cargo fmt --check`, clippy, `eon-test -p eon-runtime`; Codex per AGENTS.md.

## Verification

- `nix develop -c eon-test -p eon-runtime` exits 0.
- `cargo check --locked --target aarch64-apple-darwin -p eon-runtime` (outside the dev shell as
  the mapping bead records) shows no error from `sessions.rs`.

## Stop Conditions

- Stop if `libc` lacks a needed Apple constant and the fix needs a new crate (dependency gate).
- Stop if the shape would move identity reading into `orbit-protocol` or make Runtime depend on
  `yazelix-orbit` (Product Boundary forbids the latter; the former changes a standalone protocol
  crate). Ask Lucca.
- Stop if EON-C15 wording must change.

## Maintenance Notes

- Decision (recommended; Lucca may override in the epic's decisions): Runtime keeps its own
  reader mirroring Orbit's definition, as on Linux today. A unit mismatch fails closed on the first
  native launch, which the harness exercises, so drift cannot pass silently.
- Rejected: `kill(pid, 0)` liveness (cannot tell zombie or reused pid), PID-only fallback.
close_reason: Runtime peer identity and liveness moved behind a Runtime-private Linux/macOS seam (platform.rs); Linux unchanged apart from one recorded message; aarch64-apple-darwin check and clippy clean; eon-test -p eon-runtime green. Native macOS proof deferred to the harness.

Also confirmed: the start time at :446 reads /proc field 22 (boot ticks) while Orbit's macOS identity is microseconds from proc_pidinfo (orbit/src/platform.rs:353-356); `recorded_process_is_dead` is sessions.rs:572-596 with callers :753, :767, :1386, :1402.

comments.author: lucca
comments.text:
Reference gate (consequential: it ports the management-peer trust check and the liveness rule that decides whether a terminal's run is retired). Recorded at 2e7f6e6 before code.

Behavior and owners:
- Runtime accepts an Orbit run's management stream only when the socket peer's pid and uid equal the run's Ready identity and the pid's kernel start identity equals Ready `process_start`; otherwise it fails closed (EON-C15). A recorded run is dead only when no process has its pid or the process is a zombie; a live pid with another start identity is an error, never "dead". Runtime (`sessions.rs`) owns both decisions; Orbit owns the published identity and its unit (ORB-C13/C14); `orbit-protocol` carries `process_start` opaquely.
- New owner of the platform mechanism: one Runtime-private module, `runtime/crates/eon-runtime/src/platform.rs`, with Linux and macOS functions for (a) the peer pid and uid of a Unix stream and (b) a pid's start identity and whether it has ended, or that no process has it. `sessions.rs` keeps the policy.

Routes read: docs/REFERENCES.md has no route for process identity; the comparable implementation is Orbit's own seam at 2e7f6e6:
- `orbit/src/platform.rs:493-532` `peer_uid` (Linux `SO_PEERCRED`, macOS `getpeereid`) and `process_start_identity` (Linux /proc stat field 22; macOS `bsd_info` + `started` at :384-402 = `pbi_start_tvsec * 1_000_000 + pbi_start_tvusec`, rejecting tvusec >= 1e6, requiring a full record with `pbi_pid == pid`).
- libc 0.2.189 (already pinned) has every Apple item needed: `SOL_LOCAL`, `LOCAL_PEERPID`, `getpeereid`, `proc_pidinfo`, `PROC_PIDTBSDINFO`, `proc_bsdinfo`, `SZOMB`. No new dependency.
- XNU semantics relied on (inference from Apple's libproc behavior, to be confirmed by the native harness): `proc_pidinfo(PROC_PIDTBSDINFO)` returns 0 with errno `ESRCH` for a missing pid and still reports zombies, with `pbi_status == SZOMB`; `LOCAL_PEERPID` reports the peer's pid as captured at connect time, like `SO_PEERCRED`.

Constraints kept: Linux behavior unchanged (same /proc reads, field indices, Z/X rule, fail-closed messages); no PID-only or process-name fallback; nothing moves into `orbit-protocol`; Runtime does not depend on `yazelix-orbit`; no EONW, Orbit or Venus change.

Rejected: `kill(pid, 0)` liveness (cannot tell a zombie or a reused pid); sharing Orbit's code through a crate (Product Boundary; decision 4 on this bead keeps Runtime's own reader); `getpeereid` alone (no pid, so the Ready pid could not be checked).

Decision and check: adopt the seam above. Check: `cargo check --locked --target aarch64-apple-darwin -p eon-runtime --all-targets` clean (compile only, not proof, EON-C7); `nix develop -c eon-test -p eon-runtime` green on Linux; native macOS proof deferred to the harness, where a unit mismatch fails closed on first launch.

Portability disposition: isolated Linux and Darwin mechanisms behind one Runtime-private seam (`cfg(target_os = "linux")` / `cfg(target_os = "macos")`); other targets do not compile it, as before.

comments.author: lucca
comments.text:
Gate correction after Codex round 1 (candidate tree caa52a5), confirmed against Apple's XNU source (xnu-12377.1.9, bsd/kern/proc_info.c and bsd/kern/uipc_usrreq.c):

1. `proc_pidinfo(PROC_PIDTBSDINFO)` reports a zombie only when its `arg` is nonzero (`if (arg) findzomb = 1`); with 0 a zombie is `ESRCH`. The gate's "still reports zombies" was wrong for arg 0. The macOS reader passes 1, so an unreaped zombie's start identity is still compared (a mismatch fails closed, as on Linux) and `pbi_status == SZOMB` marks it ended. The focused test now checks the identity of the unreaped child too, which catches this on the native harness.
2. `LOCAL_PEERPID` returns the peer socket's last pid (`so_last_pid`), not a pid captured at connect. For Orbit's management socket the peer is the Orbit host itself; if another process were using the peer socket, the pid or start check fails closed. No fallback is added.
3. Deliberate Linux text change, outcome unchanged: when the Orbit process vanishes between connect and the identity read, validation still fails closed but its message ends "no such process" instead of "No such file or directory (os error 2)". No test or consumer matches that text. Keeping the old text would need the seam to pass Linux io errors through to `sessions`, which adds caller code for a diagnostic. Every other message and fail-closed outcome is the same on Linux.

Out-of-scope finding for Orbit's owner: Orbit's macOS `bsd_info` (orbit/src/platform.rs:384-392 at 2e7f6e6) also passes arg 0, so Orbit's macOS process walk never sees zombies. Whether that matters for its background-process count is Orbit's call; reported to eon-overseer, no bead created.

comments.author: lucca
comments.text:
Proof (candidate tree bd26c237364a3079f758adc572a93de56a81d2a2 = the committed code; the commit leaves .beads/ out for the coordinator's replay). x86_64 Linux, from the worktree at base 2e7f6e6, -j 4, CARGO_TARGET_DIR outside the repo:
- `nix develop -c cargo fmt --check -p eon-runtime`: exit 0.
- `nix develop -c cargo clippy --locked -j 4 -p eon-runtime --all-targets -- -D warnings`: exit 0.
- Outside the Nix shell (rustup rustc 1.96.0 with the aarch64-apple-darwin std): `cargo check --locked --target aarch64-apple-darwin -p eon-runtime --all-targets` exit 0, no warnings; `cargo clippy` of the same with `-D warnings` exit 0. No `ucred`/`SO_PEERCRED`/`/proc` remains on the macOS path. Compile check only, not native proof (EON-C7).
- `nix develop -c eon-test -p eon-runtime`: exit 0; lib `128 passed; 0 failed; 1 ignored`, including the new `recorded_process_is_dead_checks_its_identity_until_reaped`; flake eon-prune-test-flake-sj0c did not occur.
Focused test, the failure it names: a platform reader that loses an unreaped zombie's identity (macOS `proc_pidinfo` with arg 0 gives ESRCH, so a mismatched zombie would read as dead and could be reaped), or treats a live process as dead (the old `/proc` path on macOS), or a reaped pid as alive or an error. It reads the start through the seam, so it runs unchanged on the native harness.
Native macOS proof deferred to the harness (Runtime suite plus full-Eon launch; a unit mismatch with Orbit's identity fails closed on first launch). Portability disposition: isolated Linux and Darwin mechanisms behind one Runtime-private seam (runtime/crates/eon-runtime/src/platform.rs).

Review ledger (1 slice): Codex round 1 on caa52a5: 2 blocking (macOS zombie lookup needed a nonzero proc_pidinfo arg: fixed; Linux missing-process message text: kept and recorded as deliberate) plus 1 nit (gate's LOCAL_PEERPID wording: corrected). The parallel fresh Claude review of caa52a5 did not run, because the fix landed before it started; the Claude rounds then covered the fixed tree. Claude converge round 1: 1 change (test simplification, no behavior change); round 2: clean, ran the checks above. Narrow Codex re-check caa52a5 to bd26c23: clean. 2 Codex passes, 3 findings.

title: Make Eon's terminfo readable by macOS system ncurses
description:
## Why

eon-mac-launch-kz4p.1 (map at 66b32d5, open question 3) found that macOS's system ncurses most likely cannot read `TERM=eon`.
- Orbit sets TERM=eon (orbit/src/pty.rs:750; ORB-C10).
- orbit/terminfo/eon.terminfo is `use=xterm-256color`, compiled with nixpkgs ncurses `tic -x` (flake.nix:301). xterm-256color's pairs#0x10000 makes tic write the 32-bit extended format: the built entry starts with bytes 1e 02, magic 01036.
- macOS's system ncurses (5.7) reads only the legacy 0432 format, and its terminfo tree uses hex directory names (65/, not e/).
- Terminals get TERMINFO_DIRS pointing at Orbit's tree (flake.nix:646, :766). System-ncurses programs (/bin/zsh, less, vim, top, man) would therefore most likely report an unknown terminal inside Eon. That is inferred, not run.
- The `orbit-terminfo` check (nix/orbit-checks.nix:244-255) uses Nix ncurses and would not catch it.

## Decision

Lucca, 2026-10-27, to eon-overseer: "agree to all that". That answered question 3 with its recommendation: create this bead, blocking kz4p.9 and kz4p.11. Show the exact ORB-C10 text change to Lucca before landing.

## Shape

Compile a legacy-format entry for Darwin and install it under both the e/ and 65/ directory names. Example: cap pairs at 0x7fff, as kitty's entry does. Add a check that runs /usr/bin/infocmp eon on the Mac in kz4p.8's harness.

## Acceptance

- The Darwin terminfo output, inspected from Linux, starts with legacy magic 0432 and exists under both directory names.
- Linux's entry is unchanged, or any change is justified on the bead.
- The native /usr/bin/infocmp check is added to kz4p.8's harness list.
- Codex review per AGENTS.md (Nix change).

## Portability disposition

Isolated Darwin packaging of the terminfo entry.
close_reason: macOS Orbit installs a legacy-format eon terminfo entry (pairs#0x7fff, e/ and 65/) checked from Linux by orbit-terminfo-darwin; Linux entry unchanged; ORB-C10 Partially proved with the approved macOS clause; native run is ORB-C10's open proof (kz4p.8/.12).

comments.author: lucca
comments.text:
Claimed by eon-terminfo (worktree from 9729903) for eon-overseer.

Approval (relayed by eon-overseer, 2026-10-27): Lucca to eon-overseer: "do these two too, then ... i want to move closer to the 'yu testing' gate". That starts this bead. It does not cover the ORB-C10 text change, which went to Lucca on 2026-10-27 and is still pending.

Reference gate (consequential, because it changes the ORB-C10 contract):
- Behavior: Programs that link the system ncurses on macOS (/usr/bin/infocmp, /bin/zsh, less) resolve TERM=eon from the package's share/terminfo on TERMINFO_DIRS. Linux behavior is unchanged.
- Owners: orbit/terminfo/eon.terminfo stays the one source (name, description, use=xterm-256color). The flake's Orbit package owns the compiled tree, and on Darwin installs the entry built by the new `darwinTerminfo` derivation. ORB-C10 owns the contract.
- Evidence (Linux, nixpkgs ncurses 6.6 at the flake pin):
  - `tic -x` on today's source writes magic 1e 02 (01036, extended numbers), 4054 bytes, because xterm-256color has pairs#0x10000.
  - Adding `pairs#0x7fff,` before `use=` writes 1a 01 (0432, legacy), 4024 bytes. `infocmp -x` differs only in pairs. pairs is the only number above 0x7fff (colors#0x100, cols#80, it#8, lines#24).
- Comparable implementations:
  - kitty b2cb871 (~/pjs/refs/kitty): terminfo/kitty.terminfo has pairs#32767. The compiled x/xterm-kitty is legacy (1a 01, 3721 bytes), with a `78 -> x` symlink for hex-directory readers.
  - Ghostty at the flake's pinned input (src/terminfo/ghostty.zig:99): pairs 32767 on every platform.
  - WezTerm e2a98e1 (termwiz/data/wezterm.terminfo:37): pairs#0x7fff.
- Constraints kept: one source file. Linux's compiled entry and the Linux orbit derivation stay unchanged. No new dependency.
- Rejected:
  - (a) Capping pairs in eon.terminfo for all platforms. This is simpler and matches kitty and Ghostty, but it changes Linux's entry, and the bead says to keep Linux unchanged without a reason to change it.
  - (b) A second checked-in Darwin source, which would put the name in two owners.
  - (c) Rewriting `infocmp` output with sed after compiling.
  - (d) Copying the file into 65/ instead of symlinking. Kitty's symlink keeps one file.
- Inference, not run: macOS ncurses 5.7 reads only the legacy format, looks up hex directory names, and reads at most 4096 bytes per entry (MAX_ENTRY_SIZE in 5.x). These come from kz4p.1's map and ncurses history. The native /usr/bin/infocmp check in kz4p.8's harness is the proof.
- Decision check:
  - New Linux flake check `orbit-terminfo-darwin`: the Darwin tree's entry starts with 0432, is at most 4096 bytes, is reachable as e/eon and 65/eon, and differs from a fresh Linux compile only in pairs.
  - `nix eval` of the Linux orbit drvPath must be unchanged.

Portability disposition: isolated Darwin packaging of the terminfo entry. The Darwin branch in orbitPackage is evaluated only once kz4p.7 adds aarch64-darwin outputs. Until then, the Linux check builds `darwinTerminfo` itself.

title: Check on macOS that a zombie grandchild neither counts nor hides a live sibling
description:
## Why

On macOS, `proc_pidinfo(PROC_PIDTBSDINFO)` with arg 0 cannot see zombies. Orbit's macOS `bsd_info` (orbit/src/platform.rs:374-379) passes arg 0, so the background-process walk's `process()` returns None for a zombie (found in XNU source, xnu-12377.1.9, by kz4p.2 on 2026-10-27; note on kz4p.8; not observed natively). Likely harmless: the walk counts zombies as not running, and a zombie keeps no children. But no Darwin check exercises it. program_status.rs has no zombie case, and unreaped_stop.rs is Linux-only (eon-32, kz4p.8 question 1, 2026-10-28).

## Goal

A real-PTY check, run natively on macOS by the harness, shows that a zombie grandchild neither counts as background work nor hides a live sibling from the count.

## Shape

- Add a case to orbit/tests/real_pty/program_status.rs on both Linux and macOS. A foreground child forks two grandchildren into their own process group: one exits and stays unreaped (a zombie), the other sleeps. The count is exactly 1 while the sleeper lives, and 0 after it exits.
- Add the check entry in nix/orbit-checks.nix if program_status needs one. The harness (kz4p.8) builds every Darwin check the flake lists, so it needs no change.
- If the native run shows the zombie hides its sibling, fix it at Orbit's platform seam, the way kz4p.2 fixed Runtime.

## Acceptance

- Green on Linux through the orbit-program-status Nix check.
- Compile- and clippy-clean for aarch64-apple-darwin.
- Native result: recorded by kz4p.12, which this bead blocks, from its native run of orbit-program-status; it is not a condition for closing this bead (eon-overseer, 2026-10-28: "The native run belongs to kz4p.12").
- Codex review per AGENTS.md.

## Scope boundary

Orbit tests and, only if the native run demands it, orbit/src/platform.rs. No contract change.
close_reason: Linux green through orbit-program-status at 578ed1c, aarch64-apple-darwin compile- and clippy-clean, Codex and Claude converged; native run belongs to kz4p.12

Not consequential (AP-REFERENCE-001 as AGENTS.md defines it): a test case and a BEHAVIOR.md bullet, with no dependency, protocol, contract, lifecycle or trust-boundary change, so it has no reference gate.

Shape:
- The walk (orbit/src/platform.rs background_processes) already skips a pid whose record it cannot read (`continue`) and counts a readable zombie as not running (Linux `Z`, macOS `SZOMB`). So on paper neither platform needs a fix. The native run on kz4p.12 decides.
- New case `zombies_neither_count_nor_hide` in orbit/tests/real_pty/program_status.rs. A job-control foreground job starts two grandchildren in their own groups, reports `done`, then runs `exec cat "$GATE" "$GATE" > "$EXIT"`. `cat` opens the gate only after the exec, so when the check's gate write returns, the zombie's parent is a process that never waits. The line `cat` relays ends the first grandchild, which stays a zombie. The second `"$GATE"` operand keeps `cat` blocked. The check waits until the first is a zombie and the second is 1.1 s old, asserts background == 1 and that the zombie is still unreaped, then releases the second and waits for 0.

title: List detached Eon processes in mac-proof's leftovers check
description:
## Why

The harness's leftovers step (kz4p.8) checks that no Eon process survives the run. On macOS it
lists processes with `ps -U <uid> -o pid=,comm=` in `eon_processes`
(eon/tools/mac-proof/src/run.rs:528). BSD `ps` without `-x` leaves out processes that have no
controlling terminal, which is exactly what a detached Eon supervisor, Orbit host or Venus launched
from the GUI is. So a leaked background Eon process passes the leftovers check unseen. Reported by
the kz4p.9 agent; kz4p.9's scenario already lists with `ps -A -ww` filtered by uid.

## Contract

kz4p.8's acceptance: the harness reports Eon processes left after the run. No product contract
changes.

## Change

List every process of the user, with or without a terminal (`-x`, or the scenario's `-A` plus a
uid filter; prefer one shared helper if kz4p.9 has landed one).

## Acceptance

- On Linux: `nix develop -c eon-test -p mac-proof` passes, plus fmt and clippy for mac-proof on the
  host and `--target aarch64-apple-darwin`.
- The first native run (kz4p.12 or the macOS CI workflow) would show a detached Eon process in the
  leftovers; claim it only once a Mac run has exercised it.

## Scope

mac-proof's process listing only. Prerequisite: kz4p.9 lands first (both edit run.rs and the
scenario's listing). Converge plus Codex review as for any code change.
close_reason: Leftovers listing shares scenario.rs's ps -A -ww uid-filtered helper; Linux checks pass; the native detached-process claim waits on the first Mac run (kz4p.12)

description:

title: Check Venus's stalled-link reaping without /bin/ps on macOS
description:
## Why

macOS CI run 40721211773 attempt 2 (e04553c; evidence in
/home/lucca/.cache/eon-agents/eon-overseer/ci-40721211773-a2/) failed `package` because the Venus
test `application::tests::stalled_link_dispatcher_is_bounded_and_reaped` panicked inside the Nix
build: `steps/03-package.log:8714-8715`, `venus/src/application.rs:7301:14 ... Os { code: 1,
kind: PermissionDenied, message: "Operation not permitted" }`. That line (at e04553c) unwraps
`Command::new("/bin/ps").args(["-p", pid]).status()` in the `#[cfg(not(target_os = "linux"))]`
branch (7297-7302). The same test passed under cargo (`66-test-yazelix-venus.log:342`), so the
Nix build user cannot exec macOS's setuid `/bin/ps` (inference). Not timing and not a product bug.
A failed `package` also skips the GUI scenario and the Retina step.

## Change

Venus test only: drop `ps`. After `drop(opener)`, tell a reaped child from a live or zombie one
with `waitpid(pid, WNOHANG)` (ECHILD once reaped) or `kill(pid, 0)` (ESRCH once reaped; a zombie
still answers), whichever matches what the test proves. Also drop the workflow's and harness's
comments that say sandbox=false exists for this ps call if nothing else needs it, or leave them
and say why.

## Acceptance

- `nix develop -c eon-test -p yazelix-venus` passes on Linux; fmt and clippy for Venus on Linux
  and `--target aarch64-apple-darwin`.
- The test still fails if the dispatcher leaves the child unreaped (state the red check).
- The next macOS CI run's `package` step gets past this test.

## Scope

venus/src/application.rs tests only. Read venus/AGENTS.md. Codex review per AGENTS.md.

title: Keep the eon CLI's socket reads working after the supervisor closes on macOS
description:
## Why

On macOS the `eon` CLI fails against a live supervisor. macOS CI run 40721211773 attempt 2
(e04553c; evidence in /home/lucca/.cache/eon-agents/eon-overseer/ci-40721211773-a2/): 32 of 49
`workspace_control` tests in `test:eon` failed, almost all with `cannot bound Eon action result:
Invalid argument (os error 22)` (`steps/69-test-eon.log` lines 85, 96, 126, 165, 227 and others).
`runtime/crates/eon-runtime/src/control.rs:232-235` calls `set_read_timeout` before each read
(header, then body). Inference (XNU): Darwin's setsockopt returns EINVAL once a Unix socket is
shut down both ways, which happens when the supervisor writes its reply and closes; the reply is
already buffered. `supervisor.rs:578` uses the same per-read pattern. This is a product bug on
macOS, not only a test failure.

## Contract

The eon CLI's workspace actions (EON-C7 on macOS; the CLI contracts in docs/CONTRACTS.md). No
contract text changes: the CLI must behave on macOS as it does on Linux.

## Change

In Eon Runtime, set each socket's timeouts once per connection before the first read or write, or
treat EINVAL from `set_read_timeout` / `set_write_timeout` after a peer close as "read what is
buffered". Apply it at every per-read timeout site (control.rs, supervisor.rs, and any other
found by search). Prefer one helper as the single owner.

Also check `workspace_control.rs:1591`: on macOS a directory came back as `/private/tmp/...` where
the test (`...preserves_raw_directory`) expected the raw `/tmp/...`. Decide whether Eon
canonicalizes a path it should keep raw (product bug) or the test's expectation is wrong; fix
the owner. Low confidence; keep it in this bead only if the fix is small, else file a bead.

## Acceptance

- Linux: `nix develop -c eon-test -p eon-runtime -p eon` passes; fmt and clippy on Linux and
  `--target aarch64-apple-darwin`.
- A test that fails without the fix where possible on Linux (for example a peer that closes
  right after writing), else the macOS CI run is the red/green and the bead says so.
- The next macOS CI run's `test:eon` no longer shows os error 22.

## Scope

runtime/ (and eon/ tests if needed). Codex review per AGENTS.md. Consequential? It changes no
wire format; it is a lifecycle detail of one read path, so no reference gate unless the fix
grows.

The GUI scenario failure there is kz4p.34 (Venus Metal alpha mode), unrelated to this bead.

comments.author: lucca
comments.text:
Plan (Opus planner and gate; Codex implements). Base 09bff88 in worktree ~/.cache/eon-agents/sockets.

Approval, relayed by eon-overseer (AP-COORDINATOR-001), recorded 2026-10-28: Lucca, 2026-10-27: "do these two too, then ... i want to move closer to the 'yu testing' gate", standing for the macOS launch path; Lucca, 2026-10-28: "lets get to working", on the plan to fix the macOS CI failures (kz4p.23-.28) with Opus planning and gating and Codex implementing. Not covered: push, promotion, main/stable, GitHub or site posts, workflow dispatch, renting a Mac, Lucca's running Eon.

Evidence read: steps/69-test-eon.log of run 40721211773 attempt 2. Every `os error 22` failure is "cannot bound Eon action result", i.e. control.rs `send_prepared_action`'s per-read `set_read_timeout`. The other failures (corrupt instead of incompatible, stop prompt EOF, window not ready, picker did not close) are downstream of the same inspection/action failure, except workspace_control.rs:1591. Inference (XNU `sosetoptlock`): setsockopt fails with EINVAL once a socket has both SS_CANTRCVMORE and SS_CANTSENDMORE, which a Unix stream socket gets when its peer closes. The reply is already buffered, and I/O on such a socket cannot block. Linux allows setsockopt after shutdown, so it cannot reproduce this.

Approach: keep the per-read deadline (it bounds the whole exchange), and give Eon Runtime one helper that applies a socket timeout and treats EINVAL as success, with a comment naming the Darwin rule. Rejected: setting the timeout once per connection, because each blocking read could then wait the full timeout again and the shared `deadline` (supervisor inspection) would stop bounding the exchange; poll(2) with nonblocking I/O, more code for the same result.

Sites (every per-deadline timeout before I/O in runtime/crates/eon-runtime/src): control.rs send_prepared_action (write and read loops); supervisor.rs Venus startup admission (write and read loops); sessions.rs read_management_response, lease acquisition write, stop_managed_sessions write. Left as they are: connect/accept-time setup (control.rs connect and handle_client, pane_labels observe setup) and pane_labels' `set_read_timeout(None)`, where the peer cannot have closed yet or a closed peer ends the connection with the same result.

workspace_control.rs:1591 (`directory_picker_retargets_cancels_and_stops_with_venus`): Eon takes the launch directory from `env::current_dir()` (supervisor.rs:757), i.e. getcwd, which on macOS returns the physical `/private/tmp/...` for a `/tmp/...` cwd. Eon canonicalizes nothing; the test's expectation is wrong. Fix the test to expect the physical path (`fs::canonicalize` of the launch directory at that assertion and any sibling assertion with the same cause), not the temp root, since a longer root lengthens socket paths toward macOS's 104-byte limit. Whether Eon should prefer a validated logical $PWD is a product question outside this bead; reported to eon-overseer, not filed.

Red check: none possible on Linux (no EINVAL there). The red is run 40721211773 attempt 2 (`test:eon`, 32 failures); the green is the next macOS CI run's `test:eon` without os error 22. No new test: the existing workspace_control suite on macOS is the regression check, and a Linux test of the helper would only mirror its code.

Checks: `nix develop -c eon-test -p eon-runtime -p eon` (Linux), `cargo fmt --check`, `cargo clippy --locked --all-targets -- -D warnings` for eon-runtime and eon, on Linux and `--target aarch64-apple-darwin`. Codex review per AGENTS.md.

Scope: runtime/crates/eon-runtime/src and eon/crates/eon/tests/workspace_control.rs. No contract, wire, or dependency change (libc is already a dependency); not consequential. Orbit and Venus sites are out of scope (orbit/src/socket.rs ignores its result; Venus sets timeouts once).

comments.author: lucca
comments.text:
Plan amendment (after eon-overseer's review of the plan): the helper treats EINVAL as success only when the socket also shows the peer's hangup, so a timeout is never silently dropped on a live connection. On EINVAL it polls the stream with zero timeout (events POLLIN, retrying EINTR) and returns Ok only if revents has POLLHUP; otherwise it returns the original EINVAL. Linux (unix_poll, sk_shutdown == SHUTDOWN_MASK after the peer's release) and XNU (EV_EOF on the read filter) both report POLLHUP once the peer has closed, and I/O on such a socket then returns buffered data, EOF or EPIPE without blocking. Taking the setter's result as an argument makes this testable on Linux: one unit test feeds a synthetic EINVAL with (a) a peer that wrote and closed, expecting Ok and then the buffered bytes followed by EOF, and (b) a live peer, expecting the EINVAL back. It fails if the helper swallows EINVAL unconditionally or rejects the closed case. The macOS red/green stays run 40721211773 attempt 2 against the next macOS CI run.

Out of scope, recorded, not filed (eon-overseer will raise it with Lucca): on macOS a launch from a `/tmp/x` directory shows the tab directory as `/private/tmp/x`, because Eon takes getcwd's physical path (supervisor.rs `env::current_dir()`). Preferring a validated logical `$PWD` would be a product choice.

comments.author: lucca
comments.text:
Proof (revision: the commit that carries this comment; Linux x86_64, worktree at base 09bff88, CARGO_BUILD_JOBS=4). Codex implemented; Opus gated.

Change: Eon Runtime's `sessions::bound_io(stream, set)` treats a socket-timeout EINVAL as success only when a zero-timeout poll(POLLIN) reports POLLHUP; any other error, or EINVAL without hangup, passes through. Used at control.rs `send_prepared_action` (write and read loops), supervisor.rs Venus admission (write and read loops, plus the 250 ms presentation-control write timeout set after admission, since Venus may already have closed), and sessions.rs `read_management_response`, lease-acquisition write and `stop_managed_sessions` write. workspace_control.rs: eight expectations of a cwd-derived path (Eon's launch directory twice, the fake Orbit's `current_dir()` log, the child shell's `$PWD`, `eon edit`'s relative file) now expect the physical path via `fs::canonicalize`, because on macOS `/tmp` is a symlink to `/private/tmp`. Raw expectations (HOME, picker selections, explicit snapshot directories, the temporary root) are unchanged.

Checks on the final tree:
- `nix develop -c eon-test -p eon-runtime -p eon`: pass (eon-runtime lib 131 passed, 1 ignored; workspace_control 49 passed; other targets 0 tests).
- `cargo fmt -p eon-runtime -p eon --check`: pass. `cargo clippy --locked -p eon-runtime -p eon --all-targets -- -D warnings` (dev shell): pass.
- Darwin: rustup stable rustc 1.96.0 (ac68faa20 2026-05-25) `cargo clippy --locked --target aarch64-apple-darwin -p eon-runtime -p eon --all-targets -- -D warnings`: pass (compiles for Darwin; proves nothing at run time).
- Red/green of `sessions::tests::bound_io_accepts_einval_only_after_peer_hangup`: green on the final helper; red for three wrong helpers (accept every EINVAL, never accept, accept on POLLIN instead of POLLHUP), each run with the file restored afterwards.
- macOS: not run. Red is run 40721211773 attempt 2 (`test:eon`, 32 of 49 workspace_control failures, os error 22 and the `/private/tmp` mismatch); the next macOS CI run's `test:eon` is the green check.

Correction to the plan amendment: POLLHUP alone does not prove both directions are shut down on Darwin (a peer's `shutdown(Write)` also raises EOF on the read filter, so poll reports POLLHUP while writes remain possible). The guard is the pair: Darwin's setsockopt returns EINVAL only when both SS_CANTRCVMORE and SS_CANTSENDMORE are set, and POLLHUP confirms the peer's hangup; current callers pass only valid positive timeouts, so they reach EINVAL in no other way.

title: Make the Unix connect-timeout test fill the backlog on macOS
description:
## Why

macOS CI run 40721211773 attempt 2 (e04553c; evidence in
/home/lucca/.cache/eon-agents/eon-overseer/ci-40721211773-a2/): `test:eon-runtime` failed
`sessions::tests::unix_connection_attempt_obeys_timeout` at
`runtime/crates/eon-runtime/src/sessions.rs:2546:9` (`assertion failed: result...is_err()`,
`steps/68-test-eon-runtime.log:190-191`). The test (2523-2550) uses `listen(0)`, queues one
connect, and expects `unix_connect_with_timeout` (sessions.rs:380) to time out. On Linux backlog 0
holds exactly one connection; Darwin evidently admits more (inference).

## Change

Eon Runtime test only: fill the listener's backlog in a loop (non-blocking connects until one
would block, with a bound) before the timed attempt, so the test holds on both kernels. Do not
make it Linux-only unless filling cannot be made deterministic on Darwin; then say why.

## Acceptance

- `nix develop -c eon-test -p eon-runtime` passes on Linux; fmt and clippy on Linux and
  `--target aarch64-apple-darwin`.
- The next macOS CI run passes the test.

## Scope

sessions.rs tests only. Codex review per AGENTS.md.

The GUI scenario failure there is kz4p.34 (Venus Metal alpha mode), unrelated to this bead.

comments.text:
Plan (Opus, 2026-10-28). Approval relayed by eon-overseer: Lucca, 2026-10-27, "do these two too, then ... i want to move closer to the 'yu testing' gate" (standing for the macOS launch path); 2026-10-28, "lets get to working" on fixing the macOS CI failures (kz4p.23-.28) with Opus planning and gating and Codex implementing. Not covered: push, promotion, main/stable, GitHub or site posts, workflow dispatch, renting a Mac, Lucca's running Eon.

Approach: in `sessions::tests::unix_connection_attempt_obeys_timeout` (runtime/crates/eon-runtime/src/sessions.rs, ~2581 at 32e0617), replace the single `queued` UnixStream with a loop of non-blocking socket2 connects to the listener that stops at the first WouldBlock (Linux, EAGAIN on a full AF_UNIX backlog) or ConnectionRefused (BSD/XNU refuse a full AF_UNIX queue at once instead of blocking), keeping the connected ones alive until after the timed attempt. A hard bound (512 connects) fails the test with the count instead of running out of descriptors; any other error panics with the error. The timed `unix_connect_with_timeout` attempt and the 1 s recv bound and `is_err` assertion stay as they are, so on Linux the attempt still exercises the poll timeout, and on Darwin it must return promptly with an error.

Not Linux-only: the fill is deterministic on both kernels because it stops on the kernel's own full-queue signal rather than on a guessed backlog size.

Red check: none on Linux (the test passes there today; the failure is Darwin-only). The native red is CI run 40721211773 attempt 2, steps/68-test-eon-runtime.log:190-191; the native green is the next macOS CI run.

Scope: this one test in sessions.rs. No production code, no dependency (socket2 and libc are already deps), no contract.

Checks: `nix develop -c eon-test -p eon-runtime` (Linux), `cargo fmt --check`, `cargo clippy --locked --all-targets -p eon-runtime -- -D warnings` on Linux and with `--target aarch64-apple-darwin`. Codex review per AGENTS.md. Portability: neutral.

comments.author: lucca
comments.text:
Change: `sessions::tests::unix_connection_attempt_obeys_timeout` now listens with backlog 1 instead of 0 and, before the timed attempt, fills the queue with non-blocking socket2 connects until the kernel reports it full (WouldBlock on Linux, ConnectionRefused on XNU), holding the connected sockets until the attempt finishes. More than 16 connects without a full-queue signal fails the test with the count; any other connect error panics with it. The timed `unix_connect_with_timeout` attempt, its 1 s watchdog and the `is_err()` assertion are unchanged. Root cause, from XNU source (bsd/kern/uipc_socket.c solisten): Darwin maps backlog 0 to somaxconn (128), so one queued connection never filled the queue and the timed connect succeeded. With backlog 1, Linux and XNU each admit 2. Plan amendment: listen(1) and bound 16 replace "listen(0), bound 512" after the Codex review (below), because listen(0) on XNU would hold about 193 descriptors before filling.

Checks on the final tree 1826faad099050c8123fac0da8dcb8dc136418fe (x86_64 Linux, Nix dev shell, CARGO_BUILD_JOBS=4):
- `nix develop -c eon-test -p eon-runtime`: pass (lib 131 passed, 1 ignored; the test ok).
- `cargo fmt --check -p eon-runtime`: pass. `cargo clippy --locked --all-targets -p eon-runtime -- -D warnings` (dev shell): pass.
- Darwin: rustup stable `cargo clippy --locked --target aarch64-apple-darwin --all-targets -p eon-runtime -- -D warnings`: pass (compiles for Darwin; proves nothing at run time).
- Red/green: no Linux red (the test passed on Linux before the change, as Codex recorded on the unchanged tree). The red is macOS CI run 40721211773 attempt 2, steps/68-test-eon-runtime.log:190-191; the next macOS CI run's `test:eon-runtime` is the green check. macOS: not run.

Coverage note (accepted, not new): on Darwin a full AF_UNIX queue refuses at once, so the timed attempt returns ECONNREFUSED without reaching socket2's poll; the test then checks a prompt error, not expiry of the 50 ms timeout. On Linux it reaches the poll as before.

Review ledger: Codex first round on tree feddbc3: 1 blocking (listen(0) is somaxconn on XNU, so the fill could exhaust descriptors before its 512 bound; fixed by listen(1) and bound 16), 1 new-surface note (timeout coverage on Darwin, recorded above). Opus gate rounds: 2, 0 blocking. Narrow Codex re-check of feddbc3..1826faa: 0 findings. Codex passes: 2, findings 1 blocking. Implementation: Codex, 2 runs (initial plus one fix round). title: Kill every supervisor a failing eon test spawned, on macOS too
description:
## Why

macOS CI run 40721211773 attempt 2 (e04553c; evidence in
/home/lucca/.cache/eon-agents/eon-overseer/ci-40721211773-a2/): failing `test:eon` tests leaked
supervisors (`steps/72-leftovers.log:258,263,286`: `/tmp/e0/ec-38994-14/eonbase` and
`target/debug/eon`). eon-test's guard (nix/test-sandbox.nix:27-30) then refused the next two
suites (`test:eon-manifest`, `test:mac-proof`: "an Eon supervisor of this user is running").
On Linux the sandbox's PID namespace cleans up; macOS has none.
`eonbase_replaces_exact_residue_after_its_supervisor_and_session_die` (workspace_control.rs
2853-2908) holds `second` as a plain `std::process::Child` and panicked at 2906; the debug `eon`
leak is likely another test holding a plain Child.

## Change

eon test code: hold every spawned supervisor or eon process in a kill-on-drop guard (reuse the
existing `ManagedChild` / `TestProcess`), so a panicking test cannot leak it. Search all of
eon/tests and runtime tests for plain `Child` holds of supervisors.

## Acceptance

- `nix develop -c eon-test -p eon` passes on Linux; fmt and clippy on Linux and
  `--target aarch64-apple-darwin`.
- A forced panic in one such test (local red check, not committed) leaves no process behind.
- The next macOS CI run shows no leftovers from test:eon and runs eon-manifest and mac-proof.

## Scope

Test code only. Codex review per AGENTS.md.

title: Build the macOS harness's shared Nix inputs once, not per check
description:
## Why

macOS CI run 40721211773 attempt 2 (e04553c; evidence in
/home/lucca/.cache/eon-agents/eon-overseer/ci-40721211773-a2/) used 263 of the harness's 320
minutes, about 230 of them on 50 `check:` steps that each rebuilt Orbit from scratch (2.5-5 min)
before failing the same way: Nix does not cache build failures. Once Orbit builds, those checks
will do real work, so the budget will be tight, and Mac minutes (CI queue, the rental, Yu's time)
are scarce.

## Change

In eon/tools/mac-proof: build what the checks share once, and stop repeating a known failure.
Either build all check attributes in one `nix build --keep-going` and report each check from it,
or add one Orbit build step that the `check:orbit-*` steps need, so they are skipped (listed,
never passed) when it fails. Keep per-check status in summary.txt/json. Re-check the 320m
`--timeout` and the job's 360m against the new shape and say what a full green run should take.

## Acceptance

- `nix develop -c eon-test -p mac-proof` passes; fmt and clippy on Linux and darwin.
- `run --dry-run` shows the new plan; a Linux test covers "shared build failed, checks skipped".
- Report the expected macOS run time.

## Scope

mac-proof only (and the workflow's timeout if the estimate needs it). Codex review per AGENTS.md.
close_reason: mac-proof builds the checks' shared inputs once in check-inputs and skips checks whose input failed; Linux tests, fmt, clippy (Linux and darwin) pass; expected green macOS run ~165m, timeouts unchanged; native proof is the next macOS CI run

comments.author: lucca
comments.text:
Plan (Opus, 2026-10-28). Codex implements; Opus gates.

Approvals, relayed by eon-overseer with the user's words: Lucca, 2026-10-27, "do these two too,
then ... i want to move closer to the 'yu testing' gate" (standing for the macOS launch path);
2026-10-28, "lets get to working" (the plan to fix the macOS CI failures kz4p.23-.28, Opus plans
and gates, Codex implements). Not covered: push, promotion, workflow dispatch, GitHub posts,
renting a Mac.

Evidence (ci-40721211773-a2/summary.txt): 47 check:orbit-*, eonbase-closure and
managed-command-path each rebuilt the same `orbitPackage` (flake.nix:286, shared by every
nix/orbit-checks.nix real-PTY check) and failed in libghostty-vt-sys, 2.5-13 min each.

Approach: shared direct inputs, built once, per-check skip. Nix dedupes a derivation inside one
invocation, and a check's real work stays its own step (own log, time, HOUR timeout, checks still
serial, which keeps the real-PTY checks off each other's CPU).

- `check_list` (eon/tools/mac-proof/src/run.rs:525): also record each check's .drv path
  (`nix eval --json .#checks.<sys> --apply` mapping names to `drvPath`).
- New step `check-inputs` (requires `check-list`, after it, before the `check:` loop at
  run.rs:214): the union of the checks' direct input derivations (`nix-store --query
  --references <check.drv>`, lines ending `.drv`; plain-line legacy output, stable across Nix
  versions, unlike `nix derivation show` JSON), built in one `nix build --keep-going --no-link
  --print-build-logs <drv>^*...`. Afterwards it records which inputs have an invalid output
  (`nix-store --query --outputs` then `nix-store --check-validity --print-invalid`), whether
  the build passed or not.
- Each `check:<name>` requires `check-list` when all its inputs are valid, else
  `check-inputs`, so the Runner's existing skip names it: "needs check-inputs, which did not
  pass". Checks whose inputs built run as now even when `check-inputs` failed.
- If `check-inputs` cannot tell which inputs failed (timeout, query failure), every check
  requires it (all skipped), never a re-run of a known failure.
- Help (main.rs:55-70) and docs/DEVELOPMENT.md:41 name the step.

Red check: a Linux test of the real check loop with a stub nix (no PATH mutation; a Context
field for the program is acceptable), where one shared input fails: checks on it are skipped
with the message and never run; a check off it runs and passes; summary.json keeps each
check's status. Red before the change (the stub sees every check build).

Scope: eon/tools/mac-proof, docs/DEVELOPMENT.md, and .github/workflows/mac-proof.yml only if
the run-time estimate needs a different timeout. No flake change, no new dependency, no contract
change.

Checks: `nix develop -c eon-test -p mac-proof`; `cargo fmt --check`; clippy `--locked
--all-targets -D warnings` on Linux and for aarch64-apple-darwin (recipe on kz4p.1);
`mac-proof run --dry-run` shows check-inputs. Report the expected full green macOS run time
from the a2 step durations against the 320m limit and 360m job.

before this comment), x86_64 Linux, worktree at base a211379:

- `nix develop -c eon-test -p mac-proof`: pass, 19 unit + 3 integration tests, including
  `failed_shared_inputs_skip_only_the_checks_that_need_them` (two checks share a failing input:
  both skipped with "needs check-inputs, which did not pass" and never built; a check on a good
  input passes; the shared input is built once) and `failed_combined_evaluation_keeps_the_shared_build`

- `cargo fmt --check -p mac-proof`: pass. `cargo clippy --locked -p mac-proof --all-targets -- -D

Shape as landed: `check-list` discovers names only (attrNames, as before). New step

title: Keep the supervisor's side of a control connection working after the client closes on macOS
description:
## Why

macOS CI run 40779777680 (head 32c3dff; evidence in
/home/lucca/.cache/eon-agents/eon-overseer/ci-40779777680/) still fails `package` (so all 16 GUI
scenario steps were skipped), check:eonbase-closure, check:managed-command-path and test:eon on two
eon tests:

1. `lost_stop_response_still_finishes_the_supervisor`: `69-test-eon.log:71-72`, panicked at
   workspace_control.rs:1071 "Eon process did not exit" (from :5714). The test writes Stop, then
   shuts down and drops before the supervisor accepts. Inferred cause: the server side kz4p.25
   missed. `runtime/crates/eon-runtime/src/control.rs:511` (`handle_client`) does
   `if stream.set_read_timeout(timeout).is_err() || stream.set_write_timeout(timeout).is_err() {
   return false; }` without `bound_io` (sessions.rs:390), so on Darwin, after the peer has gone,
   EINVAL drops the buffered Stop and the supervisor never exits. A product bug on macOS.
2. `tab_directory_retargets_future_sessions_without_crossing_tabs`: fails in every macOS run.
   `wait_for_picker_close` times out at :1175, and in the package build the request `write_all`
   at :1111 gets BrokenPipe (`03-package.log:10287-10288`): the supervisor closed early. Cause not
   found because the test sends the supervisor's stderr to null. Candidates: the same
   handle_client EINVAL path, or the macOS /tmp -> /private/tmp mismatch.

## Change

- Wrap both timeout calls in control.rs `handle_client` with `bound_io`. Audit every other
  `set_read_timeout` / `set_write_timeout` in Eon Runtime (diagnosis named pane_labels.rs:144-145
  and 178, sessions.rs:523 and 1632) and use `bound_io` wherever a peer may already have closed.
- For test 2: first send that test's supervisor stderr to a file kept on failure (test-only), so
  the next macOS run shows the cause even if this guess is wrong. If the evidence on Linux points
  at a fix (same EINVAL path or a path mismatch), make it; otherwise leave the diagnostic and say
  so on the bead.

## Acceptance

- `nix develop -c eon-test -p eon-runtime -p eon`; fmt and clippy on Linux and
  aarch64-apple-darwin.
- A Linux test that exercises a client closing right after writing a request where possible.
- The next macOS CI run passes `package` and test:eon, or test 2's log names its cause.

## Scope

runtime/ plus eon/crates/eon/tests/workspace_control.rs diagnostics. Codex review per AGENTS.md.
Approval: Lucca, 2026-10-28, "diagnose, fix, commit, push".
close_reason: Native macOS proof: mac-proof.yml run 40808735721 (head 6f7eb99, tree d142235, aarch64-macos, macos-15 runner) passes package, check-inputs, every check:* and test:* step, and leftovers (summary.txt in /home/lucca/.cache/eon-agents/eon-overseer/ci-40808735721/). The GUI scenario failure there is kz4p.34 (Venus Metal alpha mode), unrelated to this bead.

comments.author: lucca
comments.text: Correction to the proof comment above: Rust std uses plain accept(2) on macOS, which keeps the listener's O_NONBLOCK; on DragonFly, FreeBSD, NetBSD and OpenBSD it uses accept4(SOCK_CLOEXEC) (Rust 1.96 library/std/src/sys/net/connection/socket/unix.rs:247). The inherited-nonblocking claim covers macOS only; "and the BSDs" does not hold.

comments.author: lucca
comments.text:
Plan (Opus planner, 2026-10-28; Codex implements, Opus gates).

Likely test 2 cause (inferred from the code and the CI logs; native proof pending), found at the gate and not named in the bead: `ControlListener` is nonblocking (control.rs:475). On macOS and the BSDs, accept(2) gives the new socket the listener's O_NONBLOCK, and Rust std uses plain accept() there, while Linux accepts blocking. So when the supervisor accepted before the client's request arrived, `read_request` hit WouldBlock at once, replied malformed-action and closed. The client then saw BrokenPipe on its write (03-package.log:10287-10288). A dropped picker commit would also leave the popup open (69-test-eon.log, "directory picker did not close"). This is a product bug on macOS for any control request that races the accept. The /tmp -> /private path guess was ruled out: the supervisor keeps the picker's selection as given (no canonicalization), and the test's later cwd checks already canonicalize. Orbit has no such gap: it sets the mode on every accepted stream (orbit/src/host.rs:877, orbit/src/management.rs:180, :199, :395).

title: Read CPU and RAM for the Eon Bar chips on macOS
description:
## Why

The Eon Bar's CPU and RAM chips are a 1.0 feature (EON-C30, VEN-C28) but read `/proc`, so on
macOS they never appear. A Mac user would see a bar that silently lacks two default items.

Lucca (2026-10-27, relayed by eon-overseer): "i'd rather test everything possible and fix myself,
letting to Yu only final testing and final fixes that i missed ... so the more automated, the
better."

## Evidence

- `venus/src/system.rs:13-19` CPU from `/proc/stat`, `:93-99` RAM from `/proc/meminfo`; both
  return `None` when not Linux, so the chip is hidden (VEN-C28 "an unreadable reading shows no
  label rather than 0%").
- VEN-C28 (`venus/docs/CONTRACTS.md:1826`) names Linux, `/proc/stat` and MemTotal minus
  MemAvailable; EON-C30 (`docs/CONTRACTS.md:2374`) names "users on x86_64 Linux". Both are
  contract text, so macOS readings need Lucca's approval of new wording first.

## Scope

In scope: propose VEN-C28 and EON-C30 wording for macOS (CPU: whole-machine busy ticks over the
interval from `host_processor_info`/`host_statistics(HOST_CPU_LOAD_INFO)`; RAM: a stated
definition, recommended Activity Monitor's "Memory Used" = (active + wired + compressed) pages
over `hw.memsize`), stop for approval, then implement the macOS readers in `venus/src/system.rs`
behind `cfg(target_os = "macos")` with the existing parse/reject structure.

Out of scope: chip layout, settings, EONW, Runtime, other widgets (GPU/IO beads).

## Acceptance

- Lucca approved the contract wording (quoted on this bead with date) before code.
- macOS readers return `None` on a failed call, never 0% (existing rule); Linux readers and their
  four tests unchanged.
- Deterministic parts (tick deltas to percentage, page counts to percentage) are pure functions
  with one test each that runs on Linux; the syscall wrappers compile for the Apple target.
- Native observation is deferred to the harness's GUI scenario (chip visible with a plausible
  value in the capture, and the Venus log).

## Verification

- `nix develop -c eon-test -p yazelix-venus` exits 0; `cargo fmt --check`; `cargo clippy --locked
  --all-targets -- -D warnings` for Venus (AGENTS.md Verification).
- Gate check: `cargo check --locked --target aarch64-apple-darwin -p yazelix-venus` shows no
  error from `system.rs`.

## Stop Conditions

- Stop for Lucca's approval of the VEN-C28/EON-C30 wording before implementation.
- Stop if `libc` lacks the Mach host calls and a new crate (`mach2`) seems needed (dependency
  gate); report the gap instead.
- Read `venus/AGENTS.md` first; follow its rules.

## Maintenance Notes

- Alternative if Lucca prefers no contract change before launch: leave the chips hidden on macOS
  and list "no CPU/RAM chips" as a README macOS gap (friends'-gate bead).
close_reason: macOS CPU and RAM readers implemented under the approved VEN-C28/EON-C30 wording; Linux checks and darwin clippy green; native observation deferred to eon-mac-launch-kz4p.12

comments.text:
Started 2026-10-27 by agent in worktree ~/.cache/eon-agents/chips at 0833b3c. Approval (relayed by eon-overseer): Lucca, 2026-10-27: "do these two too, then ... i want to move closer to the 'yu testing' gate". The contract text itself still needs his approval (questions comment below); code proceeds on the recommendation, landing waits.

Reference gate (consequential: adds a macOS dependency edge and Venus's first unsafe code).
- Behavior and owners: on Apple Silicon macOS the Eon Bar shows the VEN-C28 CPU and RAM chips instead of hiding them. Venus's system module (venus/src/system.rs) alone owns sampling and parsing; application.rs's 2-second wake, CpuUse::between and the labels are unchanged and shared with Linux.
- References read (clones under ~/pjs/refs/sysstat-macos/):
  - btop v1.4.7 6e39144aaf5a6bc01b9f795010b0914431067183 src/osx/btop_collect.cpp: host_processor_info per core, busy = user+nice+system, sysconf page size, hw.memsize total; memory meter used = active+wire (does not match Activity Monitor; rejected).
  - htop 3.5.3 20882b8ef8271fb49ea0eb74bbfd484e9b0a11d8 darwin/Platform.c: used = wire + (internal - purgeable) + compressor; ChangeLog 3.5.2 "darwin: fix used memory calculation to match Activity Monitor". htop 3.4.1 348c0a6b had the older active+inactive+speculative+wire+compressor-purgeable-external form (rejected: XNU counts speculative inside free and throttled inside wire, so it drifts).
  - exelban/stats v3.0.23 5cf09a8cb0561ff24c28be4e5374d579d0601818 Modules/RAM/readers.swift and Modules/CPU/readers.swift: the older used form; CPU from host_statistics(HOST_CPU_LOAD_INFO) with wrapping u32 deltas, busy = user+system (nice excluded).
  - sysinfo v0.39.6 1bc6ed4f7d0dd03606de572a1531a165438b63ec src/unix/apple/: used = internal - purgeable + wire + compressor, page size sysconf(_SC_PAGESIZE), total hw.memsize, full HOST_VM_INFO64_COUNT.
  - XNU xnu-12377.121.6 ac9718fb1af618d5ce8678d0dc6e8a58f252216f osfmk/mach/vm_statistics.h, osfmk/kern/host.c, osfmk/kern/processor.c: cpu_ticks are natural_t (u32) summed over processors, order USER, SYSTEM, IDLE, NICE, NICE never incremented, 10 ms ticks (host sum wraps about every 50 days on 10 cores); host_statistics64 fills only the revisions that fit the count; non-platform binaries get cached results past 2-10 calls per second (Venus calls each once per 2 s).
  - libc 0.2.189 src/unix/bsd/apple/mod.rs: every call and struct needed; mach_host_self is #[deprecated] toward mach2; no host_page_size.
- Kept: Activity Monitor's Memory Used as htop 3.5.3 and sysinfo compute it, over hw.memsize; one HOST_CPU_LOAD_INFO call per sample with busy = user+system+nice (nice is always 0, so stats' exclusion makes no difference); available_parallelism (sysconf _SC_NPROCESSORS_ONLN in rustc 1.96) for the logical CPU count; sysconf page size (native arm64 only, so user and kernel page sizes agree); the host port taken once per process so readings add no port references; a count check that the kernel filled at least through internal_page_count.
- Rejected: since-boot first values (btop, stats, sysinfo) and htop's back-to-back 0% (the first reading stays a baseline, as on Linux); clamping or saturating a counter that went backwards into 0% (sysinfo, btop): it shows nothing for that interval, the existing rule; wrapping u32 deltas (stats): would need a second CpuTimes shape for one hidden 2 s interval about every 50 days; per-core host_processor_info (needs vm_deallocate, more unsafe, no per-core view in scope); mach2 (new package); spawning vm_stat/sysctl/top (no cheap CPU command).
- Dependency: libc =0.2.189, macOS-only, already in Venus's macOS closure through core-foundation (Cargo.lock gains one edge, no package). Version policy: the workspace's exact libc pin. Exit: drop it when a safe std or existing-dependency API covers these readings; move to mach2 through the dependency gate if libc removes mach_host_self.
- Check: pure from_host_ticks and from_host_pages tests on Linux; cargo check/clippy for aarch64-apple-darwin; native capture deferred to eon-mac-launch-kz4p.12.

comments.text:
Review round 1 on candidate tree 4b8de0bec9f407ffbbbd15d5fbb0b050a7b7581e (base 0833b3c): Codex clean (one nit, declined: a root CHANGELOG.md entry; sibling macOS beads kz4p.19 and kz4p.4 add none while macOS is unsupported). Fresh Claude reviewer: checks green (Venus suite 156+65+21 passed, fmt, Linux clippy, aarch64-apple-darwin clippy, tree unchanged), one blocking finding, four nits.
- Blocking, fixed: requesting libc's full HOST_VM_INFO64_COUNT (104 in libc 0.2.189, whose struct carries newer tag-storage fields) makes XNU xnu-12377.121.6 osfmk/kern/host.c:831-842 log "host_statistics64() count is larger than expected ... likely a bug" on every call when the kernel's struct is shorter (64). Venus now requests exactly revision 1 (offset_of swapped_count / 4, XNU's HOST_VM_INFO64_REV1_COUNT, host_info.h:254), the first with internal and compressor counts, and requires that count back. This corrects the reference gate's "full HOST_VM_INFO64_COUNT" (sysinfo's choice, rejected for this reason).
- Nit, taken: a zero page size would read as 0%; from_host_pages rejects it, with a test case.
- Nit, recorded (gate correction): XNU's host_statistics rate-limit cache (host.c:632, HOST_STATISTICS_TIME_WINDOW 1 s) is one global cache shared by all non-platform processes, not per process. If another app polls hard, a Venus CPU sample can be up to about 1 s old, so the interval is roughly 1-3 s instead of 2 s. Samples stay monotonic and two samples 2 s apart cannot be the same cached one, so the value is valid but approximate. Accepted: no contract change, since "over the last 2 seconds" already describes Linux's wake-to-wake interval, which also stretches with event-loop delay.
- Nit, recorded: portability disposition: isolated Darwin dependency (libc and the Mach calls in one macOS-only module of venus/src/system.rs; the arithmetic is platform-neutral).
- Nit, pending: the contract Status lines carry the approval wording ahead of the answer; they will quote the date and words of Lucca's actual answer before landing.

comments.text:
eon-mac-launch-kz4p.3 — questions for Lucca (draft 1, 2026-10-27)

1. VEN-C28 and EON-C30 macOS wording. Recommendation: approve as written below.
   RAM follows htop 3.5.3's "match Activity Monitor" fix and sysinfo 0.39.6:
   (internal - purgeable) + wired + compressed pages, over hw.memsize. This is
   more exact than the bead's earlier sketch (active + wired + compressed),
   which does not match Activity Monitor.

   VEN-C28, changed fields only (unchanged sentences kept as they are):

   - **Status:** Proven on native x86_64 Linux Wayland. Amended on 2026-10-27
     (approved by Lucca, relayed by eon-overseer) by `eon-mac-launch-kz4p.3`:
     readings on Apple Silicon macOS, implemented and awaiting native proof.
   - **Consumer:** One person using a Venus surface controlled by a full Eon
     workspace on Linux or Apple Silicon macOS.
   - **Result:** (only the two reading sentences and the hover count change)
     The CPU label shows whole-machine CPU use over the last 2 seconds as a
     whole percentage, from `/proc/stat` on Linux and from the Mach host CPU
     load ticks on macOS, where user, system and nice time count as busy; it
     first appears one interval after the surface opens. The RAM label shows
     whole-machine memory use as a whole percentage read on the same wake; it
     appears with the first reading. On Linux it is MemTotal minus
     MemAvailable over MemTotal from `/proc/meminfo`; on macOS it is Activity
     Monitor's Memory Used, app memory (internal pages less purgeable ones)
     plus wired and compressed pages, over `hw.memsize`. Hover and static
     AccessKit labels say `CPU use 12% across 16 logical CPUs, over the last 2
     seconds`, counting the later sample's per-CPU `/proc/stat` lines on Linux
     and the logical CPUs online on macOS, and `RAM use 43% of 31.3 GiB`.
   - **Important failures:** (one sentence added, last sentence changed)
     ... MemAvailable above MemTotal, shows no label for that reading, never
     0%. On macOS a failed host call, a CPU counter that went backwards (the
     32-bit tick counters wrap about every 50 days on a 10-core Mac),
     purgeable pages above internal ones, or use above `hw.memsize` likewise
     shows no label. A hidden label returns with the next valid reading. ...
     Platforms other than Linux and macOS show neither label.
   - **Owner:** Venus Scene owns the text and geometry, the application owns
     the 2-second wake, and a Venus module reads and parses `/proc/stat` and
     `/proc/meminfo` on Linux and calls the Mach host statistics and
     `hw.memsize` on macOS.
   - **Boundary:** No EONW or runtime change, configuration, per-core view,
     swap, per-process or GPU memory, history, graph or platform beyond Linux
     and Apple Silicon macOS. Its one dependency is target-only libc on macOS
     (`docs/CRATES.md`).
   - **Open proof:** (new) macOS: the chips with plausible values in the
     native capture and Venus log of the macOS harness
     (`eon-mac-launch-kz4p.12`). `host_cpu_use_counts_user_system_and_nice_as_busy`
     and `host_ram_use_is_app_wired_and_compressed_over_physical_memory`
     cover the macOS arithmetic on Linux.

   EON-C30, changed fields only:

   - **Status:** Proven on x86_64 Linux Wayland. Amended on 2026-10-27
     (approved by Lucca, relayed by eon-overseer) by `eon-mac-launch-kz4p.3`:
     Apple Silicon macOS readings, awaiting EON-C7's native proof.
   - **Consumer:** Full-Eon workspace users on x86_64 Linux, and on Apple
     Silicon macOS once EON-C7 is proven.

2. Unsafe code in Venus. Mach host calls are unsafe FFI, and Venus has
   `#![forbid(unsafe_code)]`. Recommendation: (a).
   (a) Change Venus's lib root to `#![deny(unsafe_code)]` and allow unsafe in
       one macOS-only module in venus/src/system.rs: five calls
       (mach_host_self once per process, host_statistics, host_statistics64,
       sysctlbyname, sysconf), each with a SAFETY note. Add libc =0.2.189 as a
       macOS-only Venus dependency: it is already in Venus's macOS build
       through core-foundation, so Cargo.lock gains one edge and no package.
       libc marks mach_host_self deprecated in favour of mach2; Venus allows
       that one call. The binary root keeps forbid. Exit: drop it if a safe
       std or existing-dependency API appears, or move to mach2 if libc
       removes the call.
   (b) mach2 crate: a new package, and the calls are still unsafe.
   (c) Spawn `vm_stat` and `sysctl` every 2 s: no unsafe for RAM, but macOS
       has no command for cumulative CPU ticks short of `top`, which is heavy.
   (d) Leave the chips hidden on macOS and list it as a README macOS gap.

title: Drain Orbit's PTY while it waits for a stopping shell on macOS
description:
## Why

macOS CI run 40779777680 (head 32c3dff; evidence in
/home/lucca/.cache/eon-agents/eon-overseer/ci-40779777680/):

1. check:orbit-program-status: `42-check-orbit-program-status.log:15-16`, panicked at
   orbit/tests/real_pty/program_status.rs:80 `Timeout`: `stop()` got Reply::Timeout after the
   lease's 3 s read timeout (management_lease.rs:53), in `answer_time_under_load` (511-546) where

2. test:yazelix-orbit: `simultaneous_stale_socket_claim_has_one_reachable_owner`,

   termination signal). Intermittent (1 of 25 attempts; passed the run before).

blocks in `ttywait` until the PTY output queue drains, and an exiting process no longer takes

+ SIGKILL 2 s window. Linux has no ttywait.

## Contract

ORB-C12 (bounded PTY process-group shutdown). No contract text change: this keeps its bound on
macOS. If the fix would change what ORB-C12 promises, stop and send the wording to eon-overseer.

While `contain()` and `reap()` wait, keep draining (and discarding, or routing as normal output
if that is the existing owner's job) the PTY master, or close/flush the master before waiting,
whichever fits Orbit's ownership of terminal state without losing output that ORB contracts say
is delivered. First confirm the mechanism with a reproducer the Linux harness can run where
possible (it may not reproduce on Linux; then rely on the macOS CI run and say so).

- Orbit's AGENTS.md checks for the changed crate: `nix develop -c eon-test -p yazelix-orbit`, the

- Portability disposition recorded (isolated Darwin behaviour or neutral).
- The next macOS CI run passes check:orbit-program-status and test:yazelix-orbit.

## Scope

orbit/ only. Read orbit/AGENTS.md first. Codex review per AGENTS.md. Approval: Lucca,
2026-10-28, "diagnose, fix, commit, push".

title: Remove the eon check's temporary directory when its build fails
description:
## Why

macOS CI run 40779777680 (head 32c3dff; evidence in
/home/lucca/.cache/eon-agents/eon-overseer/ci-40779777680/) failed `leftovers`: "left behind:
directories [e0, e1, e2, e3]". None existed before the run (`01-host.log:21`). The eon package
check (flake.nix:737-755) makes `/tmp/e$name` in preCheck and removes it only in postCheck, which
does not run when checkPhase fails; four failed eon checkPhases (package, eonbase-closure twice,
managed-command-path) account for exactly four directories. eon-test steps clean up (EXIT trap,
nix/test-sandbox.nix:54). The harness comment at run.rs:315 already expects "a failed build
leaves its own".

## Change

Make the derivation remove its `/tmp/e$name` on failure as well as success (for example an EXIT
trap set in preCheck, or failureHook), so a failed build leaves nothing. Keep the harness's
leftovers check strict. Linux builds use the sandbox's /tmp, so show the Linux derivation output
is unchanged or rebuilt green.

## Acceptance

- Linux: the x86_64-linux preCheck/postCheck strings are byte-identical to the base, and the
  combined `nix build .#default --no-link` follows at landing (overseer), after .29, .30 and .31.
  (Amended 2026-10-28 with eon-overseer: workspaceSource includes flake.nix, so any flake.nix
  edit rebuilds the Linux packages; one combined build replaces a .31-only one.)
- A forced checkPhase failure (local, not committed) leaves no /tmp/e* directory where the
  builder's /tmp is visible, or the reasoning is recorded if that cannot run on Linux.
- The next macOS CI run's leftovers lists no e* directories from failed builds.

## Scope

flake.nix (or nix/) only. Codex review per AGENTS.md. Approval: Lucca, 2026-10-28, "diagnose,
fix, commit, push".

title: Compare the canonical directory when waiting for the picker to close
description:
## Why

macOS CI run 40797703159 (head b8ed850; evidence in
/home/lucca/.cache/eon-agents/eon-overseer/ci-40797703159/) fails `package`, `check-inputs` and
test:eon on one test, so the 16 GUI scenario steps are skipped again. kz4p.29's stderr diagnostic
names the cause (`steps/70-test-eon.log:71-75`):

    panicked at eon/crates/eon/tests/workspace_control.rs:1185:9:
    directory picker did not close: active tab directory Some("/private/tmp/e0/ec-64533-44/first"),
    expected "/tmp/e0/ec-64533-44/first"

On macOS `/tmp` is a symlink to `/private/tmp`, and Eon reports the physical cwd. kz4p.25 already
canonicalized eight such expectations in this file (for example :4674-4675); `wait_for_picker_close`
(around :1150-1190) still compares the raw path. The supervisor did not crash: the earlier
BrokenPipe was the test tearing down after this timeout.

## Change

Test-only: make `wait_for_picker_close` (or its callers) compare against the canonical directory,
matching how kz4p.25 handled the others. Check every caller and any other raw-path comparison in
workspace_control.rs that a /tmp root reaches on macOS (it runs under /tmp/e0 in the package build
and under the eon-test sandbox root in test:eon). The product fix that would show the logical path
is eon-2cm5, which will revert these expectations; do not implement it here.

## Acceptance

- `nix develop -c eon-test -p eon --test workspace_control` passes on Linux.
- A Linux red/green where possible: run the test with its root reached through a symlink (local,
  not committed) and show it fails before and passes after; otherwise record why not.
- The next macOS CI run passes `package`, `check-inputs` and test:eon.

## Scope

eon/crates/eon/tests/workspace_control.rs only. Codex review per AGENTS.md. Approval: Lucca,
2026-10-28, "diagnose, fix, commit, push".

title: Find and fix the macOS orbit-clipboard check failure
description:
## Why

macOS CI run 40797703159 (head b8ed850; evidence in
/home/lucca/.cache/eon-agents/eon-overseer/ci-40797703159/) fails check:orbit-clipboard
(`steps/11-check-orbit-clipboard.log:14-15`), after 1.06 s:

    panicked at orbit/tests/real_pty/support.rs:480:26:
    peer closed before a complete ORBS message

The same check passed in run 40779777680 (head 32c3dff). The only Orbit change between the two
heads is kz4p.30 (d8222a5): `reap()` and `contain()` in orbit/src/host.rs now call
`discard_shutdown_output()` (orbit/src/pty.rs) each tick. `reap()` runs on `Decision::Reap`
(host.rs ~1448), which may also follow a natural exit or hangup, where ORB contracts say output
still feeds the terminal. If discarding there drops bytes or closes a peer early, that is a
regression from kz4p.30; otherwise the failure is an intermittent macOS race. Unknown which.

## Change

1. Find which receive closed (observer or client, which phase of orbit/tests/real_pty/clipboard.rs)
   and why. Try to reproduce on Linux: repeat `nix build .#checks.x86_64-linux.orbit-clipboard`
   (with --rebuild) at b8ed850 and at 32c3dff, and the eon-test real-PTY path, enough times to
   tell a regression from a flake. Read when Bend decides Reap and whether pending PTY output can
   still be owed to a client or observer at that point.
2. If kz4p.30 is at fault, narrow the drain to the paths where nothing is owed (explicit stop,
   termination containment), keeping kz4p.30's macOS ttywait fix. If it is a pre-existing race,
   fix its owner. If no cause is found on Linux, add the smallest diagnostic that makes the next
   macOS run name it (which peer, last message received) and say so on the bead.

## Contract

ORB-C12 and whatever ORB contract covers clipboard writes / output delivery; no contract text
change. If a fix would change what one promises, stop and send the wording to eon-overseer.

title: Let Venus show a translucent background on Metal
description:
## Why

macOS CI run 40808735721 (head 6f7eb99; evidence in
/home/lucca/.cache/eon-agents/eon-overseer/ci-40808735721/) passes every build, check and test for
the first time, then the GUI scenario's `launch` fails in 3 s and every later scenario step is
skipped (`stop` fails only because the supervisor is already gone). Supervisor log
(`scenario/logs/g1-6b3eafce...-80952.log`):

    Eon Desktop started: pid 80954
    Error: "the GPU surface does not support premultiplied transparency"
    Eon Desktop exited: exit status: 1
    supervisor failed: cannot admit Eon Desktop presentation: Venus closed before native startup admission

Cause (confirmed from source): `surface_alpha_mode` (venus/src/render.rs:2976-2989, called at :999)
requires `CompositeAlphaMode::PreMultiplied` whenever `background_opacity < 1.0`, but wgpu-hal
30.0.0's Metal backend only ever reports `[Opaque, PostMultiplied]`
(wgpu-hal-30.0.0/src/metal/adapter.rs:468-471). Eon's default is `background_opacity = 0.80`
(docs/CONFIGURATION.md:12), so Eon fails to launch with the default config on every Mac, not
just the CI VM. A blocker for Yu's `final` run.

Lead to verify, not assume: wgpu's Metal `PostMultiplied` only does `render_layer.setOpaque(false)`
(wgpu-hal-30.0.0/src/metal/surface.rs:232-233); CoreAnimation composites a CAMetalLayer's contents as
premultiplied regardless, so on Metal `PostMultiplied` may in fact be premultiplied compositing.

## Contract

The Venus contract that owns window transparency / background opacity (find its VEN-C in
venus/docs/CONTRACTS.md) and EON-C configuration of `background_opacity`. Expected: no contract text
change (this makes the documented setting work on macOS). If the fix would change what a contract
promises (for example falling back to opaque on macOS), stop and send the wording to eon-overseer.

## Change

Plan first, with the reference gate (AGENTS.md consequential shape: platform presentation):
read the owning docs/REFERENCES.md routes and at least one comparable wgpu/Metal implementation
(wgpu upstream issues/examples on Metal alpha modes; another wgpu-on-macOS terminal or app with a
translucent window) and record what they do. Then choose the alpha mode per what the surface offers
so a translucent background works on Metal with Venus's colour math still correct (premultiplied
vs straight; check clear_color and the shaders), keep PreMultiplied where offered (Wayland), and
keep the error only where no correct mode exists. Check the macOS window is created transparent
(winit) so non-opaque layer content shows the desktop behind it. Update the unit test at
render.rs:~5800 to cover the Metal mode list.

## Acceptance

- Unit test for the chooser covering `[Opaque, PostMultiplied]` (Metal) and the Wayland lists.
- Venus's AGENTS.md checks: `nix develop -c eon-test -p yazelix-venus`, `cargo fmt --check`,
  `cargo clippy --locked --all-targets -- -D warnings`, and clippy for aarch64-apple-darwin.
- Linux behaviour unchanged (same mode chosen on Wayland; state why).
- Portability disposition recorded.
- The next macOS CI run passes `launch`, and the scenario's captures show a translucent
  background over the desktop (the colour must not be visibly wrong).

## Scope

"diagnose, fix, commit, push" and "handle it. get it done." (overnight, 2026-10-29).

title: Give the macOS scenario a known backdrop behind Venus
description:
## Why

macOS CI run 40817193873 (head 97febc7; evidence in
/home/lucca/.cache/eon-agents/eon-overseer/ci-40817193873/) is the first where Eon renders on macOS:
`scenario/captures/02-launch.png` shows the tab bar, status widgets, the project picker (fzf) and
the hints bar. Yet `launch` fails and the other 13 scenario steps are skipped:

    Venus's window is blank or differs from the desktop before launch in only 4.6% of it

The runner's desktop is pure black (`01-desktop.png`, pixel (0,0,0)), and Venus's translucent
background over it captures as (1,1,1), so only text and chrome differ. `shown()`
(eon/tools/mac-proof/src/scenario.rs:~400-433) compares the window region with the pre-launch
desktop at `SHOWN = 0.05` (:24) using `near()` with picture.rs's TOLERANCE; no threshold or
tolerance can separate (1,1,1) from (0,0,0). The check is blind on any dark desktop, so Yu's `final`
run (Environment::User) could fail the same way on a dark wallpaper. A black desktop also cannot
show translucency, which kz4p.34's acceptance needs (translucent, correctly coloured background).

## Change

Give the scenario a known, non-black backdrop behind Venus so the "window shown" check and a
translucency observation are deterministic on any Mac, in both environments. Recommended shape
(overseer): the harness shows its own opaque solid-colour backdrop window (objc2, in mac.rs where
the scenario's other AppKit code lives) covering the main display beneath Venus, before the
pre-launch desktop capture, and closes it when the scenario ends (including on failure). Rejected:
changing the desktop wallpaper (persistently changes the user's settings on Yu's Mac); lowering
SHOWN (would let a blank window pass). If the planner finds a simpler deterministic route, record
why on the bead.

With a known backdrop colour B and Venus's background C at opacity 0.8, also check that the window
body is translucent and roughly correctly blended (≈ 0.8·C + 0.2·B per channel, tolerance chosen
from the capture path, Retina/colour-profile aware), and report it as a scenario observation.
That is kz4p.34's native proof (VEN-C11 on Metal); do not edit VEN-C11's proof record here.
If the observation shows wrong blending (for example straight vs premultiplied), report it to
eon-overseer rather than loosening the check.

## Acceptance

- `nix develop -c eon-test -p mac-proof` (or the crate's existing test path), fmt, clippy on Linux
  and aarch64-apple-darwin.
- Unit tests for any new picture logic (blend check) on synthetic pictures.
- The next macOS CI run passes `launch`, its captures show Venus over the backdrop, and the
  translucency observation passes.
- The backdrop leaves nothing behind (leftovers step stays green).

## Scope

eon/tools/mac-proof only. Read the harness's README/docs first. Codex review per AGENTS.md
(gate/validator code: include the scope line). Approval: Lucca, 2026-10-28, "diagnose, fix,
commit, push"; 2026-10-29 overnight, "handle it. get it done."
