comments.text:
Plan (Opus planner, 2026-10-29). Implementer: Codex; gates: Opus first, Codex review, Opus final.

Approvals, relayed by eon-overseer: Lucca, 2026-10-27, "do these two too, then ... i want to move closer to the 'yu testing' gate" (the macOS launch path); 2026-10-28, "lets get to working" (fix the macOS CI failures with the Opus-plans/Codex-implements split) and "diagnose, fix, commit, push"; 2026-10-29 overnight, on the fourth run, "ok, going to sleep. handle it. get it done." Push, dispatch, promotion and GitHub posts are not covered by this session.

Contract (smallest observable): in the Private scenario (`run`, `scenario`, and `final`'s automatic part), when Screen Recording is granted, the harness shows an opaque solid backdrop below every normal window on the main display before its pre-launch captures, so `shown()` compares Venus against a known colour; a new `translucency` step measures the backdrop's share through Venus's default background with two backdrop colours and checks it is 1 - background_opacity within 0.05 per channel. No EON-C/VEN-C text or proof record changes; VEN-C11's record stays for kz4p.34.

Approach:
1. Backdrop process. `mac-proof` re-executes itself (std::env::current_exe) with an internal `backdrop R G B` command that only main.rs dispatches (not in USAGE). On macOS, mac.rs `backdrop(rgb)` on the main thread: NSApplication with the Accessory activation policy (no Dock icon, never activated), a borderless, opaque, shadowless NSWindow covering NSScreen::screens()[0] (the main display), sRGB background colour, level CGWindowLevelForKey(DesktopIconWindowLevel) + 1 (above the wallpaper and desktop icons, below every normal window, so below Venus and never in Venus's layer-0 window list), ignores mouse events, collection behaviour CanJoinAllSpaces | Stationary | IgnoresCycle, orderFrontRegardless (no key, no activation: desktop focus kept), prints `shown` on stdout, then runs the app. A thread reading stdin exits the process at EOF, so the window goes with the harness however it ends. Elsewhere `backdrop` errs "macOS only".
2. scenario.rs: a `Backdrop` holding the child (stdin piped, stdout read for `shown` with a 10 s limit, stderr to the step log), killed and reaped on drop. `Scenario` keeps an `Option<Backdrop>`; `clean()` drops it, and so does Scenario's drop, independent of the supervisor condition. `launch`, when Screen Recording is available: show the dark backdrop (32,32,32) and capture `backdrop`, then the light one (224,224,224) and capture `desktop` (the picture `shown()` compares with). Changing colour stops the old process, starts a new one, waits for `shown` and 1 s.
3. Config: the private config.toml also sets `[terminal] background_opacity = OPACITY` (0.8), so the check's expectation is the scenario's own input, not a mirrored default.
4. `translucency` step (needs GUI login + Screen Recording, requires launch, placed right after it, window: true): capture Venus over the light backdrop, switch to the dark one and capture again, switch back to light (also on error) so later `shown()` checks still hold. In picture.rs, pure helpers: the most common colour of a picture and its share, and the per-channel backdrop share (P_light - P_dark)/(B_light - B_dark), with B taken from the pre-launch captures cropped to Venus's window. Unavailable (left for Yu) when either pre-launch crop is not uniform (something else lies behind Venus). Check fails when a dominant colour covers under 25% of the window, the backdrops differ by under 64 in a channel, or a share is off 1 - OPACITY by more than 0.05; the log records P, B, the shares and the implied background C = (P_dark - s*B_dark)/(1 - s). A failed blend is reported to eon-overseer, not loosened.
5. Docs: `scenario --help` step text and Evidence paragraph; docs/DEVELOPMENT.md's macOS harness paragraph (one or two sentences).

Dependency note (AP-DEPENDENCY-001): no new crate. objc2-app-kit 0.3.2 and objc2-core-graphics 0.3.2 gain features (NSApplication, NSResponder, NSWindow, NSColor, NSScreen, NSGraphics; CGWindowLevel), and objc2-foundation =0.3.2 (already locked under objc2-app-kit) may become a direct dependency for MainThreadMarker/NSArray. Comparable: winit 0.30.13's macOS window setup (cargo registry) for objc2 0.6 NSWindow creation; kept: main-thread AppKit, borderless window; rejected for the harness: an in-process window (the scenario's waits never run the AppKit run loop), changing the wallpaper (changes Yu's settings), lowering SHOWN (passes a blank window), osascript/JXA (a new checked-in language).

Red check: picture.rs unit tests on synthetic pictures: dominant colour and share; backdrop share accepts 0.2 and rejects an opaque window (0) and a linear-light blend (~0.48). The CI failure itself (a (1,1,1) window over a (0,0,0) desktop) is the native red; the next macOS CI run is the native green. Linux proves only compilation and the pure logic.

Scope: eon/tools/mac-proof, Cargo.lock if features change it, docs/DEVELOPMENT.md. Not Venus, not the manual (User) part of `final`, not VEN-C11's proof record, no push or dispatch.

Checks: nix develop -c eon-test -p mac-proof; cargo fmt --check; cargo clippy --locked -p mac-proof --all-targets -- -D warnings on Linux; rustup run stable cargo clippy --locked --target aarch64-apple-darwin -p mac-proof --all-targets -- -D warnings (kz4p.1 recipe). Portability: Darwin-isolated (mac.rs native module); Linux stubs.

title: Give the translucency step a background colour Eon honours
description:
## Why

macOS CI run 40828543315 (head c03ca4b; evidence in
/home/lucca/.cache/eon-agents/eon-overseer/ci-40828543315/) passes 87 of 90 steps, including every
GUI scenario step. kz4p.35's `translucency` step fails (`steps/*-translucency.log`,
`scenario/captures/07..10-translucency-*.png`):

    P_light [39,39,39], P_dark [6,6,6], B_light 224, B_dark 32, C' 128, opacity 0.8;
    backdrop shares 0.171875; implied background C ~0.6; expected light 147.2

The blend works (share 0.17 vs 0.2; 0.172*224 ~ 39), but the window's own colour stayed ~0: the
driver's OSC 11 grey never became Venus's default background, and OSC 111 "restored" nothing.
Unknown whether Eon honours OSC 11 at all (Orbit/libghostty dynamic default colours -> frames ->
Venus's default-background fill, venus/src/scene.rs:3819 `is_default_background`, render/cells.rs)
or whether this is macOS-specific.

## Change

1. Find out on Linux whether OSC 11 changes Eon's default background today (code path, and a
   cheap Linux observation if one exists). Report the answer to eon-overseer first.
2. If Eon does not support OSC 11: that is a product gap, not this bead. Do not implement it;
   eon-overseer files it for Lucca. Make the translucency step use a reference colour the scenario
   controls through supported input (for example the scenario's own config or palette, whatever
   sets Venus's default background), keeping kz4p.35's point that an absolute colour check, not
   only the share, must pass. Keep the share check.
3. If Eon supports OSC 11 on Linux and not on macOS: that is a macOS product bug; plan its fix at
   its owner instead and say so.
Also: the share measured 0.172 against 0.2 expected (within the 0.05 tolerance). Note on the bead
whether that is expected (colour management, sRGB) or a sign of something else.

## Acceptance

- mac-proof checks (`nix develop -c eon-test -p mac-proof`, fmt, clippy Linux and darwin), plus
  the owner's checks if a product fix is chosen.
- The next macOS CI run passes `translucency` with an absolute colour check.

line). Approval: Lucca, 2026-10-28, "diagnose, fix, commit, push"; 2026-10-29 overnight, "handle

Diagnosis (step 1): Eon does not honour a lone OSC 11, on any platform; this is case 2.
- Evidence, code at the pinned revisions: Orbit sets libghostty's default palette only

  stores OSC 10/11 as overrides, but its render state (src/terminal/render.zig:1052-1066) copies
  background and foreground only when both `get()` are non-null; otherwise it keeps its initial
  (0,0,0) background and (255,255,255) foreground (render.zig:380-382). With no default foreground,
  an OSC 11 alone never reaches `snapshot.colors()` (orbit/src/frame.rs:302, :457), so Venus's
  default-background fill (venus/src/scene.rs:3560, render.rs:1557) stays black. OSC 111 then has
  nothing to restore. The same gap leaves an OSC 11 query unanswered (Terminal.zig:189-194 returns
  null with nothing set), so programs that ask for the background to choose light or dark get no
  reply.

linear-light compositing would give about 107 over 224, not 39. A transfer-curve mismatch between

title: Find and fix the macOS orbit-selection check failure
description:
## Why

macOS CI run 40828543315 (head c03ca4b; evidence in
/home/lucca/.cache/eon-agents/eon-overseer/ci-40828543315/, `steps/*-check-orbit-selection.log`)
fails check:orbit-selection after 0.08 s:

    panicked at orbit/tests/real_pty/selection.rs:208:5: assertion failed: !selected(&last)

The test's last phase (selection.rs:~186-208) expects the child's exit to clear a presented
selection, so the last Frame before Exited shows none. The check passed in runs 2-5 (heads 32c3dff
through 97febc7); no Orbit source changed since run 5 (only eon/tools/mac-proof). So likely an
intermittent race: either the test reads a frame order Orbit does not promise, or Orbit can send
Exited before the selection-clearing frame (an ordering bug under ORB contracts).

## Change

Find which: read Orbit's exit path (child exit -> selection clear -> final frame -> Exited) and the
contract that promises the clear. Try a Linux repro (`nix build .#checks.x86_64-linux.orbit-selection
--rebuild` in a loop, and under CPU load), as kz4p.33 did for clipboard. Fix the owner: Orbit if
the promised order can break, else the test. If no repro and no cause, add a test-only diagnostic
naming the frames received after the gate, and say so on the bead.

## Contract

The ORB contract covering selection and exit (find it in orbit/docs/CONTRACTS.md). No text change;
if one seems needed, stop and send the wording to eon-overseer.

## Acceptance

- Orbit's AGENTS.md checks for the changed crate (`nix develop -c eon-test -p yazelix-orbit`, the
  orbit-selection Nix check repeated, fmt, clippy Linux and aarch64-apple-darwin).
- Portability disposition recorded.
- The next macOS CI run passes check:orbit-selection.

## Scope

orbit/ only. Read orbit/AGENTS.md first. Codex review per AGENTS.md. Approval: Lucca, 2026-10-28,
"diagnose, fix, commit, push"; 2026-10-29 overnight, "handle it. get it done."
close_reason: Native macOS proof: mac-proof.yml run 40842410369 (head 0b6ef93, tree d679722, aarch64-macos, macos-15 runner): 89 of 90 steps pass, including every build, check and test step and every GUI scenario step (launch, translucency, picker ... stop) and leftovers; only retina is skipped (no HiDPI display on the runner; left for Yu by design). Evidence: /home/lucca/.cache/eon-agents/eon-overseer/ci-40842410369/.

comments.author: lucca
comments.text:
Plan (Opus, 2026-10-29, at 08e8873). Approvals relayed by eon-overseer: Lucca 2026-10-27 "do these
two too, then ... i want to move closer to the 'yu testing' gate" (macOS launch path); 2026-10-28
"lets get to working" (fix the macOS CI failures with the Opus-plans/Codex-implements split) and
"diagnose, fix, commit, push"; 2026-10-29 overnight "ok, going to sleep. handle it. get it done."
Not covered: push, promotion, workflow dispatch, posts, Lucca's running Eon.

## Cause (from source; no repro yet)

The child's exit reaches Bend by one of two orders:
- reap first: host.rs `wake` -> `drain_exited` -> `ChildExited{drained}` -> session.bend `exited`
  -> `exit_cleared`, which with a presented selection decides `Unselect{True}` + `output` (a frame
  with no selection) before the stop, then Exited;
- PTY first: the slave closes at exit before the zombie is reapable, `read_into` sees EIO,
  host.rs `pty_closed` finds no reap -> `PtyClosed` -> session.bend `ended`, which decides only
  `Unselect{presented}`. Unselect clears libghostty (host.rs:1377) but publishes nothing; the later
  `ChildExited{drained: False}` sees presented = False, so no frame follows and Exited arrives
  after the last frame that still shows the selection.

The failure at selection.rs:208 is the second order (wider window on macOS; tiny on Linux).
docs/BEHAVIOR.md already limits its claim to "when the host reaps the child while the PTY is
open". ORB-C9 says client loss or exit clears the selection; the PTY-first order leaves the client
presenting a cleared selection. Owner: Orbit's Bend policy, not the test.

## Fix

- orbit/src/session.bend `ended` (PtyClosed): when a selection was presented, publish the clear as
  `exit_cleared` does without drained output: `Unselect{True}` then `output(flags, ...)` with the
  route Idle and presented False; otherwise unchanged (`Unselect{False}`, no frame). `step` passes
  flags. Comment updated.
- Laws unchanged: LAWS.bend's PtyClosed lifecycle law is `quiet` (no lifecycle moves) and the view
  law takes a Framed act in Plain pace. Regenerate proof/ lemmas with tools/step-proof.rs if the
  step shape needs it; orbit-laws must print ALL PROOFS CHECK. If a law would have to change, stop.
- Test (red check): orbit/tests/real_pty/selection.rs keeps its first server (usually reap first,
  now passes either way) and adds a second run of the same selection-shell.sh in a close mode
  (env var): print text, host-select it, gate, close fds 0-2 (as tests/pty-reopen-shell.sh does),
  gate, exit 3. The test releases the first gate, requires a frame with no selection while the
  child still lives (deterministic PTY-first order), then releases the second gate and expects
  Exited 3 with no selected frame between. Red at the base: no frame arrives (receive timeout).
- docs/BEHAVIOR.md: drop the reap-while-open limit; describe both runs. ORB-C9 text unchanged.

Scope: orbit/ only (session.bend, proof/ if regenerated, tests/real_pty/selection.rs,
tests/selection-shell.sh, docs/BEHAVIOR.md). No host.rs, protocol, or nix change expected.
Portability: neutral (Bend policy and test; fd close is POSIX).

Checks: `nix develop -c eon-test -p yazelix-orbit`; orbit-selection Nix check repeated (--rebuild
loop); orbit-laws; orbit-boundary unchanged; cargo fmt --check; clippy -D warnings on Linux and
aarch64-apple-darwin (kz4p.1 recipe). Red/green: the close-mode run fails with 08e8873's
session.bend and passes after.

comments.text:
Correction to the previous comment's "Deterministic check" section: the next macOS CI run of
check:orbit-selection is not proof of the end-of-file order. That real-PTY check neither forces
nor records which order happened, so a pass may exercise the reap-first path again. Native macOS
regression validation remains pending, and the check's coverage of the end-of-file-first order on
macOS is probabilistic; the deterministic coverage of the policy is the worker unit test.
Ledger addition: narrow re-check of 08e8873..84c46d3's fixes: 1 blocking (that overclaim, fixed
here), 1 nit (partly synthetic facts in the unit test; not taken, it does not weaken the
assertion).

comments.author: lucca
comments.text:
Final shape and proof (Opus gate, 2026-10-29). Supersedes the plan comment where they differ.

## Cause (corrected)

`PtyClosed` arises only when a PTY master read returns 0 (end of file) before the child is
reapable. EIO never produces it: orbit/src/pty.rs `read_into` closes on EIO only after a
successful reap, which then takes the `ChildExited` path. On macOS the session's controlling
terminal keeps the slave open while the child lives (so orbit-pty-reopen passes there, CI run
40828543315 step 44); when the session leader exits and releases it, the master reads 0 while the
child is not yet reapable. session.bend `ended` then decided `Unselect` without publishing, and
the later `ChildExited{drained: False}` saw nothing presented, so `Exited` followed a frame that
still showed the selection: the CI failure at selection.rs:208. The macOS kernel mechanism is
inference from the source paths and that CI evidence, not a native observation.

## Change

- orbit/src/session.bend: `ended(flags, session)` (PtyClosed) decides `Unselect{True}` and
  `republished` when a selection is presented (route Idle, presented False, copy kept); otherwise
  exactly the base decisions. `republished`, not `output`: `output` can deliver clipboard writes
  and detach on overflow, which `lifecycle_follows_its_contracts` forbids for PtyClosed (Codex
  stopped on it, round 1). The base helper is kept as `end_sequence` for the anchor-lost tick,
  whose decisions are unchanged.
- orbit/proof/{step,view,lease}.bend: `fits_pty_closed` case splits regenerated with
  tools/step-proof.rs; no lemma statement, law, or other definition changes (checked by diff and by
  the Codex review).
- orbit/tests/real_pty/selection.rs: the last phase's assertion names the frames received after
  the exit gate (revision, selected), so a future macOS failure shows what arrived.
- orbit/docs/BEHAVIOR.md: the clear is published in either order; no real-PTY check forces the
  end-of-file order. The reap-first sensitivity claim is kept.
- Dropped from the plan: the close-mode second run. Closing fds 0-2 reaches `PtyClosed` on
  neither platform (Linux: EIO waits for the reap; macOS: the controlling terminal holds the slave).

Portability: neutral (Bend policy, test diagnostic, docs). Contract: ORB-C9 text unchanged; laws
unchanged. No CHANGELOG entry: no wire, protocol, or contract change, and the visible effect is on
unsupported macOS.

## Accepted gap

No deterministic regression check: the end-of-file-before-reap order cannot be forced by a child
from bash on either platform, and the unchanged laws permit a clear without a frame. Red evidence
is macOS CI run 40828543315 (head c03ca4b, steps/50-check-orbit-selection.log). Green is
probabilistic: the next macOS CI runs of check:orbit-selection. A law requiring a published clear
before `Exited` would make it a policy check; that is a law change, put to Lucca via eon-overseer.

## Proof (tree bb5fed43d24144f6d1c7fcbe17863463fdda58fb on base 08e8873, x86_64 Linux, Opus run)

- `nix build --no-link -L --keep-going` orbit-laws, orbit-boundary, orbit-selection,
  orbit-selection-tick, orbit-pty-reopen, orbit-lifecycle, orbit-descendant-exit,
  orbit-detached-exit: all pass; orbit-laws log `ALL PROOFS CHECK`.
- orbit-selection `--rebuild` x5: pass.
- `nix develop -c eon-test -p yazelix-orbit`: 54 unit + 18 lifecycle pass (50 real-PTY ignored,
  run through the Nix checks above).
- `cargo fmt --check -p yazelix-orbit`; `cargo clippy --locked -p yazelix-orbit --all-targets --
  -D warnings`: pass.
- `cargo clippy --locked --target aarch64-apple-darwin -p yazelix-orbit --all-targets -- -D
  warnings` (kz4p.1 recipe, rustup stable 1.96.0): pass. Compilation only; no macOS runtime claim.

Ledger: Codex implementation 1 run + 3 resumes (round 1 law stop: `output` detaches on clipboard
overflow; round 2 scope stop: close-mode run cannot reach PtyClosed; round 3 docs). Opus first
gate: 1 finding (BEHAVIOR.md dropped the reap-first sensitivity claim), fixed. Codex review

title: Give the macOS harness a HiDPI virtual display for the Retina step
description:
## Why

Every macOS CI run skips `retina` ("no HiDPI display: the main display runs 1024x768 points at
1024x768 pixels (scale 1, 60 Hz) and offers no HiDPI mode", run 40842410369), and the rented
Scaleway Mac (kz4p.12) will be headless too, defaulting to a non-Retina 1920x1080 virtual
display. So scale-2 rendering (VEN-C16's Retina item, kz4p.17's `venus: window scale factor N`)
would rest on Yu alone, and Yu's display is unknown. Lucca, 2026-10-29, agreeing with the
overseer's recommendation: rent now and, in parallel, add a HiDPI virtual display to the harness.

## Lead (verify, do not assume)

macOS has no public virtual-display API; the public route is a DriverKit extension needing an
Apple entitlement. Chromium's macOS test suite creates virtual displays through the private
CoreGraphics `CGVirtualDisplay` classes (ui/display/mac/test/virtual_display_util_mac.mm), as do
BetterDummy and go-macos/virtualdisplay (with a HiDPI flag that makes macOS advertise Retina
modes). Reference gate required (private API, platform boundary): read those, record what they
do and the macOS versions they claim, and the failure behaviour when the classes are missing.

## Contract

None changed: harness tooling. If the result would change what VEN-C16's proof can claim, say
so on the bead; contract records are not edited here.

## Change

In eon/tools/mac-proof, the `retina` step (or a helper it calls), when the main display offers
no HiDPI mode: create a virtual display through CGVirtualDisplay with HiDPI enabled, make it the
main display (or put Venus on it) for the step, run the existing Retina checks against it, and
remove it afterwards, including on failure (leftovers stays green). When the private classes are
missing or creation fails, keep today's behaviour (step left for Yu, with the reason). Never
touch a real attached display's settings beyond what the step already does.

## Acceptance

- mac-proof checks: `nix develop -c eon-test -p mac-proof`, fmt, clippy on Linux and
  aarch64-apple-darwin.
- The next macOS CI run passes `retina` at scale 2 (log shows the virtual display and
  `venus: window scale factor 2`), and leftovers stays green; or, if CGVirtualDisplay is
  unavailable on the runner, the step reports that reason and the bead records it.

## Scope

eon/tools/mac-proof only. Codex review per AGENTS.md (gate code: scope line). Approval: Lucca,
2026-10-29, "i agree with the recommended" (option 1: rent now and add the virtual display).
close_reason: Landed 0dea24b; CI run 40860567114 skipped retina with the virtual display's reason, which acceptance allows; Retina passed at scale 2 on the rental (batch close approved by Lucca 2026-10-31 'i agree')

comments.author: lucca
comments.text:
Plan (Opus planner, 2026-10-29). Implementer: Codex; gates: Opus first, Codex review, Opus final.

Approval, as relayed by eon-overseer (2026-10-29): Lucca, 2026-10-27, "do these two too, then ... i want to move closer to the 'yu testing' gate" (standing for the macOS launch path); 2026-10-28, "lets get to working" (fix the macOS CI failures with the Opus-plans/Codex-implements split) and "diagnose, fix, commit, push"; 2026-10-29 overnight, "ok, going to sleep. handle it. get it done."; 2026-10-29 on the Retina gap, "i agree with the recommended" (rent now and add a HiDPI virtual display to the harness). Not covered: push, promotion, workflow dispatch, renting, GitHub or site posts.

Reference gate (private API, platform boundary):
- Chromium ui/display/mac/test/virtual_display_util_mac.mm at e15627ed55e5 (main, 2026-10-29). Declares CGVirtualDisplay, CGVirtualDisplayDescriptor, CGVirtualDisplayMode and CGVirtualDisplaySettings from CoreGraphics; sets a non-zero vendorID and distinct serials ("macOS 14 expects"), name, maxPixels, sizeInMillimeters from ppi, colour primaries, a dispatch queue; settings.hiDPI for ppi >= 200 with one mode; nil from initWithDescriptor: is the failure. It refuses on headless Macs (every online display has model number 'virt', crbug.com/40148077) and claims no macOS range. Evidence that a GitHub VM display may block creation; inference only.
- go-macos/virtualdisplay at 22054aec4a2c (BSD-3, measured on macOS 26.6.2, Apple Silicon only). Checks every class and selector before sending (a missing one is a crash, not an error). Measured: HiDPI only advertises Retina modes (half the points, same pixels) and does not enter one; changing a virtual display's mode pins it until the creating process exits; the window server reclaims the display when that process dies, crash included; the creating process cannot read the new display's modes if it enumerated displays first, while other processes see all of them; removal is asynchronous (0.7 to 1.9 s); each name and size leaves a root-owned ColorSync profile in /Library/ColorSync/Profiles/Displays for ever, so it uses a fixed identity set. Its CI runs no creation on GitHub runners ("no window-server session").
- BetterDummy (waydabber, now BetterDisplay): same classes; its known HiDPI-on-low-DPI route mirrors the physical display to a dummy set to a HiDPI mode. Not inspected at a revision; discovery only.

Decision:
- A hidden `mac-proof virtual-display` subcommand, like `backdrop`: checks each class and selector it sends with the objc runtime, creates one display with a fixed identity (one name, vendor, product and serial, so one ColorSync profile per machine), 2048x1536 pixels at about 220 ppi with hiDPI on and that one mode at 60 Hz, prints `display <id>`, then exits when stdin closes. A missing class or selector, a nil display, or applySettings: returning NO prints the reason and exits non-zero.
- The child owns the display, so the parent's mode change cannot pin it past the step: ending the child removes it, crash or not.
- retina.rs/scenario.rs `retina`: when the main display has no HiDPI mode (today's `Unavailable` branch), start the child, wait (bounded) for its ID and for the parent's `mac::displays()` to list it with a HiDPI desktop mode (`retina::hidpi`), then in one ForAppOnly configuration switch the virtual display to that mode and mirror the main display to it (CGConfigureDisplayMirrorOfDisplay(main, virtual)), so the windows, Venus's included, move to a scale-2 master. Re-read the displays: the main display must now be the virtual one at scale >= 2. Then the existing checks run unchanged (Venus logs >= 2, `shown` capture).
- Cleanup, success or failure: unmirror (ForAppOnly), end the child, wait up to 10 s for its display to leave the active list, then wait for Venus's scale back at the original, as the mode-switch path does. Guards undo the mirror and kill and reap the child on every early return.
- Every failure before the virtual display is the scale-2 main display (missing classes, child exits, no ID, display never listed, no HiDPI mode, configuration error, main display not the virtual one afterwards) is `Unavailable` with the reason, as today, so Yu still owns the step. Failures after that are `Check` failures: they are what the step proves.
- Rejected: switching the virtual display's mode in the creating process (pins it for the run); making it main by origin alone (Venus's window stays on the real display); moving Venus's window through Accessibility (a new grant and binding for the same result); a DriverKit extension (Apple entitlement).

Interpretation of "never touch a real attached display's settings beyond what the step already does": the step already reconfigures the main display ForAppOnly and undoes it; the mirror is the same kind of change, undone at the end of the step and by macOS when the tool exits. A Mac whose main display offers HiDPI (Yu's) never reaches this path. A machine that does gains one ColorSync profile for the fixed identity, once.

Files: eon/tools/mac-proof/src/mac.rs (native virtual display and mirror calls, stubs elsewhere), main.rs (the subcommand), scenario.rs (`retina` and its `proves` text), Cargo.toml only for objc2 features already in the lockfile (objc2-foundation 0.3.2 is locked; no new crate, `Cargo.lock` unchanged unless a direct edge requires it, which Codex reports).

Red check: macOS CI run 40842410369 skips `retina` with "no HiDPI display: the main display runs 1024x768 points at 1024x768 pixels (scale 1, 60 Hz) and offers no HiDPI mode". Green is the next macOS CI run passing `retina` at scale 2 with the virtual display in its log and leftovers green, or `retina` skipped with the reason the virtual display was unavailable. Linux cannot run the native path; no unit test is added unless a new pure function earns one.

Checks: `nix develop -c eon-test -p mac-proof`; `nix develop -c cargo fmt --check -p mac-proof`; `nix develop -c cargo clippy --locked -p mac-proof --all-targets -- -D warnings`; `rustup run stable cargo clippy --locked --target aarch64-apple-darwin -p mac-proof --all-targets -- -D warnings`; `git diff --check`.

Scope: eon/tools/mac-proof only. No contract text changes. If the native run passes, VEN-C16's Retina item gains harness evidence on a virtual HiDPI display, not a physical Retina panel; contract records stay as they are and that distinction goes to the proof record.

comments.text:
Proof (Linux side; the commit carrying this comment is the proof's revision).

Change: eon/tools/mac-proof. A hidden `mac-proof virtual-display` child checks each private CoreGraphics class and selector before sending, creates one fixed-identity HiDPI virtual display ("mac-proof HiDPI", 2048x1536 pixels at 60 Hz, about 220 ppi, hiDPI on), prints `display <id>` and owns the display until its stdin closes (mac.rs, main.rs). `retina` (scenario.rs): when the main display is below scale 2 and offers no HiDPI mode, and the scenario is Private and not on a person's own Mac (`run::Options.personal_mac`, set by `final`; Environment::User always counts as personal), it starts the child, waits for the display and its HiDPI mode, switches it to that mode and mirrors the main display to it in one ForAppOnly configuration (refusing a main display already in a mirror set), and requires the main display to be the virtual one at scale >= 2. title: Re-sign the patched eon binary in the generation test on macOS
description:
## Why

Rented Mac (kz4p.12; Scaleway M2, macOS 27.2 build 26B123, real Apple hardware) run 1 on 0dea24b
(tree e77f5461): `package` fails, one eon test of 50, so terminfo and the whole GUI scenario are
skipped. The same test passed in CI's package step (macOS 15 runner VM, run 40842410369).

Test: `workspace_control_follows_the_exact_caller_across_generations`, panics at
eon/crates/eon/tests/workspace_control.rs:1050 ("one generation directory was not created in
.../r/generations").

Cause (rental operator, from the Mac's unified log, 12:56:08 UTC): the test builds a
`previous-eon` by flipping EON_WORKSPACE_DIGEST bytes in a copy of the eon binary
(workspace_control.rs:3863-3874), which invalidates the copy's linker ad-hoc code signature, and
the kernel kills it at first page-in:

    AMFI: '/private/tmp/e0/ec-51880-49/previous-eon': Unrecoverable CT signature issue, bailing out.
    CODE SIGNING: cs_invalid_page(...): p=58631[previous-eon] final status 0x23020200, denying page sending SIGKILL

The supervisor never starts, so the generations directory never appears. Enforcement differs
between the runner VM and macOS 27.2 on hardware, so CI did not catch it. Log on the Mac at
~/eon-proof/e77f5461ec8e-1793273530/evidence/steps/03-package.log:10674-10691 (the operator copies
it to /home/lucca/.cache/eon-agents/claude-rental-work/).

## Change

Test-side, Darwin only: after writing the patched copy, re-sign it ad hoc
(`codesign -s - -f <copy>`; check what the Nix Darwin build environment provides: /usr/bin/codesign
with sandbox=false, or sigtool's codesign from nixpkgs, whichever the check phase can reach on
both CI and a Mac), or produce the second generation without patching a signed binary. Grep the
workspace for every other place a test patches or rewrites a binary (same pattern elsewhere, e.g.
Orbit or installer tests) and fix them the same way. No product change.

## Acceptance

- `nix develop -c eon-test -p eon --test workspace_control` on Linux (unchanged behaviour), fmt,
  clippy, aarch64-apple-darwin clippy.
- The next macOS CI run passes `package` and the rented Mac's next run passes `package` and this
  test (native proof; the rental operator runs it).

## Scope

eon/crates/eon/tests (and any other test that patches a binary). Codex review per AGENTS.md.
Approval: Lucca, 2026-10-28, "diagnose, fix, commit, push" (macOS fix loop).
close_reason: Acceptance met: rental run on c9174bd included test:eon, fixed natively (audit 2026-10-31; batch close approved by Lucca 'i agree')

title: Fix Eon Runtime's remaining Linux-only session assumptions for macOS
description:
## Why

Beyond peer identity, Eon Runtime assumes a Linux session in a few places that would make the
first macOS launch noisy or broken: no `XDG_RUNTIME_DIR` (a warning on every launch and a long
`$TMPDIR` root), macOS's shorter Unix socket path limit, and a first-detach notification that is
a silent no-op. Fixing these on Linux before the Mac run saves rental time.

Lucca (2026-10-27, relayed by eon-overseer): "i'd rather test everything possible and fix myself,
letting to Yu only final testing and final fixes that i missed ... so the more automated, the
better."

## Evidence

- `runtime/crates/eon-runtime/src/supervisor.rs:681-692` `base_runtime_directory`:
  `EON_RUNTIME_DIR`, else `XDG_RUNTIME_DIR/<product>`, else a warning and
  `env::temp_dir()/<product>-<uid>`. On macOS `env::temp_dir()` is the per-user
  `/var/folders/xx/<hash>/T/`, about 50 bytes before Eon's own path segments.
- macOS `sockaddr_un.sun_path` is 104 bytes (Linux 108). Runtime paths:
  `root/generations/<generation>/...` (`runtime/crates/eon-runtime/src/generation.rs:55-57`)
  plus Orbit endpoint names. Memory `isolated-eon-capture-recipe` already needs a "short root" on
  Linux, so headroom is thin.
- `runtime/crates/eon-runtime/src/notification.rs:10,44-51`: Linux zbus notification; other
  platforms do nothing.
- The mapping bead's sweep list (sibling, first child) may add items; take the ones it assigns here.

## Scope

In scope: choose the macOS runtime root (recommended: `$TMPDIR` is already per-user and private,
so use it without the warning on macOS, keeping `EON_RUNTIME_DIR` first); compute the longest
socket path Eon and Orbit create for a realistic macOS root and either show it fits 104 bytes
with margin or shorten the root (e.g. a short per-user directory) with a bounded, explicit error
when a path would not fit; make the notification gap explicit (recorded as a README macOS gap,
no new mechanism); the sweep's other Runtime items.

Out of scope: a native macOS notification mechanism (needs a decision; propose it as a follow-up
only if Lucca asks), Orbit's socket code unless the length check shows Orbit must change (then
stop), Venus.

## Acceptance

- The worst-case socket path for a macOS-style root is computed in a deterministic test or
  recorded calculation, and fits 104 bytes or fails with a clear message before bind.
- No `XDG_RUNTIME_DIR` warning on macOS; Linux behavior and messages unchanged.
- The notification gap text is recorded on the friends'-gate bead for README.
- The changes compile for the Apple target (gate check) and pass Linux suites.

## Verification

- `nix develop -c eon-test -p eon-runtime` exits 0; `cargo fmt --check`, clippy.
- `cargo check --locked --target aarch64-apple-darwin -p eon-runtime` has no new error.
- Native confirmation in the harness: full Eon launches with default environment (no
  `EON_RUNTIME_DIR`) on the Mac and logs no runtime-root warning.

## Stop Conditions

- Stop if the runtime root rule is user-visible enough to need CONFIGURATION.md or contract text
  (ask Lucca with a recommendation).
- Stop if Orbit's endpoint naming must change (ORB contract owner).
- Stop on any platform blocker.
close_reason: macOS runtime root /tmp/<product>-<uid> without warning; platform socket-path bound in windows.rs and start_orbit; bounds for all roots recorded; notification gap on kz4p.14. Compile-checked for aarch64-apple-darwin; native confirmation stays with kz4p.12.

Include both in this bead's worst case. supervisor.rs:652-658 configuration_directory (XDG_CONFIG_HOME or ~/.config/eon) is the same record-or-accept case as diagnostics.rs. comments.author: lucca
comments.text:
Approval: Lucca, 2026-10-27, to eon-overseer (relayed by eon-overseer): "do these two too, then ... i want to move closer to the 'yu testing' gate". This starts the bead.

Reference gate (AP-REFERENCE-001). The change touches the runtime root's trust boundary on macOS.

Behavior and owners: Runtime owns its runtime root (supervisor.rs base_runtime_directory) and checks each terminal socket path before Orbit binds it. Orbit owns binding, unchanged. The platform module (runtime/crates/eon-runtime/src/platform.rs) owns the platform facts: the sun_path length and the fallback root without XDG_RUNTIME_DIR.

References read:
- tmux 3.8 at 7f2a35a (~/pjs/refs/tmux-3.8), tmux.c:217-243 and server.c:114-120. tmux ignores $TMPDIR and uses $TMUX_TMPDIR or /tmp, with base /tmp/tmux-<uid>. It refuses a base it does not own or one that others can access, and it checks sizeof(sun_path) before bind (ENAMETOOLONG).
- Orbit's own standalone default: orbit/src/cli.rs:138-160, /tmp/yazelix-orbit-UID with an owner and mode check.

Kept:
- EON_RUNTIME_DIR first, then XDG_RUNTIME_DIR/<product>.
- prepare_runtime's owned-0700 validation (symlink_metadata, so no symlink is followed).

Measured socket paths (Explore survey of f495068):
- The longest Orbit path is <root>/w/<8hex>/generations/g1-<32hex>/session-N.sock.management, 83+d bytes relative to the base root, where d is the number of digits in N.
- N is a counter that only goes up. It is refused only at usize::MAX, and MAX_SESSIONS=256 caps live terminals, not N.

Rejected:
- (a) $TMPDIR on macOS, the bead's first recommendation. /var/folders/xx/<28>/T/ is about 49 bytes, and 49+1+87 > 103, so a window's sockets cannot fit.
- (b) A fixed bound on the main root that assumes N<=9999. It would refuse Linux roots of 30 bytes or more that work today, for example a /dev/shm/ec-<pid>-<n>/runtime test root, so Linux would change.

Decision:
- macOS fallback root: /tmp/<product>-<uid>, with no warning. Linux keeps its warning and env::temp_dir(), unchanged.
- One platform-derived bound: sun_path length from libc::sockaddr_un, minus its NUL. It is used in the windows.rs check, which until now hardcoded 108, and in start_orbit on each terminal's exact .management path before Orbit runs. A too-long path then fails with a clear message that names EON_RUNTIME_DIR, instead of "terminal exited before publishing Ready". On Linux this changes only the error text of launches that already fail.
- Check: a platform test that binds paths at the bound and one byte past it, so a wrong constant fails on the platform the test runs on.

No dependency, no contract text. CONFIGURATION.md:361-364 already says "private per-user fallbacks".

comments.author: lucca
comments.text:
Correction to the bounds comment above. Its first-window arithmetic was off; I recomputed it with a script.
- First window, or an eonbase root: R/generations/g1-<32hex>/session-N.sock.management is len(R) + 73 + d bytes. Its first terminal, orbit.sock.management, is len(R) + 66.
- So on macOS's /tmp/eon-501 the first window fits to d=18. eonbase (/tmp/eonbase-501) fits to d=14, and an 18-byte directory-service-uid root fits to d=12.
- Roots that fit the first window's session-9999: Linux <= 30 bytes, macOS <= 26. Roots that fit its first terminal: Linux <= 41, macOS <= 37.
- The window figures (len(R) + 84 + d; reserve roots of Linux <= 19 and macOS <= 15) and the test-root figures stand.
- The gate comment's rejected option (b) refuses Linux roots of 31 bytes or more, not 30. Its /dev/shm/ec-<pid7>-<n2>/runtime example is exactly 30 bytes, at the edge. The rejection stands: one more pid or counter digit would be refused, though such a root works today.

comments.author: lucca
comments.text:
Socket path bound for all roots, product and test: the recorded calculation, which answers kz4p.1's question 4.

Limit. A socket binds when the path is at most sun_path-1 bytes: 107 on Linux, 103 on macOS. Rust std refuses len >= sun_path. The code takes this from libc::sockaddr_un as platform::SOCKET_PATH_BYTES.

Suffixes. These are relative to a root R, with d = digits in the session number N. N is never reused, so it is unbounded.
- Window: R/w/<8hex>/generations/g1-<32hex>/session-N.sock.management. Path bytes = len(R) + 84 + d.
- First window, or an eonbase root: R/generations/g1-<32hex>/session-N.sock.management. Path bytes = len(R) + 74 + d. Its first terminal is orbit.sock.management: len(R) + 70.
- eon.sock, the .record files and the lock files are shorter, or are not sockets.

Product roots:
- macOS default, no EON_RUNTIME_DIR: /tmp/eon-<uid>, 12 bytes for uid 501.
  - Window at the windows.rs reserve (N=9999): 100 <= 103, a margin of 3. Windows fit to d=7.
  - First window: fits to d=17.
  - eonbase, /tmp/eonbase-501 (16 bytes): fits to d=13.
  - A directory-service uid of 10 digits gives an 18-byte root. windows.rs then refuses new windows with its message; the first window still fits to d=11. Workaround: EON_RUNTIME_DIR. Accepted as a gap, since such uids are rare on personal Macs.
- Roots that fit the windows.rs reserve: Linux <= 19 bytes, macOS <= 15. The first window's session-9999: Linux <= 29, macOS <= 25. Its first terminal: Linux <= 37, macOS <= 33.
- Linux XDG root /run/user/1000/eon (18 bytes): unchanged.

Enforcement in this change:
- windows.rs checks the platform bound, not 108.
- start_orbit checks each terminal's exact .management path, for every root and N, before Orbit runs. It fails with "terminal socket <path> is too long; set EON_RUNTIME_DIR to a shorter runtime root", where it used to fail with "terminal exited before publishing Ready". On Linux, a launch that worked before still works.

Test roots, for kz4p.16 and kz4p.7. T is the temporary directory.
- runtime/ tests use T/eon-test-<pid>-<n>. The longest is generation.rs:1088, T + 68 + P + n bytes, where P is the pid's digits. On macOS this fits while T <= about 25 bytes.
- eon/crates/eon/tests/workspace_control.rs:5870 (window new + pane create) is the longest test path: T + 90 + h bytes, where h is 6-8 hex digits.
  - On macOS it needs T + h <= 13, so T <= 5-7 bytes.
  - The windows.rs reserve also needs T + 9 + h <= 15, so h <= 6 even with T=/tmp. macOS pids of 5 digits or fewer give h <= 6 when n < 16.
  - So on macOS the eon suite needs T=/tmp, or a root as short, and the Darwin nix build's TMPDIR (/private/tmp/nix-build-...) is far too long. kz4p.16 (eon-test) and kz4p.7 (preCheck TMPDIR) must set T to /tmp or shorter; a private short root such as /tmp/e<n> keeps the margin.
- workspace_control.rs:3786: T + 88 + P + n. Sessions at :1821 and :4617: T + 87 + P + n. Both fit with T=/tmp.

Open for native proof (kz4p.12). By default macOS's periodic daily 110.clean-tmps deletes regular files in /tmp that have gone unaccessed for 3 days; per its script, sockets and directories are kept. Runtime's .record and lock files are regular files. This is inference from FreeBSD/macOS periodic.conf defaults and is not verified on this macOS. $TMPDIR has the same 3-day dirhelper sweep, so the root choice does not change it. The harness should check whether a workspace idle more than 3 days keeps its records, or the item should be accepted as a known gap.

Accepted, no change. Configuration stays at ~/.config/eon (supervisor.rs configuration_directory) and state at ~/.local/state/eon (diagnostics.rs state_directory) on macOS too. Both are documented and portable, and they match Helix's and Yazi's ~/.config on macOS. Moving them to ~/Library would change documented paths (CONFIGURATION.md, eon config-path).

Notification: notification.rs already records the macOS no-op in its module comment. The README gap text is on kz4p.14.

comments.text:

macOS default roots:
- /tmp/eon-501 (12 bytes): the window reserve path is 100 bytes. Windows fit to d=7, the first window to d=18.
- /tmp/eonbase-501 (16 bytes): fits to d=14.

eon-test -p mac-proof, fmt, clippy Linux and darwin; the rental's next final run shows no foreign argv in the archive, no hostname in captures (or a documented warning), and no new files in HOME.

eon/tools/mac-proof and docs/DEVELOPMENT.md. Codex review per AGENTS.md (gate code: scope line).

title: Drop the hidden VS16 glyph that fails Venus's emoji shaping test on macOS
description:
## Why
Rented Mac run 4 (kz4p.12, macOS 27.2, M2) on 7485479 fails at the package step: the Venus lib test
`render::tests::shaping::wide_emoji_clusters_use_the_platform_colour_face`
(venus/src/render/tests/shaping.rs, assertion near line 148) fails 158 passed / 1 failed, so
yazelix-venus and eon-0.1.8 do not build and every later step skips. The test came with eon-wy1r
(b1f9d6b). CI run 40914474951 on the same SHA is expected to fail the same way.
Evidence: on the Mac ~/eon-proof/0a62a8258d9d-1793292310/evidence/steps/03-package.log lines 343-378,
copied to /home/lucca/.cache/eon-agents/claude-rental-work/run4 when run 4 exits.

Observations from the test (macOS 27.2):
- Pass: 🇯🇵 one glyph (491) and 👨‍👩‍👧 one glyph (1544), both from Apple Color Emoji; 中 routes to
  Arial Unicode MS (GB18030 Bitmap unconfigured); A to Menlo; ❤︎ (FE0E) is Menlo 2728+3.
- Fail: "❤\u{fe0f}" wide=true, bold false and true, configured and not: two glyphs from Apple Color
  Emoji, [(338), (3)]. The heart is 338; VS16 comes out as its own glyph id 3. Glyph 3 also follows
  the selector in the Menlo ❤︎ case.

Diagnosis (inference, unverified): the shaper (cosmic-text via glyphon) keeps the default-ignorable
variation selector as a hidden glyph (likely the font's space glyph, zero advance) instead of
removing it, as HarfBuzz does when a font has no cmap entry for the selector. Linux's Noto Color
Emoji does not show it. If the glyph is zero-advance and draws nothing, only the test's "exactly one
glyph" expectation is wrong; if Venus draws or advances it, rendering is wrong too.

## Change
1. Establish which: on Linux, reproduce with a font lacking a VS16 cmap entry if one is at hand, else
   reason from the cosmic-text/harfrust source at the pinned revision; record whether the hidden
   glyph has zero advance and whether Venus's cell renderer would draw it.
2. Fix at the owner: if Venus could draw or advance it, drop default-ignorable hidden glyphs where
   Venus consumes shaped glyphs (or set the shaper's remove-default-ignorables option if the pinned
   API exposes one). Otherwise change the test to judge the visible glyphs (exclude zero-advance
   glyphs whose cluster is a default-ignorable codepoint), keeping its colour-face check strict.
3. Keep the other observations' expectations unchanged.

## Acceptance
nix develop -c eon-test -p yazelix-venus, fmt, clippy on Linux and the darwin clippy recipe; the
next macOS CI run or rental run 5 passes this test natively and the Fonts item. Claim no Mac result
from Linux.

## Scope
venus/src/render (shaping and its tests) only. No contract change expected (VEN-C wording stays).
Portability disposition: neutral. Codex review per AGENTS.md.

comments.text:
Plan (Opus planner, 2026-10-29), at 42a3f0e.

Approvals, as relayed by eon-overseer: Lucca 2026-10-27 "do these two too, then ... i want to move closer to the 'yu testing' gate" (macOS launch path); 2026-10-28 "lets get to working" (fix the macOS CI failures with the Opus-plans / Codex-implements split) and "diagnose, fix, commit, push"; 2026-10-29 overnight on run 4 "ok, going to sleep. handle it. get it done." Push, dispatch and promotion stay with the coordinator.

Step 1 finding (source reading, pinned revisions):
- cosmic-text 0.19.0 shapes with harfrust 0.5.2 and never sets BufferFlags (src/shape.rs:134-200), so harfrust's default applies. harfrust src/hb/ot_shape.rs:906-929 hide_default_ignorables replaces every default-ignorable codepoint the font does not map (VS15/VS16 included) with the face's nominal space glyph (buffer.invisible is unset), and :839-860 zero_width_default_ignorables zeroes its advance and offset. Removal happens only with REMOVE_DEFAULT_IGNORABLES, which cosmic-text 0.19 does not expose.
- Glyph 3 after both Apple Color Emoji's heart and Menlo's heart matches the TrueType convention that glyph 3 is space. Inference: the extra glyph is each face's space glyph. Evidence on the Mac only through the next native run.
- Layout keeps a zero advance zero (cosmic-text src/shape.rs:2897-2911 rounds 0 to 0 under monospace width), and a space glyph has no ink, so glyphon draws nothing for it. Venus's own glyph consumers (shaped_preedit_placement render.rs:2398, shaped_end chrome.rs:288, label cut boundaries chrome.rs:562, shape_cell_text's emoji fallback cells.rs:236) take extents, cluster boundaries or font identity; a zero-width glyph from the emoji face changes none of them.
- So Venus neither draws nor advances the hidden glyph; only the test's "exactly one glyph" expectation is wrong. No production change.

Change (test-only, venus/src/render/tests/shaping.rs, wide_emoji_clusters_use_the_platform_colour_face):
- A glyph is hidden when it has zero width and its id is its own face's nominal space glyph (swash charmap().map(' ') of font_system.get_font(glyph.font_id, ..)). The emoji expectation counts only visible glyphs: exactly one, id != 0, from the platform emoji face. Every glyph, hidden ones included, must still come from the emoji face. Routing expectations for the other cases are unchanged.
- The observation line gains each glyph's width and hidden flag so a native failure stays diagnosable.
- Clusters cannot judge it: harfrust's default cluster level merges VS16 into the heart's cluster, so the hidden glyph's start..end is the whole "❤\u{fe0f}".

Red/green: the native red is run 4's failure (bead body). On Linux, a temporary probe (not committed) shapes a heart+selector with a face that lacks the selector in its cmap (for example DejaVu Sans Mono with "❤\u{fe0e}", if its charmap maps FE0E to 0) and records glyph ids, widths and the face's space glyph, confirming the mechanism; then the old predicate counts it as two glyphs and the new one as one visible glyph. Linux green: the test passes.

Checks: nix develop -c eon-test -p yazelix-venus; cargo fmt --check and cargo clippy --locked --all-targets -p yazelix-venus -- -D warnings; darwin clippy for yazelix-venus (rustup cargo, --target aarch64-apple-darwin, recipe on kz4p.1). No Mac claim; the next macOS CI or rental run 5 is the native check.

Scope: this one test only. No contract, dependency, configuration or production code change. Portability: neutral.

comments.text:
Result and proof (Opus gate, 2026-10-29). Implemented by Codex (gpt-6.1-sol, xhigh); test-only.

Correction to the plan comment: the hidden glyph does have an advance in Venus. harfrust zeroes it, but cosmic-text 0.19.0 then adds attrs.letter_spacing_opt to every glyph (src/shape.rs:215-217), and Venus's cell attrs carry the fitted letter spacing (venus/src/render/cells.rs:34, :83). A Linux probe through the test's own path (FontSetup, fitted_cell_font, cell_text_attrs, set_cell_layer, shape_cell_text) on "❤\u{fe0e}" gave: default fonts, DejaVu Sans Mono [(2883, w 10.0, ink 10x9), (3, w 0.625, ink 0x0)]; configured fallbacks, DejaVu Sans [(4076, w 13.75, ink 13x10), (3, w 0.625, ink 1x0)]; space glyph id 3 in both faces. Old count 2 glyphs, new count 1 visible. The probe was not committed.
Why it is still test-only: each cell is its own one-cluster buffer (venus/src/scene.rs append_glyph_runs), the hidden glyph is the last glyph, and cell buffers use no alignment, so the trailing sliver moves nothing and the glyph draws nothing. Accepted, not fixed: in a multi-cluster buffer with cell letter spacing (IME preedit such as "❤️x" on a face without a VS16 cmap entry), text after the selector shifts by that sliver (about 0.6 px at default geometry); preedit placement measures shaped glyphs, so it stays self-consistent.

Change (venus/src/render/tests/shaping.rs, wide_emoji_clusters_use_the_platform_colour_face): a glyph is hidden when its id is nonzero, equals its own face's nominal space glyph, and it rasterizes to no ink (SwashCache image None or zero-width/height placement). Each wide emoji must have exactly one visible glyph; every glyph, hidden ones included, must be nonzero and from the platform emoji face. Routing expectations are unchanged. title: Give the dev shell Nix cctools on macOS so Orbit builds without Xcode
description:
## Why

Yu's macOS final check (eon-mac-launch-kz4p.13, 2026-11-02, M4 Mac mini, macOS 26.3, no Apple
developer tools installed): the stock dev shell could not find `nmedit`, so the Cargo suites that
build Orbit (libghostty-vt-sys) failed. Yu's run added the pinned Nix cctools to PATH for that run
only; then all nine Cargo package suites passed. The package build already has it: flake.nix's
Orbit derivation adds `pkgs.cctools` on Darwin ("Ghostty runs Apple's libtool and xcrun nmedit,
absent from Darwin stdenv"). The dev shell (`devShells.default` in flake.nix) does not. CI and the
rented Mac had Xcode's command line tools, so /usr/bin supplied it and nobody saw this.

## Change

Add `pkgs.cctools` to the dev shell's packages on Darwin, beside the package build's same input
(no new dependency: the same nixpkgs input the Orbit package already uses). Check whether the dev
shell lacks anything else the package derivations add on Darwin.

## Acceptance

- On a Mac without Xcode's command line tools, `nix develop -c eon-test -p yazelix-orbit` builds.
  Proof: a mac-proof.yml CI run with the command line tools' developer directory hidden, or an
  equivalent check that `nix develop -c sh -c 'command -v nmedit'` resolves into /nix/store.
- Linux dev shell unchanged.

## Evidence

Yu's bundle, outside the repo:
/home/lucca/.cache/eon-agents/eon-overseer/yu-mac-final-0e47d26/eon-mac-final-0e47d26df690-retry-20261102T013043Z

title: Keep the managed-command-path check independent of the host's /etc/bashrc on macOS
description:
## Why

Yu's macOS final check (eon-mac-launch-kz4p.13, 2026-11-02, revision 0e47d26) failed one automatic
step: `check:managed-command-path` (nix/managed-command-checks.nix). The CI Mac and the rented Mac
passed it on the same revision. The log shows three interactive `eon-bash -i` runs (their job
control noise) and then a silent exit 1, so the failing command is the third bash run (fake mise
on PATH must set EON_MISE_PROBE=bash) or the Nushell hook step right after it.

Likely cause (unconfirmed): Nix's bash is built with SYS_BASHRC=/etc/bashrc (checked in the pinned
nixpkgs), so every interactive bash reads the host's /etc/bashrc, and Nix builds on macOS run
without a sandbox by default. A host /etc/bashrc that rewrites or prepends PATH (nix-darwin's
set-environment, Homebrew, a host mise) hides or shadows the check's fake mise, which is only
appended to PATH. Yu's Mac is a personal machine with its own setup; CI and the rental had a stock
/etc/bashrc.

## Change

1. Confirm the cause: reproduce on mac-proof.yml CI with a /etc/bashrc that prepends a directory
   holding a different `mise` (or rewrites PATH), or ask Lucca to ask Yu for `cat /etc/bashrc` and
   `bash -ic 'type -a mise'` (a question, not a re-run).
2. Make the check independent of the host's /etc/bashrc, keeping what it proves (managed bash
   activates the mise first found on PATH, and starts without it when mise is missing, fails, or
   `[shell] mise = false`). Do not change product behavior: real users' managed bash keeps reading
   /etc/bashrc like any bash.
3. Make the check say which assertion failed, so the next failure is diagnosable from the log.

## Acceptance

- The check passes on CI Linux and macOS, and on the CI Mac with the hostile /etc/bashrc from
  step 1 (red before the fix, green after).
- No change to the managed shells' behavior.

## Evidence

Yu's bundle, outside the repo:
/home/lucca/.cache/eon-agents/eon-overseer/yu-mac-final-0e47d26/eon-mac-final-0e47d26df690-retry-20261102T013043Z/run/steps/09-check-managed-command-path.log
close_reason: Landed: managed-command-path check survives a host /etc/bashrc; proven on macOS (red 41578067830, green 41578076049); Codex re-check 0/0 after the gate

comments.author: lucca
comments.text:
Evidence from Yu Sun, 2026-11-03 (relayed by Lucca): Yu's /etc/bashrc is nix-darwin's generated file. After the `$__ETC_BASHRC_SOURCED` / `$NOSYSBASHRC` guard it runs `. /nix/store/…-set-environment` whenever `$__NIX_DARWIN_SET_ENVIRONMENT_DONE` is empty. That happens before the interactive check (`[[ $- != i ]] && return`). It then sources /etc/bash.local if present. Yu's second command printed `bash: type: mise: not found`.

This confirms this bead's diagnosis from the log: in the check's build environment `__NIX_DARWIN_SET_ENVIRONMENT_DONE` is unset, so nix-darwin's set-environment replaces PATH. That puts system dirs on it (stty found) and drops the check's fake mise, which gives the silent exit 1 at "fake mise on PATH must set EON_MISE_PROBE=bash". The proof's "rewrite" hostile case models exactly this. Note for the fix: setting `NOSYSBASHRC` or `__ETC_BASHRC_SOURCED` would also skip this particular file, but this bead's approach (restore PATH in the check's ~/.bashrc) covers any host file, not just nix-darwin's.

Open product question (not this bead's scope): in a real Eon terminal on a nix-darwin Mac, does eon.bashrc's managed PATH survive set-environment? It does if Eon's terminal environment inherits `__NIX_DARWIN_SET_ENVIRONMENT_DONE` from the login session, or if eon.bashrc re-prepends its PATH after /etc/bashrc. To check after eon-mac-launch-kz4p.52.

title: Port the Runtime and Eon tests' process reads to macOS
description:
## Why

Lucca wants every possible check automated before Yu sees the Mac build. Today the Runtime and Eon
suites cannot run on macOS: their tests read `/proc` directly, and `eon-test` (the only supported
route, AGENTS.md "Testing Discipline") needs bubblewrap, which macOS lacks. Without this, the Mac
run proves only Orbit and Venus. This bead ports the tests' process reads; the sibling "Give
eon-test a macOS branch" gives `eon-test` its macOS isolation.

Lucca (2026-10-27, relayed by eon-overseer): "i'd rather test everything possible and fix myself,
letting to Yu only final testing and final fixes that i missed ... so the more automated, the
better."

## Evidence

- `nix/test-sandbox.nix:1-50`: `eon-test` refuses to run without `bwrap --unshare-all`; it hides
  live Wayland, D-Bus and Eon sockets and gives private PID/network.
- Test `/proc` reads: `runtime/crates/eon-runtime/src/sessions.rs:1676,1819,1938`;
  `runtime/crates/eon-runtime/src/supervisor.rs:2156-2161` (worker via `/proc/<pid>/task/*/children`
  and `cmdline`), `:2290`; about 25 sites in `eon/crates/eon/tests/workspace_control.rs` (`stat`,
  `environ`, `cmdline`, process existence), e.g. `:657,1013,1758,3026,4160,5491`.
- Precedent: Orbit's real-PTY checks use `lsof` on macOS where Linux reads `/proc`
  (`orbit/docs/CONTRACTS.md:831-832`); `orbit/tests/lifecycle.rs` keeps 3 tests Linux-only.

## Scope

In scope:
- A small test-only process helper (alive, start identity, environ, cmdline, children) with Linux
  `/proc` and macOS implementations (`proc_pidinfo`, `proc_listchildpids`, `sysctl
  KERN_PROCARGS2`), used by the Runtime and Eon tests in place of raw `/proc` reads; tests whose
  property is Linux-only stay `#[cfg(target_os = "linux")]` with the reason in a comment.

Out of scope: product code (Runtime port bead owns `sessions.rs` outside its test module), Orbit's
and Venus's own tests, CI, and the macOS branch of `eon-test` in `nix/test-sandbox.nix` (split out
on 2026-10-27 to its own sibling bead, "Give eon-test a macOS branch", for size).

## Acceptance

- `nix develop -c eon-test` on Linux runs the same tests as before (count unchanged except tests
  this bead deliberately splits; list any).
- The Runtime and Eon test targets compile for `aarch64-apple-darwin` (gate check with
  `--all-targets`).
- Native pass/fail is the harness's job; this bead does not claim it.

## Verification

- `nix develop -c eon-test` exits 0 on Linux.
- `cargo check --locked --target aarch64-apple-darwin --all-targets -p eon-runtime -p eon` has no
  test-code error.

## Stop Conditions

- Stop if a macOS reader needs a crate beyond `libc` (dependency gate): ask Lucca.
- Stop if a test can only be ported by weakening what it checks; keep it Linux-only and list it.
- Codex review per AGENTS.md (test code change).
close_reason: Runtime and Eon tests read processes through Linux /proc or macOS libproc/KERN_PROCARGS2 test readers (Runtime via platform::process); window test root shortened; Linux suites unchanged (130+1 ignored, 49); compile- and lint-checked for aarch64-apple-darwin; native run stays with kz4p.8/kz4p.12.

comments.text:
Correction to the proof record (narrow Codex re-check). The code is unchanged.

"h is 1-2 hex digits" holds only while one of ew0 to ewff is free in T. The loop searches 0_u32.., so stale ew<n> directories left by failed runs can push h higher, up to 8 digits. Each failed run leaves at most one, and the test removes its root on success.

So both macOS conditions remain for the harness roots:
- len(T) + h <= 10, the windows.rs reserve for this test;
- len(T) + 88 + P + n <= 103, for workspace_control.rs:3786.
Example: with T=/tmp/eon (8 bytes) and ew0 to ewff all taken, ew100 gives a 104-byte reserve path, over macOS's 103.

With eon-test's private /tmp (or a fresh short TMPDIR per run) no stale roots exist, so h = 1 and T may be up to 9 bytes. kz4p.16 and kz4p.7 should give the suite a fresh root and keep T + 88 + P + n <= 103.

title: Check CJK glyph placement in Venus at scale 1 on macOS
description:
## Why

Yu's macOS final check (eon-mac-launch-kz4p.13, 2026-11-02): item 3 (typing and input methods)
passed, with the note "CJK display seems uneven". His display is a non-Retina 1080p monitor
(scale 1); the capture (manual/03-typing-and-input-methods.png in his bundle, outside the repo:
/home/lucca/.cache/eon-agents/eon-overseer/yu-mac-final-0e47d26/eon-mac-final-0e47d26df690-retry-20261102T013043Z)
is downscaled to 960x600, so it cannot show the defect clearly. Copying CJK and emoji out was
correct (item 8).

## Change

Investigate how Venus renders CJK at scale 1 on macOS: which fallback font serves the glyphs
(Eon's bundled fonts, then the system's), whether two-cell glyphs are centered and sized to the
cell, and baseline alignment against the Latin font. Compare against Linux at scale 1 and macOS at
scale 2. Fix if Venus misplaces or mis-sizes them; otherwise record the cause.

## Acceptance

- A full-resolution capture of the same line (`Lucca 是帅哥`, in the bold prompt and in plain
  text) at scale 1 on macOS, before and after, recorded here.
- Venus tests cover any placement fix.

## Bounded investigation and proof
Owner: Venus shaping/fallback/placement path. Portability disposition: isolated Darwin observation over the shared renderer. Start by reproducing the reported unevenness at native resolution with exact Eon/font/OS/display identities; the old downscaled capture is a report, not proof of misplacement. Compare identical plain and bold strings at Linux scale 1 and macOS scales 1/2, naming fallback fonts and cell/baseline measurements. Do not change font defaults or broaden macOS support on visual inference alone.

One session may apply a small confirmed placement correction and its focused test; if it instead needs a new font/dependency, platform-host design or contract change, return that choice and split the delivery before code. If the defect cannot be reproduced or belongs to font rasterization, record the evidence/cause and propose disposition to Lucca, keeping the observed report intact. Render-path changes use the repository frame/performance route and one isolated native before/after observation; no Mac rental for this bead alone.

title: Make Eon's package build on macOS again: a workspace_control test sets a socket timeout after the peer closed
description:
## Why

Found by the eon-mac-launch-kz4p.49 agent in macOS proof round 2 (CI runs 41567707898 and 41567703816, logs in /home/lucca/.cache/eon-agents/eon-kz4p/r49/mac2/): Eon's own package fails its check phase on aarch64-darwin, so `nix build .#packages.aarch64-darwin.default` (and every macOS install of edge, and of v0.1.12, which contains it) fails:

```
test running_windows_name_each_other_and_refresh_on_start_and_end ... FAILED
panicked at eon/crates/eon/tests/workspace_control.rs:6919:50:
called `Result::unwrap()` on an `Err` value: Os { code: 22, kind: InvalidInput, message: "Invalid argument" }
```

Line 6919 is `stream.set_read_timeout(Some(remaining)).unwrap()` in the test's "burst of peer inspections" loop. On macOS, `setsockopt(SO_RCVTIMEO)` returns EINVAL once the peer has closed the socket (Linux allows it); the server likely answers and closes before the client sets its timeout (inferred from the error code and line, not yet verified). The test came with e4d0cf5 (eon-7cf0y.4, 2026-11-01). Every earlier macOS proof predates it, so nothing caught it.

## Do

1. Confirm the cause (macOS run or a reasoned reading of the BSD socket semantics).
2. Make the test portable: set each burst stream's read timeout right after `connect`, before `write_all`, or tolerate a closed peer when setting it. Check the rest of workspace_control.rs and the runtime's own socket code for the same pattern (set_read_timeout/set_write_timeout after a possible peer close), production code included: if the runtime does this on a live path, that is a product bug on macOS too.
3. Prove on macOS: a mac-proof.yml dispatch that builds `.#packages.aarch64-darwin.default` with its check phase, red on the base, green on the fix.

## Process note

The macOS proof harness last ran before e4d0cf5. Consider whether changes to eon's tests or socket code should trigger a macOS package build before landing (eon-mac-launch-kz4p.51 measures macOS build time; decide there).

## Acceptance

- `nix build .#packages.aarch64-darwin.default` passes on a macOS runner with tests on; red/green run IDs recorded here.
- No other set_*_timeout-after-peer-close site remains, or each is recorded as safe.

title: Ship a macOS app bundle so Eon starts from the Dock and Finder
description: Yu, 2026-11-03: 'I couldn't find an Eon app in the Dock or Applications ... I launched Eon from Terminal using the Nix-built binary.' Eon builds only the binary on macOS (no Info.plist or .app; flake.nix only writes the Linux .desktop entry), so Dock/Finder launch does not exist. Ship an Eon.app from the Nix build: Info.plist (bundle id, name, version), the Eon icon (.icns from assets/eon.png), and a launcher that starts the same eon as the CLI. The bundle's launch must set up Eon's managed environment itself: restore Eon's own PATH (eon CLI, Helix, bundled tools) for its terminals, and never depend on the launching terminal's environment or the bash marker that /etc/bashrc handling uses (the PATH concern raised to Yu on 2026-11-03, kz4p.49 context). # eon-mac-launch-kz4p.54: app-bundle step timeout — diagnosis and plan

Worktree at edge 1d9350d. Evidence: mac-proof run 42828287094 (head 84fe888),
`steps/82-app-bundle.log` and `scenario/app/`; run 42790023615 shows the same signature.

## Diagnosis

The timeout is a defect in the proof step, not in Eon.app. The evidence settles it, and it
exposes a second defect right behind the first. Neither needs a diagnostic-only landing.

### 1. The wait asks for a state this launch can never reach

- The step starts the app with `--args run -- eon-nu --execute "# <root>/"`
  (`scenario.rs:901-903`). The supervisor's argv in the log confirms it (log line 20).
- Runtime marks a terminal as the default shell only when it was started with no command:
  `default_shell: child.is_empty()` (`runtime/crates/eon-runtime/src/sessions.rs:1753`).
- EON-C11's busy list treats every live terminal that is not the default shell as busy, always
  (`attention.rs:697-723`: "A live terminal is idle only while it runs the default shell…").
- So p1, started with a command, is busy for as long as it lives. The wait at
  `scenario.rs:1693-1702` (one pane and an empty `busy.terminals`) cannot succeed. All 123
  polls show `busy.terminals = [terminal-1]`.
- Control: the `quit` step in the same run starts plain `eon run`, presses Escape, and reaches
  `busy.terminals = []` with one pane (`99-quit.log`). The app-bundle wait was copied from
  there, but with a launch that carries a command.

### 2. Ruled out, with the evidence

- **Key delivery to the bundled Venus works.** The first `eon session --json` reply shows quick
  search up (`selected_popup: "u1"`, `chosen: true`, no pane). After the first Escape every
  reply shows `selected_popup: null` and pane p1 present: Escape closed quick search and
  started the tab's pane (terminal-1's host starts 5 s after the supervisor).
- **The Files popup is not open.** u1 stays listed as a live but hidden popup
  (`chosen: false`, `selected_popup: null`). The passing `quit` step shows the same state after
  its Escape. The later 123 Escapes went to Nushell's prompt and did nothing.
- **The login-shell PATH adapter did not fail or start another shell.** The launcher writes
  `app-launch.log` into the state logs folder on any import failure
  (`eon-macos-launcher.rs:193-208`); that folder is copied into the evidence and holds no such
  file, and `eon.log` has no `eon app:` line. p1's program is the packaged Nushell (process
  14694, `nu --experimental-options=native-clip --execute # …`). No stray foreground process:
  the `(bash)` and CodexBar processes belong to the supervisor's quota probe.

### 3. Second defect, hidden behind the timeout: the expected paths name the wrong store path

- The step expects `which eon hx` to print `<package>/libexec/eon/bin/{eon,hx}` with
  `<package>` = the path `mac-proof` built (`scenario.rs:1719-1723`), here
  `/nix/store/p8hnz…-eon-0.1.22`.
- Since 4f53552 and 7d11137 (both after slice 1), that path is `eonProduct`: a folder of
  symlinks to `eonPackage` (`flake.nix:1063-1072`), here `/nix/store/8j686…-eon-0.1.22`.
  `Eon.app/Contents/Resources/eon-command` holds `eonPackage`'s `bin/eon`
  (`flake.nix:1045`), and the launcher builds PATH from that file's package
  (`eon-macos-launcher.rs:231-236`). The supervisor's argv in the log is
  `/nix/store/8j686…/bin/eon`.
- So the shell will print `/nix/store/8j686…/libexec/eon/bin/eon`, the same directory entry as
  the expected `/nix/store/p8hnz…/libexec/eon/bin/eon` (`p8hnz…/libexec` is a symlink), but a
  different string. The comparison at `:1724-1727` is textual and would fail once the wait is
  fixed.

### 4. Not provable from here

Everything after the wait has never run on macOS: the paste, Nushell's `which … | to json |
save`, the profile-only tool, `eon hx`, the capture and the stop. I desk-checked each against
the packaging and found only defect 3, but one dispatch costs about an hour (package 54 min),
so the plan adds failure evidence (step 3) to make any further failure name its cause in one
run.

## Plan

All changes are in `eon/tools/mac-proof/src/scenario.rs` plus one docs sentence. No product
code, contract, configuration value or CLI surface changes. No CHANGELOG entry (rule 10: proof
tooling only).

1. **Launch the default shell.** `app_command` passes `--args run --dir <root>/work` instead
   of `run -- eon-nu --execute "# <root>/"`.
   - `--dir` (ef28960, EON-C18) starts t1's first pane at once with no quick search, and with
     no command, so p1 is the default shell and the existing idle wait becomes the right
     readiness signal (the one `quit` already proves on macOS).
   - `<root>/work` contains the `<root>/` marker, so the supervisor's argv still identifies it
     for cleanup before Venus appears; the comment at `:899-900` is rewritten to say so.
   - The wait drops its Escape (no quick search to close) and keeps "one pane and an empty
     busy list". The predicate moves to a small pure function shared with the `quit` step's
     identical check, tested against three recorded replies (quick search up, p1 busy, idle).
   - Why not keep the command and wait on something else: any other signal (pane exists, text
     echoed) can be satisfied by the PTY before Nushell reads input; the busy list is the
     product's own "shell at its prompt" answer. A default shell is also what a Dock launch
     gives a user.
2. **Compare directory entries, not strings.** A pure helper resolves a path to its
   canonical parent plus file name; the check compares the shell's three paths with the
   expected three through it. This accepts the `eonProduct` symlink (and `/var` against
   `/private/var`) and still tells `eon` from `hx`, which canonicalizing the whole path would
   not (both end at `bin/eon`). The failure message keeps both raw lists. Unit test: a temp
   folder shaped like the product (a `libexec` symlink to a package folder holding two links
   to one file) passes; a different folder or name fails.
3. **Failure evidence, bounded.** When the step's body fails, before `clean`, and under its
   own 20 s deadline (the step's has passed on a timeout), log: `eon session --json`,
   `eon pane read` of each pane, the scenario's processes with parents, and, when screen
   capture is granted, one capture (`app-failure`). Each part ignores its own error. This is
   the capture the bead asked for; it stays because of Diagnosis 4. Strike it in review if
   unwanted: steps 1 and 2 do not depend on it.
4. **Tests and text.** Update
   `app_launch_supplies_private_roots_but_no_managed_tools_or_shell_marker` for the new
   arguments. `docs/DEVELOPMENT.md` (app-bundle paragraph): one sentence that a failed step
   leaves the session, pane text, processes and a capture in its log. The step's `proves`
   text stays true as written ("supplies run arguments").

## Proof

- Linux, focused, iterating: `cargo fmt --check`; clippy on `mac-proof` with `--all-targets`;
  `nix develop -c eon-test -p mac-proof` (under `nice -n 19`, `CARGO_BUILD_JOBS=6`).
- Darwin clippy for `mac-proof` (`--target aarch64-apple-darwin --all-targets`, rustup cargo
  with the dev shell's variables, recipe on eon-mac-launch-kz4p.1): `mac.rs` and the key and
  capture paths compile only there.
- Once, on the final staged tree: whole-workspace `nix develop -c eon-test` through heavy.sh.
- macOS: the overseer dispatches `mac-proof.yml` on the landed commit. Pass = `app-bundle`
  passes. No diagnostic-only landing is requested; the fix and the failure evidence land
  together, and a failure in the unproven tail would come back classified.

## Open points for the reviewer

1. Step 3 widens the fix beyond the two defects. Recommendation: keep it, for the reason in
   Diagnosis 4.
2. Whether Nushell's `which` prints the PATH entry joined with the name (expected) or a fully
   resolved file is not provable here. If it resolves fully, step 2's check fails with both
   lists in its message, and the fix is one line.

# eon-mac-launch-kz4p.54: app-bundle timeout — implementation notes

Base: edge 1d9350df14ec3f190279667aaf41707190780aa2. Plan: `00-plan.md`. Plan review (Codex):
`/home/lucca/.local/state/rota/runs/app-bundle-planreview-codex-1/report.md`, approved with
three changes through INBOX (2026-11-10T16:04:45Z).

Files: `eon/tools/mac-proof/src/scenario.rs`, `docs/DEVELOPMENT.md`. No product code, contract,
configuration value or CLI surface changes; no CHANGELOG entry (proof tooling only).

## What changed

1. **Launch.** `app_command` passes `--args run --dir <root>/work`. With no command the pane
   runs the default shell, which is the only terminal that can leave the busy list. The
   directory lies under `<root>/`, so the supervisor's argv still carries the cleanup marker.
2. **Readiness.** The wait keeps "one pane and no busy terminal" (`idle_shell`, shared with the
   `quit` step) and no longer presses Escape: `--dir` shows no quick search.
3. **Executed readiness command** (review change 1). The echoed comment is replaced by
   `$env.PWD | save --force '<root>/started'`, pasted every five seconds until the file holds an
   absolute path. The step then checks that this directory and `<root>/work` resolve to the
   same place. This proves the shell consumed input and that `--dir` reached it. The paste loop
   moved from `typed` into `pasted`, which `typed` now calls; `typed` behaves as before.
4. **Directory entries** (plan step 2; review change 2 closed the open point). `same_entries`
   compares each path as its resolved directory plus its own name, so the product's links to
   the package compare equal and `eon` stays distinct from `hx`.
5. **Failure evidence** (review change 3). `Scenario::failure_evidence` logs the session, each
   pane's text, the scenario's processes with parents, and one capture.
   - The original failure is returned unchanged; the evidence returns nothing.
   - Budget: 20 s in all, at most 5 s per command with its end included (`step::probe` kills
     outright at the deadline); once the budget is spent no command starts and the part is
     logged as unavailable. (Reworked in review round 1, see `03-review-ledger.md`.)
   - Every part that fails logs `mac-proof: failure evidence: <what> unavailable: <why>`.
   - `app_bundle` calls it before `clean` when the body failed and the supervisor still runs.
   - `stop` calls it before its own `clean` when `eon window stop all` failed or the supervisor
     did not exit. The third `stop` failure, a process left behind, gets none: by then the
     supervisor is gone and the failure message names the process.

## Deviations from the plan

- **Evidence inside the shared `stop`.** The review asked for it. `stop` also serves the main
  scenario's `stop` step and `mac-proof final` (`final_check.rs:1087`), so those now log the
  same evidence on a stop failure.
- **A personal Mac's pane text and screen stay out of the evidence** (my addition, not in the
  plan or the review). `mac-proof final` runs on Yu's own Mac and reaches `stop`; collecting
  what Yu typed, or the screen, on a failure was never agreed. The session and the process list
  were already logged there. On CI and the rented Mac (`personal_mac` false) everything is
  logged.
- The helper for the app's screen grant: `app.screen` copies the outer scenario's, and the
  `app-helix` capture reads it, so the evidence and the capture use one fact.

## Not done, on purpose

- The step's `proves` text is unchanged: it stays true ("supplies run arguments").
- No change to the launcher or the Nix packaging: the evidence shows both work.
