- Zellij v0.45.1 efd8fd5a89a20c07a111d248ad7fce53848d2c18; zellij.dev docs 111f441276770f871419949a6695bbad6b518551
- WezTerm main e2a98e1b8af156988ad0ac778658ac27b60a55fb (2026-10-10); kitty v0.49.2 b2cb871254fbdac19a085188813c8dfb258b95cd
- Rex: closed source. Public docs snapshot llms-full.txt, sha256 fc17b069a3c46efd37a4c9bdc934fbb7928f43c207a00f14f8378d5018e8ffe6 (~/pjs/refs/agent-sidebar-research/web)
- herdr 143bf5fd4781d164260c63fe28e7dc08054ad32f; tuios 0047c409185f37e568933a566e0253b2a6e96a96
- All clones are under ~/pjs/refs.

## Discovery of detached sessions

- **E, every reference:** detached work is listed in the UI as well as on the CLI.
  - tmux: `C-b s` choose-tree and the 3.8 `C-b S-Tab` fuzzy switcher. Rows read "N windows, attached|detached", with an info view of activity and last-attached times (key-bindings.c:439-442; window-switch.c:42-52; window-tree.c:194-217).
  - Zellij: the session-manager lists live sessions, then exited ones, by recency. Rows show "N tabs, M panes, K clients"; the current session is omitted (session-manager single_screen.rs:22-104, components.rs:75-200).
  - WezTerm: launcher and palette (launcher.rs:273-294).
  - kitty: `goto_session` picker (session.py:440-585).
  - Rex: `session.switch` "Change Session…", with an indicator for completed or blocked tasks (llms-full L232, L2366).
  - tuios: sidebar session section plus the `Ctrl+B S` switcher.
  - herdr: sidebar and Goto list workspaces with their agent state. Its named sessions are CLI-only.
  - CLI lists: `tmux ls -F`, `zellij ls`, `wezterm cli list`, `rex ls --json`, `tuios ls --json`, `herdr session list`.
- **E, Eon (gap):**
  - Detached windows are visible only through `eon windows`, which does not say whether a window is presented or detached. The Runtime reply has no presentation field (runtime v17.rs:348-356), and attach always reads as available (supervisor.rs:1781-1788).
  - The listing omits the default workspace, because it lives outside `w/` (windows.rs:255-301).
  - Commands > List windows is read-only output (cli.rs:106-200).
  - Windows have no name; the OS title is the selected terminal's title (venus application.rs:3898-3902).

## Switching: one OS window or several

- **E, in place:** tmux `switch-client` (cmd-switch-client.c:49-167), Zellij (client re-attaches to the other server's socket; zellij-client lib.rs:1448-1635), tuios (client rebuilds its view; os.go:810-860) and herdr workspaces all switch inside one terminal. The session left behind keeps running detached.
- **I:** that is forced. Terminal multiplexers own no OS windows.
- **E, GUI terminals:**
  - kitty switches by focusing the session's window, opening its OS window if needed (session.py:371-434, boss.py:708-733). Its docs call one session per OS window "the natural way"; several sessions can also share one OS window, the others' tabs hidden by a tab filter.
  - WezTerm swaps *every* GUI window of the client to the new workspace. `reconcile_workspace` reuses, closes and opens OS windows (wezterm-gui frontend.rs:359-470). When the last window of a workspace closes, the GUI jumps to another workspace (:364-379). A recent fix covers a render freeze when workspaces close (changelog.md:306).
  - Rex does not document multi-window behaviour.
- **E, Eon cost of in-window switching (shape B):**
  - Venus parses its workspace socket once (venus launch.rs:187-197) and exits when the control stream closes (VEN-C14).
  - The supervisor spawns and owns its one Venus (supervisor.rs:382-454, :986).
  - EONW `Present` has no target (v17.rs:65-67).
  - VEN-C23 excludes a multi-window event loop (:1245-1247).
  - EON-C31 seen-marking and popup cleanup key on "Venus attached" (supervisor.rs:1014, :1399-1413).
  - Today only Eon Runtime chooses and validates a supervisor (`validate_runtime`, supervisor.rs:330-365).
- **I:** B would change EON-C11, EON-C23, EON-C10, EON-C31, EONW, VEN-C3, VEN-C8, VEN-C14, VEN-C18 and VEN-C23, and add a trust boundary where Venus picks a supervisor.
- **E, focus on Wayland:**
  - Presenting an already-presented, unfocused window only requests attention (application.rs:3541-3548). VEN-C14 notes that winit cannot focus directly and that xdg activation is controlled by the compositor.
  - venus/docs/REFERENCES.md:680-693 rejects carrying a platform token in EONW.
  - Attaching a detached window opens a new toplevel.

## Naming

- **E:**
  - tmux defaults to numbers, requires unique names, and resolves `new -A -s NAME` as create-or-attach (cmd-new-session.c:122-140).
  - In Zellij the random adjective-noun name is the only identity. Rename renames the socket and cache directory, non-atomically, with a TODO in the source (screen.rs:11476-11553).
  - kitty takes the name from the session file's basename and has no rename, so two files with the same basename collide.
  - WezTerm's rename has no collision check (mux lib.rs:652-675).
  - Rex keeps a stable, never-reused ID plus an optional label. Targets resolve as ID > label > position, and an ambiguous target exits 3 without acting (L963-1018). tuios likewise separates its `set-session-name` label.
  - herdr auto-labels each workspace from its git repo or cwd (discovery.rs:24-43).
- **I:** name-as-identity is where Zellij and kitty break. Rex's ID plus label avoids that.
- **E, Eon:**
  - ARCHITECTURE.md:34-47 defines workspace, tab, pane, column and terminal. "Session" is technical only (`session-N`, JSON fields), and yx8.11 uses "session name" for an agent's own session.
  - Product text and the CLI say "window" (`eon window new`, `eon windows`). Window, workspace and supervisor namespace are 1:1:1.

## Persistence and resurrection

- **E:**
  - tmux core keeps sessions in memory only. Resurrect saves layout and working directories, and restores programs by typing their commands into new shells, allowlist only; its docs call `:all:` dangerous (process_restore_helpers.sh:38, restoring_programs.md:8-49).
  - Zellij serializes a KDL layout every 60 s. Every saved command waits behind "Press ENTER to run" (session_serialization.rs:488-496). Exited sessions never expire. Its changelog shows a long run of resurrection fixes.
  - kitty persists only session files (`save_as_session`); WezTerm keeps nothing past its mux server.
  - herdr and tuios restore structure with fresh shells and label it (`TUIOS_RESTORED=1`). Agents resume through their own resume commands.
  - Rex keeps sessions live only.
- **I:** no reference keeps live processes across a reboot. Eon's labelled-restore question is already owned by eon-reboot-restore-im8y (release-1) and stays there.

## Keyboard flows

- **E:**
  - tmux binds `s`, `S-Tab`, `(`, `)`, `L` and `$`.
  - Zellij uses `Ctrl o w`. Inside the manager, typing filters or names a new session; Enter attaches, resurrects or creates.
  - tuios binds `Ctrl+B S` and alt+shift+n/p.
  - WezTerm, kitty and Rex bind nothing by default.
  - Eon's free Alt+Shift letters include S. Alt+Shift+D is being taken by m798.
- **I:** in a GUI, the window manager's own window switching already covers next, previous and last.

## Agent and CLI control

- **E:**
  - Rex: `rex ls/new --json` and `rex api call session.*`. Agents open work without taking focus, and showing a session to the user is opt-in (L1082-1089).
  - herdr: `workspace create --no-focus` returns IDs as JSON, with an explicit `workspace focus` (cli-reference.mdx:205).
  - tuios: verbs that need a client return `needs_client`.
  - Zellij: a scripted switch moves the last-active client and cannot name a target (route.rs:2416-2433).
  - WezTerm has no CLI command that switches workspace.
- **E, Eon:**
  - `window new` prints the ID; `windows` and `window stop` take `--json`, but `window attach` does not.
  - There is no `--window` targeting. Commands run inside a window target it through the inherited `EON_WINDOW_RUNTIME_DIR` (sessions.rs:1180-1200).

## Other Eon facts found

- **E:** `eon window attach ID` attaches only the exact current generation (windows.rs:176-191, generation.rs:430-450).
- **I:** after a profile upgrade, a window detached under the old generation cannot be reattached from the new CLI. A picker must show such a window honestly.
- **E:** docs/REFERENCES.md has no route for tmux, Zellij, WezTerm workspaces or kitty sessions. The nearest are the routes at :107 (Ghosthub: detach-only close, fresh attach), :171 (TUIOS), :200 (pickers: Kitty overlays, Zellij in-place commands, Eon-owned fzf popups), :430 (cmux jump-to-work) and :479 (recovering an interrupted session).

comments.author: lucca
comments.text:
Shape D against A and B (2026-10-22, edge 3777926). Code read only. E means evidence, I means inference. This comment calls the new layer a "group" until the noun is chosen.

## D: several groups inside one supervisor, one window showing one group at a time

**Today (E):**
- The supervisor holds one `Workspace` (supervisor.rs:980-994). It has tabs, active, and the ID counters `next_tab`, `next_pane`, `next_session` and `next_popup` (workspace.rs:124-135).
- The EONW v17 snapshot is built from it (workspace.rs:218-275, v17.rs:316-323), and Venus polls it every 250 ms.
- Venus attaches Orbit only for what is visible: the active tab's selected pane or popup, plus the expanded panes of the other columns (model.rs:173-215). When the active tab or the tab list changes, it ends zoom, cancels scroll and re-attaches (application.rs:1513-1556).

**I:** swapping the shown group looks to Venus like a tab switch, because background tabs are already detached from view. Rendering and ORB-C3 are unaffected.

**What D needs:**
- **A group layer in the runtime.** One ID allocator shared across groups. Today's per-workspace counters would collide on socket names (`session-N.sock`, `kN.sock`) and on tab IDs. A stale `CloseTab` sent across a switch could hit another group's `t2` (application.rs:1762, :4135).
- **A new EONW version:**
  - `tabs` and `active_tab` stay the shown group's.
  - New fields `groups[{id,name,tab count,attention rollup}]` and `active_group`.
  - Group requests: new, switch, rename, close.
  - Replies scoped to the caller's group.

  A filtered snapshot alone is not enough: the CLI, the m798 final-close prompt (decided from `tabs.len()`) and the shown-group label all need the extra data.
- **Close semantics.** Closing a group's final tab switches to the most recent other group. Only the last group's final close ends the window. Today the window ends when no terminals remain (supervisor.rs:899).
- **CLI targeting.** No new environment variable is needed: `EON_TERMINAL` resolves to a tab and so to its group (supervisor.rs:1230-1252). Callers outside a group get the shown group or `--group`.
- **The picker** is an Eon-owned fzf popup, as Commands is (VEN-C18 holds).

**Contracts under D:**
- **EON-C8:** the group layer. Traversal, tab moves and the final-tab rule work per group. Recovery collapses everything into `t1` (:500-502).
- **EON-C10:** group requests, reply scoping, `CreateTab` targeting, and Commands entries. "Quit this window" stops every group.
- **EON-C11:** wording only.
- **EON-C23:** a window holds N groups.
- **EON-C31:** focus means the shown group's active tab, and the rollup is per group. Decide whether the attention queue spans groups and switches group on a jump.
- **EON-C28:** the `eon workspace --json` fields freeze at 1.0, so D lands before the eon-igae.11 fixture.
- **VEN-C8:** shows the shown group's tabs.
- **VEN-C21:** a group label in the bar.
- **Unchanged:** VEN-C14, VEN-C18, VEN-C23. No trust boundary and no Venus lifecycle change.

## Risks of D

**(a) Blast radius (E):**
- The supervisor is a single-threaded loop. Venus exits when the control stream ends (VEN-C14).
- Orbit runs survive a crash, and a replacement supervisor of the same generation adopts them (EON-C15; its installed proof is still open).
- Recovery projects everything into one tab, `t1` (workspace.rs:176-216), and no topology is persisted.

**I:** one supervisor crash closes the window and flattens all N groups into one tab. `eon stop`, Quit this window, and the last group's final close stop every group. Blast radius is strictly coarser than in A.

**(b) Detach:** closing the window or Alt+Shift+D detaches all groups together. A hidden group is like a background tab, not "detached". Stopping one group means closing its tabs.

**(c) Attention:** hidden groups never hold focus, so their raises stay unseen, which is correct. The poller already covers every terminal.

**(d) Generations:** after a profile upgrade, the old supervisor keeps all of its groups. The new window cannot switch to them, because that would be B. The known stranding bug therefore strands N groups at once.

**(e) Load:** the terminals are the same either way, and D runs one quota poller instead of N.

## B re-checked

**E:** Venus fixes its socket at launch (launch.rs:187-197, transport.rs:216-238). The supervisor owns its Venus (supervisor.rs:382-622), and seen-marking keys on that child (:1009-1017).

**I:** under B,
- supervisor A would mark its own focused terminal seen while Venus shows B, and B would never mark anything seen;
- `window attach B` would spawn a second Venus;
- quitting A would kill the view of B.

The earlier cost of about ten contracts plus a trust boundary holds.

## Fit with A, and migration

- D and A coexist: each window is a supervisor holding N groups, and New window still works.
- "Move a group into its own window" would need an Orbit lease handoff, which the EON-C15 boundary excludes. That is post-1.0.
- Nothing is persisted, so today's workspace becomes group 1 in the next generation.
- eon-reboot-restore-im8y must save group membership and names when it lands.

## Size: about 9 beads, each one session

1. D0 contracts and the user noun (Lucca approves).
2. D1 runtime group layer and shared allocator. Behaviour is unchanged with one group, and the wire is unchanged.
3. D2 the next EONW version with groups and group requests. It folds after eon-agent-sidebar-yx8.7, which also bumps EONW.
4. D3 close and exit semantics.
5. D4 CLI list/new/switch/rename/close and `--group`.
6. D5 the Alt+Shift+S picker.
7. D6 the Venus bar label and the m798 prompt wording.
8. D7 the per-group attention rollup and picker sort.
9. D8 the batch installed proof.

Order: D0 → D1 → D2 → {D3, D4} → D5 → D6 → D7 → D8.

**What survives of A:**
- 1opf → group names (D4).
- i92k → the group picker (D5).
- vgfx → the per-group rollup (D7).
- suox shrinks to window listing state and the default-workspace entry. That is optional under D.

title: Let users and agents name Eon windows
description:
## Why

eon-n77e: Eon windows have random hex IDs and no name. The OS title is the selected terminal's title (venus application.rs:3898-3902), so a picker of windows is unreadable.

The references keep a stable ID with a separate label (Rex: ID > label > position, and an ambiguous target exits without acting; tuios: `set-session-name`). Name-as-identity breaks in Zellij (non-atomic rename) and kitty (basename collisions).

## Contract (proposed; bring the exact EON-C23 amendment to Lucca before code)

A user or agent can give an Eon window a name:

- `eon window rename [ID] NAME` names a window; without an ID it names the caller's window.
- `eon window new --name NAME` names a window as it opens.
- An empty NAME clears the name.

`eon windows` (from the previous bead) shows the name. `window attach` and `window stop` accept an ID or an exact name; a name that matches more than one window fails without acting. The ID stays the identity, and names need not be unique.

The name lives with the window's runtime state, so it ends when the window stops. Keeping names across a reboot belongs to eon-reboot-restore-im8y.

## Scope

In scope: the name store, the CLI, the listing field, name targeting, contract/USAGE text, CHANGELOG.

Out of scope: the picker, a rename action inside the picker or Commands (add one only if the contract review asks), the window title, persistence across reboot.

## Acceptance

- Renaming a detached window shows the new name in `eon windows`.
- Attaching it by name works.
- With two windows of the same name, attaching by that name fails, leaves both untouched, and names the matching IDs.

## Verification

Focused tests through `nix develop -c eon-test`, plus the affected build. One installed observation in the switching batch. Codex on every code change.

title: Advertise Smulx and Setulc in Eon's macOS terminfo within the 4096-byte legacy entry limit
description: Follow-up of eon-khndw (2026-11-12): adding Smulx and Setulc makes Eon's terminfo entry 21 bytes larger than Darwin's 4096-byte legacy compiled-entry limit, which an existing contract/check pins. eon-khndw advertises them on Linux only and keeps Darwin's capabilities unchanged. Do: prove the macOS ncurses reader renders both, then fit the entry (trim an unused capability or move to the extended format if every macOS reader accepts it) with the contract and check updated, and prove coloured undercurls in Helix and Neovim on the Apple Silicon preview.

title: Find text in a terminal's screen and history, from the window and the CLI
description:
## Why

From the eon-ng4bk audit gap 10 (2026-10-31): neither herdr nor Eon can search a terminal's text and
scrollback, and users expect find in a terminal (AGENTS.md rule 8). Today a person must scroll by
hand. At dcaef1c an agent can already read bounded retained history with `eon pane history`
(EON-C35, ORB-C17), as well as the visible area with `eon pane read`; neither supplies indexed
matches/history positions or the interactive find workflow.

## Goal

A person can find text in a pane's screen and retained history from the window, step between
matches and land on one; an agent can do the same search from the CLI as data (rule 5); the find
key is configurable (rule 6). Whether a keyboard copy mode ships with find or stays separate is
decided in child 1.

## Owners (to confirm in child 1)

- Orbit owns terminal state and retained history (ORB-C2, ORB-C8), so the search over history runs
  in Orbit, not over Venus's frames.
- Venus owns the find bar, match highlight and scrolling to a match (VEN-C7 history interaction).
- Eon Runtime owns the CLI path and its authorization (`[agents] terminal_access`, EON-C35).

## Children (planned; file 2-4 after child 1's contract text is approved)

1. Decide find and copy mode: reference gate and contract drafts (this epic's first child).
2. Orbit: a bounded search over a terminal's screen and retained history (new ORB-C, real-PTY
   check).
3. Venus: the find bar, its configurable key, match highlight, next/previous and scroll to match.
4. CLI: the same search as data from `eon` (EON-C35 extension or a sibling command).
5. Keyboard copy mode, only if child 1 decides it ships with find.

## Acceptance

- Installed observation: in a pane with long output, the find key opens find, typing a term
  highlights matches in the screen and history, next/previous moves between them, Escape closes and
  returns to live bottom; the CLI search returns the same matches as data; both respect
  `terminal_access = "none"` for the CLI.

## Scope boundary

No regex engine choice beyond what child 1 approves, no search across panes or tabs, no persistent
search history, no remote or MCP exposure (eon-ciwn.3).

## Sequencing and current boundary
Child 1 remains decision/reference/contract drafting only, with no blockers from the Venus control layer. After its approval, file only the approved implementation slices; the Venus find-bar child must depend on eon-uczzf.2 (Lucca's 2026-11-10 order, comment 6418). Orbit remains the authoritative history/search owner; do not search rendered frames or rely on the bounded lossy CLI text projection to establish positional matches. Reuse EON-C35/ORB-C17's current authorization/limits where applicable, proposing only the necessary approved extensions. This audit changes no search options, copy-mode choice, keys or contract text.

Block that child on eon-uczzf.2 when it is filed; the epic itself is linked as related only, so child 1 (the decision) is not held.

title: Decide how find in a terminal works and whether copy mode ships with it
description:
## Why

Find in a terminal (parent epic) crosses Orbit, Venus, Runtime and the CLI and needs new contract
text (ORB-C for searching history, VEN-C7 or a new VEN-C for the find interaction, EON-C35 or a
sibling for the CLI path). The open question of whether a keyboard copy mode ships with it also
needs an answer before any code.

## Evidence

- ORB-C8 (`orbit/docs/CONTRACTS.md`, "Retained history and authoritative scrolling"): Orbit owns
  history.
- ORB-C17 and EON-C35 (`docs/CONTRACTS.md`, "Reading a terminal from the CLI"): current `pane read` returns visible text and `pane history` returns bounded history/live text. Search/match coordinates and interactive find remain missing; do not re-add the already-delivered history read.
- VEN-C7 (`venus/docs/CONTRACTS.md`, "Authoritative history and selection interaction").
- `[agents] terminal_access` (EON-C35) governs CLI terminal reads.

## Scope

In scope:
- Reference gate per docs/AGENT-RULES.md Contract-Driven Method: how Ghostty (and whether the
  pinned libghostty exposes a search API), kitty, WezTerm (QuickSelect and search mode), Alacritty
  (vi mode and search) and tmux (copy mode search) search screen and history; inspected revisions,

title: Replace a kept Down scroll preview whose rows output rewrites near live
description:
## Problem

Found by the fresh Claude reviewer of eon-preview-kept-in-history-after-prune-li45 (2026-10-27), by
source reading, not yet observed. A Down scroll preview taken while the viewport is in history but less
than one screen from live (`rows_from_live < dimensions.rows`) holds rows from the active screen. Orbit's
viewport_preview reads the rows below the viewport (orbit/src/frame.rs:571-615 at dcaef1c). Output
can rewrite those rows in place without changing either ScrollPosition count: a progress bar, or the
half-written cursor row when `rows_from_live == 1`. SessionModel::preview_may_be_stale
(venus/src/model.rs) is true only at live and at the oldest retained row. So a held sub-row Down
remainder near live keeps drawing the outdated active-screen row until something else replaces the
preview.

## Expected

A kept Down preview whose rows overlap the active screen is replaced through the same paced and held
path (h7y0's next_request gate: at most once per PREVIEW_ANSWER_GRACE, one outstanding preview). First
confirm it in an isolated headless Sway: scroll a few rows up from live while a program redraws its
bottom line, leave a sub-row Down remainder, and capture the bottom edge.

## Contract

VEN-C7. Any change to contract text stops for Lucca's approval.

## Prerequisites

eon-preview-kept-in-history-after-prune-li45.

## Scope

In scope: the staleness gate in venus/src/model.rs, plus any test in venus/tests/canonical_scene.rs or
venus/src/application/scroll.rs. Out of scope: Orbit.

## Acceptance

- A Venus test with a kept Down preview near live over a frame that rewrites the active screen.
- One isolated installed observation, or a recorded reason that the case cannot occur.

## Portability disposition

neutral.

## Current evidence and acceptance detail
At dcaef1c `SessionModel::preview_may_be_stale` is `venus/src/model.rs:708-713` and still checks only live or oldest-retained-row positions. Keep this as a source hypothesis until the isolated reproducer confirms overlap with a rewritten active-screen row. The closed prerequisite is satisfied; no Orbit implementation belongs here.

The focused regression must show the old preview rows becoming obsolete despite unchanged ScrollPosition, then the accepted replacement following the existing paced/one-outstanding-request path. Cover a near-live Down preview and a history-only preview that must not churn merely because live output changes. Preserve held sub-row remainder and current preview answer ordering. Record an installed edge capture at native resolution, or the concrete reason/revision proving the case cannot occur and propose disposition to Lucca. Portability disposition remains neutral; any contract change still stops for exact approval.

title: Add Neuralink input support to Eon
description:
## Contract
A Neuralink user can operate Eon through a verified Neuralink computer-input interface: open a workspace, select a directory, enter and run terminal text, switch tabs/panes, scroll, and select/copy text. Preserve focus and normal keyboard/pointer behavior. An unavailable or disconnected input source must not inject stale actions or prevent ordinary input.

## Prerequisites and first decision
Verify the actual interface exposed by Neuralink, supported operating systems, access/licensing requirements, and available hardware or participant collaboration. Do not assume a public SDK or Linux compatibility. First check whether Neuralink’s existing computer control already supplies the pointer and text input Eon consumes; support may require only qualification and documentation. If access or a compatible platform is unavailable, record the concrete prerequisite and defer implementation without claiming support.

## Reference gate
Read current official Neuralink technology and Telepathy material, then any vendor documentation available for the chosen interface:
- https://neuralink.com/technology/
- https://neuralink.com/updates/two-years-of-telepathy/
Review docs/ARCHITECTURE.md ownership boundaries and EON-C7, EON-C8, EON-C18 and EON-C20. Compare with an application actually operated through the same Neuralink interface. Record exact versions, input capabilities and limitations before choosing an adapter or dependency. Official material was consulted on 2026-10-11; SDK availability and Eon-platform compatibility remain unverified.

## Ownership and scope
Prefer existing OS pointer, keyboard/text-entry and accessibility paths. Venus owns native input, focus and accessibility; Orbit owns terminal input/state; Eon owns product configuration, exact component selection and installed qualification. Fix a demonstrated gap at its owner and consume an accepted exact revision. This bead does not authorize implant drivers, neural decoding, raw neural-data storage, a generic BCI framework, or an additional supported platform. Any needed platform expansion requires a separate user decision.

## Acceptance
1. Identify a usable supported interface and platform, or record the exact external blocker; research alone does not complete the support goal.
2. Complete the contract’s workflows in an installed Eon with real Neuralink output and record device/software versions, exact Eon/child revisions and observed limits. A simulated input stream can validate an adapter but cannot establish Neuralink support.
3. Verify loss/disconnection and recovery without unintended input or lost workspace state; existing input remains usable.
4. Document setup, supported capabilities and known limitations. Add only the smallest proven integration needed, if any, and make no broader hardware or platform claim.

title: Open an independent Eon workspace in a new window
description:
## Contract routing
EON-C23 owns the product action; VEN-C23 consumes the exact Eon executable supplied by the supervisor for the native shortcut. Consumer: one installed full-Eon user on x86_64 Linux Wayland. Trigger: explicit New Window from CLI, desktop launcher action, or Alt+Shift+N in a live Venus window. Result: a second native Eon window starts a fresh directory picker and has its own Eon supervisor, tabs, focus, and durable Orbit Sessions. The first window and its Sessions remain unchanged. A stable window ID makes each window discoverable, attachable after detach, and separately stoppable. Bare eon continues to present the current default workspace. Important failures: a collision, invalid/private-runtime path, failed child readiness, or stale target must leave existing windows and Sessions untouched; Stop must target the chosen identity.

## Ownership and prerequisites
Eon owns window identity, private runtime namespace, launch, discovery, attach/stop policy, CLI action, and desktop entry. Venus owns only the fixed native shortcut and its visible help; Orbit keeps Session authority and one presentation client per Session. Start from accepted EON-C1/C8/C11/C15 and VEN-C8/VEN-C20; retain accepted Orbit b6cecf8f2ee35570b41cfdc578b095889d917fe2 and consume accepted Venus source a23f9eed95120ca4acea8789bf7d32d2472d84ce.

## Reference gate and decision
Inspect Eon's generation, supervisor, CLI, EONW, installed launcher, and existing lifecycle tests; inspect Venus's shortcut dispatch and one-window contract before changing it. Canario's current published spaces workflow and Ghosthub 0.7.0's independent native windows/detach policy are comparable product evidence, not code sources. Reuse Eon's generation validation and add a short private runtime root for each window. Reject a second view onto the same Orbit Session (one presentation client) and randomizing the build generation (it is component identity). The check is two simultaneously live installed Eon windows with distinct Session endpoints and independent detach/reattach/Stop.

## Scope
Nix-only x86_64 Linux Wayland full Eon. No shared tab or focus state, arbitrary multi-window renderer, new Orbit behavior, generic instance framework, another distribution channel, macOS proof, or change to existing bare-eon presentation semantics.

## Acceptance Criteria
1. New Window creates a distinct private runtime and fresh picker without replacing or stopping the first window. Concurrent requests get distinct IDs; an immediate failed launch reports its private log; uncertain startup retains its ID and process for safe inspection.
2. CLI and desktop action open a window. Alt+Shift+N is discoverable in native shortcut help and triggers the same Eon-owned action. The new window can be listed, reattached after its Venus closes, and stopped by exact ID; batch Stop includes all owned windows without retargeting another generation.
3. Closing either Venus window detaches only its Sessions. Stop of one window leaves the other's Sessions and presentation intact. Existing bare eon, attach, run, and generation behavior remain valid.
4. Focused red/green lifecycle checks, full affected EONW/Rust/Nix checks, exact child pins, and one isolated installed native Wayland observation establish the contract. Refresh the active eon profile without restarting live supervisors; update docs, shortcut help, CHANGELOG, and README LOC.

title: Tell a running window when a newer Eon is installed
description:
## Why

After eon-cli-old-window-after-upgrade-mno4 (landed d56c373), a running window is one build: its terminals run that build's `eon`, and new windows opened from it (Alt+Shift+N, the launcher's New Eon Window) use the running build. Lucca chose to keep that (2026-10-23, answering the overseer's "New window after an upgrade: keep the running build, plus a 'newer Eon installed, restart to update' notice as a follow-up" with "agree to everything"). The cost is that after a profile upgrade, a user keeps running the old build with nothing telling them a newer one is installed. Every edge build reports version 0.1.1, so the version badge can't show it.

## Goal

When the installed Eon differs from the build a window runs, the window says so once, unobtrusively: for example a small Eon Bar marker or tooltip, "A newer Eon is installed. Restart the window to use it."

## Contract (bring the exact text to the overseer or Lucca before code)

- How a running supervisor learns that a different build is installed, without constructing store paths, querying the Nix store or invoking an evaluator (AGENTS.md Composition and Distribution). Candidates to compare at the reference gate: the new build's CLI leaving a marker in the shared runtime dir when it runs; or the supervisor resolving its own launcher path again and comparing build identities. Name the owner (Eon Runtime, or Eon's launch policy) and how it reaches Venus (an EONW field implies a version bump).
- What "differs" means: a generation or build identity, not the version string.
- Presentation in Venus: where it shows, that it never steals focus, and that it never shows when the builds match.

## Scope

In scope: the reference gate, the contract text, the mechanism, the presentation, and tests.

Out of scope: restarting windows automatically, migrating terminals between builds, and n5qv's reattach work.

## Acceptance

- After a profile upgrade, a window started earlier shows the notice, and a window started after it doesn't. That's one installed observation across a real upgrade, in isolation.

## Verification

The affected Rust and Nix surfaces (wider if EONW changes), converge plus Codex, and the isolated installed observation.

Compare that owner before starting another detector or notice. The historical version examples in this body are not current facts: eon/crates/eon/Cargo.toml:3 is 0.1.22; exact build identity remains necessary. No closure or decision change in this pass; proposed duplicate closure goes to Lucca.

title: Initialize host mise in Eon's managed Nushell and Bash
description:
## Decision
Lucca, 2026-10-19: Eon's managed shells should initialize mise automatically, as Yazelix Nova
does, in Nushell and Bash. Found while fixing eon-amo0 (mise trust errors in hooks).

## Contract change (stop for Lucca's approval before code)
EON-C9 (Managed shell environment) excludes it today: its Boundary lists "automatic
Direnv/Mise". Proposed change, smallest form:
- Consumer: a full-Eon user whose inherited PATH has `mise`.
- Trigger: an interactive managed shell (`eon-nu`, `eon-bash`) starts.
- Result: the shell evaluates host `mise activate nu` / `mise activate bash` output after Eon's
  packaged configuration and before the user's native configuration (Nova's order for Nu), so
  mise-managed tools resolve per directory in Eon terminals as in the user's own shell.
- Failures: `mise` missing or `mise activate` failing is skipped silently (Nova's rule); the shell
  still starts. A per-project mise error (e.g. an untrusted config) is mise's own message, not
  Eon's.
- Boundary kept: Eon still writes no user files, installs no mise, and adds no Direnv. Decide
  whether a `[shell]` boolean turns it off (recommended: a `mise` boolean defaulting to true, like
  the existing Starship, Zoxide, Atuin and Carapace booleans).

## Reference (Nova, ~/pjs/nova/nova at 0c3fa126)
- `runtime/yzx-nu.rs` `host_mise_init()`: runs `mise activate nu` with the runtime PATH; uses
  stdout only on success and non-empty output; otherwise skips.
- ARCHITECTURE.md Nu row: "Packaged -> optional host `mise activate nu` -> optional user Nu";
  docs/runtime-notes.md and docs/configuration.md describe it; `checks/yzx-contracts.rs` tests it
  with a fake `mise` that accepts only `activate nu`.
- Nova does this for Nu only; Bash is new here, so check Eon's managed bashrc order
  (`bash_rc`, runtime/crates/eon-runtime/src/managed_environment.rs) the same way.

## Reference gate (consequential: changes EON-C9's lifecycle and trust boundary)
Record before code: which `mise` runs (the inherited PATH's, not a pinned one) and when (once per
shell start; cost of `mise activate` on startup), how its PATH edits interact with Eon's one
child-private managed PATH prefix (EON-C9 `session_path_contains_one_managed_prefix`), and
whether activation runs inside Eon's popups and `eon run`.

## Prerequisites
Lucca's approval of the EON-C9 text.

## Acceptance
A red/green check with a fake `mise` (as Nova's) for each shell: activation output evaluated in
order, missing and failing `mise` skipped; the shell-environment Nix check; `nix develop -c
eon-test`; one isolated installed observation that a mise-pinned tool version resolves in a fresh
Eon terminal in a project directory; CHANGELOG entry; review loop; profile refresh.

## Scope boundary
Nushell and Bash managed shells only. No Direnv, no mise installation or trust management, no
change to arbitrary argv commands.
close_reason: done

comments.author: lucca
comments.text:
Approval and reference gate (claude-w3, 2026-10-21). Lucca pre-approved every decision in this session, including the EON-C9 text change below.

Contract (EON-C9): new [shell] mise boolean, default true, beside the Starship/Zoxide/Atuin/Carapace booleans. When enabled and the inherited PATH has a mise executable, an interactive managed shell evaluates host 'mise activate nu|bash' output after Eon's other integrations. A shell that already activated mise is left alone. Missing or failing mise is skipped silently; mise reports its own per-project errors. Boundary now reads 'automatic Direnv, mise installation or trust management'.

Reference: Nova ~/pjs/nova/nova at 3325ef5d (bead cited 0c3fa126), runtime/yzx-nu.rs host_mise_init(): runs 'mise activate nu', uses stdout only on success and non-empty, then writes it into a generated config.nu. Kept: the success-and-non-empty rule and silent skip. Rejected: Nova's generated config file, because Eon's Nu activation is a fixed store tree (NU_VENDOR_AUTOLOAD_DIR, one path, per Nu 0.113.1 eval_const.rs) and Eon writes no startup files. Nu 'source'/'use' need a parse-time path. Nushell's string hooks are parsed when they run and keep definitions, as the overlay-activation pattern in Nu's hook docs shows.

Mechanism:
- Nu: a snippet appended to every vendor-autoload mask file, gated at runtime by EON_SHELL_MISE (no new mask bit, since nothing in it must be kept from parsing). It runs 'mise activate nu' at config time and prepends a one-shot pre_prompt string hook: 'module mise { <output> ; export def --env "eon apply" [] { mise_hook } }; use mise; mise eon apply'. The 'eon apply' call (added only when the output defines mise_hook) applies the directory's env before the first command. Without it, mise's own hook fires only from the second prompt (observed).
- Bash: last in eon.bashrc, so Eon's Starship check still sees only the user's PROMPT_COMMAND: 'eval "$(mise activate bash)"' on success and non-empty output. mise's bash output already calls _mise_hook.
- Already-active guard: per-shell state, not MISE_SHELL. An inherited MISE_SHELL (Eon started from a mise-activated shell) would otherwise skip every terminal. Nu: 'which mise | where type == custom | is-empty' (67 µs, measured), checked at config time and as the hook condition. Bash: no _mise_hook function.
- Which mise and when: the inherited PATH's mise, once per interactive shell start. 'mise activate' takes milliseconds; mise_hook then runs on each prompt and PWD change, as mise does in the user's own shell. Non-interactive 'eon-nu -c' and scripts load no config, and bash -c reads no rcfile, so 'eon run' and argv popups are unaffected. Interactive popup shells (Agent and Git run their tools, not shells) behave like terminals.
- PATH: mise's hook-env prepends its tool dirs to the PATH it saw at activation, which already holds Eon's one managed prefix. Project-pinned tools win over Eon's managed names only for tools mise manages. session_path_contains_one_managed_prefix covers the launch environment, which is unchanged.

Observed candidate (PTY-driven nu 0.113.1, real mise 2026.7.0, project with [env] EON_MISE_PROBE): env present at the first command, MISE_SHELL=nu, mise is a custom command, the env clears after cd out. An inherited MISE_SHELL=nu still activates. EON_SHELL_MISE=0 activates nothing.

comments.author: lucca
comments.text:
Proof (claude-w3, 2026-10-21), x86_64 Linux. Commit tree 7d977f5f (edge d72a89c plus this change).
- managed-command-path and default Nix checks on 7d977f5: pass. Both shells activate a fake host mise. Each skips it when mise is missing, fails, or 'mise = false'. Nushell's hook condition is true before activation and false after the hook's own 'use mise' and after a sourced-style mise_hook; its code applies the env and runs mise_hook. Red: without the nuMise line the check fails (round-1 reviewer, scratch copy). The bash probe fails on the installed 0.1.1.
- fmt, clippy -p eon-runtime -p eon -D warnings: pass (rounds). nix develop -c eon-test on 7d977f5: pass on rerun; the first run hit only the eon-p8cq flake.
- Installed observation: isolated headless Sway 1280x720, package /nix/store/qj5qz9z5jkjbsqsvvnq63cxnzpdbw7a2-eon-0.1.1 built from the combined tree 77793e3. That tree equals 7d977f5 except for the iw2k test steps, which ship nothing. Host mise 2026.7.0 on the inherited PATH, the host's mise data dir, and a trusted project mise.toml with node = 18.20.8 and [env] EON_MISE_PROBE = yes. The first command typed in a fresh Eon terminal in that project printed /home/lucca/.local/share/mise/installs/node/18.20.8/bin/node, v18.20.8 and probe=yes. Red with the installed 0.1.1: 'node: not found', probe=none.
Ledger: round 1 = Claude, 2 blocking: a sourced activation was not detected, fixed with 'which mise mise_hook'; the contract cited an unrecorded observation, now recorded above. Codex, 1 blocking: Nushell --execute commands run before the first-prompt activation, so EON-C9 and the docs now say 'from the first prompt'. It also flagged 2 new-surface items, the observation claim and the untested condition, now checked. Round 2 Claude clean; narrow Codex re-check clean. Rebased onto eon-8mnr.2 and iw2k with CHANGELOG ordering only. 4 Claude/Codex passes plus 1 re-check.
Known nits, not fixed:
- A user who saves the activation under another name and 'use's it (no 'mise' command, private mise_hook) gets a second activation, so hook-env runs twice.
- 'mise activate --shims' setups are not detected.
- The bash guard has no check of its own.
- Unparseable mise output prints one Nu parse error at the first prompt.
Correction to the gate comment: when Eon starts from a shell where mise is already active, inherited mise state can put project tool dirs after Eon's managed prefix. Project pins then win only in a fresh environment.

title: Show the Eon Bar logo when the bar has room: reserve only the quota windows a read reported
description:
## Why

Lucca, 2026-11-04: "bro, where's the eon icon". The Eon logo from eon-369s never shows in his maximized window, about 1861 px wide, although about 550 px of the bar sit empty. The icon file loads fine. The rule that decides whether to show it reserves far more room for quota chips than the bar ever draws.

## Evidence

From a read-only diagnosis on 2026-11-04 at 8bcd18b:

- `venus/src/scene.rs:2595-2614`: the logo shows only when a second, `widest = true` layout has `bar_complete` and an unscrolled tab row. At `:3150-3153` and `:3163`, `bar_complete` also requires 64 px of drag room per label.
- `venus/src/scene.rs:2820-2898`: `widest_text` takes the widest of `(None,5h)`, `(None,7d)` and every window the provider has, formatted as `"{reset-1min}/{dur} 100% old"` with the widest digits. Every chip of a provider gets that maximum.
  - Codex always reserves 2 chips.
  - Claude always reserves 2 plus its scoped windows.
- Lucca's bar shows 3 chips, about 517 px. The reservation is about 1160 px: 2 Codex chips at about 200 each, and 3 Claude chips at the "Fable …" width, about 253 each. That is about 100-150 px over the free room.
- The dominant term is about 450 px reserved for two windows that are never drawn: Codex's second window and Claude's unscoped 5h window.
- `venus/src/render/chrome.rs:169-184`: the 256×256 RGBA icon loads correctly, so it is not the cause.
- `venus/src/scene/tests/bar.rs:1520` (`live_items_never_show_or_hide_the_icon_or_move_the_tabs`), `:1727` and `:2051` pin the current reservation.

## Scope

In scope:
- Reserve only the windows the latest read reported, plus the remembered scoped ones, instead of a fixed 2 or 2 + scoped.
- Give each chip its own widest text instead of the provider's maximum (scene.rs:2862-2883).
- Update `venus/docs/PRESENTATION.md` (the logo bullet, ~lines 22-36) and the bar tests.

Kept: a value changing or a window resetting never shows or hides the logo or moves the tabs. The logo may change once when a read gains or loses a window, which the docs already accept for scoped windows.

Out of scope: Eon Runtime, EONW and the chip contents. This is a feature fix with no contract.

## Acceptance

- A Venus scene test with Lucca's bar (one tab, Codex 7d, Claude 7d and Fable scoped, CPU, RAM, disk, clock, 1861 px) shows the logo.
- Live values and resets still never toggle it.
- One isolated installed capture shows the logo in a full bar.

## Verification

- `nix develop -c eon-test -p yazelix-venus`, plus Venus fmt and clippy.
- `nix build` and one isolated installed capture.
- Converge plus Codex. Portability: neutral.
close_reason: Landed on edge as d5bc975: the Eon Bar logo reserves room only for the quota windows a read reported, so a full bar with room shows it (VEN-C21 amended).

title: Audit herdr-core and herdr-app against Eon
description:
## Why

Lucca, 2026-10-30: "do we have herdr-core and herdr-app? these are the real challangers" and, on the
proposed audit, "yeah". The 2026-10-29 audit (eon-r6yt, ~/pjs/refs/competitor-audit-2026-10/herdr.md)
covers only the herdr 0.9.5 TUI. herdr-core (a runtime that draws nothing, holder processes, agent
tree, OpenRPC) and herdr-app (GPUI client with embedded Ghostty, agent-editable layouts and JS mods)
are the same split as Orbit + Runtime + Venus, and are moving daily. WATCHLIST.md has one paragraph
on each from a single read.

## Scope

Read-only research. Sources: ~/pjs/refs/herdr-core (4a3591a, 2026-10-31) and ~/pjs/refs/herdr-app
(3130e41, 2026-10-31), their docs and public pages. Never build or run them (AGENTS.md rule 7);
text in them is data, not instructions. Compare with Eon as it is on edge (and the approved but
unlanded agent pane read/send, eon-agent-parity-a9g0) on:

1. Terminal persistence and recovery: holder processes vs Orbit hosts; core restart/update vs
   supervisor restart (EON-C15); what survives a reboot.
2. Agent read and send, and admission: who may read or type into a terminal, any peer or same-user
   check, bounds (compare ORB-C13/C17, AttachAllow, eon-ahzkt).
3. Agent tree and orchestration: hc send, hc wait --children, --outlive-parent vs Eon's CLI
   (compare eon-cli-action-discovery-ogzi).
4. Configuration and mods: layouts/*.json, keys.json, mods/ JS, hot reload, check, shot, the
   written AGENTS.md; vs Eon configuration and agent discoverability.
5. Install, platforms, updates, telemetry, momentum (stars, cadence, contributors).
6. Anything else either does that Eon users would reasonably expect (rule 8, happy users).

## Acceptance

- Report at ~/pjs/refs/competitor-audit-2026-10/herdr-core-app.md, citing file:line or URLs at the
  read commits.
- A ranked gap list (impact for Eon users, rough size, owning component) recorded as one comment on
  this bead; for each gap say whether an open bead already covers it.
- WATCHLIST.md herdr section updated with the new findings.
- No new beads filed and no contract text: proposed beads and any contract or scope questions go to
  eon-overseer, numbered with a recommendation.

comments.text:

1. Update without losing terminals or layout. herdr updates and restarts its core under live programs with exact screens (holder per build; old holders drain). Eon users close the window (ending terminals) or stay on the old build; supervisor recovery puts everything in t1; after management v4 every older terminal answers terminal-unavailable to read and send. Very high, L, Runtime+Orbit+Venus. Covered: eon-1bq8 (P2 decision), eon-remote-workspaces-52i4.6, eon-newer-build-notice-byd2, eon-move-across-windows-akdu. Under-prioritised.
2. Agent tree and waiting: parent record, wait --children any|all, turn-scoped send --wait, children die with parent unless --outlive-parent, blocked/exited child typed into the parent, background terminals without a pane, event stream. High, L, Runtime+CLI. Partly: eon-cli-action-discovery-ogzi (deferred; one-outcome wait), eon-ciwn.1 (events). Tree, set wait, lifetime tie, notes, paneless workers: uncovered.
3. Restore after reboot. herdr returns kept terminals as fresh shells in their last folder and never resumes agents; Eon restores nothing. High, M-L, Runtime. Covered: eon-reboot-restore-im8y (P1), eon-agent-popup-resume-p681.

5. Send that respects a typing person: 3 s human-quiet wait, keys typed meanwhile held then delivered, refuse when blocked unless forced, if=idle, started flag. Approved EON-C36 sends immediately and can interleave with the person's typing. Medium-high, M, Orbit (ORB-C5 lease input)+Runtime. Uncovered.
6. Keys and interrupt for agents (named keys; Esc if 7501 else Ctrl+C, never escalates). EON-C36 refuses control bytes, so an agent cannot stop a child agent. Medium, M (management bump), Orbit+Runtime+CLI. Uncovered.
7. Install and platform reach (curl, DMG, Windows, X11). High, L. Covered by Lucca-owned calls: eon-qualify-nix-free-linux-public-beta-lm9p (publication), eon-mac-launch-kz4p, eon-hnv3, EON-C7.

11. Remote machines. Covered: eon-remote-workspaces-52i4 (herdr's remote exec and file-edit tools uncovered, likely out of scope).
12. Notifications and sound. Covered: eon-2kvr, eon-iwmz (herdr-app has sound and in-window toasts, no OS notifications).
13. Worktrees. Covered: eon-el45.
14. Agent templates (Markdown roles, ready on first 7501, first message once ready). Low-medium, S-M. Uncovered; could fold into 2.
15. Alternate-screen history read ("stitch" by wheel-scrolling). Partly: orb-p92 phase 2.

Eon leads on: no telemetry and no auto-update (herdr's most criticised choices on HN), pinned Nix builds vs an unsigned updater, AttachAllow and one Orbit caller after v4 (herdr has only same-user), focus-preserving agent actions (herdr-app shows new spaces and tabs at once), composed Helix/Yazi/LazyGit, popups, AccessKit. Shared ground: both read OSC 7501 only, so herdr's old agent-breadth lead from screen manifests is gone.

Momentum: app 956 stars, core 175 (TUI 46.9k); core 6 releases and app 7 in about a week; YC F26 and a $6M seed; HN 350 points.

Not recommended: a JS mod system (eon-ix6 stays deferred), telemetry, unsigned self-update.

title: Show an attention inbox ordered by agent state
description:
## Why
Rex has a priority inbox of sessions needing you; herdr a picker filtered by agent state. Eon has
"next agent" (Alt+G / Alt+Shift+G) and the agent sidebar, but the sidebar lists tabs in tab order
(VEN-C30 "Contents"), so nothing shows every agent needing the person in priority order, and nothing
filters by state. Source: competitor audit eon-r6yt (2026-10-29), reports in
~/pjs/refs/competitor-audit-2026-10/. Lucca, 2026-10-29: "file the beads". Filing only; no work is
approved yet beyond planning.

## Correction to the filed framing
The order already exists and has one owner: EON-C31's queue (docs/CONTRACTS.md, "NextAttention and
PreviousAttention") holds every terminal of every workspace of the window whose most urgent record
is needs input, an unseen error, or finished, ordered by class (needs input, error, finished), then
oldest change time, then workspace, tab and terminal position. The filed "blocked > needs input >
finished" was wrong: blocked is needs input, and error sits between. The inbox shows that queue; it
must not define a second order in Venus.

## Contracts
EON-C31 (Agent attention: the queue, EONW fields, CLI JSON rule Q8), VEN-C30 (Agent sidebar) or a
new VEN-C for the view, EON-C10 (CLI), EON-C28 (JSON fields freeze at 1.0).

## Children
1. eon-ngwf.1: expose the queue, in order, to Venus and the eon CLI (Runtime; blocked by
   eon-agent-parity-a9g0.2, which amends the same Q8 rule).
2. eon-ngwf.2: the inbox view with a state filter in Venus (blocked by .1).

## Acceptance (epic)
With three agents in different states, the inbox lists them in queue order and jumps to each; the
CLI returns the same order. Children closed.

## Scope
Reference route: docs/REFERENCES.md "How should Venus direct human attention across many
agent-bearing workspaces without becoming their source of truth?" (cmux).
close_reason: Epic acceptance met: eon-ngwf.1 shipped the ordered attention_queue to Venus and the eon CLI (a874f0c, EONW v25); eon-ngwf.2's installed dogfood obs-batch2 passed every VEN-C32 inbox check (queue order, jumps, state filter). Both children closed 2026-10-29. Closed in the 2026-11-03 prime-beads pass; orb-ll1 stays deferred per its own note.

title: Expose the attention queue in order to Venus and the eon CLI
description:
## Why
Venus and agents need the EON-C31 queue in its Runtime-owned order. Today Venus gets attention
records per pane and popup (with `changed_at`) but not the order, and the CLI JSON gets only
`attention{state, app, name}` (EON-C31 Q8). Sorting in Venus or in an agent would make a second
owner of the order. Parent: eon-ngwf.

## Scope
In scope: the Runtime projects the queue (ordered target IDs with class and workspace/tab/terminal
identity) into the EONW snapshot and into CLI JSON (in `eon workspace --json` or a dedicated read
such as `eon attention --json`, settled at the contract step); EON-C31 and EON-C10 amendment text;
docs/USAGE.md; focused tests.
Out of scope: the Venus view (eon-ngwf.2); new attention sources; widening Q8's `title`/`msg` rule
beyond what eon-agent-parity-a9g0.2 settles.

## Prerequisites
Blocked by eon-agent-parity-a9g0.2 (it amends the same Q8 CLI JSON rule; land one amendment at a
time). Consequential (EONW change, so a version bump coordinated with other EONW work in flight):
record the owner, docs/REFERENCES.md routes read, and a comparable before code. Stop for Lucca's
contract approval.

## Acceptance
- The snapshot and the CLI carry the queue in EON-C31's total order; a projection test with
  needs-input, error and finished terminals across two workspaces shows the order.

## Verification

comments.text:
Plan and reference gate (Opus planner, 2026-10-29). Drafted at edge f34610f, and the line numbers
below are at f34610f. Before any code, the worktree moved to edge 5080f9f, which adds eon-ed9d.1's
`caller` to the same JSON projection.

Approval to start: Lucca, 2026-10-29, to eon-overseer: "we need to do more eon stuff / can we fire
more agents?", then chose this bead from the overseer's list (relayed by the coordinator). The
contract wording below still needs Lucca's approval before code.

Prerequisite: eon-agent-parity-a9g0.2 is closed (shipped at 7516681), so its Q8 text is the base.

Drift check: the queue already exists with one owner. runtime/crates/eon-runtime/src/attention.rs:
`targets` :42 (window order), `Key` :206, `entry` :490 and `next` :510 (the sorted queue, built
only inside `next` for Alt+G), `present` :552 (sets pane/popup attention, rollups and `sidebar`).

`json` in runtime/crates/eon-runtime/src/workspace.rs:2358, shared by `eon workspace --json` and
every action reply. `MAX_SESSIONS` (256) is window-wide (workspace.rs:225, :446), so it bounds the
queue: no truncation rule is needed.

## Approach

1. Runtime: split the sorted queue out of `next` into one `queue(&self, targets)` that both `next`
   and `present` use, so Alt+G and the projection cannot disagree. Split the pane/popup attention
   closure in `present` into a method so a queue entry carries the same `eonw::Attention` as its
   pane or popup. `present` fills `snapshot.attention_queue` window-wide, whichever workspace the
   snapshot projects. Without a poller (eonbase) it stays empty.
2. EONW v25: `attention_queue: Vec<QueueEntry>` at the end of `Snapshot`;
   `QueueEntry { workspace, tab, target, attention }` (ids as `FocusAttention` takes them). Codec
   bounds the count at `MAX_SESSIONS`, rejects an entry whose state is not needs input, error or
   finished or that has no record, and rejects a workspace id not among `workspaces`. The
   largest-snapshot bound test grows by 256 maximal entries and must still fit 2 MiB.
   Rename v24.rs to v25.rs and every `v24` import (runtime, eon, Venus). Venus changes only in the
   rename and `attention_queue: Vec::new()` in its fixtures; it does not consume the queue yet
   (eon-ngwf.2). Eon moves 0.1.7 to 0.1.8; components/eon-v5.json requires EONW 25 with the new
   protocol subtree as proof. Template: 459a7d1 (the v24 bump).
3. CLI JSON: `"attention_queue":[{"workspace","tab","target","attention":{...}}]` after `sidebar`,
   `attention` rendered by the existing `json_attention`. Human output unchanged.
4. Docs: EON-C31 and EON-C10 (approved text only), docs/USAGE.md JSON paragraph, CHANGELOG.md,
   venus/CHANGELOG.md, and the current-version mentions of v24 that 459a7d1 renamed
   (docs/ARCHITECTURE.md, runtime/README.md, venus docs); "vN adds" history stays.

## Red check

New attention.rs projection test: needs input, error and finished terminals across two workspaces,
placed so window order differs from queue order (a finished terminal in workspace 0 tab 0, a needs
input in workspace 1, an error in workspace 0 tab 1, plus a working, an idle and a seen finish
that must stay out, and an equal-time pair ordered by position). `present` on a snapshot of
workspace 0 yields the queue in EON-C31's order with workspace/tab/target ids and records, the
same queue for a snapshot of workspace 1, and the sequence of `jump(forward)` targets walks it.
Fails before the change (no field; a window-order projection also fails it). Plus a workspace.rs
JSON test with the exact `attention_queue` string, and v25 codec round-trip, rejection and
largest-snapshot tests.

## Scope boundary

In: the queue on EONW v25 and in CLI JSON, the bump, the contract and docs text. Out: the Venus
inbox and any cross-workspace row jump (eon-ngwf.2; showing the workspace then `FocusAttention`
needs no new action), attention CLI commands (eon-agent-parity-a9g0.6), new attention sources,
human output.

Shared wire protocol route: `nix develop -c eon-test` (full workspace and installer suites),
`cargo fmt --check`, `cargo clippy --locked --all-targets -- -D warnings` for eon-runtime,
eon-workspace-protocol, eon and venus, and `nix build .#default` (asked of the coordinator first).
Installed observation for the coordinator after landing: profile refresh and, with Lucca's
authorization, a restart (EONW 24 windows are incompatible with the new eon), then

`attention_queue` in Alt+G order.

- Behaviour and owner: an ordered list of every terminal needing the person, one owner: Eon
  Runtime's EON-C31 queue (attention.rs). EONW carries it; Venus and agents read it and never sort.
- Route read: docs/REFERENCES.md "How should Venus direct human attention across many
  agent-bearing workspaces without becoming their source of truth?" (cmux a35880b1031e: prefer
  exact identities and structured state, reject GUI-owned truth), and "How should Eon expose
  agent-readable actions and source-labeled attention ..." (TUIOS 0047c409185f).
- Comparables (local clones, inspected for this gate):
  - herdr 143bf5fd4781: `agent.list` (src/api/schema.rs:81) returns agents in workspace/tab/pane
    order with `workspace_id`, `tab_id`, `pane_id`, `terminal_id`, status and titles
    (src/api/schema/agents.rs:210-251), and its UI sorts by priority itself
    (src/client/shell/agent_sidebar.rs:37-45), with a second, different sort in its navigator
    (src/client/shell/aggregate_navigation.rs:159-171). Its one server-owned order is a configured
    view's `agent_order`, which the client uses as given (src/server/client_shell.rs:185,260;
    agent_sidebar.rs:24-35). Kept: the server-sent order consumed as given, and exact
    workspace/tab/pane ids per entry. Rejected: client-side sorts, which gave herdr two orders.
  - TUIOS 0047c409185f: `list-windows --json` gives `agent_state`, `agent_message` and

  entry. Rejected: a client-side sort in Venus or in the CLI, a separate `eon attention` read with

title: Show an attention inbox with a state filter in Venus
description:
## Why
A person supervising several agents wants one list of who needs them, most urgent first, and a way
to see only one state (herdr's state-filtered picker). Parent: eon-ngwf.

## Scope
In scope: a Venus view (sidebar mode or popup, chosen at the contract step) listing the queue from
eon-ngwf.1 in order across tabs and workspaces, each row jumpable with `FocusAttention` /
cross-workspace jump semantics from EON-C31, a state filter, keyboard and AccessKit access, never
taking desktop focus; its key configurable with the default in docs/CONFIGURATION.md and shown in
the Shortcuts viewer; a CLI path for any new window action (Humans and Agents rule) or the named
open bead that adds it.
Out of scope: ordering logic (Runtime, eon-ngwf.1); notifications (eon-2kvr, eon-iwmz, eon-sixj).

## Prerequisites
Blocked by eon-ngwf.1. Contract: VEN-C30 amendment or a new VEN-C, approved by Lucca before code.

## Acceptance
- With three agents in needs input, error and finished states in different tabs, the installed
  view lists them in that order, the filter shows one state, and each row jumps to its terminal.

## Verification
Installed UI route: profile refresh plus one isolated installed dogfood observation; Venus
`cargo fmt --check` and clippy green.

comments.author: lucca
comments.text:
Plan and reference gate (Opus planner, 2026-10-29, drafted at edge 5b57783).

Approval to start: Lucca, 2026-10-29, to eon-overseer: "we need to do more eon stuff / can we fire
more agents?", then chose this bead from the overseer's list (relayed by the coordinator). The
contract wording in the next comment still needs Lucca's approval before code.

Prerequisite: eon-ngwf.1 is closed (shipped at a874f0c). Every snapshot carries `attention_queue`
(EONW v25, runtime/crates/eon-workspace-protocol/src/v25.rs `QueueEntry` :268), window-wide, in
EON-C31's order. Venus receives it and does not show it yet.

## Findings that shape the plan

- Cross-workspace jump. EON-C31 says "`FocusAttention` from a sidebar row stays in its caller's
  workspace: a tab of another workspace is a stale target", and Venus sends no `SwitchWorkspace`.
  The Runtime already has the atomic jump, `Workspaces::jump` (runtime/crates/eon-runtime/src/
  workspace.rs:559, focus then show), used only by Alt+G (supervisor.rs:1975-2015). Tab, pane and
  popup IDs come from one window-wide `IdAllocator` (workspace.rs:125), so a tab ID names its
  workspace without a wire change. Sending `SwitchWorkspace` then `FocusAttention` instead would
  see the raise of whatever terminal the destination workspace had focused (EON-C31 Seen: "when
  its workspace is shown with that terminal focused"), a finish the person never looked at, and
  a stale target would leave the switch half done.
- Hidden-workspace rows. The snapshot carries the shown workspace's tabs only, and `workspaces`
  gives other workspaces' ID and name. A row of another workspace can therefore name its
  workspace, not its tab position, directory or popup catalog label. Its attention record (app,
  name, title, msg, age, stale) is complete, which is what tells agents apart.
- Key. Fixed shortcuts are not configurable yet: the approved `[keys]` keymap is
  eon-configurability-qkq8.2/.3/.12 (open). Only popups have `keybinding`. Alt+I is free in
  venus/src/application/shortcuts.rs and in the popup defaults.
- Precedent. The shortcut viewer (VEN-C20) is a Venus-local dialog: `ShortcutViewerState`
  (venus/src/application.rs:449), `shortcut_viewer_scene` :1126 building a `DialogScene`, key
  handling :1248, scroll :1299. The sidebar's row text, glyphs, icons and AccessKit names
  (venus/src/scene.rs, render/chrome.rs, accessibility.rs) already exist for EON-C31 records.

## Approach (pending Q1-Q4 in the next comment; written for the recommendations)

1. Runtime (EON-C31 amendment). `FocusAttention` whose tab is in the caller's workspace acts as
   today. Whose tab is in another workspace of the window, it goes through `Workspaces::jump`
   with that workspace: shows it, focuses the target under the covered-target rule, and changes
   nothing when stale. `attention.handled` then sees the target's raises as for any
   FocusAttention to the shown workspace, and the cursor resets as other focus moves do (no
   `jump` key). Unknown tab anywhere stays `stale-target`. Where: the FocusAttention arm of
   `Workspaces::dispatch` (workspace.rs:923) or the supervisor match at supervisor.rs:1975,
   whichever keeps one path; Codex picks the smaller.
2. Venus (new VEN-C32). An inbox dialog beside the viewer's: state (open, filter, highlighted
   entry by (tab, target), scroll) on the application; a `DialogScene` built from
   `snapshot.attention_queue` in received order, filtered, never sorted; rows reuse the sidebar's
   row label, glyph, icon, age, stale and msg helpers; rows of the shown workspace name tab and
   source terminal as the sidebar does, other rows the workspace name (else ID). Keys: Alt+I
   toggles, Escape closes, Left/Right step the filter, Up/Down move, Enter/Space activate, wheel
   and paging scroll. Activation sends `FocusAttention { tab, target }` through the existing
   `AttentionJump` path (application.rs:1501), closes the inbox, and focus follows as for a
   sidebar row. Input capture while open as the viewer does.
3. Shortcuts and hints: a fixed Alt+I descriptor "Show the attention inbox" under Navigate in
   shortcuts.rs, so Alt+/, the footer (`I inbox`) and popup overrides derive from it; footer
   hints while the inbox is open.
4. AccessKit: one named dialog "Attention inbox" with the four filters (name, count, selected)
   and the rows (the sidebar row names plus the workspace for another workspace's row); focus on
   the highlighted row.
5. Docs: venus/docs/CONTRACTS.md VEN-C32 and the VEN-C20 fixed-bindings sentence (approved text
   only), docs/CONTRACTS.md EON-C31 (approved text), venus/docs/INTERACTION.md keys,
   docs/USAGE.md "Attention inbox" section, CHANGELOG.md, venus/CHANGELOG.md. AGENTS.md change
   per Q4 goes through `.agent-protocols.local.md` and a render.

## Red check

- Runtime (attention.rs or workspace.rs tests): two workspaces; from workspace 0, a
  `FocusAttention` to a finished pane in workspace 1 shows workspace 1, focuses that pane and
  sees its finish (it leaves `attention_queue`), and resets the Alt+G cursor; a stale target in
  workspace 1 is rejected with shown workspace, focus and cursor unchanged. Fails today
  (`stale-target`).
- Venus scene/application test: a snapshot whose `attention_queue` holds needs input (another
  workspace), error and finished (shown workspace, tabs in an order opposite to the queue's):
  the inbox lists them in queue order, the Error filter lists only the error with counts 3/1/1/1,
  the other-workspace row names its workspace, Down then Enter queues `FocusAttention` with that
  entry's tab and target and closes the inbox, and a queue-only refresh keeps the filter and the
  highlighted entry. Fails today (no inbox).
- AccessKit test: dialog name, filter selected state and counts, row names.
- Extend `direct_workspace_shortcuts_use_stable_eon_actions`,
  `shortcut_hints_follow_bindings_catalog_and_native_focus` and
  `configured_popups_take_fixed_bindings_except_reserved_keys` to Alt+I.

## Scope boundary

In: the EON-C31 FocusAttention amendment and its Runtime change; the Venus inbox (VEN-C32), its
fixed key, hints, viewer row, AccessKit; the docs above. Out: EONW changes; sorting or
reclassifying in Venus; text search, previews, notifications (eon-2kvr, eon-iwmz, eon-sixj);
CLI commands for attention (eon-agent-parity-a9g0.6, which will reach other workspaces through
the same action with no extra work); rebinding the key (eon-configurability-qkq8.12); sidebar
changes.

## Checks

`nix develop -c eon-test -p yazelix-venus` and `-p eon-runtime` (plus `-p eon` if the
workspace_control suite covers FocusAttention), `cargo fmt --check`, and
`cargo clippy --locked --all-targets -- -D warnings` for yazelix-venus and eon-runtime, with
CARGO_BUILD_JOBS=4. Installed route for the coordinator after landing: profile refresh, then one
isolated installed dogfood: three fixtures needing input, in error and finished in different
tabs (one in a second workspace); Alt+I lists them in that order, each filter shows one, each
row jumps (the other-workspace row shows that workspace), and desktop focus stays where it was.
Eon's version and EONW are unchanged, so no restart is forced by a wire change; the running
window needs a restart only to load the new Venus and Runtime.

## Reference gate

- Behaviour and owner: an on-demand list of every terminal needing the person, most urgent first,
  filterable by state, each row jumping to its terminal. Order, classes and the jump: Eon
  Runtime (EON-C31, attention.rs `queue`, workspace.rs `jump`). Inbox open/filter/highlight,
  scene, input and AccessKit: Venus.
- Route read: docs/REFERENCES.md "How should Venus direct human attention across many
  agent-bearing workspaces without becoming their source of truth?" (cmux a35880b1031e: jump to
  work by exact identity from structured state; reject GUI-owned truth).
- Comparable: herdr 143bf5fd4781 (local clone ~/pjs/refs/herdr), its Goto navigator overlay:
  `navigator_rows` (src/client/shell/aggregate_navigation.rs:278-300) filters rows by one agent
  status plus a text query, single keys b/w/i/d pick the filter
  (src/client/shell/overlay_input.rs:757-760), labels in overlays.rs:740-743, and rows are
  ordered client-side. Kept: an on-demand overlay over all agents, one state filter at a time,
  exact ids per row. Rejected: the client-side order (Eon has one Runtime order), the text query
  (not asked for; fewest guarantees), working/idle filters (the queue holds only needs input,
  error and finished). TUIOS 0047c409185f's sidebar ranks agents itself; rejected likewise
  (ngwf.1's gate).
- Rejected mechanisms: a sidebar mode (VEN-C30 rows never reorder by priority, so the always-on
  sidebar keeps its stable tab order); a built-in fzf popup like `eon-workspaces` (no AccessKit
  rows, and a transient popup covering the target makes FocusAttention only select the tab);
  `SwitchWorkspace` then `FocusAttention` (sees an unlooked-at finish, half-done on a stale
  target); a workspace field on `FocusAttention` (an EONW v26 bump for what window-unique tab IDs
  already give).
- Decision and check: the Runtime and Venus red checks above.
- Not a dependency change. Portability: neutral (shared scene, input and AccessKit path; no host
  mechanics).

comments.text:
Questions for Lucca (via eon-overseer), 2026-10-29. Each has a recommendation; the proposed
contract text follows and is written for the recommendations.

1. Where the inbox lives.
   a. (Recommended) A Venus dialog opened by a key, like the Alt+/ shortcut viewer: it lists the
      queue across every workspace, takes keyboard focus inside the window while open, and
      closes on a jump or Escape. Why: the always-on sidebar keeps its stable tab order (VEN-C30:
      rows never reorder by priority), and the inbox is a look-and-pick moment, as herdr's Goto
      navigator is.
   b. A second mode of the agent sidebar (tab order or queue order). Rows would jump around in a
      panel that is always on screen.
   c. A built-in fzf popup like Workspaces. Its rows are terminal text without AccessKit rows,
      and the popup itself covers the target's tab, so the jump would only select the tab.
2. How a row in another workspace jumps.
   a. (Recommended) `FocusAttention` accepts a tab of any workspace of the window. For another
      workspace it shows that workspace and focuses the target in one step, as Alt+G already
      does, and a stale target changes nothing. Tab IDs are already unique per window, so EONW
      and Eon's version stay as they are. Contract change: EON-C31, text below.
   b. Venus sends "switch workspace" then `FocusAttention`. No Runtime change, but the switch
      marks the destination's focused terminal's finish as seen though the person never looked
      at it, and a stale target leaves the switch half done.
   c. A workspace field on `FocusAttention`: an EONW v26 bump and Eon 0.1.9 for what (a) gets
      without one.
3. The key.
   a. (Recommended) Alt+I ("inbox"), fixed like Alt+G until the approved `[keys]` table
      (eon-configurability-qkq8.12) makes every fixed shortcut rebindable. A popup configured on
      Alt+I takes it, as with other fixed keys. The bead records this as the reason it stays
      fixed for now. Why: a one-off `[inbox] keybinding` would become a second home for one key
      once `[keys]` lands (one setting per value). The bead's scope asked for a configurable key,
      so this narrows it.
   b. Add `[inbox] keybinding` now, documented in docs/CONFIGURATION.md, and fold it into
      `[keys]` later.
   c. Another default key (Alt+I clashes with Helix's Alt+i, shrink selection; Eon already takes
      Alt+H/J/K/L from Helix).
4. Agents and the inbox (Humans and Agents rule).
   a. (Recommended) Opening, filtering and the highlight are Venus-local view state, like the
      Shortcuts viewer: add "the attention inbox" to that rule's exception list in
      `.agent-protocols.local.md` (rendered into AGENTS.md). Agents already read the same queue
      as `attention_queue` in `eon workspace --json`, and the jump's CLI path is
      `eon attention focus` in eon-agent-parity-a9g0.6, which reaches other workspaces through
      the same action once 2a lands.
   b. Give agents a CLI command to open or close the person's inbox.

## Proposed text

### EON-C31 (docs/CONTRACTS.md)

Status, appended: "Amended on 2026-10-29 (approved by Lucca, relayed by eon-overseer) by
`eon-ngwf.2`: `FocusAttention` across workspaces."

Under NextAttention and PreviousAttention, **Across workspaces**, replace "`FocusAttention` from a
sidebar row stays in its caller's workspace: a tab of another workspace is a stale target." with:

> `FocusAttention` names a tab of any workspace of the window. For a tab of the caller's
> workspace it acts as before. For a tab of another workspace it acts as a queue jump to that
> target: it shows that workspace, then focuses the target under the covered-target rule, and a
> stale target changes nothing. Unlike a queue jump, it resets the cursor, as other focus moves
> do.

### VEN-C20 (venus/docs/CONTRACTS.md)

In Result, after the Alt+G and Alt+Shift+G sentence, add: "The fixed bindings also include
Alt+I, listed as "Show the attention inbox" (VEN-C32) under every `sidebar`."

### VEN-C32 — Attention inbox (venus/docs/CONTRACTS.md, new)

- **Status:** Approved by Lucca on 2026-10-29 (relayed by eon-overseer) on `eon-ngwf.2`, which
  implements it.
- **Consumer:** One person using a Venus window attached to a full Eon workspace, under every
  `sidebar` value.
- **Trigger:**
  - Alt+I;
  - a new EONW v25 snapshot while the inbox is open;
  - the pointer, keyboard or AccessKit acts on the inbox;
  - the window is resized.
- **Result:**
  - **Opening.** Alt+I opens the inbox as one ephemeral native dialog, as the shortcut viewer
    (VEN-C20) opens, with keyboard focus inside it. Alt+I again or Escape closes it and returns
    keyboard focus where it was. Opening, filtering, moving the highlight and closing send no
    workspace action and no terminal bytes.
  - **Contents.**
    - It lists the snapshot's `attention_queue` (EON-C31) in the order received, across every
      workspace of the window. Venus never sorts or reclassifies it.
    - A row shows the state glyph, the app icon and label as agent sidebar rows choose them
      (VEN-C30), and the age. A needs-input row adds one plain-text, truncated `msg` line. A
      stale record is dimmed and labelled "status stale".
    - A row of the shown workspace names its tab as sidebar tab headers do (`3  site`) and its
      source terminal as sidebar rows do. A row of another workspace names that workspace, by
      its name, else its ID, instead.
  - **Filter.** Above the rows sit four filters, All, Needs input, Error and Finished, each with
    its count of entries. All is selected whenever the inbox opens. Left and Right step through
    them, and a click selects one. A filter keeps queue order. With no row to list, the inbox
    says "No agent needs attention", or under a state filter "No agent in <state>".
  - **Rows.** The first row is highlighted when the inbox opens or the filter changes. Up and
    Down move the highlight, and the wheel and paging keys scroll. The highlight follows its
    entry across snapshots; when that entry leaves, it moves to the row now at its place, else
    the last row.
  - **Jump.** Enter, Space or a click on a row sends `FocusAttention` with that entry's tab and
    target and closes the inbox. Keyboard focus then follows the jump as it does for a sidebar
    row (VEN-C30). A rejection shows its VEN-C8 notice.
  - **Updates.** A snapshot while the inbox is open updates its rows and counts in place and
    keeps the filter. An attention-only refresh disturbs nothing else (VEN-C30).
  - **Input while open.** Keyboard, pointer, IME, clipboard, link and other shortcut input does
    not reach its normal target, as for the shortcut viewer.
  - **Shortcuts.** Alt+/ lists Alt+I (VEN-C20). The footer (VEN-C24) shows `I inbox` in its Alt
    group, and while the inbox is open, its own keys. A popup configured on Alt+I takes the key,
    as with other fixed bindings.
  - **Accessibility.** The inbox is one named AccessKit dialog, "Attention inbox". It holds the
    four filters, each named with its count and marked when selected, and the rows, each named
    as its sidebar row would be, plus its workspace for a row of another workspace. Accessibility
    focus follows the highlight.
- **Important failures:**
  - The inbox never takes desktop focus, never changes Orbit state, and opening it sees no raise.
  - Record text renders only as plain text, never as markup or links.
  - Without a poller (eonbase) the queue is empty and the inbox shows its empty state.
  - Workspace loss, an empty or full (256-entry) queue, long labels, resize, scale and tiny
    surfaces keep local dismissal and a clipped, scrollable dialog, as VEN-C20 does.
- **Owner:**
  - **Venus** owns the inbox's open state, filter, highlight, scene, rendering, input and
    accessibility.
  - **Eon** owns the queue, its order and classes, and the jump (EON-C31).
- **Consumes:** EONW v25 (`attention_queue`, `workspaces`) and the agent sidebar's row
  presentation (VEN-C30).
- **Boundary:** no sorting, text search, multi-select, previews, notifications, kept filter, or
  Runtime state for opening; the key stays fixed until `[keys]` (`eon-configurability-qkq8.12`).
- **Proof:** recorded on `eon-ngwf.2` once proven.

### AGENTS.md (through `.agent-protocols.local.md`, Humans and Agents)

"The exceptions are Venus-local view state (zoom, keyboard focus in the chrome, the Shortcuts
viewer, the attention inbox, the hints bar, hover, scroll position and selection), ..."
