title: Apply chrome, panel and popup configuration to running windows
description:
## Why and recorded scope

The original eon-6ui6p plan found that panel/chrome settings reach Venus only at launch/reopen. This bead chose live application without reopening the native window. On 2026-11-11 the eon-overseer explicitly added popup entries: a new [popups.*] entry must become available in a running window. Preserve both outcomes, delivered as separate session-sized children.

## Current evidence (dcaef1c, 2026-11-12)

- EONW is v40 (runtime/crates/eon-workspace-protocol/src/v40.rs:21), not v39. eon-u199d.1 and .3 are closed.
- supervisor.rs:3007 reload_presentation rereads/validates config and resolves terminal_presentation/window_bar before replacing Venus. This applies presentation configuration via replacement; it is not no-reopen live repaint.
- supervisor.rs:1060 initializes the popup catalog at startup. reload_presentation does not replace that catalog. Popup catalog application is therefore a distinct Runtime lifecycle concern.

## Planned children and acceptance

1. Apply resolved panel/chrome settings to the existing Venus without reopening it. Show changed settings in the same process, keep terminal identities/layout/focus, and preserve the last accepted values on invalid input.
2. Reload popup catalog entries in a running supervisor. A configured popup becomes discoverable/actionable through both CLI and window; invalid configuration leaves the accepted catalog and running terminals intact. The plan must explicitly resolve removal/change of a running popup before changing that lifecycle.

The children own their references, exact approvals, failure cases and proof. Closure requires both outcomes and their installed evidence; no runtime behavior is claimed by this planning split.

## Prerequisites and stop boundary

Read accepted eon-u199d.1/.3 first and reuse its configuration owner rather than adding another parser. The original wire ordering remains: eon-xjzr4.1 takes the reserved post-v40 change before the chrome child's next wire version. Do not assume v41 is available. Exact contract text and any EONW change require approval; EON-C19 and EON-C32’s no-live-reload boundary must be reconciled rather than amended implicitly. No watcher, settings UI, automatic restart, or broader in-place update is introduced by this split.

Overseer question: does true no-reopen repaint remain desired now that explicit window reload applies chrome? Until Lucca changes the decision, retain the original no-reopen outcome rather than silently treating replacement as completion.

title: Apply panel and chrome settings without replacing the running Venus
description:
## Why and contract

Child 1 of eon-nhec3: preserve its original no-reopen outcome for panel/chrome configuration. eon-u199d.1/.3 already reread presentation config by replacing Venus; this child must demonstrate a changed presentation in the same Venus process. Runtime remains the sole config parser, Venus consumes resolved presentation data, and Orbit remains terminal authority.

## Evidence and prerequisites

At dcaef1c, supervisor.rs:3007 reload_presentation validates config and resolves terminal_presentation/window_bar, then replaces Venus. EONW v40 Snapshot/Response carry no live presentation-settings payload. Read eon-u199d.1/.3 and the parent. eon-xjzr4.1 owns the reserved post-v40 wire frontier: wait for it before choosing the next available EONW revision.

## Scope

Carry the resolved chrome/panel settings from the original parent scope, including pane_frames and landed heading/fill settings, through the existing workspace/presentation owner. Choose one explicit application trigger in the reference gate, reusing the existing reload/apply boundary where possible; do not add a watcher or settings UI. Preserve current terminal/bar launch/replacement behavior. Popup catalog lifecycle is the sibling, not part of this slice.

## Acceptance

- Edit a supported panel/chrome value, explicitly apply it, and observe the change with unchanged Venus PID, terminal identities/contents and workspace topology/selection.
- Invalid configuration retains the last accepted presentation and changes no runtime state; refusal is readable through the CLI, with no stolen focus.
- Runtime alone resolves config; every relevant current panel kind receives the same resolved value. No new duplicate parser/schema.
- Documentation/configuration defaults distinguish no-reopen application from explicit Venus replacement; CHANGELOG records only delivered behavior.

## Reference and verification gate

Before code, read docs/REFERENCES.md and the Runtime/Venus owner routes and compare an existing terminal's apply-config mechanism at an exact revision. Record owner/data flow, rejected alternatives and the cheapest falsifier. Draft and obtain approval for EON-C19 and any EON-C32/EON-C11 boundary amendment; a wire addition requires an EONW bump and all consumers/manifest updated together. Do not assume approval of text from this split.

Focused invalid-config/state-transition checks, then the full affected wire/lifecycle Rust/Nix route if changed, output-path frame/timing proof, repository review and isolated installed same-process observation on the exact accepted artifact. No tests in this planning pass.

## Stop and maintenance

Stop for a changed scope/contract, or if the overseer/Lucca chooses explicit replacement instead of no-reopen. Preserve live supervisors and desktop focus. Portability: neutral resolved-state policy; native behavior stays behind Venus's existing platform seam. No guarantee for unproved platforms.

title: Apply popup catalog configuration in a running window
description:
## Why and contract

Child 2 of eon-nhec3: on 2026-11-11 the eon-overseer explicitly added [popups.*] entries because a configured eon-desk popup was unavailable in a running window. Deliver that catalog application as one independent Runtime lifecycle slice. EON-C10 owns popup policy; EON-C11 owns any extension of reload. No contract text is approved by this planning split.

## Evidence and prerequisites

At dcaef1c supervisor.rs:1060 builds the popup catalog at startup. reload_presentation (:3007) rereads terminal/bar presentation settings but does not update that catalog. eon-u199d.1/.3 are closed: use their explicit command/validation owner where the reference gate finds it sufficient. This does not depend on no-reopen chrome delivery.

## Scope

Re-read and validate popup definitions through the existing Runtime parser and one explicit application entry point. Expose the accepted catalog to both the native window and CLI. Before code, record behavior for new, changed, disabled and removed entries, including any already-running popup; preserve owned live terminals and refuse unsafe application rather than discarding unsaved work. Do not select a restart/stop policy silently. No watcher, popup settings UI or generic plugin system.

## Acceptance

- Invalid configuration leaves the accepted catalog, bindings and running processes unchanged and returns a useful CLI failure.
- Under the approved lifecycle choice, exercise changing/disabling/removing an entry while its popup is running; no orphaned terminal, silent data loss, stale action target or duplicate key owner. A collision follows the current config diagnostics policy.
- CONFIGURATION/USAGE/CHANGELOG describe the delivered trigger and limits, using existing defaults and config owner.

Read docs/REFERENCES.md and the Runtime lifecycle/configuration owner before choosing the apply mechanism. Record exact inspected references, data owner and failure policy, and bring required EON-C10/EON-C11/config-boundary wording to the overseer/Lucca for approval. If catalog/bindings require an EONW change, coordinate the next available version; never edit v40 in place.

Use the existing catalog/workspace/process harness to falsify new-entry application, invalid-input rollback and the chosen live-instance policy, then the full affected lifecycle/wire Rust/Nix route, repository review and one isolated installed observation. Preserve the original parent's native-window constraint; if the implementation requires replacing Venus to expose the catalog, stop and report that scope choice. title: Highlight and open plain-text URLs in terminal output
description:
## Decision

Lucca, 2026-10-19: plain-text URLs in terminal output should highlight on hover and open like
explicit links. This covers shell output and agent TUIs such as Claude Code, which print URLs as
plain text in Eon. Today Venus highlights only explicit OSC 8 links. VEN-C5's Boundary says "No
heuristic detection", so this reverses that clause.

Evidence (eon-wt2g, 2026-10-19, edge 5dbd53c, isolated headless Sway): OSC 8 hover, highlight,
target preview, Ctrl+click and Ctrl+Shift+C all work. Plain URLs printed by the shell and by Claude
Code never highlight. Ctrl+click on them opened links only where the program itself handled the
click, with no Venus notice.

## Contract (draft; show Lucca before code; VEN-C5 change)

- Consumer/trigger: a Venus user hovers, or Ctrl+clicks, a URL that appears as plain text in a
  visible terminal row.
- Result: the same presentation and actions as an explicit link: outline, escaped target preview,
  Ctrl+click Open, Ctrl+Shift+C Copy, and the same opening limits (ASCII HTTP/HTTPS, a host, no
  credentials, 4096 bytes). An explicit OSC 8 link on a cell always wins over detection.
- Failures: unchanged from VEN-C5. Frame, geometry, scroll and focus changes retire actions. Nothing
  opens on hover.
- Contract edits: VEN-C5 Boundary and Result, venus/docs/INTERACTION.md ("ordinary URL-looking
  text is not detected"), USAGE/README if they mention it, venus/CHANGELOG.md and CHANGELOG.md.

## Open decisions (recommendations)

1. Owner: Venus Scene derives detected spans from the projected visible cell text, the same place
   it derives OSC 8 spans today. This needs no Orbit or protocol change and is not a second
   emulator (AP-TERMINAL-001: it reads projected text). Alternative: Orbit detects and publishes
   spans, which changes the protocol. Recommend Venus.
2. Scope: http:// and https:// only, matching what the opener accepts. Trim trailing punctuation
   and unbalanced closing brackets. Join soft-wrapped continuation rows so a wrapped URL is one
   target. Recommend this.
3. When to highlight: on plain hover, the same as OSC 8 today. Ghostty-style highlighting only
   while Ctrl is held is the alternative. Recommend plain hover, for consistency with VEN-C5.
4. Accessibility: whether detected links join the AccessKit Open/Copy nodes (possibly many per
   screen). Recommend yes, keeping VEN-C5's per-target pair, after checking the node count cost.
5. Complement, not a replacement: setting FORCE_HYPERLINK=1 for Orbit children would make
   supports-hyperlinks-based programs emit real OSC 8. It covers only those programs and is a
   separate Orbit or Eon decision; record it, do not bundle it.

## Reference gate (consequential: contract change)

Before code, inspect at exact revisions and record in this bead: Ghostty's link detection (default
URL regex, hover and modifier highlight rules, wrapped-row handling) and one other terminal (for
example WezTerm hyperlink_rules or foot url-mode). Note what is adopted and rejected.

## Acceptance

- Scene tests: detection on a plain row, a soft-wrapped URL, trailing punctuation and brackets, an
  OSC 8 cell overriding detection, non-HTTP text ignored, wide cells.
- One isolated installed dogfood observation: hovering a plain URL in shell output highlights it,
  shows its target, and Ctrl+click opens it through the Venus opener (the notice appears).
- Profile refresh.

## Scope boundary

Detection and presentation in Venus only. No file paths, custom schemes, Orbit or EONW change,
URL rewriting, or FORCE_HYPERLINK change.

Portability: neutral (Venus Scene).
close_reason: Plain-text http/https URLs highlight, preview and open under the revised VEN-C5; automated and isolated installed proof recorded; profile refreshed.

comments.author: lucca
comments.text: Decisions (Lucca, 2026-10-21): take eon-nlcy. Detection is scheme-only: http:// and https:// URLs, any host the opener accepts (localhost, 127.0.0.1, [::1] with a scheme already pass validate_open_uri). Bare localhost:PORT and other schemes (file, mailto, ssh) are not detected; bare forms may become a later bead if missed. Recommendations 1 (Venus Scene owns detection), 3 (plain hover), 4 (AccessKit Open/Copy pair per detected target, after a node-count check) and 5 (FORCE_HYPERLINK recorded, not bundled) stand unless Lucca objects. Next: reference gate (Ghostty + one other terminal), then final VEN-C5 wording for approval before code.

comments.author: lucca
comments.text:
Reference gate (2026-10-21, edge 2e4a914). Details: sources read at exact revisions.
- Ghostty a887df42c56f6de86c0fe6da9c4eeca37931e083 (Eon's pin), src/config/url.zig 27-121: one regex, 14 schemes plus paths, Unicode \w body; strips only trailing . and , ; allows one (word)/[word] suffix, no real balancing; matches across soft wraps, stops at hard line ends; no length cap; highlights on hover only while Ctrl/Super held; opens on release without drag; OSC 8 on the clicked cell wins.
- WezTerm 20240203-110809-5046fc22 (5046fc225992db6ba2ef8812743fadfdfe4b184a), config/src/config.rs 1634-1647: \b\w+://\S+[)/a-zA-Z0-9-]+ plus bracketed variants; trailing punctuation dropped by the last-char class; no balancing, and longest-first non-overlapping rule order links "(https://x)" as "https://x)"; logical lines across wraps; plain hover underline; OSC 8 wins per cell and can split a match.
- foot 85655c74a4ded119392ea8b632626c3920042807, config.c 109-148, url-mode.c 319-562: ASCII POSIX regex; one level of balanced () [] "" ''; last char may not be : ? ! , ; . ' ; logical lines from visible rows only; keyboard url-mode, no hover; drops any candidate overlapping an OSC 8 range.
Adopted: hand-written scanner in Venus Scene (no regex crate); http:// or https:// (any case) at line start or after a non-alphanumeric byte; body limited to validate_open_uri's byte set; join soft-wrapped rows, stop at hard row end, blank, non-ASCII, invisible or spacer-breaking cells; repeat-trim trailing . , : ; ! ? ' and a closing ) or ] while it outnumbers its opener; keep only candidates validate_open_uri accepts (one shared validator moves to scene.rs), so a highlight never promises an open that would be refused; drop a candidate touching any OSC 8 cell (foot), explicit link wins.
Rejected: other schemes, www./bare hosts, file paths (Lucca's scheme-only decision); Unicode \w or \S bodies (produce targets the opener refuses); WezTerm's rule ordering; Ctrl-held highlighting (Ghostty) — kept plain hover for consistency with VEN-C5 OSC 8 links per recommendation 3.
Accepted gap: a URL whose start has scrolled above the visible rows is not detected (foot behaves the same).
Check: scene unit tests for each adopted rule, plus one isolated installed hover/Ctrl+click observation.

comments.author: lucca
comments.text: Lucca approved the VEN-C5 wording on 2026-10-21 as proposed: title 'Native hyperlinks'; plain-text http/https detection in Scene, with the trimming, validator-gated and OSC 8-wins rules from the reference gate; plain hover (not Ctrl-held); boundary excludes other schemes, bare hosts, file paths and URLs that start above the visible rows.

comments.author: lucca
comments.text: Decision 4 node-count check (2026-10-21): each visible target segment adds two AccessKit nodes (Open, Copy). The shortest detectable target ('http://a', 8 cells) plus a separator bounds detection to about columns/9 targets per row: about 1,100 targets (2,200 nodes) on a 200x50 grid, and a wrapped target adds one pair per row. OSC 8 already allows one target per cell (10,000 targets, 20,000 nodes on the same grid), so detection does not raise the existing worst case; no cap added. Realistic screens hold a handful of URLs.

comments.author: lucca
comments.text:
Proof (2026-10-21; base edge 2e4a914, committed on top of 3907e33, which changes only .beads). Code tree b1e833bc3bcee864bd9cbae8fe996042d873d074; this commit adds only the VEN-C5 proof text.
- Automated: nix develop -c cargo fmt -p yazelix-venus --check, cargo clippy -p yazelix-venus --locked --all-targets -D warnings, nix develop -c eon-test -p yazelix-venus (104 + 53 + 18 passed, 0 failed); new tests plain_text_links_trim_punctuation_and_unopened_brackets, plain_text_links_join_soft_wrapped_rows_only, explicit_links_and_non_uri_cells_bound_plain_text_links.
- Installed: nix build path:.#default -> /nix/store/kj4lkcww8vdxrfbzyqg1zxnqmcwkvngz-eon-0.1.1, run in an isolated private headless Sway 1.12 (1280x720, pixman, fresh HOME/XDG dirs, Anima off), with a fake gio first on PATH recording dispatches. A shell printed 'dev server: http://localhost:5173/ (ready).', a 150-byte https URL soft-wrapped across two rows, and 'not links: ftp://example.com localhost:3000 xhttps://example.com'. Observed: hovering the localhost URL outlined exactly http://localhost:5173/ (the ' (ready).' trimmed) with the target preview and 'Ctrl+click Open · Ctrl+Shift+C Copy'; the wrapped URL outlined per row with the full target in the preview; bare localhost:3000 and the other non-links showed no outline. Ctrl+click (wtype holding Ctrl in one process, Sway seat cursor press/release) dispatched 'gio open -- http://localhost:5173/', and Ctrl+click on the second row of the wrapped URL dispatched the full URL with the notice 'Link handed to the desktop handler.'. Not exercised installed: Ctrl+Shift+C copy and AT-SPI activation of detected targets (same action path as OSC 8, covered by existing VEN-C5 tests).
- Profile: nix profile upgrade eon; the eon element and $(which eon) resolve to the same /nix/store/kj4lkcww...-eon-0.1.1 that was observed. Running Eon supervisors were not restarted; restart Eon to use it.
- Harness note: wdotool keydown does not hold Ctrl across invocations; wtype -M ctrl -s 2500 -m ctrl plus swaymsg 'seat seat0 cursor press/release button1' does.
Review ledger: round 1 parallel Claude + Codex on tree 4ce35e4c: Claude 2 blocking (decision-4 node-count check unrecorded; CRATES.md still rejected URL discovery) plus nits (line wraps, REFERENCES wording); Codex 1 blocking (quadratic bracket trimming in trim_uri_end). Fixed: linear trim counters, node-count comment, CRATES/REFERENCES/INTERACTION wording, rewrap, CHANGELOG example no longer names Claude Code, INTERACTION notes program-inserted line breaks. Converge round 2 (fresh Claude): clean, no changes. Narrow Codex re-check of 4ce35e4c..b1e833bc: clean. Proof-text re-check below.

title: Build and release the no-helix Nix-free archive beside the full one
description:
Plan: /home/lucca/.cache/eon-agents/eon-no-helix-plan-work/bead/plan.md (sections 3.2, 4.2,
4.6, 5). Decided 2026-11-10 (recorded on eon-igae.17): the no-Helix variant ships on Nix only
in v0.2.0; this archive comes after the release. Not a gate blocker.

## Why

The Nix-free install is README's first install line from v0.2.0 (eon-igae.15). People who use
another editor get the same choice there: a second archive without Helix and its grammars
(measured on 0.1.22: about 195 MB against 225 MB, and 658 MB against 960 MB unpacked).

## Contract

EON-C6 (variant sentence, landed by eon-igae.17.3) and EON-C5's installer lifecycle, which
does not change. EON-C5 names no archive. The archive names are in `docs/INSTALLER.md` and
`docs/MANUAL-BUNDLE.md`.

## Scope

- `nix/bundle-relink.nix` and `nix/linux-bundle.nix` take the package, its name and its
  fallbacks, so the flake builds two bundles from one recipe. The variant has no Helix runtime
  fallback, and its launch check skips `hx --health bash` (`bundle-relink.nix:238`) and
  asserts instead that `hx` is not found.
- Archive `eon-no-helix-VERSION-x86_64-linux.tar.zst`, root directory of the same name, with
  its own `provenance.json` (`package` names the variant) and the receipt's `attribute` null
  as for the full archive.
- `nix/release.nix`: both archives, the installer and one `SHA256SUMS` over all three.
  `.github/workflows/release.yml` already attests every file in `release/`; confirm the asset
  list and the timeout.
- Installer (`installer/src/main.rs:355-373, 479-483`): accept the variant's archive name and
  derive the expected version (`VERSION`, not `no-helix-VERSION`) for the `eon versions` smoke
  check. Tests for both names and for a malformed variant segment.
- Third-party notices (eon-igae.15.6's generator): one inventory per archive; the variant's
  has no Helix or grammar entries.
- Docs: `docs/INSTALLER.md` and `docs/MANUAL-BUNDLE.md` (asset names, the second install
  line), README, CHANGELOG. The site's install text follows in the release that ships it.
- Record the measured archive and unpacked sizes of both archives from the real build.

## Acceptance

- `nix build .#release` (through heavy.sh) yields both archives, the installer and
  `SHA256SUMS`; the variant archive holds no Helix or grammar path.
- The bundle checks pass for both bundles.
- An isolated install of the variant archive with the built installer into a private prefix:
  `eon versions` passes the smoke check and prints no Helix line, `hx` is absent, and
  `eon edit` runs the editor that `EDITOR` names.
- Whole-workspace `nix develop -c eon-test`.

## Out of scope

Publishing and signing a release, macOS bundles, and the direct updater (eon-no-helix-direct-update-elg9r, a prerequisite).

## Prerequisites

eon-igae.9 (v0.2.0 is cut), eon-igae.17.3 (the package), and eon-no-helix-direct-update-elg9r, so
an installed variant can update.

title: Keep the direct updater on the installed no-helix archive
description:

Decided 2026-11-10 (recorded on eon-igae.17): the no-Helix variant ships on Nix only in v0.2.0;
its Nix-free archive and this bead come after the release. Not a gate blocker.

## Why

The direct updater looks for exactly `eon-<n>-x86_64-linux.tar.zst` on a release
(`eon/crates/eon/src/update/direct.rs:653`, and `archive_version` at `:47-54`). Once a
no-Helix archive exists, a person who installed it must be offered only that archive, never
the full one.

## Contract

EON-C41, the approved text in plan section 5 for Installer-owned Linux: "the x86_64 Linux
asset of the installed variant (`eon-VERSION-x86_64-linux.tar.zst` or
`eon-no-helix-VERSION-x86_64-linux.tar.zst`, as the installed `.eon-source` URL names it)".
A trust-boundary change: record the reference gate first.

## Scope

- The variant is read from the installed `.eon-source` URL's archive name. Discovery requires
  the same variant's archive with `SHA256SUMS` and `SHA256SUMS.sig` on the latest eligible
  release, at the exact download URL. A latest release without that variant's archive gives
  the existing no-candidate result; never fall back to the other variant.
- Tests beside the existing direct-update tests: a `no-helix` prefix install finds only its
  own archive; a release with only the full archive offers nothing to it; a full install is
  never offered the `no-helix` archive.
- Docs and CHANGELOG as the change requires.

## Acceptance

The tests above; whole-workspace `nix develop -c eon-test`; fmt and clippy for the changed
crate. The fresh-host update proof stays with the bead that proves the published install.

## Out of scope

The installer's archive-name parsing and building the archive (the no-Helix archive bead),
and switching variants from `eon update`.

## Prerequisites

eon-igae.9 (v0.2.0 is cut) and eon-igae.17.4 (the Nix half of this work).

title: Investigate how much of Eon's commit and bead volume is process bookkeeping
description:
## Why

Lucca, 2026-10-30, after a project opinion pass: "create one bead to investigate each of those".
The finding: process bookkeeping may be crowding out product work. At edge 39e0a25 the history has
560 commits and the tracker 973 beads, with the oldest commit dated 2026-10-14. Of the 229 commits
since 2026-10-23, 101 subjects match a rough bookkeeping regex. Each such commit costs agent
context, review time and landing coordination.

## Evidence

- `git log --oneline | wc -l` → 560; `git log --format=%ad --date=short | tail -1` → 2026-10-14
  (history may predate this repository through imports; check).
- `git log --since=2026-10-23 --format=%s | grep -ciE 'record|proof|file |bead|defer|contract|doc'`
  → 101 of 229. The regex is crude: it also matches real doc and contract work.
- `bv --robot-triage`: 973 issues, 167 open, 7 in progress.
- AGENTS.md "Proof and Review" ("One commit per change"): proof is recorded in the owning bead
  within the change's commit, and follow-up commits that only name the source commit are forbidden.

## Scope

In scope (read-only investigation; report to Lucca):
- Classify the last ~2 weeks of commits as product code, tests, contract/docs, bead or proof
  records, or defer/file-only, using diffs (files touched), not only subjects.
- For bead/proof-only commits, find which rule or habit produced each (AGENTS.md section,
  AGENT-PROTOCOLS ID, overseer practice, or skill).
- Measure bead churn: beads created vs closed per day, and the share closed as deferred,
  duplicate or superseded.
- Propose 1–3 changes that cut bookkeeping without losing proof or decisions (for example,
  batching record-only commits, filing fewer speculative beads), each with expected savings.

Out of scope:
- Editing AGENTS.md, `.agent-protocols.local.md`, skills, or any bead other than this one.
- Closing, merging or reprioritizing existing beads.
- Review-policy cost and contract granularity (sibling beads filed the same day).

## Acceptance

- A comment on this bead with the classification table (counts and shares per class, with the
  commit range used), the rule or habit behind each bookkeeping class, and the proposals.
- Each proposal names the rule it would change and is marked as needing Lucca's approval.

## Verification

- The table's totals equal `git rev-list --count <range>` for the stated range.
- Every proposal cites the AGENTS.md or AGENT-PROTOCOLS section it touches.

## Stop Conditions

- Stop if the classification needs a judgment call that changes the conclusion; report both
  readings.
- Stop before any rule edit: rule changes are Lucca's to approve.

## Maintenance Notes

- Delegate the commit sweep to a subagent; keep only the table and conclusions in the main session.

title: Improve Nova Helix default settings
description:
## Owner changed (Lucca, 2026-11-12: "nah, i want it in nova-helix")

The defaults ship in nova-helix itself, so standalone nova-helix and Nova get them too: nova-helix embeds one default config file (include_str!) as its lowest layer, beneath the user and trusted-workspace configs. No edits to the defaults in editor.rs and no theme.rs patch: theme = "carbonfox" is in that file. Eon needs no config file or variable of its own unless the implementer gives a reason; if a HELIX_DEFAULT_CONFIG layer exists, it stays and the embedded file is the default when it is unset. Settings: Lucca's 2026-11-02 choices (soft wrap, bufferline multiple) plus question 3 (cursorline, color-modes, insert bar cursor, indent guides) and question 4 (carbonfox), plus [editor.auto-save] focus-lost = true with no timer only if focus-out is verified to reach Helix in a pane and in the Editor popup. Eon then bumps its nova-helix pin. The earlier Eon-owned file route below is superseded; the text is kept for history.

## Goal and contract
Improve the default Nova Helix editing experience shipped with Eon. With no personal Helix configuration, a fresh editor should have a small, coherent set of useful defaults for readability, navigation and editing feedback. Explicit user settings remain authoritative; preserve existing configuration files, normal Helix keybindings, workspace-trust boundaries and save safety.

The original broad defaults investigation is now constrained by Lucca’s 2026-11-02 and 2026-11-12 approvals below. Record selected before/after behavior and rationale; do not label subjective preferences as confirmed bugs.

## Current evidence
- Eon `components/eon-v5.json:269-274` and `flake.nix:24` pin `Yazelix/nova-helix` at `6ee75ad3b7b2f2ed82daae0f9bf1663c168f48ea` (dcaef1c).
- Eon `flake.nix:687` defines `helixPackage` from `yazelix_helix`, with Steel disabled; `EON_HX` points directly to that package. It does not consume Nova's managed Helix configuration.
- Nova Helix `helix-term/src/config.rs` owns configuration loading, default keymaps and user/workspace layering. `helix-view/src/editor.rs:1190` owns editor defaults; the inspected baseline disables cursorline, color modes and soft wrap. These are review candidates, not agreed replacements.
- Nova `defaults/helix/config.toml` is a useful comparison for theme, buffer visibility, cursor shapes, diagnostics, indent guides, wrapping and statusline. It also contains Nova-specific reveal commands, paths and remappings that must not be copied into Eon or standalone Helix.
- Nova Helix has no local Beads tracker; this issue lives in Eon's backlog. Existing Eon native-editor/keybinding research is deferred and is not a prerequisite.

## Scope and ownership
Review the actual zero-config packaged experience and a few representative editing tasks. Prefer existing configuration/package facilities over Rust changes. Keep generic editor behavior at Nova Helix and Eon-specific selection/composition at Eon; record the chosen owner before editing. Do not change Nova's managed-session policy, add plugins or language-server bundles, redesign keymaps, or begin the deferred native editor.

## Reference gate and prerequisites
Read current owner instructions, configuration documentation, loading code and relevant references; compare upstream Helix and Nova's managed defaults. Record exact inspected revisions, selected defaults, rejected candidates and override precedence. Coordinate sequentially with eon-xodrj.4 (closed) and .5 (open), as Lucca’s approval comment requires; recheck the fork revision before composing it. If a child revision changes, publish and verify that child before composing its exact accepted revision into Eon.

## Acceptance and verification
- Record a short justified defaults set and demonstrate its effect in a fresh packaged editor with an isolated empty config home.
- Exercise a representative file, multiple buffers and diagnostics where applicable; verify usability in a narrow pane and the Eon terminal. Check effects rather than merely asserting configured literals.
- An explicit user override still wins, existing user files are unchanged, and ordinary edit/save/reopen behavior remains safe.
- Build the affected package; for Eon composition use `nix build .#eon --no-link`. If native Helix code changes, run `cargo fmt --all -- --check`, `cargo check -p helix-term`, and focused owner tests.
- Align affected documentation/changelog and verify the installed artifact after refreshing Eon's active Nix profile. Use an isolated fresh workspace and preserve running terminals and desktop focus.

## Stop boundary
Stop at a useful settings pass. Additional editor capabilities, dependencies, compatibility promises or a broad fork refactor require separate scope.

## Approved plan and pending Lucca choices

Lucca, 2026-11-12: “all's fine, but 3 and 4 i must evaluate” (comment 6531). The approved recommendation is the generic fork-level HELIX_DEFAULT_CONFIG layer beneath the user's configuration; Eon owns the shipped file and sets the variable only for Eon-launched Helix. Preserve trusted workspace configuration even with no user file. Document $(eon config-dir)/helix/config.toml; reading the host Helix config remains separate. Use a separate fork worktree, publish/verify its accepted revision before Eon's exact pin bump. The terminfo Smulx/Setulc work is separate Orbit scope, not undercurl=true here.

Soft wrap enabled and bufferline="multiple" were already chosen on 2026-11-02. Cursorline, color-modes, insert bar cursor and indent guides (plan question 3) still await Lucca's evaluation. Theme selection (question 4) still requires coverage-based top-two-or-three captures and Lucca’s choice. Do not promote those recommendations to approved defaults or claim this bead complete without that choice. Plan: /home/lucca/.cache/eon-agents/eon-8zqa/plan.md; its 2026-11-03 code references are historical and need rechecking against the pin above.

title: Enable native Nushell clipboard commands in Eon
description:
## Contract and outcome

Extend EON-C9 for Eon-managed Nushell. A user in a new default Eon Session or running eon-nu can pipe a value to clip copy or clc, and read the native clipboard with clip paste or clp. The aliases expand to the native Nushell commands. When clipboard access is unavailable, Nushell reports its own failure; Eon does not claim a remote or headless clipboard bridge.

## Prerequisites and reference gate

Preserve the accepted EON-C9 native configuration and user-autoload order, the exact Nushell 0.113.1 manifest identity, and the current Orbit and Venus pins. The pinned Nushell source at 7b7df4aa has native clip behind the opt-in native-clip experimental flag: without the flag the installed eon-nu cannot find clip, and with it both help commands resolve. Nova at 6fceb4e uses that flag in runtime/yzx-nu.rs, defines clc and clp in defaults/nu/config.nu, and checks their expansions in flake.nix. Before editing, inspect those exact sources, Eon managed_environment.rs and nuVendorAutoload in flake.nix, and Nushell clipboard and alias precedence semantics.

## Ownership and scope

Eon owns the managed Nushell opt-in and default aliases; Nushell owns native clipboard behavior and errors. Reuse the existing managed launcher and startup layer. Keep user files and global environment unchanged, preserve user startup precedence, and leave Bash, Zsh, Fish, arbitrary shell commands, Orbit, and Venus alone. Add no clipboard dependency, EONW or OSC52 bridge, compatibility layer with Nova, or claim of macOS, remote, or headless clipboard support from Linux proof.

## Acceptance

From the built and installed eon-nu, both native help commands resolve and clc/clp expand to clip copy/clip paste. In one isolated native Wayland Eon Session, copy then paste a known value through the full commands and aliases. Verify user startup precedence and that a missing clipboard surfaces a native failure. Update EON-C9 current-state docs, configuration help, changelog, and README LOC. Run the affected package and shell checks, refresh the active eon profile from the accepted tree without restarting live Sessions, and record the exact artifact and installed observation.

title: Confirm the mac-proof check-evaluation flake is gone under nextest
description:
## Historical failure and current plan

Before nextest, mac-proof run::tests::failed_combined_evaluation_keeps_the_shared_build failed with default parallel libtest threads and passed alone or with RUST_TEST_THREADS=1. The 2026-11-09 comments retain sightings, attempted reproductions and the unproved shared-state/ETXTBSY hypotheses; neither hypothesis is a confirmed cause.

Since 985822b, eon-test runs tests in separate nextest processes; RUST_TEST_THREADS is not a workaround for this route. The 2026-11-10 accepted plan is to improve the missing-step diagnostic and gather 20 subsequent whole-workspace eon-test passes from normal landing logs. Do not commission 20 redundant full-suite runs just to collect this evidence.

## Remaining scope and acceptance

- eon/tools/mac-proof/src/run.rs:1004 still uses find(...).unwrap() in failed_shared_inputs_skip_only_the_checks_that_need_them. Make a missing step report the available calls and step logs, preserving assertions. Existing status-assertion diagnostics are already landed.
- Tally 20 whole-workspace nextest eon-test runs after 985822b, with revision/environment/log references, and no failure of either test. Historical pre-nextest runs do not satisfy that observation.
- A nextest failure is not evidence of two tests racing in one process. Read the newly printed step logs before proposing a root-cause fix. Keep this bead open until its evidence supports completion; never infer the tally from the number of commits.

## Boundary and verification

No production changes, timeout widening or retries. Use the existing mac-proof harness for a diagnostic change and the repository's current code/test review requirements; reuse unchanged accepted landing proof for the observation tally. Root-cause repair requires captured evidence; stop rather than guessing. No tests were run by this planning pass.
acceptance_criteria: 1. Make the step lookup in the sibling test (eon/tools/mac-proof/src/run.rs, the find(...).unwrap() near :1004) print the evidence logs when the step is missing. 2. Close once 20 whole-workspace eon-test runs after 985822b (nextest; landing logs count) show no failure of either test. A failure under nextest means the cause is not an in-process race: read the printed step logs before changing anything.

# eon-o5tyo — per-package workspace source

READY FOR REVIEW `d6c57607bba334f990745c2d16c524ab29155521`
BASE `1d9350df14ec3f190279667aaf41707190780aa2` (Eon 0.1.22, EONW v38).

Both measured Eon-edit builds improve: **36.87–40.65% less wall time**, with
**38.75% less aggregate wall time and 65.91% less builder CPU** across two
alternating pairs. Mean wall is **395.415 → 242.181 s**, saving 153.234 s per
sample. This is a warm-cache source-edit workload on a shared Linux host,
max-jobs=2/cores=6, not a fixed speed guarantee.

## Change and cache identity

Only flake.nix and docs/DEVELOPMENT.md change. Linux Orbit, Venus, bench and
mac-proof receive their own real crates and transitive path dependencies,
with pinned crane stand-ins for the other workspace members. Original root
Cargo.toml/Cargo.lock remain. The helper rejects omitted normal/build/dev/
target/inherited/transitive path dependencies at evaluation and asserts the
generated name `source`, preserving /build/source paths. It removes only
unselected members nested within selected roots, retaining selected protocol
children beneath unused parent crates. DEVELOPMENT describes these boundaries.

Eon retains full workspaceSource: its generation digest consumes the whole
source set. Bench's wrapper still depends on eonbase/Orbit. mac-proof remains
plain buildRustPackage and does not prime the compiled graphics cache. Darwin
returns its original crateSource and uses its original build path. Build,
test, install, feature, version, manifest, lockfile and toolchain policy stay
unchanged. No new dependency, contract or runtime default; no changelog entry.

The acceptance invariant is equality to the baseline cache at the selected
base. It also remains exactly the pre-bead cache:

- drv: `/nix/store/lj96vgfnl2hmcnwmcxg0jpg9wq18qbns-eon-workspace-deps-0.drv`
- out: `/nix/store/c693fm3zib28dbkx2zwc6lvkfxxm2qzc-eon-workspace-deps-0`

The existing overseer crane-deps root still targets that output at report time.
No cache recipe change or re-prime is needed. All later-needed builds have
explicit --out-link roots; no garbage collection ran.

## Every measured run

Order: baseline, candidate, baseline, candidate. Each pair appends the same
one-line comment to eon/crates/eon/src/main.rs; pair 2 uses a distinct comment.
Matching main.rs and Cargo.lock SHA-256 values are asserted per pair. All four
Eon/default derivations are fresh, with the same warm dependency cache.

Commands are `nix build path:<immutable snapshot>#default --max-jobs 2 --cores 6
-L --json --out-link <per-run root>`, through ordinary heavy.sh slots. Each
snapshot is retained. CPU-only proof variants append builder Bash times;
their compiled sources equal the corresponding uninstrumented inputs. Eon's
source is explicitly bound to that uninstrumented source, so instrumentation
does not alter its assembly digest. Candidate Orbit/Venus have **exact original
production drvs**, warmed once; candidate CPU logging affects only Eon.

Queue time and snapshot preparation are excluded. Nix client evaluation/build
time is included. CPU sums the Rust builders' shell/child user+system times,
not client/daemon CPU. Baseline has three reports, candidate one. Each consumer
compiles only workspace crates: baseline Orbit3 + Venus4 + Eon7 = 14;
candidate Eon7 = 7; no external recompilation. Original release checks run.

The granted turn began after the other agent's quiet window; first measured
builder started 15:41:41Z, after 15:35Z. Load is sampled every 10 s inside the
heavy slot. Start/end are Linux load averages (1/5/15 min); all samples remain
raw. These are ordinary shared-host slots, not quiet measurements.

| Pair/mode | Wall s | Builder CPU s | Compile lines | Load start | Load end | Mean load1 |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---|---|---:|
| 1 baseline | 393.324 | 1205.664 | 14 | 0.56/1.49/2.61 | 2.73/3.15/3.15 | 3.960 |
| 1 candidate | 233.419 | 414.558 | 7 | 1.52/2.75/3.02 | 2.34/2.82/3.02 | 2.836 |
| 2 baseline | 397.505 | 1319.806 | 14 | 2.32/2.81/3.01 | 2.67/4.61/4.00 | 5.969 |
| 2 candidate | 250.942 | 446.485 | 7 | 2.70/4.58/4.00 | 3.76/4.63/4.20 | 4.603 |

| Pair | Wall delta s | Wall reduction | CPU delta s | CPU reduction |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| 1 | −159.905 | 40.65% | −791.106 | 65.62% |
| 2 | −146.563 | 36.87% | −873.321 | 66.17% |

Aggregate wall 790.829 → 484.361 s; builder CPU 2525.470 → 861.043 s. Baseline
spread is 4.181 s; both deltas have the same sign and both savings exceed that
spread, so the approved third-pair trigger is false. No third pair ran. Load
varies and includes the workload itself; no claim of isolated host-wide CPU
efficiency or a universal percentage. The decisive evidence is the unchanged
Orbit/Venus drvs and absence of their builders after an Eon edit.

All four receipts match their own `eon versions` build, each binary contains
its independently calculated source digest, and component/version reports and
configuration defaults match across each pair. Raw records:
`../r3/timing-fixtures.json`, `timing-results.json`, `timing-deltas.json`, and
`logs/wall-{1,2}-{baseline,candidate}.{json,log,events.jsonl,load.json}`.
TIMING DONE was recorded 16:03:48Z, before the post-timing suite.

## Rebuild matrix

R = whole derivation changes, — = identical. Normal comment edits use existing
source files; the new Eon file is not an implicit Cargo target. Full matrix,
source/derivation maps and every exported Linux/Darwin package are in
../r2/final-rebuild-matrix.json (20 baseline/candidate rows). The source-filter
implementation and Cargo/Nix inputs are unchanged at the selected base.

| Edit | Orbit | Venus | Eon | bench | mac-proof | deps cache |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| Eon main | — | — | R | R | — | — |
| runtime implementation | — | — | R | R | — | — |
| EONW protocol | — | R | R | R | — | — |
| Venus main | — | R | R | R | — | — |
| Orbit host | R | — | R | R | — | — |
| Orbit protocol | R | R | R | R | R | — |
| governance source | — | — | R | R | — | — |
| new non-target Eon file | — | — | R | R | — | — |
| excluded governance Cargo feature | R | R | R | R | R | R |
| flake.nix comment | — | — | R | R | — | — |

Bench's compilation source changes only for its own files/protocol, but its
wrapper dependency makes the whole package follow eonbase/Orbit. Default,
eonbase, manual-bundle and release follow Eon's digest; installer and Helix
retain identical drvs. Excluded dependency-relevant manifest changes that
survive crane cleanup, lock changes and target-structure changes remain a
known cache/source invalidation limit. No claim that all Cargo.toml text edits
invalidate the cache.

At the selected base, an actual Eon edit plus re-evaluation and realized
`nix path-info --derivation` retains Orbit hj6sgr5sqg0y3ahpq1p3rcl4fs4580qw,
Venus cxvqxdr9llnw6a02wyayxgpf651jylfv and deps lj96vgfnl2hmcnwmcxg0jpg9wq18qbns.
Eon's drv changes. Current sources are checked file-for-file, with every other
workspace member a stand-in. Records: ../r3/source-regression-green.json and
final-path-info-proof.json. Every probe byte/index entry is restored.

## Artifact and final-tree proof

Full package/artifact/bundle proof ran on corrected tree
83c978340fff8164693a10a44617a339c2bc78f8, base 01573431ed11ba7c60016cfab5d9d7b01102b1a6:
all workspace package outputs, default/eonbase, changed manual-bundle/release,
64 explicit Nix checks plus two covered aliases (66 total; only unchanged
Helix grammars omitted). Strict Orbit host/worker/tests/terminfo/licenses,
Venus, bench and mac-proof bytes and normalized wrappers/file sets match.
Identical-source Eon raw bytes match SHA-256
fb41a6d56d8cef621c836f133b4024030d6aa815729b55e01da3661a1c7941b7.
Actual recipe changes intentionally change Eon's source digest, Eon/eonbase
binary and source receipt; independent digest/default/component/receipt checks
isolate and verify that input difference. No arbitrary ELF normalization.

Every one of 8,895 extracted bundle members matches after verified known
package paths/generation inputs. Static launchers match their own built bytes
and equivalent normalized table inputs; Eon code sections match its own
verified package; desktop bytes match their own packaged desktop file before
only known paths are normalized. Release checksums validate, archives equal
their corresponding manual bundle, and installers match unchanged bytes.
Reports/logs: ../r2/final-equivalence.json, final-bundle-equivalence.json,
logs/final-production-build.*, logs/bundle-proof-attempt2.log.

The overseer selected one rebase to 1d9350d and explicitly authorized retaining
Nix equivalence after unrelated Rust-only changes, with merged-tree landing
proof later. The flake blob is identical to 83c9783, upstream Cargo/Nix inputs
are unchanged, and all actual current real files are checked. This reuse is
explicit in ../r3/base-proof.json and selected-validation.json, not a claim
that every old artifact was rebuilt on the new Rust base. Selected-base
Orbit/Venus/worker/tests/wrapper bytes were additionally rechecked against
that base, and all four current default timing artifacts validate their own
receipts/defaults/components. mac-proof keeps its exact corrected-tree drv.

On final staged tree d6c57607, all-systems evaluation passes. The isolated full
workspace/installer suite passed twice: 570.617 s initially, 183.081 s after
timing as explicitly ordered by the 15:01:15Z INBOX. Both runs: 1,198 workspace
tests passed (69 skipped), 11 installer tests passed, zero failures; supported
doctest step retained. Commands use heavy.sh and `CARGO_TARGET_DIR=<r3>/target
nix develop -c eon-test`, without package filters. Exact commands/logs:
r3/logs/{selected,post-timing}-workspace-suite.{json,log}. No source probes ran
concurrently with either suite. Rust fmt passed before rebase; no Rust crate
changed in this diff, so no new crate clippy run is claimed. The overseer owns
fresh merged-tree clippy/suite/default proof. Final diff/check/index remain
on the exact staged tree; only flake.nix and DEVELOPMENT.md are changed.

## Cost, limits and review handoff

The first landing changes Orbit, Venus, bench and mac-proof derivations once,
so each may rebuild even without a consumer source edit. That migration cost
is excluded from steady-state pairs: corrected functional default/bench/
mac-proof/bundle/check batch took 534.020 s on a partly warmed shared host;
selected-base Venus warmup took 157.754 s (Orbit was already realized).
These are contextual setup observations, not a clean cold-install estimate.
The existing compiled dependency cache is reused throughout.

Native Darwin builds/runtime and CI-host timings are unproved; Darwin source
and build arguments remain original by evaluation. Two ordinary shared-host
pairs bound this workload; archive metadata/generation differences are
explicit, and later dependency/target changes still invalidate the cache.
The source-list assertions force future path-dependency additions to update
their real-source lists.

Plan review: Fable, all six findings adopted. Fresh implementation Claude/Codex
reviews are pending the overseer; the author ran no reviews. Recovery stash
4e174011b0570d99b1bc122cc51ef5cc5d2c201f and patch are retained. No author landing
commit, branch, push, br write, profile activation or supervisor operation.

Failures are retained in 01–04 and all original logs: read-only dummy overlay;
selected child removed with unused parent (fixed in shared helper, red/green
source proof before Rust); archive comparator omitted desktop path mapping
(fixed by verifying own bytes); deferred-output graph extraction; record patch
context mismatch; dynamic restore-wrapper dcg rejection (safe scoped stash
used). No unresolved failure. The report is ready for the overseer's reviews
and landing; no follow-up bead is worked in this session.

title: Decide whether Eon earns a durable native semantic editor
description:
## Contract Routing

This is the product decision gate for a possible Eon-native durable semantic editor engine. It changes no product contract and authorizes no implementation, dependency, repository, protocol, or Helix removal. EON-C4 currently preserves Helix as the sole owner of editing, language integration, and editor state. A positive decision requires explicit user approval, an updated ownership architecture, and new or revised indexed EON and owner-repository contracts before code.

User constraint recorded 2026-08-12: if Eon adopts its own editor engine, it must provide Helix-like modal editing and preserve most Helix default keybindings regardless of whether it reuses `helix-core`. `eon-specify-helix-modal-semantics-3kl` and `eon-preserve-helix-keybindings-uca` make that requirement falsifiable.

## Why

A native editor is justified only if it unlocks a user-visible contract that opaque terminal-hosted Helix cannot supply: authoritative addressable documents and revisions, durable unsaved editor state, transient Venus attachment, semantic native presentation, and explicit human/agent edit-conflict boundaries. Native appearance, fewer visible processes, code ownership preference, or the existence of reusable Helix crates are insufficient.

The important question is not “Can Eon render text?” It is whether Eon can earn the permanent editor-feature, language-support, compatibility, security, durability, and maintenance burden while remaining more valuable than Helix running inside an Orbit Session.

## Current Evidence

Repository evidence:

- `docs/ARCHITECTURE.md:16` assigns editing, language integration, and editor state to Helix; `docs/ARCHITECTURE.md:69` forbids Eon from implementing editor behavior under the accepted architecture.
- `docs/CONTRACTS.md:18` proves EON-C4's no-duplicate-child-state boundary. `README.md:249` exposes managed Helix as `eon-hx`.
- Orbit already proves a real PTY plus authoritative terminal state and complete structured attachment revisions; this does not expose Helix documents, selections, undo, diagnostics, or semantic commands.
- Venus already consumes host-authored snapshots while remaining transient. A future editor projection must preserve that ownership lesson without reusing the terminal grid as an editor schema.

Exact Helix evidence:

- Official Helix `079a789e8cb08ead67f19e1971a1b7438b37354b` (2026-07-23), MPL-2.0.
- `docs/architecture.md` describes `helix-core` as functional Rope, Selection, Transaction, and Syntax primitives, but says `helix-view` is currently tied to the terminal UI.
- `helix-term/src/keymap/default.rs` owns the default Normal, Select, and Insert tries. `helix-term/src/commands.rs` is 7,228 lines and owns substantial mappable-command behavior. Reusing `helix-core` alone therefore does not preserve Helix modal behavior or keybindings.
- `helix-core` is a credible candidate mechanism; `helix-view` and `helix-term` are not an accepted native-frontend seam at this revision.
- Recheck upstream issue #5555, issue #312, and PR #13468 at decision time for an accepted command/view/client split; their observed open work is discovery, not a supported contract.

External architecture evidence:

- CodeMirror 6 System Guide, https://codemirror.net/docs/guide/: accept immutable state and transaction lessons; reject its browser and extension architecture as an Eon requirement.
- Neovim UI protocol, https://neovim.io/doc/user/api-ui-events/: external clients are viable, but its terminal-like grid and multigrid model are a semantic ceiling Eon should not copy for a native editor.
- Kakoune client/server design, https://kakoune.org/why-kakoune/why-kakoune.html: session-owned editing with attachable clients is useful precedent; reject multiplayer and shell-extension scope by default.
- Xi retrospective, https://raphlinus.github.io/xi/2020/06/27/xi-retrospective.html: process-separated frontend/core RPC, pervasive async, CRDTs, and plugin processes consumed excessive novelty and coordination cost. Eon needs a process boundary only when dirty-buffer survival or attachment demonstrably requires it.
- Zed CRDT architecture and DeltaDB, https://zed.dev/blog/crdts and https://zed.dev/blog/introducing-deltadb/: fine-grained concurrent edit and conversation lineage are not unique Eon differentiators. Reject CRDTs and concurrent writers until a real multiplayer requirement exists.
- Agent Client Protocol at pinned Eon reference `9ef3e3800b4070632b54846b5ddf310fc4b35b03`: structured agent communication is preferable to ANSI scraping, but provider sessions remain adapter-owned and distinct from editor documents and Eon work.

## Smallest Observable Decision

Consumer: one local Eon user, with Venus as a transient native client.

Trigger: the user opens or reattaches to one editor surface after the native client was absent.

Candidate result if replacement is earned: one authoritative editor owner supplies a coherent complete semantic document/view snapshot at revision N followed by ordered revisions; accepts semantic modal commands against explicit base revisions; preserves approved Helix-like behavior and keybindings; retains bounded dirty document, selection, and undo state across Venus loss; saves safely; and reports stale edits, external file conflicts, engine loss, incompatible clients, and corrupt recovery state explicitly.

Non-result: this does not promise exact process survival, remote access, cloud sync, multiplayer, CRDT convergence, a plugin system, Helix configuration compatibility, machine-restart recovery, a standalone application, or a supported third-party client. Eon-wide reboot and machine-loss policy remains `eon-decide-eon-session-durability-qhf`.

## Candidate Shapes

1. Keep Helix as an opaque Orbit-hosted child. This remains the default and wins unless dogfood demonstrates a replacement-only contract.
2. Consume a supported upstream Helix semantic or native-client boundary if one exists at decision time. Do not build against an open PR or private fork contract.
3. Reuse selected Helix crates, especially `helix-core`, behind an Eon editor owner while implementing modal command, lifecycle, language, attachment, and Venus projection layers. Apply the dependency and MPL-2.0 license gates to exact files and artifacts.
4. Implement the minimum accepted editor primitives independently, using Helix behavior as a reference corpus. Estimate parity and maintenance honestly.

A full Helix fork, terminal-screen scraping, Neovim-style grid protocol, `helix-view` extraction by assumption, CRDT-first engine, plugin system, cloud service, or distributed process mesh is rejected unless evidence overturns the smaller candidates.

## Ownership Constraints

- The editor engine owns canonical document text, revisions, selections, modal state, transactions, undo, syntax, language integration, safe save, external-change conflicts, and bounded editor recovery state.
- Venus owns native text shaping, drawing, IME, accessibility, pointer input, focus, and ephemeral geometry. It consumes semantic editor projections and never reconstructs document authority from cells or pixels.
- Eon owns workspace topology, product policy, component selection, and references to editor surfaces; it does not implement editing mechanics.
- Orbit retains PTY, process, terminal, history, and terminal-input authority and owns no editor state.
- Provider adapters own provider sessions. Future agents may submit base-revision proposals, but direct agent mutation, isolated worktrees, context manifests, and run provenance remain separately routed through `eon-pxn` and `eon-az9` rather than being prerequisites for the first editor proof.
- Logical ownership does not imply one process per component. Prefer the fewest process and protocol boundaries; require lifecycle evidence before separating the editor engine from the long-lived local workspace host.
- Nice-to-have portability: keep the editor core free of Eon, Orbit, and Venus product types when that does not enlarge the first proof. Eon integration should enter through a narrow adapter, and Venus should be an initial client rather than an engine dependency. This prefers future embedding or a standalone client without promising or building either.

## Prerequisites

- The accepted Helix-based Eon composition remains dogfoodable and supplies concrete limitations caused by the terminal/editor boundary.
- `eon-specify-helix-modal-semantics-3kl` selects the required semantic behavior.
- `eon-preserve-helix-keybindings-uca` selects the binding coverage and workspace-shortcut collision policy.
- The user explicitly activates this decision; deferred status does not make it the active implementation frontier.

## Decision Work

1. Record exact terminal-bound limitations from dogfood and distinguish replacement-only needs from configuration, structured run records, agent worktrees, native review surfaces, or an upstream integration.
2. Reinspect exact current Helix source, relevant upstream client/server work, license, and release/API stability.
3. Compare the four candidate shapes on contract fit, owned and reused LOC, direct/transitive dependencies, language/tooling parity, keybinding and modal fidelity, security, durability, Linux/native-Wayland behavior, upgrade burden, upstream drift, and removal cost.
4. Produce before-and-after owner and data-flow maps. Select one canonical document owner and the minimum semantic projection; do not create a universal UI or action protocol.
5. Define the smallest falsifiable proof: one document, one client, open/edit/save, approved modal corpus, semantic detach/reattach, bounded dirty-state recovery, stale revision rejection, external-change conflict, and Venus-native input/presentation.
6. Decide whether process separation is necessary. If not, keep the editor owner in the smallest long-lived host; if yes, define start, attach, crash, restart, incompatibility, shutdown, cleanup, queue, and persistence semantics.
7. Obtain an explicit user decision: keep Helix, defer, integrate upstream, reuse selected Helix crates, or authorize an independent engine. Do not implement in this Bead.

## Acceptance

- Exact dogfood evidence identifies at least one valuable contract that requires editor authority, or the decision keeps Helix.
- The keep, upstream integration, selected-crate reuse, and independent-engine shapes are compared at exact revisions with license, dependency, LOC, parity, portability, security, lifecycle, and reversal costs.
- Modal semantics and keybinding continuity decisions are complete and included in every positive cost estimate; reuse of `helix-core` is never treated as automatic behavioral compatibility.
- One owner map covers document text, revisions, selections, modal state, undo, syntax, language services, saves, external changes, workspace references, native projection, terminal state, and provider sessions without duplicate authority.
- The native boundary is semantic, begins with a coherent complete snapshot followed by ordered revisions, and rejects stale or incompatible actions. It is not a terminal grid, raw byte stream, or second handwritten owner schema.
- Persistence is bounded and failure-domain specific. Venus loss may retain dirty editor state; machine restart, cloud sync, remote compute, terminal scrollback, credentials, raw environment, and arbitrary process state remain separate decisions.
- The first proof is one cohesive vertical slice and does not require plugins, CRDTs, multiplayer, remote access, generalized configuration, all Helix UI features, or agent integration.
- The option comparison reports whether the engine core can compile, test, and own documents without importing Eon, Orbit, or Venus product policy. Prefer that direction when it is no larger; record a coupling tradeoff if not. This nice-to-have does not block the Eon-first proof or create a standalone distribution commitment.
- The result records meaningful rejected alternatives, negative evidence, the cheapest proof, the future code-owning repository or explicit owner-selection gate, and an explicit user decision.
- Closure creates no implementation, repository, dependency, protocol, product contract, or Helix removal by itself.

## Verification

- `git -C /home/lucca/pjs/yazelix-dir/helix rev-parse HEAD` must report the inspected revision, or the decision must record and justify a newly inspected exact revision.
- `rg -n "Helix|editor|EON-C4" docs/ARCHITECTURE.md docs/CONTRACTS.md README.md` must confirm the current owner before proposing replacement.
- `br show eon-specify-helix-modal-semantics-3kl --json` and `br show eon-preserve-helix-keybindings-uca --json` must show accepted decisions before a positive recommendation closes.
- The final Bead state must contain reference identities, dogfood evidence, option matrix, owner/data-flow maps, modal/keybinding consequences, proof shape, platform disposition, dependency and license impact, rejected alternatives, and explicit user decision.
- No source, test, manifest, contract index, dependency, generated artifact, ambient configuration, or child repository changes during this decision.

## Stop Conditions

- Stop if no replacement-only user value is demonstrated.
- Stop if evidence requires an unapproved dependency, new repository, process boundary, EON/VEN contract, or change to Orbit authority.
- Stop if the proposed engine cannot preserve the accepted Helix modal and keybinding contracts at a credible cost.
- Stop if persistence, agent integration, remote access, CRDTs, plugins, or language parity expand beyond the first falsifiable proof.
- Stop if an upstream API, open PR, license assumption, or unmeasured performance claim is being treated as proven.

## Maintenance Notes

Priority remains P3 and status deferred: this is strategically interesting but not the active product frontier. Effort L for the decision evidence; any editor implementation is XL/HIGH-risk. The most credible positive candidate is selected Helix-core reuse plus Eon-owned modal/lifecycle/projection layers, but that is a hypothesis to test, not a chosen dependency. Helix remains Eon's accepted editor until a separate implementation and acceptance sequence proves and promotes a replacement. Preferred product shape: Eon-first distribution, Eon-independent core when cheap, standalone product deferred.

Lucca, 2026-10-29 ("ok"): keep the evidence that settled the review-tiering question
(~/.cache/eon-agents/eon-8e/review-tiering/REPORT.md, eon-zypt) complete for next time. That
analysis hit three gaps:
- Codex logs before 2026-10-25 were lost with /tmp, so the cost figures rest on four days (n=77).
- 228 of 543 commits since the consolidation name no bead; 42 code beads were matched by title and
  17 classified from bead text alone.
- 11 code beads have no review ledger line (for example eon-monorepo-2oko.4, .5, eon-pxn,
  eon-awmq.7, pg67, i2m3), although AGENTS.md "Review loop" requires one per slice.

## Scope

In scope:
1. Review logs: Codex and Claude review briefs, reports and logs live under
   ~/.cache/eon-agents/<session>/ (never /tmp or the scratchpad). The repository rule is already
   present in docs/AGENT-RULES.md "Running Codex" on dcaef1c; do not re-add it or edit generated
   AGENTS.md directly. Verify the overseer launcher scripts
   (~/.cache/eon-agents/eon-overseer/codex-run.sh, codex-resume.sh) and prompts obey it; change only

2. Commit messages name their bead: a trailer such as `Bead: <id>` on every commit that carries a
   bead's work. Draft the AGENTS.md text (in `.agent-protocols.local.md`, then render) for Lucca's
   approval. Prefer a cheap check over more instruction text if one fits (for example the
   shared-tree commit helper refusing a commit without the trailer), but no new tool unless Lucca
   agrees.
3. Ledger completeness: the converge Finish step already records rounds; add to the overseer's
   landing checklist that a code bead does not close without its ledger line.

Out of scope:
- Rewriting past commits or backfilling old ledgers; the Starcompass converge text (ap-xyb).

## Acceptance

- New review logs land under ~/.cache/eon-agents/; AGENTS.md text for the bead trailer and log
  location approved by Lucca and rendered; the overseer's landing checklist names the ledger line.

## Verification

- Planning/agent-policy route: render and import check, changed paths and diff; one landed commit
  after the change carries the trailer.

## Stop Conditions

title: Prove a Nix-free Linux bundle and installer before public beta
description:
## Contract

EON-C5 and EON-C6: a user on x86_64 Linux/native Wayland can run the accepted Eon component set from a relocatable direct bundle without installing or relying on Nix. A small user-local installer consumes that same artifact and preserves user data and active work. Nix remains the development/build and supported delivery channel; it is not a target-user prerequisite.

## Prerequisite and chosen sequence

The user approved this sequence on 2026-10-07. eon-p93 accepted the scoped graduation decision on 2026-10-10. The manual bundle and installer slices are closed and their exact development evidence satisfies this aggregate on 2026-10-11. This acceptance does not qualify or publish the public beta.

This epic records aggregate acceptance, never an implementation unit. Its two accepted slices preserve the selected order:

1. eon-prove-manual-nix-free-linux-bundle-216b accepts the immutable manual bundle in an isolated non-Nix native-Wayland user environment after eon-p93. The proof shares the host kernel; independent-machine qualification remains separate.
2. eon-prove-thin-linux-bundle-installer-8r7n accepts the thin installer consuming that exact archive, active-work-safe upgrade/rollback/removal, and its final parser correction. Exact identities and proof-reuse limits remain with the slice.

Both slices satisfy the retained aggregate development acceptance below; the closure review and remaining gates are recorded in notes. eon-qualify-nix-free-linux-public-beta-lm9p owns subsequent wider public-beta qualification. Exact blocking edges own sequencing; parent-child edges are omitted because this tracker treats them as prerequisites and would create a cycle.

## Reference and ownership gate

Read docs/DISTRIBUTION.md and its activated routes, the canonical manifest and accepted child artifact/launch contracts, and the eon-p93 decision. Retain the existing comparison of dist, a small owned assembler and credible maintained tooling, including the recorded Doodlestein/local-release evidence and spending constraints. Use only the justified release owner/tool from the gate; any material change reopens that decision. Evaluate closure relocation, system-library/driver dependencies, fonts and managed tools, archive verification, ownership, licensing, local LOC and removal cost. Select no bundler from its availability alone.

Eon owns assembly and install/upgrade/remove policy. Children retain runtime mechanisms and artifact ownership. Every path consumes the canonical component manifest; no hidden component substitution, copied child behavior or second graph.

## Success Criteria

Both slices are accepted for the same exact graph: the useful manual Nix-free Linux bundle first, then the thin installer with verified delivery and active-work-safe upgrade/rollback/removal. Wider public-beta qualification remains separate.

## Acceptance

- Produce one immutable x86_64 Linux archive, checksum and signature or attestation binding the artifact, with exact graph/provenance and retained size/closure observations. Release assets are authoritative; website installation copy points to them.
- Manual extraction runs useful Eon on a clean native-Wayland machine/user environment without a host Nix installation/store, Nix daemon/evaluator, development checkout or undeclared machine-local references. State the actual host prerequisites; prove the composed tools and child processes, not only launcher startup.
- The inspectable installer resolves a pinned release over TLS, verifies the artifact, supports dry-run, a versioned user prefix and atomic current selection, upgrade, rollback and removal. Keep manual extraction available; avoid unrequested shell-profile edits and collisions with unrelated tools or owned Nix installations.
- Partial download, verification, extraction or activation failure leaves the prior installation usable. Removal affects only owned installation/integration points and preserves configuration/data; preserve any version payload still needed by live retained work or stage its removal. Switching current never silently stops live supervisors/terminals; retained work remains usable with its prior executable under accepted generation contracts.
- Direct and Nix artifacts report the same accepted exact graph and runtime semantics. Verify fresh install plus active-work upgrade/rollback/removal at the outermost delivery boundary, with the cheapest checks for introduced deterministic logic. Record exact artifact/environment/result and limitations; align current install/usage/contract docs and LOC at implementation acceptance.
- Prepare yazelix.com installation copy without making it binary authority. Public publication/promotion requires the ordinary explicit user decision on the reviewable candidate.

## Scope boundary

One Linux bundle and small installer only. No extra architecture, macOS, X11/Xwayland, Home Manager, AppImage, Flatpak, deb/rpm, containers, system repositories, service-manager requirement, auto-updater, live handoff or restart-persistence promise. Deferred channels remain separate. This completed epic records the two accepted development slices. Public-beta qualification, release trust, redistribution clearance and publication retain separate gates.
notes:
Reference and tool routing (planning only): Doodlestein Self Releaser is required research evidence beside dist, an owned assembler, Nix-native/local release commands, cost-bounded hosted GitHub Actions, and any other credible shape. Inspect an exact revision for workflow reuse through act, compatibility gaps, artifact naming and parity, verification, upload authority, failure recovery, secrets, signing, and provenance. A local container run does not prove GitHub-hosted parity. Record the expected hosted-minute and storage envelope, timeout and cancellation policy, hard spending boundary, local fallback, and why the selected release owner does not create a second component graph. Reference status does not approve Doodlestein, act, or a workflow.

Aggregate closure accepted, 2026-10-11
The user selected closure review of eon-ohh. EON-C5/C6 already record the accepted unpublished Linux bundle/installer slice; this is aggregate metadata only, with no new implementation or expanded proof. Both child slices and p93 are closed.

Current Nix Eon/installer outputs still match f9j917vz/q93wjavp.

Acceptance map

2. Useful non-Nix execution: retained moved read-only root,hidden host Nix/checkout/home,12 managed tools,native input,detach/reopen and exact Stop pass in the isolated Pop!_OS24.04/Linux7.1.5 Sway1.12/lavapipe user environment.

All12 non-reader-metadata inputs in the final installer source receipt still match; four later reader metadata updates do not alter runtime proof inputs.
6. Website/release boundary: docs/INSTALLER.md contains unpublished yazelix.com copy. Public assets remain artifact authority; no public release signer or publication is inferred.

Reference/tool decisions remain accepted at p93/manual/installer owners, including the exact Nova ffc9df53 comparison, local locked Nix/Rust/$0 policy, unchanged Bubblewrap relocation owner and rejected duplicate graph/path-rewriting/release frameworks. No new source shape,tool,dependency or hosted job is selected; do not repeat unchanged Rust/Nix/native suites merely to close this aggregate.

Remaining gates and negatives

Same-host software-GPU evidence is not independent-machine/hardware-GPU/minimum-kernel qualification. No model turn or semantic agent resume; account-routing timeout remains retained. title: Move Linux peer_identity to rustix socket_peercred once rustix handles PID 0
description: eon-c828u.4 kept Runtime's libc SO_PEERCRED code for Linux peer_identity (with its length check) instead of the approved rustix::net::sockopt::socket_peercred: rustix 1.1.4 builds a NonZero PID from the kernel reply, and Linux legally returns PID 0 for a peer in another PID namespace (SO_PEERCRED -> pid_vnr), which is undefined behaviour before Runtime can refuse the peer. Evidence: /home/lucca/.cache/eon-agents/eon-rustix-rt-work/bead/03-review-ledger.md and the Opus code review there. Do: when a rustix release returns an Option or plain i32 PID for peer credentials, switch to it and drop the libc call; until then keep libc. Check upstream rustix first for a fix or an open issue (do not post on Lucca's behalf).

title: Define the canonical Eon component manifest
description:
Contracts:
EON-C2 and EON-C3.

Goal:
Define one small, human-reviewable manifest that pins exact child revisions, compatibility contracts, and declared package or artifact inputs. Nix consumes this graph during alpha. Later distribution tooling must extend the same graph instead of replacing it.

Reference and tool gate:
Inspect current child release and package metadata plus at least one comparable multi-component manifest. Compare a small hand-owned schema with using existing Nix metadata directly. Record versioning, validation, local LOC, maintenance, and the point at which external release tooling becomes useful. Defer cargo-dist, portable-bundle, and installer evaluation to the direct-distribution gate.

Acceptance:
- The alpha schema names project, revision, contract version, target, package or artifact input, and launch inputs.
- A focused validator rejects incompatible or incomplete component sets.
- One fixture pins the exact owner revisions and contracts required by the alpha: ORB-C1 through ORB-C9, VEN-C1 through VEN-C4, and VEN-C7, their canonical ORBS v2 and ORBF v1 package boundary, plus Helix, Yazi, and Ratconfig. Additional proved contracts may be recorded without becoming activation prerequisites. If preactivation hardening advances an owner proof, pin the final accepted proof rather than preserving an obsolete candidate.
- Eon receives resolved component paths without constructing store paths or invoking a Nix evaluator during normal use.
- Product state records stable component identities instead of resolved store paths.
- docs/CONTRACTS.md records exact proof evidence.

Scope:
Do not require portable artifacts during Nix-only alpha. Do not create a second dependency graph for a package manager or rebuild child behavior in Eon.
close_reason: Strengthened and reverified validation-owner proof with exact public diagnostics for every structured invalid-graph mutation.
