title: Decide opt-in packaged tools: br and a bead viewer as [tools] toggles
description:
## Why

Lucca, 2026-11-01 (via the starcompass-be session): "maybe we want to add beads_rust and beadseer by default inside eon. worth discussing", "starcompass too?", then "these opt-ins are interesting, they can work as 'plugins'". Every Starcompass profile tells agents to use `br` when available, so projects on Eon without it fall back to weaker planning. Nothing is decided; this bead keeps the idea and the recommendations.

## Facts

- br 0.7.2 and bv 0.25.2 are pinned in flake.nix (release tarballs by exact URL and hash, linux musl amd64 and darwin arm64) but only in the contributor devShell, not in the product package or managed tools.
- Managed tools today: Nushell, Helix, Yazi, LazyGit, Anima (docs/CONFIGURATION.md "Managed tools"). Eon does not rewrite the parent PATH, shell startup files or native tool data paths.

## Recommendation (overseer, agreed by starcompass-be)

1. Opt-in, off by default: a `[tools]` table of toggles with one uniform record each (name, pinned derivation, licence, platforms, documented default), reported as data by the CLI (e.g. `eon versions`) so agents can see what is on (rule 5). Default documented in docs/CONFIGURATION.md (rule 6).
2. Candidates: br and a viewer (bv or beadseer). Default-off because most users have no `.beads`, bundling ties each project's br version to Eon's release cadence, and it widens third-party binary trust to every user.
3. Starcompass CLI: not shipped (maintainers run it at a pinned commit; a bundled copy would drift). Starcompass skills: never installed by Eon (they write ~/.claude and ~/.codex, against Eon's no-native-data-paths boundary).
4. No plugin format yet: move to one only when a third tool or an outside contributor needs it, since an interface, versioning and trust policy would be guesswork with two tools.
5. Timing: after the macOS install path settles.

## Contract

A packaged-tools clause in the managed-tools contract; text drafted when planned. Needs Lucca's decision before planning.

## Acceptance

Decision recorded here; then a planned bead with toggles, pins, docs and CHANGELOG.

## Scope boundary

br/viewer toggles only; no plugin system, no skills installation.

title: Own one launch directory per Eon tab
description:
## Outcome

Implement `EON-C17 — Tab launch directory`: every full-Eon tab owns one authoritative launch directory, an explicit action can retarget it, and every later pane in that tab starts there.

Smallest observable contract:
- Consumer: a person creating and navigating tabs and panes in a full Eon workspace.
- Trigger: a fresh workspace or tab is created, or a trusted same-user workspace client explicitly sets one live tab's directory.
- Result: Eon stores one absolute directory on the tab, returns it in the authoritative workspace snapshot, derives the tab's visible directory label from it, and uses it as the process working directory for every later `CreatePane` in that tab.
- Failures: structurally invalid, oversized, missing, non-directory, unknown-tab, or spawn-time-invalid paths fail without mutating the wrong tab, adding topology, or leaving a child, record, or socket.

Eon owns tab identity, launch-directory policy, mutation, and recovery fallback. Orbit continues to own each Session's actual terminal CWD. Venus owns bounded native presentation of Eon-authored identity and directory state. Ordinary shell `cd`, OSC 7, and Orbit CWD/title updates never retarget or relabel the tab.

User-approved decisions on 2026-08-25:
- Add `EON-C17` and activate a versioned EONW v2; EONW v1 remains immutable.
- New workspace tab identities use compact `tN`; pane identities remain `pN`.
- The visible tab label is derived rather than separately stored: `1  eon`, `2  nova`, `3  ~`, or `4  /`. The stable identity remains `tN`.
- A new tab inherits the active tab's launch directory and uses that same value for its first Session.
- A recovered synthetic `t1` uses the replacement supervisor's absolute launch directory as new policy state and never infers prior truth from a surviving pane.
- Stage the exact Eon/Venus source update without any running supervisor accepting both EONW versions.

Impact: HIGH for current daily navigation and the planned Yazi picker. Effort: L. Implementation risk: HIGH because workspace state, launch, recovery, wire compatibility, exact consumer pins, native presentation, and installed-runtime proof meet here.

## Evidence

- Current Eon source at `fad3f01d446b33fc04b5381633e9eb4ac1976dc2` stores `Tab { id, panes, selected }` in `crates/eon/src/workspace.rs`; `CreateTab` and `CreatePane` start a Session before committing topology.
- `crates/eon/src/supervisor.rs` sends dynamic workspace starts through `start_orbit` with the configured default child and no directory argument.
- `crates/eon/src/sessions.rs` builds the Orbit command without `Command::current_dir`, so every current child inherits the supervisor process directory.
- EONW v1 snapshots/actions carry topology, endpoint, liveness, and focus only. EON-C8/EON-C10 intentionally do not promise tab launch state, command/CWD history, or workspace persistence.
- Current Venus source retains stable tab identity for hit testing, focus, and accessibility and renders that identity directly. Its pane labels already demonstrate bounded directory compaction, but pane CWD remains Orbit-authored state and is not tab policy.
- Orbit ORBF carries the current terminal working directory. Polling or copying it into the tab would create a second policy owner and make ordinary shell navigation change future process launch.
- Nova's exact `zellij-pane-orchestrator` at `e76ae565f0dc25844293544bf9b58a6dcf127947` owns one canonical root per stable tab, changes it only through explicit retarget behavior, and derives a native tab name from the root basename. Preserve the user outcome, not its Zellij calls, UTF-8-only state, shell injection, editor synchronization, or recovery heuristics.
- Upstream Zellij separates tab identity/name from an optional tab CWD and has had multiple CWD lifecycle and inaccessible-path failures; use it as failure evidence rather than as Eon architecture.

## Scope

In scope:
- One `PathBuf` launch directory on each live full-Eon tab and one raw bounded byte field on each EONW v2 tab snapshot.
- Fresh `t1` starts at the absolute process directory Eon uses for its first Session.
- `CreateTab` copies the active tab's launch directory, uses it for the new tab's first Session, then commits the new `tN` only after Session startup succeeds.
- One semantic `SetTabDirectory { tab, directory }` EONW v2 action. The CLI surface is `eon tab directory TAB -- DIRECTORY`; it carries the exact `tN` identity and one opaque Unix path argument.
- Protocol representation is a nonempty raw byte sequence bounded to 4096 bytes. Eon rejects NUL and non-absolute paths, follows the path only to verify that it currently names a directory, and preserves the accepted spelling. It promises no symlink canonicalization or stable filesystem object identity.
- An accepted set mutates only the addressed tab and returns one complete snapshot containing the authoritative value.
- `CreatePane` passes the tab directory through Rust `Command::current_dir` to Orbit. Existing Sessions, PTY children, and their current directories do not change.
- If an accepted directory later disappears, becomes inaccessible, or changes through a symlink race, the next spawn is the final authority: `CreatePane` fails without adding a pane or leaking launch residue, while the tab retains its accepted directory until another explicit set.
- Same-boot recovery projects surviving Sessions into synthetic `t1` and assigns the replacement supervisor's absolute launch directory as fresh future-pane policy. Documentation must not call that value recovered prior workspace state.
- Venus derives a bounded visual label from the authoritative tab directory: numeric identity prefix plus home marker, root marker, or final path component. Duplicate leaf names remain distinguishable by the number. Hit testing and actions continue to use `tN`; accessibility and diagnostics include stable identity plus the bounded full path.
- EONW v2 source and exact consumer staging: first publish an unactivated v2 codec surface from Eon while the running product remains v1; then update and prove the exact Venus consumer; finally activate v2 in Eon, pin that Venus revision, and remove staging-only v1 source where no accepted consumer requires it. No supervisor accepts both versions.
- Focused TDD for the codec and workspace transition plus one outer integration proof for directory inheritance, retarget, spawn failure, label/accessibility projection, and tab independence.

Out of scope:
- Manual tab names, a separately stored label, label configuration, rename commands, directory history, persistence, global/project roots, or restoration of pre-crash tab roots.
- Tracking ordinary shell `cd`, synchronizing tab and pane CWD, retargeting existing processes, polling OSC 7, or inferring policy from Orbit metadata.
- Yazi/zoxide UI or configuration, automatically opening a pane after retarget, pane-title changes, arbitrary split trees, EonTerm, or a generic settings/profile service.
- Canonicalizing symlinks, retaining directory file descriptors, filesystem watches, TOCTOU elimination, authorization beyond the existing private same-UID EONW boundary, or a new dependency.
- A second composition graph, a runtime compatibility adapter, or simultaneous EONW v1/v2 service.

## Reference gate before code

Required:
- Current EON-C8, EON-C10, EON-C11, and EON-C15 workspace/action/generation/recovery owners and exact accepted checks; EON-C6 remains distribution planning rather than runtime ownership.
- Complete EONW v1 codec, validation, caller inventory, exact Venus dependency/substitution path, generation identity inputs, and incompatibility behavior.
- Rust `std::process::Command::current_dir`, Unix `Path`/`OsStrExt`, `execve`/`chdir` failure behavior, and the impossibility of validating away a later filesystem race without retaining a stronger object handle.
- Exact Nova tab-workspace and retarget implementation at `Yazelix/zellij-pane-orchestrator@e76ae565f0dc25844293544bf9b58a6dcf127947`.
- Exact pinned Zellij source used by Nova for new-tab CWD, naming, and inaccessible/missing directory behavior.
- Current Venus workspace scene, renderer, accessibility projection, protocol transport, and exact source update mechanics.

Record in the bead before implementation:
- The inspected exact source paths/revisions and the preserved or rejected mechanisms.
- The minimal EONW v2 staging shape that avoids duplicate runtime ownership while breaking the Eon/Venus revision cycle.
- The exact protocol seed, Venus consumer, and Eon activation revisions as they become available.

Adopt one tab field, one action, `Command::current_dir`, and a Venus-derived label. Reject a stored display name, shell wrapper, environment-variable shadow state, per-pane root, Orbit-derived policy, polling, persistence scaffolding, or dependency.

## Acceptance Criteria

- EON-C17 is recorded as Candidate before implementation and names Eon as the sole tab launch-directory owner.
- Every fresh workspace uses `t1`; later tabs use checked monotonic `tN`; panes remain `pN`. EONW v1 and older live generations are not rewritten.
- Fresh `t1` owns the absolute directory used for its first Session. `CreateTab` inherits the active tab directory and uses it for its first Session.
- `SetTabDirectory` accepts an exact live `tN`, atomically changes only that tab, and returns a complete snapshot containing the exact raw directory bytes.
- Visual labels derive from the directory without another stored owner: `N  leaf`, `N  ~`, or `N  /`. Retarget updates the label; shell navigation does not. Duplicate leaves remain distinguishable, and accessibility exposes identity plus bounded path context.
- `CreatePane` after retarget starts Orbit and its child with that directory as process CWD. Existing Sessions and terminal CWDs do not change; another tab remains independent.
- Empty, relative, NUL-containing, oversized, missing, and non-directory set requests fail without state change. Unknown/stale `tN` fails without changing another tab.
- If an already accepted path is removed, made inaccessible, or raced before a later spawn, `CreatePane` returns a bounded start failure without adding topology or leaving child/record/socket residue. The accepted tab directory is not silently rolled back.
- Recovery assigns replacement-launch CWD to synthetic `t1`, identifies it as fresh fallback policy, and never projects a surviving pane's current CWD as recovered tab truth.
- EONW v1 stays immutable. Exact clients reject unsupported versions. The staged source order yields no runtime dual-stack and final Eon pins the accepted Venus consumer.
- Focused red/green checks cover v2 raw-path/action/snapshot codec validation, `tN` identity validation, active-tab inheritance, exact-tab/no-mutation transitions, derived label/accessibility parity, and spawn rollback.
- One outer installed integration check retargets one tab, creates a pane whose child reports the expected CWD, proves a second tab remains independent, removes an accepted directory and observes bounded no-topology failure, and preserves all pre-existing live Sessions during profile refresh.
- The unchanged final candidate passes the full affected Rust and Nix surfaces, manifest validation, required docs/contract/help/changelog updates, LOC scorecards, and `git diff --check`.

## Stop conditions

- Stop before implementation until the reference-gate evidence and exact EONW v2 staging mechanism are recorded. The contract identity, path representation, fresh/new/recovered semantics, `tN` identity, derived label, and no-runtime-dual-stack policy are already user-approved.
- Stop if the work requires Orbit to own tab policy, Venus to infer it from pane CWD, a shell `cd` wrapper, manual naming, workspace persistence, a new dependency, or a runtime compatibility window.
- Stop before changing EonTerm, Yazi, zoxide, existing Session CWD, pane labels, or ordinary shell navigation.
- Stop if another active frontier owns EONW, workspace, supervisor, launch, or Venus workspace-presentation surfaces.

## Maintenance notes

This bead remains the sole prerequisite for `eon-start-tabs-with-yazi-picker-1az`. It supplies the stable `tN` target, authoritative directory, and derived label needed by that later adapter, but does not choose the Yazi binding or introduce a sidebar, popup, editor integration, or manual naming.
notes:
2026-08-25 implementation baseline (codex-root):
- Inspected Eon at fad3f01d446b33fc04b5381633e9eb4ac1976dc2: crates/eon-workspace-protocol/src/lib.rs; crates/eon/src/{workspace,sessions,supervisor,cli}.rs; flake.nix; docs/CONTRACTS.md; README.md. Inspected the exact Venus consumer source at 1034817bbe2352fb4b1026bce6b1f02eedd67e37 and local accepted source 5fa49d2b06fd9ec54461dd39ef226e3f1eb499d1: Cargo.toml, src/{scene,render,accessibility,model,transport}.rs and contracts/tests. Orbit source pin 70861097a825c2fbfaea53a8ca9437f45e8602eb remains source-fresh; later local commits are documentation/planning only.
- Reference decision: preserve Nova zellij-pane-orchestrator e76ae565f0dc25844293544bf9b58a6dcf127947's one explicit per-tab root and basename-derived presentation. Reject its Zellij API, UTF-8 state, shell/editor synchronization, recovery heuristics, and any Orbit-pane-CWD inference. Rust PathBuf/OsStrExt owns raw Unix paths; std::process::Command::current_dir is the spawn boundary. A preflight directory check cannot remove later chdir/exec races, so spawn remains authoritative.
- Final shape: one PathBuf on Eon Tab, one SetTabDirectory action, one v2 raw path field, existing start-before-topology transaction, and Venus-derived label/accessibility text. No new dependency, stored display name, wrapper shell, polling, persistence, or runtime compatibility adapter.
- Exact cycle staging: seed Eon with immutable top-level v1 plus an unactivated v2 module; running Eon remains v1. Pin and prove Venus against that exact v2 module. Then activate only v2 in Eon, remove the staging-only v1 implementation, and pin the exact Venus consumer. No supervisor binary decodes both versions. Intermediate and final revision IDs will be appended when committed.
- Protocol seed: Eon 7bb50873ae27e09dfebd8a6ca2f8075bac07afe8 (unactivated v2 module; full workspace Cargo proof passed; v1 runtime unchanged).
close_reason: Third fresh-eyes correction complete: initial tab-directory validation now precedes Session lifecycle work; red/green, full Rust/Nix, exact installed proof, profile refresh, docs, and simplification convergence pass.

title: Close the attention inbox when the person clicks outside it
description:
## Why

Lucca, 2026-11-04: "the shortcuts popup should vanish when i click outside of it". eon-gl1xo did this for the shortcut viewer (VEN-C20). The attention inbox (Alt+Q, VEN-C32) copies the viewer's dismissal ("as the shortcut viewer"), but it did not pick up the change: while the inbox is open, a press outside still does nothing (eon-gl1xo record 001).

## What

Give the attention inbox the same rule: a pointer press outside its dialog, from any button, closes it as Escape does. That press and its release reach no other target, and prior focus is restored. Reuse eon-gl1xo's `viewer_button` path rather than copying it.

## Contract

Amend VEN-C32's dismissal to match VEN-C20's amended trigger: "Escape or a pointer press outside the dialog closes it, and that press reaches no other target". Approved by eon-overseer under Lucca's standing rule, as the consistent follow-on to his request.

## Acceptance

The same shape of proof as eon-gl1xo:
- unit tests for outside and inside presses and release capture, in venus/src/application/tests/;

title: Say on stderr when an eon command is waiting on a busy supervisor
description:
From the Opus review of eon-g3vdz (2026-11-11): with the wider start bound a CLI request can now wait up to 76 s (Stop 81 s) for a busy supervisor without printing anything (36 s before), and the window's 'not answering' notice now appears after 76 s instead of 6 s (its 'slow to answer' notice still shows at 2 s). Print one stderr line after about 2 s ('waiting for the window: starting a terminal…') and nothing on stdout, so JSON output stays clean. Rule 6 for the delay. Follows eon-g3vdz.

## Owner, scope and acceptance (dcaef1c)

The wait boundary is Runtime's shared CLI control request path (runtime/crates/eon-runtime/src/control.rs:237-284), not one individual pane command. CONTROL_TIMEOUT/STOP_TIMEOUT derive from named lifecycle bounds in eon-workspace-protocol/src/lib.rs; reload has its own longer bound in control.rs. Reuse that path and its supported harness instead of adding a timer to every caller.

- A fast success or failure prints no waiting line. A deliberately held request prints one line on stderr after the selected delay, never repeats it, and stops the notification when the request completes or fails.
- With --json, stdout remains exactly the existing single JSON result/error; exit status and final failure diagnostics are unchanged. Do not claim the supervisor is starting a terminal unless that action is actually known; generic “waiting for the window…” is honest for other busy requests.
- Record how Rule 6 is satisfied for the delay (configuration/default documentation, or an explicit fixed-value rationale under the allowed policy).
- Capture a deterministic held-response observation through the existing control harness; run the affected checks and whole-workspace eon-test before code review. No timeout widening, retries, supervisor-responsiveness redesign (eon-pimct), or Venus notice change.

Prerequisite: eon-g3vdz is closed; its longer start bound motivates this notice. Read the lifecycle reference route if adding an asynchronous worker, and ensure cancellation/cleanup cannot leave a late stderr line or owned thread behind.

title: Close a workspace from the Alt+Shift+S picker with Ctrl+X
description:
## Why

Lucca, 2026-11-04: "i think we could add closing support to the current alt
shift s", then "lets work on it now". The picker already lists every workspace
of the window; closing one today needs Commands > Close this workspace (only
the shown one) or `eon workspace close WS`.

## Evidence

The picker is `eon-workspaces` (symlink to `eon`, cli.rs:73 → `workspace_picker`
cli.rs:170 → `pick_and_run_workspace` cli.rs:255-298), an fzf list in a
transient popup terminal; `workspace_pick_arguments` (cli.rs:334-342) maps fzf's
`--print-query` output to `workspace switch wN` or `workspace new --name Q`, run
in-process by `run_as_caller` (cli.rs:353). `eon workspace close` confirms on the
popup's TTY (cli.rs:1121-1165, generation.rs `confirm`), as Commands > Close this
workspace already does from a popup (cli.rs:216-234). fzf 0.73.1 binds no
ctrl-x; Venus binds no Ctrl+X (shortcuts.rs:113-260).

## Scope

- The picker adds `--expect=ctrl-x`; Ctrl+X on the highlighted row runs
  `workspace close wN` through `run_as_caller` (same confirmation), then lists
  the remaining workspaces again; closing its own workspace ends it with that
  workspace; the last workspace's close is the window's final close.
- Footer: `Enter Switch · Ctrl+X Close · No match: Enter Create · Esc/Ctrl+C Cancel`.
- Commands > Switch workspace (same list) gets it too.
- Contract text approved by Lucca 2026-11-04 ("agree"): EON-C33 Picker
  sentence, EON-C33 Status amendment line, EON-C10 Workspaces popup sentence
  (exact text in 2-01-picker-approval.md).
- Docs: docs/USAGE.md picker passages (~189, ~352-363), README.md ~63,
  CHANGELOG.md Unreleased line.
- Configurability: Ctrl+X stays fixed, like the picker's Enter and Esc: it is
  an fzf key inside an Eon-owned list, not a window chord.
- Agent path: `eon workspace close WS` already exists. Portability: neutral.

## Acceptance

- Unit: `workspace_pick_arguments` maps a ctrl-x row to `workspace close wN`
  and keeps Enter, no-match create and cancel as before.
- Integration (workspace_control.rs picker test, fake fzf): Ctrl+X on another
  workspace's row with "yes" closes it and the picker lists again without it;
  "no" keeps it; Ctrl+X on the picker's own workspace closes it and shows the
  most recently shown remaining one.
- Installed, isolated: Alt+Shift+S, Ctrl+X on a row, y → the workspace is gone
  from the list and from `eon workspaces --json`.

## Verification

`nix develop -c eon-test -p eon-runtime -p eon`, clippy/fmt for eon-runtime,
the default Nix check, one isolated installed dogfood of Alt+Shift+S Ctrl+X,
converge with Codex, then the profile refresh by the overseer.

title: Fix the intermittent generation discovery cleanup test
description:
## Defect
eon-runtime's generation::tests::discovery_bounds_dead_cleanup_and_rejects_unsafe_metadata fails intermittently at runtime/crates/eon-runtime/src/generation.rs:738, assert!(!dead.exists()): the second, uncontended discover_generations does not remove the dead generation's control metadata. Seen twice on 2026-10-21 under machine load (1-minute load about 15-30 while several agents built and tested), in eon-test runs on edge cd1f4cf and 9f972e5. It passed 3/3 alone and on rerun. Reported by claude-w3 while working on eon-awmq.8 and eon-popup-covered-pane-reorder-iw2k; neither change touches generation.rs.

## Contract
No contract change. The test protects dead-generation cleanup (EON-C11 lifecycle). Either the cleanup has a timing dependency (for example a liveness probe or lock that is still held, or races the inspection thread joined just before), or the test does.

## Acceptance
- Name the cause from the code and a reproduction under load (for example the test looped while a parallel build runs).
- A fix that makes the test deterministic without weakening what it checks; red/green evidence from the load reproduction.
- nix develop -c eon-test -p eon-runtime.

## Scope boundary
This test and the cleanup path it exercises only.
close_reason: Test-only fix: wait for the dead socket to refuse, unlock the fixture lock explicitly; red 11/40, green 0/80 and 0/30 on the exact tree; cause was fork inheritance of open file descriptions, not a cleanup defect

comments.author: lucca
comments.text: Update (claude-w3, 2026-10-21): it also failed at low load (1-minute load about 1-2) in an eon-test run on edge b764c63 plus an unrelated change, then passed on rerun. So it is not only load-driven. Four failures seen today in about eight full runs.

comments.author: lucca
comments.text: Cause (2026-10-21): fork inheritance of the test's open file descriptions, not a cleanup defect. Instrumented loops of eon-test -p eon-runtime --lib: the dead generation's probe reports 'Connection refused' (dead) as intended, but right after drop(held) the lifecycle flock is still held (try_lock Ok(None)) and frees within about 0.3 ms; no /proc fd still names the lock by the time it is scanned. Failing runs: 11 of 40 full-suite runs at load about 1-2 (10 at the uncontended !dead.exists() assertion, 1 at the contended state == dead assertion, the listener variant), 0 of 25 with --test-threads=1, 0 of 40 running the test alone. Other eon-runtime tests spawn children (sessions.rs, supervisor.rs, quota.rs); a child forked by a concurrent test shares this test's file descriptions until it execs, so a dropped lock briefly stays held and a dropped UnixListener briefly accepts. Product impact: none beyond a cleanup deferred to the next discovery. Fix (test only): wait until the dead socket refuses connections, and retry the uncontended discovery until it removes the metadata (5 s deadline). Rejected: probing the lock with try_lock before the uncontended discovery, which still failed 1 of 60 because the probe's own lock descriptor is inherited the same way. Green: 0 of 80 full-suite runs fail this test. Seen once in those 80 runs, out of scope: quota::tests::workers_isolate_failure_and_bound_output_timeout_and_shutdown at quota.rs:447 (snapshot still None after 2 s), plausibly the same inheritance class on a worker pipe.

comments.author: lucca
comments.text:
Fix and proof (2026-10-21), superseding the fix described in the earlier cause comment. The diagnosis there stands; the retry fix and its 0 of 80 green were for an earlier candidate and are not this fix's proof.

Fix (test only, runtime/crates/eon-runtime/src/generation.rs, code tree 6eeaff1d206e93d902f6fa5d582600f28fef7074 on base 9e0bb86):
- After dropping the listener, wait (5 s deadline) until the dead socket refuses connections. A refused socket cannot accept again, so the contended inspection sees a dead generation.
- Call `held.unlock()` before dropping the fixture's lock. flock belongs to the open file description, so an explicit unlock releases it even where a concurrently forked child still holds a copy; dropping alone does not. The single uncontended discovery and `assert!(!dead.exists())` stay as they were.
- Rejected: retrying the uncontended discovery until cleanup (it accepts cleanup that needs several passes, e.g. a swapped socket/directory removal order; both reviewers flagged it) and probing with try_lock first (1 of 60 still failed: the probe's own descriptor is inherited the same way).

Red/green (eon-test -p eon-runtime --lib, full suite, x86_64 Linux, load about 1-13):
- Red, base: 11 of 40 runs failed this test (10 at the uncontended assertion, 1 at the contended state == dead assertion); 0 of 25 with --test-threads=1; 0 of 40 alone.
- Green, this fix: 0 of 80 runs (working tree with generation.rs at 6eeaff1, load 2.5-4.3) and 0 of 30 on the exact tree in a detached worktree (fresh reviewer, load 8.5-13); cargo fmt --check and clippy -D warnings clean.

Out of scope, reported: quota::tests::workers_isolate_failure_and_bound_output_timeout_and_shutdown failed once (quota.rs:447) in one 80-run loop of an earlier candidate; not seen in the 110 runs above.

Ledger: Claude pass 1 (1 blocking: the retry accepted multi-pass cleanup) + Codex pass 1 (same finding; proposed the explicit unlock) -> fixed tree 6eeaff1; Claude pass 2 clean on code (1 blocking on this bead's record, fixed by this comment).

title: Graduate Linux distribution after repaired Nix reliability
description:
User-approved exception — 2026-10-10
The user accepts the demonstrated Orca #757 stale Say All reading-position failure as a known upstream limitation while its correction is reviewed: https://gitlab.gnome.org/GNOME/orca/-/work_items/757#note_2894216. It no longer blocks this distribution-graduation decision or its downstream bundle development. This exception covers the reproduced terminal-to-picker query/path omission and GNOME Terminal/Vim skipped-page text only. Full screen-reader qualification remains open under eon-qualify-repaired-linux-screen-reader-tvkf; retain its negative and do not advertise full screen-reader support. Other accessibility defects, child-source acceptance, active-work protection, trust boundaries and delivery/public-beta proof are not waived. Revisit when upstream accepts a correction or the relevant candidate/behavior changes. No patched Orca is installed or selected as the product reader.

Planning activation and order — user decision 2026-10-07:
The user selected a Nix-free x86_64 Linux native-Wayland bundle and small user-local installer before beta aimed beyond Nix users. This is the named planning gate for that direction, after repair and accepted Nix reliability through eon-accept-repaired-nix-linux-reliability-ws9g. Existing alpha/early dogfood remains Nix-only until the separate bundle, installer and public-beta delivery gates are accepted.

This decision finalizes the accepted product evidence, first direct target, release owner/tool and maintenance envelope. It does not infer acceptance from the closed No-Go eon-qualify-nix-linux-beta-bxoh. After this gate, eon-ohh is delivered by eon-prove-manual-nix-free-linux-bundle-216b first and eon-prove-thin-linux-bundle-installer-8r7n second; eon-qualify-nix-free-linux-public-beta-lm9p qualifies the wider beta. The user approved this planning sequence, not immediate publication or expansion to other targets/formats.

Contract:
EON-C5 and EON-C6, informed by EON-C1 through EON-C4 and every accepted active-work lifecycle contract.

Required evidence:
- The Nix composition launches one accepted Orbit and Venus pair with Helix, Yazi and Ratconfig through their owned contracts.
- Sustained fresh-session dogfood covers launch, detach, reattach, configuration, diagnostics, upgrades, Venus restart, declared Eon relaunch semantics, partial-child failure, and the real coding-agent lifecycle required by eon-ax4.
- An upgrade cannot silently terminate an active Orbit-backed agent or other long-running process.
- Orbit or machine restart persistence remains an explicit limitation unless a separate accepted child contract proves it.
- Exact selected component revisions have no unresolved P0 or P1 integration defect except the narrowly accepted upstream Orca #757 limitation above.
- Product code accepts explicit component paths, invokes no Nix evaluator during normal use, and persists stable component identity instead of store paths.
- The component manifest describes the accepted product without using derivation identity as a runtime contract.
- The team has capacity to maintain artifacts, verification, safe staging, upgrades, rollback and removal.

Decision record:
Compare staying Nix-only longer with one direct Linux bundle. Name the user value, first target, release owner, expected CI and maintenance cost, active-work upgrade policy, tool-gate evidence, and deferred features.

Scope:
This Bead authorizes one direct-distribution decision. It does not implement a bundle, live handoff, restart persistence, provider integration, or another package channel. If safe replacement requires a new Orbit lifecycle contract, route that separately before distribution proceeds.
design:
Treat active agent and terminal work as user data at risk during upgrades.

Before approving direct distribution, exercise the exact update path while an ordinary long-running process and the selected real coding-agent workload are active. Replacing Venus may reconnect through accepted contracts. Replacing Orbit must not be assumed safe: when no accepted live-handoff contract exists, stage or defer the incompatible Orbit update until affected sessions stop, or require explicit informed confirmation naming the processes and state that will be lost. Automatic or background update must never kill active work silently.

Inspect exact current Herdr session-state and live-handoff behavior as comparison evidence for preserving PTYs across runtime replacement, plus official platform update and process-lifecycle sources relevant to the selected bundle. This selects no handoff architecture. A live-handoff, external PTY owner, daemon-restart persistence, or agent-native restore path requires its own Orbit or Eon contract and proof.

The release tool gate still compares staying Nix-only, local owned or Nix-native commands, one direct Linux bundle and credible maintained tooling. Record artifacts, verification, signing or attestation, rollback, removal, CI cost and the user hard spending boundary.

Proof reuse: eon-accept-repaired-nix-linux-reliability-ws9g accepted Eon 84a6e6f with Venus a27aad2 and the recorded exact graph. It is evidence only for unchanged identities/behavior exercised there; it does not blanket-accept a later component candidate. Select the graduation candidate, reuse unaffected evidence, and identify the cheapest remaining outermost checks without repeating complete suites for metadata alone.
acceptance_criteria:
1. The Nix-only Eon composition has sustained fresh-session dogfood for launch, detach, reattach, configuration, diagnostics, upgrades, Venus restart, declared Eon relaunch semantics, partial-child failure, and one real coding-agent lifecycle.
2. The exact upgrade path is exercised while both an ordinary long-running process and a real agent process are active.
3. No upgrade, rollback or automatic update silently terminates an active Orbit-backed process. If Orbit replacement cannot preserve it, the update is staged or deferred until sessions stop, or explicit confirmation names the affected sessions, processes, unpersisted state and exact loss.
4. Orbit and machine restart persistence is either backed by a separately accepted child contract or recorded as an explicit limitation. Distribution code does not simulate or imply it.
5. Any proposed live handoff, external PTY owner, agent-native restoration or new recovery behavior is routed to a separate approved owner contract before distribution consumes it.
6. The accepted component set has no unresolved P0 or P1 integration defect except the user-approved 2026-10-10 Orca #757 limitation described above. New or broader accessibility failures are not covered.
7. The selected Venus revision retains exact scoped structured-accessibility evidence under VEN-C1/VEN-C2/VEN-C4 and the relevant history/workspace contracts. Retain native composed reader observations for bounded scene-derived semantics, keyboard/AT actions and failure UX, plus the demonstrated Orca #757 negative. The user permits distribution graduation/development with this specific upstream limitation; complete Linux reader qualification stays open under eon-qualify-repaired-linux-screen-reader-tvkf and full screen-reader support remains unqualified. Closed ven-q3w or AT-SPI tree inspection alone is insufficient evidence. The separately owned Venus caret repair must be accepted and adopted exactly; closed ven-expose-authoritative-accessible-caret-zki and eon-adopt-venus-authoritative-caret-45yu fulfill that source gate at 58f2eaa. No new reader failure is waived.
8. Product code invokes no Nix evaluator during normal use and persists no store path as stable component identity.
9. The component manifest describes the accepted product without derivation identity as a runtime contract.
10. The tool gate compares staying Nix-only with one direct Linux bundle and records maintenance, CI, active-work staging, artifact verification, rollback and removal costs. Before Go, name the responsible release operator and explicitly accept a bounded maintenance/cost envelope: available local build/verification measurements, provisional artifact/storage/transfer estimates with uncertainty, expected release/support cadence and capacity for failed staging, rollback and removal. Keep $0 additional hosted spend unless the user explicitly changes it; this selects no hosted job or service. The downstream bundle proves actual delivery costs and reopens this decision if they exceed the accepted envelope.
11. Record the user-approved 2026-10-07 direction and first target: x86_64 Linux on native Wayland, one Nix-free direct bundle and small user-local installer before broader public beta. Accepted repaired Nix reliability is required before completing this graduation decision.
12. The decision records the exact component manifest, Orbit and Venus proof revisions, agent-work and accessibility dogfood environments, proof commands, active-work upgrade policy, known limitations, artifact authority and rollback condition.
13. Approval covers one direct-distribution slice and no additional package channel or runtime feature.
14. eon-accept-repaired-nix-linux-reliability-ws9g remains the historical exact Eon 84a6e6f reliability record. The selected repaired candidate needs accepted scoped crash/reliability evidence from eon-isolate-unclean-orbit-exit-1v4a, valid reuse of unchanged earlier boundaries, accepted exact Venus repair adoption and retained composed reader observations. Complete reader qualification is a related follow-up rather than a blocking prerequisite under the narrow Orca #757 exception in criterion 7. The historical bxoh closure remains No-Go. eon-ohh retains separate manual-bundle (216b), installer (8r7n) and public-beta (lm9p) proofs; this exception does not close or pre-accept them.

Accepted Go decision — 2026-10-10

title: Drop split-repository wording from packaged notices
description:
## Outcome
The two notice files that the Nix package installs drop their split-repository wording.

## Known text
- `runtime/NOTICE`: "transferred without modification from https://github.com/Yazelix/eon at e431d7583c84ff574054d2edf556e9827114987e". That commit exists only in the private archive, and the URL now resolves to this repository. Proposed: "from Eon's pre-consolidation history at e431d75…".
- `venus/THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md`: "Eon Desktop's Apache-2.0 license" and "Repository history also contains a removed Codex application mark", both false or stale in this repository. The root `THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md` was already corrected in eon-monorepo-2oko.6.

## Why deferred
Both files are installed into the package (flake.nix installs runtime/NOTICE and venus/THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md under share/licenses), so editing them changes the Eon and EonTerm store paths. eon-monorepo-2oko.6 kept them byte-identical so the published tree builds the store paths it proved.

## Prerequisites
Fold this into the next slice that changes the packaged Eon artifact anyway, so it costs no separate rebuild, profile refresh or generation.

## Acceptance
- Both files carry the corrected wording and the root and Venus notices agree.
- That slice's normal package proof covers the changed artifact; the profile is refreshed per Local Runtime Synchronization.

## Scope boundary
Notice wording only; no license terms change.

title: Extend edge cell backgrounds into pane padding, like Ghostty's window-padding-color
description:
## Report

Lucca, 2026-10-24 (screenshot of opencode in an Eon pane): "this gap is weird". A full-screen TUI
that paints its own background (opencode, also Helix, lazygit and other full-screen apps) leaves a
visible frame between its cells and the pane's outline. Venus pads the terminal grid inside the
pane card, because the grid rarely divides the pane exactly, and paints that padding with the
translucent card, so the window background's warm glow shows through. With a shell using the
default background the padding blends in; with a TUI's darker background it reads as a gap.

Filed on Lucca's request, P1 (2026-10-24, "do it. p1.", answering the overseer's item 35).

## Reference

Ghostty's `window-padding-color` setting:
- `background` (pad with the terminal background);
- `extend` (extend the nearest edge cells' background into the padding, except where that would
  look wrong, e.g. when the edge cells differ along the row or column);
- `extend-always`.

Read Ghostty's implementation (renderer padding extension) and record what it extends and when it
declines, before choosing. Check ~/pjs/refs for a Ghostty clone first.

## Change

Venus paints each pane's padding from the terminal's edge cells, Ghostty-style `extend`: the
padding next to a row or column takes the background of the edge cell beside it, so a full-screen
TUI looks edge to edge. Keep today's look when the edge cells use the default background. The pane
outline, card corners and header are unchanged.

## Configurability

A user may prefer today's frame, so expose a Venus-rendered setting parsed by Eon Runtime (Venus
parses no config), with values modeled on Ghostty's (`background` / `extend` / `extend-always`)
and default `extend`. Document it in docs/CONFIGURATION.md.

## Contract

Find the VEN-C that owns terminal presentation and padding, and bring any wording change to Lucca
first. The setting adds a resolved value on the Runtime-to-Venus path; check whether that touches
EONW, which would need a version bump (memory eonw-codec-change-needs-bump).

## Acceptance

- A Venus scene test: a grid whose edge cells have a non-default background extends it into the
  padding; default-background edges keep today's look. It fails on today's code.
- One installed observation: opencode or Helix in a pane shows no frame.

## Scope

Venus padding rendering plus the one setting. Not pane chrome (eon-mur2) or themes
(eon-eon-themes-or3q).

title: Research sending text to an existing pane or popup, and draft its contract
description:
## Why

Eon can start a command in a new pane (`eon pane create -- COMMAND`), but it can't send input to a pane or popup that's already running. Every comparable multiplexer can: tmux `send-keys`, WezTerm `cli send-text`, kitty `@ send-text`, Zellij `action write-chars`. Agent orchestrators depend on it; ntm drives its agents through tmux `send-keys`. In Eon, the overseer can message Claude sessions but has no way to reach a Codex, Grok, OpenCode or Pi agent running in a pane, and users and scripts can't drive a REPL or re-run a command in a live shell.

Lucca asked for it on 2026-10-23 and chose its shape and order from the overseer's numbered items: "yeah, it need a very deep research. create". That accepted:
1. One CLI command along the lines of `eon pane send TARGET [--enter] -- TEXT`, P2, after the agent sidebar epic (eon-agent-sidebar-yx8).
2. Targets cover panes and popups, by their IDs.

## Deliverable of this bead: deep research, then a contract for approval

This bead is research and contract drafting only, with no product code. Its output, recorded on this bead:

1. **References.** Read the source of each comparable implementation, not just its docs, at a recorded revision, and note what Eon should take from it or reject. That includes the input path (pty write, key encoding or paste), the target addressing, the paste handling, and the safety and focus behavior:
   - tmux `send-keys` (`-l`, `-H`, paste buffers);
   - WezTerm `cli send-text` (`--no-paste`, bracketed paste by default);
   - kitty `@ send-text` and `send-key` (remote-control auth and password, `--match`);
   - Zellij `write-chars` and `write`;
   - ntm's use of `send-keys` to drive agents (what it sends, how it submits a prompt, its failures), and how Claude Code, Codex and the other launchable agents treat bracketed paste and Enter in their prompts.
   Use `~/pjs/refs` clones where present (see the refs-research-folder memory).
2. **Eon owners and path.** Trace how a request would flow (CLI → EONW request → Runtime → Orbit input write) through the current code and contracts (the EON_TERMINAL rule, the CLI and generation contracts, the Orbit attach and input contracts), and name the single owner of each step. Say whether Orbit's existing input path covers it or a new ORB-C or EONW request is needed, and whether this bumps EONW.
3. **Trust boundary.** Who may send (same user via the existing socket permissions; from inside an Eon terminal only, or any process of the user), and whether that's enough, compared with kitty's remote-control model. Size limits, and how control and escape bytes are handled.
4. **Safety defaults.** Paste by default (bracketed when the program enabled it) and submit only with an explicit flag. How Enter is sent to programs that ignore a newline inside a paste. What happens when the target is dead, stale, in another generation, or the wrong kind of terminal.
5. **Focus.** It never moves desktop, tab, pane or popup focus, and never shows a hidden popup. Confirm a hidden keep-alive popup can receive input.
6. **Contract draft.** Exact text for the new or amended EON-C (and ORB-C or EONW if needed): consumer, trigger, result, failures and exit codes, JSON output. Bring it to Lucca for approval.
7. **Implementation split.** Propose small implementation and proof beads, each one fresh-session sized, for Lucca to approve. Don't file them before the contract is approved.

## Scope

In scope: research, the reference gate record, and the contract draft and bead split above.

Out of scope: any product code, wire or contract edit before approval; reading back terminal output (a separate capability: tmux `capture-pane`, WezTerm `get-text`; mention it if the research shows the two belong together); and macros or key-chord sending beyond what a minimal contract needs.

## Acceptance

- The bead records the reference findings with sources and revisions, the owner and path trace, and the trust, safety and focus decisions with their reasons.
- Lucca approves, or revises, a contract draft and an implementation split.

## Verification

Planning route: bead state and the recorded research; no runtime profile refresh.

comments.text:
Research and contract draft (fo4p session, 2026-10-30, Eon edge 39e0a25). Planning only: no code, contract or AGENTS edit. Amends n8ic's provisional contract rather than starting a second one. Working copy: ~/.cache/eon-agents/claude-panesend-work/fo4p-draft.md; reference reports with file:line cites in the same folder (ref-tmux-wezterm.md, ref-kitty-zellij-herdr.md, ref-ntm-agents.md); trust-boundary options in ~/.cache/eon-agents/agent-parity/authorization-fo4p.md.

## 1. References (source read, nothing built or run)

Revisions: tmux 3.8 7f2a35ad; WezTerm e2a98e1b (2026-10-10); kitty v0.49.2 b2cb8712; Zellij v0.45.1 efd8fd5a; herdr 143bf5fd; ntm 0ea3fd92 (2026-10-29, cloned); Codex rust-v0.163.0 83086188; OpenCode 171dbd6a, OpenTUI 07f513ae, pi-mono 8bc94b19 (all cloned 2026-10-30); Claude Code from ~/pjs/refs/cc-docs and cc-changelog only (closed source; Grok too).

- tmux: `send-keys` turns each argument into key events, so its bytes depend on the key mode; under modifyOtherKeys 2 a bare LF or ^C is dropped (input-keys.c:452,684). `paste-buffer -p` brackets only when the app enabled mode 2004, converts LF to CR, and turns control bytes except TAB, LF, CR, BS and BEL into visible text (cmd-paste-buffer.c:52-124). Unnamed paste buffers are server-global, so concurrent callers race. With no `-t`, a command targets the session's active pane, not the caller's (cmd-find.c:945). A dead pane is a silent success for send-keys and an error for paste-buffer.
- WezTerm `cli send-text`: by default it sends a paste, bracketed per the live mode, with newlines rewritten only when not bracketed. It removes 200~/201~ markers in one pass and keeps every other ESC sequence (terminalstate/mod.rs:943). `--no-paste` writes raw bytes. With no pane given it targets the most recently focused pane. Size is unbounded. The socket is trusted by permissions alone.
- kitty `@ send-text`: escapes are expanded, text is sent in 2 KiB chunks with no filtering, `--bracketed-paste auto` strips 201~, and errors are never reported (send_text.py:72,90). Remote control is off by default. It accepts a socket peer only with the same UID, supports passwords with per-action allowlists, and prompts only for an unknown password. A per-process socketpair (`KITTY_LISTEN_ON=fd:N`) is a real per-terminal capability. kitty's own docs say none of this stops a same-user process.
- Zellij 0.45: `write`, `write-chars` and `paste` take `--pane-id`. Without it they target the human's last-typed pane. An unknown pane is a silent success with exit 0 (screen.rs:11652). Every write scrolls the human's focused pane to the bottom. The trust model is socket permissions only.
- herdr: a pane id is required, and an unknown one returns `pane_not_found`. `agent prompt` brackets per the mode, waits 300 ms, then sends Enter in the terminal's own encoding. It refuses empty text and blocked agents. Queues are bounded and report errors. The socket is 0600 with no peer check.
- ntm drives agents with `load-buffer` plus `paste-buffer -p -d` under a unique buffer name, or with `send-keys -l` in 4 KiB chunks. Enter is a separate key, sent after 100-150 ms and in practice twice (stage the text, wait 1 s, Enter, wait 500 ms, Enter). It then checks the screen with capture-pane and sends one rescue Enter if the composer still holds the text (session.go:2402-2530, 3453-3600). Its main failure modes are Enter swallowed during or after a paste, a dialog or autocomplete eating Enter, and the TUI not being ready yet.
- How the agent TUIs take a paste and Enter:
  - Codex brackets, sanitizes and collapses pastes over 1000 chars. A newline inside a paste never submits, and Enter right after the paste submits. Without bracketing, a burst heuristic turns an Enter within 120 ms of fast input into a newline (paste_burst.rs:157-352).
  - OpenCode inserts a paste asynchronously, and an early Enter submits a partial prompt (prompt/index.tsx:373,1099,1798).
  - Pi brackets. Without bracketing, CR submits at once.
  - Codex, OpenTUI and Pi all end the paste at the first `ESC[201~`.
  - Claude Code collapses pastes over 800 chars or 3 lines, and its docs say the model treats pasted text as material from elsewhere, not as instructions (cc-docs terminal-config.md.txt:326-328).
- Take:
  - Orbit decides bracketing from the live mode, as WezTerm, herdr and tmux `-p` do.
  - Sanitize the whole message, not chunks.
  - Enter is a separate key event in the terminal's own encoding, after a short delay (herdr, ntm).
  - Targets by explicit, never-reused ID; an unknown or ended target is a loud failure.
  - Never touch the person's focus or scroll (contrast Zellij).
  - Bounded queues that report errors.
- Reject:
  - Text sent as key events (tmux send-keys).
  - A global staging buffer.
  - Defaulting to the focused or active pane.
  - A raw mode that writes bytes unfiltered.
  - Silent success.
  - Passwords and per-send prompts: they add no protection against a same-user process, and prompts take focus.

## 2. Eon owners and request path (current code)

Path: CLI → EONW request (with `caller`) → Runtime resolves the target → Runtime's management lease → Orbit encodes against terminal state → PTY.

- **CLI** (runtime/crates/eon-runtime/src/cli): parses and validates TEXT, picks the supervisor by `EON_TERMINAL`, `--generation` or `--window` (EON-C10, docs/CONTRACTS.md:879-901), and maps failure codes to exits 0/1/2/3/4 (:864-871). Owner: Eon Runtime.
- **EONW** (eon-workspace-protocol v25): `Request { id, caller, action }` (v25.rs:205). No current Action carries terminal input. A new `Action` variant means EONW v26, or the next free version at landing; per EON-C28 and the bump checklist it is never an in-place amendment. Owner: Eon Runtime.
- **Runtime**: resolves the pane or popup ID to its Orbit run. `Popup` records always name a `session` and `endpoint` (v25.rs:393). Runtime already holds each terminal's exclusive management lease, with one request in flight; ProgramStatus is the precedent (sessions.rs:487-542, 797-800; ORB-C13, ORB-C15). It also holds the one read-only metadata observer (pane_labels.rs). Owner: Eon Runtime, for target resolution and send policy.
- **Orbit**:
  - Input encoding exists for the attached client: `Paste` brackets per `Mode::BRACKETED_PASTE` and, through libghostty `paste::encode`, replaces NUL, ESC, DEL and other unsafe bytes with spaces and rewrites LF to CR when not bracketed (orbit/src/input.rs:122-130; libghostty-vt paste.rs:129-145). `Key` uses libghostty's key encoder, kitty keyboard modes included (ORB-C5). `MAX_PASTE_BYTES` is 1 MiB.
  - That path belongs to the one ORBS attachment (ORB-C3). Management is limited to Acquire, Status, Stop and ProgramStatus, with 4 KiB messages (management.rs:11,149).
  - Owner: Orbit, for encoding and for enforcing that only the lease holder sends.
- **Venus** attaches only visible terminals: the shown popup, or the active tab's selected pane plus each other column's expanded pane (venus/src/model.rs:488-530). Collapsed panes, background tabs, hidden workspaces and hidden keep-alive popups have no attached client, so a path through Venus is ruled out. Venus is unchanged.

Conclusion: the existing input path does not cover a second party, so this needs:

- Orbit: a management request that carries one paste or one Enter key from the lease holder. That means management generation 4, a breaking change with no adapter, as generation 3 was in 2e7f6e6. Old live terminals stay with their own generation's supervisor, which does not offer send.
- Amendments to ORB-C13 and ORB-C5.
- EONW v26.
- A new EON-C.

## 3. Trust boundary (options in authorization-fo4p.md; recommendation, not a decision)

- **Orbit (A1).** Runtime is the only sender, over the exclusive lease, so Orbit enforces "one sender" with a mechanism it already proves, with no tokens and no new role.
- **Eon (B1).** Any same-user caller; `EON_TERMINAL` is validated when present, as an intent check (EON-C10 says so for `pane create -- COMMAND`).
- **No second factor (C0), plus one kill switch shared with reading.** `[agents] terminal_access`, decision 3, agreed with the p92 session. This matches tmux, WezTerm, Zellij and herdr, and kitty's own threat statement.
- **Sandbox note (with p92).** An agent sandbox that allows `AF_UNIX` connect reaches EONW, and `pane send` lets it type into an unsandboxed shell, which is stronger than `pane create -- COMMAND` only in convenience. It is unverified for the Codex and Claude Code sandboxes; Lucca should know before approving.
- **Deferred.** Per-terminal capabilities wait for a consumer that needs a boundary narrower than the UID (MCP, sandboxed agents); kitty's socketpair is the model for that.
- **Existing gap found:** any same-user process can `Hello` an unattached terminal over ORBS and type into it today. While it holds the attachment, Venus gets Busy when the person switches to that pane. This is outside this bead; I propose a separate Orbit bead.

## 4. Safety defaults

- **Paste only.** Orbit brackets when the program enabled it. TEXT must be UTF-8 and is refused, never rewritten, if it has ESC or another C0 control other than TAB, LF and CR, or DEL or a C1 control. Rewriting to spaces would hide the error from the sending agent. Special keys stay out of scope.
- **Submit only with `--enter`.** It is a separate Enter key event in Orbit's key encoding, sent after a delay (decision 4). A newline in TEXT never submits:
  - If the program has not enabled bracketed paste, Orbit refuses TEXT containing LF or CR (`unbracketed-newline`), since each line would run.
  - Single-line TEXT is still pasted.
  - The reply says whether the paste was bracketed, which doubles as a cheap readiness signal while an agent starts up.
- **Targets.**
  - A pane or popup ID from `eon workspace --json`; no default target and no "focused pane".
  - Unknown → exit 3 (`unknown-pane`, `unknown-popup`).
  - Ended pane → exit 1 `terminal-ended`, rejected and never queued.
  - A popup with no running terminal does not appear in the snapshot, so it is unknown.
  - A target in a hidden workspace is allowed and leaves the shown workspace unchanged.
  - A terminal of another generation: the existing supervisor selection and caller validation apply, and a supervisor without send answers as any older build does.
- **Size.** At most 64 KiB of TEXT (decision 5); larger → exit 2 `input-too-large`. Empty TEXT without `--enter` → exit 2.
- **Reconciliation.** The authorization answer is shared with orb-p92 (authorization-p92.md): same caller rule, scope, broker, lease and setting.
- **Concurrent typing.** Orbit writes each paste as one encoded write in its owner loop's order, so a person's keystrokes fall before or after it, never inside. This is a claim for Orbit's proof.

## 5. Focus

The send never mutates workspace state: no snapshot change, no Venus event, and the active tab, selection, shown popup, shown workspace and desktop focus stay as they are. It does not scroll the person's view (contrast Zellij). A hidden keep-alive popup keeps its Orbit run and Runtime's lease while hidden, so it receives input without being shown. That is inferred from the lease covering every live terminal, and it is the first thing the proof checks.

## 6. Contract draft (for Lucca's approval; IDs assigned at approval)

### New EON-C (next free, EON-C34 today): Agent terminal input

- **Consumer:** a person, script or AI agent running as the same local user, inside or outside an Eon terminal.
- **Trigger:** `eon pane send TARGET [--enter] [--json] [-- TEXT]`.
  - TARGET is a pane or popup ID from `eon workspace --json`.
  - TEXT is one operand. Without one, the command reads stdin when stdin is not a terminal; with neither, it sends only Enter (`--enter` required).
  - The usual `--generation`/`--window` targeting and `EON_TERMINAL` caller validation apply.
- **Result:**
  - Eon pastes TEXT into the target's terminal. Orbit brackets it when the program enabled bracketed paste.
  - With `--enter`, Eon then sends one Enter key, encoded for the terminal's current keyboard mode, after the configured delay.
  - Nothing else changes: the active tab, selected pane and column, shown popup, shown workspace, scroll position and desktop focus stay as they were. A hidden popup receives the input and stays hidden.
  - On success, exit 0. JSON reports `target`, `terminal` (`session-N`), `generation`, `window`, `bytes`, `bracketed` (bool, null when only Enter was sent) and `enter` (bool).
- **Important failures:**
  - Exit 2: TEXT is not UTF-8 (`invalid-text`), or contains ESC, other C0 controls except TAB, LF and CR, DEL or C1 controls (`invalid-text`); over 64 KiB (`input-too-large`); empty with no `--enter`.
  - Exit 3: unknown target (`unknown-pane`, `unknown-popup`) or invalid caller (existing codes).
  - Exit 1: `[agents] terminal_access = "none"` (`terminal-access-off`, nothing sent); target terminal ended (`terminal-ended`, never queued); TEXT has a newline and the program has not enabled bracketed paste (`unbracketed-newline`, nothing sent).
  - Exit 4: supervisor missing.
  - If the paste succeeds and the Enter fails, the reply says so and exits 1. The text stays in the program.
  - No failure changes focus or workspace state.
- **Owner:** Eon Runtime (CLI, validation, target resolution, Enter delay) over Orbit's lease input (ORB-C13/ORB-C5).
- **Boundary:** No special keys or chords beyond Enter, no raw bytes, no read-back (`orb-p92`), no wait for the program to consume the text, no per-terminal consent or capability, and no MCP or remote access.

### ORB-C13 amendment

Management also carries one bounded input request from the lease holder: a paste of up to 64 KiB, or one Enter key; the management message bound rises from 4 KiB to fit that request only. There is still one request in flight. The reply says whether the paste was bracketed, or refuses it as `unbracketed-newline` or as ended. This takes management generation 4.

### ORB-C5 amendment

- Consumer: also the management lease holder.
- Result: lease input is encoded exactly as an attached client's `Paste` and `Key(Enter)` are.
- Ordering: each lease paste is written whole, in owner-loop order with the attached client's input, never interleaved.
- A lease input needs no attachment and changes no presentation state.

### EONW v26

One new `Action`, `SendInput { target, input: Paste(String) | Enter }`, accepted with or without a caller, plus a reply carrying `bracketed`. Venus never sends it. The CLI composes `--enter` as a second request after the delay, so Runtime never sleeps on its request path, and an Enter-only send needs no TEXT.

## 7. Implementation split (proposed; filed only after the contract is approved)

1. **orb:** management generation 4 lease input (paste and Enter), with the newline and ended refusals and the bracketed reply. Amend ORB-C13 and ORB-C5. Real-PTY checks: bracketed and unbracketed programs; an unattached terminal; an attached client typing during a lease paste (no interleaving); ended terminal; over-size input.
2. **runtime:** EONW v26 `SendInput`, target resolution (pane, popup, hidden workspace), queueing behind an in-flight ProgramStatus, failure codes. Unit tests on the codec goldens and resolution.
3. **cli:** `eon pane send`, TEXT validation, stdin, the Enter delay and `[agents] terminal_access` (keys and defaults in docs/CONFIGURATION.md; the setting is shared with orb-p92, so whichever lands first owns it), JSON, plus docs/USAGE.md and CHANGELOG.
4. **proof:** one isolated installed dogfood observation.
   - From one pane, send a prompt with `--enter` to Codex in a background pane and to a hidden keep-alive Agent popup. Both submit, and the active tab, selection and hidden popup are unchanged.
   - A shell target writes a file, used as evidence until `pane read` exists.
   - Denial cases: an ended pane, an unbracketed newline, oversized input.

## 8. Decisions for Lucca (each with a recommendation)

1. **Path to Orbit:** Runtime is the only sender, over its exclusive management lease. Recommended: it reaches hidden and background terminals, never competes with Venus's attachment, and Orbit enforces it with a lease it already proves. Alternatives: an ORBS injector role (only the socket protects it) or a relay through Venus (fails when nothing is attached).
2. **Who may call:** any same-user process; `EON_TERMINAL` is validated when present. Recommended: matches tmux, WezTerm, Zellij, herdr and EON-C10's "intent, not security", and lets outside orchestrators work. The alternative is Eon terminals only, as for `pane create -- COMMAND`.
3. **Kill switch, no second factor:** one shared setting, `[agents] terminal_access = "window" | "none"`, default `"window"`, governing both read (orb-p92) and send. It is documented as a preference, not a security boundary; `none` refuses with `terminal-access-off`, exit 1. Recommended jointly with the p92 session: it satisfies the Configurability rule with one value, and passwords, consent or per-terminal capabilities protect nothing against a same-user process (kitty's docs agree), while prompts would take focus. Capabilities on kitty's socketpair model wait for MCP or sandboxed agents.
4. **Enter delay:** 300 ms by default, configurable. Recommended: herdr ships 300 ms for agent prompts, ntm needed 100 ms or more plus retries, and OpenCode inserts pastes asynchronously.
5. **Size limit:** 64 KiB of TEXT. Recommended: it covers any prompt, fits a raised management bound, and is easy to raise later, while 1 MiB would promise more than any consumer needs. Longer material goes in a file.
6. **Newline without bracketed paste:** refuse, with no override in the first slice. Recommended: otherwise each line runs, which breaks the approved "submit only with an explicit flag" default.
7. **Control bytes in TEXT:** refuse loudly instead of letting Orbit rewrite them to spaces. Recommended: the sending agent learns its text was wrong, and keys stay a separate, later feature.
8. **Claude Code marks long pastes as material from elsewhere.** Only a collapsed paste (`[Pasted text #N]`, over 800 chars or 3 lines) is marked "pasted from somewhere else", and Claude follows instructions inside it only where the typed part asks (cc-docs terminal-config.md.txt:326-328, checked). Shorter sends arrive as typed. Recommended: document that orchestrators keep a send under that size and point at a file for long material, and add no "typed" mode in the first slice; typed input hits burst heuristics and key-mode bytes (tmux's failures). Verify in dogfood.
9. **Existing gap:** today any same-user process can attach to an unattached terminal over ORBS and type, and Venus then gets Busy. File a separate Orbit bead. Recommended: it is real, small and independent of sending.
10. **Approve the contract draft (§6) and the four-bead split (§7).**

title: Deliver rounded pane frames enabled by default in Eon
description:
## Outcome
The installed full-Eon workspace presents the rounded pane borders proved by ven-pane-stack-chrome-suu. Per the user's decision on 2026-09-09, Eon exposes the persistent pane_frames boolean, defaulting to true so each pane has rounded borders; false disables the decorative frames.

## Contract routing and ownership
Consume exact accepted Venus VEN-C8/VEN-C19 behavior through EON-C1/EON-C2/EON-C3; preserve EON-C4, EON-C8/EON-C10 workspace actions, EON-C11 lifecycle and EON-C18 picker behavior. Eon owns component selection, product configuration and startup serialization. Venus retains layout/rendering/accessibility; Orbit retains terminal authority. Any product-setting contract is settled before configuration code.

## Prerequisites and reference gate
Prerequisite eon-desktop:ven-pane-stack-chrome-suu is closed and accepted at exact Venus source 5c23b0fe206fb2ed9e027603ae61ba366913cbe1, with visual proof and the strict --pane-frames true|false startup contract. A design conclusion alone is not a shipped visual proof.
Required before code: the complete Venus Bead and proof; current Eon manifest/locks, configuration and venus_command owners; EON-C8/EON-C18/EON-C19; current README appearance documentation and installed-profile rules. Recheck accepted Orbit/Venus revisions at activation. Reuse Eon's existing configuration pattern; no additional config owner.

## Acceptance Criteria
- Pin the exact accepted Venus artifact in the canonical graph and verify manifest/lock identity and affected builds.
- Document and consume pane_frames through the accepted startup boundary. Omitted configuration defaults to true and shows rounded borders around each pane; explicit true has the same behavior. Explicit false removes decorative frames while retaining pane handles, selection and keyboard focus. Invalid values fail before the new launch, preserving running work. This task does not implement frame rendering.
- Full Eon owns this workspace policy; EonTerm retains its absence of workspace chrome.
- Refresh affected installed profiles to the built artifacts while preserving existing supervisors/Sessions; report any restart needed for older windows without restarting them.
- One isolated installed Wayland observation covers the selected appearance, multiple/overflowing panes, pointer and keyboard focus, long labels, and the omitted default and both explicit setting values. Confirm picker layout and requested terminal-grid accounting still follow the accepted contracts.
- Update current README/config help, accepted user-visible changelog and exact proof metadata. Preserve fractional-scale, screen-reader and compositor qualifications not independently exercised.

## Scope boundary
Eon composition and the pane_frames product setting only. No child renderer edits, tab redesign, new layout model, arbitrary themes, live reload, unrelated upgrades or additional platform promise.

## Planning status
Added during the user-requested prime-beads pass on 2026-09-09 to close the missing Eon delivery handoff. Activated by the user on 2026-09-09. Implementation, affected profile refresh and isolated installed proof are complete; source remains uncommitted for review.

title: Add the inline value to the panel heading position setting: title and buttons on a straight edge, with and without fill
description:
## Why

Lucca chose two panel heading settings on 2026-11-10: where the title sits (notch or inline) and
whether the heading has a grey fill. eon-ve7dc holds his words and the drawings
(https://claude.ai/artifact/84vXbE9p889TT6RN7KJwDt) and delivers the fill setting for notches. The
bead this one depends on introduces the position setting with the "connected" value and holds the
table of all six looks. This bead adds the "inline" value, so it delivers the two inline looks.

His words on the drawings: pills on a straight edge (F) "cool, strong option"; title in the line (G)
"nice, but i'd also inline-in-border the close button. given the adjustment, also strong option". He
approved a small down-chevron for Hide in the unfilled inline look only ("ok"), because a `–` in a
gap in a horizontal line reads as a piece of the line.

Contract: as eon-ve7dc. Presentation is a feature; extend the VEN-C8/VEN-C18 wording,
docs/CONFIGURATION.md and venus/docs/PRESENTATION.md. The key follows EON-C19's rules.

## Evidence

- Position (eon-6ui6p) and the connected default (eon-j7ii2) are landed. Fill is still owned by open eon-ve7dc; this bead must wait for it to deliver both filled looks, then read the accepted code. This bead adds a value, not another setting.
- Collapsed panes already draw "text in a gap in a horizontal rule" (venus/src/render/chrome.rs,
  title types around :1118-1544 at 040cb56); reuse that treatment where it fits.

## Scope

In scope:
- A third value, "inline", for the existing panel heading position setting (notch, connected).
  The default stays "connected" (eon-j7ii2, closed). Apply with the existing explicit eon window reload path, as for the other values. No-reopen live repaint remains eon-nhec3, not an implicit wire change here.
- "inline": the panel's top edge is straight, with the card's usual corner radius. The title is
  centred on that edge at the left; each heading action (Hide; Stack Zoom and Close) is centred on
  the edge at the right.
  - Fill off: the title and each action sit in a gap in the edge, with nothing behind them. In this
    look only, Hide draws as a small down-chevron instead of `–`; its target, accessible name,
    tooltip and behaviour do not change.
  - Fill on: the title sits in a small filled capsule on the edge, in the unselected-tab fill, and
    each action in its own small capsule. Hide keeps `–`. Use the shared capsule and text tokens
    from eon-wuau8.1.
- One setting covers Stacks, popups, the Agents sidebar and dialogs alike.
- Same actions, targets, keyboard stops, focus feedback, accessible names and CLI paths in every
  combination; only the drawing changes.

Out of scope:
- The notch and connected looks (unchanged), the defaults, pane titles inside a Stack, colours.

## Acceptance

- With "notch" or "connected" (either fill value), rendering is pixel-identical to before this
  change.
- With "inline", no panel draws a notch or a curve in its top edge, in every panel kind (lone
  Stack, collapsed rows, zoomed, popup, Agents sidebar, dialog) and both fill values.
- The focus frame colour and width follow the edge on both sides of every gap or capsule.
- The bead records the terminal rows each panel kind gets in all six combinations. The drawings
  suggest the count does not change, since the title sits at about the same height; if inline costs
  or gains a row, say so and keep row fitting consistent with the drawn chrome.
- With fill off, title text keeps at least 4.5:1 contrast on the translucent terminal background at
  `background_opacity` 0.8 over a light wallpaper; if not, stop (see eon-0kq2c and eon-jg86j).

## Configurability (rule 6)

The key is the setting, documented in docs/CONFIGURATION.md with its default. The chevron is fixed:
it exists only to keep Hide legible on a line. Capsule fill, radius and padding stay fixed tokens.

## Verification

- Venus scene and render tests for both inline looks in every panel kind at scale 1, 1.125 and
  2; a config parse and reload test. Run through `nix develop -c eon-test` (docs/DEVELOPMENT.md).
- No capture gate: Lucca reviews in his own window after the profile refresh.

## Stop Conditions

- Stop if the plan shows both inline looks do not fit one session: deliver fill on (pills) here and
  ask the overseer for a follow-up bead for fill off (line and chevron).
- Stop if the gap treatment cannot reuse the collapsed-pane code without changing collapsed panes.
- Stop if a panel's heading and the collapsed pane rows inside it become hard to tell apart with
  fill off; report with a capture instead of inventing a new distinction.
- Stop if carrying the value to Venus changes the EONW codec without a version bump.

## Maintenance Notes

- CHANGELOG.md: new value for the panel heading position setting.

## Current ordering

Lucca’s 2026-11-11 default decision (comment 6517) is reflected above; this bead never chooses a new default. eon-ve7dc now owns fill for both notch and connected after the reordered eon-6ui6p landing; it is a real prerequisite for the two inline looks. Preserve both inline values in this one geometry slice unless its concrete plan shows it cannot fit a fresh session; the original split stop condition remains. Rebase the historical 040cb56 render citations before coding. Configuration format/wire changes still require their normal approval; no live repaint is claimed merely from replacement.
