title: Give Eon a beautiful, grouped, colorful CLI help screen
description:
## Problem and evidence

The user wants readable, organized, colorful, beautiful CLI help. On the installed `/nix/store/40bb9d041r46qiplaisd1rav5cl0w2ng-eon-0.1.0` artifact, `eon -h` exits 1 and prints the entire command grammar on one stderr line.

At Runtime revision `fb3c9c1b08c7a8c03ca4a8cc57628579c09bdeb4`, `crates/eon-runtime/src/cli.rs` has an `EON_USAGE` megastring and no help arm. Eon's `crates/eon/src/main.rs` prints returned errors. Runtime's `control.rs::write_stdout` already handles stdout; Eon's `crates/eon/tests/workspace_control.rs` checks executable behavior and Anima forwarding.

## Contract

Top-level `eon -h` and `eon --help` print useful multiline help to stdout, leave stderr empty, and exit 0. They work without a running workspace or valid user configuration and do not start Sessions, windows, or child tools, or create product configuration/runtime state.

Group current commands by user intent: launch/windows, attachment/lifecycle, tabs/panes/focus, inspection/configuration, and tools. Use clear headings, aligned descriptions, breathing room, a few copyable examples, and tasteful color. Cover supported command forms accurately, including the difference between `eon` and `eon run`, detach versus Stop, and `config-path` creating the configuration root. Keep the result readable at 80 columns and on dark/light terminal backgrounds; color must not carry meaning alone.

Use color when stdout is a terminal, except for `TERM=dumb` or a nonempty `NO_COLOR`. Redirected output has no ANSI escapes. `NO_COLOR` disables color; it need not disable other terminal emphasis.

Unknown or malformed top-level syntax stays a concise nonzero stderr error pointing to `eon --help`. Preserve operational errors and command behavior, including child help through `eon anima --help` and arguments after `--`; do not intercept help flags globally.

## Ownership, scope, and prerequisites

Eon owns the product help policy/content and installed acceptance; the existing Runtime CLI owns dispatch/output mechanics. Reuse those owners without copying the CLI or adding a second independently maintained command schema. Prefer existing helpers and standard-library formatting/terminal detection over a framework; any dependency must satisfy the repository's crate gate.

No unresolved prerequisite or duplicate help bead was found. Before implementation, rebaseline accepted component revisions and adopt any Runtime change through Eon's exact-pin workflow.

This bead covers Eon's top-level help and immediate usage-error path. EonTerm, managed aliases, child configuration, lifecycle policy, public command syntax apart from the two help flags, and supported platforms remain outside scope. Do not add a help hierarchy or color configuration setting. Broader CLI redesign needs a separate user scope decision.

## Reference gate

Follow the applicable instructions and matching `docs/REFERENCES.md` routes. Read the current dispatcher/output helpers, executable forwarding tests, and `docs/USAGE.md`. Before choosing formatting, inspect a comparable CLI help implementation and record its exact revision and the useful constraints, without adopting its framework by default.

Primary references checked during review: Rust's [IsTerminal documentation](https://doc.rust-lang.org/std/io/trait.IsTerminal.html) for terminal detection, and the [NO_COLOR convention](https://no-color.org/) for nonempty-variable semantics. Recheck against the implementation toolchain and record the chosen mechanism and falsifier.

## Acceptance checks

- Executable checks cover both flags, stdout/stderr/exit behavior, meaningful grouping and representative commands/examples, and absence of startup/configuration side effects. Avoid a literal whole-help mirror test.
- Redirected output is escape-free. A terminal observation verifies color, layout at 80 columns, and dark/light readability; terminal checks cover nonempty `NO_COLOR`, empty `NO_COLOR`, and `TERM=dumb`.
- Invalid syntax remains an error with help guidance. Existing child-help, forwarding, EonTerm, and alias behavior stays intact.
- Apply the affected-owner verification route from AGENTS.md and Eon's prepared-source/downstream route in `docs/DEVELOPMENT.md`. During implementation, align docs/CHANGELOG/README LOC, refresh the Eon profile, and verify the installed help without disturbing live Sessions.
close_reason: Accepted installed grouped/colorful help with exact-source Rust/Nix proof, preserved forwarding and live Sessions.

title: Make eon windows output and failing-child notices readable
description:
## Why

Small rough edges seen in lm9p.2 (Ubuntu 26.04, installed candidate, 2026-10-19) that make Eon's
CLI and notices harder to read. Presentation only.

## Evidence and items

1. Human `eon windows` prints "window 55566f03" followed by a raw generations JSON blob (the
   `component_report` with embedded newlines). Expected: a human summary per window, as `eon
   generations` prints. Contract: EON-C23 / EON-C10 (human and --json describe the same result).
2. A failing child shows only internal wording: CLI "terminal ended before its management lease was
   acquired"; the in-window footer notice reads "Eon workspace session-start: cannot create
   terminal Ready claim /run/us..." and is cut off at the window width. Expected: a bounded notice
   that says the terminal's command failed (and its exit status when known), readable in the
   window. Contracts: VEN-C4 (bounded truthful notices), EON-C10. The wedge itself is the separate
   runtime bead.
3. Record only (decide, maybe no change): `eon workspace --json` encodes directory and endpoint
   paths as arrays of byte values; scripts reading it need to decode them. If kept for non-UTF-8
   safety, document it in docs/USAGE.md "CLI commands".

Not included: Starship's SSH hostname emoji renders as a missing-glyph box on hosts without an
emoji font; that is host font policy, noted on lm9p.2 only.

## Scope

Eon CLI human formatting and the session-start notice text; Venus notice layout only if the
truncation is Venus's. Docs alignment for any changed output. No protocol or JSON shape change
without Lucca's approval.

## Acceptance

- `eon windows` human output shows readable per-window lines; --json unchanged.
- A failing configured shell produces a notice naming the failure that fits or wraps in a 640 px
  wide window (one isolated installed screenshot).
- Item 3 decided and recorded (doc line or no change with reason).
close_reason: eon windows prints human per-window lines; failing startup names the command's exit status and the Venus notice wraps to 3 lines (640 px installed screenshot); eon workspace --json prints UTF-8 paths as strings, byte arrays otherwise (EON-C10 updated).

title: Rebuild the README around the agent workspace and hand user docs to eonterm.com
description:
## Decision
Lucca, 2026-10-15: rebuild the README around the agent-workspace story and keep it short, starting
slice 1 now. The same
day Lucca decided that eonterm.com owns Eon's user documentation (eon-site `eon-site-4p9`), whose
follow-up asks Eon to remove or redirect its GitHub user docs and update the README and the
`AGENTS.md` documentation rules. This bead owns that Eon-side follow-up too.

## Contract
- Consumer: a first-time visitor to the GitHub repository.
- Result: within a minute they learn what Eon is (terminals that survive closing the window, built
for long-running agents and project work), install it with one pinned command, run it, and find the
full guides. Every claim matches the current release; planned or unproven behavior is labelled.

## Evidence (edge 068efcb)
`README.md` (133 lines) leads with "native Wayland workspace" and covers Accelerando glyph flags,
quota chip details, the bar version label and cache trust details before or alongside first use.

## Slices
1. README rewrite: lead with terminals that survive, the agent workflow (Agent popup, quota,
persistent sessions) and one install command; then first run, limits and links. Move animation and
glyph options, quota details and cache setup into the existing guides. Do not advertise agent
terminal-control commands until they ship.
2. After eon-site `eon-site-4p9` publishes its docs: remove or redirect `docs/USAGE.md`,
`docs/CONFIGURATION.md` and the user parts of `docs/DISTRIBUTION.md` to eonterm.com, point the README
there, and update the documentation rules through `.agent-protocols.local.md` (render, do not edit
`AGENTS.md`). Maintainer docs stay in the repository.

## Prerequisites
Slice 2 waits for eon-site `eon-site-4p9` (separate tracker, so not a Beads dependency). The
documentation-rule wording is Lucca's policy; get approval for it.

## Acceptance
Docs-only proof: changed Markdown paths and diff, every link resolves, claims checked against the
current release tag; render check when `AGENTS.md` changes. No runtime profile refresh.

## Stop boundary
No product behavior, contract or install-path change. Website changes stay in eon-site.

title: A reap error on a terminal that was never stopped still ends the supervisor
description:
## Report

Residual found by eon-d8 while fixing eon-tab-close-kills-supervisor-7iap (2026-10-23). After 7iap,
a terminal whose stop failed stays in its tab, and the main-loop reap logs its error once and keeps
the supervisor running. But a reap error on a terminal that was never sent Stop still ends the
supervisor, as before 7iap. That covers a terminal that exits on its own and whose ended record is
then corrupt, missing, or unreadable: the main loop's `reap_finished_sessions` returns the error
with `?` (runtime/crates/eon-runtime/src/sessions.rs and the supervisor main loop).

No incident has hit this path yet. It is the same failure class as 7iap: one terminal's bad state
ends every tab and the window.

Approved by Lucca, 2026-10-23 ("create the beads", answering the overseer's item 10: file it, P2,
outside 7iap's scope).

## Change

Make a reap error for any one terminal local to that terminal. Log it, mark or remove the
terminal in its tab, report it (EON-C10 failure kind), and keep the supervisor and other tabs
running. Reuse 7iap's containment rather than adding a second path.

## Contract

EON-C8 and EON-C10. Check whether the current text already covers a natural exit; bring any
wording change to Lucca first.

## Acceptance

- A Runtime red/green test: a terminal exits on its own with a corrupt or vanished ended record,
  and the supervisor and other tabs keep running, with the failure logged.
- One isolated observation, if the change reaches installed behavior differently from 7iap's.

## Prerequisites

eon-tab-close-kills-supervisor-7iap landed (it adds the containment this reuses).
close_reason: Runtime red/green plus isolated installed observation with eon-7vb4's batch

comments.author: lucca
comments.text: Residuals from eon-tab-close-kills-supervisor-7iap (landed in abe8d07), recorded here at eon-overseer's request (eon-7iap, 2026-10-23). (a) The main-loop reap spares only a terminal whose Stop failed: runtime/crates/eon-runtime/src/supervisor.rs:1078 (RunningSession::stop_failed, sessions.rs:947, which is true only once stop_sent is set at sessions.rs:1425). A tab close can fail before Stop is written, for example 'terminal did not answer program status before stop' (sessions.rs:1457). Then stop_sent stays false, and a later reconcile error on that terminal still ends the supervisor through 'finished => finished?' (supervisor.rs:1088). That is the same class as this bead. (b) For a failed-stop terminal whose lease has closed but which never reconciles (record gone while Orbit still runs, endpoints never removed, or a child that is never reaped), every reap_finished_sessions call, from the main loop and from each control request, re-enters session_finished and can block up to SESSION_START_TIMEOUT (5 s) in wait_and_finalize_tombstone (sessions.rs). The note is logged once, but nothing caps the retry. Orbit bounds its own linger, so this is unlikely.

comments.author: lucca
comments.text:
Decisions (eon-hfzr, 2026-10-23).
- Contract: EON-C8 and EON-C10 stay as written (eon-overseer agreed, 2026-10-23). C8's "Ended terminals leave no dead pane" means a confirmed end. A terminal whose end does not reconcile is not confirmed ended, so it keeps its pane, as a failed stop does.
- EON-C10 reporting: the main-loop reap has no requester, so the failure is logged once in the diagnostic log. A later request that touches that terminal, such as a tab or pane close, returns that request's own failure code ('tab-close-failed', 'pane-close-failed'). No new failure kind is needed.
- Containment covers every session_finished error in reap_finished_sessions: a natural exit, residual (a) (a close that failed before Stop was written) and a failed stop. Integrity errors such as 'terminal final record does not match the acquired run' no longer end the supervisor either, which matches the bead's "any one terminal". Residual (a) has no test of its own: it reaches the same general Err arm as the natural-exit case the test covers.
- Residual (b): once a failure is reported, session_finished retries with a zero wait, so one terminal cannot stall the loop or requests. A close retry of such a terminal also no longer waits; it fails at once and can be retried. Retries that fail through operation_timeout keep its generic "exceeded five seconds" text.
- Known limit: such a terminal cannot be closed while its end does not reconcile. The close fails, and the pane stays until a reap reconciles it. Before this change, the whole supervisor ended.
- Accepted gap: a transient picker whose stop fails, or whose end does not reconcile, still ends the supervisor when Eon Desktop exits (supervisor.rs cancel_transient_popups, stop_owned_session `?`). Containment for it was drafted during review and taken out by eon-overseer's call (option 1), because it needs its own test with a workspace-picker fixture and possibly EON-C18 wording. It is filed as eon-popup-cancel-failure-ends-supervisor-k9sx. hfzr does not make that case worse: before hfzr, the same picker ended the supervisor earlier, in the reap.
- Installed proof: batch observation with eon-orbit-stop-not-reaped-7vb4 (eon-overseer, 2026-10-23); no separate isolated observation for hfzr.

comments.author: lucca
comments.text:
Proof (eon-hfzr, 2026-10-23). The change has three parts:
1. supervisor.rs reap_finished_sessions: 7iap's containment arm now catches every session_finished error, not only those of terminals whose stop failed. The terminal stays in its tab, the failure is logged once ('stays in its tab after a failed stop' or 'stays in its tab until its end reconciles'), and the supervisor and other tabs keep running.
2. sessions.rs: the flag stop_failure_reported is renamed reap_failure_reported. Once it is set, session_finished retries with a zero wait instead of SESSION_START_TIMEOUT (residual (b)).
3. One CHANGELOG entry.

Test: supervisor::tests::a_terminal_whose_own_exit_cannot_be_reconciled_stays_only_in_its_tab.
- session-1 exits on its own (status 7) and its final record is then made invalid.
- session-3's lease is closed while its run still holds its Live record.
- session-2 stays healthy.
- The reaps return Ok, every terminal stays tracked, and each failure is logged once.
- A retry after the reported failure returns in under 1 s.
- Once the record is valid again, session-1 ends with status 7. session-3 reconciles as owner-lost after its Orbit's worker is killed. session-2 then stops cleanly.

Red, on the tree with the test and without the fix:
- Restoring the old match arm makes the reap return Err with the record-validation error, which is the error that ends the supervisor's main loop.
- Restoring a full SESSION_START_TIMEOUT wait on retries fails the under-1 s retry assertion.

Green: `nix develop -c eon-test -p eon-runtime` gives 86 passed, 0 failed, 1 ignored. `cargo fmt -p eon-runtime --check` and `cargo clippy --locked -p eon-runtime --all-targets -- -D warnings` are clean. Environment: x86_64 Linux, worktree at base efa9565, final tree 58d48cacba8ed4f63e0a0c8709b22f2079950c52; the Claude reviewer reran these checks and the tree did not change.

Installed proof: batch observation with eon-orbit-stop-not-reaped-7vb4, after both land and eon-overseer refreshes the profile.

Review ledger: 2 Codex passes and 3 Claude rounds.
- Codex round 1 on e44e6c2 found 2 blocking items. (i) The retry bound was untested; fixed by the closed-lease terminal and the timed retry. (ii) A retained picker could still end the supervisor through cancel_transient_popups on detach; containment was drafted, then taken out by eon-overseer's call (option 1) and filed as eon-popup-cancel-failure-ends-supervisor-k9sx.
- Claude round 1 on e44e6c2 had no code findings. It asked for the contract judgement and EON-C10 reporting to be recorded, which the decisions comment does.
- Claude round 2 on f726306 blocked the popup containment on scope (no test, EON-C18 wording); resolved by the same option 1.
- Claude round 3 on 58d48ca found nothing blocking. Its 3 optional nits were not applied: merge the CHANGELOG entry with 7iap's, add a close-retry assertion, and add local time imports.
- Codex's narrow re-check of e44e6c2..58d48ca found nothing blocking.

comments.author: lucca
comments.text:
Installed batch observation (eon-orbit-stop-not-reaped-7vb4 + eon-reap-error-unstopped-hfzr), 2026-10-23 18:27 -03. Profile refreshed by eon-overseer from edge b1143190 (clean tree): /nix/store/ddxhzscqiqfysjas2ha6qrhkgk3h32d3-eon-0.1.1, run by that exact store path. x86_64 Linux, one isolated window: private headless Sway (pixman), env -i, private HOME and runtime dirs. Driver ~/.cache/eon-agents/orbit-7vb4/iso/observe.sh; evidence in iso/out1 (steps.txt, supervisor-logs, tracer.txt, workspace JSON). Each terminal's shell was held.py, which calls prctl(PR_SET_PTRACER_ANY) and then execs /bin/sh under the same PID.
(1) 7vb4: tab t2's shell (PID 1518888) was ptrace-seized, and `eon tab close t2 --json` ran. The tracer released the child 3.5 s after the close began; the child was then in state Z (killed, but not reapable by Orbit), and its exit status was SIGKILL. The close exited 0 after 3.55 s, and the supervisor logged "closed tab t2 in 3501 ms". Afterwards the workspace lists only t1 (session-1), and the supervisor runs on. Before this change, Orbit removed the record about 2.5 s in and the close failed (the incident).
(2) hfzr: tab t3's live record (session-3.sock.record) was overwritten in place with 7 bytes of garbage (same inode, mode 600), and its shell got SIGKILL. The supervisor logged once: "terminal session-3 stays in its tab until its end reconciles: invalid terminal record …: truncated management value". 10 s later `eon workspace --json` exited 0, listing t1 (session-1) and t3 (session-3); the supervisor and window kept running. The cleanup's exact-generation `eon stop` reported stop-failed for session-3, as expected for its deliberately corrupted record; the isolated leftovers were stopped by exact PID (processes whose environment had the private HOME or runtime dir), and the private dirs were removed.
Both observations pass. 7vb4 is closed; hfzr is closed by its acceptance (Runtime red/green recorded earlier plus this installed observation).

title: Reattach a window detached under an older generation after an upgrade
description:
## Report

Found during the eon-n77e reference gate (2026-10-22). Lucca confirmed filing it as P1 ("do it", relayed by the overseer).

`eon window attach ID` attaches only the exact current generation (windows.rs:176-191, generation.rs:430-450). After a profile upgrade, a window detached under the previous generation cannot be reattached from the new CLI. Its terminals keep running, and the user cannot get back to them except through internals.

Under the eon-n77e shape, one window holds several workspaces, so a stranded window strands all of them.

## Contract

EON-C23 and EON-C11. A detached window from an older, still-running generation can be re-presented after an upgrade. Where re-presenting is impossible, the CLI and the listing say so, and they name a supported way to recover or stop it. Nothing is stranded silently.

## Constraints

- Keep exact generation checks. EON-C11 and the trust boundary validate the generation, the EONW version and the component graph (`validate_runtime`, supervisor.rs:330-365).
- Eon code must not construct Nix store paths or query the store (AGENTS.md).
- A fix probably asks the old supervisor to present its own Venus, which it already owns. Record the gate: this crosses a lifecycle boundary.

## Acceptance

1. Detach a window.
2. Upgrade the profile.
3. `eon window attach ID` re-presents it, or exits non-zero with a message that names the recovery.
4. `eon windows` shows its generation.

## Verification

Installed observation across one real profile upgrade, plus focused tests. Codex on every code change.
close_reason: Window attach reaches older generations, through their own recorded eon when needed; ended windows listed as ended. Proven on the installed product in isolation (see proof comment).

comments.author: lucca
comments.text: Evidence (overseer eon-a8, 2026-10-23 ~02:00 -03, profile at edge 6bd4f02, g1-8e4e55026979eb685fab1e4363283c8f): `eon windows` lists five independent windows (5a3c52a9, a196e37b, ac23119e, cea691e2, d787e55f). Their runtime dirs under /run/user/1000/eon/w/ date from 2026-10-22 10:02 to 20:37, with empty generations/ dirs and supervisor locks from older generations (g1-48059d2c…, g1-992ed67e…, g1-a74d2b04…, g1-1a68d290…). Each prints `current g1-8e4e… dead terminals=0 / attach=false generation has not started`. The listing attributes long-ended windows to the current generation and says 'has not started'; it should say the window ended, or prune it. Fold this into this bead's listing behavior ('Nothing is stranded silently'), or split it out if it is cheaper alone.

comments.author: lucca
comments.text: Evidence from eon-c9's mno4 reference gate (2026-10-23): every control call runs prepare_generation_runtime (runtime/crates/eon-runtime/src/supervisor.rs:671), which creates an empty generations/<cli-build> directory in the window's runtime dir, even when that build has no supervisor there. That is the source of the 'empty g1-00d891 dir' evidence, and it feeds this bead's misleading 'has not started' listing. Fix it here, not in mno4: control calls should not create a generation directory for a build that isn't running.

comments.author: lucca
comments.text:
Reference gate (eon-90, 2026-10-23, edge 6ee477a). Behavior: after an upgrade, `eon window attach ID` re-presents a window started by an older build, or names how to recover it; the listing does not show ended windows as current. Owners: Eon Runtime owns generation selection, discovery and Present (EON-C11) and window identity (EON-C23). The old supervisor owns its Venus and terminals.

Read: runtime windows.rs window_action/list_windows, generation.rs attach_generation/inspect_generation, supervisor.rs probe_supervisor/validate_runtime/present_at, control.rs protocol_endpoint_failure, EON-C11, EON-C23, EON-C28 Upgrades/Boundary. Live: window afacc679 runs g1-8e4e (EONW 18). The profile eon (EONW 19) attach fails with "generation g1-f501… has not started", exit 1. The v18 CLI sees the generation as attach=true, but `window attach` targets only the CLI's own generation. Supervisor exe is .eon-wrapped. Its environment comes from the bin/eon wrapper, so a recorded `eon` must be the wrapper (session bin `eon`, d56c373), never /proc exe.

Comparables:
- tmux 3.8 7f2a35ad: PROTOCOL_VERSION 8 per message (tmux-protocol.h:23, proc.c:134-177). On mismatch the client prints "protocol version mismatch (client N, server M)" and exits 1 (client.c:659-667). ls, attach and kill-server all fail. Nothing records or execs the old binary. Recovery is the old binary or killing the PID by hand (CHANGES:2608).
- zellij v0.45.1 efd8fd5a: the socket dir is versioned by contract (consts.rs:26,90-91). Same-contract sessions interoperate across versions (CHANGELOG 0.44 #4439). ls only probes the current contract dir and silently omits the rest (sessions.rs:19-44). No mismatch message.
- wezterm e2a98e1b: the server reports executable_path in its codec version response (codec/src/lib.rs:617-622, sessionhandler.rs:864-870). On a codec mismatch the client says to install the same version on both ends (wezterm-client client.rs:64-77). It does not re-exec the old binary.

Kept constraints: exact generation/EONW/graph checks; no store-path construction or store query; no PID kill fallback.
Rejected: silent omission like zellij (violates "nothing stranded silently"); a bare mismatch error like tmux (names no recovery); deriving bin/eon from /proc exe (constructs a store-layout path).
Decision: pending Lucca on choices 1-5 (relayed via overseer). Candidate: record the build's own `eon` like wezterm's executable_path, but as a runtime-dir record, not an EONW field, so older-EONW CLIs can read it, and optionally delegate attach to it. Check: focused tests plus one installed observation across a real profile upgrade.

comments.author: lucca
lucca
comments.text:
Decision (Lucca, 2026-10-23, relayed by overseer eon-a8 with quote "agree to everything" to the numbered list "1. yes; 2. C; 3. yes; 4. (a), with folder removal as a follow-up bead; 5. yes; 6. approve eon-90's EON-C23 and EON-C11 wording"):
1. `eon window attach ID` targets the window's live generation: current if live, else its one other live generation; several -> fail listing them.
2. C: each eon supervisor records its own `eon` wrapper (session bin eon) as a symlink in its 0700 generation dir; attach of a generation this eon cannot present (other EONW or component graph) runs the recorded `eon attach GENERATION`; without a record it exits 1 naming the generation, its Eon/EONW versions and that its own build can attach or stop it.
3. Delegation lives in attach_generation, so `eon attach GENERATION` gains it too.
4. (a) `eon windows` lists a window with no live supervisor as ended, not as current; removing ended window dirs is a follow-up bead (overseer files it).
5. Stop of incompatible generations stays as today (no delegated Stop).
6. EON-C23 Result and EON-C11 wording approved as proposed by eon-90 (see the overseer message text recorded in the reference gate comment thread).
Verification: full affected Rust and Nix surfaces, converge plus Codex, installed observation across a real upgrade planned with the overseer.

comments.author: lucca
comments.text:
Approved contract wording (item 6 of the 2026-10-23 decision, as proposed by eon-90):

EON-C23 Result, replacing "`eon window attach ID` presents its current generation after detach":
"`eon window attach ID` presents the window's live generation, whichever Eon build started it. When this `eon` cannot present it (another EONW version or component graph), the command runs the `eon` of the build that started it, as that generation recorded it, to present it. When no such record exists, it exits 1 and names the generation, its Eon and EONW versions, and that the build that started it can attach or stop it. `eon windows` shows each window's live generation, and lists a window with no live supervisor as ended instead of as the current generation."

EON-C11 Result, added line:
"A generation records the `eon` executable of the build that started it, an opaque launch input, so a later build can name or run it; `eon attach GENERATION` delegates to it when this build cannot present that generation."
Boundary unchanged: no store-path construction, no Nix query, no cross-EONW codec.

comments.author: lucca
comments.text:
Wording amendment (2026-10-23, relayed by overseer eon-a8 under Lucca's same-day standing approval, quoted: "i give you auto-approval to everything, until 700k / but the focus is landing the sidebar / our mission is: happy users"): in the EON-C23 no-record sentence, "its Eon and EONW versions" becomes "the versions it reports". Reason: when EONW differs the old supervisor answers only with a failure frame in its own EONW, so the new eon learns the EONW number but not the Eon version.
Installed proof plan approved by the overseer: one isolated slot after convergence. B1 = candidate, B2 = B1 plus a comment-only runtime change. (a) B1 window new; the generation dir records eon -> B1 session bin eon; detach. (b) B2 eon windows lists it; B2 eon window attach re-presents it. (c) run the recorded link: attach GEN. (d) fallback: a window started by r18mya (EONW 18, no record); B2 eon window attach exits 1 with the recovery text. Nix: nix build .#eon plus the managed-command-path check; full sandboxed eon-test -p eon -p eon-runtime on the final tree.

comments.author: lucca
comments.text:
Accepted gaps (eon-90, 2026-10-23), from slice 2 review round 1:
- Trust: any process running as the same user can replace a generation's `eon` record and redirect delegated attach. The record lives in the user's 0700 runtime directory, and the check requires a symlink owned by that user with an absolute target. A same-UID process can already change the user's shell startup files or the profile, so the record grants no new privilege. Ownership is not build provenance.
- Rollback: an Eon build from before this change removes a dead generation's directory with a plain remove_dir. That fails on a directory holding the `eon` record, so after a rollback the older `eon` keeps listing a crashed newer generation as dead. The newer build and the generation's own supervisor do remove it. This only matters across versions.
- Loop guard: a delegated attach carries EON_ATTACH_DELEGATED=<generation>, and it never delegates that generation again. Otherwise an unwrapped dev build started inside an Eon terminal would inherit the outer build's EON_SESSION_BIN and record the outer build's `eon`.

title: Restore sessions after a machine restart
description:
## Decision
Lucca, 2026-10-15: plan restoring a workspace after a machine restart, honestly labelled as a
restore with fresh processes, not terminal survival. Design and contract are not chosen yet.

## Contract (provisional)
After a machine restart, a full-Eon user can restore their last workspace: tabs with their launch
directories, pane order and the tab popups, started as new terminals. Agent popups restart through
the client's own resume command. The product never presents this as process, scrollback or terminal
state survival.

## Open design decisions
Automatic or opt-in restore; what is saved (layout and directories only, never arbitrary pane
commands); where and when it is written and how stale or partial state fails; privacy of saved
paths; how it interacts with generations and independent windows.

## Historical evidence (edge 5ae4e0f; relocate by contract ID)
- Restarting the machine ends live terminals (README "Status and limits"; EON-C15 at

## Stop boundary
No process checkpointing, scrollback persistence or remote state.

no-scrollback boundary. Ask Lucca in the design step; resume-by-ID must also be decided and

Requirement from eon-c8ytm (upgrade policy accepted by Lucca 2026-10-31; contract 'Upgrades within 0.x' approved the same day). Saved workspace state is Eon's first durable state that outlives a generation, so its design must meet policy B:

(3) A non-additive change writes a new versioned file name and migrates on read from the newest older file present. It never rewrites or deletes a file an older supported build still reads, so a Nix rollback, or an older live window beside a newer one, finds its own file intact.

title: Decide the session restore design and draft its contract
description:
## Why
Parent: eon-reboot-restore-im8y (Restore workspaces after a machine restart). The parent's
2026-10-27 comment asks for a split at start: design and contract first (stop for Lucca), then a
save slice and a restore slice. This child is the design and contract step. No product code.

## Deliverable (recorded on this bead)
1. Reference gate (AGENT-RULES Contract-Driven Method; consequential: new persisted state and a
   lifecycle). Inspect at recorded revisions:
   - tmux-resurrect and tmux-continuum (~/pjs/refs/tmux-resurrect, ~/pjs/refs/tmux-continuum);
   - Zellij session resurrection (~/pjs/refs/zellij-v0.45.1);
   - herdr (layout snapshots, agent resume after restart; ~/pjs/refs/herdr and
     ~/pjs/refs/competitor-audit-2026-10/herdr.md:21,44,55);
   - herdr-core kept terminals that return as fresh shells in their last folder
     (~/pjs/refs/herdr-core, competitor-audit herdr-core-app.md:55,217);
   - docs/REFERENCES.md TUIOS route (restore is never presented as survival).
   Record what is kept and rejected, with reasons.
2. Owner and data trace: Eon Runtime owns saved workspace state and restore; Orbit and Venus are
   unchanged. Name the exact Runtime structures serialized (workspaces per EON-C33, tabs, launch
   directories, pane order, tab popups, per-window sidebar visibility) and what is never saved
   (arbitrary pane commands, scrollback, environment).
3. Answers, each with a recommendation for Lucca:
   a. automatic or opt-in restore, and its configuration key and default (docs/CONFIGURATION.md);
   b. the `eon` CLI path for restore (Humans and Agents rule 5), for example
      `eon workspace restore [--json]`, and the window action if any;
   c. where and when the file is written (path under the state dir, write cadence, atomic
      rename), and privacy of saved paths;
   d. how agent popups resume (the client's own resume command, product.rs agent defaults;
      related eon-agent-popup-resume-p681);
   e. generations (EON-C11) and independent windows: which window's state wins;
   f. the read path for same, older, newer and corrupt files under the upgrade policy B
      recorded on the parent (2026-10-31 comment from eon-c8ytm): version header, additive
      evolution, unknown fields kept, newer file ignored with a warning, fixtures in the
      configuration and state corpus (eon-embg6).
4. Contract draft: a new EON-C (or amendments to EON-C15 and EON-C33), with honest labelling
   text ("restored with fresh processes"), and confirmation or revision of the two sibling
   slices (save, restore).
5. The cheapest falsifier for the design.

## Acceptance
- The bead records the references with revisions, the owner trace, answers a-f with reasons, the
  contract draft and the falsifier.
- Lucca approves or revises the contract draft and the answers; his words and the date are
  recorded on the parent.

## Verification
Planning route: bead state and recorded research; no runtime profile refresh.

## Scope boundary
No code, no contract text in docs/CONTRACTS.md (it lands with the slice that makes it true). No
process checkpointing, scrollback persistence or remote state.

## Stop conditions
Stop for Lucca before any contract or code change.


## Prerequisite reconciliation

Lucca's 2026-11-04 10:31 UTC "agree" (relayed by eon-overseer and recorded in the earlier comment) unblocks this design from eon-hyil8 (session ownership and naming decision). Proceed on today's window-owned workspaces. The design must state how its saved layout and restore flow carry over when sessions become supervisor-wide under eon-8mw1v (deferred sessions epic): save sessions rather than windows where that costs little now, without implementing the deferred model. Preserve the existing save/restore acceptance, versioned-file safety and reference questions. No new aliases, shims or compatibility layer is approved here.

## Current reconciliation

The parent requires persistent EON-C38 IDs, .11 approved checkpoint text and one shared layout serializer, not the deferred global-session model. Proposed CLI spelling is eon session restore; exact syntax stays for design approval. At dcaef1c session_registry.rs owns identity only and uses deny_unknown_fields. Explain how shared checkpoint representation meets durable policy B, including unknown-field retention and migration into a new filename, despite .6.1 having a different lifetime/private runtime directory. Keep per-window sidebar visibility and same/older/newer/corrupt-file questions. Flow lazy shells and read-only restored history remain suggestions; scrollback persistence is unapproved. Resume-by-ID must not duplicate an agent conversation. No code or contract edits before Lucca's approval.

title: Attribute receiver and Venus render scheduling tails
description:
## Why

The completed bounded-drain diagnosis retained long input tails after Orbit had handed off a complete frame and after Venus had decoded it. Identify the scheduling segment and an actionable remedy. The overseer's 2026-11-11 03:23:55Z decision places this P3 follow-up outside the v0.2.0 gate and leaves the current drain candidate unlanded with its relative-tail acceptance condition intact.

## Evidence

- /home/lucca/.cache/eon-agents/eon-perf-research-work/bead-drain/28A-partial-results.md contains ten measured direct launches after two warmups and the qualified native full-observer pair.
- The worst candidate concurrent-host sample is 16.604056 ms, including 15.561856 ms after an observed empty-queue Orbit handoff. A minimal-observer concurrent-host sample is 11.413779 ms with 9.629129 ms after handoff.
- The worst candidate typing sample takes 34.361737 ms from last input ingress to post-render, including 21.808888 ms from decoded frame to render begin.
- /home/lucca/.cache/eon-agents/eon-perf-research-work/bead-drain/29-trade-off.md records losses, gains and limitations. The native cohort stopped on an inconclusive baseline visual interval of 128.325165–307.069880 ms around a 250 ms bound. The post-render marker is not a visual completion bound.
- venus/src/transport.rs:1268 traces frame_read. venus/src/application.rs:5244 traces render_begin and :5472 traces present_revision. These anchors were checked at dcaef1c; measurements and candidate identity remain those of research base fdb7a72.

## Scope

Attribute receiver availability/read/decode scheduling and Venus decoded-frame-to-render scheduling with existing canonical counter, revision, PID and marker observations. Preserve ORB-C4 and VEN-C1 ownership, ordering and complete-frame semantics. Keep this a bounded research slice with a measured explanation and one concrete remedy proposal. Publication pacing, wire changes, renderer framework replacement and throughput redesign remain owned by their existing beads.

## Acceptance

- A fresh agent can reproduce a qualified tail or report that it did not recur, retaining every failure and ambiguity.
- Explain the handoff-to-receiver and decoded-to-render segments using same-sample observations, per-launch distributions and matched controls. Retain overlap bounds when sender stamps follow receiver stamps.
- Distinguish thread CPU, descheduling, delivery, render scheduling and observation delay only where the data supports it.
- Record one actionable remedy with its owner and a falsifiable check, or the specific unresolved evidence needed to choose it.
- Preserve the full native visual oracle and its inconclusive results alongside trace endpoints.

## Implementation Notes

1. Prime current Orbit and Venus rules and the cited reports. Reuse sealed source/probe metadata from the work directory as reference, checking identities before reuse.
2. Start with raw ../drain-eio-measurements from the report directory. Inspect receiver scheduling and the matching Venus event/render path before adding counters.
3. For any fresh measurement, obtain a quiet grant and drain earlier heavy jobs before timing. Use isolated headless Sway and explicit Orbit selection or verified literal wrappers.
4. The TCPU sensor peaked at 102.05°C in this run. Log hardware throttling indicators along with temperature, frequency and AC in a future run and correlate them to sample intervals.
5. Keep the direct receiver and native client observations distinct. Their endpoints and scheduling paths differ.

## Verification

Use the existing direct canonical counter/revision probe and native typing/burst response probe. Retain 10+2 direct launches, full/minimal observer controls, complete sequences, loss counters and independent native repeats when making a comparable performance claim. Reject ambiguous joins and retain the 250 ms native qualification. Record exact artifacts, workload, CPU affinity, timing distributions and raw paths.

## Stop Conditions

A changed contract or an expanded implementation outcome goes back to the owning scope decision. Preserve data if qualification, trace identity or join checks fail. A failed or inconclusive visual result must remain visible in the report.

## Maintenance Notes

Any future attached-drain change must carry the continuation EIO yield repair or prove equivalent prompt publication. The preserved candidate is tree 891cc93f9f87ff233c1c36402082b6524ffbe724 on fdb7a72. Its complete patch and reconstruction receipt are /home/lucca/.cache/eon-agents/eon-perf-research-work/bead-drain/30-unlanded-drain.patch and 30-preserved-candidate.json. The overseer cancelled the standalone EIO landing at 03:25:37Z.

This Eon composition refresh hardens EON-C1, EON-C2, and EON-C4 by consuming the newest mutually compatible accepted ORBS v3 child sources. title: Remote Eon workspaces over SSH
description:
## Decision
Lucca, 2026-10-15: SSH is a good match for Eon. Remote workspaces reach the server through the
user's existing OpenSSH (config, aliases, keys, jump hosts). Eon opens no network listener and owns
no authentication, encryption or login; it does not replace SSH (unlike Superlogical's Rex, which
claims to). This decision authorizes planning only; each child below still needs its own contract
approval. It is the explicit user direction `orbit/AGENTS.md` requires before any remote use of
Orbit, limited to SSH-carried Unix sockets with Orbit unchanged.

## Outcome
A user keeps Eon's window on their local Wayland desktop while terminals, editor, Git and agents run
on a headless server. Closing the window or losing the connection leaves the remote work running;
reconnecting returns to it; disconnecting stays distinct from stopping.

## Source
GitHub issue Yazelix/eon#1 (bioinformatist, 2026-10-15) describes the full experience: remote
Project browsing, tabs and panes inheriting the remote target, remote Git and Agent popups,
Machine -> named workspace -> tabs -> panes, and disconnect versus stop. Recovery after a server
reboot is explicitly separate.

## Plan (children)
1. `waypipe` spike: run the whole Eon remotely and forward only its window with Waypipe over SSH;
zero Rust. Decide whether a documented recipe suffices.
2. Remote work survives the SSH session: supervisor and terminals outlive SSH logout and the login
session's runtime directory. Needed by every path.
3. Only if the spike falls short: local Venus with a remote supervisor and Orbit over SSH-forwarded
Unix sockets, measured first.
The issue's machine switcher and named workspaces are decided after the spike, inside child 3 or a
later child.

## Related
`orb-permanent-ssh-terminal-access-hd6` (reach a session from any SSH terminal, such as a phone);
`eon-az9` (isolated execution targets); `eon-pxn` (execution-target references);
`eon-next-expansion-0wfb` (remote is a third expansion competing for the same attention).

## Stop boundary
No own transport, listener, login or crypto; no Mosh/QUIC path unless measured latency demands it
and Lucca chooses it; no multi-client attachment; no macOS client in this epic.

title: Spike: run Eon remotely with waypipe over SSH
description:
## Contract
- Consumer: a user with a local x86_64 Linux Wayland desktop and a headless Linux server reachable
by OpenSSH.
- Trigger: `waypipe ssh HOST eon` (and `waypipe ssh HOST eon attach` to return).
- Result: Eon runs entirely on the server and its native window appears locally, with no desktop
environment on the server. The Project picker, tabs, panes, Git and Agent popups all act on the
server automatically. The spike decides whether this is enough to document as the supported first
remote path, or what is missing.

## Why this first
Waypipe (in the pinned nixpkgs, 0.11.0) forwards Wayland applications over SSH: `waypipe server`
gives remote applications their own compositor socket, buffers travel lz4/zstd-compressed or as
h264/vp9/av1 video for DMABUF, and the whole thing rides the user's OpenSSH (6.7+ Unix socket
forwarding). Eon is already Wayland-only, and Venus can render with Mesa lavapipe on a server
without a GPU. If it is good enough, remote Eon costs documentation, not thousands of lines.

## Measure and record
Typing latency and full-screen update bandwidth on a LAN and on a slower link (`waypipe bench`,
compression and video options); server CPU for lavapipe; clipboard and primary selection;
IME; accessibility (AT-SPI does not cross Waypipe, a likely gap); blur protocol pass-through;
cursor trail smoothness; window close and connection loss behavior (does the remote supervisor and
its terminals survive? see the survival bead); reattach.

Known Waypipe caveats to weigh: no reconnection (a dropped link closes the window; reattach starts a
new window); the man page disclaims strong security guarantees against untrusted servers and its
packet timing is observable; buffers may hold screen contents (encrypted swap advised).

## Acceptance
A recorded comparison with exact revisions, hosts, link conditions and numbers, plus a go/no-go
recommendation for Lucca: document `waypipe ssh` as the remote path (with any small Nix packaging),
or proceed to the local-Venus design bead with the specific failures that justify it. No contract
claims remote support until Lucca approves one.

## Stop boundary
No Rust changes. Read-only and disposable test hosts; never disturb Lucca's live sessions.
close_reason: Superseded by eon-remote-workspaces-52i4 (Lucca 2026-10-27, relayed by eon-overseer, 'ssh: okay'): local Venus with a remote supervisor over SSH-forwarded sockets is decided; Waypipe rejected.

title: Keep remote Eon work alive after the SSH session ends
description:
## Contract (provisional; changes EON-C15's boundary, needs Lucca's approval)
- Consumer: the user of the headless supervisor started or found by eon window attach --host HOST (slice 3 of eon-remote-workspaces-52i4).
- Trigger: the SSH session ends: window closed, network lost, or logout.
- Result: the Eon supervisor and its Orbit terminals keep running and stay reachable by a later
`eon attach` or `eon generations` from a new SSH session. `eon stop` still ends them.

## Historical evidence (edge 7d97dee)
- EON-C15 excludes "logout/reboot survival" (`docs/CONTRACTS.md:867`, `:894`).
- Only independent windows detach with `setsid` (`runtime/crates/eon-runtime/src/windows.rs:133`);
the default supervisor's session and SIGHUP behavior under an SSH session end is unverified.
- Sockets live under `XDG_RUNTIME_DIR` (`/run/user/<uid>`), which systemd-logind removes when the
user's last session ends unless lingering is enabled; `KillUserProcesses=yes` would also kill the
work. Eon must stay independent of any init system (root `AGENTS.md`, Platform Discipline), so the
design cannot require systemd, but must behave correctly with it.

## Previously open decisions (settled by the approval below)
Whether the supervisor detaches from the login session itself, where sockets live when the login
runtime directory disappears (EON_RUNTIME_DIR already exists as an override), and what Eon reports
when logind policy would kill or clean up its work.

## Acceptance
Contract approved and indexed first. Then an isolated two-host (or VM) check: start Eon over SSH,
end the SSH session in each way, reconnect, attach, and stop; with and without lingering. Full
affected Rust surfaces via `eon-test`.

## Stop boundary
No reboot recovery (`eon-reboot-restore-im8y`), no systemd unit or service-manager requirement.


## Operative decision and evidence
Lucca's 2026-10-27 "ssh: okay": setsid plus a private per-UID socket directory when logind owns
the login runtime directory; report KillUserProcesses=yes, never enable linger. His 2026-10-28
order puts this after .5 identity/registry (closed) and .6 original-layout recovery.
Current windows.rs:636 uses setsid for independent windows; this does not prove headless SSH
logout survival. EON-C15 is at docs/CONTRACTS.md:2822. Its exact logout amendment still needs
approval. Runtime owns lifecycle/sockets; OpenSSH owns connection/auth; Orbit owns terminals.
Use eon window attach --host HOST and current discovery CLI, not the historical attach/generations
examples above. Compatibility is identical wire versions, not exact build identity.
Yu owns this work ("ssh is with Yu", Lucca 2026-11-07); agents start only on assignment.
Read the owning SSH reference route and record exact revisions before implementation. Prove
portable hosting without a systemd user service, and separately report logind policy without
changing it. Remote close detaches (Lucca 2026-11-03); explicit Quit/Stop still stops accepted
targets. Preserve private sockets and UID/PID/start/inode/lease checks. No reboot, managed
service or silent fallback here. Use the lifecycle proof route and record installed identities.

title: Design local Venus with a remote supervisor over SSH-forwarded sockets
description:
## Activation
Only if the `waypipe` spike shows that forwarding the whole window is not good enough, and Lucca
chooses this path. Design first.

## Contract (provisional)
Venus runs on the local desktop and renders locally; the Eon supervisor and Orbit run on the server;
the workspace (EONW) and terminal (ORBS) Unix sockets are carried over the user's OpenSSH
connection. The window shows which machine it is attached to and distinguishes disconnected from
stopped; reconnecting reattaches without restarting remote terminals.

## Lowest-code mechanism to evaluate first
OpenSSH stream-local forwarding (`ssh -L /local.sock:/remote.sock`, `StreamLocalBindUnlink`) with a
ControlMaster connection, adding forwards for terminal sockets as the workspace announces them
(`ssh -O forward`). Venus already connects to socket paths (`venus/src/transport.rs`), so most of
the work is path mapping, a headless supervisor start, and reconnect. Compare with a single stdio
multiplexer over `ssh HOST eon proxy` (Zed and VS Code Remote style) only if forwarding fails.

## Open design decisions
- Bandwidth: Orbit sends complete frames per revision; measure over a slow link first. If needed,
Orbit's planned revisioned row patches (`orbit/docs/PROTOCOL.md:80-85`) become a prerequisite
(an `orbit-protocol` change needing Lucca's approval; consumers Venus, Eon Runtime, Eon,
bend-orbit).
- Version skew: presentation requires the exact same build on both ends; decide how the remote build
is provisioned (for example `nix copy`) and how mismatch is reported.
- Headless supervisor: today the supervisor spawns Venus itself.
- The issue's Machine -> named workspace -> tabs model, machine switcher, and workspace naming
(windows have only random IDs today).
- Where quota collection runs (local or remote credentials).

## Prerequisites and reference gate
Blocked by the `waypipe` spike and the survival bead. Consequential (contracts, lifecycle, possibly
protocol). Inspect at exact revisions: Zed remote development, VS Code Remote-SSH, WezTerm SSH and
TLS domains, and Mosh's state synchronization. Stop for Lucca's design and contract approval.

## Acceptance
Design approved; then installed two-host dogfood: start, work, drop the link, reconnect, stop; with
recorded latency and bandwidth.

## Stop boundary
No own transport, listener or authentication; no Mosh/QUIC path without measured need and Lucca's
choice; no multi-client attachment.

title: Remote workspaces: local Venus, remote Runtime and Orbit over OpenSSH
description:
## Why

GitHub issue #1 (Yu, bioinformatist, a Yazelix member) asks for Eon's window on a PC while terminals, Git, editors and agents run on a headless server, with work surviving window close and connection loss. PR #2 is Yu's working prototype (9.2k lines, two-machine proof, base no longer merges).

## Decisions

- Lucca, 2026-10-23 ("2 ok" to the overseer's item proposing a reply that agrees on the direction and slicing): Venus stays local; Runtime and Orbit run remote; they connect over OpenSSH-forwarded Unix sockets; no new protocol in v1; land in slices on current edge; the remote supervisor must not require systemd (AGENTS.md keeps Linux contracts service-manager independent; systemd user service and linger are optional help for hosts with KillUserProcesses=yes). Reply posted on PR #2: https://github.com/Yazelix/eon/pull/2#issuecomment-6368463120
- Proposed slice order (to settle with Yu): contracts and IDs; one workspace model shared with EON-C33 (eon-workspace-switching-shn4); transport; remote supervision without systemd; recovery; incremental frames and history paging.
- Yu's four overlap questions (identity, Stop, discovery, protocols) are open in the PR thread; the overseer's leaning is recorded in the reply.

## Competitive context

Superlogical's Rex (macOS, public beta) uses the same server/client split, a custom binary screen frame, a Mosh-inspired responsive protocol for low-latency typing, and acts as a full SSH replacement with system logins. Eon deliberately reuses OpenSSH for authentication. OSC 7501, which Eon's agent sidebar reads, is Rex's published generic protocol.

## Scope

Children are filed; the original overlap questions and proposed order above are historical, superseded by the decisions below. Yu ports the slices as a Yazelix member through the normal bead, contract, review and proof loop.

## Acceptance

- Issue #1's recovery goal on two machines: close, connection loss and supervisor restart keep remote tabs, panes and popups running and reattachable, with disconnect distinct from stop.

## Current operative decisions
Lucca's 2026-10-28 plan, amended 2026-11-03: identity/registry (.4/.5, closed), same-boot
recovery (.11 approval and .6), portable SSH hosting/attach (x7dr.2/.2), takeover (.10),
optional managed hosting (.7), discovery/switching (.3), incremental frames (.8), history and
end-to-end proof (.9). Read docs/REMOTE-WORKSPACES.md for the acceptance matrix.
- Identical EONW, Orbit management and ORBS/ORBF versions define compatibility, not identical
  build identity; refuse mismatches without changing work and name both sides.
- One machine per window. Several computers may stay attached: takeover on touch chooses one
  active input/size owner, passive views are dim/frozen, first touch only takes over.
- Remote close detaches that computer (Lucca 2026-11-03 "agreed"); local close quits.
  Explicit Quit/Stop/tab/pane close retains its approved stopping semantics.
- Local configuration owns presentation; host configuration owns launches. Keep UID/PID/start,
  inode/lease checks, CLI parity and explicit cached-state labels. Composition retains store
  resources; Runtime never queries the Nix store.
- EON-C38 exists. Recovery amendments wait on .11. EON-C34 is reserved for .2 and takeover
  amendments belong to .10. The 2026-10-27 draft is not current exact contract text.
Yu owns the SSH work and scope (Lucca 2026-11-07: "the ssh stuff is also pre 0.2"; "ssh is with
Yu"). Agents do not begin these slices without assignment. Preserve OpenSSH-only transport,
no remote installation/automatic linger, no mixed-host window and no live passive mirroring.
Each slice proves its matrix rows; end-to-end acceptance covers compatible reconnect, no leaked
SSH masters, wrong host keys, stale endpoints, logout, supervisor recovery and Stop/Forget.
Prediction (.1) remains separately sequenced after incremental frames.

comments.text:
SSH owner and first slice: Lucca's decisions (2026-10-27, relayed by eon-overseer).

A coordinator research agent compared eon-remote-ssh-x7dr and this epic (both epics, their children, docs/CONTRACTS.md, docs/REFERENCES.md, Yu's PR #2 and issue #1). Lucca was asked nine numbered decisions, each with the recommendation yes, and replied "ssh: okay":

1. Owner epic: keep eon-remote-workspaces-52i4. Move x7dr.2 ("Keep remote Eon work alive after the SSH session ends") under it as its remote-supervision slice; close x7dr, x7dr.1 (Waypipe spike) and x7dr.3 (local Venus with remote supervisor) as superseded by the 2026-10-23 decision; carry x7dr's recorded decision (OpenSSH owns the connection; Eon opens no listener, owns no auth or crypto; Orbit used remotely only through Unix sockets carried over SSH, Orbit unchanged) and its Related list here; point eon-igae's exclusion at 52i4.
2. First slice: `eon attach --host HOST` = SSH transport plus a detached supervisor with no display on HOST, keeping today's EON-C33 model (one remote supervisor shows as one local window). The workspace registry, persistent IDs and the machine switcher (Yu's Q1-3) move to slice 2. This reorders the 2026-10-23 plan.
3. Surviving logout: setsid, plus sockets in a private per-UID directory when logind manages the login runtime directory (tmux precedent). A host with KillUserProcesses=yes is reported; Eon never enables linger.
4. Versions across machines: exact build match for now, failing closed and naming both builds.
5. Configuration split: local configuration decides presentation; HOST's configuration decides what its supervisor launches.
6. Host visibility: an Eon Bar host label (amends VEN-C21), not only the window title.
7. On disconnect: the window stays, shown disconnected with input off; no automatic reconnect yet.
8. Approve the EON-C34 draft text below, with 1-7 applied.
9. eon-remote-workspaces-52i4.1 (Mosh-style prediction) stays P3, after incremental frames.

Adopted contract text (EON-C34; the next free ID; implementation lands it in docs/CONTRACTS.md):

EON-C34 — Remote workspace over SSH
- Consumer: A full-Eon user on local x86_64 Linux Wayland whose work runs on an x86_64 Linux host they reach by OpenSSH. That host needs no display.
- Trigger: `eon attach --host HOST`, closing the window, losing the connection, ending the remote login, or Commands > Quit this window.
- Result:
  - Eon runs the user's `ssh` with their config, keys, host-key checks and ProxyJump. On HOST it starts or finds one supervisor with no display, detached from the SSH session, and Orbit runs there.
  - Venus runs locally and reaches HOST's workspace and terminal sockets only through forwards that this window owns, each with mode 0600.
  - The local configuration decides presentation; HOST's configuration decides everything its supervisor launches.
  - The Eon Bar shows HOST.
  - Closing the window or losing the connection only disconnects: Venus shows the window as disconnected with input off, and HOST's terminals keep running.
  - Reattach shows the same terminals. Quit stops them under EON-C11/EON-C15.
- Important failures:
  - A different EONW version or component graph on HOST is refused, naming both builds, without stopping anything.
  - Connecting never installs or upgrades software and never enables linger.
  - A host whose logind policy would kill the work at logout is reported, not changed.
- Owner: Eon Runtime owns the SSH launch, the forwards and the supervisor with no display; Venus owns presentation; Orbit owns terminals; OpenSSH owns the connection and authentication.
- Boundary:
  - No Eon listener, login or crypto.
  - No workspace registry or names surviving a supervisor restart.
  - No mixed-host windows, multiple clients or Waypipe.
  - No reboot recovery or service-manager requirement.
  - The x86_64 Linux limit applies to both ends.

Amendments the slice needs (their exact text still comes to Lucca with the implementation): EON-C11 drops "remote runtime" from its Boundary; EON-C15's Boundary allows logout survival for the supervisor with no display; EON-C7: the remote host needs no Wayland; VEN-C14: Venus presented by a local launcher; VEN-C21: the host label. No ORB change.

First-slice acceptance (proposed): two x86_64 Linux hosts or a VM over SSH with the same Eon build: panes run on HOST (`hostname`; the picker browses HOST); close the window, kill the SSH master, end every SSH login with linger off, and a counter in a pane keeps advancing on HOST after each; reattach shows the same terminals; Commands > Quit this window ends them; a mismatched build is refused, names both builds and stops nothing; `nix develop -c eon-test` passes.

Reference gate additions (route docs/REFERENCES.md:143 already covers OpenSSH stream-local forwarding and ControlMaster, Zed, VS Code Remote-SSH, WezTerm SSH domains, Mosh): tmux's per-UID socket directory (logout survival), the kitty ssh kitten (rejected: installs on the remote), Zellij (rejected as owner), Ghosthub and Unpeel (reconnect), the trust boundary (local socket mode; Orbit's SO_PEERCRED UID check sees sshd as the remote user), and the version policy (exact build now; Yu's protocol/build compatibility split as the exit condition).

Yu's PR #2 is reference only for Yazelix-org work (Yu is inside the org): it needs porting off systemd+linger, off the EON-C29 ID (now the clock) and from EONW 13 to the current EONW.

title: Make remote typing feel local with Mosh-style prediction
description:
## Why

Lucca approved filing this on 2026-10-23 ("yeah" to the overseer's item: "Add a responsive remote typing (Mosh-style prediction) bead to the future remote epic, measured after incremental frames"). Over SSH, every keystroke in a remote Eon workspace waits for a full round trip before it shows. Superlogical's Rex, Eon's closest competitor, advertises a Mosh-inspired responsive protocol for low-latency remote typing. On a slow or distant link, Eon will feel worse than Rex until it hides that latency.

## Scope

In scope, after incremental frames land in this epic:
- Measure first (AP-PERF-001): keystroke-to-glyph latency over representative RTTs (for example 20, 80 and 200 ms, with loss), against a local baseline.
- Research Mosh's speculative local echo and its confidence and undo rules, Eternal Terminal, and whatever Rex publishes. Decide where prediction lives. Venus showing tentative echo over Orbit frames is the likely owner, since Orbit stays the sole authority on terminal state.
- Bring the contract and any protocol change to Lucca before code.

Out of scope: replacing SSH, UDP roaming (a separate decision), and changes to local workspaces.

## Acceptance

- At 200 ms RTT, typed characters in a shell prompt appear within one frame locally, and mispredictions are corrected without corrupting the screen; measured and recorded.

## Verification

The measurement harness under realistic RTT and loss, plus the proof route that the eventual contract change requires.

## Execution split (prime-beads 2026-11-12)

Two ordered slices: measure and choose the exact prediction/safety contract after incremental frames; then implement and prove that approved design. All original latency/correction acceptance remains on this rollup; the likely Venus owner remains a hypothesis until the design records it.

title: Let a second attached computer take over a workspace on its first key or click
description:
Slice 3b of eon-remote-workspaces-52i4: when two computers attach the same workspace (Yu's office PC and home PC on one server), both stay attached and the one last used owns the workspace.

## Decided (Lucca's model on PR #3, 2026-11-03 05:05Z; Yu agreed 06:13Z: "The takeover interaction you described fits how I actually use the two PCs ... A frozen inactive view and using the first key or click just to take over work for me.")
- Both computers stay attached. The one that last typed or clicked is active: it receives input and sets the terminal size.
- The other keeps its connection and shows the workspace where it was left, dimmed and frozen (no live updates), with a line saying the workspace is active on HOST.
- The first key or click on the inactive computer only takes over: it is not sent to the program. The workspace then redraws at that computer's size.
- Out of scope: a passive computer that keeps updating live (wall monitor). That needs frames to every client and size negotiation in Orbit; revisit only on a real need, with an Orbit spike first.
- One host per window (decided 05:17Z, Yu agreed).

## Contract
Takeover amendments to EON-C34 (written in slice 3, eon-remote-workspaces-52i4.2), plus the Orbit attachment clause that today answers a second client with Busy (the "one active client per workspace: a second client gets a busy result" line in eon-remote-workspaces-52i4.4's goal is superseded by this model). Exact text stops for Lucca's approval. Rule 5: an agent can see which computer is active and take over from the CLI. Rule 6: the dim level and the notice text are visible values (config or recorded reason).

## Prerequisites
eon-remote-workspaces-52i4.2 (SSH attach). Local two-client takeover may be provable before SSH; the plan decides.

## Acceptance
Two clients on one workspace: the inactive one shows the frozen dimmed view and the "active on HOST" line; its first key or click takes over without reaching the program; the size follows the active client; detach or loss of either client leaves the other working; CLI reports the active client. Installed proof with two clients (local first, then over SSH).

## Scope boundary
Takeover between attached clients only. No live passive mirroring, no multi-host windows, no change to Quit or Stop.

## Execution split (prime-beads 2026-11-12)

Three ordered slices: approve the exact workspace-wide ownership/attachment contract; implement its Orbit mechanism; integrate Runtime/Venus/CLI and two-client installed SSH proof. This changes execution size only. Both stay attached; exactly one input/size owner; passive view frozen/dimmed; first touch consumed; no live passive mirroring or mixed-host windows.

title: Attach to a remote host's workspace with eon window attach --host HOST
description:
## Why

Slice 3 of `eon-remote-workspaces-52i4` (GitHub issue #1): a person on local x86_64 Linux
Wayland runs `eon window attach --host HOST` and gets an Eon window whose terminals run on HOST. Lucca
chose this first slice on 2026-10-27 (relayed by eon-overseer, "ssh: okay" to nine numbered
decisions recorded on 52i4): SSH transport plus a supervisor with no display on HOST, keeping
today's EON-C33 model (one remote supervisor shows as one local window). That original SSH-first order is superseded: identity/registry (.5, closed) and recovery (.6) precede this slice.

Owner: Yu (bioinformatist), a trusted Yazelix-org member (AGENTS.md "Outside Contributions" does
not apply to him), ports this through the normal bead, contract, review and proof loop. His PR #2
is reference only: port it off systemd and linger, off the EON-C29 ID (now the clock) and from
EONW 13 to the current EONW.

## Contract

EON-C34 "Remote workspace over SSH", adopted text recorded verbatim on 52i4's 2026-10-27
comment; this bead lands it in `docs/CONTRACTS.md` (reserved ID; the original next-free assumption at 01f5e3c is historical). Amendments this slice needs, whose exact text still goes to Lucca with the
implementation: EON-C11 drops "remote runtime" from its Boundary; EON-C7: the remote host needs
no Wayland; VEN-C14: Venus presented by a local launcher. (EON-C15's logout amendment belongs to
`eon-remote-ssh-x7dr.2`; VEN-C21's host label to the presentation sibling.) No ORB change.

## Scope

In scope (Eon Runtime owns the SSH launch, the forwards and the supervisor with no display):
- `eon window attach --host HOST`: runs the user's `ssh` with their config, keys, host-key checks and
  ProxyJump; on HOST starts or finds the supervisor with no display delivered by
  `eon-remote-ssh-x7dr.2`; never installs or upgrades software and never enables linger.
- Forwards owned by this window (OpenSSH stream-local forwarding) of HOST's workspace and terminal
  sockets to local sockets with mode 0600; Venus runs locally and reaches HOST only through them.
- Configuration split: local configuration decides presentation; HOST's decides what its
  supervisor launches.
- Wire-version check: identical EONW, Orbit management and ORBS/ORBF versions permit compatible different builds; a wire mismatch is refused, naming both builds/versions, without stopping anything.
- Reattach shows the same terminals; remote close only detaches, while explicit Quit/Stop stops the accepted targets under EON-C11/EON-C15.
- Humans and Agents: the attach and quit paths are CLI paths; record any window action this slice
  adds and its CLI path.

Out of scope: the disconnected window state and the Eon Bar host label (presentation sibling);
logout survival (x7dr.2); implementing the existing registry, mixed-host windows, takeover (.10), Waypipe,
reboot recovery, automatic reconnect, any Eon listener, login or crypto (EON-C34 Boundary).

## Reference gate (consequential: lifecycle, trust boundary, contract)

Record on this bead before code: route `docs/REFERENCES.md:143` (OpenSSH stream-local forwarding
and ControlMaster, Zed, VS Code Remote-SSH, WezTerm SSH domains, Mosh) plus 52i4's additions
(kitty ssh kitten rejected: installs on the remote; Zellij rejected as owner; Ghosthub and Unpeel
for reconnect), the trust boundary (local socket mode; Orbit's SO_PEERCRED UID check sees sshd as
the remote user), and the approved version policy (identical wire protocol versions, not exact build identity).

## Acceptance

- Two x86_64 Linux hosts, or a VM, over SSH with the same Eon build: panes run on HOST
  (`hostname`; the picker browses HOST); close the window and kill the SSH master, and a counter
  in a pane keeps advancing on HOST; reattach shows the same terminals; Commands > Quit this
  window ends them; a protocol mismatch is refused, names both builds/versions and stops nothing; a different compatible build reconnects.
- EON-C34 and the approved amendments land in `docs/CONTRACTS.md`; `docs/USAGE.md` and
  CHANGELOG.md updated.
- `nix develop -c eon-test` passes; Codex review per AGENTS.md.

## Stop Conditions

- Stop for Lucca's approval of each amendment's exact text before editing contracts.
- Stop if the slice needs a new protocol or EONW change (52i4: no new protocol in v1).
- Stop if HOST needs anything installed beyond a compatible Eon build.


## Later decisions superseding historical draft text
EON-C34 is reserved for this slice, not the next unused ID. The 2026-10-27 text must be updated
for the approved 2026-10-28 compatibility rule and 2026-11-03 remote-close decision before exact
text approval. Its old no-registry/multiple-client clauses do not undo identity or separately
sequenced takeover (.10). Existing registry consumption is in scope; implementing the registry
and takeover is not. No Orbit change is assumed for SSH transport itself.
Remote close detaches only that computer and stops no host terminal (Lucca "agreed");
Alt+Shift+Q / eon quit and explicit Stop keep their accepted targets. Yu owns implementation.
Use eon window attach --host HOST consistently in help/docs. Wire additions require a new
version and exact approval; never mutate one in place. Reference/version-policy wording above
that says exact-build is historical, superseded by identical wire versions.

## Goal

1. **EON-C38, Planned.** Contract text, approved by Lucca before any code, for slice 2a
   (eon-remote-workspaces-52i4.5): persistent host-owned workspace identity and the host
   registry. Fresh ID EON-C38: EON-C29 (retired 2026-10-30, demoted to a feature) and every other
   used ID are never reused; EON-C34 stays reserved for SSH attachment and hosting (slice 3).
2. **Plan and acceptance matrix in `docs/REMOTE-WORKSPACES.md`**, not as contract text. The plan
   records, for the slices that will contract them:
   - the compatibility rule: builds are compatible exactly when their wire protocol versions match
     (EONW, Orbit management, ORBS/ORBF); an incompatible attach fails clearly and stops nothing;
   - portable and managed hosting, each with its own startup owner and proof; managed is opt-in,
     never inferred, never a silent fallback; Linux contracts stay service-manager-independent;
   - the multi-client model: takeover on touch (Lucca 2026-11-03, confirmed by Yu the same day),
     replacing the 2026-10-28 "one active client, second gets busy" rule: any number of clients
     stay attached, exactly one is active, a passive client shows a frozen dimmed frame, and its
     first key or click only takes over (slice 3b, eon-remote-workspaces-52i4.10);
   - one machine per window (Lucca 2026-11-03, decided);
   - remote identity: the UID, PID, start-time, inode and lease checks stay;
   - Nix store: retention through GC roots or profiles; the runtime never queries or records store
     paths;
   - CLI parity for every new action, and cached remote state labelled as cached;
   - the acceptance matrix: simultaneous bootstrap attempts; a wrong host key; stale or replaced
     sockets; PID reuse; corrupt or unknown snapshots; SSH loss and window close; supervisor
     normal exit and crash; the last logout; reconnecting without SSH masters piling up.

Moved out of this bead (2026-11-03 decisions), each to the slice that implements it:
- Recovery, CLI and close: amendments to EON-C15, EON-C33, EON-C10 and EON-C8 in their slices

  status are not adopted.
- EON-C34 (SSH attachment and hosting): slice 3 (eon-remote-workspaces-52i4.2).
- Takeover amendments to ORB-C3/ORB-C13: slice 3b (eon-remote-workspaces-52i4.10).

title: Give every workspace a persistent host ID and registry
description:
## Why

Slice 2a of the remote-workspace plan Lucca adopted on 2026-10-28 (decision comment on eon-remote-workspaces-52i4). Yu ports it as a PR.

## Goal

Every workspace, local or remote, gets a persistent host-owned ID and a versioned host registry entry (name, run membership, layout). Window `wN` values become local handles. Directories stay attributes, not identities. Eon Runtime owns the registry and is its only writer. Snapshots are written atomically and never replace live process, socket and lease validation.

## Contract

The slice 1 amendments to EON-C33 and EON-C15.

## Acceptance

- The registry survives a supervisor restart.
- A corrupt or unknown registry fails without stopping unrelated work.
- The CLI lists workspaces by persistent ID.
- Affected Rust suites pass, plus an installed isolated observation.
- Review loop and Codex.

## Reference

PR #2's atomic snapshot and exact-run reconciliation code, as specification only: pr2.diff:9710 and :14783 in /home/lucca/.cache/eon-agents/eon-overseer/pr2/.

## Scope boundary

No SSH and no recovery into groups (that is 2b).
