title: Recover sessions into their original groups and layout after a supervisor restart
description:
## Why

Slice 2b of the remote-workspace plan Lucca adopted on 2026-10-28 (decision comment on
`eon-remote-workspaces-52i4`). Today, when a window's supervisor exits or crashes, a replacement
supervisor recovers the surviving Orbit terminals into one unnamed session `s1` with one tab `t1`
(EON-C15, EON-C33). Every terminal is still running, yet the sessions, their names and persistent
IDs, tabs, columns, pinned pane names, popups and selection are gone. SSH attach
(`eon-remote-workspaces-52i4.2`) and logout survival (`eon-remote-ssh-x7dr.2`) wait on this slice
so that they attach to the same sessions after a restart, not to a flattened one.

## Owner

Yu (bioinformatist, Yazelix member) owns this slice and its scope (Lucca, 2026-11-07: "ssh is with
Yu"; Yu took 2b on Yazelix/eon PR #6, issuecomment-6731634374). Agents start a child bead only when
Lucca or Yu assigns it.

## Goal

After a supervisor exit or crash on the same boot and login, a replacement supervisor for the same
window restores the original sessions (with their confirmed persistent IDs and names), tabs,
columns, panes, pinned pane names, persistent popups and last committed selection around the
surviving Orbit runs it has validated under EON-C15.

- The structure comes from a recovery checkpoint that Eon Runtime owns. It is separate from the
  EON-C38 registry, which holds identity and names only, never membership or layout.
- A saved slot whose run is gone shows as stopped in its place beside live runs. Recovery never
  starts a terminal, replays a command or input, or guesses a grouping.
- A stale, mismatched or unsafe run still refuses the whole recovery set, as EON-C15 requires.
- When the checkpoint cannot be trusted, the validated runs stay usable in a visibly degraded
  recovered session, and the person and the CLI can both read why.

## Decisions

- 2026-11-03 (Lucca, comment on `eon-remote-workspaces-52i4`): recovery, CLI and close are
  amendments to EON-C15, EON-C33, EON-C10 and EON-C8 in this slice. No new contract ID.
- 2026-11-09 (eon-overseer under Lucca's auto-decide): the `eon-hyil8` dependency was dropped. This
  slice stays inside today's window-owned session collection and needs no global session manager.
- 2026-11-10 (Lucca's review of Yu's draft,
  https://github.com/Yazelix/eon/pull/7#issuecomment-6768242579): the direction is settled (a
  checkpoint separate from the registry, whole-set EON-C15 refusals, no replayed starts). The draft
  needs one more round before it is contract text. The review's positions are: commit the start
  intent before Runtime creates the management record and spawns; one `stopped` state with a
  reason; extra runs in one freshly registered "Recovered" session; a damaged or over-capacity
  checkpoint is renamed aside and a fresh one started; no recovered window when no run is live; a
  recovered placeholder stays when a sibling exits, and the window's last live exit still ends the
  window; a completed Stop reports `checkpoint_cleared` and keeps no persistence-retry owner; the
  new wire fields need a new EONW version. These are review positions, not approved text.
- 2026-11-10: split into three child beads (checkpoint; restore and reconcile; degraded mode and
  CLI), as that review promised.

## Contract

No new ID. Amendments to EON-C15 and EON-C33, consistency amendments to EON-C8, EON-C10, EON-C11,
EON-C17, EON-C18, EON-C38, EON-C39 and the Planned EON-C42, and a new EONW version. The draft is
`docs/LOCAL-SESSION-RECOVERY.md` in Yazelix/eon PR #7 (head `185357d` on 2026-11-10). The slice 2b
contract bead tracks its approval. No child starts before Lucca approves the exact text.

## Children

In order; each blocks the next:

1. eon-remote-workspaces-52i4.11, the slice 2b contract bead (a sibling under `eon-remote-workspaces-52i4`): Lucca approves the
   exact text and PR #7 merges.
2. `eon-remote-workspaces-52i4.6.1`: write the recovery checkpoint.
3. `eon-remote-workspaces-52i4.6.2`: restore sessions and layout from the checkpoint and reconcile
   them with the surviving runs.
4. `eon-remote-workspaces-52i4.6.3`: degraded recovery, its CLI and event projection, and the
   slice's installed proof.

## Acceptance

- The three children are closed.
- Installed isolated observation on x86_64 Linux Wayland: three named sessions with several tabs
  and columns, a pinned pane name and a persistent popup; SIGKILL to the exact supervisor PID, and
  separately a supervisor exit without Stop; a fresh `eon` shows the same sessions, persistent IDs,
  layout and selection; every terminal keeps its PID and start identity, and a counter in a pane
  keeps advancing.
- A stale, mismatched or unsafe run among healthy ones still refuses the whole recovery set: no
  partial session, no signal, nothing stopped.
- A damaged checkpoint leaves the validated runs usable in a degraded session, and
  `eon session ls --json` names the reason and the kept file.
- The amended EON-C15 and EON-C33 clauses carry proof records naming revision, platform and
  artifact. `eon-igae.7.1` re-proves EON-C15 on the beta candidate afterwards.

## Scope boundary

Local, same boot and login, same recovery namespace and generation. No SSH, no logout or reboot
survival, no cross-build takeover, no Orbit restart recovery, no moving sessions between windows,
no Forget. eonbase's single-terminal recovery is unchanged.

title: Write a recovery checkpoint of a window's sessions and layout
description:
## Why

Recovery can restore only what a supervisor wrote down before it died. Today Eon Runtime keeps a
window's sessions, tabs, columns, panes, popups and selection in memory only, so a replacement
supervisor has nothing to restore from and flattens every surviving terminal into `s1`/`t1`. This
bead makes that structure durable. It changes nothing about what recovery shows: the next bead
(`eon-remote-workspaces-52i4.6.2`) reads what this one writes.

First of three children of `eon-remote-workspaces-52i4.6` (slice 2b). Owner: Yu; agents start it
only when Lucca or Yu assigns it.

## Contract

The approved slice 2b text (`docs/LOCAL-SESSION-RECOVERY.md`, Yazelix/eon PR #7), not this
summary. This bead implements, and folds into `docs/CONTRACTS.md` with an "Amended on <date> ...
by <this bead>" line each:

- EON-C15: one recovery owner, durable structure, publication, the creation boundary, and the
  checkpoint part of shutdown effects; its Boundary's "no prior-topology persistence".
- EON-C10: the reply fields and refusal code for a mutation whose effect landed but whose
  checkpoint commit failed.

Positions the text is expected to carry (Lucca's review, 2026-11-10,
https://github.com/Yazelix/eon/pull/7#issuecomment-6768242579); the landed text wins where it
differs:

- A structural change succeeds only after the temp-file, fsync, rename and parent-sync commit.
- The start intent (exact slot, terminal ID and run ID) commits before Runtime creates the empty
  management record and spawns.
- A process effect followed by a failed commit reports the effect with
  `durability: "failed" | "uncertain"`, exit 1, code `checkpoint-failed`, and claims no rollback.
- The checkpoint lives in the per-window runtime directory beside the management records, so
  nothing survives a reboot. The text states its bounds and what allocator exhaustion does.
- A completed Stop finishes shutdown and reports `checkpoint_cleared`; there is no
  persistence-retry owner.

## Prerequisites

- The slice 2b contract bead is closed (this bead's `blocks` dependency): Lucca approved the exact
  text and PR #7 is merged.
- Slice 2a (`eon-remote-workspaces-52i4.5`) is on edge: `a20504d`, `c5f40f0`.

## Evidence

Edge `0157343`, EONW v38. `R` is `runtime/crates/eon-runtime/src`, `P` is
`runtime/crates/eon-workspace-protocol/src`.

- `R/workspace.rs:191` `WorkspaceSet` (sessions, `shown`), `:1251` `Workspace` (one session:
  `persistent_id`, `name`, `tabs`, `active`), `:94` `Tab` (`directory`, `pending`, `columns`,
  `selected_column`, `popups`), `:88` `Column` (`panes`, `expanded`), `:64` `Pane`
  (`pinned_name`), `:71` `Popup` (`entry`, `launch_directory`): the structure, in memory only.
- `R/workspace.rs:123` `IdAllocator`: hands out `terminal-N`, `tN`, `pN`. Its counters are not
  saved, so a restart continues from `max(N)+1` of the survivors (`R/workspace.rs:379-397`).
- `R/sessions.rs:1649` `start_orbit`: takes the run ID at `:1668` and creates the empty mode-0600
  management record at `:1696` (`ReadyClaim::create`, `R/sessions.rs:63`). Nothing is written
  before that point. `R/supervisor.rs:2298` `apply_session_operation` calls it.
- `R/supervisor.rs:905` `prepare_generation_runtime` and `R/generation.rs:65`
  `generation_directory`: management records are `<window runtime root>/generations/<generation>/
  terminal-N.sock.record`.
- `R/session_registry.rs:568` `publish` (temporary file at 0600, `sync_all`, rename,
  `sync_directory` at `:714`, an uncertain result after the rename) and `:147` `Worker` (its own
  thread, `submit` refuses while one operation is in flight, `poll`): the pattern slice 2a landed
  for durable writes off the control loop.
- Mutations that would commit before replying, all in `R/workspace.rs`: `create_tab` `:1730`,
  `create_pane` `:1697`, tab and pane close `:1028` and `:1041`, `invoke_popup` `:1834`,
  `stop_popup` `:2830`, the `RenamePane` arm of `apply_action` `:881`, `set_tab_directory` `:2717`,
  `move_direction` `:2606`, the `NewWorkspace` arm `:901`, `prepare_close_workspace` `:795`, and
  natural exit through `session_ended` `:1054`.
- `R/supervisor.rs:2792` `stop_window` answers with `Reply::Stopped {generation, terminals}`
  (`P/stop.rs:38`), the Reserved Stop. `runtime/AGENTS.md:19` forbids changing it.
- `R/generation.rs:1758` `stopped_json`: the CLI's JSON for a completed Stop.

## Scope

In scope:
- A private Runtime module for the checkpoint: a versioned format; a bounded read of a private
  file; validation (bounds, duplicate identities, cross-session references, wrong generation,
  owner, mode and type); encode and decode; atomic publication, sharing slice 2a's routine rather
  than copying it; a worker off the control loop, where a stale completion never overwrites a
  newer committed state.
- What it records: session membership and order with confirmed persistent IDs; tab order and each
  tab's directory; column and pane order and expansion; pinned pane names; popups with their entry,
  launch directory and whether they are persistent (today that comes only from the catalog entry's
  `keep_alive`, `R/managed_environment.rs:563`); the last committed shown session, active tab and
  selection; exact terminal IDs and run IDs; the allocator high-water marks. It records no
  terminal contents, commands, input or request history.
- Commit before reply for the structural operations the text lists, and the start intent before
  `ReadyClaim::create`.
- Selection changes coalesced. The interval is a configuration key documented in
  `docs/CONFIGURATION.md`, or this bead records why it stays fixed (AGENTS.md rule 6).
- The failed-commit reply (`durability`, `checkpoint-failed`, exit 1), including the partial
  outcome where a registration committed and the membership write failed. A late completion after
  Stop never relaunches or republishes a removed target.
- Stop: a completed Stop clears the checkpoint and the CLI reports `checkpoint_cleared`. The
  Reserved Stop's bytes stay as they are.
- Startup: a supervisor that finds an earlier checkpoint never overwrites it in place. It renames
  it aside, keeps it, and starts a fresh one. Recovery stays flat until the next bead.
- The EONW version bump the new reply fields need (v39 if edge is still at v38), with its version
  goldens; `CHANGELOG.md` and `docs/USAGE.md` for the reply fields.

Out of scope:
- Reading the checkpoint to restore anything: `eon-remote-workspaces-52i4.6.2`.
- The window `recovery` field, pane and popup `state`, the EON-C39 events, `checkpoint-unavailable`
  and `stopped-not-persisted`: `eon-remote-workspaces-52i4.6.2` and `.6.3`.
- Disk I/O on the supervisor's control loop.
- The EON-C38 registry's format, EON-C15's acquisition rules, Orbit, and Venus beyond what the
  EONW bump forces.
- No compatibility path for a window started before this change (Lucca, 2026-11-06).

## Acceptance

- After each structural operation that replied success, killing the supervisor and decoding the
  checkpoint gives the same sessions, tabs, columns, panes, popups and pinned names, with the exact
  terminal IDs and run IDs.
- Crash points: before the intent commits, neither an intent nor a record exists; after the intent
  and before the record, the checkpoint holds the intent and no record exists; after Ready, the
  slot carries the run ID of the live run. Later creation never reuses a terminal ID in any case.
- With a write, rename or fsync failure injected during create, close and rename: the reply is exit
  1 with `checkpoint-failed` and `durability` `failed` or `uncertain`, it reports the process
  effect that happened, and the previous complete checkpoint still decodes.
- While a checkpoint write is held open, terminal input, inspection, attention and Stop still
  answer.
- A completed Stop clears the checkpoint and reports it. When the clear fails, Stop still finishes
  and reports `checkpoint_cleared: false`, and a later launch starts no terminal from that file.
- An earlier checkpoint found at startup is renamed aside with identical bytes.
- Recovery is unchanged: `replacement_eon_adopts_exact_runs_and_projects_numeric_workspace`
  (`eon/crates/eon/tests/workspace_control.rs:9794`) passes unmodified.

## Verification

- `nix develop -c eon-test -p eon-runtime` and `nix develop -c eon-test -p eon` exit 0 while
  iterating; `nix develop -c eon-test` over the whole workspace exits 0 on the final tree.
- `cargo fmt --check` and `cargo clippy --locked --all-targets -- -D warnings` for each changed
  crate.
- One isolated installed observation: create two sessions with tabs and panes through the CLI,
  decode the checkpoint, SIGKILL the exact supervisor PID, start `eon`: the terminals come back
  flat as before and the earlier checkpoint is kept aside.
- Review loop, plus Codex for the code and the contract text.

## Reference gate

Consequential (lifecycle and wire format). Record on this bead before code:
`docs/REFERENCES.md:171` (live terminal continuity versus workspace reconstruction; TUIOS at
`0047c409185f`) and `:508` (recovery experience). Comparable implementation, as specification
only: PR #2's `workspace/layout.rs` (`/home/lucca/.cache/eon-agents/eon-overseer/pr2/pr2.diff:9605`,
bioinformatist/eon `610b053`). Keep its versioned structure, bounded private reads, atomic
publication and allocator high-water marks. Reject its synchronous `save_layout` calls on the
control loop and its second supervisor for named workspaces.

## Stop Conditions

- Stop if the cited code has drifted materially, or the landed contract text moves work between
  the three child beads.
- Stop if `checkpoint_cleared` cannot be reported without changing the Reserved Stop's bytes.
- Stop if commit-before-reply needs a disk write on the control loop.
- Stop if the plan shows this will not fit one session, and hand back a split at this seam: the
  format, store, worker, startup and Stop handling; then commit-before-reply, the start intent and
  the failure replies.
- Stop if verification fails twice for the same reason after a reasonable fix attempt.

## Maintenance Notes

- No session reorder action exists today (`move_direction` moves tabs and panes only). Session
  order in the checkpoint is list order.
- The checkpoint has its own format version, separate from EONW.

## Execution split (prime-beads 2026-11-12)

Two ordered slices at the existing Stop Conditions seam: format/private store/worker/startup and Stop handling; then all structural commit-before-reply/start intents/failure replies. This rollup retains its original complete acceptance and blocks .6.2/reboot save until both children finish. No current contract position or Yu ownership changes.

title: Restore sessions and layout from the checkpoint around the surviving terminals
description:
## Why

With the checkpoint written (`eon-remote-workspaces-52i4.6.1`), the structure is on disk and
recovery still ignores it: a replacement supervisor puts every surviving terminal into one unnamed
session `s1` with one tab `t1`. This bead makes recovery rebuild the original sessions, tabs,
columns, panes, popups and selection around the runs that survived, and show a slot whose run is
gone as stopped in its place.

Second of three children of `eon-remote-workspaces-52i4.6` (slice 2b). Owner: Yu; agents start it
only when Lucca or Yu assigns it.

## Contract

The approved slice 2b text (`docs/LOCAL-SESSION-RECOVERY.md`, Yazelix/eon PR #7), not this
summary. This bead implements, and folds into `docs/CONTRACTS.md` with an "Amended on <date> ...
by <this bead>" line each:

- EON-C15: live reconciliation, missing and extra runs, registry-only failure, no implicit replay,
  recovered placeholders after a natural exit.
- EON-C33: the recovery sentence (`docs/CONTRACTS.md:4441-4446` at edge `0157343`), the Boundary
  (`:4467-4470`) and the Emptying exception for placeholders.
- Consistency: EON-C8 (synthetic `t1` becomes the fallback; pinned names are restored; "no dead
  pane" yields to recovered placeholders), EON-C10 (the pane-name sentence, the "durable
  restoration" boundary, pane and popup state fields), EON-C11's "no persisted topology", EON-C17,
  EON-C18, EON-C38 (a fresh registration only for flat recovery and the "Recovered" session), and
  the Planned EON-C42 (only a valid checkpoint restores a tab's worktree tie). VEN-C8 only where it
  contradicts.

Positions the text is expected to carry (Lucca's review, 2026-11-10,
https://github.com/Yazelix/eon/pull/7#issuecomment-6768242579); the landed text wins where it
differs:

- One `stopped` state with `reason: "ended" | "start-unconfirmed"`. The namespace was fully
  enumerated under EON-C15, and Eon creates the record before spawning and removes residue only
  after the process is dead, so an intent without a record means no live run has that identity.
  The high-water mark still blocks reuse of its ID.
- Pane and popup: `state: "live" | "stopped"` and `stopped_reason`; endpoints are null unless the
  slot is validated live.
- Extra validated runs go to one freshly registered "Recovered" session after the original ones.
- When recovery acquires no live run, no recovered window opens. The checkpoint is kept for
  diagnosis. Stopped slots appear only beside a live run.
- A placeholder stays when a sibling exits. The window's last live exit still ends the window.
  Closing a placeholder removes it without a Stop.
- An inert pane-free tab and a live popup whose configuration was removed each get an explicit
  representation. Neither reuses `pending`.

## Prerequisites

- `eon-remote-workspaces-52i4.6.1` is closed (this bead's `blocks` dependency).

## Evidence

Edge `0157343`, EONW v38. `R` is `runtime/crates/eon-runtime/src`, `P` is
`runtime/crates/eon-workspace-protocol/src`.

- `R/supervisor.rs:1028`: `supervise` calls `recover_sessions` (`R/sessions.rs:718`), which
  acquires through `acquire_generation_sessions` (`R/sessions.rs:777`; more than 256 records refuse
  at `:803`). These are EON-C15's acquisition rules and stay as they are.
- `R/supervisor.rs:936` `recovered_workspace_sessions`, `R/workspace.rs:370`
  `WorkspaceSet::registered_recovered` and `R/workspace.rs:1315`
  `Workspace::with_recovered_sessions`: the flat projection (one `s1`, one `t1` in the launch
  directory, one column, panes `p{N}`, no popups), called at `R/supervisor.rs:1151` and `:1277`.
- `R/supervisor.rs:1066` submits a fresh `Operation::Register` for the recovered `s1`;
  `R/workspace.rs:492` `registered_recovery` then sets `persistent_id` or `registration_error`.
- `P/v38.rs:387` `Pane` already carries `live: bool` (`:393`). Runtime always sets it true
  (`R/workspace.rs:1409`). Venus draws a pane that is not live in `DEAD_PANE_TEXT`
  (`venus/src/render/chrome.rs:3046`).
- `P/v38.rs:2486` refuses a tab with no pane and no popup; `:2527` refuses a popup whose entry is
  not in the current catalog. Both restored states need these to change.
- `R/workspace.rs:1054` `session_ended` and `:769` `prune_empty`: natural-exit pruning and the
  rule that the last session's emptying ends the window (`R/supervisor.rs:2055`
  `closed_response`).
- Tests: `replacement_eon_adopts_exact_runs_and_projects_numeric_workspace`
  (`eon/crates/eon/tests/workspace_control.rs:9794`) with its `assert_recovery_failure` cases
  (`:9860`), and `PairWindow::crash` (`:3015`), which kills a supervisor and starts a replacement.
  Runtime-side: `c38_restart_keeps_live_terminals_reachable_when_registry_is_unavailable`
  (`R/supervisor.rs:3977`).
- `docs/USAGE.md:275-319` and `:1301` describe today's merged recovery and say pins are not
  recovered.

## Scope

In scope:
- After the whole run set has passed EON-C15's acquisition, read and validate this generation's
  checkpoint with the decoder from `.6.1`. When it is valid, build the window's sessions from it
  instead of the flat projection.
- Sessions in saved order with their recorded persistent IDs, confirmed by looking up the exact ID
  on the registry worker. With the registry unavailable the grouping stays, the member has a null
  `persistent_id` and a `registration_error`, and a retry resolves the recorded ID, never a new one
  or one with the same name.
- Tabs with their directories, columns and expansion, panes with pinned names, persistent popups
  with their launch directories, and the last committed selection. A selection whose target is
  gone falls back deterministically. Recovery takes no desktop focus.
- A slot is live only when both its terminal ID and its run ID match a validated run. Missing runs
  become stopped slots; extra runs go to the "Recovered" session; no live run means a normal fresh
  launch with the checkpoint kept aside.
- Placeholder lifecycle: sibling exit, the window's last live exit, and explicit close by ID
  through the existing `eon pane close`, `eon tab close` and `eon session close` paths.
- The wire representation of stopped panes and popups, the inert tab and the popup without a
  catalog entry, with EONW validation changed to match and the EONW bump this needs. The existing
  `live` field is replaced, not kept beside `state` (no legacy code).
- Venus: draw the new states. Read `venus/AGENTS.md` first.
- No replay: recovery starts no terminal, picker, popup command or agent. EON-C18's stale initial
  pair fallback applies to flat recovery only.
- Tests in the existing harness for the outcomes under Acceptance; `docs/USAGE.md`, `CHANGELOG.md`
  and the R1 and R2 rows of `docs/REMOTE-WORKSPACES.md`.

Out of scope:
- EON-C15's acquisition, bounds, lease and cleanup rules. A stale, mismatched or unsafe record
  still refuses the whole set, and its existing tests pass unmodified.
- What happens when the checkpoint is missing, damaged, of an unknown version or over capacity:
  until `eon-remote-workspaces-52i4.6.3` lands, that is today's flat recovery into a freshly
  registered `s1`, with the file kept aside. The window `recovery` field, the EON-C39 events,
  `checkpoint-unavailable` and `stopped-not-persisted` are also `.6.3`.
- eonbase, moving sessions between windows, SSH, reboot.

## Acceptance

- Three named sessions, two sharing a name and a directory, with several tabs and columns, a
  pinned pane name and a persistent popup. After the supervisor is killed, the replacement shows
  the same persistent IDs, names, membership and order, tab directories, expansion, pinned names,
  popup and selection. Every terminal has the same terminal ID, run ID and PID, and no Orbit
  process was started.
- Two replacements racing: one wins; the other changes nothing.
- A missing run shows as stopped with `ended` in its place; a saved intent without a record shows
  as stopped with `start-unconfirmed`, and its ID is not reused; an extra run appears in the
  "Recovered" session with a fresh persistent ID.
- Every run dead: a normal fresh launch, no dead panes, the checkpoint kept.
- Stopped `p1` beside live `p2`: when `p2` exits and other live runs remain, `p1` stays; when `p2`
  was the window's last live run, the window ends; `eon pane close p1` removes it and sends Orbit
  no Stop.
- A valid layout with the registry unavailable keeps its grouping, shows null `persistent_id` with
  `registration_error`, and later confirms the recorded ID.
- A popup whose configuration entry was removed stays live and usable. A saved tab directory that
  no longer exists blocks only a new spawn in it.
- `eon session ls --json` and inspection show each pane's and popup's `state` and
  `stopped_reason`.

## Verification

- `nix develop -c eon-test -p eon-runtime`, `-p eon` and the Venus crate exit 0 while iterating;
  `nix develop -c eon-test` over the whole workspace exits 0 on the final tree.
- `cargo fmt --check` and `cargo clippy --locked --all-targets -- -D warnings` for each changed
  crate.
- One isolated installed observation on x86_64 Linux Wayland of the first acceptance item: SIGKILL
  to the exact supervisor PID, a counter in a pane keeps advancing, and a fresh `eon` shows the
  same sessions.
- Review loop, plus Codex for the code and the contract text.

## Reference gate

Consequential (lifecycle and wire format). Record on this bead before code:
`docs/REFERENCES.md:171` and `:508`, and PR #2's exact `(terminal ID, run ID)` reconciliation and
stopped placeholders (`/home/lucca/.cache/eon-agents/eon-overseer/pr2/pr2.diff:9605`,
`supervisor/named.rs:630-648`), as specification only. Reject its "load the layout before
acquiring anything" order: acquisition comes first and never waits for the checkpoint or the
registry.

## Stop Conditions

- Stop if the cited code has drifted materially, or the landed contract text moves work between
  the three child beads.
- Stop if restoring needs any change to EON-C15's acquisition rules.
- Stop if a restored state can only be expressed by reusing `pending`.
- Stop if the checkpoint from `.6.1` lacks a field this needs: record the format change on this
  bead and bump the checkpoint version; do not infer the value.
- Stop if the plan shows this will not fit one session, and hand back a split at this seam:
  restoring the live structure, identities and selection; then stopped slots, extra runs,
  placeholder lifecycle and the inert tab and popup representations.
- Stop if verification fails twice for the same reason after a reasonable fix attempt.

## Execution split (prime-beads 2026-11-12)

Two ordered slices at the existing Stop Conditions seam: exact all-live structure/identity/selection restore; then missing/extra runs, stopped placeholders and inert/unconfigured representations. Original acceptance remains the full rollup, and .6.3 waits for both. Contract positions/owner/acquisition rules are unchanged.

Original acceptance is complete only after all children finish.

title: Keep recovered terminals usable when the checkpoint cannot be trusted, and show why
description:
## Why

After `eon-remote-workspaces-52i4.6.2`, a checkpoint that is missing, damaged, of an unknown
version or too large for the window's bounds still falls back to today's flat recovery, and nothing
tells the person or an agent that the original grouping was lost or why. This bead makes that
fallback an explicit degraded state that both can read and act on, keeps the terminals usable
through it, and closes the slice with its installed proof.

Third of three children of `eon-remote-workspaces-52i4.6` (slice 2b). Owner: Yu; agents start it
only when Lucca or Yu assigns it.

## Contract

The approved slice 2b text (`docs/LOCAL-SESSION-RECOVERY.md`, Yazelix/eon PR #7), not this
summary. This bead implements, and folds into `docs/CONTRACTS.md` with an "Amended on <date> ...
by <this bead>" line each:

- EON-C15: checkpoint failure, empty or over-capacity projections, degraded operations.
- EON-C33: the degraded-recovery paragraph.
- EON-C10 and EON-C39: the window's recovery state, the refusal codes and their exits, and the
  events. EON-C38: the degraded session's fresh registration.

Positions the text is expected to carry (Lucca's review, 2026-11-10,
https://github.com/Yazelix/eon/pull/7#issuecomment-6768242579); the landed text wins where it
differs:

- Degraded recovery renames the damaged file aside (kept, never deleted), starts a fresh
  checkpoint for the synthetic layout and names the kept path. Over capacity takes the same path.
- The degraded synthetic session is registered fresh, as slice 2a does. Old registrations stay
  untouched.
- Window snapshot: `recovery: null | {state: "restored" | "degraded", reason: {code, detail},
  preserved_path}`.
- In degraded mode, input, read, inspect, navigation, close and canonical Stop always work.
  Creation works once the damaged file is set aside. Only a persistent I/O error (EACCES, ENOSPC)
  keeps writes refused.
- Refusals `checkpoint-unavailable` and `stopped-not-persisted` (which lists the stopped targets),
  both exit 1. Exit 2 stays syntax, 3 a missing target, 4 unreachable or a lost reply.
- EON-C39 events `recovery-degraded` and `checkpoint-failed`. Inspection, the initial and gap
  snapshots and live events agree. `registration_error` stays for the registry only.

## Prerequisites

- `eon-remote-workspaces-52i4.6.2` is closed (this bead's `blocks` dependency).

## Evidence

Edge `0157343`, EONW v38. `R` is `runtime/crates/eon-runtime/src`, `P` is
`runtime/crates/eon-workspace-protocol/src`.

- `R/workspace.rs:370` `WorkspaceSet::registered_recovered` and `:1315`
  `Workspace::with_recovered_sessions`: today's flat projection, which becomes the degraded one.
- `P/v38.rs:653` `Snapshot` and `:595` `WorkspaceInfo` (`persistent_id`, `registration_error`):
  no field says how the window was recovered.
- `R/control.rs:868-886`: exit statuses (1 failed, 2 usage, 3 missing, 4 unreachable).
  `R/session_registry.rs:68-74` assigns `registry-busy`, `registry-uncertain` and
  `session-registry`: the pattern for a typed refusal that exits 1.
- `R/events.rs:179` `Event::name` (`session-registration-failed` at `:186`), `:498`
  `Projection::diff`; `P/v38/subscription.rs:134` `WorkspaceChange`; the initial snapshot at
  `R/subscriptions.rs:559` `window_snapshot` and the gap snapshot at `:318` `serve_gap`.
- `R/cli.rs:1597-1724` renders inspection and `eon session ls` (`registration_json` at `:1684`);
  `R/workspace.rs:3366` `json` builds the snapshot JSON.
- `venus/src/model.rs:415-485`: Venus shows a registration error as an `Eon <code>: <detail>`
  notice. The degraded state can use the same notice.
- `R/sessions.rs:803`: more than 256 records refuse the whole set. That refusal stays.

## Scope

In scope:
- The degraded path. When the checkpoint is missing, malformed, oversized, of an unknown version,
  has the wrong owner, mode, type or generation, holds duplicate references, or its structure plus
  the extra runs exceed 32 sessions or 256 terminal slots, and the whole run set passed EON-C15
  with at most 256 live runs: one freshly registered synthetic session holds every acquired run,
  the file is renamed aside and kept, a fresh checkpoint starts, and the window's `recovery` says
  `degraded` with a reason code, a detail and the kept path.
- `recovery` after a valid restore says `restored`; a window that was not recovered has null.
- A persistent I/O error on the checkpoint: launches and structural writes refuse with
  `checkpoint-unavailable`; a close that stopped its target but could not record it answers
  `stopped-not-persisted` with the stopped targets; everything else keeps working.
- The events `recovery-degraded` and `checkpoint-failed`, with the initial and gap snapshots
  agreeing with inspection.
- CLI: `eon session ls --json` and inspection carry `recovery`; the human output prints one line
  naming the reason and the kept path. Venus shows the same as a notice and takes no focus.
- The EONW bump these fields need, `docs/USAGE.md`, `CHANGELOG.md`, the R3 and R4 rows of
  `docs/REMOTE-WORKSPACES.md`, and `docs/LOCAL-SESSION-RECOVERY.md` marked as implemented with a
  pointer to `docs/CONTRACTS.md`.
- The slice's proof records on the amended EON-C15 and EON-C33 clauses.

Out of scope:
- A repair or reset command. Renaming the file aside is the way out.
- Deleting kept files.
- The restore logic of `eon-remote-workspaces-52i4.6.2` and the write path of `.6.1`.
- More than 256 live runs, or an exceeded acquisition bound: EON-C15 still refuses the whole set.
- SSH, reboot, cross-build takeover.

## Acceptance

- For each kind of damage (truncated, unknown version, oversized, wrong mode, wrong generation,
  duplicate reference): every validated run is usable in one session with a fresh persistent ID,
  the old registrations are unchanged, `recovery.state` is `degraded` with a code naming the
  damage, the file at `preserved_path` has the damaged file's bytes, and `eon tab create` works
  straight after.
- Original structure plus extra runs over the bounds, with exactly 256 live runs: degraded, every
  run shown. With 257: the whole set is refused, nothing is stopped and the checkpoint is intact.
- With checkpoint writes failing persistently (EACCES or ENOSPC injected): input, read,
  inspection, navigation, close and Stop work; `eon tab create` exits 1 with `checkpoint-unavailable`; closing a live pane stops it
  and exits 1 with `stopped-not-persisted` naming it.
- A subscriber sees `recovery-degraded` once; a subscriber that connects later reads the same
  state from its initial snapshot, and a gap snapshot matches inspection.
- Everything the Venus notice shows is in the `--json` output.
- The parent's installed observation passes on the final candidate.

## Verification

- `nix develop -c eon-test -p eon-runtime`, `-p eon` and the Venus crate exit 0 while iterating;
  `nix develop -c eon-test` over the whole workspace exits 0 on the final tree.
- `cargo fmt --check` and `cargo clippy --locked --all-targets -- -D warnings` for each changed
  crate.
- Isolated installed observation on x86_64 Linux Wayland, on the final candidate: the restore
  after SIGKILL and after a supervisor exit without Stop (the parent's acceptance); a corrupted
  checkpoint giving the degraded session, its notice and its JSON; one unsafe record among healthy
  runs refusing the whole set.
- Review loop, plus Codex for the code and the contract text.

## Reference gate

Consequential (lifecycle and wire format). Record on this bead before code: `docs/REFERENCES.md:508`
(recovering without guessing or silently reopening the wrong work; Power Failure Resumer at
`318d24fbab1b`) and slice 2a's registry-failure behaviour as the in-repository precedent
(`eon-remote-workspaces-52i4.5`: recovered work stays usable and the error is visible). Reject
PR #2's stderr warning as the only sign of an unclaimed run.

## Stop Conditions

- Stop if the cited code has drifted materially, or the landed contract text moves work between
  the three child beads.
- Stop if the degraded state needs a new window surface beyond the existing notice: that is new UI
  and needs Lucca.
- Stop if a degraded window cannot reach a writable checkpoint without deleting the damaged file.
- Stop if verification fails twice for the same reason after a reasonable fix attempt.

## Current evidence and portability

0157343/v38 anchors above are historical. At dcaef1c canonical protocol is v40.rs (Snapshot :671; WorkspaceChange in v40/subscription.rs:134); choose a fresh version with all consumers/goldens. WorkspaceSet::registered_recovered is workspace.rs:391 and recover_sessions is sessions.rs:742. .11 exact text remains unapproved. Portability neutral for checkpoint/JSON/events policy; private-file mechanics stay at Runtime's platform owner. Preserve whole-set unsafe-record refusals and exact Reserved Stop bytes. Final proof covers complete parent/degraded behavior rather than reusing earlier child claims beyond their exercised surface.

title: Add opt-in managed hosting: a host service and a Home Manager module
description:
## Why

Slice 4 of the remote-workspace plan Lucca adopted on 2026-10-28. Yu ports it as a PR.

## Goal

Opt-in managed hosting. An explicitly configured host service owns starting the remote supervisor: a systemd user service, and a Home Manager module for Nix users. SSH asks that owner to start it, then performs the same readiness and compatibility handshake as portable hosting. A service failure never silently falls back to an unmanaged launch. Orbit lifetimes stay outside the supervisor's service, so restarting the service never kills terminals. Logout-policy problems (logind KillUserProcesses, linger) are diagnosed and documented, never changed silently.

## Contract

The slice 1 hosting text. Portable hosting (eon-remote-ssh-x7dr.2) stays independent of this slice.

## Acceptance

- Home Manager switch and rollback, and a compatible upgrade, keep live work.
- The service failure path is shown.
- Proof on a systemd host. Portable hosting's own proof stays separate.
- Review loop and Codex.

## Reference

PR #2's independent Orbit scope approach, as specification only.

## Scope boundary

No change to the portable path. No service required anywhere.

## Ownership, acceptance detail and portability

Yu retains assignment control (remote epic, Lucca 2026-11-07 "ssh is with Yu"). Reuse .2's accepted portable handshake/launch owner. Compatibility is identical EONW/Orbit management/ORBS/ORBF versions, not build IDs. Exact EON-C34/EON-C15/configuration amendments require Lucca; record reference revisions, tool version policy and exit condition before code. Portability: isolated Linux/systemd opt-in; no service-manager requirement in portable hosting. Runtime accepts opaque component inputs and never queries Nix; one component graph.

Prove compatible service restart, Home Manager switch and rollback preserve terminal/run/PID identity and live work; selected-service failure reports honestly without unmanaged fallback; incompatible readiness refuses without changing work. Diagnose logout/linger policy, never change it. Document opt-in/disable/defaults and CLI/data visibility. title: Send incremental terminal frames with bounded backpressure over remote attach
description:
## Why

Slice 6 of the remote-workspace plan Lucca adopted on 2026-10-28. Yu ports it as a PR.

## Goal

Over a remote attach, terminal updates travel as incremental frames with bounded backpressure, and resynchronize with a full snapshot when they fall behind. Correctness is checked against the full-frame baseline.

## Acceptance

- The same screen content as the full-frame path across a test corpus.
- Measured wire bytes, CPU, input latency and queue memory under constrained RTT and bandwidth, against the baseline, per AP-PERF-001.
- Review loop and Codex.

## Scope boundary

No history paging (slice 7), no prediction (eon-remote-workspaces-52i4.1).


## Owner and approval gate
Yu owns this slice; agents start only on assignment. Orbit owns authoritative frames/revisions,
orbit-protocol any encoding, Venus canonical-frame consumption, Runtime SSH attachment.
Read orbit/AGENTS.md, venus/AGENTS.md, ORB-C4/C6/C7 and the remote-plan matrix. Before code,
record the reference revisions, full-frame baseline, chosen version policy and exact contract
amendments for approval. A wire change bumps the version and names Venus, Runtime and Eon as
consumers. No Runtime frame schema or second terminal owner.

## Concrete correctness and pressure checks
Compare reconstructed rich frames to the full-frame oracle across resize, synchronized output,
wide/combining text, styles, cursor, links and graphics. Text-only equality cannot prove ORB-C6.
State queue/byte caps before measurement. A deliberately slow receiver must stay bounded and
resynchronize to one coherent snapshot plus ordered revisions, never mixed state or replayed input.
Invalid/missing deltas fail or resync explicitly under the approved format; disconnect stops no
terminals. Record wire bytes, CPU, peak queue memory and input-latency distributions at specified
RTT/bandwidth/grid/workload, exact before/after identities and negative results.
Use the affected protocol proof route, frame invariants, machine-local performance gate and
isolated two-host delivery. Coalesce work is related, not a new blocker. Portability: neutral wire
with socket/SSH mechanics at existing owners. The child split below bounds producer and consumer work; confirm each scope after exact contract approval.

## One-session split
This is the incremental-frame epic, not a single implementation session.
1. eon-remote-workspaces-52i4.8.1: reference/design and exact contract approval.
2. eon-remote-workspaces-52i4.8.2: canonical producer/codec and bounded publication.
3. eon-remote-workspaces-52i4.8.3: canonical consumer/resync and installed remote pressure proof.
Each blocks the next. All original correctness, bytes/CPU/latency/memory and bounded-resync
acceptance remains on this parent and is distributed across those children.

title: Remove inert component launch selection
description:
## Contract routing

Harden EON-C2 after eon-authoritative-component-launch-declarations-iam. Consumers are Eon manifest validation, raw generation identity, Nix composition, and Rust launch policy. When a canonical graph is validated, it must contain no launch declaration that Nix and Rust ignore. Schema 3 removes component.launch; non-library roles must still declare at least one file artifact. An obsolete launch field must fail validation before generation selection, runtime state, or child spawn.

## Confirmed defect

On the current schema-2 graph, changing Orbit launch.artifact from executable to terminfo validates. Renaming the executable artifact and its launch reference together also validates. Nix reads neither launch nor artifacts for program selection; Rust launches EON_ORBIT with hardcoded serve. The exact production digest changed from g1-ce32c5dc7d666f554a285d8565af9d03 to g1-62d75c6ec347f316f6d1a5d98ced7d8f and g1-b441f19b7638ef7df08fa342d78aaebf respectively. This violates the prior Bead acceptance that inert graph edits cannot select a false fresh generation.

## Reference gate and decision

Read the complete prior Bead and explicit schema-2 approval, current EON-C2 proof, canonical manifest, complete validator, every launch/artifact reference, Nix component resolution and package wiring, Rust generation hashing/version reporting/program launch, and architecture/distribution ownership text. Architecture assigns launch policy to Rust and physical paths to Nix; the graph owns abstract artifact identity and compatibility. The user has now authorized the recommended deletion, superseding the prior decision to retain Launch.artifact.

Adopt schema 3 with no schema-2 compatibility path: delete Launch and every launch object, preserve abstract Artifact id/kind, and replace launch-plan validation with the existing role-level requirement that each non-library component has a declared file artifact. Reject Nix assertion plumbing, generic launch translation, path metadata, dependencies, and child changes.

## Scope

In scope: canonical manifest schema/file name, eon-manifest types/validation/focused rejection test, embedded/runtime and Nix references, EON-C2 current-state proof wording/status, architecture/distribution/README current-state paths, changelog, LOC, generation preflight, exact build/profile proof.

Out of scope: artifact path restoration, general launcher schemas, changing actual Orbit/Venus or managed-tool argv, direct distribution, schema compatibility/migration, dependencies, component revisions, child repositories, or other contracts.

## Acceptance

- Schema 3 contains no Launch type or launch field and rejects any launch object as unknown.
- Every service, client, and tool still declares at least one file artifact; libraries remain non-launch policy.
- The prior terminfo swap and coordinated rename cannot be expressed as a launch selection.
- Nix and Rust retain their current single owners and exact program/argv behavior.
- Invalid old launch bytes fail before generation identity or runtime effects.
- Abstract artifact identity, compatibility, version reporting, generated-runtime coverage, and live Sessions remain intact.

## Verification

TDD the old launch object rejection; focused eon-manifest tests; locked workspace fmt/check/test/clippy; canonical manifest validation; invalid embedded graph command matrix; exact Nix build and flake check; git diff check; LOC; active profile and installed versions/dogfood without restarting supervisors.

## Stop conditions

Stop before adding a dependency, compatibility path, generic launcher, physical artifact metadata, child change, or launch behavior change. Stop if removing Launch would weaken the non-library file-artifact invariant or if any independent consumer of schema 2 is found.

title: Rename EonTerm to eonbase
description:
## Outcome
The standalone exact-command product is named eonbase. Its command is `eonbase`, with the
same CLI EonTerm has today, and `eonterm` is gone from product, package and docs.

## Decision (user, 2026-10-15)
- Name: eonbase. "eonterm" reads as Eon itself, and the site is eonterm.com. The product is
  the base layer: Orbit terminals, Venus windows and the runtime lifecycle, with Eon adding the
  workspace and managed tools on top (flake.nix eontermPackage, cli.rs LaunchMode::Terminal).
- Command: `eonbase`, a separate binary, not `eon base`. The slim closure must exclude the eon
  package and every managed tool (eonterm-closure check), so a subcommand would defeat it.
- No `eonterm` alias. One alpha tag shipped it and stays usable at its pin. One spelling per
  product (docs/ARCHITECTURE.md naming boundary).
- No short `eb` command: the AWS Elastic Beanstalk CLI (nixpkgs awsebcli) installs `eb`. User
  docs may suggest `alias eb=eonbase` as an optional shell alias.
- Rejected names: eonlet, eonling, eontiny, eonlite, eonmini, eonslate, eonplate, eonboard,
  eonb, beon. eonbase was absent from nixpkgs, PATH and a web search on 2026-10-15.

## CLI contract
eonbase [--no-decorations] [--application-id ID] -- COMMAND...
eonbase generations [--json]
eonbase attach [GENERATION]
eonbase stop GENERATION [--json]

## Scope
- runtime/crates/eon-runtime: argv[0] dispatch (cli.rs `eonterm` check), EONTERM_USAGE,
  lifecycle hints and errors, LaunchMode::Terminal display name, runtime namespace directory,
  default application ID, sessions.rs and supervisor.rs messages, test names.
- flake.nix: package pname, bin rename, license paths, `eonterm` package/app outputs,
  `eonterm-closure` check, EONTERM_BIN; .github/workflows/cachix.yml build target.
- demo/record.rs features take, docs/DEVELOPMENT.md.
- docs: ARCHITECTURE.md naming boundary, CONTRACTS.md EON-C12 and EON-C16 and other mentions,
  USAGE.md, CONFIGURATION.md, DISTRIBUTION.md, REFERENCES.md, README.md,
  venus/docs/CONTRACTS.md consumer text, CHANGELOG.md entry ("eonterm is now eonbase").
- Leave dated benchmark records (docs/benchmarks, venus/docs/benchmarks) and historical proof
  commits as written.

## Prerequisites and reference gate
- Confirm no approved EON-C16 composition invokes `eonterm` or depends on its default app ID.
- Decide and record the runtime namespace move: live generations under the old `eonterm`
  directory stay reachable only through the old pinned binary. Document that or migrate.
- Related: eon-4is.6 (EonTerm on Nova systems) and eon-readme-agent-workspace-06m3 use the old
  name and need their text updated when this lands.

## Acceptance
- `rg -i eonterm` outside .beads, target, dated benchmarks and CHANGELOG history finds nothing.
- `eonbase -- COMMAND`, generations, attach, stop and both flags behave as EON-C12 and EON-C16
  state, re-proved in the automated tier and installed checklist item 11 under the new name.
- The renamed closure check passes. eonbase's closure excludes the eon package and every managed
  tool, and `eon` plus `eonbase` coinstall.
- Invoking the binary under any other name fails with the eonbase usage.
- Release notes tell alpha users to reinstall with `#eonbase`.

## Boundary
Naming only. No CLI, behavior, contract-semantics or packaging-content change. Eon, Orbit,
Venus and the eonterm.com domain keep their names. The site guides follow in eon-site after a
release tag ships eonbase.
close_reason: EonTerm is now eonbase across command, package, app, closure check, runtime namespace, application ID, tests and docs; retired eonterm name fails with eonbase usage. Proof and ledger in comments.

title: Spike: host Venus's terminal grid inside Rune on Linux, with the bottom bar drawn by Rune
description:
## Why

Lucca, 2026-11-07: "would like to check against gpui and rune options". Lucca, 2026-11-10: "is venus
a local maximum? will we hit a wall? what does adopting rune (or forking it!) would buy for us?
would we be able to simplify things, delete loc?". Research that day (the 2026-11-10 comment on this
bead) found:

- Venus's strain is its chrome, not its grid: about 1,000 lines per new control, no text field,
  list, rich text or theming.
- Rune (anomalyco/rune, MIT, pre-release) is the first framework that fits Venus's base: wgpu 30,
  winit 0.30.13 and AccessKit 0.25.2, with an in-pass custom render hook (`Compositor` plus
  `El::effect` hand the app a `wgpu::RenderPass` in painter order, scissored). It has no terminal,
  grid or positioned-glyph primitive, so the grid would stay Venus's own pipeline inside that hook.
- Everything Rune measures is Apple Silicon headless. Its Linux side is the unknown: CI tests run on
  macOS only, and open issues include a covered Wayland window spinning a core (#139), a focused
  field redrawing every frame (#225), no popup menus on Linux (#529) and no primary selection (#541).

Retargeted 2026-11-10 with Lucca's approval ("ok:" to: "Rune after v0.2.0: a bounded hosting spike?
I recommend yes, with no adoption or fork now. The spike would put Venus's cell pipeline inside
Rune's hook on Linux with one chrome surface (the bottom bar) drawn by Rune, and measure idle CPU,
frame cost, Wayland behaviour and line count. ... I would retarget that bead rather than file a new
one."). The earlier body asked to draw the grid in GPUI and in Rune and compare speed; Rune cannot
draw a grid itself, so that comparison does not exist.

Lucca, 2026-11-10, on forking: "venus already has a high cost, so a rune fork would not be that bad
imo, but i could be wrong". Adoption and fork are both undecided; this spike supplies the evidence.

## Spike (throwaway, outside the product, nothing lands in Eon)

After v0.2.0 is cut (blocked by eon-igae.9).

1. In a throwaway program outside the Eon workspace, at a recorded Rune `dev` commit (research read
   3686e94), open a Rune window on Linux Wayland with Vulkan and draw Venus's terminal cell pipeline
   inside Rune's effect hook, fed by a recorded Orbit frame corpus (the eon-bench final screens:
   80x24 and a large window, dense styled cells and Unicode).
2. Draw one real chrome surface with Rune: the bottom bar (clock, version, CPU, RAM and disk chips,
   quota), matching Venus's look as closely as Rune's styling allows.
3. Measure, each with a distribution and against the same corpus in Venus on the same machine: idle
   CPU (visible, covered and unfocused window), frame time to present for a full-grid change and for
   a one-cell change, startup time, memory. Use the change-sized probes from
   eon-venus-scroll-text-baseline-juo5, and separate Orbit's pacing cost from the renderer's (see
   eon-orbit-coalesce-gu13n and eon-benchmarks-xl2bp.4).
4. Observe on a real Wayland session and record: fractional scale, IME in a Rune text field, clipboard
   and primary selection, device loss, the accessibility tree as Orca reads it, and the open issues
   above.
5. Count lines: the Rune view code for the bottom bar against Venus's code for it across scene,
   chrome, application and accessibility.

## Report

- The numbers, and a plain verdict on whether Venus's grid can live inside Rune on Linux at Venus's
  current frame cost and idle CPU.
- What using Rune would cost Eon in each form: a pinned upstream commit; a Yazelix-owned fork pinned
  by revision (as Eon already does for winit); a frozen snapshot with Eon's patches. For the fork
  forms: which Rune modules Eon had to touch or would have to fix for Linux, upstream churn per week
  at that date, and whether Rune's releases, Linux CI and issue turnaround have changed (2026-11-10:
  no releases, 253 open and 13 closed issues, pull requests not accepted).
- Frictions found: Eon's patched winit against Rune's crates.io winit; text moving from cosmic-text
  to Parley (VEN-C19 typography); the seven chrome contracts that would need re-proof.
- A recommendation. Adoption or a fork is a separate decision for Lucca.

## Scope boundary

- No change to Venus or any Eon crate; nothing vendored or copied into Eon.
- GPUI is not measured here: upstream GPUI has no custom render hook, so its grid cannot be hosted
  the same way. GPUI stays under the deferred decision eon-ua5e; the fork gpui-ce's texture hook can
  be a follow-up only if Lucca asks.
- Building Rune runs its build scripts and 600-odd dependencies. Build it outside the product at the
  pinned commit; recommended (the filing session's view, not Lucca's instruction): in a sandbox or
  disposable VM without credentials. Follow the agents' machine-load rule.

## Acceptance

- The report above is recorded on this bead with revisions, machine, commands and results.
- A numbered list of decisions for Lucca, each with a recommendation.

## Current execution state (2026-11-12)

The spike specification above is historical. Comments 6425-6469 lifted the original
post-v0.2.0 timing and staged the work; the 2026-11-11 overseer completion comment
records tracks A-I done and Lucca's decision to invest in Rune through a Yazelix
fork tracking upstream. Do not rerun the original five-step spike or seek the
already-recorded adoption choice. The adopted terms and exits are in

Estimate if a framework drew the chrome and owned windowing, text, accessibility and IME: gross 7,000-10,850 non-test lines removed, net 4,000-8,000 after replacement view code, plus 8,000-14,000 test lines deleted or rewritten (estimate from outlines, not a port; assumes a custom render hook). 20 active VEN-C contracts: 13 constrain renderer/text/input/windowing, 7 specify chrome to the pixel.

Rune (clone ~/pjs/refs/rune, dev 3686e94, 2026-11-10): same base as Venus (wgpu 30.0.1, winit 0.30.13, AccessKit 0.25.2). Has an in-pass custom render hook (Compositor + El::effect hands the app a wgpu::RenderPass in painter order, scissored), Taffy layout, text fields with IME, widgets (tab strip, lists, popover, menu, scroll), springs, AccessKit tree from elements, and headless --snap/--tree/--script on the real renderer (what eon-qdcgw wants). No terminal, grid or positioned-glyph primitive (rune#542): the grid would stay Venus's pipeline inside the hook, so this bead's step 1 ("draw the grid in Rune") does not fit as written. No damage tracking; the paint walk re-emits visible instances each drawn frame. Text is Parley/swash, not cosmic-text. Maturity: 20 days old, 1,956 commits, no releases or tags, 253 open / 13 closed issues, CI tests on macOS only, churn 40k-280k lines a week. Linux gaps: covered window spins a core (#139), focused field redraws every frame (#225), no popup menus on Linux (#529), no primary selection (#541), no blur. Device-loss recovery landed 2026-11-10 (ba5e7c80), a no-op on its native Metal backend. Fork: crates/rune is a 196k-line monolith (322k workspace), PLAN.md tenet 7 says optimised for agents "not for human readability". Eon pins a patched winit; Rune binds crates.io winit. All performance numbers in the repo are Apple Silicon headless; Linux/Vulkan cost with a grid inside is unknown.

Other stacks (checked 2026-11-10): GPUI upstream still has no release, no hook, damage PR zed#62455 closed 10-30. gpui-ce 0.3.0 has a shared-device texture hook (ce#237). Options that keep a custom wgpu grid and delegate chrome: Rune (in-pass hook), gpui-ce (texture composite), egui (paint callback, immediate mode), Iced (shader widget, no accessibility), zgui (one month old, one author), Slint (licence fails), or stay custom and add pieces (taffy, Parley). Masonry/Xilem has no hook (xilem#1319).

Competitors: 13 agent apps are Electron/Tauri (11 xterm.js, 2 libghostty-vt WASM); 4 on GPUI (herdr-app, Agentaps, Zeron, Zed) painting cells with GPUI primitives, with terminal-quality bugs (herdr-app #851 wide glyphs, #794 30 fps, #844 emoji) and all pinning snapshots or forks; Ghostty/cmux/Flow host libghostty's renderer in native toolkits; Warp alone built its own framework; the hand-rolled group (kitty, WezTerm, Alacritty, foot, Rio, Venus) ships no diff, chat or settings UI from its own renderer. No product was found sharing one wgpu surface between its own grid pipeline and a general framework.

If this spike runs, the question worth measuring for Rune is not grid speed but hosting: Venus's cell pipeline inside Rune's effect hook on Linux Wayland/Vulkan with one chrome surface in Rune, measuring idle CPU, frame cost, Wayland behaviour and line count.

title: Repair Stop completion and owned picker cleanup
description:
## Contract

Under EON-C11, C15, C18 and C23, an explicit Stop of a selected disposable window or generation completes its owned terminal and transient-helper cleanup, reports an accurate bounded result, and preserves peer and older-generation work. Orbit retains process/PTY containment; Runtime retains lifecycle policy, inventory and action-result ownership.

## Evidence and prerequisites

The completed eon-qualify-nix-linux-beta-bxoh is No-Go for Eon 92e0d7b379a14d003f37e5c2df9c468cb43e74b7. An independent-window Stop returned exit 2 with an action-result read timeout even though its intended terminals subsequently ended. A later generation Stop returned success and inventory reported dead while its Orbit directory picker, helper and fzf remained live; bare Eon recovery plus another owner Stop was needed. These are observed failures, not an established shared root cause. See /home/lucca/.local/state/eon/proofs/eon-beta-bxoh-2026-10-07-1845/qualification.json and observations; the compact qualification.txt preserves the exact component graph and environment.

## Reference gate

Read the governing contract sections and the retained observations. Trace Runtime control, supervisor, generation and sessions callers, transient-picker cleanup and Orbit management/containment at the exact accepted revisions. Inspect crates/eon/tests/workspace_control.rs, especially lost-result, failed-picker-Stop and independent-window coverage. Resolve the owner before choosing a fix; route any child mechanism correction to that child and consume only its accepted revision.

## Acceptance

- Reproduce or explain both failures with retained exact evidence and identify their responsible owner(s).
- The installed independent-window Stop completes without the observed spurious result timeout and leaves its peers unchanged.
- A successful generation Stop with an active picker leaves no test-owned managed Orbit/helper/fzf process or endpoint. Genuine partial cleanup remains diagnosable and retryable; inventory and result do not falsely imply completion.
- Preserve bounded shutdown, exact process authority and the existing exception for deliberately detached processes. Add the cheapest meaningful regression check at the changed owner; verify affected Rust/Nix surfaces and one isolated installed observation at the accepted graph.

## Scope boundary

Repair these two Stop failures only; if diagnosis finds independent causes, record them without assuming one patch fixes both. No process-wide kill, blanket timeout increase, cgroup/service dependency, new lifecycle guarantee or protocol framework. Preserve live user terminals and desktop focus. EonTerm package build failures are separately tracked.

title: Report invalid focus actions before supervisor connection
description:
## Contract routing

Harden EON-C10 while preserving EON-C8. The consumer is the canonical local `eon` CLI; the trigger is a syntactically valid `eon focus ID` command whose ID cannot be encoded by the shared EONW owner; the result is a bounded local `malformed-action` failure before any supervisor connection attempt. Valid focus actions and genuine missing, unreachable, incompatible, or corrupt supervisor failures retain their current behavior.

This is a defect correction. It adds no EONW value, validation rule, public command, dependency, compatibility window, Venus behavior, or workspace policy.

## Why

`send_action` connects before `send_action_on` encodes the request. An empty or longer-than-128-byte focus ID is therefore reported as `supervisor-unavailable` with advice to run Eon even when a healthy endpoint accepted the connection. The same invalid action is classified differently when the socket is absent. The command sends no request bytes and mutates no workspace, but its diagnosis points at the wrong owner.

Impact: LOW. Effort: S. Implementation risk: LOW. Confidence: HIGH.

## Evidence

- Closed audit `eon-audit-eonw-boundary-k3y`, comments 285-286, records the exact `57d7acc22f9f01c7f15d9d381845318b67f760e1` snapshot, reproduction, reference gate, and verification.
- `crates/eon/src/main.rs:121-123`: `send_action` connects before delegating request encoding.
- `crates/eon/src/main.rs:184-204`: `send_action_on` encodes only after it owns a stream and classifies encoding failure as endpoint corruption.
- `crates/eon/src/main.rs:1352-1368`: `control` maps every non-dead local client failure to `supervisor-unavailable` and appends `run eon first`.
- `crates/eon/src/main.rs:1387-1414`: focus IDs become `Action::FocusId` without duplicating protocol limits.
- `crates/eon-workspace-protocol/src/lib.rs:168-197` and `:570-580`: the shared encoder correctly owns the nonempty and 128-byte FocusId constraints.
- `crates/eon/src/main.rs:2110-2116`: `malformed-action` is already Eon's bounded EONW failure code for an invalid action; reuse it instead of creating another public token.
- Audit reproduction with an owned mode-0600 Unix listener: `eon focus '' --json` exited 2 with `supervisor-unavailable`, told the user to run Eon, connected, and sent zero bytes. A 129-byte ID behaved identically.

## Prerequisite and reference gate

- No implementation prerequisite.
- Rebaseline the cited symbols and read EON-C8, EON-C10, the complete EONW request encoder, all `send_action`/`send_action_on` callers, and the focused workspace-control test before editing.
- Existing EONW and CLI failure owners completely define the correction. No external reference or dependency comparison is required unless those owners have materially changed.
- This Bead blocks the final cross-subsystem integration audit: applying this client-path correction afterward would invalidate that audit's unchanged-snapshot convergence.

## Scope

In scope:
- The smallest request-preparation/send boundary in `crates/eon/src/main.rs` that encodes ordinary actions before endpoint connection and preserves the already connected, identity-checked presentation path.
- One deterministic real CLI/socket regression in `crates/eon/tests/workspace_control.rs`.
- EON-C10 current-state proof metadata, `CHANGELOG.md`, and the README LOC scorecard as required by the accepted behavior correction.

Out of scope:
- Changing EONW framing, tags, bounds, validation rules, or the `Failure` schema.
- Duplicating FocusId length or emptiness checks in CLI parsing.
- Changing valid focus behavior, direction keywords, workspace state, supervisor-side rejection, Venus, Orbit, runtime discovery, or connection security.
- A generic transport framework, new error hierarchy, protocol dependency, or broader `main.rs` refactor.

## Implementation notes

1. Write the real-process regression first using the existing test helpers and an owned mode-0600 Unix listener. Prove both empty and 129-byte focus IDs return exit 2, structured `malformed-action` JSON, empty stderr, and no `run eon first` guidance; prove the listener receives no connection and the workspace cannot mutate.
2. Prepare and encode the request through `eon_workspace_protocol::encode_request` before `send_action` calls `connect_control`. Keep one shared encode/send path for path-based and already-connected callers where practical, without weakening the socket-identity check in `present_at`.
3. Distinguish local encoding failure from endpoint failure only as much as needed to route `control` to the existing bounded `malformed-action` result. Do not copy protocol constants or semantic validation into the CLI.
4. Preserve `missing-supervisor` and `supervisor-unavailable` plus their launch guidance for genuine endpoint failures.
5. Update current-state EON-C10 proof evidence after the proof-bearing commit, refresh the installed profile, and leave running supervisors and Sessions untouched.

## Acceptance

- `eon focus '' --json` and a 129-byte focus ID exit 2 with bounded `malformed-action` JSON, write nothing to stderr, and do not advise starting Eon.
- Neither invalid command attempts a Unix connection or sends request bytes; no workspace or Session state changes.
- The result is independent of whether a supervisor socket exists.
- A valid focus ID still reaches the current supervisor and returns its complete accepted snapshot.
- A valid workspace command with no supervisor still returns `missing-supervisor`; genuine endpoint failures retain their current classification and guidance.
- EONW remains the sole owner of FocusId validation. No new public failure code, protocol value, dependency, child change, or compatibility promise is introduced.
- The owner-bound `present_at` flow still revalidates socket identity before sending its valid presentation action.

## Verification

- `cargo test --locked -p eon --test workspace_control invalid_focus_is_rejected_before_supervisor_connection` should exit 0 and prove the exact failure shape plus absence of a connection.
- `cargo test --locked -p eon --test workspace_control missing_supervisor_is_a_structured_workspace_failure` should exit 0.
- `cargo fmt --all --check`
- `cargo check --locked --workspace`
- `cargo test --locked --workspace`
- `cargo clippy --locked --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings`
- `cargo run --locked -p eon-manifest -- components/eon-alpha-v1.json`
- `nix build --no-link --print-out-paths --no-update-lock-file path:.#default`
- `nix flake check --no-build --no-update-lock-file path:.`
- `git diff --check`
- After the proof-bearing commit, refresh the active `eon` profile from the working tree without stopping live supervisors; verify it resolves to the just-built artifact and report that existing generations require restart for changed installed behavior.

## Stop conditions

- Stop if EONW validation, CLI failure projection, or the owner-bound presentation send path has materially changed.
- Stop if the correction requires a new failure code, protocol/schema change, duplicated validation, dependency, Venus/Orbit edit, or weakening socket ownership.
- Stop if the regression cannot prove absence of a connection deterministically.
- Stop if the same verification failure repeats twice after a reasonable correction.

## Maintenance notes

Reuse the existing encoder and `malformed-action` code. Reject CLI-side length checks, preflight-by-double-encoding, a generic request framework, or a broader endpoint taxonomy redesign.
notes: Implemented at source proof d0c2208d628fa0dc1e186899b45e0b73534ff9bc. EONW encode_request remains the only FocusId validator; send_action prepares once before connect, while the owner-checked present_at path keeps its connect and identity order. Local preparation failure alone maps to existing malformed-action. The regression covers empty and 129-byte IDs with absent and listening sockets and proves no connection; genuine missing-supervisor behavior remains covered. No dependency, protocol, manifest, Orbit, or Venus change. The current canonical manifest is components/eon-alpha-v3.json; it replaces the stale v1 path in the issue verification list.
close_reason: Invalid FocusId actions are now rejected locally before any supervisor connection, with exact source, regression, Nix, and installed-runtime proof.

title: Resolve public EonTerm lifecycle build failures
description:
## Contract

The exact public x86_64 Linux EonTerm Nix candidate must build and install through its required package checks, then run the EON-C12 exact-command terminal contract. Shared lifecycle checks remain meaningful; successful Eon or a prior EonTerm artifact does not substitute for this delivery proof.

## Evidence and prerequisites

eon-qualify-nix-linux-beta-bxoh recorded two failures at Eon 92e0d7b379a14d003f37e5c2df9c468cb43e74b7: the serial lifecycle suite failed five cases with 16 build cores, then replacement_eon_adopts_exact_runs_and_projects_numeric_workspace failed with one core (Ready not published within five seconds; rollback Ready claim remained busy). The first failures covered Anima handoff, picker Stop, EonTerm residue replacement and launch overlapping terminal exit. Both suites were serial. Concurrent host builds were present; load has not been established as the cause. Eon built successfully. Logs: /home/lucca/.local/state/eon/proofs/eon-beta-bxoh-2026-10-07-1845/public-eonterm-build-failed.log and public-eonterm-build-one-core-failed.log.

## Reference gate

Read EON-C11, C12, C15 and the retained package logs. Inspect crates/eon/tests/workspace_control.rs, the consuming Nix package check configuration and exact Runtime/Orbit readiness, recovery and teardown owners. Distinguish a product lifecycle defect, test-observer defect and declared environment limitation using evidence before choosing a change.

## Acceptance

- Accept the demonstrated delivery repairs with retained failures and focused regression proof. Keep the original Ready timeout's initiating cause explicitly unknown; a passing retry or induced delay does not diagnose that historical event. By user decision on 2026-10-08, that unknown historical cause does not block this delivery-repair acceptance.
- The immutable public candidate passes its required lifecycle package checks and installs in a fresh, credential-free user environment. Bind exact public source/graph, hosted build, signed artifacts and installed observation; distinguish the fresh user environment from its shared daemon/store and retain the limits of the evidence.
- An installed candidate runs an exact command, detaches/reopens the same terminal and stops only its selected disposable work.
- Use the verification route required by the actual changed owner; exact accepted child fixes must pass downstream delivery. Coordinate overlapping root causes with the Stop repair instead of duplicating mechanisms.

## Scope boundary

No skipped checks, blanket timeout increases, unproved load excuse, speculative compatibility layer or platform expansion. Scope is the failed delivery boundary and its responsible source/test owner. Both repair issues occupy the same sequential lifecycle frontier; no parallel product work is implied. The user approved delivery-repair acceptance on 2026-10-08 with the original Ready initiating cause retained as unknown. This decision does not diagnose that event or accept sustained reliability, beta, distribution graduation or another product frontier.

title: Return committed workspace action results within the client deadline
description:
## Contract

Harden EON-C10: when `eon tab create` or `eon pane create` starts an Orbit Session within the supervisor's accepted work bound, the original CLI request returns the committed typed workspace snapshot. It must not report `supervisor-unavailable` after the Session has been accepted, and one request must create at most one Session.

Consumer: the local `eon` CLI and agents consuming its structured action results. Trigger: Session startup completes after the current client control timeout but before the supervisor's Session-start timeout. Result: the initiating client receives the single truthful committed result within one bounded deadline. Important failures: a pre-commit startup failure preserves the prior workspace; a response failure never encourages an unsafe retry after an unknown commit; unrelated actions remain bounded.

## Steps to Reproduce

The final pass of `eon-audit-eon-runtime-lifecycle-wqz` at exact edge revision `88a57f066e426cb2882c4969b9036c4e358fc48b` reproduced the defect with a delayed Orbit substitute: `eon pane create --json` exited 2 after about 2.048 seconds with `supervisor-unavailable`, while the supervisor completed inside its five-second bound and a later workspace snapshot showed the new `session-2` live. Current edge `d8cf277731f112c898843354edb941d02d04cb21` still defines a two-second `CONTROL_TIMEOUT` and five-second `SESSION_START_TIMEOUT`; no existing Bead owns this defect.

Impact HIGH; effort S; implementation risk LOW/MEDIUM; confidence HIGH. A user or agent may retry after the false failure and create another unwanted Session, which has no individual stop action.

## Prerequisites and reference gate

The lifecycle audit and independent replacement-socket correction are closed. Before code, reread EON-C10, the action request/response path, workspace dispatch commit ordering, the delayed-Session audit reproduction, and the matching `docs/REFERENCES.md` route. Keep one Eon-owned bounded deadline policy across client wait and maximum server work, or use the smallest action-aware equivalent. Preserve the private EONW control boundary and Orbit/Venus ownership.

Reject a retry framework, request journal, deduplication protocol, new dependency, child change, public timeout setting, asynchronous action API, or compatibility surface unless the smallest deadline-owner correction cannot satisfy the contract.

## Scope

In scope: the shared action-response deadline invariant in `crates/eon/src/main.rs`, one deterministic real-process regression with Session startup strictly between the old client and server bounds, required EON-C10 proof/current documentation, CHANGELOG and README LOC updates when runtime behavior changes, locked Rust/Nix/profile verification, and a post-change fresh-eyes/simplification pass.

Out of scope: socket cleanup, supervisor replacement, retry or idempotency infrastructure, individual Session stop, durability across supervisor or machine loss, configurable deadlines, child behavior, new contracts, dependencies, compatibility windows, or interruption of live supervisors.

## Acceptance Criteria

- A deterministic red/green check delays CreatePane or CreateTab startup beyond the old client deadline but within the accepted server bound; the original command returns the accepted typed snapshot and exactly one new Session exists.
- A startup failure before commit returns one bounded failure and leaves the accepted workspace and Sessions unchanged.
- The client cannot report `supervisor-unavailable` solely because accepted server work is still inside its owner-approved bound.
- One owner defines the complete request/work/response deadline relationship; the correction remains bounded and adds no retry, journal, protocol field, dependency, or public setting.
- Existing workspace actions, malformed-action handling, control framing, concurrent startup, lifecycle, and replacement-socket checks remain green.
- Locked format, check, tests, Clippy, Nix build/check, LOC, and `git diff --check` pass.
- The active Eon profile resolves to the exact working-tree artifact without restarting running supervisors or Sessions.
- A complete post-change correctness and simplification pass finds no further in-scope correction.
notes: Published Eon proof source a390fc5c007900c3fc8c9c49df85f9b8acc06d4a and Eonova rollout source 247265c44f759f8142783af7dfd5415c25211c5c on origin/edge. EON-C10 is Proven. The named eon, eonterm, and eonova profile elements resolve the verified artifacts recorded in the acceptance comment. Existing live Eonova generations were not restarted.

title: Scale the review loop by risk
description:
## Decision
Lucca, 2026-10-15: scale the per-slice review loop by risk instead of repeating fresh-context
passes until one finds nothing.

## Contract
- Consumer: the implementing agent and its reviewers.
- Result: review depth follows the Verification table's change classes. Docs, planning and agent
policy get one fresh-eyes pass; a pass converges when it has no blocking findings (incorrect claims,
lost information, broken links, scope breaches), while style nits are optional. Code that touches a
contract, protocol, lifecycle, security or trust boundary keeps the full loop.

## Evidence
`eon-readme-agent-workspace-06m3` slice 1 (a 100-line README) took four fresh review passes, about
270k subagent tokens; each new reviewer surfaced different wording nits, and only the fourth found
nothing actionable. The current rule is in `AGENTS.md` "Proof and Review" (rendered from
`.agent-protocols.local.md`).

## Prerequisites
Agent policy is Lucca's: get approval for the exact wording. Coordinate with
`eon-slim-agent-instructions-jr9k`, which edits the same file. Validate directly with structural
checks (recorded AP-TEST-001 exception).

## Acceptance
`.agent-protocols.local.md` states the tiers and the convergence rule; render and check pass; the
rendered `AGENTS.md` diff is recorded. Policy proof only.

## Stop boundary
No change to proof requirements, contract rules or the Verification table's routes.
