title: Show the cursor color and its name in the Eon Bar
description:
## Why

Lucca, 2026-10-21: show the cursor color's name in the Eon Bar, with the color
itself as a filled circle next to the name (for example `● ice`). When
`cursor_trail_color` is omitted, the random preset is otherwise hard to identify
and retain in configuration.

## Evidence (dcaef1c, 2026-11-12)

- `venus/src/launch.rs:16` owns `CURSOR_COLOR_PRESETS`; `:608` parses choices;
  `:627` resolves random choices from the live endpoint. `LaunchArguments.cursor_tail`
  at `:58` retains color/duration, not the preset name/random provenance.
- `runtime/crates/eon-runtime/src/supervisor.rs:480` passes the configured color
  to Venus; Runtime does not presently own that random resolution.
- `docs/CONFIGURATION.md` documents cursor trail choices and `[bar] widgets`.
- `docs/CONTRACTS.md:4562` EON-C32 owns the widget names, omission and order.
  VEN-C27/28/29 and EON-C29/30 are retired presentation contracts. The label is
  a feature under Contract-Driven Method; create no new mirrored VEN/EON ID.
- Scene/chrome/accessibility project existing bar labels; reuse those owners
  and a rounded square at half-side radius for the circle.

## Scope and boundary

Show a read-only trail-color circle followed by its preset name or custom hex;
hover/AccessKit state whether it was random or configured. No label when the tail
is disabled. Preserve the choice across attach. The label neither handles input
nor resizes terminals. It describes the trail setting, not a program's OSC 12
cursor color. No cycling action or new preset.

Affected surfaces after the choices below: launch choice representation, Scene
layout/yield/hover, chrome drawing, accessibility; EON-C32's widget clause,
`docs/CONFIGURATION.md`, `docs/USAGE.md`, `venus/docs/PRESENTATION.md` and product
changelog. If approved random ownership/CLI work needs Runtime/EONW, scope that
prerequisite separately before expanding this Venus slice. Related themes work
`eon-eon-themes-or3q` does not change which trail setting this label describes.

## Pending choices for Lucca (recommendations, not decisions)

1. Add `cursor_color` to EON-C32's widget names and default list, yielding first
   under width pressure. Recommend this: the existing widgets list then supplies
   the hide option; the obsolete no-hide proposal needs no separate setting.
2. Make the resolved random choice readable to agents. Recommend Runtime-owned
   resolution plus `eon session --json`, with its exact scope/contract draft first.
   Today only Venus knows the result; do not silently promise CLI parity, move
   ownership or introduce EONW work in this bead without that choice.
3. Keep the label tied to the configured trail color even when a program changes
   its terminal cursor via OSC 12. Recommend this because it names the setting
   the person can retain.

## Acceptance and verification

- Record those choices and Lucca's exact EON-C32/any CLI contract approval before
  changing contract text or implementing dependent behavior.
- Preset, random and custom choices have correct text/color/provenance; disabled
  tail has no label; attach preserves identity and approved yield order holds.
- Focused deterministic checks cover choice projection and width yielding; one
  isolated installed observation covers random/configured labels, hover and
  accessible text on the accepted artifact. Follow the current Verification
  route and required whole-workspace author check/review; no runtime proof is
  claimed by this planning pass.
- Defaults/order and visibility are documented through the same widget list.

Portability: neutral. Stop if the approved slice cannot preserve one preset-table
owner or requires an unapproved protocol, Runtime ownership or contract change.

title: Roll refreshed Eon runtime into Eonova
description:
## Contract Routing

This is the explicitly chosen Eon planning owner for the trackerless Eonova repository. It changes no EON, ORB, VEN, or Nova product contract. It consumes the exact published Eon proof produced by the prerequisite refresh and preserves Eonova's current one-surface x86_64 Linux composition.

Consumer: a local user launching Eonova from its named Nix profile.

Trigger: Eonova evaluates, builds, installs, or launches its exact Eon input.

Result: Eonova pins and packages the refreshed accepted Eon artifact, while retaining the exact current Nova source, Mars-free boundary, one private runtime namespace, wrapper, desktop entry, and existing live generations.

Important failures: an unpublished or unproved Eon source, changed Nova identity, Mars/Rio closure entry, failed package/profile verification, or interrupted live process leaves the rollout incomplete.

## Why

Eonova has no tracker and currently pins Eon `a390fc5c007900c3fc8c9c49df85f9b8acc06d4a`. After Eon accepts the child-source refresh, new Eonova launches must consume that exact immutable Eon proof through the repository's existing pin-only update path. Keeping this as a dependent Bead prevents the Eon implementation run from editing two code-owning repositories.

## Evidence

- Eonova `AGENTS.md`: the repository owns only exact Eon/Nova pins, package, namespace, wrapper, desktop entry, and current-state docs; later work requires an explicitly chosen planning owner.
- Eonova `flake.nix:6-29`: the Eon input and assertion both pin `a390fc5...`.
- Eonova `flake.nix:11-31`: Nova is independently pinned and must remain unchanged.
- Eonova `flake.nix:34-94`: the wrapper, Mars-free package, namespace check, desktop entry, license, and app are existing proof owners.
- Prior closed `eon-refresh-clipboard-runtimes-0pt` shows the accepted exact-pin, lock, build, profile, and live-process-preservation workflow.
- Prerequisite Eon refresh produces the only acceptable new Eon source identity for this rollout.

## Prerequisites and Reference Gate

Required before editing:

- Current Eonova `AGENTS.md`, this complete Bead, `flake.nix`, `flake.lock`, README, LICENSE, desktop/package checks, and current profile/process state.
- The exact published Eon proof from the prerequisite Bead, its graph report, package identity, and accepted child revisions.
- The exact current Nova pin and Mars-free package proof, only to establish preservation.
- The prior Eonova pin refresh mechanism, without copying superseded identities.

Rejected scope:

- Eon, Orbit, Venus, or Nova edits; a second runtime protocol; Eon workspace mode; an updater/channel; new package surfaces; macOS; restarting live supervisors; or changing Eonova identity.

No crate/tool decision is involved.

## Scope

In scope:

- Eonova `flake.nix` exact Eon input/assertion, affected `flake.lock` nodes, current-state README/LOC only if the accepted pin changes documented facts, and the named active `eonova` profile.
- Exact Nix evaluation/build, Mars/Rio closure exclusion, desktop/license/wrapper inspection, installed artifact comparison, and isolated native smoke where needed.
- Preserve the current exact Nova revision and every other package/runtime boundary.

Out of scope:

- Any child repository mutation, Eon implementation, Nova update, new wrapper behavior, workspace mode, runtime protocol, packaging channel, or contract change.

## Implementation Notes

1. Begin only after the Eon refresh publishes and records one immutable accepted proof.
2. Record baseline Eonova HEAD, instruction hash, current Eon/Nova pins, profile artifact, and all live Eonova process PID/start identities.
3. Verify the accepted Eon source and package report, then advance only the Eon input/assertion and affected lock nodes.
4. Run the exact package and boundary checks.
5. Refresh the named profile without stopping or restarting live supervisors, verify the installed artifact, and record that existing generations remain immutable.
6. Update only current-state documentation and LOC if required.

Portability disposition: isolated x86_64 Linux Nix composition; no macOS claim.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. Eonova's input, assertion, lockfile, build, and installed profile consume the exact published Eon proof from the prerequisite.
2. The Nova revision and Mars-free package identity are unchanged.
3. The default package/app, wrapper, namespace, desktop entry, icon, and license remain valid.
4. The built closure contains neither Mars nor Rio.
5. The active `eonova` profile resolves to the exact verified artifact.
6. Recorded live Eonova supervisors, Orbit Sessions, and Venus processes retain their PID/start identities through the profile refresh.
7. No child code, runtime semantics, contract, dependency, updater, or unrelated pin changes.
8. README LOC and `git diff --check` pass if documentation changes.

## Verification

- `nix flake check --no-update-lock-file` should exit 0.
- `nix build .#default --no-link --print-out-paths --no-update-lock-file` should produce the exact Eonova artifact.
- Inspect the realized closure for forbidden Mars/Rio paths.
- Validate the desktop entry when `desktop-file-validate` is available; inspect installed licenses and exact wrapper argv.
- Compare the installed profile artifact and embedded Eon identity with the prerequisite proof.
- Compare recorded live process PID/start identities before and after refresh.
- Verify README LOC if changed and run `git diff --check`.
- `br lint <this-id>` and `br sync --flush-only` should pass in the owning Eon tracker.

## Stop Conditions

- Stop if the prerequisite Eon proof is not published, accepted, or exact.
- Stop if the current Nova pin changed or the update would pull Mars/Rio into the closure.
- Stop if another active run owns Eonova's flake, lock, profile, or docs.
- Stop rather than interrupting a live supervisor or Session.
- Stop if the update needs behavior beyond an exact child pin and package refresh.

## Maintenance Notes

Eonova remains a thin trackerless composition. This Bead owns only this one rollout; future pin changes need a newly selected planning owner.

title: End the popup card on the sidebar's and columns' bottom edge
description:
Contract: VEN-C18 (a selected popup draws over the column area and preserves its outer side and bottom bounds). No contract text change in this bead.

Problem (Lucca, 2026-10-26, screenshot): with the Agent popup open, the popup card's bottom edge sits below the sidebar card's bottom edge. Column cards and the sidebar already share one painted bottom; only the popup differs.

Cause: column and sidebar paint use `WorkspaceScene::card_rect`, whose bottom is `painted_bottom(...)` (an inset from the allocated bottom, kept clear of the visible grid). The popup outline (render/chrome.rs) and its fill (`card_fill`, scene.rs) use `popup_card_rect`, which runs to the allocated bottom. `scene::tests::popup_outer_chrome_reuses_the_pane_stack_rectangle` even asserts that popup bottom equals `chrome.bottom()`.

Change: the popup card keeps `popup_card_rect`'s top (including its rise on short windows) and takes `card_rect`'s painted bottom, so its outline and fill end on the same edge as the column cards and the sidebar. Presentation-only: no wire, contract, dependency or configuration change. Portability: neutral.

Acceptance: at default and small geometries and scales, the popup card's bottom equals the painted bottom of the column card it replaces and of the sidebar card; the scene test asserts that equality in place of the old chrome-bottom one. Installed check: one isolated dogfood capture showing the popup and sidebar bottoms on one line.

Scope boundary: removing the `[popup]` margin settings is a separate bead (contract change, needs Lucca's approval).

title: Define Eon's concrete runtime library and assembly contract
description:
## Contract and prerequisite
Sequence step 1 for eon-runtime-extraction-l4wh. No open functional prerequisite. The fourth-repository/library direction is chosen; resolve only the minimum input and ownership details needed for extraction.

Consumer: Eon's actual executable and Nix packager. Trigger: assembling/invoking the selected runtime library. Result: explicit product inputs select existing Eon/EonTerm behavior while runtime has one owner for state and mechanisms. Preserve graph-validation timing, bounded startup errors, exact component compatibility and generation isolation.

## Evidence
Eon baseline cda9662c2cfac092d98a998b3a54c9b0fb4f2b7a, 2026-10-04.
- crates/eon/src/main.rs:1-25 already delegates to nine modules; it owns exit/error projection and directory-picker failure delay.
- supervisor.rs:37/:320/:647/:1423-1425 embeds/queries the graph and reports Eon product version.
- cli.rs:380 uses CARGO_PKG_VERSION; moving it unchanged would report the library version.
- generation.rs:24-53 hashes runtime/protocol/validator/Cargo/graph/Nix bytes; eon-generated-runtime-identity-h4g protects generated managed behavior.
- managed_environment.rs:29-160/:317-346 combines chosen defaults with strict parsing/popup validation.
- eon-manifest's parse_and_validate/version_report/component_revision stay Eon's sole graph authority.

## Scope and design
Document one concrete invocation boundary and necessary immutable inputs: Eon version, validated component report/exact Orbit revision, generation contributions, chosen defaults/popup/provider values, opaque launch inputs. Package version plus exact source pin selects the runtime API; promise no compatibility with arbitrary releases. EONW has its own exact package identity/proof within the same repository, independently selected from the runtime implementation.

Eon keeps canonical graph/validator/schema, chosen policy/default values, packaging and actual executable. title: Separate Eon runtime into a fourth repo and keep Eon assembly thin
description:
## Current disposition — 2026-10-06
Completed and accepted. All seven sequence children are closed. Eon retains product assembly, its canonical component graph and Nix distribution; the independent Eon Runtime repository owns runtime mechanisms and canonical EONW. The accepted cutover is Eon `51666e2fcb925a7d2abde204ac402ecf83d1769f`; later runtime evolution and child adoption remain separately owned.

The current working-tree graph selects Runtime `a57e105a5da87d9c65402c1c4c8ea8b5dc8adc45` independently of EONW `b8f18b4374ca0818a64d9cac6a3fcd02d9f2f2aa`, Orbit `6bc269c40b18f08b95778939518f77556ba91c67`, and Venus `c7a0d07612e710854275a31500aaec651cc50a6f`. The existing uncommitted Venus adoption is separate from this metadata-only closure. Native platform and distribution limits are unchanged.

## Chosen outcome
On 2026-10-04 the user chose a fourth repository after evaluating the thin-orchestrator direction and authorized this planning-only batch. The accepted fourth repository is Yazelix/eon-runtime, with separate eon-runtime and eon-workspace-protocol packages. This is an extraction program, not another decision about whether to split.

The installed Eon and EonTerm products keep their existing commands and behavior. Eon becomes product assembly: its small actual executable supplies product defaults/version, selects components, validates its sole canonical graph, and owns Nix distribution. eon-runtime supplies the cohesive Rust runtime library and EONW package. Orbit retains PTY/session/terminal authority; Venus retains native client authority. No additional daemon or process/wire boundary is introduced.

## Historical evidence and planning baseline
Inspected Eon edge cda9662c2cfac092d98a998b3a54c9b0fb4f2b7a, Venus edge 4b5cc0cf8e5c3567f83d94ac0862adbf0c0e23d1, and Orbit edge 68ad73ff2e466f8d028f664c1079468348eb9949 on 2026-10-04. Rebaseline before implementation; discovery is not runtime proof.
- crates/eon/src/main.rs:1-25 is already thin; closed eon-v28 and eon-5rp established internal modules. Repeating thin-main refactoring would not deliver a thin repository.
- Nine runtime modules still compile in Eon; supervisor.rs:37 embeds its graph and generation.rs:24-53 reaches across runtime, protocol, validator, Cargo, graph and Nix sources.
- Venus Cargo.toml:10 pins EONW from Eon f41a41c9aecc4c436edfa2f394b832aa6d8711ad. Its protocol tree equals current Eon's: 8409c419a3496d6f01eeef65295f5d95b943313e.

## Ownership and fixed constraints
Eon keeps components/eon-alpha-v3.json, eon-manifest implementation/schema/validation, product version and chosen defaults, actual executable/error exit handling, assets, Nix graph translation and distribution. Runtime receives explicit validated facts and immutable product inputs, with no dependency back on Eon.

Move cli, codex_quota, control, generation, managed_environment, sessions, supervisor, windows and workspace together; retain internal invariant owners. Runtime owns their mechanisms and strict user-config parsing, not a second product graph or defaults owner. EONW moves with runtime, retaining package identity and v2-v7 exports/bytes. Product diagnostics report Eon's supplied version separately from the runtime component version.

One generation owner covers immutable runtime/EONW inputs plus Eon assembly/defaults/graph/validator/Cargo/Nix projection inputs. Store paths, mutable user config and live state are not identity. Moving source intentionally changes generation. Exact graph comparison can refuse new-client presentation of old generations; keep historical discovery and owner-routed Stop, and preserve old work with its exact prior executable.

## Independent package acceptance
On 2026-10-04 the user approved this refinement: runtime implementation changes that leave EONW unchanged do not require a new Venus source revision or EONW pin. The initial provider move still requires the one-time Venus rebind in this sequence.

Treat eon-runtime and eon-workspace-protocol as separate logical package identities in the existing canonical graph, with one fourth-repository owner. Exact source pins/proofs remain mandatory; runtime source R1 and Venus's codec source P0 may be different commits of that repository. Record package name/version, exact provenance, EONW wire/API proof and unchanged package content including manifest and relevant dependency/build inputs. Matching version labels alone is insufficient.

Prefer existing schema-3 library component records for these package identities; keep exact requirement checks scoped to the named package. Do not weaken revision equality globally, duplicate the graph, create a fifth repo, invent a compatibility resolver or force coupled version bumps. Nix supplies the graph-selected exact codec artifact; any source substitution must prove package equivalence before compiling it.

Acceptance includes an A/B composition: advance only the accepted runtime implementation revision while retaining Venus source and its exact EONW pin/proof; unchanged codec identity permits the build and runtime generation changes. Package drift under unchanged version labels fails closed. This does not relax exact old-generation Present, add protocol negotiation, promise mixed-version compatibility or eliminate composed runtime/package proof.

## Completed sequence
1. eon-runtime-contract-26eu — Define Eon's concrete runtime library and assembly contract.
2. eon-runtime-product-inputs-1dbd — Make the current runtime consume Eon-owned product inputs.
3. eon-runtime-seam-2tes — Move the proved runtime behind a local library.
4. eon-runtime-producer-68hq — Extract and accept the independent runtime and EONW producer.
5. eon-runtime-venus-rebind-tbmn — Rebind Venus to accepted runtime-owned EONW without changing the wire.
6. eon-runtime-package-identity-dmbj — Prove exact runtime/EONW package selection before cutover.
7. eon-runtime-cutover-y1wy — Activate pinned composition and remove Eon's duplicate implementation.

Size review, 2026-10-05: the former eight-hour local-seam task bundled semantic product-input changes with crate relocation; they are now two independently accepted outcomes. The former cutover bundled deterministic package identity with source binding/installed migration; selection is now a prerequisite. Rough effort estimates are 2h contract, 4h inputs, 4h library move, 6h producer, 2.5h rebind, 3h selection, 5h cutover; these are estimates, not guarantees or arbitrary task-size limits.

Keep producer transfer/independent acceptance together: one source-identical independently consumable artifact, not empty scaffolding or per-module tasks. Keep source removal, profile refresh and installed migration proof together: cutover is incomplete until its required installed check passes. Do not create separate implementation and later mandatory-verification tasks.

The local seam is a migration step, not prolonged incubation or a requirement for a second consumer. Freeze its source after transfer; only the independent producer may evolve. Complete bounded cutover before unrelated runtime feature work. This epic is a completion container: do not claim it. Organizational links are non-blocking; actual sequence prerequisites use blocks.

## Scope and reference gate
Follow EON-C1-C23 at their current proof phases, especially C1-C4, C8-C12, C15-C19, C22-C23; preserve planned distribution and unproved-platform limits. Read docs/REFERENCES.md routes for composition, generation and managed environment; use exact current owner code/tests and accepted Orbit/Venus contracts. Reuse Rust/Cargo/Nix, existing dependencies and checks. No plugin system, generic host interface, framework, runtime graph parser, compatibility adapter, code rewrite, or new feature.

The original planning baseline selected Orbit b6cecf8f2ee35570b41cfdc578b095889d917fe2 and Venus a23f9eed95120ca4acea8789bf7d32d2472d84ce, ORBF v2/ORBS v13/EONW v7; it does not select the current composition. Verify accepted freshness at execution; any refresh remains an exact separately evidenced change. Mac proof, Nova/Eonova cutover, direct distribution and eon-canonical-contract-index-6lck are not extraction prerequisites. Existing unrelated work remains unchanged. Deferred eon-4is is the broader product/consumer horizon, not this executable extraction program; keep its Nova transition unactivated.

## Completion
Each sequence task closes with its own exact proof and owner references; the runtime-only A/B check confirms that an unchanged EONW package does not force a Venus repin. Final installed Eon/EonTerm consumes one accepted runtime source and one graph; runtime builds independently without Eon; Venus consumes the exact selected EONW package identity, independently of the runtime implementation revision; Eon retains only assembly responsibilities and its actual process integration checks. Existing live supervisors/Sessions survive profile refresh. README LOC and affected current-state contracts/docs agree with final ownership.

Planning validation: br dep cycles; br ready --limit 50 --json; reread the sequence with br show; br sync --flush-only; git diff --check. No runtime proof is claimed by creating this batch.

Effort L overall; implementation risk MED-HIGH (identity and packaging boundaries); confidence HIGH in ownership split, MED in final code reduction. No arbitrary LOC target: assembly-owned Nix/policy remains legitimate code.

Publish only under normal repository/user authorization and linear history; no new release channel.

No profile activation/live interruption. Prior Eon composition stays selected until final activation. Remove frozen local copy at cutover rather than retaining a maintained fork.

title: Remove separate-repository residue from Eon Runtime
description:
## Decision
Lucca, 2026-10-15: keep the `eon`/`eon-runtime` crate split (chosen in `eon-monorepo-2oko` for agent
legibility) and remove what is left over from Runtime being a separate repository.

## Contract
Generation identity has one owner for its source inputs, and the architecture doc describes the
current runtime boundary rather than its extraction history. Users see no change except that the
next build selects a new generation, as any build change does.

## Evidence (edge 068efcb)
- `runtime/crates/eon-runtime/src/generation.rs:28-47` hand-lists Runtime and EONW source files with
`include_bytes!`, while `eon/crates/eon/build.rs` already digests every in-tree source file into the
assembly contribution. In the monorepo the hand list is a duplicate that can silently go stale when
a module is added.
- `docs/ARCHITECTURE.md:262-375` ("Runtime library boundary") is largely extraction and cutover
history; its acceptance table cites closed extraction beads. `docs/CONTRACTS.md` says history
belongs in Beads and Git.
- `runtime/README.md` describes the self-hash and transfer provenance.

## Slices
1. Make the assembly digest the only source-input hash; keep Runtime as owner of the generation
algorithm and `g1-` format. Update `runtime/README.md`, the architecture text and any contract text
naming the self-hash (check EON-C3 and EON-C11; a contract edit needs Lucca's approval).
2. Reduce `docs/ARCHITECTURE.md` "Runtime library boundary" to current-state facts.

Not included unless Lucca chooses: removing `eon-runtime` from `components/eon-alpha-v3.json`
(component graph, EON-C2), and moving `json_escape` out of `workspace.rs`.

## Acceptance
Slice 1 touches the generation and lifecycle boundary: full affected Rust and Nix surfaces in the
isolated sandbox; prove stable identity for identical inputs, a new identity after a Runtime-only
change, and that an older generation stays discoverable and stoppable; refresh the active Nix
profile without restarting live work. Slice 2 is docs-only proof.

## Stop boundary
No change to the crate split, EONW, Orbit or Venus.

title: Move the proved runtime behind Eon's local Rust library
description:
## Outcome and prerequisite
Sequence step 3 for eon-runtime-extraction-l4wh, blocked by eon-runtime-product-inputs-1dbd.
Consumer: Eon's actual executable. Trigger: invoking the same accepted runtime through a local Rust library. Result: all existing runtime mechanisms move together behind the already proved concrete product inputs, preserving commands, config behavior, lifecycle and wire bytes. Product-input semantics are owned by the prerequisite, not redesigned during this move.

## Evidence and scope
Eon discovery cda9662c2cfac092d98a998b3a54c9b0fb4f2b7a has a 25-line main.rs and nine internally coupled runtime modules. Rebaseline against the exact accepted product-input candidate before moving source.

Move cli, codex_quota, control, generation, managed_environment, sessions, supervisor, windows and workspace together into crates/eon-runtime. Retain their internal invariant owners/visibility. Expose only the accepted concrete invocation/input boundary; do not turn each file into a public service or separate crate.

Eon keeps its assembly/default values, eon-manifest/graph authority, product version, actual main/exit/error projection, assets and Nix. The library receives the existing product inputs, has no reverse Eon dependency/include and owns no graph parser/schema/copy or chosen defaults. Parser/state/limits remain runtime-owned. EONW stays the unchanged local package with separate manifest/version and v2-v7 exports/bytes.

Update source-generation contribution paths to the new owners, including runtime/codec manifests and relevant build inputs. The one runtime generation owner combines them with Eon's supplied immutable assembly/default/validator/graph/Cargo/Nix/generated-command contribution. No store/path identity, live state, mutable config, Nix evaluator or fingerprint framework. Source relocation may change generation; preserve g1 grammar and historical lifecycle behavior.

Move unit tests with runtime. Keep crates/eon/tests/workspace_control.rs on CARGO_BIN_EXE_eon, the real aliases/self-launch and its self-launched Orbit substitute. Relocate existing dependencies correctly; retain actual assembly/integration-test dependencies, not a shipped harness. Scope includes Cargo/locks, necessary existing Nix packaging, narrow current owner/proof docs and README LOC. Changelog only for accepted relevant behavior/packaging.

## Reference and dependency gate
Read eon-runtime-contract-26eu and eon-runtime-product-inputs-1dbd with their exact accepted source/artifact proofs; complete moved paths/callers/tests; current affected EON-C1-C4/C8-C23 phases and matching reference routes; closed eon-v28/eon-5rp/eon-validate-component-graph-before-launch-1jd/eon-generated-runtime-identity-h4g/eon-6ux. Compare existing direct protocol/manifest crate consumers and official Cargo workspace/dependency documentation. Record owned-library responsibility, relocated dependencies and removal cost; reuse existing Rust/serde/Cargo/Nix.

Check accepted child freshness before implementation under normal gates. Discovery pins: Orbit b6cecf8f2ee35570b41cfdc578b095889d917fe2, Venus a23f9eed95120ca4acea8789bf7d32d2472d84ce; ORBF v2/ORBS v13/EONW v7. No child implementation or speculative API.

## Acceptance and falsifiers
1. The real executable invokes the library; Eon contains assembly/defaults/exit handling and runtime contains the nine cohesive mechanisms. No duplicate state, defaults, graph or private-operation API.
2. The unchanged actual-binary suite preserves graph failure before owner/socket/child effects, native/terminal admission failure before Session creation, help/tool/picker ordering, aliases, window routing, config/default/reread semantics and historical lifecycle checks.
3. Deliberately unequal library/product versions still report Eon's supplied version in CLI and EONW snapshots; Nix metadata follows Eon Cargo.
4. Identical immutable inputs yield stable g1 generation. A disposable runtime-only source A/B changes generation while complete EONW content/build inputs/version and accepted Venus source/pin stay unchanged. No protocol bump or consumer source edit is required. Confirm the prerequisite's product/default/generated-projection contribution is still consumed after source relocation; add no duplicate A/B matrix solely for unchanged semantics.
5. Existing managed-command-path/shell-environment/eonterm-closure checks preserve actual executable projection and EonTerm's separate slim package.

For one unchanged candidate use the full affected Rust/Nix route: cargo fmt --all --check; cargo check --locked --workspace; cargo test --locked --workspace; cargo clippy --locked --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings; existing graph validator; both default/eonterm Nix builds and flake check; git diff --check. Add only missing library-boundary falsifiers, not a parallel suite.

Refresh active eon profile from accepted current-tree artifact, verify store equality and one isolated installed Linux native Wayland lifecycle observation covering both products. Preserve live supervisors/Sessions without automatic restart. Record exact sources/components/artifact/environment/result/phase; metadata follow-ups reuse proof. Profile failure is incomplete.

No fourth-repo creation, external selection or independent package-identity machinery yet; those belong to producer/selection/cutover tasks. No new feature/wire/process/platform/channel/framework. This is a short migration checkpoint; transfer promptly after acceptance. Effort M; risk MED; confidence HIGH.

title: Publish an Eon config schema and edit configuration with Ratconfig
description:
## Why

Approved as "configurable later" (`eon-configurability-audit-twdr`, Lucca, 2026-10-23). Ratconfig
is pinned (`eon-v4.json:332-347`, `flake.nix:26`, `:650`), but no crate uses it, and there is no
config schema. A hand-written Ratconfig field list would be a second owner of the serde structs
and defaults (`runtime/crates/eon-runtime/src/managed_environment.rs:23-135`,
`eon/crates/eon/src/product.rs`).

## Shape

Runtime generates one schema from its own config table, for example `eon config schema --json`
with key, type, default, bounds and doc. Ratconfig reads it, and validation stays in Runtime. The
same schema serves agents under the Humans and Agents rule. Contract owners: EON-C4 (Thin orchestrator ownership, which lists Ratconfig as a consumer)
and a new configuration-editing contract.

## Historical scheduling rationale (superseded below)

It is a consequential shape (dependency and integration). It follows the docs coverage test
child, which first proves the key enumeration.


## Current approved plan and acceptance
Lucca 2026-11-11: "they have to come before 0.2." This supersedes the post-beta recommendation.
Children in order: .1 key table/schema, .2 get/set/unset and one safe writer, .3 Eon-owned

title: Describe every configuration key in one Runtime table and print it with eon config schema --json
description:
## Why

Lucca chose a Ratconfig Configuration popup built CLI-first (decisions on the parent eon-s0oj,
2026-11-10; research in `~/.cache/eon-agents/eon-config-popup-research-work/bead/report.md`).
Everything after this bead (`eon config get/set/unset`, the `eon-config` Ratconfig host, the popup)
needs one machine-readable description of every configuration key. Today the only description is
the serde structs plus hand-written text, so agents cannot list keys, types or bounds, and a
hand-written Ratconfig field list would be a second owner of Eon's defaults.

## Historical evidence (edge 1d9350d; current corrections below)

- `runtime/crates/eon-runtime/src/managed_environment.rs:33` `EonConfig` and the per-table settings
  structs (`:230` bar, `:461` anima, `:471` session, `:481` sidebar, `:503` agents, `:521` editor,
  `:529` popup entry, `:584` shell, `:635` terminal): the only schema.
- `managed_environment.rs:656` `print_defaults`: `[terminal]`, `[shell]`, `[anima]` serialize from
  the resolver structs; `[bar]`, `[session]`, `[sidebar]` and the popups are hand-listed.
- `runtime/crates/eon-runtime/src/cli.rs:837-843`: `eon config path`, `dir`, `defaults [--json]`.
- `docs/CONFIGURATION.md:65-188`: the defaults block a test compares with `eon config defaults`
  (`eon/crates/eon/tests/workspace_control.rs`, `config_defaults_ignore_user_configuration_and_have_documented_values`).
- When a key takes effect is prose only (`docs/CONFIGURATION.md:217`, `:477-519`, `:684`).

## Contract

A new configuration-editing contract: take the next unused `EON-C` ID after EON-C42 (EON-C34 and
EON-C40 do not appear in `docs/CONTRACTS.md`; confirm they are not reserved, never reuse). This bead
drafts the editing contract (schema JSON here; get, set, unset and the write rule for the later beads, citing EON-C9 for check) and indexes only the schema clause as implemented. Write rule Lucca approved
(decision 5 on eon-s0oj): Eon changes `config.toml` only when a person or agent sets or unsets a
named key; it changes only that key, keeps the rest of the text, validates before writing and
writes atomically. EON-C28/EON-C37's "never rewrites `config.toml` on its own" stays as written.
Contract text goes to the overseer for approval before code (AGENTS.md rule 1).

## Prerequisites

- eon-configurability-qkq8.10 is closed; keep its derived-default coverage as the schema-table foundation. The existing closed prerequisite needs no change.

## Scope

In scope:
- One table in Eon Runtime with a row per configuration key: dotted path (with `popups.<id>.<field>`
  as the one dynamic family), value type, default (or unset), bounds or allowed values, the one-line
  description `eon config defaults` already prints, when it takes effect (for example next file,
  next terminal, next window presentation, next supervisor start), and whether it is Eon-owned or
  required for a given built-in popup.
- `eon config schema --json` printing that table; like `defaults`, it reads no user configuration
  and works with a broken `config.toml`.
- Tests: a document that sets every table key parses with no unknown-key warning; the table's keys
  and defaults equal `eon config defaults --json` plus its documented unset keys.
- `docs/USAGE.md` command row, a `docs/CONFIGURATION.md` sentence, the shipped Eon skill
  (`eon/skills/eon/SKILL.md`) if it lists config commands, `CHANGELOG.md`.

Out of scope:
- `eon config check`, `get`, `set`, `unset` (eon-configurability-qkq8.13 and the next child).
- Any Ratconfig or other new dependency.
- Changing a key, default or validation rule.
- Deriving `print_defaults`' hand-listed sections (`[bar]`, `[session]`, `[sidebar]`, popups) from
  the structs: that is the rest of eon-configurability-qkq8.10, which blocks the parent eon-s0oj
  and so lands before this bead. This bead's equality test then ties the table to those derived
  defaults, so a key added to a struct without a table row fails.

## Acceptance

- `eon config schema --json` lists every key `eon config defaults` shows or names as unset, each
  with type, default, bounds or choices, description and when it takes effect.
- Each "takes effect" value was read from the code path that consumes the key, and the bead records
  where (the a9g0.7 bead says `[terminal]`, `[bar]` and `warning_close_last_tab` are re-read when
  the window is presented again, and popups, `[sidebar]` and `[anima]` need a supervisor restart;
  re-check, do not copy).
- Adding a table row for a key the parser does not accept, or changing a default in only one place,
  fails a test.

## Implementation Notes

1. Plan first (PLAN READY), including the JSON shape and the contract draft.
2. Keep the table next to the structs in `managed_environment.rs` or a sibling module; descriptions
   move into it so `print_defaults` and the schema share one string.
3. JSON: additive-friendly objects (consumers ignore unknown fields, as EON-C28 says for other
   JSON).

## Verification

- `nix develop -c eon-test -p eon-runtime -p eon` passes, including the two new tests; red/green by
  adding a scratch key to the table only.
- Whole-workspace `nix develop -c eon-test`, fmt and clippy for changed crates before review.

## Stop Conditions

- Stop if a key's "takes effect" cannot be determined from the code; report the key.
- Stop if the table forces restructuring the serde structs beyond adding metadata.
- Stop if the cited code has drifted materially.

## Maintenance Notes

- Rejected: a JSON Schema document as the format (Ratconfig's helper reads only path, kind and enum
  from one, and the host links Runtime directly); a hand-written field list in the Ratconfig host
  (second owner, as Nova's `crates/yzx-config/src/catalog.rs` is).
- Portability: neutral.


## Current evidence and prerequisite correction (2e93c69)
qkq8.10 and qkq8.13 are closed. managed_environment.rs:706 defaults_config derives the
configuration object; :886 print_defaults consumes it; :2444 parse_config uses the shared parser,
and :2459 validate_configuration_text already validates text without a supervisor.
cli.rs:862-876 includes config check and defaults; schema/get/set/unset are still absent.
Do not repeat the completed derivation work or weaken coverage by dropping it. Tie the metadata
table to the current derived defaults and documented unset/dynamic fields; preserve the existing
unknown-key and resolver checks.
EON-C9 alone owns config check (overseer 2026-11-11): exit 0/1, JSON path/valid/error and
invalid-configuration/unreadable-configuration codes. The editing contract references that clause,
not a second definition. Allocate a genuinely unused ID; EON-C34 is reserved, not available.

comments.author: lucca
comments.text: 2026-11-11 eon-overseer: eon config check is owned by EON-C9 (amended in eon-configurability-qkq8.13: exit 0/1, --json {path, valid, error: null or {code, detail}}, codes invalid-configuration and unreadable-configuration). The configuration-editing contract this bead drafts cites EON-C9 for check and does not redefine it.

comments.author: prime-beads-chunk03-2026-11-12
comments.text: prime-beads 2026-11-12: Refreshed derived-defaults evidence and made EON-C9 the sole owner of config check. Review: 1 fresh read-only pass; material finding corrected, no remaining blocker.

title: Read and change one configuration key with eon config get, set and unset, keeping comments
description:
## Why

Configuration is on the Humans and Agents list (AGENTS.md rule 5): what a person will do in the
Config popup needs a CLI path. Today an agent edits `config.toml` as text and cannot change one key
safely. Lucca approved `eon config set` and the popup writing `config.toml` under one write rule
(decision 5 on the parent eon-s0oj, 2026-11-10). The popup host (next child) saves through this
bead's code, so there is one write path.

## Historical evidence (edge 1d9350d; current corrections below)

- `runtime/crates/eon-runtime/src/cli.rs:837-843`: the `eon config` family (`path`, `dir`,
  `defaults`); `schema` arrives with the first child of eon-s0oj and `check` with
  eon-configurability-qkq8.13.
- `runtime/crates/eon-runtime/src/managed_environment.rs:2140` `parse_config`: the one parser.
- `runtime/crates/eon-runtime/Cargo.toml`: `toml` with `parse`, `serde`, `display`; nothing that
  preserves comments.
- Ratconfig `src/toml_adapter.rs:34` `set_toml_value_text`, `:60` `unset_toml_value_text`
  (comment-preserving, on `toml_edit`); they build with `default-features = false`, without
  `ratatui`.
- Pin: `components/eon-v5.json` names `https://github.com/luccahuguet/ratconfig.git` at `e6ec2eb`
  (6.0.0); `flake.nix:31-34` and `:909` hold the input and the assert. The repository moved to
  `Yazelix/ratconfig`; Nova pins `675a21f17900df47585b2a8290c5436204d120e4` there, one commit later
  (the move). No crate depends on it yet.
- Nova's write path, the comparable implementation: `~/pjs/nova/nova/crates/yzx-config/src/root_config.rs:169-213`.

## Contract

The configuration-editing contract drafted by the first child of eon-s0oj: this bead implements
and indexes its `get`, `set`, `unset` and write-rule clauses. EON-C10 if it indexes commands. This
is a consequential shape (first use of a dependency): record the reference gate (Nova's
`root_config.rs`, Ratconfig's patcher at the pinned revision, version policy: exact revision pin,
upgrades chosen) in this bead before code.

## Prerequisites

- First child of eon-s0oj (key table and `eon config schema --json`): types and Eon-owned keys.
- eon-configurability-qkq8.13 (`eon config check`), including an internal "validate this text"
  entry point; add it there or here, whichever lands first, but keep one validator.

## Scope

In scope:
- `eon config get KEY [--json]`: the effective value, whether it comes from the file or the
  default, and the default.
- `eon config set KEY VALUE` and `eon config unset KEY`: re-read the file, patch only the named
  key, validate the whole resulting text with Runtime's validator, write atomically (temporary file
  and rename in the same directory); create the file only when the first key is set; refuse
  unknown keys, Eon-owned keys and invalid values with a documented exit status and no write.
- The Ratconfig crate as a dependency with `default-features = false`, repinned to
  `Yazelix/ratconfig` (manifest, flake input, lockfile, Nix cargo hashes).
- One function the popup host can call for set and unset.
- `docs/USAGE.md` rows, `docs/CONFIGURATION.md`, the shipped Eon skill, `CHANGELOG.md`.

Out of scope:
- The Ratconfig UI, `ratatui`, `crossterm`, the popup.
- Applying a change to a running window (eon-agent-parity-a9g0.7); `set` reports when the key
  takes effect, from the table.
- Adding or removing whole `[popups.<id>]` tables beyond setting their documented fields.
- Fixing Ratconfig: report gaps to the overseer (a Ratconfig agent files them in Ratconfig's
  repository).

## Acceptance

- `eon config set terminal.font_size 16` on a commented file changes that one value and keeps every
  other byte; `eon config unset terminal.font_size` returns it to the default; `get` shows both
  states, as text and as JSON.
- An invalid value, an unknown key and a value that makes the whole file invalid each exit non-zero
  with the reason and leave the file byte-identical.
- A test states what happens to a comment on the same line as the edited value
  (`key = 1 # note`). If it is lost, report it to the overseer before review: Lucca's decision 6
  is to fix that in Ratconfig before the popup ships.

## Implementation Notes

1. Plan first (PLAN READY). Decide there: VALUE syntax (a TOML value, with a bare word accepted as
   a string where the key's type is a string), whether `unset` leaves an empty file in place
   (recommended: yes; Eon does not delete a person's file), and which crate holds `set`/`unset`.
   Product Boundary: Runtime keeps parsing and validation; the Ratconfig dependency may need to sit
   in `eon/crates/eon` (as `update` does, `eon/crates/eon/src/main.rs:17`).
2. `orbit/tools/governance/src/main.rs:894`
   `workspace_crates_keep_their_dependency_direction` may need the new edge.
3. Runtime's "validate this text" must run every resolver that can fail (bar levels, popup
   catalog, terminal presentation), not only the TOML parse.

## Verification

- Process tests on the real binary in an isolated `EON_CONFIG_HOME`
  (`nix develop -c eon-test -p eon`): the acceptance cases above.
- Whole-workspace `nix develop -c eon-test`, fmt and clippy for changed crates before review; the
  overseer's landing builds the package (the dependency changes the Nix cargo hashes).

## Stop Conditions

- Stop if Ratconfig's patcher cannot express a needed edit (for example a key inside
  `[popups.<id>]`); report rather than hand-rolling a second patcher.
- Stop if validation cannot run on text without supervisor state.
- Stop if the cited code has drifted materially.

## Maintenance Notes

- Rejected: `toml_edit` used directly in Runtime (a second comment-preserving writer beside
  Ratconfig's, which the popup uses anyway); rewriting the file from the parsed structs (loses
  comments and writes defaults into the file).
- Portability: neutral.


## Current dependencies and failure acceptance (2e93c69)
qkq8.13 is closed: managed_environment.rs:2459 validate_configuration_text is the existing
offline all-resolvers validator. Reuse/export that owner as needed; do not create a second one.
The first consumer must use Yazelix/ratconfig 09149da or later (parent refresh 2026-11-10),
which fixes same-line comment loss. Keep a regression check for that comment rather than treating
the known older bug as a reason to ship loss. Record the exact adopted pin and dependency gate.
Atomic rename must preserve unrelated text and the existing file on validation, permission or
write failure; prove a failure leaves it byte-identical, alongside the invalid/unknown-key cases.
Unsetting an absent key in a missing config must not create a defaults file. Document intentional
first-set creation and permissions; do not add background file watching or automatic live apply.

comments.author: prime-beads-chunk03-2026-11-12
comments.text: prime-beads 2026-11-12: Recorded the existing shared validator and the approved minimum Ratconfig revision; strengthened no-write-on-failure acceptance. Review: 1 fresh read-only pass; material finding corrected, no remaining blocker.

title: Build eon-config, the Ratconfig host that edits Eon configuration in a terminal
description:
## Why

Lucca chose Ratconfig in a popup with an Eon-owned host (decision 1 on the parent eon-s0oj,
2026-11-10). Ratconfig is a library: it owns the screen (tabs, rows, search, details, staged edits)
and the host owns loading, the field list, validation and writes. This bead builds that host,
`eon-config`, as a program that runs in any terminal; the next child makes it a built-in popup.

## Evidence

- Ratconfig 6.0.0 (`~/pjs/nova/ratconfig`, `README.md:11-36` ownership split, `:212-220` field
  capabilities, `:327-398` the optional crossterm runner and intents).
- Nova's host, the comparable implementation (`~/pjs/nova/nova/crates/yzx-config`): run loop
  `src/ui.rs:28-84`, model `src/model.rs:34`, write path `src/root_config.rs:169-213`. Its
  hand-written catalog (`src/catalog.rs`) is what Eon must not copy.
- Eon edge 1d9350d: Commands and Sessions are the `eon` binary under other names
  (`runtime/crates/eon-runtime/src/cli.rs:79-83`); the workspace has no terminal-UI crate.
- Fit and gaps: `~/.cache/eon-agents/eon-config-popup-research-work/bead/report.md` section 3.

## Contract

The configuration-editing contract (drafted by the first child of eon-s0oj): the host adds no
clause of its own; it must save only through the `set`/`unset` function. EON-C4 gets a proof note
(Ratconfig is already its named consumer). Consequential shape (new dependencies `ratatui` and
`crossterm` through Ratconfig's `ui` feature): record the reference gate, version policy and exit
condition before code.

## Prerequisites

- The `eon config get/set/unset` child of eon-s0oj (the write function and the Ratconfig pin).

## Scope

In scope:
- `eon-config`: builds a `ConfigUiModel` from Runtime's key table and the current `config.toml`
  (tabs per table; each field's intent from the file, baseline from the default, "takes effect"
  from the table; toggles, choices, ordered multi-choice for `bar.widgets`, text for the rest;
  Eon-owned keys read-only with the reason).
- Set and Unset intents call the `set`/`unset` function; a refused value shows as a notice and the
  staged edit stays. The file is re-read before every write.
- A broken `config.toml` opens as a source diagnostic, not a crash.
- An "Open config.toml" row and Ratconfig's external text edit run `[editor] command`; disabled
  with a reason when no editor resolves (the no-Helix variant, eon-igae.17).
- Existing `[popups.<id>]` tables show their documented fields; adding a popup goes to the
  "Open config.toml" row (decision 7).
- Measure and record cold and warm build time and the `eon` binary's size before and after.

Out of scope:
- The built-in popup entry, its key, packaging names and user docs (next child).
- Live apply, file watching, an Overview set of recommended keys, mouse.
- Changes to Ratconfig: report gaps to the overseer.

## Acceptance

- In an isolated `EON_CONFIG_HOME`, `eon-config` lists every key from `eon config schema --json`
  with its default; toggling a boolean and resetting it changes and restores exactly that key in
  the file; an out-of-range number is refused with Runtime's message and no write.
- Opening it on a syntactically broken file shows the error and the "Open config.toml" row.
- The bead records the build-time and size measurements and whether `eon-config` is a name of the
  `eon` binary or a separate binary.

## Implementation Notes

1. Plan first (PLAN READY). Decide there, from the measurements: one binary (another name for
   `eon`, like `eon-commands`) or a separate `eon-config` binary that keeps `eon` and `eonbase`
   free of `ratatui`. The host belongs with Eon's product crates, not in Runtime.
2. Own the event loop (as Nova does) rather than Ratconfig's runner if the editor hand-off needs
   terminal suspend and restore.
3. Keep model building a pure function of (table, file text) so tests need no terminal.

## Verification

- Unit tests for model building and intent handling; one real-PTY process test of open, edit, quit
  through `nix develop -c eon-test` (real-PTY notes:
  `~/.claude/projects/-home-lucca-pjs-eon-eon/memory/real-pty-sensitivity-runs.md`).
- Whole-workspace `nix develop -c eon-test`, fmt and clippy for changed crates before review.

## Stop Conditions

- Stop and report if the build-time or size cost is large enough that Lucca should choose (he
  cited build time when asking for the no-Helix variant).
- Stop if a needed control is missing in Ratconfig and text entry is not an acceptable fallback.
- Stop if the cited code has drifted materially.

## Maintenance Notes

- Rejected by Lucca's decisions: a custom fzf editor (a second config editor beside Ratconfig), a
  native Venus settings screen (no bead; revisit after 1.0), an editor-only first stage.
- Portability: neutral (`crossterm` supports Linux and macOS).

title: Add the built-in Config popup on Alt+Shift+K running eon-config
description:
## Why

Lucca, 2026-11-10: "we also need a config popup"; decision 3 on the parent eon-s0oj: a built-in
`[popups.config]`, label "Config", on Alt+Shift+K (Nova's key). This bead makes the `eon-config`
host from the previous child a built-in popup and documents it.

## Evidence (edge 1d9350d)

- `eon/crates/eon/src/product.rs:89-173`: the built-in popup catalog (ID, label, key, command,
  keep-alive); `commands` and `sessions` are the models.
- `flake.nix:1021-1023`: the popup PATH names `eon-files`, `eon-commands`, `eon-sessions`; the
  Nix-free archive is built from the same package (`nix/bundle-relink.nix`).
- `runtime/crates/eon-runtime/src/managed_environment.rs:656` `print_defaults` lists each built-in
  popup's settable fields; `docs/CONFIGURATION.md:138-186` is the checked block.
- Alt+Shift+K is free: absent from `docs/USAGE.md:328-359`, from the popup defaults and from the
  code. Alt+K and Ctrl+Alt+K are pane keys, as J and L already pair with Git and Agent.
- `docs/CONFIGURATION.md:586-661`: popup rules (a configured key wins over a built-in default).

## Contract

No new contract: built-in popups, their settable fields and key precedence are under EON-C28 and
the popup clauses of EON-C10/EON-C18; a built-in popup added later "never changes the meaning of a
configured `[popups.<id>]` with the same ID" (EON-C28). Check whether any contract enumerates the
built-in popups; if adding one amends contract text, send it to the overseer before code.

## Prerequisites

- The `eon-config` host child of eon-s0oj.

## Scope

In scope:
- The catalog entry: ID `config`, label "Config", Alt+Shift+K, command `eon-config`, not kept
  alive; settable `keybinding`, `label`, `enabled`, `command`, `keep_alive` like Commands.
- The `eon-config` name on the popup PATH in the Nix package and the Nix-free archive.
- `docs/USAGE.md` (shortcut table and popups text), `docs/CONFIGURATION.md` (defaults block and
  Popups section), `CHANGELOG.md`, including what happens to an existing custom `[popups.config]`.
- Tests that pin the built-in popup list or the defaults block.
- One isolated installed dogfood observation: the key opens the popup, an edit lands in the
  isolated root's `config.toml`, the key or `q` closes it.

Out of scope:
- A Commands entry that opens the popup: Commands runs `eon` CLI commands, and opening a popup
  from the CLI is eon-agent-parity-a9g0.1 ("Show, hide and focus popups from the CLI"); add the
  entry there or after it.
- Changes to the host's behaviour, Venus, or EONW (the catalog already travels over EONW).
- The website text: it follows the release this ships in (AGENT-RULES Website).

## Acceptance

- A fresh window shows Config under the Alt+Shift keycap and in Alt+/; Alt+Shift+K opens it on the
  active tab and again dismisses it.
- `eon config defaults` and the docs block list `[popups.config]`; `enabled = false` removes it and
  `keybinding = ""` leaves it without a key.
- A custom popup already on Alt+Shift+K keeps the key, and Alt+/ lists Config as overridden.
- Rule 5: the editing action's CLI path is `eon config get/set/unset`; the bead names
  eon-agent-parity-a9g0.1 for opening the popup from the CLI.

## Implementation Notes

title: Idea: make the Eon icon the session switcher, with a pink name pill
description:
## Idea (Lucca, 2026-11-04)

"record this idea bead: since the icon occupies the same place the 'session switcher' occupied before, we might as well make the icon the session switcher, and add a sort of pink-icon-color pill to it that shows the session name"

"later we analyze this idea and variations of it"

## The idea

The Eon icon in the Eon Bar now sits where the session or workspace switcher used to be. Make the icon itself the switcher:
- Clicking the icon, or its key, opens the session or workspace switcher.
- A pill in the icon's pink shows the current session or workspace name beside it.

## Status

An idea to analyze later. Nothing is decided and nothing is to be built yet.

## For the analysis (later)

- Which switcher: workspaces today (the Workspaces picker, Alt+Shift+S), or sessions under the sessions model (eon-hyil8, undecided).
- Where the current name shows today. The tab bar's "main 1/2" style label could move into the pill or stay.
- Variations to compare:
  - the icon only, opening the picker;
  - the icon plus a name pill;
  - a pill that also counts windows or workspaces;
  - a hover or keyboard hint.
- Room on narrow bars. eon-nfrbn reserves room for the icon by the chips shown, and the pill must fit that budget or shrink first.
- Accessibility name and keyboard path. Rule 5 needs a CLI path for any new window action, which `eon workspace` and `eon workspaces` already cover.
- Configurability (rule 6): the pill color, whether to show the pill, and its truncation.
- Contracts it would touch: the Eon Bar contract (VEN-C21) and EON-C33 for workspaces.

## Current analysis boundary (2026-11-12)

The request remains an idea, not permission to implement. `eon-30skm` has already
renamed the product/CLI concept to session; the ownership redesign in `eon-hyil8`
is still deferred. Analyze today's Sessions picker without assuming that redesign.
The Eon icon now opens the Window menu (EON-C32, `docs/CONTRACTS.md:4562`, and
VEN-C21); it is not an unused former switcher position. A proposal must preserve
access to that menu or explicitly present the replacement to Lucca.

Acceptance for this decision bead: compare the recorded variants and auto-naming
addition, retain the needs-input signal and narrow-width behavior, show keyboard,
pointer and accessible discovery, and present numbered choices/recommendations.
Coordinate the alternative label-placement investigation `eon-t2ez2`; neither
bead authorizes the other's layout. Any eventual configuration/CLI/lifecycle
contract wording comes to Lucca before implementation. No mock capture or
mechanical check is proof of runtime behavior.

title: Add one sandboxed test command for humans and agents
description:
## Decision
Lucca, 2026-10-15: give humans and agents one checked-in command that runs Eon's Rust test suites
in the isolated sandbox `AGENTS.md` requires.

## Contract
- Consumer: a maintainer or coding agent, including one working inside a live Eon terminal.
- Trigger: one documented command from the repository root, accepting extra cargo arguments.
- Result: the suites run with private PID, network, `/dev` and `/tmp` namespaces, an empty
`XDG_RUNTIME_DIR` with no Wayland or D-Bus, a cleared environment keeping only toolchain variables,
and `FONTCONFIG_FILE` set to the packaged Venus font configuration. Live Eon windows and terminals
are unaffected.
- Important failures: missing user-namespace support or toolchain reports a clear error and runs
nothing outside the sandbox.

## Evidence
- `AGENTS.md` (Testing Discipline) describes the sandbox only in prose; flake apps are `default`,
`eonterm` and `record-demo` (`flake.nix:615-627`).
- 2026-10-14 incident: running `cargo test --locked --workspace` from a live Eon terminal coincided
with the live Venus window and the agent dying. A working bubblewrap recipe passed all 339 tests:
`--die-with-parent --new-session --unshare-all --ro-bind / / --dev /dev --proc /proc --tmpfs /tmp
--tmpfs /run/user/<uid>`, read-write binds for only the repository and `~/.cargo`, `--clearenv`
with PATH, HOME=/tmp/home, CARGO_HOME, RUSTUP_HOME, USER, LANG and XDG_RUNTIME_DIR=/tmp/run.
- Nix package builds already run selected tests in the Nix build sandbox (`cargoTestFlags` at
`flake.nix:211,252,422`); that path is slower and is not the edit-test loop.

## Owner and shape
Nix owns the command (a flake app or dev-shell command); the bubblewrap call is irreducible process
glue, so a small shell wrapper is acceptable under the language rules. bubblewrap comes from the
pinned nixpkgs: record it under the dependency gate. x86_64 Linux only; name the platform limit.

## Acceptance
- From inside a live Eon terminal, the command runs the full workspace suite (and the installer
suite) green while the live window and its terminals stay up.
- `docs/DEVELOPMENT.md` and the Testing Discipline rule (via `.agent-protocols.local.md` and a
render) point to the command instead of describing the sandbox.

## Stop boundary
No hosted CI change and no test-harness framework.
close_reason: nix develop -c eon-test runs the workspace and installer suites in bubblewrap; 347/0/7 from inside a live Eon terminal with the session untouched; docs and AGENTS.md point to it.

comments.author: lucca
comments.text:
## Implementation record (2026-10-15)

Shape: `nix/test-sandbox.nix` owns `eon-test`, a writeShellApplication on the default dev shell, run as `nix develop -c eon-test [cargo test args]`. The dev shell now shares Orbit's and Venus's existing build environment through single bindings (`ghosttyBuildEnv`, `venusBuildInputs`, `venusFontsConf`) and adds Zig, ncurses and pkg-config, so builds use the pinned Ghostty source instead of cloning it. `cargo fetch --locked` (workspace and installer) runs first outside the sandbox; it builds nothing. The sandbox: `--unshare-all`, read-only `/`, private `/dev` and `/proc`, empty `/tmp` and `/run`, writable repository, CARGO_HOME and any target directory, HOME and a 0700 XDG_RUNTIME_DIR under the private /tmp, `--clearenv` plus a toolchain allowlist, and a PATH without Eon's managed `*/libexec/eon/bin` wrappers. Guards stop with a clear error outside the dev shell (no GHOSTTY_SOURCE_DIR/FONTCONFIG_FILE/cargo) or without user namespaces. `AGENTS.md` Testing Discipline (via `.agent-protocols.local.md`, rendered and checked with Starcompass at the pinned 4af5a32) and the development docs point to the command; `nix/test-sandbox.nix` owns the isolation.

Dependency gate: capability is unprivileged namespace isolation for one process tree. bubblewrap 0.11.2 from the pinned nixpkgs (567a49d1913ce81ac6e9582e3553dd90a955875f), no new flake input. Rejected: the Nix build sandbox (already runs selected package tests, but rebuilds from scratch and forbids set-ID chmod Orbit's suite needs), `unshare(1)` (needs hand-built mounts, more shell), systemd-run scopes (systemd dependency the platform rules forbid), containers/firejail (heavier, extra daemon or setuid). Replacement cost: one small file. Exit: drop it if a Rust-owned harness or upstream test isolation replaces it. Platform: x86_64 Linux; proved on a non-NixOS host (Pop!_OS kernel 7.1.5); on NixOS the hidden /run hides /run/current-system and /run/wrappers (documented). Portability disposition: isolated Linux dependency.

Refactor check: `nix derivation show` gives identical `yazelix-orbit` (qh46awyq…) and `yazelix-venus` (hmchvhcg…) derivations at HEAD f916b56/e11bbef and in the working tree; `eon`/`eonterm` change only because `flake.nix` is in their source set.

Proof (revision = this commit; x86_64 Linux, run from inside Lucca's live Eon terminal, Venus pid 4639 with six Orbit processes): final tree `nix develop -c eon-test` passed 347, failed 0, ignored 7 across 21 targets (workspace and installer) in 1m16s; `eon-test -p eon-manifest` and `eon-test --manifest-path installer/Cargo.toml` (7 passed) green; the live Venus process and all Orbit PIDs were unchanged after every run. A sandbox probe showed empty /run, no system D-Bus socket, private PID 1, no network, zero EON_/WAYLAND/DBUS variables and plain /usr/bin/bash. The guard outside the dev shell toolchain prints its error and exits 1.

Observed flake (not caused by this change): one intermediate full run failed `yazelix-orbit` `platform::tests::management_ready_claim_has_one_winner_and_survives_record_removal` with WouldBlock. 30/30 isolated runs and 5/5 Orbit binary suite runs then passed, and four later full runs passed. Likely cause: a parallel test forking while `RecordGuard::publish` holds its O_CLOEXEC flock claim, so the child briefly shares the lock. A separate Orbit bead is proposed to Lucca (pending decision), including whether the server path shares the race.

Review ledger: 7 passes; findings 7, 5, 5, 3, 4, 1, 0. Fixed: /run masking for the system D-Bus socket, guards before fetching, target-dir binds and relative paths, env values ending in `=`, Eon wrapper PATH, coreutils input, installer fetch, toolchain guard, TERM dropped, one sandbox owner in docs, display-test exception, stale doc pointers. Declined: filtering by EON_SESSION_BIN (only set in Eon terminals; the glob covers both), editing proof commands in contract indexes (historical evidence), Nix daemon socket reachability (outside the contract; no Eon socket lives there).

title: Send at most one outstanding scroll preview while output keeps arriving
description:
## Problem

During an active Venus terminal scroll (wheel, trackpad or momentum), every frame Venus drains rebases the scroll and clears its preview (venus/src/scroll.rs:216-224, 266; venus/src/model.rs:333). `drive_terminal_scroll` (venus/src/application.rs:3479) then sends a new `PreviewVertical` for that frame revision. `preview_pending` only suppresses a resend for the same revision, so while a program prints, Venus sends one preview request per frame and several can be outstanding. Orbit answers each with a `VerticalPreview` between its frames. Found while diagnosing eon-10qt. That bead made a full event queue apply backpressure, so this flood no longer drops the attachment, but it still wastes round trips and queue slots during output bursts.

## Expected

At most one outstanding preview per scroll gesture or batch. A newer frame supersedes a pending preview without sending a new request per revision, and scroll feel stays the same.

## Contract

VEN-C7 (authoritative history and selection interaction). Keep the existing scroll behavior; no contract text change is expected. If one turns out to be needed, stop for Lucca's approval.

## Prerequisites

eon-10qt landed.

## Scope

In scope: Venus scroll preview request pacing in venus/src/scroll.rs and application.rs, plus a focused regression. Out of scope: Orbit wire or Orbit queue changes, and the eon-10qt queue.

## Acceptance

- A Venus suite check: a scroll active across N frame revisions sends at most one outstanding PreviewVertical.
- Existing scroll tests stay green.
- One isolated installed observation: wheel scrolling while a program prints a burst feels unchanged.

## Portability disposition

neutral.
close_reason: Venus keeps one scroll preview outstanding across frames, with a 50 ms retry after a frame that may have replaced its answer; tests, review loop and installed A/B recorded

comments.author: lucca
comments.text:
Design (2026-10-27, implementing session in worktree /home/lucca/.cache/eon-agents/hhzy at base db378f4).

Cause: TerminalScroll::preview_pending named the frame revision the request was sent for, and every plain Frame called rebase(), which cleared it. While output kept arriving, drive_terminal_scroll sent one PreviewVertical per frame revision until an answer landed. ORB-C8 says a lagging preview resolves against current authority and its answer "names the current authoritative revision whose state it inspected", so answers rarely matched the per-revision marker either. Under DEC 2026 Orbit holds at most one unresolved vertical request and fails a second with InvalidInput ("vertical interaction is already deferred"), which Venus treats as a scroll failure and resets the gesture.

Fix (venus/src/application/scroll.rs, venus/src/application.rs):
- preview_pending becomes a bool: set when PreviewVertical is written, cleared only by its answer (any VerticalPreview; at most one is outstanding and Orbit answers in order) or by reset() (send failure, server Failure, reconnect, lost attachment).
- next_request sends nothing, preview or ScrollVertical, while a preview is outstanding, so a newer frame never adds a request. When the answer lands, a stale-revision answer that the model drops leaves exactly one fresh request for the current revision.
- cancel() keeps the outstanding flag, like the written batch it already preserves, so a new gesture after a cancel waits for the old answer.
- rebase() and its plain-frame call are removed; accept_batch no longer clears the flag (a batch and a preview are never outstanding together now).
- active() no longer counts the outstanding preview: pixels, velocity and a pending batch already cover a live gesture, and a cancelled gesture must stay inactive while its answer is in flight (link surface, redraw and model preview clearing keep their behaviour).

Reference gate: not consequential under AP-REFERENCE-001 as AGENTS.md defines it. No dependency, protocol or wire format, contract, lifecycle, security or trust boundary changes; it only paces Venus's requests within the existing ORBS v13 vertical exchange. VEN-C7 text unchanged. Portability: neutral.

Regression: venus unit test terminal_scroll_keeps_one_preview_outstanding_across_frames (10 frame revisions send one PreviewVertical; a stale answer leaves one fresh request; cancel keeps the hold; reset clears it). The existing coalescing test asserted one preview per revision (9, then 10 after rebase); it now asserts the second waits for the answer.

Known residual (unchanged): a server Failure that answers some other request resets the scroll and clears the flag while the preview answer is still in flight, so one extra request can overlap briefly.

comments.author: lucca
comments.text:
Review record (2026-10-27).

Converge after the plan change: round 1 (fresh Claude) deleted a duplicated segment of the old coalescing test, which the new regression already covers; checks green. Round 2 (fresh Claude) was clean on fixed tree 184ed264e6ea39af93f563666d105310e8933863: no edits, Venus suites 221 passed / 5 ignored, fmt and clippy -D warnings clean, tree unchanged.

Narrow Codex re-check (f0f91c02 -> 184ed264): it found the replaced-answer recovery sound (including output stopping right after), no busy loop at the deadline, and the opposite-direction late answer handled. One finding [P2], accepted as a residual and corrected here:

Correction to the plan-change comment. The 50 ms retry is not limited to output backpressure. A frame already in flight when Venus writes the preview can start the grace. If Orbit then holds the request under DEC 2026 synchronized output for more than 50 ms, the retry overlaps it. Orbit fails the retry with InvalidInput "vertical interaction is already deferred", and Venus shows the Orbit notice and resets the gesture, losing its distance and momentum. Base Venus had the same exposure on the very next frame, without the 50 ms wait, so this change narrows it and does not add it.

Why it stays here: Venus cannot tell a replaced answer from a held one, because Orbit's OutputQueue may drop an unsent preview answer for a newer frame. venus/AGENTS.md says to report an insufficient Orbit contract to Orbit instead of compensating in the client, and this bead excludes Orbit queue changes. Follow-up: eon-preview-answer-survives-frames-u979, which keeps unsent preview answers across frames so Venus can drop the timer.

Accepted residuals, complete list:
- A DEC 2026 hold of more than 50 ms after an in-flight frame can make the retry fail and reset the gesture. Base had this sooner. Follow-up 4ry3.
- A server Failure or a local InvalidInput for some other message, or a same-direction late answer from a retained column, can release the hold early. Each costs one extra request at most.
- If an answer really was replaced, a gesture's first preview can start up to about 50 ms later than in base.

comments.author: lucca
comments.text:
Review round 1 on candidate tree f0f91c02fb3d3ea4e82958e1a73be696bdf77d84 (2026-10-27): fresh Claude reviewer reported nothing blocking (checks green, tree unchanged). Codex (gpt-6.1-sol, xhigh) reported two blocking findings, both accepted:

1. [P1] Orbit's client OutputQueue (orbit/src/socket.rs:215-266) lets a newer Frame or ScrollOutcome replace a VerticalPreview it has not started writing. Under output backpressure an answer can vanish while the attachment stays healthy, so the candidate's hold (cleared only by an answer or a reset) could stay set forever and stop all scrolling. The design comment's claim "Orbit answers each PreviewVertical once" was wrong. This is also why the base code re-armed on every frame.
2. [P2] A terminal still visible in another column keeps its transport when the selected pane moves (set_orbit_attachment keeps the outgoing connection; owes_viewport looks only at pending_viewport). Switching away and back before an old preview answer lands let that late answer release a newer request in the other direction.

Change of plan (relying on Lucca's standing approval, relayed by eon-overseer: Lucca, 2026-10-26, "everything is pre-approved. autonomous." and "also pre-aprove changes of plan if a clearly better alternative appears"; applied here to the pacing mechanism within this bead's scope, venus/src/application/scroll.rs and application.rs; no contract text adopted or changed, VEN-C7 and ORB-C8 unchanged):

Venus cannot tell from a frame whether Orbit dropped the answer, and the wire stays as is (out of scope). So the hold is released by the answer in the requested direction, by reset(), or by a fixed grace after the first frame that follows the request:
- preview_pending is Option<(direction, first frame after the request)>.
- frame_arrived(now) records the first frame-class message (Frame, WheelOutcome::Viewport, ScrollOutcome::Viewport) after the request.
- PREVIEW_ANSWER_GRACE = 50 ms after that frame, retry_preview(now) drops the hold. about_to_wait checks it each loop turn and drives the scroll, and preview_retry_at() joins the event-loop deadlines, so a dropped answer is retried even if output stops after the replacing frame.
- preview_arrived(direction) releases only for an answer in the requested direction (fixes the P2 scenario); a same-direction late answer from a retained column can still release early, which costs at most one extra request and never a stuck hold.

Effect: while output keeps arriving, Venus sends at most one PreviewVertical per answer or per 50 ms grace, instead of one per frame revision. If an answer really was replaced, a gesture's first preview can start up to ~50 ms later than base, which re-asked on the next frame; this only happens under Orbit output backpressure.

Configurability: PREVIEW_ANSWER_GRACE stays fixed. It is internal request pacing within the ORB-C8 exchange, felt only as a start latency under backpressure, and a setting would cost more support than users could gain by differing.

Regression extended: terminal_scroll_keeps_one_preview_outstanding_across_frames now also covers frames inside the grace (no resend), the grace retry after a frame (exactly one new request), the direction-mismatched late answer, cancel keeping the hold, and failure/reset clearing it.

Accepted residuals: a server Failure or local InvalidInput for some other message, or a same-direction late answer from a retained column, can release the hold early; each costs one extra request at most.

title: Square the sheet's bottom corners and thicken its top border
description:
## Decision
Lucca, 2026-10-17, looking at the installed round corners: 'make the top borders of the main area thicker' and 'fix the bottom corners, they should be flush instead of this' (screenshot: the footer's rounded lower-left corner left a wedge inside the window corner). The sheet's bottom corners become square, flush with the window's bottom corners (the footer, and the sheet itself when hints are hidden); only the top corners stay rounded. The sheet's top border, including its rounded corners, becomes 2 px; seams, separators and side edges below the corner curves stay 1 px. The popup frame reuses the sheet and follows both changes.

## Contract (edits approved by this decision)
EON-C8, VEN-C8, EON-C24, VEN-C24, VEN-C18 if needed, PRESENTATION.md and changelogs: square lower corners on the window's bottom corners; 2 px top border. Footer hints return to the plain edge padding (no bottom corner to clear); header labels clear only the top corners.

## Acceptance
Venus suites, fmt, clippy, nix build; isolated capture with hints shown and hidden and a popup; review loop; profile refresh.

## Scope boundary
Bottom corner shape and top border weight only; no color, radius or tab change.
close_reason: Bottom corners square and flush on the window corners; 2 px top edge and curves; popups follow. Proof and ledger in comments.

comments.author: lucca

title: Round the workspace sheet's outer corners to the header height
description:
## Decision
Lucca, 2026-10-17 ('yeah, i love it', after the schematic mockup): the workspace sheet's outer corners use a radius equal to the pane header height, so the top curve meets the window's side edge exactly at the first header's bottom separator. The bottom corners use the footer height (with hints hidden too, for symmetry). The first header's label and the footer hints move right enough to clear the curve (about 8 px at default typography). Rule kept: objects round, dividers straight; the sheet, as the outermost container, carries the largest radius.

## Contract (edits approved by this decision)
- Sheet outer corners: top radius = pane header height, bottom radius = footer height; they scale with typography. Seams, separators and inner header edges stay straight.
- Header fills, the pane-focus outline where it touches an outer corner, the popup outer frame and the footer follow the same corners.
- The outer columns' first header label and the footer hints inset clear of the curve; terminal grids, hit targets and other headers are unchanged.
- pane_frames = false keeps its current inset shapes.
- Wording: VEN-C8, EON-C8 (and C24 where they name the footer corners), PRESENTATION.md, USAGE.md and INTERACTION.md, plus changelogs.

## Prerequisites
After eon-flush-sheet-bottom-f68t (same frame code).

## Acceptance
Venus suites, fmt, clippy and nix build green; one isolated installed capture at one and several columns, hints shown and hidden, with a popup; review loop; profile refresh.

## Scope boundary
Corner radii and the label/hint insets they require only; no color, typography or configuration change.
close_reason: Sheet corners rounded to the first header's height with the first tab pill centered over the top-left curve; labels, pill and hints clear the curves; one clamped radius owner. Proof and 7-pass ledger in comments.
