title: Give every program that reports over OSC 7501 an icon in the Agents sidebar and inbox
description:
## Why

Lucca, 2026-11-07: "investigate the icons we support, in the sidebar / agy has an icon? / long term we want every program that supports that OSC protocol to have an icon".

## Today (investigation 2026-11-07)

- Only `app=claude-code` and `app=codex` get an icon in the Agents sidebar and attention inbox: a hardcoded match in venus/src/scene.rs:2071-2076 on the `app` field of OSC 7501 (Program Status Protocol, ORB-C15, orbit/docs/CONTRACTS.md:1021). Any other `app` shows the state glyph and the raw app string, no icon; VEN-C30 (venus/docs/CONTRACTS.md:2003-2005) states this.
- The icon type is `QuotaProvider { Codex, Claude }` (scene.rs:519), shared with the quota chips; assets are 104x104 alpha masks (venus/assets/claude-splat-104.alpha, openai-blossom-104.alpha) drawn tinted (render/chrome.rs:313, 2515-2525).
- OSC 7501 has no icon field, there is no user mapping, and no generic fallback. agy (Antigravity) gets none; whether agy emits OSC 7501 at all is unverified.

## Goal

Every program that reports over OSC 7501 shows an icon:
1. A sidebar app-icon type separate from QuotaProvider.
2. A generic fallback for any `app` (for example a monogram of its first letter in the icon slot), so no row is iconless.
3. Built-in icons for the agents Eon launches or knows (Claude Code, Codex, agy/Gemini, opencode, Grok, pi), with assets whose licence allows it.
4. Optionally, a configuration table mapping an `app` value to a built-in icon (rule 6: defaults documented in docs/CONFIGURATION.md).
5. Check whether agy emits OSC 7501 (and its `app` value); if not, note what reporting it needs.
VEN-C30's icon sentence changes (minor amendment). An icon field in OSC 7501 itself is out of scope unless the research shows a strong reason.

## Current plan (2026-11-12)

The 2026-11-07 research and 2026-11-10 contrast decisions in comments supersede
Goal items 3-5 wherever tentative: .1 observes exact app keys; .2 owns the shared
slot/monogram/generic behavior; .3 re-sources Claude; .4 adds opencode/pi; .5 adds
only app values proven by .1; .6 supplies the approved configuration overrides.
Do not add an icon key to OSC 7501. Stable research:
`/home/lucca/pjs/refs/eon-app-icons-research/00-today.md` through `04-slices.md`.

At dcaef1c the two-app match remains at `venus/src/scene.rs:2704-2705`, with
QuotaProvider at `:635`; VEN-C30 starts at `venus/docs/CONTRACTS.md:2307`.
One-color marks use vendor black on light backgrounds/white on dark, as decided;
colored marks stay in vendor colors. Children carry the current acceptance and
approval boundaries. Sequence .2 -> .4 -> .5 -> .6 so the final mark-name set is
known before config validation; .1 gates .5. .3 has no semantic blocker on .2, but shared notices/test edits and landings are serialized; do not run them in parallel.
Epic acceptance: all six slices meet their own observable acceptance, preserving
no-app/unavailable observations and sidebar/inbox parity. No guessed identities,
provider detection, arbitrary images or new contract approval in this pass.

title: Collapse and expand Agents sidebar sections by clicking their header
description:
## Why

Lucca, 2026-11-07: "post 0.2 bead: let sections in the sidebar be collapsable
(click) / im not that heavy a use and see how fast it fills". This remains outside
the v0.2.0 gate.

## Evidence and recorded decisions

`SidebarHeading { tab, label }` (`venus/src/scene.rs:345`) and its construction
at `:2888` group the shown session's rows by tab, not by session. VEN-C30
(`venus/docs/CONTRACTS.md:2307`) and USAGE own the present sidebar; Hide buttons
`eon-5g0e5` and pane-header work `eon-2ibdd` are both landed prerequisites.

On 2026-11-10 eon-overseer, under the standing auto-decide rule, chose per-window,
per-run collapse state like scroll position, with one `[sidebar]` start-collapsed
setting. No wire change or CLI path; the plan adds section collapse to the Humans
and Agents view-state exceptions. Preserve that decision, show the rule-text change
in the READY note, and obtain required final contract wording approval before edits.

## Scope and acceptance

- Click a tab section heading, or Enter/Space on its keyboard stop, to collapse or
  expand that tab's rows. Leave the Agents title's Hide control and CLI alone.
  Use collapse/expand names and a disclosure chevron, never Hide for this action.
- Collapsed headings retain row count and highest urgency (blocked, done, working)
  so attention remains visible. Hidden rows neither hit-test nor remain in the
  accessible tree or keyboard traversal; AccessKit exposes expanded/collapsed state.
- Up/Down/F6 include headings and skip collapsed rows; the implementation plan
  records focus fallback when collapsing a focused/current row, behavior for Alt+G
  and jumps into a collapsed section, and stale/removed/recreated tab identity.
  No guessed jump behavior: present any consequential choice before code.
- Collapse persists across redraws in the same window run; reopening uses the
  documented start-collapsed setting. No durable persistence or new EONW state.
- Update CONFIGURATION default, USAGE/PRESENTATION, product changelog, and the
  Humans and Agents exception. Scope the VEN-C30 navigation/accessibility clause
  for approval; no contract is amended by this planning pass.

## Verification and boundary

Focused Scene/accessibility checks cover toggle, count/urgency, traversal and
focus/jump transitions. One isolated installed observation covers click, keys,
AccessKit and light/dark contrast, using the current author proof/review route.
Portability: neutral at existing Venus owners. No other-session grouping here:
`eon-vzpvj` consumes this control later. Stop for unapproved lifecycle, wire,
contract or durable-state work; keep one implementation slice.

title: Show a pane's pinned name in the Agents sidebar instead of the bare app name
description:
## Why

Lucca, 2026-11-07, screenshot of the Agents sidebar: six Codex agents all listed as "Codex" (rows "Codex · 2h · p3", "Codex · 1m · p10", ...), after the overseer pinned informative pane names with `eon pane rename` ("events ciwn.8", "bend chat", ...). He had asked "can we rename p10 pane or agent so it's more informative? all panes in this tab are just Codex". Claude rows show the session name (eon-overseer) because Claude reports one; Codex reports none, so its rows fall back to the app name and the pinned name is ignored. Happy users: a person who names a pane expects that name where the pane's agent is listed.

## Goal

An Agents sidebar row (and the same row's text wherever attention is listed: the attention inbox, `eon session --json` attention entries if they carry a display name) shows the pane's pinned name when the person pinned one, keeping the app icon so the agent kind stays visible: e.g. "events ciwn.8" with the Codex icon, "2h · p3" underneath. Without a pinned name, today's behavior stays (the agent's own name, else the app name). Decide in the plan whether a pinned name should also win over an agent-reported name (recommendation: yes; the person's choice outranks the agent's), and how a popup agent (no pane name) is shown.

## Contract and scope

Feature (presentation; venus/docs/PRESENTATION.md, Agents sidebar). Check whether EON-C attention or session JSON contracts define the display-name field; if the JSON changes, that is a contract amendment (minor, overseer-approvable). Configurability: no new key expected (the person's pinned name is the setting). Humans and Agents: `eon pane rename` already exists, so agents can set it.

## Acceptance

A scene test: a Codex attention row in a pane with a pinned name renders that name; without one, "Codex"; a reported agent name with and without a pinned name per the plan's decision. One installed observation in an isolated window.

title: Fill the sidebar row of the agent terminal that has keyboard focus
description:
## Why

Lucca, 2026-10-23, looking at the agent sidebar's popup markers: "it was supposed to highlight the
row of the agent my keyboard is focused on?". Today no row marks the agent whose terminal has
keyboard focus. VEN-C30's row highlight (venus/src/scene.rs ~130, "The keyboard-focused row's target
while the sidebar holds focus") only follows the sidebar's own F6 or arrow navigation, plus mouse
hover. The tab heading's "popup shown" glyph (from eon-agent-sidebar-yx8.16) is the only
current-state mark, and it is small and a line away from the row it concerns.

Approved by Lucca, 2026-10-23 ("yes to everything", answering the overseer's items 1 and 2):
replace the heading's popup-shown glyph with a "you are here" fill on the row of the agent terminal
that has keyboard focus, panes and popups alike; keep the always-on popup glyph on rows
(eon-popup-marker-always-52rk). File now; start after eon-orbit-stop-not-reaped-7vb4 and
eon-reap-error-unstopped-hfzr.

## Change

- The sidebar row whose source terminal has keyboard focus in the active tab (a pane or the shown
  popup) gets a "you are here" fill: a faint accent (mint) tint, about 10-15% of
  `accent`, distinct from the navy `selected` fill used for hover and sidebar navigation. Hover and
  sidebar-focus highlight and outline draw over it unchanged. Rows in other tabs never get it.
- If that terminal has several records, the one row it leads carries the fill.
- The tab heading no longer ends with the popup-shown glyph, and its accessible label drops
  "popup shown". The current row's accessible label adds a state such as "current" (pick the word
  with the AccessKit convention used elsewhere in Venus; record it).
- Rows keep the popup glyph after their catalog label, as 52rk made them.

## Contract (VEN-C30; wording to Lucca through the overseer before code)

Replace the heading half of the "Popup marker" bullet, and add a "Current row" bullet. Draft the
exact text in the bead.

## Configurability

The tint derives from the theme's accent. It becomes themeable through eon-eon-themes-or3q; record
that as the configuration route rather than adding a separate setting.

## Acceptance

- A Venus scene test: with keyboard focus on a pane agent's terminal, its row carries the
  current-row state and no other row does; with the Agent popup shown and focused, the popup's row
  carries it; the heading carries no popup glyph; sidebar F6 focus on another row keeps both states
  distinct. It fails on today's code.
- Venus fmt and clippy, `nix develop -c eon-test -p yazelix-venus`, Codex review.
- One installed observation after the profile refresh: focus a pane agent, then open the Agent
  popup, and the fill follows.

## Scope

Venus sidebar only. Not the Eon Bar tab pills, the glyph's shape, or light-theme colors (or3q).

title: Move panes sideways with Ctrl+Alt+H/L and tabs with Ctrl+Alt+Shift+H/L
description:
## Decision
Lucca, 2026-10-17: Ctrl+Alt+H/L moves the selected pane sideways between columns, so Ctrl+Alt+H/J/K/L moves the selected pane in every direction, matching Alt+H/J/K/L navigation. Tab moves go to Ctrl+Alt+Shift+H/L, and `eon tab move left|right` stays the CLI route. Compared and rejected: a column move that falls through to a tab move at the edge (the same keys sometimes move the whole tab); a separate column chord (awkward, and leaves the pane-move grid incomplete); a tab mode with an entry key (new mode state, an indicator, exit rules and focus edge cases, and it breaks EON-C8/VEN-C8's "without a mode" rule for a rarely used action). Fallback if Ctrl+Alt+Shift+H/L is unavailable: Ctrl+Alt+H/L (or Shift+Left/Right) moves the tab while F6 focus is on the tab strip.

## Contract (to draft and show Lucca before code)
- Ctrl+Alt+H/L moves the selected pane into the neighbouring column of its tab, at the same position or the end of that column's stack (exact rule to propose), and it stays selected. Moving a column's only pane out removes that column, which also reorders columns. At the tab's outer edge: open a new column with that pane if the tab has fewer than four (proposed), otherwise stop quietly, like other moves. In a popup-covered or picker-bound tab, unavailable, as moves are today.
- Ctrl+Alt+Shift+H/L sends today's tab Move left/right, non-repeating, without a mode.
- Failures: a fifth column, an unknown or stale identity, or an invalid transition leaves the accepted topology unchanged.

## Changes needing approval
- EON-C8: drop "cross-column … pane movement" from the Boundary and add the move rule; the key mapping text changes.
- EONW: a new revision or action carrying a cross-column pane move (the v10 WorkspaceAction is v3's and stays unchanged; follow the slice 2 CreateColumn precedent of a top-level action). Historical revisions stay unchanged.
- VEN-C8: Ctrl+Alt+H/L and Ctrl+Alt+Shift+H/L mappings; shortcut viewer, hints, USAGE, README, INTERACTION, CHANGELOG (Ctrl+Alt+H/L changes meaning during the 0.x beta).
- Runtime reserves Ctrl+Alt+Shift+H/L from popup keybindings.

## Prerequisites and first check
After eon-splits-opwv (closed). First check, before drafting code: whether COSMIC and Sway (and their default configs) bind Ctrl+Alt+Shift+H/L, and whether Venus receives the chord with exact modifiers; a conflict switches to the F6 fallback, which needs Lucca's choice. Reference gate: consequential (contract, EONW wire). Record inspected references (for example Zellij move-pane and tmux join-pane at exact revisions) before code.

## Acceptance
- Runtime tests: a cross-column move keeps identities and selection, removes an emptied column, refuses a fifth column, and leaves topology unchanged on failure; codec tests for the new action; a Venus mapping test for both chords.
- One isolated installed dogfood observation: moving a pane across columns and reordering a tab with the new chords.

## Scope boundary
No vertical splits, column resizing, drag and drop, a tab mode, or cross-tab pane moves.
close_reason: Ctrl+Alt+H/L moves the selected pane into the neighbouring column and Ctrl+Alt+Shift+H/L moves the tab over EONW v12; eon pane move left|right; covered tabs refuse. Full suite, flake check, isolated dogfood of the profile's store path, graph at EONW 12. Proof and ledgers in comments.

comments.author: lucca
comments.text: Open decisions raised by Lucca 2026-10-17, with recommendations (not yet chosen). (1) Outer-edge move: block quietly; move into the neighbouring tab's stack (conflicts with tabs as launch-directory groups and EON-C8's no cross-tab moves; needs popup, picker and emptied-tab rules); as a vertical split (out of scope, rejected); or open a new column at that edge while the tab has fewer than four columns, else block. Recommended: the new-column rule; a pane alone in its column stops quietly at the edge. (2) Landing: join the neighbour column's stack, inserted just below its expanded pane and becoming expanded and selected; or always create a new column beside it (no way to merge into a stack without another key, and the four-column cap refuses it quickly). Recommended: join the stack. Resulting model: Ctrl+Alt+K/J reorders within a stack (existing); Ctrl+Alt+H/L moves to the neighbouring stack and splits out into a new column at the outer edge; an emptied column disappears, so columns reorder by moving their panes. Cross-tab pane moves stay out of the first cut.

Zellij 16beceaa0afcdb559316909ed87b84d487356fa6 (zellij-utils/assets/layouts/default.swap.kdl, zellij-server/src/tab/swap_layouts.rs): per-tab swap layouts over the same panes (vertical, horizontal, stacked, plus BASE), picked by pane-count constraints and cycled with Alt+[ and Alt+]; a manual change marks the layout damaged. comments.text:
Lucca, 2026-10-20: contract approved (agent's recommendations accepted).
First check: COSMIC (cosmic-settings-daemon 1.10.0, /usr/share/cosmic/com.system76.CosmicSettings.Shortcuts/v1/defaults, empty user custom) and Sway 1.12 default config bind H/L only with Super; no Ctrl+Alt+Shift+H/L conflict, F6 fallback not needed. Reference: niri aee25c9efcfa85b6029d5d1a2b7aaac7d87ae9d1 src/layout/scrolling.rs consume_or_expel_window_left: a lone window joins the end of the neighbouring column (no-op at the edge); a stacked window is always expelled to a new column beside its source, with no column cap. Rejected: niri's expel-from-stack as the landing rule (moving a stacked pane one column over takes two presses, and the four-column cap refuses it often).
Decisions:
1. Landing: the pane joins the neighbouring column's stack directly below that column's expanded pane and becomes expanded and selected. In the source column the following pane expands, otherwise the preceding one. An emptied column disappears.
2. Outer edge: a stacked pane opens a new column at that edge while the tab has fewer than four columns, under Alt+Shift+M's 40-terminal-column refusal notice; a lone pane at the edge, or a fifth column, stops quietly.
3. Wire: EONW v12 adds one top-level action, MovePaneSideways { direction }, on the selected pane (v11 ClosePane precedent); v4 Move and older revisions keep their bytes.
4. Keys: Ctrl+Alt+H/L moves the pane sideways; Ctrl+Alt+Shift+H/L moves the tab; both non-repeating, no mode. Runtime reserves Ctrl+Alt+Shift+H/L from popup keybindings.
5. Added scope: eon pane move left|right sends the same v12 action.

title: Simplify Eon's proof and planning ceremony
description:
## Chosen outcome — Lucca, 2026-10-14
Simplify Eon's proof and planning ceremony. Scope narrowed by Lucca on 2026-10-14: only Eon's policy changes. It becomes the root policy of the consolidated repository. Eon Sessions, Eon Desktop and Eon Runtime are frozen until consolidation and their policies are not rewritten. Their subsystem rules are rewritten once, already simplified, as subsystem instructions during `Consolidate Eon into one repository`. Keep exact identities at acceptance, installed proof before handoff, live-terminal preservation and ownership rules. Remove per-iteration bookkeeping. On the same date Lucca also approved the isolated-candidate workflow in rule 2.

Evidence, 30 days to 2026-10-14: about 80 of Eon's 193 commits begin Record/Accept/Consume, and about 64 of Venus's 139–178 do (counts vary by method). The shortcut-hints bar took about ten rounds, each a Venus commit, an Eon "Select/Consume" pin and an installed-proof commit. The version badge and footer followed the same Consume → Accept pattern. The cause is policy granularity: "exact accepted revisions" applies to every iteration, and Venus proof requires a separate metadata commit. The repository split multiplies that cost.

## Rules (contract)
1. **Batch proof.** Iterate freely. Do one installed proof per accepted batch. Intermediate rounds produce candidate observations, not accepted proof.
2. **Authorized isolated candidates.** Use a disposable Eon source snapshot that changes only `components/eon-alpha-v3.json`, `flake.nix`/`flake.lock` and, when needed, `crates/eon/Cargo.toml`/`Cargo.lock`, pointing at exact child candidate commits. Revision assertions and build gates stay unchanged. Clean commits only, no dirty trees. Never commit the snapshot. Observe in isolated runtime and configuration roots. Record candidate evidence separately. Refresh the normal profile only after batch acceptance. Limited to changes that preserve accepted protocol contracts; protocol evolution needs its own authorization.
3. **One commit per change.** The proof record (revision, check, environment, result) lives in the owning bead and references the commit. `CONTRACTS.md` holds the contract, its checks and its status, not the latest proving SHA. This removes the rule that a source commit must be followed by a metadata commit.
4. **Tiered gates.** Execution baseline, Reference gate and Crate gate comments are required only for: new or changed dependencies; protocol or wire changes; new or changed contracts; lifecycle, security or trust boundaries. Presentation-only changes need one dogfood observation.

## Owners
Eon's `.agent-protocols.local.md` and `.agent-protocols.exceptions.json`, re-rendered with Starcompass. Child repository policies are out of scope. If a canonical protocol conflicts, change Starcompass or record an AP-EXCEPTION-001 exception approved by Lucca. Never resolve a conflict silently.

None. This precedes `Consolidate Eon into one repository`, so that consolidation doesn't run under the old ceremony.

## Reference gate
Read Eon's current overlay and the canonical AP-PROOF-001, AP-PLAN-001, AP-TEST-001 and AP-GIT-001 text at the chosen Starcompass commit, plus Starcompass's README render/check contract. No external references needed.

## Scope boundary
Eon policy and repository tooling only. No edits to child repository policies. No product behavior or contract changes. No renumbering. No rewrite of existing proof records or history: existing indexed proofs stay valid as written.

title: Create a five-minute new-user path through Eon docs
description:
## Why

A first-time user must currently cross maintainer-level lifecycle, wire, geometry, and subsystem detail before understanding the product and completing the first durable-session workflow. The documentation is rigorous, but its entry path is too dense.

Contract: a first-time x86_64 Linux Wayland user opens `README.md`, understands what Eon does and its support boundary, installs it, starts work, closes and reopens the window without losing the Session, finds shortcut help, and knows how to report a problem within about five minutes. The path must not require reading the contract ledger or learning Orbit and Venus names first.

## Evidence

- Baseline `18f1874f3357aa7f082db004c735a10347fac646`: `README.md` is 602 lines and `docs/CONTRACTS.md` is 1,503 lines.
- `README.md:7-31` leads with component-graph, EONW, generation, process, and platform-proof detail before a newcomer task.
- `README.md:93-115` contains installation, but current credentials and support constraints are separated from the first-use lifecycle at `README.md:125-149`.
- `README.md:184-540` places detailed workspace, picker, popup, rendering, configuration, and protocol behavior in the main entry document.
- `README.md:562-580` already routes maintainers to architecture, contracts, distribution, references, and Beads.
- `README.md:582-602` records the required LOC scorecard.

Impact: HIGH onboarding and evaluation friction. Effort: M. Risk: LOW if claims retain one canonical owner. Confidence: HIGH.

## Scope

In scope:
- Reshape `README.md` into a concise public entry: promise, supported platform, prerequisites, install, first launch, detach/reconnect, F1 shortcut discovery, limitations, troubleshooting/reporting, and links for deeper use.
- Move maintainer-only explanations to the existing owning documents when they are not already there; link instead of copying.
- Keep `docs/CONTRACTS.md` as the complete proof ledger, but give it a compact orientation/index if navigation remains poor after README routing.
- Put public product terms before Orbit, Venus, EONW, manifest, or generation internals.

Out of scope:
- Runtime, package, configuration, keybinding, platform, or product-contract changes.
- Removing proof evidence, weakening support limitations, duplicating truth, creating a documentation framework, adding a build dependency, or implementing `eon-yvw`.
- Claiming credential-free installation before its separate alpha-source task is accepted.

## Implementation Notes

1. Write the shortest newcomer journey first, against the exact accepted product revision.
2. Retain one owner for each detailed fact. Prefer links into existing architecture, contracts, distribution, benchmark, and reference documents over new files or repeated prose.
3. Keep exact support and private-input limitations prominent next to installation.
4. Preserve a clearly labeled maintainer section and the LOC scorecard. Target a README below roughly 300 lines; exceed that only when the newcomer journey is demonstrably clearer and no detailed fact is duplicated.
5. If the 1,503-line contract ledger needs easier lookup, add navigation only; do not split it or rewrite proof history without evidence that navigation is insufficient.

## Verification

- `wc -l README.md docs/CONTRACTS.md` records the before/after size without treating line count alone as quality.
- `rg -n "Project status|Install|attach|F1|Supported|Troubleshoot|Report|Maintainer|LOC scorecard" README.md` finds the complete newcomer and maintainer routes.
- `rg -n "EON-C[0-9]+|Status:|Evidence" docs/CONTRACTS.md` confirms the proof ledger remains present.
- `git diff --check` exits 0; the changed Markdown links resolve to tracked files; the README LOC scorecard matches all tracked handwritten surfaces.
- A clean reader walkthrough can answer: what Eon is, whether their platform is supported, how to install and launch it, what survives window close, how to reconnect, where keys are shown, and where to report a failure without opening `docs/CONTRACTS.md`.

## Stop Conditions

- Stop if shortening would delete unique accepted proof, obscure a material limitation, or make README and canonical docs disagree.
- Stop for user choice before adding a site, generator, dependency, durable non-Rust tooling, or public deployment.
- Stop if current product behavior has materially drifted from the cited baseline; refresh claims before editing.

## Maintenance Notes

This fixes documentation hierarchy, not contract rigor. The contract ledger remains maintainer evidence. The deferred interactive explainer `eon-yvw` is optional presentation work and does not replace this entry path.
close_reason: README provides the verified five-minute newcomer path and keeps detailed proof with its existing owners.

title: Push agent attention to the person's phone
description:
## Why
All four competitors reach the person away from the desk: push notifications to a phone and a mobile
client (Rex iOS TestFlight, T3 Code iOS/Android, Amp apps, herdr via Moshi). Eon covers desktop
notification and sound (eon-2kvr, eon-iwmz); mobile only through frozen beads
orb-native-mobile-access-bwg and orb-permanent-ssh-terminal-access-hd6. Source: competitor audit
eon-r6yt (2026-10-29), reports in ~/pjs/refs/competitor-audit-2026-10/. Lucca, 2026-10-29: "file the
beads". Filing only; no work is approved yet beyond planning.

## Scope of this bead (narrowed 2026-10-29, prime-beads pass)
Push only: send "agent needs you / finished" to the person's phone through a channel they already
use, off by default. The mobile client scope stays where it already lives: orb-native-mobile-access-bwg
(native mobile client), orb-permanent-ssh-terminal-access-hd6 (any SSH terminal, including a phone)
and eon-remote-workspaces-52i4 (remote host). This bead does not unfreeze them.

## Contracts
EON-C31 (Agent attention) amendment for the trigger, or a new EON-C for push delivery. Consequential:
trust boundary (attention data leaves the machine; agent-authored `title` and `msg` may hold
sensitive text) and possibly a dependency (HTTP client). Lucca approves the text before code.

## Design options for the reference gate
1. Built-in channel: Runtime POSTs to an ntfy or Pushover endpoint from `[attention]` settings.
2. Command hook: Eon runs a configured argv on each raise (the person's `ntfy publish`, `curl`, or
   anything), so Eon adds no HTTP client and no third-party trust.
3. Recipe over the event stream (eon-ciwn.1): a documented script subscribes and pushes; Eon ships
   nothing new for push.
Compare ownership, dependency weight (AP-DEPENDENCY-001), privacy defaults (which fields leave the
machine; default to state and pane only), and failure behaviour (never blocks the Runtime).
References: docs/REFERENCES.md cmux route (notifications) and the cross-device route; ntfy and
Pushover APIs; how Rex and T3 Code push, at recorded revisions.

## Prerequisites
The mechanism decision can run now: eon-2kvr's shared-trigger/settings design was approved on 2026-11-06. Its open implementation is a prerequisite only for a chosen push implementation that relies on it, not for comparing options here. Preserve one owner for the EON-C31 trigger/quiet rule and `[attention]` settings. Related: eon-2kvr and EON-C39 (delivered event stream); eon-ciwn.1 records option 3's original research.

## Acceptance
- With push configured, an attention raise reaches the configured endpoint within the bound the
  contract sets (seconds), observed in an isolated installed run against a local test endpoint, not
  a third-party service.
- With push off (the default), no network connection is made, shown by a focused test of the
  trigger path.
- Defaults documented in docs/CONFIGURATION.md; contract and mechanism approved by Lucca before code.

## Verification
- Focused trigger and privacy test in the owning crate via `nix develop -c eon-test -p <crate>`.
- Installed runtime route: profile refresh plus one isolated installed observation.

## Decision-first boundary (2026-11-12)

This bead now records the bounded mechanism decision and contract proposal before
implementation. The desired push outcome and conditional acceptance above remain
requirements for the chosen implementation, not authorization to ship one of the
three options. `eon events` is delivered under EON-C39 (`docs/CONTRACTS.md:5579`);
option 3 can be assessed against the existing stream today. `eon-ciwn.1` is the
closed research record, not the implementation owner. `eon-2kvr`'s shared-trigger
settings were approved on 2026-11-06; its open implementation still gates any
implementation that depends on that new trigger/quiet behavior. A recipe must
state differences from it rather than claiming equivalence.

Decision acceptance: compare the three mechanisms at recorded source revisions,
including privacy of names/title/msg, credentials, bounded nonblocking failures,
quiet/dedup/reconnect behavior and off-by-default zero traffic. Record a numbered
recommendation and exact proposed contract/config text where needed, then seek
Lucca's choice before scoping implementation. A local endpoint proves emission,
not delivery to a phone; eventual acceptance must separately observe a configured
test phone under an approved service/account and state best-effort limits. Never
send real terminal contents, credentials or live attention in an experiment.
No mobile client, remote transport or frozen-bead scope is unfrozen here.

title: Halve the always-loaded agent instructions
description:
## Decision
Lucca, 2026-10-15: cut the always-loaded agent instructions roughly in half. The root `AGENTS.md`
becomes a short, practical page; the full protocol text loads on demand.

## Contract
- Consumer: any coding agent starting work in this repository.
- Result: the root `AGENTS.md` is about half its current size and still states who owns what, the
build and sandboxed test commands, the Git rules and when to stop and ask (contracts, scope,
dependencies, publishing). The canonical protocol text stays available in a file the root page
names and loads only when needed. No rule silently changes meaning.

   eon-igae.7.3.

4. VEN-C26 sub-contracts: fold them into VEN-C22/VEN-C26 as clauses, or index them. Indexing would

  contract heading appears once.

old composite statuses have since become a defined status plus a gap. Retired

the 2026-10-29 list survives. Existing EON Proven/Orbit Proved spellings are each

Acceptance concerns live records only: a defined primary status with honest gaps,
unique contract headings, and exact check/revision/platform/artifact for each
claimed proof, or explicitly unproved where original evidence is unavailable.
Do not require nonexistent artifacts for unproved claims or infer passing proof
from a known commit. Present only the remaining numbered choices and exact wording
for approval; no behavior, new guarantee, retirement or new ID is authorized here.

## Why
Parent: eon-so8o (contract audit 2026-10-29 at fb7fe98; findings in
/home/lucca/.cache/eon-agents/eon-overseer/contract-audit-2026-10-29.md, section 2). Editing a
contract record needs Lucca's approval of the wording (AGENTS.md Contract-Driven Method).

23 EON-C proofs (docs/CONTRACTS.md audit lines :132, :237, :338, :579, :770, :1113, :1294, :1348,
:1389, :1424, :1509, :1570, :1615, :1755, :1824, :1885, :1958, :2034, :2114, :2168, :2235 and
others; see the epic's line note) and 26 hash uses in venus/docs/CONTRACTS.md cite 795d735
(2026-10-14), before the Bend Orbit import (6818aee, 2026-10-19), EONW v9..v23 and 474 commits. The
installed tier ran the legacy Rust Orbit, yet they say bare Proven. eon-igae.7 (and .7.1, .7.2)
re-proves only some installed halves (EON-C15, C17, C19, C27, VEN-C29, and contracts changed for
1.0); about 18 others have no re-proof bead. Orbit's own pre-Bend evidence is eon-so8o.2's.

## Change
List each affected EON-C and VEN-C contract with its last proof revision and whether its owner
changed since. Present Lucca a numbered list: per contract (or per group), either mark the proof as
pre-Bend candidate evidence until re-proved, or add it to eon-igae.7's 1.0-candidate run (preferred
over a separate proof campaign). Then draft the record wording for his approval. Adding contracts to
eon-igae.7's scope is a change to that bead, made only after Lucca chooses.

## Acceptance
- Every Proven EON-C and VEN-C proof either ran on the current (Bend) Orbit, or says plainly that it
  predates it and which bead re-proves it.
- Lucca's choices and approval of the wording are recorded on this bead (his words, date) before the
  commit; eon-igae.7 (or its child) lists any contracts he added to its run.

## Verification
Docs and contract-record route: changed paths, contract IDs and diff; Codex reviews the contract
record change. No runtime profile refresh; this bead runs no proofs.

## Scope
docs/CONTRACTS.md and venus/docs/CONTRACTS.md only. No behaviour change, no re-proof here. Priority
P1 because 1.0 (eon-igae) must not ship contracts that claim Proven on an Orbit Eon no longer
ships.

description:

amendment history in Status and Proof; VEN-C30's Status is a 20-line bead history. The audit also
found restated duplicates: EON-C27's quota-chip text restates the chip layout that VEN-C22 and
VEN-C26 own (docs/CONTRACTS.md audit :2186-2275 vs venus :1488-1815), and EON-C7, ORB-C14 and
VEN-C16 each restate the macOS status (EON-C7 carries the narrative).

## Change
Draft, for Lucca's approval: move amendment history to the owning beads or CHANGELOG, keeping each
contract's current promise, checks, status and proof; replace restated text with a reference to its
one owner. Leave the macOS restatement until eon-mac-launch-kz4p settles those three contracts
(record that here if so).

## Acceptance
- Each of the five reads as current state; the chip layout has one owner; a promise-by-promise diff
  review (recorded on the bead) confirms no promise, check or proof was removed.
- Lucca's approval of the wording is recorded on this bead (his words, date) before the commit.

## Verification
Docs and contract-record route: changed paths, contract IDs and diff, plus the promise diff review;
Codex reviews the contract record change. No runtime profile refresh.

## Scope
The three CONTRACTS.md files (and CHANGELOG.md if history goes there). No behaviour change.
Blocked by eon-agent-parity-a9g0.9, which edits VEN-C30 wording; prefer landing after
eon-so8o.1-.4 too, since they edit lines inside these five records (not a hard block). If the five
contracts do not fit one session, split by file.

## Split execution boundary (2026-11-12)

This is a container for one cleanup per contract-index owner/file, so promise
mapping, approvals and proof preservation fit fresh sessions. The current baseline
is dcaef1c, not the old line counts. The supposed quota-layout duplicate is partly
moot: VEN-C22/VEN-C26 and EON-C29/30 were retired on 2026-10-30, and live EON-C27
owns quota *collection* (`docs/CONTRACTS.md:3818`), not a second presentation owner.
Do not restore retired widget contracts or delete Runtime collection promises.

Children cover root EON-C8/C10/C31, Venus VEN-C8/VEN-C30, and only the identified
Orbit platform-history overlap (ORB-C14), respectively. Preserve every promise,
check and exact historical proof identity; use a clause/evidence map before and
after. Current macOS partial/native proofs have evolved since the audit, so
revalidate EON-C7/ORB-C14/VEN-C16 before deciding whether any overlap is removable.
No record is a substitute for another owner's distinct proof surface.

Use owning Beads/Git for execution history. Planning-only relocation does not earn
a fresh product changelog entry under AGENTS.md rule 10; preserve existing accepted
chronology without rewriting it. Lucca's exact wording approval and Codex contract
review remain required. Epic acceptance is the three bounded children meeting
those requirements; no behavior or contract promise changes.

title: Source trustworthy Codex quota for the Eon Bar
description:
## Outcome and routed contract

Create the source half of `EON-C22 — Trustworthy Codex quota in the Eon Bar` after the native Eon Bar is proved.

Consumer: one installed full-Eon user who already has a compatible authenticated `codex` executable on the inherited user `PATH`.

Trigger: full Eon starts with that compatible provider available, then the bounded provider refresh becomes due.

Result: one Eon-owned Codex provider adapter talks only to Codex's stable app-server JSON-RPC surface, reads `account/rateLimits/read`, selects the current Codex rate-limit bucket, and normalizes at most the primary and secondary windows into an optional typed EONW snapshot field. Each window carries duration, remaining percentage, reset time when supplied, observation time, and explicit freshness. Backend `ordinaryUsageAllowed = false` becomes an explicit blocked state; null never becomes inferred recovery. No credential, transcript, token-history, plan, credit, account identifier, upsell, or provider-private payload crosses EONW.

Important failures: missing or incompatible Codex, no authenticated account, malformed or oversized JSON-RPC, changed account, timeout, EOF, provider crash, network loss, out-of-order response, absent bucket, invalid percentage/time, or Eon shutdown leaves the quota absent or explicitly stale, never guessed, and never delays product startup, workspace actions, terminal attachment, or shutdown.

Impact: HIGH from direct user dogfood (“I do miss the quota widget quite a bit”). Effort: M. Risk: MEDIUM at the provider/auth/process boundary. Confidence: HIGH in the selected source boundary; MEDIUM in its exact lifecycle until the pinned implementation gate.

## Evidence

- `crates/eon-workspace-protocol/src/v5.rs:92-98` has one complete workspace `Snapshot` and no provider facts; a truthful native projection needs an explicit versioned owner boundary.
- `crates/eon/src/workspace.rs:173-221` is the single Eon snapshot constructor. `../eon-desktop/src/transport.rs:214-333` already polls complete EONW snapshots, so Venus does not need a provider poller or event bus.
- `crates/eon/src/managed_environment.rs:512-589` already discovers user-installed agent executables on Eon's inherited Session/user path without making them product components.
- Installed Codex CLI `0.154.0` (`codex app-server generate-json-schema`) exposes non-experimental `account/rateLimits/read`, `GetAccountRateLimitsResponse`, `RateLimitSnapshot`, `RateLimitWindow`, `accountId`, `ordinaryUsageAllowed`, and sparse `account/rateLimits/updated` notifications. The read request can exclude reset-credit details and decline Luna Reserve support.
- Nova Bar exact source `bfbf8a7be28b69f9d822c0843bf2dd5066dd49e3` demonstrates the value of one-minute official quota refresh, explicit stale output, reset-aware retention, and bounded backoff, but obtains data through `tokenusage` and a command-widget/cache layer that Eon must not copy.
- `eon-deliver-native-eon-bar-w4d` owns the prerequisite product surface. This bead owns facts only; `eon-desktop:ven-render-codex-quota-eon-bar-wfe` will own native presentation after this source is accepted.

## Prerequisites and reference gate

Hard prerequisite: `eon-deliver-native-eon-bar-w4d` is closed with exact EON-C21/VEN-C21 proof. No other Eon/Orbit/Venus implementation frontier is active unless the user explicitly changes it.

Before code:
- Regenerate the stable schema from the exact selected Codex release and inspect its source, release identity, license, initialization, shutdown, account switching, response ordering, size limits, `account/rateLimits/read`, and notification behavior. Record whether Eon consumes a user-installed executable or must ask the user to approve a pinned product tool; do not silently add Codex to the component graph.
- Compare a dedicated bounded `codex app-server --stdio` child using standard process/I/O plus the workspace's already locked `serde_json`, the Codex daemon/proxy, Nova's `tokenusage` mechanism, direct HTTP, and no feature. Prefer the dedicated official app-server child if the exact gate confirms it: it owns auth and account semantics without Eon reading tokens or adding a generic service.
- Request no reset-credit details, advertise no Luna Reserve support, and perform no provider mutation. Treat notifications as hints to refetch; do not merge sparse values into a second semantic owner.
- Record EON-C22 as Candidate and seed the smallest EONW v6 typed field before implementation. Preserve explicit v5 incompatibility rather than adding a compatibility window.

## Scope

In scope:
- One optional, fail-closed Codex quota provider adapter owned by Eon's existing supervisor lifecycle.
- Exact JSON-RPC initialization, bounded framing/queues/timeouts, one in-flight read, one-minute-or-slower refresh, failure backoff, child cleanup, account-change invalidation, and in-memory-only last-good state.
- Eon-owned normalization of the selected Codex bucket into at most two bounded windows, explicit fresh/stale/blocked/unknown state, and an optional EONW v6 snapshot field.
- The smallest source/configuration-free default: try the existing authenticated `codex` when available; otherwise publish no quota. No widget registry or order setting.
- EON-C22 Candidate text, EONW codec/failure tests, provider-substitute integration checks, current docs/changelog/LOC alignment, and affected Rust/Nix proof.

Out of scope:
- Venus rendering, bar geometry, installed visual acceptance, attention/sidebar state, other providers, token counts, cost estimates, credit purchase/reset actions, provider login/logout, account selection, or provider configuration UI.
- Reading Codex auth/config/history files, direct undocumented HTTP, terminal/process/screen inference, `tokenusage`, Nova Bar code, persistent disk caches, arbitrary command widgets, generic provider/event/status frameworks, plugins, or a second row.
- Bundling Codex, adding a daemon, changing Orbit, macOS support/proof, remote accounts, or any provider compatibility claim beyond the exact accepted evidence.

## Implementation notes

1. Add the bounded optional quota data to the canonical EONW snapshot and validator first. Carry only presentation-safe normalized facts; never carry raw JSON or `accountId`.
2. Resolve `codex` through the existing inherited executable path. Start at most one dedicated child, complete the required app-server initialization, continuously drain bounded JSON-RPC messages, and match replies by request id.
3. Read at startup and no faster than once per minute. On an update notification, schedule a normal refetch rather than interpreting sparse provider state. Use bounded exponential or fixed backoff after failure and never overlap reads.
4. Keep last-good facts only in memory. A failed refresh marks them stale immediately; each window expires no later than its provider reset time. A changed private account identity discards all prior facts before publishing another snapshot.
5. Prefer no new crate. If direct JSON parsing is required, evaluate a direct use of the exact `serde_json` already locked in the workspace against handwritten parsing; do not add a JSON-RPC framework for this one method.
6. Protect one codec boundary and one provider-substitute lifecycle test covering fresh, stale, blocked/unknown, account change, malformed/oversized input, crash/backoff, and clean shutdown.

## Acceptance criteria

- A compatible authenticated Codex yields an optional EONW v6 quota snapshot containing at most two normalized windows with 0–100 remaining percentage, duration, provider reset when present, observation time, and explicit freshness; the current account id and raw provider fields never cross the boundary.
- `ordinaryUsageAllowed = false` publishes blocked. Null or absent permission remains unknown; Eon never derives availability from percentages or reset time.
- Eon requests `excludeResetCreditDetails = true`, does not advertise Luna Reserve support, and performs no provider mutation, login, logout, credit, or account-selection action.
- Missing executable, unauthenticated account, unsupported schema, malformed/oversized response, timeout, provider crash, network loss, and absent quota keep full Eon usable and quota absent or stale with bounded retry work.
- Refresh is no faster than once per minute, only one read is in flight, notifications trigger refetch rather than duplicate interpretation, and failure backoff prevents a hot loop.
- Last-good values are process-memory-only, become stale on the first failed refresh, expire by their provider reset, and are discarded immediately when the private account identity changes or Eon restarts.
- No auth token, account id, plan, balance, credit/reset detail, upsell, transcript, token count, command output, or raw JSON appears in EONW, logs, diagnostics, cache/state files, or documentation.
- EONW v6 bounds and validates every new field, rejects invalid percentages/times/counts/trailing bytes, and remains explicitly incompatible with v5; Orbit protocols and terminal authority are unchanged.
- Focused red/green protocol and provider-substitute checks plus complete affected locked Rust/Nix checks, README LOC, and `git diff --check` pass on one unchanged candidate.
- EON-C22 remains Candidate until the exact Venus child and installed full-Eon delivery are accepted.

## Stop conditions

- Stop if the selected exact Codex release lacks a stable machine-readable rate-limit read or requires Eon to read credentials, use undocumented HTTP, scrape terminal/history, or mutate provider state.
- Stop for explicit user choice before adding Codex, `tokenusage`, a daemon, a new runtime crate/tool, persistent cache, provider login UI, another provider, or a general widget/provider framework.
- Stop if safe integration requires copying the Codex protocol/schema wholesale, publishing account identity, or making provider availability a product-startup dependency.
- Stop while another implementation frontier is active and before Venus/UI or platform-support work.

## Maintenance notes

This first slice is deliberately Codex-only and conditionally present by default. It creates neither a general widget configuration surface nor a multi-provider promise. A disable/order setting is deferred until at least two proved first-party fact chips create real configuration pressure.
close_reason: Ninth fresh-eyes pass corrected overbroad privacy and lifecycle claims; implementation remained unchanged.

comments.text:
Reference gate and code-shape decision — 2026-09-17

Exact provider evidence: installed codex-cli 0.154.0 resolves to the standalone x86_64 Linux binary; stable schema generation and a redacted live stdio probe confirm account/rateLimits/read without experimental opt-in. Exact Apache-2.0 source is rust-v0.154.0 at 6b9826e3aa83b1a5947db50f4332cb9c65f1b340. The source defines newline-delimited requests, initialization before reads, account/rateLimits/updated as a refetch hint, account/updated as an identity invalidation hint, private accountId, nullable ordinaryUsageAllowed, codex bucket selection with historical fallback, and primary/secondary windows. Official developer documentation describes app-server generally but does not publish this method schema, so the exact release schema and source—not memory or docs inference—govern this candidate.

Adopted: seed explicit incompatible EONW v6, then run one dedicated user-installed codex app-server --stdio child from inherited PATH inside the Eon supervisor lifecycle. Use standard process/thread/I/O primitives and direct serde_json 1.0.150 already locked by the workspace. Request excludeResetCreditDetails=true and supportsLunaReserve=false; refetch notifications rather than merging them; keep private identity only for invalidation; publish only bounded normalized facts. This mirrors the established v5 source-candidate sequence: current installed v5 stays untouched while Venus consumes the exact v6 source, then final Eon delivery activates the accepted pair.

Rejected: Codex daemon/proxy adds shared lifecycle and state; Nova tokenusage and direct HTTP require a second auth/private-contract owner; handwritten JSON parsing is less correct than the already-locked parser; no feature contradicts the selected high-value outcome. No bundled Codex, provider framework, configuration, cache, or compatibility window is introduced. Eon will bound line size and work because upstream stdio reading has no line-size limit, fail closed on auth/schema/process errors, close stdin then bounded-wait/kill on shutdown, and never log provider payloads.

title: Specify Helix-like modal editing semantics for an Eon editor
description:
## Contract Routing

This is a planning and research decision. It changes no EON product contract and implements no editor behavior. EON-C4 continues to preserve Helix as the sole owner of editing and language integration. If `eon-ofb` later selects an Eon-native editor, that owner must receive an explicitly approved indexed contract before code.

## Why

The user requires any eventual Eon editor engine to retain Helix-like modal editing regardless of whether it reuses `helix-core`. The modal model is behavior, not a crate choice: normal, select, and insert modes; selection-first operations; multiple selections; command composition; and undo grouping must be specified independently from rendering and physical key assignments. Without this contract, a native editor could reuse Helix data structures while losing the editing model users actually rely on.

## Evidence

- `docs/ARCHITECTURE.md:16` assigns editing, language integration, and editor state to Helix; `docs/ARCHITECTURE.md:69` forbids Eon from duplicating editor behavior under the current contract.
- Official Helix revision `079a789e8cb08ead67f19e1971a1b7438b37354b`, `docs/architecture.md`: `helix-core` supplies functional Rope, Selection, and Transaction primitives, while Document, History, editor lifecycle, and commands live above core.
- The same revision, `helix-core/src/selection.rs` and `helix-core/src/transaction.rs`: multiple selections and invertible transactions are core primitives.
- The same revision, `helix-term/src/keymap/default.rs`: Normal, Select, and Insert are distinct modes, with Select derived from Normal through extension semantics.
- The same revision, `helix-term/src/commands.rs`: user-visible command semantics and undo checkpoints are substantially implemented in the terminal frontend rather than supplied by `helix-core` alone.
- CodeMirror 6 System Guide, https://codemirror.net/docs/guide/, is comparison evidence for an immutable transaction core and derived editor state; it is not a modal-compatibility source.

## Scope

In scope:
- Define the editor-owned modes and transitions required for a Helix-like mental model.
- Define selection-first cursor/range semantics, multiple selections, motion versus extension, operator application, transaction and undo grouping, registers, yank/paste, search/find, text objects, repeat, macros, shell filters, and language-aware command disposition.
- Classify each behavior as required in the first editing proof, required before Helix replacement, or explicitly deferred.
- Assign each accepted behavior to the future editor owner, Venus, Eon workspace policy, or an external language/tool process without duplicate authority.
- Define a deterministic behavioral corpus: initial text, selections and mode plus semantic command sequence produce exact final text, selections, mode, and undo boundaries.

Out of scope:
- Choosing `helix-core`, copying or adapting Helix code, creating a repository, adding dependencies, or implementing an editor.
- Physical key assignments; the separate keybinding-continuity decision owns those after this semantic vocabulary is stable.
- Venus rendering, Eon workspace shortcuts, user keymap configuration syntax, Helix plugin or Steel compatibility, terminal emulation, CRDTs, multiplayer, remote access, or cloud persistence.
- Promising complete Helix feature parity; unsupported behavior must be explicit rather than silently reinterpreted.

## Decision Work

1. Inspect the exact accepted Helix revision required by `eon-ofb`, including the complete default command inventory and the state each command reads or mutates.
2. Produce a semantic command matrix grouped by navigation, selection, transformation, insertion, history, search, registers, macros, shell/tool interaction, language intelligence, views, and application UI.
3. Separate the core modal contract from Helix terminal-frontend and widget behavior.
4. Define the minimum behavioral corpus and how an independent implementation can compare observable results against the pinned Helix reference without sharing editor authority.
5. Record the owned-LOC and maintenance consequences for reusing `helix-core`, using an upstream semantic boundary, and implementing the accepted primitives independently.
6. Obtain an explicit user decision on the required-before-replacement and deferred sets. Do not implement during this Bead.

## Acceptance

- Normal, Select, and Insert modes and every accepted transition have one editor owner and deterministic failure behavior.
- Selection-first and multiple-selection semantics are explicit, including head/anchor direction, overlapping range normalization, empty selections, and mapping selections through transactions.
- The record defines transaction and undo boundaries for insertion, command sequences, repeat, macros, formatter or LSP edits, and rejected or stale external edits.

title: Draw the working badge as Nova's braille dots at 10 Hz, with a setting to keep it still
description:
## Problem

Lucca, 2026-10-27: "i dont like our spinner too much / because of the fps. it ticks too slowly".
Venus's working badge (VEN-C21 "Attention badges"; also the agent sidebar's working row) is a
270° arc with 8 phases (venus/src/render/chrome.rs `SPINNER_PHASES`, `push_arc`) turned every
200 ms (venus/src/application.rs `SPINNER_INTERVAL`): 45° steps, 1.6 s per turn, which reads as
choppy. VEN-C21 caps it at 5 Hz.

## Decision (approved)

Approved by Lucca 2026-10-27, relayed by eon-overseer. Asked: "1. Style: braille dots, like Nova
(⠋⠙⠹⠸⠼⠴⠦⠧⠇⠏, nova-zj-radar crates/core/src/status.rs), drawn as 8 small dots. 2. Speed: 10 per
second (100 ms per frame, one second per cycle); changes VEN-C21's 'at most five times a second'.
3. Settings: one option to turn the animation off (accessibility); style and rate stay fixed.
4. One small Venus bead, after orb-j2i.11 lands." Lucca: "ok".

- Style: the 10-frame braille "dots" sequence ⠋⠙⠹⠸⠼⠴⠦⠧⠇⠏, drawn by Venus as dots in a 2x4 cell
  grid (rectangle quads, as the arc is now; no font dependency), in ATTENTION_WORKING.
- Rate: 100 ms per frame (10 Hz), only the badge repaints, only while shown, as today.
- Software (CPU) adapters keep a still badge that never repaints (a fixed dots frame instead of the
  still arc), as VEN-C21 requires now.
- One configuration value turns the animation off (a still badge on every adapter). Eon Runtime
  parses it and sends the resolved value; Venus parses no configuration. Default: animated.
  Document it in docs/CONFIGURATION.md. Style and rate stay fixed; record that reason (support cost
  of several styles; the dots match Nova, Claude Code and Codex titles) on this bead.

## Contract

VEN-C21 "Attention badges": the working-badge clause changes from "a still open arc ... the arc
turns, repainting at no more than 5 Hz under AP-PERF-001" to braille dots turning at no more than
10 Hz, still on software adapters or when the setting turns animation off. Record the exact adopted
text on this bead. The setting crosses EONW (Runtime to Venus): if it needs a wire field, that is
an EONW version bump (memory: never amend EONW in place); keep it inside this bead only if small,
otherwise stop and ask. Any other contract change needs Lucca's approval.

## Prerequisites

- Start after orb-j2i.11 lands (both touch venus/src/render).
- Read VEN-C21, venus/AGENTS.md, AP-PERF-001, docs/CONFIGURATION.md.

## Acceptance

- Replace `spinner_phases_rewrite_only_alpha_in_place` and
  `spinner_turns_at_most_five_times_a_second_and_only_while_shown` with their dots / 10 Hz
  equivalents; keep `software_adapters_draw_working_badges_still_and_never_tick` and add the
  setting-off case.
- AP-PERF-001: measure Venus CPU over 20 s with and without a working badge on the GPU adapter, as
  VEN-C21's proof did (11 ticks of 10 ms at 5 Hz); record the numbers.
- One isolated installed observation (headless Sway on the Intel GPU): captures 100 ms apart show
  successive dots frames; with the setting off, identical captures.
- CHANGELOG.md, venus/CHANGELOG.md and docs/CONFIGURATION.md updated.
- Review per AGENTS.md (converge plus Codex); cargo fmt and clippy for yazelix-venus.

## Scope boundary

Only the working badge's glyph, rate and the animation toggle. Not: the other badge glyphs, the
Finished-versus-Working rule (eon-eon-attention-working-hides-finish-7df0), sidebar layout.

Adopted VEN-C21 text (venus/docs/CONTRACTS.md, Attention badges):


title: Compare readable working-badge spinners at real size
close_reason: Research done: Lucca picked C2 (an antialiased 270° arc) and approved the VEN-C21 wording, both relayed by eon-overseer on 2026-10-23. The eon-overseer files the implementation bead.

comments.author: lucca
comments.text:
Research result (eon-fd, 2026-10-23). Research only: nothing changed on edge except this bead.

Method: a throwaway local harness, not committed, at
~/.cache/eon-agents/eon-fd/harness/spinners.py. It ports Venus's badge drawing from edge 8a25211:
push_badge, push_badge_glyph, and RectangleBatch push/push_quad/push_rounded/push_span. It keeps
Venus's rasterization: one sample per pixel (MultisampleState::default), so a pixel is lit when its
centre is inside, and alpha blending in linear light on the sRGB target. Geometry uses the default
metrics: font 16, cell height 18, padding 12. That gives a 12 px badge with a 10 px glyph at scale 1,
and 24 px with 20 px at scale 2, in both the tab corner and the sidebar row. Shape candidates are
drawn the way Venus draws other badges: quads, plus 1x1 coverage quads for antialiasing, which is the
same technique as push_span. Braille is text in DejaVu Sans, a font Venus ships (DejaVu Sans Mono
has no braille). The harness approximates the real renderer: text uses FreeType through Pillow, not
glyphon/swash. It is not an installed capture.

Venus has no light theme: chrome is dark and fixed. "Light" therefore means the sidebar card at Eon's
default 0.80 opacity over a white desktop, the only place a light backdrop shows through. There,
every badge and the row text lose contrast equally. That comes from the card's opacity, not from
any candidate, and it doesn't change the ranking.

Images in ~/.cache/eon-agents/eon-fd/spinner/:
- contact-sheet.png: every candidate at real size. For each: the scale-1 tab strip, the scale-1
  sidebar dark and light, the same at scale 2, and zoomed frame strips at x8 and x4 with the still
  form first.
- contact-sheet-x3.png: the scale-1 tab strip and sidebar row, x3, one row per candidate.
- compare.gif: all candidates animating together at 5 Hz, at real size, x2 and scale 2.
- <key>/: per-candidate stills (tab-s{1,2}-still.png, sidebar-s{1,2}-{dark,light}-still.png),
  GIFs (tab-s{1,2}.gif, sidebar-s{1,2}-dark.gif) and frames-s{1,2}-zoomed.png.

Why today's spinner is hard to read: the 8 segments are aliased quads. At a 10 px glyph each one
rasterizes to a 1-2 px blob, so the ring reads as a gear or a dotted circle. The trail fades by 0.11
alpha per segment, which is too faint to show direction at that size. A2, the same ring
antialiased, is smoother but still a blurry donut at scale 1.

Candidates against the constraints (frozen = reads as working when still; distinct = differs from
idle ring, ◆ ✕ ✓; Claude = doesn't look like Claude's ◐ title spinner; cost = ≤5 Hz, badge only;
s1 = legible at scale 1):
- A, today's ring: frozen weak (a gear), distinct yes, Claude yes, cost yes, s1 poor.
- A2, the same ring antialiased: frozen weak (a donut), distinct borderline (close to the idle ring
  in shape), Claude yes, cost yes, s1 fair.
- B, braille ⠋⠙⠹ (still ⣿): frozen poor (⣿ is a dot block), distinct yes, Claude yes (it's Codex's
  look instead). Cost is a problem: a font glyph lives in the text layer, so each turn
  re-prepares text, which breaks today's vertex-only rewrite. s1 poor: the dots are 1 px and the
  glyph is half the badge wide.
- C1, a 120° arc on a faint track: frozen weak (a ring with a dark patch), distinct borderline
  (the track reads as the idle ring), Claude yes, cost yes, s1 fair.
- C2, a 270° arc with no track (still: the same arc): frozen good (it's the universal loading
  glyph), distinct yes (an open blue arc vs a closed thin grey ring, ◆ ✕ ✓), Claude yes, cost yes,
  s1 good.
- D, half-circles ◐◓◑◒ (still ◐): frozen fair, distinct yes, Claude no (it's Claude's own title
  spinner, side by side in rows that show the Claude splat), cost yes, s1 good.
- E, a pulsing dot: frozen poor (a plain dot, which reads as status, not progress; close to the
  unavailable dot), distinct borderline, Claude yes, cost yes, s1 good.
- F (extra), a dot orbiting a faint track: frozen fair, distinct borderline, Claude yes, cost yes,
  s1 poor (it smears at 10 px).

Recommendation: C2, an antialiased 270° arc with no track, turning in 8 steps of 45° at 5 Hz (1.6 s
a turn); on CPU adapters the still arc. Reasons:
1. It's the only candidate that reads as "working" when frozen, which the CPU-adapter still badge
   needs.
2. At scale 1 it stays a clean C. Its open gap shows rotation even at 5 Hz.
3. Blue, open and thick, it can't be confused with the thin grey closed idle ring or with ◆ ✕ ✓.
4. It doesn't echo Claude's ◐ or Codex's braille, so Eon's badge stays distinct from the agents'
   own titles.
5. It keeps today's cost model. Each phase emits the same fixed grid of 1x1 coverage quads over the
   glyph box: 100 at scale 1, 400 at scale 2, with zero-alpha pixels kept so the length never
   changes. Only alpha changes, so spinner_phases_rewrite_only_alpha_in_place and the 5 Hz,
   badge-only tick still hold. Per tick that is about 600 to 2400 vertices per badge instead of
   48. The implementation bead should measure it against the yx8.2 baseline.

VEN-C21 wording draft (for Lucca's approval, landed only with the implementation):
- current: "on a software (CPU) graphics adapter the working badge is a still segmented ring that
  never repaints to animate; otherwise its spinner turns, repainting at no more than 5 Hz under
  AP-PERF-001, and only the badge;"
- proposed: "on a software (CPU) graphics adapter the working badge is a still open arc that never
  repaints to animate; otherwise the arc turns, repainting at no more than 5 Hz under AP-PERF-001,
  and only the badge;"
The other mentions ("corner badge (◆, ✕, ✓, or a spinner)", the EON-C31 proof text) stay as they
are. Existing proof records keep their wording.

Decision (relayed by eon-overseer, 2026-10-23): Lucca picked C2. The overseer asked him "1. Pick
C2, the antialiased 270° arc whose frozen form is the same arc", and he replied "1. approve". The
VEN-C21 wording approval is pending until Lucca confirms the exact text above. The eon-overseer
files the implementation bead, which lands the arc in chrome.rs push_badge_glyph together with the
VEN-C21 edit and installed dogfood.

title: Add split support to Eon workspaces
description:
## Decision
Lucca, 2026-10-15: Eon will support splits, so a user can see more than one terminal at once. The
design is not chosen yet. This bead first produces a design for Lucca to approve, then implements it.

## Contract (provisional)
A full-Eon user can view and use more than one pane's terminal at the same time in a workspace,
create and close that arrangement with the keyboard, and move focus between the visible panes.
Terminals stay persistent and independent; detach and reattach preserve the arrangement the design
chooses to persist. The exact shape, persistence and controls are open decisions below.

## Open design decisions
- Shape: arbitrary split tree, fixed layouts, side-by-side expanded panes inside the existing
accordion, or another model. How splits relate to tabs, the accordion stack and pane frames.
- Controls: creating, closing, resizing, focusing and moving splits; which shortcuts, without
breaking existing Alt/Ctrl+Alt bindings.
- Persistence: whether the arrangement survives detach/attach, profile refresh and same-boot
recovery (EON-C15).
- Resize: how each visible terminal's grid is sized and when Orbit receives resizes.
- Accessibility: how the visible panes appear to screen readers and keyboard focus.
- Scope of the first slice and what stays out (for example, popups inside splits).

## Current boundary this changes
Splits contradict accepted contracts and directory rules, so each needs Lucca's approval before it
changes:
- `docs/CONTRACTS.md` EON-C8: "exactly one pane is expanded" and the Boundary excluding arbitrary
split trees and simultaneous expanded panes.
- `venus/docs/CONTRACTS.md` (pane accordion around exactly one expanded pane) and
`venus/docs/PRESENTATION.md` (excludes split trees and simultaneous expanded panes).
- `venus/AGENTS.md`: arbitrary split trees and simultaneous expanded panes are outside Venus. Change
its `.agent-protocols.local.md` and re-render; do not edit the generated file.

## Owners
Eon owns product defaults and the shortcut/configuration policy. Eon Runtime owns workspace state,
the arrangement model and its EONW representation (likely a new EONW revision; historical revisions
stay unchanged). Venus owns geometry, rendering, input, focus and accessibility for several visible
Orbit surfaces. Orbit keeps one terminal per session with one attachment; any Orbit change is a
separate `orbit-protocol` decision with its consumers named.

## Prerequisites and reference gate
No unmet dependency. This is consequential (contract, wire protocol and Venus scope changes). Before
implementation, read the affected `AGENTS.md`, contracts and `docs/REFERENCES.md` routes, and inspect
at least two comparable implementations at exact revisions (for example Zellij, tmux, WezTerm or
Ghostty splits). Record inspected revisions, constraints kept, rejected approaches, the chosen design
and its cheapest falsifying check here. Stop for Lucca's design and contract approval before code.

## Acceptance
- Design phase: Lucca approves a recorded design, the contract changes and the first slice.
- Implementation: installed Eon shows several terminals at once per the approved design; keyboard
create/close/focus work; terminals keep running across detach and reattach; existing tab, pane and
popup behavior still works. Prove with the owners' existing harnesses plus one isolated installed
dogfood observation, then refresh the active Nix profile without interrupting live workspaces.

## Stop boundary
No implementation, contract edit, EONW revision or Orbit protocol change before the design is
approved. Adds no platform promise.
close_reason: Columns of accordions shipped and dogfooded: up to four live side-by-side columns per tab, Alt+Shift+M with Venus width refusal and Eon capacity refusal, column/tab traversal, click selection, per-column resize, persistence across detach/attach. Proof and ledgers in comments.

comments.author: lucca
comments.text:
Design input (Lucca 2026-10-16, after eon-venus-modules-oagt): Venus is structured around one attached Orbit terminal per window, and splits must change that first.
Evidence at edge 0fd606c: Application (venus/src/application.rs) has 57 fields; about 20 are singleton state for the one attached terminal: transport, model, presentation, active_endpoint/active_endpoint_live, orbit_retry, retry_suppressed, last_resize, deferred_selection, selection_gate, links/link_opener, terminal_scroll, selection_scroll, pending_viewport, pending_return_to_live, scrollback_press. set_orbit_attachment (application.rs:1090) clears and re-attaches all of it on every pane or popup switch. Renderer (venus/src/render.rs) has 40 fields mixing window/GPU state with one terminal's draw state: content_key, text, cursor_animation/cursor_handoff/last_cursor_frame, hyperlink, scrollback_label/rect. Largest bodies: window_event 493 lines (pointer arms), handle_transport 221, Renderer::build_workspace 337, rebuild_if_needed 288.
Decision: after the split design is approved, the first implementation slice is a behavior-preserving extraction of per-terminal state (a TerminalView in Application, a per-terminal draw layer in Renderer) with one instance, proved by the existing Venus suites; later slices add more instances. Do not extract before the design: which state is per-terminal vs per-window depends on design choices (whether unfocused splits stay live, whether scroll/selection/links are per pane, focus model). Rejected: splitting impl Application/Renderer into per-concern impl files now (navigation only; every file still touches the same fields, and splits reshape those methods).

comments.author: lucca
comments.text:
Reference gate and design proposal (2026-10-16, awaiting Lucca's approval; no code).
Question: how should full Eon show several terminals at once without a second terminal or layout owner?
Contract (proposed): a tab is an ordered row of 1..=4 columns; each column is today's accordion (ordered panes, exactly one expanded). Every column's expanded pane is a live, visible, independently sized terminal. One column is focused; its expanded pane receives keyboard input. A one-column tab behaves exactly as EON-C8 today.
Sources and revisions (inspection only, nothing copied): Zellij v0.45.1 efd8fd5a (MIT); tmux 3.8 7f2a35ad (ISC); WezTerm 20240203-110809-5046fc22 5046fc22 (MIT); Ghostty v1.3.1 332b2aef (MIT); Rio/Canario 3e41b8b1 (MIT, REFERENCES.md route).
Findings that shape the design: Zellij's default stack-list mode is Eon's accordion placed inside a split layout (hidden members keep the expanded member's size, so switching costs no resize). Canario uses a fixed two-level grid (columns of panels), not a tree. tmux/WezTerm/Ghostty use id-keyed split trees with one top-down size owner; WezTerm's client-computed sizes reconciled on the server is a two-owner anti-pattern. All coalesce or debounce PTY resizes; Zellij documents shells mishandling resize bursts. Directional focus: edge-touching and overlapping candidates, tie broken by most recent focus. Zellij Alt+h/l moves focus across panes and falls through to tabs at the edge.
Constraints preserved: Orbit keeps one terminal per session and one attachment; N visible terminals are N ordinary attachments to N sessions (no ORB change). Runtime owns topology/focus/EONW; Venus owns geometry, sizing, input, accessibility; Eon owns defaults.
Options compared: (A) columns of accordions [proposed]; (B) split tree with accordion leaves (Zellij-like, most general); (C) split tree of single panes with the accordion as a zoom view (Ghostty-like; discards the accordion).
Proposed decisions: columns only, equal widths, max 4, refuse below a minimum column width; Alt+Shift+M opens a new column to the right of the focused one with a new pane in the tab directory; Alt+M still adds a pane to the focused column; Alt+H/L move focus between columns and fall through to tabs at the outer edges; Alt+K/J traverse the focused column's accordion; Ctrl+Alt+H/L keep moving tabs; closing a column's last pane removes the column (focus: following column, else preceding); popups stay tab-wide overlays; focused column shown by the existing frame/selection treatment, no dimming; arrangement lives in runtime topology so it survives detach/attach; EON-C15 same-boot recovery still projects into one column of synthetic t1.
Out of first cut: column resize, moving panes between columns, nested/vertical splits, zoom, popups inside columns, restoring arrangement after supervisor loss.
Contract changes needing approval: EON-C8 (one expanded pane per column; boundary drops 'simultaneous expanded panes', keeps 'no arbitrary split tree'), VEN-C8, venus/docs/PRESENTATION.md, venus/AGENTS.md via .agent-protocols.local.md + re-render, a new EONW revision (v10: Tab carries columns), CHANGELOG at delivery.
Slices: (1) Venus per-terminal state extraction, one instance, no behavior change; (2) EONW v10 + runtime column model and actions; (3) Venus N attachments and column layout; (4) installed dogfood and profile refresh.
Cheapest falsifying checks: runtime test that adding then closing a column returns the exact one-column snapshot; Venus headless test that two columns yield two terminal rects with independent grids and one resize each; installed dogfood showing two live terminals side by side updating.

comments.author: lucca
comments.text: Slice 2 decisions (2026-10-16): (a) CreateColumn is a variant of the top-level v10::Action (request tag 22), not of WorkspaceAction: WorkspaceAction is v3::Action re-exported unchanged through v9, so adding a variant there would change the historical v3-v9 types the approval keeps unchanged. Behavior and wire meaning are as approved. (b) Left/right entry column, reasoned from first principles at Lucca's request: Alt+H/L is spatial, so the visible columns of all tabs form one strip and crossing into a tab enters at its nearest edge column (rightmost moving left, leftmost moving right); this makes right-then-left reversible, lets one direction reach every column, and depends only on what is visible; Zellij efd8fd5a does the same (focus_pane_on_edge, screen.rs:2103). Tab focus by position or id keeps the last selected column. One tab wraps between its columns. (c) In a tab without columns, CreateColumn acts exactly as CreatePane (Codex finding: otherwise dismissing a transient popup can remove the tab and give a neighbor a fifth column). (d) The component graph's EONW entries stay at 9 in this commit; slice 3 bumps them to 10 citing this slice's commit as producer and consumer proof, per docs/ARCHITECTURE.md (graph changes after the consumer proof) and the no-self-naming commit rule. comments.author: lucca
comments.text: Slice 3b decisions (2026-10-17, live columns; no key binding yet, so users still cannot create columns): (a) Application keeps the selected column's TerminalView as Application.terminal plus column_views, one display-only TerminalView per other visible column's live expanded pane (WorkspaceModel::column_attachments; none while a popup covers the tab). (b) PresentationState and LinkInteraction move from TerminalView to Application: one renderer presents one frame, so the generation is window-wide; column output calls content_changed, swaps and column-set changes invalidate. (c) Moving selection to a visible column swaps views without reconnecting; the outgoing view stays attached as a column view unless Orbit still owes it a viewport response (pending_viewport), in which case it reattaches fresh; only a view with a live transport is swapped in, a lost one gets a fresh attachment as a pane switch did. Before a kept swap Venus cancels any server selection gesture on it; retire_orbit_generation sends it Focus(Lost); the incoming attached view gets the latest focus. (d) A column view sends Focus(Lost) after attaching and is resized to its own column rect (send_resize covers every column); background handling applies frames, clipboard writes (honored; the notice stays on that terminal), losses and supervised Busy/retryable retries. (e) Venus notices stay per terminal (rejected moving them to the window: SessionModel clears them with each attachment's lifecycle, so a window owner would duplicate that lifecycle); status shows the selected column's. (f) Cursor trail only on the selected column; other columns draw a static cursor; each column strip takes its own terminal's default background (DEFAULT_BACKGROUND while unattached). (g) Pointer: a left press on another column's terminal area (new WorkspaceHit::ColumnTerminal) sends FocusId and focuses the terminal; the click is not forwarded. The wheel over another column's terminal or headers does nothing (deferred: scrolling an unfocused column needs per-view scroll handling). (h) Metadata observers wait for every unattached view's endpoint, as for the selected pane. Accepted gaps for 3c/4: other columns' terminal text is not exposed to accessibility; a column's scrollback position shows without its pill; window shrink below the minimum grid (3c); per-column rebuild cost is unmeasured.

comments.author: lucca
comments.text: Slice 3c decisions (2026-10-17, delivery): (a) Alt+Shift+M maps to v10 Action::CreateColumn; workspace_shortcut now returns the top-level v10 Action because CreateColumn is not a v3 WorkspaceAction. It is non-repeating like the other structural shortcuts. (b) 40-column minimum: before sending, Venus computes the narrowest column (scene-owned workspace_column_width, floor(window width / (columns + 1)), the same formula the layout uses) and refuses when its surface grid would be under MIN_COLUMN_CELLS = 40. The refusal is a WorkspaceModel Action notice (new reject_action), with the same lifetime and announcement as an Eon rejection: kept across unchanged polls, cleared by a workspace change. A tab without columns always fits; Eon still refuses a fifth column. (c) Window shrink below the minimum (3a carry-over): the minimum applies only when a column is created; shrinking the window narrows existing columns and removes none (recorded in VEN-C8).
