title: Stop a sub-row wheel step from drawing a stale history row over live output
description:
## Problem

Seen in both base Venus (Lucca's profile package /nix/store/dkdls8mz83nscb6flyc7184d69lk4v05-eon-0.1.3, built 2026-10-27 02:00 -03 from the main checkout) and the eon-scroll-preview-per-frame-hhzy candidate, in an isolated headless Sway (pixman, 1600x900, wdotool wlr-protocols wheel). While a program prints a continuous burst, `wdotool scroll 0 -3` over the terminal leaves the pane in a partial-row scroll state. The top edge shows part of an old history row ("burst line 6197"), taken from the first preview answer, above live rows that keep advancing (7709, then 10762, then 15749). The scroll never commits into history while output runs. When the burst ends, the pane is back at live output.

Likely mechanism, not yet verified: the wheel accumulates less than one row of pixels, so `next_request` never commits. The model keeps a compatible Viewport preview across frames (venus/src/model.rs, Frame arm), so `offset()` keeps drawing that old preview's rows above the newest frame.

Evidence: /home/lucca/.cache/eon-agents/hhzy-work/base1/{burst,up1,up2,up3,up4,back1,back2,live1,live2,done}.png (base) and /home/lucca/.cache/eon-agents/hhzy-work/obs2/ (candidate). Driver: /home/lucca/.cache/eon-agents/hhzy-work/run.sh with obs.sh and burst.sh beside it.

## Expected

A wheel step during output either moves into history and holds there, or leaves the view at live with no stale row drawn. Decide which by checking what wdotool's axis event delivers to Venus (LineDelta or PixelDelta, and its size), and how a one-click wheel behaves with no output.

## Contract

VEN-C7 (authoritative history and selection interaction). If the fix changes contract text, stop for Lucca's approval.

## Prerequisites

None. eon-scroll-preview-per-frame-hhzy touches the same module; land it first to avoid conflicts.

## Scope

In scope: Venus scroll preview offset and commit thresholds in venus/src/application/scroll.rs, plus preview retention in venus/src/model.rs. Out of scope: Orbit.

## Acceptance

- A Venus test reproducing the stale preview row drawn over a newer frame.
- One isolated installed observation with the run.sh driver: no stale row, and a wheel step during a burst behaves as decided above.

## Portability disposition

neutral.

comments.text:
Plan note (2026-10-27): this bead was taken up tonight under Lucca's change-of-plan pre-approval, relayed by the coordinator eon-overseer, because lane B's planned beads are done or waiting on orb-j2i.5. Lucca, 2026-10-26, to eon-overseer: "focus on finishing the worspace-switching beads, but try to advance on kitty-graphics too / everything is pre-approved. autonomous. / and sprinkle the ones the subagent listed that are important." and "also pre-aprove changes of plan if a clearly better alternative appears". It applied to taking up this bead. No contract text was adopted: the fix implements VEN-C7 as written.

Diagnosis (by source, before code):
- wdotool 0.5.3's wlr-protocols `scroll 0 -3` (wdotool-core/src/backend/wlr_protocols.rs, do_scroll) sends one zwlr_virtual_pointer_v1.axis of 3.0 with no axis_discrete and no source, then a frame. So Venus gets a PixelDelta of 3 logical pixels, which VEN-C7's precision rule presents as 6 pixels. That is a sub-row nudge, not a wheel click. A physical wheel sends discrete steps, which Venus maps to LineDelta at three rows per click, and those commit at once. With no output, the nudge holds a 6 px offset over a fresh preview, as VEN-C7 intends.
- During output, the model keeps a compatible Viewport preview across frames (venus/src/model.rs, Frame arm), as VEN-C7 requires: "Venus keeps only that bounded revision-bound preview until Orbit supplies its replacement instead of presenting the remainder as zero or freezing finger movement." But TerminalScroll::next_request (venus/src/application/scroll.rs) asks for a preview only when it holds none in the gesture's direction, so it never asks for that replacement. Base before eon-scroll-preview-per-frame-hhzy had the same branch. The first answer's rows ("burst line 6197") then stay drawn above every later frame.

Decision: a sub-row step at live during output keeps its offset (VEN-C7) and draws current history. When the retained preview names an older revision than the current frame and no row was crossed, next_request asks for one replacement PreviewVertical at the current revision, under hhzy's one-outstanding hold. A crossed row still commits first, because the scroll outcome carries the next preview. Residual: until the replacement arrives (one Orbit answer, normally the message right after the frame), the sub-row band shows the row that was above the previous frame. Two alternatives were rejected because each contradicts VEN-C7's text: committing an uncrossed row ("commits crossed rows"), and presenting the remainder as zero ("instead of presenting the remainder as zero").

Not consequential under AGENTS.md's definition: no dependency, protocol, contract, or lifecycle change. No Orbit change is needed. Configurability: no new value. Portability: neutral.

comments.text:
Decision revised after the first review round (a fresh Claude reviewer and Codex, on candidate tree 3b7d4caabb7c3b8bb9c5258be7893d663e3a6442). Both reported the same blocking finding. The one-outstanding hold limits concurrency, not rate: with a sub-row remainder held, every answered frame re-armed a replacement request. That happened both at live and while scrolled into pinned history, where the rows never change. The Claude reviewer also noted that it multiplied hhzy's accepted DEC 2026 residual (a retry under a held synchronized update fails with InvalidInput).

The replacement is now bounded in two ways:
- Gate: Venus asks for a replacement only while the accepted frame is at live (`rows_from_live == 0`, new `VenusModel::at_live` in venus/src/model.rs). VEN-C7: "after history entry, later output leaves the authoritative viewport pinned", so a preview retained in history still shows current rows.
- Pacing: at live, a replacement is sent at most once per PREVIEW_ANSWER_GRACE (50 ms), and it still goes through hhzy's one-outstanding hold. The pacing deadline (`replace_after`) joins `preview_retry_at`, which is already an event-loop deadline, so a stale preview left by the last frame of a burst is still replaced after output stops. When `retry_preview` reaches that deadline it clears it, so the loop does not spin.

So at live during output, with a held sub-row remainder, Venus sends at most about 20 previews per second. In history, and with no output, it sends none. The residual changes to: the sub-row band (less than one row tall) shows rows up to one grace plus one Orbit answer old, about 50 ms, while output runs at live. The DEC 2026 exposure is limited to that same paced state, which is rare: it needs an upward total of less than one row from live while output runs. That residual stays with eon-preview-answer-survives-frames-u979, which owns Orbit's queue.

Configurability: no new value. Pacing reuses PREVIEW_ANSWER_GRACE, which hhzy recorded as fixed internal request pacing within the ORB-C8 exchange.

Regression: sub_row_remainder_replaces_a_preview_older_than_the_frame (venus/src/application/scroll.rs) now covers no request in pinned history, one request through the hold at live, one request per grace across 19 answered frames 5 ms apart, the deadline request after output stops, and the deadline clearing. On base 827aeef it fails at the first live replacement: base returns None. title: Choose every new Eon tab directory before its first pane
description:
## Outcome

Every newly created full-Eon tab chooses its launch directory before Eon starts that tab's first durable pane.

Smallest observable contract:
- Consumer: a person starting a fresh full-Eon workspace or creating a tab with Ctrl+T.
- Trigger: Eon needs the first pane for a new tab.
- Result: Eon creates one active pending tab and one transient packaged Zoxide/fzf picker before any durable pane exists in that tab. Accepting a valid directory atomically commits the tab directory and starts exactly one normal pN Session there. The picker never becomes a pane.
- Important failures: cancelling the first workspace picker starts p1 at Eon's validated launch directory; cancelling a later new-tab picker abandons that pending tab and restores the prior tab and focus. Picker start, helper, selection, target, or presentation failure follows the same respective fallback without a partial tab, durable Session, or transient residue. Existing generations attach without an automatic picker.

Alt+Z remains available on a tab that already has panes and keeps its current retarget-only behavior. Eon never injects cd, restarts an existing pane, or changes a running process working directory.

Impact: HIGH in current dogfood. Effort: L across EONW, Eon Desktop, and Eon. Implementation risk: MEDIUM. Confidence: HIGH in the pending-tab shape.

## Approved interaction and geometry

User decision on 2026-08-26:
- Picker-first applies to the initial tab of a fresh workspace and every newly created tab.
- No shell or other durable pane starts behind the picker.
- The first-tab picker keeps t1 visible in the tab bar. A later pending tab is appended and active while its picker is open.
- Existing picker geometry remains: tab bar visible; picker is the only tab-body terminal; one-cell inset on every side when the grid permits it.
- Accept creates and focuses the first pane at the selected directory.
- First-tab cancel falls back to the validated Eon launch directory. Later-tab cancel removes the pending tab and restores the exact prior workspace focus.
- Attach, recovery, EonTerm, and existing-tab Alt+Z do not auto-open a picker.

## Ownership

- Eon owns pending-tab creation, fallback policy, exact picker command, target validation, first-pane startup, atomic commit, rollback, and cleanup.
- Venus owns pending-tab projection, tab-bar context, modal focus/input, geometry, rendering, notices, accessibility, and exact focus restoration.
- Orbit owns the transient picker PTY and each committed durable pane Session. No Orbit change is expected.
- Zoxide owns ranked directory history; fzf owns selection UI.

## Frontier and protocol order

1. Eon publishes the smallest EONW v4 seed that explicitly represents a pending tab with no selected pane and requires its picker endpoint. EONW v3 remains unchanged.
2. Eon Desktop changes VEN-C18 under its own implementation Bead and accepts one exact v4 consumer revision.
3. Eon pins that exact Venus revision, implements the bootstrap/new-tab lifecycle, refreshes the installed profile, and completes native dogfood.

One frontier moves in that order. Do not build Eon runtime behavior against a speculative Venus consumer.

## Evidence and reference gate

Required:
- Eon source 9f6599d103162061ee666126c2eddce03383afb6 and EON-C17/EON-C18.
- Exact Venus picker source df88b2867d50c59a316418471abd000da02940bc and current VEN-C18 model, scene, focus, accessibility, and transport owners.
- Exact Orbit 70861097a825c2fbfaea53a8ca9437f45e8602eb startup, exit, attachment, and Stop contracts.
- Existing EONW v2/v3 codecs and version-rejection tests.
- Existing Zoxide/fzf dependency decision and packaged helper.

Adopt:
- A versioned pending-tab state, not an empty-string sentinel, placeholder pane, hidden shell, injected cd, restarted Session, or generic modal.
- One transient picker Session followed by one durable pane Session; they never overlap as pane topology in the pending tab.

## Acceptance criteria

- Fresh Eon publishes t1 plus its picker before session-1 exists. Accept starts p1/session-1 exactly once at the selected directory.
- Ctrl+T publishes one appended active pending tab and picker before allocating or starting its first pN/session-N. Accept commits one pane with the next canonical identities.
- First-tab cancel/failure starts p1 at the original validated launch directory. Later-tab cancel/failure restores the previous tab/focus and consumes no pane or Session identity.
- No picker outcome changes or restarts existing pane CWDs or processes.
- Alt+Z on an existing tab retains explicit retarget-only behavior.
- Pending state is impossible without exactly one picker bound to the active pending tab; durable tabs retain exactly one selected pane and at least one pane.
- Venus preserves the existing tab bar, inset, input, focus, narrow-grid, notice, and accessibility behavior without inventing a popup framework.
- Recovery stops stale transient pickers and never restores pending tabs.
- Full affected Rust, EONW, manifest, Nix, lifecycle, accessibility, and installed native Wayland surfaces pass on exact revisions. Profile refresh preserves live Sessions.

## Scope boundary

No generic popup, zero-pane durable tab, placeholder shell, pane replacement, shell integration, cd injection, arbitrary command, Yazi path, persisted pending tab, recovery of pending topology, EonTerm behavior, compatibility window, other platform, or automatic picker on attach. Starting each tab with Yazi remains separate.

## Stop conditions

- Stop before Venus production edits until its own implementation Bead is selected and baselined.
- Stop before Eon runtime edits until exact accepted Venus v4 proof exists.
- Stop if the design requires an Orbit protocol change, simultaneous picker and durable-pane presentation in a pending tab, or a second workspace schema owner.

title: Fix the flaky startup-anima picker test
description:
## Defect
One full `nix develop -c eon-test` run (run 8 of 18 during eon-orbit-ready-claim-flake-3si2, 2026-10-17, x86_64 Linux, eon-test sandbox) failed `failed_or_stuck_startup_anima_reports_and_continues_to_picker` (eon/crates/eon/tests/workspace_control.rs:396): exit code 1 where 0 was expected. The other 17 runs passed it. Not caused by that bead's test-only Orbit change.

## Contract
The test passes deterministically under the full parallel workspace run, or its failure exposes a real startup-anima or picker defect that is then fixed at its owner.

## Acceptance
Root cause named with red/green evidence; the fix at the owner (test or product); repeated full eon-test runs pass. Scope: this test and its owner only.
close_reason: ETXTBSY from a concurrently forked child holding the test's script writer; the helper now writes scripts from a child process. Red/green and proof in comments.

comments.author: lucca
comments.text: Root cause: ETXTBSY. executable() wrote each fake script with fs::write in the test process. A concurrent test in the same workspace_control process can fork while that write descriptor is open; the child keeps it until its exec, and exec of a file with an open writer fails with ETXTBSY. title: Stop previous or all Eon generations with eon stop
description:
## Contract
Consumer: Eon users cleaning up generations. Trigger: `eon stop previous [--json]` or `eon stop all [--json]`. Result: previous attempts every non-dead generation except installed current. Previous does not require current to be live; each previous target remains explicit and validated. Fixed-namespace legacy reports its own unavailable reason. All attempts every non-dead generation, with current last. Each target uses validated, version-aware supervisor Stop and human confirmation; declining one reports no Stop for that target while prior outcomes remain and later targets continue. JSON mode is noninteractive like single Stop. While the caller remains running, continue after an unavailable or failed target and exit nonzero if any Stop attempt fails. Stopping the caller's own Session can terminate the CLI before later targets or a complete JSON result. Fixed-namespace legacy and unknown EONW remain unavailable. No PID, systemd, or process-name fallback.
Owner: EON-C11 in docs/CONTRACTS.md. No wire change or dependency.

## Evidence and reference gate
Question: how can one invocation stop selected generations while preserving supervisor authority and live work after a profile refresh?
Primary: Eon generation discovery, selected inspection, and per-generation Stop in crates/eon/src/generation.rs; CLI dispatch in crates/eon/src/cli.rs; EON-C11; Orbit ORB-C12/C13 accepted management Stop at 0233f4d34b294a50c5bc7f373859cf4ec04d2414.
Comparable: local tmux 3.4 manual distinguishes kill-session -a and kill-server; its server-wide mechanism is not copied.
Child pins: Orbit f8ad14e5195109ba8cb421f30e5ae4a9619a1419 and Venus f6c1ebdb16df2960077dbd88ab6728a921b789d8 match latest accepted code revisions. Baseline Eon ed4d09b82e6105fbf3e0c64b34f18b6281aefe63.
Adopt: compose discovery with existing Stop; select previous independently of current's live state; retain per-target validation and confirmation.
Reject: process kill, systemd control, duplicate Stop implementation, automatic eviction, silently skipping unavailable targets, and a current-live prerequisite that blocks explicit previous Stop.

## Acceptance
Private runtime with two previous and one current proves previous preserves current, all includes current last, and one failed target does not suppress another. Previous attempts an older versioned generation while current is unstarted. Verify help, docs, LOC, locked Rust, Clippy, Nix flake, profile identity, installed private-runtime behavior, and preservation of live user Sessions.

title: Streamline dense documentation across Eon repositories
description:
## Observable outcome

Consumer: a human or coding agent reading canonical engineering documentation in Eon, Eon Sessions, Eon Desktop, or Eonova.

Trigger: the reader needs one ownership boundary, dependency decision, reference route, proof case, or status entry.

Result: the reader can find and understand that item without horizontally parsing paragraph-sized Markdown table cells. Tables remain for compact repeated fields and real comparisons; dense records use stable headings with short labeled fields or bullets.

Important failures: no contract, proof identity, accepted revision, source link, owner, rejection, status, scope boundary, or current limitation may disappear or change meaning. This repository-tooling and documentation task changes no EON, ORB, or VEN product contract, runtime behavior, dependency decision, component revision, platform promise, or compatibility boundary.

## Why and evidence

The current table shape compresses long-form decision records into raw Markdown rows that are hard to scan, review, diff, and maintain. This is one coordinating P1 task because the user chose a consistent pass across all four repositories. Effort M; risk LOW-MEDIUM because most edits are structural documentation, with one narrow repository-governance parser update.

Inspected baselines:

- Eon Sessions at `1f90809d9141b4faff110ec54c4e886aaa3bb193`: `docs/CRATES.md` stores six-field dependency decisions in rows up to 3,329 characters; `docs/CONTRACTS.md` has conformance rows up to 456 characters.
- Eon at `9a56aeb18fc83dccbcf8887f63cc17a08d3cbf53`: `docs/REFERENCES.md` has routing rows up to 1,942 characters, `docs/ARCHITECTURE.md` ownership rows up to 459, and `docs/DISTRIBUTION.md` conditional routes up to 530.
- Eon Desktop at `d3dea8868f5b841be56d149f31457a7acf77609f`: `docs/CRATES.md` decision rows reach 661 characters. Its measured-comparison table is genuinely tabular and is not a conversion target without a concrete readability failure.
- Eonova at `f4717efe7c68f6061209a225c2a551031da82060`: the only table is a compact README LOC scorecard, so review is expected to produce no change.
- Eon Sessions `tools/governance/src/main.rs` currently parses the exact `docs/CRATES.md` six-column table and rejects malformed status, missing exact version or commit, missing credible alternatives, missing evidence Beads, and unknown contract references. `README.md` documents that row-shape contract. A document-only scope would therefore make the main rewrite unimplementable.
- Closed Eon Beads `eon-tighten-reference-routing-g0h` and `eon-contract-index-current-state-iuh` own the accepted routing and current-state decisions. This task changes presentation, not those decisions.

## Prerequisites and reference gate

Before implementation, reread each repository `AGENTS.md` and the exact target documents. In Eon Sessions, also read the governance description in `README.md`, `check_crates`, the shared Markdown helpers, and the existing governance fixtures in `tools/governance/src/main.rs`.

Adopt the repository-native heading-plus-labeled-field pattern already used for `docs/CONTRACTS.md` where it fits. Keep Markdown itself as the source of truth. Reject a generator, documentation framework, general Markdown parser, new dependency, universal template, or separate lint script: none removes an owned responsibility here.

## Scope

In scope:

- Handwritten Markdown in the Eon, Eon Sessions, Eon Desktop, and Eonova repositories, addressed by repository name and repository-relative path.
- Inventory every non-generated table containing multi-sentence rationale, conditional routing, evidence history, or paragraph prose.
- Convert confirmed dense records to the smallest readable shape: stable headings plus only the labels each record needs, with a compact index only when it materially improves navigation.
- Retain compact matrices, version maps, scorecards, dependency counts, and short ownership mappings when comparison across columns is clearer.
- In Eon Sessions only, update `tools/governance/src/main.rs` and its co-located tests so the governance command validates the new canonical `docs/CRATES.md` section shape. Update the corresponding README governance description.
- Refresh relative links, heading references, and README LOC scorecards where repository policy requires them.

Out of scope:

- Generated `AGENTS.md`, protocol imports, Beads storage other than this task, source code or tests outside the Eon Sessions governance owner, manifests, lock files, Nix, runtime profiles, and CHANGELOG behavior records.
- Product-contract edits, proof promotion, dependency decisions, reference selection, content expansion, or factual corrections hidden inside reformatting.
- A documentation generator, framework, renderer, new dependency, compatibility layer, summary mirror, or second source of truth.

## Implementation notes

1. Record the exact repository revisions, dirty paths, table candidates, record headings, contract IDs, Bead IDs, 40-hex revisions, and external URLs before editing.
2. Start with Eon Sessions `docs/CRATES.md`. Replace the paragraph-cell table with one section per decision using the same six owned fields: boundary, selected shape, status, credible alternatives, rationale, and evidence. Add a compact index only if the headings alone are insufficient.
3. Adapt the existing governance parser and fixtures to that section structure, preserving every current rejection. Do not build a generic Markdown parser.
4. Apply the same prose-versus-comparison test to the named Eon, Orbit, and Venus documents. Review Eonova and leave its scorecard unchanged unless a concrete failure appears.
5. Compare the semantic inventory after each repository. Keep repository commits independently reviewable and follow each repository Git and LOC policy.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Every handwritten Markdown table row currently longer than 300 characters is reviewed. No remaining table cell contains multi-sentence rationale, conditional routing, evidence history, or paragraph prose.
- A row longer than 300 characters may remain only when its cells are compact parallel data and the table is clearer than separate records; retained candidates and the reason are recorded in this Bead.
- Every converted record has a stable heading and remains reachable from its document or a compact index.
- Per-record owners, statuses, selected shapes, alternatives, rationale, evidence, contract IDs, Bead IDs, exact 40-hex revisions, source links, and scope boundaries retain their meaning. Baseline and final identifier and URL inventories are identical unless the user separately approves a current-state correction.
- Eon Sessions governance accepts the new canonical crate-decision structure and still rejects malformed canonical decision structure, unknown contract references, invalid decision status, missing exact version or commit, missing credible alternatives, and missing existing evidence Beads.
- The existing governance tests are adapted rather than mirrored; no new dependency, generator, general parser, or standalone linter is added.
- Repository-local documentation and LOC policies are satisfied. No runtime or Nix artifact build, profile refresh, product proof, or behavior claim is made.

## Verification

- Use a read-only `awk` inventory of long Markdown table rows as a review list, not as a zero-row formatting quota.
- Compare sorted `rg` inventories for contract IDs, Bead IDs, exact 40-hex revisions, and `https://` URLs, then review each converted record field-for-field.
- Resolve changed relative links and headings locally, check changed external targets, and preview representative converted documents.
- In Eon Sessions run `cargo fmt --check`, `cargo check --locked`, `cargo test --locked`, `cargo run --locked --quiet -p orbit-governance -- .`, `cargo clippy --locked --all-targets -- -D warnings`, and `git diff --check`.
- In every changed repository verify the exact README LOC scorecard and run `git diff --check`. Review final Git status and preserve unrelated dirty state.

## Stop conditions

- Stop if preserving meaning requires a new product contract, proof decision, dependency choice, reference-selection change, or ownership change.
- Stop if the rewrite would create a second canonical owner or generated mirror.
- Report factual drift separately rather than hiding a semantic correction inside structural reformatting.
- Stop if concurrent edits overlap a target document and cannot be preserved safely.

## Maintenance notes

Prefer deleting table syntax and separating independent records. Do not replace compact scorecards or true comparison matrices with repetitive prose. The goal is lower cognitive and diff complexity, not a character-count score.

title: Keep Eon responsive under heavy machine load: measure input latency and isolate the UI from busy terminals
description:
## Why

Lucca, 2026-11-07: "id like eon to behave better under stress, it's often irresponsive under load".

Earlier work (eon-8wh7h, closed 2026-11-04) bounded tab-close stops and made Venus say plainly when Eon is slow; it looked for a blocker on the supervisor's request path under CPU load. Today's slowdown was different: with six agents building, IO pressure was full ~45% and iowait ~25% (one whole-workspace eon-test writing target/), swap held 11 GB with parts of Venus and Eon swapped out, and Venus itself used ~25% of a core redrawing busy agent panes. Load was ~19 on 16 threads.

Machine facts (2026-11-07): cgroup v2 with cpu, memory and pids delegated to the user manager (no io controller); NVMe scheduler kyber, so ioprio/ionice has no effect; ext4.

## Scope (investigate first, then propose; no contract change without approval)

1. Measure what the person feels: input-to-frame latency in Venus (key press to the glyph on screen, tab switch, popup open) and supervisor answer time, idle versus under a reproducible stress profile that covers CPU, disk writes with journal pressure, and memory pressure with swap, in an isolated Eon session. Stress runs need a quiet window coordinated with the overseer (the machine is shared); a VM is acceptable.
2. Find where the time goes under each profile: Venus's own thread (redraw cost per busy pane, blocking IPC, allocation), the supervisor's request path, Orbit hosts, page faults and swap-in of Eon's processes, fsync or file IO on a UI path.
3. Evaluate mitigations, with numbers:
   - Eon-side: coalesce redraws of panes that are not visible or not focused, cap per-frame work, keep IPC off Venus's UI thread.
   - Resource policy Eon owns at launch: run Venus and the supervisor in a systemd user scope with higher CPUWeight and MemoryLow (keeping them out of swap), and terminals' process trees in a lower-weight scope; what happens without systemd (macOS, non-systemd Linux).
   - Anything that needs root or an io controller is out of scope; say so.
4. Report with a recommendation and small slices. Configuration for any policy follows rule 6.

## Current container acceptance (2026-11-12)

Slice 1 is already landed as recorded above; do not repeat instrumentation.
This epic is complete only after the measurement container .1 and the chosen
conditional .2/.3/.4 outcomes are resolved with their recorded approval gates.
A measured no-Venus-bottleneck or no-policy-benefit recommendation is a valid
report, never permission to invent a mitigation. The original systemd-scope
suggestion is a private experiment under .4, not approval of a shipped systemd
requirement; current Platform Discipline remains binding. This planning pass
adds no pressure run, performance claim, platform promise or product policy.

title: Measure and attribute native input latency under bounded resource pressure
description:
Suggested type: task. Parent/context: `eon-stress-responsive-ap1j6`.

## Why

Lucca reported both general unresponsiveness and clicks with no visible effect.
The incident involved CPU work, ext4 write/journal pressure, swap residency and
busy-pane rendering; CPU-only stress previously failed to reproduce the older
supervisor stall. Slice 1 supplies the accounting/oracles, but no scheduled
stress matrix has run. Choose a mitigation only after locating the delay.

## Evidence

- Parent bead and its 2026-11-07 input-test comment are the behavioral spec.
- `eon/tools/eon-bench/src/response.rs`: private native fixture, response cases,
  monotonic stage records, visible intervals, loss checks and bounded cleanup.
- `venus/src/application.rs`, `transport.rs`, `render.rs`; Runtime
  `control.rs`, `supervisor.rs`, `diagnostics.rs`; Orbit `host.rs`, `pty.rs`:
  the opt-in composed-path stages. No wire timestamp extension is needed.
- Accepted `00-plan.md` stress table and `01-paths.md`; slice-1 native results
  and their capture-under-contention failures are retained in the records above.

## Scope

One scheduled measurement session in one approved Linux environment, producing
one reproducible workload matrix and attribution report. Reuse `eon-bench
response`, its native fixtures, corpora, JSON and statistics. Limit durable
support to essential bounded pressure/busy-writer/telemetry controls in the
existing benchmark tool and its development recipe. First preflight the chosen
sample count, trace capacity, case/run deadlines and fixture shutdown; a trace
bound hit is a harness failure, never evidence of lost product input.

Fix one representative busy topology before the full matrix. Screen one then
two visible unfocused columns, the equivalent hidden-tab/collapsed-pane control,
zoom-hidden columns and a popup-covered view with short observations; retain
which topology was selected and why. Do not run an open-ended Cartesian product
of devices, platforms, topologies and pressure intensities in this child.

Use these bounded profile shapes, recording exact tools/versions, arguments,
seeds, rates, bytes and abort thresholds **before** measurement:

- CPU: half then all allowed CPUs, no busy output in the first CPU-only control;
  at most 120 seconds of active pressure per case, with an independent deadline.
- Disk/journal: private ext4 files on the relevant filesystem; begin with one
  sequential buffered writer and one small-file create/write/fsync/rename/unlink
  plus directory-fsync worker. At most two of each, 4 KiB metadata files, two
  data files of at most 512 MiB each, at most 2 GiB allocated, and at least
  15 GiB free initially. Demonstrate journal pressure, not just throughput.
- Memory/swap: prefer a coordinator-provided disposable VM, initially proposed
  as 8 GiB RAM/4 GiB swap, with its own approved limits. A shared-host alternative
  must contain the entire isolated experiment in a delegated memory cgroup with
  approved high/max/swap limits and leave more than 6 GiB host RAM available.
  Require actual reclaim/swap-in of the isolated Eon processes; pre-existing
  SwapUsed alone does not establish pressure.
- One combined incident-shaped validation only after individual profiles attain
  their targets. The historical ~45% IO-full/~25% iowait/11 GiB swap are context,
  not mandatory host-wide targets.

Collect roughly 1 Hz CPU/IO/memory PSI, vmstat, dirty/writeback, filesystem/device,
cgroup events and owned-process CPU/faults/IO/RSS/swap. Use the same deterministic
busy-writer byte/sequence checks in matched conditions. Recheck delegation and
device facts; do not assume ionice works on kyber. No root, IO-controller
requirement, raw-device writes, global sync/cache dropping, swap reconfiguration,
sysctl/mount changes, production mitigation or live-user observation.

## Acceptance

- Idle, CPU, disk/journal and memory/swap results exist for the fixed workload;
  combined validation is included only after its prerequisites are attained.
  Unsupported/unattained conditions are explicit and routed for a VM or scope
  decision rather than silently treated as successful measurements.
- Successful full conditions account for at least 100 stimuli per warm case in
  three independent runs. Failed cases retain every attempt, the last confirmed
  stages and right-censored latency; never omit them to improve a percentile.
  Use 250 ms idle/1000 ms stressed test budgets and a separate 6 s cold-popup
  budget, unless Lucca approves different preregistered experimental settings.
- Every visible transition and subsequent selected-fixture receipt is checked;
  header navigation uses documented Escape to return keyboard focus without CLI
  re-selection. Dialog consumption, invalid ingress, explicit discard, missing,
  late and inconclusive capture remain distinct. No failed input is retried.
- Pressure attainment, writer work/throughput, stage distributions, capture
  uncertainty, adapter/software identity and exact artifacts accompany results.
  Include an outer trace-off comparison where the existing fixture permits it;
  otherwise label perturbation unproved and keep that limit on all conclusions.
- Report the dominant confirmed segment per profile (or insufficient evidence),
  and the one candidate each for Venus, Runtime or resource-policy follow-up.
  Do not diagnose a capture/trace/injector failure as a product drop.
- Owned workers, fixtures and scopes stop at bounded deadlines and clean up on
  normal exit, failure and cancellation, with zero private survivors.

## Implementation Notes

1. Read root/owner AGENTS and the required contract, testing, proof, configuration
   and platform rules; re-read the parent, accepted plan and current tool help.
2. Predeclare the workload/envelope and smallest required benchmark additions.
   Prefer existing/pinned tools; a missing general harness capability is a
   prerequisite to scope, not permission to build a new profiling framework.
3. Smoke the accounting/pressure attainment, then execute the fixed matrix and
   summarize the retained raw records without changing budgets after results.

## Verification

For measurement-only work: retain commands, artifacts, environment, attained
pressure, raw samples, all failures and cleanup scans in this bead. For any
code/test/script change: fmt, changed-crate all-targets clippy, meaningful focused
checks and full `nix develop -c eon-test` on the exact staged tree, plus exact Nix
candidate/on-demand proof appropriate to the changed tool. Rust suites run only
through `eon-test`; use six Cargo jobs and the current overseer heavy-run wrapper
for Nix/full-workspace jobs. Native runs use Nix out-link candidates and private
HOME/config/state/D-Bus/display/short runtime roots; never the live profile.

## Dependencies and Lucca's Approval

Blocked by landed slice 1 and explicit approval of this child's workload, bounds
and scheduled quiet window or supplied VM. Before pressure starts, write exactly
`BLOCKED: need a quiet window for stress runs` to STATUS.md and wait for INBOX.
A VM resource envelope is approved before provisioning/running it; do not apply
host RAM guards blindly inside the guest. On the shared host abort at available
RAM ≤6 GiB, disk free <10 GiB, unexpected OOM, lost monitoring/control or unrelated
heavy work. Fresh approval is needed for new dependencies, contract changes or
expansion beyond the fixed matrix. The slice-1 native exception grants none of this.

## Stop Conditions and Maintenance Notes

Stop before pressure if isolation, cleanup or monitoring cannot be established.
If supporting the matrix needs product hooks/lifecycle changes or a general tool
redesign, propose the prerequisite split to the overseer before expanding scope.
If the approved envelope cannot attain swap/journal pressure, record that negative
and request a suitable VM. Fit one matrix/report in one fresh session; no product
fixes here. Future children consume these exact workloads rather than inventing
new benchmarks to favor a mitigation.

---

## Current execution model (2026-11-12)

This task was already split with overseer approval on 2026-11-09 because it takes
2-3 sessions; it is now typed as an epic, not another runnable implementation.
The full scope/envelope/acceptance above is the unchanged shared measurement spec.
Child .1.1 landed the pressure-worker/telemetry harness, .1.2 supplies busy writers
and topology screening, and .1.3 alone executes the approved matrix and attributes
results. A separate bounded prerequisite repairs .1.1's four recorded attainment
and failed-start reporting findings before .1.3; it supplies no stress result.

Parent acceptance is child completion with the original accounting, safety,
pressure-attainment and attribution requirements met (or a clearly blocked/
negative condition routed for decision). .2/.3/.4 continue to wait on this
container so they consume accepted evidence. No new workload envelope, product
fix, threshold relaxation or pressure-run approval is created by the split.

  none`, a low-`MemAvailable` host does not fail an idle run (the guard
  protects the machine from our pressure, not the measurement).
- Owned processes are found by the existing private-root environment marker,
  rescanned every 5 s by the sampler, and aggregated per command name to keep
  rows bounded. Workers do not carry the marker, so they are not counted as Eon
  processes; they are stopped by their `Child` handle (unreaped, so exact),
  PDEATHSIG and their own monotonic deadline.
- Pressure covers warm cases only; the cold popup and dialog capture controls
  run unpressured (documented).
- Disk worker counts are pairs (`--pressure-workers` 1..2 = one sequential
  writer + one metadata worker each), matching the bead's "at most two of each".

## Known limits (for .1.3)

- The memory profile's driver and capture share the containment cgroup.
- 100 samples per case must fit in `--pressure-seconds` (max 120 s, warm-up
  included); slice-1 idle cases ran ~0.3-1 s per sample with routing, so the

5-7 are review considerations for preflight, not permission to expand tooling

comments.author: lucca
comments.text:
# Follow-ups for eon-stress-responsive-ap1j6.1.3 (from the Opus review of .1.1)

Source: fresh Opus review of 2f98932a (~/.local/state/rota/runs/stress-opus-1/log),
which approved .1.1 with nothing blocking. The overseer (INBOX 2026-11-09T22:05Z)
ruled findings 1-4 out of scope for .1.1; they must be settled before .1.3 runs
any real profile.

1. The memory profile never forces reclaim inside its cgroup. Preflight keeps
   cgroup use + request + 512 MiB under `memory.max` and host MemAvailable
   above guard + 512 MiB, so it is safe but never puts Eon under reclaim or
   swap-in, which the .1 bead requires ("actual reclaim/swap-in of the
   isolated Eon processes"). `memory.high` is never read, and any finite
   `memory.swap.max` passes. Direction: size the hog above `memory.high` and
   below `memory.max` minus headroom; guard `memory.swap.current` against
   `memory.swap.max`; report `memory.high` throttling (memory.events `high`).
2. The disk writer probably reaches the device little, and over-reports. It
   truncates (`set_len(0)`) every 512 MiB, which drops dirty pages before
   writeback, and 512 MiB is under typical background-writeback thresholds.
   Its report counts bytes handed to the page cache. Direction: wrap with a
   seek instead of truncating (or sync_file_range/fdatasync periodically),
   and report `write_bytes` and `cancelled_write_bytes` from /proc/self/io.
3. The attainment span is wider than the measured samples: begin is taken
   before workers spawn (includes the 5 s warm-up ramp), end after SIGTERM
   plus up to 2 s grace. Direction: a `measure` snapshot after warm-up and a
   `stop` snapshot before SIGTERM, with attainment between them (keep begin
   and end rows for the full window).
4. A window that fails inside `begin` (guard trip during warm-up, worker spawn
   failure, refused start) leaves no `pressure_cases` record and no end row;
   the plan promised a failed case with `aborted: <reason>`. Safety holds
   (Window::drop kills and reaps; the run error and abort row survive).
   Direction: record a failed attainment from `begin`'s error paths.

Further non-blocking points from the same review, for whoever scopes .1.3:

5. `--guard-available-mib` accepts 0 on the shared host; only the docs say
   "VM only". Consider a floor without an explicit VM flag. A hand-run
   `pressure-worker` trusts its deadline and size; clamping inside the worker
   (MAX_SECONDS, SEQUENTIAL_FILE, MAX_MEMORY_MIB) would add a second bound.
6. A long-lived process first tracked mid-case (`track` from `pump`) counts
   from zero, so the case is charged its lifetime CPU ticks. Direction:
   record a first-sight baseline instead of zero, or flag first-seen-mid-case.
7. Test gaps: dropping a Window without `end` killing its workers; the memory
   worker under SIGTERM as a real process; `WARM_CASES = 12` not tied to the
   case list (a 13th case shortens the session deadline and fails the run).
8. Stale text: fixed in .1.1 round 2 (`response.rs` deadline message; the
   `launcher.rs` marker note in 01-implementation.md).

description:
## Why

Split the four mandatory Opus follow-ups (2026-11-09) out of
`eon-stress-responsive-ap1j6.1.3` so the matrix consumes an accepted harness.
The overseer routed these findings from landed .1.1 to .1.3; no finding is dropped.

## Evidence (dcaef1c)

`eon/tools/eon-bench/src/pressure.rs`: preflight (:263) ignores memory.high;
begin (:746) snapshots before warm-up and can return without a failed case;
sequential (:1219, :1225) truncates on wrap. The .1.3 comment records the review.

## Scope

Only pressure.rs, consuming response/result paths, focused tests and development
docs needed for these four outcomes. Preserve the parent .1's caps, containment,
owned cleanup and default no-pressure behavior. No resource matrix, topology
work, product mitigation, host changes, root operations or new workload envelope.

- Memory preflight/attainment respects memory.high, memory.max and swap headroom,
  reports high throttling and can establish actual contained reclaim/swap-in.
  Refusal/unattained pressure remains explicit; never force shared-host pressure.
- Sequential writing no longer drops its dirty range by truncating each wrap;
  actual write_bytes/cancelled_write_bytes are distinct from page-cache bytes.
  Private-file and allocated-space caps remain unchanged.
- Attainment aligns after warm-up/before worker stop, retaining begin/end rows
  for the full lifecycle too.

  pressure_cases entry with aborted reason/final available telemetry and bounded

## Implementation Notes and Verification

and record any schema/consumer impact. Items 5-7 are considerations, not added
scope. Focused deterministic checks/tiny bounded workers must falsify the four

the exact tree; no real stress matrix is needed here. .1.3 alone proves real
attainment with separate resource approval.

Stop for broader harness scope rather than merging implementation into the

title: Reduce one measured Venus bottleneck without losing input or terminal state
description:
Suggested type: task, conditional on S2 evidence. Parent/context:
`eon-stress-responsive-ap1j6`.

## Why

The parent incident included busy-pane redraw cost, but no current measurement
establishes that a new scheduler, queue or renderer is needed. Existing hidden
pane/tab detachment and frame coalescing must be understood before adding more.
Deliver one small Venus change against one confirmed expensive segment.

## Evidence

- S2's exact workload, profile, raw stage spans and pressure-attainment report.
- `venus/src/application.rs`: UI drain/model apply/redraw path and workspace
  geometry; `venus/src/transport.rs`: existing bounded queues/coalescing;
  `venus/src/render.rs` and `scene.rs`: scene/text/frame work.
- `01-paths.md` identifies zoom-hidden columns as a measurement candidate;
  hidden tabs/collapsed panes already detach. This is a hypothesis, not approval
  to stop their state/input work.
- Preserve `VEN-C2` input/geometry and `VEN-C8` response UX and Orbit's authority.

## Scope

One measured offender, one mechanism and one bounded owner change: e.g. avoid a
proven redundant rebuild after one column changes, or bound/coalesce the proven
frame work in its existing owner. Read the actual hot path before selecting it.
No renderer replacement, speculative threads/queues, Runtime lifecycle change,
resource policy or unrelated notice/refusal work (`eon-ih692`, `eon-u24pw`).

Keep non-frame event order, canonical newest frame, attachment/focus transitions,
images, clipboard, selection, resize and published input geometry correct.
Skipping terminal authority updates or starving writer throughput is not an
acceptable latency optimization. Other panes must remain current when revealed.

## Acceptance

- A regression check falsifies the specific defect before the fix and passes
  afterward; e.g. one-column changes no longer perform the identified redundant
  work while final rendered/state inputs remain equivalent.
- Matched before/after native measurements use S2's profile, workload, delivered
  bytes, sample counts, budgets, adapter and correctness oracles. Record median,
  p95/max, uncertainty and stage cost. Demonstrate the preregistered improvement
  in that segment and no dropped, duplicate, misrouted or stale visible response.
- Busy-writer completion/sequence and throughput are retained so lower work does
  not mean hidden data loss. Include representative reveal/zoom/popup/focus and
  image/clipboard/selection controls affected by the selected mechanism.
- If S2 shows no Venus bottleneck, or the proposed change has no measured benefit,
  retain that negative and recommend no change instead of shipping speculative code.

## Implementation Notes

1. Select one S2 finding and the cheapest falsifier; show Lucca the precise proposed
   behavior/work policy and obtain approval before implementation.
2. Use existing coalescing/owner boundaries. Inspect the reference route at an
   exact revision before any consequential new mechanism; no second terminal model.
3. Implement the one fix, run its targeted proof, then compare identical conditions.

## Verification

Use `nix develop -c eon-test -p yazelix-venus`, fmt and all-targets clippy, followed
by the repository-required full workspace suite on the exact staged candidate.
Build the exact Nix candidate with an out-link and run the isolated on-demand
native A/B under an approved window/VM. Record source/artifact identity, all
attempts and cleanup. Quantify observer/capture limitations; tracing overhead and
hardware performance remain unproved unless measured. Follow current heavy-run
scheduling and CARGO_BUILD_JOBS=6. The overseer supplies fresh required reviews.

## Dependencies and Lucca's Approval

Blocked by S2's reproducible Venus attribution and explicit approval of this
single mitigation. A new frame/time/work threshold must be configurable and
listed in `docs/CONFIGURATION.md`, or have an approved rule-6 fixed-bound reason.
Stop before changing any EON-C/ORB-C/VEN-C contract. Scheduled stress A/B requires
its own quiet-window/VM grant; write `BLOCKED: need a quiet window for stress runs`
to STATUS.md and wait for INBOX.

## Stop Conditions and Maintenance Notes

Stop if attribution moves outside Venus, a second independent mechanism is needed,
or correctness requires a wire/lifecycle change. Propose the next slice instead
of expanding this one beyond a fresh session. Preserve platform seams; do not
claim macOS/hardware/scanout support from Linux software-headless proof. All native
work uses private roots/display, exact owned PID/start identity cleanup, and Nix
candidates; never Lucca's windows, supervisors, Orbit hosts, profile or focus.

title: Attribute Runtime start/churn stalls and hand the reproduction to eon-pimct
description:
Suggested type: task (diagnosis/handoff). Parent/context:
`eon-stress-responsive-ap1j6`. Existing implementation owner: `eon-pimct`.

## Why

The earlier `eon-8wh7h` reproduction found Inspect waiting about 3.8 s behind a
terminal start under IO+CPU load. Stops were bounded there; starts are the subject
of existing `eon-pimct`. Current native slowness must distinguish a busy supervisor
from Venus work or a slow Orbit Ready publication, without duplicating that redesign.

## Evidence

- Re-read `eon-pimct` and its current state: it owns keeping the loop answering
  during a pending start, including failure, concurrent creators and cleanup.
- `runtime/crates/eon-runtime/src/supervisor.rs`: accept/dispatch/reply loop;
  `control.rs`: request transport; `sessions.rs`: Orbit launch/Ready wait.
- Slice-1 monotonic Runtime/Venus/Orbit stages and S2's exact pressure artifacts.
  Historical 25 ms polling/5 s waits are evidence to recheck, not current facts
  or an approved replacement mechanism.

## Scope

One bounded attribution/reproducer session. Run independent read-only Inspect
probes alongside the existing native cases. Add controlled terminal creation and
close churn as a **separate** workload, including the historical three-creator
case only inside the approved envelope. Match request IDs, dispatch/Ready spans
and visible outcomes; retain maximum and distribution before any fix.

Prefer existing diagnostics and the supported Runtime process harness. Add only
missing bounded diagnostics/reproducer support if needed. No start-state-machine,
read-only-pump or deferred-reply implementation here: route confirmed start-loop
blocking to `eon-pimct`. Stop-path redesign, UI notices, failure wording and Orbit's
own startup performance remain outside this child.

## Acceptance

- Distinguish terminal-start wait, control queue/dispatch/reply, Orbit readiness,
  and Venus render/capture delay with evidence; a generic timeout is insufficient.
- Retain a deterministic reproducer when supported: hold one isolated Orbit Ready
  pending and observe whether an independent Inspect completes before release or
  timeout. Exercise never-ready/failure and concurrent creators without leaving
  phantom workspace objects or private children. Do not land a permanently failing
  default test; attach a disposable reproducer if the existing harness cannot
  express the pre-fix failure yet.
- If start-loop blocking is confirmed, hand exact artifacts, commands, target
  identities and the falsifier to `eon-pimct` and record that linkage. If it has
  already landed, verify its relevant behavior and avoid a duplicate fix.
- Negative results or another confirmed blocker get an honest attribution and a
  narrowly proposed owner/scope; they do not justify silently rewriting Runtime.

## Implementation Notes

1. Check S2 and `eon-pimct`, then fix one controlled churn workload and Inspect probe.
2. Use only owned-process sampling; collect no user-terminal contents or credentials.
3. Summarize the blocking segment and publish the handoff on the owning bead using
   the tracker only when that future session is authorized to write it.

## Verification

A diagnosis-only child records exact source/artifact/environment, probe timings,
all attempted runs and cleanup; it claims no runtime fix. If diagnostics/test/script
code changes, run meaningful focused Runtime checks, fmt/clippy, full workspace
`nix develop -c eon-test` and the affected Nix/isolated process proof required by
current rules, all on the staged tree with six Cargo jobs and proper heavy slots.
Never use live Eon supervisors/windows/Orbit hosts; use separate roots/display and
owned exact PID/start identities. Review belongs to the overseer.

## Dependencies and Lucca's Approval

Blocked by S2 Runtime evidence and approval of this attribution slice and its
churn envelope/quiet window or VM. Write `BLOCKED: need a quiet window for stress runs`
and wait before pressure/churn stress. This child is not blocked by the implementation
of `eon-pimct`: its job is to supply or validate that bead's reproduction. If the
parent requires the eventual lifecycle fix, depend separately on `eon-pimct`;
do not introduce a dependency cycle or competing implementation bead. A contract,
new response-time guarantee or lifecycle redesign requires Lucca's approval and
the owning bead's reference gate before code.

## Stop Conditions and Maintenance Notes

Finish with one reproduction/negative report and handoff, leaving session room
for proof. A different Runtime blocker or missing test framework needs a newly
scoped proposal, not extra implementation here. The 250/1000 ms probe budgets are
experimental observations, not new EONW response-time contracts.

title: A/B private CPU/memory protection and recommend whether Eon should adopt it
description:
Suggested type: task (optional experiment/decision). Parent/context:
`eon-stress-responsive-ap1j6`.

## Why

The incident included swap-in and CPU contention. The parent proposes protecting
Venus/supervisor relative to noisy application trees, but CPUWeight and MemoryLow
have no measured Eon default yet. They cannot supply an unavailable IO controller,
and MemoryLow is best-effort reclaim protection, not mlock or a no-swap guarantee.

## Evidence

- S2 pressure/attribution data determines which CPU or memory condition is worth
  this experiment and supplies matched terminal throughput/input oracles.
- Recheck the reported cgroup-v2 CPU/memory/pids delegation, absent IO controller,
  and device/scheduler facts in the actual approved environment.
- Eon owns launch policy/configuration; Runtime `generation.rs`/`sessions.rs` own
  generic launch mechanisms; Orbit `pty.rs` owns application-child launch. Read
  owner AGENTS and composition/platform/reference routes before choosing a seam.

## Scope

One private Linux systemd-user experiment and one recommendation. No shipped
policy, persistent user units, product default or automatic launch change.
Use a disposable VM or an explicitly approved private user hierarchy. Keep
protected Venus/supervisor/interactive Orbit host and Bend worker distinct from
noisy terminal **application** descendants. Place competing groups under one
experiment parent so effective sibling weights are meaningful; keep driver/
capture placement identical across A/B. Verify actual membership and ancestors,
not unit names or requested settings alone.

Predeclare a small CPUWeight/MemoryLow A/B setting pair based on S2 residency and
CPU evidence. Keep both treatments within the same containment high/max/swap
limits. Use one selected S2 stress/topology condition, same bytes/rates/seeds and
settings, with ordinary launch as control. No host/root/io-controller/sysctl,
cache/swap/scheduler changes, ionice claim, broad tuning search or accidental
low-weight assignment of the interactive Orbit/Bend path.

## Acceptance

- Record actual process/descendant cgroup membership, effective weights and reclaim
  protection, ancestor limits, PSI, faults/swap, resource events and cleanup.
  Prove the controlled workload's descendants stay in the intended hierarchy,
  enumerate any escape limits, and ensure protected components do not
  inherit a noisy application group by accident.
- Matched ordinary/protected runs retain all input-response verdicts, pressure
  attainment, writer completion/throughput, sample distributions and artifact IDs.
  Attribute any difference with uncertainty; preserve a no-benefit/worse result.
- Treatment disabled/unavailable retains ordinary process launch and correctness;
  report absent protection plainly. A Linux experiment does not prove installed
  non-systemd Linux or macOS protection/support.
- Every experimental scope/worker is bounded and removed on success, error and
  cancellation by exact owned identity/unit name. No live user window, host,
  profile, desktop focus or unrelated systemd unit is touched.
- End with adopt/reject/defer, measured reasons, platform/fallback limits and one
  bounded next proposal. Product adoption is a separate approved change, not a
  hidden second half of this experiment.

## Implementation Notes

1. Obtain approval of the hierarchy, setting pair and pressure envelope before
   creating private scopes. Inspect an exact reference implementation and the
   actual delegation; use the smallest measurement-only launch adapter needed.
2. Verify membership/cleanup without pressure, then perform matched A/B.
3. Document best-effort behavior and unsupported cases before recommending policy.

## Verification

Keep the S2 native visible-response/receipt suite, same correctness and throughput
oracles and experimental budgets. Use at least three independent runs and 100
accounted warm stimuli per measured case/condition, or label an incomplete/failed
condition explicitly. Store cgroup configuration and actual membership beside
results. Native observations use Nix out-link candidates with private roots/display.
Any code/test/script change gets fmt, changed-crate all-targets clippy, meaningful
focused checks, full `nix develop -c eon-test`, and the affected Nix/lifecycle proof
on the exact staged tree; six Cargo jobs and current heavy scheduling apply.
The overseer supplies fresh reviews. No stress runs in default `eon-test`.

## Dependencies and Lucca's Approval

Blocked by S2's evidence, a coordinator-provided delegated environment and Lucca's
approval of this optional experiment, hierarchy, settings and quiet window/VM.
Write `BLOCKED: need a quiet window for stress runs` and wait before pressure.
If safe containment/delegation is unavailable, use the supplied VM or report the
experiment blocked; never add a systemd requirement to Eon. Product adoption,
perceived thresholds/defaults/configuration, lifecycle or contract changes require
separate approval, configuration documentation/rule-6 rationale and platform proof.

## Stop Conditions and Maintenance Notes

Stop if separation requires demoting the interactive host, privileged operations,
changing user services or a multi-owner production launch redesign. Scope that
adoption separately rather than expanding this child beyond one fresh session.
Keep resource-policy ownership at Eon and mechanisms at existing seams. Preserve
negative findings so future work does not repeatedly propose unmeasured defaults.

title: Persistent bounded diagnostic log for Eon supervisors and Venus
description:
## Why

eon-jqxr: a Venus window exited after Alt+Shift+W while its supervisor and terminals lived on, and
nothing recorded why. A COSMIC launch runs `eon` with stdout/stderr on /dev/null, the supervisor
runs in that process, and Venus inherited its stderr, so panics and supervisor diagnostics vanished.
Lucca, 2026-10-21: "maybe we could improve our logging and wait for it to happen again?"; chose a
persistent, bounded log over a runtime-directory one.

## Contract (no stable ID; documented in docs/USAGE.md troubleshooting and CHANGELOG)

Consumer: the user or an agent diagnosing a window that ended unexpectedly.

- Every Eon supervisor (workspace and eonbase) that holds its generation's lifecycle lock writes
  one diagnostic log, `$XDG_STATE_HOME/eon/logs/<generation>-<unix-seconds>-<pid>.log`
  (`$HOME/.local/state/eon/logs` when XDG_STATE_HOME is unset or relative). The file is 0600; the
  logs directory must be owned by the user and not a symlink, and is set to 0700.
- Each line carries a local ISO 8601 timestamp. It records: supervisor start (generation, mode,
  pid) and its final result (exit status or error, including configuration errors before
  launch); each Eon Desktop (Venus) start with its pid and each Venus exit with its exit code or
  signal, once, on every reap path (observed exit, admission failure, supervisor shutdown); each
  terminal that ends on its own (its program exited, or Orbit exited without a result) with its
  status; each tab close's terminals, duration and outcome, also when it fails; and the supervisor
  diagnostics that used to go only to stderr. Per-terminal lines cover terminals the supervisor
  reaps on their own. A terminal stopped by a pane, popup or tab close or by `eon stop`, including
  one that exits by itself while that stop runs, gets no per-terminal line. For a tab close, the
  close's record stands for it.
- Venus's stderr goes through a pipe that the supervisor copies verbatim into the log and onto
  its own stderr. Before recording a Venus exit, the supervisor waits up to 1 s for that copy to
  drain. Venus runs with RUST_BACKTRACE=1 unless the environment already sets it.
- Bounds: copied output stops 64 KiB short of 1 MiB, with one marker line. That reserve keeps
  room for the supervisor's own lines, which stop at 1 MiB. At start, a supervisor creates its
  own log, which it holds locked, and then deletes all but the newest 20 regular files named
  `<valid generation>-<seconds>-<pid>.log`. Logs locked by running supervisors are never deleted.
  Anything else in the directory is left alone, and symlinks are never followed.
- Failure: if the log cannot be created, Eon warns on stderr (best effort) and starts without it.
  If the copy thread cannot start, that Venus launch fails like any other start failure.
- Accepted gap: if the supervisor's own stderr stops draining (e.g. a suspended terminal), the
  copy blocks and Venus's stderr writes then block. Before this change Venus wrote to that same
  stderr directly, so it blocked the same way. Bytes already read land in the log first.
  Supervisor death by signal leaves no end line.

## Owner

Eon Runtime supervisor (`runtime/crates/eon-runtime/src/diagnostics.rs`, used by `supervisor.rs`).
Out of scope: Orbit's stderr, which stays on /dev/null, and Eon CLI clients.

## Reference gate

- Routes: docs/REFERENCES.md has no logging route, so I inspected comparable implementations
  instead.
- WezTerm `20240203-110809-5046fc22`, `env-bootstrap/src/ringlog.rs`: one
  `<exe>-log-<pid>.txt` per process in its runtime dir, still logging to stderr, and pruning logs
  older than a week when the GUI starts. Kept: one file per process, stderr kept, prune at start.
  Changed: a persistent state dir (Lucca's choice: a log must outlive the window and a reboot),
  and count/size bounds instead of age, with live logs protected by a lock.
- Ghostty `8c425a7bd57d`: logs to stderr (and the macOS unified log) via GHOSTTY_LOG; no Linux file
  log. Rejected: it relies on the launcher keeping stderr, which COSMIC does not.
- No dependency change: timestamps use libc localtime_r/strftime (libc is already pinned). Turning
  on `time` formatting features was rejected as a dependency change for one format call.

## Acceptance

- Focused tests through `nix develop -c eon-test -p eon-runtime -p eon` (the eon crate's
  `workspace_control` suite asserts a real supervisor's log has a failed and a successful tab close):
  - real log names round-trip through pruning;
  - live and foreign files survive;
  - modes are 0600 and 0700;
  - the bound and its marker hold, with the reserve keeping room for records;
  - Venus stderr is copied ahead of its exit signal line, exactly once;
  - an admission failure records the exit.
- Installed dogfood (isolated headless Sway): launch the built package, kill its Venus, and find
  the start and exit lines in the log.

## Scope boundary

No log viewer, no `eon` subcommand, no Orbit stderr, no log levels or config. Prerequisite for
eon-jqxr's diagnosis.

description:
## Why

A flaky eon-runtime test fails suites at random and costs reruns for every agent that runs `eon-test -p eon-runtime`.

## Evidence

title: Switch to another Eon window from an in-Eon picker (Alt+Shift+S)
description:
## Why

eon-n77e: inside Eon, the only way to see other windows is Commands > List windows, which prints read-only text. Every reference has an in-app picker over detached work:

- tmux `C-b s` and `S-Tab`
- the Zellij session-manager
- WezTerm's launcher
- kitty's `goto_session`
- Rex's "Change Session…"
- the tuios switcher

Eon keeps one workspace per OS window, so a switch attaches or raises that window (kitty's "natural" shape). It does not swap content in place.

## Contract (proposed; bring the exact EON-C23, EON-C10 and Venus shortcut wording to Lucca before code)

Alt+Shift+S, and a Commands entry "Switch window" that replaces the read-only "List windows", open an Eon-owned fzf popup (VEN-C18: no native Venus picker). It lists every other Eon window from the listing bead:

- the name, or else the tab summary;
- open or detached;
- the tab count.

Choosing a row acts as follows:

- **Detached:** attaches it, which opens its OS window.
- **Open:** asks the compositor for attention, the only thing Wayland allows (VEN-C14). The docs say so plainly.
- **Not attachable:** the row says why and does nothing.

Esc closes the popup without acting. The current window is not listed. The popup never stops a window.

## Reference gate

This adds a shortcut and a popup, with no EONW change.

- Read docs/REFERENCES.md:200 (pickers: Eon-owned fzf popups, Kitty overlays and Zellij in-place commands; reject a generic popup protocol).
- Read the session-switching route that the listing bead adds.
- Check that Alt+Shift+S is free once m798 has taken Alt+Shift+D.

## Scope

In scope: the popup command, the shortcut, the Commands entry, the hints and Shortcuts help text, USAGE and contract text, CHANGELOG.

Out of scope:

- in-window swapping;
- create or rename from the picker, since New window stays in Commands;
- next, previous and last-window keys;
- attention badges (the next bead).

## Acceptance

From an installed Eon, with one other window open and one detached:

- Alt+Shift+S lists both.
- Choosing the detached one opens it.
- Choosing the open one raises an attention hint, without stealing focus beyond what the compositor grants.
- Esc does nothing.

## Verification

Installed route: profile refresh plus one isolated dogfood observation for the batch. Codex on every code change.

title: Send a selection from any pane into an agent's prompt without submitting it
description:
Delta lets you comment on any message or diff span, and the comment goes to the agent with your next message (https://delta.dev/docs/agents/comments). The terminal version: select text in any pane (a failing test, a diff hunk, a log line), run a window action "Send selection to agent…", and pick an agent from the sidebar list. Eon pastes the text into that agent's input as a quoted block and does not press Enter, so the person adds a note and submits. It keeps EON-C36's rule and refuses while someone is typing in the target. The CLI path exists already (`eon pane send TARGET --stdin`, without `--enter`); this bead adds the window action and documents the pairing. It needs a VEN-C change for the new action and a configurable key. Owners: Venus for selection and the action, Eon for the binding.

From the Zed Delta threads research (report /home/lucca/.cache/eon-agents/eon-zed-delta-work/report.md, screenshots in shots/ there). Lucca, 2026-11-09, on the report's proposals: "i agree".

## Current evidence and unchosen details (dcaef1c, 2026-11-12)

Canonical EONW is v40, not the comment's historical v38. The supervisor routes
SendTerminal through `terminal_access` (`supervisor.rs:3690,4240`), which enforces
`[agents] terminal_access` and caller/target checks; direct Workspace::apply rejects
that action (`workspace.rs:1594`). This does not prove a Venus presentation-stream
caller can use the CLI request unchanged: trace that route before choosing the
implementation. No bypass of the same-user, person-typing or input-size boundary.

Acceptance to retain: select text in A; a keyboard/accessible picker identifies
reporting targets by stable pane/session identity; choosing B inserts the selected
text as a quoted block with no Enter, no submission and no partial send on refusal.
No selection disables the action; an ended/busy/refused target produces a bounded
notice. Preserve selection and unrelated terminal/focus state until the approved
action requires changing it. The paired `eon pane send TARGET --stdin` path remains
available without selecting or raising the person's target window.

Still unchosen: quoted-block format, picker navigation/accessibility and whether
choosing B moves local keyboard focus there, plus the policy for human sends when
terminal_access=none. The 2026-11-10 comment's focus move is a recommendation,
not Lucca's recorded decision. Present these as numbered choices/recommendations
with the exact affected trust/CLI contract wording before implementation. The new
binding must be configurable/documented. Reuse the existing paste path and one
selection owner; provider-native delivery is related research, not a substitute
for this requested non-submitting paste. If Runtime/EONW work is needed, stop and
split the prerequisite before expanding this Venus feature. Final proof covers
quoted/Unicode/multiline input, no submission, refusal and one isolated installed
cross-pane observation under current rules. Portability: neutral.

description:

  the ChatGPT desktop apps (macOS and Windows: companion window/launcher, conversation sidebar,
  task and agent progress, notifications) with web search.
- Record concrete, verifiable UX lessons for Eon (agent sidebar, attention, switching between
  agents, launching, perceived speed), with sources and access dates, as a comment here.
- Add one short entry for each to docs/VISUAL-REFERENCES.md in its existing style and caveats,
  naming exactly which Eon questions each informs.

Out of scope: any code, contract, or other doc change; filing follow-up beads.

comments.author: lucca
comments.text:
## Research (accessed 2026-10-23; two web-research subagents, key claims spot-checked by the implementer)

Evidence tags: [v] fetched and checked by the implementer on 2026-10-23; [s] subagent report only; [inf] inference.

### T3 Chat (https://t3.chat)

- Source: no public T3 Chat repository. GitHub user pingdotgg lists no T3 Chat repo [v, API]; the FAQ does not mention open source [s]. T3-Content/t3-cloneathon is an MIT starter for a 2025 contest, last pushed 2025-07-09, not T3 Chat [v]. pingdotgg/t3code is MIT, pushed 2026-10-23, and is a separate coding-agent app [v]. So T3 Chat is proprietary; only its public behaviour is reference material.
- Speed: Theo's build video (2025-01-20, https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=QLvIoi2s1zY) describes client-side routing ("I didn't want the server to be involved in navigation"), streaming into a local Dexie/IndexedDB store read through live queries, and memoized finished markdown blocks so only the streaming block re-renders [s]. Moved to Convex as sync engine (Theo, 2025-06-01, https://x.com/theo/status/1929264138544615464) [s]; Convex postmortem (2025-06-03, https://news.convex.dev/how-convex-took-down-t3-chat-june-1-2025-postmortem/): "every online user is subscribed to the first 20 messages for preloading" [s].
- Sidebar: date groups, pins synced across devices, archive and temporary chats (Theo, 2026-02-19) [s]. Cmd/Ctrl+K search, Cmd+Shift+O new chat, Cmd/Ctrl+B sidebar; recent chats removed from Cmd+K as duplicating the sidebar (https://feedback.t3.chat/p/cmd-k, 2025-12-16) [s]. Branching makes each branch a new chat; users say it clutters history (https://feedback.t3.chat/p/branching-chats) [s].
- In-progress marker: "Show Loading Spinner in sidebar on actively generating threads" is Completed; its request says users in other threads otherwise had to check each thread by hand while long responses streamed (https://feedback.t3.chat/p/show-loading-spinner-in-sidebar-on-actively-generating-threads, undated) [v].
- Attention gap: "Notification when request is complete" (tab title/favicon, optional notification) is still "Gathering Interest" (https://feedback.t3.chat/p/notification-when-request-is-complete, undated) [v]. No verified done/unread signal found; only the working spinner [s].
- Launch: `/new?q=&model=&effort=&search=&search_limit=&profile=&temporary=` opens a fully configured new chat; only `q` is required (https://t3.chat/faq, undated) [v]. A choosable default model vs last-used is an open request; users report wasted premium credits when the last-used model carries over [s].
- Limits: the app pages sit behind a Vercel bot checkpoint, so nothing was observed in-app [s]. Board statuses are not in-app proof that a feature shipped.

### ChatGPT desktop apps (macOS, Windows)

- Product line: on 2026-07-09 OpenAI turned the Codex desktop app into the new ChatGPT desktop app with Chat, Work and Codex modes; the old app became "ChatGPT Classic" (macOS release notes https://help.openai.com/en/articles/9703738; https://help.openai.com/en/articles/20001276) [s]. Linux preview 2026-08-11 [s]. Current docs at learn.chatgpt.com are undated. Proprietary: no public source found [s, inf]; the Codex CLI is separately open source.
- Launcher: Option+Space (macOS) / Windows+Alt+P show floating "pets" and focus Quick Chat; a pet "can float above other app windows"; clicking a thread opens it in the main app (https://learn.chatgpt.com/docs/pets) [v]. Classic companion window "stays in front of all other windows" (Aug 2024 notes) [s]. Windows Classic Alt+Space fails silently when another app holds it (https://help.openai.com/en/articles/9982051) [s].
- Statuses and priority: Needs input > Blocked (failed or system error) > Ready (finished with unread activity) > Running (pets doc) [v].
- Activity view: bell in the sidebar or Cmd+Option+U / Ctrl+Alt+U lists chats that are "unread, running, or waiting for your response", with filters and "Mark all as read" (https://learn.chatgpt.com/docs/notifications) [v].
- Shortcuts (https://learn.chatgpt.com/docs/reference/commands) [v]: new chat Cmd/Ctrl+N; toggle sidebar Cmd/Ctrl+B; go to chat 1-9; next/previous chat Ctrl+Tab / Ctrl+Shift+Tab; mark unread Cmd/Ctrl+Shift+U; clear all unread Shift+Esc (Codex only); next chat needing attention Cmd+Option+A / Ctrl+Alt+A (Codex only).
- Notifications: turn completion "never, only while ChatGPT is in the background, or always"; permission and question requests have separate toggles (notifications doc) [v].
- Long work: `/goal` progress row with pause, resume, edit, clear; side chat for status without interrupting (https://learn.chatgpt.com/docs/long-running-work) [s]. Agent mode narrates on screen and lets the user take over (https://openai.com/index/introducing-chatgpt-agent/, 2025-07-17) [s].
- Work with Apps (Classic, macOS): reads Terminal, iTerm, Warp via Accessibility, sending the last 200 lines of open panes, with a banner naming what is attached (https://help.openai.com/en/articles/10119604) [s]. Windows Computer Use "take[s] over the foreground" (https://learn.chatgpt.com/docs/computer-use) [s].
- Criticism: closing the Companion "no longer returns focus to the previous app" (forum, 2026-07-25; support 2026-07-29 called the old behaviour undocumented but said closing should return focus) (https://community.openai.com/t/companion-window-no-longer-returns-focus-to-the-previous-app/1388206) [v]. Option+Space repointed from ChatGPT to Codex without a choice (2026-07-10, https://community.openai.com/t/companion-window-should-stay-available-for-chatgpt-not-only-codex/1386295) [s]. Companion position settings removed (2026-07-17) [s]. New windows do not focus the input (2026-10-05) [s].

### Lessons for Eon (inference from the above)

1. Attention states: ChatGPT's four ranked states (needs input > blocked > ready-unread > running) and T3 Chat's spinner-only gap both argue for distinct waiting, error, done-unseen and working states, ranked, with a "next agent needing attention" key.
2. Unread as state: mark-unread, clear-all and an activity filter; per the Humans and Agents rule each needs an `eon` CLI path.
3. Notifications: never / background-only / always for completion, separate toggles for permission requests.
4. Focus: a transient launcher or popup must return focus where it came from, and must focus its input when the user opened it; users noticed the loss within weeks.
5. Launch: T3 Chat's one-URL fully parameterized launch maps to `eon pane create`; an explicit default profile beats "last used".
6. Speed: switch from locally held state, preload, render only what changes.
7. Grouping: forks as new top-level rows clutter the list; keep spawned agents under their parent.

The 'next chat needing attention' key is Codex-mode only. T3 Chat's client-side routing and Dexie streaming come from 2025 sources that predate or straddle its Convex move.
