title: Spike: keep Runtime ownership across a same-PID exec into a new build
description:
### S1 — Spike inherited Runtime ownership across same-PID exec

**Why:** prove the proposed hardest boundary before building its product shape.

**Evidence:** `sessions.rs:1648`, `:1925`, `:2028`; `supervisor.rs:841`;
`control.rs:540`; systemd/HAProxy sources above.

**Scope:** disposable isolated spike and report only, using real Orbit hosts
and two explicit manager images in a private runtime/display; no public update
command, canonical contract edits, installed user profile, durable compatibility
code or new process owner. Portability disposition: POSIX mechanisms isolated
in Runtime; Linux native Wayland is the only exercised target.

**Acceptance:** record before/after manager PID, Orbit PID/start/run identities,
listener/lock/endpoint objects and management lease continuity; an Orbit exiting
during exec is reaped once; an explicit Stop after resume still confirms PTY
child and host cleanup. Prove old-Venus control **and stderr-pipe** continuity;
exercise diagnostics while the relay thread is absent, record backpressure
and establish whether the actual old build exits/panics if a reader closes.
Classify Venus's EONW subscription (`venus/src/transport.rs:581`), all CLI
subscriptions, accepted-but-unanswered CLI exchanges and the Update reply
connection exactly as transition step 3 requires. List carried, drained,
closed and recreated fds/workers, not just listeners. Inject target exec
failure and malformed transport/checkpoint header before mutation. A full
layout/pending-picker roundtrip belongs to S3, after checkpoint code exists.

Measure the **exec gap** from last old-image control/poll service to first
restored service: record timestamps, queued-client latency, host-exit reap
delay, stderr buffering and whether programs/Orbit continue progressing. Do
not claim zero pause from same-PID exec or invent a timing guarantee before
measuring. Inventory old CLI/tool closure roots after the old manager/client
images are gone using isolated `nix-store --gc --print-roots`; record the
effective daemon/procfs permissions and exact rooted output. Do not delete
roots or invoke collection against Lucca's environment. The Linux environment
scanner is the default hypothesis, not a reason to add retention machinery.
Observe effective shell PATH, `command -v eon` and resolved build before/after
the transition and in a newly created terminal; compare that to the environment
at exec seen by root discovery. EON_SESSION_BIN is present in product assembly;
shell overrides mean its presence alone does not prove command resolution.
Report success or a concrete no-go; a negative spike closes with evidence and
blocks later children for Lucca's decision.

**Implementation notes:** inventory first; use existing canonical protocols,
not a fake terminal or copied upstream code. Do not turn the probe into the
production implementation or add a generic handoff framework.

**Verification:** one isolated real-process spike through the repository's
sandbox/proof surface; retain exact image revisions, observations and failure
results. Commands/harness are selected and recorded by that session, after
reading `docs/DEVELOPMENT.md`; never exercise the person's live window.

**Stop conditions:** parentage/lease/lock invariants fail; full layout needs
terminal-state reconstruction; a new platform assumption, protocol or owner is
needed; source has drifted materially; the same check fails twice after a
reasonable fix. **Maintenance:** no new dependency; report minimum viable
handoff schema and estimated follow-on scope, then return for approval.


**Context:** the design and the abbreviated evidence paths are in eon-1bq8 record 001-decision ("Reference gate" and "Proposed transition"). Lucca approved S1 first, 2026-11-04: "agreed". Never touch the person's live Eon windows, supervisor or Orbit hosts. Use a private runtime directory and display only. Also report how often the private checkpoint and update.sock versions would have changed over recent history (opus-gate re-check).
close_reason: Spike done: GO with conditions (Opus gate)

# eon-t3fyd.1 — S1 evidence report: same-PID Runtime exec into a new build

**Verdict: GO** for the same-PID re-exec mechanism. No stop condition was hit.
One availability finding needs Lucca's attention before S2–S5 are filed (§9).

Spike session, 2026-11-05 (UTC-3 times below). Worktree tree `7e1dc72`
(`7e1dc7222687010f9679045d9f96d1b1ece6568c`), clean. Everything below ran in a
private headless Sway with a private HOME and `XDG_RUNTIME_DIR=/run/user/1000/kt3f`.
No live Eon window, supervisor, Orbit host, profile or GC root of Lucca's was
touched. No commit, branch, `br` write or collection was made.

## 1. What was run

- **Base package**: `nix build git+file:///home/lucca/pjs/eon/eon?rev=7e1dc72…#default` was
  already valid locally: `/nix/store/c27g74xhsfaymf2by3gp2xq0vrglfkr0-eon-0.1.16`. It
  supplies Orbit (`z7qmaz43…-yazelix-orbit-0.1.0`), Venus (`k8bg7fkr…-yazelix-venus-0.1.0`)
  and every tool. Both manager images use these same Orbit and Venus binaries,
  matching the design: Orbit hosts keep their binaries.
- **Probe**: a temporary patch, never committed, in a scratch copy of the tree
  (`spike/tree`, its own `git init`). It is `spike/probe-2.patch`: 960 added and 12 removed
  lines: `runtime/crates/eon-runtime/src/spike.rs` plus hooks in
  `supervisor.rs`, `sessions.rs`, `control.rs`, `subscriptions.rs` and `lib.rs`.
  It uses only existing owners and validators. There is no fake terminal and no
  copied upstream code.
- **Two manager images**: release `cargo build -p eon` of that tree, differing only in
  `spike.rs` `MARK` (`image-A`/`image-B`), so they have different source digests.
  - A: `eon-A2.bin` sha256 `e660b2cc…b6e5`.
  - B: `eon-B2.bin` sha256 `c5c5c778…b42d`.
  - Each binary is wrapped exactly like the package's `bin/eon`, including every
    `eon-*` multi-call launcher, with `EON_SESSION_BIN` naming the image's own
    `libexec/eon/bin`. The images were added to the store and rooted under `spike/root-*`:
    - A3 `/nix/store/6bymcbl7r4h3y59r0l4cjk8cjcn83xqa-img-A3`
    - B3 `/nix/store/ysngfsc0gcdjknbil5kkx04hy0r3b8j1-img-B3`
- **Harness**: `spike/scripts/run.sh A3 B3 OUT`. It launches A, creates a committed
  directory tab with a nushell pane `p1`, a ticker pane and an exiter pane, and
  leaves the startup tab pending on its Files picker. It then drives these steps:
  1. Target exec failure.
  2. Malformed checkpoint header.
  3. A→B, with a 3 s gap injected at the resume entry. During the gap the exiter
     is released, a CLI client queues and Venus's stderr pipe is filled.
  4. B→A with the old Venus's stderr read end closed in the target.
  5. Explicit Stop from A's CLI.
- **Trigger**: a spike-only `spike-exec` file in the generation directory, read
  between loop turns. It is not a product mechanism.
- **Runs**: run4 and run5 are complete and agree. run0–run3 were harness
  iterations; their causes are recorded in §8.

## 2. Ownership continuity (acceptance: PID, Orbit identities, objects, lease)

| Item | Before (A) | After A→B and B→A | Evidence |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Manager PID | 3136533 (run4), 3213660 (run5) | same PID; `/proc/PID/exe` A3→B3→A3 | `trace.log` pid fields; `snap-3`, `snap-4` |
| Orbit hosts | 4 hosts, e.g. `session-1` pid 3137047, start 21557646, run `3136533-1793884292470715591-2` | identical PID, start and run IDs | `exec: carry …` vs `resume: adopted …` |
| Record, presentation and management objects | e.g. run4 `session-2` record 55:17351, presentation 55:17349, management 55:17350 | identical | same trace lines |
| Management lease | lease fd 7/11/14/17, one per host | the same fds, adopted after `read_management_record` plus `validate_management_identity(require_live_endpoints)` plus `validate_management_peer`; no reacquire, no second reader | `resume: adopted live …` |
| Lifecycle lock | `supervisor-<gen>.lock` fd 3, flock | still held: a fresh open in the target got `WouldBlock` | `resume: lifecycle lock still held by the inherited description` |
| `eon.sock` listener | fd 5, socket inode 55:17346 | adopted fd 5 after a path inode and `SO_ACCEPTCONN` check; never rebound | `resume: listener adopted fd=5 obj=55:17346` |
| Window start | `started_at` from A | carried in the checkpoint and reused | probe |
| Launcher record | `→ img-A3/libexec/eon/bin/eon` | `→ img-B3/…`, then back to A3 | `resume: launcher record …` |
| Zombie children of the manager | 0 | 0 in every snapshot (run4: 6 snapshots) | `snap-*` zombie section filtered on ppid |

- **Orbit exiting during exec.** `session-4`'s program exited 77 ms after `execve`,
  inside the injected gap (`exiter-exit-ns`). The target found its record already a
  tombstone. It adopted the lease from the tombstone identity plus the lease's
  `SO_PEERCRED`. Existing reconciliation then ran: lease EOF, then
  `wait_and_finalize_tombstone`, then exact-PID `reap_untracked_child`.
  - The supervisor log has exactly one `terminal session-4 ended with status 7`.
  - The session is absent from the next exec's carry list.
  - No zombie remained.
  - Timing (run4): the program's exit marker came 77.2 ms after `execve` (run5:
    69.5 ms). The reconciliation line was logged about 2.94 s after that marker,
    after the injected gap.
  - The Orbit host's own exit and the `waitpid` completion have no timestamps, so
    the host-exit-to-reap delay is **unmeasured**. It is bounded by the gap
    plus one turn.
- **Stop after resume.** `eon stop GEN --json` ran from image A after A→B→A. It
  returned `{"stopped":{…"sessions":["session-2","session-1","session-3","session-5"]}}`,
  exit 0. After 3 s the supervisor, all 5 Orbit host PIDs (one had already ended) and all 8 PTY-side processes
  recorded before the Stop were gone, and the generation directory was removed
  (run5 `after-stop.txt`). The target's supervisor ended `Ok(0)`.
- **Target exec failure.** `execve(<B>.missing)` returned ENOENT. The old image
  restored CLOEXEC on every carried fd, closed the memfd and kept serving. Its
  snapshot after the failure shows the same supervisor, hosts and objects.
  - **Not undone:** the probe had already closed the subscriptions before
    `execve`, so a failed exec still cost Venus one resubscribe.
  - The product must treat ending subscriptions as the irreversible first step,
    or end them only after the last refusable check.
- **Malformed checkpoint header.** The target's read-only validation child
  (`EON_SPIKE_VALIDATE`, checkpoint on stdin) refused `unsupported checkpoint header`
  before any mutation. No fd flag was changed and no subscription was dropped.
  Validation costs 10–31 ms per attempt.

**Correction to the design record:** the record says a started session has
`child: None`. That holds only for acquired sessions. `start_orbit` stores the
`std::process::Child` (`runtime/crates/eon-runtime/src/sessions.rs:1755`). A `Child`
cannot cross exec. The target therefore carries `child: None`, and the existing
exact-PID `reap_untracked_child` path does the reaping (`sessions.rs:1931`,
`:2058`). That path proved sufficient. No new reaper is needed.

## 3. Exec gap (measured; no zero-pause claim)

**Service gap: a proxy; the exact S1 measure is incomplete.** Each loop turn runs
`accept` (serve one request), then `end_turn`, and only then reads the trigger
(`spike/tree/…/supervisor.rs:1162`, `:1189`). The old image's last control/poll
service is therefore the `accept` of the turn that logged `exec: trigger`. That
accept's own timestamp was **not logged**. The interval below runs from the
trigger read, just after the last service, to the first restored turn. It
understates the true gap by that turn's unlogged accept-to-trigger time. S4b
should log both service boundaries.

| Exec | Trigger read → first restored loop turn |
| --- | --- |
| B→A, no injected gap | 18.9 ms (run3), 25.8 ms (run4), 44.1 ms (run5) |
| A→B, 3 s injected | 3 043 ms (run3, run4), 3 056 ms (run5) |

The old-image share before `execve` (export, the validation child, inventories)
was about 21.5 ms in run4. Validation alone is 10–31 ms and could move ahead of
the safe boundary in the product.

**From `execve`.** Times from `execve` in the old image to each event, in
CLOCK_REALTIME microseconds from the trace:

| Exec | Checkpoint decoded | Ownership adopted | First loop turn | Target Venus named | First request served |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| run4 B→A (no injected gap) | 13 584 | 14 076 | 14 858 | 36 712 | 62 024 |
| run3 B→A | 7 632 | 7 810 | 8 133 | 19 694 | 44 848 |
| run5 B→A | 20 599 | 21 180 | 22 268 | 43 969 | 69 173 |
| A→B (3 s injected) | 19 191–21 670 | +3 000 ms | 3 021.7 ms (run4), 3 023.8 ms (run5) | 3 045.8–3 065.9 ms | 3 021.8 ms (run4), 3 023.9 ms (run5) |

"First request served" is the first turn that accepted any connection. The probe
does not log which client it was (the queued CLI or Venus's resubscribe), and one
connection is accepted per turn.

- **Floor.** Without an injected gap, the old image's last service is the turn that
  read the trigger. The target's first loop turn followed 8–22 ms after `execve`.
  That interval covers the bash wrapper, the dynamic loader, decode and adoption.
  Venus was replaced and named to the hosts 20–44 ms after `execve`.
  - These are three samples on a lightly loaded machine. `uptime` before the runs
    read 3.74 (run3), 1.42 (run4) and 1.61 (run5), from this session's shell; it
    is not in the run directories.
  - No timing guarantee is claimed.
- **Queued client.** It started during the injected gap, 74 ms after `execve`. It
  was `eon workspace --json` from A's CLI, so the request crossed into the B image
  under the same EONW.
  - The listener backlog held it, and the target answered it.
  - Its latency was 2.993 s (run4) and 2.989 s (run5), about the remaining gap. It exited 0 with the
    correct generation.
- **Programs and Orbit kept progressing.**
  - The ticker pane printed and logged every 50 ms. It shows no inter-tick gap over
    80 ms within ±4 s of `execve` (median 53 ms).
  - The exiter's program ended inside the gap, and its Orbit published a tombstone.
- **Wayland surface.** The old Venus exited 0 on control EOF, 20–43 ms after the
  target's first turn. The target Venus is a new process and a new surface on the
  private Sway. No surface continuity is claimed; this matches approved question 3.

## 4. Venus control, stderr pipe and backpressure

- **Control continuity.** Venus's presentation-control socket (fd 6) and its stderr
  read end (fd 9) crossed exec. The old Venus process stayed alive through the 3 s
  gap (its window was not captured). It exited cleanly when the target
  deliberately shut down control.
  The target reaped it with exact-PID `waitpid`: `Ok(Some(0))` in all 4 replacements.
- **Stderr while no relay thread exists.** The pipe capacity is 65 536 bytes
  (`F_GETPIPE_SZ`).
  - During the gap, `/proc/<venus>/fd/2` (the same pipe) absorbed a 40-byte marker
    and 65 472 filler bytes, then returned EAGAIN.
  - The target found 65 512 unread bytes and restarted the relay. The old Venus's
    output reached the supervisor log, and the relay thread finished when Venus
    exited.
  - **Backpressure is real.** A gap long enough for Venus to write more than 64 KiB
    would block a blocking `stderr` writer in Venus until the target's relay
    resumes. The product should restart the relay first.
  - In run4 and run5 the filler stayed within DiagnosticLog's 983 040-byte copy
    bound (`diagnostics.rs:23`): the resumed log is 65 897 bytes. The bound's
    warning appeared only in the earlier run1/run2, where the probe ran against an
    unrelayed old image.
- **Reader closed (EPIPE).** In B→A with `close-stderr`, the target dropped the
  inherited read end before detaching the old Venus.
  - That Venus still exited 0, with no panic.
  - Venus ignores SIGPIPE (`SigIgn: 0000000000001000`, signal 13), so a write fails
    with EPIPE instead of killing it. The helper ignores write errors
    (`venus/src/application.rs:5490` at this tree).
  - **Limit:** nothing forced the actual Venus to write after the close beyond its own
    exit path. "No panic" is proved only for that path. Keep the read end, as the
    design says.

## 5. Subscriptions and connections (transition step 3 classification)

- **Venus's EONW subscription** (`venus/src/transport.rs:581`): the old image had
  exactly one subscriber each time. It was closed without a frame (the spike's
  stand-in for `updating`).
  - Venus's `run_subscription` retries on EOF.
  - Its reconnect queued in the backlog and was served by the target. The run5
    `snap-0` `ss` listing shows the subscriber as its own `eon.sock` connection.
  - Classification: **ended before exec, recreated by the client.** No partial
    frame crossed exec.
- **CLI subscriptions**: none exist at this revision. `eon events` and `eon pane wait`
  are still `eon-ciwn.8` and `.9` (`runtime/crates/eon-runtime/src/cli/parity.rs:97`).
  Classification for when they land: end before exec with `updating`.
- **Accepted-but-unanswered CLI exchanges**: none can exist at the exec point.
  `handle_client` accepts, dispatches and writes inside one turn
  (`runtime/crates/eon-runtime/src/control.rs:553`–`:586`), and the probe execs only
  after `end_turn`.
  - Connections not yet accepted stay in the inherited listener's backlog. The
    target answered one (the queued client above).
  - Classification: **drained by construction; the backlog is carried.** This
    proves connection ownership only. The handler bounds I/O and ignores a write
    failure (`control.rs:562`, `:586`), so a slow, partial or lost reply was not
    injected and remains unexercised.
- **Update reply connection**: **not exercised.** The spike has no `update.sock` and
  uses a trigger file. Its classification is carried, like a lease: fd plus request
  ID plus reply progress. That remains unproved and is S4a/S4b work.

## 6. File descriptors and workers

From `exec: fds before` and `resume: entry fds` (run4; run5 has the same shape):

| Class | Descriptors |
| --- | --- |
| **Carried** (CLOEXEC cleared, re-set on adoption) | lifecycle lock (3), `eon.sock` listener (5), Venus presentation control (6), Venus stderr read end (9), each management lease (7, 11, 14, 17), checkpoint memfd (8 in the target) |
| **Inherited by default** | stdin `/dev/null` (0), stdout and stderr to the launch log (1, 2) |
| **Closed** | Venus's subscriber stream: closed by the probe before exec; its fd 8 was then reused for the memfd. Per-generation diagnostic log file (4): CLOEXEC; the target creates a fresh timestamped file (`diagnostics.rs:237`, `create_new`). 3 `try_clone` pairs of connected Unix stream sockets (10/12, 13/15, 18/19 in run4): CLOEXEC. Their exact owners were **not identified**; the likely mechanism is the pane-metadata observer (`pane_labels.rs:143`). The target ran normally without them, and S4b must name each one. |
| **Recreated** | diagnostic log (a new file), Running window-scan worker, quota workers, pane-metadata workers, Venus stderr relay, attention poller state, subscriber streams, target Venus process |

- **Threads.** Before exec: main, `eon-running-win`, `eon-diagnostic-` (relay),
  `eon-codex-quota`, `eon-claude-quot` and `eon-pane-metada`×N. At the target's
  entry, only the main thread exists. Every worker was restarted through ordinary
  startup.
- **Leak check.** Only the allowlist plus stdio and the memfd reached the target.
  A future product must also close the memfd after reading it (the probe does) and
  must not let a carried fd reach later children. Every carried fd was set back to
  CLOEXEC on adoption, and `held_child=false`.

## 7. Old CLI, PATH and Nix roots

- **Old terminal, before and after the transition.**
  - Pane `p1` was created by A. Its shell's effective PATH is
    `~/.config/carapace/bin`, then `img-A3/libexec/eon/bin`. `command -v eon` gives
    `img-A3/libexec/eon/bin/eon`, which resolves to `img-A3/bin/eon`. All of this
    holds both before and after A→B (`path-old-before.txt`, `path-old-after.txt`).
  - `/proc/<shell>/environ` at exec starts PATH with `img-A3/libexec/eon/bin`;
    the shell's startup added carapace ahead of it afterwards.
  - The old terminal stays pinned to its creation build's CLI.
- **New terminal.** A pane created by B after the transition resolves `img-B3`, with
  `EON_SESSION_BIN` and PATH from B (`path-new-pane.txt`). The shell's PATH comes from
  the multi-call `eon-nu` launcher of the build that started the terminal.
- **Implicit CLI targeting.** B's CLI without `--generation` answered
  `missing-supervisor … generation g1-d40ee4f5b28e7b130d332754bb05eb98`, its own build's
generation (run4 `snap-3`). With
  `--generation` it worked. A's old CLI kept working, since EONW is equal and the
  generation is unchanged. This is S2's active-build selection work, now observed.
- **GC roots.** Run while the manager executed B3, by
  `nix-store --gc --print-roots`, read-only:
  - Determinate Nix 3.21.2 (2.34.7); the `nix-daemon` runs as root.
  - `kernel.yama.ptrace_scope=1`; `/proc` is mounted without `hidepid`.
  - Every old Orbit host and its PTY programs rooted `img-A3` through
    `/proc/PID/environ`, for example `/proc/3137050/environ -> …img-A3`.
  - The manager rooted `img-B3` through `environ`, `exe` and `maps`.
  - The old CLI closure therefore stays live while any old terminal lives,
    through the Linux environment scanner, without retention machinery.
  - **Limit:** the images were added with `nix-store --add`, which registers no
    references. Rooting of their dependencies through the images is therefore not
    shown. The base package was also rooted by an out-link.

## 8. Harness iterations (not product findings, except where noted)

| Run | Cause |
| --- | --- |
| run0 | The default window's runtime is `$RUN/eon`, not `w/<id>`. |
| run1–2 | The startup tab stayed pending on its Files picker. The probe correctly **refused** exec: "session-2 is starting, stopping or finished". The refusal exposed the held-`Child` correction in §2. |
| run3 | `eon windows` and `window stop all` cover only independent windows, so the queued client and the Stop did not reach this supervisor. The image's `eon-nu` was a symlink to the base package's launcher, which re-pinned PATH to the base build. Fixed by copying the image wrapper under every launcher name. |

Each fix touched only the harness or the probe's own guard. No product behaviour
was altered.

## 9. Recent version churn (Opus gate re-check request)

The private checkpoint and `update.sock` do not exist yet, so their churn is
estimated through proxies, from `git log --since=2026-10-16` on this tree.

- **Orbit management** (`orbit/crates/protocol/src/management.rs` `VERSION`)
  changed **5 times in 20 days**:
  - `0c2c70f` gen 2, `2e7f6e6` gen 3, `9c90032` v4, `016e9ad` v5, `eba3f80` v6.
  - Under the approved exact-gate, no-adapter rule, a target Runtime refuses old
    hosts on an older management version. Every update spanning one of these
    bumps would be refused: about one in every 4 days, comparable to the EONW
    concern the gate fixed.
- **Checkpoint-relevant Runtime state.** Over the same window, `workspace.rs` had
  46 commits, `attention.rs` 26, `sessions.rs` 54 and `supervisor.rs` 71.
  - A coarse search of struct declaration lines found 3 commits:
    `git log --since=2026-10-16 -G 'pub\(super\) struct (WorkspaceSet|Tab|Workspace)|^struct SupervisorState|struct Attention' -- runtime/crates/eon-runtime/src`.
    It undercounts field changes, which edit lines other than the declaration:
    `a928317` added `RunningSession.default_shell`, and `ff6aeb4` changed `number`'s
    type.
  - **Hypothesis, pending S3:** a checkpoint schema that versions only on field
    changes would change less often than these files. S3 must measure that from
    the schema.
- **`update.sock`**: no history. It carries only lifecycle data, so it should be the
  most stable of the three.

**Decision input for Lucca, not a stop.** The management gate, not the mechanism,
is likely the binding availability limit. That is a prediction: it is measured
for management, and checkpoint churn is unmeasured until S3. The options are:

- accept refusal across a management bump;
- make Orbit management changes additive under one version;
- choose a bounded compatibility rule.

The last option conflicts with "no legacy code" and is only named, not
recommended.

## 10. Minimum viable handoff schema (for S3/S4b; draft)

One versioned private format with an exact header and no negotiation. It is
transported over one inherited fd: the probe used a Linux `memfd`. A POSIX
product should use a pipe or unlinked file, written before exec and bounded. A
Linux-only data field must not appear in it.

```
header            format id + exact version         (refuse on mismatch, before mutation)
lifetime          generation, runtime dir, launch mode, window started_at
                  creation build, active build (from S2)
exec              realtime ns at execve; monotonic rebase input (S3 timers)
listener          fd, socket dev:ino                (path rechecked; SO_ACCEPTCONN)
locks             lifecycle-lock fd; namespace launch-lock fd (S2)
update_reply      fd, request id, reply progress    (S4a/S4b; unproved here)
venus[]           pid, process start, control fd, stderr-read fd
                  (probe used pid only; add start time)
session[]         lease fd, record path, record dev:ino, default_shell, origin_build
workspace         S3's logical topology/allocator/dedup/attention payload
```

Excluded: Rust `Child` objects (they become exact-PID tracking), threads, event
buffers, subscriber streams, worker sockets, raw pointers and `Instant`.

## 11. Follow-on scope estimate

- **S4b (re-exec).** The probe is 960 added lines with no tests; part of it is tracing and fd and thread inventory that a product would not carry.
  Productised (`/proc/self/cmdline`, memfd and trigger file replaced; failure undo
  and restore-failure outcome; real-process integration test), expect 700–1 000
  lines plus tests in Runtime. That is one fresh session once S3 exists.
- **S3 (checkpoint).** Encoding `WorkspaceSet`, attention and the session extras
  (pending picker, which run1–2 showed must cross exec) is the largest slice. It may
  need splitting into model encode/validate and supervisor wiring.
- **S2, S4a and S5** are unchanged by this evidence. S2 gains one concrete falsifier:
  the target CLI's implicit target (§7).
- Keep the planned order. Add the §9 decision before filing S2.

## 12. Stop-condition check

| Condition | Result |
| --- | --- |
| Parentage, lease or lock invariant fails | No: all held |
| Full layout needs terminal-state reconstruction | No: only Runtime state (S3); Orbit untouched |
| New platform assumption, protocol or owner | None needed. `memfd` and `/proc/self/cmdline` are probe conveniences with POSIX replacements (§10, §11). |
| Source drift | Not material. Management v6 (`eba3f80`) landed after the design tree `83103ff`. Line numbers are re-cited here at `7e1dc72`. |
| Same check fails twice after a fix | No: run4 and run5 agree |

## Evidence files

All under `/home/lucca/.cache/eon-agents/eon-t3fyd-1-work/spike/`:

- `run4/` and `run5/`: `trace.log`, `steps.txt`, `snap-*.txt`, `path-*.txt`,
  `gc-roots.txt`, `queued-client.txt`, `stderr-probe.txt`, `stop.txt`,
  `after-stop.txt`, `ticker.log`, `exiter-exit-ns`, `venus-signals.txt` and the
  supervisor log.
- `probe-2.patch`, `scripts/` and `eon-A2.bin` / `eon-B2.bin`.

comments.text:
# Opus gate: eon-t3fyd.1 (S1 same-PID exec spike)

**Verdict: GO WITH CONDITIONS.** The mechanism holds. The probe hooks the real supervisor, validators, Orbit and Venus, with no stubs. Two complete runs agree on every ownership invariant and on Stop after resume. Several items were only partly exercised; the report omits one.

## Findings, ranked

1. **High: helper children cross exec and are never reaped.** CodexBarCLI quota fetches (`quota.rs:827`, 8 s timeout) and zoxide visits (`supervisor.rs:1839`) spawn children. The target reaps only the exact PIDs it has recorded, and there is no SIGCHLD handler, so a helper in flight at exec becomes a permanent zombie. No helper was in flight in the spike, so quiescing was never exercised.
2. **Medium: the layout was silently collapsed.** Before, run5 had a pending picker tab t1 plus t2 (`snap-0`). After, it had a single t1, where the picker's Yazi is an ordinary pane (`snap-3`). The report (§11) blames run1–2's refusal on the picker. The trace shows that refusal was the held `Child` guard, which every started host trips (`held_child=true` on all four).
3. **Medium: lease drain was never exercised.** Export refuses while a request is in flight, but that case never occurred. `answered_status` (`sessions.rs:882`) is dropped without a word.
4. **Medium: the whole environment passes through exec.** `spike::exec` forwards the old environ. Shared component paths hid the leak. With different Orbit paths, `TERMINFO_DIRS` grows on each update, and variables a newer wrapper drops survive.
5. **Medium: failure injection was narrow.** Only ENOENT and a bad header were injected. Never tested: a failed restore after exec, an identity mismatch, or a management-version mismatch. A and B share their Orbit and Venus binaries.
6. **Low: the measurements are proxies.** The gap figure is a proxy from 3 samples. Unmeasured: host-exit-to-reap, and the user-visible window gap. Old-Venus actions queued during the gap are discarded.
7. **Low: two loose ends.** The clone pairs are pane-metadata observers (`pane_labels.rs:143`), not leases, so closing them is fine. The old Venus was reaped by PID with no start-time check.

## Handoff schema

It is minimal and right for ownership, and the exclusions are correct. Peer credentials survive exec in the kernel. Missing:
- the helper children: quiesce them, or record their PIDs for reaping only;
- per Venus: the window and session mapping and admission state (eon-hyil8);
- named pending pair and picker state in S3's payload;
- a carry or discard rule for `answered_status`;
- in `update_reply`: the validated caller, its origin build and the target;
- the launch-time argv and environment;
- naming-retry deadlines and the attention epoch, under the monotonic rebase.

## Conditions for the follow-on

**S4b**
- Quiesce workers and their children before the point of no return.
- Drain lease requests, with a bound.
- Exec from the launch-time environment.
- End subscriptions only after the last check that can still refuse.
- Restart the stderr relay first, and keep the read end until Venus exits.
- Check the Venus start time.
- Log both service boundaries.
- Test a host exiting before, during and after exec.
- Inject restore failure, identity mismatch and a real management mismatch.
- Use distinct Orbit and Venus paths.

**S3**
- Round-trip the pending picker, or refuse while one is pending. Never flatten it.
- Version the checkpoint only on schema changes, and report its churn. If it changes more often than management does, return to Lucca.

**S5**
- Freeze old-Venus window actions during the transition.
- Measure the user-visible gap.

**Sizing.** The estimate is optimistic.
- S4b: the probe is 960 lines with no tests, and product work adds failure paths, quiescing and tests. Split it:
  - S4b-1: exec, adoption, reap, undo, integration test;
  - S4b-2: quiescing, draining, restore-failure outcome, Venus carry.
- S3: split it now into model encode/validate and supervisor wiring.
- S5 has no estimate. Split it:
  - Venus replacement and the C39 `updating` end;
  - `eon update`, the stale-origin guard, docs and the Wayland proof.
- Expect about 9 sessions after eon-hyil8.

## Decision for Lucca

**1. Orbit management bumped 5 times in 20 days (3 since 10-31). Should Update keep refusing when the hosts' version differs from the target's?**

- **(a) Keep the exact gate (approved Q2).** A window that spans a bump keeps running with a reasoned refusal, and you move it by hand once per bump instead of after every refresh. No compatibility code.
- **(b) Additive management changes under one version.** This needs capability detection in every Runtime and an ORB-C change: compatibility code by another name.
- **(c) The target also speaks version N−1.** A shim, which the no-legacy rule excludes.

**Recommend (a).** Update still removes most manual moves, and the refusal path is required anyway. Batching management bumps costs nothing. Revisit if dogfooding shows that refusals dominate.

title: Add a Close button to Stack tabs that always asks before closing
description:
## Why

Lucca 2026-11-10, on header buttons for every titled element: "the problem is consistency, we cant
double notch the notched elements and leave stacks behind.. or we could, but we should land it right
after". This lands right after eon-5g0e5 (popup and sidebar Hide buttons). Treatment (Lucca, comment
2026-11-10 13:11 UTC): dual notch, a mirrored right action notch holding the button, shared with the
popup and Agents headings; panes never get notches.

Closing a Stack closes every pane in it, so it must not lose work. Overseer decision, 2026-11-10: a
Stack close ALWAYS asks, like closing a window with many tabs. The prompt lists every terminal the
close stops and marks the ones known to be running; Enter consents to exactly that list; any change
to the list while the prompt is open asks again.

This bead is slice B, the Venus half. Slice A (the column close that always needs consent,
`eon column close`, and SetSidebar) is the Runtime and CLI bead eon-cq38r, which this one depends on.

Plan: /home/lucca/.cache/eon-agents/eon-stack-close-replan3-work/bead/t5boa-plan-v5.md, sections 2
(safety model), 5 (this bead) and 9 (landing), and section 1.1 for the Enter rule. Read it before
planning; it holds the exact contract text and the test list.

Codex re-checks of the plan, both "implement with these changes", both folded into plan v5:
/home/lucca/.local/state/rota/runs/stack-close-v3-recheck-codex-1/report.md and
/home/lucca/.local/state/rota/runs/stack-close-v4-recheck-codex-1/report.md.

## Scope

- Each Stack tab gets the right action notch with a Close button (eon-5g0e5's shared notch, button
  drawing, `HeadingAction` and input plumbing). No button while a pane is zoomed or where it cannot
  fit. Pointer, keyboard (Tab stop after the pane's Close) and AccessKit.
- The button sends the column close with no consent, for every Stack, one pane or many. Runtime
  stops nothing and answers `Confirm` with what the close would stop.
- Venus shows one close prompt worded from that answer alone: every terminal the close stops, by
  name, the running ones marked, runs no tab tracks included, and the final-close consequence when
  it is a final close. Escape sends nothing.
- Confirmation delay: after the prompt's list is first presented, and again each time it is
  presented with a changed scope, Enter (and any confirm control added later) is ignored for 400 ms,
  and until one full event-loop turn that began after that presentation has finished. A key press
  that arrives inside the delay is discarded, not deferred: it does nothing then or later, and the
  prompt stays open. A queued Enter is delivered within milliseconds of the presentation, so it
  cannot confirm. No winit change and no dependency change (overseer decision, 2026-11-10: eon-9rtt
  is retiring the forks). The split comment below that says the rule needs the winit fork to carry
  key event time is superseded by this.
- An accepted Enter sends the consent for exactly that answer: its generation, the run IDs of its
  terminals and untracked runs, and its end. A second `Confirm` means the list changed: the prompt
  shows again from the new answer, says so, and starts its delay again.
- The prompt does not depend on `warning_close_last_tab` or on what is running.
- Contract text: VEN-C8, VEN-C18 and one EON-C8 sentence. Docs (USAGE, PRESENTATION,
  CONFIGURATION), CHANGELOG, venus/CHANGELOG.

Out of scope: busy prompts for pane and tab closes (eon-qi5nh, which reuses this prompt); the Enter
rule for the existing tab, pane and quit prompts; any change to what Runtime checks; new settings.

## Contract and reference gate

Changes VEN-C8, VEN-C18 and EON-C8: a consequential code shape. Record the owners (Runtime: what a
close stops, the running marks, and whether a consent matches; Venus: the button, the prompt, the
confirmation delay, and sending a consent only on an accepted Enter) and the references the Runtime
bead recorded, plus one comparable for the delay at an exact revision (candidates: Firefox's
`security.dialog_enable_delay`, Chromium's `InputEventActivationProtector`). Portability
disposition: neutral. The overseer approves the contract text; Codex reviews code and contract text.

Fixed values (rule 6), recorded here with their reasons:

- The confirmation delay is fixed at 400 ms and has no setting. It is a safety floor, not a
  preference: it decides whether a key press can count as consent to stopping terminals. A shorter
  value lets a queued or double-pressed Enter approve a list nobody read; 400 ms is far above the
  milliseconds a queued key takes to arrive after the presentation, above a person's reaction time
  (about 250 ms), and at the usual double-press interval, while a deliberate answer never waits for
  it. If it is ever exposed, 400 ms is its minimum.
- The prompt has no setting and ignores `warning_close_last_tab` (safety: the answer is the consent
  that binds the close to its runs).
- The button's glyph, label and geometry stay fixed as the pane buttons' do (eon-ipc6f's recorded
  reason).

## Prerequisites

eon-cq38r (slice A, Runtime and CLI), and eon-5g0e5 (which needs eon-2ibdd). It lands with or after
slice A, in the window restart slice A needs (plan section 9).

## Size

One session. The confirmation delay is one pure function, one counter and two fields.

## Acceptance

- Close on any Stack (idle, busy, one pane, the last Stack of the last tab with the warning setting
  off) shows the prompt first, listing every terminal it stops and marking the running ones; Esc
  keeps the Stack; Enter closes exactly the listed terminals.
- Venus sends a consent only on an accepted Enter in that prompt, never from a snapshot
  (regression).
- A queued Enter delivered right after the prompt's list was presented is ignored and discarded:
  nothing is sent then, and nothing is sent when the delay ends. This includes a second Enter behind
  the first when Runtime answered with a larger list, and an Enter delivered before the list was
  presented at all. A new Enter after the delay confirms (regressions: early delivery, delayed
  delivery, discarded not deferred, Enter after the delay).
- With the prompt open, a pane joining or leaving the Stack, the anchor pane moving, a terminal
  started under a listed terminal's number, or the close becoming final makes Enter show the prompt
  again, saying the Stack changed, instead of closing (regressions). Work starting in a listed
  terminal does not: Enter closes it.
- A `Confirm` that arrives after local input opens nothing.
- Captures in dark and light, narrow width and zoomed, from a candidate package under an isolated
  display and Eon root; Venus focused tests; fmt and clippy; whole-workspace `eon-test` once.
- After landing and Lucca's window restart: one isolated installed observation from the refreshed
  profile.

title: Venus AccessKit focus may name a hidden Shortcuts header button
description:
## Defect (suspected, found while fixing eon-accesskit-orphan-content-9nbd; not reproduced)

`Snapshot::tree` (`venus/src/accessibility.rs`, focus match) maps `WorkspaceFocus::Header(control)`
to `control_node_id(control)`, but the header-control loop skips any control whose
`rect.width <= 0.0`. Only Shortcuts can have zero width: `scene.rs` hides it when the hints bar
is complete and `keep_shortcuts` is false. If the accessibility snapshot's `workspace_focus` is
`Header(Shortcuts)` while its scene hides Shortcuts, the update's focus names a node that is not in
the tree, and accesskit_consumer 0.38.0 unwraps it in `State::focus` (`tree.rs:546`) while the
host is focused, so Venus exits.

The scene keeps Shortcuts while focus is on it (`keep_shortcuts`, `scene.rs:812`), so this needs
the snapshot focus and the scene's focus to diverge. Whether any path sets
`Snapshot::workspace_focus` without rebuilding the scene with that focus is unverified.

## Contract

Venus accessibility (VEN-C18 workspace header controls): Venus must not exit.

## Acceptance

First establish reachability: trace every writer of `Snapshot::workspace_focus` and of the scene
passed to `set_workspace`. If reachable, add a red/green test through accesskit_consumer's Tree
(the dev-dependency eon-accesskit-orphan-content-9nbd added; its `IgnoreChanges` handler) and make
focus fall back to the selected tab when the control is hidden. If unreachable, record the proof
and close.

## Scope boundary

Only header-control focus. No change to hints or header layout.

## Revalidation at dcaef1c (2026-11-12)

The originally suspected hiding condition no longer exists: no keep_shortcuts

title: Research whether Codex and Claude Code sandboxes can reach the Eon socket
description:
## Why

Approved item 8 (eon-agent-parity-a9g0, 2026-10-30). If an agent sandbox allows connect() on AF_UNIX sockets, it reaches EONW: `eon pane create -- COMMAND` already runs an unsandboxed command for it, and `eon pane send` would let it type into an unsandboxed shell. Unverified for Codex's Linux sandbox and Claude Code's sandbox. Answer before `eon pane send` ships.

## Scope

In scope: run, from inside each sandbox (Codex read-only and workspace-write, Claude Code's sandboxed Bash), `eon workspace --json` and `eon pane create --no-focus -- true` against an isolated Eon; record which succeed and why (socket path visibility, seccomp, network rules). Recommend what Eon should say or do (docs warning, refusing callers whose credentials show a sandbox, nothing).

Out of scope: changing Eon; the hardening bead.

## Acceptance

- A comment with the result per sandbox and mode, and a recommendation for Lucca.

## Verification

- Each result cites the exact command, sandbox mode and output.
close_reason: Answered in this bead's 2026-10-30 result comment: default Codex and Claude Code sandboxes block the Eon socket; Codex network_access and Claude Code allowAllUnixSockets reach it and escape via pane create. eon-overseer decided a docs warning only (2026-10-30), added to eon-agent-parity-a9g0.18's scope.

comments.author: lucca
comments.text:
Result (2026-10-30, eon-t85gf research; no product code or git changes).

Setup: one isolated Eon (installed profile eon /nix/store/8s4gif4cdj6l70akszv87z1iyikc6ixc-eon-0.1.8,
private headless Sway, HOME and XDG_RUNTIME_DIR=/run/user/1000/kt85 of its own, cleanup by exact
PID; Lucca's Eon untouched). Each sandbox ran `bash probe.sh TAG` with the environment copied from
one of that Eon's terminals (EON_TERMINAL, XDG_RUNTIME_DIR; that Eon was launched as a single
window, so no EON_WINDOW_RUNTIME_DIR, as in Lucca's terminals). The probe prints its seccomp and
namespace state, raw `connect()` on eon.sock, orbit.sock and orbit.sock.management, then
`eon workspace --json`, `eon pane create --no-focus -- true`, and
`eon pane create --no-focus -- sh -c '{ id; grep Seccomp…; readlink ns/mnt ns/net; } >$HOME/marker-TAG; sleep 15'`
(the marker path is outside every sandbox's writable roots). Codex 0.166.0 (gpt-6.1-sol, low
effort, personal account checked); Claude Code 2.1.303 (`claude -p --model claude-haiku-5-5
--settings …`, API credits, isolated HOME). Scripts, briefs and full logs:
~/.cache/eon-agents/claude-t85gf-work/ (harness.sh, probe.sh, run-codex.sh, run-claude.sh,
log-*/report-*).

| Sandbox and mode | Command | Socket visible | connect() | eon workspace --json | eon pane create |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| None (baseline) | `bash probe.sh baseline` | yes | OK | OK (caller t1/p1) | OK; marker: Seccomp 0, host mnt/net ns |
| Codex `-s read-only` | `codex exec -s read-only` | yes | EPERM | `supervisor-unavailable … Operation not permitted (os error 1)` | same error, exit 4; no marker |
| Codex `-s workspace-write` | `codex exec -s workspace-write` | yes | EPERM | same error | same error, exit 4; no marker |
| Codex workspace-write + network | `codex exec -s workspace-write -c sandbox_workspace_write.network_access=true` | yes | OK (all three) | OK | `-- true`: reached Eon (`session-start: terminal command exited with status 0 during startup`, the baseline answer); marker pane p3 created, marker written: Seccomp 0, NoNewPrivs 0, host mnt and net ns |
| Claude Code sandbox, default | `--settings '{"sandbox":{"enabled":true,"autoAllowBashIfSandboxed":true,"allowUnsandboxedCommands":false}}'` | yes | `socket()` itself EPERM | same `Operation not permitted` error | same error, exit 4; no marker |
| Claude Code sandbox + `network.allowAllUnixSockets: true` | same plus `"network":{"allowAllUnixSockets":true}` | yes | OK (all three) | OK | marker pane p4 created, marker written: Seccomp 0, NoNewPrivs 0, host mnt and net ns |

The workspace exit status is not recorded: the probe printed echo's status there, not eon's.

Why:
- Path visibility never stops it. Both sandboxes mount the real filesystem read-only, so
  /run/user/1000/…/eon/generations/G/eon.sock is visible and stat-able in every mode.
- Codex: read-only and workspace-write run in new user, mount and net namespaces with a seccomp
  filter (Seccomp: 2). `socket(AF_UNIX)` succeeds and `connect()` returns EPERM, which matches Codex's
  network seccomp filter (allows only AF_UNIX sockets, denies connect). A pathname Unix socket is
  not scoped by the net namespace, so the namespace alone would not stop it. With
  `network_access=true` the process stays in the host net ns and the filter allows connect.
  Inferred from the observed errno and namespace state, not from Codex source.
- Claude Code: bubblewrap with its own net ns and a seccomp filter that denies `socket(AF_UNIX)`
  (EPERM at socket()). `allowAllUnixSockets: true` drops that filter (Seccomp: 0 inside), and
  connect to any same-user socket then works. A path list (`allowUnixSockets`) is not tested;
  seccomp cannot filter by path, so on Linux it is not expected to narrow anything.
- Once connected, Eon treats the caller as any same-user process (approved item 1): the pane
  command runs as a child of Eon's Orbit, outside the sandbox. The same opt-in modes also reach
  orbit.sock and orbit.sock.management (raw connect OK), i.e. the ORBS attach eon-ahzkt closes.
- Lucca's own setup has no sandbox to escape: ~/.codex/config.toml sets
  `sandbox_mode = "danger-full-access"`, and Claude Code here runs with sandboxing off (Seccomp 0).

So the escape exists today, before `eon pane send`: any sandbox mode that permits Unix-socket
connect turns `eon pane create -- CMD` into unsandboxed execution. Send adds typing into an
existing unsandboxed shell, which is the same class. Default modes of both tools block it.

Recommendation: a docs warning, not refusal.
1. Docs (in the pane create/send/read docs and eon/skills/eon/SKILL.md, shipped with a9g0.18 or
   earlier): "A sandboxed agent that may connect to Unix sockets (Codex workspace-write with network
   access, Claude Code with allowAllUnixSockets) can drive Eon, and `eon pane create`/`pane send`
   then run commands outside its sandbox. The default sandbox modes of both block this.
   `[agents] terminal_access` is not a security boundary." Recommended: cheap, accurate, and both
   opt-ins are explicit user choices.
2. Refusing sandboxed callers: rejected for now. The only signal is a heuristic on the SO_PEERCRED
   pid (seccomp filter, NoNewPrivs, or a mount ns differing from the supervisor's). It misses
   Landlock-only and macOS Seatbelt sandboxes, refuses legitimate callers in Flatpak, distrobox or
   container shells, races with pid reuse, and still leaves orbit.sock reachable unless Orbit
   repeats it. It would read as a boundary that it is not.
3. Nothing: rejected; the escape is non-obvious and worth one paragraph.
Send need not wait on this beyond carrying the docs paragraph.

title: A failed tab close ends the supervisor and the whole window
description:
## Report

Lucca, 2026-10-23 ~13:22 -03: "last window crashed when i tried close tab 2". The window was supervisor g1-f1f6b48b14309a0f4484891c8b29f1b5 (PID 3357673, profile r18mya95…-eon-0.1.1, EONW 18, started 06:28).

## Evidence (supervisor log ~/.local/state/eon/logs/g1-f1f6b48b14309a0f4484891c8b29f1b5-1792743714-3357673.log)

```
13:22:03.882 closing tab t3: stopping session-31, session-32
13:22:08.005 tab t3 close failed after 4122 ms: session-32: session-32: ended terminal record /run/user/1000/eon/generations/g1-f1f6…/session-32.sock.record disappeared; cannot reconcile terminal after failed stop: …
13:22:08.518 Eon Desktop exited: exit status: 0
13:22:08.519 supervisor failed: ended terminal record …/session-32.sock.record disappeared
```

So one terminal whose stop did not confirm, and whose ended record then vanished, turned a tab close into a supervisor failure. Venus exited and the whole window ended. Other tabs' terminals (Claude agents in tab t1) survived as orphaned Orbit hosts, still running, but with no supervisor or window to reach them.

## Expected

Closing a tab never ends the supervisor or other tabs. A terminal that can't be reconciled after a stop is reported (a VEN-C8 notice and a log line) and removed from the tab, or the tab stays with that terminal marked, but the workspace keeps running.

## Related

eon-jqxr (Closing tab 1 closed the whole window, 2026-10-21, EONW 13): same symptom, which was undiagnosed then because the supervisor logged nothing. This log is the first evidence of a mechanism; check whether jqxr is the same bug and fold it in. Contract owners: EON-C8 (tab close) and EON-C10 (failure kinds).

## Scope

Reproduce in an isolated session: close a tab whose terminal's stop times out or whose ended record disappears, for example by making the stop exceed its grace or removing the record mid-stop. Make the failure local to that tab. Add a red/green test at the Runtime level.

## Acceptance

- A Runtime test: an unreconcilable terminal during tab close leaves the supervisor running and other tabs intact, and reports the failure.
- An installed observation of the same in an isolated window.
close_reason: Failed tab close stays local; Runtime red/green and isolated installed observation recorded

comments.author: lucca
comments.text: Diagnosis (eon-7iap, 2026-10-23). Orbit's host failure path (orbit/src/host.rs run, Err arm: failed host, dead or stalled Bend worker) drops its RecordGuard, which removes the Live record and publishes no tombstone (orbit/src/management.rs Drop for RecordGuard). wait_and_finalize_tombstone failed on a missing record ('ended terminal record ... disappeared'). The failed stop left the terminal tracked, and the main loop's reap_finished_sessions returned the same error with '?', which ended the supervisor. Fix (Runtime sessions.rs): a vanished record whose recorded Orbit process is dead reconciles as owner-lost (endpoints checked and removed, child reaped), the same as a dead process with a Live record. While that Orbit still runs, the Runtime waits within the deadline. A tab close then prunes the terminal (status 1) and succeeds. No EON-C8/C10 wording change: EON-C8 already keeps a failed close local (eon-overseer agreed, 2026-10-23). eon-jqxr is a different bug: there the supervisor survived. Orbit's stderr gap (no trace of why its host failed) is out of scope; eon-overseer will raise it with Lucca. Red/green: supervisor::tests::a_terminal_whose_orbit_fails_during_a_close_ends_only_that_terminal kills one leased Orbit's worker, then runs the tab close's per-terminal stop. Red on 0ca4a64 failed with the incident's exact error; green: eon-runtime 85 passed, 1 ignored; fmt and clippy clean.

comments.author: lucca
comments.text: Evidence (eon-overseer found it; eon-7iap checked it, 2026-10-23). Lucca's windows run Orbit through a stderr-logging wrapper. ~/.local/share/eon/orbit-window/logs/675175.log (Orbit /nix/store/7vv3pwvpyir2r0vgmjczf90gw3ji2fbg-yazelix-orbit-0.1.0, started 16:21:57Z, 6 s before the 13:22 -03 close) ends with 'PTY child was not reaped after canonical session exit', which is the Bend worker's IO.die at orbit/src/main.bend:56. A dead worker takes Orbit's host failure path (orbit/src/host.rs run, Err arm): Orbit contains the child and drops its RecordGuard, removing the Live record without a tombstone. That matches the diagnosis above. The red/green test reproduces the same path by SIGKILLing a leased Orbit's worker. Why the worker found its PTY child unreaped during Stop is an Orbit defect outside this bead (reported to eon-overseer). Codex review round 1 (gpt-6.1-sol xhigh) on candidate tree abe1cf52: nothing blocking.

comments.author: lucca
comments.text: Proof (eon-7iap, 2026-10-23). Change: (1) sessions.rs wait_and_finalize_tombstone reconciles a vanished record whose recorded Orbit process is dead as owner-lost; while that Orbit still runs, it waits within the deadline. (2) supervisor.rs reap_finished_sessions no longer ends the supervisor for a tracked terminal whose Stop failed (RunningSession::stop_failed). The terminal stays in its tab for a retry, as EON-C8 says, and the log gets one note: 'terminal <id> stays in its tab after a failed stop: <error>'. CHANGELOG entry added. Test supervisor::tests::a_terminal_whose_stop_fails_during_a_close_ends_or_stays_only_in_its_tab covers three leased Orbits. One's worker is SIGKILLed: its close stop now returns Ok(Some(1)); red on 0ca4a64 with the incident error. One has a mode-0644 record, so its stop fails: two reaps return Ok, with exactly one note. Red with the containment disabled: reap returned Err(record must be mode-0600). The third terminal still stops normally. Checks on tree d68e57c3: nix develop -c eon-test -p eon-runtime gave 85 passed, 1 ignored; cargo fmt --check and clippy -D warnings are clean. Installed: build /nix/store/3q4g5b92q200xhp8dh2jnc7ds1ppyhsy-eon-0.1.1 from that tree, in an isolated headless Sway (pixman), x86_64 Linux, with ~/.cache/eon-agents/eon-7iap/iso/check.sh. Two tabs. Run A SIGKILLed t2's Orbit worker: the reap logged 'terminal session-2 ended with status 1; Orbit exited without publishing a terminal result' and pruned t2; the supervisor, Venus and t1 survived. Run B SIGSTOPped t2's worker, then ran eon tab close t2: 'closing tab t2: stopping session-2', then 'closed tab t2 in 2044 ms', exit 0. The supervisor's stderr shows the owner-lost line. The supervisor, Venus and t1 survived, with t1 active. Review ledger: 2 Claude rounds (round 1: 1 blocking, the missing containment, fixed; round 2: clean); Codex 2 passes (full: clean; narrow re-check abe1cf52..d68e57c3: clean, 1 nit not taken). Residuals sent to eon-overseer, who will put them to Lucca: a close that fails before Stop is written leaves stop_sent false, so a later reap error there still ends the supervisor; a failed-stop terminal whose lease closed and that never reconciles can make each reap wait up to 5 s; reap errors on never-stopped terminals still end the supervisor; the Orbit worker's 'PTY child was not reaped' defect. eon-jqxr is a different bug and stays open.

title: Create a tab with a directory and command, without the picker
description:
## Why

Eon is used with one tab per project. An orchestrating agent (the overseer) cannot start an agent in another project's tab. `eon tab create` always opens a pending tab with its directory picker, which waits for a person (EON-C18 Picker-first tab directories). `eon pane create -- COMMAND` adds a pane only to the caller's own tab (or the active tab). On 2026-10-23 the overseer moved nova's Claude session into Lucca's window and could put it only in a pane of the eon tab. Lucca asked "why not a new tab? it's a tab per project, normally" and then had to create the tab and type `claude --resume ...` by hand. Lucca asked for this bead the same day ("create the new bead").

## Goal

From an Eon terminal, one command creates a new tab with a given directory and, optionally, runs a command as that tab's first pane, with no picker and without moving the user's active tab or desktop focus. A sketch to settle at the contract step: `eon tab create [--json] [--no-focus] [--directory DIRECTORY] [-- COMMAND...]`.

## Contract (draft at the reference gate; Lucca approves the exact text before code)

- EON-C18 (docs/CONTRACTS.md:1443) amendment: a tab created with a directory skips the picker. The picker stays the default for a bare `eon tab create` and for the UI's new-tab action.
- EON-C8 (docs/CONTRACTS.md:357) and the CLI and EONW sections: the request carries the directory and the optional command. EONW v18 `WorkspaceAction::CreateTab` takes no payload (runtime/crates/eon-workspace-protocol/src/v18.rs:79), so this probably needs a new action or field and an EONW bump. Coordinate the version with the other EONW changes in flight (yx8.11 takes EONW 19).
- `--no-focus`: the user's active tab, selected pane, shown popup and desktop focus stay as they are, mirroring `pane create --no-focus`.
- Failures: a missing or unreadable directory, and a call from outside an Eon terminal, are each refused with a defined exit code, as for `pane create -- COMMAND`.
- The command runs exactly as given (no shell) at the tab's directory, as `pane create -- COMMAND` does.

## Reference gate

Consequential: the CLI, an EONW request and a contract change. Before code, record on this bead: the owner of each step (CLI → EONW → Runtime tab creation → Orbit terminal), the docs/REFERENCES.md routes read, and comparable implementations at inspected revisions: tmux `new-window -d -c DIR [cmd]`, WezTerm `cli spawn --new-window/--cwd`, kitty `@ launch --type=tab --cwd`, Zellij `action new-tab --cwd --layout`. Note what was kept and what was rejected.

## Scope

In scope: the contract text for Lucca's approval, the CLI, the EONW request, Runtime tab creation with a directory and an optional first-pane command, docs/USAGE.md, CHANGELOG.md, and focused tests.

Out of scope: sending text to existing panes (eon-pane-send-research-fo4p), naming tabs, Venus UI changes beyond rendering the new tab, and moving a live terminal between tabs.

## Acceptance

- A Runtime or CLI test: `tab create --no-focus --directory D -- cmd` yields a new non-pending tab at D whose only pane runs cmd, while the active tab and selected pane are unchanged.
- Bare `eon tab create` still opens the picker.
- One installed observation: from the overseer's popup, launch `claude` into a new `~/pjs/nova` tab; Lucca's view and focus stay where they were.

## Verification

Shared wire route: the affected Rust and Nix surfaces, converge plus Codex, the profile refresh, and one isolated installed observation.

Split before implementing if the EONW change and the CLI and Runtime work don't fit one fresh session (small-beads rule).
close_reason: Shipped at 459a7d1 (EONW v24, Eon 0.1.7); combined Nix proof and installed observation recorded. Site text follows in the release that ships it.

comments.author: lucca
comments.text:
Plan (Opus, 2026-10-29, base 0b6ef93). Fits one session: the EONW bump is mechanical (f495068 is the template), and the new behavior is one action.

Shape (pending the contract approval in the next comment):
- CLI: `eon tab create [--json] [--no-focus] --directory DIRECTORY [-- COMMAND [ARGS...]]`. Flags go in any order before `--`. A relative DIRECTORY resolves against the caller's working directory, as `eon edit FILE` does (std::path::absolute, so no symlink resolution). `--no-focus` or `-- COMMAND` without `--directory` is a usage error (exit 2). An empty or missing command after `--` is a usage error, as for `pane create --`. Bare `eon tab create [--json]` keeps sending CreateTab, so it still opens the picker.
- EONW v24 (if v23 is still the latest at landing; otherwise the next free version): a new `Action::LaunchTab { directory: Vec<u8>, argv: Vec<Vec<u8>>, focus: bool }` on the next free action byte (37). An empty argv means the default pane. The codec bounds the directory with validate_directory and a non-empty argv with validate_command. `WorkspaceAction::CreateTab` keeps its payload-free encoding, so Venus's new-tab code changes only in the v23→v24 rename.
- Runtime (runtime/crates/eon-runtime/src/workspace.rs): handle LaunchTab in `Workspace::apply`, next to `create_tab`. The order: a command without a caller fails with `caller-required`; `validated_directory` failures give `invalid-directory`; the MAX_TABS and identity checks give `capacity`; the argv goes through `prepare` at DIRECTORY (`pane-command`). Then push a non-pending tab with no popups and start its one pane with `start_pane_in(.., LaunchCommand::Pane | Tool(argv))`. If the start fails, pop the tab and fail with `session-start`. Advance `ids.next_tab` only on success. Set `self.active` only when focus is true. The workspace is the caller's, or the shown one without a caller (the existing WorkspaceSet::dispatch routing). All failures exit 1; nothing changes on failure.
- Owners: CLI parses and resolves the path → EONW carries directory, argv and focus → Runtime validates, owns the tab and selection → Orbit runs the terminal (SessionOperation::Start, unchanged).

Files: runtime/crates/eon-workspace-protocol/src/v23.rs→v24.rs and lib.rs; runtime/crates/eon-runtime/src/{workspace.rs, cli.rs, cli/parity.rs} and every v23 import; eon/crates/eon (version 0.1.7, product.rs, tests/workspace_control.rs); components/eon-v5.json and Cargo.lock as f495068 did; venus/src rename only, plus venus/CHANGELOG.md and venus/docs mentions; docs/CONTRACTS.md (approved text), docs/USAGE.md, docs/ARCHITECTURE.md and runtime/README.md version mentions, CHANGELOG.md.

Red check: on the base, `eon tab create --no-focus --directory D -- cmd` is a usage error (exit 2), and the new runtime test cannot build. Green:
- codec: golden bytes and round-trip for LaunchTab with and without argv; decode rejects an over-bound argv and a relative directory;
- runtime unit: from a caller in t1, LaunchTab focus=false at D with argv gives t2, non-pending, one selected pane started at D with Tool(argv), and t1 stays active with its selected pane and shown popup. focus=true makes t2 active. A command without a caller fails with caller-required and changes nothing. Directory-only without a caller succeeds. Full `nix develop -c eon-test`, fmt and clippy (`--locked --all-targets -D warnings`) for eon-workspace-protocol, eon-runtime, eon and venus, and the affected Nix checks. The docs/REFERENCES.md route read is "How should full Eon choose every new tab directory before starting its first pane" (owner: pending-tab and picker lifecycle). It rejects client-supplied commands for the picker; this change keeps the picker free of commands and reuses EON-C10's existing calling-terminal command request instead. Comparable implementations, at the clones in ~/pjs/refs:
- tmux 3.8 at 7f2a35a, cmd-new-window.c: `new-window [-d] [-c start-directory] [shell-command [argument ...]]`. `-d` leaves the current window alone.

Kept: an explicit directory, an optional exact argv after `--`, a flag that leaves focus alone (tmux -d, kitty --keep-focus), and the caller's environment choosing the target (WezTerm). title: Park a live Agent in a pane when the tab folder changes
description:
## Decision (Lucca, 2026-10-21)

Eon and Yazelix Nova share one policy for a tab-folder change. The Nova twin of
this bead implements the same policy; keep both texts aligned.

Shared policy:
- When a tab's folder changes explicitly, a live Agent popup terminal is
  **parked**: it leaves the popup and becomes an ordinary pane in the same tab,
  keeping its process, conversation and old directory. Its pane label names that
  old folder.
- The next Agent invocation starts a fresh agent at the new tab folder.
- Git keeps today's rule (restart at the new folder on next invocation); its
  state is cheap. A Yazi popup, when present, is kept as is (Nova already does
  this).
- No agent from the old folder ever appears as the tab's current Agent, and no
  agent is ever stopped by a folder change.

Why: Nova's `yazelix-5vl-f69` rejected keeping the old agent in the popup
("permits an agent from the old workspace to masquerade as current"). Both
products then restart it, which silently ends a live conversation. Parking keeps
both guarantees, and matches how running panes already keep their old folder.
Rejected: keep the old instance with a cue (masquerade), confirm on invocation
(modal friction), footer warning only (still destroys the session).

## Evidence

- `runtime/crates/eon-runtime/src/workspace.rs:420`: on invocation, a keep-alive
  popup whose `launch_directory` differs from the tab directory is stopped and a
  replacement started.
- `runtime/crates/eon-runtime/src/workspace.rs:2112`
  `popup_identity_reuses_hides_and_replaces_only_after_retarget` pins that rule.
- `docs/CONTRACTS.md` EON-C10 "Runtime policy" (~line 688): "explicit
  retargeting changes no process until the next invocation, which stops the
  exact old terminal before starting a fresh one at the new directory."
- `docs/USAGE.md:159`: user text for Project/Git/Agent directory behavior.
- Tab folder changes today come from the Alt+Z Project chooser and
  `eon tab directory TAB -- DIR`. The Yazi popup epic (Alt+Shift+Y, Alt+Enter)
  adds another route and retires Alt+Z; this policy applies to every route.

## Scope

In scope: EON-C10 runtime-policy text; runtime popup/pane topology for the
parked transition; its tests; Venus only if a parked terminal cannot already
render as a pane; `docs/USAGE.md`, `CHANGELOG.md`.

Out of scope: Git and custom popup policy beyond keeping today's restart;
transient popups (Anima, Project); the Yazi popup itself; agent provider
selection; moving any process's cwd or injecting `cd`.

## Proposed contract (stop for Lucca's approval before code)

- Parking happens when the folder change commits, so the Agent popup is never
  stale. The parked pane goes into the active tab's selected column, reusing the
  same Orbit terminal (no restart, no new process).
- If the agent terminal has already exited, nothing is parked.
- If the tab cannot take another pane (column/pane bounds), the folder change is
  refused with a clear error and changes nothing, rather than stopping the agent.
  Confirm this fallback with Lucca.

## Acceptance

- Lucca approved the contract text; EON-C10 states it.
- Start Agent, change the tab folder, then: the old agent is a normal pane with
  its conversation intact and its old folder visible; Alt+Shift+L opens a fresh
  agent at the new folder; no agent terminal was stopped.
- Git still restarts at the new folder on its next invocation.
- A refused park leaves tab folder, Agent popup and panes unchanged.

## Implementation Notes

1. Read EON-C10, EON-C18 and `workspace.rs` popup/pane topology; check whether a
   popup terminal can become a `pN` pane without an EONW change. An EONW change
   is a protocol change: record the reference gate (AGENTS.md) and stop for
   approval.
2. Replace the stop-and-restart branch for the Agent entry with park-on-commit;
   keep Git's branch.
3. Update the pinned test to the new policy, plus one test for the refused park.
4. Update USAGE.md and CHANGELOG.md.

## Verification

- `nix develop -c eon-test -p eon-runtime` passes.
- If Venus changes: `nix develop -c eon-test -p yazelix-venus`, `cargo fmt
  --check`, `cargo clippy --locked --all-targets -- -D warnings`.
- Refresh the `eon` profile, then one isolated installed observation of the
  acceptance flow; never restart the live supervisor.

## Stop Conditions

- Stop before code until the contract text is approved.
- Stop if parking needs an EONW version change the user has not approved.
- Stop if verification fails twice for the same reason.
close_reason: Agent parks as a pane on tab retarget; EON-C10 amended and proven (automated + installed), see proof comment

comments.text: Nova twin: yazelix-5vl-875h in the Yazelix Nova repository (same shared policy text).

comments.author: lucca
comments.text:
Investigation (eon-2e, 2026-10-21, edge a2592dd):

- No EONW change needed. An Agent popup's Session is `session-N` / `session-N.sock` (workspace.rs popup_candidate), the same shape as a pane's, so a Pane can carry the same Session. Snapshot panes and popups both carry session plus endpoint.
- Parking cannot fail on capacity. The terminal count is unchanged (session_count counts panes plus popups). The only pane bound is MAX_COLUMNS = 4 columns, and appending to the selected column, or creating a tab's first column, never exceeds it. The proposed "refuse the folder change" fallback is therefore unnecessary; dropped from the draft.
- Both commit routes need the park: commit_directory (Project chooser) and set_tab_directory (`eon tab directory`). Neither needs a process operation.
- An exited agent is already gone: session_ended removes the popup, so nothing is parked.
- Label risk: Venus labels a pane `pN  <cwd>` from Orbit metadata, which is libghostty's OSC 7 pwd (orbit/src/frame.rs:83). An agent that never emits OSC 7 gets a bare `pN` label, so "its label names the old folder" is not guaranteed without an Orbit or EONW change. Unverified which providers emit OSC 7.
- Unknown until implementation: whether Venus moves an endpoint from popup to pane without a reconnect glitch. It is in scope if needed.

comments.author: lucca
comments.text:
Decision (Lucca, 2026-10-21): EON-C10 contract approved, with these choices.

1. Placement: the parked pane goes at the end of the tab's selected column, or into a new first column when the tab has no panes. It stays collapsed and the tab's selection is unchanged, unless the Agent popup was the tab's shown popup. In that case the parked pane becomes the selected, expanded pane, so the conversation stays in view. Rejected: always collapsed (an agent that retargets its own tab vanishes from view); always selected (every folder change moves focus).
2. Label: accept that a bare `pN` label appears when the agent emits no OSC 7. Record which providers report a cwd during the installed check, and file a launch-directory fallback follow-up if it matters. Rejected for now: an Orbit fallback (ORB-C change while eon-a9tr is moving Orbit); dropping the clause from the shared policy.
3. The refusal fallback is dropped: parking cannot fail on capacity.
4. Approved EON-C10 runtime-policy text: when a tab's directory changes explicitly (Project chooser completion or SetTabDirectory), a live Agent terminal launched at another directory is parked in the same step. It leaves the popup and becomes an ordinary pane, keeping its Orbit terminal, process and directory, so parking starts and stops nothing and cannot fail on capacity. The next Agent invocation starts a fresh agent at the new directory. Git keeps restart-on-next-invocation.

comments.author: lucca
comments.text: Contract wording correction (eon-2e, 2026-10-21, from review round 1 by Claude and Codex): in a tab with no panes, the parked Agent necessarily becomes the selected, expanded pane even when its popup was hidden, because a tab with columns always has a selected column (workspace.rs Tab invariant). EON-C10 now says 'when its popup was shown or the tab had no panes'. The capacity claim is narrowed to 'terminal or column capacity', because retarget keeps an unreachable pane-identity exhaustion guard that fails before any mutation. This only states a forced consequence of the approved placement; flagged to Lucca at handoff.

comments.text:
Proof (eon-2e, 2026-10-21). The revision is this bead's closing commit. The code tree is 21a9c05b82a0547507376789a335a0b054c67a58; the commit adds only this proof text.

- Automated: `nix develop -c eon-test -p eon-runtime` passed, 54 tests, including `retarget_parks_the_agent_and_restarts_git_only_on_its_next_invocation` and `chooser_retarget_parks_a_hidden_agent_as_the_first_pane_of_a_paneless_tab`. `cargo clippy --locked -p eon-runtime --all-targets -D warnings` and `cargo fmt --check` are clean.

  1. Agent shown at work/, then `eon tab directory t1 -- other/` (exit 0). The popup became pane p2, selected and expanded. It was the same pid, 1330813, with its transcript intact, and it still took input.
  2. Alt+Shift+L started a fresh agent (pid 1331357) at other/.
  3. Hid it, then Alt+Z chose third/. It parked as p3, collapsed at the column's end, with p2 still selected. Both pids were live.
  4. `eon focus p3`: Venus drew the parked terminal's content with no reconnect error.
  The isolated session was cleaned up with no leftover processes.
- Label finding (decision 2): parked agent panes show a bare `pN`, because the stub emits no OSC 7. Real providers were not checked for OSC 7.
- Venus needed no change.
- Ledger: Claude review rounds: 4.
  - R1: 3 blocking (clippy `cloned_ref_to_slice_refs`; stale test name in EON-C10 evidence; paneless-tab selection wording). Also: Alt+Z and paneless routes untested, so a test was added.
  - R2: 2 blocking (custom keep-alive popups dropped from EON-C10; changelog selection claim).

title: Report a lost Orbit or signalled program's real end status instead of status 1
description:
## Why

When a terminal's Orbit dies abnormally, the supervisor records a status that hides what
happened. In eon-orbit-worker-exit-reason-ztcq's installed check, SIGKILL to a terminal's Orbit
worker made the Orbit host exit 137, but the supervisor log said "terminal session-1 ended with
status 1; Orbit exited without publishing a terminal result; Orbit log: ...". With its only
terminal gone, the isolated supervisor then exited with status 1. A person or agent reading the
log or the exit status cannot tell a killed terminal from a program that exited 1.

Source: eon-orbit-worker-exit-reason-ztcq, comment 4282 (2026-10-27, its proof record, "Side
observation, unchanged by this bead"; landed in 872f00a). Approved by Lucca 2026-10-27 (morning
report question 6): "6. ok", accepting the recommendation "one bead for the exit-status
mapping". Relayed by eon-overseer.

## Evidence

- runtime/crates/eon-runtime/src/sessions.rs:2366-2368 (`session_finished`):
  `SessionEnd::Managed(_, ProcessOutcome::Signal(_)) | SessionEnd::OwnerLost => 1`. Both a
  signalled program and an Orbit that exited without publishing a result become 1.
- runtime/crates/eon-runtime/src/sessions.rs:2218 (`owner_lost`): the OwnerLost end keeps no
  Orbit exit status or signal.
- runtime/crates/eon-runtime/src/supervisor.rs:1950 (`session_end_line`): formats "terminal {id}
  ended with status {code}".
- runtime/crates/eon-runtime/src/supervisor.rs:2031 and 1463/1482: session-1's code becomes
  `initial_status`, which the supervisor returns as its own exit status when no terminals remain.
  That is why the isolated supervisor exited 1.
- Installed evidence: ~/.cache/eon-agents/ztcq-work/obs1/ (eon.log, steps.txt), package
  /nix/store/fcd9grzqv5ka19iqccbnkd0ixldxy1fv-eon-0.1.3.
- Tests that pin today's text: supervisor.rs:8171 and :8623 assert "ended with status 1; Orbit
  exited without publishing a terminal result".

## Contract

Check EON-C8 (durable tab and pane workspace, terminal end), EON-C10 (typed workspace control,
`eon stop` statuses) and EON-C28 (1.x stability: documented exit statuses must not change
silently) for text that fixes these statuses, and docs/USAGE.md for the supervisor's exit status.
If the change needs any EON-C text added or changed, stop and bring the exact wording to Lucca
for approval first, as AGENTS.md requires.

## Prerequisites

None. eon-orbit-worker-exit-reason-ztcq (closed) already writes why the worker died to Orbit's
log.

## Scope

In scope:
- Decide and implement one mapping for a terminal's end status: a signalled program reported as
  128+signal (shell convention) or by signal name, and an Orbit lost without a result reported
  distinctly (for example naming Orbit's own exit status or signal when the supervisor reaped it)
  rather than as 1.
- Decide whether the supervisor's own exit status when its last terminal ends should follow
  session-1's status, and document the answer.
- The supervisor log line and the tests that pin it.

Out of scope:
- Orbit's worker-exit stderr line (done in ztcq).
- The EONW wire format; if the status must cross EONW, stop (protocol change, needs an EONW bump
  and Lucca's approval).

## Acceptance

- A runtime test: a terminal whose Orbit is lost without a result, and one whose program dies by
  signal, each produce the decided status in the supervisor log line, and the test fails on
  today's code.
- docs/USAGE.md (and contracts, if approved) state the supervisor's exit status when the last
  terminal ends.
- One isolated installed check: SIGKILL a scratch terminal's Orbit worker; the supervisor log
  shows the decided status (not a bare 1).

## Verification

- `nix develop -c eon-test -p eon-runtime` passes.
- `cargo clippy --locked -p eon-runtime --all-targets -- -D warnings` clean.
- The installed check above, in isolated headless Sway with a private HOME and runtime dir, never
  against Lucca's running Eon.

## Stop Conditions

- Stop if any EON-C text must change (Lucca's approval).
- Stop if the status must travel over EONW or ORBS.

## Maintenance Notes

ztcq's proof driver ~/.cache/eon-agents/ztcq-work/installed.sh shows how to SIGKILL the exact
worker PID; never use pkill patterns (Orbit hosts carry prompts in argv).


## Current scope and mapping choices (dcaef1c, 2026-11-12)

The collapse to 1 still exists in `session_finished_within`; do not infer an
Orbit result where the process has not been reaped or a valid tombstone exists.
Before code, present one explicit mapping for program ExitCode, program Signal,
owner loss with known host ExitStatus, and owner loss without a known status,
plus the supervisor's initial-terminal/last-terminal exit rule. Keep the known
program result authoritative even if later Orbit cleanup fails. Distinguish
unknown loss in diagnostics instead of inventing a signal or false success.

A narrow Runtime regression must falsify the selected loss/signal behavior and
retain ordinary exit codes/other-live-terminal survival. The isolated installed
scratch-worker SIGKILL observation exercises the abnormal-owner case with exact
owned identities only; no live session or pattern killing. Update user docs and
product changelog for accepted exit/log behavior, run the current lifecycle and
whole-workspace proof/review route, and refresh the accepted profile as required.
