title: Document phone access: Remote Control for Claude panes, Tailscale plus SSH and eon pane for the rest
description:
## Why
Lucca wants to reach Eon and its agents from his phone (2026-11-12; "yeah" to filing in eon-desk). The research (/home/lucca/.cache/eon-agents/eon-desk/mobile-report.md) found a free answer that needs no Eon change, but nothing documents it.

## Goal
A short docs/USAGE.md section (or a docs/PHONE.md linked from it) covering:
- **Claude panes:** Claude Code Remote Control. Run `/rc` per pane, then use the Claude app's Code tab. Recommend it for the coordinating pane only, not `remoteControlAtStartup`, which is account-wide. https://code.claude.com/docs/en/remote-control
- **Every pane, Codex included:** Tailscale (or Headscale), SSH from a phone app (Termius, Blink, Moshi, Termux), then `eon session --json`, `eon pane read`, `eon pane send --stdin --enter` and `eon events --json` on the desktop. The CLI works with `EON_TERMINAL` unset, with caller null (docs/CONTRACTS.md:1626).
- **Security rules:** tailnet only; never Funnel or public relays; key-only SSH with a separate revocable phone key, or Tailscale SSH `check`; no TCP listener in the Runtime; 2FA on the claude.ai account. Phone access equals a shell, because agents run with approvals bypassed. `pane send` refuses within 2 s of desktop typing (EON-C36, CONTRACTS.md:5345).
- **Notifications:** point to the eon-sixj recipe.

Fold item 3 of eon-headscale-p15dq here ("SSH on a tailnet") and comment there.

## Acceptance
Docs exist, every command in them was run, and they promise nothing Eon doesn't do. Depends on the SSH-login proof bead for the environment details.

## Verification
Doc review; commands checked against the installed build from an SSH login.

title: Give tab pills and Eon Bar widgets one centred height, widgets outlined instead of filled
description:
## Why

eon-i2m3 decision (Lucca, 2026-10-24): Eon Bar widgets and tab pills get one height, the widgets
told apart by a thin rounded outline instead of a fill (frame OUTLINE in
~/.cache/eon-agents/i2m3/research/mock/png/). Lucca then: "id like the tabs to change their height
instead", "we should also make tab and widget pills automatically center vertically, with equal
gap between top edge of the window and top edge of the sidebar/project line", and on today's
centring (widgets 4..36, line at 50): "current doesnt work. look at this. it's so uneven ... figure
it out", allowing "a 'middle path'". The overseer chose H30 (mock:
~/.cache/eon-agents/i2m3/research/mock/png/centre-zoom.png, centre-strips.png; script
~/.cache/eon-agents/i2m3/centre-mock.py). Research: ~/.cache/eon-agents/i2m3/research/*.md.

## Behaviour

- One height and one centre line for tab pills and the quota, CPU, RAM and clock widgets: each
  spans from half the card title height (text_height / 2) below the window's top edge to the top
  of the allocated card areas, so the space above equals the space between it and the cards'
  shared top line. At default typography, scale 1: 30 px pills at y 10..40 (tabs grow from 24,
  widgets shrink from 32), shared top line at 50. Scene derives it from its existing title metric
  and card-area top; no second constant.
- Tabs keep their fills, text, attention badge, hover and keyboard-focus outline (re-centred).
- Widgets draw no fill: each is a rounded outline (radius half its height) at the pane cards'
  neutral border width (`[terminal] border_width`) and outline colour, text and provider icons on
  the opaque bar background.
- The version label stays plain text; New tab (+), Keyboard shortcuts (?) and Close centre on the
  same line (header button width unchanged).
- Bar height, allocated card areas, terminal rects and grids unchanged. Hover and AccessKit
  rectangles, item order, width fitting, narrow hiding and the blank drag region unchanged. On a
  short window the extra inset yields before the pills do, as today.
- Configurability: no new setting. border_width (1 to 3, default 1) also sizes the widget
  outlines; docs/CONFIGURATION.md says so.

## Contract (approved wording, see the Approval comments)

- VEN-C21 Result, after "The existing workspace tab strip remains one row at its existing
  height.", add: "Tabs keep their filled pills. Tab pills and the quota, CPU, RAM and clock widgets
  share one height and centre line: each spans from half the card title height below the window's
  top edge to the top of the allocated card areas, so the space above it equals the space between
  it and the cards' shared top line. The widgets draw no fill: each is a rounded outline at the
  pane cards' neutral border width and outline color, with its text and icons on the opaque bar
  background. The version label stays plain text, and New tab, Keyboard shortcuts and Close centre
  on the same line. Hover and accessibility rectangles, order, width fitting and the blank drag
  region stay unchanged."
- VEN-C8: "the tab pills keep the gap from the window's top and left edges" becomes "the tab pills
  keep the gap from the window's left edge"; "Pill size, the gap between pills and header button
  width stay as before" becomes "Pill height follows VEN-C21; the gap between pills and header
  button width stay as before"; "from the tab pills above" is dropped from the card-gap list.
- EON-C8 (docs/CONTRACTS.md ~391-396): the matching sentences change the same way: card areas keep
  the gap from the window's sides and from each other; "The tab pills keep the same gap from the
  window's top and left edges, in both modes." becomes "The tab pills keep the same gap from the
  window's left edge, in both modes, and are centred with the Eon Bar widgets as VEN-C21
  describes."
- VEN-C27 and VEN-C28: "on the quota chips' rounded fill" becomes "in the quota chips' rounded
  outline". Proof records stay as written.

## Acceptance

- Venus scene/paint tests (fail first): tab pills and widgets share height and centre; top gap ==
  gap to the shared top line (within snapping) at scales 1 and 1.3 and line_height 1.125/2; no
  widget fill pixels; outline at border_width 1/2/3; version label and controls centred on the
  same line; tabs keep fill; bar height, card areas and terminal grids unchanged.
- Isolated capture with Lucca's opacity and the six default widgets.

Portability: neutral.

title: Open a pane's scrollback in the configured editor, from the window and the CLI
description:
## Why

Lucca, 2026-11-04: "do we have a bead for opening scrollback in the user editor?" No bead covered it.

A person often wants a pane's long output in a real editor, to search, select, copy or save it. Zellij's edit-scrollback is the familiar reference, and Yazelix Nova users had it. Since eon-ecupy (23316e8), `[editor] command` names the person's editor, so Eon can open the text there.

Today:
- `eon pane read` returns only the visible screen (EON-C35; its Boundary leaves history out).
- Venus shows history only by scrolling (VEN-C7).

## Goal

From the window, one key opens the focused pane's retained history plus its screen, as plain text, in the configured editor. An agent gets the same text from the CLI (rule 5).

## Shape (to settle in the first child, with contract text)

1. Orbit: a bounded, read-only export of a terminal's retained history plus its screen as plain text (ORB-C2 and ORB-C8 own history). It may share its mechanism with the find epic eon-ndep0 child 2, and with orb-p92 phase 2 (bounded history).
2. Runtime and CLI: `eon pane history PANE` (name to decide), which writes that text to stdout or to a file. It is authorized like `eon pane read` (`[agents] terminal_access`, EON-C35 extension).
3. Window action: the history goes to a private temporary file, which opens in a transient popup running `[editor] command` with the path, as `eon edit` opens files (EON-C10). The file is deleted when the popup ends.
   - The key is configurable (rule 6), with its default in docs/CONFIGURATION.md.
   - The CLI path ships in the same change (rule 5).

Decisions for the first child:
- Size bound and truncation notice.
- Whether colors are dropped (plain text) or kept as ANSI.
- Where the temporary file lives, and its permissions: 0600 under the Eon runtime directory.
- Read-only or editable: edits are discarded, and the file is a snapshot.

## Acceptance

- Installed observation: in a pane with output longer than the screen, the key opens the editor showing the earliest retained line through the current screen. Closing the editor returns to the pane, and the temporary file is gone.
- The CLI command returns the same text.
- A real-PTY Orbit check of the export's bound.

## Verification

- Orbit Nix checks, plus `nix develop -c eon-test -p eon-runtime -p eon`.
- fmt and clippy.
- One isolated installed observation.
- Converge plus Codex.
- Contract text (new or extended EON-C35, ORB-C and EON-C10) stops for approval before code.

## Related

- eon-ndep0: find in a terminal's screen and history.
- orb-p92: agent observation.
- eon-ecupy: configured editor.
- eon-74x0: scrollback size.


## Fresh-session split

This is an epic. Keep every original goal, decision question, authorization rule and installed acceptance above. Children deliver, in order: design/contract proposal; Orbit bounded text export; Runtime authorized CLI export; configured-editor window action and end-to-end proof. Implementation children are provisional and blocked by the design decision; approved names, bounds, formatting and temporary-file lifetime replace the examples before implementation. Reuse the history owner with eon-ndep0 (find in terminal screen/history) and orb-p92 (bounded agent observation), without waiting for unchosen full search/observer scope or creating a second export owner.

title: Decide bounded scrollback export and editor-opening semantics
description:
## Why

Opening retained output in the configured editor crosses Orbit history, Runtime authorization and a window action. Parent: eon-u5bvd (open scrollback in the configured editor). Settle those boundaries before code.

## Evidence

- docs/CONTRACTS.md: EON-C35 visible-screen read boundary and EON-C10 editor/popup actions.
- orbit/docs/CONTRACTS.md: ORB-C2/ORB-C8 retained history ownership.
- eon-ecupy (configured editor, delivered) supplies [editor] command; eon-ndep0 (terminal find) and orb-p92 (bounded observation) also need history.

## Scope

In: reference gate (Zellij edit-scrollback and current libghostty history APIs at inspected revisions), one owner trace, contract proposals, and all parent decisions. Settle retained-history plus current-screen ordering, alternate screen, Unicode/wrapped lines, export bound/truncation notice, plain text versus ANSI, snapshot/edit semantics, CLI name/stdout/file path, authorization, configurable key and private temporary file lifecycle (0600 under Runtime directory). Out: implementation, actual contract-index edits, persistent transcript, another terminal/history authority.

## Acceptance

- Give Lucca a recommendation and reason for each parent question, including whether the bound can truncate the earliest retained line and how that is honestly reported.
- Explain reuse with find/observation without expanding their scope.
- Exact EON/ORB contract text and relevant wire changes are approved before implementation; record choice/date, and confirm or revise the three implementation siblings without losing acceptance.
- Define the cheapest falsifier for each boundary. This decision stays open until its owning decision workflow is complete, not closed by this audit.

## Implementation Notes

1. Read parent, contracts and owning REFERENCES routes; compare existing retained-history operations and editor launch.
2. Trace Orbit export → Runtime policy/CLI → private snapshot → editor popup → cleanup.
3. Present the choices and proposed contract text for Lucca; implementation remains gated.

## Verification

Planning route: recorded source revisions, data/owner trace, choices, proposed checks and graph. No code, builds or runtime probe is part of this planning slice.

## Stop Conditions

Stop for unchosen product/contract semantics, a new dependency or platform boundary; never touch the running Eon.

## Maintenance Notes

No aliases, shims, automatic transcript capture or raw PTY reparse. The current screen/history remain authoritative in Orbit.

- item 9: `eon pane history TARGET [--json]` prints the history; `--edit` opens it in the editor in the target's tab, active tab only in v1, otherwise refused with not-active.
- item 13: amend ORB-C17, EON-C35 and EON-C10 rather than adding new contracts.
- item 14: Orbit management v6 -> v7 and EONW v32 -> v33, with no compatibility code. Fold in any Orbit change approved by the time .2 starts (e.g. eon-0um2b), but wait for none.

comments.author: lucca
comments.text:
# eon-u5bvd.1 record 1: reference gate

Session: eon-u5bvd-1 worktree at edge `570d0ad`, 2026-11-05. Read-only; no
builds, no runtime probe.

## Sources and inspected revisions

| Source | Revision | Where |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Zellij | `v0.45.1`, `efd8fd5a89a20c07a111d248ad7fce53848d2c18` | `~/pjs/refs/zellij-v0.45.1` |
| Ghostty (libghostty-vt C/Zig) | `521cf2c5d30bd48028ca61546c64e7913764073d` (Eon's `flake.lock` pin and libghostty-rs's `GHOSTTY_COMMIT`) | `/nix/store/845skyrkk1m00q3sa2x2dv0024yh8j7m-source` |
| libghostty-rs (`libghostty-vt`) | `9ede35b8ea94a55ed3608408d67e102883129f1e` (`orbit/Cargo.toml` pin) | `~/.cargo/git/checkouts/libghostty-rs-28fee7453bdb2b25/9ede35b` |

`~/pjs/refs/ghostty-7501` and `~/pjs/refs/libghostty-rs-7501` are not git
checkouts, so their revisions cannot be recorded. I did not use them. The
pinned sources above are the ones Orbit builds.

## Zellij edit-scrollback (`zellij-server/src/tab/mod.rs:6055-6160`)

Evidence:
- `EditScrollback { ansi }` dumps the active pane to
  `temp_dir()/<uuid>.dump`, then opens `scrollback_editor` on it "in place",
  replacing the pane until the editor exits.
- The dump (`grid.rs:2136`, the `dump_screen!` macro at `grid.rs:570`) is
  `lines_above` (scrollback) followed by the viewport. Soft-wrapped rows join
  into one logical line (`is_canonical`), and trailing spaces are trimmed.
  An `ansi` flag gives a second, SGR-styled dump.
- Bound: only the scrollback line limit (`scroll_buffer_size`, default
  10,000 lines). The export itself has no byte bound and no truncation
  notice.
- In the alternate screen, the primary `lines_above` and viewport go into
  `AlternateScreenState` (`grid.rs:5156`), so the dump holds only the
  alternate screen.
- File: `File::create` (`os_input_output.rs:655`) in the shared temp
  directory, created with the umask's mode (usually 0644, readable by every
  local user). Nothing deletes it: no `remove_file` touches `.dump` files.
- Editor position: it passes the scroll position as a line number by
  guessing the editor's syntax from its name (`+N` for vim, nvim, emacs,
  nano and kak; `file:N` for hx; nothing for any other editor;
  `os_input_output.rs:163-180`).

Kept: history then screen in one ordered text; soft wraps joined; trailing
blanks trimmed; alternate screen exports only itself; one key opens the
editor, and the person returns to the pane when it exits.

Rejected:
- A world-readable file in the shared temp directory that is never deleted.
- Guessing editor syntax from the editor's name. Eon's `[editor] command`
  contract (EON-C10) only appends a path.
- ANSI export.
- The unbounded dump.

## Ghostty's own write-scrollback (`src/Surface.zig`, `writeScreenFile`)

Evidence:
- Ghostty writes the file into a fresh private temp directory as
  `history.txt` or `screen.txt`, with mode 0600.
- It formats the active screen's PageList with `unwrap = true`, so soft
  wraps are joined.
- Its `.screen` location covers history plus the active area. Its
  `.history` location returns nothing while the alternate screen is active.
- It opens the file through the OS opener, or copies or pastes the path.
- It does not bound the output, and it keeps the directory afterwards.

Kept: a private directory with a 0600 file, `unwrap = true`, and the
`.screen` coverage (history plus active area).

Rejected: keeping the file after use, and no bound.

## libghostty history APIs at the pinned revisions

Evidence (libghostty-rs `crates/libghostty-vt/src`):
- `fmt::Formatter::new(terminal, FormatterOptions)` formats "a terminal's
  active screen". Ghostty `c/formatter.zig:71-73`: a null selection
  formats "the entire screen". In `formatter.zig:701` and `:931`, the
  PageListFormatter runs from `getTopLeft(.screen)` to
  `getBottomRight(.screen)`, which is history plus the active area, in
  order.
- Options:
  - `with_format(Format::Plain | Vt | Html)`;
  - `with_unwrap(bool)`, which joins soft wraps;
  - `with_trim(bool)`, which trims trailing whitespace; trailing blank
    lines are always trimmed;
  - `format_alloc`, `format_buf`, and `format_len` (size first).
- No option selects the inactive screen. `c/formatter.zig` takes only a
  terminal and a selection. While the alternate screen is active, the
  primary history cannot be formatted without an upstream change.
- `Point::{Active, Viewport, Screen, History}` with `grid_ref`, plus
  `total_rows()` and `scrollback_rows()`. `grid_ref` on Screen or History
  points "may require traversing the full scrollback page list" and
  should not be used row by row over the history (`terminal.rs:407-422`).
- `search::Search` searches the active area and scrollback of both
  screens incrementally (`feed`/`tick`) and returns matches as
  `Selection`s (`search.rs:1-40`). This API belongs to find (eon-ndep0),
  not to export.
- `Terminal::compress` exists. Orbit never calls it (no `compress` in
  `orbit/src`), so no history is compressed. If Orbit adopted compression,
  an export would decompress pages transparently (`terminal.rs:555-570`).
- `set_scrollback_max_bytes` prunes at page granularity, about 400 KB a
  page. Orbit sets 16 MiB (`orbit/src/frame.rs:27`, `pty.rs:200`; ORB-C8).

Inference, labelled as such:
- A Ghostty cell is 8 bytes of page memory, and a codepoint is at most 4
  UTF-8 bytes. So a full 16 MiB history of single-codepoint cells yields
  about 8 MiB of plain text, plus the active area. That is typical, not a
  ceiling: multi-codepoint graphemes are stored apart from the cell, so
  emoji sequences or stacked combining marks can yield more text per byte
  of budget (Opus gate finding 3).
- Typical ASCII output yields about 2 MiB or less (80 or 200 columns, full
  rows).
- Record 4 names the falsifier.

Adopted mechanism: one `Formatter` pass over the active screen with
`Format::Plain`, `unwrap = true` and `trim = true`, in one Orbit host turn
at one presentation revision. Then the same control-character
sanitization as ORB-C17, and a leading-line bound.

Rejected:
- Row-by-row `grid_ref` over the history, which is slow by the API's own
  note.
- Chunked extraction across host turns. PTY output between chunks would
  break the one-revision snapshot.
- `Format::Vt`/ANSI.
- Patching Ghostty to read the primary screen while the alternate screen
  is active, which would be a new upstream dependency boundary.

Unresolved (not needed now): whether a later Ghostty adds an inactive-screen
formatter option.

## Constraints kept from Eon contracts

- ORB-C2 and ORB-C8: Orbit is the sole owner of terminal state and history.
  The export comes from Orbit's libghostty, never from Venus frames or raw
  PTY bytes.
- ORB-C17: one management request on the validated lease, one request in
  flight, a typed failure and never partial text, no side effects, waits
  for a held DEC 2026 update, 1 MiB leading-row bound with an omitted
  count. Text has no control characters besides line feeds.
- EON-C35: the supervisor resolves TARGET, `[agents] terminal_access`
  governs reads, and no failure carries content. The supervisor blocks up
  to `TERMINAL_DEADLINE` (2 s, `sessions.rs:974`) for the reply.
- EON-C10: `[editor] command` with the absolute path appended. The editor
  argv does not cross EONW. `PopupCommand::Edit(file)` exists
  (`managed_environment.rs:380-385`, `:1272`), but it builds the `eon edit`
  pane command, and the popup catalog refuses it (`:532`). It is not a
  popup reuse (Opus gate finding 1, record 2). Transient popups stop on
  dismissal, replacement or tab close, and show again the popup they
  covered (`eon-knowp`).
- Size ceilings:
  - EONW `MAX_MESSAGE_BYTES` is 2 MiB (`v32.rs:22`).
  - Orbit management sets a ceiling per message type
    (`MAX_VISIBLE_MESSAGE_BYTES`, `management.rs:37`).
- The window runtime directory is owned and 0700
  (`supervisor.rs:738-770`, test `runtime_directory_is_private`).

# eon-u5bvd.1 record 2: owner trace

Edge `570d0ad`, 2026-11-05. "Today" marks existing code; "proposed" marks
what the siblings would add. Each step names its one owner.

## Data path

1. **Trigger (Venus, unchanged).** A person presses the Scrollback popup's
   key. Venus already sends EONW `Action::InvokePopup { tab, entry,
   intent }` for every configured popup key
   (`eon-workspace-protocol/src/v32.rs:181`). Venus does not change: the
   new entry arrives in the existing popup catalog (`PopupEntry`), and the
   Shortcuts viewer and Alt+/ list it like any popup.
   - Agent trigger: `eon pane history TARGET --edit` (proposed, record 4,
     Q9) sends a Runtime action that names TARGET.
2. **Target and policy (Eon Runtime supervisor).**
   - Today: `workspace.rs:1128` dispatches `invoke_popup`
     (`workspace.rs:1415`). It refuses a tab that is not active
     (`not-active`), and it starts the entry's fixed catalog command
     through `prepare`. The catalog refuses `PopupCommand::Edit`
     (`managed_environment.rs:532`, "a default popup cannot edit a file"),
     and the Orbit read lives in the supervisor (`supervisor.rs:2704-2750`),
     not in the workspace owner.
   - Correction (Opus gate finding 1): Scrollback is **not** a reuse of
     the catalog path. It needs a new popup kind whose command is built on
     each press, after the supervisor has read the history and written the
     file. The supervisor handles `InvokePopup` for the `scrollback` entry
     itself:
     1. It resolves the source terminal: the popup the active tab shows
        (the one the new popup will cover), else the tab's selected pane.
        A tab that shows neither changes nothing.
     2. It reads the history (step 3) and writes the snapshot (step 5).
     3. It asks the workspace owner to start a transient popup of the new
        kind with the built argv (step 6).
     The `not-active` refusal stays: the key acts only on the active tab,
     and in v1 `--edit` on a hidden tab refuses with `not-active` (exit 1).
   - The CLI path resolves TARGET exactly as `eon pane read` does
     (`supervisor.rs:2720-2750`: `terminal_target`, `caller_session`, the
     `terminal_access` check).
   - The key is the person acting in their own window, so
     `[agents] terminal_access` does not govern it. The CLI path is
     governed (record 4, Q8).
3. **Export (Orbit).**
   - Today: `sessions::read_visible` sends
     `ManagementClientMessage::ReadVisible` on the validated lease and
     blocks up to `TERMINAL_DEADLINE` = 2 s (`sessions.rs:974`, `:1350`).
     Orbit's Bend management policy admits the request, and the Rust host
     answers from `visible::read` (`orbit/src/visible.rs`).
   - Proposed: a sibling `ReadHistory` request on the same lease and
     admission (`management_read_needs_a_live_settled_lease`).
     - The host runs one libghostty `Formatter` pass over the active screen
       (history plus active area), plain and unwrapped, at revision N.
     - It sanitizes control characters as ORB-C17 does, applies the 8 MiB
       leading-line bound, and replies `History { revision, screen, rows,
       columns, title, directory, omitted_lines, lossy, text }`.
     - Orbit management goes v6 → v7. Its one consumer is Eon Runtime. v7
       also carries any other Orbit management change approved by the time
       .2 starts (for example eon-0um2b's agent keys and interrupt), but
       waits for none.
     - Stall: the supervisor blocks on this reply (up to 2 s,
       `supervisor.rs:2704`), so a slow full-size read freezes every pane
       of the window, not just this terminal. Record 4's falsifiers measure
       this.
4. **CLI projection (Eon Runtime).** Proposed: EONW v32 → v33 adds
   `Action::ReadTerminalHistory { target, edit }` and a `TerminalHistory`
   response. Only that response, which the CLI receives, gets the larger
   ceiling (8 MiB of text plus metadata). Every other message, and every
   message Venus receives, keeps the general 2 MiB `MAX_MESSAGE_BYTES`. The
   window path never sends the text over EONW: the supervisor writes it to
   the file itself. The CLI
   prints the text to stdout, or `--json` prints the object. A truncation
   notice goes to stderr in human mode.
5. **Private snapshot (Eon Runtime supervisor).** Proposed, for the window
   key and `--edit` only:
   - The supervisor creates `<window runtime dir>/snapshots/` with mode
     0700 and an owner check, as `prepare_runtime` does
     (`supervisor.rs:738-770`).
   - Inside it goes one directory per snapshot, named for the supervisor's
     pid and start time plus a counter, mode 0700.
   - Inside that goes `<pane-or-popup-id>-scrollback.txt`, created with
     `O_CREAT|O_EXCL|O_NOFOLLOW`, mode 0600.
   - The file may start with one notice line: when the text was truncated,
     or when the source was on the alternate screen (record 3). The text
     follows exactly as the CLI prints it.
6. **Editor (Eon Runtime, new popup kind).** The supervisor starts a
   transient popup of the new kind in the active tab. Its argv is built
   from `[editor] command` with the snapshot path appended, which is the
   same rule `eon edit` uses (`managed_environment.rs:1272`). It is built
   on each press and never stored in the catalog. The kind reuses the
   transient lifecycle: covering the shown popup (`covered_popup`,
   `workspace.rs:101`), stop on dismissal, and showing the covered popup
   again.
   - If the read fails or times out, or the editor is missing or not
     executable, no popup starts. The person sees the existing popup
     start-failure notice, and the snapshot directory, if one was made, is
     removed.
7. **Cleanup (Eon Runtime supervisor).**
   - When that popup's Orbit terminal ends, the supervisor removes that
     snapshot's directory without following symlinks. Endings include the
     editor exiting, the person dismissing it (the key again), replacement,
     tab close, `eon popup hide`, and window quit.
     They all pass through `session_ended` (`workspace.rs:1671`), then
     `remove_popup` (`workspace.rs:2388`).
   - The covered popup or the pane shows again (`eon-knowp`).
   - At start, a supervisor removes every snapshot directory whose recorded
     supervisor (pid plus start time) is no longer alive. That covers a
     supervisor killed with snapshots open. A recovering supervisor that
     adopts a live Scrollback popup's terminal (EON-C15) takes ownership of
     that popup's directory and does not sweep it; it removes the directory
     when that adopted popup ends. .4a settles how the record names the
     adopted directory.
   - On Linux, `$XDG_RUNTIME_DIR` is tmpfs and is cleared at logout. The
     macOS fallback `/tmp/eon-<uid>` is not tmpfs, so the start sweep
     alone carries cleanup there.
   - Outside Eon's reach: an editor's own state files outside the
     directory. Examples are Neovim's swap, undo and shada files under
     `~/.local/state/nvim`. They survive a killed editor; Eon documents
     this and does not clean them.
   - Dismissing or replacing the popup (for example with Alt+Shift+J)
     stops its terminal and kills the editor, so unsaved edits are lost.
     The snapshot is discarded anyway; to keep edits, save under another
     name first.

## Owners, one per invariant

| Invariant | Owner |
| --- | --- |
| Terminal state, retained history, export content, order, bound, revision | Orbit host + Bend management policy (ORB-C2, ORB-C8, ORB-C17 as amended) |
| Who may read (CLI), target resolution, CLI and JSON projection | Eon Runtime (EON-C35 as amended) |
| Which terminal the key exports, snapshot file, privacy, lifetime, editor popup | Eon Runtime (EON-C10 runtime policy as amended) |
| Editor argv | Eon Runtime `[editor] command` (EON-C10, unchanged) |
| Key binding, label, enabled | Eon Runtime config (`[popups.scrollback]`); Venus only dispatches |
| Showing and scrolling history in the window | Venus (VEN-C7, unchanged) |

No second history reader: Runtime never parses terminal bytes, and Venus
never exports frames.

## Reuse with find and observation, without widening them

- **Find (eon-ndep0).** Find needs match positions that stay correct as
  output moves, across both screens, and incremental work. libghostty's
  `search::Search` gives exactly that, and record 1 shows export cannot.
  Find shares:
  - the owner (Orbit host);
  - the management lease and admission;
  - the CLI authorization (`terminal_access`).

  Find must not search the exported text, which would add a second history
  reader and lose positions. The export adds nothing to find's scope.
- **Observation (orb-p92 phase 2).** Phase 2 waits for "bounded history
  only after their owner contracts are accepted". The amended ORB-C17
  history read is that accepted owner contract. orb-p92 keeps its own
  observer role, handshake and Eon authorization. Nothing here creates an
  observer role or widens ORB-C3.

comments.text:
# eon-u5bvd.1 record 3: approved contract text (not yet applied)

Revised 2026-11-05 after the Opus gate (PASS WITH FIXES). This revision
folds in findings 1, 3, 4, 5, 6 and 8.

Approved by Lucca on 2026-11-05, relayed by eon-overseer: "yyes", in
answer to "I recommend yes to all four" (record 4, items 4, 9, 13 and 14).
None of this text is applied to `docs/CONTRACTS.md` or
`orbit/docs/CONTRACTS.md` yet. Each sibling applies its part, with status
and proof lines:
- ORB-C17: .2.
- EON-C35's `history`: .3.
- EON-C35's `--edit`: .4b.
- EON-C10: .4a, with the `--edit` reference in .4b.

## 1. ORB-C17: amend, renamed "Bounded terminal text reads"

Reason: one behavior, one contract. The history read shares the consumer,
lease, admission, one request in flight, failures, no-side-effect rule and
host extractor. ORB-C17's Boundary currently excludes history, so this is
a change to an `ORB-C` contract and needs approval.

Replace the title, Trigger, the Result's "What the text covers" and "Size
bound" items, and the Boundary's first item. Add a Result item for
history. Everything else stays as it is.

> ## ORB-C17 — Bounded terminal text reads
>
> - **Trigger:** The lease holder sends one management `ReadVisible` or
>   `ReadHistory` request.
> - **Result:**
>   - *(unchanged snapshot fields; for `ReadHistory`, `omitted_lines` and
>     `cut_bytes` replace `omitted_rows`)*
>   - **What the text covers.** `ReadVisible`: the rows a client at live
>     bottom would see, whatever any client's scroll position. `ReadHistory`:
>     the active screen's retained history followed by its live area, oldest
>     first, as one text. On the alternate screen, which retains no history,
>     that is its live area alone, and the reply names the alternate screen.
>     Output that the ORB-C8 history budget already evicted is not part of
>     the terminal and is not reported.
>   - **How the text is laid out.** `ReadVisible` as above. `ReadHistory`:
>     one line per logical line, so a soft-wrapped line is joined into one;
>     a hard line break ends a line; trailing blanks on each line and trailing
>     blank lines are trimmed; wide-cell spacers are omitted; combining
>     marks and other grapheme parts are kept.
>   - **Size bound.** `ReadVisible` text is at most 1 MiB; `ReadHistory` text
>     at most 8 MiB. When the text would exceed its bound, Orbit keeps the
>     last whole rows (`ReadVisible`) or lines (`ReadHistory`) that fit and
>     reports how many leading ones it omitted, so the earliest retained
>     lines are the ones left out. When the newest line alone exceeds the
>     `ReadHistory` bound, Orbit keeps that line's last part, cut at a
>     character boundary to fit, omits every earlier line, and reports both
>     the omitted lines and the bytes cut from that line (`cut_bytes`, else
>     0). The text is never empty because of the bound.
> - **Owner:** *(unchanged; "plain-text formatter" covers both reads)*;
>   canonical `orbit-protocol` management v7.
> - **Boundary:**
>   - No primary history while the alternate screen is active, semantic
>     command regions, escapes, styles, raw PTY bytes or ORBF frames.
>   - *(remaining items unchanged)*

Note: 8 MiB is sized to typical full ORB-C8 histories, which hold about
8 MiB of single-codepoint text. It is not a ceiling on what the budget can
hold, because multi-codepoint graphemes are stored apart from cells.
Larger text truncates and says so.

Wire: management v6 → v7. Add `ManagementClientMessage::ReadHistory` (no
payload) and `ManagementServerMessage::History`. `History` carries the
`VisibleText` fields with `omitted_lines: u32` and `cut_bytes: u32`, and
has its own `MAX_HISTORY_MESSAGE_BYTES` = header + fixed +
`MAX_METADATA_BYTES` + 8 MiB.
- It is a breaking exact-version change.
- Known consumers:
  - Eon Runtime, the only management lease holder, which moves in the same
    change set;
  - Eon, through the generation identity.
- Venus does not speak management.
- Per memory `orbs-orbf-wire-bump-checklist`, the bump also updates the
  version goldens and the manifest subtree-hash proof.
- Batching: v7 carries any other Orbit management change approved by the
  time eon-u5bvd.2 starts (eon-0um2b plans to share a bump), and waits for
  none.

## 2. EON-C35: amend, adding `eon pane history`

Reason: EON-C35 owns CLI terminal reads. Its Boundary currently excludes
history.

Add to Trigger:

> - `eon pane history TARGET [--json] [--edit]`, with the same TARGET and
>   selection.

Add to Result:

> - `eon pane history` reads TARGET's retained history and live area through
>   ORB-C17's `ReadHistory` and carries the same JSON fields as `eon pane
>   read`, except that `omitted_lines` and `cut_bytes` replace `omitted_rows`.
>   Human output prints the text alone on stdout; when either is nonzero it
>   also writes one notice to stderr naming them and the 8 MiB bound, and
>   exits 0.
> - `eon pane history TARGET --edit` opens that text in the configured editor
>   as the window's Scrollback popup does (EON-C10), over TARGET in its tab,
>   and prints nothing (`--json` prints the target and the popup). TARGET's
>   tab must be its window's active tab in the shown workspace; otherwise it
>   changes nothing and fails with `not-active`, exit 1. It changes no active
>   tab, shown workspace or desktop focus.

Change the Boundary's first item to:

> - styles, streaming or waiting (eon-cli-action-discovery-ogzi), and
>   history beyond ORB-C17's retained history;

Failures:
- The existing failures stay. `terminal_access = "none"` refuses `history`
  and `history --edit` with `terminal-access-off`, and no failure carries
  content.
- `--edit` adds `not-active` (above), and EON-C10's `edit-command`
  (exit 1) for a missing or unexecutable editor.

Wire: EONW v32 → v33. Add `Action::ReadTerminalHistory { target, edit:
bool }`, and a `Response::History` carrying the `TerminalText` fields with
`omitted_lines` and `cut_bytes`.
- Only `Response::History`, a reply the CLI receives, gets the larger
  ceiling (8 MiB of text plus metadata).
- Every other message, and everything Venus receives, keeps the general
  2 MiB `MAX_MESSAGE_BYTES`.
- With `edit: true`, the reply carries the target and popup, not the text.
- Consumers:
  - Eon Runtime and the Eon CLI;
  - Venus, which consumes EONW by path and needs no code change beyond the
    version.
- Per memory `eonw-codec-change-needs-bump`, this is a version bump, not
  an in-place amendment.

## 3. EON-C10: runtime-policy clause for the Scrollback popup

Reason: this adds a window action, a new popup kind and a private file's
lifetime, which is a lifecycle and trust rule (Contract-Driven Method items
2 and 3). The popup's look and its label stay a feature.

Add to Runtime policy, after Anima:

> Scrollback defaults to Alt+Shift+E. Pressed in the active tab, the
> supervisor exports the terminal the tab shows (its shown popup, else its
> selected pane) through ORB-C17's `ReadHistory`, writes that text to a new
> private file, and then opens a transient popup over it whose command,
> built for that press, is `[editor] command` with the file's path
> appended, as `eon edit` builds it. The file is mode 0600 in a fresh
> mode-0700 directory under the window's private runtime directory. Its first
> line is a notice when the text was truncated (how many earlier lines were
> left out, and any cut of the newest line), or when the terminal was on the
> alternate screen ("This pane is in a full-screen app; Eon shows only its
> screen. Quit the app to see the history."). It is a snapshot: edits change
> no terminal, and the file is not kept. When the popup's terminal ends
> (the editor exits, or the popup is dismissed, replaced, hidden, or its tab
> or window closes), the supervisor removes that directory without following
> links, and the popup it covered, or the pane, shows again. Dismissing or
> replacing the popup stops the editor, discarding unsaved edits; to keep
> them, save under another name first. A supervisor removes, when it starts,
> every snapshot directory whose supervisor is no longer running, except one
> that belongs to a popup it adopts in recovery, which it removes when that
> popup ends. A tab showing no terminal changes nothing. If the export fails
> or times out, or the editor is missing, no popup starts, the window shows
> the existing popup start-failure notice, and no snapshot is left. The window
> key is the person's own action, and `[agents] terminal_access` does not
> govern it; its CLI path, `eon pane history --edit`, is governed (EON-C35).

Add to the configuration paragraph: Scrollback accepts `keybinding`,
`label` and `enabled`, and rejects `command` and `keep_alive = true`, as
Anima does. Its command is not part of the popup catalog.

Amend the Boundary's terminal-content exception list:

> EON-C35's read of visible text, retained history, title and working
> directory, the Scrollback popup's private snapshot, and EON-C36's input

## 4. docs/CONFIGURATION.md (feature text, .4a and .4b land it)

```toml
[popups.scrollback]
enabled = true # Enable this feature or popup.
keybinding = "Alt+Shift+E" # Popup shortcut using physical keys.
label = "Scrollback" # Popup display name.
```

The Editor section adds:
- The editor must stay in the foreground until it is done. A GUI editor
  needs its wait flag (for example `code --wait`), or the snapshot is
  removed when it returns.
- Dismissing the Scrollback popup stops the editor. Save under another name
  to keep edits.
- Eon removes the snapshot's directory but not the editor's own state
  files kept elsewhere, such as Neovim's swap, undo and shada files under
  `~/.local/state/nvim`.

Fixed values and their reasons (Configurability record for the siblings):
- 8 MiB bound: a protocol bound sized to typical full ORB-C8 histories.
- Plain, unwrapped layout: a format contract.
- 0600/0700 under the runtime directory: safety.
- Deletion at popup end: data lifetime and safety.

The key, label and enabled flag are configurable.

comments.text:
# eon-u5bvd.1 record 4: choices, falsifiers, sibling plan

Revised 2026-11-05 after the Opus gate (PASS WITH FIXES, all eight
findings folded in).

- **Approval state:** eon-overseer approved items 1-3, 5-8, 10-12 and 15
  on 2026-11-05 (relayed in INBOX), with gate findings 3 and 4 folded into
  record 3.
- **Approved by Lucca, 2026-11-05:** items 4, 9, 13 and 14 (contract and
  wire), as the Opus gate framed them. Relayed by eon-overseer with his
  words: "yyes", in answer to "I recommend yes to all four". Record 3's
  contract text is approved with them. Every choice in this record is now
  decided.

## Choices

1. **Order: retained history, then the current screen, oldest first, as
   one text.** *(Overseer-approved.)* Reason: it matches the parent
   acceptance, Zellij and Ghostty's `.screen`, and one `Formatter` pass at
   one revision.
2. **Alternate screen: export only its live area, with `screen:
   alternate` and a first-line notice in the editor file.**
   *(Overseer-approved; notice per gate finding 4.)*
   - Reason:
     - libghostty keeps no alternate history.
     - The pinned formatter cannot read the inactive screen.
     - Without a notice, the file in less, vim or opencode silently shows
       one screen.
   - Upstream follow-up, not filed by me (rule 8): a Ghostty formatter
     option to format the inactive (primary) screen, so a full-screen app
     need not hide the history.
3. **Lines: one per logical line, with soft wraps joined.** Trailing
   blanks are trimmed, spacers dropped and grapheme parts kept. Controls
   other than LF become U+FFFD. *(Overseer-approved.)*
4. **Bound: 8 MiB of text. Past it, Orbit drops the earliest whole lines
   and counts them in `omitted_lines`.** When the newest line alone exceeds
   8 MiB (for example a single-line JSON dump), Orbit keeps its tail, cut at
   a character boundary, and reports `cut_bytes`. The text is never empty
   because of the bound. *(Approved by Lucca 2026-11-05, relayed; edge case per gate finding 3.)*
   - Yes, the bound can truncate the earliest retained line. It is
     reported:
     - in JSON;
     - in one stderr line for human output;
     - in the editor file's first line.
   - Reason: 8 MiB is *typical* for a full 16 MiB history of
     single-codepoint cells. It is not a ceiling, since grapheme storage
     can yield more. 2 MiB would truncate ordinary wide-pane histories.
5. **Plain text, no ANSI.** *(Overseer-approved.)*
6. **A writable snapshot that is discarded.** Dismissing or replacing the
   popup kills the editor and its unsaved edits; save under another name
   first, documented in record 3 §4. *(Overseer-approved; finding 8.)*
7. **CLI: `eon pane history TARGET [--json]` on stdout only.**
   *(Overseer-approved.)*
8. **Authorization: `terminal_access` governs the CLI; the window key is
   not governed.** *(Overseer-approved.)*
9. **Window action's CLI path: `eon pane history TARGET --edit`.** In v1
   it works only when TARGET's tab is the active tab of the shown
   workspace; otherwise it refuses with `not-active`, exit 1, changing
   nothing. *(Approved by Lucca 2026-11-05, relayed; restriction per gate finding 1.)* Reason:
   - It gives exact parity with the key in one supervisor path.
   - `invoke_popup` already refuses inactive tabs.
   - An editor waiting in a hidden tab is easy to forget.
10. **Key: built-in transient `[popups.scrollback]` on Alt+Shift+E, with
    `keybinding`, `label` and `enabled`.** *(Overseer-approved; the gate
    confirmed the key is free and overridable.)*
    - Correction (gate finding 1): this is a **new popup kind**, not a
      catalog command.
    - The catalog refuses `PopupCommand::Edit`
      (`managed_environment.rs:532`), and `invoke_popup` starts only fixed
      catalog commands.
    - The supervisor handles the entry: it reads, writes the file, then
      starts a transient popup whose argv it builds for that press.
    - Venus still needs no code change: it sends the existing
      `InvokePopup`.
11. **Temporary file: Runtime-owned.**
    - **Layout:** `<window runtime dir>/snapshots/<supervisor pid+start>-<n>/<target>-scrollback.txt`;
      0700 directories, a 0600 file, `O_EXCL|O_NOFOLLOW`.
    - **Removal:** when the popup's terminal ends.
    - **Start sweep:** at start, the supervisor sweeps the directories of
      supervisors no longer running, except the directory of a popup it
      adopts in recovery, which it removes when that popup ends.
    - **Documented gaps** *(gate finding 7)*:
      - editor state outside the directory (Neovim swap, undo and shada
        under `~/.local/state/nvim`);
      - on the macOS fallback `/tmp/eon-<uid>`, which is not tmpfs, only
        the start sweep cleans up.

    *(Overseer-approved; .4a settles how the recovery record names an
    adopted directory.)*
12. **Editor position: top of the file, with no line argument.**
    *(Overseer-approved.)*
13. **Contract placement: amend ORB-C17, EON-C35 and EON-C10, with no new
    IDs.** *(Approved by Lucca 2026-11-05, relayed.)*
14. **Wires: Orbit management v6 → v7 and EONW v32 → v33, breaking and
    exact-version, with no adapter.** *(Approved by Lucca 2026-11-05,
    relayed; batching and the ceiling scope per gate finding 5.)*
    - v7 carries any Orbit management change approved by the time .2
      starts (eon-0um2b plans to share a bump). It waits for none, since
      this is P1 and Ronald is waiting.
    - The larger EONW ceiling applies only to `Response::History`, which
      the CLI receives. Everything else, including everything Venus
      receives, keeps 2 MiB.
15. **Failures and GUI editors.** On an export failure or timeout, or a
    missing editor, the window shows the existing popup start-failure
    notice, starts no popup and leaves no snapshot *(gate finding 6)*. GUI
    editors need their wait flag, which is documented and not detected.
    *(Overseer-approved.)*

## Cheapest falsifier per boundary

| Boundary | Falsifier | Sibling |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Order, unwrap, trim, spacers, graphemes, control chars, empty history, alternate screen only | libghostty unit tests in `orbit/src` (like `visible.rs`): history+screen order; a wrapped line joined; `漢字e\u{301}` kept; empty history = screen; `?1049h` gives `screen: alternate` and its rows only | .2 |
| Eviction starts at the earliest retained line | unit test with a small `set_scrollback_max_bytes`: the first exported line is the first retained one | .2 |
| 8 MiB leading-line bound, count, single-line tail cut | unit tests of the fit function: past 8 MiB drops whole lines; one 9 MiB line keeps an 8 MiB tail on a char boundary (a multi-byte char straddling the cut), `cut_bytes` correct, text non-empty | .2 |
| Bound sized to the budget | real-PTY check: fill the 16 MiB history with 4-byte characters at 200 columns, then record the text size and reply time | .2 |
| **Window stall** (gate finding 2) | under load (another pane running `yes`, load average recorded), measure keystroke echo latency in a second pane while a full-budget `ReadHistory` runs, against the idle baseline (EON-C35's 82-86 ms method). It fails if echo stalls past the read's own duration, or if the reply misses the 2 s deadline | .2 (Runtime half in .3) |
| Unread answer at size (gate finding 2) | extend `orbit-visible-text`'s unread-answer and slow-peer check to an 8 MiB `History`: the lease holder loses its lease and PTY processing never blocks | .2 |
| No side effects, no partial update | real-PTY: viewport offset, selection and revision unchanged; no PTY input; a held DEC 2026 update delays the reply | .2 |
| Lease admission, one in flight | extend law `management_read_needs_a_live_settled_lease` and `orbit-lease-input`'s pipelined refusal to `ReadHistory` | .2 |
| Wire bounds | protocol tests: `History` round-trips at the bound and rejects one byte more; v6 peers are refused; an EONW non-`History` message over 2 MiB is still refused | .2 / .3 |
| Authorization | extend `terminal_access_none_refuses_every_read_and_send` to `history` and `--edit` | .3 / .4b |
| CLI text, JSON, notice, exits | process test like `pane_read_prints_the_text_or_json_and_exits_by_failure` | .3 |
| File privacy and lifetime | supervisor tests: 0700/0600; a planted symlink refuses; the directory is gone after editor exit, dismissal and tab close; stale-owner sweep; an adopted popup's directory survives recovery and goes when the popup ends | .4a |
| Failure notice | supervisor test: export timeout and missing editor show the popup start-failure notice and leave no directory | .4a |
| Alternate-screen notice | supervisor test: a source on the alternate screen gives the first-line notice | .4a |
| `--edit` on a hidden tab | process test: `not-active`, exit 1, nothing changes | .4b |
| End to end | one isolated installed observation (parent acceptance): Alt+Shift+E opens hx at the earliest retained line through the screen; `:q` returns to the pane; the directory is gone; `eon pane history` text = file text minus any notice line | .4b |

## Sibling plan (re-split per the gate; acceptance kept)

- **Prerequisite: triage eon-zmq4b** (orbit-visible-text's unread-answer
  bound fails under load) before .2 lands. It is the same slow-peer path
  at 8× the size.
- **eon-u5bvd.2 (Orbit export): confirm,** with:
  - `ReadHistory`/`History` on management v7 inside ORB-C17;
  - plain, unwrapped, trimmed text from the active screen only;
  - the 8 MiB bound with `omitted_lines` and `cut_bytes`;
  - folding in any Orbit change approved by the time it starts.

  Add to its acceptance:
  - the window-stall echo measurement under load;
  - the 8 MiB unread-answer check.
- **eon-u5bvd.3 (CLI): confirm,** with:
  - `eon pane history TARGET [--json]` on EONW v33;
  - the larger ceiling on `Response::History` only;
  - `terminal_access` governing it;
  - the stderr notice;
  - stdout only.
- **eon-u5bvd.4 splits into:**
  - **.4a, snapshot store and Scrollback popup:**
    - the new popup kind whose argv is built on each press;
    - the private store, removal at popup end, the start sweep and the
      recovery-adoption exception;
    - the notices (truncation, alternate screen) and the start-failure
      path;
    - `[popups.scrollback]` on Alt+Shift+E, with its defaults in
      CONFIGURATION.md.

    It names .4b as its rule 5 CLI path, and is blocked by .3.
  - **.4b, `--edit`, docs and end-to-end proof:**
    - `eon pane history TARGET --edit` (with `not-active` for a hidden
      tab);
    - USAGE, the CONFIGURATION Editor notes (wait flag, save under another
      name, editor state files) and CHANGELOG;
    - the isolated installed observation.

    It is blocked by .4a.
- The parent stays as is. The design is decided: all fifteen items and
  record 3's contract text are approved. The overseer replays these
  records, closes .1, files .4a and .4b, and starts .2.

## Done

Design done on 2026-11-05. Nothing in these records is still waiting for
a choice.

comments.text:
# Opus gate: eon-u5bvd.1 (scrollback in the editor)

Read-only Opus gate, 2026-11-05, edge `570d0ad`.

## Verdict: PASS WITH FIXES

The evidence holds. I spot-checked:
- libghostty-rs `fmt.rs`: unwrap, trim, alloc, and "no selection = entire screen";
- Ghostty `formatter.zig:931` and `PageList.zig:6758` (history first), and `Surface.zig` (0600, unwrap);
- Zellij `File::create` at `efd8fd5`;
- ORB-C17, EON-C35, management v6, EONW 2 MiB, the 2 s deadline and the 16 MiB budget.

One claim is wrong (finding 1).

## Findings, ranked

1. **Major: the window path is not reuse.**
   - `PopupCommand::Edit` builds the `eon edit` *pane* command (`workspace.rs:1170`). The popup catalog refuses it (`managed_environment.rs:532`).
   - `invoke_popup` (`workspace.rs:1415`) starts a fixed catalog command and refuses tabs that are not active. The Orbit read lives in the supervisor.
   - So Scrollback is a new popup kind, whose command is built per press after a read and a file write.
   - **Fix:** correct trace steps 2 and 6 and record 3. Make `--edit` on a hidden tab refuse with `not-active` in v1. Split .4.

2. **Major: the whole window can stall.**
   - A terminal read blocks the supervisor for up to 2 s (`supervisor.rs:2704`). An 8 MiB read can freeze every pane in the window.
   - eon-zmq4b: a 1 MiB unread answer already broke slow-peer timing under load.
   - **Fix:** the .2 falsifier measures keystroke echo in another pane during a full-budget read, under load. Extend the unread-answer check to an 8 MiB `History`. Triage eon-zmq4b before .2 lands.

3. **Medium: the bound has an edge case.**
   - With unwrap on, one logical line can pass 8 MiB (single-line JSON). "Last whole lines" then keeps nothing, which breaks "the live area is kept".
   - The size inference also ignores grapheme storage.
   - **Fix:** when the newest line alone exceeds the bound, keep its tail cut at a character boundary and report it. Call 8 MiB "typical", not a ceiling.

4. **Medium: the alternate screen is silent in the editor.**
   - In less, vim or opencode, the file shows one screen with no explanation.
   - **Fix:** add a first-line notice: "This pane is in a full-screen app; Eon shows only its screen. Quit it to see the history." File an upstream follow-up for an inactive-screen formatter option (rule 8).

5. **Medium: wire cost.**
   - The bump cannot be avoided. Changing `ReadVisible`'s meaning also bumps, and reading through ORBS/ORBF frames would be a second history reader.
   - Lucca's eon-t3fyd.1 gate: "batching management bumps costs nothing".
   - **Fix:** when .2 starts, put into v7 any Orbit change approved by then (eon-0um2b plans to share a bump). Don't wait on undesigned work for a P1. Raise the EONW ceiling only for responses the CLI receives.

6. **Minor: the failure surface is unspecified.**
   - Nothing says what the person sees on an export timeout or a missing editor.
   - **Fix:** reuse the popup start-failure notice, and test it.

7. **Minor: the temp-file lifecycle has three gaps.**
   - Security is sound. Under the private 0700 parent, symlink and TOCTOU risks are same-user only, which EON-C35 excludes.
   - Gaps:
     - Neovim's swap, undo and shada files live outside the directory and survive a killed editor.
     - On macOS, `/tmp/eon-<uid>` is not tmpfs, so the start-time sweep carries the cleanup there.
     - A recovered supervisor must not sweep the directory of a popup it adopted.
   - **Fix:** settle the sweep rule in .4, and document the editor gaps in CONFIGURATION.

8. **Minor: edits can be lost.** Dismissing or replacing the popup (for example with Alt+Shift+J) kills the editor. **Fix:** document "save under another name first".

9. **OK: the key.** Alt+Shift+E is free in `shortcuts.rs` and the CONFIGURATION defaults. `[popups.scrollback]` makes it configurable (rule 6). A user popup already on that key overrides it (`Overridden`) and does not fail startup.

10. **OK: the CLI.** `eon pane history` fits beside `read`/`send` and keeps `read`'s rows intact. Record 3 correctly limits "changes nothing" to the read, not `--edit`.

## Bead sizing

- .2 is heavy (wire-bump checklist, Bend, goldens, real PTY) but fits one session.
- .3 fits one session.
- .4 is too big. Split it:
  - **.4a:** the snapshot store, sweep, popup kind and key;
  - **.4b:** `--edit`, the docs and the installed end-to-end proof.

  .4a names .4b (rule 5).

## Decisions for Lucca

1. **Size limit.** A snapshot holds at most 8 MiB of text, about 100,000 long lines. Past that, the oldest lines are dropped, and the editor file and CLI say how many. The newest output is never cut. **Recommend yes:** Orbit's own history memory rarely holds more.

2. **Agent path.** `eon pane history p3` prints p3's history. `--edit` opens it in your editor in p3's tab. **Recommend yes, for the tab you're viewing only:** an editor waiting in a hidden tab is easy to forget.

3. **Where the rules live.** Extend three existing rule sets (Orbit's screen read, the CLI read, the popup rules) rather than adding new ones. **Recommend yes:** same permissions and failures, all in one place.

4. **Version bumps.** Orbit's internal protocol goes v6 to v7, and the window protocol v32 to v33. Older windows get moved by hand once, as with every bump, and there is no compatibility code. **Recommend yes,** folding in any other Orbit change approved by then, but waiting for none, since Ronald is waiting.

The overseer approves the other eleven, folding findings 3 and 4 into record 3.

title: Export bounded retained history and screen as text from Orbit
description:
## Why

The editor/CLI need one authoritative bounded text snapshot. Parent: eon-u5bvd (scrollback in the configured editor); its design child must approve the boundary first.

## Evidence

- orbit/src/pty.rs: terminal owner and retained state.
- orbit/crates/protocol/src: canonical management/observation codec.
- orbit/docs/CONTRACTS.md: ORB-C2/ORB-C8 history and current observation boundaries.

## Scope

In: only the approved bounded read-only history-plus-screen export, owner-loop mechanism, canonical codec and required consumers, docs/identity updates and a real-PTY bound check. Out: search UI, editor launch, input mutation, durable transcripts, another interactive client or full observer enrichment.

## Acceptance

- One bounded snapshot follows approved ordering, format and truncation semantics across empty history, wrapped/Unicode text, retention eviction and active/alternate screen.
- Export does not consume or alter the terminal's input, retained state or interactive attachment.
- Real-PTY verification proves the bound and content through the canonical boundary.
- Every breaking protocol change and consumer update is approved first; record portability disposition and references on the bead.

## Implementation Notes

1. Read parent/design decision and confirm exact approved fields/bounds.
2. Reuse the accepted history owner and canonical codec; update every affected consumer in the same slice where exact versions require it.
3. Align approved ORB records/docs and protocol identities; no compatibility adapter.

## Verification

Approved real-PTY export check plus full affected Orbit/protocol/consumer Rust and Nix boundary surfaces using the supported eon-test sandbox, fmt/clippy for changed Orbit/Venus crates. Fresh reviews; record exact artifact/revision/environment.

## Stop Conditions

Stop if the design child is not approved, owner shape drifts, another client role or raw-state reconstruction is needed, or verification fails twice.

## Maintenance Notes

Intended portability: neutral history/text logic; record any actual isolated platform dependency. Do not claim rich-presentation fidelity from this text projection.

comments.text:
# eon-u5bvd.2 record 1: implementation

Worktree `eon-u5bvd-2` at edge `179a6ea` (includes eon-zmq4b), 2026-11-05.
Implements eon-u5bvd.1 records 02 to 04 as approved (Lucca, 2026-11-05,
"yyes" to items 4, 9, 13 and 14).

## Folded in

Nothing. eon-0um2b (agent keys and interrupt) is still an open, undecided
decision, so no other Orbit management change was approved when this
started; v7 waits for none, as approved.

## Wire: Orbit management v6 -> v7 (breaking, exact-version, no adapter)

- `ClientMessage::ReadHistory` (tag 8, no payload) and
  `ServerMessage::History(HistoryText)` (tag 76).
- `HistoryText`: the `VisibleText` fields with `omitted_lines: u32` and
  `cut_bytes: u32` in place of `omitted_rows`; payload order revision,
  screen, rows, columns, title, directory, omitted_lines, cut_bytes, lossy,
  text.
- `MAX_HISTORY_TEXT_BYTES` = 8 MiB; `MAX_HISTORY_MESSAGE_BYTES` = header +
  fixed fields (34 bytes) + `MAX_METADATA_BYTES` + 8 MiB. Every other bound is
  unchanged.
- `--management-v6` becomes `--management-v7` (Orbit CLI, Eon Runtime's
  launch, the Eon test helper, every real-PTY check, LIFECYCLE.md). No alias.
- Consumers: Eon Runtime (moves in this change; it sends no `ReadHistory`
  yet, which eon-u5bvd.3 adds) and Eon through the generation identity. Venus
  does not speak management. ORBS, ORBF and EONW are unchanged, so
  `components/eon-v5.json` (which lists only ORBF/ORBS for Orbit) needs no
  subtree-hash change, and Eon's package version stays (that convention is
  for EONW bumps).
- Goldens: `management_v7_messages_have_canonical_bytes` (generation byte 7,
  `ReadHistory` and `History` bytes), the `ProgramStatus` golden's version
  byte, the per-kind bound test (History at its bound and one byte over, a
  client message of kind 8 bounded at 4 KiB), decoder rejections (false
  lossy, control characters, trailing payload on `ReadHistory`), and v6/v8
  peers refused by the existing `VERSION - 1`/`VERSION + 1` test.

## Orbit host and worker

- `src/history.rs` (new): one libghostty `Formatter` pass over the active
  screen with `Format::Plain`, `unwrap = true` and `trim = false`; Orbit then
  trims only real trailing spaces and trailing blank lines, and turns
  controls other than LF into U+FFFD; then `fit`, the 8 MiB leading-line
  bound with the over-bound newest line's tail cut at a char boundary.
- Review round 1 (Codex finding 1): the formatter's own trim drops a
  combining mark that sits on a blank cell. `src/visible.rs` had the same
  defect for `ReadVisible`, so it also formats each row untrimmed and trims
  only real spaces; this is a fix to the existing ORB-C17 promise ("combining
  marks kept"), with no contract text change.
- `src/management.rs`: the connection keeps which text the read asked for
  (`read: Option<TextRead>`), answered by Bend's existing `ManageRead`.
  Bend decides both reads alike (same admission, held-update wait, one in
  flight), so the boundary schema and the laws keep one `Read` event.
- Bend: the management answer `Visible{}` is renamed `Readout{}` (it now
  answers either read; `Text` collides with Base, BEND.md updated). The law
  `management_read_needs_a_live_settled_lease` keeps its statement; its
  comment now names both reads, which is the approved "extend the law to
  `ReadHistory`" (record 4 falsifier table). The boundary was regenerated
  with `tools/boundary.rs` (comments only, new schema hash).

### Bug found and fixed during proof

The first version kept the read's kind in `pending`, which `respond` clears
when the host declines a request sent while a read is held. The held read
then reached `ManageRead` with no kind and the host closed the connection.
The unchanged `orbit-visible-text` check caught it
(`held_updates_delay_the_read`). The kind now has its own field.

## Contract and docs

- ORB-C17 renamed "Bounded terminal text reads" and amended exactly as record
  3 gives it (title, Trigger, the `omitted_lines`/`cut_bytes` note, What the
  text covers, How the text is laid out, Size bound, Owner v7, Boundary's
  first item), plus a `Proof (ReadHistory)` entry.
- Deviations for the overseer to confirm (consequential, no new behavior):
  1. ORB-C17 "What the text drops" said "selection and history are
     dropped", which would contradict the amended read. It now says
     "cursor and selection are dropped, and `ReadVisible` also drops
     history".
  2. ORB-C13 lists the `ReadHistory` request and the `History` reply's
     8 MiB text bound beside `ReadVisible`'s 1 MiB, and its proof line names
     the `eon-u5bvd.2` commit for management v7, as `eon-buys1.1` did for v6.
  3. ORB-C1's Boundary says the lease holder "reads visible text and history
     through ORB-C17".
  4. Consumes lines: ORB-C5 and ORB-C13 (Orbit index), and the three root
     `docs/CONTRACTS.md` lines that named management v6 or generation 6.
- BEHAVIOR.md: new "History text" section with the unit and real-PTY
  coverage; HOST.md: the read event covers both requests; LIFECYCLE.md: the
  8 MiB reply bound.
- CHANGELOGs: `orbit/CHANGELOG.md` (generation 7 entry) and `CHANGELOG.md`
  (Unreleased: the proven ORB-C17 change; no user command yet).

## Portability

The history text logic is platform-neutral libghostty and string handling;
no platform seam changed. Linux proof only, as for ORB-C17 before.

## References

libghostty-rs `9ede35b` `fmt.rs` (`Formatter`, `with_unwrap`, `with_trim`,
`format_alloc`), Ghostty `521cf2c` `formatter.zig` (null selection = whole
screen, history first), as record 1 of eon-u5bvd.1 inspected.

## Not done here

- Codex review skipped: `rota status` showed Codex with no quota
  ("quota limit", 0% left) at 2026-11-05 13:50 UTC, and the brief says to
  skip it then.
- Upstream follow-up (rule 8, record 4 item 2): a Ghostty formatter option to
  format the inactive (primary) screen. Not filed, per record 4.

# eon-u5bvd.2 record 2: proof

x86_64 Linux (16 threads, 31 GB), worktree `eon-u5bvd-2` from edge
`179a6ea`, 2026-11-05. Route: the Orbit/protocol/consumer Rust and Nix
boundary surfaces (bead Verification), plus the gate's acceptance additions.
Superseded proof: tree `8a29686` (before review round 1) passed the same
checks; the numbers below are for the final tree.

## Checks on the commit's tree (git tree `98c114e`)

Tree `98c114e` differs from `825118b` only in `orbit/docs/BEHAVIOR.md` and
`orbit/docs/CONTRACTS.md` (the measurement summaries, review round 1's last
nit). Rerunning the same 63-check `nix build` on `98c114e` exited 0 and
built nothing (log `eon-u5bvd-2-work/nix-proof-98c114e.log`): no check
derivation reads those files, so every check result below holds for the
commit's tree. No Rust source changed, so the `eon-test`, fmt, clippy and
real-PTY results stand.

### Run on tree `825118b`


- `nix build --keep-going --max-jobs 2 --cores 6` of 63 checks: every
  `orbit-*` check (58, including `orbit-laws`, `orbit-boundary`, both
  terminfo checks and the new `orbit-history-text`), `default`,
  `bundle-launch`, `bundle-relink`, `eonbase-closure` and
  `managed-command-path`: exit 0, no failure (log
  `eon-u5bvd-2-work/nix-proof-825118b.log`).
- `nix develop -c eon-test -p orbit-protocol -p yazelix-orbit -p eon-runtime
  -p eon`: 465 passed, 0 failed, 55 ignored (the 54 real-PTY checks the Nix
  checks run, and one Runtime test).
- `cargo fmt --all -- --check`: clean. `cargo clippy --locked -p
  orbit-protocol -p yazelix-orbit -p eon-runtime -p eon --all-targets -- -D
  warnings`: clean (Orbit rechecked after a touch).

## Real-PTY runs (release Orbit, sandboxed `eon-test`)

`ORBIT_BIN=<target>/release/yazelix-orbit nix develop -c eon-test -p
yazelix-orbit --test real_pty -- --ignored --exact NAME`, on tree `825118b`:

- `history_text`: passed idle, and 3 of 3 beside 12 `yes` burners.
- `visible_text` and `lease_input`: passed.

Measurements printed by `orbit-history-text`:

| Case | Idle (load 2.1) | 12 burners (load 7.95 / 9.04 / 10.17) |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Full history, 16,000 lines of `U+1D11E` at 200x50 | 7,448,135 bytes, 9,476 lines kept, 6,524 evicted, 0 omitted; read in 87 ms | same text; read in 149-156 ms |
| Unread answer (16,000 lines of `é`) | 3,752,495 bytes; title reached the client within 1 s; lease lost in 0.9-2.5 s | same, 3 of 3 |
| Echo in another Orbit, idle baseline | median 4.9 ms, max 5.3 ms | median 2.1-2.7 ms, max 3.2-3.9 ms |
| Echo during back-to-back full reads | 15 reads (median 74 ms, max 103 ms): echo median 1.7 ms, max 2.5 ms | 8 reads each (median 142-169 ms, max 157-181 ms): echo median 2.3-4.6 ms, max 4.2-12.9 ms |

The check asserts, per eon-u5bvd.1 record 4's window-stall falsifier, that
the slowest echo stays below the slowest read's own duration (it did: at most
12.9 ms beside reads of at least 157 ms) and that no read takes the 2 s
deadline. Separate Orbit runs share only the machine, so this bounds their
contention; a full read holds its own Orbit's owner loop for at most its
reply time, about 90 ms idle and 180 ms at load 10. The supervisor-blocking
half (EONW, 2 s `TERMINAL_DEADLINE`) is in eon-u5bvd.3's acceptance.

The bound check: the real 16 MiB budget of single-codepoint four-byte cells
yields 7.45 MB, under the 8 MiB bound, as eon-u5bvd.1 record 1 inferred. The
8 MiB truncation paths are proved by unit tests (`src/history.rs`:
`long_text_keeps_the_last_lines_that_fit`,
`an_over_bound_newest_line_keeps_its_tail`), per the refined acceptance.

## Sensitivity checks (each made its check fail)

1. `with_unwrap(false)` in `src/history.rs`: `orbit-history-text` failed,
   the wrapped 100-cell line split (`history_text.rs:93`).
2. `ReadHistory` mapped to the visible read in `src/management.rs`:
   `orbit-history-text` failed, "expected History, received Visible".
3. The formatter's own trim turned back on (`with_trim(true)`) in
   `src/history.rs` and `src/visible.rs`: both
   `space_backed_combining_marks_are_kept` unit tests failed with
   `"A B\nC\nD"`. Before the round 1 fix, the same tests failed against the
   unfixed tree, confirming Codex finding 1.

Each mutation was reverted (and the release Orbit rebuilt for 1 and 2). The
unchanged `orbit-visible-text` check also caught a real bug in the first
version (the held read's kind cleared by an in-flight refusal; record 1).

title: Expose authorized bounded pane history through the eon CLI
description:
## Why

Agents need the same retained-output snapshot a person opens in the editor (rule 5). Parent: eon-u5bvd (scrollback in the configured editor); design and Orbit export precede this slice.

## Evidence

- runtime/crates/eon-runtime/src/cli.rs: pane read parsing.
- runtime/crates/eon-runtime/src/sessions.rs: authorized Orbit reads.
- runtime/crates/eon-runtime/src/supervisor.rs: terminal targeting and policy; docs/CONTRACTS.md EON-C35.

## Scope

In: approved CLI spelling/targeting, canonical EONW request if required, [agents] terminal_access authorization, bounded Orbit text export, stdout/file behavior approved in design, help/USAGE/configuration/CHANGELOG and process checks. Out: window shortcut/editor popup, search, persistent capture or compatibility aliases.

## Acceptance

- CLI returns the approved history-plus-screen text with honest bound/truncation information, including empty and stale-target cases.
- Denied terminal access sends no terminal content; stale/gone targets and protocol failures preserve approved machine status/data.
- Explicit targets preserve the shown tab/popup and desktop focus.
- CLI matches the canonical Orbit export and all approved EON-C35/EON-C10 changes; configurable bounds/defaults or valid fixed-value reasons are documented.

## Implementation Notes

1. Read parent, approved design and Orbit sibling; replace proposed command names with approved spelling.
2. Reuse pane-read authorization/targeting and the canonical export, never scrape Venus frames.
3. Update all touched protocol callers and identity/doc fixtures.

## Verification

Focused Runtime/CLI process checks via `nix develop -c eon-test -p eon-runtime -p eon`, affected Rust/Nix boundary checks, and an isolated installed long-output CLI observation. Fresh reviews and exact proof record.

## Stop Conditions

Stop before any unapproved EONW/contract/default change, if the Orbit export is unavailable, or after two identical verification failures.

## Maintenance Notes

One history export owner; no second scrollback parser or file format. Temporary snapshots belong to the window sibling unless the approved CLI explicitly writes a requested file.

comments.author: lucca
comments.text:
# eon-u5bvd.3 record 1: implementation

Worktree `eon-u5bvd-3` at edge `9a2031d` (includes eon-u5bvd.2, Orbit
management v7), 2026-11-05. Implements the approved design (Lucca,
2026-11-05 14:10 UTC: `eon pane history TARGET [--json]` on EONW v33, the
larger ceiling only on `Response::History`, governed by `terminal_access`,
the truncation notice on stderr and the text on stdout only) and the EON-C35
and EON-C10 text of eon-u5bvd.1 record 03.

## Wire: EONW v32 -> v33 (breaking, exact-version, no adapter)

- `v32.rs`/`v32/` renamed to `v33.rs`/`v33/` across every importer
  (Runtime, Eon, Venus); `VERSION = 33`; every hex golden's version byte and
  the two `Runtime` goldens' `workspace_protocol` field moved to 33.
- `Action::ReadTerminalHistory { target }`, request tag 41 (the test that
  probed 41 as an unknown tag now probes 42).
- `Response::History(TerminalHistory)`, kind 141 (136-140 are the
  subscription's). `TerminalHistory` carries `TerminalText`'s fields with
  `omitted_lines: u32` and `cut_bytes: u32` in place of `omitted_rows`;
  payload order target, caller, revision, screen, rows, columns, title,
  directory, omitted_lines, cut_bytes, u32-length text. Text bound
  `MAX_HISTORY_TEXT_BYTES` = 8 MiB, asserted equal to Orbit's
  `management::MAX_HISTORY_TEXT_BYTES` in `sessions.rs`.
- The ceiling: `MAX_HISTORY_MESSAGE_BYTES` = header + two largest targets +
  caller flag + fixed fields + `MAX_TERMINAL_METADATA_BYTES` + 8 MiB
  (exactly the largest encodable `History`, asserted by test). `frame` and
  `unframe` take the bound from the message kind, so only kind 141 may pass
  2 MiB. `declared_message_len` still bounds every kind at 2 MiB; the new
  `declared_response_len` admits a `History` header up to its own bound, and
  only the CLI's reply reader (`control.rs`, `send_prepared_action`) uses it. Venus,
  the supervisor's request reader and subscriptions keep
  `declared_message_len`, so nothing Venus reads can exceed 2 MiB.
- `Error::MessageTooLarge` gains `maximum`, so its text names the bound that
  applied (it used to always print 2 MiB).
- Component graph `components/eon-v5.json`: EONW 33 in its four places, proof
  = subtree hash of `runtime/crates/eon-workspace-protocol`
  (`ab8b6b342d0e2d90c8190dd154ce950b42cec06a`). Eon 0.1.16 -> 0.1.17
  (`eon/crates/eon/Cargo.toml`, `Cargo.lock`), the EONW-bump convention.

## Runtime and CLI

- `sessions::read_history`: `ReadHistory` through the existing
  `terminal_request` (same lease, one request in flight, 2 s
  `TERMINAL_DEADLINE`, no failure with content).
- Supervisor: `ReadTerminalHistory` is dispatched with `ReadTerminal` and
  `SendTerminal` to `terminal_access`, which now takes an `Operation`
  (`Read`, `History`, `Send`); the `terminal-access-off` check, caller
  projection and target resolution are unchanged and shared.
- CLI: `eon pane history TARGET [--json]` (parser beside `pane read`), help
  line "Print a pane's or popup's history" (review round 1), the help paragraph now says read,
  history and send reach hidden workspaces and `terminal_access` governs all
  three. Human output: the text and a newline on stdout; when
  `omitted_lines` or `cut_bytes` is nonzero, one stderr line, e.g. `eon: the
  history is over its 8 MiB bound; left out the 5 earliest lines` (the figure
  derived from `MAX_HISTORY_TEXT_BYTES`; plus `and
  the first N bytes of the newest line`), exit 0. `--json`: `eon pane read`'s
  fields with `omitted_lines` and `cut_bytes` for `omitted_rows`, no stderr
  notice. Parity map (`cli/parity.rs`) maps the action to `pane history`.
- Reply write (review round 1, Codex 1): `handle_client` writes every reply
  through `write_reply`, which writes nonblocking and polls for room. It
  checks the deadline before every write attempt (review round 2). It drops
  the client once `REPLY_DEADLINE` (2 s for the whole reply) passes, or once
  `CLIENT_IO_TIMEOUT` (the existing 250 ms, now named) passes with no byte
  taken. Before, a blocking `write_all` renewed its 250 ms timeout on every
  bit of progress, so a client draining an 8 MiB History slowly could hold
  the supervisor for tens of seconds.
- Venus: the new response arm in `model.rs` (Venus never reads terminals over
  EONW); no behavior change.

## Deviations (for the overseer)

1. **No `edit` field on the wire** (accepted by eon-overseer, INBOX
   2026-11-05 18:45Z). Record 03 names `ReadTerminalHistory { target, edit:
   bool }`. `--edit` is out of this bead (eon-u5bvd.5) and its reply shape
   (target plus popup) is undefined, so a field now would likely change again
   and bump EONW anyway. .4/.5 add their own action, batched into one EONW
   bump if .4 also needs one.
2. **EON-C35 text applied without its `--edit` parts.** Record 03 assigns
   EON-C35's `--edit` text to .4b (now eon-u5bvd.5): the Trigger lists
   `eon pane history TARGET [--json]`, and the `--edit` Result bullet and
   failures wait for .5.
3. **EON-C10 Boundary, part applied now.** Record 03 §3 assigns EON-C10 to
   .4a, but its terminal-content exception list must name "retained history"
   as soon as EONW carries history, which this change does. Applied: "EON-C35's
   read of visible text, retained history, title and working directory".
   The Scrollback snapshot part waits for .4a. A one-line status amendment
   records it.
4. **Venus contract index**: only its preamble moves to v33 (its other EONW
   mentions record when behavior entered the wire). Root `docs/CONTRACTS.md`
   current-state EONW mentions move to v33 as the v32 bump did; two
   historical ones (EON-C36's amendment line and its owner's "v32 request")
   stay.
5. EON-C35's Owner line names "the EONW v26 request (v33 for `history`)".

## Configurability (rule 6)

The values a person sees: the 8 MiB bound (fixed: the ORB-C17 protocol bound,
approved in eon-u5bvd.1 record 03 §4), the stderr notice text (fixed: a
contract's honest-report text, like other CLI failure text), `pane history`
spelling (approved). `REPLY_DEADLINE` (2 s, review round 1) is fixed for
the reason the 2 s terminal-read deadline is: it is a performance budget
that keeps every pane's window actions and Venus's snapshot polls from
waiting on one slow client, not a preference a person tunes. A larger value
only lets a misbehaving client stall the window longer. A smaller one would
cut off honest CLI reads of a full 8 MiB history under load: they took up
to 264 ms in record 02. `[agents] terminal_access` already exposes the policy;
its CONFIGURATION.md description and the generated config comment
(`managed_environment.rs`) now name `history`.

## Docs

EON-C35 (status, trigger, result, failure scope, owner, boundary), EON-C10
(status line, boundary exception), current EONW version mentions in
`docs/CONTRACTS.md`, `docs/ARCHITECTURE.md`, `runtime/README.md`,
`venus/docs/{CONTRACTS,CRATES,PRESENTATION}.md`; `docs/USAGE.md` (command
table and Reading a terminal), `docs/CONFIGURATION.md`, `eon/skills/eon/SKILL.md`;
`CHANGELOG.md` (user-visible command, EONW v33 restart note) and
`venus/CHANGELOG.md` (consumes v33). EON-C35's proof entry for `history` is
added after the final proof (record 02).

## Tests added or extended

- Protocol: `history_alone_exceeds_two_mib_and_only_where_asked` (largest
  History = its bound exactly, round-trips; `declared_message_len` refuses
  it; one byte more refused by `declared_response_len` and `decode_response`;
  a non-History header over 2 MiB still refused by `declared_response_len`;
  over-bound and control-character text refused on both sides), goldens for
  the request and the response, the bad-target loop.
- Runtime: parser test covers `history`; JSON projection test;
  `control::tests::a_slow_reader_holds_the_supervisor_no_longer_than_the_reply_deadline`
  (review round 1);
  `control::tests::a_reply_past_its_deadline_stops_even_while_the_client_takes_bytes`
  (review round 2).
- Process (`workspace_control.rs`, fake Orbit answers `ReadHistory`):
  `pane_history_prints_the_text_or_json_and_names_what_the_bound_left_out`
  (human and JSON output, a 3 MiB answer through the CLI, the stderr notice
  for omitted lines and for a cut newest line, empty history, unknown and
  malformed targets, `terminal-ended` and `terminal-unavailable` without
  content, workspace unchanged, a popup's history by `uN`, `terminal_access =
  "none"`);
  `terminal_reads_and_sends_reach_a_hidden_workspace_and_change_nothing`
  reads a hidden workspace's history; `terminal_access_none_refuses_every_read_and_send`
  covers `ReadTerminalHistory`.
