comments.text:
# eon-u5bvd.3 record 2: proof

x86_64 Linux (16 threads, 31 GB), worktree `eon-u5bvd-3` from edge `9a2031d`,
2026-11-05. Route: shared runtime and wire protocol (EONW v33) plus the
installed CLI. That means the full affected Rust and Nix surfaces, plus one
isolated installed observation with the window-stall measurement from the
acceptance addition. This record covers the tree after review round 2
(record 03).

## Trees

- Final tree (committed): git tree `8eff8b211497b8445cfa37bb5773563d4ea014b3`.
  It differs from round 2's `2ea884e` only in one line of
  `docs/CONTRACTS.md`: EON-C35's proof summary now says the slow-reader
  test drains every 100 ms (round-2 re-check nit). Checks on `8eff8b2`:
  - the docs route: the diff, no contract ID changed, `git diff --cached
    --check 9a2031d` clean. No Rust test or Nix check reads the root
    `docs/CONTRACTS.md`.
  - the same 65-check `nix build`: exit 0, built nothing, same default
    package `hi2h40jw…` (log `nix-proof-commit.log`).
- Round 2's staged tree was `2ea884e6bd588fcdd8462271ad86995273c1c2d6`.
- eon-test, fmt, clippy, the 65-check Nix build and the sensitivity checks
  ran on tree `535d37b` (chain `round2-proof.sh`). The Nix build rebuilt the
  Rust derivations and produced
  `/nix/store/hi2h40jwi1jwny9dl5ggm62j0w8m0zfx-eon-0.1.17` (log
  `nix-proof-round2.log`).
- The final tree differs from `535d37b` only in `docs/CONTRACTS.md` (one
  wording fix to EON-C35's proof environment). The same 65-check
  `nix build` on it exited 0 and built nothing, with the same default
  package (log `nix-proof-final.log`). So every check result holds for the
  final tree.
- Round 1 (tree `8a0832f`, package `z39fsqy8…`) passed the same 65 checks
  and eon-test 679/0/13. The window-stall rerun and the full read below
  ran on that package. Round 2 changed only the reply write's deadline
  check (before every write) and tests, and the timing for a client that
  keeps reading is the same: one clock read per write. So the rerun was not
  repeated, as INBOX allows.
- The round-2 Nix run on the first variant (tree `1cbf5f0`) failed `eonbase`
  and `default` on the slow-reader test (record 03, round 2; log
  `nix-proof-1cbf5f0.log`). That variant was replaced.
- The EONW proof in `components/eon-v5.json` is the subtree hash from
  `git rev-parse <final tree>:runtime/crates/eon-workspace-protocol`:
  `eba18a865da9036d95b556e9b1fab7140aa7d5ac`. It changed from `ab8b6b3`
  because review nit 3 edited a docstring in `v33.rs`; all three places in
  the manifest were updated. Rounds 1 and 2 changed nothing else in the
  protocol crate.
- Round 0 (tree `475183f`, package `n2ra62y8…-eon-0.1.17`) passed the same
  65 checks and eon-test 678/0/13. Its installed outputs are kept in
  `dog/out-475183f/`.

## Checks on the final tree

- `nix build --keep-going --max-jobs 2 --cores 6` of all 65 flake checks
  (58 `orbit-*`, `default`, `bundle-launch`, `bundle-relink`,
  `eonbase-closure`, `helix-grammars`, `managed-command-path`,
  `quick-search-guard`): exit 0.
- `nix develop -c eon-test -p eon-workspace-protocol -p eon-runtime -p eon -p
  yazelix-venus`: 680 passed, 0 failed, 13 ignored (log `test-round2.log`).
  Two tests are new since round 0: the slow-reader test (round 1) and the
  writable-socket deadline test (round 2). The popup case extends an
  existing test.
- `cargo fmt --all -- --check`: clean. `cargo clippy --locked -p
  eon-workspace-protocol -p eon-runtime -p eon -p yazelix-venus --all-targets
  -- -D warnings`: clean.

## Sensitivity checks

- I switched the CLI reply reader (`control.rs`) back to
  `declared_message_len`, the 2 MiB bound. Then
  `pane_history_prints_the_text_or_json_and_names_what_the_bound_left_out`
  failed: the 3 MiB answer exited 4 instead of 0. Reverted from the index
  (round 0).
- Reply deadline (round 1): restoring the old blocking `write_all` made
  `a_slow_reader_holds_the_supervisor_no_longer_than_the_reply_deadline`
  fail its hold assertion. That took 12.99 s on tree `535d37b`, where the
  peer drains every 100 ms, and 25.07 s on round 1's tree, where it drained
  every 200 ms. Each time the file was restored and the tree hash checked
  unchanged. While developing the fix, a write timeout bounded by the time
  left also held the supervisor for 24.95 s.
- Deadline before every write (round 2): removing the check made
  `a_reply_past_its_deadline_stops_even_while_the_client_takes_bytes`
  fail; the other 7 control tests passed. Restored. A variant
  that dropped the client on its first poll timeout dropped a
  still-draining client after 363 ms, which fails the lower bound. The
  final `write_reply` holds it for 2.0 to 2.5 s and passes. So does it in
  the Nix sandbox, where round 2's first variant dropped the client after
  263.8 ms (record 03).

## Isolated installed observation

Package `/nix/store/z39fsqy85sa5fygzqjpsy8715agakn0c-eon-0.1.17` (round 1's
`.#default`) ran in a private headless Sway 1.12 at 1600x900
(pixman):
- own HOME, `XDG_RUNTIME_DIR=/run/user/1000/ku5b3`, every command under
  `env -i`;
- driver `eon-u5bvd-3-work/dog/driver.sh`, round-1 sequence
  `dog/rerun.sh`, outputs in `dog/out/`.

Lucca's windows, supervisors and Orbit hosts were not touched. Cleanup
signalled only PIDs that carried the run's HOME or runtime dir, plus the
burners by PID. Cleanup reported no leftover PIDs.

- p1 (127x43) ran `fill.py`: 30,000 numbered lines of U+1D11E, past the
  16 MiB history budget. `eon pane history p1`:
  - exit 0, 7,317,572 bytes in 140 ms (JSON 156 ms);
  - the text starts at `015005`, the earliest retained line;
  - `omitted_lines` 0, `cut_bytes` 0, empty stderr;
  - JSON `screen` primary, `revision` 3601.
- `eon pane --help` lists `pane history PANE|POPUP [--json]   Print a
  pane's or popup's history`.
- From round 0 on `n2ra62y8…-eon-0.1.17`, whose tree differs only in the
  reply write's deadline, two tests and wording (outputs in
  `dog/out-475183f/`):
  - the human text equals JSON `text` plus a newline;
  - its last 43 lines equal `eon pane read p1`;
  - Hidden tab: after `eon tab create` showed t3, reading t1's p1 (7.32 MB,
    142 ms) left `eon workspace --json` (quota fields aside), `swaymsg -t
    get_seats` and `get_tree` identical before and after;
  - Alternate screen: p3 printed a primary line, entered `?1049h` and
    printed `alt-screen-marker`. `eon pane history p3 --json` gave `screen`
    `alternate` and `text` `alt-screen-marker` alone;
  - Failures: `p99` exited 3 `unknown-target` (human on stderr, JSON on
    stdout), and so did p3 after `eon pane close p3`.
- Not observed installed (unit and process tests cover them):
  `terminal_access = "none"`, a truncated (over 8 MiB) answer, and
  `terminal-unavailable`.
  - Truncation was not observed installed. The measured workload (a full
    16 MiB history budget of single-codepoint lines) produced 7.32 MB here,
    and 7.45 MB in eon-u5bvd.2's measurement. Other content, such as
    multi-codepoint graphemes, can produce more.
  - Unit and process tests prove the truncation path: the protocol test
    `history_alone_exceeds_two_mib_and_only_where_asked`, and the process
    test's `omitted_lines` and `cut_bytes` notices.
- The supervisor's 2 s reply deadline was not observed dropping a client
  installed; the control test covers it. Every installed read finished
  well inside it (at most 239 ms).

## Window-stall measurement (acceptance addition, rerun on round 1)

All in one window:
- p2 ran `keylog.py` (raw mode; logs each byte's arrival time and echoes
  it).
- Keys: `x` via wdotool into p2, 150 ms apart.
- Reads: `eon pane history p1` of the full 7.3 MB history, back to back.
- Load: 12 `yes` burners, started and stopped by PID.

`dog/analyze.py` output (`dog/out/summary.txt`):

| Phase | Keys to PTY (n=30) | Reads beside |
| --- | --- | --- |
| idle (load 1.6-1.8) | median 20.2 ms, max 32.1 ms | none |
| idle, reads | median 14.0 ms, max 30.7 ms | 43 reads, median 142 ms, max 158 ms, all exit 0 |
| 12 burners (load 4.7-5.3) | median 26.9 ms, max 37.8 ms | none |
| 12 burners, reads (load 5.3-7.3) | median 27.8 ms, max 45.9 ms | 33 reads, median 205 ms, max 239 ms, all exit 0 |

Drawn echo (`dog/echo.sh`): p2's text area was captured with grim until it
changed, so each figure includes up to one capture's time. n=15:

| Phase | Drawn echo | Reads beside |
| --- | --- | --- |
| idle (load 1.6) | median 76.5 ms, max 104.8 ms | none |
| idle, reads | median 51.1 ms, max 73.3 ms | 39 reads, median 129 ms, max 161 ms, all exit 0 |
| 12 burners (load 8.5-8.8) | median 87.7 ms, max 100.3 ms | none |
| 12 burners, reads (load 8.8-9.3) | median 84.2 ms, max 122.4 ms | 30 reads, median 190 ms, max 211 ms, all exit 0 |

What the supervisor's blocking does cost: other supervisor requests wait for
the read in progress. `eon workspace --json` (n=20, 200 ms apart):

| Phase | Inspection | Reads beside |
| --- | --- | --- |
| idle | median 71.9 ms, max 77.3 ms | none |
| idle, reads | median 73.8 ms, max 106.5 ms | median 140 ms, max 157 ms |
| 12 burners | median 49.0 ms, max 50.4 ms | none |
| 12 burners, reads | median 123.1 ms, max 156.9 ms | median 164 ms, max 193 ms |

Round 0 for comparison (same scripts, `dog/out-475183f/summary.txt`):
- keys at most 52.6 ms;
- drawn echo at most 133.9 ms;
- reads at most 264 ms;
- inspection during reads at most 194.7 ms;
- load up to 13.3.

Reading the results:
- Keystrokes and their echo go from Venus to Orbit directly, so a full
  history read never slowed them. Record 4's falsifier: the slowest key
  (45.9 ms) and the slowest drawn echo (122.4 ms) stayed below the slowest
  read (239 ms).
- No read came near the 2 s reply deadline, so the round-1 deadline cost
  honest reads nothing.
- The stall is real only for supervisor requests (window actions, Venus's
  snapshot polls, other CLI calls). They wait at most one read's time: up
  to about 107 ms more than without reads in this run.
- Reply-writing time is now bounded at 2 s, so a slow or stalled client
  can no longer stretch the write of its reply past that (record 03, Codex
  1). The bound covers only the write: the reply timer starts after
  dispatch and encoding, and a terminal read has its own 2 s allowance
  from Orbit before that.

comments.text:
# eon-u5bvd.3 record 3: review ledger (round 1)

Round 1 reviewed staged tree `475183f` (base edge `9a2031d`). Reviewers: Codex
(`codex-review.md`, LAND WITH FIXES) and Opus (`opus-review.md`, LAND).
eon-overseer's INBOX of 2026-11-05 ~19:10Z set the dispositions. Every
finding is listed below. The round-1 tree is in record 02.

## Codex

1. **Should-fix: a slow History reader can hold the supervisor**
   (`control.rs` reply write). **Fixed.**
   - The reply write now has an absolute deadline: `REPLY_DEADLINE` = 2 s
     for the whole reply, beside the existing 250 ms `CLIENT_IO_TIMEOUT`.
   - `write_reply` writes nonblocking and polls for room. It drops the
     client when the deadline passes, or when 250 ms go by without the
     client taking a byte. That is the per-write timeout's old behavior,
     now also for a peer that keeps draining.
   - Why the writes don't block: a blocking Unix-socket write renews
     `SO_SNDTIMEO` whenever the peer frees room. My first attempt bounded
     `set_write_timeout` by the time left and still held the supervisor for
     24.95 s.
   - Why the write is retried after every poll: `POLLOUT` waits for about a
     quarter of the send buffer to be free. A second attempt that dropped on
     a poll timeout dropped a still-draining client after 363 ms.
   - The value is fixed. Record 01 gives the rule 6 reason.
   - Regression check: `control::tests::a_slow_reader_holds_the_supervisor_no_longer_than_the_reply_deadline`.
     It sends an 8 MiB History reply to a peer that drains 64 KiB every
     200 ms (about 25 s for the whole reply). It asserts three things:
     - `handle_client` returns within `[REPLY_DEADLINE, REPLY_DEADLINE + 500 ms)`;
     - the peer received less than the whole reply;
     - the next client's request is then served in full.
   - Sensitivity: restoring the old `write_all` on the final tree made the
     test fail its hold assertion after 25.07 s (record 02).
   - No contract or EONW change was needed. EON-C35's existing failure text
     already covers a reply the CLI cannot read.
2. **Should-fix: 02-proof.md:68 treats 7.45 MB as a ceiling.** **Fixed.**
   Record 02 now says truncation was not observed installed and that the
   measured workload produced 7.45 MB. It keeps the unit and process
   evidence for truncation and drops the claim that a real terminal cannot
   reach the bound.

Codex accepted all five recorded deviations. Its remaining-risk note (slow
EONW readers prolonging supervisor stalls) is closed by Codex 1.

## Opus

1. **Nit: the help row is vague** (`cli.rs:840`). **Fixed, with a
   deviation.**
   - The requested text, "Print a pane's or popup's history and text",
     pushes the row past 80 columns. The description column starts at
     column 46, and `help_is_readable_and_does_not_start_or_prepare_a_workspace`
     enforces the limit.
   - The row now reads "Print a pane's or popup's history". The help
     paragraph and `docs/USAGE.md` already say that the screen follows the
     history.
2. **Nit: the notice hard-codes "8 MiB"** (`cli.rs:1365`). **Fixed.** The
   notice now derives the figure as `MAX_HISTORY_TEXT_BYTES / (1024 * 1024)`.
3. **Nit: a docstring overstates the narrowing** (`v33.rs:3328`). **Fixed.**
   It now says "only the CLI's reply reader uses it". This changes the
   protocol subtree hash, so `components/eon-v5.json` was updated (record 02).
4. **Nit: the CHANGELOG omits the cut-line case** (`CHANGELOG.md:10`).
   **Fixed.** The entry now says "or the start of the newest line when that
   line alone is longer".
5. **Nit: the proof sentence merges two load ranges** (`docs/CONTRACTS.md:3833`).
   **Fixed.** The EON-C35 `history` proof entry was rewritten from the
   rerun, and it gives each phase's load separately.
6. **Nit: a stalled CLI produces a misleading failure** (`control.rs:588`).
   **Resolved by Codex 1, not changed further.**
   - The supervisor still drops a client that takes nothing for 250 ms, as
     before. That client still sees EOF, which EON-C35 classes as a reply
     it cannot read.
   - What Codex 1 changes is the duration: a client that keeps draining
     slowly is now also cut off at 2 s, where before it could hold the
     supervisor indefinitely.
   - The overseer asked for no follow-up bead.
7. **Nit: no test reads a popup's history.** **Fixed.**
   `pane_history_prints_the_text_or_json_and_names_what_the_bound_left_out`
   now opens the Commands popup through the protocol and reads
   `eon pane history uN --json`. It asserts `pane` null, `popup` uN, the
   popup's terminal, and the fake Orbit's history text for that terminal.

# Round 2

The Codex re-check of staged tree `8a0832f` (`codex-recheck.md`) returned
LAND WITH FIXES. eon-overseer's INBOX of 2026-11-05 ~19:40Z set the
dispositions:

- Codex round-1 finding 2 and Opus nits 1, 2, 3, 4, 5 and 7: resolved.
- Opus nit 6 (EOF on a dropped client): accepted residual.
- Accepted as is: a healthy reader that needs more than 2 s of continuous
  writing under extreme load is cut off. The installed proof's largest read
  took 239 ms.

1. **Should-fix: the reply deadline was checked only after `WouldBlock`**
   (`control.rs` `write_reply`). **Fixed.**
   - The problem: successful writes and `Interrupted` retries looped without
     checking the deadline, so a socket that stayed writable kept taking
     bytes after expiry.
   - The fix: `write_reply` checks the absolute `REPLY_DEADLINE` before
     every write attempt, including after a poll and after `Interrupted`.
     On expiry it returns and drops the client, as before.
   - The `CLIENT_IO_TIMEOUT` no-progress drop is still decided only after a
     write finds no room. Both values are unchanged (2 s, 250 ms).
   - A first version checked both limits before every write. The Nix
     checks caught it: in the build sandbox, `eonbase` and `default` failed
     `a_slow_reader_holds_the_supervisor_no_longer_than_the_reply_deadline`,
     dropping the still-draining client after 263.8 ms (log
     `nix-proof-1cbf5f0.log`). The cause: a poll that times out at the
     250 ms mark has not seen the client's reads, because `POLLOUT` waits
     for a quarter of the buffer to be free. The write after the poll is
     what tells a stall from a slow drain, and the pre-check skipped it.
     That version passed under `eon-test`.
   - The slow-reader test's peer now drains 64 KiB every 100 ms (was
     200 ms), so its gap between reads sits further below the 250 ms stall
     limit. The whole reply would still take about 13 s against the 2 s
     deadline.
   - Regression check:
     `control::tests::a_reply_past_its_deadline_stops_even_while_the_client_takes_bytes`.
     The socket has room for the whole reply. Past the deadline the peer
     receives nothing; within it, the peer receives the whole reply.
   - Sensitivity: without the pre-write check, the test fails at its
     "nothing received" assertion. The check was removed, run and restored
     (record 02).
   - Timing for healthy readers is unchanged: the only addition per write
     is one clock read. So the stall measurement was not rerun, as INBOX
     allows; record 02's numbers come from the round-1 package.
2. **Nit: 02-proof.md:167 overstated the bound.** **Fixed.** It now says
   reply-writing time is bounded at 2 s. The timer starts after dispatch
   and encoding, and a terminal read has its own 2 s allowance from Orbit
   before that.

# Round 2 re-check

The Codex re-check of `2ea884e` (`codex-recheck2.md`) returned LAND.
eon-overseer's INBOX of 2026-11-05 ~20:30Z:

1. **Nit: EON-C35's proof summary said the slow-reader test drains every
   200 ms**, but the test now drains every 100 ms (`control.rs:912`).
   **Fixed** (text only, `docs/CONTRACTS.md:3828`). The final tree is

title: Open a private scrollback snapshot in the editor from a Scrollback popup (Alt+Shift+E)
description:
## Why

Ronald, an Eon user, asked to open a pane's scrollback in his editor; Lucca made it P1. This is the window half of eon-u5bvd: one key opens a private snapshot in the configured editor. Re-scoped on 2026-11-05 to the design's ".4a" after the Opus gate split the old .4. The `--edit` CLI path, docs and the end-to-end proof moved to eon-u5bvd.5.

## Contract

EON-C10 (popup rules), amended as approved in eon-u5bvd.1 record 03. Lucca approved items 4, 9, 13 and 14 on 2026-11-05; read eon-u5bvd.1's comments first.

## What

- A new Scrollback popup kind whose argv the supervisor builds on each press, after the Orbit history read (eon-u5bvd.2) and the file write. `PopupCommand::Edit` is not reusable: the popup catalog refuses it (managed_environment.rs:532).
- A private snapshot store: a 0700 per-snapshot dir under the window runtime dir holding a 0600 file, removed when the popup ends. A start-time sweep removes dead supervisors' dirs, except a popup adopted on recovery.
- Notices: truncation, the alternate-screen first line, and the popup start-failure path for an export timeout or a missing editor.
- `[popups.scrollback]` on Alt+Shift+E, with its defaults in docs/CONFIGURATION.md (rule 6). A user's popup already on that key takes it over without failing startup.

Rule 5: its CLI path is eon-u5bvd.5 (`eon pane history TARGET --edit`).

## Acceptance

Supervisor tests, per the eon-u5bvd.1 falsifier table:
- the dir is 0700 and the file 0600, and a planted symlink refuses;
- the dir is gone after editor exit, dismissal and tab close;
- the stale-owner sweep works, and an adopted popup's dir survives recovery;
- an export timeout and a missing editor show the start-failure notice and leave no dir;
- an alternate-screen source gives the first-line notice.

Prerequisites: eon-u5bvd.3.

comments.text:
# eon-u5bvd.4 record 01: implementation notes

Session: eon-u5bvd-4 worktree, detached at edge `acc60cd` (EONW v33, Orbit
management v7, Eon 0.1.17), 2026-11-05. Implementer: sclaude (Claude Opus
5.5).

## What changed

- **New popup kind.** `PopupCommand::Scrollback`
  (`runtime/crates/eon-runtime/src/managed_environment.rs`) is the built-in
  `scrollback` entry's command. It is never prepared from the catalog:
  `prepare_popup_command` refuses it ("the supervisor builds Scrollback's
  command for each press"), and `print_defaults` omits its `command` and
  `keep_alive`, as for Anima. `popup_catalog` rejects
  `popups.scrollback.command` and `keep_alive = true` (the Anima rule, now
  shared by id), and accepts `keybinding`, `label` and `enabled`. The product
  default (`eon/crates/eon/src/product.rs`) is `scrollback`, "Scrollback",
  Alt+Shift+E, transient. The existing key resolution already lets a
  configured popup on Alt+Shift+E take the key (`PopupKey::Overridden`)
  without failing the load.
- **Workspace owner** (`workspace.rs`):
  - `WorkspaceSet::scrollback_source(caller, tab, entry)` names the terminal a
    press would snapshot, as `(pane or popup ID, terminal)`. It is set only
    when the entry's command is Scrollback, the tab is the caller workspace's
    active tab, the tab is not pending, and no Scrollback popup is live in
    it. The source is the tab's shown popup, else its selected pane
    (`Workspace::shown_terminal`).
  - `invoke_popup`: an existing Scrollback is exempt from the
    relaunch-on-new-directory path (a snapshot belongs to no directory), so
    its key toggles it off as for any transient. A tab showing no terminal
    returns `Ok` without change ("A tab showing no terminal changes
    nothing").
- **Snapshot store** (new `runtime/crates/eon-runtime/src/scrollback.rs`),
  owned by the supervisor (`SupervisorState::scrollback`):
  - Root `<generation runtime dir>/snapshots/`, created 0700 by
    `prepare_runtime` (owner and mode checked) at each write. Each snapshot is
    a fresh `<pid>-<start>-<n>/` directory (mode 0700, `DirBuilder` without
    `recursive`, so anything planted at that name refuses), checked by
    `validate_private_directory`. The file is `<target>-scrollback.txt` (for
    example `p1-scrollback.txt`), opened `O_CREAT|O_EXCL|O_NOFOLLOW|O_CLOEXEC`,
    mode 0600. A failed write removes what it made.
  - Contents: an optional notice line, then the text exactly as `eon pane
    history` prints it (text plus a final line feed). The truncation notice
    reads "Eon left out the N earliest lines [and the first B bytes of the
    newest line] to keep this snapshot within its 8 MiB bound." and shares
    its phrase with the CLI's stderr notice through the new
    `cli::history_left_out`. The alternate-screen notice is record 03's
    contract text. When both apply they share the one line.
  - Removal: each loop turn's `tend`, the supervisor's exit, and the
    rollback after a failed Venus launch call
    `SupervisorState::retain_snapshots`. It removes the directory of every
    owned snapshot whose terminal the supervisor no longer tracks or tracks
    as finished (it ended, or a Stop for dismissal, replacement, hide, tab or
    window close removed it). A terminal whose Stop failed stays tracked and
    keeps its snapshot. A removal that fails, including a failed start's
    discard, is logged once and kept pending; every later turn retries it
    silently, and the empty root goes only once nothing is pending.
    `remove_dir_all` does not follow links; a link planted in place of a
    directory is unlinked. The empty root goes with the last snapshot and at
    exit, so the generation runtime directory can still be removed.
  - Start sweep (`Snapshots::sweep`, right after `recover_sessions`): every
    entry whose `<pid>-<start>` names no running process is removed, unless
    its `.terminal` record names a terminal this supervisor adopted, which it
    takes over and removes when that terminal ends. A running supervisor's
    entries are kept; an unparsable name counts as stale; an unreadable
    process identity counts as running, so the sweep keeps what it cannot
    judge.
- **Supervisor press path** (`supervisor.rs`, `dispatch_control_request`):
  for `InvokePopup` with a Scrollback source, it reads the source through
  `sessions::read_history` (ORB-C17 `ReadHistory`, the `TERMINAL_DEADLINE`
  2 s bound) and writes the snapshot before dispatching. The dispatch's
  `prepare` closure turns `PopupCommand::Scrollback` into
  `PopupCommand::Edit(<snapshot path>)`, so the argv is `[editor] command`
  plus the path, as `eon edit` builds it, including its executable check.
  The dispatch's `operate` closure calls `mark_before_start`, which writes
  the snapshot's `.terminal` record with the terminal ID of the editor's
  `SessionOperation::Start` before it applies that Start, so the record
  exists before the editor runs. A failed write fails the start. After the
  dispatch, `settle_snapshot` gives the snapshot to the started (or still
  tracked) terminal (`Snapshots::own`). A failed start whose launch record
  remains (`sessions::launch_record_remains`, the existing sign that its
  rollback could not confirm cleanup, as for a pending pair's marker) may
  leave the editor running: its recorded snapshot stays, logged, and the
  store owns it against that terminal and its endpoint. `retain_snapshots`
  keeps it while the launch record remains, so a stop that ends the editor
  (the stop acquires untracked terminals and clears their records) removes it
  and the store at exit, through the same retain and retry path. A recovery
  that adopts the editor adopts it too; one the editor outlives without a
  stop leaves it to the next start sweep. Any other failure discards it. A request with a `caller` (a terminal's, so an
  agent's read) for a Scrollback entry is refused with
  `terminal-access-off` when `[agents] terminal_access = "none"`, by the
  entry's kind (`WorkspaceSet::is_scrollback`), whether or not a Scrollback
  is already shown, before any read or write. The window key carries no
  caller and is not governed by it (record 03).
- **Docs:** EON-C10 (status line, Runtime policy clause with a
  `terminal_access` sentence, Configuration sentence, Boundary list, proof
  entry); `docs/CONFIGURATION.md` (defaults
  block and Popups prose); `docs/USAGE.md` (key row); `CHANGELOG.md`.

## Decisions settled here

1. **How the recovery record names an adopted directory** (record 4 item 11
   left this to .4a). Once its popup starts, each snapshot directory holds
   `.terminal` (0600, `O_EXCL|O_NOFOLLOW`) with the popup's Orbit terminal
   ID, such as `session-5`. Recovery adopts every live terminal as a pane
   under its own ID (`recovered_workspace_sessions`), so the sweep keeps a
   dead supervisor's directory exactly when its `.terminal` names one of
   the adopted terminals. Rejected: naming the directory for the terminal,
   since the terminal ID is allocated inside the workspace after the file
   must exist, and renaming the directory after the start would move the
   editor's file. The record is written with the candidate terminal ID from
   the editor's `SessionOperation::Start` before that Start runs, and a
   failed write fails the press (`popup-start`) and discards the snapshot. So
   any editor a recovery can adopt has its record. A supervisor that dies
   between the record and the spawn leaves a recorded directory whose
   terminal no recovery adopts, and the next start sweep removes it, as
   `the_start_sweep_keeps_adopted_and_running_snapshots_and_ends_remove_them`
   shows for a recorded, unadopted directory. A real crash at that point is
   not reproducible without fault injection, so that unit case is the
   closest testable equivalent. The record write failing (nothing starts,
   no snapshot left) and the order (the record exists when the Start runs)
   are covered through `mark_before_start` and `settle_snapshot`, the
   functions the dispatch calls, by
   `a_scrollback_record_precedes_its_editor_and_only_a_confirmed_failure_discards`.
   A process test cannot make the record write fail without a fault hook:
   the directory is fresh, private and created a moment before. Every
   Scrollback process test also checks the order at the launch boundary:
   the fake Orbit reads `.terminal` before it publishes Ready, and the
   supervisor's start returns only after Ready.
2. **Failure codes.** A failed or timed-out export fails the press with
   `popup-start` and the detail "cannot read the terminal's history: …". A
   missing or unexecutable editor fails with `popup-command`, as any popup
   whose executable is unavailable does. Venus shows either as its existing
   "Eon workspace CODE: DETAIL" notice. Note for eon-u5bvd.5: record 03's
   EON-C35 `--edit` text names EON-C10's `edit-command` for a missing
   editor, so `--edit` maps or names its own code.
3. **No EONW change.** The window path never sends the text over EONW, and
   `eon-workspace-protocol` is untouched, so its subtree hash and
   `components/eon-v5.json` are unchanged. eon-u5bvd.5 has no bump of mine
   to batch with: its `--edit` action needs its own EONW bump.
4. **Supervisor stall.** A press blocks the supervisor for its read, as
   `eon pane history` does: bounded by the 2 s deadline, and measured in
   eon-u5bvd.3 (a read held other supervisor work for up to about 120 ms).
   Keystrokes go from Venus to Orbit directly. Worst case: a read at the 2 s
   deadline followed by an editor start near its 5 s deadline exceeds
   Venus's 6 s workspace exchange (`WORKSPACE_EXCHANGE_TIMEOUT`, sized as the
   start deadline plus 1 s). Venus would then report a lost connection, and
   "Eon is slow" after 2 s, while the popup still opens. Accepted: the
   typical read is about 120 ms, an editor start past 4 s needs a machine
   already in trouble, and the outcome is a misleading notice, not a lost
   snapshot or terminal. The timeout is unchanged.
5. **The start sweep covers its own generation.** It lists only this
   generation's `snapshots/`; sweeping sibling generations would break their
   own recovery adoption. A dead supervisor of a generation that never starts
   again (for example after a profile update) keeps its snapshot until logout
   on Linux (tmpfs) or reboot on macOS. eon-u5bvd.5's CONFIGURATION gap notes
   (record 03 §4) should list this beside the macOS non-tmpfs gap.

## Deviations from the bead and record 03

1. **EON-C10's last sentence.** I applied record 03 §3 as written, except its
   final clause "its CLI path, `eon pane history --edit`, is governed
   (EON-C35)". Record 03 assigns the `--edit` reference to .4b, which is
   eon-u5bvd.5, and `--edit` does not exist yet.
2. **Docs landed here, not in .5.** The bead body gives .5 USAGE, the
   CONFIGURATION Editor notes and CHANGELOG. AGENTS.md rule 10 binds this
   change, since it adds a user-visible key, so I added:
   - a CHANGELOG entry;
   - the USAGE key-table row;
   - Scrollback's sentences in CONFIGURATION's Popups section, beside the
     required defaults block.

   The Editor notes (wait flag, save under another name, editor state files)
   and README stay with .5.
3. **`cli::history_left_out`.** I factored it out of the CLI's
   `history_notice` so the file notice and the stderr notice say the same
   thing. The CLI output is unchanged, and the existing CLI test still
   passes.
4. **Test double.** The fake Orbit in `workspace_control.rs` gained one
   reply script, `slow-history`, which answers `ReadHistory` after 2.5 s,
   past the deadline.
5. **One EON-C10 sentence beyond record 03 (round 1, Opus finding 1).**
   After "The window key is the person's own action, and `[agents]
   terminal_access` does not govern it" I added: "a Scrollback request a
   terminal sends is an agent's read, which `terminal_access = "none"`
   refuses with `terminal-access-off`." `docs/CONFIGURATION.md`'s
   `terminal_access` list says the same. It states the guard the overseer
   asked for; it narrows nothing record 03 grants the window key. It needs
   the overseer's (or Lucca's) approval as contract text.

## Configurability (rule 6)

- Configurable: the key, label and enabled flag (`[popups.scrollback]`), with
  defaults in `docs/CONFIGURATION.md`'s checked defaults block.
- Fixed, with reasons (record 03 §4):
  - the 8 MiB bound: a protocol bound;
  - the plain unwrapped layout: a format contract;
  - 0600/0700 under the runtime directory: safety;
  - removal at popup end: data lifetime and safety.
- Also fixed: the two notice lines. The alternate-screen line is contract
  text. The truncation line derives its numbers from the reply and the
  protocol bound and shares its words with `eon pane history`'s notice, so a
  setting would only let the two drift apart.

## Humans and agents (rule 5)

The window action's CLI path is eon-u5bvd.5 (`eon pane history TARGET
--edit`), an open bead.

Round 3: staged tree `74fb75a6820ffef6a073d8f1329455899fc948d7`, on edge

comments.text:
# eon-u5bvd.4 record 03: review ledger (round 1)

Round 0 candidate: staged tree `b2daeccd443a0bd93d22f87d893bbeafb219149e`.
Reviewers: Codex (`codex-review.md`, LAND WITH FIXES) and a fresh Opus
(`opus-review.md`, LAND WITH FIXES). The overseer's round-1 INBOX set the
dispositions below. Both reviewers accepted the four declared deviations and
decisions 1-3.

## Codex

1. **Blocker: recovery can delete a live editor's snapshot (the editor
   started before `.terminal` was written).** Fixed. The dispatch's
   `operate` closure writes `.terminal` with the candidate terminal ID of
   the editor's `SessionOperation::Start` before applying it, and a failed
   write fails the start and discards the snapshot; `Snapshots::own` no
   longer writes. `WorkspaceSet::popup_session` is gone. Tests:
   - `a_snapshot_whose_record_cannot_be_written_refuses_its_terminal` (a
     planted `.terminal` makes the write fail);
   - every Scrollback process test: the editor logs the record it finds at
     start, and `open_scrollback` asserts it names the popup's terminal;
   - crash between record and spawn, closest testable equivalent: the start
     sweep removes a recorded directory whose terminal was not adopted
     (`the_start_sweep_keeps_adopted_and_running_snapshots_and_ends_remove_them`).
     A real crash at that point needs fault injection (record 01 decision 1).
   - Sensitivity: writing the record after the start instead failed
     `scrollback_opens_…` ("left: \"\", right: \"session-3\"").
2. **Should-fix: failed cleanup is forgotten.** Fixed. Failed removals
   (from `retain` and from a failed start's `discard`) stay in a pending
   list, logged once and retried silently on every later turn; the empty
   root goes only when nothing is pending. Test:
   `a_failed_removal_is_retried_on_later_turns` (0500 store: removal fails
   and the directories stay; 0700: the next turn removes them and the root).
   Sensitivity: no retry failed it.
3. **Should-fix: Venus-launch rollback skips snapshot cleanup.** Fixed. The
   rollback calls `retain_snapshots` and `remove_empty_root` after
   `stop_managed_sessions`; a terminal counts as live only while tracked and
   not finished, so stopped editors' snapshots go and a failed stop's stays.
   Test: `recovery_whose_venus_cannot_start_removes_adopted_snapshots`.
   Sensitivity: dropping the rollback call failed it.

Codex's note that the stop assertions ran after the snapshots had gone is
answered by Opus 3's test below.

## Opus

1. **Should-fix: a terminal caller's press ignored `terminal_access`.**
   Fixed. A request with a caller is refused with `terminal-access-off` when
   `terminal_access = "none"`, before any read or write; the window key is
   unaffected. EON-C10 and CONFIGURATION gain one sentence each (record 01
   deviation 5, needs approval as contract text). Test:
   `scrollback_refuses_callers_without_terminal_access_and_ends_with_its_window`.
   Sensitivity: dropping the guard failed it.
2. **Should-fix: the press can exceed Venus's 6 s exchange.** Recorded, no
   code change, as directed: record 01 decision 4 names the worst case
   (2 s read + 5 s start against 6 s), the measured typical read (~120 ms,
   eon-u5bvd.3) and why it is accepted.
3. **Should-fix: no test removes a live snapshot at supervisor stop.**
   Fixed. The terminal_access test opens Scrollback by the window key, stops
   the generation with it live, and asserts the directory and `snapshots/`
   are gone. Sensitivity: dropping the exit `retain_snapshots` call failed
   it.
4. **Nit: misleading text in an unreachable arm.** Fixed:
   `PopupCommand::Scrollback => unreachable!("Scrollback's command is
   Eon-owned")`; Edit keeps its message.
5. **Nit: the sweep covers one generation.** Recorded as record 01 decision
   5, for eon-u5bvd.5's CONFIGURATION gap notes.
6. **Nit: no test of the window key under `terminal_access = "none"`.**
   Fixed by the same test as Opus 1 and 3.
7. **Nit: same-user TOCTOU after the checks.** Accepted as is, as the
   reviewer advised and the overseer confirmed: same-user, outside the
   gate's threat model.
8. **Nit: a dangling `selected_popup` names no source.** Accepted as is:
   workspace invariants make it unreachable.
9. **Nit: Darwin is not compiled in the proof.** Recorded in record 02's
   route.

## Round 2: Codex re-check of `05efc2b32cbdf5be703e9e68be37fed9aa182355`

Codex (`codex-recheck.md`, LAND WITH FIXES) found every round-1 item
resolved except as below. The overseer approved deviation 5 (the EON-C10
`terminal_access` sentence) as minor policy text.

1. **Blocker: a failed start can still delete a live editor's snapshot.**
   Fixed. `settle_snapshot` discards only when no terminal can be using the
   snapshot. A failed start whose launch record remains
   (`sessions::launch_record_remains`, the existing unconfirmed-rollback
   sign the pending-pair marker uses) keeps its recorded snapshot, logged,
   for the recovery that adopts the editor or the next start sweep. A
   failure after a start that left the terminal tracked gives the snapshot
   to that terminal. Tests:
   - `a_scrollback_start_whose_rollback_is_unconfirmed_keeps_its_snapshot`:
     the editor's fake Orbit publishes Ready after the start and rollback
     deadlines (5.1 s, as `a_pending_pair_left_by_a_failed_rollback_is_stopped_by_recovery`
     does). The press fails with `popup-start`, the editor runs, and its
     recorded snapshot stays. A recovery adopts the editor and its snapshot
     and removes it when the editor exits.
   - the unconfirmed and confirmed cases of
     `a_scrollback_record_precedes_its_editor_and_only_a_confirmed_failure_discards`.
   - Sensitivity: discarding on every failure failed both.
2. **Should-fix: marker coverage.**
   - (a) Fixed at the dispatch's own functions. The record step is now
     `mark_before_start`, which the dispatch's `operate` closure calls. The
     unit test plants `.terminal`, then asserts that the Start never runs,
     nothing is marked, and `settle_snapshot` leaves no snapshot. A
     process-level record failure needs a fault hook, because the directory
     is fresh, private and created a moment before. I did not add one.
     The old `a_snapshot_whose_record_cannot_be_written_refuses_its_terminal`
     only tested `mark()` itself, so I removed it. Sensitivity: ignoring
     the record error failed the unit test ("the editor started without its
     record").
   - (b) Fixed. The fake Orbit reads `.terminal` before it publishes Ready
     and logs it to `snapshot.log`. Since the supervisor's start returns
     only after Ready, a record written after the start cannot pass.
     `open_scrollback` asserts the line. The editor script no longer reads
     the record. Sensitivity: recording after the start failed
     `scrollback_opens_…` at `open_scrollback`.
3. **Should-fix: the access guard is narrower than the approved sentence.**
   Fixed. A terminal caller's `InvokePopup` is refused by the entry's kind
   (`WorkspaceSet::is_scrollback`), whether or not a Scrollback is shown.
   `scrollback_refuses_callers_without_terminal_access_and_ends_with_its_window`
   now also sends Toggle (with the instance) and Focus for the shown
   Scrollback. Both are refused, and the tab is unchanged. Sensitivity:
   guarding by source availability failed it at "toggle".

## Round 3: Codex re-check of `386aac4c55e4cf410ec86d3c3e9b7a75797ff742`

Codex (`codex-recheck2.md`) resolved every earlier item and accepted the
helper-boundary marker-failure test.

1. **Should-fix: an uncertain start forgets its cleanup.** Fixed. The
   unconfirmed-rollback branch of `settle_snapshot` now registers the
   snapshot in the store's `owned` list against the candidate terminal ID
   and its endpoint (`Snapshots::own(.., Some(endpoint))`).
   `retain_snapshots` treats it as live while its launch record remains
   (`sessions::launch_record_remains`). A stop acquires the untracked
   terminal, stops it and clears its record, so the exit's retain removes
   the snapshot and the empty store, by the existing retain and retry path.
   Tests:
   - `a_scrollback_start_whose_rollback_is_unconfirmed_keeps_its_snapshot`
     is now the direct-stop regression. The delayed-Ready start fails with
     its rollback unconfirmed, the editor runs, and a later turn keeps the
     snapshot. The original generation then stops, and the directory and
     `snapshots/` are gone.
   - The recovery case moved to
     `a_recovery_adopts_the_snapshot_of_an_unconfirmed_scrollback_start`.
     Both share `unconfirmed_scrollback`.
   - The supervisor unit test's unconfirmed case: retain keeps the snapshot
     while the record exists and removes it, and the store, once the record
     goes.
   - Sensitivity (`sensitivity-r3.log`): leaving the snapshot unowned
     failed the direct-stop test (the directory remained). Not counting the
     record as live failed both process tests at the later-turn check (the
     snapshot went while the editor ran).

## Round 3 re-check

Codex re-check of `74fb75a6820ffef6a073d8f1329455899fc948d7` (`codex-recheck3.md`): LAND, no findings.

title: Open pane scrollback in the editor from the CLI (--edit), with docs and the installed proof
description:
## Why

The rule 5 CLI path and the user-facing proof for eon-u5bvd.4: an agent can open a pane's scrollback in the editor just as a person can with Alt+Shift+E. This is the design's ".4b" (eon-u5bvd.1, approved by Lucca 2026-11-05).

## Contract

EON-C35, amended as approved in eon-u5bvd.1 record 03.

## What

- `eon pane history TARGET --edit` opens the snapshot in the target's tab. In v1 it works only in the active tab; on a hidden tab it refuses with `not-active` (exit 1), and nothing changes.
- Docs: USAGE; the CONFIGURATION Editor notes (the wait flag, saving under another name before dismissing, since dismissing kills the editor, and editor state files such as Neovim swap, undo and shada living outside the snapshot dir); a CHANGELOG entry.
- The isolated installed observation (the parent's acceptance).

## Acceptance

- A process test: `--edit` on a hidden tab gives `not-active`, exit 1, and no change.
- The terminal_access refusal test covers `history --edit`.
- One isolated installed observation, never in Lucca's windows: Alt+Shift+E opens hx at the earliest retained line through the screen; `:q` returns to the pane; the dir is gone; and `eon pane history` text equals the file text minus any notice line.

Prerequisites: eon-u5bvd.4.

comments.author: lucca
comments.text:
# eon-u5bvd.5 record 01: implementation notes

Session: eon-u5bvd-5 worktree, detached at edge `ad5faac` (EONW v33, Orbit
management v7, Eon 0.1.17, with eon-u5bvd.4's Scrollback popup), 2026-11-05.
Implementer: sclaude (Claude Opus 5.5). Implements the approved design
(eon-u5bvd.1 records 03 and 04, item 9; Lucca 2026-11-05, "yyes") for the
`--edit` part of EON-C35 and the last EON-C10 clause.

## Wire: EONW v33 -> v34 (breaking, exact-version, no adapter)

- `v33.rs`/`v33/` renamed to `v34.rs`/`v34/` across every importer (Runtime,
  Eon, Venus); `VERSION = 34`; every hex golden's version byte and the two
  `Runtime` goldens' `workspace_protocol` field moved to 34.
- `Action::EditTerminalHistory { target }`, request tag 42 (the test that
  probed 42 as an unknown tag now probes 43). It has its own action, not the
  `edit: bool` field record 03 sketched, as eon-u5bvd.3's note on this bead
  says: the reply is a different shape.
- `Response::Editing(Editing { target, caller, popup })`, kind 142: the
  source terminal, the caller, and the Scrollback popup as a
  `TerminalTarget`. Both sides refuse an `Editing` whose `popup` is not a
  popup (`editing popup`). It keeps the general 2 MiB bound.
- Component graph `components/eon-v5.json`: EONW 34 in its four places, proof
  = subtree hash of `runtime/crates/eon-workspace-protocol` (record 02 has
  the value on the final tree). Eon 0.1.17 -> 0.1.18 (`eon/crates/eon/Cargo.toml`,
  `Cargo.lock`), the EONW-bump convention.

## Runtime and CLI

- CLI: `eon pane history TARGET --edit [--json]` (`--edit` before or after
  TARGET). A bare `eon pane history --edit` is a usage error. Human output
  prints nothing; `--json` prints `generation`, `window`, the target's
  `workspace`, `tab`, `pane`, `popup`, `terminal`, `caller`, and
  `scrollback: {popup, terminal}`. The help row reads `pane history
  PANE|POPUP [--json] [--edit]`, and the help paragraph gains two lines on
  `--edit`. The parity map gives the action `pane history TARGET --edit`.
- `WorkspaceSet::scrollback_target(request_id, id)` resolves TARGET in any
  workspace and refuses, changing nothing:
  - `not-active` unless TARGET is in the shown workspace's active tab;
  - `choose-directory-first` while that tab is pending (invoke_popup's own
    refusal, checked before the read);
  - `unknown-popup` when no enabled entry is Scrollback;
  - `unavailable` while that tab already has a Scrollback popup.
  It checks replay protection without remembering the request; the dispatch
  that opens the popup accepts it.
- Supervisor `edit_terminal_history`: `workspace-unavailable` and
  `terminal-access-off` as `terminal_access` does; the caller projection;
  `scrollback_target`; ORB-C17 `ReadHistory` of TARGET's terminal through
  `sessions::read_history` (EON-C35's own failures: `terminal-ended`,
  `terminal-unavailable`); the snapshot written by eon-u5bvd.4's store under
  TARGET's ID (`p2-scrollback.txt`); then the workspace owner's
  `InvokePopup` for the Scrollback entry in TARGET's tab, dispatched without
  a caller (the shown workspace, which holds TARGET), with the same
  `prepare` substitution and `mark_before_start`/`settle_snapshot` as the
  window key. So the editor argv, the record before the start, the transient
  cover, the cleanup, the sweep and the recovery adoption are all .4's path.
  The reply names the popup the record marked, and fails with `popup-start`
  if none started.
- `snapshot_command` is factored out of the window key's `prepare` closure so
  both paths share the Scrollback-to-`Edit` substitution.
- Venus: the new response arm in `model.rs` (Venus never reads, edits or sends
  to terminals over EONW); the launch-mode probe in `control.rs` lists it as
  a wrong reply. No behavior change.
- In passing: `scrollback_source`'s doc comment had landed above
  `is_scrollback` (eon-u5bvd.4); it is back above its function.

## Deviations (for the overseer)

1. **Failure codes for `--edit`.** Record 03 names EON-C10's `edit-command`
   for a missing editor. Scrollback's path fails with `popup-command` there
   (eon-u5bvd.4 record 01, decision 2, flagged this), so EON-C35 names
   `popup-command`, and `popup-start` when the snapshot or the editor cannot
   start. A failed or timed-out read keeps EON-C35's existing
   `terminal-ended` and `terminal-unavailable` ("The existing failures
   stay"), where the window key shows `popup-start`.
2. **Three refusals beyond record 03, as contract text (needs approval as
   minor policy text).** In EON-C35's failures:
   - `unavailable` (exit 1) while TARGET's tab already shows a Scrollback
     popup. Toggling it off, as the key does, or replacing it would stop an
     editor the person may be using and lose their edits; refusing changes
     nothing.
   - `choose-directory-first` (exit 1) while TARGET's tab is pending, the
     code `invoke_popup` already gives.
   - `unknown-popup` (exit 3) when Scrollback is disabled, the code a
     disabled popup already gives.
3. **JSON for "the popup".** Record 03 says `--json` "prints the target and
   the popup". The target's fields already use `popup` (null for a pane), so
   the Scrollback popup is `scrollback: {popup, terminal}`.
4. **EON-C35 Boundary item** "`--edit` outside the shown workspace's active
   tab", which states the v1 restriction (record 04, item 9).
5. **EON-C35 Owner line** names "v34 for `--edit`" and the Scrollback popup
   (EON-C10).
6. **Docs that eon-u5bvd.4 deferred here.** The CONFIGURATION Editor notes add
   two items beyond record 03 §4, from eon-u5bvd.4 record 01 (decisions 4 and
   5): the generation-local start sweep (a snapshot of a generation that never
   starts again stays until logout on Linux, or until the system clears
   `/tmp` on macOS), and the worst case where the history read plus the
   editor start pass Venus's 6 s workspace exchange, so the window can report
   Eon as slow or unavailable while the popup opens.

## Configurability (rule 6)

No new tunable value. The `--edit` flag's spelling and the refusals are
approved contract text (record 03, record 04 item 9) or existing codes; the
help and documentation text derive from them. Scrollback's key, label and
`enabled` stay configurable through `[popups.scrollback]` (eon-u5bvd.4);
`enabled = false` also turns `--edit` off (`unknown-popup`). The 6 s figure
in the docs is Venus's fixed `WORKSPACE_EXCHANGE_TIMEOUT`, unchanged.

## Humans and agents (rule 5)

This is the CLI path of eon-u5bvd.4's window action (Scrollback,
Alt+Shift+E). It names its target by ID and leaves the active tab, shown
workspace, selected pane and desktop focus as they are; the popup it opens is
what the agent asks for. v1 refuses hidden tabs and workspaces (record 04,
item 9).

## Docs

- `docs/CONTRACTS.md`: EON-C35 (status, trigger, result, `terminal_access`
  line, failures, owner, boundary; the `--edit` proof entry is added after
  the final proof), EON-C10 (status line, the last Scrollback clause naming
  `eon pane history --edit` as governed), current EONW mentions to v34
  (historical proof and status mentions stay).
- `docs/USAGE.md`: command table row and a Reading a terminal paragraph.
- `docs/CONFIGURATION.md`: `terminal_access` names `--edit`, the Popups
  paragraph points at `--edit`, and the Editor section gains the Scrollback
  notes (wait flag, save under another name, editor state files, the sweep
  gap, the slow-machine notice).
- `docs/ARCHITECTURE.md`, `runtime/README.md`, `venus/docs/{CONTRACTS,CRATES,PRESENTATION}.md`:
  EONW v34.
- `eon/skills/eon/SKILL.md`: `--edit` for agents.
- `CHANGELOG.md` (user-visible command, the Editor notes, EONW v34 restart
  note) and `venus/CHANGELOG.md` (consumes v34).

## Tests added or extended

- Protocol: goldens for the `EditTerminalHistory` request and the `Editing`
  response; the bad-target loop covers the new action; an `Editing` whose
  popup is a pane is refused on encode and decode; the unknown-tag probe
  moves to 43.
- Runtime: the parser test covers `--edit` in both positions, with `--json`,
  and its malformed forms; the JSON projection test covers
  `terminal_editing_json`; the parity test samples the action.
- Process (`workspace_control.rs`, real `eon run` supervisor and fake Orbit):
  - new `pane_history_edit_opens_its_target_in_scrollback_in_the_active_tab_only`:
    `--edit p2` on a pane the tab does not show opens the editor on
    `p2-scrollback.txt`, whose text after the alternate-screen notice is
    `eon pane history p2`'s; p1 stays selected under the Scrollback popup,
    whose record names its terminal; a second `--edit` while it shows exits 1
    `unavailable` and changes nothing; the editor's exit removes the snapshot;
    `--edit --json` prints the exact object; in a hidden tab and in a hidden
    workspace it exits 1 `not-active` (human on stderr, JSON on stdout),
    changes nothing and leaves no snapshot.
  - `terminal_access_none_refuses_every_read_and_send` covers
    `EditTerminalHistory`.

comments.text:
# eon-u5bvd.5 record 03: review ledger

Round 1 reviewed staged tree `cc3298f478663f4cda437f5f875976acfbeaaf6b` on
edge `ad5faac`. Reviewers: a fresh Opus, read-only (`opus-review.md`, LAND
WITH FIXES: 2 should-fix, 6 nits), and Codex (`codex-review.md`, LAND WITH
FIXES: 2 doc should-fix). Neither found a blocker. The overseer approved, as
minor contract text under Lucca's standing rule: record 01's deviations 1-2,
the three extra `--edit` refusals, and the `--json` `scrollback` key. They
also approved S1's refusal (INBOX, ~00:40Z).

## Dispositions

- **Opus S1: `--edit` stopped a shown transient popup.** Fixed.
  `WorkspaceSet::scrollback_target` now refuses with `unavailable` (exit 1,
  no change) while the target tab's selected popup is transient
  (`keep_alive = false`). It runs before any snapshot, so it leaves none.
  EON-C35's failures, USAGE, the eon skill and CHANGELOG say so. The window
  key (Alt+Shift+E) is unchanged, as approved. Test: the `transient` case of
  `pane_history_edit_refusals_leave_no_snapshot_and_change_nothing`. Commands
  stays shown, the tabs are unchanged, there is no snapshot, and it hides
  afterwards. Sensitivity mutation 5 is caught.
- **Opus S2: missing failure tests, and record 02 overstated them.** Fixed.
  There are two new process tests:
  - `pane_history_edit_refusals_leave_no_snapshot_and_change_nothing` covers:
    - a transient popup: `unavailable`;
    - Orbit `busy`: `terminal-unavailable`;
    - a pending tab: `choose-directory-first`, on its Files popup, since a
      pending tab has no pane;
    - a missing editor: `popup-command`, which runs after the snapshot is
      written and must remove it;
    - a read past the 2 s deadline: `terminal-unavailable`, last.

    Each case asserts exit 1 and the code, no snapshot directory, and the
    active tab and stable tabs unchanged. No editor ever ran.
  - `pane_history_edit_with_scrollback_disabled_refuses_with_unknown_popup`
    asserts exit 3 with `unknown-popup` for human and JSON output, empty
    stdout for human output, and nothing changed.

  EON-C35's `--edit` evidence lists both. Record 02 is corrected.

  Unlike the key, `--edit` reports export failures as EON-C35's
  `terminal-unavailable`, not EON-C10's `popup-start`, because it reads
  before the snapshot (record 01). Sensitivity mutation 6 is caught: it
  reported them as `popup-start`.
- **Codex 1 + Opus N1: failure guarantees overstated.** Fixed in EON-C35.
  - The preflight refusals and the read failures come before any snapshot,
    and each leaves none and changes nothing.
  - After the write, `popup-command` and `popup-start` change no tab and
    remove the snapshot.
  - The exception is a `popup-start` whose rollback Eon cannot confirm. The
    editor may still run, so the snapshot is kept until that terminal ends.
    EON-C10's recovery, stop and next-start paths remove it, and .4's safety
    behaviour is unchanged.
  - Codex's second point is moot after S1: replacing a transient popup can
    stop it before startup fails. `--edit` now refuses before it would
    replace one.
- **Codex 2 + Opus N2: recovery adoption missing from the crash-gap note.**
  Fixed in the CONFIGURATION.md Editor note. A recovering supervisor adopts a
  still-running editor's snapshot and removes it when that terminal ends. The
  next start removes only snapshots no live editor holds.
- **Opus N3: USAGE did not list every `--edit` failure.** Fixed. USAGE lists:
  - the refusals: `not-active`, `unavailable` (Scrollback shown, or a
    transient popup), `choose-directory-first`, and `unknown-popup` (exit 3);
  - the post-write failures: `popup-command` and `popup-start`.

  The shared paragraph already covers the read failures.
- **Opus N4: "over TARGET in its tab".** Fixed: "over TARGET's tab".
- **Opus N5: copied wiring.** Applied in part:
  - `WorkspaceSet::find_terminal_target` now holds the lookup that
    `terminal_target` and `scrollback_target` share.
  - The supervisor's dispatch wiring stays separate from the key's. The key
    reaches the launch through the generic `InvokePopup` dispatch, which
    interleaves pair, picker and attention state. Pulling a shared helper out
    of it is not the small, clean extraction the overseer allowed.
  - The duplicated read-then-write is deliberate: `--edit` reports EON-C35's
    read codes.
  - Behaviour is the same, and both paths share `snapshot_command`,
    `mark_before_start` and `settle_snapshot`.
- **Opus N6: the file was named from the raw request string.** Fixed:
  `edit_terminal_history` names the snapshot from the resolved `target.id`.
  It is the same value, since the lookup matches exactly.

## Found while fixing

- The S1 refusal subsumes the "already shows a Scrollback popup" check in
  every state I know of: Scrollback is always transient (its `keep_alive` is
  Eon-owned), and a live transient popup is its tab's selected popup. The
  earlier check stays, and runs first, for its precise message.
- The process test now asserts that message
  (`tab t1 already shows a Scrollback popup`). Sensitivity mutation 2, which
  removes the check, passed until the assertion was added, and is caught
  with it. The installed observation saw the same message, so its record
  stays true.

## Round 1 re-check

Codex re-checked staged tree `e80e2df014e0facffa19a313d9e46a7e41f804a0`
(`codex-recheck.md`) and returned LAND: every round-1 item was resolved. It
raised one nit.

- **Codex re-check nit: USAGE said a launch failure "opens nothing".** Fixed.
  Now no popup is shown and Eon removes the snapshot, with one exception: a
  `popup-start` whose stop Eon cannot confirm. Then the editor may still run,
  and Eon keeps its snapshot until it ends. This matches EON-C35.

# eon-u5ooj — crane dependency cache spike

Bound 2026-11-10 to the detached worktree `/home/lucca/.cache/eon-agents/eon-crane`, initial clean baseline `6dd17c2f8c3dd541b026d4db2895d2e221a319e5`; final comparison baseline updated to `be9a23a10e0bd755da486f7b6779955c440f633c` per the 02:57:28Z INBOX (Eon 0.1.22, EONW v38). Read `br show eon-u5ooj`, its comments, efficiency `report.md` item 6 and `data.md`, root AGENTS and protocols, and AGENT-RULES (including dependency, platform, verification, proof, testing, humans/agents and configurability rules).

Authorization: Lucca, 2026-11-10, “prioritize eon-u5ooj”; the task expressly approves adding crane and permits the necessary `nix build` runs through heavy.sh. Records live here rather than in br; the overseer reviews, commits and lands. No branches, live supervisors, profile changes, desktop activation, or checkPhase policy changes.

## Observable result and ownership

Eon's Nix composition owns the build dependency cache. Existing package consumers get the same binaries, worker, test executable, terminfo, licenses, wrappers, component versions and source receipt semantics. An ordinary workspace source edit with unchanged dependency manifests/lock does not rebuild external Rust crates. No runtime, CLI, configuration, protocol or distribution contract is intentionally changed; no contract edit or user-facing changelog entry is needed for internal build caching.

## Layout and cache identity

1. Pin crane, instantiate it with the existing nixpkgs and Rust 1.96.1 toolchain.
2. One Linux `buildDepsOnly` holds a dummy copy of this Cargo workspace and all external artifacts needed by the existing package build/test selections. Its identity includes Cargo.lock, dependency-relevant Cargo.toml contents, target structure, toolchain, flags, native dependencies and pinned Ghostty/Zig. It intentionally excludes ordinary Rust/Bend source content; “keyed on Cargo.lock” does not mean ignoring manifests or compiler changes.
3. Keep `rustPlatform.buildRustPackage` for the real packages, including cargo vendoring/auditable builds, exact build and check selections, release profile, worker/test installation, wrappers and fixups. Restore `cargoArtifacts` using crane's inheritance hook. Use the same nixpkgs vendor/configuration hook and compiler flags in the deps build so fingerprints can be reused.
4. Populate artifacts with each package's existing Cargo selection separately rather than replacing it with one `--workspace` invocation. This preserves feature sets, including each package's current production/test feature selection (edge c029b44 removed Venus's noop dev feature before the final comparison), and addresses crane #396 without adding cargo-hakari or changing Cargo manifests.
5. Wire Orbit first and prove its artifact/test/terminfo parity and cache behavior before wiring Venus, then Eon/default, then bench/mac-proof and Rust-consuming checks. eonbase already copies eon and remains unchanged. Installer, launcher and relink have separate locks and stay outside this workspace spike; Orbit's schema checker deliberately uses bare rustc, not Cargo.

Scope reaches flake.nix and flake.lock, existing package/check derivations, and external proof records/scripts. No Rust API, callers, fixtures or product configuration change is planned. Failures to guard: missing worker/real-PTY output; dummy workspace code escaping the cache; changed auditable/vendor/compiler fingerprints; feature cache misses; changed checks or receipt identity; Linux-specific cache wiring breaking Darwin evaluation.

## Dependency/reference gate

- Capability: pure Nix cache of compiled Cargo dependencies independent of ordinary workspace source; crane owns dummy-source generation and artifact transfer, Eon retains package/test/composition policy.
- Chosen dependency: `ipetkov/crane` exact revision `79fd63528501446749c09f08cad486a58c7d173e` (upstream HEAD inspected 2026-11-10, commit dated 2026-11-04). MIT license inspected. Its flake has no inputs, so it adds one locked node and no independent nixpkgs/toolchain graph. No runtime dependency or cache trust configuration is added.
- Evidence inspected: upstream `lib/buildDepsOnly.nix`, `mkDummySrc.nix`, `mkCargoDerivation.nix`, `buildPackage.nix`, configure/inherit/install hooks and LICENSE at that revision; official workspace example https://crane.dev/examples/quick-start-workspace.html and API https://crane.dev/API.html; https://github.com/ipetkov/crane/issues/396 explains differing workspace/package feature selections. Comparable implementation: upstream's workspace example, with per-package consumers sharing one cargoArtifacts value; retain its cache boundary, reject its optional hakari/nextest and test-policy changes. Local `docs/REFERENCES.md` runtime-composition route and `docs/ARCHITECTURE.md#in-tree-package-selection` require one workspace/lock and no second component graph.
- Alternatives: existing buildRustPackage vendors but recompiles on every source change; retaining it without an artifact layer cannot satisfy the bead. Handwritten dummy source/fingerprint pruning would duplicate crane's responsibility. naersk would replace the packaging owner more broadly. sccache inside Nix requires impurity and does not provide this pure derivation boundary. No additional dependency is needed.
- Version policy: exact input rev and narHash in flake.lock; update only with this cache/equivalence proof. Lock effect: crane alone; Cargo.lock and other flake input pins unchanged. Build-time MIT license fit; it is not a shipped runtime component.
- Exit: if source-only edits still rebuild external crates or artifacts/checks diverge, keep the negative proof and revise or drop the spike. Removal is deleting the one input, cache definition and inheritance hook wiring; real packages remain buildRustPackage.

## Proof and timings

All Nix builds go through `/home/lucca/.cache/eon-agents/eon-overseer/heavy.sh`, one own run at a time, with `--max-jobs 1 --cores 6`, closed stdin, timeout and captured logs. Queue waits are separated from build wall time. Updated by overseer INBOX 2026-11-10T02:45:24Z: build comparisons need no quiet booking when reporting builder CPU user+system and compiled crate counts; wall time is contextual on the shared host. The initial 90-minute quiet request is withdrawn. No store/cache deletion.

Save baseline derivation identities and package metadata before editing. Cold means no inherited Rust artifacts in that package build (baseline), versus cache construction plus consuming package (candidate); already-realized derivations can be reproduced with `--rebuild`, explicitly reported. Warm no-change is the identical normal `nix build` cache hit. A one-line Rust comment creates a distinct source snapshot with unchanged Cargo.lock, and must leave the candidate deps derivation unchanged. Retain exact snapshots, staged tree IDs, commands, logs, builder CPU user+system, contextual elapsed wall time and every Cargo `Compiling` line, classifying workspace/external counts per phase. A single sample is a measured bound, not a distribution claim. Reuse a combined build's per-derivation phase data instead of unnecessary duplicate full builds.

Equivalence: compare output file lists, strict executable/worker/test byte equality for unchanged embedded inputs, licenses and terminfo bytes, ELF dependencies/auditable metadata and safe help/version commands. For Eon, compare component/version output and validate the source receipt against that candidate's build ID: flake recipe/lock changes intentionally affect the embedded generation identity, so old/new build IDs need not equal. Existing package checks and exact isolated real-PTY checks provide behavior evidence; never start or touch a live Eon session. Test receipts name their own exact tree.

Evaluate all affected `aarch64-darwin` package/check derivation attrs and confirm the Linux-only helper adds no artifact restore there. This host cannot compile Darwin; the shipped Darwin path stays on plain buildRustPackage. macOS follow-up must build the same package/cache selections, confirm zero external recompiles for source-only changes, run existing package/real-PTY checks, compare binary metadata/worker/terminfo/wrappers/receipt, and check the native font/toolchain paths. Linux timing results make no macOS performance claim.

Rebase the local flake edits onto edge after eon-vhbmp lands and retain its checkPhase commands unchanged. Final proof: Nix evaluation/formatting, affected package/check builds, required workspace fmt/clippy and one whole-workspace isolated eon-test on the final staged tree. Report in bead/report.md, stage all repository changes, write `READY FOR REVIEW <tree>` to STATUS.md, then await overseer review. No author-run reviews or commits.

## Plan review

Opus review: `/home/lucca/.local/state/rota/runs/crane-planreview-opus-1/log`, relayed by INBOX 2026-11-10T03:48:49Z. Resolutions:

1. **Orbit first — completed.** The fixed run postdates the review. Complete file/byte equality and zero external compiles pass for cold consumer and source edit. Source-edit CPU is 441.878 → 69.230 s; shared-cache startup is separately charged (721.165 CPU s). Venus wiring followed that proof.
2. **Environment identity — checked, blanket superset rejected.** Disposable assertions prove identical vendor and auditable-wrapper paths across cache/all five consumers (`vendor-auditable-identities.json`). Unused native inputs need not match; require zero external recompiles for each actual selection, and fix any demonstrated watched-variable mismatch rather than adding GUI/Zig inputs everywhere.
3. **Stub invalidation — checked; manual pruning rejected.** Pinned mkDummySrc injects a dummy build-script path into every package, changing Cargo metadata from real manifests. buildPackage adds no missing fingerprint-deletion mechanism. Require every reachable workspace crate to recompile, plus strict artifact bytes; do not duplicate crane's invalidation owner.
4. **Byte equality — adopted.** Orbit/worker/real-PTY/Venus/bench/mac-proof must match exactly; wrapper component paths are compared separately. Eon build.rs hashes sources into 32-hex EON_WORKSPACE_DIGEST, not raw recipe embedding. Explain normalized digest/linker-ID differences; use an identical-source paired build if any further binary difference remains. Validate the actual candidate receipt/generation/components.
5. **Darwin — fallback adopted.** Only Linux uses the cache. Darwin retains original buildRustPackage arguments, with evaluation required. Native mac-proof and cache-reuse proof must precede enabling it there; no hosted workflow is dispatched by this Linux task.
6. **Cold cost — report explicitly.** First cache+Orbit is 788.661 CPU s versus 403.408 baseline; measure whole default closure too. This host uses max-jobs=1; claim nothing about parallel builders. Version bumps intentionally invalidate Cargo.lock/cache. Masking versions adds an unrequested lock-rewrite owner and is rejected.
7. **Features — adopted.** Separate package selections stay. Require zero external compiles through each full checkPhase, including Eon's ignored-test pass.
8. **Checks/logging — adopted.** Keep eon-vhbmp parallel regular/serial ignored checks unchanged. CPU logging is removed from shipping code; retained proof-only variants log both baseline/candidate. Final production tree gets uninstrumented delivery proof.
9. **Toolchain — agree.** Existing toolchain/hook derivation inputs invalidate the cache correctly.
10. **Dependency ownership — adopted.** Eon's Nix maintainer owns crane upgrades; crane/nixpkgs/toolchain updates repeat cache-key, reachable-workspace, zero-external and byte-equality proof. The vendor timestamp reset is an owned workaround for pinned cargoSetupHook, rechecked on nixpkgs upgrades. Exit retains Darwin's original path and disables Linux caching if unproved. Per the task's no-br/no-commit workflow, the overseer imports these records into the owning bead/landing commit.

The source-digest integration also owns a pinned crane hook workaround: move its linkCandidates scratch list into TMPDIR with mktemp -t, guarded by --replace-fail. Recheck on crane upgrades. Red/green reproducer proves source-root cleanliness; Eon binary/digest equivalence and final production builds prove delivery. CPU proof uses exact retained logging variants; production ships neither CPU log code nor a generic cache switch.

Mac-proof equivalence exception found during proof: only five local LLVM numeric module-ID suffixes differ in .strtab; all other sections and symbol identities/addresses/sizes match. A narrow metadata checker plus stripped whole-byte equality explains this exception; code/prefix mutation negative checks reject real changes. Report mac-proof as executable-equivalent, not byte-identical. The strict bar remains for every other unchanged binary. Details and upstream LLVM source are in 02-proof.md.

## Implementation review round 1 (2026-11-10)

Overseer requires wall-time benefit before landing. Retain the old 38% CPU result as a measured CPU claim only: serial component wall sums 999 s before versus 949 s after are inconclusive shared-host samples. Adopt Codex: prune only Ghostty Zig local/global caches before saving dependency artifacts; keep upstream use-symlink (zstd restores require materializing every Rust library); narrow nixpkgs post-build install snapshot to top-level output files, preserving the production snapshot across test compilation while avoiding deps/build copies. Keep real install/check hooks and their selections; verify Orbit worker/test discovery still uses the original target tree. Restore mac-proof to plain buildRustPackage and remove it from cache population. Add Opus shared-input ownership comment with all three examples; remove unused Darwin cctools cache input.

Warm/root the new cache separately, then three alternating baseline/candidate pairs of default builds with the same fresh comment in eon/ for each pair, fresh across all three pairs. max-jobs=1, cores=6, ordinary heavy slots, no own overlap. Capture builder child+shell CPU, wall including Nix client but excluding queue, loadavg start/end and samples, compiled crate names and rooted output/derivation identities. Production flake is restored byte-for-byte after collecting proof-only CPU fixtures. Evaluate uninstrumented final tree and build changed Nix surfaces/equivalence after measurement as required; prior unchanged Rust source-suite proof remains recorded separately.

Opus follow-ups owned/filed by overseer: landing max-jobs=2 to overlap Venus/Orbit, package-specific source filtering, eon-psque checkPhase/profile/nextest policy. Overseer will root the shared cache in the landing script. None is implemented in this bead.

Measurement clarification: every one of the six runs appends one fresh, unique comment line to the same eon/crates/eon/src/main.rs file, as requested. All six source hashes/default drvs are asserted distinct and Cargo.lock identical. Old same-comment-per-pair fixture evaluations were retained but never built.

Review-round outcome: all three default source-edit pairs pass the wall-time gate, 27.81–40.12% less wall (34.46% aggregate) and 35.51–45.22% less CPU. # eon-u5uv2 implementation notes

Base: edge `f4396b9`. Worker: Fable 5.2 pane agent.

## Decision

Lucca, 2026-11-10, relayed by eon-overseer (INBOX 19:05Z), after comparing five
captured candidates (today, A 24 px, B 28 px, C 32 px rows, D): "1. D plus the
gap fix". Contract text for VEN-C8 and VEN-C18 was approved in the same INBOX
entry under his auto-decision mode. Option B, which was implemented first as
the plan's recommendation, is kept only as `bead/option-B.patch`.

## What changed

1. **Band only on the expanded pane.** `PaneTitleTab::workspace`
   (`venus/src/render/chrome.rs`) fits a band for the expanded pane alone (a
   lone or zoomed pane is expanded). A collapsed pane gets none, so the
   existing compact drawing takes over: its title and its Zoom and Close
   buttons sit in gaps in its row's line, as the last collapsed row always
   did. Buttons keep their size, place, targets and behaviour.
2. **Mirrored-band path deleted.** Only collapsed rows below the expanded pane
   used it: `PaneTitleTab.flip` and `PaneTitleTab::reflect`
   (`venus/src/render.rs`) and the reflection in `PaneTitleTab::fit`. `fit`
   now takes the pane above instead of a neighbour-and-row pair.
3. **The gap fix** (`venus/src/scene.rs`, column layout). The band's cap rises
   one tab rise (`title_tab_rise`, a third of the title padding: 4 px at the
   defaults) above its title row. It used to rise into the collapsed row above
   and was then clamped onto that title's descenders (0 px clear). Now, in a
   column of several panes, the expanded pane's row starts one tab rise lower
   when a collapsed row sits above it, so the cap's line lands on the lower
   edge of that row and never inside it. Measured in the capture: 1 clear
   pixel under the deepest descender and 5 under the baseline, against 0 and
   4 before; the band's own title keeps its 5 px above the ascenders.
   - With no collapsed row above (the expanded pane is first), the cap rises
     into the stack band as before and the same space follows the expanded
     terminal instead. A column's terminal therefore has one height whichever
     of its panes is expanded, so moving focus inside a Stack never resizes a
     terminal.
   - A lone or zoomed pane reserves nothing.
   - The space is `title_tab_rise(metrics).ceil()`: whole pixels, so it moves
     no row off the pixel grid. That alone does not keep the cap out of the
     row above: at some fractional scales a pane row ends on half a pixel
     (scale 1.125: the row above ends at 129.5, the cap floored to 129). Review
     round 1 found it. `PaneTitleTab::fit` now bounds the cap's snapped top
     against the row above's lower edge whenever the column kept its whole
     space (the cap lands on 130 there). "Kept its whole space" compares the
     space between the two rows with the tab rise within a hundredth of a
     pixel: fractional rows can sum to a hair under a whole rise (scale 1.75,
     16.3 px font: 6.9999847 against 7), which the re-check found.
   - On a window too short for it the space yields, whole or in part, before
     the terminal loses its last padded row, as the bar's gaps and the stack
     band already do. The cap then falls back to the old clamp against the
     title's ink. Two existing checks caught the first version, which kept the
     space in a 1 × 1 window and in a scrolled short column. Because the
     space yields first, a column that keeps any of it never scrolls its
     headers, so the reveal scroll needed no change.
   - The space belongs to no pane row: like the cap pixels that already sat
     outside a header row, it is not a click or accessibility target.
   - `WorkspaceScene::initial_overhead` counts the same space, so a window
     opened for a requested grid in a column of several panes still fits that
     grid. Both places read one helper, `band_cap_space`.
4. **Bottom line with the first pane expanded** (review round 1, accepted as
   is unless Lucca says otherwise). The column frame's bottom follows the next
   row, so with the first pane expanded the 4 px of space sits between the
   terminal and the first collapsed row: the line under the terminal is about
   6 px above the terminal's lower edge instead of 10 px. The grid is
   unaffected. Seen in `captures/final-stack-first-dark.png`.

## Rule 6 (configurability)

No setting. The clearance is the tab rise, which is a third of the title
padding and scales with the display scale; it is the same token that sets the
cap's height and the stack band, so the three stay in step. A separate
"band gap" setting would let the cap overlap the title above (too small) or
detach the band from its Stack (too large) and adds a second geometry policy
to every clearance and tiny-window case, for a 4 px value. The band or
title-on-a-line choice has no style setting either: Lucca chose one look, and
eon-2ibdd records why a second header style is not offered. Recorded in
`docs/CONFIGURATION.md` beside eon-27deg and eon-2ibdd.

| Scene | Edge today | D final | Note |
| --- | ---: | ---: | --- |
| 1 pane, 1920 × 1080 | 51 | 51 | no space reserved |
| 2 panes | 50 | 50 | 7 px spare, 4 px used |
