# eon-u5uv2 — Give stacked pane header bands more breathing room

Plan, 2026-11-10. Worker: Fable 5.2 pane agent. Worktree
`/home/lucca/.cache/eon-agents/eon-pane-band-gaps`, base edge `1d9350d` (to be
rebased onto the edge that contains eon-5g0e5 before any code edit).

## Decision (2026-11-10T19:05Z, after the captures)

Lucca picked **"D plus the gap fix"** from the five captured candidates; the
overseer relayed it and approved the VEN-C8 and VEN-C18 text under his
auto-decision mode. The recommendations for B further down are history. What
was built, on edge `f4396b9`:

- No band on a collapsed pane; every collapsed title and its Zoom and Close
  sit in gaps in its row's line. The band stays on the expanded, lone or
  zoomed pane. The mirrored-band path is deleted.
- The gap fix: one tab rise (a third of the title padding, 4 px at the
  defaults) of space before the expanded pane's band when a collapsed title
  sits above it; when the expanded pane is first, the same space follows its
  terminal. It yields on windows too short for it.
- Rule 6: the clearance is a fixed derivation of the title padding, with no
  setting of its own; reason in `01-implementation-notes.md` and
  `docs/CONFIGURATION.md`.
- Rows: 51 / 50 / 49 / 47 for one to four panes at 1920 × 1080 (today
  51 / 50 / 49 / 48); 29 for seven panes at 1280 × 800 (today 29). Four panes
  lose one row: 3 px spare, 4 px needed.

Pane headers have bands; "panel" is kept for Stacks, popups and the Agents
sidebar (the rename is eon-guqrt).

Details: `01-implementation-notes.md`; checks: `02-proof.md`.

## Request

Lucca, 2026-11-10, on the Rex-like band (eon-2ibdd, `8c77875`): "i like it, but
it may be worrth increasing the margins/gaps a bit more".

## Current geometry, measured from the code

Defaults: font 16 px, line height 1.125 (cell 10 × 18 px), title padding 12 px,
`border_width` 1, scale 1. Lucca's own config changes none of these, so his
screenshot shows the defaults.

| Quantity | Derivation (owner) | Default |
| --- | --- | ---: |
| Pane header row: allocation, click and accessibility target | `header_heights().1` = chrome title text height = max(line height, 1.25 × font size) (`venus/src/scene.rs`) | 20 px |
| Pitch of stacked pane rows | rows are laid edge to edge, `position × pane_height` | 20 px |
| Gap between stacked bands | none: a band's top line is the next band's bottom edge | 0 px |
| Band cap rise above its row | `title_tab_rise` = padding / 3; the cap is then pushed down to the previous title's real glyph ink (`PaneTitleTab::fit`, `venus/src/render/chrome.rs`) | 4 px, clearance to the neighbour's descenders as low as 0 px |
| Visible band (cap line to next cap line) | one row, shifted up by the rise | 20 px |
| Space cap line → capital tops; baseline → next line | from Lucca's screenshot: lines at y 34/54/74, capitals 38–50 | 4 px / 4 px; descenders (`p`, `j`, `g`, `_`) touch the next line |
| Title left inset from the card edge | title padding (`FrameTitleTab::at`); the terminal's first column sits at the same 12 px | 12 px |
| Zoom and Close targets | two squares one row high, ending padding / 2 from the row's right edge | 20 × 20 px each, 6 px |
| Close glyph's right edge from the card edge | 6 px + centred glyph | about 11–12 px |
| Stack band above the first pane row | title text height + rise | 24 px |
| Card gap and corner radius | round(padding × 2 / 3) | 8 px |

Measured in a baseline capture (1920 × 1080, dark, Lucca's scene;
`captures/before/dark/1080-stack.png`): p1's row is y 76–96 and its cap
line is at y 72. The title's ink runs from y 78 (ascenders) to y 94
(descenders), baseline at y 90. p2's cap line belongs at y 92 but would cut the
descenders, so the clamp moves it to y 95, one pixel under them. Clear pixels
around a title today: **5 above the ascenders, 0 below the descenders** (4 below
the baseline). Terminal rows read from `eon pane read --json`: 51 / 50 / 49 / 48
for one to four panes, as the formula below gives.

So the tight look has one cause: a pane row is exactly one title text box
(20 px for a 16 px font), and the next band's cap rises 4 px into it. The room
is missing below the title, not above it. Horizontally the title has 12 px and
lines up with the terminal text below it; the Close glyph ends about as far
from the right edge.

## Options

Each option grows every pane row by a multiple of the existing rise
(padding / 3) and puts the extra space between one title and the next band's
line: the title keeps its place under its own cap, so it ends up centred
between the two lines. Rows below the expanded pane mirror this, as their bands
already do. The cap rise, Stack band (24 px), card gap, title padding,
typography, title inset and button size stay. No setting is added (rule 6,
below).

Terminal rows at 1080p and the defaults: a 1920 × 1080 window with the hints bar
shown has 971 px for one column's pane rows and terminal (1080 − 33 hints − 52
bar and margin − 24 Stack band); a terminal has 12 px padding top and bottom and
18 px rows.

| | Row | Clear above ascenders / below descenders | 1 pane | 2 panes | 3 panes | 4 panes |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| Today | 20 px | 5 / 0 px | 51 rows | 50 | 49 | 48 |
| A: + one rise | 24 px | 5 / 1 px | 51 (−0) | 49 (−1) | 48 (−1) | 47 (−1) |
| B: + two rises (= the card gap) | 28 px | 5 / 5 px | 51 (−0) | 49 (−1) | 47 (−2) | 46 (−2) |
| C: + one title padding | 32 px | 7 / 7 px | 50 (−1) | 49 (−1) | 47 (−2) | 45 (−3) |

Rows are for the expanded pane of a column with that many panes; each column
pays only for its own panes. Every pane row grows, collapsed or expanded, so
the expanded pane's title gains the same space above its terminal.

- **A (24 px)** moves the lines 4 px apart but leaves the descenders 1 px from
  the next line. Costs at most one terminal row up to four panes.
- **B (28 px)** is the first balanced step: 5 px above the ascenders and 5 px
  below the descenders. The 8 px it adds is the gap the cards already keep
  between each other. Costs nothing for a lone pane, one row for two panes, two
  for three or four.
- **C (32 px)** gives 7 / 7 px, close to the Rex proportion (its header is
  about twice its text height). Costs a row even for a lone pane and three rows
  at four panes.

**Recommendation: B.** A does not fix what the screenshot shows: the next line
still runs right under the descenders. C spends a row on every window,
including the common one-pane case. B is the smallest step that centres the
title between its lines, and its 8 px is a spacing already in the design.

Horizontal: no change. The title's 12 px inset lines up with the terminal's
first column, and the Close glyph ends about 12 px from the right edge; moving
either would break that alignment. The Zoom and Close targets keep their 20 px
squares, in the title's row.

Scope: panes only. Stack tab, popup, Agents and dialog headings keep their
geometry; none of them stack, so none has the problem. The last collapsed row
keeps its compact label on the column's bottom line; its row grows like the
others. `pane_frames = false` headers take the same row height (one policy).

## Option D (added by Lucca, INBOX 2026-11-10T17:25Z)

Lucca, on a seven-pane Stack: "this large title&border sandwich". D draws every
collapsed row as one thin line with its title inlined in the line, the look
before the notches, and keeps the band only on the expanded (or lone, or
zoomed) pane. Built as a fifth candidate on the unchanged edge tree and
captured with the same scenes.

- **Row height:** unchanged, 20 px. No terminal rows are lost (51 / 50 / 49 / 48
  at 1080p; a seven-pane Stack at 1280 × 800 keeps 29 rows, where B has 26).
- **Zoom and Close on collapsed rows:** they stay, same size and place. The
  row's line stops before them and they sit in that gap, exactly as the last
  collapsed row draws them today.
- **What it does not fix:** titles are still 20 px apart, and the expanded
  pane's band line still runs right under the last collapsed title's
  descenders (0 px clear), as today. The lines no longer run between titles,
  so the stack reads as a list rather than as cramped boxes; it does not read
  as separate rows. D could take B's taller rows as well (the two are
  independent); that was not built.
- **Two shapes again:** eon-2ibdd made every pane header one shape. With D the
  band means "expanded", collapsed panes look different from full ones, and a
  column's headers change shape when focus moves inside a Stack (the titles
  themselves do not move: both shapes centre the title in the same row).
- **Contract text D would touch:** VEN-C8, "Framed pane headers use one
  continuous raised band, including first, lone and zoomed panes" (becomes:
  expanded, lone and zoomed panes), "Interior collapsed edges mirror this
  treatment toward their pane. The final collapsed title stays a compact gap
  in the column's bottom edge" (becomes: every collapsed title is a compact
  gap in its row's line), and the hover and focus sentence that follows.
  VEN-C18, "Pane headers use VEN-C8's continuous band" and "Pane headers keep
  VEN-C8's final collapsed-title and clearance exceptions". Plus the same
  passages in `docs/CONFIGURATION.md`, `docs/USAGE.md` and
  `venus/docs/PRESENTATION.md`.
- **Code cost:** the capture candidate is one changed condition
  (`PaneTitleTab::workspace` returns no band for any collapsed pane, so the
  existing compact drawing takes over). Done properly it also deletes the
  mirrored-band path that only collapsed rows below the expanded pane use, and
  rewrites the outline and padding tests that assert collapsed bands and their
  joined strokes. Smaller in production code than B, larger in tests and
  contract text.

For comparison, B changes about 45 lines in `venus/src/scene.rs` and eight
one-word sites in `venus/src/render/chrome.rs`, updates fixed-pixel
expectations in eleven tests, and amends one VEN-C8 sentence ("row allocation
and button targets keep their existing geometry": the buttons keep theirs, the
row grows).

**Recommendation stays B**, as the INBOX entry asks unless D is clearly
simpler: D is not simpler once tests and contracts are counted, it brings back
a second header shape one bead after eon-2ibdd removed it, and it leaves the
band line under the descenders. If Lucca prefers D's lighter collapsed rows,
the cleanest version is D plus B's row height.

## Rule 6

No setting. The band stays one geometry policy derived from the configured font
size, line height and title padding, as `docs/CONFIGURATION.md` records for
eon-27deg, eon-2ibdd and eon-whjhd; this bead changes the derivation. Lucca
asked for a roomier default, not for a knob, and a row-height setting would add
a second axis to every stroke, clearance and tiny-window case the band already
handles. A user who wants denser or roomier bands changes the font size or line
height, which the band follows.

## Implementation

1. Wait for eon-5g0e5 on `origin/edge`, then move the detached worktree onto it.
2. `venus/src/scene.rs`: one derivation for the pane row height
   (`header_heights().1` = title text height + 2 × `title_tab_rise`), and each
   pane carries its title row: one title text height at the top of its row, or
   at the bottom for rows below the expanded pane. All painted geometry (cap,
   frame line, corners, joins, title, scrollback pill, buttons) reads the title
   row where it read the pane row, so every contour keeps its shape and only
   the distance between titles grows. Allocation, clipping, click and
   accessibility bounds keep the whole row. The popup branch of
   `initial_overhead` and the popup, Agents and dialog rows keep the title text
   height.
3. Buttons: targets stay title-height squares in the title row.
4. Tests: update the existing geometry expectations in the Venus scene and
   render suites; add no new test unless an existing one cannot express a
   failure the change can cause (the descender clearance and joined-stroke
   checks in `render/tests/outlines.rs` already run on the real layout).
5. Text: `docs/CONFIGURATION.md` (band derivation and default), 
   `venus/docs/PRESENTATION.md`, `docs/USAGE.md` if it states the height,
   `CHANGELOG.md`; VEN-C8 / VEN-C18 only where their wording states the row
   allocation is unchanged or gives a number (flagged to the overseer as a small
   contract amendment before review).

## Captures (done 2026-11-10, before Lucca's pick)

Index: `/home/lucca/.cache/eon-agents/eon-pane-band-gaps-work/captures/README.md`.
Nineteen isolated runs, all exit 0, no process left behind. Terminal rows read
from `eon pane read --json` match the tables above for every option: today
51 / 50 / 49 / 48, A 51 / 49 / 48 / 47, B 51 / 49 / 47 / 46, C 50 / 49 / 47 / 45,
D 51 / 50 / 49 / 48 (one to four panes, 1920 × 1080); seven panes at 1280 × 800:
29, 27, 26, 24, 29.

Proof (Venus suite, fmt, clippy, whole-workspace eon-test through heavy.sh)
follows Lucca's pick. A first Venus suite run on the B tree: 368 passed, 12
failed. One was a test helper that placed titles by the pane row and now reads
the title row (it passes); the other eleven are fixed-pixel expectations and
window-height thresholds to update for the chosen option.

title: Make the workspace label read-only, and clicking the shown tab under a popup returns to the tab
description:
## Approved outcome

Lucca's final scope is in comments 5245/5247 (2026-11-03, "ok, i agree"). It supersedes the earlier proposal to close window pickers on tab switches; that proposal is not implementation scope.

1. The workspace/session label in the tab bar is read-only information: no click action, Tab focus/Enter action or button outline. Hover names the configured Workspaces shortcut (currently Alt+Shift+S); preserve the name, position such as "notes 2/3", needs-input badge and accessible name. Workspaces stays reachable by its key and Commands > Switch workspace/session using current product naming.
2. Clicking the active shown tab while a popup covers it reveals that tab's panes: transient Workspaces/Commands/Anima instances are dismissed; keep-alive Agent/Files/Git instances stay alive hidden. A pending tab's Project chooser stays because there are no panes to reveal.
3. Per-tab popup retention when switching to a different tab stays as VEN-C18 and INTERACTION.md specify.

## Current evidence and owner

At dcaef1c: runtime/crates/eon-runtime/src/workspace.rs:2594 focus_id sets the active tab and returns without dismissing its popup. venus/src/scene.rs:4604 still hit-tests the workspace label as a control; venus/src/accessibility.rs:591 makes it a button when the tooltip exists, so read-only hover text must not accidentally retain Click/Focus actions. Pointer FocusId routing is venus/src/application.rs:6110. Treat the old line numbers and transient_sessions discussion as historical evidence, not extra scope.

## Acceptance and boundaries

- In an isolated one-tab window reproduce Lucca's original click report, then verify every popup class above, including pending Project chooser and clicking another tab and back.
- Read-only label remains legible, hoverable and accessible while absent from interactive navigation and activation.
- Name and prove the existing CLI hide/dismiss equivalent (eon popup hide POPUP); do not make agent focus of an already-active tab unexpectedly dismiss a popup unless that API change is approved.
- Draft exact EON-C33 label and VEN-C18/INTERACTION wording for approval before edits. EON-C18's pending chooser stays intact. No automatic picker cleanup on arbitrary tab switches or unrelated lifecycle redesign.
- Record neutral portability (shared scene, input/model and AccessKit paths). Follow current whole-workspace proof/review and isolated installed dogfood; user docs and CHANGELOG follow the visible behavior.

title: Clarify Eon public and technical naming
description:
Contract:
No EON runtime contract changes. This decision controls names in Eon documentation and planning metadata.

Prerequisites:
- The user selected Yazelix Eon as the product-line name.
- Eon owns the cross-project composition language while Orbit and Venus keep their technical ownership.

Reference gate:
- Directional collision research: https://www.npmjs.com/package/@demgun/eon, https://www.eon.io/, and https://orbit.build/ show that short Eon and Orbit names already exist in adjacent software markets.
- Treat this evidence as a reason to lead with Yazelix Eon and to perform package, command, domain, and trademark clearance before public release; it is not legal clearance.

Decision:
- Public product: Yazelix Eon, shortened to Eon after first mention.
- Platform labels, only after those surfaces exist: Eon for desktop, Eon for mobile, and Eon for the web.
- User-facing capability: Sessions.
- Technical roles: the Eon orchestrator, Venus client, and Orbit session runtime. Role words remain lowercase descriptors, not three public product names.
- Promote a component name publicly only if users can independently install, choose, configure, or use that component.

Acceptance checks:
- README distinguishes public names, future platform labels, user-facing capabilities, and technical roles without implying unimplemented surfaces exist.
- Architecture documentation records the same naming boundary and uses semantic role labels in the composition diagram.
- Contract IDs and ownership remain unchanged.
- README LOC scorecard, Markdown paths, Beads state, and git diff checks pass.

Scope boundary:
Documentation and mutable Eon planning metadata only. No runtime, command, repository, package, domain, contract, proof-state, child-repository, or historical Bead-ID rename is included.
close_reason: Documented the approved hybrid naming model in README.md and docs/ARCHITECTURE.md: Yazelix Eon is the public product, Sessions is the user-facing capability, and Eon orchestrator, Venus client, and Orbit session runtime are technical role descriptions. Future platform labels remain conditional. No runtime contract, command, repository, package, child-project, or historical ID changed. Verified Bead lint, Markdown paths, EON-C identifiers, absence of live Astra wording, the 611-line LOC scorecard, and git diff checks.

title: Decide whether GPUI becomes Venus's UI stack (deferred: not now)
description:
## Why

Lucca, 2026-10-29: "research gpui / think if it makes sense for us long term" and "if gpui is good,
it could be a eon v2 target". herdr-app, Agentaps and Zeron all build on Zed's GPUI. Research in
session eon-8e concluded: not now and not as a v2 target yet; re-check against the triggers below.
Lucca approved recording that ("1 ok", 2026-10-29). Decision only; no work approved.

## Findings (read 2026-10-29; Zed main 0373366f43e3)

Against, for Eon:
- No stable releases: crates.io `gpui` stops at 0.2.2 (2025-10-22); README "still pre-1.0. There
  will often be breaking changes"; 165 commits to crates/gpui in three months. Apps pin third-party
  snapshots or patch forks (herdr-app `gpui-pre =0.3.8` vendored and patched; Zeron its own fork
  zeronsh/zui). The ecosystem is split (gpui-pre, gpui-fast, gpui-ce, zui).
- Zed first: gpui.rs "For the near future, GPUI is tied to Zed"; custom-shader PR
  zed-industries/zed#42905 closed ("without a Zed use case, I can't validate this code"); #43273
  closed not planned. No custom render pass hook, so Venus's image pipeline, budgets, draw order and
  cursor trail would need a renderer fork on three backends.
- Linux backend young (wgpu since #46758, 2026-02-13): no damage regions (#15166), GNOME sluggishness
  (#53522), COLRv1 emoji wrong on Linux (#42255), KDE-only blur (#53746 open for
  ext-background-effect), no GPU device-loss recovery (#23288; VEN-C4 needs it).
- Zed's terminal crates are GPL-3.0-or-later and cannot be reused; gpui crates are Apache-2.0.

For:
- Wayland: fractional-scale, text-input-v3, primary selection, xdg-decoration, DnD, cursor-shape;
  native Metal on macOS; AccessKit upstream (#56065, 2026-05-27).
- Grid drawing works (Zed, herdr-app on libghostty-vt, Agentaps gpui-rio, Zeron, Termy).
- gpui-kit (longbridge, 18.8k stars) speeds up building panels.

Venus today (edge d668142): wgpu 30 + winit 0.30 + glyphon 0.12 + AccessKit; about 10.5k lines of
render/text code, 4.2k of accessibility, about 30 VEN contracts touching renderer, text, input or
windowing; product logic (scene, model, transport, launch, about 8k lines) would mostly survive a
swap. venus/docs/CRATES.md already rejected Iced and Slint for owning "unnecessary widget, layout,
runtime, and renderer policy for one custom surface".

## Decision

No GPUI for Venus now or as a committed v2 target. Revisit only when both hold:
1. Eon decides to own many non-terminal panels (eon-u9bs).
2. GPUI is dependable: semver releases from Zed or a Zed-endorsed fork, a supported custom
   rendering hook, and a Linux backend with damage tracking, device-loss recovery and
   ext-background-effect blur.

## Acceptance

- At revisit: re-read the triggers at a recorded Zed revision; if both hold, propose a one-popup
  spike inside Venus (compare code size, text quality, Wayland behaviour) for Lucca's approval;
  otherwise extend the deferral with the evidence.

## Maintenance Notes

- Report sources: crates.io gpui, gpui-pre, gpui-ce; longbridge/gpui-kit v0.8.1 release notes and
  issue #2234; gpui-ce#50; the Zed PRs and issues above; herdr-app b41b5cb; Zeron a046850;
  Agentaps 66c7116 (~/pjs/refs/agentaps).

comments.author: lucca
comments.text: Source: "A Critique of GPUI", https://blog.zortax.de/posts/a-critique-of-gpui (2026-11-08). Lucca asked for this review on 2026-11-09 ("get an agent on this"); analysis in ~/.cache/eon-agents/eon-ideas-work/gpui-critique.md (Venus read at edge 97bbd4c). Recommendation 7: new evidence for "not now". The post measures GPUI's update cost growing with tree size (one label edit at 3,000 rows: 8.4 ms; 92 ms with plain elements; equal writes as costly as real ones without hand-written guards), and Zed's own retained-view work measured 1-3% slower on ordinary workloads (draft zed#63800 closed 2026-09-24). At revisit, add a third trigger: GPUI's update cost scales with what changed, not tree size, through a retained-node engine upstream rather than forks such as gpui-fast. Caveats: one unreviewed harness on one machine, by the author of a competing framework (zgui).

comments.author: lucca
comments.text:
Evidence update, 2026-11-10 (Fable session research for Lucca; full record on eon-renderer-gpui-rune-xsvwn). Checked against crates.io and GitHub on 2026-11-10; findings only, the deferral stands.

- Releases: still none (crates.io gpui 0.2.2, 2025-10-22). Zed staff said on 2026-10-30 they are "setting up automated releases of GPUI… following the weekly release cadence", "not quite ready" (zed#66275, discussion #55271).
- Custom render hook: upstream still none. The fork gpui-ce 0.3.0 (2026-10-20) has one: the app shares GPUI's wgpu device and composites its texture (ce#237, merged 2026-09-09). A texture composite, not an in-pass hook; clipping and z-order unverified.
- Damage and retention: staff damage-tracking PR zed#62455 closed 2026-10-30 ("we are now taking a different approach"); retention PR zed#63800 closed 2026-09-24 with no successor.
- Correction to this bead's findings: gpui_wgpu on Zed main now has device_lost() and recover() plus a headless renderer (zed#64718, merged 2026-09-25), so "no GPU device-loss recovery (#23288)" is out of date. Landing date of the recovery path not established.
- GPUI terminals in the field (herdr-app, Agentaps, Zeron, Zed) paint cells with GPUI primitives; herdr-app's tracker shows the cost (wide glyphs #851, 30 fps redraw #794, blank colour emoji on Windows #844). All pin snapshots (gpui-pre) or fork.
- Venus contract count is 20 active VEN-C IDs (12 retired), not "about 30".

title: Venus control layer: declare each chrome control once
description:
## Why

Every piece of Venus chrome is wired by hand through four layers: a rect in the scene, a branch in
hit-testing, a hover or press field with its setter, a node in the accessibility tree, and draw
code. Venus has no control or layout abstraction, so each new control repeats all of it:

- Zoom and Close header buttons (8b5ee2d): +676 source, +460 test lines, 11 files.
- Hide buttons (ad01d8c): +639 source, +381 test, 9 files.
- Window menu (d82e3b7): +918 source, +604 test, 9 files.

`venus/src` grew from 23,272 lines (2586d7c, 2026-10-14) to 65,251 (27b3909, 2026-11-10), mostly
chrome. About 60% of Venus's ~30,550 non-test lines are chrome drawing, layout, hit-testing and
accessibility. The find bar (eon-ndep0), a command palette (eon-5za8) and themes
(eon-eon-themes-or3q) will each add controls. Research record: the 2026-11-10 comment on
eon-renderer-gpui-rune-xsvwn.

Lucca, 2026-11-10, approved this from a numbered list ("ok:"): "A Venus-owned control layer before
the find bar and command palette? I recommend filing it, outside the gate. One description per
control would feed layout, hit-testing, hover, accessibility and drawing, so a button costs about
100 lines instead of 1,000. It attacks the cost slope now and makes a later move to Rune smaller. It
is a new Venus module, so it needs your approval as product scope." That approval covers the new
Venus module (venus/AGENTS.md: "A new Venus module is product scope").

## Goal

One Venus-owned description per chrome control (its identity, where it sits, what it does when
pressed, its hover and press states, its accessible role and name, and how it is drawn) from which
Venus derives layout, hit-testing, hover handling, the accessibility node and the draw calls. Adding
a simple button then touches one place.

## Contract

None changes. Presentation is a feature (docs/AGENT-RULES.md, Contract-Driven Method). This is a
behaviour-preserving refactor of how the chrome under VEN-C8, VEN-C18, VEN-C20, VEN-C21, VEN-C23,
VEN-C30 and VEN-C32 is built, and VEN-C6 (accessibility) must keep passing. No visible change, no
new configuration value, no new window action.

## Evidence (dcaef1c; re-check before implementation)

- `venus/src/scene.rs:858` `WorkspaceHit` and `:4588` `hit_test`: a hand-ordered if-chain over named
  rect fields.
- `venus/src/scene.rs:3511` `from_snapshot_with_zoom`: about 840 lines placing every control by
  arithmetic.
- `venus/src/render/chrome.rs:1896-1940`: one hover setter per control (`set_hovered_header`,
  `set_version_hovered`, `set_cpu_hovered`, `set_clock_hovered`, `set_quota_hovered`, ...).
- `venus/src/render/chrome.rs:2666` `build_workspace`: about 740 lines of draw code per surface.
- `venus/src/application.rs:5542` `window_event`: pointer and key routing per control.
- `venus/src/accessibility.rs`: chrome nodes built by hand beside the terminal nodes.

## Scope boundary

In scope: Venus chrome controls (bar chips and tabs, pane and popup header buttons, sidebar rows,
menu and dialog rows) and the module that describes them.

Out of scope:
- The terminal grid, images, cursor trail and their pipelines.
- Any UI framework or new dependency, unless child 1 records a dependency decision under
  AP-DEPENDENCY-001 and Lucca approves it. Default: none.
- A text input control. It is the first new control built on this layer and belongs to the find
  bar's Venus child (eon-ndep0).
- Visible changes of any kind; the calmer-chrome epic (eon-wuau8) owns those.
- The v0.2.0 gate (eon-igae): this epic is not a gate member.

## Children

1. Design the control description and prove it on one surface in a throwaway branch (filed).
2. Land the control layer with that first surface migrated, no visible change (filed, blocked by 1
   and by eon-wuau8.1, which renames the same style call sites).
3. Planned, file after child 2 lands: migrate the remaining surfaces one per bead (bars, sidebar,
   menus and dialogs), each with no visible change, deleting the hand wiring it replaces.

## Acceptance

- Every chrome control is declared once, and layout, hit-testing, hover, accessibility and drawing
  derive from that declaration.
- Venus's existing scene, chrome, outline and accessibility tests pass without changed expectations,
  apart from tests of deleted internals.
- A recorded before/after: lines and files touched to add one simple button.
- Net non-test lines in `venus/src` fall.

## Maintenance Notes

- Order with other work: the find bar's Venus child and any palette implementation come after this
  layer (Lucca, 2026-11-10). eon-wuau8.1 (named radii, paddings and text styles) is the style half;
  this is the structure half.
- A later move to a framework such as Rune (spike: eon-renderer-gpui-rune-xsvwn) is easier from one
  declaration per control than from four hand-wired layers. Do not shape this layer as a Rune
  adapter; it must pay for itself in Venus alone.
- Historical open question (settled by later comments; see current disposition below): adopting or forking Rune. Lucca, 2026-11-10, after approving this epic: "venus
  already has a high cost, so a rune fork would not be that bad imo, but i could be wrong". If Eon
  moves its chrome to Rune, most of this layer is redundant. Open question put to Lucca the same
  day: whether child 2 (landing) waits for the Rune spike's verdict. Until he answers, child 1
  (throwaway prototype) is safe to run and child 2 is not started without checking this note.
- GPUI stays deferred (eon-ua5e).

## Current disposition

Comment 6421 records Lucca's "2 ok": landing child .2 waits for the Rune spike; prototype .1 does not. The spike's latest overseer record (2026-11-11, eon-renderer-gpui-rune-xsvwn) says tracks A-I are done, Lucca chose investment through a Yazelix fork tracking upstream, and follow-ups are eon-azfsx, eon-t1rtk and eon-1cyzr. This supersedes the historical "adoption undecided / D paused" notes, but does not itself cancel this approved epic or authorize landing a redundant layer.

Keep .2's blocker until the overseer/Lucca records whether the accepted Rune path retains, narrows or retires this layer. No implementation decision is made by this audit. eon-wuau8.1 is closed; remaining surfaces are still filed one per meaningful independently verifiable slice after .2. Portability: neutral shared chrome/AccessKit paths, with native Linux installed proof and no new platform promise.

title: Design the Venus control description and prove it on one surface in a throwaway branch
description:
## Why

The parent epic wants one description per Venus chrome control to feed layout, hit-testing, hover,
accessibility and drawing. Whether one description can do that while Venus's pixel-level chrome
tests keep passing is unproved. This bead proves or disproves it on one surface before anything
lands, and records the shape for child 2. Read the parent first.

## Evidence (dcaef1c; re-check before implementation)

- `venus/src/scene.rs:858` `WorkspaceHit`, `:4588` `hit_test`: hand-ordered if-chain.
- `venus/src/scene.rs:3511` `from_snapshot_with_zoom`: control rects by arithmetic.
- `venus/src/render/chrome.rs:1896-1940`: one hover setter per control.
- `venus/src/render/chrome.rs:2666` `build_workspace`: per-surface draw code.
- `venus/src/application.rs:5542` `window_event`: per-control pointer routing.
- `venus/src/accessibility.rs`: hand-built chrome nodes.
- Cost of one control today: 8b5ee2d (Zoom and Close header buttons) +676 source, +460 test lines
  over 11 files. Use `git show --stat 8b5ee2d -- venus/` as the worked example of what a description
  must replace.

## Scope

In scope:
- Read the four layers above for one small surface with two or more buttons. Pick a surface no open
  bead is changing; check eon-2ibdd (pane header band, in progress) and the eon-wuau8 children
  before choosing. Popup header buttons or the bar's reading chips are candidates.
- References, read at exact revisions and recorded: Rune's element and hit-test model
  (`~/pjs/refs/rune`, 3686e94, reference only: do not build, run or copy it), WezTerm's
  `box_model.rs` (`~/pjs/refs/wezterm`), and how Rio hand-draws its palette and tabs
  (`~/pjs/refs/rio`).
- In a throwaway branch or worktree, prototype the control description and derive that surface's
  rects, hit result, hover state, accessibility node and draw calls from it. Nothing lands.
- Decide and record on the parent epic: the description's fields; who owns hover and press state;
  how the hit result maps to the existing `WorkspaceHit` actions; how accessibility nodes keep their
  ids; whether layout stays arithmetic helpers (row, stack, fit-or-drop) or needs a crate. Default:
  no new dependency. A crate such as Taffy needs the AP-DEPENDENCY-001 record and Lucca's approval.

Out of scope:
- Landing any code. Visible changes. The terminal grid. A text input control.
- Shaping the layer as an adapter for Rune or any framework.

## Acceptance

- The parent epic carries a comment with the chosen description shape, the decisions above with
  reasons, rejected shapes, and the surface chosen for child 2.
- The prototype's result is recorded: existing tests for that surface pass unchanged (or the exact
  ones that cannot, and why), and the line count before and after for that surface.
- A plain verdict: proceed with child 2 as filed, change its scope, or stop the epic, with evidence.

## Verification

- `nix develop -c eon-test` on the prototype tree (never inside a live Eon
  session's environment; see docs/DEVELOPMENT.md). Record revision, command and result on this bead.
- Planning output only otherwise: bead state.

## Stop Conditions

- Stop if every candidate surface is being changed by an open bead; report which.
- Stop if the prototype needs a visible change or a contract change to work.
- Stop if the same test failure survives two reasonable attempts; record it as the finding.

## Maintenance Notes

- Follow the machine-load rule before building. One bead per agent session.
- The package name for `-p` must be checked in `venus/Cargo.toml`.

## Current planning constraints

At dcaef1c the evidence addresses above are relocated; historical line-count claims stay attributed to their original revisions. Portability is neutral (shared scene, drawing, input and AccessKit). The full current workspace check/review rules apply to a prototype or landing; the rendered-surface route also needs Tier 1 and the existing machine's Tier 2 gate, or a named missing Tier 2 observation.

Prototype .1 remains allowed independently of the Rune landing gate; it must still pay for its result as evidence, not assume adoption of the control layer. Re-check surface availability rather than assuming eon-2ibdd is still in progress.

title: Decide whether managed commands need an unprefixed toggle
description:
## Origin
Split from closed `eon-pxn` on 2026-10-16 (deferred managed-environment horizon).

## Decision needed
Whether Eon needs a toggle for its unprefixed managed commands inside terminals (`hx`, `yazi`,
`lazygit` and the shells) versus only the stable `eon-*` names. Take this up only with real
collision evidence from a user's own installed tools.

## Constraint

title: Update button: update Eon from the window or the CLI for Nix branches, release pins and Nix-free installs
description:
## Why

Ronald (an Eon user) asked for an update button that runs the update commands for him. Lucca, 2026-11-07: "we'd have to think about where to put it, and how to handle users on a release, vs a branch, vs nix-less users". Today docs/USAGE.md#update tells a main or edge install to run the update commands by hand, says a tag install never updates, and the Nix-free install (eon-igae.15) has its own path. Related: eon-t3fyd (update a running full-Eon window without moving its terminals), eon-1bq8 (decide in-place window update), eon-5cwzy (release classes and changelog prefixes).

## Deliverable (research and a proposal; no product code)

Recorded in the agent's work dir, for Lucca:
1. How each install kind updates today, exactly: Nix profile on main, on edge, on a tag; the Nix-free install; Home Manager or nix-darwin users; macOS. What command, what it changes, what a running window and its supervisor see afterwards, and what can go wrong (an EONW change, a running old supervisor, a failed build).
2. How others do it: Ghostty, kitty, WezTerm, Zed, VS Code, Warp, Rex if public; update checks, notification vs one-click vs automatic, channels, and how Nix-managed installs are handled (most refuse and tell the user to update through Nix).
3. Where a button belongs in Eon: the version badge's session menu (eon-7cf0y.6), the Eon Bar, the command palette, a notice when a newer version exists; and its CLI path (AGENTS.md rule 5: a window action ships with an `eon` command, such as `eon update` with `--check` and JSON).
4. A recommended design per install kind (what the button does, what it refuses, how it reports progress and failure, how it relates to restarting the window and eon-t3fyd), with configuration keys and defaults (rule 6), and any contract it would need.
5. A slice plan of small child beads, marking what could fit before v0.2.0 and what must wait. Scope is Lucca's call: do not mark anything as gating v0.2.0.
close_reason: All seven slices landed (f10d1.1-.7): eon update --check and --install for Nix profile entries and Nix-free prefixes, from the CLI, the Commands popup and the Window menu. Follow-up eon-update-button-f10d1.8 (P3, installer smoke socket lifetime) stays open outside the v0.2.0 gate.

description:

target made reviewable. **Prerequisite:** S1.

**Scope:** `--install` for validated official moving-ref user-profile entries;
target revalidation, confirmation/`--yes`, manager argv/process ownership,
progress/error reporting and actual selected-build result. Include consumed
profile/entry configuration defaults and usage/changelog. Keep tag,
declarative, local-source, eonbase and unknown installations as refusals.
Contract: approved install-update boundary; preserve C3/C11.

**Acceptance:** A disposable profile updates only the selected Eon entry on
its original ref; an unrelated package remains selected. Custom path/name,
unchanged target, build failure, cancellation and concurrent source/entry
changes report the actual selected state. A live isolated A window keeps its
terminals/layout/build after installation of B. A command from A does not
accidentally upgrade another profile or run A's ordinary window-routing path.

**Verification:** Focused behavior/failure checks, full workspace suite and
affected package build; one isolated outermost update observation with exact
profile/artifact/build identities and no user's profile involved. Prove the
adapter's real concurrency limits; do not claim an unimplemented transaction
guard. **Stop:** If target ownership cannot be proved, return the typed

comments.author: lucca
comments.text:
Notes for --install from eon-update-button-f10d1.2 (2026-11-07): # 03. Notes for the Install slice (`eon-update-button-f10d1.3`)

Facts from `.2` that `.3` must honour; the overseer copies this to `.3`.

- **Exact entry names.** `nix profile upgrade ENTRY` treats ENTRY as a
  regular expression on Nix before 2.20 (later Nix matches element names and
  needs `--regex` for patterns). Install must address the one entry `.2`
  reports by its exact name, never a pattern: on Nix older than 2.20, refuse
  or escape so the name matches only itself, and prove it with a name that
  holds regex characters (`eon.1`, `eon+x`). `.2`'s printed manual
  `next_step` (`nix profile upgrade --profile P --refresh ENTRY`) carries
  the same caveat for those Nix versions.
- **Which nix.** `.2` reads profiles with the person's own `nix` from PATH
  (`Host::profile_list`), bounded at 30 s (`NIX_LIMIT`); curl is pinned
  (`EON_CURL`, `curlMinimal`) and missing curl is `curl-unavailable`.
  Pinning nix was deferred: see the round-1 rebuttal in `04-review.md`.
  Install inherits whatever the overseer settles there.
- **Target binding.** Discovery accepts an owner only when the path that
  started `eon` (argv0, unresolved) runs through that profile's selected
  generation (`through`), not when outputs are equal. Inside an Eon terminal
  argv0 is the window build's `libexec/eon/bin/eon`, so discovery is
  `install-ambiguous` there; the Commands popup (`.4`) and agents must carry
  an explicit `--profile`/`--entry` (or `.3`'s configured target).
- **Configuration keys**

description:

cannot assume `eon-install` exists on PATH. **Prerequisite:** S0 and the

Nix-free bootstrap/path/provenance proof; root installer's supported checks and
full workspace suite if the change touches code/tests/scripts. Record C6
identity and the artifact/platform, not a generic portability claim.

or tag operation belongs to this slice.

title: Install a found Nix-free release through the existing installer
description:
From the update-button research (eon-update-button-f10d1, /home/lucca/.cache/eon-agents/eon-update-button-work/bead/04-slices.md, slice S6; 00-today.md to 03-design.md hold the evidence). In the v0.2.0 gate (Lucca put all seven update slices in it on 2026-11-07).

**Why:** Nix-free users need the same explicit action once trusted delivery
and discovery exist. **Prerequisites:** S4 and S5.

**Scope:** Invoke the exact trusted bootstrap with pinned HTTPS asset,
signer record and validated prefix; reuse S2's public result semantics and S3's
presentation. Preserve C5's lock/retention/recovery. Add consuming defaults,
help, usage and changelog. No shell scripts, auto-prune or payload overwrite.

**Acceptance:** In an isolated Nix-free host/prefix, B becomes current while
A's terminals remain alive on A. Bad signature/hash, failed smoke check,
interrupted extraction, lock contention and cancellation never produce a
false installed result. Report actual selected digest on interruption. A
rollback remains the existing explicit installer command. Do not repeat the
installer's parser tests where its own existing tests already prove them;
exercise the integration's exact arguments, trust and selected state.

**Verification:** Full workspace suite and root installer/affected package
checks; one isolated outermost signed install observation, binding archive,
signer, helper and running identities. Follow the current AGENT-RULES for
review/delivery. **Stop:** If the published host/artifact differs from the
qualified one, obtain the additional proof rather than reuse its label.

## Later optional work, after the manual route

These are not blockers for the manual feature or v0.2.0:

- **Menu integration:** extend the existing `eon-7cf0y.6` scope with an Updates
  item once its corrected placement and S3's operation exist. Keep Commands.
- **Installed-build notice:** continue `eon-newer-build-notice-byd2`; consume
  the same install identity and one shared notice setting. Its local notice
  does not need remote update discovery or automatic installation.
- **Remote periodic check:** a separate optional child after S1/S5. Add
  `updates.check = "periodic"` opt-in, 24-hour configurable interval,
  versioned discardable metadata cache, rate bounds, one check per install,
  offline/rate-limit/freshness states and non-focusing notice/CLI parity.
  Prove its network budget and disabled/manual behavior. No auto-download,
  auto-install or auto-restart. Split scheduling from notice presentation if
  their consuming files/proof exceed one session.
- **Use installed build in live work:** continue `eon-t3fyd` after its
  `eon-hyil8` reconciliation and fresh canonical-contract approval. The menu
  consumes its eventual capability/refusal result. Do not make package
  installation depend on live adoption or its roughly nine-session plan.
- **Repin/switch channels from the UI:** later explicit decision and one
  transaction-proved slice if requested. The first feature explains pins.

Suggested dependency order: S0 → S1 → S2 → S3; S0 → S4;
S1 → S5; S4 + S5 → S6. S4/S5/S6 are later work pending direct-delivery
prerequisites. S0/S1 and, if discovery/transaction proof stays bounded, S2/S3
could be considered before v0.2.0. This is feasibility advice, **not a release
commitment, milestone assignment or gating dependency**.

## Common verification and landing rule for future slices

Before code, read affected directory AGENTS and reference routes. Run Rust
suites only with `nix develop -c eon-test`; authors run the full workspace on
the exact staged tree, plus required changed-crate fmt/clippy and affected Nix
proof. Installed proof uses isolated roots/displays and throwaway profiles or
prefixes, preserving focus and live processes. The overseer schedules heavy
runs and reviews. No current research command authorizes those future runs.

Refresh an active profile only if the future approved implementation session

title: Drop the installer smoke command's socket write end right after spawn, so a version line without a newline fails at once
description:
From the Opus re-check of eon-update-button-f10d1.7 (2026-11-08, non-blocking): in installer/src/main.rs (~235-247) the smoke step's Command keeps its copy of the socket's write end open until smoke returns, so if eon versions exits without printing a newline the read never sees end-of-file and waits the full 30 s deadline before reporting preflight-failed. Bounded and fails safe. Fix: drop(command) right after spawn(); add a test with a child that prints no newline and exits, asserting a prompt failure. Proof: eon-test --manifest-path installer/Cargo.toml, nix build .#installer.

## Current evidence and precise regression

At dcaef1c installer/src/main.rs:237 smoke still retains the Command after spawn at :246-255; no drop(command) precedes the read. Keep the fix within smoke and its existing tests. EON-C5/installer preflight behavior remains the owner boundary; current link and installed version stay unchanged on every failure.

Preserve the original acceptance: a child prints a version line without a newline and exits, and smoke promptly reports preflight-failed with current unchanged. Include otherwise-valid version words as well as malformed/incomplete output so the regression cannot pass only because the contents are invalid. Inspection shows today's validator splits whitespace without checking line termination, so drop(command) alone may change timeout failure into success; reconcile that with the owning smoke contract before implementation rather than silently weakening the requested failure. The overseer report flags this ambiguity. Also retain the descendant-holds-stdout deadline/cleanup behavior and successful newline-terminated case. Use a generous bounded timing check rather than a fragile subsecond scheduling limit.

The standalone crate package is eon-install (installer/Cargo.toml). Before implementation choose its supported isolated harness from docs/DEVELOPMENT.md; whole-workspace eon-test alone does not cover a standalone manifest. Follow current review and affected installer artifact proof.

title: Report an unmarked eon-install prefix as not owned instead of os error 2
description:
## Why

lm9p.1 found that `eon-install` gives a misleading message when the prefix is an existing
user-owned 0700 directory without the `.eon-install` marker. The behavior is right (exit 1,
contents untouched, nothing adopted), but the message is "eon-install: No such file or directory
(os error 2)" instead of "prefix is not owned by eon-install".

Cause: installer/src/main.rs:123 checks the marker with `fs::symlink_metadata(&marker)?`; the
NotFound error returns through `?` before the intended `invalid("prefix is not owned by
eon-install")`.

## Contract

docs/INSTALLER.md's prefix ownership rule: an existing prefix that eon-install did not create is
refused with a message naming the ownership problem. No behavior change beyond the message.

## Prerequisites

None. Reference gate: not consequential (no dependency, protocol, contract or trust-boundary
change; the refusal itself stays).

## Acceptance

- An existing 0700 prefix without `.eon-install` exits 1 with "prefix is not owned by
  eon-install", contents untouched. Falsifier: a focused red/green test in installer/src/tests.rs
  if it adds coverage beyond the existing prefix tests, else a red/green reproducer recorded here.
- Installer crate builds; `nix develop -c eon-test` for the installer suite passes.
- Codex and converge review per AGENTS.md (code change).

## Scope boundary

Message only. Any published Nix-free candidate built after this lands differs from lm9p's
6379a43c and needs the re-run named in lm9p's 2026-10-21 harness comment; this bead does not
build or publish a candidate.

title: List and stop other-EONW generations through their recorded eon
description:
## Why

After every EONW bump, the new `eon` cannot list, inspect or stop windows
started by an older build. Each changelog entry tells users to "stop the ones
you no longer need with the old `eon` first". The old build is still present
while its window runs:
- its closure is a Nix /proc runtime GC root (verified 2026-10-31 with
  `nix-store --gc --print-roots`: a live eon-0.1.8);
- installer payloads are retained;
- its `eon` is recorded as `<gen>/eon`.
So the new `eon` can hand the work to the old build instead of keeping old
codecs. Lucca accepted this (eon-c8ytm decision 6) on 2026-10-31.

## Contract

The EON-C28 Upgrades text is approved (2026-10-31, eon-c8ytm): "The new `eon`
lists and stops every older 1.x generation through EON-C11, with its own codec
or by running the generation's recorded `eon`." The contract indexing bead
applies it.

NOT yet approved: EON-C11 (docs/CONTRACTS.md, around line 1336) says "A
generation from a build with another EONW version is listed as incompatible;
this `eon` neither inspects nor stops it, and the build that started it can."
Draft its replacement and bring the exact text to Lucca (via eon-overseer)
before code.

## Evidence

- `runtime/crates/eon-runtime/src/generation.rs:64` `EON_ATTACH_DELEGATED` and
  `:741` `attach_generation`: attach already runs the recorded `eon`.
- `runtime/crates/eon-runtime/src/generation.rs:450` `inspect_generation`,
  `:527` the incompatible state; `:636` `generations_command`.
- `runtime/crates/eon-runtime/src/control.rs:294-307`: the `Incompatible`
  failure, "the Eon build that started it can attach or stop it".
- `runtime/crates/eon-workspace-protocol/src/v26.rs:10-12`: the 12-byte EONW
  header (magic and version).

## Scope

In scope:
- For a generation whose EONW differs, `eon generations`, `eon stop GEN`,
  `eon stop previous` and `eon stop all` run the generation's recorded `eon`,
  with a recursion guard like attach's, and merge its result into this build's
  listing and JSON.
- Fallback: today's "incompatible" listing, with the reason, when `<gen>/eon` is
  missing or fails.
- Remove the "stop ... with the old `eon` first" guidance from docs and the
  changelog template; add a `CHANGELOG.md` entry.

Out of scope:
- Moving a live window to a new build (eon-1bq8), and presenting old
  generations (EON-C11 attach is unchanged).
- Capability negotiation or old codecs in EONW.

## Acceptance

- In isolation, an older-EONW generation started by a previous build is listed
  with its real state and stopped by the new `eon stop previous`, and its
  terminals end.

## Verification

- `nix develop -c eon-test` on eon-runtime (lifecycle tests), plus the Nix
  check that covers previous-generation Stop. converge plus Codex. One
  installed observation across two real builds.

## Stop Conditions

- Stop before code until the EON-C11 text is approved.
- Stop if delegation would need a writable store path or Nix evaluation
  (docs/AGENT-RULES.md Composition and Distribution).

## Maintenance Notes

- Policy: eon-c8ytm proposal, section C. herdr-core's holder-per-build drain is
  the related prior art for eon-1bq8, not for this bead.

title: Codex agents show the three background dots whenever they are not working
description:
Lucca 2026-11-11: 'why are all agents with ...'. Every Codex pane in the Agents sidebar shows the three still dots (waiting on background work) instead of finished or idle. Cause, verified on codex-cli 0.167.1: Codex starts its own long-lived helpers at session start (node_repl, MainThread, codex-code-mode), each in its own process group under the same session; Orbit's background count (orbit/src/platform.rs background_processes, ORB-C15) counts any settled non-foreground-group descendant, so these helpers always count. Same likely for Claude Code sessions holding Monitor/background shells legitimately (those are real background work and should keep the dots).
Do: stop counting an agent's own persistent helpers without hiding real background work the agent started (a build, a server, a watcher). Candidate: baseline the processes present when the agent first reports, or count only processes started after the agent's latest working turn began; decide in the plan, with a red/green test using a fake agent that spawns a helper at start and a background job later. Owners: Orbit (count) or Runtime (interpretation); a wire change needs an ORBS/EONW bump, prefer the Runtime side if it suffices. Re-proved by eon-igae.7.4.2.

## Evidence and acceptance boundary (2e93c69)
orbit/src/platform.rs:230 background_processes counts settled non-foreground-group descendants
of foreground-group members, bounded by a 512-process walk and u8 saturation. This count is
authoritative under ORB-C15; it does not itself identify agent helpers.
The plan must choose one owner using actual agent/process evidence. Do not silently equate
"existed at startup" or "older than this turn" with "not real work": a real server/watcher can
predate a turn and a persistent helper can start lazily. Keep those counterexamples in the
fake-agent red/green check along with helper-only idle, active foreground work, later real
background work and its exit. Preserve genuine Claude/Codex background builds, servers and
watchers, stale-PID safety and the existing bounded walk.
Before changing Orbit count semantics, present the exact ORB-C15 amendment for approval; any
wire change gets a version bump and named consumers. Runtime interpretation must not relabel
unidentified work as known idle. Read the owner references before this consequential choice.
Use focused regression plus affected build and the installed Agent sidebar observation; re-proof
link stays eon-igae.7.4.2. Portability: neutral policy, with Linux/Darwin process mechanics isolated.

title: Modularize Eon runtime by orchestration ownership
description:
## Contract routing

This planning container reorganizes Eon's internal Rust ownership without changing any user-visible contract. Eon remains the thin product orchestrator defined by EON-C1 through EON-C15; Orbit retains Session and terminal lifecycle ownership, Venus retains native presentation ownership, and the component manifest remains the sole composition graph.

## Why

`crates/eon/src/main.rs` is 3,677 lines and currently owns several independent concerns: CLI projection, generation discovery and lifecycle, EONW control transport, the Orbit management adapter, and supervisor composition. The file is harder to review because those owners are interleaved. The desired end state is a genuinely thin `main` that parses/invokes concrete repo-owned modules, not a forwarding layer over arbitrary helper files.

## Scope

In scope:
- the dependency-ordered child issues under this epic
- moving existing behavior into concrete modules named for their invariant owner
- preserving public behavior, wire bytes, filesystem layout, component pins, and error projection

Out of scope:
- implementing any child in this planning run
- changing EON contracts, CLI behavior, EONW, Session topology, component pins, dependencies, or distribution
- traits, service containers, factories, generic frameworks, or compatibility shims
- splitting files solely to meet a line-count target

## Success Criteria

- Every child identifies one concrete owner, affected contracts, and the cheapest falsifying checks.
- `crates/eon/src/main.rs` ends as CLI/process composition and top-level error reporting only.
- Existing `workspace.rs` and `managed_environment.rs` remain the owners of their current invariants.
- The current `eon-g3k` Ready-claim lifecycle work is completed before any overlapping extraction begins.
- The completed sequence preserves all EON-C1 through EON-C15 behavior and passes the repository's required Rust, Nix, installed-profile, and dogfood proof for the touched runtime surfaces.

## Reference Gate

Use the current Eon contracts, tests, and accepted Orbit/Venus revisions as normative evidence. Comparable thin-main layouts are shape evidence only. Prefer direct concrete modules already implied by the code; reject new abstraction layers or dependency additions.

## Stop Conditions

Stop if a proposed extraction needs a new public surface, duplicates a child component's ownership, changes a contract, or cannot be proved as a behavior-preserving move.
close_reason: All five ownership-extraction children are accepted; main.rs is the thin executable boundary and the complete Rust, Nix, profile, and installed proofs passed.

title: Extract Eon generation lifecycle from main
description:
## Contract routing

Preserve EON-C10 command/lifecycle projection and EON-C11 runtime generation semantics. This is an internal ownership move only: generation identity, discovery, classification, selection, and cleanup retain identical observable behavior and paths.

## Why

`crates/eon/src/main.rs` lines 44-1000 contain the generation data model, filesystem discovery, current-generation selection, lifecycle transitions, and generation command output. This is a coherent state owner independent of CLI dispatch and supervisor mechanics.

## Scope

In scope:
- extract the generation value types and lifecycle/discovery operations to `crates/eon/src/generation.rs`
- move their directly coupled unit tests with the owner
- keep configuration/runtime root inputs explicit and concrete

Out of scope:
- changing generation layout, retention policy, output, component graph, locks, or public CLI
- moving workspace or Session lifecycle into the generation module
- adding traits, repositories, caches, or dependencies

## Implementation Notes

Complete `eon-g3k` first so extraction starts from the accepted Ready-claim candidate. Move code with minimal visibility; callers should consume generation-owned results rather than reconstruct classification. Keep the component manifest as the only version/compatibility graph.

## Acceptance Criteria

- One module owns generation identity, discovery, classification, selection, and lifecycle transitions.
- Existing generation commands and failure messages remain observably identical.
- No generation policy remains duplicated in `main.rs`, `workspace.rs`, or the control transport.
- Focused generation tests and the affected Eon crate build pass; the final integrated sequence satisfies the repo's runtime/profile proof rules.

## Verification

Compare before/after command output and generation filesystem effects through existing focused tests, then run the affected crate checks. Treat a pure file move as unproven until the outer consuming command still passes.

## Stop Conditions

Stop if the move changes persisted layout, component selection, cleanup policy, or requires a new abstraction or dependency.

title: Extract Eon EONW control transport from main
description:
## Contract routing

Preserve EON-C10 producer/CLI error projection and EON-C11 supervisor lifecycle behavior. EONW bytes and framing remain unchanged. The module owns transport and request/response projection; workspace and Session policy remain with their existing concrete owners.

## Why

`crates/eon/src/main.rs` contains both client-side control discovery/send/probe logic and server-side listener, framing, response serialization, and dispatch plumbing. Keeping the protocol seam together makes the trust boundary reviewable while avoiding a second schema or generic RPC layer.

## Scope

In scope:
- extract EONW client transport, listener setup, request framing, response framing, and bounded error projection to `crates/eon/src/control.rs`
- invoke concrete supervisor/workspace operations without copying their policy
- move directly coupled protocol unit tests with the owner

Out of scope:
- changing EONW bytes, commands, timeouts, paths, CLI text, or trust validation
- moving workspace topology or Orbit lifecycle policy into control transport
- introducing async runtimes, traits, middleware, or dependencies

## Implementation Notes

Complete `eon-g3k` first. Keep one schema owner and use concrete callbacks/method calls already required by the supervisor; do not create an interface hierarchy for one server. Policy decisions must remain above transport framing.

## Acceptance Criteria

- `control.rs` is the sole owner of EONW connection, framing, parsing, serialization, and transport failures.
- Supervisor and workspace owners retain command semantics and state transitions.
- Existing EONW bytes, paths, timeouts, and user-facing error projection are unchanged.
- Existing control protocol tests and affected Eon crate build pass; the final integrated sequence satisfies required runtime/profile proof.

## Verification

Run the narrow EONW/control tests that exercise both client and listener framing, then the affected crate checks. Reuse the full integrated proof after all children converge.

## Stop Conditions

Stop if extraction requires a second schema, changes wire behavior, moves product policy below the transport boundary, or adds a runtime/dependency.

title: Extract Eon Orbit session lifecycle adapter from main
description:
## Contract routing

Preserve EON-C1 composed launch and EON-C15 pre-lease rollback while consuming Orbit's accepted ORB-C12 management shutdown and ORB-C13 Ready ownership contracts. This module remains an Eon adapter; it must not become a second Session lifecycle owner.

## Why

`crates/eon/src/main.rs` lines 1575-2706 mix Ready claims, management-record validation, recovery, Orbit start/rollback/stop, and running-Session bookkeeping with the higher-level supervisor. These operations form one boundary adapter whose correctness depends on keeping the Ready/lease authority transition together.

## Scope

In scope:
- after `eon-g3k` is accepted, extract ReadyClaim, management record validation/acquisition, recovery, Orbit start/rollback/stop, and RunningSession bookkeeping to `crates/eon/src/sessions.rs`
- retain concrete inputs for component paths, runtime directories, workspace identity, and management transport
- move directly coupled unit tests with the owner

Out of scope:
- changing Ready authority, recovery, Stop routing, process signaling, record layout, Session identity, or component pins
- copying Orbit mechanism into Eon
- introducing a generic process manager, lifecycle trait, or dependency

## Implementation Notes

This child is blocked by `eon-g3k`; extract only the accepted lifecycle candidate. Keep the post-Ready prohibition on Child/PID/signal fallback explicit and colocated with rollback. The supervisor should request Session outcomes, not reinterpret management records.

## Acceptance Criteria

- One concrete adapter owns Eon's entire Orbit Ready/lease/management transition.
- EON-C15 authority rules and ORB-C12/ORB-C13 consumption are unchanged and remain directly testable.
- Supervisor code no longer reads or reclassifies Orbit management records.
- The rejected-Ready regression, affected Eon tests/build, and final required Rust/Nix/profile proof pass without interrupting live Sessions.

## Verification

Run the exact rejected-Ready regression first, then the affected workspace-control surface and crate build. Because this is a lifecycle boundary, retain the final full Rust/Nix and installed-profile proof required by repository policy.

## Stop Conditions

Stop if `eon-g3k` is not accepted, if the move changes authority or recovery semantics, or if Orbit source/API changes are required.

title: Extract Eon supervisor runtime from main
description:
## Contract routing

Preserve EON-C1 composition, EON-C10 control behavior, EON-C11 generation lifecycle, and EON-C15 rollback. The supervisor owns Eon's composition and lifecycle policy while delegating generation state, EONW transport, workspace topology, managed environment, and Orbit mechanisms to their concrete modules.

## Why

After the generation, control, and Session-adapter seams are extracted, `crates/eon/src/main.rs` still contains Programs/LaunchMode/PresentationProcess, launch/reap flow, and the central supervision loop. Those form the concrete product-runtime owner.

## Scope

In scope:
- extract Programs, LaunchMode, PresentationProcess, supervisor state, launch/reap operations, and the supervision loop to `crates/eon/src/supervisor.rs`
- consume `generation`, `control`, `sessions`, `workspace`, and `managed_environment` directly
- move directly coupled tests with the owner

Out of scope:
- altering launch ordering, retry/recovery, signals, child ownership, Session/workspace behavior, or error text
- adding a service locator, trait graph, event bus, dependency injection framework, or dependency
- moving CLI parsing into the supervisor

## Implementation Notes

Begin only after the generation, control, and Session-adapter children are complete. Prefer a concrete state object and direct calls. Keep platform/process details behind the smallest existing functions rather than inventing interfaces.

## Acceptance Criteria

- One concrete supervisor module owns product composition and process lifecycle policy.
- Generation, EONW, workspace, managed-environment, and Orbit adapter invariants are consumed rather than reconstructed.
- `main.rs` contains no supervision loop or child lifecycle policy.
- Existing workspace-control/lifecycle tests and affected build pass; final integrated Rust/Nix/profile proof passes.

## Verification

Run existing supervisor/workspace-control tests and the affected crate build, then reuse one unchanged-candidate full integrated proof for the completed modularization sequence.

## Stop Conditions

Stop if prerequisite module ownership is unsettled, if behavior changes are needed, or if the extraction adds indirection without removing duplicate responsibility.

title: Reduce Eon main to CLI composition
description:
## Contract routing

Preserve every existing Eon CLI command, default, output, exit status, and EON-C1 through EON-C15 behavior. This final child proves that `main` is a thin executable boundary, not a new policy owner.

## Why

Once the concrete runtime owners are extracted, the remaining CLI parsing and command selection can live in `crates/eon/src/cli.rs`. `src/main.rs` should only invoke that owner and project the top-level result to process exit.

## Scope

In scope:
- move CLI argument parsing, command selection, eon/eonterm entry dispatch, and directly coupled tests to `crates/eon/src/cli.rs`
- leave `crates/eon/src/main.rs` as minimal executable composition and error reporting
- remove obsolete imports, forwarding helpers, and duplicated tests exposed by the move

Out of scope:
- changing commands, flags, defaults, help, output, exit status, launch policy, or binary packaging
- a public library API, command framework, trait, factory, or new dependency
- enforcing an arbitrary line-count ceiling

## Implementation Notes

Begin after the supervisor child. Prefer one concrete `cli::run`-style entry over wrappers for every command. Thin means few responsibilities, not merely few lines.

## Acceptance Criteria

- `main.rs` owns only executable startup, invocation of the concrete CLI/runtime owner, and top-level error-to-exit projection.
- All CLI behavior and help remain byte-for-byte or observably equivalent where environment paths vary.
- No one-use abstraction or forwarding layer is introduced to make the file appear thin.
- The complete Eon test/build surface, Nix check, refreshed profiles, and installed outermost dogfood observation pass as required, preserving live Sessions.

## Verification

Run focused CLI parsing/projection checks, then one complete unchanged-candidate Eon Rust/Nix/profile proof after all modularization children land.

## Stop Conditions

Stop if thinning `main` requires public API growth, behavior changes, new dependencies, or wrappers that do not own an invariant.

title: Keep an overseer state file that agents read before asking
description:
From eon-meta-overseer's decision study (/home/lucca/.cache/eon-agents/eon-meta-overseer/REPORT-decisions.md, 2026-11-11, proposed bead 2): the overseer overruled agents on 38% of cross-bead asks, usually with facts the agent lacked. Write /home/lucca/.cache/eon-agents/eon-overseer/STATE.md and keep it current: EONW/ORBS/version and contract-ID reservations, the landing queue, quiet-slot bookings, in-flight beads with the files they change, release-gate members, and Lucca's standing rules with dates (from memory). The common agent rules already tell agents to read it before asking (2026-11-11). Ideally generated by a script from beads, heavy.log, quiet-slots.txt and worktree diffs rather than by hand. Measure the share of cross-bead asks over the next week against the study's baseline.

## Acceptance and authority boundary

STATE.md is an index of current facts, not a second source of decisions. Each reservation, standing grant and exclusion cites its owning bead/comment or dated Lucca instruction; memory alone is discovery, never authority. Show generation time, source freshness and any unavailable/stale input so an absent entry cannot be read as permission or an empty landing queue.

The target STATE.md did not exist when checked on 2026-11-12. Start with the smallest useful documented snapshot/update workflow; the proposed generator remains optional. If a durable generator is chosen, Rust owns it under Implementation Languages, reuse existing br/queue inputs, and bound failure behavior without scanning or exposing terminal contents. No new backend, agent launch or cross-project approval surface.

Acceptance: an agent can identify the current wire/ID reservation owners, landing/quiet-slot coordination, in-flight file overlaps, gate membership and the provenance/exclusions of a standing grant from one read; stale/missing facts direct it to their owner instead of asserting authority. Record who refreshes the file and when. title: Spike: keep the machine from idle-suspending while an agent reports working
description:
## Why

K3 of ~/.cache/eon-agents/eon-ideas-work/ideas.md (Lucca's idea request,
2026-11-09; filed by eon-overseer's "auto-decide" note). The default is
Lucca's call: the idea run recommends `working`.

Eon is for long-running work, but a laptop's idle suspend (GNOME's power
daemon suspends after roughly 15 to 20 idle minutes by default; confirm per
desktop) freezes every agent while the person is away. Eon already knows each
terminal's `working` attention state (EON-C31) and eon-runtime already pins
zbus for desktop notifications, so no new dependency.

## Spike scope

On an isolated supervisor, hold a logind inhibitor
(`org.freedesktop.login1.Manager.Inhibit("idle:sleep", "Eon", "<n> agents
working", "block")` on the system bus) while a stub terminal reports working
over OSC 7501, and drop it a grace period after the last one stops. Record
`systemd-inhibit --list` before, during and after. Note: logind's
LidSwitchIgnoreInhibited defaults to yes, so lid close still suspends.
Record the reference gate: systemd-inhibit, caffeine-ng, and why the Wayland
idle-inhibit protocol does not fit (it inhibits only while a surface is
visible, so it fails when the window is detached). Check how GNOME, COSMIC
and KDE react.

Out of scope for the spike: configuration (`[agents] keep_awake =
"working"|"never"`, grace seconds), macOS (`/usr/bin/caffeinate -i -w PID`),
`eon session --json` exposure, docs. These go to a feature bead after it.

Contracts: likely an EON-C31 clause plus EON-C7 platform scope; approval
before the feature. Owner: Eon Runtime. Portability: isolated Linux (logind
or elogind, no-op without) and Darwin mechanisms.

## Acceptance

Spike notes with the inhibitor observed and released, the desktops checked,
and a recommendation for the feature bead.

## Spike safety and falsifiers

This remains an isolated Linux experiment, not a product default or platform dependency. Keep the existing logind/elogind proposal as a mechanism to verify, including the exact Inhibit arguments, desktop power-policy behavior and permission/failure modes; do not present them as already proved. No actual suspend or lid-close test on the shared maintainer desktop.

Observe acquire while working, release after the proposed grace, repeated working/idle transitions, multiple working terminals and cleanup on isolated supervisor exit. Record denied/unavailable bus behavior as a supported no-op for this spike, never a startup failure or a new requirement for systemd. Bound the run and retain only owned inhibitor handles/processes.

Record which GNOME/COSMIC/KDE environments were actually available and which remain unproved; absence of a desktop is a proof gap, not grounds to invent a result. EON-C31/EON-C7 amendments, feature/default approval, grace/config values, CLI visibility and Darwin work still belong to the later feature decision. Read the owning reference routes at pinned revisions before lifecycle code; the existing zbus pin is reuse evidence, not an approval of new platform guarantees.

title: Validate the canonical component graph before child launch
description:
## Contract routing

Harden EON-C1 and preserve EON-C2 through EON-C4. The consumer is a local Eon launcher; the trigger is creation of a new supervisor from an invalid embedded canonical component graph; the result is a bounded validation failure before Eon creates runtime ownership state or starts Orbit, Venus, or another child. A valid graph retains the current launch, attach, and version-report behavior.

This correction adds no component, schema, launcher framework, compatibility window, distribution channel, child behavior, or public configuration.

## Why

The existing canonical validator is not on the new-supervisor launch path. A locally built or future non-Nix artifact can therefore start a child before discovering that its embedded graph is invalid. The current official Nix package rejects the audited malformed graph indirectly because an Eon test reaches version reporting; this Bead fixes the runtime failure order rather than adding another packaging gate.

Impact: MEDIUM. Effort: S. Implementation risk: LOW. Confidence: HIGH.

## Evidence

- Closed audit `eon-audit-eon-component-graph-g5x`, exact subject `1b8836e616222f29c57ac697916872010db14685`, finding 1.
- `launch_current` reaches `supervise`; `supervise` creates the control listener and starts Orbit before any call to `eon_manifest::parse_and_validate` or the existing validated version-report owner.
- On an exact disposable archive, duplicate Orbit artifact IDs made `eon-manifest` exit 1 and `cargo test --locked -p eon` fail, but `cargo build --locked -p eon` succeeded. Running that binary with bounded fake children wrote the Orbit spawn marker before exiting on child startup.
- The later endpoint-byte commits through `57d7acc22f9f01c7f15d9d381845318b67f760e1` did not change the graph, validator, launch owner, flake, or EON-C1 through EON-C4 evidence.

## Prerequisite and reference gate

- Rebaseline the cited launch and validation owners at the execution baseline and read the complete closed component-graph audit, EON-C1 through EON-C4, `components/eon-alpha-v1.json`, the complete `eon-manifest` crate, the launch path, and the focused runtime tests.
- Reuse the audit's exact Nova `124308bfa128203f843839346c88296cd266568a` comparison only for immutable revisions and resolution assertions; its component set and runtime remain rejected surrounding scope.
- The existing `eon-manifest` validation/report path is the required owner. No external reference, dependency, crate feature, or schema change is expected. Stop for the applicable gate and user approval before any manifest or dependency change.
- Platform classification: neutral preflight policy with the current Nix packaging isolated; no new macOS blocker.

## Scope

In scope:
- The smallest shared new-supervisor preflight in `crates/eon/src/main.rs` using the existing canonical validator/report owner.
- One focused regression or exact disposable build proof that an invalid embedded graph starts no child and creates no durable runtime owner.
- EON-C1 current-state proof metadata, `CHANGELOG.md`, and README LOC only as required after acceptance.

Out of scope:
- A second validator, `build.rs` policy, Nix-only validation, generic launch abstraction, new manifest field, compatibility window, direct distribution, or child-repository change.
- Revalidating the trusted graph before every command, deriving package paths, changing launch arguments, or resolving the separate inert-declaration finding.
- Broad `main.rs` refactoring or changes to attach, stop, workspace, shell, or generation-selection policy.

## Implementation notes

1. Write the cheapest check that fails when fake Orbit is started from an invalid embedded graph; avoid a production injection framework solely for the test.
2. Invoke the existing canonical validation owner once before the first runtime-directory, socket, or process side effect for a new supervisor.
3. Preserve the current valid-graph launch and diagnostics; return the validator's bounded error rather than reconstructing it.
4. Keep attach to an already validated current supervisor unchanged unless exact evidence proves it also needs the same check.

## Acceptance

- An invalid embedded graph fails before a control socket, child process, or child spawn marker exists.
- The failure uses the existing canonical validator and identifies the graph defect.
- A valid graph starts exactly the same accepted Orbit and Venus pair and retains current attach, version-report, lifecycle, and workspace behavior.
- The official Nix build remains green; no duplicate packaging validator or second schema is introduced.
- No new product contract, dependency, component identity, public configuration, or compatibility promise is added.

## Verification

- The focused invalid-graph launch check exits 0 and proves the fake-child marker remains absent.
- `cargo fmt --all --check`
- `cargo check --locked --workspace`
- `cargo test --locked --workspace`
- `cargo clippy --locked --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings`
- `cargo run --locked -p eon-manifest -- components/eon-alpha-v1.json`
- `nix build --no-link --print-out-paths --no-update-lock-file path:.#default`
- `nix flake check --no-build --no-update-lock-file path:.`
- `git diff --check`
- After the proof-bearing commit, refresh the active Eon profile without stopping live supervisors and report whether a restart is required for existing generations.

## Stop conditions

- Stop if graph acceptance has moved away from `eon-manifest` or the launch owner has materially changed.
- Stop if the correction requires a new schema, dependency, build-time code generator, child change, or public distribution promise.
- Stop if the check can prove only validator behavior and cannot prove child-spawn ordering.
- Stop if the same verification failure repeats twice after a reasonable correction.

## Maintenance notes

Use the validator that already exists, once, at the first side-effect boundary. Do not create another graph owner.
