title: Adopt a session-restart rule for context compaction
description:
## Chosen outcome — Lucca, 2026-10-14
Adopt option C: restart chats at each bead boundary, and inside a bead after the second compaction or at the first sign of lost context. If the restarts cost too much, Lucca may switch to option E later (same chat until the second compaction, then finish the current bead).

Evidence (web research, 2026-10-14):
- Task-level loss per compaction is small: SWE-bench methods land within 2.6 points of each other.
- Side constraints are lost often: at best about 55% are retained.
- User corrections spike after a compaction: 41.9% vs 17.7% in one case study.
- Loss compounds across rounds.
The guardrails target chat-only decisions and the period right after a compaction.

## Contract

- Every chain stays at or under 32,768 bytes.

title: Add a panel heading fill setting: a grey row behind notched panel headings, off by default
description:
## Why

Lucca, 2026-11-10, after opening the EONW v39 window: "new eon looks so fucking alien, i love the
double notches on panels. hopefully im not the only one. create a bead to add a setting to let
double notches become normal headers (like rex-style panes but now in the panel itself)".

Later the same day, in his Fable session, he compared drawings of the alternatives
(https://claude.ai/artifact/84vXbE9p889TT6RN7KJwDt, private to him; the letters below are that
page's) and decided:

1. Two settings instead of one list of styles. His words: "what if B, C, F, G are only two settings
   - fill / not fill - notch / inline", then "ok, lets go" to this plan.

   |            | no fill                 | fill                          |
   | ---------- | ----------------------- | ----------------------------- |
   | **notch**  | B: today's double notch | C: notches plus a grey row    |
   | **inline** | G: title in the line    | F: pills on a straight edge   |

2. The default stays today's look, notch without fill ("ok"), to be revisited after he has lived
   with the calmer bar (eon-wuau8) and flipped the settings in his own window.
3. Rejected, with reasons: a single notch ("i prefer the double notch to single notch"), and notches
   made tall enough to hold the whole title (it changes the notch proportions he likes). On the grey
   row he said "im open to C".
4. This bead delivers the fill setting for notch and connected positions (later approved ordering in comment 6495). The inline position, with and
   without fill, is the follow-up bead this one blocks (eon-pdstn).

Contract: VEN-C8 and VEN-C18 describe the notched headings. Presentation is a feature
(docs/AGENT-RULES.md, Contract-Driven Method): amend their wording, docs/CONFIGURATION.md and
venus/docs/PRESENTATION.md, citing the approval above. The configuration key sits under the
configuration boundary contract (EON-C19); follow its rules for a new key.

## Evidence (line numbers at 040cb56; verify)

- Panel title layout venus/src/scene.rs:4101-4147; paint venus/src/render/chrome.rs:3056-3302; title
  types chrome.rs:1118-1544; outlines venus/src/render.rs:3035-3158 and scene.rs:73-185.
- Today every panel (Stacks, popups, the Agents sidebar, dialogs) heads its outline with two
  notches: the title notch at the left and the action notch at the right. The title sits half in the
  notch and half below the valley line between the notches. Lucca's correction, 2026-11-10:
  "currently the panel headers only have their top half on the notch, and the rest is below the
  notch so the gray part would actually have to cover a 'row' across the entire width of each
  panel".
- An existing look setting to copy the path of: `pane_frames` (eon/crates/eon/src/product.rs,
  runtime/crates/eon-runtime, venus/src/launch.rs, venus/src/render.rs).
- docs/CONFIGURATION.md's fixed-look policy ("no style setting", eon-27deg, eon-2ibdd, eon-u5uv2,
  eon-whjhd) is what this setting amends for panel headings; update that text.

## Scope

In scope:
- A setting, suggested `[panels] heading_fill = true | false`, default false. The implementer picks
  the final name in the plan, choosing it so the follow-up position setting (suggested
  `[panels] heading = "notch" | "inline"`) reads well beside it. Eon Runtime parses it and sends the
  resolved value; Venus parses none. Live reload like the other look settings.
- With fill on, a panel's heading row is filled in the unselected-tab fill: one shape that follows
  the notched outline at the top (inside both notches and the valley between them) and runs across
  the panel's full width down to the bottom of the title row. No separator line under it. The
  outline, the notches, the title and the actions do not move.
- One setting covers Stacks, popups, the Agents sidebar and dialogs alike; no per-panel variants.
- Same actions, targets, keyboard stops, focus feedback, accessible names and CLI paths; only the
  drawing changes.

Out of scope:
- The inline position (eon-pdstn). Changing the notch geometry. Pane titles inside a Stack (the
  expanded band and collapsed rows). Colours beyond existing palette roles.

## Acceptance

- With the setting absent or false, rendering is pixel-identical to before.
- With fill on, every panel kind (lone Stack, Stack with collapsed rows, zoomed, popup, Agents
  sidebar, dialog) draws the grey row, and no panel's terminal row count changes.
- The bead records how the row looks directly above an expanded pane's own band in a Stack (two
  fills in a row is the known risk of this look), with a capture for reviewers.
- Title and action glyph contrast on the fill is at least 4.5:1; record the ratios.
- Changing the value in the configuration file changes a running window without a restart.
- `pane_frames` off keeps today's frameless behaviour unless the plan argues otherwise.

## Configurability (rule 6)

The new key is the setting; its default is documented in docs/CONFIGURATION.md. The fill colour
stays a fixed palette role (themes own colours: eon-eon-themes-or3q).

## Verification

- Venus scene and render tests for both values in every panel kind at scale 1, 1.125 and 2; a
  config parse and reload test. Run through `nix develop -c eon-test` (docs/DEVELOPMENT.md).
- No capture gate: Lucca reviews in his own window after the landing's profile refresh.

## Stop Conditions

- Stop if carrying the value to Venus changes the EONW codec: that needs a version bump, never an
  in-place amendment. Report before going further.
- Stop if the fill cannot follow the notched outline without moving it.

## Maintenance Notes

- Lands after eon-wuau8.3 (same file, and it uses the tokens from eon-wuau8.1) and after eon-t5boa,
  so it covers the final set of panel actions.
- Related legibility beads: eon-jg86j (header bands in Eon's own fill) and eon-0kq2c (titles on
  light and translucent backgrounds); check whether fill on answers either, and say so there.
- CHANGELOG.md: new configuration key.

## Current accepted baseline and remaining scope

eon-6ui6p and the existing style/action prerequisites are closed. Its landed position key is [panels] heading; the current default is connected (docs/CONFIGURATION.md:430-441, eon-j7ii2), superseding the historical default discussion above. This bead preserves that default and adds fill=false by default. No additional position key.

As comment 6495 requires, fill=true draws both notch C and connected H2. For connected, fill the full heading row from its straight top edge to the title-row bottom, no separator; position, focus-outline ownership and terminal geometry stay as landed. For notch, retain the described contour. Test both positions x both fill values over the existing panel kinds/scales; inline remains eon-pdstn.

Portability: neutral shared scene/draw inputs, Runtime configuration, existing Venus launch arguments. Use the existing heading launch path unless an approved boundary change is required. Presentation remains a feature; exact configuration/wire contract edits still need their normal approval, and no EONW is amended in place. Keep Lucca's no-mockup gate decision from comment 6379; captures serve reviewers and installed proof.

## Live-application scope retained

The original live-apply acceptance above remains part of this feature. The landed heading predecessor currently applies on open/reopen/explicit eon window reload; that is baseline evidence, not approval to narrow this bead's promised application behavior. Resolve with the overseer whether this slice supplies the planned live application or explicitly sequences with eon-nhec3. Do not treat a manual reload-only observation as discharging the original acceptance without a recorded scope decision.

title: Fix the intermittent new-window shortcut test in Venus
description:
## Why

A flaky test fails package builds at random. Lucca approved filing this on 2026-10-22.

## Evidence

- On 2026-10-22, eon-78's `nix build .#default` on tree d4007e6 failed in Venus's in-build test run with:
  `application::tests::new_window_shortcut_invokes_the_supplied_eon_command` panicked at
  venus/src/application.rs:6084, `assertion failed: run_new_window(&script).is_ok()`.
- 53 of the 54 binary tests passed.
- The identical rebuild passed, and the test passed in two `eon-test -p yazelix-venus` runs.
- The machine was heavily loaded at the time.

## Likely cause (to confirm)

- The test writes a shell script, makes it executable and runs it. It then rewrites the same file
  with `fs::write` and runs it again.
- Other tests in the same process spawn children in parallel. A child forked while the write fd is
  open inherits it, and exec of the script then fails with ETXTBSY ("Text file busy"). This is the
  classic Rust test race.
- The assertion hides the error text.
- Same class as `eon-p8cq` (closed; the cause there was fork inheritance of open file descriptions)
  and the open `eon-1fxc` (quota worker test, ETXTBSY suspected). Check whether one shared
  test-helper pattern fixes both; if so, say so on `eon-1fxc` rather than fixing it here.

## Scope

- Confirm the cause: run the test in a loop under parallel spawning, or print the error.
- Fix the test only, for example:
  - write each script to a fresh path and never rewrite an executable in place;
  - and assert on the error so a future failure names its cause.

Out of scope: `run_new_window` itself, unless the cause turns out to be there.

## Acceptance

- The test passes many repeated runs under load. Record the loop count.
- `nix develop -c eon-test -p yazelix-venus`, fmt and clippy green for Venus.
- Review loop per AGENTS.md (test-only change).
close_reason: Cause confirmed (ETXTBSY from fork inheritance); test-only fix proven and reviewed; see proof comment

comments.author: lucca
comments.text:
Proof and review (2026-10-27, x86_64 Linux, nix develop shell). The commit carrying this comment is the proof's revision: base 6a3ee78, code tree 5db9f6c58ddcf2b4efdaa54effe7ebc08b06a7ca (the commit adds only this bead record).

Cause confirmed: ETXTBSY from fork inheritance. Evidence is a disposable standalone reproduction (~/.cache/eon-agents/66gm-work/repro/main.rs, outside the repository). Four threads fork `/bin/sh -c :` in a loop, while the main thread writes a script to a fresh path, chmods it 0700 and execs it.
- Old pattern (`fs::write` in the test process): 162/2000, 758/10000 and 177/2000 (reviewer's run) rounds failed with "Text file busy (os error 26)", and nothing else failed.
- Fix pattern (a child `/bin/sh` writes the file): 0/2000, 0/10000, 0/10000 and 0/2000 (reviewer's run).
- The descriptor that a concurrently forked child inherits stays open until that child execs or exits. A fresh path alone does not help, and the first exec in the old test was exposed too, not only the in-place rewrite.

Fix (test only, venus/src/application.rs, new_window_shortcut_invokes_the_supplied_eon_command):
- A local closure has a child `/bin/sh` write each script to a fresh path with `printf '%s' "$1" > "$0"`. The test process never opens the file for writing; it only chmods by path.
- The assertions now print the error: `assert!(error.contains("window|new"), "{error}")` and `assert_eq!(run_new_window(&succeeding), Ok(()))`.
- run_new_window is unchanged.

Checks:
- `nix develop -c eon-test -p yazelix-venus`, CARGO_BUILD_JOBS=4, on the same change based at c56372f: exit 0.
- After moving the uncommitted change onto 6a3ee78 (no overlap; the Venus diff is byte-identical apart from line offsets), the review round re-ran these on tree 5db9f6c, all exit 0:
  - `eon-test -p yazelix-venus`: lib 140 passed, 1 ignored; bin 61 passed, 4 ignored, including this test; canonical_scene 18 passed; doc-tests 0.
  - `cargo fmt --check -p yazelix-venus`: clean.
  - `cargo clippy --locked --all-targets -p yazelix-venus -- -D warnings`: clean.
  - The checks left the tree unchanged.
- Loop: `eon-test -p yazelix-venus --bin yazelix-venus -- --test-threads=4`, 30 consecutive runs, 30/30 passed at 1-minute load 7.7-10.9, with the standalone reproduction running alongside for part of it. The bin suite finishes in about 0.01 s and the old test almost always passed, so the loop is weak evidence alone; the reproduction's red/green is the cause and fix proof.

Review ledger: 1 pass, on candidate 5db9f6c. A fresh Claude reviewer (it also ran the checks) and Codex (gpt-6.1-sol, xhigh, read-only) ran in parallel, and both found no code findings. The Claude reviewer's one blocking item was this proof record, written here, and its nits were left as they are: scripts are removed only on success, as before; the comment could add that the inherited descriptor outlives fs::write. A narrow Codex re-check covers this record. An earlier Codex run on the c56372f-based candidate was stopped unfinished when the base moved.

title: Keep an idle blinking cursor from reshaping the whole Venus grid
description:
## Why

When a program asks for a blinking cursor, Venus flips `blink_visible` every 500 ms, and
`blink_visible` is part of the full-rebuild key, so an idle window reshapes every visible cell
twice a second although the selected column's cursor is drawn in the separate dynamic layer.
Nobody has measured the idle cost. This bead measures it first (AP-PERF-001) and then keeps a
blinking cursor from rebuilding the grid.

Source: Venus GPU audit, eon-overseer, 2026-10-27
(`/home/lucca/.cache/eon-agents/eon-overseer/gpu-audit-2026-10-27.md`). Lines below re-checked on
edge `4e705bc`.

## Evidence (re-located at 2e93c69)
- venus/src/scene.rs:5481 has_blinking_content accounts for visible cursor and SGR text blink.
- venus/src/application.rs:73 BLINK_INTERVAL stays 500 ms; :6538-6539 checks content and
  updates blink_visible/redraw through update_blink.
- venus/src/render.rs:237 ContentKey contains blink_visible (:243), assigned at :1791;
  rebuild_if_needed is :1764, build_scene_text :2367 and push_cell_text :2590.
- build_scene_text iterates glyph_runs, and push_cell_text builds/shapes a Buffer per run/layer;
  old per-cell/line citations predate glyph-run grouping. Blink remains a whole-content key.
- Selected cursor rebuilding is invoked at render.rs:1581-1582 when unshifted/no dialog;
  nonselected/static cursor and visible SGR text still consume the blink phase.
- DECSCUSR blinking-block output is the existing workload trigger; Orbit owns canonical state.
- orb-j2i.11 is closed. To suppress attention-badge repaints, the current table is
  [session] animate_working_badge = false, not the historical [workspace] table in comments.

## Contract

Expected none. VEN-C1 keeps the cursor's authoritative shape, visibility and blink, and the
500 ms cadence stays. If the change needs any VEN-C* text change, stop and ask Lucca with the
proposed text.

## Relation to the per-row cache

Independent of the per-row text cache beads (linked as related) and may land first. Both change
`ContentKey` and `rebuild_if_needed`; whichever lands second rebases. With the row cache, a
blink-only change would already be cheaper; this bead still removes the rebuild entirely for a
blinking cursor.

## Prerequisites

- `orb-j2i.11` has landed or is rebased onto (both touch `venus/src/render.rs`).
- Read `AP-PERF-001`, `venus/AGENTS.md`, VEN-C1.

## Scope

In scope:
1. Baseline first, recorded on this bead before any code change: idle Venus CPU over 20 s
   (`utime+stime` ticks of 10 ms from `/proc/<pid>/stat`, as the VEN-C21 proofs did) with a
   blinking cursor and with a steady one, at 1 and 4 columns of dense text, on lavapipe (pixman
   Sway) and on the Intel GPU (Vulkan Sway on `renderD129`), three runs each; exact revision,
   store path, window size and workload recorded. Stop and report to Lucca if a blinking cursor
   costs no material CPU over a steady one.
2. Take the cursor's blink phase out of the full-rebuild trigger: draw the blinking cursor (and
   the static cursors of other columns) in the dynamic layer, or key the rebuild on blink only
   while a visible SGR-blink cell exists. Choose and record the shape.
3. Focused tests that a cursor-only blink does not rebuild the scene text and that blinking cells
   still blink.

Out of scope:
- The per-row text cache, scroll, adapter choice, image upload.
- Changing the blink interval or default (`BLINK_INTERVAL` is a timing a person sees; changing it
  is a configuration question for Lucca under AGENTS.md Configurability).
- Blinking SGR text cells beyond keeping them correct.

## Acceptance

- The baseline and after numbers, on the same workload and environments, are recorded here; with a
  blinking cursor at 1 and 4 columns, idle CPU drops to near the steady-cursor figure.
- Cursor shape, visibility, blink phase and cadence, and SGR-blink cells look the same: installed
  capture bursts over two blink periods match the pre-change build.

## Verification

- `nix develop -c eon-test -p yazelix-venus` exits 0.
- `cargo fmt --check` and `cargo clippy --locked --all-targets -- -D warnings` for `yazelix-venus`.
- Refresh the `eon` profile and record one isolated installed observation (do not restart a live
  supervisor).

## Stop Conditions

- Stop and report if the baseline shows no material cost.
- Stop if the cited code has drifted materially.
- Stop if verification fails twice for the same reason after a reasonable fix attempt.

## Review

Code change: converge rounds plus the Codex round (AGENTS.md "Codex on every code change"), with
the ledger line on this bead.

## Approval

Lucca, 2026-10-27, relayed by eon-overseer. Asked: "1. Cache prepared text per row, and move it
instead of re-preparing it when scrolling; first record a baseline (scroll frame time, idle CPU
with a blinking cursor), as AP-PERF-001 requires. 2. Stop cursor blink from re-preparing the whole
window; measure first too. 3. Choose the GPU on purpose: prefer the low-power one, log which one
Venus picked, and slow the cursor-trail animation when there's no GPU. 4. Move the image upload
wait off Venus's main thread, a small follow-up after orb-j2i.11 lands. Should I file 1–4 as beads,
with 1 and 2 each starting from a recorded baseline?" Lucca: "go ahead".

The approval is to file this bead. Any VEN-C* contract text change or new configuration value it
needs still needs Lucca's approval during implementation: stop and ask with the proposed text.

title: Choose Venus's GPU adapter deliberately, log it, and slow the cursor trail on software adapters
description:
## Why

Venus takes whatever GPU adapter wgpu enumerates first. It asks for no power preference and
ignores the `WGPU_*` environment overrides, so on a hybrid laptop it can wake the discrete GPU, and
nobody can tell which adapter it picked without reading `/proc`. On a software adapter (lavapipe)
only the working spinner adapts; the 16 ms cursor-trail timer and full redraws still run there,
and software rendering made the spinner cost 738 vs 51 CPU ticks per 20 s before
`eon-agent-sidebar-yx8.15` stilled it. This bead chooses the adapter deliberately, logs the
choice, and slows or stops the cursor trail on a software adapter as the spinner already does.

Source: Venus GPU audit, eon-overseer, 2026-10-27
(`/home/lucca/.cache/eon-agents/eon-overseer/gpu-audit-2026-10-27.md`). Lines below re-checked on
edge `4e705bc`.

## Evidence (dcaef1c)

- venus/src/render.rs:1220-1234 still creates the instance from display inputs and requests the adapter with default power preference.
- :1235-1244 records AdapterInfo only through transport::bench_trace("gpu", ...); this does not satisfy always-on startup logging.
- :1245 calls spinners_turn(adapter_info.device_type, animate_working_badge). The badge has both a CPU-adapter and a user-setting stillness cause.
- venus/src/application.rs:80 retains the 16 ms animation interval; scheduling is at :6599 and :6673-6675.
- eon-configurability-qkq8.6 is closed: cursor_trail_duration=0 is the existing user off switch; do not add a second one.
- Historical GPU tick/device-node measurements above and below are attributed to the 2026-10-27 machine, not portable hardware identities.

## Contract

- VEN-C1 (cursor trail, `venus/docs/CONTRACTS.md:208-221`): slowing or stopping the trail on a
  software adapter adds a clause like VEN-C21's still badge. VEN-C16 (native platforms) may name
  the adapter policy. Both are contract text changes: stop and ask Lucca with the proposed text
  before editing them.
- Configurability: adapter preference and the software-adapter trail rate are values a person
  feels. Either record on this bead why they stay fixed (recommendation: low power is right for a
  terminal and the software-adapter rate is a performance budget; wgpu's own environment
  overrides cover debugging), or propose a configuration key to Lucca; a new key needs his
  approval and an entry in `docs/CONFIGURATION.md`. WezTerm exposes `webgpu_power_preference`;
  weigh that in the decision.

## Humans and Agents

Adapter choice is not something a person sees in the window, so AGENTS.md "Humans and Agents" does
not require an `eon` CLI path; the log line is the diagnostic, and an agent can read the
supervisor's log. Record whether an agent-readable surface (for example a field in a future
`eon` diagnostics command) is warranted; recommendation: not now. `eon-gpu-widget-eon-bar-ri16`
(GPU chip in the Eon Bar) is the place if one is ever shown.

## Reference gate

Record on this bead before code:
- wgpu 30.0.0 source (the pinned version, `venus/docs/CRATES.md` "GPU and text"): how
  `PowerPreference::LowPower` ranks adapters in wgpu-core; which environment helpers exist in 30.0.0
  (`util::power_preference_from_env`, `WGPU_ADAPTER_NAME` adapter selection, instance backends and
  flags from the environment) and what each overrides. Verify exact names in that source.
- Comparable: WezTerm at `e2a98e1` (`~/pjs/refs/wezterm`): `wezterm-gui/src/termwindow/webgpu.rs:237`
  (preferred adapter), `:294-298` (power preference), `config/src/frontend.rs:48-56` (default
  `LowPower`).
- Decision: `LowPower` fixed, or `LowPower` as the default with wgpu's `WGPU_*` overrides honoured
  (recommended: honour `WGPU_POWER_PREF`/`WGPU_ADAPTER_NAME` so users can debug without a key), the
  rejected alternatives and the check.

## Portability disposition

`neutral`: power preference, `AdapterInfo` and `DeviceType::Cpu` are wgpu API on every backend;
on Apple Silicon there is one GPU and the choice is a no-op. The lavapipe/pixman and
`renderD129` observations are Linux evidence only.

## Prerequisites

- `orb-j2i.11` has landed or is rebased onto (it touches `venus/src/render.rs` and the renderer's
  construction).
- Read `venus/AGENTS.md`, VEN-C1, VEN-C16, VEN-C21, `AP-PERF-001`.

## Scope

In scope:
- Adapter request with `PowerPreference::LowPower` (and the environment overrides if the gate
  chooses them).
- One `venus:` log line at startup with the adapter's name, backend, device type and driver.
- On `DeviceType::Cpu`, slow the cursor-trail animation (a longer frame interval) or skip it
  (draw the cursor without a trail), chosen with numbers; keep the spinner's existing behaviour.
- Focused tests in the existing Venus test modules for the software-adapter animation policy.

Out of scope:
- Frame-callback pacing, damage tracking or present-mode changes.
- A configuration key or an `eon` CLI field unless Lucca approves one.
- Text caching and blink (their own beads), image upload.

## Acceptance

- Isolated installed observation on lavapipe (pixman Sway): the log names a CPU adapter;
  `llvmpipe-N` threads present; Venus CPU over 20 s while the cursor moves (typing) is lower than
  the pre-change build, with numbers for both; the cursor still lands exactly on Orbit's position.
- Isolated installed observation on the Intel GPU (Vulkan Sway on `renderD129`): the log names the
  Intel adapter; `drm-engine-render` time on `renderD129`; the trail animates as before.
- Optional: with the host NVIDIA Vulkan ICD added (`VK_ADD_DRIVER_FILES`), `LowPower` still picks
  Intel, and the override (if chosen) can select NVIDIA.

## Verification

- `nix develop -c eon-test -p yazelix-venus` exits 0.
- `cargo fmt --check` and `cargo clippy --locked --all-targets -- -D warnings` for `yazelix-venus`.
- Refresh the `eon` profile and record both installed observations (do not restart a live
  supervisor).

## Stop Conditions

- Stop and ask before any VEN-C1/VEN-C16 text change or new configuration key.
- Stop if the cited code has drifted materially.
- Stop if verification fails twice for the same reason after a reasonable fix attempt.

## Review

Code change: converge rounds plus the Codex round (AGENTS.md "Codex on every code change"); a
contract text change also gets its Codex review. Ledger line on this bead.

## Approval

Lucca, 2026-10-27, relayed by eon-overseer. Asked: "1. Cache prepared text per row, and move it
instead of re-preparing it when scrolling; first record a baseline (scroll frame time, idle CPU
with a blinking cursor), as AP-PERF-001 requires. 2. Stop cursor blink from re-preparing the whole
window; measure first too. 3. Choose the GPU on purpose: prefer the low-power one, log which one
Venus picked, and slow the cursor-trail animation when there's no GPU. 4. Move the image upload
wait off Venus's main thread, a small follow-up after orb-j2i.11 lands. Should I file 1–4 as beads,
with 1 and 2 each starting from a recorded baseline?" Lucca: "go ahead".

The approval is to file this bead. Any VEN-C* contract text change or new configuration value it
needs still needs Lucca's approval during implementation: stop and ask with the proposed text.

## Current decision (supersedes the historical contract/config questions)

Use the 2026-11-03 plan-refresh comment 5193 as already recorded: LowPower fixed, honour the pinned wgpu environment overrides for debugging after verifying their actual API/precedence, and a measured fixed software-adapter trail budget. A slower trail is presentation under a named focused test and venus/docs/PRESENTATION.md, not automatically a VEN-C1 edit. Adapter policy belongs in references/launch documentation unless the reference gate finds a relied-on promise. Ask only if exact contract text still needs changing.

orb-j2i.11 and the cursor off-switch prerequisite have landed. Measure baseline/candidate on the same workload/backend and record exact artifact identities; discover/log the real adapter instead of assuming renderD129/Intel is present. Missing hardware is a named gap. Follow current workspace, output/Tier-2 and installed proof rules; no profile/supervisor restart of live terminals.

title: Move Venus's image-upload GPU waits off the event-loop thread
description:
## Why

`orb-j2i.11` uploads Orbit images into Venus's GPU cache with two blocking GPU waits on the
event-loop thread: one before allocating (so freed textures are released and the VEN-C31 budget is
never exceeded) and one on the staging copy. While the GPU works, Venus cannot paint, read input
or answer the compositor, so a large image (up to 4096x4096, 64 MiB) can hitch the window. This
small follow-up moves those waits off the event-loop thread, on the landed orb-j2i.11 upload path.

Source: Venus GPU audit, eon-overseer, 2026-10-27
(`/home/lucca/.cache/eon-agents/eon-overseer/gpu-audit-2026-10-27.md`).

## Evidence

orb-j2i.11 is closed and its upload path is on this tree. At dcaef1c:
- venus/src/render/images.rs:794 waits indefinitely before allocation; :891-895 waits on the staging submission with no timeout.
- venus/src/application.rs:3207 calls renderer.upload_image while processing resource effects on the event-loop thread.
- The original filtering/mipmap evidence is not part of the requested fix; re-locate it only if needed.

## Contract

VEN-C31 (Static terminal images, `venus/docs/CONTRACTS.md:2183-`): its budget (256 MiB at 4 bytes
per pixel, checked before allocating), validation, refusal markers and resync behaviour must stay
exactly as written. Expected no contract text change; if one is needed, stop and ask Lucca with the
proposed text.

## Prerequisites

- `orb-j2i.11` closed (blocking dependency).
- Read `venus/AGENTS.md`, VEN-C31, `AP-PERF-001`.

## Scope

In scope:
- Replace the blocking waits with non-blocking completion: submit the copy, keep the upload
  pending, and poll without blocking (or use `map_async`/`on_submitted_work_done` callbacks) from
  the event loop; draw the image once its copy completes, a marker or nothing until then as
  VEN-C31 allows. Keep the budget exact: count textures freed but possibly still in flight against
  the budget until the GPU has released them, instead of waiting for it.
- A worker thread only if non-blocking polling cannot keep the budget exact; record why.
- Focused tests for the pending-upload state and budget accounting in the existing image tests.

Out of scope:
- Budget size, eviction policy, validation and resync (VEN-C31).
- Mipmaps for heavily downscaled images: optional note for a later bead, not this one.
- Text, blink, adapter choice.

## Acceptance

- Baseline and after, recorded here (AP-PERF-001): the largest frame-to-frame gap while a
  4096x4096 Kitty image uploads (for example `kitten icat` of a fixed PNG in an isolated installed
  Eon, with continuous output in another pane to keep frames coming), on lavapipe and on the Intel
  GPU, several runs each with exact revisions and store paths. After the change, no frame gap
  during upload exceeds the no-image baseline's spread materially.
- VEN-C31 behaviour unchanged: the existing image tests pass, the budget refusal still shows
  markers, and the ignored live test `images_draw_in_panes_and_popups_and_refusals_keep_the_renderer`
  (`venus/docs/DEVELOPMENT.md`) still passes on its isolated display.

## Verification

- `nix develop -c eon-test -p yazelix-venus` exits 0.
- `cargo fmt --check` and `cargo clippy --locked --all-targets -- -D warnings` for `yazelix-venus`.
- Refresh the `eon` profile and record one isolated installed observation (do not restart a live
  supervisor).

## Stop Conditions

- Stop if `orb-j2i.11` landed a different upload shape that already avoids these waits; report the redundancy to the overseer with evidence rather than changing unrelated code.
- Stop if keeping the budget exact requires a VEN-C31 change.
- Stop if verification fails twice for the same reason after a reasonable fix attempt.

## Notes

- Optional, not scope: images shown much smaller than their pixels sample with a single level and
  a linear filter (`images.rs:725-726`, `:829`), which can alias; mipmaps would fix that at a
  memory cost against the budget.

## Review

Code change: converge rounds plus the Codex round (AGENTS.md "Codex on every code change"), with
the ledger line on this bead.

## Approval

Lucca, 2026-10-27, relayed by eon-overseer. Asked: "1. Cache prepared text per row, and move it
instead of re-preparing it when scrolling; first record a baseline (scroll frame time, idle CPU
with a blinking cursor), as AP-PERF-001 requires. 2. Stop cursor blink from re-preparing the whole
window; measure first too. 3. Choose the GPU on purpose: prefer the low-power one, log which one
Venus picked, and slow the cursor-trail animation when there's no GPU. 4. Move the image upload
wait off Venus's main thread, a small follow-up after orb-j2i.11 lands. Should I file 1–4 as beads,
with 1 and 2 each starting from a recorded baseline?" Lucca: "go ahead".

The approval is to file this bead. Any VEN-C* contract text change or new configuration value it
needs still needs Lucca's approval during implementation: stop and ask with the proposed text.

## Pending-upload boundary

Include malformed/rejected resources, disconnect/resync, window shutdown, GPU completion error/device loss, and overlapping replacements in the existing image state/budget checks: neither pending nor retired in-flight storage may escape the exact VEN-C31 budget, resurrect a stale resource, or schedule unbounded busy polling. Keep GPU/device ownership in the renderer, not a second image cache.

Before changing code, freeze the image/no-image workload, baseline spread and quantitative comparison rule from measured data; "materially" is not a result. Record the largest frame gap and input responsiveness on each available adapter with repeated samples. Current whole-workspace, render Tier 1/Tier 2 and isolated installed-image checks apply. Do not broaden this into device recreation (eon-venus-renderer-device-loss-recovery-qvft).

title: Decide named-key encoding for remapped and virtual keyboards in Venus
description:
## Why

Venus sends Orbit the physical key code for every key event (venus/src/input.rs:151,
`physical_key(code)`), by design under VEN-C2 ("maps_layout_independent_physical_keys"). Keys
without text (Return, Escape, Tab, arrows) and shortcuts are then decided by the physical code,
not the keysym the keymap produces. lm9p.2 (2026-10-19) saw this break input from a keyboard whose
keymap differs from the evdev layout: with wtype's virtual keyboard, Return reached the terminal as
a lone ESC (raw pane bytes), Alt+Shift+J did nothing and some printable characters dropped. Real
users likely affected: on-screen keyboards and remote-desktop input that use virtual-keyboard
keymaps, and possibly xkb remaps such as caps:escape (unverified).

## Evidence

- lm9p.2 proof comment (raw bytes: "ab", Return -> `a b 033`; QMP scancodes through libinput work).
- VEN-C2 (owner: Venus native input; Orbit encodes, ORB-C5 via ORBS v13).

## Scope

Step 1 (no code): verify which real setups break. In an isolated headless session, check
caps:escape (or another xkb option remap) and one virtual-keyboard client (wtype as stand-in), and
read how Ghostty's own apprt chooses the key for named keys. Record results here.
Step 2: if a real user setup breaks, propose the smallest VEN-C2/ORB-C5 change (for example, derive
named keys from the logical keysym while keeping physical keys for layout-independent shortcuts) and
stop for Lucca's contract approval before code. If only synthetic tools break, record that and close
with a note in VEN-C2's boundary.

Out of scope: IME, macOS (VEN-C16), Eon shortcut policy.

## Acceptance

- Step 1 results recorded with the exact setups observed.
- If changed: an approved contract update, a focused Venus test for a remapped named key, and one
  isolated installed observation that Return/Escape/Alt chords work from the affected keymap while
  ordinary layouts keep working; fmt/clippy clean for venus.

## Portability

Disposition to record in the bead: neutral expected (keysym vs physical choice exists on both
Wayland and macOS).
close_reason: Step 1 found a real-user break (caps:swapescape/caps:escape drop Escape; virtual keyboards turn named keys into ESC). Step 2 landed the approved VEN-C2 change: named keys outside the numpad follow the keymap for terminal input and Venus's own key handling, with per-press pinning; proof recorded in VEN-C2 and this bead. Gap eon-lihr accepted.

comments.author: lucca
comments.text:
Step 1 results (eon-48, 2026-10-21, no code). A real setup breaks.

Setup: installed /nix/store/qr5a1z10c5k5icmpj3p0a15rc9zk79lz-eon-0.1.1 (generation g1-fd445623a32b91dc47ef97dfefafe4ca; venus/src/input.rs unchanged on edge since 2586d7c). Private headless Sway 1.12 (WLR_BACKENDS=headless, pixman, no libinput devices), isolated HOME/XDG. Keys from wdotool 0.5.3's wlr virtual keyboard, whose keymap comes from xkbcommon names (XKB_DEFAULT_LAYOUT/OPTIONS), so it reproduces what a compositor forwards for a physical keyboard with that layout and those options. The pane ran `stty raw -echo; timeout --foreground 15 cat > FILE`. The test sent a, Escape, b, Return, c, Tab, d, BackSpace, e, Up, f. Raw bytes from od -c:

- base (us): `a 033 b \r c \t d 177 e 033 [ A f`, correct.
- caps:swapescape (Escape's keysym is on the physical CapsLock key, xkb keycode 66): `a b \r c \t d 177 e 033 [ A f`. The Escape is lost, with no byte and no notice. Venus sends PhysicalKey CapsLock with no text, and Orbit encodes nothing for it. caps:escape puts the same keysym on the same keycode, so it breaks the same way (inferred, not run separately). Helix and Vim users commonly use this remap, and GNOME/KDE expose it in their keyboard settings, so this is a real-user break, not only a synthetic-tool one.
- wtype 0.4 (custom keymap, keysyms on low keycodes): `a 033 b 033 c 033 d 033 e 033 f`. Return, Tab, BackSpace, Up and Escape all arrive as ESC. This confirms lm9p.2. On-screen keyboards that upload their own keymaps (e.g. wvkbd) are inferred to behave the same; not run.
- An unrelated observation that did not reproduce: in the first run (before the capture script was fixed), every `m` and one `i` were dropped from a 90-character `wdotool type` command line. Two later runs typed `echo m1 mm2 Mm3 nmn4` correctly. Not pursued.

Venus also matches its own named keys on the physical code, so these break under the remap too: Escape returns focus to the terminal (shortcuts.rs:148), the shortcut viewer handles Escape and the arrows (application.rs:3923), the header handles Tab and Enter (application.rs:1788, :1802), and Arrow keys traverse chrome (shortcuts.rs:155-176).

Ghostty reference (a887df42c56f6de86c0fe6da9c4eeca37931e083, read by a subagent): the GTK apprt maps the XKB keycode through the evdev table, and maps the keyval with gtk key.zig keyFromKeyval. If either result is a non-writing-system key (input/key.zig shouldBeRemappable: everything except letters, digits and punctuation), the keyval-derived key wins (apprt/gtk/class/surface.zig:1361-1381, from PR #9454 "fix xkb mapping not working in Linux"). The doc comment names caps:swapescape. The encoder and bindings then use that key. Letters stay physical, so layout-independent letter shortcuts keep working. Known weak spot: keysyms that keyFromKeyval does not know (e.g. Cyrillic letters from wtype) fall back to the physical key.

Portability: neutral. winit exposes the keymap's logical key on Wayland and macOS alike.

Proposed contract change (step 2; needs Lucca's approval before code). VEN-C2 only. ORB-C5 and ORBS are unchanged: the key field already carries a canonical key, not a promise about which physical key was pressed.
- VEN-C2 Result, add: "Venus resolves each native key event to one key. When the active keymap's key or the physical key is a non-writing-system key (anything other than a letter, digit or punctuation key), and the keymap's key has a canonical Orbit key, Venus uses the keymap's key. Otherwise it uses the physical key. Venus's terminal input and its own named-key actions (focus return, chrome traversal, the shortcut viewer, header activation) use the resolved key."
- VEN-C2 Boundary, add: "Letter, digit and punctuation keys stay physical, so letter shortcuts stay layout-independent, and keymaps that place letters on unrelated keycodes (some virtual keyboards) remain unsupported for chords."
- Evidence to add: a Venus unit test that the resolver maps physical CapsLock with logical Escape to Escape, keeps physical KeyA with logical 'q' (AZERTY) as A, and keeps NumpadEnter as NumpadEnter. Plus one isolated installed observation (this script): swapescape Escape gives 033, wtype Return/Tab/BackSpace/Up give \r, \t, 177 and ESC [ A, and the us baseline is unchanged.
- Implementation shape: one resolver in venus/src/input.rs that maps winit's KeyEvent.logical_key (Key::Named plus location) to a KeyCode, used by InputState::key and the native-shortcut and viewer matching. No Orbit change.

comments.author: lucca
comments.text: Lucca, 2026-10-21: approved the proposed VEN-C2 Result and Boundary text, evidence and implementation shape as written in the step 1 comment (named keys follow the active keymap, writing-system keys stay physical; Venus-only, no ORB-C5/ORBS change).

comments.author: lucca
comments.text: Lucca, 2026-10-21: approved the revised VEN-C2 Result wording to match the implementation: 'When the active keymap produces a named key (such as Escape, Return, Tab, an arrow, a function or modifier key) outside the numpad and Orbit has a key for it, Venus uses that key; otherwise it uses the physical key, so letter, digit, punctuation and numpad keys stay physical.' Why: the earlier wording taken literally would drop numpad identity (NumLock-off 7 -> Home, NumLock-on 1 -> Digit1, breaking Kitty reporting) and needed a character-to-key table for letters on non-writing keys. Boundary text unchanged.

comments.author: lucca
comments.text: Progress (eon-48, 2026-10-21): implementation in detached worktree /tmp/claude-1000/-home-lucca-pjs-eon-eon/aee87891-bf19-4fb0-a5cc-d862c34c3cd6/scratchpad/wt on edge 9f972e5, candidate tree 1acfa397. Shape: InputState::resolve_key at the top of the KeyboardInput arm (venus/src/application.rs) overwrites event.physical_key with the resolved key; resolved_key/named_key_code apply the approved VEN-C2 rule; pin_key pins each press's resolution per native key (level changes while held), lets every press through, consumes a release while another live key holds the same resolved key, drops repeats of retired pins, marks pins retired only when their key was pressed or captured, and when a press meets a capture held by another key it ends that capture and retires the other key. paste_shortcut matches the resolved Paste key. Checks on 1acfa397: cargo fmt --check, eon-test -p yazelix-venus (101+53+18 pass), clippy -D warnings all green; red/green for each pin behavior. Installed observation on the 7d94c0a build: base, caps:swapescape and wtype all give a 033 b \r c \t d 177 e 033 [ A f, viewer closes on the scenario's Escape, Alt+Shift+T opens a tab under swapescape; red on qr5a1z10 (0.1.1): swapescape drops Escape and the viewer stays open. Out of scope, for Lucca: orbit/docs/PROTOCOL.md:17 still says 'Keys retain physical identity'.

comments.text: Lucca, 2026-10-21: accepted as a recorded gap (recommended), rather than another review cycle: with caps:backspace and a configured Alt+Backspace popup, hold physical Backspace (sent to the terminal), then Alt+CapsLock starts a Backspace capture; if the popup request fails and the attachment stays, one Backspace release never reaches Orbit until the next attachment retirement or native focus loss. title: Split Venus's large source files into cohesive modules
description:
## Decision
Lucca, 2026-10-15: refactor Venus's oversized source files into smaller, cohesive private modules so
humans and agents can navigate and change them cheaply. This is a structure-only change: no
user-visible behavior, contract, wire, dependency or platform change.

## Contract
- Consumer: maintainers and coding agents working in `venus/`.
- Result: each concern has one private module that can be read on its own; `application.rs` keeps
event dispatch, focus and action execution, and `render.rs` keeps GPU rendering. Existing behavior,
public items and tests are unchanged, and tests move with the code they cover.
- Important failures: behavior drift, a second owner for any moved policy, a new framework or trait
hierarchy introduced "for modularity", or lost test coverage.

## Evidence (inspected at edge 068efcb)
- `venus/src/application.rs`: 8,036 lines (production 1-4857, tests 4858-8036). `impl Application`
spans about 1472-3424 and `impl ApplicationHandler` about 3438-4139.
- `venus/src/render.rs`: 5,970 lines (production 1-3785, tests 3786-5970). `impl Renderer` spans
about 736-2768.
- `venus/src/scene.rs` (2,780) and `accessibility.rs` (2,340) are next largest; leave them unless a
slice shows a concrete structural problem.
- `eon-monorepo-2oko` (2026-10-14 Codex discussion, spot-checked by Claude) proposed the first two
slices below; neither has been done.

## Slices (one commit each, in order)
1. Shortcut policy out of `application.rs`: `NativeShortcutAction`/`Trigger`/`NativeShortcut`, the
catalog, matching, platform labels, and help and hint projection (about lines 626-1226) into one
private module. One catalog, no keymap framework. Its existing tests are the oracle.
2. Font resolution and fallback out of `render.rs`: `FontSettings`, `OrderedFallback`, `FontSetup`
(about lines 117-400). Keep one `CellMetrics` owner and the existing shaping.
3. Then reassess with Lucca. Candidates seen, not chosen: terminal scroll and selection autoscroll
(`application.rs` about 79-460), link handling and clipboard (about 554-650 and 1227-1330, 4540-4680),
and cursor-trail geometry in `render.rs` (about 478-680, 3505-3740). Add slices only on evidence that
the split makes the code easier to read and change.

## Owners and boundary
Venus owns all of this. Keep modules private to the crate; keep one protocol validator, model, scene,
draw-input, renderer, accessibility and semantic-action path (`venus/AGENTS.md`). A new Venus module
is product scope under `venus/AGENTS.md`; this bead is Lucca's approval for the modules named in
slices 1 and 2 only. Not consequential under the root `AGENTS.md` (no dependency, protocol, contract,
lifecycle or trust change), so no reference gate.

## Acceptance
- Per slice: no behavior change; the moved tests and the rest of the Venus suite pass unchanged in
the isolated sandbox; `cargo fmt --check` and `cargo clippy --locked --all-targets -- -D warnings`
are green for Venus; `nix build --no-link .#default` builds. No new tests, since no behavior changes.
- Each slice gets the fresh-eyes and simplification review loop; record one ledger line per slice
here.

## Stop boundary
Stop for Lucca if a slice would change behavior, a public item, the wire schema or another owner, or
if the right cut is unclear. No Orbit, Runtime or Eon changes in this bead.
close_reason: All four approved slices landed as pure moves with unchanged tests: shortcuts and scroll out of application.rs (8036 -> 6390 lines), fonts and cursor trail out of render.rs (5970 -> 5350). Link handling and clipboard stay by Lucca's 2026-10-16 decision. Further shrinking impl Application and impl Renderer needs its own design decision.

Kept in application.rs: link_hint_for/link_copy_shortcut (link handling, slice-3 candidate), shortcut_viewer_command, sends_workspace_shortcut, dispatch call sites. title: Recreate Venus's renderer after non-destroyed GPU device loss so images resync
description:
## Why

When the GPU device is lost without being destroyed, Venus today treats it as VEN-C4's terminal
renderer failure: the window stops rendering for good. With Kitty images shipped (orb-j2i.11), every
image texture dies with the device too, and VEN-C31's resync (reattach to recover images) can only
run "once the renderer works again", which never happens today. Recreating the renderer after
such a loss lets the window, and its images, recover.

Source: orb-j2i.2, comment 4263 (2026-10-27), "Questions for Lucca", question 1 ("Device loss:
should Venus gain renderer recreation after non-destroyed device loss, so that VEN-C31's resync
can recover images? Recommendation: yes, as its own small bead under VEN-C4, after orb-j2i.11"),
listed as question 2(a) in eon-overseer's morning report of 2026-10-27. Approved by Lucca
2026-10-27 (morning report question 2): "2 yes. yes.". Relayed by eon-overseer.

## Evidence

- venus/docs/CONTRACTS.md:384 VEN-C4 (Bounded explicit failure UX): device loss blocks surface
  recovery; its evidence names `uncaptured_errors_remain_fatal_until_device_loss` and
  `device_loss_blocks_surface_recovery_but_destroy_does_not`.
- venus/docs/CONTRACTS.md:2258-2262 VEN-C31 Resync: "after device loss, once the renderer works
  again ... Today non-destroyed device loss keeps VEN-C4's terminal renderer failure, so this
  applies only to recoveries VEN-C4 allows". :2300: Venus keeps no CPU copy of an uploaded image,
  so recovery reattaches instead of re-uploading.
- venus/src/render.rs:848, :966-975: the `device_lost` flag set by
  `device.set_device_lost_callback`; :993-995 `ensure_device_available` fails rendering after it.
- Earlier work: ven-distinguish-device-from-surface-loss-d96 and
  ven-expose-persistent-renderer-failures-4xj (closed).

## Contract

VEN-C4 (owner of renderer lifecycle and failure UX) and VEN-C31 (its Resync clause and "Today
..." sentence). Both texts change: each contract-text change in this bead needs Lucca's approval
per AGENTS.md. Draft the exact VEN-C4 and VEN-C31 wording, stop, and bring it to him before
editing venus/docs/CONTRACTS.md; the change also takes AGENTS.md's Codex review. Changing the
renderer lifecycle is a consequential code shape (AP-REFERENCE-001): record the reference gate
(venus/docs/REFERENCES.md routes, a comparable wgpu device-loss recovery, rejected approaches)
on this bead before coding.

## Prerequisites

- orb-j2i.11 (Venus uploads and draws images under a GPU budget) lands first (blocks dependency),
  so recovery can be proved with images.

## Scope

In scope:
- Venus renderer lifecycle: on non-destroyed device loss, drop the renderer, request a new
  adapter and device, rebuild pipelines and surfaces, and resync every attached terminal by
  reattach (VEN-C31), with a bounded retry and VEN-C4's notice while it recovers.
- A destroyed device, and recreation that keeps failing, stay VEN-C4's terminal failure.

Out of scope:
- Orbit, the ORBS/ORBF wire, and Eon Runtime.
- Keeping CPU copies of images (VEN-C31 rejects it).
- Surface-loss handling that already recovers.

## Acceptance

- Lucca has approved the VEN-C4 and VEN-C31 wording; the approval is quoted here.
- A Venus test drives a simulated non-destroyed device loss and shows the renderer recreated and
  terminals resynced; it fails on today's code. The existing VEN-C4 tests are updated to the new
  rule, not deleted.
- If a real device loss can be forced (for example a GPU reset or wgpu's test hooks), one
  isolated observation shows a window with a Yazi image preview recovering; otherwise record the
  gap with its reason.

## Verification

- `nix develop -c eon-test -p yazelix-venus` passes.
- `cargo fmt --check` and `cargo clippy --locked -p yazelix-venus --all-targets -- -D warnings`
  clean.

## Stop Conditions

- Stop before editing VEN-C text until Lucca approves.
- Stop if recovery needs a wire or Orbit change.

## Maintenance Notes

Portability disposition: neutral (wgpu device-loss callback and adapter request on every
backend; macOS Metal recovery stays unproved until the Apple Silicon work resumes).

## Current evidence and bounded acceptance

orb-j2i.11 is closed. On dcaef1c, venus/src/render.rs:1249-1262 owns the loss flag/callback, and :3474-3492 records non-destroyed loss and refuses further rendering. VEN-C4 is venus/docs/CONTRACTS.md:454; VEN-C31's current resync clause is :2796-2818. The original addresses are historical.

The approved feature is recovery, not a particular unbounded retry mechanism. The contract draft must name the bounded retry/terminal-failure rule and how shutdown, a second loss during recreation, and a destroyed device are handled. Tests exercise successful recreation plus reattach of all attached terminals, repeated-loss exhaustion and destroyed-device failure while preserving terminal identities and VEN-C31's no-CPU-copy/budget rules. Old GPU resources/completions must not act on the new renderer.

Use the current full affected lifecycle/render proof route, including workspace eon-test and Tier 1/Tier 2 or an explicit missing observation; one installed isolated recovery observation is distinct from a simulated lifecycle test. Never force a reset of the shared desktop GPU to manufacture proof. Keep the existing approval stop and Darwin proof limitation.

title: Cache Venus's shaped text per row and translate it when scrolling
description:
## Why

Scrolling a dense grid re-shapes every visible cell on every frame, because scroll_offset is in Venus's full-rebuild key and every rebuild shapes fresh cosmic-text buffers for its visible glyph runs. Caching
prepared text per terminal row and translating it by the scroll offset should make a scroll frame
cost a translation plus the rows that newly enter the viewport, not a whole-window reshape. This
bead builds that cache, only if the baseline bead that blocks it shows a material cost and
supports a cache shape.

Source: Venus GPU audit, eon-overseer, 2026-10-27
(`/home/lucca/.cache/eon-agents/eon-overseer/gpu-audit-2026-10-27.md`). Lines below re-checked on
edge `4e705bc`; re-locate them before starting.

## Evidence (2e93c69)
- venus/src/render.rs:237 ContentKey includes scroll_offset (:241) and blink_visible (:243).
- :1764 rebuild_if_needed rebuilds on key changes; :2367 build_scene_text obtains glyph_runs,
  and :2590 push_cell_text shapes a fresh Buffer per run/layer. It is not necessarily one buffer
  per cell: current code groups glyph runs, but a whole-grid key change still rebuilds them.
- venus/src/application.rs:73 BLINK_INTERVAL is 500 ms; :6538-6539 handles blink/redraw.
- venus/src/scene.rs:5481 has_blinking_content includes cursor/text blink.
- orb-j2i.11 is closed. Existing Rune spike evidence (2026-11-11, linked on gxb4/h222) attributes
  high one-cell/all-grid prepare cost to text rebuild; it does not replace this bead's exact
  workload, identity, scroll or blink proof.

## Owner and invariants

- Owner: the Venus renderer (`venus/src/render.rs` and its `venus/src/render/` modules). Orbit,
  Eon Runtime and the wire protocols are untouched; Venus still materializes only the Orbit
  frame it has (`venus/AGENTS.md` Boundary).
- Identical rendered output: for the same Scene, scroll offset, preview and window state, the
  cached path draws exactly what the full rebuild draws. Checked by a comparison of the renderer's
  text and rectangle inputs (cached vs uncached) in unit tests, and by pixel-identical captures of
  the installed build against the pre-change build at fixed scroll positions.
- Invalidation: a cached row is reused only while its content, style, selection, hyperlink hover,
  blink phase (for blinking cells), column width, font metrics, scale and clip are unchanged.
  Font, scale or geometry changes drop the cache. Memory stays bounded by the rows visible plus a
  stated margin.

## Contract

Expected none: this keeps VEN-C1 (presentation), VEN-C7 (history and kinetic scroll) and VEN-C19
(typography) behaviour as written. If the change needs any VEN-C* text change, stop and ask Lucca
with the proposed text.

## Prerequisites

- The baseline/spike bead that blocks this one is closed with a "go" and a cache shape.
- `orb-j2i.11` has landed or is rebased onto (both touch `venus/src/render.rs`).
- The blink bead (linked as related) is independent; whichever lands second rebases onto the other's
  `ContentKey` change.

## Scope

In scope:
- A per-row cache of prepared text (shaped buffers and their glyphon text areas) in the Venus
  renderer, reused across frames and translated by the scroll offset; only rows that change or
  enter the viewport are shaped.
- Taking `scroll_offset` out of the full-rebuild trigger for terminal text, in the shape the
  baseline bead chose.
- Focused unit tests for reuse and invalidation in the existing Venus test modules.

Out of scope:
- Blink handling (its own bead), adapter choice, image upload.
- Chrome text (Eon Bar, headers, popups) unless the baseline shows it matters.
- SDF/instanced shaders, sRGB in the vertex shader, `wl_surface` damage or incremental present
  (not pursued, Lucca 2026-10-27).
- Any configuration value. If a size or margin needs to be user-visible, stop and ask (AGENTS.md
  Configurability); otherwise record why it stays fixed (performance budget).

## Acceptance

- On the baseline bead's exact workload and environment, the frame-gap and rebuild-time
  distributions beat the recorded baseline, with the before/after numbers and revisions recorded
  here (AP-PERF-001).
- Cached and uncached renderer inputs are identical in the new tests; installed captures at fixed
  scroll positions are pixel-identical to the pre-change build.
- Kinetic scroll, preview rows, selection and hyperlink hover behave as before in one isolated
  installed observation.

## Implementation Notes

1. Re-read the baseline bead's attribution and chosen cache shape; re-locate the cited lines.
2. Add the row cache and its key; translate cached rows by the offset; shape only new or changed
   rows.
3. Add reuse and invalidation tests; compare cached vs full-rebuild inputs.
4. Re-run the baseline reproducer; record the after numbers.

## Verification

- `nix develop -c eon-test -p yazelix-venus` exits 0.
- `cargo fmt --check` and `cargo clippy --locked --all-targets -- -D warnings` for `yazelix-venus`.
- Refresh the `eon` profile from the tree and record one isolated installed observation
  (AGENTS.md Local Runtime Synchronization; do not restart a live supervisor).

## Stop Conditions

- Stop if the baseline bead closed no-go.
- Stop if the cited code has drifted materially.
- Stop if identical output cannot be kept (for example shaping that depends on neighbouring rows);
  report the case instead of accepting a visual change.
- Stop if verification fails twice for the same reason after a reasonable fix attempt.

## Review

Code change: converge rounds plus the Codex round (AGENTS.md "Codex on every code change"), with
the ledger line on this bead.

## Approval

Lucca, 2026-10-27, relayed by eon-overseer. Asked: "1. Cache prepared text per row, and move it
instead of re-preparing it when scrolling; first record a baseline (scroll frame time, idle CPU
with a blinking cursor), as AP-PERF-001 requires. 2. Stop cursor blink from re-preparing the whole
window; measure first too. 3. Choose the GPU on purpose: prefer the low-power one, log which one
Venus picked, and slow the cursor-trail animation when there's no GPU. 4. Move the image upload
wait off Venus's main thread, a small follow-up after orb-j2i.11 lands. Should I file 1–4 as beads,
with 1 and 2 each starting from a recorded baseline?" Lucca: "go ahead".

The approval is to file this bead. Any VEN-C* contract text change or new configuration value it
needs still needs Lucca's approval during implementation: stop and ask with the proposed text.


## Current proof and measurement constraints
Use the repository's output-path route: Tier 1 frame invariants plus the machine-local
eon-bench performance gate, along with this bead's own matched visual/performance oracle.
Whole-workspace eon-test precedes code review; converge includes the required Codex reviewer,
rather than adding a duplicate independent Codex round. No timing/build/test runs are authorized
by this planning pass. Share xl2bp.10's harness and keep negative or rejected results.
To exclude working-badge repaints, use a window without working agents or
[session] animate_working_badge = false (not the obsolete [workspace] table); record the choice.
Portability: neutral renderer policy, with the named Linux adapters as proof environments only.

The 2026-11-11 overseer decision remains binding: candidate all-cells regressions of 21-25%
were not accepted. The bounded retime must stay within the recorded 5% all-change condition
or stop/report. Preserve the per-row shared-storage/bypass candidate and its measured evidence;
this pass does not authorize a fresh attempt or change that threshold.

title: Record a Venus scroll and text-rebuild baseline and spike a per-row shaped-text cache
description:
## Why

Every change to Venus's content key reshapes every visible non-blank cell, and scrolling puts
`scroll_offset` in that key, so kinetic or wheel scrolling reruns the whole text rebuild on every
frame. Dedicated scroll/blink evidence must be recorded or reused with a matching identity; the later Rune spike already measured change-sized text-rebuild cost. AP-PERF-001 requires a fixed workload, a baseline and a measured
attribution before redesigning for speed. This bead records that baseline and decides whether the
per-row cache (the implementation bead this one blocks) is worth building, and in what shape.

Source: Venus GPU audit, eon-overseer, 2026-10-27
(`/home/lucca/.cache/eon-agents/eon-overseer/gpu-audit-2026-10-27.md`). Lines below re-checked on
edge `4e705bc`.

## Evidence (2e93c69)
- venus/src/render.rs:237 ContentKey includes scroll_offset (:241) and blink_visible (:243).
- :1764 rebuild_if_needed rebuilds on key changes; :2367 build_scene_text obtains glyph_runs,
  and :2590 push_cell_text shapes a fresh Buffer per run/layer. It is not necessarily one buffer
  per cell: current code groups glyph runs, but a whole-grid key change still rebuilds them.
- venus/src/application.rs:73 BLINK_INTERVAL is 500 ms; :6538-6539 handles blink/redraw.
- venus/src/scene.rs:5481 has_blinking_content includes cursor/text blink.
- orb-j2i.11 is closed. Existing Rune spike evidence (2026-11-11, linked on gxb4/h222) attributes
  high one-cell/all-grid prepare cost to text rebuild; it does not replace this bead's exact
  workload, identity, scroll or blink proof.

## Contract

Touches no contract: this is measurement. VEN-C1 (authoritative presentation), VEN-C7 (history and
kinetic scroll) and VEN-C19 (typography) must stay unchanged by anything it recommends.

## Prerequisites

- `orb-j2i.11` is changing `venus/src/render.rs`; the measurement can run on the
  installed or edge build now, but note the exact revision.
- Read `AP-PERF-001` (`docs/AGENT-PROTOCOLS.md`), `venus/AGENTS.md`, VEN-C1 and VEN-C7.

## Scope

In scope:

  Intel GPU, `renderD129`), a fixed window size (for example 2560x1440 and 1280x720), four columns

  for example a fixed file `cat` into each pane), scrolled through retained history by a recorded
  input driver (synthetic wheel steps, and a touchpad-style pixel stream if one can be driven).
- Measurements, each with a distribution (median, p95, max) over repeated runs: frame-to-frame
  gap while scrolling; wall time of `rebuild_if_needed` and of the glyphon prepare per frame;
  Venus CPU ticks over a fixed scroll; and a `perf record -g` attribution of where the rebuild
  time goes (cosmic-text shaping, font fallback, glyphon prepare, vertex upload).
- A temporary, uncommitted timing probe is fine for this; keep the reproducer script and raw

- A short spike, if the numbers warrant it, that prototypes the cheapest cache shape (shaped

  committed.

Out of scope:
- Committed renderer changes (the implementation bead owns them).
- Blink (its own bead, linked as related), GPU adapter choice, image upload.
- SDF/instanced shape shaders, sRGB in the vertex shader, `wl_surface` damage or incremental

## Acceptance

- The bead records: the workload (exact generator, sizes, columns, input driver), the environment

  known), the baseline distributions above, the `perf` attribution, and a go/no-go.

title: Version Eon by number: 0.x is beta, 1.0.0 leaves beta
description:
## Decision
Lucca, 2026-10-16: drop the alpha/beta stage words in favour of version numbers. Every 0.x release
is beta; 1.0.0 means out of beta. Installing without Nix is a delivery milestone inside 0.x, not a
stage. Releases are tagged `vX.Y.Z` after bumping Eon's product version; date tags stop.

## Contract
- Product text calls Eon beta and names the 0.x/1.0.0 meaning; no document presents "alpha" as the
current stage or "public beta" as the Nix-free milestone.
- Eon's product version in `eon/crates/eon/Cargo.toml` is the one user-facing number. Orbit, Venus,
Eon Runtime and EONW keep their own package versions as compatibility identities.
- Platform and channel claims are unchanged: Nix-only, x86_64 Linux on native Wayland.
- `linux-alpha-2026-10-14` was version 0.1.0; the next release is `v0.1.1`.

## Scope
Docs, agent overlay and planning wording, plus retitling `eon-qualify-nix-free-linux-public-beta-lm9p`
and reframing `eon-next-expansion-0wfb`. The manifest file and its `eon-alpha` graph ID keep their
names until the next graph version, because renaming them changes the component report that live
generations compare. The `v0.1.1` version bump, tag and profile refresh are a separate release step.

## Acceptance
No product or policy text uses alpha or public beta as a stage; rendered `AGENTS.md` passes
`starcompass check-consumer`; changed Markdown paths and diff reviewed.
close_reason: Versioning policy and wording applied; v0.1.1 release is a separate step

title: Alt+Shift+S twice switches to the previous workspace
description:
## Why

Lucca, 2026-11-04, in the p4 agent's pane, asked how to switch workspaces faster than Alt+Shift+S then Enter.
- Rejected: tap-versus-hold, because it delays the picker, misfires, and is a fixed timing.
- Rejected: a separate "previous" chord. Lucca: "the problem is having to remember two keys ... its mentally costly", and "if the new chord was S-based, it would be less costly".
- Chosen: on this option and its sibling (Alt+Shift+1..9), Lucca said "lets do both".

## Scope

- While the Workspaces picker is shown, its own key (`[popups.workspaces] keybinding`, Alt+Shift+S by default) confirms the highlighted entry, as Enter does, instead of hiding the picker. Esc and Ctrl+C still cancel.
- The picker already highlights another workspace first, so Alt+Shift+S twice switches back and forth. Holding Alt+Shift and tapping S twice works like a double Alt+Tab.
- To verify: the first highlighted entry is the most recently used other workspace when there are three or more. If not, make it so.
- Owners: runtime cli.rs (the picker, extended by eon-p7omw) and the popup-invoke path for a shown Workspaces popup (workspace.rs).
- Rule 5: no new window action; the existing workspace switch is used.
- Rule 6: no new value, because the key is the existing `[popups.workspaces] keybinding`.
- Contract: EON-C33 or EON-C10 may need a clause, because the popup key no longer hides this popup. That is small contract text, approved by the overseer under Lucca's standing rule.

## Acceptance

- A runtime test shows the popup key confirming the highlighted entry while the Workspaces picker is shown. It fails on the current edge and passes with the change.
- The most-recent-first order holds with three workspaces.
- An isolated installed run: Alt+Shift+S twice toggles between w1 and w2.

## Verification

- `nix develop -c eon-test -p eon-runtime -p eon`, fmt and clippy.
- One isolated installed run.
- Converge plus Codex.
close_reason: Landed on edge as 5a7472b: in the Workspaces picker its own key confirms, so Alt+Shift+S twice switches to the previous workspace (EON-C33, EON-C10 amended).

title: Demote wave-1 presentation contracts to features and retire their IDs
description:
## Why

Lucca approved eon-4f1n's contract criterion and its wave-1 demotion on 2026-10-30 (quote: "accecpt
all", relayed by eon-overseer; the decision comment is on eon-4f1n). Presentation-only contracts are
demoted to features: their user docs and beads keep the behavior and proof, and each ID is retired
with a pointer. The IDs are never reused.

## Contract

Demotes and retires 16 IDs: EON-C13, EON-C14, EON-C24, EON-C25, EON-C29 and EON-C30, and VEN-C9,
VEN-C11, VEN-C15, VEN-C22, VEN-C24, VEN-C25, VEN-C26, VEN-C27, VEN-C28 and VEN-C29. Marks the
unrecorded gaps VEN-C6 and VEN-C12 Retired. Changes the pointer text, but not the meaning, of the
contracts that cite the retired IDs: EON-C19, EON-C20, EON-C27 and EON-C32, and VEN-C8, VEN-C20,
VEN-C21, VEN-C29, VEN-C30 and VEN-C31. Preserves EON-C28.

## Evidence

- eon-4f1n investigation comment (classification table, criterion, demotion path). Full tables:
  ~/.cache/eon-agents/claude-4f1n-work/{eon,ven}-table.md.
- Find citations with `rg -i -n '<ID>\b' . --glob '!.beads/**' --glob '!target/**'`. Also check the
  short forms that this rg misses: "VEN-C19/C20/C21", "VEN-C21/C24" and "EON-C19/C20/C21".
- `components/eon-v5.json` lists VEN-C9, C11, C15, C22, C24 and C25 in
  `activation.required_contracts`, and C9, C11, C15 and C22 to C26 in the Venus proof list.
  `eon-manifest` (`eon/crates/eon-manifest/src/lib.rs:428`) rejects activation that references an
  unproved contract.

## Scope

In scope:
1. **Docs.** For each demoted ID, confirm its user-facing behavior and defaults are in
   `docs/USAGE.md`, `docs/CONFIGURATION.md` or `venus/docs/PRESENTATION.md`, and add whatever is
   missing. Keep the patched-winit rationale (VEN-C15) and jiff (VEN-C27) in `venus/docs/CRATES.md`.
2. **Proof records.** Copy each demoted contract's Proof field (test names, proof beads,
   environments) into a comment on this bead.
3. **Retire the sections.** Replace each with its heading,
   `Status: Retired <date> by Lucca: demoted to a feature; behavior in <doc#anchor>; proof in <beads>`
   and a `Reason`. Add Retired headings for VEN-C6 and VEN-C12 that say what the bead history shows:
   C6 was a dropped accessibility plan, and C12 was an identity ID lost in consolidation and
   replaced by VEN-C17.
4. **Index rules.** In each of the three CONTRACTS.md files (Orbit's included, for one rule), extend
   the Status definition of Retired to "explicitly replaced, removed, or demoted to a feature".
   Replace the "Only ... belong here" rule with the approved criterion's index wording: wire or
   format, lifecycle, trust, ownership invariant, script/agent surface, platform; presentation is a
   feature in its bead and user docs.
5. **Retarget pointers.** Point citing contracts at the owning doc or at the boundary contract that
   remains, without changing their meaning. Retarget code comments too. EON-C32 absorbs the one-line
   facts of C25, C29 and C30.
6. **Manifest.** Remove the retired IDs from `components/eon-v5.json`, applying the rule that
   eon-08w18 settles.

Out of scope: wave 2 (EON-C21 and VEN-C21, VEN-C32); the 11 mixed-contract splits (deferred until
each contract is next amended); the AGENTS.md text (eon-946u); any behavior change.

## Acceptance

- Each of the 18 IDs has a Retired heading with a pointer. Searching the 16 demoted IDs finds only
  Retired headings, CHANGELOG history and bead text.
- Every behavior the demoted contracts described can be found in the named doc.
- The manifest validates, and activation references no retired ID.
- EON-C28 still holds: every `[terminal]` and `[bar]` key is documented in CONFIGURATION.md, the
  default shortcuts are unchanged in the Alt+/ viewer, and EON-C20 and VEN-C20 are intact.

## Verification

- This is a component-manifest change, so it takes the full Rust and Nix route:
  `nix develop -c eon-test` and `nix flake check` on the exact tree.
- Codex reviews the change under the AGENTS.md rule: it is a manifest change and it alters
  contract text.
- No runtime profile refresh is needed unless the built closure changes. The manifest is in the
  closure, so check this and refresh if it is.

## Order

eon-08w18 (the rule for the manifest activation list) lands first, so this bead edits the list once.

## Stop Conditions

- Stop if a demoted contract turns out to hold a boundary clause (a bound, a trust rule or an
  interface) that no remaining contract or test carries. Report it rather than dropping it.
- Stop if any change would weaken EON-C28.
close_reason: Landed: 16 wave-1 contracts retired as features with pointers, VEN-C6/C12 Retired headings, index Rules criterion, manifest per eon-08w18; proof and ledger in comments. Follow-ups: eon-bar-item-wake-test-t2ss4, eon-blur-backdrop-reproof-5ht7n.

## Developer facts from the demoted contracts that stay out of user docs

Each entry names what carries it: a test, an internal-interface doc, a boundary
contract or, where noted, only code. The full pre-change contract text is at
edge `9d5a059`.

- Launch arguments (internal interfaces, `venus/docs/LAUNCH.md`): `--no-decorations`
  (VEN-C9), `--background-opacity` (VEN-C11), `--background-blur` (VEN-C15),
  `--eon-version` with its 128-byte ASCII bound (VEN-C25), and `--bar-items` and its
  validation (VEN-C29). Unknown options and excess positional arguments fail before
  window creation (`venus/src/launch.rs:237-243`). A repeat of `--background-opacity`,
  `--background-blur`, `--eon-version` or `--bar-items` fails the same way. A repeated
  `--no-decorations` is accepted, because it only sets `decorations = false`
  (`venus/src/launch.rs:161`). Old VEN-C9 said "Unknown, duplicate, or excess arguments
  fail", which the code did not do for that flag before this bead either. Tests:
  `arguments_are_complete_bounded_and_defaulted`,
  `launch_values_project_to_native_window_attributes`,
  `eon_version_is_bounded_workspace_identity`, `bar_items_are_an_ordered_workspace_choice`.
- Eon passes `--background-opacity` and `--background-blur` before the Venus endpoints, and
  an invalid opacity or blur value starts no supervisor, Orbit or Venus (EON-C13, EON-C14):
  `bare_eon_attaches_only_to_the_live_current_generation`,
  `invalid_presentation_configuration_precedes_supervisor_generation_and_children`.
- Venus never reads or wakes for a left-out CPU, RAM or clock item (VEN-C29). Only the
  gating at `venus/src/application.rs:4739` carries this, with its comment "Items Eon leaves
  out of the bar are never read and never wake Venus", and `venus/docs/PRESENTATION.md`
  (Eon Bar, item order) states it in user terms. No test checks it:
  `eon_orders_and_omits_bar_items` checks only the scene. The gap predates this bead, since
  old VEN-C29 cited the same scene test as its evidence.
- Quota-only refreshes are not structural (they replace no attachment and send no Orbit
  resize; VEN-C22, VEN-C26): `quota_refresh_and_workspace_failures_preserve_structure`,
  which VEN-C8 and VEN-C30 cite. That test proves nothing about caching. The rule that
  Venus keeps no quota cache outside the current EONW snapshot and never refreshes or
  infers provider state rests on EON-C27's ownership of collection: its Ownership field
  says "Pinned CodexBar owns provider collection and credential access; Runtime owns
  bounded subprocesses, validation, freshness and the stored readings; [...] Venus
  consumes typed facts through its existing chip owners."
- CPU and memory reading rejection (VEN-C28): a non-advancing CPU sample, missing per-CPU
  lines, a missing MemTotal or MemAvailable, a zero MemTotal, MemAvailable above MemTotal;
  on macOS a failed host call, a CPU tick counter that went backwards (32-bit counters wrap
  about every 50 days on a 10-core Mac), purgeable pages above internal ones, or use above
  `hw.memsize`: `cpu_use_rejects_bad_readings_instead_of_showing_zero`,
  `ram_use_rejects_bad_readings_instead_of_showing_zero`,
  `host_cpu_use_counts_user_system_and_nice_as_busy`,
  `host_ram_use_is_app_wired_and_compressed_over_physical_memory`.
- jiff resolves the zone from `TZ`, then `/etc/localtime`, and the application owns the
  minute wake (VEN-C27): `venus/docs/CRATES.md#local-time-zone`. The patched winit backport
  for blur (VEN-C15): `venus/docs/CRATES.md#native-background-blur-decision`. macOS libc
  (VEN-C28): `venus/docs/CRATES.md#macos-cpu-and-memory-readings`.
Citing contracts edited by eon-vn0nk that its Contract line does not list (all pointer-only, retired ID to its new home):

- EON-C21 Native workspace header (Result): "Shortcuts when EON-C24 needs its fallback" -> "Shortcuts when the bottom shortcut hints ([Eon Bar and tabs](USAGE.md#eon-bar-and-tabs)) need its fallback".
- EON-C22 Retired entry (Status): "Venus `VEN-C22` owns the Codex chip" -> "Venus's Codex chip is described in [Eon Bar](../venus/docs/PRESENTATION.md#eon-bar)"; date and Reason unchanged.
- EON-C26 Retired entry (Status): "Venus `VEN-C26` owns the Claude chip" -> "Venus's Claude chip is described in [Eon Bar](../venus/docs/PRESENTATION.md#eon-bar)"; date and Reason unchanged.
- VEN-C32 Attention inbox (Shortcuts bullet): "The footer (VEN-C24)" -> "The footer ([Eon Bar and tabs](../../docs/USAGE.md#eon-bar-and-tabs))".

Note on a listed contract: VEN-C30's Status changed "(draft 15 on `eon-agent-sidebar-yx8.1`, there named VEN-C29)" to "there under an earlier draft ID". That removes a historical mention of the retired ID rather than re-pointing it. Listed EON-C20 and VEN-C20 cite no retired ID and are unedited.
