title: Control Eon workspaces by voice
description:
## Contract
A user can control Eon with spoken commands: open a window, create a tab or pane, and navigate tabs/panes without using physical shortcuts. Provide a discoverable, bounded command vocabulary, an explicit listening state, and pause/cancel. Unrecognized or ambiguous speech produces visible feedback without acting. Closing work or stopping terminals requires explicit confirmation tied to the intended target.

## Prerequisites and reference gate
Choose and verify a voice-input provider on Eon’s supported Linux Wayland environment, including microphone permissions, activation, recognition quality, resource use, licensing and any external-service/data requirements. Compare an existing desktop voice-control tool with a local speech-recognition component before considering owned recognition code. Read their current primary documentation and inspect a comparable command-mapping integration. Inspect EON-C8, EON-C10, EON-C18 and EON-C20 and the actual Eon CLI/EONW/native-action surfaces before selecting mappings. Record exact references, decisions and limits; no recognition engine or cloud service is selected by this bead.

## Ownership and implementation boundary
Keep audio capture and recognition with the selected provider. Eon owns the product command vocabulary, activation/configuration and installed integration; Eon Runtime owns existing typed workspace actions and target validation; Venus owns native interaction, focus and feedback. Prefer a thin integration with existing controls. Resolve the intended window/tab/pane explicitly and revalidate it before execution so delayed recognition cannot affect a different workspace. Do not parse screen text or treat recognized speech as arbitrary shell code. Decide terminal dictation separately from command recognition before adding a text-input path; it must not implicitly execute commands.

## Acceptance
1. Document the chosen input system, platform, activation method, vocabulary and data handling. Listening is opt-in, visibly indicated, and can be paused or cancelled.
2. In an installed Eon, actual microphone speech opens a window, creates a tab/pane and navigates them; record exact component/provider revisions and the observed environment. Synthetic transcripts alone do not prove voice usability.
3. Ambiguous speech, silence, unavailable recognition, cancellation and stale/missing targets cause no unintended action. Duplicate recognition does not repeat a non-idempotent command. Confirmed close/stop affects only the identified work.
4. Ordinary keyboard/pointer input and live terminals remain usable when voice control is off or fails. Add the smallest checks for any new mapping/dispatch logic and one installed end-to-end voice workflow.
5. Document setup, supported commands and known recognition limits. Use existing dependencies and action owners where sufficient; no generic voice assistant, autonomous command execution, new platform promise or unrelated input framework.

## Scope
One voice-control integration for core Eon workspace actions. Independent of Neuralink support; no dependency on that bead. Implementation remains unclaimed until this work is selected.

title: Orbit logs any terminal startup stage slower than about 1 s, without a trace flag
description:
From the Opus review of eon-g3vdz (2026-11-11): the first-try pane create failure under load was mitigated (15 s start bound, cleanup ownership, per-stage timings in the timeout error) but its natural cause was never reproduced (20/20 creates at load 17). Orbit's own stage timings appear only with EON_BENCH_TRACE set, so a recurrence in a real window would again leave an empty Orbit log. Write one log line per startup stage (spawn, Bend spawn, bounds, PTY spawn, Ready) whose duration exceeds about 1 s, always on, so the next recurrence names the slow stage. Rule 6: the threshold is a diagnostic, record why it stays fixed. Follows eon-g3vdz.

## Current owner, prerequisites and acceptance

eon-g3vdz is closed; keep its mitigated 15 s bound and cleanup ownership unchanged. At dcaef1c Orbit's existing stage events are orbit/src/host.rs:543-550 (PTY/Ready), :1867-1872 (worker spawn/bounds), with bench_trace gated by EON_BENCH_TRACE at :1966-1982. Measure each interval once at its owner; Orbit cannot measure time before its own process starts, so any parent spawn latency remains the Runtime's diagnostic, not a fabricated Orbit stage.

Acceptance: with trace unset, a controlled slow startup stage emits one diagnostic naming terminal/stage/elapsed time; below-threshold stages remain quiet. The trace path still works without duplicate always-on records. Do not log terminal content/environment/secrets. Record the fixed approximately-one-second choice as diagnostic signal/noise policy under rule 6, not a startup timeout.

ORB-C13 startup semantics and docs/HOST.md boundaries remain unchanged; stop for approval if this needs worker-schema/law or lifecycle changes. Portability: neutral monotonic elapsed timings and existing logging, with Linux proof only. One existing startup-harness regression plus current workspace/build/review requirements; no product dependency, benchmark redesign or session-wide tracing by default.

title: Spike: seeded fault simulation for one Eon Runtime lifecycle path, with planted-bug controls
description: From the Blaze evaluation (eon-vydf9, 2026-11-12; report /home/lucca/.cache/eon-agents/eon-blaze-eval-work/report.md). Take one Runtime lifecycle path where a failure loses live terminals (spawn deadline, rollback or owner loss), express its decisions as a sans-I/O core that emits effects, and drive it under a seeded faulting clock and process model that replays exactly. Give each oracle a deliberately broken variant that must fail (planted-bug control), so the test is proven to bite. Runtime keeps ownership of the mechanism. Spike only: report whether the pattern finds real orderings and what it costs; no product change without a follow-up bead.

# eon-vzf2k — Focused pane header buttons

Approved with changes by eon-overseer at 2026-11-10T21:29:18Z after Fable's
plan review. All five findings are accepted; implementation is authorized.
Records live in `/home/lucca/.cache/eon-agents/eon-focused-buttons-work/`.

## Binding scope and baseline

- Work only in this detached worktree at
  `c7da9c85502239bdea35a43f3c183fc5af7a8d17` (EONW v39, Eon 0.1.22).
  `9f1afff` (`eon-u5uv2`) is an ancestor; the initial working tree is clean.
- Read `br show eon-vzf2k` and all six comments with `br comments eon-vzf2k`
  from `/home/lucca/pjs/eon/eon`, read-only. The 16:36Z comment fixes the
  three-bead split. Lucca's 16:37Z clarification removes the earlier proposed
  no-release constraint: "eon is keyboard focused / mouse was never the
  priority". The 20:37Z comment records his prioritization; this session's
  instruction authorizes proceeding to the plan review gate.
- This bead owns drawing and mouse hit-test gating only. Hover is
  `eon-kgr2x`; configuration is `eon-qnvcu`. Do not implement either, band
  clearance (`eon-xaq6c`), or Stack Close (`eon-t5boa`). Panel headings keep
  their own controls.
- Read root `AGENTS.md`, `docs/AGENT-PROTOCOLS.md`, all of
  `docs/AGENT-RULES.md`, and `venus/AGENTS.md`. Inspected the development
  instructions and isolated-capture/real-PTY notes named in the brief.

## Observable behavior

1. The active tab's selected pane shows Zoom/Restore and Close when the two
   full targets fit. Other pane headers hide both their painted controls and
   their mouse action targets, including collapsed Stack title lines and
   expanded panes in other columns. A Stack with exactly one pane always
   retains its controls, including in an unselected column, subject to the
   existing fitting and popup-occlusion rules. A one-pane tab retains its
   disabled Zoom button.
2. Focus means the tab's canonical `selected_pane`, not the keyboard focus
   region. Moving keyboard focus to the Agents sidebar retains the last
   selected pane's controls. A shown popup already replaces and covers all
   pane headers; preserve that behavior and the selected pane so its controls
   return when the popup is dismissed.
3. Reserve the same action geometry even when the controls are hidden. Title
   and scrollback fitting, header/body rectangles, terminal grids and header
   shape do not move because button visibility changes. An invisible control
   leaves no mouse action or stale button tooltip; its space remains ordinary
   pane-header input, so clicking it can select the pane. The same press/release
   cannot activate the newly shown button; a second click can.
4. AccessKit continues exposing both actions for every laid-out pane header
   whose existing targets fit, including unfocused panes. An unfocused native
   window retains its buttons; window focus is not an eligibility input. Existing keyboard
   traversal, shortcuts, exact-pane activation, final-close confirmation,
   `eon pane close` and `eon pane zoom` remain unchanged. Popup occlusion and
   clipped/narrow-header accessibility behavior remain as before.

## Owner, evidence and smallest implementation

Portability disposition: **neutral**. No new native-host dependency, schema,
configuration input, protocol, lifecycle, or runtime behavior is needed.

The existing owner is `WorkspaceScene`/`WorkspacePane` in
`venus/src/scene.rs`. It already projects canonical selection and real column
membership, reserves `WorkspacePane.actions`, fits titles with
`header_content`, and supplies `pane_action` to keyboard and accessibility
consumers. `WorkspacePane.selected` means expanded within its column, so it
alone cannot identify the tab's focused pane.

Adopt that existing geometry/semantic-action path. Add scene-owned paint/mouse
eligibility computed from the canonical selected pane and actual column pane
count, separate from `actions`. A small accessor can return the eligible
paint/mouse rectangles without changing the reserved rectangles. All four
consumers use that decision: scene hit testing (`scene.rs:4509`), button
drawing/feedback (`chrome.rs:3200`), compact rule gaps (`chrome.rs:3179`), and
tooltip admission (`chrome.rs:2058`). Test keyboard selection changing while
the pointer stays on the former button: its tooltip and hover fill disappear.
Reject deleting `actions` from
unfocused panes: it would expand titles and remove AccessKit actions. Reject
using keyboard focus or hover state: it would violate the approved scope.

Inspected the established comparison and ownership route
`venus/docs/REFERENCES.md#rounded-pane-frames` (Nova
`e6c29312fc8ca11da41fe9da1809ea0e9a9116c8`, inspection-only reference already
recorded there). No new external code or architectural mechanism is adopted.
The direct implementation references are this tree's `eon-ipc6f` action path
and `eon-u5uv2` collapsed-title rendering.

Change reach:

- `venus/src/scene.rs`: the sole `WorkspacePane` initializer, paint/mouse
  eligibility, and `WorkspaceScene::hit_test`. Preserve `actions`,
  `header_content`, `pane_action` and canonical selection.
- `venus/src/render/chrome.rs`: use eligible controls for button drawing and
  feedback, compact action-rule gaps, and mouse tooltip admission. Hidden
  collapsed-row buttons leave an uninterrupted right-hand rule while the
  title still fits to the reserved slot. Leave band clearance, outline
  allocation, panel heading buttons and continuous expanded bands alone.
- `venus/src/scene/tests/bar.rs`: adapt the existing exact-target regression
  and cover focused/collapsed/other-column and one-pane-Stack cases, retained
  geometry, focus changes and popup cover/dismiss transitions.
- `venus/src/render/tests/outlines.rs`: use the existing render/draw-input
  harness to check that only eligible pane controls and their feedback are
  emitted, compact hidden action gaps disappear, and reserved title fitting
  stays stable; exercise framed and frameless presentation.
- `venus/src/accessibility.rs` tests only, if needed to strengthen the existing
  `pane_buttons_are_independent_accessible_targets_with_disabled_zoom` test:
  both actions on an unfocused pane remain named, focusable and activatable.
  Existing application keyboard/semantic-action tests remain the regression
  evidence for unchanged activation; no application behavior edits planned.
- `venus/docs/CONTRACTS.md`, `venus/docs/PRESENTATION.md`,
  `venus/CHANGELOG.md`; one product entry in root `CHANGELOG.md` as required
  by rule 10. No configuration key, export, dependency, fixture format,
  Runtime, Orbit or CLI implementation changes.

## VEN-C8 amendment — approved with the review changes below

Record the overseer's 2026-11-10T21:29:18Z approval for `eon-vzf2k`. Also
change the earlier clause "its title and buttons are compact gaps in its row's
line" to "its title and any visible buttons are compact gaps in its row's line".
Replace the existing passage starting "Each pane header carries Zoom" through
the statement about popup-covered headers with:

> Each pane header reserves room for Zoom (Restore while zoomed) and Close at
> the right; the title and scrollback pill fit to their left even while the
> buttons are hidden. The buttons are drawn and accept pointer actions only
> on the active tab's selected pane, except that a Stack containing one pane
> retains that pane's buttons, subject to the same fit requirement. This
> selection is retained while keyboard focus is in the Agents sidebar. Where
> both buttons cannot fit at full size the header shows neither. Stack, Agents,
> popup and dialog headings carry no pane actions, nor does a header a popup
> covers. Pane-header keyboard actions and AccessKit actions
> retain their existing availability for every laid-out pane header.

Keep the following keyboard/AccessKit clauses and one-pane Zoom behavior intact.
This is a feature policy recorded in this bead, with a narrowly approved
amendment to its existing boundary contract; no new contract ID.

VEN-C18 is unchanged, including popup replacement/occlusion and popup/Agents
Hide. Baseline SHA-256 of its complete Markdown section (heading through just
before the next level-two heading):
`75d20f29eb420e9117be72aea66722b08a6bcbf5577155bffe59728e05c7526e`.
Recompute and compare after the documentation edit.

Rule 6 reason for a fixed policy: Lucca explicitly chose three sequential
beads, first focused-only controls, then hover, then evaluation of a setting.
Introducing configuration here would duplicate that follow-up's scope and
require unnecessary Runtime/launch changes before the interaction is
evaluated. The temporary fixed policy keeps that support cost out of this
slice; `eon-qnvcu` owns evaluating configuration. Keyboard, CLI and accessibility
stay available while mouse-only gaps are accepted per Lucca's 16:37Z comment.

## Proof and delivery

Name each meaningful failure before extending an existing test. Add no new
harness. Scene tests must falsify accidental actions on collapsed or
unselected expanded headers, incorrect one-pane-Stack treatment, accidental
layout changes, and loss of the retained pane when chrome has focus. Render
tests must falsify hidden glyphs/feedback still being emitted or empty action
cutouts remaining on collapsed lines. Accessibility tests protect the semantic
actions specifically excluded from mouse gating.

Iterate with focused scene/render/accessibility tests through the existing
`nix develop -c eon-test -p yazelix-venus <filter>` harness. Per the latest
overseer instruction, fmt, changed-crate clippy (`--locked --all-targets --
-D warnings`) and the Venus suite all run through heavy.sh, which supplies
`nice -n 19` and `CARGO_BUILD_JOBS=6`. Clippy must be clean before the full
suite and captures.

Run the complete Venus suite through
`bash /home/lucca/.cache/eon-agents/eon-overseer/heavy.sh nix develop -c eon-test -p yazelix-venus`.
Do not run the whole workspace: the overseer explicitly narrowed proof to
Venus in the 21:29:18Z review instruction. Review fixes get fmt, clippy and the
Venus suite. Record every attempt, environment, result,
test count and source/staged identity in numbered `bead/` files. Do not claim
a timed Tier 2 output gate from untimed suite proof; explicitly name any
missing Tier 2 check under the Verification route. No performance claim.

For Lucca's visual acceptance, use an exact candidate package built with a
GC-rooted `nix build --out-link` through heavy.sh. The common rules also say
agents do not run package builds, so request that candidate from the overseer
when source checks are clean; do not build or refresh a profile independently.
Run native capture sessions through heavy.sh, with a private headless Sway,
private HOME/configuration and short isolated Eon/runtime roots, retained
candidate identity and exact-PID cleanup. Preserve Lucca's desktop focus and
all live supervisors. Use the real-look opacity and a colored wallpaper from
the capture recipe.

Capture both dark and light themes (six images):

1. A three-pane Stack with the middle pane selected, showing both collapsed
   title lines and the focused controls.
2. Two columns with a multi-pane unselected column, required by the review:
   even its expanded pane hides buttons. Test the one-pane-Stack exception
   separately.
3. A focused popup, with its own heading controls intact; dismiss it to verify
   that the retained selected pane's controls return. Also observe Agents
   sidebar keyboard focus retaining that selected pane's controls.

Inspect the real captures and give their paths to the overseer for Lucca to
see before landing. No mocks, live-window manipulation, focus stealing, timed
benchmarks without a booked quiet slot, or package-build proof substitutes.

## Review and stop points

Write `PLAN READY <path>` to `STATUS.md` and end this turn. The overseer runs
the Opus plan review and approves or returns findings, including the VEN-C8
text. Fold in or rebut every finding before implementation. Codex does not
poll INBOX; resume when nudged.

After implementation, proof and captures, stage the accepted candidate, record
its tree, and write `READY FOR REVIEW <staged tree hash>` to `STATUS.md`.
The overseer owns fresh Claude/Codex reviews and landing. Keep a numbered
review ledger, handle only this bead's findings, and never commit, push, open a
PR, write with br, or refresh the installed profile. Stop after this bead lands
or is handed back.

title: Show other sessions' agents in the Agents sidebar as collapsed sections
description:
A Rex beta user's main complaint about Rex is that its agent activity view is a flat list in a floating native window. They want a sidebar grouped by session, and later by host (X post, 2026-11-09; report.md in eon-rex-notes-work). Eon's in-window sidebar already groups agents by tab, but it lists only the shown session's terminals (docs/CONTRACTS.md:4391). Agents in other sessions reach the person only through the Alt+Q inbox and Alt+G. This bead adds one section per other session below the shown session's tabs. Each section is collapsed by default and shows the session's name (or ID), a count, and the most urgent state, using the header and collapse control from `smqg8`. Clicking a row, or pressing Enter on it, shows that session and jumps to the agent, as Alt+G does. Runtime already derives every session's attention for Alt+G and `attention_queue` (EON-C31). The work is presentation, an EONW field if the per-terminal rows are not already carried, and a VEN-C30 and EON-C31 amendment that Lucca approves before code. Rule 5 needs the CLI to expose the same grouping, for example as a session field on each `attention_queue` entry. Rule 6 needs a setting to keep today's shown-session-only view. Yu's host sections (remote slice 5) should reuse this grouping, not invent another.

## Plan shape and unresolved approval

Treat this feature as an epic, not a one-session Runtime/wire/Venus implementation. The 2026-11-10 comment 6252 already establishes the missing full per-terminal data. At dcaef1c runtime/crates/eon-workspace-protocol/src/v40.rs:613 WorkspaceInfo holds only a session rollup; :671 Snapshot carries one session's tabs and the window attention queue. The queue cannot supply other sessions' working/idle agents.

1. File a planning-only child to settle the intended feature approval, data owner/bounds, contract drafts and cross-session grouping/selection behavior.
2. After approval, file a Runtime/EONW/CLI child delivering bounded complete cross-session agent data with a fresh version and unchanged authorization.
3. File a Venus sections child after that and eon-sidebar-collapse-smqg8; reuse its tab sections and the approved per-run view-state rule. Other-session grouping adds a level; it does not redefine existing sections as sessions.

No Lucca approval is recorded here; implementation must wait for a recorded approval of the feature scope and exact boundary text. The existing proposal remains intact, not accepted by this audit. Remote-host grouping is a future consumer constraint, not permission to implement remote transport.

Preserve proposed acceptance: other sessions appear collapsed by default with count/urgency, expand/collapse via pointer and keyboard/accessibility, agent activation switches session and targets it, and an opt-out preserves shown-session-only behavior. Include working/idle, unseen attention, removed/stale targets and no-focus behavior. Existing attention_queue JSON already includes session/tab/target; additional full-row data must share Runtime's source rather than duplicate queue policy. CLI exposes model data; collapse state follows the separately recorded view-state exemption instead of an unnecessary wire mutation.

title: Settle cross-session agent sidebar approval, bounded data model and contract drafts
description:
## Why

eon-vzpvj proposes other sessions' agent sections, collapsed by default, but its comment 6252 records missing full per-terminal data and no recorded Lucca approval. Settle that decision before a multi-owner Runtime/EONW/Venus implementation.

## Evidence

At dcaef1c runtime/crates/eon-workspace-protocol/src/v40.rs:613 WorkspaceInfo has only session urgency; :671 Snapshot carries one session's tabs plus a queue that excludes working/idle agents. JSON queue entries already identify session/tab/target. eon-sidebar-collapse-smqg8 owns existing per-tab disclosure and the recorded per-run view-state rule.

## Scope

Planning only: present the existing feature for scope approval, record Runtime's single bounded cross-session row model, ordering/count/urgency and stale-target rules; draft exact EON-C31/VEN-C30 and required wire/CLI/config changes. Preserve existing tab grouping underneath the new session level. No new remote transport, code, wire version or edits to approved contract text.

## Acceptance

- Approval or unresolved decision is quoted on the parent; absent approval does not become permission through this split.
- The plan covers working/idle plus urgent agents, session removal, pointer/keyboard/AccessKit activation, collapse view-state and configured shown-session-only opt-out.
- CLI/model parity reuses Runtime facts without a second attention queue or duplicate sorting.
- After approval, file one Runtime/wire/CLI child and one Venus sections child; Venus waits for the data child and eon-sidebar-collapse-smqg8.
- Remote-host reuse is a constraint for later work, not expansion of this local feature.

## Verification

Planning text/source evidence and dependency graph only; no runtime proof.

## Stop Conditions

Stop for missing Lucca scope/exact-contract approval, unclear row bounds/authorization or a decision that changes the proposed outcome.

## Maintenance Notes

Keep full feature acceptance on the parent. Do not block this planning task on a presentation dependency that only the later Venus implementation needs.

title: Make the quota pace scale reach a true red, and sooner
description:
## Why

Lucca, 2026-11-04, relaying his friend Ronald: "ronald said he'd rather have the quota coloring be less forgiving / so the 'worst' color should be red, not just dark orange".

Today the quota pace scale (venus/src/render/palette.rs `QUOTA_PACE`, documented in venus/docs/PRESENTATION.md, Eon Bar) ends at rgb(255, 107, 107). That is a light coral that reads as orange on the bar. Full colour arrives only when the window runs out half a window or more before its reset:

| Anchor | Colour |
| ---: | --- |
| -0.25 | green |
| 0 | light green |
| 0.10 | yellow |
| 0.25 | orange |
| 0.50 | coral |

## What

1. **A true red.** The worst anchor becomes a saturated red that reads as red, not coral, while keeping at least 4.5:1 contrast on the bar background. Compute the contrast and record it. `LOAD_CRITICAL` (CPU, RAM and disk at critical) shares this colour, and follows on purpose.
2. **Less forgiving.** Reach the colours sooner. Overseer's recommendation, approved under Lucca's standing rule:
   - yellow at 0.05;
   - orange at 0.10;
   - full red at 0.25, so a window that runs out a quarter of a window early is fully red.

   Green and light green stay as they are.
3. **The docs.** Update the PRESENTATION.md sentence "full red runs out at least half a window before the reset" to match, and the palette comments.

## Rule 6 (configurability)

The scale stays fixed. One palette is shared with the load chips, and per-user colour and threshold settings belong to a theme setting, not to this slice. A person who wants other colours is the case for a theme bead. Search for an existing one, link it as related, and say so in the record; if there is none, report it rather than filing one.

## Acceptance

- Palette tests (the existing ones beside `QUOTA_PACE`, or in venus/src/application/tests/chrome.rs) cover the new anchors: a window a quarter early is the full red, and on pace is unchanged.
- The contrast check passes for every anchor.
- Installed dogfood on a private headless Sway (never Lucca's windows): a capture of a quota chip at full red, using a fixture or fake reading, viewed as a PNG.
- CHANGELOG.md entry (user-visible).
- Rule 5: no new action; nothing to add.
close_reason: Landed on edge with its proof and review records

title: Investigate a Google subscription quota chip in the Eon Bar
description:
## Why

Lucca, 2026-11-04: "create a bead to investigate a agy quota widget". Eon agents now run on agy (Google's Antigravity CLI), using Claude Opus 5.5 through Google's quota, to preserve the Claude Max quota. Lucca and the overseer need to see agy's remaining quota at a glance, as they already see Codex and Claude in the Eon Bar.

## Questions to answer (investigation; no product code)

1. Data source:
   - Does the pinned CodexBar CLI have an Antigravity or Gemini provider?
   - If not, `agy -p /usage` prints a tab-separated table (no model turn) with "Claude and GPT models" five-hour and weekly Remaining and UTC reset times, and maybe Gemini rows. How stable is that format? Is there a JSON or endpoint form?
   - What does one read cost, and how long does it take?
2. Which windows to show: Claude and GPT models, Gemini, or both. How they map onto the existing quota fact shape (EONW quota facts, `windows[]` with duration, remaining and resets_at, plus an optional scope).
3. Contracts:
   - A new provider is a new EONW quota fact provider and a new `[bar] widgets` entry (`agy_quota`?). Which EON-C, VEN-C and EONW text changes, and is a version bump needed? Compare with the OpenCode Go precedent (eon-opencode-go-quota-eon-bar-5tt9) and CodexBar's provider model (docs/CONFIGURATION.md "Agent quota").
   - New contract text and a wire change are MAJOR under Lucca's standing rule, so the implementation beads stop for his approval.
4. Read policy: only while the chip is listed in `[bar] widgets`, as for the other providers, and the stored last good reading in `$XDG_STATE_HOME/eon/quota`.

## Deliverable

- A decision comment on this bead: the source, mapping, contract drafts and recommended chip text.
- Then file the implementation beads (Runtime reader, Venus chip, configuration and docs), each with its verification.

## Verification

Evidence quoted in the decision comment:
- the commands run with their output, `agy -p /usage` format samples, and the CodexBar provider list;
- the contract sections cited by file and line.


## Scope correction and acceptance

Lucca, 2026-11-04: "not agy, more like the google sub, right?" Investigate the Google subscription budget and which Antigravity/agy/Gemini surfaces actually share it; do not infer sharing from their provider name. `agy -p /usage` is one candidate reader, not the selected provider identity. Report supported and unsupported windows, authenticated-read cost/latency and format stability, with secrets excluded from samples. The deliverable includes source evidence, existing quota-fact mapping, proposed provider/chip naming and every contract/config boundary touched. Ask Lucca to choose the source/scope and approve required contract text before filing or building Runtime/Venus slices. This pass only queues that investigation.

# eon-w31ps — Google subscription quota: investigation and proposed decision

Investigated 2026-11-05 against Eon **22f7d02c700e5b74c19dfd903cc6cc59950c3145** (detached, initially clean). All repository `file:line` citations below refer to that revision. This is a proposal, not approval or implementation. No beads were filed or changed.

## Recommendation

Use **`agy -p /usage --output-format json`**, reading **`command.data.groups[].buckets[]`**, as the first Google reader. Name the fact/provider **`google_quota`**, and identify each chip with **Google**, its model group, its window and its remaining percentage. Preserve every supplied active group/window separately; there is no defensible single “Google remaining %.” Keep Google **opt-in** through `[bar] widgets`, with existing defaults unchanged.

This reads the **Google subscription's Antigravity baseline allowance**, including Gemini models and third-party models served there. It does **not** measure a separate agy allowance. It also does not establish that Gemini Apps, Gemini API, Vertex AI or legacy Gemini CLI debit that same allowance. The supplied report proves within-group sharing; same-account desktop/CLI pooling still needs a matching real-source observation before being advertised as proved.

Prefer direct structured agy output over the already-pinned CodexBar Antigravity adapter because it preserves the original groups and explicit disabled state, while leaving credentials and requests with Google's CLI. CodexBar is a viable alternative if Lucca prefers one collector dependency: use its **all-bucket extras**, not primary/secondary, and resolve the scope-loss and fallback issues below first. TSV is a fallback only if structured output disappears; Gemini's CodexBar provider and direct private Google APIs are unsuitable first choices for this scope.

**Two corrections drive this proposal:** JSON contains real structured quota data, not merely a table in `response`; and eon-8r9a4's `[bar.quota] hide` proposal was superseded by Lucca's window-level widget policy. Neither disabled→0% nor the old hide key should be copied into Eon.

## Window mapping and chip selection

`runtime/crates/eon-workspace-protocol/src/v32.rs:492-520` already represents duration, whole remaining percent, optional reset and optional scope. Scope means what a window limits, not necessarily a single model. Model **groups** therefore fit the concept; all Google rows should be scoped because no all-Google pool is demonstrated.

Proposed normalization: `5h → 300`, `weekly → 10080` minutes; `remaining_percent = floor(100 × remaining_fraction)` after validating finite `[0,1]`; RFC 3339 reset → Unix seconds. Preserve the exact group name as `scope`. Record local successful-read completion as `observed_at`, since the supplied quota data has no provider observation timestamp. This means “read at,” not a fabricated server timestamp. A valid reset at or before completion omits that expired window; a malformed timestamp fails the read. Admitted windows therefore have an absent reset or one strictly after `observed_at`. JSON output uses Unix **milliseconds** through the existing conversion (`runtime/crates/eon-runtime/src/workspace.rs:3062-3104`); EONW/storage use seconds.

Google quota has the fresh/stale state, observation and window form used by the other quota facts, with at most six scoped windows, only 300/10080-minute periods, and unique scope/duration pairs. Scope bounds and value/reset validation remain canonical. Codex and Claude's existing provider-specific bounds remain unchanged. EONW times remain Unix seconds. Encoder, decoder, empty snapshots and size bounds include the new slots. Version 32 bytes are not reinterpreted as version 33, and older live generations are not stopped to adopt the new wire.

VEN-C8/VEN-C21 need only their current EONW consumption references advanced and their existing refresh/layout invariants preserved. The Google feature text below belongs in `venus/docs/PRESENTATION.md`, not a new contract:

> Google quota uses one read-only text chip for each selected active model-group window. Its label is `Google <scope> <position>/<duration> <remaining>%`; without a reset it omits the position and slash. A stale chip retains `old`. Hover and accessibility identify the Google subscription's model group, period, remaining allowance, reset availability and observation freshness. Disabled and missing windows have no chip. Chips follow the configured order and the existing whole-chip hiding, logo-room and tab/control priority. Google-only updates do not move tabs, reset navigation or erase coherent workspace notices. Google transport loss clears its presentation with the other quota facts.

### Configuration documentation — proposed verbatim addition

> Google quota is optional and uses your already signed-in `agy` executable on PATH. Initially only version 1.4.1 is supported; another version stays unavailable until its turn-free `/usage` report is verified and Eon's accepted-version rule is updated. It shows the Google subscription's Antigravity baseline model-group allowances, including Gemini models served there; it does not report Gemini Apps, Gemini API or AI-credit balances. Eon does not sign in, read credential files, switch accounts or change agy's settings. Initial support is the consumer-OAuth source verified on Linux native Wayland.
>
> Add exact Google group/window selectors to `[bar] widgets`. For all windows in the observed report, use the example below. Remove an entry to hide that window; no `[bar.quota] hide` setting exists. The scope text must match the source report, so a renamed group requires an updated selector. Existing defaults include no Google entries. `5h` selects a five-hour window and `7d` a weekly window. Disabled or missing windows do not show; weekly-only groups get no invented five-hour chip. The full reading remains available through `eon workspace --json` while any Google selector is listed.

```toml
[bar]
widgets = [
  "codex_quota_5h", "codex_quota_7d",
  "claude_quota_5h", "claude_quota_7d", "claude_quota_scoped",
  "google_quota:Gemini Models:5h",
  "google_quota:Gemini Models:7d",
  "google_quota:Claude and GPT models:5h",
  "google_quota:Claude and GPT models:7d",
  "google_quota:Gemini 4 Argon:7d",
  "cpu", "ram", "disk", "clock", "version",
]
```

> To show only the third-party Google allowance, keep its two `Claude and GPT models` entries and remove the three other Google entries. To hide Argon, remove its weekly entry. To stop Google reads, remove every Google entry and reopen the window. Hiding a chip because the window is narrow does not stop collection.
>
> Google reads start at least five minutes apart, including after failure or enabling it again. Windows share a schedule when the state directory supports it; otherwise each supervisor keeps its own. Provider refusals back off to 30 minutes, then one hour and then two hours until success. Collection has a ten-second deadline and keeps the last good normalized reading at `$XDG_STATE_HOME/eon/quota/google.json` (`~/.local/state/eon/quota/google.json` by default). A retained reading appears immediately when enabled, becomes `old` after an hour and disappears after 24 hours; each supplied reset expires its window. Missing data does not mean zero allowance. Google chips use a fixed Google label with the reported group name, window position and remaining percentage.

At observed 3.48–4.20 seconds/read, five-minute spacing means up to about **12 starts/hour or 288/day** while continuously enabled, about **1.2–1.4% wall-time occupancy** for the one shared reader. These are arithmetic estimates from two process timings, not CPU measurements. No inference tokens were recorded; the report still performs authenticated backend reads and Google publishes no read-rate guarantee here. A failed shared-schedule fallback can multiply starts by supervisor count. Do not poll every bar redraw or launch one process per selected window. The first read is asynchronous; retained data avoids a four-second empty bar after restart. The cadence and bounds are proposed fixed performance/safety policy, to be recorded in the future owning bead under Configurability (`docs/AGENT-RULES.md:223-240`).

## Proposed implementation slices — do not file yet

All depend on Lucca approving source/scope and the above contract/wire/configuration choices. Each is a sequential slice small enough for a fresh agent session; if its actual scope grows, split it before implementation. No slice owns a new daemon, credential store, generic widget framework, billing operation, Orbit change or platform expansion. Rust owns product logic. Every code/test/script slice finishes the repository's independent review loop, including Codex, and records exact proof in its eventual bead/commit (`docs/AGENT-RULES.md:72-161`).

| Slice | Scope and acceptance | Cheapest sufficient verification |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **1. Canonical Google fact and CLI projection** | Land approved fact text, next EONW version, bounded Google slots/codec and JSON projection; update all in-tree consumers/constructors and the single manifest. Fields remain null until a reader supplies them. Five simultaneous scoped windows round-trip; sixth accepted, seventh rejected; existing provider bounds unchanged; seconds→milliseconds correct; older wire rejected honestly without stopping live generations. | Focused codec boundaries/round-trip/frame-size and workspace JSON checks, then full affected Rust/Nix surfaces because the wire/manifest changes. Use `nix develop -c eon-test -p eon-workspace-protocol -p eon-runtime -p eon -p yazelix-venus`; fmt, affected clippy and exact product/eonbase builds/checks. No authenticated collection claim. |
| **2. Runtime Google parser** | Add only the structured agy parser/normalizer and approved source-version rule, dormant until collection is wired. Cover all supplied active groups, disabled omission, weekly-only, floor conversion, read-time semantics, absent resets, unsupported duration, excessive windows, bad scopes/fractions, empty valid reports and conflicting repeats. Do not parse the table or account identity. | Deterministic parser red/green on sanitized supplied JSON plus one parameterized invalid-boundary check; affected Runtime build. No bespoke test harness, credential copies or model calls. |
| **3. Window selector configuration and launch** | Add exact Google scope/duration selectors, owned scope values and recognition separate from defaults; update config corpus/default comments and internal argv transport. Preserve explicit-empty and omission behavior, commas/colons in scope, ordering, unknown warnings and duplicate errors. Venus accepts resolved selectors, with no Google chip until slice 5. No new hide key or bare provider alias. | Focused Runtime corpus/parser, supervisor argv and Venus launch/selector checks; affected Runtime/Eon/Venus builds, Venus fmt/clippy. Prove old default order unchanged and `widgets=[]` remains empty. Update CONFIGURATION/LAUNCH text in the same slice rather than leaving broken examples. |
| **4. Runtime Google collection and retention** | Connect the parser to existing bounded worker/process ownership and Google selector enablement. Resolve/verify supported agy without invoking an inference fallback; use null stdin, empty private cwd and sanitized environment. Add shared schedule/backoff and versioned `google.json` using existing mechanisms. Failures retain facts; unlisting cancels in-flight work; success/missing/expiry/reset/cache restart behavior is correct. CLI JSON sees every active group, including unselected windows. No bundled agy dependency. | Extend existing worker/cache/schedule checks for the new source's object/error envelope, cancellation/deadline/output cap, provider isolation, restart and two-supervisor scheduling. Full affected Rust/Nix lifecycle surfaces. Then one approved real-source read on the verified consumer-OAuth account, recording version, latency, zero turns/tokens and sanitized groups; do not claim desktop pooling without a paired same-account observation. |
| **5. Venus Google chips** | Add Google provider identity to existing scene/hover/accessibility and last-read room reservation; use text label, no new bitmap or collector. Include Google in quota-only structural-change comparison and workspace-loss clearing. Selected windows only, stable IDs before filtering, source scopes distinct, no invented disabled/weekly-only chips. Preserve controls, tabs, focus and narrow-width priority. Portability disposition: neutral. | Focused scene/accessibility/model checks (wide/narrow, stale, missing reset, hidden Argon, Google-only refresh and loss), affected Venus suite/build, fmt/clippy. One isolated installed native Wayland observation of final chips plus same-session raw JSON retaining hidden groups; inspect hover/accessibility. |
| **6. Final Eon delivery and documentation** | Reconcile approved text with actual proved behavior across configuration/defaults, Runtime README/EONW docs, Venus PRESENTATION/LAUNCH, usage, contracts/proof status and product changelog. Verify manifest and exact installed identity. Update no historical proof claims. Refresh the active eon profile under the repository's delivery rules; preserve every live supervisor and terminal. | Reuse unchanged accepted lower proof, build the exact final product and run one isolated installed end-to-end observation: selected real-source groups, retained start, hidden-window JSON, unlisting stops reads, failure retention and narrow bar. Record exact revision/artifact/environment and only then claim delivery. Coordinate the profile operation; never restart the live supervisor. |

Implementation reach to include in those scopes:

- Runtime starts quota collection only in full workspace mode (`supervisor.rs:1050-1051`), reapplies selection on reopen (`:2416-2417`) and adds facts to Inspect (`:1243-1244`). `quota.rs:700-795` owns slots/apply, `:797-886` command/bounded collection, `:205-319` age/cache and `:387-514` shared scheduling. Existing shared scheduling/backoff is Claude-only (`:550-554,626-627`), so Google reuse must be explicit, not assumed.
- CLI projection is `workspace.rs:2916-2946,3062-3104`. Product defaults are `eon/crates/eon/src/product.rs:16-20`; Runtime test defaults are `runtime/crates/eon-runtime/src/fixtures.rs:18-22`. Config fixtures live under `runtime/crates/eon-runtime/testdata/config-corpus/`.
- Venus selection/defaults and last-read reservation are `scene.rs:633-750`; quota-only comparison and loss clearing are `model.rs:433-434,536-544`; provider node IDs are `accessibility.rs:1034-1042`; `render/chrome.rs:1816-1817` assumes the current two icon-backed providers. Extend these existing owners instead of adding a second quota pipeline.
- Comparable native presentation is recorded in `venus/docs/REFERENCES.md:89-108,127-131`; it keeps provider polling/auth out of Venus. Product boundaries remain `docs/AGENT-RULES.md:251-257`; configuration remains Runtime-owned (`:223-231`) and the full agent-readable data path remains Inspect/JSON (`:211-221`).

## Open choices for Lucca

1. **Source and initial supported scope?** Recommend direct agy structured `/usage`, initially accepting exactly 1.4.1 consumer OAuth, named `google_quota`. Keep CodexBar for Codex/Claude. Restricting eligibility costs support work when agy updates, but avoids assuming untested slash-command behavior; later versions need recorded source/report verification and an accepted-rule update. Alternative: pinned CodexBar Antigravity extras, accepting work to recover distinct scopes and constrain its source/fallback behavior. Direct Google OAuth/API ownership buys nothing necessary for this slice.
2. **Which “Gemini” surfaces must this promise cover?** Recommend “Google subscription baseline groups served by Antigravity,” including the supplied Gemini group, with paired same-account desktop/CLI evidence before a pooling claim. Do not include Gemini Apps or legacy/enterprise/API Gemini CLI on the strength of the Google name. If Gemini Apps allowance is required, treat its source/pool verification as additional investigation before approving that scope.
3. **Select exact groups/windows how?** Recommend the parameterized `google_quota:<scope>:5h|7d` entries above, no `[bar.quota] hide`, no model enum and no bare provider alias. Offer the five-entry example; Lucca can keep only the third-party pair. This follows his later eon-8r9a4 direction and permits hiding Argon individually. Group names have no proven stability guarantee; source renaming needs a config edit.
4. **Default inclusion and text?** Recommend opt-in, existing global defaults unchanged; each enabled window says `Google`, its exact group, window position and remaining percent. No combined percentage or new icon. Wider labels may mean fewer visible chips; users can select the windows they use.
5. **Disabled windows?** Recommend omit the disabled five-hour fact/chip and retain weekly 0%. A visible `disabled`/dash chip is possible, but needs an additional window-state contract/wire field; 0% would invent a measurement and 100% would imply usable allowance.
6. **Approve wire and bounded read policy?** Recommend next EONW version with separate Google fields, at most six active scoped windows, the existing 32-byte scope bound, five-minute user-shared cadence with Claude-style fallback/backoff, ten-second/64 KiB process limits and existing last-good retention/expiry. These are proposed bounds, not latency/rate-limit guarantees. Only after approval should implementation beads be filed.

Investigation review: one fresh read-only full pass found two blockers in the draft (reset classification and source-version eligibility). Both were fixed; the same reviewer checked those fixes and found no remaining blocker or new contradiction in them. File-reference existence and Markdown fence checks passed. No collector or runtime test formed part of this review.

No product/configuration/contract/test files were changed and no runtime behavior is proved by this memo. Remaining material uncertainty is source/account/desktop pooling and compatibility beyond the supplied agy report; a Google subscription name alone cannot resolve it.

title: Show that Eon is starting when a launch is slow, and log why a launch gives up
description:
Lucca, 2026-11-10 ~18:41Z: "eon is not opening" from the COSMIC desktop entry. Load was about 19 on 16 threads and a Nix garbage collection had just evicted Eon's files from the page cache. Three launches: app-cosmic-eon-1004646 (15:41:51 local) started a new supervisor (g1-185468b0...) but showed no window and its scope ended after about 30 s; 1006837 (15:41:57) and 1012603 (15:42:27) followed, and the third showed its window after a slow start. The journal holds nothing from the first two scopes except wgpu thread-priority warnings, so why the first gave up is unknown.

Scope: (1) find what the desktop launch waits for and what makes it exit without a window (a startup deadline, the supervisor lock, Venus connect), reproducing under bounded CPU and cold page cache; (2) give the person feedback within about a second that Eon is starting (an early window or a startup notification), so a slow start never looks like a failure; (3) log a launch that gives up, with the reason, where eon logs can show it. Rule 6 applies to any new timeout. Acceptance: a reproduced slow launch shows feedback early and either opens or leaves a logged reason.

## Delivery as an epic

The report does not establish whether the 30 s exit came from an Eon bound, desktop activation, a lock or GPU admission. Do not turn the suspected cause or "about a second" into a new guarantee without evidence.

Split into (1) bounded isolated diagnosis plus durable launch-failure logging, and (2) early user feedback using the resulting measured launch path. The first child provides a useful standalone diagnostic even if the intermittent failure cannot be reproduced; the second owns the user-visible feedback and is blocked by the first. The parent retains the complete early-feedback plus opens-or-explains outcome.

Scope remains Linux desktop launch, with init-independent Eon behavior: the COSMIC journal/scope is incident evidence, not a systemd requirement. No shared-host cache drop, load injection, real-user window manipulation or supervisor restart; reproduce with isolated runtime/configuration and bounded disposable load only. A log must be discoverable through the existing diagnostics path with window/generation identity when available and no secrets.

Lifecycle/launch owner is Eon Runtime composed by Eon's desktop entry; Venus owns any chosen early window. Child 1 records the current EON-C7/EON-C11/EON-C23 and comparable startup-feedback reference gate; any exact lifecycle/config/CLI contract change needs approval. New visible delay/timeout values follow rule 6. Current full affected lifecycle/delivery proof applies; a mocked waiting banner cannot prove an installed desktop launch.

title: Diagnose the isolated slow desktop launch path and retain a reason when launch gives up
description:
## Why

eon-w65o2 records Lucca's 2026-11-10 COSMIC launch incident: several starts under load/cache pressure, the first ending around 30 s without a window and no useful reason in the journal. The cause is unproved. Durable failure diagnostics are useful even when the natural incident cannot be reproduced.

## Evidence

Read the parent's exact incident and identities; current Eon Runtime launch/supervisor/diagnostics owners and EON-C7/EON-C11/EON-C23 before selecting code. Do not confuse cli.rs startup_notice (a Quick Search running-window notice) with pre-map startup feedback.

## Scope

Trace desktop entry -> Eon Runtime supervisor/locks -> Venus admission; record waits and exit ownership. Use an isolated runtime/config/display and bounded disposable load to attempt reproduction. Add missing failure logging at the owning existing boundary so eon logs can reveal the reason. Keep successful launch quiet and preserve existing deadlines/cleanup. No new timeout or early UI in this child.

## Acceptance

- The bead records observed paths, wait bounds and the reason or explicitly unproved hypothesis for the original disappearance.
- A controlled launch-failure regression reaches a diagnostic through the existing log path with safe identity/context; secrets and terminal contents are absent.
- A slow isolated launch either opens or leaves a specific diagnosable reason. No leaked child/lock or disruption to existing terminals.
- The sibling feedback child gets the earliest observable startup point and actual activation/window lifecycle constraints, plus approved contract text if any is needed.

## Verification

Focused supported failure-harness regression and the current full affected lifecycle/build/review route; one isolated installed desktop-entry observation with exact artifact and environment. No proof is claimed by planning.

## Stop Conditions

Stop before lifecycle/contract changes need approval; never drop shared page cache, load the real desktop or restart Lucca's supervisor to reproduce.

## Maintenance Notes

Eon remains init-independent; COSMIC/systemd scope/journal entries are incident evidence only. A failed reproduction must remain a named gap, not a guessed root cause.

title: Show early startup feedback during a slow installed Eon desktop launch
description:
## Why

eon-w65o2's approved outcome includes early feedback (about a second) so a slow launch does not look dead. Its diagnostic sibling identifies the actual wait/activation path first; this child picks the smallest supported feedback mechanism and proves the user-visible launch.

## Evidence

Read the parent incident and the completed diagnostic child's measured launch path, lifecycle owners and comparable startup-feedback reference record. The existing cli.rs startup_notice is an in-terminal Quick Search notice, not evidence of early desktop feedback.

## Scope

Provide early startup feedback using the existing desktop activation or Venus boundary that the reference gate supports, then end it on success/failure. Runtime retains lifecycle/failure diagnostic authority; Venus owns any window. Document shipped behavior and CHANGELOG. The explicit feedback/delay policy follows rule 6 with a documented setting or fixed-value rationale.

Out: unrelated desktop integration, new init/service-manager dependency, new distribution channel, speculative generic startup framework or changes to terminal persistence.

## Acceptance

- An isolated installed slow launch records feedback latency relative to invocation, with the agreed approximately-one-second intent and any approved bound stated explicitly.
- Successful launch proceeds to the actual window and removes/transitions feedback without duplicates; failure removes/transitions it and leaves the sibling's reason in eon logs.
- Existing-window/lock/admission paths do not steal focus or show misleading duplicate starts; ordinary fast launch remains usable.
- Exact lifecycle/config/CLI boundary changes receive approval before edits; pending state and application timing are documented.

## Verification

Current affected lifecycle/delivery proof and one isolated installed desktop-entry slow-success/failure observation with exact revision/artifact/environment, after profile refresh. A mock banner alone cannot prove desktop startup. Keep live terminals and desktop focus intact.

## Stop Conditions

Stop if the sibling cannot identify the feedback point, the mechanism needs unapproved scope/platform guarantees, or the agreed latency cannot be met without a new lifecycle decision.

## Maintenance Notes

Blocked by the diagnostics child. The parent retains the combined outcome; new limits are decided from evidence rather than guessed from the original 30 s incident.

title: Skip unknown list values in configuration and fail trust settings closed
description:
## Why

An older live window must keep working after the user adopts a newer value of a
key it already knows. Today a newer `[bar] widgets` name such as a future
widget makes an older build fail the whole config. That is the known limit
eon-i6yf recorded, and it is live because old windows reread `config.toml` for
every terminal and every reopen. Lucca accepted decision 5 of eon-c8ytm on
2026-10-31:
- skip unknown list values with a warning;
- a trust setting with an unknown value takes its most restrictive choice.
The EON-C28 amendment text was approved on 2026-10-31.

## Contract

Contract text approved 2026-10-31 (eon-c8ytm, approval comment). The EON-C28
Important failures sentence becomes: "In a configuration written for a newer
1.x, an older release skips list values it does not know, with a warning; a
trust setting with an unknown value takes its most restrictive choice; any
other unknown value of a known key may still fail." The new contract "Upgrades
within 0.x" applies the same from the announcement. The contract indexing prerequisite eon-z7kku is closed; both approved texts are indexed.

## Evidence

- Historical unknown-widget failure is already fixed on dcaef1c: managed_environment.rs:460-473 skips unknown names; :2377-2383 emits their warnings.
- `runtime/crates/eon-runtime/src/managed_environment.rs:506-519`
  `TerminalAccess {Window, None}`: `[agents] terminal_access`, today the only
  trust setting. Its doc comment calls it "a preference and a kill switch, not
  a security boundary"; an unknown value must still read as `none`.
- `docs/CONFIGURATION.md` "Configuration behavior": "Known keys with wrong
  types or values still fail, including unsupported widget names."

## Scope

In scope:
- `[bar] widgets`: an unknown name is skipped with one warning naming the value,
  the key and the file. A repeated name stays an error, because it is a
  mistake rather than a newer value.
- `[agents] terminal_access`: an unknown string reads as `none`, with a warning.
- Any other list-valued setting with a closed set of names, if one exists, gets
  the same treatment; list each in the bead's proof.
- Corpus fixtures for both cases. `docs/CONFIGURATION.md` sentence update and a
  `CHANGELOG.md` Unreleased entry.

Out of scope:
- Wrong types, which still fail, and unknown scalar enum values outside trust
  settings, which still fail.
- Popup tables (their own validation).

## Acceptance

- A config with `widgets = ["clock", "future_widget"]` opens a window that shows
  the clock and logs one warning. `terminal_access = "future"` refuses
  `eon pane read`.

## Implementation Notes

1. Warn through the existing `note_once` path; do not add a second warning
   channel.

## Verification

- `nix develop -c eon-test -p eon-runtime` exits 0.
- converge plus Codex; installed observation of the acceptance in an isolated
  window.

## Stop Conditions

- Stop if another setting looks like a trust setting and its most restrictive
  choice is unclear: ask on eon-c8ytm.

## Maintenance Notes

- Policy: eon-c8ytm proposal, section A.

## Remaining work at dcaef1c

Do not redo the landed unknown-widget skip/warning implementation or EON-C32's matching Result text (docs/CONTRACTS.md:4595-4600). Existing config_warnings and its unknown-widget checks provide regression coverage to retain. Known duplicates and wrong types still fail; list any other closed-name list settings actually found rather than assuming all lists are widget lists.

The trust-value gap remains: TerminalAccess still derives enum deserialization (:506-519), and the :3095 parser test expects "all" to fail. The NUL gap remains: disk_path at :275 accepts an absolute path containing NUL. Complete those two missing acceptance items in the same owned parser slice, keep known wrong types failing, and warn once naming key/value/file through the existing path. Unknown trust values resolve to none on every parser consumer, including startup/reload and eon config check.

Reconcile docs/CONFIGURATION.md:215's blanket "unsupported widget names" failure claim and only contract text that is actually stale after inspecting EON-C32's Important failures. The 2026-10-31 EON-C28 text approval is preserved; any additional EON-C32 exact wording still needs approval. Inventory other launch-argument strings for NUL as the existing acceptance requires; don't expand into unrelated validation refactors.

Retain corpus fixtures for skipped widgets, closed trust and NUL rejection, plus the installed read-refusal observation. Use current whole-workspace/parser/trust proof and live-terminal preservation, not just the historical per-package command.
acceptance_criteria:
- [ ] EON-C32 Important failures and docs/CONFIGURATION.md:171 say an unknown widget name is skipped with a warning (EON-C28); a repeated name still fails
- [ ] A NUL in [bar] disk_path fails at configuration load with an error naming bar.disk_path; the proof lists other launch-argument string settings and their NUL handling

comments.text: Reported by eon-overseer (2026-10-31), routed here from eon-wc119: a NUL byte in `[bar] disk_path` (e.g. `disk_path = "/data\u0000x"`) passes config validation and fails only at Venus launch, since a NUL cannot cross into a process argument. The check belongs in `disk_path()` (runtime/crates/eon-runtime/src/managed_environment.rs, the fn after `struct Bar`, from eon-d7itl), which accepts any absolute or ~/ string. Recommendation: reject a NUL there with an error naming bar.disk_path, so it fails at config load with live terminals kept, as EON-C32's Important failures already say for a bad disk_path; and check other string settings that become launch arguments for the same gap. Not fixed in eon-wc119 (out of its scope).

comments.author: lucca
comments.text:
Plan refresh, 2026-11-03 (prime-beads P2 pass, group 2). Both blockers are closed (eon-z7kku indexed the EON-C28 sentence at docs/CONTRACTS.md:2608 and EON-C37; eon-embg6 seeded the corpus), and the code is unchanged, so this is ready.

1. Drifted lines: the unknown-widget error is runtime/crates/eon-runtime/src/managed_environment.rs:257; `TerminalAccess` :300-304; the existing test that expects `terminal_access = "all"` to fail is at :1823 and changes with this bead (it should then read as `none` with a warning).
2. EON-C32's Important failures still say "An unknown or repeated name ... fails" (docs/CONTRACTS.md ~3110), which contradicts the approved EON-C28 sentence once this lands. Amend it in the same change; draft for Lucca: "A repeated name, a non-string entry, a value that is not a list, ... fails through the existing startup and replacement handling, preserving live terminals. An unknown name is skipped with one warning naming it (EON-C28)." docs/CONFIGURATION.md:171 ("including unsupported widget names") changes too.

title: Load deprecated configuration keys through an alias table; show_version becomes an alias
description:
## Why

A configuration key Eon removed must not stop the window. Today `[bar]
show_version`, removed in ddc6c44 (2026-10-21), is a tombstone that fails the
whole file: a config that still has it gets no window. From a desktop launch,
the error reaches only `launch.log`. Lucca accepted the eon-c8ytm policy on
2026-10-31 (decisions 2 and 4):
- Never rewrite `config.toml` automatically.
- Migrate by read-time translation from an alias table, warning with the exact
  replacement.
- A removed key fails only if ignoring it would widen access, run something the
  user did not configure, or lose data.

## Evidence

- `runtime/crates/eon-runtime/src/managed_environment.rs:134-142`: the
  `removed_show_version` tombstone, a hard parse error.
- `runtime/crates/eon-runtime/src/managed_environment.rs:41` `unknown_keys`
  and `:1274-1290` `read_config`: the unknown-key warning path, which reaches
  the supervisor log once per key.
- `runtime/crates/eon-runtime/src/managed_environment.rs:191-202`: how
  `[bar] widgets` resolves; `show_version = false` maps to the default widgets
  without `version`, and `true` maps to the default.
- `/home/lucca/pjs/nova/ratconfig/src/migration.rs:8-24`: Ratconfig's
  `MigrationOp::{Rename, Delete, AddDefault, Transform}`, the vocabulary to
  borrow (decision 3). Ratconfig is not a Rust dependency, and this bead does
  not add it.

## Scope

In scope:
- An alias table in Eon Runtime, applied to the parsed `toml::Value` before
  deserializing. Each entry is an old dotted key, a presence-detected operation
  (rename, delete, or transform to the current key), the release it was
  deprecated in, and the warning text naming the replacement. The new key wins
  when both are present, with a warning.
- `[bar] show_version` becomes the first entry: `false` gives the default
  widgets without `version`, and `true` gives the default. Remove the tombstone.
- Deprecation warnings go through the same `note_once` path as unknown keys,
  with distinct text: "eon: <old> is deprecated; use <new>".
- A corpus fixture per entry (corpus bead), and flip the `show_version`
  expected failure to a pass.
- `docs/CONFIGURATION.md` "Configuration behavior": deprecated keys load with a
  warning naming the replacement. `CHANGELOG.md` Unreleased entry.

Out of scope:
- Any automatic write to `config.toml`. `eon config migrate` is deferred
  (eon-c8ytm item 8).
- A config version field: rejected in eon-i6yf and again in eon-c8ytm.
- Showing deprecations to a person or in `eon config check` (that is the
  follow-up bead that this one blocks).

## Acceptance

- A config containing `[bar] show_version = false` opens a window whose bar
  omits the version, and logs one deprecation warning naming `bar.widgets`.
- The corpus test passes with the `show_version` fixture no longer an expected
  failure.

## Implementation Notes

1. Keep the table data-only (one line per entry); a test asserts each entry's
   warning text names a key that `eon config defaults --json` knows.
2. Apply the table before serde, on a clone of the parsed value; do not mutate
   the file.

## Verification

- `nix develop -c eon-test -p eon-runtime` exits 0.
- converge plus Codex; the installed observation of the acceptance in an
  isolated window (docs/AGENT-RULES.md Verification).

## Stop Conditions

- Stop if an alias would need a contract change beyond EON-C28's existing
  "deprecated setting still loads and warns" clause.
- Stop if the corpus bead has not landed (this bead adds to its corpus).

## Maintenance Notes

- Policy: eon-c8ytm proposal, section A. An entry may be deleted only below the
  declared migration floor.
- Rejected: Ratconfig's joined-contract migration. It stamps a version into the
  file and rewrites it, which breaks rollback, older live windows and read-only
  home-manager files.

title: Build Eon's public website
description:
Goal and observable contract
A visitor evaluating Eon can understand what it does, see the real product, learn its current availability and limitations, and reach the canonical documentation, source, and supported installation instructions. Deliver a focused public product website with a coherent Eon visual identity and a clear path from discovery to trying the product.

Initial scope
Explain the terminal workspace and durable work across window close/reconnect using concise copy and real screenshots or a short demo of accepted behavior. Describe Eon and EonTerm accurately where relevant. Keep platform, installation, release-status, and durability claims aligned with the current README and proven contracts; distinguish planned capabilities from supported ones. Start with the smallest useful landing/onboarding surface rather than a general content platform.

Ownership and prerequisites
Eon owns website content and composition. README, docs/CONTRACTS.md, docs/ARCHITECTURE.md, and distribution documentation remain the authorities for product behavior and installation. The user purchased eonterm.com and selected it as the website domain (2026-10-12, America/Sao_Paulo). The selected approach is a neutral Yazelix/site-starter repository extracted from Nova's website, then a separate Yazelix/eon-site seeded from that template. Reuse Nova's Astro static-site foundation and Bun/Node development tooling, with TypeScript limited to website components, configuration, and checks. This website toolchain remains separate from Rust-owned Eon runtime and repository policy. Hosting remains undecided. Website work does not activate public beta, distribution graduation, or unsupported platforms. Publishing requires an explicitly chosen destination and authorization.

Starter extraction decision
The user accepted this approach after source inspection of /home/lucca/pjs/yazelix-dir/nova-site at 5917e42b31db6c746c82a3295ada69a9448d31bc (clean working tree). Inspected README.md, ARCHITECTURE.md, Astro configuration, components, styles, browser tests, and the Nix development shell. This is source evidence only; the extracted starter and Eon site have not been built or browser-verified.

- Extract the static build/development setup, responsive shell and navigation, metadata/canonical URL handling, accessible media components, and applicable browser checks. Retain Starlight docs/search only if the initial Eon site consumes it.
- Keep customization small: site identity, navigation, metadata, and CSS tokens. Preserve direct Astro composition rather than adding a generator, plugin framework, or generic page-schema system.
- Replace hardcoded Nova identity, repository links, social imagery, and content assertions with neutral examples or explicit site inputs. Keep Nova release claims, articles, compatibility redirects, product pins, screenshots, and recording recipes out of the generic starter. The base development shell must not require Nova's recording machinery.
- Eon owns its copy, visual identity, screenshots, installation guidance, product evidence, and deployment configuration. Do not transfer Nova's website-owned canonical-guidance policy into Eon; Eon's existing canonical documents remain authoritative.
- Use a starter template rather than a shared runtime package. Generated sites evolve independently, and later template fixes do not propagate automatically. Reconsider a shared component package only after repeated maintenance across real sites demonstrates a common owner is worthwhile.
- Prove the extracted starter by using it to seed Eon's site. Do not migrate or refactor Nova as part of this issue. Establish appropriate source/asset licensing for the extracted repository before redistribution.

Reference gate
Before design or code shape, read the current canonical product and distribution docs and the relevant docs/REFERENCES.md routes. Inspect primary sources and at least one comparable product website for product explanation, onboarding, accessibility, and visual hierarchy; record inspected identities/dates, adopted mechanisms, rejected alternatives, and the simplest sufficient build/hosting option in this bead. Consider eon-yvw (the deferred public interactive explainer) as optional related work; do not make it a prerequisite or reactivate it. Preserve source-license boundaries and avoid copying branding or unapproved source.

Acceptance
- A neutral starter builds independently, and Eon's site can be seeded from it without Nova-specific content, product dependencies, or recording tools. Preserve applicable accessibility, navigation, metadata, and overflow behavior in browser verification of the generated Eon site.
- Visitors can identify Eon's purpose and main benefit, inspect real product imagery, and find documentation, source, and the current supported installation path.
- Claims and examples match accepted product behavior and current platform/release status; website links point to canonical installation and release authorities rather than creating a second distribution graph.
- The site works at desktop and narrow mobile widths, with semantic structure, keyboard navigation, visible focus, readable contrast, and reduced-motion behavior if motion is used.
- Verify the built site in a real browser at both widths and exercise navigation and installation links. Record the revision, environment, and observations; document how to reproduce the chosen build and deployment.
- If publication is authorized, verify the actual published artifact and links at the approved destination. A local preview alone does not prove publication.

Boundary
This issue is website work only: no browser terminal client, remote access, accounts, payments, analytics, mailing list, new release channel, or product feature work. Do not require the interactive explainer to ship the initial website. Keep implementation and publication for a later activation; leave this planning issue open and unclaimed.

title: eon generations reports terminals=0 for an older-protocol generation that still holds terminals
description:
Observed 2026-10-31 on installed eon 0.1.9 (EONW 26): `eon generations` listed the previous generation g1-3ff7d443… (EONW 25 supervisor, eon 0.1.8) as 'previous … incompatible terminals=0'. Stopping it with its own build (0.1.8 libexec eon stop) then reported sessions session-10, session-11 and session-41 stopped: three live terminals (an idle Claude agent, a Codex pane, an overseer pane). The human and JSON listings (runtime/crates/eon-runtime/src/generation.rs, line ~658 prints terminals=) show 0 when the current Eon cannot query that supervisor.

Why it matters: a person or agent reading the listing concludes stopping the old generation loses nothing (AGENTS.md rule 5: agents read workspace state as data; this datum is wrong).

Fix direction: when the supervisor speaks an older EONW, report the terminal count as unknown (JSON null, human 'terminals=?'), or derive it from data that does not need the supervisor's protocol (e.g. the generation's session sockets), whichever the generation contract allows; check the owning contract (EON-C for generations/stop) before changing output. Acceptance: a test with an incompatible live generation holding terminals never prints terminals=0.

## Current schema and boundary evidence

At dcaef1c runtime/crates/eon-runtime/src/generation.rs:1002 failed_generation uses an empty sessions vector when inspection fails; :1085 generations_human prints its length; :1133 generations_json emits a terminals array, not a numeric count. window_json at :1189 and window_human consume the same record, so the sibling window listing must be covered too. The original "JSON null" suggestion is a schema proposal, not permission to replace a numeric field that does not exist.

Draft EON-C11/EON-C23 listing semantics for known-empty versus unknown terminal data and obtain exact output/JSON approval first. Prefer one owner of availability in GenerationRecord and preserve live incompatible/unreachable state, labels, stop safeguards and old-generation lifecycle delegation. Do not treat socket enumeration as an exact count unless its ownership/freshness is proved.

Acceptance: incompatible live generation with a terminal, temporarily unreachable generation, compatible empty generation and compatible nonempty generation are distinguishable in both human and JSON generations/window listings. Unknown never claims zero or a known empty array without an explicit unknown indicator agreed by the contract; genuine zero remains zero. Preserve failure/refusal behavior and keep stop conservative. One focused record-format regression and an isolated old/new installed observation follow the current lifecycle/CLI proof route; no compatibility codec is added by this bead.
