title: Use workspace and terminal consistently in Eon product terminology
description:
## Contract
Use workspace for the collection of tabs and panes, tab for a directory-based grouping, pane for the visual view, and terminal for one persistent Orbit-backed PTY/process/terminal-state instance. Product README, guides, launcher copy, help, human CLI output and Eon-owned diagnostics use this vocabulary consistently. Closing a native window detaches; Stop ends its terminals.

## Ownership and scope
Eon owns product vocabulary and documentation; the existing private Runtime CLI/output owners project it. Preserve session-N IDs, socket paths, JSON session/sessions keys, EONW/ORBS/management fields, symbolic error codes, existing lifecycle and Eon Sessions repository/component identity. Record this technical-to-product mapping explicitly rather than adding aliases, migrating live state or inventing a larger Session namespace. Child protocol names and historical proof identities stay exact. No feature, platform expansion, repository rename, beta release or supervisor interruption.

## Prerequisites and reference gate
User selected workspace/tab/pane/terminal on 2026-10-07 after comparison. Eon baseline 8578cf81275a2a61eefdc0d4cc5a72cb1485f904; Runtime 9780ccff908a7e5e506351ad017f219697e17681. title: Wrap directional tab and pane traversal at workspace edges
description:
## User-visible contract

Consumer: one local Eon workspace user.

Trigger: the user invokes semantic focus left, right, up, or down through the CLI or the existing Venus shortcuts while the selected tab or pane is at that ordered axis edge.

Result:
- With at least two tabs, left from the first tab selects the last tab and right from the last tab selects the first.
- With at least two panes in the active tab, up from the first pane selects the last pane and down from the last pane selects the first.
- Non-edge movement keeps its current adjacent-target behavior.
- Moving between tabs preserves each tab own selected pane.

With only one target on an axis, the direction remains unavailable and does not report a successful self-focus. A pending tab with no pane, modal directory picker, unknown identity, or invalid workspace state retains its existing bounded failure and last accepted topology.

The user selected circular edge traversal on 2026-08-26. This changes EON-C8 current direction-without-target and non-wrapping behavior; it creates no new EONW version, action, keybinding, or child contract.

## Ownership and evidence

Eon workspace focus policy is the sole owner. Venus continues to emit the existing semantic directional actions and render the resulting authoritative EONW snapshot. Orbit Sessions, PTYs, terminal state, pane lifetime, and working directories are untouched.

Current crates/eon/src/workspace.rs uses checked subtraction and explicit upper-bound failures in focus_direction. README documents traversal "without wrapping", and the original eon-pxn.1 proof explicitly rejected wrapping. The new behavior belongs at that shared Eon owner rather than in CLI or Venus callers.

## Reference gate

Required before code: current AGENTS.md; EON-C8; eon-pxn.1 historical decision/proof; focus_direction, dispatch, CLI parsing, process-level action checks, pending-tab picker rules, and exact current Venus VEN-C8 shortcut consumer. Inspect exact current Zellij directional-focus wrapping only as a comparable interaction; copy no code or broader layout behavior.

Rejected: per-caller wrapping, Venus-owned topology, configurable wrap policy, cross-axis traversal, arbitrary layout graphs, focus history, new keybindings, protocol changes, and dependencies.

## Scope boundary

In scope: Eon directional focus transition policy, focused deterministic and process-level proof, EON-C8/current docs/changelog, README LOC, exact Nix build/profile refresh, and one installed native observation.

Out of scope: focus-by-ID behavior, pane/tab creation or deletion, picker modal policy, reordering, split trees, simultaneous panes, new shortcuts, Orbit/Venus code, configuration, persistence, or platform expansion.

## Acceptance Criteria

The structured acceptance_criteria field is authoritative. Both axes wrap only when at least two targets exist, ordinary movement and failure atomicity remain intact, and the existing CLI/Venus action path is proved without a protocol or keybinding change.
design:
1. Write one deterministic red check at the existing Workspace action owner covering both axes, both edges, ordinary adjacent movement, remembered per-tab pane selection, and the one-target failure.
2. Change only focus_direction. Use the existing ordered vectors and selected indices directly; add no abstraction, configuration, or dependency.
3. Preserve dispatch atomicity and current errors for empty/pending axes, modal picker restrictions, unknown IDs, duplicate request handling, and invalid state.
4. Prove the existing control/CLI projection returns the wrapped authoritative snapshot. No EONW or Venus protocol change is expected.
5. Update EON-C8 and current user documentation, build the exact Nix candidate, refresh the active eon profile without restarting live supervisors, and dogfood the existing Venus shortcuts on a fresh isolated surface.
acceptance_criteria:
1. With at least two tabs, left from index zero selects the final tab and right from the final tab selects index zero. Intermediate left/right movement remains adjacent and every tab retains its selected pane.
2. With at least two panes in the active tab, up from index zero selects the final pane and down from the final pane selects index zero. Intermediate up/down movement remains adjacent and no other tab changes.
3. With exactly one tab or one pane, directional focus on that axis returns the existing unavailable failure and leaves the topology byte-for-byte unchanged.
4. Pending tabs with no pane, an active directory picker, unknown/stale identities, duplicate requests, invalid transitions, and malformed actions retain bounded failures with no partial mutation.
5. Focus movement never starts, stops, detaches, replaces, or changes an Orbit Session, pane directory, tab directory, picker, or child process.
6. CLI human and JSON output plus the existing Venus shortcuts consume the same wrapped Eon action result. No new keybinding, action value, EONW version, compatibility adapter, configuration, dependency, or child-repository edit is introduced.
7. The focused red/green transition check, affected process-level workspace control check, locked Rust checks, manifest check, Nix build, installed profile refresh, fresh native dogfood, README LOC, EON-C8, changelog after acceptance, and git diff pass on one immutable candidate.
8. Profile refresh preserves live supervisors and Sessions; no running Eon process is restarted without explicit user authorization.
notes: Priority P1: high-frequency workspace ergonomics, but lower urgency than the P0 continuous-output scrollback regression. Independent of the scrollback fix; no false dependency is added.

Adopt only circular ordered-edge interaction. Reject its source, geometry, MoveFocusOrTab cross-axis behavior, host bubbling, protocols, and broader layout model.
- Chosen mechanism: change only focus_direction using the existing indices and vector lengths. Require at least two targets before any wrapped or adjacent transition. Add no helper, abstraction, configuration, dependency, or compatibility surface.

title: Restore link hover highlight and target preview in Eon
description:
## Why

Lucca reported on 2026-10-19 that hovering a link in Eon no longer highlights it, while Ctrl+click
still opens it. Lucca sees this in the installed `eon` and in their Eon build with a modified Orbit
("eon-bend"/"eon-bead"), which they are using now. VEN-C5 (venus/docs/CONTRACTS.md) requires "The
hovered link is highlighted and its escaped target is shown with Open and Copy actions", and
venus/docs/INTERACTION.md says the same. Ctrl+click opens only the current hovered target, so hover
detection still works; only the hover presentation is missing.

## Evidence (edge d4960d4, source reading only, not reproduced yet)

- Hover focus: application.rs `pointer_link`, `inspect_pointer_link`, `focused_link`. The highlight
  is `highlighted_link = self.focused_link()` and is passed to `Renderer::set_hyperlink`
  (application.rs ~2694, ~2724), which is the same focus Ctrl+click uses.
- Drawing: render.rs `build_hyperlink` draws a 1px hollow rectangle (137,180,250) around the link in
  the workspace path, after the scene rectangles and before the card separators and outlines.
- Target preview: `link_status` becomes the status line through `status()`.
- Recent candidate causes, all on 2026-10-18: ab697a2 (panes drawn as gapped rounded cards, with the
  shortcut hints moved bare below the cards) and the flush-sheet commits before it (00e282d,
  cca9f14). Hypotheses to test: the status line or notice that carried the target preview is no
  longer drawn in workspace mode; the outline is clipped or covered under the new card geometry;
  hover no longer triggers a redraw.
- First step: find out whether the outline, the target preview, or both are missing, then bisect
  with ab697a2^ if needed.

## Contract

VEN-C5, unchanged. This restores existing behavior; no contract edit.

## Acceptance

- In an installed Eon workspace on Linux, hovering an OSC 8 link draws its highlight and shows its
  escaped target. Ctrl+click and Ctrl+Shift+C still work.
- This also holds with pane frames on and in a non-first column.

## Verification

- A focused render or application test that would have failed on the regression, if the cause is
  deterministic logic (AP-TEST-001: name the failure it catches).
- One isolated installed dogfood observation of hover, highlight and target preview (for example
  `printf '\e]8;;https://example.com\e\\link\e]8;;\e\\\n'`), plus the profile refresh.

## Scope boundary

Restore VEN-C5 hover presentation only. Heuristic URL detection, new schemes and restyling the
highlight are out of scope. The "eon-bend" variant is not in this repository; confirming it there
is a dogfood note, not a change.

Portability: neutral (Venus rendering).
close_reason: Not a regression: VEN-C5 OSC 8 hover, highlight, preview and actions work in stock Eon (isolated reproduction, see comments). The real gap is plain-text URLs, which Lucca decided should highlight; tracked in eon-nlcy.

comments.author: lucca
comments.text: Narrowed (Lucca, 2026-10-19): hovering a link changes nothing. The outline and the target preview are both missing, while Ctrl+click still opens the link. Source reading (edge d4960d4, not reproduced): CursorMoved calls inspect_pointer_link, which sets links.focus from pointer_link() and calls refresh_client_view; the Ctrl press path calls the same pointer_link(). So both use the same hit test, and the likely break is between hover focus and presentation: hover does not trigger a redraw or presentation update, or focus is cleared before the frame (refresh_client_view clears it when focused_link() is None; the CursorMoved over-scrollback branch sets it to None). First check: log links.focus and highlighted_link on hover in an isolated session before bisecting from ab697a2^.

comments.author: lucca
comments.text: Narrowed (Lucca, 2026-10-19, in eon-bead = Eon composed with /home/lucca/pjs/eon/bend-orbit 220c71bc): running `'https://example.com' | ansi link --text 'example'` in Nushell 0.113.1 leaves a blank line. The text inside the OSC 8 link is not drawn at all, so there is nothing to hover. Nushell emits a correct sequence (checked: ESC ]8;;https://example.com ESC \ example ESC ]8;; ESC \). Ctrl+click on links Lucca saw earlier opened them with no 'Opening link…' notice, so the opener was probably the program in the terminal, not Venus. Source reading finds no hyperlink-specific text filtering in Venus scene/render or in either Orbit's frame builder (orbit/src/presentation.rs, bend-orbit src/frame.rs). Next discriminator: the same command in the installed stock-Orbit eon. Blank there too means a Venus or stock Orbit regression (this bead); visible there means a bend-orbit defect, which belongs in bend-orbit.

comments.author: lucca
comments.text: Reproduction (2026-10-19, edge 5dbd53c, installed profile /nix/store/syncqqchdqxxz2lx0riz019yv6q0gyqa-eon-0.1.1, isolated headless Sway 1.12 at 1280x720, wdotool pointer): a script printing OSC 8 links with ST and BEL terminators renders 'before example after' and 'bel belink end'. Hovering 'example' draws the blue outline and the status shows 'https://example.com / Ctrl+click Open · Ctrl+Shift+C Copy'. VEN-C5 hover presentation works in stock Eon, so no Venus regression is reproduced. Lucca's blank line came from typing the command into interactive Nushell (the same bytes from nu -c are correct); why interactive nu printed nothing is unexplained and outside Eon. The links Lucca hovered were probably plain-text URLs opened by the program itself (Ctrl+click showed no Venus notice); VEN-C5 deliberately excludes heuristic URL detection. Orbit's TERM=eon/COLORTERM=truecolor has been unchanged since 2586d7c (2026-10-14). Not checked: eon-bead (bend-orbit) under the same script.

title: Help never names config.toml: config-path prints only the directory
description:
## Report (Lucca, 2026-11-02)

"the help does not say what should the config file be named. only the dir where it is."

`eon --help` lists `config-path  Create and print the config root`, and `eon config-path` prints `/home/lucca/.config/eon`. Neither names the settings file. Only docs/CONFIGURATION.md says settings live in `config.toml`, so a user who reads the help is left guessing which file to create or edit inside that directory.

## Contract

A person or agent reading `eon --help`, or running the config command, learns the settings file's exact name and full path without opening the docs. `config-path` is a CLI surface scripts may rely on (stdout is the root directory today), so any change to its output, or a new command or flag such as printing the file path, goes through the CLI contract that owns it, with old behaviour kept or the change approved. Lucca has auto-approved everything this session (2026-11-02), contract text included.

## Scope

- Help text names `config.toml` beside `config-path` (and `config defaults`).
- Give a direct way to get the file path (for example `eon config-path --file`, or a second printed line on a TTY only), choosing the shape that does not break scripts that read the directory.
- Keep docs/CONFIGURATION.md and docs/USAGE.md aligned; changelog entry.

## Acceptance

Help output names config.toml; the chosen command prints the full settings-file path; existing `eon config-path` stdout for scripts is unchanged unless the contract says otherwise; focused CLI test plus the affected build.
close_reason: eon config-path --file prints the config.toml path; help names config.toml. Proof and ledger in the landing comment.

title: Clear a ProgramStatus request whose reply header fails to decode
description:
## Report

A reviewer on eon-agent-sidebar-yx8.6 (eon-b6, 2026-10-22, edge e87b9f8) found this outside that
diff, in code eon-agent-sidebar-yx8.10 landed (7267b8a, "Read ProgramStatus replies on Runtime
leases without misreading Stop or EOF"). Lucca approved filing it (2026-10-22).

## Defect (reviewer finding; confirm first)

If a ProgramStatus reply header fails to decode, `advance_program_status` (eon-runtime) leaves the
request in flight. That terminal's program status then stays stale, because no new request is
sent, and a later Stop drain on that lease returns the decode error instead of stopping cleanly.

## Expected

A malformed or undecodable ProgramStatus reply ends that request: it's logged, the request
clears, and the terminal's status becomes "unknown" or keeps its last value under the EON-C31 rule.
Status polling resumes on a later poll. Stop is never blocked or failed by an old bad reply.
If the lease itself is no longer trustworthy after a framing error, it's retired the documented
way, not left half-open.

## Contract

EON-C31 (agent attention, Runtime model) and the lease and Stop rules yx8.10 relies on. Check
whether the intended failure behavior is already stated. If not, bring Lucca the exact wording
before code.

## Scope

In scope: confirming the path with a focused unit test (red first), the fix in
`advance_program_status` and its Stop drain interaction, and the contract text if needed.
Out of scope: the ProgramStatus wire format, and sidebar presentation (yx8.7 and yx8.3).

## Acceptance

- A Runtime unit test feeds an undecodable reply header. The request clears, the next poll sends a
  fresh request, and Stop on that lease succeeds.
- No change to well-formed replies.

## Verification

`nix develop -c eon-test -p eon-runtime`, plus fmt and clippy.
close_reason: An Orbit that stops on its own signal, and any unsolicited, undecodable or unexpected bytes on a terminal's lease, now affect only that terminal; the supervisor no longer fails (EON-C15 text approved by Lucca 2026-10-22). Proven by eon-test (eon-runtime, eon) and the eon and eonbase package builds on tree cdf3d2d.

comments.author: lucca
comments.text: Escalation (Lucca, 2026-10-22 ~22:15 -03): raised to P1 and widened. At 22:06:58 Lucca's supervisor g1-caca13d0 (installed ckisr53k, EONW 15) failed with 'supervisor failed: terminal sent an unsolicited management result' (~/.local/state/eon/logs/g1-caca13d0b514d3f810ccd8ca773d498b-1792695618-251291.log). That error comes from session_finished (runtime/crates/eon-runtime/src/sessions.rs:1356), whose `?` carries it up to the supervisor loop. The window closed (VEN-C14), and the terminals were orphaned in Orbit with no supervisor. The trigger: the overseer sent SIGTERM to a Claude agent (eon-a2) in one terminal; about ten earlier SIGTERMs that day didn't crash it, so it's a race. Inference, unconfirmed: a ProgramStatus reply was in flight, or arrived after the request state cleared, when the terminal ended. Widened goal: no per-terminal management anomaly (undecodable header, unsolicited or late reply, framing error) ever fails the supervisor. It's confined to that terminal: logged, status unknown, lease retired the documented way, terminal end still reaped and reported. Acceptance gains a deterministic Runtime test that writes an unsolicited reply byte before EOF on a terminal's lease and asserts the supervisor keeps running and the other terminals stay unaffected. Contract check: EON-C31 and the EON-C11/EON-C14 failure rules. If the 'fatal' behavior is contracted anywhere, bring Lucca the wording. Runs before yx8.7 and shn4.2.

comments.author: lucca
comments.text: Trigger confirmed (overseer, 2026-10-22). The 22:06:58 kill was `kill -TERM $(pgrep -f 'claude prime, then continue eon-agent-sidebar-yx8.7' | head -1)`. pgrep -f matches full command lines, and the Orbit host's ends with `-- claude prime, then continue ...`. pgrep lists PIDs in ascending order, so head -1 picked the Orbit host (the parent), not claude. The earlier kills that day took claude's PID from ~/.claude/sessions and logged 'ended with status 143'. Mechanism (source, edge 6edf631): under ORB-C12, Orbit takes a host SIGTERM as an explicit stop. orbit/src/host.rs finish_management(ExplicitStop) writes an ExplicitStop tombstone and calls reply_stopped (orbit/src/management.rs:387), which writes an unrequested Stopped(tombstone) on the held lease. Runtime's EOF probe (session_finished, sessions.rs:1356) reads that as 'unsolicited management result' and its ? fails the supervisor. Even with no Stopped bytes, the probe finalizes with NaturalExit, and wait_and_finalize_tombstone rejects the ExplicitStop tombstone ('final record does not match'), which is also fatal. Separately, a ProgramStatus header that fails to decode makes advance_program_status return Err with the request left in flight, so every later EOF probe or Stop drain on that lease errors (the original finding). Deterministic repro: SIGTERM the Orbit host of a leased_orbit test run.

comments.author: lucca
comments.text: Red (edge 6edf631 plus two new tests only; nix develop -c eon-test -p eon-runtime ends_only_its; x86_64 Linux): an_orbit_stopped_by_a_signal_ends_only_its_terminal fails with 'terminal sent an unsolicited management result' after SIGTERM to a real leased Orbit host, which is the production error. an_undecodable_or_unsolicited_result_ends_only_its_request fails with 'invalid terminal program status result: invalid management magic' from session_finished. Proposed EON-C15 wording is with Lucca (Result: an Orbit that stops on its own termination signal is reconciled like a natural exit; Important failures: lease anomalies fail only that terminal's in-flight request, and the lease is kept). The fix waits for approval.

comments.author: lucca
comments.text: Decision (Lucca, 2026-10-22): 'approve' accepts all four recommendations. (1) The EON-C15 wording as proposed, Result plus Important failures. (2) After an anomaly the lease is kept, not retired: dropping it would orphan a live run (ORB-C13), and Stop already waits for the tombstone. (3) No separate log line; the terminal's end is already logged. (4) One CHANGELOG line.

comments.author: lucca
comments.text: Review ledger (candidate tree 034b89a on edge 6edf631): pass 1 converged. Claude found 0 blocking and 4 nits, not applied: a stricter is_err assert in the undecodable test; the tests drive session_finished, not the supervisor loop; a leftover-garbage Stop reads 'wrong stop result' and fails without waiting for the tombstone; Orbit's reply_stopped can interleave with a partly flushed reply. Codex gpt-6.1-sol xhigh found 0. The repro of the 22:06:58 trigger is an_orbit_stopped_by_a_signal_ends_only_its_terminal, which SIGTERMs a real leased Orbit host: red before the fix with the production error, green after. Final proof after rebase (overseer, AGENTS lifecycle route): nix develop -c eon-test -p eon-runtime -p eon, plus nix build #default #eonbase (the package check runs the release-Orbit Stop-under-load test).

comments.author: lucca
comments.text: Proof, tree cdf3d2d, the eon-wt6l change rebased onto edge be5273a8; x86_64 Linux, sandboxed nix develop, CARGO_BUILD_JOBS=6. (1) nix develop -c eon-test -p eon-runtime -p eon passes: eon-runtime 80 passed, 1 ignored; eon workspace_control 39 passed. Includes both new tests, red before the fix (see the red comment). (2) nix build path:<tree>#default #eonbase passes: eon-0.1.1 /nix/store/j283p7l9paw4cjkjchbabjf8kws7i1r9 and eonbase-0.1.1 /nix/store/3npi3gnrdnmac3s6xx3lsw1apvck96qy. The eon package check ran all 81 eon-runtime tests, including the release-Orbit stop_waits_only_orbit_answer_time_for_an_in_flight_reply_under_pty_load: median 86us, p99 802us, max 1.23ms. (3) Earlier on the same code: cargo fmt --check and clippy -D warnings for eon-runtime are clean. The checks left the tree unchanged. Not run: the profile refresh (Lucca runs it after landing) and installed dogfood of a signalled Orbit in a live window, which is not to be triggered there.

title: Calmer chrome: fewer style families across the bar, sidebar and hints
description:
## Why

Lucca, 2026-11-10: "eon has a few different styles going on. tabs have one style, widgets another,
clock and eon version another, and the panel titles another ... it looks good but it makes the whole
thing less cohesive" and "its ok for elements that have different meanings to have different looks.
the problem is maybe doing it in excess".

A read of Venus's chrome code and a screenshot of his window (2026-11-10, commit 040cb56) found one
shared colour palette (venus/src/render/palette.rs) but no shared shapes, sizes or text styles:
- shapes: filled capsules (tabs), outline-only capsules (widgets), an outlined circle (`?`), notched
  title tabs, radius-6 rectangles (sidebar rows, keycaps, hovers), bare text (clock, version);
- two fonts in the top bar: the interface sans, and the terminal monospace for CPU, RAM and disk;
- three ways to mark "selected": a fill step (tabs), a neutral outline (sidebar row), a focus-colour
  frame (panes);
- four accent hues: focus purple, mint, cyan (clock and version only), light blue (key hints only).

The elements differ in about four meanings (something you select, a reading, a container's label, a
hint), so about half of that variety carries none. Rex, for comparison, uses one neutral surface
ramp, one sans text style in three greys and one accent, and shows state by brightness, not shape.

## Decisions (Lucca, 2026-11-10, answering a numbered list in his Fable session)

- One font for bar readings: "ok". Clock and version are excluded and stay exactly as they are:
  "they look really good how they are, and they fill up the two bottom corners that would otherwise
  be empty".
- Widgets as quiet filled capsules without outlines: "ok".
- One way to say "selected" (fill for list items, focus frame for the pane with the keyboard): "ok".
- Accents trimmed to roles: "ok".
- Same label pattern for tab, sidebar heading and pane title: "ok".
- `?` loses its ring: "ok, but im not so sure". Ships with the bar change; he judges it live.
- A shared module for shapes and text styles, first: "agree".
- Panel titles: NOT decided. He loves the double notches (see eon-ve7dc) and asked whether they can

title: Name Venus chrome radii, paddings and text styles once, with no visible change
description:
## Why

Venus's chrome colours come from one role-named palette (venus/src/render/palette.rs, eon-3bhr), but
every radius, padding and text style is an inline fraction of `metrics.padding` repeated per call
site. That is how the chrome grew six unrelated shapes (parent epic). Naming them once makes the two
visible children a few lines each and stops new chrome inventing its own values. It also prepares
the themes epic (eon-eon-themes-or3q).

Contract: none changes. Presentation is a feature (docs/AGENT-RULES.md, Contract-Driven Method);
this is a behaviour-preserving refactor of how VEN-C8, VEN-C18, VEN-C21, VEN-C24 and VEN-C30 chrome
is drawn. Approved by Lucca, 2026-11-10: "agree".

## Evidence (line numbers at 040cb56; verify before relying on them)

- venus/src/render.rs:61-67: `DEFAULT_METRICS {width 10, height 18, font_size 16, padding 12}`.
- Capsule radius `visual.height / 2.0`: venus/src/render/chrome.rs:2765 (tabs), :1682 (widgets).
- `padding / 2.0` (6 px): chrome.rs:3188 (title hover), :3325 (header buttons), :1903 (sidebar rows),
  :2378 (tooltip), :2691 (keycaps), :2426 (dialog chips).
- `padding / 3.0` (4 px): chrome.rs:2499 (dialog focused row), venus/src/scene.rs:2406
  (`title_tab_rise`), scene.rs:2369 (`tab_gap`).
- Card gap and card radius, round(padding*2/3) = 8: scene.rs:2446.
- Text styles: `DrawStyleKind` in render.rs:2716-2769 (Status, Monospace, PopupLabel, Heading);
  `chrome_title_metrics` at scene.rs:2480 is the only shared text metric.

## Scope

In scope:
- One Venus module (beside palette.rs) that names the chrome's radii (capsule, card, inner),
  paddings/gaps and text styles, each defined once as a function of the metrics.
- Every chrome draw and layout site in venus/src/render/chrome.rs, venus/src/render.rs and
  venus/src/scene.rs uses those names instead of an inline fraction.

Out of scope:
- Any visible change: no value changes, no merged roles that differ today.
- New configuration keys. Colours (palette.rs already owns them).
- Terminal cell rendering.

## Acceptance

- No pixel changes: the existing Venus scene and render tests pass unchanged, with no golden or
  expected-geometry edits.
- `grep` finds no remaining `padding / 2.0`, `padding / 3.0` or `height / 2.0` radius literals at
  chrome call sites; each is a named token.
- The bead records the final token list (name, value at default metrics, where used).

## Verification

- Venus suites through `nix develop -c eon-test <nextest filter for the Venus crate>` (see
  docs/DEVELOPMENT.md); never run them inside a live Eon session's environment.
- fmt and clippy clean for the Venus crate.

## Stop Conditions

- Stop if a call site needs a different value to keep today's pixels than its neighbours share;
  give it its own named token and record why, do not round it into another.
- Stop if the change needs a contract text edit.

## Maintenance Notes

- Two roles may share a value and still be separate names, as palette.rs does for outlines.
- Rejected: exposing these as configuration now. The fixed-look policy in docs/CONFIGURATION.md
  (eon-27deg, eon-2ibdd, eon-u5uv2, eon-whjhd) stands; themes own that later.

title: Top bar: readings in the interface font, widgets as quiet filled capsules, plain ?
description:
## Why

The top bar mixes two fonts and two capsule recipes. Tabs are filled capsules in the interface sans;
widgets are outline-only capsules, and the CPU, RAM and disk readings inside them use the terminal
monospace while the quota chips beside them use the sans. `?` alone has an outlined circle. Five
rings and a second font compete with the tabs for no meaning (parent epic).

Approved by Lucca, 2026-11-10: one font for readings "ok"; filled quiet capsules without outlines
"ok"; plain `?` "ok, but im not so sure" (he judges it live after landing).

Contract: VEN-C21 (Native Eon Bar session header) describes outline-only widgets. Presentation is a
feature (docs/AGENT-RULES.md, Contract-Driven Method): amend the VEN-C21 wording, CFG and
venus/docs/PRESENTATION.md to the new look, citing the approval above. No trigger, CLI, wire or
lifecycle clause changes.

## Evidence (line numbers at 040cb56; verify)

- Widget layout venus/src/scene.rs:3584-3869; paint venus/src/render/chrome.rs:2815-2909; outline
  `push_bar_widget` chrome.rs:1674 with `CHIP_OUTLINE (86,106,126)` at `border_width`, inset 4 px
  (chrome.rs:1664).
- CPU, RAM, disk: terminal monospace, fixed 6 cells + 24 px, coloured by load (chrome.rs:296);
  icons in venus/src/system.rs:13-15.
- Bar controls `+`, `?`, `×`: scene.rs:597, chrome.rs:2910-2990; only `?` draws an outlined circle.
- Tab fills: `TAB_IDLE (30,40,54)`, `TAB_HOVER`, `TAB_SELECTED` in venus/src/render/palette.rs:36-38.

## Scope

In scope:
- Every bar widget (quota chips, CPU, RAM, disk, session label, and any other reading in
  `[bar] widgets`) is a filled capsule in the unselected-tab fill, with no outline.
- CPU, RAM and disk readings use the interface (Status) text style. Their slot keeps a fixed width
  sized to the widest value so the bar does not shift as numbers change.
- `?` draws as a bare glyph with the same hover treatment as `+` and `×`.
- docs/CONFIGURATION.md: `border_width` no longer affects widgets; update the text. CHANGELOG.md.

Out of scope and unchanged:
- The clock and version: bottom corners, terminal monospace, their cyan. Lucca: "they look really
  good how they are, and they fill up the two bottom corners".
- Tabs, text and load/pace colours, icons, tooltips, hover and keyboard-focus behaviour, widget
  order and `[bar] widgets`, hit targets, accessible names, CLI paths.
- Panel titles and notches.

## Acceptance

- At scale 1, 1.125 and 2 no widget draws an outline at rest; its fill equals an unselected tab's.
- A CPU reading going from 9% to 100% does not move any other bar item.
- Keyboard focus on a widget or bar control still shows the mint outline.
- Text contrast of every reading colour (secondary, load and pace colours) against the new fill is
  recorded in the bead; flag any below 4.5:1 instead of changing a colour silently.

## Configurability (rule 6)

The fill stays a fixed palette role: the fixed-look policy in docs/CONFIGURATION.md applies and the
themes epic (eon-eon-themes-or3q) owns colour settings. The interface font is eon-l41xa's setting;
readings follow it.

## Verification

- Venus scene and render tests for the bar, through `nix develop -c eon-test` (docs/DEVELOPMENT.md).
- After landing and the profile refresh, Lucca looks at it in his window.

## Stop Conditions

- Stop if the sans face cannot give a stable slot width without a per-digit layout change.
- Stop if a reading colour fails contrast on the fill and fixing it means a new colour.

## Maintenance Notes

- Depends on the shared tokens child: use its capsule and text style names.
- Rejected alternative: widgets as bare icon and text with no capsule. Calmer, but Lucca likes that
  tabs and widgets share a format.

- Sidebar rows: layout venus/src/scene.rs:2526-2800, paint venus/src/render/chrome.rs:2587-2684 and

title: Mark the current Agents sidebar row with a focus-colour outline instead of the grey fill
description:
## Why

Lucca, 2026-11-11 (eon-desk): "i dont like the greyed out background of selected panes in the
sidebar rows. its light gray. the dark gray on hover is okayish. my suggestion instead is outlines".
eon-wuau8.3 gave the current Agents sidebar row the selected tab's fill (TAB_SELECTED
(79,96,114), adapted to 3:1). As a full-row block it is nearly as bright as the panel outline
CARD_OUTLINE (86,106,126) and reads heavy.

Design approved by Lucca ("ahhh i like it") after this discussion:
- Current row: a 1 px outline in the configured focus colour (`[terminal] focus_color`, default
  purple), the same colour that frames the selected pane, so the row visibly points at the pane
  you are in. No fill.
- Hover: keep today's dark CHROME_HIGHLIGHT fill (40,54,70), on current and non-current rows alike.
- Keyboard focus: keep the mint outline; on the current row draw it 1 px inside the purple one so
  both stay visible.
- No mint pressed flash on sidebar rows, if one exists: the outline appearing is the click feedback.
- Tabs keep their selected fill. This is a deliberate sidebar exception to eon-wuau8.3's "one
  selection treatment": a tab reads as raised, a row as pointed-at.

Why these choices (from the discussion): hover and selection use separate channels (fill vs
outline) so a click never swaps one grey for another in place. Mouse enters: fill appears. Click:
outline appears, fill stays. Mouse leaves: fill goes, outline stays. Rejected: panel-grey outline
(a grey ring inside the grey sidebar card reads as structure, not selection); mint outline (mint
means keyboard focus only, per eon-wuau8.3); hover as an outline (two outlines toggling with
pointer movement is noisy). Considered and not chosen: a 2-3 px focus-colour bar on the row's
left edge. A short hover fade (~100 ms) is optional and left out unless the live result feels
harsh; adding it would need a setting under rule 6.

Contract: VEN-C30 (agent sidebar) describes the current-row fill in its Current row clause and
Status. Presentation is a feature (docs/AGENT-RULES.md, Contract-Driven Method): amend the
wording to match and cite this approval; no behaviour clause changes.

## Evidence (line numbers at 481fe27; verify)

- `venus/src/render/chrome.rs:918` `push_attention_row_surface`: current row fills
  TAB_SELECTED blended to 3:1; hover/focus fill CHROME_HIGHLIGHT with a contrast-ladder fallback;
  `row.focused` adds an ACCENT outline; current takes precedence over hover (no hover fill on the
  current row today); text colours and the badge backing derive from the fill.
- `venus/src/render/chrome.rs:834` `Spinners::new(turning, focus_color)`: the focus colour is
  already passed into chrome painting.
- `venus/src/render/chrome.rs:5139` test
  `selected_and_hovered_sidebar_rows_keep_readable_fill_focus_text_and_badges`.
- `venus/docs/CONTRACTS.md:2308-2316` (VEN-C30 status) and `:2437-2442` (Current row clause).
- `venus/docs/PRESENTATION.md:503-515` (Agents sidebar row colours).

## Scope

In scope:
- Sidebar row painting in `venus/src/render/chrome.rs` and its tests.
- VEN-C30 wording, `venus/docs/PRESENTATION.md`, `CHANGELOG.md`, `venus/CHANGELOG.md`.

Out of scope and unchanged:
- Tabs, pane frames, popup frames, hints, bar widgets.
- Row layout, geometry, text roles of non-current rows, badges' attention colours.
- Accessible names ("popup", "current").
- Configurable colours: palette roles stay fixed per the fixed-look policy in
  docs/CONFIGURATION.md; the focus colour is already `[terminal] focus_color`.

## Acceptance

- The current row has no fill at rest and a 1 px outline in the configured focus colour, adapted
  only as needed for 3:1 against the sidebar background.
- Hovering any row, including the current one, shows the CHROME_HIGHLIGHT fill; on the current row
  the purple outline stays visible over it.
- Keyboard focus on the current row shows both outlines (mint inside purple), distinguishable.
- Row text keeps 4.5:1 against whatever is behind it (terminal background or hover fill).
- Changing `focus_color` changes the current-row outline.
- No mint pressed state on sidebar rows.

## Verification

- Update the scene/render test at `chrome.rs:5139` to assert the states above (current: no fill,
  focus-colour outline; current+hover: both; current+keyboard: both outlines).
- `nix develop -c eon-test` over the workspace (not inside a live Eon session environment), plus
  `cargo fmt --check` and `cargo clippy --locked --all-targets -- -D warnings` for Venus.
- Installed: one dogfood observation after the overseer's profile refresh; Lucca judges it live
  (no capture gate).

## Stop Conditions

- Stop if the cited row painting has drifted materially from the Evidence.
- Stop if the focus colour fails 3:1 on light terminal backgrounds in a way adaptation cannot fix
  without changing the colour's hue; record the case and ask.
- Stop if the change needs a new configuration key.

## Maintenance Notes

- Parent eon-wuau8 (calmer chrome). This bead records the sidebar exception to eon-wuau8.3's
  single selection treatment.
- Review focus: contrast fallbacks for light and translucent terminal backgrounds, and that the
  badge backing still gets a readable disc when there is no fill.

title: Right-align the value in the CPU, RAM and disk bar chips; icon stays left
description:
## Why

Lucca, 2026-11-11 (eon-desk), with a screenshot of the CPU, RAM and disk chips reading "5%",
"50%", "49%": "these should not be left aligned". Each reading chip reserves the width of "100%"
so it never resizes, and the icon and value are drawn from the left, leaving a gap on the right
whenever the value is shorter than 100%.

Lucca chose option 1 ("i agree"): the icon stays at the left padding, the value is right-aligned
to the right padding. Rejected: centring the icon and value as a group (the icon jumps when the
value changes width, 9% to 10%); sizing each chip to its text (the bar shifts sideways as readings
change, which the reserved width exists to prevent).

Contract: none. Bar chip layout is presentation (a feature, docs/AGENT-RULES.md Contract-Driven
Method); update venus/docs/PRESENTATION.md's chip wording if it describes alignment.

- `venus/src/application.rs:1779` and `:2753`: `HeaderText::Reading` uses

- `venus/src/render/chrome.rs:583` `chip_label_box`, `:1993` `push_chip_label`: where the label is
  placed inside the chip.

## Scope

In scope:
- CPU, RAM and disk reading chips (`HeaderText::Reading`): value right-aligned within the

Out of scope:

title: Move bar chip grade colours from the text to a thin meter along each chip's bottom
description:
## Why

Lucca, 2026-11-11 (eon-desk), about the Eon Bar quota chips: "these colored fonts on grey
background, they look off for me". The chip text is coloured by grade (quota pace green to red,
`palette::QUOTA_PACE`; CPU, RAM and disk load yellow/orange/red), so the colour sits on the very
text being read. Saturated red or orange on the mid-grey chip fill reads muddy, and it goes against
eon-wuau8's calmer chrome (accents by role, not on text).

Lucca chose option 1 ("1 ok, do it, no mockup"): all chip text neutral, and a thin meter along the
bottom edge inside each chip carries the level and its colour. Rejected: tinting the whole chip fill
in warning grades (loud; two red capsules side by side today); a coloured dot at the chip's right
(less information). The provider icons (Codex white mark, Claude orange splat) are brand marks and
keep their colours. CPU, RAM and disk get the same meter so the bar reads as one system.

Contract: chips are presentation (a feature, docs/AGENT-RULES.md Contract-Driven Method). Amend the
wording that says the text carries the colour: venus/docs/CONTRACTS.md:2276 area (Claude chip
"pace colour" reason), venus/docs/PRESENTATION.md (Eon Bar), docs/USAGE.md:398-410 and
docs/CONFIGURATION.md:255-285 (levels "turn yellow/orange/red"). The configured levels and their
meaning do not change; only where the colour is drawn.

## Evidence (line numbers at 481fe27; verify)

- `venus/src/render/palette.rs:90` `QUOTA_PACE` (5 anchors, the red one chosen for 4.5:1 text on
  the chip fill) and `:102-104` `LOAD_NOTICE/HIGH/CRITICAL` (reuse pace colours).
- `venus/src/render/chrome.rs:297` `load_color` (Normal = SECONDARY_TEXT) and `:306`
  `quota_pace_color` (blend by shortfall).
- `venus/src/render/chrome.rs:1993` `push_chip_label` and `:583` `chip_label_box`: label placement.
- `venus/src/scene.rs:3898` reading chip width (eon-wuau8.5 right-aligns reading values; same
  chips).

## Scope

In scope:
- Quota chips (Codex, Claude, scoped Claude) and CPU, RAM, disk chips:
  - Text: neutral text roles, at least 4.5:1 on the chip fill.
  - Meter: a thin bar (about 2 px at scale 1, scaled) along the bottom inside the capsule, inset to
    clear the rounded corners, never past the chip's outline.
  - Meter length: the percentage the chip shows (quota: remaining; CPU, RAM, disk: in use). An
    empty track is not drawn, or is drawn at a quiet neutral step (agent's call, consistent across
    chips).
  - Meter colour: today's grade colour (quota pace blend; load colour, with CPU temperature as
    today). A quota window with no pace (missing reset) and a Normal load use a quiet neutral.
  - Stale ("old") readings dim the meter as they dim text today.
- Docs listed above; CHANGELOG.md.

Out of scope:
- Chip widths, order, yield order, tooltips and accessible text (they already say in words why a
  chip is coloured; keep that).
- Brand icon colours, clock and version chips, the thresholds and their configuration keys.

## Acceptance

- No chip draws its text in a grade colour; text meets 4.5:1 on the chip fill.
- Each graded chip shows a meter whose length matches its shown percentage (0% no fill, 100% full
  inner width) and whose colour matches today's grade colour for the same reading.
- The meter stays inside the capsule at scale 1 and 2, crisp, clear of rounded corners.
- Hover and screen-reader text unchanged.

## Verification

- Scene or render tests: text colour neutral; meter rect width proportional to the percentage;
  meter colour equals `quota_pace_color` / `load_color` for sample readings.
- `nix develop -c eon-test` over the workspace (not inside a live Eon session environment), plus
  Venus `cargo fmt --check` and `cargo clippy --locked --all-targets -- -D warnings`.
- Installed: one dogfood observation after the overseer's profile refresh; Lucca judges it live.

## Stop Conditions

- Stop if the meter cannot fit inside the chip without changing chip height or bar height; record
  the sizes and ask.
- Stop if it needs new configuration keys.

## Maintenance Notes

- Rule 6: the meter's look is a fixed palette/geometry choice under the fixed-look policy; the
  levels stay configurable as today.
- Runs after eon-wuau8.5 (same chips, label placement): rebase onto it.

## Planning reconciliation (2026-11-12, dcaef1c)

Current evidence: chrome.rs:297 load_color, :306 quota_pace_color, :583
chip_label_box, :2022 push_chip_label; scene.rs:3899 reading width. The old
481fe27 positions are historical. VEN-C26/VEN-C29 are retired presentation
history; appearance lives in PRESENTATION.md#eon-bar. Preserve retired proof
identities. Any live contract amendment still requires exact-text approval.

Missing/blocked/unknown readings must not invent a percentage meter; preserve
their text/accessibility behavior. Verify numeric 0/100%, stale dimming and scale
1/2 with the existing scene/render owner. The one approved meter recipe keeps
the bar coherent and bounds geometry variants; configured grade thresholds keep
their existing owner. Portability: neutral. Use the current render route (Tier 1,

title: Drop the dark disc behind attention spinners; adapt badge colour, square fallback only
description:
## Why

Lucca, 2026-11-11 (eon-desk): "and the spinners, i dislike the black background". Attention badges
(working/background spinner dots and the other attention glyphs) on tabs, edge badges and current
or hovered Agents sidebar rows sit on a near-black disc (`Backing::Disc(palette::BAR_BACKGROUND)`),
which also puts a circle around the square spinner.

Decision (Lucca: "ok, do it" on the desk's recommendation, choosing among A: drop the disc and
adapt the badge colour; B: make the backing a square; C: a combination):
- Draw badges with no backing; adapt the badge colour to 3:1 against the surface under it, as
  `Backing::Surface` already does for dots.
- Fallback only where the surface is unknown or 3:1 cannot be reached by blending (translucent
  cards, very light terminals): a rounded-square backing whose corners match the spinner's shape,
  in a quiet tone near the surface. Never near-black.
Rejected: B alone (a black square is still black).

Contract: badges are presentation (a feature, docs/AGENT-RULES.md Contract-Driven Method). Amend
venus/docs/PRESENTATION.md:512 ("its attention badge keeps the bar's dark disc") and any VEN-C30 /
tab wording about the disc.

## Evidence (line numbers at 481fe27; verify)

- `venus/src/render/chrome.rs:807` `enum Backing { Disc, Surface, Translucent }`.
- `venus/src/render/chrome.rs:848` `Spinners::push_badge`: Disc draws a `capsule_radius` circle;
  Surface draws none and blends dots with `blend_to_contrast(self.focus, under, 3.0)`;
  Translucent dots fall back to the bar disc.
- `venus/src/render/chrome.rs:2882`, `:2887`, `:2933`: tab and edge badges always use
  `Backing::Disc(palette::BAR_BACKGROUND)`.
- `venus/src/render/chrome.rs:953-958`: sidebar rows pick Disc for current rows and adapted fills.
- Tests near `:5235`, `:5451-5487` assert disc behaviour.

## Scope

In scope:
- Badge backing for tabs, edge badges and sidebar/inbox rows; the fallback square; non-dot glyph
  colours where they need adapting for 3:1.
- Tests and docs above; CHANGELOG.md.

Out of scope:
- Badge glyph shapes, sizes, animation and the attention state colours' meaning.
- Row and tab fills (eon-wuau8.4 changes the current sidebar row; this bead runs after it).

## Acceptance

- On opaque tabs (selected and unselected) and sidebar rows (resting, hovered, current), no backing
  shape is drawn and every badge keeps at least 3:1 against the surface under it.
- Where the fallback applies, the backing is a rounded square matched to the spinner, in a tone near
  the surface, never `BAR_BACKGROUND`.
- No near-black disc remains anywhere in the chrome.

## Verification

- Update the disc tests to assert no backing on opaque surfaces, 3:1 contrast for sample surfaces
  (selected tab fill, hover fill, dark and light terminal backgrounds), and the square fallback on
  translucent cards.
- `nix develop -c eon-test` over the workspace (not inside a live Eon session environment), plus
  Venus `cargo fmt --check` and `cargo clippy --locked --all-targets -- -D warnings`.
- Installed: one dogfood observation after the overseer's profile refresh; Lucca judges it live.

## Stop Conditions

  without changing its hue; record the case and ask.

## Maintenance Notes

- Blocked by eon-wuau8.4 (same sidebar row painting).
- Rule 6: fixed look under the fixed-look policy; no setting.

## Planning reconciliation (2026-11-12, dcaef1c)

Current backing evidence replaces old coordinates: chrome.rs:807 Backing,
:849 Spinners::push_badge, :984-987 sidebar backing, :2911/:2916/:2962 tab/edge
calls, tests near :5263 and :5551-5618; PRESENTATION.md:520. .4 is closed;
preserve its outline/hover behavior. Portability: neutral. The single approved
backing/contrast recipe bounds state variants while retaining configured focus
colour. Exact live VEN-C30 text still needs approval. Use current render proof:
Tier 1, local two-run Tier 2 comparison or named missing check, affected build,
reviews and one isolated installed observation. No glyph/animation redesign.

title: Copied wrapped text loses characters at row joins
description:
## Why

Lucca, 2026-10-21: text copied from an Eon terminal and pasted elsewhere came
out corrupted. Copy silently changes what the user copied, so pasted prompts,
commands and notes can be wrong without anyone noticing.

## Evidence

Lucca copied a four-bullet message (wrapped across several rows in the
terminal) and pasted it. The original and the paste differ at row joins:

- "It is a record of one issue's investigation, not a pattern guide" pasted as
  "It is a record of one isstern guide": 29 characters gone.
- "the smallest way to reuse the queries, as the issue asked" pasted as
  "the smallest way to reussked": 29 characters gone.
- "Some scenarios may be tested twice" pasted as "Swice": 29 characters gone.
- "has no description" pasted as "has nodescription", and "a quick check for"
  as "a quick checkfor": the space at a row join is gone.
- Every pasted line also starts with two spaces, the indentation as drawn.

Both patterns sit at points where one terminal row continues on the next, so
the copied text likely joins wrapped rows wrongly. The exact source program,
terminal width and selection gesture (drag, triple or quadruple click) are not
yet recorded.

Owners: Orbit owns selection boundaries and copied text through libghostty
(ORB-C9, "Authoritative bounded selection and copy"; spans and logical lines
cross soft wraps). Venus owns the selection gesture and clipboard delivery
(VEN-C7, VEN-C13).

## Scope

In scope: reproduce in an isolated Eon with text that wraps across rows
(including a program that redraws, such as Claude Code); find which layer
drops the text (the program's own drawing, libghostty's text extraction,
Orbit's frozen copy, or Venus's clipboard delivery); fix it at that owner, or
file it upstream if the cause is libghostty or the drawing program.

Out of scope: copy formatting choices (indentation, trailing whitespace) other
than lost characters; rich-text copy.

## Acceptance

- Copying wrapped text from an Eon terminal pastes exactly the characters
  shown, with nothing dropped at row joins, for drag, word, span and line
  selections.
- If the cause is outside Eon (the drawing program or libghostty), the bead
  records the evidence and the upstream issue instead.

## Verification

- A failing reproduction first (red), then green: an Orbit or Venus test at the
  owning layer if one exists, else a retained reproducer.
- One isolated installed observation of the copy and paste.

## Stop Conditions

- Stop for Lucca's approval before changing ORB-C9 or VEN-C7 text.
close_reason: Cause is outside Eon: Claude Code fullscreen selection loses text on drag autoscroll (anthropics/claude-code#83961), reproduced without Eon. Orbit host copy is exact.

comments.author: lucca
comments.text:
Investigation (claude, 2026-10-22 01:30 -03). Negative results so far, no reproduction:

- Routing: a plain drag in a mouse-tracking app (Claude Code fullscreen, Lucca's settings.json has "tui": "fullscreen") goes to the app; Orbit's host selection takes it only with Shift (orbit/src/selection.bend:38). So the copy may be Claude Code's own (OSC 52) or Orbit's.
- Orbit host copy (libghostty format_selection, unwrap+trim) is exact in a scratch unit test at 20 columns: soft wrap with a space in the last column, mid-word soft wraps with indentation, hard-wrapped indented rows, and cursor-positioned padded rows. No characters lost.
- Claude Code 2.1.303 fullscreen own copy, driven in a PTY (pyte emulator) with SGR drag across a four-bullet assistant reply and across the prompt, at 40/60/77/101/133 columns: the OSC 52 payload is exact every time. Assistant-reply copies drop drawn indentation ("\n- "); prompt copies keep it ("\n  - "), so Lucca's two-space indentation fits Orbit's host copy or a prompt-area copy.
- The 29-character losses each span exactly one row join, mid-word on both sides, which fits one whole drawn row of 29 text cells lost per join. Leading hypothesis to test: the app drew for a width different from the terminal's (pane width changed), or a selection across an autoscroll lost a row.
- Reading Lucca's transcripts was blocked by the auto-mode PII classifier; asked Lucca for the gesture, source and layout instead.

comments.author: lucca
comments.text:
Cause found (claude, 2026-10-22 ~02:00 -03): Claude Code's own fullscreen selection loses text when its drag autoscrolls. Eon is not in the path.

Lucca's answers: plain drag (Claude Code's 'sent N chars via OSC 52' toast), an assistant reply, and the drag went past the pane edge so the view scrolled.

Reproduction without Eon: Claude Code 2.1.303 with "tui": "fullscreen" resumed in a Python pty with a pyte screen at 40x16. WAYLAND_DISPLAY and DISPLAY are unset, so the copy arrives as OSC 52 in the PTY output. The session holds a four-bullet reply taller than the transcript area. Press at the end of bullet 3, then send one SGR motion per row up to row 1. That is what Venus sends: it clamps to the grid edge and sends no motion while the cell stays the same (venus/src/input.rs:498). Release at row 1.
- No hold: the OSC 52 payload has '- Soice,and that is fine for now.' and '  th,without a new helper.' (expected 'Some scenarios may be tested twice, and ...' and 'the queries, as the issue asked, without ...').
- Hold 3 s: more of the same, e.g. '- Itinvestigation, not a pattern guide,' and '  and ickcheck for anything.'
- This matches Lucca's paste: row-join text gone ('Swice'), and the space at a join gone ('has nodescription').
- Control: the same drag within the visible rows (no autoscroll) copies exactly at 40/60/77/101/133 columns, and Orbit's host copy (Shift+drag) is exact (earlier comment).

Workaround: Shift+drag uses Orbit's host selection, which autoscrolls and copies exactly (ORB-C9). Claude Code's toast also says to hold Shift.
Script: kept only in the session scratchpad (disposable Python; Python is not checked-in policy). The steps above are enough to rebuild it.
Next: file upstream at anthropics/claude-code with Lucca's approval, record the URL here, then close per Acceptance (cause outside Eon).

comments.author: lucca
comments.text: Upstream: https://github.com/anthropics/claude-code/issues/83961 (open, labeled reproduced, opened 2026-08-04 on 2.1.221; Linux tmux and WSL reports since). Same bug: the fullscreen renderer's own mouse selection drops fixed-width runs when the drag autoscrolls, and '/tui default' avoids it. Not filing a duplicate. Eon needs no change: Orbit's host copy (Shift+drag) is exact, and Eon routes plain drags to mouse-tracking apps as ORB-C9/VEN-C7 specify. Workarounds until upstream fixes it: Shift+drag in Eon, or '/tui default' in Claude Code.

environment/result. Acceptance: each named test resolves at the revision claimed
and the absent-reset/value-boundary clauses are mapped. If genuinely missing,
retain the original option of a minimal owning codec assertion, no wire meaning
change. Docs-only proof is symbol/diff review plus required Codex coverage; test

title: Check that bead IDs named in AGENTS.md exist and open-gap pointers are open
description:
## Why

eon-hgrq (2026-10-30) found that AGENTS.md names bead IDs as owners and open-gap pointers, and nothing checks them. `starcompass check-consumer` checks only hashes and a byte-exact render. eon-overseer, 2026-10-30, applying Lucca's standing direction not to raise minor choices: "File the bead-ID flake check as its own small bead (P3, Rust, planning/docs route), related to eon-946u."

## Evidence

- The four AGENTS.md files name 9 bead IDs, all in the root file (`grep -ohE '\beon-[a-z0-9-]+(\.[0-9]+)?\b' AGENTS.md orbit/AGENTS.md venus/AGENTS.md runtime/AGENTS.md`). Three are named as present owners or future work but are closed: eon-omq, eon-ax4 and eon-qualify-nix-free-linux-public-beta-lm9p (see eon-hgrq's comment).
- `orbit/tools/governance` already reads `.beads/issues.jsonl` to check bead and contract references in Orbit's docs. It belongs to Orbit and is run by hand.
- No CI job or flake check reads AGENTS.md content: `.github/workflows` has only cachix.yml and mac-proof.yml.

## Scope

In scope:
- A small Rust check over the rendered `AGENTS.md`, `orbit/AGENTS.md`, `venus/AGENTS.md` and `runtime/AGENTS.md`. It reads `.beads/issues.jsonl` directly, not through br.
  - Every bead-ID-shaped token must name an existing bead. Crate and package names that share the `eon-` prefix (eon-runtime, eon-workspace-protocol, eon-site, eon-test, eon-manifest) are excluded by an explicit list.
  - Every bead ID on a line starting "Open gaps:" must be open, not closed.
- Exposed as a flake check under `checks.x86_64-linux`. It lives in Eon's root tooling, not orbit-governance, which stays Orbit's. Reuse orbit-governance's JSONL-reading pattern; do not depend on it.
- Name the check in the AGENTS.md Verification table's planning/docs row. That is a rule edit: fold it into eon-946u's approved diff, or propose the wording to Lucca.

Out of scope:
- Judging prose ("owns", "comes next"). eon-946u removes the Status section instead.
- Checking named repo paths or contract IDs. Add these only if they stay cheap and need no new dependency.
- Running the check in CI.

## Acceptance

- The check fails on a planted unknown ID, and on a closed ID on an "Open gaps:" line, in a scratch copy. It passes on the tree after eon-946u.
- No new crate dependency, or an AP-REFERENCE-001 record if one is needed.
- AGENTS.md's Verification table names the check (Lucca-approved wording).

## Verification

- Red/green in a scratch copy, then `nix build .#checks.x86_64-linux.<name>`, and Codex plus a fresh Claude review per AGENTS.md.

## Stop Conditions

- Stop before any AGENTS.md text change until Lucca approves the wording, or eon-946u carries it.

## Planning reconciliation (2026-11-12, dcaef1c)

Comment 4940 is operative: include docs/AGENT-RULES.md along with all four
AGENTS.md files, and edit the hand-maintained Verification row there directly
with approved wording. eon-946u is closed; never edit generated AGENTS.md files.
The original nine-ID/workflow inventory is historical; release.yml also exists.

Recognise explicit Open gaps: passages even when the label is mid-line or the
ID wraps to the next line (AGENT-RULES.md:212 and :221-222). Preserve closed
historical owner references; only explicit open-gap passages require open IDs.
Include current non-bead tool/package tokens such as eon-bench/eon-tests in the
explicit exclusions. Read a consistent br-exported JSONL snapshot, no database
writes in the checker. Acceptance adds wrapped/mid-line gap, excluded package
and accepted historical-closed-reference fixtures to the existing unknown/closed
negative cases. Existing root Rust/flake check scope remains; no CI job. Use
fixture red/green, affected build, current pre-review suite/review requirements;
no runtime profile refresh. Rule wording still requires approval.

The bead IDs eon-agent-parity-a9g0 and eon-configurability-qkq8 ("Open gaps:" lines) and eon-awmq moved there, and so did the Verification table this bead edits. title: Render colour emoji and flag sequences in Venus
description:
## Why
eon-cts4 fixed cell widths (Orbit now clusters 👍🏽, 🇯🇵, 👨‍👩‍👧 into one two-cell grapheme), but its installed observation on Linux (obs-cts4/RESULT.md, profile build d2nw83j6...-eon-0.1.8) shows Venus still draws: 🇯🇵 as a boxed J plus a clipped boxed P inside its two cells; 👨‍👩‍👧 joined but monochrome; ❤️ (VS16) white instead of red. 👍🏽 renders correctly. The rented Mac's Fonts item (macOS 27, stock fonts) showed the flag and skin-tone split before eon-cts4; macOS after eon-cts4 is not yet observed. Caveat: the Linux run used a private HOME that may lack a colour emoji font.

## Change
1. Reproduce with Lucca's real fonts (installed Eon, his fontconfig) and with the font Eon packages or expects; record which font Venus picks for each cluster.
2. Venus shapes each grapheme cluster as one run with emoji-presentation fallback: a colour emoji font (Noto Color Emoji on Linux, Apple Color Emoji on macOS) for emoji clusters, regional-indicator pairs shaped together so the font's flag ligature applies, VS16 selecting colour presentation. Check how Venus's shaping and fallback chain (venus/src/render, text and font code) treats clusters today, and VEN-C16 and the Venus text contracts.
3. If Eon must ship or declare a colour emoji font for Nix installs, that is a dependency decision (reference gate).

## Acceptance
Red/green shaping test with 🇯🇵, 👨‍👩‍👧 and ❤️ (cluster to one glyph run from the emoji font); Venus checks per venus/AGENTS.md incl. darwin clippy; installed dogfood on Linux with real fonts; the next macOS Fonts item passes (rental or Yu).

## Scope
venus/ (and a font dependency only through the reference gate). Codex review per AGENTS.md.
close_reason: done

comments.author: lucca
comments.text:
Approval (relayed by eon-overseer): Lucca, 2026-10-29, to eon-overseer: "we need to do more eon stuff / can we fire more agents?", then chose this bead from the overseer's list. Roles: Opus plans and gates, Codex implements. Contract wording still needs Lucca's approval through eon-overseer.

## Plan (Opus, 2026-10-29, worktree at 90efde8)

### Cause (from code, to be confirmed by the red check)
Each wide cell is its own GlyphRun (`DrawRow::append_glyph_runs`, venus/src/scene.rs), so the whole cluster reaches one Buffer in `push_cell_text` (venus/src/render.rs). The fault is font choice in cosmic-text 0.19 (`FontFallbackIter::next_item`, `shape_run`): with a Monospace or named primary, every installed monospaced face that covers some of the word's codepoints is tried before the script and common lists, and later fonts only fill clusters whose glyph id is 0. So a mono face with text-style regional-indicator glyphs (boxed J, boxed P) wins for 🇯🇵 and the flag ligature never runs; the primary's text ❤ (U+2764) wins for ❤️ because VS16 is default-ignorable; Noto Color Emoji sits last in the platform common list, behind Noto Sans Symbols2. 👍🏽 works only because no text font covers it. Installed Venus does see system fonts: its FONTCONFIG_FILE (flake.nix `venusFontsConf`) includes /etc/fonts/conf.d and /usr/share/fonts.

### Approach
Add a colour-emoji route in `cell_text_attrs` (venus/src/render/cells.rs), the existing owner of per-cell family routing (Accelerando, Nerd Font):
- Platform family constant: "Noto Color Emoji" on Linux, "Apple Color Emoji" on macOS (cfg(target_os)), the same families cosmic-text's own platform fallback names.
- A cell routes when it is two cells wide, has no U+FE0E, and contains U+FE0F, a regional indicator (U+1F1E6–1F1FF), an emoji modifier (U+1F3FB–1F3FF), U+200D, U+20E3, a tag (U+E0020–E007F), or starts with a scalar in U+1F000–1FAFF or U+2300–2BFF. This follows kitty's `has_emoji_presentation` (multicell and emoji, VS16 or emoji default, not VS15) without a Unicode property table: Orbit's two-cell width already carries the presentation decision. Narrow cells never route (mode 2027 off, or text-default pictographs), so no colour glyph is clipped to one cell.
- The route applies whether or not a font override is configured (installed Eon always passes fallbacks, so `cell_font.family` is Some there), and returns before bold/italic like the Nerd branch: the emoji face is Regular-only, and a bold request would miss it and fall back to text faces.
- With an explicit non-mono family, cosmic-text uses that face first and the ordinary order fills anything it lacks; if the family is not installed, the order is today's.
- Plumbing: pass the run's width (GlyphRun.columns == 2) to `cell_text_attrs`; both callers (`build_scene_text`, `build_preview_text`) have it via `push_text_clipped`/`push_text`/`push_cell_text`. Keep the change minimal (e.g. carry columns in `DrawStyleKind::Cell`).

### Red check
New test in venus/src/render/tests/shaping.rs (Venus lib tests, run by `nix develop -c eon-test -p yazelix-venus`): build `FontSetup` with Eon's default fallbacks (Symbols Nerd Font Mono, Accelerando Terminal; so `cell_font.family` is Some as installed) and with no overrides; shape 🇯🇵, 👨‍👩‍👧 and ❤️ (wide) through `cell_text_attrs` + `set_cell_layer` in a cell Buffer (monospace width, Wrap::None); assert one glyph, glyph_id != 0, from a face whose family is the platform emoji family; also bold ❤️. Controls that must not route: 中 (wide CJK), ❤︎ (U+FE0E), narrow ❤️, A. The failure message prints the chosen face per cluster, which records bead step 1 (which font Venus picks today). Red on 90efde8, green after.

### Font dependency (Q2)
The venus Nix package runs its tests in the build sandbox with only `venusFonts` (DejaVu, Symbols Nerd Font, Accelerando), so the shaping test needs a colour emoji face there. Proposed: add nixpkgs `noto-fonts-color-emoji` (2.051 at the pinned nixpkgs, OFL-1.1, one 10.8 MB file) to `venusFonts` on Linux only. macOS keeps stock Apple Color Emoji.

### Reference gate (for the font dependency)
- Behaviour: two-cell emoji clusters, flags and VS16 sequences draw as one colour glyph. Owners: Venus owns presentation and face routing; Eon's Nix composition owns the packaged font set (EON-C19 Packaged fonts); nixpkgs owns the font version.
- Routes read: docs/REFERENCES.md Accelerando font route (packaged font composed into the Venus font configuration).
- Comparables: kitty b2cb871254fbdac19a085188813c8dfb258b95cd kitty/fonts.c `has_emoji_presentation` and fontconfig.c (wide + emoji + VS16/VS15, "emoji" family, no bold/italic for emoji); Ghostty 8c425a7bd57de848aa83cb9b003b1ecd6037c56a src/font/CodepointResolver.zig (UCD emoji presentation, explicit VS presentation, colour-glyph check); WezTerm e2a98e1b8af156988ad0ac778658ac27b60a55fb config/src/font.rs and wezterm-font/src/parser.rs (bundles Noto Color Emoji as a fallback).
- Rejected: a Unicode emoji-property crate (new dependency for a table that Orbit's width already decides); a fontconfig "emoji" alias query (fontdb does not expose it; Linux-only); relying on host fonts alone (the Nix check cannot see them, and minimal hosts lack one).
- Version policy: the pinned nixpkgs owns it, no separate pin. Exit: drop when a Nix-free bundle carries its own emoji font or hosts are relied on.
- Check: the shaping test in the Nix venus package build, plus installed dogfood.

### Scope
In: venus/src/render.rs, venus/src/render/cells.rs, venus/src/render/tests/shaping.rs; flake.nix `venusFonts` (Linux-only addition, if Q2 is approved); VEN-C19 and EON-C19 text (if Q1/Q2 approved); docs/CONFIGURATION.md packaged-fonts sentence; CHANGELOG.md; venus/CHANGELOG.md.
Out: Orbit widths; narrow cells (mode 2027 off); BMP emoji-default code points outside the listed ranges; emoji glyph scaling inside the two cells; configuring the emoji family (Q3).

### Checks
`nix develop -c eon-test -p yazelix-venus` (red then green); `cargo fmt --check`; `cargo clippy --locked -p yazelix-venus --all-targets -- -D warnings`; Darwin clippy recipe; the venus Nix package build (its sandboxed tests see only packaged fonts). Installed dogfood (coordinator, after landing): obs-cts4's `p.sh` line in a fresh terminal: 🇯🇵 is one flag, 👨‍👩‍👧 colour, ❤️ red, bars in place; the next macOS Fonts item (rental or Yu).

## Questions for Lucca (through eon-overseer)

1. Change VEN-C19 so emoji clusters prefer the platform colour emoji font ahead of named overrides? Recommended: yes; today "named overrides precede specialty/platform fallback", and that order is what puts text glyphs on flags and ❤️. Proposed wording:
   - In **Result**, "Named overrides precede specialty/platform fallback." becomes "Named overrides precede specialty/platform fallback, except for colour emoji below."
   - New bullet after **Accelerando specialty font**: "**Colour emoji:** A two-cell cluster with emoji presentation (U+FE0F, a regional-indicator flag, an emoji modifier, a ZWJ, keycap or tag sequence, or a two-cell pictograph) and no U+FE0E shapes first from the platform colour emoji family, Noto Color Emoji on Linux and Apple Color Emoji on macOS, at regular upright style, ahead of the primary and named fallbacks. Code points that family lacks, and every cluster when it is not installed, follow the ordinary order."
2. Ship Noto Color Emoji with Eon on Linux? Recommended: yes, Linux only; it makes the shaping test run in the Nix build sandbox and gives colour emoji on hosts without an emoji font, as WezTerm does; cost is one 10.8 MB OFL-1.1 file in the closure, versioned by the nixpkgs pin. EON-C19 **Packaged fonts** wording: "The Venus font configuration includes DejaVu, Symbols Nerd Font Mono, Anima's font-only Accelerando Terminal artifact and, on Linux, Noto Color Emoji." Alternative: a test-only font conf for the check, leaving installed emoji to host fonts.
3. Configure the emoji family? Recommended: not in this slice (it spans Eon Runtime config, the Venus CLI and docs); record it as an open gap under eon-configurability-qkq8 and keep the platform family until then.

comments.author: lucca
comments.text:
Decisions (Lucca, 2026-10-29, "all ok", relayed by eon-overseer, who showed him each question with its recommendation and the proposed wording verbatim):
1. VEN-C19: approved as proposed. Result gets "Named overrides precede specialty/platform fallback, except for colour emoji below." and a new **Colour emoji** bullet in the wording of the plan comment.
2. Ship Noto Color Emoji with Eon on Linux in flake.nix `venusFonts`: approved. EON-C19 **Packaged fonts** becomes "The Venus font configuration includes DejaVu, Symbols Nerd Font Mono, Anima's font-only Accelerando Terminal artifact and, on Linux, Noto Color Emoji."
3. No emoji font setting in this slice. The gap is recorded under eon-configurability-qkq8, and the platform family stays until then.
Go for checks (eon-overseer): eon-test -p yazelix-venus, fmt, clippy (Linux and darwin), -j 4, venus Nix package build at --max-jobs 1 --cores 4.

title: Shorten the footer hints: drop next/previous agent, mv for move, col for column
description:
## Why

Lucca, 2026-11-02: "we are putting too much space pressure on the hints-bar. we should remove the 'next/previous agent' bindings from it, so smaller screens will still show important stuff. we can also change 'move' to 'mv' and column to col".

## Change

In the footer hints only (venus/src/application/shortcuts.rs `shortcut_hints_for`):
- Drop the `next agent` (Alt+G) and `previous agent` (Alt+Shift+G) hints. The bindings stay, and the Shortcuts viewer keeps listing them ("Jump to the next/previous agent needing attention", VEN-C20 unchanged).
- `move tab` -> `mv tab`, `move pane` -> `mv pane`.
- `+column` -> `+col`.
- Screen-reader labels keep the full chords and action names (unchanged).

Docs: docs/USAGE.md and venus/docs/INTERACTION.md paragraphs that list the hint labels; CHANGELOG.md entry (user-visible); venus/CHANGELOG.md only if it records footer labels as behavior.

## Contract

None: VEN-C24 keeps presentation as a feature; VEN-C20's viewer rows are unchanged. Check VEN-C24/VEN-C30 text for any sentence that names the footer's agent hints as current behavior and report it (historic evidence lines stay).

## Configuration (rule 6)

Fixed: hint labels are Venus presentation text derived from the bindings; the bindings themselves stay configurable. Record on close.

## Acceptance

title: Mark a zoomed tab with a magnifier glyph instead of the word zoom
description:
## Why

Lucca, 2026-10-25: "what about a looking glass instead of 'zoom' in the tab marker?". Overseer
mock over the eon-tfsg capture: ~/.cache/eon-agents/tfsg/dog/out/glass-mock.png (script
~/.cache/eon-agents/tfsg/glass-mock.py); Lucca chose the magnifier with a plus: "do it".

## Behaviour

- While a tab is zoomed, its pill shows a zoom-in magnifier glyph (Symbols Nerd Font,
  nf-fa-search_plus U+F00E) after its label instead of the text ` · zoom`, in the label's colour,
  sized and baseline-aligned with the label text; tab width fitting accounts for it as today.
- The accessible name keeps `, zoomed`; nothing else about zoom changes.
- Configurability (AGENTS.md): fixed. One indicator glyph; a setting would cost more support than
  users would gain. Recorded here as the reason.
- The glyph comes from the Symbols Nerd Font Venus already ships; if a build lacks that face, the
  marker falls back to the existing ` · zoom` text (no tofu box).

## Contract (approved, see the Approval comment)

VEN-C8: "The active tab's label gains ` · zoom`" becomes "The active tab's label gains a zoom-in
magnifier glyph (Nerd Font U+F00E) after its name"; ", zoomed" in the accessible name unchanged.
EON-C8's "The active tab's pill and accessible name mark the zoom" stays true. Guides and
changelogs that quote ` · zoom` follow.

## Acceptance

- Venus test (fails first): a zoomed tab's label carries the glyph, not ` · zoom`; accessible
  name unchanged; fallback text when the face is missing.
- Isolated capture of a zoomed tab.

Portability: neutral.

description:

comments.text:
# Comment for eon-xjzr4.1 (overseer to transfer; no br write from this session)

Source: eon-xjzr4.2, dbf18c9 baseline and candidate shell PTYs, x86_64 Linux,
private homes. Baseline/candidate logs and raw transcripts are under this work
directory. These observations must constrain consumption of OSC 133:

- A D with no open C is not a command completion. Nu 0.113.1 sends D with the
  previous LAST_EXIT_CODE on Ctrl+C at an idle prompt. After a failed command,
  pressing Ctrl+C at a fresh idle prompt can therefore repeat its status.
- Nu also sends C for an empty submission, without D, then a new A/B prompt.
  An A returning to the prompt must terminate a pending empty submission;
  do not turn an empty line followed by idle Ctrl+C into a failed running job.
  Foreground-process observation remains necessary for actual running commands.
- Interrupted external commands have shell-native signed status: Bash reports
  130; Nu reports -2. A D status must retain signed values. Nu's pipeline policy
  can differ from Bash (the observed ^false | ^true reports 1 in Nu, 0 with
  Bash pipefail off). Do not reconstruct status from individual processes.
- Nested interactive shells share the byte stream: outer C, inner C/D pairs,
  then outer D when the inner shell returns. Explicit shell exit/exec may not
  return to an inner prompt; Ctrl+D at an empty Bash prompt adds no inner C.
- The exact pinned libghostty-vt 0.2.1 binding, revision
  9b598d6528c08c013407052767bb2e885ba869ba, exposes
  SemanticPromptKind::CommandEnd and SemanticPrompt::exit_code() -> Option<i32>.
  It uses has_exit_code, preserving Some(0) versus None, and negative codes.
  Its semantic_prompt_reports_each_command_step test checks D;0, D;-1;err=boom
  and D with no status. Orbit currently drops all but PromptStart in
  Turn::prompt, so slice 1 must retain C and D there. No new parser is needed.

Managed Nu now selects native osc133=true/osc633=false without changing
TERM_PROGRAM. Native user autoload remains last. Bash gains C/D only, no A;
ORB-C15's existing foreground-return drop rule is intentionally unchanged.

comments.author: lucca
comments.text:
Opus review follow-up (2026-11-11):

- Bash emits D;148 when a foreground job stops under Ctrl+Z. D means the shell
  regained control, not necessarily process exit. Use foreground/process facts
  to distinguish a stopped job from one that finished; do not label every D
  as proof the process died. The shell-mark slice adds a real Ctrl+Z check and
  corrects EON-C9's wording.
- Some integrations (for example a named iTerm2 hook calling a second helper)
  hide the actual C/D emitter one call beyond Eon's deliberately plain-text,
  directly-named-hook guard. Their C/D can therefore be duplicated. Treat a C
  while a C is already open as a no-op; never turn duplicate C marks into an
  accumulating completion count. Consider this with the existing nested-shell
  facts above and retain foreground sampling as the independent running fact.
- If user code replaces only PROMPT_COMMAND, Eon heals at the next PS0 start,
  closes the previous pending submission with its saved status, then emits C
  for the new submission. This may delay that one D until the next command;
  arbitrary user shell configuration is not monitored with a DEBUG trap.

Unix `hx --listen PATH [FILE...]` starts after argument files open. The parent
must already exist, be private/current-user owned, and have trusted canonical
ancestry (user/root owned, no group/other writes unless sticky). Helix resolves
the parent once; all socket operations use the verified canonical path. Socket
mode is 0600; active/non-socket paths are refused, matching stale sockets recover,
and close/drop removes only the owned device/inode.

S3 creates a unique per-editor private socket directory and starts hx with the
absolute socket path. S4 sends one newline-terminated UTF-8 JSON object per
connection and reads one newline-terminated reply, for example:

```json
{"version":1,"id":"eon-edit-1","action":"open","paths":["/absolute/file.rs:12:3"],"timeout_ms":750}
{"version":1,"id":"eon-edit-1","status":"ok"}
{"version":1,"id":"eon-edit-1","status":"error","error":{"class":"rejected","message":"...","path_index":0}}
```

id is 1..256 UTF-8 bytes, paths nonempty/absolute/no NUL/non-directory, unknown
fields rejected, timeout_ms integer 1..2000 (default 2000), total frame <=65536
bytes including newline. FILE:LINE[:COL] uses Helix's parser and literal-file
priority. Missing files become named buffers; existing buffers are not reloaded.
Opens preserve dirty buffers/undo history, cancel pending commands, close
document-bound prompts and retain picker filter/selection. Multiple paths are
ordered without rollback. Rejected editor errors include zero-based path_index.
Closed error classes: invalid, unsupported, rejected, timeout, unavailable.

S4 plan correction: a 1-second client timeout does not guarantee nothing changed.
Only an explicit server timeout reply guarantees queued work was abandoned.
unavailable/lost replies can have unknown outcomes; IDs are correlation only.
Do not retry or launch another editor assuming the first request did not run.
