# eon-xodrj.3 plan: build Eon's Helix without Steel and pin the native listener (S2)

Agent eon-helix-no-steel (Fable 5.2), 2026-11-10. Worktree at edge 1d9350d.
No code changed yet. Sources read: the bead and its parent, eon-xodrj.1/.2 with
comments, the approved plan (report.md, sections 5, 7, 8), AGENTS.md,
docs/AGENT-RULES.md (Contract-Driven Method, Verification, Proof and Review,
Testing Discipline, Configurability, Product Boundary, Composition and
Distribution), runtime/AGENTS.md is read before the Rust edit.

## 1. Facts checked

- nova-helix `main` is `6ee75ad3b7b2f2ed82daae0f9bf1663c168f48ea` (`git ls-remote`,
  2026-11-10). Its workspace version is still 25.7.1, so the manifest version
  stays. S1 changed no `Cargo.lock`, `flake.lock`, `grammars.nix` or
  `languages.toml`, so the vendored crates and grammar derivations stay as built.
- nova-helix at 6ee75ad3 has **no** Steel-free flake output: `packages` holds
  `helix`, `yazelix_helix` (both the default-feature build), `grammar-sources`
  and `yazelix_helix_steel`. `helix-term` features: `default = ["git", "steel"]`;
  `default-members = ["helix-term"]`, so the package's `cargo build` selects only
  `helix-term`.
- Pinned nixpkgs (567a49d) `buildRustPackage` reads `buildNoDefaultFeatures` and
  `buildFeatures` from its **call arguments** and writes them to the derivation
  as `cargoBuildNoDefaultFeatures` and `cargoBuildFeatures`, which
  `cargo-build-hook.sh` reads. So `overrideAttrs { buildNoDefaultFeatures = true; }`
  would be silently ignored; an override has to set the `cargoBuild*` attributes.
- Steel-enabled Helix runs `init.scm` inside `Application::new`
  (`helix-term/src/application.rs:160`), before the first frame. Without
  `HELIX_STEEL_CONFIG` it would read a repository's `.helix/{helix,init}.scm`
  when both exist, else the config directory's (`steel/mod.rs:2247-2260`).

## 2. How `helixPackage` is built: an Eon-side override

```nix
# Steel is a default feature of nova-helix; Eon's Helix is built without it (EON-C9).
helixPackage = helix.packages.${system}.yazelix_helix.overrideAttrs {
  cargoBuildNoDefaultFeatures = true;
  cargoBuildFeatures = [ "git" ];
};
```

Why not the nova-helix output the bead prefers ("so the store path is shared
and cached"):
1. The sharing does not exist. Eon's `helix` input follows Eon's nixpkgs
   (`inputs.nixpkgs.follows`), so any nova-helix output evaluated by Eon already
   has a store path nova-helix's own lock never produces. Nova builds with
   Steel, so Eon is the only consumer of the Steel-free build. Eon's CI pushes

title: Add the built-in Editor popup running [editor] command with a listen socket (Editor popup S3)
description:
Lucca approved 2026-11-10 in the planning pane: "cool. i agree" (option 1: a native Rust --listen on nova-helix, Steel compiled out, steps S1-S4; Mitos after v0.2.0). Plan: /home/lucca/.cache/eon-agents/eon-editor-plan-work/bead/report.md (sections 1-9: mechanism, failure cases, options, contract drafts in section 7, configuration and CLI in section 8). Earlier Lucca words are on eon-xodrj.1.

## Step

**S3: built-in Editor popup.**
- Add a product default entry `editor` beside Git and Agent (`product.rs`
  defaults; `managed_environment.rs` popup catalog):
  - label "Editor", default key Alt+Shift+O, which is Lucca's dogfood key (S3 runs
    the usual conflict check against pinned Helix, Yazi, lazygit, shells and agent
    CLIs);
  - `keybinding`, `label` and `enabled` accepted;
  - `command` and `keep_alive` ignored with a warning naming `[editor] command`,
    so one setting governs each value. Lucca's existing custom `[popups.editor]
    command = ["hx"]` gets that warning and keeps working.
- It runs `[editor] command` at the tab directory, keep-alive. Unlike Git, it
  keeps its process and buffers across tab-directory changes, as Files does,
  because a retarget restart would discard unsaved edits.
- When the command is the packaged Helix (the existing `Tool::Helix`
  classification, `managed_environment.rs:912`), the supervisor creates
  `<window runtime>/editor/` as 0700 and appends `--listen <dir>/<instance>.sock`.
  It removes the socket when the terminal ends and sweeps leftovers at supervisor
  start, as the Scrollback snapshot dirs are swept.
- Contract: EON-C10 runtime policy, the Editor sentence. Docs: CONFIGURATION.md
  and `eon config defaults`; CHANGELOG.
- Tests: catalog, defaults round trip, a warning fixture, a retarget that keeps
  the process, and socket-path lifecycle with a fake editor.
- No file routing in this step: the popup only opens and hides with its key.

# Owning-bead clarification — fixed native-listener budgets

For eon-xodrj.5, to be replayed into its Beads record by the overseer. The user
requires this session's bead writes in numbered Markdown files, not br.

- **100 ms connect / 1 s answer:** fixed performance budgets from the approved
  S4 design (report section 8). The synchronous exchange runs in the supervisor;
  changing these bounds also delays unrelated workspace and lifecycle actions.
  Keeping a short, predictable maximum supervisor stall outweighs differing
  timeout preferences, so there is no configuration key for either value.
- **750 ms editor callback budget:** fixed within the 1 s answer budget to
  reserve time for transport/reply delivery. This is an internal scheduling
  allowance, not an independent user timeout. An explicit server timeout can
  confirm queued work was abandoned; the shorter budget does not make a lost
  client reply prove cancellation.
- **64 KiB frame ceiling:** fixed native-v1 protocol/interoperability bound of
  the pinned Helix listener, including newline framing. An Eon-only setting
  cannot enlarge what the server accepts; exposing one would add an unsupported
  protocol variation. The client enforces the same bound on requests/replies.

These reasons clarify the existing approved limits; the review fix changes no
value, configuration surface, contract bound or runtime policy. Existing client
and integration tests cover the deadlines, frame ceiling and failure behavior.
A new literal-mirror runtime test for this planning text would prove nothing.

title: Open files from the Files popup as a new buffer in a running Neovim Editor popup
description:

title: Make the EON-C11 cgroup gate directly testable
description:
## Contract Routing

This hardens EON-C11's existing Linux cgroup launch gate without changing its observable policy.

Consumer: Eon immediately before it spawns an Orbit Session.

Trigger: Eon inspects its current unified cgroup-v2 membership within the shared launch deadline.

Result: launch proceeds only when the resolved cgroup directory is safe, user-owned, not writable by group or others, and contains Eon's exact PID. Missing, malformed, unsafe, foreign, or stale evidence fails explicitly. Retry timing remains owned by `wait_for_orbit_parent_cgroup`.

## Why

The 2026-08-28 audit found `current_cgroup_is_inheritable` at cyclomatic complexity 11, cognitive complexity 4, 0% coverage, and CRAP 132. The function is skipped under `EON_TEST_MANAGED_ORBIT`, so existing integration tests prove retry behavior but none of the security-sensitive membership, pathname, ownership, mode, or PID checks.

Impact HIGH, effort S/M, implementation risk MEDIUM because this is a launch trust boundary, confidence HIGH.

## Evidence

- `crates/eon/src/sessions.rs:746`: `current_cgroup_is_inheritable` directly reads `/proc/self/cgroup`, resolves beneath `/sys/fs/cgroup`, checks path components and directory metadata, then checks `cgroup.procs`.
- `crates/eon/src/sessions.rs:784`: retry policy is already separately injectable through `wait_for_orbit_parent_cgroup`.
- `crates/eon/src/sessions.rs:825`: managed-Orbit tests bypass the real cgroup inspection.
- `crates/eon/src/sessions.rs:1223`: current focused tests cover retry success and deadline failure only.
- `docs/CONTRACTS.md:389`: EON-C11 requires the exact user-owned, non-writable-by-others directory and own-process membership gate.

## Scope

In scope:
- `crates/eon/src/sessions.rs`.
- The smallest deterministic validation seam needed to test membership parsing, safe path resolution, directory ownership/mode, and exact PID membership.
- Focused unit tests for accepted and rejected evidence.
- Unchanged Linux filesystem observation and unchanged launch retry/deadline behavior.
- Required locked Rust/Nix proof and local profile refresh if production source changes.

Out of scope:
- A filesystem trait, mock framework, cgroup library, dependency, service-manager integration, cgroup creation/delegation, platform abstraction, macOS/X11 support, or wider lifecycle policy.
- Weakening validation so tests are easier.
- Splitting helpers solely to lower a score.

## Implementation Notes

1. Re-read EON-C7, EON-C11, the launch call path, and the complete existing cgroup gate.
2. Separate observation from deterministic validation at the smallest existing boundary. Prefer plain values or a direct helper; add no trait or generic provider.
3. Cover unified-hierarchy selection, required absolute path, unsafe components, directory kind/UID/mode, and exact line-based PID membership, including lookalike PIDs.
4. Keep `/proc/self/cgroup`, `/sys/fs/cgroup`, effective UID, and current PID observation in the Linux adapter that already owns them.
5. Preserve exact user-facing failures unless a current message is demonstrably misleading.
6. Rerun coverage-aware diagnostics, then the lifecycle-required Rust and Nix proof. Refresh the active `eon` profile from the working tree without restarting live supervisors.

## Verification

- `cargo test --locked -p eon sessions::tests` should exit 0 and exercise every deterministic cgroup validation class plus retry behavior.
- `cargo fmt --check` should exit 0.
- `cargo test --locked --workspace` should exit 0.
- `cargo clippy --locked --workspace --all-targets --all-features -- -D warnings` should exit 0.
- `cargo run --locked -p eon-manifest -- --check` should exit 0.
- `nix flake check --no-update-lock-file` should exit 0 for the unchanged component graph.
- `nix profile upgrade eon --flake .#default` should refresh the active profile from this working tree if production source changed; verify `nix profile list --json` resolves `eon` to the just-built store path.
- `git diff --check` should exit 0.

## Stop Conditions

- Stop if a testable seam would duplicate cgroup policy or require a trait/dependency.
- Stop before changing the accepted ownership, mode, containment, deadline, or failure semantics.
- Stop before adding cgroup creation, delegation, service-manager, or portability behavior.
- Preserve live Sessions; do not restart the running supervisor without explicit user authorization.

## Maintenance Notes

The production owner should remain one small Linux adapter plus deterministic validation, not a reusable cgroup subsystem. cargo-crap is diagnostic only; no score threshold or CI policy is part of this issue.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Deterministic tests accept a valid unified cgroup-v2 membership and reject missing hierarchy, non-absolute or unsafe paths, wrong file kind/UID/mode, absent exact PID membership, and lookalike PID lines.
- The production observer still reads only the current Linux `/proc/self/cgroup`, resolved `/sys/fs/cgroup` directory, `cgroup.procs`, effective UID, and current PID, and `wait_for_orbit_parent_cgroup` retains its deadline/retry ownership.
- EON-C11's fail-closed ownership, mode, containment, and diagnostic behavior is unchanged; no validation is weakened or duplicated.
- Focused and complete locked Rust/Nix checks pass. If production source changes, the active `eon` profile resolves to the just-built working-tree artifact without restarting live supervisors.
- No filesystem trait, mock framework, cgroup dependency/subsystem, service-manager requirement, or platform expansion is introduced.

EON-C11 no longer requires membership or delegation. Reintroducing this gate or its tests would contradict the current contract. User authorized backlog reconciliation on 2026-09-08.

title: Add a per-pane tag: eon pane rename --tag, tag in session JSON
description:
## Why

Lucca approved separating an agent's short pinned name from its work identifier so Venus can align them independently. This bead delivers the generic per-pane tag as Runtime data, CLI and JSON; eon-e5qjv consumes it for presentation. Eon must not interpret tags as Beads IDs.

Source of truth: `/home/lucca/.cache/eon-agents/eon-desk/bead-sidebar-tag-columns.md` (Lucca, 2026-11-11: "i like it", popup option 1), with `/home/lucca/.local/state/rota/runs/desk-popup-rows-sol-1/report.md`. This pass sharpens that design without changing it.

## Evidence

Checked in the reading worktree at edge `2e93c69b2250cb30346c2306502116ebfaebcd87`; these replace the spec's ~481fe27 pointers.

- `runtime/crates/eon-runtime/src/workspace.rs:68`, `:882`, `:1431`, `:3381`: private pin state, rename mutation, snapshot projection and shared pane JSON writer.
- `runtime/crates/eon-runtime/src/cli.rs:1154`, `:2775`, `:3332`: rename help, parser and literal/validation tests; `runtime/crates/eon-runtime/src/cli/parity.rs:142`: existing window-action-to-CLI mapping.
- `runtime/crates/eon-workspace-protocol/src/v40.rs:20`, `:243`, `:405`, `:1517`, `:2332`, `:2486`: VERSION=40, RenamePane, Pane, name validation and positional pane encode/decode. Adding a pane field or changing the action changes bytes and requires a new EONW version.
- `runtime/crates/eon-runtime/src/events.rs:602` detects pin/label changes as pane-renamed; `runtime/crates/eon-workspace-protocol/src/v40/subscription.rs:200` carries the same Pane in events. Tag must follow these existing pin projections too.
- `venus/src/model.rs:313`, `:351`: metadata-only comparisons strip labels and pins; include tag so its updates preserve navigation/attachments. `venus/src/scene.rs:2148` looks up the pin for shown-session inbox rows; remote queue entries carry no pin (`v40.rs:388`).
- `runtime/crates/eon-runtime/src/workspace.rs:4469` and `eon/crates/eon/tests/workspace_control.rs:7437`: pin lifecycle/focus and CLI integration checks to extend.
- `docs/CONTRACTS.md:605` (EON-C8), `:1520` (EON-C10), `:5632` (EON-C39); `docs/USAGE.md:1437` documents naming and nullable pinned_name.

## Scope

In scope:
- Runtime owns one optional tag on each pane, separate from pinned_name and automatic label composition; expose it through canonical EONW Pane and the rename action.
- `eon pane rename PANE NAME --tag TAG`; `--tag ''` clears the tag. Existing rename/clear-name operations without --tag preserve it. Distinguish omitted, set and clear; validate the whole requested mutation before changing either field.
- Nullable `tag` beside `pinned_name` in `eon session --json`, action-reply pane objects, subscription snapshots/gaps and pane events wherever the pin already travels. Detect a tag-only change through the existing pane-renamed event, not a new event family.
- Same lifecycle and input rules as the pin; protocol validators/codecs/bounds, CLI parser/help/parity, Runtime mutation/projections, tests and fixtures. Update all in-tree protocol consumers/imports and Pane/Action constructors, including Venus's metadata-only comparisons, without drawing the tag yet.
- Lucca-approved owning EON contract wording, `docs/USAGE.md`, any affected protocol/version documentation, and `CHANGELOG.md`. Keep EON-C8's pin summary aligned with EON-C10; include EON-C39's pane-renamed wording in the approval if tag changes extend it.

Out of scope:
- Venus row layout, visible tag rendering, popup uN discovery and accessible row names (eon-e5qjv).
- Popup tags/pins, a Beads integration, new persistence/recovery guarantees, a new window tag editor, or new tag-only CLI syntax beyond the approved rename form.
- Cross-session inbox queue enrichment (eon-inbox-pinned-name-yiogr); no new terminal observer, process inspection or Orbit change.

## Acceptance

- `eon pane rename p9 x --tag t` sets pin x and tag t; session/action JSON returns `"pinned_name":"x","tag":"t"`. An untagged pane, including one without attention, returns `"tag":null`; `--tag ''` clears to null. Omitted --tag preserves a tag through ordinary rename and the existing `--clear` name operation.
- Tag uses the pin's trimmed, plain-text validation: empty after trimming clears; at most 80 Unicode characters / 320 UTF-8 bytes; controls and invisible format characters are refused. Bad tag, bad name, malformed flags or unknown pane leave both fields unchanged; preserve existing usage/action error statuses and literal `--` handling.
- Explicit pane targeting works in a hidden tab and preserves shown session, active tab, pane/popup selections and desktop focus. Tag follows pane moves, survives presentation detach/reattach, and ends with the pane or supervisor; recovery does not restore it.
- Wire round trips preserve absent and present tags and the action's omitted/set/clear distinction. Snapshot, action and subscription JSON expose the same full value; a changed tag produces pane-renamed with it. Existing name-only window and CLI callers leave tag intact. Metadata-only tag updates do not trigger topology/attachment resets.
- Current CLI, Runtime and Venus use one matching EONW schema. Incompatible clients are refused by existing exact-version rules; Reserved Stop and its frozen six-byte prefix remain unchanged. Do not claim cross-version attachment support.

## Implementation Notes

1. Before implementation, propose the exact EON-C10 delta to Lucca, with aligned EON-C8 and any EON-C39 wording. Feature-design approval is not contract-text approval. Runtime owns tag state and validation; canonical eon-workspace-protocol owns the wire; CLI/Venus consume it.
2. Reference gate: read `docs/REFERENCES.md` "How should shared popups extend the workspace wire contract without breaking the installed client?" and `venus/docs/REFERENCES.md` "Read-only pane metadata: historical Venus observer and Runtime ownership" / "Canonical workspace protocol provider". The local comparable is the pin path at the exact revision above. Keep its bounded data, single Runtime owner, lifecycle and exact-version pairing; reject a second schema, negotiation, or Venus-owned tag state. Record the adopted mechanism and first falsifying check before code.
3. Version coordination: v41 is already held by eon-agent-parity-a9g0.1.1 and its joint landing with .1.3 (also .1.4); it is not free merely because edge is v40. Do not amend v40 in place or take/extend that other agent's v41 schema independently. Coordinate with the overseer and parity owner before choosing the next distinct free version. At this baseline that is v42, subject to other reservations. If tags land first, parity must rebase onto them and take the next free version above the landed one; it must never land its old v41 schema over tags. If parity lands first, tags rebase onto that version and bump once after it. Record the allocated version/order in this bead before implementation; no dependency that waits on all agent parity is justified by the feature itself.
4. Add state/action/codec/JSON coverage together, extend existing checks, and mechanically adapt every consumer. No rendering belongs here; hand the accepted data surface to eon-e5qjv.

## Verification

Future implementation proof, not run by this planning pass:
- Focused codec/parser/Runtime checks and `pane_rename_cli_sets_clears_and_reports_the_runtime_label` cover set/clear/omitted, atomic refusal, JSON/events and unchanged selection; extend the existing pin move/detach lifecycle and Venus metadata-only regression coverage.
- Shared-wire route in `docs/AGENT-RULES.md`: whole-workspace `nix develop -c eon-test` through its isolation harness, fmt and affected-crate clippy; full affected Rust/Nix surfaces and the overseer's `nix build` before landing. Codec assertions alone do not prove installed pairing.
- After the accepted batch/profile refresh, one isolated installed CLI observation sets/reads/clears a tag using matched binaries in a fresh session, preserving live supervisors and terminals. Record exact revision/artifact, environment, command and result; normal code/contract review requirements apply.

## Stop Conditions

- Stop for Lucca's approval of the proposed EON contract text before implementing; do not edit contracts in this planning pass.
- Stop before wire work if the next free EONW version and landing coordination are not recorded, or if preserving the installed CLI/Venus pairing needs unapproved compatibility policy. A bump is required, not an unresolved yes/no question.
- Stop if code drift changes the approved behavior/owner, if new persistence, remote inbox metadata, popup tagging or other out-of-scope work is required, or if the slice no longer fits one fresh session. Return a split proposal instead of expanding scope.
- Stop if verification fails twice for the same reason after a reasonable fix attempt. Never restart a live supervisor without Lucca's explicit authorization.

## Maintenance Notes

- Size: one independently verifiable data feature across its existing Runtime/protocol/CLI path plus mechanical consumers; one shared-wire proof route, bounded to one fresh session. No further split is needed at this baseline.
- eon-e5qjv is blocked by this bead. eon-inbox-pinned-name-yiogr is optional later work, not a prerequisite: whichever lands second carries tag wherever it adds pin metadata; this bead supplies shown-session pane data only, not a queue pin/tag extension.
- eon-xjzr4.3 and eon-qczl0 own future command/background content, not tag storage or this CLI; coordinate shared pane/wire projections with their data owners if concurrently scheduled, without importing their scope.
- Rule 5: the approved write path is the explicit-ID rename CLI; full tag data is readable in JSON independently of attention. Rule 6: null is the optional-data default; validation bounds stay fixed for plain-text safety and the existing bounded protocol budget, not as a configurable display preference. Visual colours/layout are recorded in eon-e5qjv.
- Not a release blocker and not added to eon-igae (existing overseer call, 2026-11-12, relayed via eon-desk). After both beads land, the overseer can pin short slugs and set --tag at agent start; until then keep existing `slug bead` names.

```markdown
  - `eon pane rename PANE NAME [--json]` pins a name; `eon pane rename PANE --clear [--json]` restores automatic naming. `--` permits an option-looking NAME. Names are trimmed; an empty result clears the pin. Invalid names fail without mutation. Rename addresses an explicit pane anywhere in the addressed session and changes no session, tab, pane or popup selection or desktop focus. Window rename and clear actions use the same mutation. Pins follow pane moves, survive presentation detach and reattach, and end with the pane or supervisor; recovery does not restore them. Session inspection and action replies expose each pane's `label` and nullable `pinned_name`, independently of attention records.
```

Proposed:

```markdown
  - `eon pane rename PANE NAME [--tag TAG] [--json]` pins a name and optionally
    sets a separate per-pane tag. `eon pane rename PANE --clear [--json]`
    restores automatic naming. `--` permits an option-looking NAME. Names and
    tags are trimmed; an empty result clears that field, so `--tag ''` clears
    the tag. Tags use the pin's plain-text bounds: at most 80 Unicode characters
    and 320 UTF-8 bytes; controls and invisible format characters are refused.
    Runtime validates the whole mutation before changing either field;
    invalid input or an unknown pane changes neither. Rename addresses an
    explicit pane anywhere in the addressed session and changes no session,
    tab, pane or popup selection or desktop focus. Window rename and clear
    actions use the same mutation. Omitting `--tag`, including ordinary rename
    and clear-name actions, preserves the tag. Runtime owns the tag separately
    from the pin and automatic label; Eon treats it as plain text.
    Pins and tags follow pane moves, survive presentation detach and reattach,
    and end with the pane or supervisor; recovery does not restore them.
    Each canonical EONW pane record carries the optional tag. `eon session
    --json`, action replies, subscription snapshots/gaps and pane events expose
    `tag` beside `pinned_name`, as a string or null wherever the pin travels,
    independently of attention records; `label` remains available.
```

Reason: define the approved tag write/read path, atomic refusal and existing pin lifecycle.

### EON-C39 — pane-renamed (`docs/CONTRACTS.md:5735`)

Current:

```markdown
    - `pane`: `pane-created`, `pane-moved`, `pane-renamed`, `pane-ended`,
      `pane-closed` and `pane-selected`, each with its `session`, `tab`
      and the pane. Each `pane` event, `pane-renamed` included, also carries
      `columns`, the tab's columns in order as `{panes, expanded}` with pane
      IDs.
```

Proposed:

```markdown
    - `pane`: `pane-created`, `pane-moved`, `pane-renamed`, `pane-ended`,
      `pane-closed` and `pane-selected`, each with its `session`, `tab`
      and the pane, including EON-C10's nullable `tag`. A change to the pane's
      label, pin or tag emits `pane-renamed`, including a tag-only change.
      Each `pane` event, `pane-renamed` included, also carries `columns`, the
      tab's columns in order as `{panes, expanded}` with pane IDs.
```

Reason: expose tag changes through the existing event family.

### EONW recommendation and trade-off

**Recommend a distinct EONW bump, taking the next free version at xvz5c's own landing.**
The current canonical codec is v41. Its positional `Pane` encoding places
`pinned_name` before `attention`; adding `tag` changes those bytes, and rename
must distinguish omitted, set and clear tag updates. Neither can amend v41 in place.

Editor-popup routing (`eon-xodrj.5`) has landed as `825dd62`. Coordinate tags
with `eon-agent-parity-a9g0.1.1` jointly with `.1.3` after `.1.4`,
and `eon-u199d.6`. Each later landing rebases onto the landed schema, retains
all intervening changes and takes the next free version; it must never restore
an older checkpoint schema. Record the landing order and allocated versions
on the owning beads. This draft reserves no version and adds no dependency.

Runtime, CLI and Venus must consume the same canonical version, with rename's
omitted/set/clear distinction and tag on every existing pin projection.
Shown-session inbox rows obtain it from that pane data; remote queue pin/tag
enrichment stays with `eon-inbox-pinned-name-yiogr`. Metadata-only tag updates
must preserve navigation, scroll and attachments. Align current-version/package
references with the allocated version at implementation; retain historical
amendment/proof versions. Reserved Stop and the frozen six-byte EONW prefix stay unchanged.

Trade-off: a distinct version preserves exact-schema pairing and lets tags land
without waiting for all parity work, but whichever lands second must rebase and
repeat its affected proof. Existing windows route CLI calls through their recorded
old build, where `--tag` is unavailable; cross-version `eon window reload` is
refused. Tags require a fresh window with matching Runtime, CLI and Venus;
incompatible workspace clients remain refused. Preserve existing windows and
terminals: stopping their supervisor needs Lucca's separate authorization.
Lucca's approval must include that version incompatibility before implementation.

## eon-e5qjv — aligned line 2

Contracts: **VEN-C30** owns shared row presentation; **VEN-C32** keeps inbox
context while adopting the columns, both in `venus/docs/CONTRACTS.md`.
The VEN-C30 row clauses apply to both sidebar and attention inbox.

### VEN-C30 — line-2 contents (`venus/docs/CONTRACTS.md:2422`)

Current:

```markdown
      - the age;
      - the source terminal, by the pane's `pN` identity as in pane headers
        and AccessKit (VEN-C8), or, for a popup, its catalog label such as
        "Agent popup", because the spec says shown status should name its
        source terminal.
```

Proposed:

```markdown
      - line 2: on the left, the pane's canonical tag (blank when absent), or
        the popup's catalog label, including the Agent popup's Claude label;
        "+N" and "status stale" follow on the left. Retain the inbox's
        tab/session context (VEN-C32) and use only available metadata. On the
        right, a fixed-width,
        right-aligned age slot, then a left-aligned `pN` or `uN` ID column
        sized to the widest ID shown in that list, then a line-2 marker lane
        reserved on every row. Across mixed rows and tabs in each sidebar or inbox
        list, tag/label left edges, age right edges, ID left edges and marker
        lanes align in rendered pixels, not character padding. The left side
        truncates first; age and ID remain whole in a narrow inbox and at the
        sidebar's narrowest shown width under its 80-cell remaining-column
        hide rule. The marker lane and ID column stay clear of the sidebar's
        scroll-thumb gutter.
        Keep existing age formatting, including multi-digit days and absent
        ages. Age and ID remain left-to-right after RTL tags or labels.
```

Reason: state the approved columns, clipping order and scrollbar clearance while preserving inbox context.

### VEN-C30 — popup marker lane (`venus/docs/CONTRACTS.md:2433`)

Current:

```markdown
    - **Popup marker.** In the shown session, a row whose source terminal is a
      popup always shows two thin overlapping rounded-square outlines at the row's right edge,
      inside its padding and vertically centered across the row, larger than
      the label text. In both the sidebar and attention inbox, every text line stops
      before the marker, and the accessible label adds "popup".
```

Proposed:

```markdown
    - **Popup marker.** In the shown session, a row whose source terminal is a
      popup always shows two thin overlapping rounded-square outlines in the
      shared marker lane at the row's right edge, inside its padding and
      vertically centered across the row, larger than the label text. Pane
      rows leave the lane empty. In both the sidebar and attention inbox,
      every text line stops before the marker, and the accessible label adds
      "popup".
```

Reason: place the existing popup marker in the shared lane without changing its geometry.

### VEN-C30 — dim line 2 (`venus/docs/CONTRACTS.md:2456`)

Current:

```markdown
      Current text starts in the primary role and retains 4.5:1, including
      stale text; its badge keeps the bar's dark disc at rest.
```

Proposed:

```markdown
      Current line-1 and line-3 text starts in the primary role and retains 4.5:1,
      including stale text. All line-2 text uses the existing dim roles on
      every row, including current and hovered rows, retaining stale treatment
      and 4.5:1 contrast adaptation. The current row's badge keeps the bar's
      dark disc at rest.
```

Reason: keep all of line 2 dim while retaining line 1, contrast and badge behavior.

### VEN-C30 — accessible names (`venus/docs/CONTRACTS.md:2499`)

Current:

```markdown
  - **Accessibility.** The sidebar is one named AccessKit region after the
    header and before the panes. Each row's accessible name gives the state
    word, app, Claude Code's session name, tab, source terminal and message.
```

Proposed:

```markdown
  - **Accessibility.** The sidebar is one named AccessKit region after the
    header and before the panes. Each row's accessible name gives the state
    word, app, full row name, Claude Code's session name, full tag or popup
    label when available, target ID (`pN` or `uN`), tab location and
    message, regardless of visual clipping. It retains popup/current, age,
    "+N", stale and needs-input information.
```

Reason: expose full names, metadata, address and location despite visual truncation.

### VEN-C30 — tag-only refresh (`venus/docs/CONTRACTS.md:2510`)

Current:

```markdown
- **Attention-only refreshes.** A snapshot that differs only in attention or
  `sidebar` keeps rejected-action notices (VEN-C8) and disturbs no navigation,
  scroll, attachment or resize, as quota-only refreshes already do
  (`quota_refresh_and_workspace_failures_preserve_structure`); a change in the
  sidebar's visibility resizes the columns as Layout says. VEN-C8 and EON-C8
  carry this clause.
```

Proposed:

```markdown
- **Attention-only refreshes.** A snapshot that differs only in attention or
  `sidebar` keeps rejected-action notices (VEN-C8) and disturbs no navigation,
  scroll, attachment or resize, as quota-only refreshes already do
  (`quota_refresh_and_workspace_failures_preserve_structure`); a change in the
  sidebar's visibility resizes the columns as Layout says. VEN-C8 and EON-C8
  carry this clause. Tag-only updates repaint both row surfaces without
  changing selection, the inbox filter, scroll or attachment.
```

Reason: let tag edits update both row surfaces without disrupting the workspace view.

### VEN-C30 — consumed pane tag (`venus/docs/CONTRACTS.md:2516`)

Current:

```markdown
- **Consumes:** EONW v32 and the Codex and Claude marks of the quota chips
  ([Eon Bar](PRESENTATION.md#eon-bar)), which sidebar rows reuse.
```

Proposed:

```markdown
- **Consumes:** EONW v<landing version>, including EON-C10's nullable pane
  `tag`, and the Codex and Claude marks of the quota chips
  ([Eon Bar](PRESENTATION.md#eon-bar)), which sidebar rows reuse.
```

Reason: name the canonical tag data that the shared row presentation consumes.

Fill `<landing version>` with the allocated tag-bearing EONW version at
landing; this placeholder reserves no version.

### VEN-C32 — inbox context and shared columns (`venus/docs/CONTRACTS.md:2918`)

Current:

```markdown
    - A row shows the state glyph, the app icon and label as agent sidebar rows choose them
      (VEN-C30), and the age. A needs-input row adds one plain-text, truncated `msg` line. A
      stale record is dimmed and labelled "status stale".
    - A row of the shown session names its tab as sidebar tab headers do (`3  site`) and its
      source terminal as sidebar rows do. A row of another session names that session, by
      its name, else its ID, instead.
```

Proposed:

```markdown
    - Rows use VEN-C30's shared presentation, including its age, target-ID
      column and marker lane. A needs-input row adds one plain-text, truncated
      `msg` line. A stale record is dimmed and labelled "status stale".
    - On line 2's left, after the tag or popup label and before "+N" and
      "status stale", a shown-session row names its tab as sidebar tab headers
      do (`3  site`); another-session row names its session, by name, else ID,
      instead of the tab. This context does not shift the tag/label's left
      edge. The ID column always shows the queue entry's `pN` or `uN` target.
      Other-session rows retain their name fallback and use only available metadata.
```

Reason: preserve inbox location context while showing every target ID in the shared column.

Line 1, needs-input line 3, marker shape/size/stroke/vertical centering, row
geometry and navigation retain their existing rules. Rule 5 uses xvz5c's
explicit-ID CLI and JSON; no window action is added. Rule 6's fixed-layout
and existing-palette rationale remains in eon-e5qjv; tag validation bounds
remain fixed for plain-text safety and protocol size in eon-xvz5c.
Sidebar scrolling (`eon-r1scq`) has landed as `4b714f4`, with its trackless
thumb in its own gutter, clear of row fills, focus outlines and popup markers.
eon-e5qjv preserves that gutter clearance in its VEN-C30 text and layout.

Planning only: no implementation, contract edits, commits, builds, tests or
installed UI observation. These proposals claim no runtime proof.

Review: the initial fresh read-only pass has four findings addressed and the
fixed-age-slot objection rebutted. All five subsequent Opus review points are
adopted per the overseer's latest instruction. See [review dispositions](REVIEW.md)
and [Opus revision record](bead/00-plan.md).

title: Show Amp quota in the Eon Bar through CodexBar
description:
## Why

Lucca, 2026-10-29: "is it easy to support amp quota's widget" / "create a bead". Amp is an agent
people run inside Eon (ampcode.com; on ~/pjs/refs/WATCHLIST.md as a complement). Eon's bar shows
Codex and Claude quota through pinned CodexBar (EON-C22, EON-C26, EON-C27; VEN-C22, VEN-C26).

## Evidence (read 2026-10-29)

- Pinned CodexBar 0.74.1 (`7c08c0a`, components/eon-v4.json `codexbar`, flake.nix:199) already has
  an Amp provider: Sources/CodexBarCore/Providers/Amp/ (AmpProviderDescriptor.swift: source modes
  auto, api, web, cli; AmpCLIProbe.swift runs `amp usage` with NO_COLOR and a 15 s timeout and
  parses its text; AmpSettingsReader.swift: `AMP_API_KEY` for the api source).
- Amp's data differs from Codex and Claude (AmpUsageSnapshot.swift): Amp Free quota and amount used
  with hourly replenishment; individual and per-workspace credit balances (dollars); an optional
  subscription with plan, used percentage, orb hours and a reset date. Eon chips today show only
  windows, remaining percentages and resets, so a balance is a new presentation.
- CodexBar's latest release is v0.82.0 (2026-10-26); Eon pins 0.74.1.

## Scope

In scope:
1. First, evidence (Lucca agreed 2026-10-29): check CodexBar 0.74.1 to 0.82.0 release notes and the
   Amp and Codex provider diffs for output changes, and run `codexbar --provider amp --source cli`
   (exact flags per `codexbar --help`) on a signed-in Amp account; record the JSON shape here.
   Lucca's Amp account status is unconfirmed; if there is none, stop and park this bead.
2. Then, from that evidence, draft for Lucca's approval: an EON contract (Runtime reads Amp through
   CodexBar with an explicit CLI source, refresh interval, freshness, EONW field) and a VEN contract
   (an `amp_quota` widget in `[bar] widgets`, what the chip shows for Free, credits and a
   subscription, compaction and disappearance like VEN-C26), plus CONFIGURATION.md.
3. After approval: implementation in Runtime and Venus, an EONW version bump if a new field is
   needed (see the EONW bump rules), tests, and an installed observation.

Out of scope: account management, cost history (eon-7klz), changing Codex or Claude chips
(eon-7iml), a CodexBar version bump beyond what the evidence shows is needed (file it separately).

## Acceptance

- Step 1 recorded with revisions and the observed output; contract drafts approved before code;
  with a signed-in account, the installed bar shows Amp's chip and its hover and accessible label
  name Amp and the values' freshness.

## Verification

- Step 1-2: planning route. Step 3: shared runtime/wire route if EONW changes (full Rust and Nix
  surfaces), plus profile refresh and one isolated installed dogfood observation.

## Stop Conditions

- Stop if no Amp account is available for proof.
- Stop for contract approval before code.
- Stop if `amp usage` needs interactive login or a browser.

## Planning reconciliation (2026-11-12, dcaef1c)

Comments 4894/4902/4903 supersede unconfirmed-account/unfinished-Step-1 prose:
Lucca has an account and credits-only CodexBar evidence is recorded; no Amp pin
bump was needed by that historical comparison. Comment 4905 controls: Lucca
said 'if it's too hard, we can defer it'; no billing exception/code approval,
and questions 1-4 were withdrawn unanswered. Preserve status/defer_until; this
audit does not contact the account, reactivate or renew old contract drafts.
Reconsider only on observed Amp Free/subscription data or a relevant provider
change; recheck then-pinned JSON and exact contract choices first. Old EONW v26,
product 0.1.9 and versioned-manifest references are historical, not reservations
(current EONW v40). Scope the implementation only after this reopen gate and
selection; retain all original candidate presentations pending Lucca's choice.

No Amp Free quota line, no workspace balance, no subscription. So on this account the chip would show only a dollar balance, with no window or reset. comments.text:
## Step 2: questions for Lucca (claude-ampchip, 2026-10-29); code waits for answers

Lucca's account reports only an individual credit balance ($4.98), with no window or reset. So the chip has to show a dollar balance, and EON-C27 today keeps billing data out of EONW, logs and stored readings.

1. **Show Amp's individual credit balance (billing data) as the Amp chip?** Recommended: yes, as the only billing fact allowed, because without it the chip shows nothing on your account. Exact contract text:

   **EON-C27** amendments:
   - Consumer, trigger and result:
     - "for Codex (`--source cli`) and Claude (`--source oauth`)" → "for Codex (`--source cli`), Claude (`--source oauth`) and Amp (`--source cli`)".
     - "Codex reads start at least one minute apart and Claude reads at least five minutes apart" → "Codex reads start at least one minute apart and Claude and Amp reads at least five minutes apart".
     - After "No reset is invented for an idle window." add: "For Amp, Eon reads only the individual credit balance CodexBar reports, in whole US cents, and shows it in one chip (VEN-C33); Amp windows and workspace balances are not read, and a reading without that balance has no chip."
   - Failure policy: add "An Amp balance that is not a non-negative US-dollar amount with cents fails the read."
   - Boundary: "No credential, identity, raw output or billing data enters EONW, Eon logs or the stored readings." → "No credential, identity, raw output or billing data enters EONW, Eon logs or the stored readings, except Amp's individual credit balance (`eon-xw4l`)."

   **EON-C10** CLI JSON:
   - "`sidebar`, `codex_quota` and `claude_quota` on the snapshot." → "`sidebar`, `codex_quota`, `claude_quota` and `amp_quota` on the snapshot."
   - Append after the windows sentence: "`amp_quota` is null while Runtime holds no Amp reading, else `state` (`fresh` or `stale`), `observed_at` and `credits_cents`, the individual credit balance in whole US cents."

   **New VEN-C33 — Amp credits chip:**
   - **Status:** Proposed (`eon-xw4l`).
   - **Consumer:** One person using a Venus surface controlled by a full Eon workspace.
   - **Trigger:** A complete canonical EONW v26 snapshot supplies, changes or removes its optional Amp observation while `--bar-items` lists `amp_quota`.
   - **Result:** Venus shows one read-only Amp chip in the existing Eon Bar row: Amp's mark, then the individual credit balance in US dollars with cents and thousands separators, such as `[mark] $4.98`, followed by `old` when stale. Its hover text and static accessible label name Amp and its individual credits, the amount, and whether the reading is fresh or old.
   - **Ownership:** Runtime alone supplies the balance, age and invalidation (EON-C27). Venus formats the amount and uses its existing Scene, renderer, hover and AccessKit owners. The chip hides with the other quota chips, one by one, the one closest to the tabs first, before tabs, controls or drag space. The Codex and Claude chips are unchanged.
   - **Failure:** An absent observation has no chip, gap or accessible node. Workspace transport loss removes it while keeping the last useful topology. Quota-only changes do not replace attachments, scroll positions or navigation. The chip has no action, keyboard focus target or threshold color.
   - **Consumes:** Canonical EONW v26 quota fields; the in-tree Orbit codec stays unchanged.
   - **Boundary:** No provider parsing, credential access, client polling, pace color, low-balance alert, workspace balance, Amp window, account identity, new module, dependency, framework, row or platform promise. Amp's mark comes from Amp's own published artwork, recorded in venus/docs/REFERENCES.md, and appears only in this chip.

2. **Is `amp_quota` on by default?** The proposal lists it after `claude_quota`. Recommended: yes. Without Amp it shows nothing, and the cost is one failing CodexBar call every five minutes, using the same login-shell PATH lookup Codex already uses. Exact text:
   - **EON-C32:**
     - "`codex_quota`, `claude_quota`, `cpu`, `ram`, `clock` and `version`" → "`codex_quota`, `claude_quota`, `amp_quota`, `cpu`, `ram`, `clock` and `version`".
     - "Omitting the key shows all six in that order." → "Omitting the key shows all seven in that order."
     - Boundary "No per-widget option, configurable hiding priority, new widget, …" → "No per-widget option, configurable hiding priority, new widget other than `amp_quota` (`eon-xw4l`), …".
   - **VEN-C29:** the same name list and default order with `amp_quota` after `claude_quota`. Boundary "…configurable hiding priority or new item." → "…configurable hiding priority or new item other than `amp_quota` (VEN-C33)."
   - The alternative, valid but off by default, needs a default-versus-valid split that EON-C32 does not have.

3. **Credits only in this bead; Amp Free, subscription and orb windows and workspace balances in a follow-up bead?** Recommended: yes. No observed account has those, and today's `amp usage` printed no Free line, so CodexBar's Free and subscription parsers can't be checked against real output. A subscriber without individual credits would see no chip until the follow-up lands. I file the follow-up when this lands.

4. **Which Amp mark?** Recommended: Amp's official mark, monochrome like Codex's, taken from an Amp-owned source, with its file, revision, hash and brand terms recorded as for OpenAI's. ## Step 1 evidence (2026-10-29, claude-ampchip)

- Pinned CodexBar v0.74.1, tag commit `7c08c0ae783b72040b728757eb85a6cfe4fc2443` (matches components/eon-v5.json). Latest v0.82.0, `7749f7b94ae8f1b84b9ffb2046643cec810f4078` (2026-10-26).

The CLI JSON gains only optional keys Eon does not read (RateWindow `title`/`quotaLimit`/`quotaUnit`, `throughput`, row `severity`, `ageSeconds` for `codexbar-app` cache fallback, which needs no `--source`). Codex `codex-cli` labels and primary/secondary encoding are unchanged. **No CodexBar bump is needed for Amp.**
- amp `0.0.1792051250-g2fc5c0` (released 2026-10-15). `NO_COLOR=1 amp usage </dev/null` exited 0 in 0.51 s with no login, browser or prompt. It printed no `Amp Free:`, subscription, tier or workspace line.
- `CodexBarCLI usage --provider amp --source cli --format json --json-only --web-timeout 8 </dev/null` exited 0 in 0.57 s with empty stderr:

  `--source auto` gave the same content, still `"source":"cli"`. The web source was not tried, because it can read browser cookies.
- From the source (v0.74.1, inference about other accounts):
  - Credits are formatted by `UsageFormatter.usdString`: en_US USD currency, such as `$4.98` or `$1,234.56`.
  - Amp Free and subscription windows map to `primary`/`secondary`. `windowMinutes` may be absent (Free dollar form without replenishment, tier without a period line), and a subscription's two windows share one duration.

**Approach.** Runtime reads Amp through the existing CodexBar worker as a third provider (`amp`, `--source cli`, at least five minutes apart, same 10 s deadline, 64 KiB cap, freshness and stored-reading rules). It takes the one `details` section titled `Credits`, row `Individual`. That row's value must match en_US USD with cents (`^\$\d{1,3}(,\d{3})*\.\d{2}$`); anything else fails the read. The result is stored as whole cents. Workspace rows, windows and identity are ignored. A successful read without the Individual row clears the reading.

EONW v25 to v26 adds `amp_quota: Option<AmpQuota { state: Fresh|Stale, observed_at, credits_cents: u64 }>` at the end of the snapshot. CLI JSON gains `amp_quota`. Venus shows one chip, `[Amp mark] $4.98`, with `old` when stale.

**Files and functions.**
- runtime/crates/eon-runtime/src/quota.rs: the provider slot table, the argv `--source`, an Amp branch of `normalize`, and the stored-reading shape for `amp.json`.
- runtime/crates/eon-workspace-protocol: `v25.rs` becomes `v26.rs`, with `VERSION`, encode/decode/validate, inline goldens and the frame budget. Every `v25` import is updated.
- runtime/.../workspace.rs (CLI JSON `json_quota` and the golden) and supervisor.rs (`apply`, `--bar-items` default test).
- eon/crates/eon/src/product.rs (`bar_widgets` default) and fixtures.rs.
- eon/crates/eon/Cargo.toml and Cargo.lock: product version 0.1.8 to 0.1.9, per DISTRIBUTION.md's bump rule.
- components/eon-v5.json: the EONW versions and the protocol subtree proof hash.
- venus/src/launch.rs (`parse_bar_items`), scene.rs (`BarItem::AmpQuota`, `QuotaProvider::Amp`, projection, text and description), render/chrome.rs and palette.rs (the Amp mark mask), accessibility.rs (node id) and model.rs (repaint and transport loss).
- Docs: CONFIGURATION.md (Agent quota, `[bar] widgets`), USAGE.md, both CONTRACTS.md, CHANGELOG.md, venus/CHANGELOG.md, venus/docs/REFERENCES.md (mark provenance), runtime/README.md (EONW history) and the `EONW v25` mentions.

**Red checks.**
1. A quota.rs worker test fed the observed credits-only payload (redacted) yields an Amp reading of 498 cents. A malformed value, a negative or currency-less value, `source:"oauth"`, a stale `updatedAt` or a non-null `error` never becomes a reading. A payload with no Individual row clears it.
2. An EONW v26 golden that round-trips `amp_quota` and rejects v25 frames.
3. A Venus scene/accessibility test: chip text `$4.98` and `$4.98 old`; `$1,234.56`; hover and the accessible label name Amp credits and freshness; no node when absent; the chip falls with the quota chips under pressure.
4. The CLI JSON golden includes `amp_quota`.

**Checks.**
- `nix develop -c eon-test -p eon-runtime`, `-p eon-workspace-protocol`, `-p yazelix-venus` and `-p eon`.
- `cargo fmt --check` and `cargo clippy --locked --all-targets -- -D warnings` for Venus and the Runtime crates.
- Shared wire route: the affected Nix checks (orbit-free; Venus and the eon package build) and the manifest proof hash. A full `nix build .#default` runs only after a go from eon-overseer.

**Scope boundary.** In: the individual credit balance, `amp_quota` widget, EONW v26, CLI JSON and docs. Out:
- Amp Free, subscription and orb windows, and workspace balances (follow-up bead, Q3);
- a sidebar Amp icon (VEN-C30);
- a low-balance alert or color;
- account identity;
- any CodexBar bump;
- the web and api sources;

**Reference gate (consequential: wire format, contract, dependency use).**

title: Show Eon Bar widget tooltips as short lists without repeating the chip
description:
## Why

Lucca, 2026-11-06: "i think the widgets tooltips would read better in list format instead of a large string", "and we could consider not repeating the same info", then "i meant up for you to decide": the overseer decides the format and the cuts.

Today each Eon Bar widget's hover tooltip is one long sentence that is also its accessible text, built in Venus (no protocol change): quota `quota_text` (venus/src/scene.rs ~2391-2466), CPU/RAM/disk (venus/src/system.rs ~153-394), clock (scene.rs ~800-805), version (scene.rs ~3173). Example: "Codex quota state: fresh. 7d window: 50% remaining; observed 2d15h into 7d. At this pace it runs out about 1d18h before reset." The tooltip already renders `\n` as line breaks (venus/src/render/chrome.rs ~1000-1059, wrapped, capped at 40 em).

## Decisions (overseer, under Lucca's delegation)

1. **Visual tooltip becomes a short list**, one fact per line. The first line names the widget; the following lines give only facts the chip itself does not already show (no repeated percentage or elapsed/duration the chip prints).
2. **Accessible text stays a full sentence and unchanged** (screen readers announce the whole fact set, including what the chip shows); the visual tooltip and the accessible text become separate strings.
3. **Normal states stay quiet:** "fresh" and normal load are not listed; stale data, blocked or unknown permission, high load, memory pressure and a filling or nearly full disk each get their own line.
4. Target shapes (exact wording may be tuned in implementation; record the final strings):
   - Quota: `Claude 5h window` (or `Fable-only 7d window`) / `Resets in 50m` (or `Reset time unavailable`) / `Lasts until reset at this pace` or `Runs out about 1d18h before reset` or `Used up until reset` / `Data is stale` (only when stale) / `Permission blocked` (only when so).
   - CPU: `CPU · 8 logical CPUs` / `18% on average over the last 60 s` (when the average exists) / `Under high load` (when so).
   - RAM: `RAM · 16.0 GiB` / `Under pressure` (when so).
   - Disk: `Disk · /home` / `15.0 GiB free of 100.0 GiB` / `Filling up` (when so).
   - Clock: `Wednesday 21 October 2026` / `UTC−03:00`.
   - Version: `Eon version 0.1.18` (the full version string, which the chip may shorten).

## Acceptance

- Each widget's tooltip shows the list above on hover; accessible text is unchanged (existing accessibility assertions still pass unchanged).
- venus/docs/PRESENTATION.md (Eon Bar, "Hover and accessibility") and docs/USAGE.md (~239-252) describe hover as the list and accessibility as before; CHANGELOG entry.
- Tests assert each widget's tooltip lines (including the stale, blocked, high-load, pressure and disk states); an isolated installed screenshot of at least the quota and disk tooltips.

comments.text:
# eon-y22fl implementation notes

Base: edge 605cca5, moved to edge 03f72d3 for review round 1 (that commit touches only
eon/crates/eon/tests/workspace_control.rs and .beads; no overlap), then to edge 78e14de for
round 2 (runtime window CLI; CHANGELOG.md conflict resolved keeping both Unreleased
entries, this one first; docs/USAGE.md merged cleanly). Venus-only presentation
change: no EONW, protocol, contract or configuration change.

## Shape

Each Eon Bar widget now carries two strings:

- `tooltip`: the hover list (`\n`-separated lines, drawn by `build_header_tooltip` in
  venus/src/render/chrome.rs, which already renders `\n` as line breaks).
- `description`: the accessible text, byte-for-byte unchanged from before.

Changed holders: `QuotaText`/`WorkspaceQuota` and `WorkspaceLabel` (venus/src/scene.rs),
`LocalClock` (scene.rs), `CpuUse`, `RamUse`, `DiskUse` (venus/src/system.rs). The tooltip
renderer reads `tooltip` for quota, version, CPU, RAM, disk and clock; accessibility
(venus/src/accessibility.rs ~534, ~547) still reads `description`. The render content key
(venus/src/render.rs) keeps keying on the CPU/RAM/disk descriptions, which hold every fact
those tooltips list plus the use the label shows; only its comment changed.

Review round 1: the reset line is now the reset's local wall-clock time, so `EonBar` gained
`now: Option<&jiff::Zoned>`, the local time the scene is built at. The app fills it with
`local_now()` (venus/src/application.rs), the same system time zone lookup the clock widget
uses (`read_local_clock` now calls it), at each scene build; the scene is rebuilt on demand,
including on hover, so the day it judges against is current when the tooltip is drawn.
Tests pass a fixed `now`. The round-0 `quota_unit` helper is gone again (the pace code keeps
its original inline unit) and the description uses `quota_window_position` as before.

## Final tooltip strings

Quota (first line names provider, optional scope and window; `{name} quota` when there is no
window, i.e. blocked/unknown):

- `Codex 5h window` / `Claude 7d window` / `Claude Fable-only 7d window`
- Reset, from `resets_at` in the local time zone (overseer decision, review round 1):
  `Resets at 18:30` when the reset falls today, `Resets Tue 18:30` within the next six days,
  `Resets 14 Nov 18:30` after that (jiff strftime `at %H:%M`, `%a %H:%M`, `%-d %b %H:%M`;
  minutes truncated). `Has reset since this reading` when the reset is at or before now
  (a stale reading whose window has since reset). `Reset time unavailable` without a reset.
  Without a local time zone (`now` none) the reset line is left out, as the bar leaves out
  the clock rather than show UTC.
- Pace (fresh windows with a basis only): `Lasts until reset at this pace`,
  `Runs out about {t} before reset`, `Used up until reset`.
- `Data is stale` (stale), `Permission blocked` (blocked), `Permission unknown` (unknown).

Examples: `Codex 7d window\nResets Sun 21:00\nRuns out about 1d18h before reset`;
`Codex 5h window\nResets at 12:30\nData is stale`; `Codex quota\nPermission blocked`.

CPU: `CPU · {n} logical CPU(s)` / `{a}% on average over the last {s} s` (once the average
window is spanned; `{s}` is `[bar] cpu_average_seconds`) / `Under high load` (when high).

RAM: `RAM · {total:.1} GiB` / `Under pressure` (orange) or `Under heavy pressure` (red).

Disk: `Disk · {mount}` / `{free:.1} GiB free of {size:.1} GiB` / `Filling up` (orange) or
`Nearly full` (red).

Clock: `{Weekday D Month YYYY}` / `UTC±HH:MM` (U+2212 minus, as the accessible text).

Version: `Eon version {version}` (the full version; accessible text stays
`Running Eon version {version}`).

## Deviations and wording tuned

- Scoped quota first line is `Claude Fable-only 7d window` (the bead's target was
  `Fable-only 7d window`): decision 1 says the first line names the widget, and the
  provider name keeps it consistent with unscoped chips.
- The bead named critical states only as "memory pressure" and "nearly full disk"; RAM's
  red level reads `Under heavy pressure`, matching the accessible words, and disk's orange
  reads `Filling up`, red `Nearly full`.
- Added `Has reset since this reading` and `Permission unknown`, states the target list did
  not spell out.
- Round 0 used `Resets in {t}` counted from the observation; review round 1 replaced it with
  the absolute local time above, which stays right however old the reading is.
- The clock's first line is the date, not the item's name (overseer, round 1: the date is
  self-evident); PRESENTATION.md names that exception.
- Review round 2: the render content key (venus/src/render.rs `ContentKey`) now includes
  every quota tooltip's text, so any redraw after the local day turns shows the current
  wording. No day-boundary timer was added (overseer, round 2): a tooltip lives only while
  hovered, and the next hover rebuilds it, so a tooltip held open across midnight keeps
  its wording only until the bar next redraws (any hover change, clock minute, reading or
  snapshot change). PRESENTATION.md says so.
- Review round 2: once `now` is at or past the reset, hover shows `Has reset since this
  reading` and drops the pace line, which looks ahead to the reset; the accessible
  description keeps the pace sentence unchanged. `quota_reset` returns none for a passed
  reset so `quota_text` can tell.
- The DST test uses a POSIX rule zone (`EST5EDT,M3.2.0,M11.1.0`, New York's rule) rather
  than `America/New_York`: Venus's jiff reads named zones from the system zoneinfo
  (`tzdb-zoneinfo`), which the test sandbox and Nix builds need not have.

## Contracts and docs

- No contract text change: EON-C32's "the average CPU use that its hover and accessibility
  text also give" and EON-C27's "reset details on hover" still hold. No
  bead/01-contract-step.md was needed.
- venus/docs/PRESENTATION.md (Eon Bar): each "Hover and accessibility say X" now says what
  accessibility says and what hover lists, plus one bullet on the hover list rule (with the
  clock's exception) and the reset's local-time forms.
- docs/USAGE.md: quota hover line and one sentence on hover lists vs screen readers.
- docs/CONFIGURATION.md unchanged: its "Hover and accessible labels report that absence"
  stays true (`Reset time unavailable`).
- CHANGELOG.md Unreleased entry.

## Configurability (rule 6): why the tooltip wording stays fixed

The tooltip lines are product text, fixed like the accessible descriptions beside them and
like every other Venus label: the support cost of making hover wording configurable (a
template language for hover lines, its validation and docs) outweighs users differing on
wording. Every value the lines show already derives from one setting: the CPU averaging
window (`[bar] cpu_average_seconds`), the load levels behind the load lines
(`[bar] *_warning_percent`, `*_critical_percent`), the disk path (`[bar] disk_path`), which
widgets show (`[bar] widgets`), and the reset's time zone (the system's, as for the clock).
No new setting.

## Humans and agents (rule 5)

Hover is Venus-local view state, an exception in Humans and Agents; no window action
changes, so no CLI path is needed.

title: Let agents wait for a heavy-job slot: eon slot run --class heavy
description:
## Why

Filed on Lucca's approval relayed by the Starcompass session (starcompass-8c, 2026-11-02, Lucca: "agreed."). Starcompass owns the policy (AP-COORDINATOR-001: one coordinator schedules heavy runs and installs against machine load); Eon owns the mechanism. On 2026-11-02 six Eon pane agents ran builds and test suites at once and load reached 30 on 16 cores. Starcompass will add a tool-neutral AP-COORDINATOR-001 clause ("run heavy builds, tests, and installs through the host's job-slot mechanism when one exists") once this ships.

## Change

- `eon slot run --class heavy -- COMMAND...`: waits until one of N heavy slots is free, runs COMMAND, frees the slot when COMMAND exits, including on crash or kill (the slot is held by a lock tied to the running process, so a dead holder never leaks a slot).
- `eon slot list [--json]`: holders (pid, command, start time, caller pane if any) and waiters.
- Scope: per user, machine-wide, through a per-user lock directory (e.g. under the user runtime dir), so it covers every Eon window and agents outside Eon. Works without a running supervisor.
- N from config, e.g. `[agents] heavy_slots = 2`, default documented in docs/CONFIGURATION.md (rule 6).
- Not in scope: lower nice or cgroup limits for slot holders (unfiled option (c)); any scheduling policy (Starcompass's).

## Prerequisites

The `load` figures bead (filed alongside) comes first.

## Contract

New EON-C text; stop for Lucca's approval of exact text.

## Acceptance

Tests: N=1 serializes two commands; a killed holder frees its slot; `--json` shape; works with no supervisor. Isolated installed check with two concurrent `eon slot run` commands. docs/USAGE.md, CONFIGURATION.md, CHANGELOG.
close_reason: Duplicate of eon-eon-agent-lr8sx.21 (the machine-wide heavy-run queue Lucca asked for on 2026-11-09, which adds FIFO order, quiet windows and wait alerts to the same slots). The decisions recorded here (Lucca 2026-11-02: Starcompass owns policy, Eon the mechanism; per-user scope without a supervisor; one flock file per slot; the eon slot name; the open model-checker choice) are carried in eon-eon-agent-lr8sx.21.1. The ordering after eon-7i3t9 (load figures) is not carried: the slot mechanism reads no load figures. Closed by prime-beads 2026-11-10.

comments.text: Decisions (Lucca, 2026-11-02, 'agreed', relayed by starcompass-8c after a read-only study of Eon's Bend2 use): 1 a model checker is accepted as a design-time tool for this bead under docs/AGENT-RULES.md's new-language rule (around lines 251-255), scoped to TLA+/PlusCal as a design-time spec language that ships nothing; that rule text still needs recording in AGENT-RULES.md (overseer to do in the landing commit that next touches rules); 2 PlusCal checked with TLC; 3 lock primitive: one flock'd file per slot (the kernel frees a crashed holder's lock); 4 Bend2 stays on Orbit's policy only. Contract work for this bead now includes a PlusCal model (150-250 lines; acquire, release, crash, wait; small N) checked by TLC for: never more than N holders; a crashed holder's slot is eventually freed; no starvation under fairness (flock waiters are not FIFO, so a ticket or queue file may be needed). Model and code are linked through this bead's tests (N=1 serializes; a killed holder frees its slot). Not covered: slot code before Lucca approves the EON-C text; how TLC and a JVM are pinned (dependency rule, probably Nix). Estimate 0.5-1.5 agent-days.

comments.text: Correction, relayed by the Starcompass session (starcompass-8c), 2026-11-02. Lucca reopened the spec-language choice. The earlier relayed 'PlusCal/TLA+ checked with TLC' is no longer decided. Lucca's words: "ok". They were answering: "1. Settle it with a tiny spike in Eon before eon-y5ndl's contract work. I recommend this: write a minimal slot model of about 50 lines in Quint, and confirm three things: the simulator finds a known bug, export to TLC checks one fairness property, and the ITF Rust crate can read a trace. The three facts I'm unsure about decide this, and the spike costs a few hours instead of a day. 2. Pending the spike, lean toward Quint. I recommend it, because only it gives model-based tests against the Rust code. 3. Correct eon-y5ndl. The bead currently records PlusCal/TLC as your choice. I recommend sending a correction to Eon saying the language is open until the spike, so the next overseer doesn't build on a decision you've since reopened." Why Quint: its ITF trace format and the Rust itf crate let Rust tests replay model traces against the real slot code, which closes the model-to-code gap that Orbit's Bend work warns about. Quint's simulator needs only Node, which is present. Fairness and liveness checks probably still go through TLC, either via Quint's TLA+ export or directly, so a JVM is still needed for those. Unverified, and the spike settles it: how far Apalache's liveness support goes, whether quint/apalache are in nixpkgs, and how mature the itf crate is. Still decided and unchanged: a model checker as a design-time tool, an flock per slot file, Bend2 staying on Orbit's policy only. Next step: run the spike before the EON-C contract text. The AGENT-RULES.md new-language entry should name the language the spike picks.

# Plan review disposition — eon-yooz3

2026-11-10: newest overseer INBOX entry at 09:25:36Z instructs implementation with the fresh Opus plan review at `/home/lucca/.local/state/rota/runs/flaky-tests-planreview-opus-1/log`. The user explicitly directed this session to read and act on that entry. No author-run review was performed.

All findings accepted:

1. Establish actual peer closure with `shutdown(Shutdown::Both)` and retain a `try_clone` through acquisition as a deterministic inherited-descriptor regression. Show red with clone plus old drop-only fixture, green with shutdown. Untouched-baseline loaded failure: **not reproduced**, and no baseline repetition campaign will be run.
2. Remove both update tests' 200 ms scheduler assertions and 300 ms sleeping writers. Run interrupted confirmation in a worker with `recv_timeout(10 s)` solely as a hang safeguard. Preserve Interrupted/WouldBlock, descriptor flags, decline and EOF checks.
3. Leave the attention 50 ms assertion unchanged; create its own P2 bead now with br from `/home/lucca/pjs/eon/eon`. This explicit newest-entry authorization replaces the earlier prohibition on br writes/main-checkout activity only for that issue creation and flush. No implementation in the main checkout.
4. Leave the ignored ORB-C15 latency measurement unchanged; no follow-up absent an actual flake.
5. Build once, then 20 loaded iterations of one `eon-test` invocation naming the three exact tests. Run fmt, all-target clippy and touched-crate suites for `eon-runtime` and `eon`. Skip whole-workspace proof under this explicit review instruction: only test code in those crates changes.
6. macOS remains unproved locally. Rely on mac-proof after landing. If BSD socket shutdown semantics reject the Linux approach, the fallback is polling for hangup without consuming the queued reply; retain the clone regression while designing that fallback.

No contracts, production behavior, package build, installed profile, live process, or desktop focus changes. The overseer owns fresh implementation reviews and landing; this session stages without committing and reports `READY FOR REVIEW <tree> BASE <edge>`.

# Implementation — eon-yooz3

Only three existing tests change, in two files. No product helpers, callers, fixtures, exports, configuration, contracts or changelog changes are needed. Shared imports remain used by production update code. All eight management reply/peer cases and existing update error/descriptor/decline/EOF assertions remain.

- Management fixture retains a clone to model fork inheritance, then explicitly shuts down the peer before drop. Clone-only red at tree dc0b8fc failed with the historical Ok(()) error; final shutdown candidate is 24bfde3.
- Interrupted confirmation runs in a scoped thread; the channel's 10 s timeout is a hang safeguard. Reset the global interrupt flag and shut down the peer before the scoped join so a broken reader can return and the test can report the timeout.
- Drained-input read remains on the existing nonblocking descriptor and checks WouldBlock directly. Only then write the decline line and shut down Write; subsequent confirmation calls retain both decline and EOF coverage.
- No 200 ms assertions or 300 ms sleeping writers remain in those two tests. No bound was widened and no retries were added.

Plan review changes and macOS fallback are recorded in 01-plan-review.md. The attention follow-up is eon-l9ra7. The ignored ORB-C15 latency test is untouched. Tests and proof runner operate only through eon-test; the disposable loaded runner is external to the repository and not part of the candidate.

# Round 1 findings and author fixes — eon-yooz3

The user directed action on the newest INBOX entries. Overseer entries at 2026-11-10T09:42:16Z and 09:43:34Z authorize the following combined fix round after both reviews arrived. Reviews were run by the overseer, not the author.

- Opus report: `/home/lucca/.local/state/rota/runs/flaky-tests-opus-1/log`.
- Codex report: `/home/lucca/.local/state/rota/runs/flaky-tests-codex-1/report.md`.
- Reviewed tree: `24bfde3d6530b0932a062045d2babbbada09fcae`.

1. **Opus 1 / Codex 1, Darwin retained-peer semantics — accepted.** Gate only the retained `try_clone()` binding with `#[cfg(target_os = "linux")]`. Linux retains its deterministic inherited-descriptor red/green; Darwin drops the last test-owned peer descriptor. Production code and all error/reply cases are unchanged. The macOS inheritance gap gets a separate P2 bead from the main checkout as explicitly authorized. Reviewer Darwin findings are source-derived; no native run is claimed.
2. **Opus 2, scoped join hang limit — accepted as-is per overseer.** Keep the worker/scope cleanup. The 10 s receiver guard catches the current broken-reader path, shutdown releases poll/read, and scoped join avoids a stray thread. An arbitrary infinite loop ignoring EOF still needs the enclosing command timeout.
3. **Opus 3, nonblocking precondition — accepted.** Assert `flags & O_NONBLOCK != 0` before the drained-input test's raw read. Descriptor flag preservation and the Interrupted/WouldBlock/decline/EOF checks remain.

The original record's polling fallback is qualified by the reviews: polling alone cannot disconnect a socket while a test-owned clone remains. Any Darwin fallback must first release that clone, then wait for hangup without consuming queued reply bytes. The new follow-up records this explicitly.

Proof is authorized now that both reviews are in: fmt; Linux and aarch64-apple-darwin all-target clippy; focused sessions/update tests. Native Darwin runtime proof remains with mac-proof. Prior Linux loaded/suite proof belongs to the original reviewed tree and is not relabeled as proof of the revised tree. Each reviewer rechecks only its own finding.

## Why

The Runtime management-close fixture assumes dropping its socket peer makes an Acquire request unsendable. A concurrent fork can inherit the descriptor and keep that socket connected, allowing the valid queued Lease to be accepted. eon-yooz3 fixes the Linux fixture using peer shutdown and retains a duplicate descriptor to make the race deterministic. On macOS, the reviewers predict that retaining the duplicate defeats the expected failure even after peer shutdown, so the regression clone is Linux-only and the original macOS inheritance gap remains.

## Evidence

- `runtime/crates/eon-runtime/src/sessions.rs:2424`, `management_close_cannot_grant_an_unvalidated_or_unsent_lease`, at base `8b5ee2dfad19c15f73754cd370e79164cf2881fa` and eon-yooz3 review tree `24bfde3d6530b0932a062045d2babbbada09fcae`.
- The old drop-only fixture with a retained `peer.try_clone()` deterministically fails on Linux: `unwrap_err()` receives `Ok(())` for a valid peer with a full Lease. Shutdown makes that case green on Linux. Historical intermittent workspace failure: eon-ipc6f's `workspace-final.log`, summarized on eon-yooz3.
- Opus implementation review: `/home/lucca/.local/state/rota/runs/flaky-tests-opus-1/log`. Concern is that Darwin peer credentials remain available while a clone is held, and writes to a peer whose read side is shut down can report success while discarding bytes.
- Codex independently raised the same concern from Apple's published XNU send/shutdown implementation: https://github.com/apple-oss-distributions/xnu/blob/xnu-11417.121.6/bsd/kern/uipc_usrreq.c#L565-L746 and buffer discard implementation: https://github.com/apple-oss-distributions/xnu/blob/main/bsd/kern/uipc_socket2.c#L847-L857 . Its report is `/home/lucca/.local/state/rota/runs/flaky-tests-codex-1/report.md`.
- These Darwin semantics are source-derived review findings, **not a native macOS reproduction**. The overseer explicitly requested the P2 follow-up at 2026-11-10T09:42:16Z; subsequent user direction authorizes acting on that INBOX entry.

## Scope

Make the management-close test fixture independent of concurrent descriptor inheritance on macOS while preserving its full/malformed/truncated/empty queued replies and valid/invalid peer cases. Keep the observable rejection of an unvalidated or unsent acquisition request. Ownership is Runtime; this is a test-fixture issue under existing acquisition behavior, not a product guarantee change.

Out of scope: changing production acquisition, widening time bounds, adding retries, changing contracts/protocols, changing Linux's deterministic clone/shutdown coverage, or unrelated timing tests.

## Acceptance

- Native macOS evidence establishes what peer shutdown, retained descriptors, queued replies and peer credential lookup actually do.
- The fixture reaches real peer disconnection before asserting an unsent request; no scheduler-dependent drop assumption remains.
- A deterministic regression demonstrates the unsafe drop-only fixture and a corrected fixture passes repeated loaded native runs without weakening existing error assertions.
- No hangup wait is introduced while the test itself still holds a peer clone: release owned peer references first, and wait without consuming the queued reply.

## Implementation Notes

Use a fresh session and inspect Runtime's platform credential and socket helpers. Consider a non-consuming hangup wait after releasing the controlled duplicate, or another small platform-correct fixture. Do not copy Linux shutdown assumptions into Darwin. Record a neutral/test-only portability disposition unless native investigation finds a production defect; that broader boundary needs a separate decision.

## Verification

Use isolated native macOS `nix develop -c eon-test` or the supported mac-proof route with the exact candidate revision. Include deterministic red/green, 20 loaded repetitions of the affected test and the eon-runtime suite. Linux focused regression stays green. Run fmt and all-target clippy for the touched crate on supported target routes. A Linux cross-target clippy pass does not prove Darwin socket behavior.

## Stop Conditions

Stop and report if current test or acquisition code has materially drifted, or a complete fix requires a production/contract change. Do not change acquisition simply to satisfy a closed-peer fixture.

## Maintenance Notes

P2 follow-up from eon-yooz3's first Opus and Codex reviews. The temporary Linux-only clone gating preserves the pre-existing Darwin close path but does not claim the macOS fork-inheritance race is fixed. It can be removed only after equivalent native Darwin regression evidence. No dependency on changing product behavior; native macOS execution is a prerequisite for closing this issue.

description:

### Why

### Planned children / proof and stop rules

eon-yp6vg.1–eon-yp6vg.20, eon-yp6vg.7's three children and eon-yp6vg.21 in the table, ordered where ownership
and acceptance depend. Copy the parent
plan's end-state table, contract-draft table, P0–P3 routes, decision-41 rule,

## Durable approved plan

This accepted snapshot preserves ownership, exact proposed clauses, proof routes, collisions and exits. Its planning-phase filing instructions are historical; the current authorization permits filing only. Runtime gates remain binding.

# Venus onto Rune — migration plan for review

Planning snapshot: 2026-11-12; Eon worktree
`/home/lucca/.cache/eon-agents/rune-migration-plan`, HEAD
`afbd5b266343481b9c7aae9dca9e941f6eabecda`, EONW v41, Eon 0.1.23.
This file proposes future work. It changes no product, contract, tracker state,
release gate, or installed profile. Draft keys eon-yp6vg–eon-yp6vg.20, eon-yp6vg.7.1–eon-yp6vg.7.3 and eon-yp6vg.21 in `01-beads.md` are
local references, not Beads IDs. eon-yp6vg is an ordinary epic, not a milestone.

## Authority and absolute start gate

Read the **last** comment on `eon-t1rtk` and the final decisions in
`/home/lucca/.cache/eon-agents/rune-h-memo/MEMO.md`, not the superseded first
three bead bodies. Lucca's conditional go was relayed through eon-desk on
2026-11-12: plan/file now; start implementation without another migration ask
only after all of:

1. `eon-1cyzr` has **landed and passed its timing window**. A closed bead
   without the landing and timing receipts is insufficient.
2. `eon-t1rtk.1`, `.2`, `.3` are done with accepted proof. eon-yp6vg and eon-yp6vg.1 have
   direct blocking dependencies on `.3`; its existing `.2 -> .1 -> eon-azfsx`
