   eon-yp6vg.1 and their parent epic. Re-read that chain before starting.
3. **`eon-igae.9` is closed with the actual v0.2.0 cut receipt.** This is the
   cut task, whereas `eon-igae` includes post-tag site/demo/announcement work.
   Do not wait for that larger epic, depend on a re-proof instead, or add this
   migration as a blocker of the beta cut.

eon-yp6vg and eon-yp6vg.1 carry the three direct edges: `eon-1cyzr`, `eon-t1rtk.3`,
**`eon-igae.9`**. Every other implementation/proof/spike task is blocked
transitively by eon-yp6vg.1 as well as its parent epic. eon-yp6vg.1 acceptance explicitly
requires the hosted-refactor landing SHA and timing-window PASS receipt,
accepted t1rtk.1–.3 receipts, and the real v0.2.0 cut receipt before any
downstream session starts. Closing 1cyzr alone never releases that gate. Nothing
of this migration lands in Eon before the three gates. Neither this plan nor
the conditional go authorizes a release, promotion, public message, fork
publication, new platform, or unreviewed contract amendment.

The public Cargo pin additionally waits for `eon-t1rtk.4` publication and
read-back of its immutable commit. The prompt/final memo retain the typed-words
publication gate. That bead also contains a 13:29Z approval comment (answer
`1`), corrected at 14:24Z to Yazelix/eon-rune. The overseer must reconcile the
receipt there; migration agents never publish or infer completion from it.
This extra delivery dependency does not replace the three adoption gates.

## End state and one owner per responsibility

| Owner | Owns after migration |
| --- | --- |
| Orbit | PTYs, VT parsing, terminal state, history/selection, semantic input encoding, image resource authority and ORBF/ORBS. |
| Runtime / Eon | Canonical EONW, topology/lifetimes/consent, attention normalization and ordering, configuration parsing/resolution, exact composition, updates and distribution. |
| Venus | Canonical validation/model/transport, terminal Scene and grid draw inputs, glyphon/cosmic-text grid shaping and row cache, image validation/budget/drawing, cursor trail, terminal input admission and revision gates, scroll/selection policy, terminal font metrics, workspace/product interaction policy, the Rune views and the Eon-specific contour/fitting bridge. |
| Rune via Yazelix/eon-rune | Native window/event loop, graphics adapter/device/surface/submit/present and existing surface-failure handling, redraw scheduling, native input/IME/clipboard mechanisms, chrome layout/text/control mechanics, hit testing/hover/press/focus plumbing and one native AccessKit host/tree for Rune chrome. |

Rune is a Venus dependency, not a new runtime process or Eon component graph.
Venus still has one native window per process. Orbit frames become the same
Venus grid inputs inside `Compositor` / `El::effect` / `draw_with`; stable
terminal/attachment identities key resources. Rune owns final painter order,
slot clipping and target lifetime; Venus retains image/text/cursor ordering
within each grid. No PTY, vt100 parser or hand-copied EONW schema from the spike
examples enters Venus. Those examples demonstrate hosting, not the production
terminal authority boundary.

Remove the custom Venus native event loop/surface/present owner, native
clipboard workers and native AccessKit adapter after their replacements work.
Remove manual chrome draw batches, text buffers, SceneRects, hit chains,
hover/press fields, focus traversal and chrome AccessKit node construction
surface by surface in the final deletion inventory. Retain contour/coverage,
cluster-safe fitting and geometry helpers with live grid/feature consumers;
track I explicitly did **not** prove all of those deletable. Preserve semantic
consent, stable-target, focus and terminal regressions while replacing tests of
deleted internals. No compatibility alias, old-renderer option or product
fallback remains after cutover. eon-yp6vg.21 removes inventoried unreachable chrome immediately after eon-yp6vg.20; the small
bounded interval exposes no old selectable backend. A reviewed revert is the
rollback mechanism.

Terminal screen-reader text is a deliberate, separately approved gap until
Anomaly supplies Rune's terminal accessibility (#542). No fork implementation
or second AccessKit host is planned. Chrome names/actions and failure notices
remain required. See the contract drafts below; the memo's reference to VEN-C6
is stale, and must not revive that retired ID.

GPU device loss remains **terminal** under VEN-C4/VEN-C31: withdraw presented
input, show bounded truthful failure where presentation permits, and release
client resources without stopping Orbit. Rune automatic device-loss recovery
must not resume this Venus client. Surface reconfiguration still follows
existing accepted behavior. DeviceKey/format checks protect resource identity;
they do not authorize hot device replacement or image resync after terminal
device loss.

## Evidence and limits

required in the brief), venus/AGENTS, Venus CONTRACTS/PRESENTATION/DEVELOPMENT,
the native-host/history/input/reference routes in venus/docs/REFERENCES.md,
manifests and the affected application/renderer/accessibility entry points.
Runtime/Orbit implementation is excluded; a future need to edit either first
requires its directory instructions and a separately scoped decision.

Primary local source inspected: upstream `/home/lucca/pjs/refs/rune` and dirty
spike `/home/lucca/pjs/refs/rune-spike` both at
`3686e94ae09545fd5f2a61e22aabfbeba1cd896f`. `compose.rs` documents device-key

## Dependency decision

Adopt the chosen fork only in the first slice exercising the real candidate
host (eon-yp6vg.7), after the mechanism spikes. Pin
`rune = { git = "https://github.com/Yazelix/eon-rune.git", rev = "<reviewed published sha>", optional = true, default-features = false, features = ["accessibility"] }`
subject to exact-pin feature inspection. Accessibility is needed for chrome;
add another feature only with its demonstrated current consumer. Omit
`metal-backend` (Rune's custom backend) and `ogg-audio`; Apple uses the existing
wgpu Metal path. Terminal glyphon/cosmic-text stays; chrome uses Rune's
Parley/swash with the actual registered packaged sans face and existing metrics.

`7c209ec5bebbd2963f75a39f79b320af6b03f72c` unless separately approved.

Rejected for this chosen migration: a parallel Venus control framework,
replacing the terminal renderer, Rune-specific look patches, terminal

(inbox); VEN-C1/C5/C7/C8/C10/C13/C14/C16/C17/C19/C20/C21 beyond the clauses above.

drafts no recoverable-loss amendment.

Composed Eon contracts touched only in proof: EON-C1/C2/C3/C4/C5/C6 (exact
graph, distribution-neutral build and archive), C10/C11/C12/C16 (canonical
actions, admission/reload/recovery, standalone, identity), C19/C20/C21/C24
(configuration, shortcuts, header and hints), C22/C25/C26/C27/C29/C30/C31/C32

Any wider contract diff returns through the overseer before implementation.

## Proof routes for future sessions

No checks in this section have been run by this planning session.

**P0 — planning/contracts.** Re-read IDs, dependencies, exact changed text,
diff and current approval receipts. Planning gets the overseer's one fresh
read-only Opus review. Contract edits also need required Codex text review;
no runtime claim or suite for text alone.

**P1 — correctness.** A few meaningful checks in existing Venus scene,
application, renderer and accessibility suites protect canonical state,
presented revision/geometry, input suppression, close-consent races and each
surface's named failures. Port existing semantic tests; do not replace them
with snapshots of a hand-written model. Use
`nix develop -c eon-test -p yazelix-venus` while iterating; fmt and locked
all-target clippy for changed crates. Final code/test/script tree gets one
whole-workspace `nix develop -c eon-test` before review, Tier 1 frame invariants,
fresh Claude and required Codex via the overseer, then the narrow finder rule.
Reviewers do not run checks. Text-only fixes need no re-run.

**P2 — frame timing, required for every changed render path.** Use the same
machine's parent artifact and its local baseline, matched workload, fonts,
adapter/driver, scale, window/grid size, build/profile and settings. Two complete
`eon-bench gate --baseline "${XDG_STATE_HOME:-$HOME/.local/state}/eon-bench/baseline-<machine>.json"`
runs. Without a baseline, record the parent with `--record-baseline`; a missing
check is a gap, not a pass. The standard gate fails when the same cell's p50
**and** p95 exceed baseline by >25% in **both** runs. Preserve gxb4's accepted
all-change comparison and do not silently trade away its ~5% constraint.
Measure one-cell/all-cell at the existing three grid sizes, equal write, scroll,
blink and link/chrome hover so caching regressions cannot hide in throughput.

Separately run the accepted azfsx **no-fade** transition scenario at 120 Hz in
two granted quiet runs: popup show/hide, split, split restore, solo/zoom switch,
tab switch, and selection ending zoom. Require positive before/after witnesses
for the exact target and layout, plus negatives proving missing transitions,
stale hook/buffer geometry and dropped trace records cannot pass. Include all
frames; no allowlist, raised threshold, synthetic F6 fade or discarded slow
transition. Record frame maxima/distributions and layout/prepare/encode/submit
attribution; CPU-side 8.33 ms is not scanout/presented-latency proof. Combine
the relative runs and no-fade runs into **one estimated quiet-slot booking per
bead**, preparing all builds/scripts first; use multiple bookings only if the
combined estimate exceeds 90 minutes, with a recorded reason.

**Decision 41:** re-measure **restore and selection-ends-zoom** at the first
Rune-hosted Venus grid in eon-yp6vg.2 (including a record if a terminal-failure path
prevents a transition), then at the real production-grid candidate eon-yp6vg.7, again after composition/geometry
changes (especially eon-yp6vg.9/eon-yp6vg.12), after a relevant fork bump, and on eon-yp6vg.20's exact
final candidate. **Report every frame over 8.33 ms to the overseer**, with
trace, exact identities and attribution. Relative Tier 2 success does not waive
that report or the absolute transition gate. Stop acceptance/landing of the
failing candidate while applying the bounded patch-and-report exit below.
Do not demand an arbitrary extra headroom margin; the recorded ~8 ms tradeoff
was accepted. General full-grid throughput may still exceed 8.33 ms; report it
against the existing workload baseline, never mislabel it a 120 Hz pass.

**P3 — native/delivery.** Exact candidate artifact and parent at fixed scenes:
strict terminal pixels and contour coverage; chrome shape/bounds/fitting and
reviewed shaper differences; scale 1/1.25/1.5/2, tiny/narrow/overflow windows,
background/opacity/blur, empty/popup-only/multi-session states. Real Linux input
through an isolated seat, IME/dead-key+Space, regular+primary clipboard and
frozen Orbit selection, attention focus reports, detach/reload/crash/reconnect,
image clips/budget/refusal resync and **terminal** GPU device-loss handling.
Rune DeviceKey, format, blend mode and actual applied size must reject stale
resources and invalidate presentation/input at the existing boundary. No
continued rendering after device loss or new image-resync recovery is accepted. A displayed old scene never admits
stale input. One native AccessKit tree exposes required chrome roles/actions.

`eon-qdcgw.1` builds static offscreen PNG proof on 1cyzr's hosted constructor;
add its dependency on eon-1cyzr in the overseer's authorized reconciliation.
`eon-qdcgw.2` retains its dependency on .1 and additionally waits for eon-yp6vg.20: its
scripted input and JSON dump use the production Rune AccessKit tree, never the
removed Venus AX tree. These are the existing implementation owners, not new
migration tasks; eon-yp6vg.20 does not wait for qdcgw.2, avoiding a cycle. Before eon-yp6vg.20,
use native/candidate tests of the same view; do not implement a second PNG/tree
harness. Headless proof cannot establish desktop/IME/physical input, scanout
or terminal reader support.

eon-yp6vg.17 uses a real isolated COSMIC session, plus Sway reference. eon-yp6vg.18 exercises
NVIDIA Vulkan, covered/unfocused/hidden/focused-field idle and resumed output;
no new GNOME/KDE proof campaign (eon-igae.8's approved scope). Any real failure
reported on GNOME/KDE still triggers the stop condition. eon-yp6vg.19 proves the shared
candidate on a physical/approved native Apple Silicon environment, including
Retina, Kotoeri and lifecycle. Missing hardware is a named block, never a pass.

Build only for required candidate observations/packaging, using out-links and
the same graph. No agent package build merely as a check: the overseer owns
the landing build. Packaging changes in eon-yp6vg.7 require their affected Nix route,
locked dependency hash and notice/source/archive coverage, not a second build
matrix. eon-yp6vg.20's final product observation covers full Eon and eonbase, same-build
reload, delivery identity and an explicit Humans and Agents CLI-parity check: all
existing window actions keep their explicit-ID CLI path and data projection;
view-state exceptions remain the documented exceptions. eon-yp6vg.21 does not add
behavior and reuses eon-yp6vg.20 timing only for demonstrably unchanged reached paths. The overseer owns accepted profile refresh;
never restart existing supervisors. Each proof receipt records exact staged
tree, Eon/fork/Orbit/tool identities, artifact, command, environment, result,
every failed attempt and owned cleanup.

All heavy/timed work follows heavy.sh, booked daily quiet slots (03:00Z/15:00Z,
90 minutes; request a measured estimate, <=90 per booking), build/script ready
before grant, explicit exemption only after grant, and `QUIET DONE` afterwards.
Private display/runtime/home/D-Bus roots, non-activating surfaces and exact-PID
cleanup preserve the user's windows and focus. No runs are requested now.

## Stop/exit checks and risks

| --- | --- |
| Gate failure | Every P2/eon-yp6vg.2–eon-yp6vg.4/eon-yp6vg.7/eon-yp6vg.9/eon-yp6vg.12/eon-yp6vg.20 check. Profile with rune/frame-profile + perf and patch Rune/view at its owner. A rewrite of a Rune subsystem, or 3 hours / 3 failed approaches without a lead, stops for Lucca with trace and estimate. Never drop Rune autonomously. Original fade hitch alone is not this gate. |

The original memo says back out/resume uczzf for conditions 2–5; the later

**Overseer action:** retain a dated six-week patch-stack checkpoint for
**2026-12-23**, even if chrome ports are still in progress. At that date inspect

record the receipt on the fork/migration epics and apply the memo exits. Do not
defer this check until eon-yp6vg.20 or create an automatic scheduler in this plan.

Main risks: input API loss/rebase churn; accepted near-budget restore/zoom cost
combined with live Venus prepare; Rune automatic recovery bypassing the
required terminal device-loss outcome; accidental
Orbit authority leakage from copied spike code; differing chrome text metrics;
transparent clip/painter-order errors; lost accessibility beyond the authorized
terminal gap; Apple preview regression; dependency/closure and archive-notice
growth; duplicating qdcgw/uczzf or erasing newer Venus features. Spike first,
matched proof, preserved canonical tests and a prepared deletion inventory

## Adopted memo and dated supersessions

Earlier clauses below are historical where later dated decisions supersede them; the approved plan above states current migration scope.

# Rune for Venus: adoption plan

For Lucca, 2026-11-11. Decided: Eon invests in Rune through a Yazelix fork that tracks upstream. This page gives the terms, the exits and the first three beads.

**What the spikes proved.** Venus's grid runs inside Rune's render hook on Linux with 0 idle frames, and the hook adds 0.02 ms. Input, IME, the regular clipboard, fractional scale and two live panes work. The notch look ports at pixel parity with no Rune change. Two chrome surfaces took 924 lines in Rune, against 2,392 replaceable Venus lines.
**Not proved:** 120 Hz on pane changes (track E), real desktops beyond headless sway, a terminal that screen readers can read. Venus's own one-cell rebuild takes 15 ms whichever toolkit hosts it; the row cache (gxb4) and blink fix (h222) own that cost.

## 1. Fork terms

**Day-one patch stack** (about 300 lines, one commit per patch, each naming its upstream issue):
- #372 self-resize fix: the 20-line candidate from stage B. It still hangs in 1 of 4 runs, so finish it first.
- Primary selection (#541), from track I: i-00 extraction +47/−26, then i-01 feature +196/−7.
- Dead-key + Space fix from track F, +5/−4.
- A Wayland `app_id`.
- E's fix, if the fix lands in Rune.

**Not in the fork:**
- The look. Track I's 566/168-line geometry bridge stays in Venus.
- Eon's winit fork. Eon's root `[patch.crates-io]` (Yazelix/winit-0.30 `7c209ec5`) already places it under Rune; tracks C–I proved this.
- Terminal accessibility. Anomaly builds it (#542), as you decided. At switch-over, Venus's terminal-accessibility contract (VEN-C6) still needs a wording change that you approve.

**How Eon pins it.**
- Cargo: `rune = { git = "https://github.com/Yazelix/eon-rune.git", rev = "<sha>", default-features = false, features = [...] }`. Drop `metal-backend` and `ogg-audio`. Never track a branch.
- Nix: add `outputHashes."rune-0.0.1"` beside `dpi` and `libghostty-vt` in `flake.nix` `workspaceCargoLock`. Each rev bump changes that hash.
- Toolchain: Eon pins rustc 1.96.1, but the spikes built Rune on 1.99.1. Check this on day one.

**Upstream first.** Rune takes issues, not pull requests (its README: "We don't take pull requests"). So "upstream" means an issue that links our patch as a reference. Order:
1. E's trace, if the cost is Rune's.
2. #372, where we already commented.
3. #541 primary selection.
4. Dead-key + Space.
5. `app_id`.

Drop each fork patch when upstream ships its own fix.

**Who owns rebases.** Lucca owns the fork and approves every rev bump. Once a week, eon-overseer files a sync bead for one agent session. That session does five things:
- rebases `eon` onto upstream `dev`;
- runs the focused tests (8 primary-selection, 30 clipboard);
- runs track I's real primary round trip;
- runs the idle check and E's motion gate;
- proposes the new rev.

A failed sync never blocks Eon: Eon stays on the last good rev.

**Rebase risk: medium to high, almost all of it in input.** Last week's commit counts:
- `runtime/frame.rs`: 24
- `runtime/input/pointer.rs`: 15
- `el/tx.rs`: 13
- `runtime/input/action.rs`: 13
- the clipboard backend: 0

Upstream made 100 commits touching 300+ files in the 24 hours after our pin (3686e94 to 16697fee). All five of our tracked issues are still open; 303 are open in total, 14 closed.

## 2. Stop conditions

Back out, and resume eon-uczzf's Venus-owned control layer, if any of these happens:
1. **E's stutter has no fix.** Bead 1's time box ends without a fix, in the fork or in our view code, that passes E's unchanged 120 Hz gate. Then nothing lands in Eon. Bead 3 still stands alone.
2. **The patch stack never shrinks.** After six weeks, no issue of ours is fixed upstream, or the stack passes 1,000 lines.
3. **Syncs get too expensive.** Two weekly syncs in a row each need more than one agent session. Or upstream removes or breaks the render hook (`Compositor` / `El::effect`) that hosts the grid.
4. **Real desktops fail where headless sway passed.** For example: the covered-window core spin (#139), the redraw every frame while a field has focus (#225), or broken NVIDIA presentation on GNOME, KDE or COSMIC.
5. **Rune leaves the MIT licence or drops Linux/Vulkan.**

## 3. First three beads

**Bead 1. Rune: find and fix the 11–18 ms frame when a pane remounts into a fade**

Track E (`rune-spike-a-work/REPORT-E.md`) found two frames over budget:
- frame 120: F6 switches Solo(0) to Solo(1);
- frame 202: a split restores.

Each costs 10.9–17.8 ms of thread CPU, almost all in Rune's encode/submit. No Venus work runs, and layout takes under 0.09 ms. The budget is 8.33 ms, the 120 Hz gate.

Steps:
1. Re-run E's unchanged audit on upstream `dev` head. If it passes there, record that and close.
2. If it fails, use `rune/frame-profile` plus `perf` to split the cost. The candidates are allocating opacity-layer textures (Rgba16Float at scale 2; `render/upload.rs:187`, `render/layers.rs:444`), creating pipelines, and submitting.
3. Fix it in the smallest place. In Rune, that means reusing layer textures or pre-creating pipelines: a fork commit plus an upstream issue with the trace. In our view code, that means keeping the terminal element's identity across F6 and the split restore, as track G did.

Done when: E's scenario passes unchanged in two quiet-slot runs, with no allowlist. Time box: 3 hours or three failed approaches. Nothing lands in Eon.

**Bead 2. Create the Yazelix/eon-rune fork with its day-one patch stack and a weekly sync check**

Fork anomalyco/rune into Yazelix/eon-rune. Create branch `eon` from a recorded `dev` rev, with one commit per patch listed in section 1, each naming its upstream issue. The #372 patch must pass 10 of 10 resize runs. Patch sources:
- the stage B resize candidate;
- track I's `i/patches` (i-00, i-01);
- track F's `patches/dead-key-space.patch`.

Then:
- File or refresh the matching upstream issues.
- Write `sync.sh`: rebase, the focused tests, the real primary round trip, the idle check and E's gate.
- Check that the fork builds with rustc 1.96.1.

Ask Lucca before creating the GitHub fork or posting anything upstream. No Eon change.

**Bead 3. Venus: hosted-renderer entry and dependency alignment, no visible change**

Port stage B's one-file refactor into Venus (`render.rs` +242/−84):
- an optional window and surface;
- a hosted constructor that takes a device, queue and format;
- a prepare/draw split;
- the pass viewport as a sub-rectangle.

Also move wgpu `=30.0.0` to 30.0.1, and relax the exact pins that collide with Rune (`objc2` 0.6.4 vs 0.6.5). Add no Rune dependency yet.

Done when: standalone Venus captures are pixel-identical before and after at fixed scenes, and Venus's tests pass. Contract: none. This refactor touches `render.rs`, which gxb4 and h222 also change: whichever lands second rebases.

## Gate re-scoped (Lucca, 2026-11-12 ~05:00Z)

Lucca, typed in eon-desk and relayed to eon-overseer: "yeah, we have to facilitate rune". This replaces stop condition 1's "E's unchanged 120 Hz gate" and bead 1's acceptance:

- Eon on Rune does not fade panes in; Venus has no pane fades today (none in VEN contracts or PRESENTATION.md). F6 was a spike test key.
- The gate is the transitions Eon actually has, with no fade: popup show and hide, split and split restore, solo/zoom switch, and tab switch, each within the 8.33 ms budget at 120 Hz, in two quiet-slot runs. Each measured transition must be shown to actually run (Codex's check); a pass that hides a transition Eon uses does not count.
- The fade-on-mount hitch (frames 120 and 202) becomes a Rune upstream issue: its body with the trace is written to a file for Lucca; nothing is posted. It no longer decides adoption, and exit rule 1 does not fire on it.
- This does not authorize migration. Past azfsx, t1rtk and 1cyzr, Rune migration still needs Lucca's explicit go; t1rtk local prep follows a pass of this gate.

## Exit rule 1 changed (Lucca, 2026-11-12 ~05:05Z)

Lucca, typed in eon-desk and relayed to eon-overseer: "if rune fails, is not to drop it, but to patch it to our needs / unless it's too hard". This replaces stop condition 1. The re-scoped gate above stays.

- A failing gate run no longer stops Rune. Find the cause with rune/frame-profile and perf and patch Rune itself; the patch goes on the Yazelix fork's day-one patch stack (eon-t1rtk), with an upstream issue body written to a file for Lucca. Nothing is posted.
- "Too hard" means the fix needs a rewrite of a Rune subsystem, or the bead's time box (3 hours or three failed approaches) runs out without a lead. Then stop and report to Lucca with the trace and an estimate. No agent drops Rune on its own.
- Patching Rune inside the fork and the spike trees is adoption work, not migration. Migrating Venus past azfsx, t1rtk and 1cyzr still needs Lucca's explicit go.

## Decisions 2026-11-12 (Lucca via eon-desk, ~14:30Z)

- Fork name: Yazelix/eon-rune (matches nova-helix; distinct from upstream anomalyco/rune and the Rune scripting language). Crate names unchanged.
- Decision 41: the self-resize patch cost shift is accepted (about 8 ms of 8.33 on zoom-end/restore). Re-measure restore and selection-ends-zoom frames once Venus runs hosted in Rune; report any frame over 8.33 ms.
- Migration: conditional go (Lucca delegated; eon-desk decided). Plan and file the migration beads now. Implementation starts with no further ask once (a) eon-1cyzr has landed and passed its timing window, (b) eon-t1rtk.1-.3 are done, (c) v0.2.0 is cut. Publishing the fork still needs Lucca typed words (eon-t1rtk.4). Until then nothing of the migration lands in Eon: a renderer swap during the release gate would invalidate the beta Venus proofs and collide with Venus work in flight.

## Durable governing record

The approved migration plan, exact proposed contract clauses, proof-route definitions and adopted memo are preserved in `eon-yp6vg`. References to the numbered Markdown drafts denote that embedded plan; they do not require a disposable local path.

Plan key: eon-yp6vg.1. Approved migration planning batch: overseer INBOX 2026-11-12T15:10:35Z. Implementation stays blocked by the adoption receipts and approved contract boundary.

### Why

uczzf and qdcgw tasks could otherwise build parallel replacements.

In: exact contract proposal/approval record and collision/ownership disposition.
Out: implementation, changes to retired IDs, product support or release scope.

title: Compress cold terminal history with libghostty's existing lossless compression
description:
## Why

From eon-ypy0a's investigation (2026-11-08, findings: ~/.cache/eon-agents/eon-memory-reduce-work/bead/00-findings.md, section 2 and proposal 1). Lucca, 2026-11-08: "agree" to filing and starting this. A terminal holding 10,000 72-column lines costs Eon about 6.2 MiB of history against tmux's 4.4 MiB: Ghostty's page layout stores each 80-column row at 80x8 + 8 = 648 bytes, and the growth sits in libghostty's anonymous page mappings. The pinned libghostty-rs (9b598d65) already exports `Terminal::compress`, `compression_activity` and `memory_usage`; Orbit never calls them. A disposable probe on the pinned library (Debug build) compressed 17 of 18 pages, dropped 6.3 MiB anonymous PSS, kept all 9,976 retained rows exact, took about 22 ms over 20 incremental calls, and a full history read restored the pages (recompression returned them to 0.517 MiB).

## Goal

Orbit schedules libghostty's existing lossless history compression: cold retained pages compress after terminal activity settles, and again after full history reads or scrolling. libghostty stays the only owner of terminal state and history; the 16 MiB history byte budget stays. Use the library's incremental API and activity token, as bounded steps in the existing host loop, with input and output always ahead of compression work. No new codec, second history copy, thread, dependency or product setting; the internal idle budget is fixed and its reason recorded here (performance/support, per Configurability).

## Expected saving

5-6 MiB per 10,000-line terminal in a release build (about 250-300 MiB at 50 filled terminals). Estimate until the integrated release measurement; less for incompressible or continuously hot history.

## Contract and wire

No intended contract text change; ORBS/ORBF/EONW unchanged. Stop and ask if integration needs a host-worker schema, Bend law or policy ownership change. Honor the library's unsupported result; Darwin benefit needs its own proof.

## Acceptance

- Release `eon-bench memory` before/after on the same corpus with equal retained history, recorded beside the published rows.
- Rich content unchanged: Unicode, styles, graphemes, selection, history reads, resize and reflow, Kitty images.
- Proof that pages recompress after a history read and after output goes idle.
- Orbit's checks (`nix develop -c eon-test -p yazelix-orbit`, the orbit-* Nix checks including real-PTY), whole-workspace eon-test, package build, and isolated interaction and throughput evidence (eon-bench orbit) showing no latency or data-retention regression.
close_reason: Landed: Orbit compresses cold history with libghostty's lossless compression, 7.23 -> 1.18 MiB PSS per filled terminal; proof and review ledger in comments

comments.text:
Landed (eon-overseer, 2026-11-09). By the eon-history-compress pane agent (Codex); reviewed tree 437349fc on 4c01816, applied to edge with land-apply.sh. Records: ~/.cache/eon-agents/eon-history-compress-work/bead/ (00-plan through 06-results; 05-review is the ledger).

What: Orbit's host loop schedules libghostty's existing lossless incremental page compression for cold history. libghostty stays the only history owner; no new codec, copy, thread, dependency, setting or wire change. Ready I/O and timers always win; each step tries at most one page; input and history reads restart a 250 ms delay; output and ordinary frames no longer postpone a scheduled pass, so busy terminals (spinners, TUIs over history, tail -f) still compress. Unsupported or an API error disarms compression for that terminal only.

Result (release eon-bench memory, same corpus, equal retained history: all 200 hosts per artifact keep 9976 history + 24 live rows): filled marginal PSS 7.23 -> 1.18 MiB per terminal (-6.04 MiB, 83.6%). Attached throughput medians on the final tree, pinned ABBA: ASCII -0.29%, styled +1.36%, Unicode +2.97%; matched PTY input and read latency unchanged; longest single compression step 125 us (release unit). An earlier tree's -2.54% ASCII median, inside overlapping ranges, was accepted by the overseer as no material regression and is superseded by these numbers. Distributions in bead/06-results.md.

title: Try wgpu's MemoryUsage allocation hint in Venus and keep it only if GPU memory falls
description:
## Why

From eon-ypy0a's investigation (2026-11-08, findings: ~/.cache/eon-agents/eon-memory-reduce-work/bead/00-findings.md, section 4 and proposal 2). Lucca, 2026-11-08: "agree" to filing and starting this. On Intel, one Venus window's DRM fdinfo reports 230.5 MiB allocated and 228.5 MiB resident on the GPU (outside the 66 MiB process PSS row). `Renderer::new` requests `DeviceDescriptor::default()`, so wgpu 30 uses `MemoryHints::Performance`, whose Vulkan allocator starts device and host blocks at 128 and 64 MiB; `MemoryHints::MemoryUsage` starts them at 8 and 4 MiB.

## Goal

An accept-or-revert experiment on one existing field: request `MemoryHints::MemoryUsage` in Venus's device descriptor, using wgpu's own allocator policy. No custom allocator knobs, no renderer or surface path change. If accepted, the hint is fixed policy and this bead records why (performance budget, per Configurability).

## Expected saving

Up to about 180 MiB less GPU allocation per window if one block of each kind suffices. CPU PSS saving unproven: budget 0 MiB until measured. In software rendering the 64 MiB allocator mapping is only 1.7 MiB resident, so its shrink is not a PSS win there.

## Contract and wire

None intended; no EONW/ORBS/ORBF change. The API is portable; the Linux Vulkan effect is measured first, Metal is unproved.

## Acceptance

- Intel and lavapipe: smaps rollups and deduplicated DRM fdinfo before and after, same corpus and viewport, through the isolated `eon-bench headless` launcher and the memory suite's Venus row.
- Exercise resize, rich text and Kitty images (allocation churn), and check frame time and input latency show no meaningful regression.
- Accept only with a real reduction; otherwise revert and record the numbers here.
- Venus suite, whole-workspace eon-test, package build.
close_reason: Landed: MemoryHints::MemoryUsage on hardware adapters (-180 MiB GPU per window on Intel); CPU adapters keep Performance; proof and review ledger in comments

title: Propose a safe way to stop loading unused Vulkan drivers in Venus
description:
## Why

From eon-ypy0a's investigation (2026-11-08, findings: ~/.cache/eon-agents/eon-memory-reduce-work/bead/00-findings.md, section 4 'Hardware loads unused driver stacks' and proposal 3). Lucca, 2026-11-08: "agree". Eon points the Vulkan loader at the pinned Mesa ICD directory, which holds Intel, lavapipe and Dozen; choosing the Intel adapter does not stop the loader mapping the others, LLVM included. One A/B run on Lucca's Intel machine, changing only the ICD set to the Intel JSON files, cut Venus's client delta from 65.6 to 46.4 MiB PSS (19.2 MiB) and 85.1 to 52.4 MiB RSS; LLVM, lavapipe and Dozen mappings alone were about 17.8 MiB PSS. Software rendering already loads only lavapipe, so this does not help there.

## Goal

Investigation and proposal only, one session: turn the private ICD experiment into the smallest safe product proposal. Read how the official Vulkan loader discovers and filters drivers, how Eon's Nix composition sets VK_DRIVER_FILES or equivalents today, and how Venus picks an adapter. Resolve: automatic choice across several GPUs and drivers, systems without a hardware driver, and the software fallback. Driver choice stays with the composition and native graphics owners. No static Intel filter, no new GPU configuration framework, no fallback shim.

## Deliverable

bead/00-proposal.md: the mechanism, what it changes per platform and GPU vendor, failure and fallback behavior, the expected saving with evidence, and any contract text it needs (a narrowed driver or platform promise needs Lucca's approval of the owning contract before code). Then stop for Lucca. Implementation is a separate bead filed only after he picks.

## Expected saving

About 18-19 MiB PSS and 33 MiB RSS per Intel window on this host; 0 MiB promised on other hardware or in software rendering until qualified.

## Planning reconciliation (2026-11-12, dcaef1c)

Current composition supplies Vulkan loader libraries and Mesa share discovery
via flake.nix:561/:608 (XDG_DATA_DIRS), not a demonstrated VK_DRIVER_FILES
override. render.rs:1227 uses wgpu's compatible-surface adapter request defaults.
Private Intel savings remain one-host evidence, no cross-GPU promise.
Keep the proposal/decisions in this bead durably; a scratch proposal may support
it but is not the sole owner. Acceptance names multi-GPU, hardware-absent/software
fallback and Nix versus signed Nix-free Linux effects, with Darwin Metal outside
the filter. Name the eventual same-workload A/B and lost-adapter falsifier before
composition changes. Portability: isolated Linux Vulkan proposal. Preserve the
investigation-only scope, approval and separately selected implementation; no
code/build/test or profile refresh here.

title: Draw programming ligatures in terminal text (on by default, split under the cursor)
description:
## Why

Lucca, 2026-11-12 (eon-desk): "does eon support those fancy icons that appear when you join two
symbols, like :>, or smt like that? ligaments?", then "yeah" to filing it as P2, on by default, and
broken apart under the cursor. Venus draws no programming ligatures (`->`, `=>`, `!=`, `>=`, `::`,
`</`), although his font, Iosevka, has them. Ghostty, WezTerm and kitty support them by default;
Alacritty doesn't.

## Current behaviour (verify at edge)

- Terminal text is shaped one cell at a time: `shape_cell_layers` (venus/src/render.rs ~:3287)
  builds a buffer per cell's text, so no shaping run ever spans two cells.
- `shaping()` (venus/src/render.rs ~:3348) uses `Shaping::Basic` for ASCII, which applies no
  OpenType features; `liga` and `calt` never run.
- Text goes through glyphon =0.12.0 / cosmic-text, with swash rasterisation.
- The per-row shaped-text cache landed in eon-venus-row-text-cache-gxb4 slice 1 (e5e9710); reuse
  its row ownership, not a parallel cache.

## Design

- Within a row, shape maximal runs of adjacent cells that share font, style and colour as one
  `Shaping::Advanced` run, with the font's `liga` and `calt` features. Each resulting glyph
  cluster is placed on the cell grid, so a ligature covers exactly the cells it replaces and
  monospace alignment never drifts.
- Break a run (so no ligature forms across the boundary) at:
  - the cursor cell: kitty's "cursor" behaviour, so the character under the cursor is always visible;
  - selection edges, foreground/background or attribute changes, wide characters, box-drawing,
    braille and symbol-font fallback cells.
- Configuration (rule 6): one key in `[terminal]` or wherever font keys live, e.g.
  `ligatures = true | false`, default true. Name and placement follow docs/CONFIGURATION.md
  conventions. No per-feature lists unless the plan finds a strong reason.
- Chrome text (bar, sidebar, headers) is out of scope; terminal cells only.

## Contract

Check VEN contracts on cell rendering and text shaping (venus/docs/CONTRACTS.md). If one promises
per-cell drawing, its wording changes and needs Lucca's approval before code.

## Performance (AP-PERF-001)

Measure before and after with the existing frame-timing log (xl2bp.9, EON_VENUS_FRAME_TIMINGS) and
the gxb4 benchmark (one-cell change, four columns, full-change control) at 200x60. A typing or
scrolling regression beyond the gate's stop bound (~5%) stops the work for a trade-off note.

## Acceptance

- With Iosevka (and one other ligature font, e.g. JetBrains Mono or Fira Code), `->`, `=>`, `!=`
  and `>=` render as ligatures in an Eon pane, aligned to the grid.
- With the cursor on any cell of a ligature, that sequence draws as separate characters.
- Selecting half of a ligature shows the selection on the correct cells and copies the correct text.
- Colour changes inside a sequence (syntax highlighting) break the ligature cleanly.
- `ligatures = false` restores today's rendering exactly.
- Timing within bounds.

## Verification

Scene/render tests for run splitting (cursor, selection, style changes) and grid placement;
`nix develop -c eon-test` (not inside a live Eon session); fmt and clippy; installed captures in
Helix and a shell; frame-timing comparison.

title: Fit the hints bar on a 13-inch screen
description:
## Why

Lucca, 2026-11-06: "we need to make the hints bar text fit in a 13-incher". On a 13-inch laptop the bottom hints bar drops hints. The full-width text today (derived from venus/src/application/shortcuts.rs and venus/src/scene.rs; no test holds it) is about 209 characters across four modifier groups:

`[A] H/L · K/J · 1..9 focus  Q inbox  M +pane  W close pane  / keys` · `[C-A] M +col  H/L · K/J mv pane` · `[A-S] T +tab  W close tab  Z zoom  N +window  D detach  Q quit  B hints  H sidebar  L Agent  A Anima  M Commands  Y Files  J Git  E Scrollback  S Workspaces` · `[C-A-S] H/L mv tab`

## Decisions (Lucca agreed 2026-11-06 to the overseer's proposal, items 1-8)

1. Directional pairs show as `HJKL` instead of `H/L · K/J` (focus and mv pane).
2. Creating hints drop the `+`: `M pane`, `M col`, `T tab`, `N window`.
3. Drop the `Q inbox` hint (Alt+Q still works and stays in full help); VEN-C32's sentence that the footer shows `Q inbox` changes.
4. Drop the `/ keys` hint, together with showing the header `?` Shortcuts button always (today it shows only when hints are hidden or dropped), so full help stays discoverable.
5. Drop the `Q quit` hint (closing the window quits; Alt+Shift+Q stays in full help).
6. Drop the Ctrl+Alt+Shift group: its only hint, `H/L mv tab`, stays in full help.
7. Keep the space between key and description; tighten the gap between groups if that is still needed.
8. Only if the text cuts are not enough at the target width: a configurable hints font size (default about 90% of the terminal font size, documented in docs/CONFIGURATION.md).

Target: every remaining hint fits at 1280 logical pixels wide (a 13-inch 2560x1600 panel at scale 2) with the default font size. If it still does not fit, report before going further (next step would be shorter popup labels, which needs Lucca).

## Acceptance

- At 1280 logical px with default config, the bar shows every remaining hint and the `?` button; narrower windows still drop whole hints by priority.
- The Alt+Q inbox, Alt+/ viewer, Alt+Shift+Q quit and Ctrl+Alt+Shift tab moves keep working and stay listed in full help.
- docs/USAGE.md, venus/docs/INTERACTION.md and the affected contract text (VEN-C32, and wherever the `?` button's visibility is fixed) match the new behaviour; CHANGELOG.md entry.
- Tests assert the new hint strings and the always-visible `?`; an isolated installed screenshot at 1280 px shows the bar.

# eon-yvhke 02 — Width measurement

## Method

A scratch test (not for commit) in `venus/src/application/shortcuts.rs` builds
the hints with `shortcut_hints_for(Linux, Terminal, default popups, Sidebar::Open,
running)`, the default popups copied from `eon/crates/eon/src/product.rs`
(Quick search, Git, Agent, Files, Anima, Commands, Workspaces, Scrollback),
and lays them out with the real `ShortcutHintsScene::new`, measuring each text
with the renderer's own header shaping (`fit_header_text`, sans-serif,
`FontSettings::default()`, size 16 at scale 1). Fonts: the packaged set from
the test sandbox's `FONTCONFIG_FILE` (DejaVu, Nerd symbols, Accelerando).
It binary-searches the narrowest window (logical px) where the bar is
complete, at scales 1, 1.5 and 2.

Run: `nix develop -c eon-test -p yazelix-venus --bin yazelix-venus zz_measure -- --nocapture`,
CARGO_TARGET_DIR `~/.cache/eon-agents/eon-yvhke-target`, x86_64 Linux,
2026-11-06. Logs: `../measure1.log` (before), `../measure2.log`,
`../measure3.log` (after). The second run started at load 12.7 (above the
agreed 8; it was an incremental one-test build); the third waited for load < 8.

## Results

| Bar | Minimum width (logical px, scales 1/1.5/2) |
| --- | ---: |
| Today (edge 605cca5), 23 hints in 4 groups | 2180 |
| After decisions 1-7 (cuts done), 19 hints in 3 groups | 1743 |
| Target | 1280 |

The cuts save 437 px; the bar is still 463 px over.

## Breakdown after the cuts (scale 1)

Groups as drawn: A (focus, pane, close pane), C-A (col, mv pane),
A-S (tab, close tab, zoom, window, detach, hints, sidebar, then the popups).

- Hint text and modifier badges: 1478 px.
- Gaps: 16 in-group gaps × 12 = 192; 2 group gaps × 24 = 48; 2 edge paddings × 12 = 24.
- Configured popup hints alone: Git 30, Agent 56, Files 46, Anima 62,
  Commands 104, Workspaces 103, Scrollback 89 = 490 px, plus 84 px of gaps.

At 1280 the bar drops exactly the five priority-4 popup hints (Files, Anima,
Commands, Workspaces, Scrollback) and shows everything else. At 1440 it drops
Commands, Workspaces and Scrollback.

## What would close the 463 px

- Decision 7 (group gaps 24 → 12): −24 → 1719. Not enough.
- Decision 8 (hints font 90%): text −148 → about 1595. Not enough; it would
  take about 70% (unreadable) to fit by font alone.
- Shorter popup labels (e.g. Commands → Cmds, Workspaces → Spaces,
  Scrollback → Scroll): about −110. Not enough alone.
- Leaving the five priority-4 popup hints (Files, Anima, Commands, Workspaces,
  Scrollback) out of the bar: −464 → 1279, with decision 7 → 1255. Fits, with
  Git and Agent still shown and the always-visible `?` / Alt+/ listing all.

## After Lucca's three cuts (INBOX ~04:30Z: `side`, `Scroll`, dashless `CA`/`AS`)

`../measure4.log`, load 7.5: complete bar 1672 px (text and badges 1408).
Badges: `A` 34.1, `CA` 44.2, `AS` 42.9; `side` 46.4 (was `sidebar` 71.7),
`Scroll` 53.7 (was `Scrollback` 88.5).

## Final: Lucca's width decision (INBOX ~04:55Z) plus decision 7

Lucca: "1 agreed, but make it dynamic. not need to drop if they fit". The five
priority-4 popup hints stay in the list and drop only when they do not fit
(the existing whole-hint dropping; no new mechanism). Decision 7: the gap
between groups tightens from 2 × padding (24 px) to the in-group gap
(12 px); spare width still spreads the groups.

`../measure5.log`, load 5.3, scales 1/1.5/2 identical. Complete bar: 1648 px.
Narrowest logical width at which each hint set shows (scan 900-1800 px, the
scene's own drop rule):

| From width | Hints shown |
| ---: | --- |
| 1219 | every fixed hint, Git, Agent (14) |
| 1278 | + Files |
| 1352 | + Anima |
| 1468 | + Commands |
| 1583 | + Workspaces |
| 1648 | + Scroll (all 19) |

At 1280: the 14 required hints (every fixed hint, Git, Agent) plus Files; Anima, Commands,
Workspaces and Scroll drop. Margin for the 14 required hints at 1280: 61 px.

Drop order among the five: the existing rule drops the highest
(priority, group, position) first, so equal-priority popups drop from the end
of the catalog: Scroll, Workspaces, Commands, Anima, Files. That follows the
configured catalog order, which a person controls; kept as is.

## Correction: packaged fonts measure wider (2026-11-06 ~05:30Z)

The figures above came from `eon-test`, whose bwrap sandbox also sees the
host's fonts. The Nix package build (`nix build .#default`, Venus checkPhase,
fonts only from Eon's packaged `fonts.conf`: DejaVu, Nerd symbols,
Accelerando, Noto Color Emoji), which matches what the installed app loads,
failed the new fit test. Venus-only debug builds of the same tree (with Eon's
default `font_fallbacks`) measured, at scale 1
(`../fonts-nix.log`, `../fonts-nix-2.zz`):

| Hint | badge text | key | space | label | hint width |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| [A] HJKL · 1..9 focus | 10.9 | 81.9 | 5.1 | 42.7 | 129.7 |

| [AS] T tab | 21.1 | 9.8 | 5.1 | 26.2 | 41.1 |
| [AS] W close tab | | 15.8 | 5.1 | 72.5 | 93.4 |
| [AS] Z zoom | | 11.0 | 5.1 | 43.6 | 59.7 |
| [AS] N window | | 12.0 | 5.1 | 60.7 | 77.8 |
| [AS] D detach | | 12.3 | 5.1 | 55.0 | 72.4 |
| [AS] B hints | | 11.0 | 5.1 | 39.3 | 55.4 |
| [AS] H side | | 12.0 | 5.1 | 32.8 | 49.9 |
| [AS] J Git | | 4.7 | 5.1 | 23.1 | 32.9 |
| [AS] L Agent | | 8.9 | 5.1 | 47.4 | 61.4 |
| [AS] Y Files (p4) | | 9.8 | 5.1 | 36.3 | 51.2 |
| [AS] A Anima (p4) | | 10.9 | 5.1 | 50.9 | 66.9 |
| [AS] M Commands (p4) | | 13.8 | 5.1 | 90.6 | 109.5 |
| [AS] S Workspaces (p4) | | 10.2 | 5.1 | 96.7 | 112.0 |
| [AS] E Scroll (p4) | | 10.1 | 5.1 | 44.2 | 59.4 |

Each badge adds 2 × padding (24 px) to its text. Hint width excludes the badge.

Required groups (everything but the five p4 popups), with badges and in-group gaps:

- A: 34.9 badge + 295.6 hints + 2 × 12 gaps = 354.5
- CA: 46.1 + 153.3 + 1 × 12 = 211.4
- AS: 45.1 + 543.9 + 8 × 12 = 685.0
- Between groups 2 × 12, window edges 2 × 12: 48
- Total: 1299 (search: 1300).

Narrowest window showing each set (packaged fonts): required 1300; + Files
1363; + Anima 1442; + Commands 1563; + Workspaces 1687; all 1758.
At 1280 the drop rule removes the last priority-3 hint of the AS group,
`N window`, and keeps the other 13 required hints.

### Why the environments differ (probe, `../probe-2.log`)

Venus's fontdb takes the sans-serif face from fontconfig aliases. The
`fonts.conf` that both the devshell and the packaged Venus wrapper export
(`/nix/store/ga3wzlhvb6zlpvay50c013jdnfkhfcks-fonts.conf`) includes the host's
`/etc/fonts/conf.d`. Under `eon-test` on this host fontdb loaded 659 faces and
resolved sans-serif to Open Sans (a host font); the Nix build sandbox has no
`/etc/fonts`, so it uses the packaged DejaVu Sans, which is wider. An installed
Eon on this host therefore draws hints in Open Sans; on a host without its own
fontconfig (and in the Nix build) it uses DejaVu Sans.

### Deterministic fit test

`default_hints_fit_a_1280_pixel_window` calls
`FontSetup::set_header_family("DejaVu Sans")` (new; fails if the family is
missing) before measuring, so `eon-test` and the Nix build measure the same,
packaged face, the wider case.

## Final: overseer option 1 (INBOX ~06:00Z): hint gap 12 → 9 px

One gap of 0.75 × padding (9 px at scale 1) separates every hint; window-edge
padding stays 12 px. `../measure6.log` (pinned DejaVu Sans, eon-test, load
< 8), scales 1 and 2 identical:

| 1321 | + Files |
| 1397 | + Anima |
| 1515 | + Commands |

| 1704 | + Scroll (all 19) |

catalog entry first. Below 1261 the drop rule removes `N window` first, then
`Z zoom` (1174), `W close tab` (1105), `HJKL mv pane` (1003).

    unchanged; the legend function is shared but its compact branch is used
    only by the footer.
- `venus/src/scene.rs`:
  - `ShortcutHintsScene` loses `keep_shortcuts` and `new` loses its `focus`
    parameter (it only fed `keep_shortcuts`); every call site updated.
  - `workspace_header_geometry` and `WorkspaceScene::layout` lose
    `show_shortcuts`: the Shortcuts control always takes its slot (decision 4).
    `has_control(Shortcuts)` callers stay: they also cover windows too narrow
    for any control width.
  - Decision 7 plus overseer option 1 (INBOX ~06:00Z): one gap of
    0.75 x padding (9 px at scale 1) separates every hint; before, hints in a
    group were 12 px apart and groups at least 24 px. Window-edge padding
    stays 12 px. Spare width still spreads the groups, so group gaps stay at
    least as wide as hint gaps.
- `venus/src/render/fonts.rs`: `FontSetup::measure_header_text`, the
  renderer's own header shaping (`fit_header_text`) for code holding a
  `FontSetup` without a GPU renderer, and `FontSetup::set_header_font_file`
  (round 2; replaced round 1's `set_header_face` and the first
  `set_header_family`), which loads exactly one font file, removes every
  other face of that file's family, makes the family the sans-serif face, and
  errors unless the sans-serif query then resolves to a face from that file.
  Both serve the new fit test; the product does not call them.
- `flake.nix`: `venusTestEnvironment` sets `EON_VENUS_TEST_SANS_FONT` to
  `${pkgs.dejavu_fonts}/share/fonts/truetype/DejaVuSans.ttf` (the package in
  `venusFonts`, which the product's fonts.conf names) for the Venus package's
  build and checks and for the dev shell. `nix/test-sandbox.nix` passes
  `EON_VENUS_TEST_*` into the eon-test sandbox. Test-only; the installed
  wrapper's environment is unchanged (`venusEnvironment` does not include it).
  Without the variable the fit test fails with a message naming it.

## Tests

- New `default_hints_fit_a_1280_pixel_window` (bin): the default popup catalog
  (mirrored from `eon/crates/eon/src/product.rs`, which the bin cannot import)
  through `shortcut_hints_for`; asserts `Scroll` for the default label and a
  configured label kept; lays out every hint below priority 4 in the packaged
  DejaVu Sans file, the exact path `EON_VENUS_TEST_SANS_FONT` names (pinned
  with `set_header_font_file`, so neither host fontconfig aliases such as Open
  Sans nor any other DejaVu Sans copy, such as this host's in
  `/usr/share/fonts` or another Nix revision's, can change the result) at 1280 logical px, scales 1
  and 2, and asserts the bar is complete. Failure it catches beyond existing coverage: a new or longer hint
  that pushes required hints off a 13-inch screen.
- `shortcut_hints_follow_bindings_catalog_and_native_focus`: new strings
  (`HJKL`, `HJKL · 1..9`, `CA`, `side`, `pane`…), and Alt+/, Alt+Shift+Q and
  Ctrl+Alt+Shift+H/L listed in full help with their chords and absent from the
  footer; Alt+Q stays covered by the inbox/agent-jump loop.
- `quit_key_lists_hints_and_yields_to_a_popup` (tests/shortcuts.rs): its
  hint-tier assertions are gone (Quit has no hint; the main test proves it).
  The name is kept because EON-C20 and VEN-C20/VEN-C8 proof records cite it.
- `configured_popups_take_fixed_bindings_except_reserved_keys`: the kept
  reserved-key hint example moves from the removed viewer hint to Alt+3's
  `Focus tab by position` (the same popup list tries to take Alt+3).
- Scene `workspace.rs` footer test: the Shortcuts control is present with a
  complete and with an incomplete footer.
- Accessibility: `shortcut_hints_are_read_only_and_retire_hidden_help_actions`
  renamed `shortcut_hints_are_read_only_and_keep_the_shortcuts_button` (no
  document cites it): with a footer, Shortcuts stays in the tree and
  clickable. The version-label test asserts Shortcuts unconditionally.
- `bar.rs` drop test: hint gap `0.75 x padding`, group gap at least that.

## Docs and contracts

- C1-C4 as approved (`01-contract-step.md`), applied verbatim.
- D1-D5 applied, extended with the later INBOX decisions: `side`, `Scroll`
  unless configured, dashless legend (`AS`, `CA`), and the dynamic popup
  hints: "dropping popup hints other than Git and Agent first, from the end of
  the popup catalog. With the default font a 1280-pixel-wide window shows every
  other hint."
- `venus/docs/REFERENCES.md:77`: example header `A-S` → `AS`.
- `CHANGELOG.md` and `venus/CHANGELOG.md` (VEN-C21, VEN-C32) entries.

## Deviations and decisions

- Scrollback → `Scroll`: popup labels are configurable, so the shortening is
  keyed on the default label; renaming the popup in config wins. A hint-only
  label key would need an EONW change; not done.
- Mac compact legend joins the same way, so a Super/Cmd chord with other
  modifiers reads e.g. `ACmd`; no default binding uses that.
- Configurability (rule 6), reason these changed values stay fixed: the
  hint gap (12 → 9 px, group gaps now at least 9 px), the shortened labels
  (`HJKL`, `pane`, `col`, `tab`, `window`, `side`, `Scroll`, dashless `CA`/`AS`)
  and the always-shown `?` are the 1280 px layout budget that
  `default_hints_fit_a_1280_pixel_window` enforces. Per-user overrides of
  them could silently break the 13-inch fit Lucca asked for, a support cost
  that outweighs differing preferences. Popup labels, the text most people
  would want to change, are already configurable (`[popups.*] label`), and a
  configured label replaces `Scroll`. Decision 8 (hints font size) is not
  used (Lucca, INBOX ~04:55Z).
- Humans and Agents: the hints bar and Shortcuts viewer are Venus-local view
  state, an exception in AGENT-RULES; no CLI path changes.
- Load rule: the second measurement run started at load 12.7 (incremental
  one-test build); every later heavy run waited for load < 8.
- First candidate `nix build` (tree `f6304438`) failed in the Venus
  checkPhase: the fit test, then using the platform sans-serif face, measured
  host Open Sans under `eon-test` but DejaVu Sans in the Nix sandbox, where
  the required hints needed 1300 px. Reported BLOCKED; the overseer chose the
  9 px gap and a deterministic packaged-font test (`02-width.md`).
- Product consequence (not changed here): on a host whose fontconfig names
  another sans-serif face, the installed bar uses that face (Open Sans on
  this host) and may be narrower or wider than DejaVu Sans.
- The fit test's popup catalog copies `eon/crates/eon/src/product.rs`
  (the bin cannot depend on the eon crate); a comment says to keep them in
  step. A default popup or label change there does not move this test.
- Venus keys the `Scroll` shortening on Eon's default id and label
  (`scrollback`/`Scrollback`), the same pattern as the existing `project` and
  `git`/`agent` special cases (Opus review nit 9, kept). If Eon's default
  label changes, the shortening silently stops; only the fit test's copied
  catalog covers it.
- Round 1: rebased (detached checkout with the staged change carried) from
  `605cca5` onto edge `03f72d3`, which touches only `.beads/issues.jsonl` and
  `eon/crates/eon/tests/workspace_control.rs`.
- Landing overlap (reviews): `eon-y22fl` prepends the first Unreleased bullet
  at the same `CHANGELOG.md` line, so the second lander resolves a textual
  conflict; both touch `scene.rs`, `application.rs`, `accessibility.rs`, scene
  tests and `docs/USAGE.md` in non-overlapping hunks. With `?` always taking a
  header slot, rerun `eon_bar_keeps_tabs_controls_and_drag_hits_disjoint_under_pressure`
  after integrating.

title: Build a public interactive explainer for Eon
description:
## Why

Eon's defining behavior is easy to lose in architecture prose: a person can close the native window while the Orbit-owned Session keeps running, then reopen Eon and reconnect to the same work. One small interactive explainer can show that lifecycle before introducing subsystem names.

## Evidence

- `README.md:28-37` defines Eon and EonTerm as products, Sessions as the user-facing durability concept, and Orbit and Venus as engineering subsystems.
- `README.md:109-142` documents exact-generation launch, detach-only window close, surviving Sessions, and later presentation through `eon attach`.
- `docs/VISUAL-REFERENCES.md:8-17` pins System Atlas at `6b3c91bc54e638ff58699b04199d994369ba7e3c` as the preferred visual reference and records the ownership, reuse, narrow-screen, keyboard, and reduced-motion constraints.
- System Atlas uses progressive chapters and inspectable flows from one authored data model. Its MIT source includes a 104-line Node build script and a 396-line HTML renderer, but the current template is desktop-first and loads Google Fonts.

Impact: MEDIUM for onboarding and product explanation. Effort: M. Implementation risk: LOW if kept as a static documentation artifact. Confidence: HIGH.

## Scope

In scope:
- One release-stamped interactive explainer derived from accepted Eon documentation and exact component revisions.
- A short user-first sequence: open Eon; start work in a durable Session; close the window while work continues; reopen and reconnect; organize Sessions in the workspace; then inspect Eon, Orbit, and Venus ownership.
- Public product language before engineering names. The final technical chapter may expose the owner boundaries.
- One shareable static artifact with keyboard navigation, useful narrow-screen behavior, a reduced-motion mode, readable text alternatives, and no telemetry or required network assets.
- A source-reuse and toolchain gate comparing a small Eon-owned artifact with bounded reuse of the exact MIT System Atlas renderer.

Out of scope:
- Changing Eon, Orbit, Venus, EONW, ORBS, runtime behavior, installation, or product contracts.
- Creating Eon for the web, a website framework, a documentation platform, analytics, live product state, or remote access.
- Treating generated `SYSTEM.md`, atlas decisions, or atlas question IDs as canonical. Eon contracts, README, architecture docs, and Beads retain ownership.
- Adding Node, npm, a bundler, durable JavaScript, copied MIT source, an external font, or a publishing service without the required user and toolchain decision.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. One release-stamped static artifact explains open, durable work, detach, reconnect, workspace organization, and the Eon, Orbit, and Venus owner boundary without claiming behavior beyond the cited accepted Eon revision.
2. The default chapter order uses public product language; engineering subsystem names appear only in the final technical chapter or an explicit detail view.
3. A real-browser check passes on a wide desktop and narrow viewport with keyboard-only navigation, reduced motion, readable text alternatives, and offline loading.
4. Eon contracts, README, architecture docs, and Beads remain canonical. The artifact contains no duplicate decision store, question tracker, generated `SYSTEM.md` authority, telemetry, required network asset, runtime state, or Eon Web scope.
5. The issue records the selected implementation shape, exact source and license identity, user approval for any source reuse or non-Rust toolchain, build and validation command, owned LOC, replacement cost, revision label, and any approved publishing location. Canonical documentation links and the README LOC scorecard match the accepted files.

## Implementation Notes

1. Re-read the accepted Eon contracts, naming model, and exact component proofs. Record the release or proof revision represented by the explainer.
2. Inspect System Atlas at exact commit `6b3c91bc54e638ff58699b04199d994369ba7e3c`. Record its MIT terms, useful interaction mechanisms, rejected planning machinery, owned LOC, toolchain cost, and replacement cost.
3. Stop for user approval before source reuse, a durable non-Rust language, a build tool, or public hosting. Prefer an existing approved documentation surface and no package dependency.
4. Author the smallest chapter set that explains Session durability and workspace composition. Keep representative payloads hidden from the default public path.
5. Generate or author one artifact, verify it with a real browser, and link it from canonical docs only after its revision label and hosting location are stable.

## Verification

- `git diff --check` exits 0.
- `rg -n "Eon|EonTerm|Sessions|Orbit|Venus" README.md docs/ARCHITECTURE.md docs/CONTRACTS.md` confirms that the explainer's nouns and owner boundaries map to canonical text.
- The selected build or validation command recorded at the source-reuse and toolchain gate exits 0 and produces one self-contained static artifact.
- Manual browser checks cover a wide desktop, a narrow viewport, keyboard-only navigation, reduced motion, and offline loading. Every user-visible lifecycle claim cites the exact accepted Eon revision it represents.
- The README LOC scorecard and changed documentation links match the final tracked files.

## Stop Conditions

- Stop if Eon's product naming or detach and reconnect behavior changes before authoring completes.
- Stop if the artifact would become another owner for contracts, decisions, questions, or runtime state.
- Stop for user choice if implementation requires a new language, dependency, copied source, external service, or public deployment.
- Stop if the explainer cannot communicate the user outcome without exposing speculative behavior.

## Maintenance Notes

Treat the explainer as a release-stamped projection, not a live architecture database. Update it when a public release changes one of its shown flows. Skip System Atlas's generated `SYSTEM.md`, question tracker, and decision table. No runtime dependency or Eon contract changes are expected.

title: Keep an agent's tool-runner settings (pager, colour, locale, GIT_EDITOR) out of Eon terminals
description:
## Why

Found while implementing and reviewing eon-geigu (2026-11-01). When the Eon supervisor starts from an agent's shell, every terminal also inherits that agent's generic tool settings, not just its session identity:

- Claude Code's Bash tool sets `GIT_EDITOR=true`, so a bare `git commit` in such a terminal gets an empty message.
- Codex unified exec (`codex-rs/core/src/unified_exec/process_manager.rs:95-104`, ref ~/pjs/refs/codex-0163 at 8308618) sets `NO_COLOR=1`, `LANG`/`LC_CTYPE`/`LC_ALL=C.UTF-8`, an empty `COLORTERM`, and `PAGER`/`GIT_PAGER`/`GH_PAGER=cat` beside `CODEX_CI=1`. The result is no colour, no pager and a forced locale in every terminal. Orbit already overrides `TERM` and `COLORTERM`.
- Codex's credential broker swaps real API keys for dummy values that only its proxy accepts, so such an Eon carries the dummies.

These are names people also set on purpose, so eon-geigu's exact-name removal cannot cover them. Eon is the terminal for humans and agents: an agent starting Eon must not break the person's next terminal either.

## Options (decide in planning)

1. Remove the known agent-set values only when the matching agent marker was inherited (e.g. Codex's set only when `CODEX_CI=1` arrived; Claude's `GIT_EDITOR=true` only when `CLAUDECODE` arrived). This needs the supervisor to know the marker before eon-geigu's removal drops it.
2. Start the supervisor's terminal environment from a clean login environment (the user's session environment from systemd/the desktop) instead of the caller's shell.
3. Warn only: the CLI says so when it starts a supervisor from an agent shell.

Recommendation to evaluate: option 1, as the narrowest change.

## Contract

EON-C9 (managed shell environment), next to eon-geigu's agent-session clause. Contract text needs Lucca's approval.

## Prerequisites

eon-geigu (agent-session removal) landed.

## Acceptance

Tests: start a supervisor from an environment carrying Codex's unified-exec set plus `CODEX_CI=1` → a terminal has the user's own values or none. The same values without the marker pass through unchanged. Installed check in an isolated root.

## Scope boundary

Only values an agent's own tool runner sets. No general environment policy, and no change to the supervisor's own environment.
close_reason: Agent tool-runner settings (Claude Code / Codex markers, Codex's forced C.UTF-8 locale) no longer leak into Eon terminals; the desktop locale is restored from the systemd user manager by a bounded, cancelled, drained and capped read. Proof, review ledger and gate PASS recorded above; follow-up eon-yxo2y.1 stays open.

title: Ask before Alt+W closes a pane that is running something
description:
## Why
2026-10-29: Lucca lost a live Claude conversation (the herdr investigator, pane p3) to a stray Alt+W
while typing; it was recoverable only because Claude can resume. Alt+W closes the selected pane and
stops its terminal at once; Eon asks first only for the final tab's last pane
(`warning_close_last_tab`, docs/CONFIGURATION.md "Closing the last tab"). Alt+W sits next to Alt+Q,
which just became the attention inbox (VEN-C32). For a terminal whose promise is persistent terminals,
one keystroke killing an agent, editor or build is the costliest cheap mistake.
Lucca, 2026-10-29, on the overseer's proposal: "1 ok".

## Change (proposal; contract wording goes to Lucca first)
1. Alt+W on a pane whose terminal is busy asks first, reusing the last-tab close prompt (Enter closes,
   Escape cancels). An idle shell closes at once, as now.
2. One setting governs it, default on, documented in docs/CONFIGURATION.md (a sibling of
   `warning_close_last_tab`, or a widening of it: decide in the plan). Eon Runtime parses it and sends
   the resolved value; Venus parses none.
3. `eon pane close` keeps its current behaviour; `--json` never asks.

Open decision for the plan (numbered question to Lucca with a recommendation):
- What counts as busy. (a) The PTY's foreground process group is not the shell (WezTerm's default:
  confirm unless the foreground process is a known shell). This covers agents, editors and builds,
  but Orbit owns terminal state and may need to expose it, which changes the protocol and makes this
  a consequential shape. (b) The pane has agent attention (EON-C31) other than none. That data is
  already in EONW, but it only covers agents that report attention.

## Reference gate (consequential if (a))
Read docs/REFERENCES.md routes; compare WezTerm (`skip_close_confirmation_for_processes_named`),
kitty (`confirm_os_window_close` with its running-process count), tmux (`kill-pane` confirm on
prefix-x) and Zellij. Record the inspected revisions, what is kept and what is rejected.

## Acceptance
Linux: a red/green test at the owner for the busy/idle decision; one isolated installed observation
showing that Alt+W on a pane running an agent or other busy process asks, Escape keeps it, Enter
closes it, and an idle shell closes at once.

## Scope
Venus close prompt, Runtime config, Orbit only if (a) is chosen. Out of scope: undo-close, tab close
(already covered), and CLI prompts. Sequence after the Yu testing gate (eon-mac-launch-kz4p).

## Planning reconciliation (2026-11-12, dcaef1c)

Proposed consolidation only: later eon-qi5nh owns this native busy pane/tab
close outcome and the 2026-11-10 exact-scope-consent replan, including two
unresolved safety choices and Lucca's explicit post-v0.2.0 decision. Reuse that
owner rather than the older snapshot/next-response shape. EON-C10:1720-1746
already gives CLI pane/tab close busy confirmation; the original no-prompt CLI
statement here is historical, not an override. Preserve this bead's Alt+W,
config/default proposal, reference comparisons and Enter/Escape/idle checks in
that plan before closing this duplicate with Lucca's approval. No status change,
new beta edge, contract edit or safety/config decision here; reconcile the old
Yu sequencing note against the later explicit post-beta decision with overseer.

title: Re-prove the VEN-C16 macOS foundation natively on the Apple Silicon Mac
description:
## Decision
Lucca, 2026-10-18 15:05 UTC-3: before the rented Scaleway Mac lapses (2026-10-19 01:24 UTC-3), collect a native Venus baseline at current edge and record it in its own bead, then start ven-prove-macos-accessibility-lifecycle-identity-c3b if time remains.

## Contract
VEN-C16's open proof lists the Apple Silicon opaque AppKit/AccessKit/Metal foundation, the native interaction partial proof, and Kotoeri composition as pending re-proof in this repository. They were accepted before consolidation (ven-bring-up-opaque-appkit-metal-g4a at af3804a, ven-deliver-macos-input-pasteboard-links-zfw). No contract change: this either re-proves what those slices accepted, at one exact edge revision, or records exactly what fails.

## Acceptance
- At one exact edge revision, shipped as git archive: a locked all-target build of yazelix-venus on aarch64-darwin, plus its test suite run natively. Record hardware, macOS, Rust, Zig, and Ghostty identities.
- In a logged-in GUI session, launch Venus against native yazelix-orbit built from the same tree and observe the following: AppKit window creation, AccessKit initialization, Metal adapter and surface, visible opaque presentation, resize and native-scale redraw, Unicode text, Command copy/paste with general-pasteboard edge cases, link Open/Copy, ordinary typing, Kotoeri IME commit, click/drag and scrolling, and clean close with Orbit surviving.
- Record each item as passed, failed, or not observed, with the reason. Only this native evidence may narrow VEN-C16's open proof; the remaining children's acceptance stays open.
- The Mac is left clean (~/eon-venus-nm7 removed; ~/bend-orbit untouched).

## Scope boundary
Evidence only. No production code change unless a regression is found; if one is, stop and ask. No c3b, yzw, or piy acceptance, Eon composition, Nix on Darwin, signing, notarization, or support claim.

Prerequisites: eon-orb-c14-mac-reproof-l8rz (ORB-C14 Proved at 4910b81; Orbit unchanged through e0aa47e).

title: Give agents routine services without an overseer turn
description:
Lucca, 2026-11-11: "agree. create the beads" (option 1 of eon-meta-overseer's "smooth production" options).

## Why

eon-meta-overseer measured eon-overseer's transcripts from 2026-11-08 20:14Z to 11-11 18:29Z (about 70 h):
- 5,840 assistant messages, each re-reading about 230k tokens of context. The context was compacted 18 times.
- 60% of messages were triggered by background notifications. 851 of them were Monitor events, about 690 of those agent STATUS requests.
- 30% were triggered by Lucca's messages, and 7% by peer sessions.

Agents' requests split about 520 service requests (slots, builds, nudges, landings, filing beads) to 150 decisions (/home/lucca/.cache/eon-agents/eon-meta-overseer/evidence-decisions.md). The service requests are mechanical. Each one costs the overseer a turn at full context and adds agent wait time.

## Goal

Agents get routine services without an overseer turn. The overseer wakes only for decisions, failures and Lucca. The children each remove one class of request. The wait study is complete: children .5 (short lane) and .6 (quiet-window policy) already hold its chosen work.

## Measure

Baseline: about 12 monitor events per hour, and 60% of overseer messages triggered by notifications. Measure with `python3 -I /home/lucca/.cache/eon-agents/eon-meta-overseer/overseer-triggers.py <overseer session id prefixes>`, one week after the children land.

## Acceptance and boundaries

- Each child records its delivered service, the failure/recovery cases it exercised, and the handoff to its operational owner. This epic aggregates the six existing outcomes; it does not authorize new product commands, scheduling policy or contracts.
- One week after the services land, compare the same notification/trigger measures against the historical baseline above; identify the session IDs, observation dates and sample sizes. Report missing evidence rather than claiming a saving from the old estimate. Desk intake is already operational according to its 2026-11-11 handoff; .4 verifies that deployment and its measure.
- Preserve coordinator approval of landings and fleet orders, serialized br writes, exact-tree proof, live terminals and desktop focus. .1 owns the landing service, .2 filing, .3 notifications, .4 intake, .5 short jobs and .6 timing isolation. Parent-child edges are containment, not a requirement to finish the parent before starting a child.
- Existing overseer helpers are the internal reference. eon-eon-agent-lr8sx.23 owns reconciliation into the shipped workflow skill/Rust repository tools; .21/.21.1 own public heavy-run queue design. Lucca's newer Eon-first/rota-fixes-only decision (lr8sx comment 6556, 2026-11-12) supersedes references here to adding rota features. Do not create duplicate product owners or a durable shell/Python policy engine.

## Verification

Planning is verified by bead readback/dependency review. Future implementation children use the repository's appropriate script/tooling checks and fresh review; the week-long observation measures operational effect and is not replaced by a build. No implementation, builds, runtime actions or measurements were performed by this planning pass.

Keep the approved service: the overseer alone appends an approved bead/tree/base/check-class/refresh entry; a serial lander consumes it under a lock, invokes existing landing checks and required heavy-run builds, lands according to existing Git rules, and records the result. Wake the overseer on failure or when the queue empties. Preserve batching of nearby approved landings.

## Children and order

This is an epic because correcting the measurement extractor and implementing the mutation/landing service are independently verifiable changes in different owners. `eon-z7zdx.1.1` repairs full-ID/ownership/READY FOR LANDING attribution first; `eon-z7zdx.1.2` (blocked by .1.1) then establishes a comparable baseline and pilots two approved landings. Neither child adds an Eon product landing CLI or takes over coordinator approval.

## Accepted constraints carried from comment 6499

- Landing checks get first claim on the next free heavy slot (priority only); no running job is preempted.
- Historical approved-to-landed p90 was 163.6 then 42.6 minutes, but is only a proxy because landq.py truncated IDs, guessed ownership from mention counts and sometimes started before approval. Correct the metric before asserting improvement; target p90 under 30 minutes remains a target, not a promise or a two-sample percentile claim.
- Quiet-window policy is settled by eon-z7zdx.6/comment 6500: only fmt/non-compiling landing checks may run inside an absolute gate window. Clippy, builds and suites stay held. Priority never bypasses that hold.

## Acceptance

- Both children are complete with exact source/artifact identities, check results and recovery evidence recorded on their own beads.
- Two actual, separately approved queue entries produce the same required checks/proof/commit form as hand dispatch, and each is landed at most once. A stale tree/base, changed proof class, missing approval, failed check or failed refresh stops that entry and reports the cause; retries do not silently duplicate a landing or lose the queue record.
- Record corrected approved-to-landed samples and overseer messages per landing before/after. A small pilot proves routing and safety; longer-period p90 remains an explicit measurement gap until enough observations exist.

## Scope and reference gate

Internal workflow service only, using existing landing, heavy-run and Git owners. Before implementation inspect current helpers at an exact revision/recorded identity; the scripts are outside this reading worktree and were not audited in this pass. Read docs/AGENT-RULES.md Git Workflow, Proof and Review, Implementation Languages and relevant reference routes. eon-eon-agent-lr8sx.23 reconciles the shipped workflow skill/tooling owner; no second product scheduler, new public CLI, contract edit, release promotion or automatic scope approval is implied. ## Verification and stops

Bead graph/readback now. Future children name their smallest falsifiers and use current whole-workspace/check/review rules for actual code or script changes.
