title: File agents' follow-up beads in batches from bead/followups.md
description:
Agents write follow-up bead bodies to a file, and a filer creates them in one batch, so filing needs no overseer turn per bead.

## Now

Agents ask the overseer to file follow-ups through STATUS REQUEST lines, and each request costs an overseer turn. The overseer has also filed duplicates (shortcuts; see evidence-decisions.md).

## Change

1. Agents append follow-up bodies to `<work-dir>/bead/followups.md`: title, priority, labels, parent if any, and body. The format comes from the create-beads skill.
2. A filer runs on a schedule or on demand. It can be a Sonnet subagent or eon-desk. It runs `br search` for each title to avoid duplicates, creates the beads one write at a time, writes each new ID back next to its entry, and sends the overseer one digest line per batch.
3. The overseer only looks at P0/P1 items and items that touch the release gate (eon-igae).

## Proof

One batch from two work dirs is filed with no duplicates, and the IDs are recorded. Count overseer turns spent on filing in a week, before and after.

## Scope, ownership and prerequisites

One bounded internal filing workflow, not a new Beads database, scheduler or product CLI. The filer uses the repository's br/create-beads workflow and current approved follow-up scope; a submitted draft is not approval of a new feature/contract. Keep unresolved scope/approval items visible for the coordinator rather than filing them as settled decisions. Preserve Lucca's P0/P1/release-gate escalation above. eon-eon-agent-lr8sx.23 owns eventual shipped skill/tooling reconciliation; use the existing file workflow, Rust for durable repository policy and shell only for process glue.

Reference gate before implementation: inspect the actual work-dir follow-up records, create-beads body template and current filer/desk workflow at recorded identities. The existing process descriptions are historical evidence; no external script was read or executed in this worktree-only pass.

## Acceptance and verification

- A batch containing two work dirs, a unique item, an already-filed item and a duplicate draft across dirs yields exactly one bead per distinct chosen outcome. Search by meaning/owner as well as title; preserve the canonical existing ID and record it beside every matching entry.
- Re-running the batch, or resuming after creation succeeded but recording the returned ID failed, does not create another bead. Malformed/unapproved entries remain intact with an actionable disposition; successful bodies, parent/labels and IDs are not lost.
- Only one filer writes br at a time, including overlapping scheduled/on-demand invocations. One short batch digest includes created/reused IDs and exceptions; P0/P1 and release-gate issues reach the coordinator. No message is sent by this planning pass.
- One small observable check covers repeat/recovery behavior; use a disposable tracker/fixture or read-only preview for error injection, never create duplicate production beads as a test. Then one authorized real batch proves routing. Record exact source, environment and result. Future code/script work follows normal workspace proof and review.
- Retain the original week-long overseer-turn comparison; missing historical data is a reported gap, not a fabricated baseline.

## Stop conditions

Stop for missing filing authority, material draft ambiguity, a required contract change or a conflict with the .23 workflow owner. Do not change release membership, close/defer another bead, or invent follow-ups under this service.

title: Wake the overseer only for actionable agent lines, digest the rest
description:
Replace the overseer's several STATUS monitors with one watcher that wakes it only for actionable lines and sends everything else as a digest.

## Now

Several overlapping monitors ("agent STATUS requests" 319 events; "Pane agent milestones and requests" 150+41+34+9+9; "STATUS lines needing the overseer" 84+49; heavy.sh queue alerts about 70) produced 851 events in about 70 h. Each one wakes the overseer at about 230k context. Several watchers also broke silently: history-compress waited 25 min unanswered, and kz4p resumed 33 min late (evidence-decisions.md).

## Change

1. One watcher script covers every active work dir.
2. It wakes the overseer immediately for:
   - BLOCKED:
   - REQUEST lines that need a decision
   - READY FOR REVIEW / READY FOR LANDING
   - failures
   - Lucca relays
3. Milestones, progress lines and queue status go into a digest every 30 min, or are dropped once child 1 (landing queue) and the heavy.sh slot child handle them.
4. A heartbeat line makes it obvious when the watcher dies.

## Proof

Run it for one day alongside the old monitors and confirm no actionable line was missed. Then switch over and count overseer wake-ups per hour (baseline about 12) and messages per hour.

## Scope, ownership and prerequisites

One internal event-routing owner replaces overlapping monitors; no product watcher service or new public configuration. Read the current monitor inventory and STATUS grammar at recorded identities before implementation. This planning pass verified the historical report, not the external monitor scripts. eon-eon-agent-lr8sx.23 owns eventual shared skill/tooling reconciliation; use Rust for durable policy and existing launch/monitor owners rather than a parallel scheduler.

Children .1/.5 are optional service consumers, not blockers: until they handle a request, retain its actionable notification. Only proven handled events may be dropped. Keep the approved 30-minute digest policy and heartbeat; the operational heartbeat interval and failure detection bound must be recorded before rollout, not left implicit.

## Acceptance and verification

- Fixture replay covers every actionable class above, duplicate monitor inputs, progress-only lines, repeated/changed STATUS lines and a new work dir. Every new actionable occurrence reaches the coordinator once; ordinary progress cannot produce an immediate wake or hide a request/failure.
- A watcher restart and file replacement/truncation do not silently lose unread actionable lines. The heartbeat has a defined observable stale/failure signal, so the watcher cannot die with no notice.
- During the approved one-day shadow run the old monitors stay authoritative; log comparison reports actionable inputs and missing/duplicate deliveries. Avoid double-notifying the live coordinator merely to collect shadow evidence.
- Switch to the single watcher only with zero unexplained missed actionable events, record how to restore the old monitors, then compare wake-ups/hour and messages/hour against the same historical measurement definition. Source checks alone do not prove the one-day observation.
- One small replay check covers routing/restart logic; actual script/tool changes retain normal workspace/check/review rules. Record identities, dates, command/observation and results. No monitors are run or changed in this planning pass.

## Stop conditions

Stop before dropping an unhandled event class, changing the coordinator/desk authority, or adding a product CLI/contract. Do not adopt a stale event list without checking current STATUS producers.

description:

- venus/src/application.rs:6404: initial Wayland admission waits for the surface to enter an output; later scale/resize remains native behavior. This path is newer than the original four-second observation.

## Scope and prerequisites

One investigation-only session. Read venus/AGENTS.md, its development/native test route and the pinned winit version before the run. Reuse the current native startup probe or isolated installed Eon on a private scale-2 Sway output configured before launch, with a bounded wait long enough for mapping/output admission. Record compositor output/scale and surface mapping/output entry as independent witnesses of the requested setup, then Venus's log and actual physical/logical geometry. A scale-1 comparison separates a bad setup from a real scale failure. If the probe itself cannot map/admit the output, report an inconclusive harness gap instead of a product defect.

If Venus still stays at 1 after confirmed admission, trace the current pinned winit Wayland scale path (wl_output, fractional-scale-v1/preferred_buffer_scale as actually used) against compositor events and record the cause. No implementation, dependency upgrade, contract edit or assertion of Darwin/fractional-scale support here. Portability: isolated Linux/Wayland investigation; no wire or durable-format change.

- An isolated observation identifies exact source/binary, compositor/backend, scale configuration, output-entry evidence, wait bound and the scale Venus reaches. Describe whether text/grid geometry uses that scale; a lone startup log is not sufficient.

An inconclusive setup/hardware result is an unfinished handoff: record the gap and next falsifying observation, and keep the bead open. Do not infer a cause solely from elapsed time.
- Use the existing isolated display/native probe recipe from venus/docs/DEVELOPMENT.md; no broad Rust suite/build for an observation-only investigation. Preserve logs needed to reproduce a disputed scale claim and report missing native coverage.

Never use Lucca's live Eon or desktop, change physical output settings, take desktop focus, or stop a live supervisor. Own and clean only the isolated proof processes/storage. title: Let eon pane create add a pane without taking focus (--no-focus)
description:
## Why

On 2026-10-22 the orchestrating agent, running in Lucca's Agent popup, started two agents with `eon pane create --json -- claude "..."` (eon-n6ga). Each launch dismissed the popup and selected the new pane, which took Lucca away from the conversation he was in. He asked: "should it steal focus, or mantain the popup? the current behaviour steals focus". Then he approved the recommendation below ("yeah").

## Decision (Lucca, 2026-10-22)

Add `--no-focus` to `eon pane create`, for both the plain and the `-- COMMAND` form. It adds the pane, but the caller's popup stays shown and the tab's selected pane does not change. The default stays as it is: the new pane is selected and a calling popup is dismissed. That matches Alt+M, today's EON-C10, and all four reference tools: tmux `-d`, Zellij `--no-focus`, kitty `--keep-focus`, and WezTerm, which always focuses. Orchestrating agents always pass `--no-focus`. Rejected: never focusing when a command is given. It differs from every comparable tool and from plain `pane create`, and users would have to switch to the pane by hand. Ship it on its own EONW bump (v16), but hold the profile refresh so that one restart covers it together with whatever lands alongside. Sharing yx8.7's bump was rejected because it would wait behind yx8.6/yx8.7.

## Evidence (edge 7849484)

- `docs/CONTRACTS.md` EON-C10 (calling-terminal bullet): "so `pane create` selects the new pane and dismisses the tab's popup".
- `runtime/crates/eon-runtime/src/workspace.rs`: `dispatch` selects the target pane before `apply`; `create_pane(target, called, ...)` and `dismiss_for_pane_action` do the dismissal.
- `runtime/crates/eon-workspace-protocol/src/v15.rs`: `WorkspaceAction::CreatePane` has no payload, and `Action::CreateCommandPane { argv }` (tag 27) has no focus field. Carrying the option needs an EONW change (v16).
- Reference evidence for the four tools at pinned revisions is on eon-n6ga (comment "Reference evidence").

## Scope

In scope: the EON-C10 text change (Lucca approves the exact wording before code); EONW v16 carrying a keep-focus flag on both pane-create requests; the Runtime behavior (no selection change, no popup dismissal, and the new pane placed exactly as now); CLI parsing of `--no-focus` in either flag order alongside `--json`; `eon --help`; `docs/USAGE.md`; `CHANGELOG.md`; `venus/CHANGELOG.md` (rename only); the component graph in a second commit, as eon-n6ga did (0c066f1 then 6c582e3).

Out of scope: Alt+M and the Commands popup "New pane" entry (they keep focusing); `eon edit`; focus flags on other commands.

## Acceptance

- From the Agent popup, `eon pane create --no-focus -- sh -c 'sleep 30'` adds a pane in the tab's selected column. The popup stays shown and `selected_pane` is unchanged in `eon workspace --json`.
- Without `--no-focus`, the behavior is identical to today.

## Verification

- Codec wire bytes and bounds tests, a Runtime unit test for popup and pane callers, and the end-to-end CLI test in `eon/crates/eon/tests/workspace_control.rs`, all through `nix develop -c eon-test -p eon-workspace-protocol -p eon-runtime -p eon`.
- Full affected Rust and Nix surfaces for the wire change, plus one isolated installed observation on headless Sway, with a popup caller.

## Stop Conditions

- Stop for Lucca's approval of the EON-C10 wording and the v16 bump timing.
- Stop if the cursor or selection model cannot add a pane without selecting it. Record why and ask.

Observation (2026-10-22, window g1-934c7cca): the overseer launched the eon-be, eon-77 and eon-ff agents with 'eon pane create --no-focus --json -- claude ...' from the Agent popup, and Lucca's focus stayed on the popup. comments.text:
Decision (Lucca, 2026-10-22 ~16:25 -03, "Approve as drafted"; confirmed to the coordinator as "1. ok"): EON-C10 gains this Result bullet after `pane create -- COMMAND`:

"`eon pane create --no-focus [--json]`, with or without `-- COMMAND`, adds the same pane in the same place but takes no focus: the tab's selected column and pane stay as they were, a shown popup stays shown, and the new pane joins the end of its column collapsed. title: Benchmark Eon and EonTerm terminal memory
description:
## Outcome

Measure the Linux system-memory footprint of one idle and loaded terminal Session in full Eon and EonTerm against two controls on the same COSMIC Wayland machine:

- Foot: the lean independent full-terminal baseline. The installed package is foot 1.16.2 +pgo; upstream describes it as fast, lightweight, minimal, and Wayland-native.
- Ghostty: the same-engine full-GUI control. The installed snap is Ghostty 1.3.1 using the GTK runtime and OpenGL renderer.

This benchmark changes no EON product contract, runtime behavior, dependency, package, or platform promise. It is evidence for later optimization decisions only.

## Why both controls

EonTerm already uses libghostty inside Orbit. Ghostty is a useful related-engine GUI control, though its different engine revision, packaging, and renderer prevent isolating the cost of Eon's supervisor + Orbit + Venus split, while Foot tests whether the complete product is competitive with a deliberately lean independent terminal. Comparing only Alacritty or only libghostty would not answer either product question.

Mitchell Hashimoto's 2026-07-27 library benchmark is comparison evidence, not an Eon result: at 120×40 and 10,000 history rows, compressed libghostty reports 2.65–5.41 MiB versus alacritty_terminal 34.09–36.91 MiB; uncompressed libghostty reports 12.19–13.98 MiB. It measures terminal state in one shared Rust harness on macOS, not Linux GUI/process-tree cost.

Sources:
- https://x.com/mitchellh/status/2081788657078505732
- https://codeberg.org/dnkl/foot
- https://codeberg.org/dnkl/foot/src/branch/master/doc/benchmark.md
- https://github.com/ghostty-org/ghostty

## Contract and owner

Consumer: Eon product development.
Trigger: evaluate idle or scrollback memory cost before choosing optimization work.
Result: one reproducible table reports Eon, EonTerm, Ghostty, and Foot under identical workloads, with process-level attribution for Eon supervisor, Orbit, and Venus.
Important failures: do not compare RSS sums that double-count shared pages, different grid/font/scrollback settings, different child workloads, warm versus cold processes, or GUI memory against a terminal-state-only library number.

Eon owns this cross-product measurement. Orbit and Venus remain unchanged; a confirmed owner-specific problem must be separately chosen and routed before implementation.

## Method

- Use the installed COSMIC Wayland session and record kernel, compositor, GPU/backend, scale, exact executable/package revisions, configuration files, and environment.
- Recorded grid: 120×30, deviating from the planned 120×40 because of COSMIC startup geometry. Use 16 logical-pixel text, 18 logical-pixel row, opacity 1, and the same inert child. Orbit and Ghostty have 16 MiB history budgets; Foot requests 10,000 rows. Retained row counts are unmeasured; loaded labels describe emitted content.
- Measure empty, full-screen, and 10,000-row plain, styled, Unicode, and mixed workloads matching the published libghostty categories closely enough to state differences explicitly.
- Run at least 10 fresh processes per terminal after a fixed settle interval. Recorded cohort: 55 each for Eon, EonTerm and Foot, 54 for Ghostty; n=9 per workload except n=10 plain for Eon/EonTerm/Foot. The expanded 240-run plan was interrupted at 219; no ten-per-cell completion claim. Report median and empirical p05–p95 with actual counts.
- On Linux, sum proportional set size from /proc/*/smaps_rollup across each owned process tree; report unique/private memory when available. Report RSS only as secondary data. Exclude the identical child workload or show totals both with and without it.
- For Eon and EonTerm, report supervisor, Orbit, Venus, and total separately. Include all Ghostty/Foot descendants under the same rule.
- Keep any harness disposable unless repeated measurement proves a checked-in owner is worth maintaining. Do not add a benchmarking dependency.
- Do not count Nix closure size as runtime memory. Do not claim GPU memory unless a reliable backend-specific measurement is recorded separately.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. One table reports median and p05–p95 PSS for all four products and every workload under one recorded environment.
2. Eon and EonTerm process totals are attributable to supervisor, Orbit, Venus, and identical child; Foot and Ghostty use the same process-tree rule.
3. Grid, typography, opacity, scrollback, payload, child command, settle time, run count, warm/cold policy, and cleanup are identical or every unavoidable mismatch is explicit.
4. The result distinguishes terminal-state evidence from complete GUI/process memory and does not extrapolate Mitchell's macOS result to Linux.
5. Repeated runs leave no benchmark supervisors, Sessions, sockets, windows, or temporary configuration behind and do not stop existing Eon/Eonova Sessions.
6. Record raw observations or a lossless table, exact commands, summary, uncertainty, and whether any product-owned optimization is justified. Create no remediation bead without separate user approval.

## Scope boundary

No runtime edit, optimization, benchmark framework, CI job, dependency, child-repository change, terminal feature comparison, throughput claim, GPU-memory claim without evidence, or cross-platform conclusion. Stop if matching workloads would require changing user configuration or interrupting existing Sessions; use isolated temporary roots instead.
notes: Completed report: docs/benchmarks/eon-zlf-2026-09-08.md; lossless numeric observations: docs/benchmarks/eon-zlf-2026-09-08.csv (658 process rows, SHA256 f9477a676657e1744f213b382ab428a4b5eb22b4ed9d73b6eba3af5cc671cd24). Mechanically verified installed cohort: 219 runs, 55 Eon/EonTerm/Foot and 54 Ghostty, n=9 per cell except n=10 plain for Eon/EonTerm/Foot. Original minimum ten launches per terminal is met; expanded 240-run plan remains interrupted, with no ten-per-cell completion claim. Baseline edge dd74bacfdee000aa109f2bea855aa4651a7c04e7; installed runtime 0b0b6312531229270c157df31ba49800a6daef03, Venus ec80e36625dec73544c0cb64becf4b135c932a63, Orbit 91999d79546422b49bdbc124166a65859d0bd872. Exact COSMIC/Linux/artifacts/configs in report. Ghostty snap 820 is 1.3.1 ReleaseFast stable; official release list checked 2026-09-08 confirms latest stable, so no Home Manager change was needed. Installed packaging/renderer differences remain qualified. Summed PSS medians excluding identical child: empty Foot 11.21, EonTerm 71.05, Eon 71.20, Ghostty 182.61 MiB; mixed 24.73, 97.44, 97.40, 187.87 MiB. Venus is largest owner, but no waste or optimization is proved. Limits: 120x30 instead of planned 120x40, emitted history rather than measured retained rows, warm active host and uncontrolled focus/occlusion, related but unequal engine revisions/font bytes, no GPU-memory/long-term-growth claim. Three stray-input Foot runs flagged; exclusion sensitivity leaves ordering unchanged. Validation: offline analyze.py checks all scheduled labels, raw smaps fields, process identities/roles, geometry/barrier/settle, zero SwapPss and cleanup; independent CSV calculation verifies all 360 distributions. No GUI launches in this follow-up. All benchmark identities gone and 240 private roots absent; original desktop state and baseline user processes preserved at measurement cleanup. Evidence retained at ~/.local/state/eon/proofs/eon-zlf-20260908, final verification.json and summary.json supersede the historical partial-summary snapshot. Focus rule remains in local policy/generated AGENTS; source-backed import check reused, final overlay/Markdown/LOC/diff checks pass (18084 LOC). No runtime, optimization, package, or child changes. Pre-commit review normalized the generated CSV to LF; every parsed field is unchanged and the canonical CSV hash above is refreshed.
close_reason: Completed the original cross-product memory comparison with 219 verified runs and raw observations. Report explicitly preserves interrupted 240-run plan, n=9/10, 120x30 geometry, retention, desktop activity, and packaging limitations. Latest stable Ghostty 1.3.1 verified; no further desktop launches.

title: Show other workspaces' waiting agents in the sidebar, then re-evaluate the inbox
description:
## Why and recorded decision

Lucca asked on 2026-11-02 whether the attention inbox (VEN-C32, Alt+Q) duplicates the agent sidebar (VEN-C30). He agreed to keep both for now. They overlap within the shown session while the sidebar is open; the inbox currently provides the cross-session attention list. This is the possible later merge, not a scheduled inbox retirement.

## Current evidence (dcaef1c)

- venus/src/scene.rs:2858 sidebar_contents walks snapshot.tabs in the shown session; :2109 builds inbox rows from attention_queue, :2148 obtains shown-session pins. Queue entries from other sessions use their session name/ID fallback.
- docs/USAGE.md Agent sidebar/Attention inbox and EON-C31 describe the queue, its order/classes and cross-session FocusAttention. VEN-C30/VEN-C32 own the two surfaces; EON-C33 permits FocusAttention across sessions of one window.
- eon-ngwf.2 rejected turning the always-visible shown-session sidebar into a priority-ordered list because rows would reorder. Preserve tab order there.

## Approved outcome, children and order

2. `eon-zlulm.2` (blocked by .1) evaluates the resulting sidebar against the inbox's urgency order, filters, hidden-sidebar access and keyboard/accessibility flows. It records a recommendation for Lucca; any retirement is a separately approved outcome.

title: orbit-visible-text's unread-answer bound fails under load
description:
Found in eon-buys1.1's final Nix proof, 2026-11-04.

## Why

The real-PTY check `orbit-visible-text` failed once in the `nix build
--keep-going` proof of eon-buys1.1's tree `0f4ec83`, while the same build
compiled Venus and Eon (load about 10, peaking near 14):

```
orbit-visible-text> thread 'visible_text' panicked at orbit/tests/real_pty/visible_text.rs:329:5:
orbit-visible-text> the unread answer held the PTY or the client for 1.644704301s
```

The step is `a_holder_that_stops_reading_loses_the_lease`. It asserts that a
command's title reaches the attached client within 1.0 s while the lease
holder leaves a 1 MiB `ReadVisible` answer unread. Rerun alone on the same
tree at load 2.5, it passed (`ok. 1 passed`, 7.95 s). eon-buys1.1 does not
touch this path; its only host change is a timestamp in `Orbit::apply` and
`flush_writes`.

This is the same class as eon-etgwm (Stop-reply checks under load) and
eon-detached-turns-flaky-yvua, but a different check and bound. Such
failures stall the final proof of unrelated beads and invite "probably a
flake" judgments.

## Change

Find whether the 1.0 s bound measures Orbit (a real stall of the owner loop
behind the unread answer) or the test's own scheduling under load. Then
either widen the test's margin to what the contract promises (ORB-C17 and
ORB-C13's slow-peer rule never block PTY or presentation), or fix a real
delay if one exists.

## Acceptance

`orbit-visible-text` passes reliably while a parallel build keeps load above
10, for example in 5 of 5 runs next to a `nix build` of `.#default`.

Labels: flaky, orbit, proof, tests. Related: eon-etgwm,
eon-detached-turns-flaky-yvua.
close_reason: No Orbit stall; the check now orders the title after the queued answer and records answer timing

comments.author: lucca
comments.text:
# eon-zmq4b record 1: cause

Worktree `eon-zmq4b` at edge `570d0ad`, 2026-11-05, x86_64 Linux (16 threads,
31 GB). Instrumentation was temporary and is not in the commit; the patch is
kept at `~/.cache/eon-agents/eon-zmq4b-work/orbit-trace-instrumentation.patch`
(it also holds the sensitivity mutation in `management.rs`).

## Question

Does `a_holder_that_stops_reading_loses_the_lease`'s 1.0 s bound measure a
stall of Orbit's owner loop behind the unread 1 MiB `ReadVisible` answer, or
the check's own scheduling under load?

## Method

- Timestamps inside Orbit's release host: every fact with its Bend round
  trip and carry-out time, every poll wait of 20 ms or more, and every write
  to the management connection and to the interactive client.
- Timestamps in the check (request, command, titled frame, lease lost) and in
  the child (bash's `$EPOCHREALTIME` as it evaluates the command).
- A temporary loop ran the step N times per Orbit start, idle and under
  reproducible load:
  - 20 to 24 bounded CPU burners (`timeout`-limited busy loops);
  - a real `nix build .#default` that rebuilt Orbit, Venus and Eon;
  - both together.
- Each iteration was split into child (request to bash eval), Orbit (bash
  eval to the titled frame's last byte written) and test client (last byte
  to the check seeing the title).

## Evidence

Orbit never waits on the unread answer. In every one of 160 traced
iterations, Orbit wrote the titled frame while the answer stood at 219,264 of
1,046,684 bytes written, and the 1 s answer bound dropped the holder later
(`lost` 1.01 to 1.28 s). `Management::flush` returns on `WouldBlock`, and the
owner loop served the PTY and the client meanwhile.

What fills the window is CPU work that grows with contention:

| Load | Iterations | Request to title | Orbit's share | Longest single turn |
| --- | ---: | --- | --- | --- |
| idle, debug check | 5 | 72 to 87 ms | about 20 ms | 13 ms (frame) |
| idle, release check | 5 | 31 to 34 ms | | |
| `nix build .#default`, load 12 to 16 | 55 | 30 to 81 ms | | |
| 20 burners, load about 15, debug check | 10 | 222 to 441 ms | 59 to 125 ms | 81 ms |
| `nix build` plus 20 burners, load 12 to 25, release check | 25 | 57 to 375 ms | 31 to 295 ms | 184 ms (frame) |

- The two heavy turns are both the check's own construction:
  - extracting the 1 MiB answer: 7.5 ms idle, up to 135 ms loaded;
  - building the titled frame: about 13 ms idle, up to 184 ms loaded. Every
    ORBF frame of the 400 by 250 screen is a full frame, about 3.5 MB with
    `fill`'s six codepoints a cell.
- The test client decodes that frame: 52 ms idle and up to 328 ms loaded in
  a debug check. The Nix check is release-built, where decoding costs much
  less.
- The 1.64 s failure (load 10 to 14 in eon-buys1.1's proof) did not
  reproduce, not even in Nix's sandbox. Edge `570d0ad`'s unchanged
  `orbit-visible-text` check passed 10 of 10 at load 11.2 to 22.0, beside a
  `.#default` rebuild and a CPU-bound derivation in the nix-daemon (record
  3). The worst in the traced loops was 441 ms.
- So CPU contention at load 10 to 22 does not explain 1.64 s. That needs
  Orbit and the check both stalled for more than a second. The likeliest
  cause is the machine at that moment, not Orbit: swap was in use (7 to 9
  GB) while eon-buys1.1's build linked Venus and Eon. This is inference; it
  was not reproduced.

## A second defect: the step could prove nothing

The child's title command raced the request. When the title's PTY output
reached Orbit before the `ReadVisible` request, Orbit presented the title
before the answer existed, so the step passed without an unread answer:

- 12 of 25 iterations under `nix build` plus burners;
- 3 of 20 at load 14 to 29;
- 1 of 10 at load about 15;
- 0 of 30 under `nix build` alone.

Under load, the old step could pass against an Orbit that does block.

## Why the bound is not widened

A blocked Orbit would present nothing until the 1 s answer bound (ORB-C13,
ORB-C17) dropped the holder, so the title would arrive just after 1 s. The
1.0 s bound, counted from the request, is the threshold that tells "blocked"
from "slow". Any wider bound would pass a blocked Orbit.

## Change (test and docs only; no Orbit change)

`a_holder_that_stops_reading_loses_the_lease`:
1. After posting `ReadVisible`, it waits until the answer's first bytes are
   readable (`Manager::await_answer`, a `poll` for `POLLIN` that reads
   nothing). Orbit queues the whole answer in one turn, so the title now
   always follows a queued, unread answer.
2. The child clears the screen as it sets the title (`\e[2J`), which keeps
   `fill`'s combining marks out of the titled frame. The frame is still a
   full 2.4 MB frame of the 400 by 250 grid, so this saves Orbit's frame turn
   and the client's decode, but not the frame's size.
3. The bound stays 1.0 s from the request, which still includes the
   extraction.

In an A/B run at load 14 to 29 (24 burners plus the tail of a `nix build`),
alternating old and new 20 times each:

| Sequence | Median | Max | Orbit's median share | Orbit's max share |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| old | 78 ms | 217 ms | 58 ms | 161 ms |
| new | 44 ms | 169 ms | 28 ms | 82 ms |

`orbit/docs/BEHAVIOR.md` states the new order and lists the new sensitivity
check.

## Close

- The original 1.64 s cause was not reproduced, in Nix's sandbox or outside
  it, at loads up to 29.
- The memory-pressure idea above is untested. Every acceptance run had about
  14 GB available.
- Reopen this bead if the step fails again. Its assertion now reports how
  long the answer took to begin (`the answer began after ...`) beside the
  total, so a recurrence shows whether the time went to building the answer
  or to the turns after it.

comments.text:
# eon-zmq4b record 2: what an 8 MiB answer does on this path (input for eon-u5bvd.2)

Same session and tree as record 1. Measured with temporary code, not kept.

## The write path, from the code

- `Connection::respond` encodes the whole answer into `connection.output`
  and starts the answer bound (`NEGOTIATION_MS`, 1 s) when it is queued.
- `Management::flush` writes it without blocking on every loop turn and
  returns on `WouldBlock`.
- An 8 MiB `History` answer therefore behaves like the 1 MiB one:
  - A holder that stops reading loses its connection 1 s after queueing,
    whatever the size, and the PTY and presentation go on (record 1's
    traces).
  - Orbit holds up to about 8 MiB of encoded answer until it is written or
    dropped. The formatter's buffer is transient on top of that.

## Risks for .2

1. **A reading holder must take 8 MiB within 1 s.** The bound covers the
   whole answer, not progress, so a `History` reader needs 8 times the
   throughput of a `ReadVisible` reader: at least 8 MB/s sustained, including
   the supervisor's decode, under load. Today that reader is Eon Runtime's
   supervisor, the only lease holder, and it blocks the window while it
   reads (eon-u5bvd.1 record 2). If it falls behind, the supervisor loses its
   management lease. Record 4's falsifier "Bound sized to the budget" should
   record the reply time against this 1 s bound under load. A longer bound
   for `History` would change ORB-C13 or ORB-C17 text, which needs approval.
2. **The extraction blocks the owner loop for its duration.** It is one
   host turn by design. One full-history `Formatter` pass (`Format::Plain`,
   unwrap, trim) over a terminal filled to Orbit's 16 MiB scrollback budget,
   release, idle:

   | Fill | Rows kept | Text | Format | Sanitize |
   | --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
   | ASCII, 200 columns | 9,502 | 1.9 MB | 4.9 ms | 2.9 ms |
   | 4-byte wide emoji, 100 a row (200 cells) | 18,817 | 3.8 MB | 4.7 ms | 6.6 ms |
   | `e` plus 5 combining marks, 200 columns | 881 | 1.9 MB | 7.7 ms | 3.9 ms |

   - Under load, record 1 saw the 1 MiB visible read grow from 7.5 ms to
     135 ms (18 times). By that factor a full history read would hold the
     PTY and presentation for about 10 to 15 ms idle and up to about 250 ms
     under heavy load.
   - The window-stall falsifier (keystroke echo during a full-size read)
     measures this end to end.
3. **The 16 MiB budget gave at most 3.8 MB of text here, not 8 MiB.** Row and
   page overhead count against the budget. eon-u5bvd.1 record 1's inference
   that a full budget gives about 8 MiB of single-codepoint text is high by
   about 2 to 4 times, at least for these fills. The 8 MiB bound still holds
   as a ceiling, but the truncation paths (`omitted_lines`, `cut_bytes`) need
   unit tests: a real-PTY fill may never reach them. Recommendation: keep
   8 MiB (it is approved and harmless) and say "typical full histories are
   2 to 4 MB" in the record. Do not resize it from this alone.
4. **The unread-answer check at full size is a 2 to 4 MB answer, not
   8 MiB.** A real terminal fill tops out near 3.8 MB of text (point 3), so a
   real-PTY check cannot reach 8 MiB. .2's check becomes a full-budget
   `History` answer of 2 to 4 MB, awaited with `Manager::await_answer`. Unit
   tests of the fit function cover the 8 MiB truncation paths
   (`omitted_lines`, `cut_bytes`). The overseer updates eon-u5bvd.2.
5. **The full-size unread-answer check must order its title after the answer.**
   Use `Manager::await_answer` before the child's title command, as this
   bead's fix does. Otherwise the title can be presented before the answer
   exists, and the check passes without testing anything (record 1: 12 of 25
   runs under heavy load).
6. **Stop path.** `Management::reply_stopped` writes the rest of a partly
   written answer blocking, with at most 1 s in all, during cleanup. With
   8 MiB unread, a stop while a slow holder holds the answer spends up to
   that second in cleanup. This is bounded, as today.

comments.text:
# eon-zmq4b Opus review (diff sha256 5b08cfb0)

Verdict: **FINDINGS**. None blocks the change. Fix 1 and 2 before commit.

## Answers

1. **Verdict.** Supported for CPU contention. The traces ran inside the owner loop (fact turns, poll waits, management and client writes). In all 160 iterations the titled frame went out with 219,264 of 1,046,684 bytes unwritten. The 1.64 s failure is still unexplained. The swap explanation is a guess, and every acceptance run had about 14 GB free.
2. **The new test.** It checks the right thing. Orbit sends no unsolicited management messages, and `allow_self` leaves the socket empty, so the first POLLIN is the answer. The bound counts from `asked`, before the answer is queued, so a blocked Orbit always reaches 1.0 s or more. The red result (1.04 s) is therefore deterministic, and the bound is justified, not just widened. If the whole answer fit in the socket, the lease would stay and `leased()` would panic, so "unread" cannot pass vacuously either.
3. **management_lease.rs.** It adds `Manager::await_answer`, a POLLIN poll that reads nothing. The stream is private, so the helper belongs here.
4. **BEHAVIOR.md.** Accurate.
5. **Scrollback.** Record 02 is sound. It uses Orbit's real 16 MiB budget, and the 1 s bound does cover the whole answer. See finding 3.
6. **Code.** Matches the surrounding style. Gaps are in finding 2.

## Findings, ranked

1. **Medium: the acceptance does not tell old from new.** Edge's old check also passed 10 of 10 under the same harness. The change's value is the vacuity fix and a cheaper frame. If 1.64 s recurs, the message will not say where the time went.
   *Fix:* capture `answered = asked.elapsed()` after `await_answer` and put it in the assertion message. In the close record, write: "1.64 s cause not reproduced; memory-pressure hypothesis untested; reopen on recurrence with the split timing".

2. **Low: `await_answer` robustness.** `poll` returns 1 on POLLHUP or POLLERR alone, and is not retried on EINTR. On timeout it prints a stale errno. It ignores bytes already in `self.unread`.
   *Fix:* assert `ready.revents & libc::POLLIN != 0`. Report a timeout as "no answer within 3 s". Add `assert!(self.unread.is_empty())`.

3. **Low, for eon-u5bvd.2:** the full budget gave at most 3.8 MB of text, so ".2's unread-answer check at 8 MiB" probably cannot be reached with a real-PTY fill.
   *Fix:* reword it as a full-budget history answer (2–4 MB) with `await_answer`. Cover the 8 MiB truncation paths with unit tests, as record 02 says.

4. **Process.** Under rule 2, records 01–04 and this review land in the bead within the commit. Ledger 04 still says "Opus review: pending".
   *Fix:* update 04, then replay the records via `br` at landing.

Not a regression: the step proves PTY output and presentation, not PTY input, while the answer is unread. That was already true before.

title: Zoom the selected pane across a tab's columns
description:
## Decision
Lucca, 2026-10-17: keep the shipped columns of accordions (`eon-splits-opwv`) as Eon's split model
and add zoom. Rows (one accordion whose open pane splits into up to four side-by-side terminals) was
considered and not chosen: it gives new panes full width, but hides everything outside the open pane
while switching, and costs another EON-C8/VEN-C8 change, an EONW revision and a conversion of saved
column workspaces. Layout presets (tmux `select-layout`, kitty `enabled_layouts`, Zellij swap
layouts, Nova's stacked/split families) were rejected for now: they add a second owner of the
arrangement beside the workspace structure (Nova needed eight named swap layouts plus
`zellij-pane-orchestrator`; Zellij leaves overflow placement unspecified). Revisit rows or presets
only with dogfood evidence that narrow column panes still hurt with zoom.

## Contract (provisional; approve before code)
- Consumer: a full-Eon user in a tab with one or more columns.
- Trigger: one zoom toggle shortcut (proposed Alt+Shift+Z: tmux's `z`; Alt+F would take the
  shell's forward-word) and its `eon` command if the design adds one.
- Result: the selected pane's terminal fills the tab's whole content area; other columns are hidden
  but their terminals keep running. Toggling again restores the same columns, widths and selection.
  The zoomed state is visible (header or Eon Bar indicator) and announced to accessibility, which
  lists only the zoomed column's panes while zoomed. The frame follows the flush workspace sheet of
  `eon-flush-workspace-sheet-5779` with no seam.
- Important failures: a hidden column's terminal stops or loses state; unzoom restores a different
  arrangement; keyboard input reaches a hidden terminal; a zoomed grid keeps the column-sized grid.

## Open design decisions (recommendation first)
- Persistence: transient Venus view state, not persisted across detach/attach (recommended: no
  EONW change), or Eon Runtime state in a new EONW revision.
- Actions while zoomed: Alt+H/L, Alt+K/J, Alt+M, Alt+Shift+M, Ctrl+Alt+K/J, close, and the
  sideways pane move (Ctrl+Alt+H/L) and tab move (Ctrl+Alt+Shift+H/L) of
  `eon-sideways-pane-moves-k9ca`. Recommended: any action that changes the selected column, moves a
  pane across columns or creates a column leaves zoom first; Alt+K/J and Ctrl+Alt+K/J within the
  zoomed column stay zoomed. Ghostty's default unzooms on any focus or layout change
  (`split-preserve-zoom`).
- Hidden columns' attachments: keep each attached at its column size (recommended: no Orbit resize
  churn on toggle) or detach while hidden.
- One-column tabs: zoom is a no-op with a notice, or still hides pane headers (recommended: no-op).
- Popups and pickers over a zoomed tab keep their current geometry.

## Owners
Eon owns the shortcut default and EON-C8's product text. Venus owns geometry, rendering, input,
focus and accessibility for the zoomed view (VEN-C8, VEN-C20 shortcut viewer, VEN-C24 hints). Eon
Runtime and EONW are unchanged: the 2026-10-22 approved design leaves the zoom chord unreserved,
so a user popup on it takes it as with other fixed bindings (EON-C20). Orbit is unchanged (one
resize per zoomed terminal through the existing path).

## Reference gate
Consequential: changes EON-C8 and VEN-C8, and possibly EONW. Before code, read the affected
`AGENTS.md`, both contracts and `docs/REFERENCES.md` routes, and inspect at exact revisions at least
Ghostty `toggle_split_zoom` (`~/pjs/yazelix-related/ghostty` 45db2c255) and WezTerm
`TogglePaneZoomState` (`~/pjs/yazelix-related/wezterm` 577474d); Zellij fullscreen
(`~/pjs/yazelix-related/zellij` 16beceaa0) is optional. Record constraints kept, rejected approaches,
the chosen design and its cheapest falsifying check here. Stop for Lucca's design and contract
approval before code. Portability: neutral.

## Prerequisites
After `eon-flush-workspace-sheet-5779`, so the zoomed frame is designed once on the decided sheet
and the two do not edit `venus/src/render/chrome.rs` in parallel (`eon-7rk3` closed 2026-10-17).

## Acceptance
- Design phase: Lucca approves the design, the EON-C8/VEN-C8 changes and the shortcut.
- Implementation: installed Eon zooms and unzooms the selected pane in a multi-column tab; hidden
  terminals keep running and reappear unchanged; input reaches only the zoomed terminal; shortcut
  viewer, hints, `docs/USAGE.md` and CHANGELOG list the binding; a user popup on the zoom chord takes
  it and Alt+/ lists zoom as overridden. Prove with the owners' existing harnesses plus one isolated
  installed dogfood observation; Venus fmt and clippy green; refresh the active Nix profile without
  interrupting live workspaces.

## Scope boundary
No rows, layout presets, column resizing, arbitrary split trees or Orbit protocol change. Adds no
platform promise.
close_reason: Alt+Shift+Z zooms the selected column across the tab as Venus view state; hidden columns keep running and attached; EON-C8/VEN-C8 updated. Venus suite, fmt and clippy green; isolated installed dogfood; profile refreshed. Proof and ledger in comments.

comments.author: lucca
comments.text:
Design approved by Lucca, 2026-10-22 (eon-43 session).

Reference gate. Read root, venus/ and runtime/ AGENTS.md, EON-C8, VEN-C8, EON-C20 (reserved popup keys), docs/REFERENCES.md "Terminal workspace experience", venus/docs/REFERENCES.md "Rounded pane frames" and "Required for shared popup presentation".
- Ghostty 45db2c255 (local checkout ~/pjs/refs/ghostty-7501/repo): the per-tab split tree holds `zoomed: ?Node.Handle` (src/datastruct/split_tree.zig:59-62). A single leaf refuses zoom (apprt/gtk/class/application.zig:2689-2691). A new split resets zoom (split_tree.zig:566-567). goto_split unzooms unless `split-preserve-zoom = navigation` (Config.zig:1089-1103, 8681-8683). Only the zoomed subtree is laid out, so hidden surfaces get no size updates. The tab title gets a 🔍 prefix (gtk/class/tab.zig:529-532). No zoom-specific accessibility.
- WezTerm e2a98e1 (the only local clone, shallow; 577474d unavailable): per-tab `zoomed` plus `size_before_zoom` (mux/src/tab.rs:40-49). `resize` resizes only the zoomed pane, and unzoom re-runs layout at the current size (891-912, 1139-1147). `unzoom_on_switch_pane` defaults true, and with it off the switch is silently dropped (1439-1453, config.rs:835). Splitting while zoomed is refused or unzooms (1925-1927, 1966-1968; issue #723). `[Z]` title prefix. A single pane can be zoomed, so an indicator shows with no effect.
- Zellij 16beceaa0 (~/pjs/nova/nova-zellij): per-tab `fullscreen_is_active` (tiled_panes/mod.rs:71). Hidden panes keep their geometry and are not rendered. Navigation moves the fullscreen along (2591-2596). A new split, close or relayout exits. A single pane is a no-op. "(FULLSCREEN)" on the tab bar.
Constraints kept: one zoom reference per tab, not per pane; hidden terminals are not resized while zoomed; structural change ends zoom; refuse a one-column zoom; an indicator at tab level. Rejected: move-the-zoom navigation (Zellij, Ghostty `navigation`), because it needs more rules; WezTerm's silently dropped switch; persisting zoom (WezTerm's wire field, Ghostty's macOS restore path), because it needs an EONW revision for view state; reserving the chord from popups (would change EON-C20's reserved set; every other fixed binding is popup-overridable and listed as overridden in Alt+/).

Approved design (EON-C8 and VEN-C8 gain a zoom bullet; VEN-C20 and VEN-C24 list the binding):
- Alt+Shift+Z toggles zoom of the active tab's selected column. Not reserved: a user popup on that key takes it and Alt+/ lists zoom as overridden (existing EON-C20 rule). No Runtime, EONW, Orbit or `eon` command change. CHANGELOG records the binding (not as a breaking change).
- Zoomed: the selected column's card covers the tab's whole card area (the area a popup card covers) and shows that column's headers and terminal at full width. It is one gapped rounded card (`ab697a2` replaced the flush sheet this bead assumed). Other columns stay attached at their last column size and keep running. They are not drawn, hit-tested, resized or listed to accessibility while zoomed. Unzoom restores the same columns, widths and selection at the current window size.
- Zoom is transient Venus view state: not persisted, and not restored by a new window or attach.
- Zoom lasts while the active tab, its column count and its selected column index stay the same. Any change ends it: Alt+H/L (unzoom, then move), tab focus, column creation, sideways moves, or closing the zoomed column's last pane. Alt+K/J, Ctrl+Alt+K/J, Alt+M, and closing a pane that leaves the column non-empty stay zoomed.
- A one-column tab consumes the shortcut without zooming and shows a rejected-action notice. While a popup or picker covers the tab, the toggle is consumed without effect. A popup over a zoomed tab keeps its usual geometry, and the zoomed view returns when it hides.
- Indicator: the active tab pill shows a zoom marker while zoomed, and its accessible name says zoomed. The tab panel is named "Zoomed column N of M" and lists only that column's panes.
- Cheapest falsifiers: Scene tests (the zoomed geometry spans the card area; hidden columns are absent from draw, hit and accessibility), a model/application test of the end-of-zoom rule, and one isolated installed dogfood observation.
Portability: neutral.

title: Make the Nix-free Linux bundle namespace-free
description:
## Why

The Nix-free Linux bundle is a No-Go as built. Evidence is on eon-qualify-nix-free-linux-public-beta-lm9p (comment of 2026-10-18; candidate ef238be, archive sha256 5f08ec4d...):
- Stock Ubuntu 26.04.1 LTS (kernel.apparmor_restrict_unprivileged_userns=1) cannot start it. `eon --help` and `eon versions` exit 1 with "bwrap: setting up uid map: Permission denied", denied by AppArmor's unprivileged_userns profile. Only a root-installed per-path AppArmor profile makes it run.
- On every host, the user namespace and bwrap's PR_SET_NO_NEW_PRIVS reach every Orbit terminal: sudo, su, pkexec and setuid helpers fail, root-owned files show as nobody:nogroup, and supplementary groups collapse to nogroup. orb-prove-no-survivor-session-shutdown-btg already rejected unmapped root as "not an acceptable Orbit terminal contract".

User decision (Lucca, 2026-10-18): open this redesign. Lucca accepted the recommended direction, namespace-free relocation, as the starting hypothesis; the mechanism itself is still decided by the first child.

## Outcome

A user-owned extracted Eon bundle starts on stock Ubuntu 26.04 LTS without root, AppArmor changes, or user namespaces. Every Orbit terminal it spawns behaves like a native host terminal (no NoNewPrivs, real uid/gid/groups, sudo works where the host allows it). Nix and direct delivery keep consuming the one canonical component graph (EON-C2, EON-C6), and EON-C5's install/upgrade/rollback/remove lifecycle and eon-install stay intact.

## Acceptance

- On a fresh stock Ubuntu 26.04 LTS VM with no Nix, verify plus extract plus `eon versions`, `eon --help`, and the eon-install dry run and install all succeed with no root step.
- Inside an Eon terminal from the bundle, /proc/self/status shows NoNewPrivs 0, `id` matches the host, `stat -c %U /usr/bin/sudo` shows root, and `sudo -n true` behaves as on the host.
- The candidate is ready for lm9p's qualification matrix (Ubuntu 26.04 and 24.04, Fedora Workstation).

## Children

Mechanism decided on eon-zti4.1 (closed 2026-10-18): host-glibc relink, GLIBC_2.42 floor first, host Vulkan driver, approved EON-C6 host-input statement, new installer layout only. In order:
1. eon-zti4.2 Make Eon shell integration location-neutral (after eon-8olu).
2. eon-zti4.3 Relink the eon closure for the host glibc as a Nix check.
3. eon-zti4.4 Replace bundle makeWrapper scripts with a static launcher env table.
4. eon-zti4.5 Relocate compiled-in data roots for the relinked bundle.
5. eon-zti4.6 Switch manual-bundle and eon-install to the relinked layout.
6. eon-zti4.7 Update bundle docs and the EON-C6 host-input statement.
7. eon-zti4.8 Lower the bundle glibc floor to 2.39 for Ubuntu 24.04 (after eon-8olu).
8. eon-zti4.9 Prove the namespace-free bundle on Ubuntu 26.04 and 24.04 (last; hands the candidate to lm9p).

## Scope boundary

No release, tag, signing anchor, publication, new distribution channel (deb, rpm, Flatpak, Snap, AppImage), or support expansion. No change to Orbit's terminal contracts except removing the namespace from the bundle's launch path. macOS is out of scope.
close_reason: All children closed; acceptance met by eon-zti4.9 (stock Ubuntu 26.04.1 and 24.04.5 VMs, no root step, no namespace). Candidate b396b4a2... handed to lm9p. Closed by Lucca's decision, 2026-10-19.

title: Decide the namespace-free relocation mechanism for the Linux bundle
description:
## Why

The bundle must leave user namespaces, but a Nix closure is full of absolute /nix/store references, so the mechanism that replaces bwrap's /nix projection is a consequential code shape (AGENTS.md reference gate: dependency, lifecycle and trust boundary). That choice needs evidence before any implementation slice. Parent epic and No-Go evidence: see the parent and eon-qualify-nix-free-linux-public-beta-lm9p.

## Evidence

- bundle/src/main.rs:8-16: entrypoint execs libexec/bwrap --unshare-user with the host root bound and the bundle's nix/ ro-bound at /nix, then runs EON_BUNDLE_PROGRAM.
- nix/linux-bundle.nix:3,9,11,31-41: static pkgsStatic.bubblewrap helper; the closure of eonPackage copied whole via closureInfo.
- flake.nix:616-620: manual-bundle consumes eonPackage plus components/eon-alpha-v3.json and flake.lock.
- docs/MANUAL-BUNDLE.md "Execution and host boundary": the current bwrap /nix projection and its "no ELF/config path rewriting" decision, which this bead may supersede.
- Prior candidate: 488 MB archive, about 1.8 GB unpacked closure.

## Scope

In scope:
- An inventory of /nix/store references in the candidate closure, split by kind: ELF PT_INTERP, RUNPATH, dlopen targets (Vulkan ICD and loader, Wayland, xkbcommon, fontconfig), script shebangs, wrapper scripts, and text or config references (Nushell, Helix runtime, Yazi, LazyGit, Anima, terminfo, fonts, CA certificates). Name which components run inside Orbit terminals and which only in Venus.
- A comparison, with sources and inspected revisions, of: (a) a static launcher invoking the bundled ld.so with --library-path (Exodus pattern; fzakaria 2026-06-21 "Nix needs relocatable binaries"); (b) static or musl builds for eon, Orbit, eon-install and the managed CLI tools; (c) install-time prefix rewriting with padded placeholders (the conda pattern, which needs a long storeDir and a world rebuild); (d) a hybrid where only Venus is relocated and terminals run fully static tools; (e) rejected references: bwrap or userns (this No-Go), PRoot (nix-portable fallback; ptrace overhead, and it would also wrap terminals), and Guix -RR packs (userns by default).
- A throwaway prototype of the chosen mechanism on the riskiest piece (Venus rendering through the host or bundled Vulkan on Wayland), plus one terminal tool, run from an extracted directory with no /nix.

Out of scope:
- Changing the shipped bundle, docs/MANUAL-BUNDLE.md, docs/CONTRACTS.md or installer code. Those belong to later children after acceptance.
- Distribution channels, signing, publication.

## Acceptance

- The bead records the inventory counts by kind, the chosen mechanism, rejected alternatives with reasons, its dependency and version policy and exit condition, the effect on EON-C2/C5/C6 and on the MANUAL-BUNDLE decision, and the GPU stance (host driver or bundled lavapipe).
- The prototype shows red/green evidence: on a stock Ubuntu 26.04 VM (cloud image, no Nix), the prototype Venus window or headless render plus the terminal tool run without userns, and NoNewPrivs is 0 in the spawned shell.
- It proposes ordered implementation children for the epic, each sized for one session. They are not filed until Lucca accepts.

## Implementation Notes

1. Build `nix build .#manual-bundle --out-link <scratch>/mb` and inventory references with `readelf -l/-d`, `file`, and `grep -rl /nix/store` over the extracted nix/ tree.
2. Read the reference sources and record the inspected revisions.
3. Prototype in scratch space only. VM recipe: lm9p's 2026-10-18 comment (official cloud image, cloud-init NoCloud seed via cloud-localds, qcow2 overlay, QEMU -display none, SSH on a forwarded port, QMP socket under a path shorter than 108 bytes).

## Verification

- The VM run outputs (`eon`-equivalent prototype exit 0, `grep NoNewPrivs /proc/self/status` showing 0 inside its child shell) are recorded in the bead with the image sha256, kernel and prototype source revision.

## Stop Conditions

- Stop and ask Lucca if every viable mechanism needs root, a new distribution channel, or a contract change beyond EON-C5's bundle mechanism.
- Stop if the inventory shows a component that cannot be made relocatable without forking it.

## Maintenance Notes

- Desktop focus: run GUI checks headless (VM or isolated compositor), never on Lucca's desktop.
- Run tests only through `nix develop -c eon-test`.
close_reason: Mechanism decided and accepted by Lucca (host-glibc relink, GLIBC_2.42 floor first, host Vulkan driver, EON-C6 host-input statement approved, new installer layout only). Inventory, references, red/green prototype on stock Ubuntu 26.04 and the ordered children are recorded in comments; children await a separate go-ahead to file.

Inside Orbit terminals: bash-interactive, zsh, fish (pulls python3 134 MB, coreutils, man-db, groff, gettext, util-linux), nushell, starship, zoxide, fzf, atuin, carapace, helix (+ runtime and grammars), yazi/ya, lazygit, anima, the directory picker, Orbit terminfo. Supervisor side: eon, Orbit, CodexBarCLI (262 MB Swift runtime), and bash as the makeWrapper interpreter.
- glibc symbol floor of what actually runs: eon, Orbit, Venus, nu, starship, zoxide, atuin, anima <= GLIBC_2.39; carapace 2.34; fzf static; Venus's wayland/vulkan/xkbcommon <= 2.38. ncurses 6.6 (so bash-interactive, zsh, readline) and coreutils 9.11 (from fish) need GLIBC_2.42 through the new cfgetospeed/cfsetospeed/cfgetispeed/cfsetispeed versions. No closure object uses GLIBC_PRIVATE. Bundled libgcc_s (gcc 15.2) and Ubuntu 26.04's (gcc 16) both top out at GCC_14.0.0.

MECHANISMS COMPARED (sources and revisions below):
(f) CHOSEN: host-glibc relink. At bundle build time every ELF gets PT_INTERP = /lib64/ld-linux-x86-64.so.2 (the x86-64 psABI loader path every glibc distribution ships) and every store RUNPATH entry becomes $ORIGIN-relative inside the bundle's own nix/store tree; glibc entries are dropped and glibc leaves the payload; absolute store symlinks become relative. No namespace, no ptrace, no install-time rewrite, no launcher in front of each ELF; /proc/self/exe stays the real program; host NSS, locales and GPU drivers work natively. Cost: a declared host glibc floor equal to the newest symbol version the shipped executables need, enforced at build time.
(a) Exodus-style bundled ld.so --library-path: works on any host glibc, but /proc/self/exe becomes ld.so (breaks self-re-exec and exe-relative data lookup, e.g. fish, nu and helix fallbacks), needs a launcher per ELF, and keeps Nix glibc, so host GPU drivers cannot be loaded and Venus is stuck on bundled lavapipe. Rejected as the primary path.
(b) static/musl builds of eon, Orbit, eon-install and the managed tools: removes the loader question for those, but Venus cannot be static (it must dlopen host Vulkan and Wayland), many managed tools need per-package static work, and a second build of the components is a separate artifact set that would need to be reconciled with EON-C6. Kept only as a fallback lever for lowering the glibc floor (bash and zsh).
(c) conda-style padded-prefix install-time rewriting: needs a long storeDir world rebuild with no binary cache plus install-time binary patching, and eon-install and manual extraction would both have to own a rewrite step. Rejected.
(d) Venus relocated, terminals static: subsumed by (f), which needs no static rebuild for terminals.
(e) bwrap or userns (this epic's No-Go), PRoot (nix-portable fallback: ptrace overhead, and it would wrap every terminal child), Guix -RR packs (user namespaces by default, PRoot fallback): rejected for the same reasons as the No-Go.

GPU STANCE: host driver. In the prototype, the bundled vulkan-loader under the host glibc enumerated and loaded the host Mesa ICDs (/usr/lib/x86_64-linux-gnu/libvulkan_lvp.so and libvulkan_nouveau.so) and rendered. Recommendation: drop bundled Mesa and LLVM (806 MB unpacked) and declare a host Vulkan driver as a prerequisite (Ubuntu Desktop and Fedora Workstation ship Mesa Vulkan, including lavapipe). Take libwayland-client from the host (the AppImage excludelist does the same because of a Mesa conflict). The bundled vulkan-loader may stay, since it loaded host ICDs here. libxkbcommon comes either from the host or from the bundle with its data roots set: the bundled copy logged "No Compose file for locale C.UTF-8" because its Compose root is compiled in. Child 4 decides with evidence. Venus's RUNPATH should carry no bundled gcc runtime, so host drivers never inherit an older libgcc_s/libstdc++.

PROTOTYPE (throwaway relink.py in session scratch: copy the closure minus glibc, Mesa and LLVM; patchelf 0.15.2 sets the interpreter on 246 ELFs and rewrites RUNPATH on 899, dropping 897 glibc entries; 314 symlinks made relative; 73 scripts and 51 Eon-owned text files rewritten to ${EON_BUNDLE_ROOT}; fonts.conf <dir> -> prefix="relative", which fontconfig-parser 0.5.8 supports; a /bin/sh top-level eon). Archive eon-proto.tar.zst sha256 726c0dcd847e3778d2c956620a140e8d050c0c4f6925145eae3bdcc27e46e8de, 1.2 GB unpacked versus 2.1 GB.
VM: official ubuntu-26.04-server-cloudimg-amd64.img sha256 8800651811af9a85465ad1d552add729947bb16488dddb4a9b5305a3d97332b2 (same image as lm9p), Ubuntu 26.04.1 LTS, kernel 7.0.0-34-generic, glibc 2.43-2ubuntu2.4, kernel.apparmor_restrict_unprivileged_userns=1, no /nix, QEMU 11.1.1/KVM with a cloud-init NoCloud seed. Stand-in desktop packages: sway 1.11 headless (pixman), grim, wtype, mesa-vulkan-drivers 26.0.8, libvulkan1 1.4.341. User eon in groups adm, sudo, video with NOPASSWD sudo.
- RED, same VM: the ef238be bwrap bundle `eon versions` -> "bwrap: setting up uid map: Permission denied", exit 1.
- GREEN: `eon versions` exit 0 and `eon --help` exit 0. `eon run -- eon-bash -c ...` opened the Venus window (sway app_id eon, title Venus); Venus NoNewPrivs 0 on host libc with the host lvp ICD. After the picker was confirmed by Enter from a held wtype virtual keyboard, the bundled bash ran in pane p1 while Venus was alive and recorded: NoNewPrivs 0; Uid/Gid 1000; Groups 4 27 44 1000; id matches the host; user ns user:[4026531837], the same as the SSH login; /usr/bin/sudo root root; /etc/shadow root shadow; `sudo -n true` exit 0; exe = bundled bash-interactive; libc = /usr/lib/x86_64-linux-gnu/libc.so.6; bundled nu 0.113.1, helix 25.07.1 and lazygit 0.62.2 ran from $EON_SESSION_BIN. The grim screenshot shows the bash pane under Venus chrome.
- Prototype failures (design inputs, not blockers): (1) Eon does not forward arbitrary environment to terminals, so eon.bashrc's rewritten ${EON_BUNDLE_ROOT} paths expanded empty and Starship/Zoxide/Atuin/Carapace init warned "cannot initialize" (EON-C9's warn-and-continue path). Eon-owned shell init must name managed artifacts through variables Eon itself supplies. (2) An env-bash shebang resolved `bash` through the terminal's private PATH to Eon's own bash wrapper and recursed; host-shell shebangs are unsafe, so the bundle needs a static launcher, not rewritten scripts. (3) fonts.conf absolute dirs -> "terminal font family is unavailable: Symbols Nerd Font Mono" until made relative. (4) The xkbcommon Compose root (above).

CONTRACT EFFECT: EON-C2 unchanged (same manifest and lock bytes, same `eon versions`). EON-C3 unchanged and better served: the bundle launcher supplies bundle-relative opaque component paths; runtime code still never constructs store paths. EON-C5: lifecycle and eon-install unchanged; only the bundle mechanism changes, and payloads stay relocatable while stopped. EON-C6: needs one explicit statement in its proof text that the direct bundle takes libc, NSS, locales and the Vulkan driver as declared host inputs (the bwrap bundle already treated resolver, user, timezone and desktop services as host inputs); component identities are unchanged. MANUAL-BUNDLE "Execution and host boundary" is superseded: no bwrap, no /nix projection, build-time ELF relink plus launcher env table instead of "no ELF/config path rewriting"; host prerequisites become glibc >= floor, a Vulkan driver, and native Wayland. No contract change beyond EON-C5's mechanism and the EON-C6 host-input statement, so no stop condition is triggered; both texts change only after Lucca accepts.

DEPENDENCY AND VERSION POLICY: patchelf (build-time only, from the flake-locked nixpkgs; no runtime dependency) and the existing static Rust bundle entrypoint, which becomes the env-table launcher. The relinker itself is Rust repository tooling, not Python. The glibc floor is declared in the bundle builder and enforced by a build gate that fails if any shipped ELF needs a newer GLIBC_x or any GLIBC_PRIVATE; a nixpkgs glibc bump that raises it fails the build rather than shipping silently. bubblewrap and its vendored source leave the payload. Exit condition: drop the relinker if nixpkgs gains relocatable outputs (the fzakaria proposal) or if Eon's terminal set becomes fully static, and revisit if any supported target ships a glibc below the floor.

OPEN DECISION FOR LUCCA (glibc floor): with today's closure the floor is GLIBC_2.42 (Ubuntu 26.04 LTS 2.43, Fedora 43/44, Debian 14+; not Ubuntu 24.04's 2.39 or Debian 13's 2.41). Recommendation: ship floor 2.42 for the first namespace-free candidate and move Ubuntu 24.04 to a follow-up that lowers the floor to 2.39 (static musl bash and zsh, and fish's coreutils/man-db chain). eon, Orbit, Venus, nu, hx, yazi, lazygit and the other tools already meet 2.39.

PROPOSED CHILDREN (not filed; each one session):
1. Location-neutral Eon shell integration: Eon-owned init (bash, zsh, fish, nu autoload, shell-init, directory picker config) resolves managed artifacts through an Eon-supplied input such as EON_SESSION_BIN, not absolute store paths, in both channels. EON-C9 behavior unchanged; Nix dogfood plus the existing EON-C9 tests.
2. Relinking bundle builder: nix/linux-bundle.nix replaces bwrap with a Rust relink step (interpreter, $ORIGIN RUNPATH, relative symlinks, glibc/Mesa/LLVM excluded), the glibc-floor gate and the static-bootstrap check, and drops bubblewrap from payload, licenses and provenance.
3. Static launcher env table: the bundle entrypoint becomes a multi-call launcher that applies the makeWrapper env (EON_*, TERMINFO_DIRS, FONTCONFIG_FILE and so on) relative to its own directory and execs the real binary; the table is generated from the same Nix wrapper definitions so one owner holds the env list; no host-shell shebangs.
4. Third-party data roots: helix runtime, zsh fpath and modules, fish data and helpers, ncurses terminfo, CA certificates (host /etc/ssl), relative fonts.conf, and Venus on host libwayland/libxkbcommon/libvulkan with no bundled gcc runtime; check each inside an Orbit terminal.
5. Docs and contract text after acceptance: MANUAL-BUNDLE execution boundary and host prerequisites, the EON-C5 mechanism wording and the EON-C6 host-input statement (user approval of the contract text first), then the Ubuntu 26.04 VM proof of verify, extract, `eon versions`, eon-install install/upgrade/rollback/remove and the terminal NoNewPrivs/id/sudo checks; hands the candidate to lm9p.
6. (If Lucca wants Ubuntu 24.04 in the matrix) lower the glibc floor to 2.39.

REFERENCES READ (2026-10-18; inspected revisions):
- Exodus github.com/intoli/exodus @ ef3d5e92c1b6: one launcher per executable that runs `exec "${linker}" --library-path ... --inhibit-rpath "" "${executable}"` (templates/launcher.sh:9); copies ld.so beside each binary so /proc/self/exe yields the right directory (bundling.py:800-802), i.e. /proc/self/exe is the linker; Known Limitations (README:469-492): isolated from host driver libraries, shebangs not rewritten. Kept: the per-ELF relocation idea. Rejected: bundled-loader invocation (host GPU and self-exec).
- fzakaria "Nix needs relocatable binaries", 2026-06-21: $ORIGIN/../../<hash>-pkg RUNPATHs; the kernel cannot expand $ORIGIN in PT_INTERP or shebangs; options are a kernel change, a static self-locating wrapper, or language-level relative paths. Kept: $ORIGIN RUNPATH and the static wrapper for env/shebang cases; PT_INTERP is solved by the host psABI loader instead. Unshipped proposal.
- conda-build @ 6ab6f8e74ed1 / conda @ 4604464d9c3c: 255-char padded placeholder prefix (config.py:107), NUL-padded binary rewrite with _PaddingError (portability.py:253-305), install-time and fixed thereafter. Rejected.
- nix-portable @ 91122e3d94ba: runtimes nix, bwrap (host or bundled), proot (host or bundled); falls back to proot without userns, with "significant performance overhead" (README 159-166, 194-195). Rejected.
- Guix manual "Invoking guix pack" (1.5.0 dev): -R needs userns; -RR falls back to PRoot (ptrace overhead per syscall) or Fakechroot ("erratic behavior"). Rejected.
- AppImage docs @ b29179c8f913 and pkg2appimage excludelist @ 19e30b276ffe: build on the oldest supported base (best-practices.rst:23,82-84); ld-linux, libc, libGL/EGL/GLX, libdrm, libgbm and libwayland-client come from the host (excludelist :9,:14,:38-46,:90); libvulkan and libxkbcommon are bundled. This is the closest shipped comparable to (f): host glibc and graphics, everything else bundled, with a glibc floor.
- patchelf @ 382d8bc12db9: --set-rpath '$ORIGIN/...' documented (patchelf.1:171-176); --set-interpreter takes a literal path. psABI x86-64 @ e1ce098331da dl.tex:404-421: Linux interpreter /lib64/ld-linux-x86-64.so.2.
- glibc-2.42 d2097651cc57: NEWS:25-27 termios arbitrary baud rates, speed_t redefined; x86_64 libc.abilist:2752-2760 adds GLIBC_2.42 cf{get,set}{i,o}speed and cfsetspeed.
- Vulkan-Loader @ 3aba6aeb8786 docs/LoaderDriverInterface.md:736-742 (relative library_path resolves against the manifest), :381-452 (Linux search through XDG dirs, /etc and /usr/share vulkan/icd.d).
- Distro glibc: Ubuntu 24.04 2.39-0ubuntu8.9, Ubuntu 26.04 2.43-2ubuntu2.4, Debian 13 2.41-12+deb13u4, Fedora 43 2.42-17.fc43, Fedora 44 2.43-2.fc44.

Corrections after fresh-eyes review pass 1 (supersede the matching parts of the record above):
1. EON-C5 effect was wrong. eon-install requires libexec/bwrap when it installs a payload (installer/src/main.rs:388) and when it validates a selected version (installer/src/main.rs:200), and its fixture creates the file (installer/src/tests.rs:77). It validates the new layout and keeps retained bwrap-era payloads selectable for rollback, so live work under either layout is preserved. EON-C5's text names no mechanism, so the earlier "EON-C5 mechanism wording" edit is withdrawn. The contract text is unchanged and the installer's validation code changes.
2. The glibc floor against the epic: eon-zti4 Acceptance names Ubuntu 24.04 in lm9p's matrix. Lucca's "2.42 now, 24.04 later" is applied inside the epic without amending it. The first candidate targets Ubuntu 26.04 and Fedora 43/44, and the floor-2.39 child is mandatory before eon-zti4 closes.
3. Inventory addendum: zoxide 0.9.9 has a compiled-in store path to fzf (a nixpkgs patch), so `zi` breaks without /nix, and child 4 covers it. A looser scan counts 116 ELFs with extra store strings against the 104 above. The other additions are inert: lazygit's mailcap, libpsl's publicsuffix list and the wayland-cursor icons.
4. Inventory precision: only 6 of the 20 libexec/eon/bin entries are absolute store links. The rest are relative links to bin/eon-*, which point to the single bin/eon makeWrapper script that dispatches on argv0, so the launcher must keep the `exec -a "$0"` dispatch and replace that in-closure wrapper too. The GLIBC_2.42 users also include python3's termios module (fish) and util-linux agetty, sulogin and ldattach (man-db chain). The floor gate either scopes to reachable executables or the floor-2.39 child covers these as well. CodexBarCLI is a statically linked binary with debug info; only its wrapper's SSL_CERT_FILE store default matters.

Bundled-loader evidence: VM run 4's Venus maps list /home/eon/t/eon-proto/nix/store/d6vnmfmcz5b299180issiaad4m96wh8k-vulkan-loader-1.4.341.0/lib/libvulkan.so.1.4.341 next to host /usr/lib/x86_64-linux-gnu/libvulkan_lvp.so and libvulkan_nouveau.so, so the bundled loader, not the host's libvulkan1, loaded the host ICDs.

Prototype source revision: relink.py sha256 8208ab32140c8022b36a50301a3510a17cca6a756f5812c48b3705fd3f35167f and run-proof.sh sha256 fceb78c11cef649948e3c351e7646840407d29644e642870ae170b0ff48dc885; both are kept in the next comment as the runnable reproducer. A fresh relink.py run reproduces the proven tree except 5 inert files: fzf-tmux, fzf share/update.sh and helix's hx.bash completion. Their upstream `#!/usr/bin/env bash` shebangs were also changed to /bin/bash by the manual shebang fix before archive 726c0dcd....

Revised proposed children (still unfiled; each one session):

2. Static launcher env table (the multi-call entrypoint keeps argv0 dispatch and replaces the makeWrapper scripts in the bundle). It lands before or with child 3, because the bundle is not runnable with only one of them.

6. Docs and contract text: MANUAL-BUNDLE's execution boundary, receipts (absolute symlinks), licence and userns copy, and the EON-C6 host-input statement after Lucca approves the text.

Runnable reproducer for the prototype (disposable investigation tooling, not checked-in policy). Usage: nix path-info -r <eon package> listed into closure.txt; python3 -I relink.py closure.txt <out>/eon-proto <patchelf>; tar the tree; in the VM, run-proof.sh with eon-proto.tar.zst and the ef238be archive in $HOME.

=== relink.py (sha256 8208ab32...)
#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Disposable prototype: relocate a Nix closure to run on the host glibc, no namespace.

ELF: PT_INTERP -> /lib64/ld-linux-x86-64.so.2 (psABI path), store RUNPATH entries ->
$ORIGIN-relative, glibc entries dropped. Absolute store symlinks -> relative.
Shell wrappers and eon-owned shell text: /nix/store -> ${EON_BUNDLE_ROOT}/nix/store
(prototype only; the proposed design replaces this with a launcher env table).
"""
import os, re, shutil, stat, subprocess, sys

closure_file, out, patchelf = sys.argv[1], sys.argv[2], sys.argv[3]
EXCLUDE = re.compile(r"-(glibc-2\.42-61|mesa-26\.1\.2|llvm-21\.1\.8-lib)$")
GLIBC = re.compile(r"^/nix/store/[0-9a-z]{32}-glibc-2\.42-61(/|$)")
INTERP = "/lib64/ld-linux-x86-64.so.2"
store_out = os.path.join(out, "nix/store")
os.makedirs(store_out, exist_ok=True)
paths = [l.strip() for l in open(closure_file) if l.strip()]
kept = [p for p in paths if not EXCLUDE.search(p)]
for p in kept:
    dst = os.path.join(out, p.lstrip("/"))
    if not os.path.lexists(dst):
        subprocess.run(["cp", "-a", "--reflink=auto", p, dst], check=True)
subprocess.run(["chmod", "-R", "u+w", store_out], check=True)

def inbundle(abs_store_path):
    return os.path.join(out, abs_store_path.lstrip("/"))

stats = dict(interp=0, runpath=0, symlink=0, script=0, text=0, dropped_glibc_rp=0)
for p in kept:
    root = inbundle(p)
    for dirpath, dirnames, filenames in os.walk(root):
        for name in dirnames + filenames:
            f = os.path.join(dirpath, name)
            if os.path.islink(f):
                t = os.readlink(f)
                if t.startswith("/nix/store/"):
                    os.unlink(f)
                    os.symlink(os.path.relpath(inbundle(t), dirpath), f)
                    stats["symlink"] += 1
                continue
            if not os.path.isfile(f):
                continue
            with open(f, "rb") as fh:
                head = fh.read(4)
            if head == b"\x7fELF":
                ro = subprocess.run(["readelf", "-ldW", f], capture_output=True, text=True).stdout
                args = []
                if "Requesting program interpreter" in ro:
                    args += ["--set-interpreter", INTERP]
                    stats["interp"] += 1
                m = re.search(r"\((?:RUNPATH|RPATH)\)\s+Library r(?:un)?path: \[([^\]]*)\]", ro)
                if m and "/nix/store/" in m.group(1):
                    new = []
                    for e in m.group(1).split(":"):
                        if GLIBC.match(e):
                            stats["dropped_glibc_rp"] += 1
                            continue
                        if e.startswith("/nix/store/"):
                            e = "$ORIGIN/" + os.path.relpath(inbundle(e), dirpath)
                        new.append(e)
                    args += ["--set-rpath", ":".join(new)]
                    stats["runpath"] += 1
                if args:
                    subprocess.run([patchelf, *args, f], check=True)
                continue
            data = open(f, "rb").read()
            if b"/nix/store/" not in data:
                continue
            owner = p.split("/")[3].split("-", 1)[1]
            is_script = data.startswith(b"#!") and os.access(f, os.X_OK)
            if not (is_script or owner.startswith("eon")):
                continue
            text = data.decode("utf-8", errors="surrogateescape")
            if is_script:
                first, rest = text.split("\n", 1)
                interp = first[2:].strip().split()
                prog = os.path.basename(interp[0])
                first = "#!/bin/" + prog if prog in ("bash", "sh") else first
                # makeWrapper bodies are bash; run them with the host bash.
                if "/nix/store/" in first:
                    first = "#!/usr/bin/env " + prog
                text = first + "\n" + rest
                stats["script"] += 1
            else:
                stats["text"] += 1
            text = text.replace("'/nix/store/", "\x00Q")
            text = text.replace("/nix/store/", "${EON_BUNDLE_ROOT}/nix/store/")
            text = text.replace("\x00Q", "\"${EON_BUNDLE_ROOT}\"'/nix/store/")
            mode = os.stat(f).st_mode
            open(f, "w", encoding="utf-8", errors="surrogateescape").write(text)
            os.chmod(f, mode)

# fonts.conf sits directly in nix/store, so its store dirs become prefix="relative".
for p in kept:
    if p.endswith("-fonts.conf"):
        f = inbundle(p)
        text = re.sub(r"<dir>/nix/store/([^<]+)</dir>", r'<dir prefix="relative">\1</dir>', open(f).read())
        os.chmod(f, 0o644)
        open(f, "w").write(text)

eon = [p for p in kept if re.search(r"-eon-0\.1\.1$", p)][0]
launcher = os.path.join(out, "eon")
open(launcher, "w").write(
    "#!/bin/sh\n"
    'EON_BUNDLE_ROOT=$(dirname "$(readlink -f "$0")")\n'
    "export EON_BUNDLE_ROOT\n"
    f'exec "$EON_BUNDLE_ROOT{eon}/bin/eon" "$@"\n')
os.chmod(launcher, 0o755)
print(stats, "kept", len(kept), "of", len(paths))

=== run-proof.sh (sha256 fceb78c1...)
#!/bin/bash
# Disposable eon-zti4.1 prototype proof, run inside the stock Ubuntu VM as user eon.
set -u
cd "$HOME"; pkill -x sway; pkill -u eon -f "t/eon-pro[t]o|sleep 60[0]"; sleep 1; chmod -R u+w t eon-0.1.1-x86_64-linux eon-proto 2>/dev/null; rm -rf t ev eon-0.1.1-x86_64-linux eon-proto; mkdir t ev && cd t || exit 1
EV=$HOME/ev
echo "== host"; . /etc/os-release; echo "$PRETTY_NAME $(uname -r) $(ldd --version | head -1)"; id
echo "outer userns $(readlink /proc/self/ns/user)"; ls -d /nix 2>&1

echo "== RED: current bwrap bundle (ef238be candidate)"
tar --zstd -xf "$HOME/eon-0.1.1-x86_64-linux.tar.zst"
./eon-0.1.1-x86_64-linux/eon versions; echo "red versions exit=$?"

echo "== GREEN: host-glibc relinked prototype"
sha256sum "$HOME/eon-proto.tar.zst"
tar --zstd -xf "$HOME/eon-proto.tar.zst"
./eon-proto/eon versions | head -3; echo "green versions exit=${PIPESTATUS[0]}"
./eon-proto/eon --help >/dev/null; echo "green help exit=$?"

export XDG_RUNTIME_DIR=/tmp/zr; rm -rf "$XDG_RUNTIME_DIR"; mkdir -m700 "$XDG_RUNTIME_DIR"
export XDG_DATA_DIRS=/usr/local/share:/usr/share
printf 'output HEADLESS-1 resolution 1280x800\n' > "$EV/sway.conf"
WLR_BACKENDS=headless WLR_RENDERER=pixman WLR_LIBINPUT_NO_DEVICES=1 \
  sway -c "$EV/sway.conf" >"$EV/sway.log" 2>&1 </dev/null &
for _ in $(seq 50); do [ -S "$XDG_RUNTIME_DIR/wayland-1" ] && break; sleep 0.2; done
export WAYLAND_DISPLAY=wayland-1 SWAYSOCK=$(ls "$XDG_RUNTIME_DIR"/sway-ipc.*.sock)
vulkaninfo --summary 2>/dev/null | grep -E 'deviceName|driverName' | head -2

cmd='s='"$EV"'/shell; { echo "venus_alive=$(pgrep -fc yazelix-venus)"; echo "pid=$$"; grep -E "NoNewPrivs|^Uid|^Gid|^Groups" /proc/self/status;
  id; echo "inner userns $(readlink /proc/self/ns/user)"; stat -c "%n %U %G" /usr/bin/sudo /etc/shadow;
