comments.author: lucca
comments.text:
User decisions (Lucca, 2026-10-18), after fresh-eyes pass 2:
- EON-C6 host-input statement approved in principle. The direct bundle takes libc, NSS, locales and the Vulkan driver from the host as declared inputs while the Nix channel pins them; component identities and the graph are unchanged. Its exact wording comes back to Lucca in the docs child. This settles the stop condition: the only contract change beyond EON-C5's mechanism is this approved EON-C6 statement. The record's earlier "no stop condition is triggered" was wrong.
- eon-install accepts only the new layout. No bwrap-era payload stays installable or selectable, because those candidates were never published. This replaces correction 1's "keeps retained bwrap-era payloads selectable".
- Zsh and Fish stop shipping (eon-8olu, P1). The fish chain (python3, coreutils, man-db, groff, gettext, util-linux, python termios) and zsh's ncurses use then leave the closure. The GLIBC_2.42 floor then comes only from bash-interactive and readline through ncurses 6.6, and the floor-2.39 child shrinks to that.

Further corrections from pass 2:
- The installer trust boundary was missing. installer/src/main.rs:63-70 accepts absolute /nix/store symlinks because they "resolve through the bundle's private /nix at execution" (:64). Without the namespace they would resolve against the host's /nix or dangle, so the installer child must reject absolute links in the new layout.
- Gates: the floor gate checks every shipped ELF against GLIBC_2.42, with an explicit reviewed exclusion list for executables Eon never runs. A second gate fails the build when a NEEDED library resolves nowhere in the bundle and is not on the declared host-library list (libc, libm, libgcc_s and libwayland-client for Venus). This catches silent fallback to the host's /usr/lib under the host ld.so. The relinker uses patchelf as a subprocess and readelf for inspection; it adds no ELF-parsing crate. A crate added later goes through AP-DEPENDENCY-001.
- GPU wording: the bundled vulkan-loader stays (correction 5), so child 4 takes only libwayland-client from the host, not libvulkan. "Ubuntu Desktop and Fedora Workstation ship Mesa Vulkan" is an assumption; lm9p's desktop-image matrix verifies it.
- provenance.json and closure-paths.txt (nix/linux-bundle.nix:13-24, :42) must describe the relinked, partial payload: glibc, Mesa and LLVM are excluded and the bytes are patched. The switch child owns this.

Final proposed children, replacing both earlier lists (unfiled; each one session; in order):
1. Location-neutral Eon shell integration: Eon-owned init resolves managed artifacts through an Eon-supplied input, in both channels. It lands after eon-8olu, so it covers only Bash and Nushell.
2. Relinker as a standalone Nix check: a Rust relink step over the eon closure (interpreter, $ORIGIN RUNPATH, relative symlinks, glibc/Mesa/LLVM excluded) plus the floor gate and the NEEDED-resolution gate, producing a relinked tree. manual-bundle is unchanged, so nothing breaks.
3. Launcher env table, checked against child 2's tree: the static multi-call entrypoint applies the makeWrapper env generated from the same Nix wrapper definitions, keeps the argv0 dispatch and replaces in-closure makeWrapper scripts. manual-bundle is still unchanged.
4. Third-party data roots in the relinked tree: helix runtime, zoxide's fzf path, ncurses terminfo, CA certificates, relative fonts.conf, Venus on host libwayland-client with no bundled gcc runtime, and the xkbcommon data roots. Each is checked inside an Orbit terminal.
5. Switch: manual-bundle ships the relinked tree and launcher; bubblewrap and its source leave the payload, licences and provenance; provenance.json and closure-paths.txt are updated. eon-install validates the new layout (no libexec/bwrap requirement at installer/src/main.rs:200 and :388), rejects absolute symlinks and updates its tests and fixture (installer/src/tests.rs:77). The bundle and installer change in one commit, so no intermediate archive breaks install.
6. Docs and contract text: MANUAL-BUNDLE's execution boundary, receipts, licence and userns copy, and the EON-C6 statement with the wording shown to Lucca first.
7. Lower the floor to GLIBC_2.39 for Bash: bash-interactive and readline, via ncurses built without the 2.42 termios symbols or a static bash. It runs after eon-8olu and is required before eon-zti4 closes.
8. Final installed proof on Ubuntu 26.04 and Ubuntu 24.04 VMs: verify, extract, `eon versions`, `eon --help`, eon-install install, upgrade, rollback and remove with two archives, and the terminal NoNewPrivs, id and sudo checks. It runs last because child 7 changes the candidate, then hands the candidate to lm9p.

title: Make Eon shell integration location-neutral
description:
## Why

The namespace-free bundle (epic eon-zti4; mechanism accepted on eon-zti4.1) moves the payload away from /nix. Eon-owned shell init files embed absolute store paths at build time. In the eon-zti4.1 Ubuntu 26.04 prototype, eon.bashrc's Starship, Zoxide, Atuin and Carapace sources failed ("eon: cannot initialize Starship" and the rest). Eon does not forward arbitrary environment to terminals, so a bundle-root variable never reached the shell. The init must name managed artifacts through an input Eon itself supplies, in both the Nix channel and the bundle.

## Evidence

- `nix/shell-environment.nix:5-60`: the `eon-shell-init` store directory (starship-*, zoxide-*, atuin-*, carapace-*).
- `nix/shell-environment.nix`: the bash rc, the nu vendor autoload and the directory-picker config `source` ${shellInit}/... as absolute store paths.
- `flake.nix:493-511`: the eon wrapper sets EON_BASH_RC, EON_NU_VENDOR_AUTOLOAD, EON_DIRECTORY_PICKER_CONFIG and EON_SESSION_BIN as store paths.
- `eon/crates/eon/src/product.rs:115-125`: Eon reads those inputs as opaque paths (EON-C3).

## Scope

In scope: Eon-owned Bash and Nushell init, the shell-init directory, the directory-picker config, and the inputs that carry them. Resolve artifacts through one Eon-supplied input (for example a shell-init root next to EON_SESSION_BIN) that Eon passes into the child environment.
Out of scope: Zsh and Fish (removed by eon-8olu, which lands first); EON-C9 semantics; bundle builder changes.

## Acceptance

- No Eon-owned shell init or picker config contains an absolute /nix/store path; each resolves through the Eon-supplied input.
- In the Nix channel, EON-C9 behavior is unchanged for Nushell and Bash, including Starship, Zoxide, Atuin and Carapace activation and warn-and-continue on failure.

## Verification

- `nix develop -c eon-test` exits 0; `nix build .#default` exits 0.
- `grep -r /nix/store` over the built eon-shell-init, the bash rc, the nu autoload and the picker config finds only references Eon resolves through the input. List any that remain.
- Refresh the `eon` profile and make one isolated installed observation that a new Bash and a new Nushell terminal initialize all four integrations. Do not restart the live supervisor.

## Stop Conditions

- Stop if this needs an EON-C3 or EON-C9 contract change.
- Stop if the child environment cannot carry the input without changing Orbit.
close_reason: Shell init resolves through a relocatable tree; proof recorded

comments.author: lucca
comments.text:
Handoff (not started; base f9979f6, eon-8olu landed). The session that would have taken this was past the 100k start-fresh mark, so this records findings only. No code changed.

Facts checked at f9979f6:
- Child launch carries the session bin only through PATH (runtime sessions.rs:986, managed_environment.rs:714). No EON_SESSION_BIN or other root variable reaches the shell.
- 11 eon-shell-init files embed absolute tool store paths: starship-{nu,bash}, zoxide-{nushell,bash}, atuin-{nu,bash}[-nobind], carapace-{nushell,bash}. eon.bashrc and every nu autoload eon.nu embed the shell-init store path.
- Bash sets ${BASH_SOURCE[0]} to the --rcfile path inside the rcfile (checked with managed bash 5.3).
- Nushell 0.113 `const p = path self ../bin/x` resolves relative to the file at parse time; `source`/`overlay use` take const paths. It errors under -c, so test from a file.

Proposed shape (recommended; no new child input, no runtime or Orbit change, so it avoids both stop conditions):
- Build eon.bashrc, the nu vendor autoload tree and the shell-init files into the eon package under libexec/eon/ next to bin/, so EON_BASH_RC and EON_NU_VENDOR_AUTOLOAD (existing EON-C3 opaque inputs) point inside one relocatable tree.
- eon.bashrc captures its directory from ${BASH_SOURCE[0]} before sourcing ~/.bashrc and sources shell-init files and calls tools from bin/ relative to it. Nu files use `const ... = path self ...` for both the source paths and the tool paths (^$const in defs and closures).
- Replace the sed/substituteInPlace store-path rewrites with rewrites to those relative references, keeping exact managed tools (not bare PATH lookup, which a user's rc could reorder).
Alternative rejected for now: a new child env variable naming the root. It adds an input that the runtime must forward, touches runtime launch enforcement, and may need an EON-C3/EON-C9 change.

Open: the directory-picker config (EON_DIRECTORY_PICKER_CONFIG) is not inspected yet; check what store paths it embeds. Check fzf references too.
Next step: claim, inspect the picker config, then implement the shape in nix/shell-environment.nix and flake.nix; verify with the bead's grep over the built tree, eon-test, nix build/flake check, profile refresh and one isolated Bash and Nushell observation (the eon-8olu dogfood probes work: nu needs --config <autoload>/15/eon.nu, not -c alone).

comments.author: lucca
comments.text:
Proof (revision = this commit; x86_64 Linux, native host, Nix):

Decision: adopted the handoff shape. The eon package installs one shell tree at libexec/eon/shell
(eon.bashrc, init/, nu/<mask>/eon.nu) next to the session bin. Each file resolves its sibling
files and the managed tools relative to its own location: Bash uses ${BASH_SOURCE[0]%/*} and
_eon_<tool>=.../../../bin/<tool>, and Nushell uses `const ... = path self ../../...`. The existing
EON-C3 inputs EON_BASH_RC and EON_NU_VENDOR_AUTOLOAD point into the tree. Scope's "one
Eon-supplied input" is met by these inputs. A new root variable forwarded to the child was
rejected because it would change runtime launch, so there is no runtime, Orbit or contract change.
Atuin's Nu keybinding command runs later in REPL scope, where consts from a file sourced inside

popup uses ${_eon_atuin@Q}. Known gap: in that same upstream Atuin line, PATH='$PATH' and
ATUIN_SESSION are still single-quoted without escaping, so the opt-in tmux popup breaks if PATH
contains an apostrophe. That is upstream behavior and out of scope.

Store-path grep: grep -rn /nix/store over the built libexec/eon/shell finds nothing. The picker
config (keymap.toml, init.lua) contains no store path. It stays its own opaque EON_DIRECTORY_PICKER_CONFIG
input. fzf is not referenced by path; zoxide finds it on the session-bin PATH. Store paths remain only

Checks:
- nix develop -c eon-test: exit 0, 363 passed, 0 failed. It ran on the first candidate; later

- nix flake check on the final tree: exit 0 (default, eonbase-closure, managed-command-path).

running supervisor was not restarted; a restart is needed to pick up the change.

Isolated installed observation, on that store path: env -i with a private HOME/XDG and a pty via

- eon-bash -i: argv carries --rcfile .../libexec/eon/shell/eon.bashrc; EON_SHELL_*=1111;

- eon-nu: NU_VENDOR_AUTOLOAD_DIR=.../libexec/eon/shell/nu/15; the starship-nu overlay is active;
  __zoxide_z exists; the Starship prompt renders; the Carapace completer returns 82 entries; the

Review ledger: 2 passes. Each pass used a fresh Claude subagent plus Codex (gpt-6.1-sol, xhigh,

- Pass 1. Blocking (Codex): unescaped apostrophe in the tmux-popup path; fixed with @Q. Nits

  the layout check was added.
- Pass 2. Nothing blocking. Nits not applied:
  - no Nu check beyond mask 0 (a pre-existing gap);
  - the picker config is not in the automated grep;
  - the bash check tests variables, not hook functions;
  - new visible non-exported names: Bash _eon_<tool> globals, needed at call time, and Nu

title: Relink the eon closure for the host glibc as a Nix check
description:
## Why

Mechanism accepted on eon-zti4.1 (epic eon-zti4): relink the Nix closure to run on the host glibc. Every ELF gets PT_INTERP=/lib64/ld-linux-x86-64.so.2 (the x86-64 psABI path) and $ORIGIN-relative RUNPATHs inside the bundle's own nix/store tree. glibc, Mesa and LLVM are excluded, and absolute store symlinks become relative. Build it first as a standalone Nix check, so manual-bundle keeps working until the switch child.

## Evidence

- eon-zti4.1 inventory: 1,224 ELFs, 250 with PT_INTERP (all nixpkgs glibc-2.42-61), 929 with store RUNPATHs, 314 absolute store symlinks. The prototype relinked 246 interpreters and 899 RUNPATHs with patchelf 0.15.2; the reproducer relink.py is in an eon-zti4.1 comment.
- `nix/linux-bundle.nix:1-45`: the current builder (closureInfo copy plus bwrap).
- Remaining ELFs NEED glibc sonames: libdl (17), libpthread (22), libresolv (18), librt (5), ld-linux (21).

## Scope

In scope: a Rust relink step (repository tooling must be Rust; Python is disposable only) that runs patchelf as a subprocess and readelf for inspection, with no new ELF crate (any crate goes through AP-DEPENDENCY-001); a Nix check, e.g. `checks.x86_64-linux.bundle-relink`, producing the relinked tree; and two gates:
1. The floor gate: every shipped ELF needs GLIBC_x <= 2.42 and no GLIBC_PRIVATE, with an explicit reviewed exclusion list for executables Eon never runs.
2. The NEEDED-resolution gate: each NEEDED soname resolves inside the bundle via RUNPATH, or is on the declared host set (every glibc soname, libgcc_s, and libwayland-client for Venus).
Out of scope: changing manual-bundle or eon-install, the launcher, and data-root fixes.

## Acceptance

- The check builds a relinked tree with no PT_INTERP other than the psABI path, no RUNPATH entry outside $ORIGIN, no absolute store symlink, and no glibc, Mesa or LLVM store paths.
- Both gates pass on the current closure, and each fails on a seeded violation.

## Verification

- `nix build .#checks.x86_64-linux.bundle-relink` exits 0, and its gate output lists counts by kind.
- A red/green check of both gates on a deliberately bad input (for example an ELF that needs GLIBC_2.43, and a NEEDED with no provider). Keep it in the supported harness.
- `nix develop -c eon-test` exits 0 for the relink crate's unit tests.

## Stop Conditions

- Stop if a needed object cannot be relinked by patchelf (for example a Go or static-PIE edge case) without forking a component.
close_reason: bundle-relink check builds the host-glibc relinked tree; both gates pass on the current closure and fail on seeded violations

comments.author: lucca
comments.text:
Reference gate and code shape (2026-10-19, repo edge b1c374e, untracked review-corners.md not part of this work; eon package /nix/store/7ps5hzi0fizmgfqphyi6mc767xi3861v-eon-0.1.1, nixpkgs 567a49d1913c, patchelf 0.15.2).
Question: how should the eon closure be relinked for the host glibc and gated, as a standalone Nix check?
Contract: no contract change; check-only. Consumers are eon-zti4.4/.5/.6, which take the relinked tree.
Owners: nix/bundle-relink.nix owns policy: the root (eon package), the host-provided store paths excluded (pkgs.glibc, pkgs.mesa), the glibc floor (2.42) and the declared host libraries (every soname in the excluded glibc's lib/, libgcc_s.so.1, libwayland-client.so.0). A standalone std-only Rust crate relink/ (eon-relink) owns the mechanism: closure pruning from closureInfo's registration, copying, the psABI interpreter, $ORIGIN RUNPATHs, relative symlinks, and the gates. patchelf and readelf run as build-time subprocesses from the flake-locked nixpkgs.
Sources and revisions: eon-zti4.1's record (patchelf @ 382d8bc12db9 patchelf.1:171-176; psABI x86-64 @ e1ce098331da dl.tex:404-421; AppImage excludelist @ 19e30b276ffe for host glibc and libwayland-client; fzakaria's $ORIGIN RUNPATHs); nixpkgs 567a49d1913c pkgs/build-support/closure-info.nix:70 (registration: path, narHash, narSize, empty deriver, reference count, references).
Inventory of that closure, excluding glibc, Mesa, libgbm and LLVM: 651 ELFs, 59 with PT_INTERP, 645 with RUNPATH, 0 with DT_RPATH, 3 with an empty RUNPATH; 640 RUNPATH entries name glibc; 306 absolute store symlinks, none into an excluded path; GLIBC needs above 2.39 come only from ncurses libncursesw and tset, python3's termios module and util-linux sulogin (all 2.42); there is no GLIBC_PRIVATE and no non-numeric GLIBC_ name; every NEEDED resolves through RUNPATH or the host set.
Decision: exclude glibc and Mesa, and ship only what eon reaches without passing through them. That also prunes 41 paths (186 MB) referenced only through Mesa or glibc: llvm-21.1.8-lib, mesa-libgbm, python3, util-linux-minimal (lib, login), libdrm, elfutils, curl, openssl and others. With python3 and sulogin gone, only ncurses stays above 2.39, which narrows eon-zti4.8.
Failure conditions: the relinker exits 1 on a stale exclusion (path not in the closure), a RUNPATH entry or symlink naming a store path the tree does not ship, or a readelf or patchelf failure. The gates reject an interpreter other than /lib64/ld-linux-x86-64.so.2, a RUNPATH entry outside $ORIGIN, DT_RPATH, a rewritten symlink that does not resolve inside the tree, any GLIBC_ need that is non-numeric (GLIBC_PRIVATE) or above the floor, and a NEEDED that neither resolves inside the tree through RUNPATH nor is a declared host library.
Rejected: (1) copying the closure minus only the excluded directories, as the prototype did, which ships 186 MB that nothing reaches and keeps 2.42 objects Eon never runs. (2) A workspace-member crate: crateSource would include it, so a relinker edit would rebuild Orbit, Venus and eon and change eon's generation identity. It stays standalone like installer/ and bundle/. (3) An ELF crate (goblin or object): readelf suffices, and the bead forbids one without AP-DEPENDENCY-001. (4) A floor exemption list: it would be empty at 2.42 on this closure, so none is added; eon-zti4.8 adds one if it chooses exemption over a fix.
Cheapest proof: nix build .#checks.x86_64-linux.bundle-relink with the gate counts; unit-test red/green that seeds a GLIBC_2.99 need into a real ELF and adds a NEEDED with no provider, run by nix develop -c eon-test --manifest-path relink/Cargo.toml and in the relinker's Nix build.
Exit condition (from eon-zti4.1): drop the relinker if nixpkgs gains relocatable outputs or Eon's terminal set becomes fully static.

comments.author: lucca
comments.text:
Gate rules and accepted gaps (2026-10-19), from glibc 2.42's elf/dl-load.c (glibc-2.42.tar.xz in the pinned nixpkgs 567a49d1913c):
Gate rules. A RUNPATH entry must begin with $ORIGIN as a whole path component and resolve step by step (each symlink before a later "..", as the kernel does) without leaving the tree. A missing directory holds nothing to search. fillin_rpath searches the working directory for an empty entry inside a nonempty RUNPATH, so such an entry fails. decompose_rpath ignores an entirely empty RUNPATH, which 2 shipped objects (anima, gcc libgcc_s) keep. A NEEDED library counts as in the tree only if it resolves to a shipped ELF shared object ("DYN (Shared object file)"): glibc refuses a PIE executable as a dependency. A library found through a symlink from another directory takes that directory as its $ORIGIN, so such a provider fails if it has a RUNPATH. Version needs declared in the dynamic section (VERNEEDNUM) that readelf cannot list, for example because the section headers are stripped, fail the floor gate. Only an interpreter from an excluded path is replaced; any other stays for the gate to report. readelf runs with LC_ALL=C because the parser matches its untranslated messages.
Accepted gaps, with reasons:
1. LLVM and libgbm leave through pruning, not an explicit exclusion. If a kept path ever references LLVM directly, LLVM ships because something kept needs it; the check prints the pruned count, and the host-driver stance is enforced where Venus's environment changes (eon-zti4.4, eon-zti4.5).
2. No floor exemption list: at GLIBC_2.42 it would be empty. eon-zti4.8 adds one only if it chooses exemption over fixing ncurses.
3. eon-test with no arguments does not run the relinker's suite; the suite runs in the relinker's Nix build, which the check requires, and with eon-test --manifest-path relink/Cargo.toml, as docs/DEVELOPMENT.md says. Adding it to the default run would also mean re-rendering AGENTS.md, whose text lists the suites.
4. The GLIBC_PRIVATE and DT_RPATH rejections have no seeded test: no same-length edit seeds GLIBC_PRIVATE, and neither occurs in the closure. Both are one-condition rules beside seeded ones.
5. The declared host set holds every glibc soname, including ones some distributions split out (libnsl.so.1, libnss_db, libnss_hesiod, libc_malloc_debug.so.0). This follows the bead's policy, and no shipped object NEEDs them.

comments.author: lucca
comments.text:
Gate rules, addendum (2026-10-19): the NEEDED gate follows the loader's search order. The first RUNPATH candidate that exists decides, and it fails unless it is a shipped shared object; glibc stops with an error there rather than searching on. Each step of a search path must be a directory, because the kernel answers ENOTDIR for file/... Every symlink in the tree, not only the rewritten ones, must resolve inside the tree. The relinker's Nix source is a fileset of Cargo.toml, Cargo.lock and src, as in nix/installer.nix.
Accepted gaps, continued:
6. Any non-numeric GLIBC_ need fails the floor gate, including public markers such as GLIBC_ABI_DT_RELR that every host at the floor satisfies. None occurs in the closure. If one appears, the gate fails loudly; the fix then maps the marker to the glibc release that introduced it.
7. The "found away from its $ORIGIN" rule is conservative: it also rejects a same-depth cross-directory library link with a RUNPATH, which would resolve the same way. None occurs today.

title: Replace bundle makeWrapper scripts with a static launcher env table
description:
## Why

Mechanism accepted on eon-zti4.1 (epic eon-zti4). The Nix closure's makeWrapper scripts have /nix/store shebangs and absolute env values, so a relocated bundle cannot run them. In the prototype, rewriting them to a host shell failed: an `env bash` shebang found Eon's own `bash` session wrapper first on the terminal's private PATH and recursed. The bundle needs a static launcher that applies the same env relative to its own directory and execs the real binary.

## Evidence

- `flake.nix:493-511`: the eon wrapper (EON_ORBIT, EON_VENUS, EON_* tool paths, EON_SESSION_BIN, TERMINFO_DIRS). `flake.nix:289`: the Venus wrapper (FONTCONFIG_FILE, LD_LIBRARY_PATH, XDG_DATA_DIRS). `flake.nix:183`: CodexBarCLI (SSL_CERT_FILE).
- libexec/eon/bin: 6 of 20 entries are absolute store links; the rest point to bin/eon-*, which point to the single bin/eon makeWrapper script that dispatches on argv0 via `exec -a "$0"`.
- `bundle/src/main.rs`: the current static Rust entrypoint (it execs bwrap).

## Scope

In scope: a multi-call static launcher (an evolution of bundle/src/main.rs) that keeps the argv0 dispatch, plus an env table generated from the same Nix wrapper definitions so one owner holds each env list (refactor the wrapper args into a shared Nix attrset if needed). The launcher replaces the in-closure wrapper scripts inside child 2's relinked tree. Check it against that tree in a Nix check.
Out of scope: shipping it in manual-bundle (switch child), eon-install, third-party data roots.

## Acceptance

- In the relinked tree, every former wrapper entry (eon, eon-* commands, yazelix-venus, CodexBarCLI, session bin) runs through the launcher with bundle-relative values and no host shell.
- The Nix channel's wrappers and the bundle table derive from one definition.
- Moving the tree to another directory keeps it working.

## Verification

- A Nix check runs `eon versions` and `eon --help` from the relinked tree at two different paths, with no /nix lookups. Use env -i and strace or LD_DEBUG to show that no /nix/store path is opened.
- `nix develop -c eon-test` exits 0.

## Stop Conditions

- Stop if generating the table needs a second hand-maintained copy of the env lists.
close_reason: Static launcher env table replaces the relinked tree's makeWrapper scripts; one definition for both channels; bundle-launch check

comments.author: lucca
comments.text:
Design and reference gate (2026-10-19, edge b85d82f).
Owner: flake.nix defines each wrapper environment once (eon, yazelix-venus, CodexBarCLI) as {set, setDefault, prefix}. One renderer turns it into makeWrapper args for the Nix channel; nix/bundle-relink.nix renders the same attrsets into the launcher's compiled-in table. The eon environment takes its own out path: placeholder "out" for makeWrapper, the real path for the table. The closure has exactly these three makeWrapper scripts (scan of every file for 'exec -a "$0"'); there are no makeBinaryWrapper binaries.
Launcher: a new static std-only crate, launcher/, built with pkgsStatic.rustPlatform like the current entrypoint. A copy replaces each wrapper script in the relinked tree. It finds its own entry by the suffix of /proc/self/exe, so the tree root is whatever precedes the wrapper's store path. It prefixes every value with that root and execs wrapProgram's .NAME-wrapped with argv[0] passed through. bundle/ (the bwrap entrypoint) stays as it is, so manual-bundle keeps building until eon-zti4.6 switches it and deletes bundle/.
Semantics: --set, --set-default and --prefix follow shell makeWrapper, which the Nix channel runs: drop the first equal element, then prepend; a set-but-empty value counts as unset. Values inside the tree's excluded paths drop out of the table. Today that is only Mesa's share in Venus's XDG_DATA_DIRS, per eon-zti4.1's host Vulkan decision. A gate requires every other value to exist in the tree.
References: nixpkgs 567a49d makeWrapper output (the three scripts in the closure) and pkgs/by-name/ma/makeBinaryWrapper/make-binary-wrapper.sh. Its wrapProgram uses --inherit-argv0, so argv[0] is passed through; the launcher does the same. Rejected: its set_env_prefix semantics, which differ from shell makeWrapper on set-but-empty values (it yields 'value:').
Check: a new Nix check runs the tree as a host without Nix would. bwrap binds a stand-in host glibc (nixpkgs glibc) and its loader at /lib64/ld-linux-x86-64.so.2, the tree at two locations and nothing else from /nix, with --clearenv. Probe: nested bwrap inside this host's Nix sandbox works (userns-probe-2). The bundle itself stays namespace-free; only the check needs nested user namespaces, so it cannot run on hosts that restrict them.

title: Relocate compiled-in data roots for the relinked bundle
description:
## Why

Mechanism accepted on eon-zti4.1 (epic eon-zti4). Several components read data from store paths compiled into the binaries, so they misbehave without /nix even after the relink and launcher. The prototype hit fonts.conf (Venus refused to start: "terminal font family is unavailable") and the xkbcommon Compose root ("No Compose file for locale C.UTF-8").

## Evidence (eon-zti4.1 inventory)

- helix-term: compiled-in helix-runtime path; HELIX_RUNTIME overrides it.
- zoxide 0.9.9: compiled-in fzf store path (a nixpkgs patch), which breaks `zi`.
- ncurses: default terminfo dir. bash-interactive: lib dirs. openssl: etc/ssl; use the host CA store via SSL_CERT_FILE/SSL_CERT_DIR, or the host default.
- The fonts.conf store `<dir>` entries become `prefix="relative"` (supported by fontconfig-parser 0.5.8, which Venus uses through fontdb).
- Venus: take libwayland-client from the host (as the AppImage excludelist does). Keep the bundled vulkan-loader, which loaded host ICDs in the prototype. libxkbcommon comes from the host or the bundle with XKB and Compose roots set. Venus's RUNPATH must carry no bundled gcc runtime, so host GPU drivers never get an older libgcc_s.

## Scope

In scope: launcher env and build-time relative rewrites in the relinked tree for the items above; the launcher table from the launcher child.
Out of scope: Zsh and Fish (gone after eon-8olu); manual-bundle shipping; installer.

## Acceptance

- Inside an Orbit terminal started from the relinked tree with no /nix: hx finds its runtime (`hx --health` shows the runtime dir), `zi` runs fzf, the terminfo lookup for Orbit's TERM succeeds, and an HTTPS fetch from a managed tool verifies certificates.
- Venus starts with the bundled fonts and logs no xkbcommon Compose error.

## Verification

- An isolated headless run with no /nix, either a VM (recipe on eon-zti4.1) or a Nix check where possible, recording each item above. Desktop focus rule: never on Lucca's desktop.
- `nix develop -c eon-test` exits 0.

## Stop Conditions

- Stop if a component cannot be pointed at relocated data without forking it.
close_reason: Compiled-in data roots relocated for the relinked bundle (helix fallback link, zoxide fzf from PATH, ncurses terminfo, relative fonts.conf, host libwayland-client and gcc runtime for Venus, xkb roots); bundle-launch checks and Ubuntu 26.04 VM proof recorded

Inventory changes: openssl is no longer in the tree (it left with Zsh and Fish). nu and atuin verify TLS through rustls-platform-verifier, and lazygit through Go crypto/x509; all three read the host CA store (/etc/ssl/certs/ca-certificates.crt, /etc/pki/tls/certs/ca-bundle.crt, ...). CodexBarCLI keeps its SSL_CERT_FILE default. So the CA item needs no change, only the HTTPS proof. Inert: Go tzdata, iana-etc and mailcap fallbacks (carapace, fzf, lazygit); bash's loadables dir, locale and bashdb.

- Helix (helix 817dcbc helix-loader/src/lib.rs:50-86): after the config dir, HELIX_RUNTIME and the compiled HELIX_DEFAULT_RUNTIME, it falls back to <canonical exe dir>/runtime. The tree gets helix-term/bin/runtime, a relative link to helix-runtime (a "fallback" in nix/bundle-relink.nix). Rejected: HELIX_RUNTIME, which Eon strips from managed hx on purpose (runtime managed_environment.rs:701).
- zoxide (nixpkgs 567a49d pkgs/by-name/zo/zoxide/package.nix: withFzf patches "fzf" to nixpkgs's own fzf store path): zoxidePackage sets withFzf = false in both channels, so zoxide runs fzf from PATH. Eon puts its session bin first on every terminal and managed-shell PATH (sessions.rs orbit_command, managed_environment.rs command); the directory picker already runs "fzf" that way (cli.rs:178). The closure loses the second, unmanaged fzf. Rejected: patching the binary.
- ncurses 6.6: its only compiled terminfo dir is its own store path. Orbit sets TERM=eon (orbit/src/platform.rs:72), and the eon wrapper's TERMINFO_DIRS already resolves that. The bundle adds the bundled ncurses database after Orbit's, for other terminal types (for example inside tmux). It is bundle-only, so host programs in Nix-channel terminals keep their own lookup.
- Fonts: venusFontsConf rewrites makeFontsConf's store dirs to prefix="relative" in both channels (one file; relative to /nix/store under Nix). Venus parses it with fontdb 0.23.0 / fontconfig-parser 0.5.8 and links no libfontconfig. A build gate fails if any store path remains.
- Venus libraries: libwayland-client comes from the host (pkgs.wayland joins the excluded paths, so its LD_LIBRARY_PATH entry and libffi drop out). Only xkbcli helpers inside libxkbcommon NEED it, and it is already a declared host library. This matches the AppImage excludelist (eon-zti4.1 references). The bundled vulkan-loader stays. libxkbcommon stays bundled; the bundle environment sets XKB_CONFIG_ROOT and XLOCALEDIR (as set-default, the env names in libxkbcommon 1.13.1) to the bundled xkeyboard-config and libx11 data. The new eon-relink --host-runtime removes its RUNPATH, so the gate requires each of them on the host, and a host driver never meets the bundled gcc 15 libgcc_s.
- Ownership: wrapper environments stay single-sourced. A wrapper's new `relocated` attrset holds environment for the bundle only (data roots that only the relocated tree misses). The launcher table and the bundle-launch makeWrapper comparison both use the merged environment.
Checks: bundle-launch in its no-/nix stand-in host runs hx --health bash (parser and highlight queries found), tput -T eon and -T xterm-256color through eon-bash (compared with the Nix product), and zoxide query --interactive through fzf on PATH (--filter). The store-lookup trace gate exempts only the fallback targets. Venus fonts and xkb, Orbit-terminal checks and HTTPS go to the Ubuntu 26.04 VM. Dependency effect: zoxide loses its fzf edge; nothing is added.

title: Switch manual-bundle and eon-install to the relinked layout
description:
## Why

Mechanism accepted on eon-zti4.1 (epic eon-zti4). This child ships it: manual-bundle switches from the bwrap /nix projection to the relinked tree and launcher, and eon-install changes in the same commit, because it rejects any payload without libexec/bwrap. User decision (Lucca, 2026-10-18): eon-install accepts only the new layout, with no bwrap-era compatibility (those candidates were never published).

## Evidence

- `nix/linux-bundle.nix:1-45`: the bwrap helper, the closure copy, provenance (bubblewrap fields at :13-24) and closure-paths.txt (:42).
- `installer/src/main.rs:200` and `:388`: `executable(libexec/bwrap)` checks. `:63-70`: accepts absolute /nix/store symlinks because they "resolve through the bundle's private /nix" (:64). `installer/src/tests.rs:77`: the fixture creates libexec/bwrap.

## Scope

In scope:
- manual-bundle ships the relinked tree plus launcher; bubblewrap and its vendored source leave the payload, licences and provenance.
- provenance.json and closure-paths.txt describe the relinked, partial payload: glibc, Mesa and LLVM excluded, bytes patched.
- eon-install validates the new layout, rejects absolute symlinks in it, and its tests and fixture are updated.
Out of scope: docs and contract text (next child); the glibc floor change; the final VM proof.

## Acceptance

- `nix build .#manual-bundle` produces an archive with no bwrap, no absolute store symlink and no glibc/Mesa/LLVM. The bundle's `eon versions` matches the Nix product's (EON-C2/C6: same manifest and lock bytes).
- eon-install's tests cover installing the new layout and rejecting an absolute symlink.

## Verification

- `nix develop -c eon-test` exits 0, including the installer suite.
- `nix build .#manual-bundle` exits 0. Extracting outside /nix and running `env -i ./eon versions` exits 0 on this host.
- Shared lifecycle/trust boundary route: full affected Rust and Nix surfaces (`nix flake check`).

## Stop Conditions

- Stop if eon-install needs an EON-C5 contract change, not only validation code.
close_reason: manual-bundle ships the relinked tree with a relative eon entry link and schema 2 provenance; bubblewrap and bundle/ are gone; eon-install rejects absolute symlinks and requires the linked entrypoint; end-to-end install, eon-test and flake check pass

comments.author: lucca
comments.text:
Design and reference gate (2026-10-19, edge f973ce0, clean apart from the unrelated untracked review-corners.md).

title: Update bundle docs and the EON-C6 host-input statement
description:
## Why

After the switch (epic eon-zti4), docs and contracts still describe the bwrap bundle. User decision (Lucca, 2026-10-18, on eon-zti4.1): EON-C6 gains a statement that the direct bundle takes libc, NSS, locales and the Vulkan driver from the host as declared inputs, while the Nix channel pins them. Component identities and the graph stay unchanged. Lucca approved this in principle; the exact wording must be shown to him before it is written.

## Evidence

- `docs/MANUAL-BUNDLE.md` "Execution and host boundary" (around :14-40): the bwrap /nix projection, "No ELF/config path rewriting", the userns host requirement, and the bundled Mesa software driver. Its receipts section explains absolute /nix/store symlinks resolving within the bwrap view. The licence text covers bubblewrap.
- `docs/CONTRACTS.md:285-305` EON-C6; `:251-283` EON-C5, which names no mechanism and stays unchanged.

## Scope

In scope: MANUAL-BUNDLE execution boundary and host prerequisites (glibc >= the declared floor, a host Vulkan driver, native Wayland, no userns), receipts, licence and userns copy; the EON-C6 host-input statement; a CHANGELOG entry if user-visible bundle requirements change.
Out of scope: EON-C5 text; runtime code.

## Acceptance

- No doc claims bwrap, a /nix projection or a userns requirement for the bundle; host prerequisites match the builder's declared floor and the GPU stance.
- The EON-C6 text Lucca approved is in docs/CONTRACTS.md.

## Verification

- Planning/docs route: changed Markdown paths and contract IDs listed in the bead, and a grep showing no stale bwrap/userns claims in docs/.

## Stop Conditions

- Stop for Lucca's approval of the exact EON-C6 wording before editing CONTRACTS.md.

title: Lower the bundle glibc floor to 2.39 for Ubuntu 24.04
description:
## Why

User decision (Lucca, 2026-10-18, on eon-zti4.1): the first namespace-free candidate uses a GLIBC_2.42 floor, but Ubuntu 24.04 (glibc 2.39) stays required before eon-zti4 closes. After eon-8olu removes Zsh and Fish, and with glibc, Mesa and LLVM out of the payload, the only GLIBC_2.42 objects are ncurses 6.6: lib/libncursesw.so.6.6 and bin/tset. They use glibc 2.42's new cfgetospeed, cfsetospeed, cfgetispeed and cfsetispeed versions (glibc-2.42 NEWS:25-27; x86_64 libc.abilist:2752-2760). bash-interactive, readline and bc (reachable through fzf-tmux) need 2.42 only through libncursesw. A static bash alone would still ship the 2.42 library.

## Evidence

- objdump -T on the eon closure (eon-zti4.1): libncursesw.so.6.6 references cfgetospeed@GLIBC_2.42 and the other three.
- Distro glibc: Ubuntu 24.04 2.39, Debian 13 2.41, Ubuntu 26.04 2.43, Fedora 43 2.42, Fedora 44 2.43.

## Scope

In scope: make the shipped ncurses (or its consumers) need GLIBC <= 2.39, then lower the relinker's declared floor to 2.39. Record the chosen technique and why it keeps EON-C6's one component graph; a rebuilt shared library is not a different component version.
Out of scope: other components, which already need <= 2.39.

## Acceptance

- The floor gate passes at GLIBC_2.39 with no new exclusions for reachable executables.
- Bash in an Orbit terminal works on a glibc 2.39 host.

## Verification

- The relink check at floor 2.39 exits 0, and a red run at 2.39 before the fix shows the ncurses failure.
- A headless Ubuntu 24.04 VM run of a Bash terminal from the bundle. The full proof is the final child.

## Stop Conditions

- Stop if the only fix means forking ncurses or diverging the Nix channel's bash; present options to Lucca.
close_reason: Floor 2.39 passes: the bundle ships ncurses rebuilt with a termios-speed header under its original store path (bundle-only, recorded in provenance); Bash runs in an Orbit terminal on this glibc 2.39 host

comments.author: lucca
comments.text:
Investigation (2026-10-19, edge d4960d4).
- Correction to the bead body: the shipped ncurses-6.6 (wl2nw5l4...) needs only cfgetospeed@GLIBC_2.42, in lib/libncursesw.so.6.6 and bin/tset. It does not need the other three speed functions. ncurses calls it in ncurses/tinfo/lib_baudrate.c:294-298 (baudrate(), ospeed) and progs/tset.c:853. Linking ncurses: bash-interactive, readline (libreadline, libhistory), bc and dc, ncurses's own programs and libformw, libmenuw and libpanelw. Only ncurses's tset imports ospeed, and nothing else imports cfgetospeed or baudrate.
- Why the symbol cannot simply be bound to the old version: glibc 2.42 made speed_t numeric (bits/termios-baud.h: B9600 is 9600U; the kernel encodings are now __B9600 = 0000015 in bits/termios.h and termios-cbaud.h), and cfgetospeed@GLIBC_2.42 returns numbers. ncurses's speeds table (lib_baudrate.c DATA(n) = {B##n, n}) is built from the same header. Binding cfgetospeed@GLIBC_2.2.5 while keeping the 2.42 header, or clearing the symbol version (an unversioned reference binds to the oldest version), returns encoded values that the numeric table cannot match, so baudrate() returns ERR.
- Prototype (scratch only): pkgs.ncurses.overrideAttrs with NIX_CFLAGS_COMPILE += -include termios-speed.h, a ~25-line header that defines cfgetospeed as an inline decode of c_cflag & CBAUD (the kernel ABI, filled by tcgetattr on any glibc) into the numeric B constants, falling back to c_ospeed for BOTHER. Result /nix/store/31rryq6s8pv2i5p64zy2dd0j64hi42jl-ncurses-6.6: libncursesw.so.6.6 now needs at most GLIBC_2.38 and tset at most GLIBC_2.34, with no cfgetospeed reference. tput colors (xterm-256color) prints 256; tset -q and tset -s run in a pty. No ncurses source is patched.
- Stop condition reached: shipping this either rebuilds bash, readline and bc in the Nix channel (diverging the Nix channel's bash) or needs a bundle-only substitution, and it adds a checked-in C header (AGENTS.md: another implementation language needs an explicit user decision). Asking Lucca.

comments.author: lucca
comments.text: User decision (Lucca, 2026-10-19): ship the fix bundle-only. eon-relink gains a substitution: the bundle ships the rebuilt ncurses (same source, forced-include termios-speed header) under the original ncurses store path, with its self-references rewritten to that path, and provenance records the swap. The Nix channel keeps stock nixpkgs ncurses, bash, readline and bc. Lucca accepted the checked-in C header (about 25 lines, build glue for the C ncurses build; no ncurses source patch). Rejected: rebuilding bash, readline and bc against the shim in both channels (diverges the Nix channel's bash), and keeping 2.42 (drops Ubuntu 24.04).

comments.author: lucca
comments.text:
Design gate (2026-10-19, edge d4960d4). RED: with glibcFloor 2.39 and no fix, bundle-relink fails with exactly two glibc-floor violations, ncurses-6.6 lib/libncursesw.so.6.6 and bin/tset (needs GLIBC_2.42); the other 463 ELF files pass.
Owners: nix/bundle-relink.nix owns the floor, the substitution list and the rebuilt ncurses (pkgs.ncurses with NIX_CFLAGS_COMPILE -include nix/ncurses-termios-speed.h). eon-relink owns the swap: --substitute ORIGINAL=REPLACEMENT copies REPLACEMENT's tree in place of the shipped ORIGINAL. It rewrites every occurrence of REPLACEMENT's store name (hash-name, same length) to ORIGINAL's in file contents and symlink targets, before the usual relink. It fails if ORIGINAL is not shipped or the names differ. linux-bundle.nix records each pair in provenance.json relink.substituted (schema 2 is unpublished; the field is additive).
Mechanism and references: nixpkgs replaceDependencies (pkgs/build-support/replace-dependencies.nix) rewrites a store path's hash in its dependents. Rejected here because it renames every dependent up to eon itself, breaking EON-C6's same store paths and the Nix product's identity. The equal-length self-reference rewrite is the same technique applied only to the replacement's own files. Rejected: both channels (Lucca, above); binding cfgetospeed@GLIBC_2.2.5 or clearing its version (encoded speeds against the numeric table, so baudrate() returns ERR); an ncurses source patch (the header needs none).
EON-C6: every shipped store path keeps its name and component identity; ncurses-6.6 is the same source and version rebuilt with one compile flag, which the receipts name.
Checks: a relink unit test for the rewrite (multiple occurrences, absolute self-symlink); bundle-relink at floor 2.39 green; bundle-launch (bundled tput through eon-bash still matches the Nix product, and the trace gate catches any unrewritten compiled-in path); manual-bundle on this glibc 2.39 host: the bundle's eon-bash runs (red with the current archive: GLIBC_2.42 not found), plus an Orbit terminal running Bash in an isolated headless sway; eon-test; flake check.

Reviewers seeded invalid --substitute values: a different name, a different length or a subpath gives "not a store path with the same name"; an unshipped original gives "not shipped"; a missing "=" prints usage; each exits 1 before writing.

title: Prove the namespace-free bundle on Ubuntu 26.04 and 24.04
description:
## Why

The final outcome check for epic eon-zti4: a user-owned extracted bundle starts on stock Ubuntu without root, AppArmor changes or user namespaces, and its terminals behave like native host terminals. It runs last because the floor change rebuilds the candidate, and lm9p's rule is that material candidate changes invalidate earlier proof.

## Evidence

- eon-zti4 Acceptance: verify plus extract plus `eon versions`, `eon --help`, the eon-install dry run and install, all with no root step; inside a terminal, NoNewPrivs 0, `id` matches the host, `stat -c %U /usr/bin/sudo` shows root, and `sudo -n true` behaves as on the host.
- eon-install dry run: `installer/src/main.rs:14-16`.
- VM recipe and the red/green baseline: eon-zti4.1 (official cloud images, cloud-init NoCloud seed, QEMU -display none, headless sway, `wtype -s 6000 -k Return` to confirm the directory picker).

## Scope

In scope: one exact candidate archive (and a second one for upgrade and rollback) built from the final edge revision; Ubuntu 26.04 LTS and Ubuntu 24.04 LTS cloud-image VMs with no Nix; manual verify and extract, `eon versions`, `eon --help`, the eon-install dry run, install, upgrade, rollback and remove, a Venus window, and the terminal checks above. Record image sha256s, kernels, glibc versions, archive sha256s and the repository revision.
Out of scope: Fedora (lm9p's matrix), publication, signing anchors, tags.

## Acceptance

- Every listed step passes on both VMs with no root step beyond installing the stand-in desktop packages, and the terminal checks match the host.
- The candidate identity is recorded and handed to eon-qualify-nix-free-linux-public-beta-lm9p.

## Verification

- The VM transcripts are recorded in this bead, with the old bwrap archive's failure as the red baseline on Ubuntu 26.04.

## Stop Conditions

- Stop if any step needs root, a namespace or a host policy change.

title: Let the Darwin build run in a sandboxed builder: drop the /bin/ps test dependency
description:
## Why and remaining goal

The Darwin package/checks should run with the builder sandbox enabled. The original bead attributed the need for an unsandboxed builder to Venus's absolute /bin/ps reaping test (eon-mac-launch-kz4p.7, c24d4ab). That specific dependency was removed by c9c01d1, "Check Venus's stalled-link reaping with kill -0 instead of /bin/ps". Do not implement the obsolete replacement again. Sandbox-enabled native proof remains a distinct gap.

## Current evidence (dcaef1c)

- venus/src/application/tests/selection.rs:4-29, stalled_link_dispatcher_is_bounded_and_reaped: now checks reaping with `kill -0` via PATH; no absolute /bin/ps there.
- eon/tools/mac-proof/src/run.rs:382-386 still says only unsandboxed Darwin builds are proved and records `nix config show sandbox`.
- nix/orbit-checks.nix:64-72 supplies the Darwin pgrep -P shim using nixpkgs ps; orbit/tests/real_pty/support.rs:763 calls pgrep. This is a declared Nix input, not proof of another absolute-host-tool bug.
- Orbit and Runtime already have isolated Darwin libproc seams (orbit/src/platform.rs and runtime/crates/eon-runtime/src/platform.rs); prefer an existing local mechanism only if a remaining failure actually requires one.
- eon-mac-launch-kz4p.8 is closed and provides the SSH-driven native harness. Native proof belongs on an authorized Apple Silicon Mac, not Linux evaluation.

## Scope and prerequisites

One native verification session with bounded fixes only for confirmed sandbox-specific test-tool failures. First run the current package and affected Darwin checks through the existing mac-proof route with sandbox enabled on the actual builder. Record local/remote builder identity and its effective sandbox setting; client-side config or a substituted cached output alone does not prove sandboxed execution. Preserve the original goal and Linux behavior. Do not replace pgrep/libproc merely to remove an already declared build input; remove a shim only if a necessary change leaves it unused.

Contract boundary: EON-C7/VEN-C16/ORB-C14 platform scope, not a new contract or support expansion. Portability: isolated Darwin test/build mechanics. Read root, Venus and any touched Orbit rules, plus Platform Discipline/Testing Discipline before a fix; record applicable reference routes and the exact existing test seams first.

## Acceptance and verification

- The current stalled-link test continues proving kill/reap behavior without an absolute host tool; no absolute /bin tool dependency remains in the supported Darwin test paths (declared Nix store inputs are allowed). A static search identifies the current dependencies rather than assuming /bin/ps still exists.
- A real sandbox-enabled build of packages.aarch64-darwin.default and affected checks runs in the existing harness. Evidence names source tree/revision, builder/OS/Nix, effective sandbox, exact derivations/artifacts, commands and outcomes, and distinguishes rebuilt checks from substitutions.
- If current code passes unchanged, record verification only. If a minimal test/build fix is needed, keep Linux unchanged, preserve the reaping assertion and error handling, run normal whole-workspace/affected Darwin proof and fresh review, and update only the docs/proof caveats justified by actual evidence. No product behavior is changed merely to make the tests pass.

## Stop conditions

Stop for no authorized sandbox-capable Mac/builder, new paid rental/access, a product lifecycle/platform contract change, or a failure outside bounded test-tool scope; report the exact gap instead of widening the bead. Do not claim sandbox support from source inspection/Linux cross-compilation. No native commands, builds or tests run in this planning pass.

Retained sandbox-enabled native build/check proof as the remaining goal, with actual builder identity/setting and no substitution-only claim; no redundant test rewrite or speculative shim removal.

title: Adopt Starcompass's risk-based review (decided against: keep Codex on every code change)
description:
## Why

Lucca chose (2026-10-29) review by risk: Codex before commit only for heavy changes, light changes
after one clean Claude round, and a Codex sweep over light commits. It is implemented upstream in
Starcompass bead ap-xyb (converge trigger and sweep mode, AP-PROMOTION-001 v3). Eon then adopts it
by re-pinning and cutting its local override.

## Prerequisites

- ap-xyb landed in Starcompass (github.com/Yazelix/starcompass) with a recorded commit. Do not start
  before that.

## Scope

In scope:
- Re-pin `.agent-protocols.json` to the Starcompass commit carrying ap-xyb and render AGENTS.md from
  it (apply-agent-protocols skill).
- In `.agent-protocols.local.md` Proof and Review: replace "Codex on every code change" with the
  Eon-only parts: Eon's heavy list (consequential code shape as defined under Contract-Driven
  Method, plus any change that adds or changes an `eon` command or `--json` field, plus contract
  text, status or proof records), the model and effort (`gpt-6.1-sol`, `xhigh`), the candidate-tree
  and narrow re-check loop for the Codex path, and where the last swept commit is recorded (a
  standing bead). Keep "Running Codex" as is.
- Create the standing sweep bead it names.

Out of scope:
- Any code change; the Starcompass text itself (ap-xyb).

## Acceptance

- AGENTS.md renders from the new pin with no drift (audit-agent-protocols), and the local text no
  longer says Codex reviews every code change.
- Lucca approves the exact local text before it is committed.

## Verification

- Planning, docs and agent-policy route: render and import check, changed paths and diff; no
  runtime profile refresh.
close_reason: Decided against (Lucca, 2026-10-29): the evidence in ~/.cache/eon-agents/eon-8e/review-tiering/REPORT.md shows the risk tier would save about one Codex run in eight while giving up real Codex-only defects, and Claude and Codex overlap on only about a fifth of blocking findings. Eon keeps Codex on every code change. Starcompass ap-xyb is rewritten to make both models the converge default.

comments.author: lucca
comments.text: Evidence (2026-10-29, eon-8e; data in ~/.cache/eon-agents/eon-8e/review-tiering/REPORT.md): classifying 246 closed code beads by the proposed rule gives 201 HEAVY and 45 LIGHT. Codex-only real blocking findings (missed by every Claude round): 239 in HEAVY (1.19 per bead) and 25 in LIGHT (0.56 per bead), some serious (Orbit worker exit status, a harness that could delete an existing directory, a proof harness passing after failed cleanup). Venus rendering and proof/gate tooling, both counted LIGHT in the draft, carry most of them. LIGHT beads used about 12.5% of Codex runs (74 of 591). So the rule as drafted saves about one Codex run in eight and gives up about 10% of Codex-only defects. Do not adopt the draft as written; wait for Lucca's decision on the revised direction.

title: Record a recurring Orbit-Venus performance baseline
description: Recurring internal performance verification for the exact accepted Eon, Orbit, and Venus graph. Store one small manual harness in Orbit, reuse the pinned upstream vtebench corpus for PTY-consumption throughput, and retain the accepted orb-bi4.5.4 lifecycle envelope. This changes no EON-C, ORB-C, or VEN-C contract and cannot promote product proof by itself. Confirmed regressions route to one separately authorized owner.
design:
1. Keep one manually invoked shell harness under tools/perf; do not add a framework, crate, package, product mode, protocol, trace format, telemetry, CI schedule, or vendored benchmark source.
2. Require caller-supplied exact Orbit and Venus binaries, a pinned upstream vtebench checkout, and an evidence directory. Record binary hashes, tool revision, host, display, font/grid, power, locale, commands, repetitions, and raw samples.
3. Reuse the complete existing vtebench default corpus. Run three independent invocations with one warmup and up to five samples per file within a ten-second per-benchmark allowance, first after Venus establishes and releases the fixed grid, then with Venus attached. Report raw milliseconds and attached delta only as PTY-consumption and presentation-boundary cost.
4. Reuse orb-bi4.5.4 idle, shell, Neovim, Yazi, sustained-output, resize, detach, reattach, and final-convergence shapes. Keep Orbit, Venus, child, compositor, and benchmark attribution separate.
5. Typometer remains conditional on a display path it can truly observe. Native Wayland is unobservable to its X11 capture owner; record unavailable rather than substitute a proxy.
6. Compare regressions only on the same machine and fixed condition. Retain first-run values as baseline; later runs require both p50 and p95 to exceed baseline by more than 25 percent in two complete runs before routing a defect.
7. Preserve raw evidence outside the repository. Update this Bead with exact summaries and limitations. No CHANGELOG entry.
acceptance_criteria:
1. One tracked, readable manual harness reuses upstream vtebench without copying or vendoring it and has a runnable self-check.
2. The harness records exact component and tool identities, environment, fixed grid, commands, repetitions, warmup, and numeric gates before accepted samples.
3. The full pinned vtebench corpus runs as the real Orbit PTY child three times detached and three times attached under identical geometry, retaining raw DAT and process samples.
4. Idle, shell, Neovim, Yazi, sustained output, 50 resize cycles, Venus loss, and reattachment run under the fixed lifecycle condition with separate process attribution.
5. Native visual latency or visibility that cannot be observed is explicitly unavailable; no internal timestamp, title, Xwayland, wrong-output screenshot, or subjective proxy replaces it.
6. Any rejected calibration or sample is retained and excluded with the exact reason. Every accepted failure names one likely owner boundary and is repaired only in another authorized Bead.
7. README documents the manual command, prerequisites, scope, output, and privacy/focus warning. LOC accounting includes the harness.
8. No product code, product test mode, runtime dependency, manifest, protocol, public result schema, Nix package, CI, schedule, telemetry, or release automation is added.
9. Shell syntax/self-check, repository governance, canonical Rust verification, Beads sync, and git diff checks pass.
10. Closure records either an accepted same-machine baseline or one held-open owner regression, exact raw-evidence location, limitations, and recurring rerun triggers.
notes:
Twelfth convergence candidate is committed in 848445a178b1590cb7b446cdf65aa2b82314421e and remains in progress pending repository governance. The executable manual harness remains 647 lines with SHA-256 ca48618cb3c3691fb2a1ae1fb9b2623f60a3d5224fa3bdb052864471284544c9. README now satisfies the missing privacy half of acceptance criterion 7: beside the existing focus/tiling warning, it states that evidence contains local paths, machine/display details, and process logs and should be reviewed before sharing. This is one sentence at the existing warning owner; no redaction machinery, privacy manifest, helper, or output duplication was added. LOC accounting remains 647 harness lines and 10,206 total implementation lines.

Second-convergence throughput BnX5Bd remains the accepted same-machine baseline, summary SHA-256 437523652be8835514082ecb89891f87282a325040bd1448c9839d8144fb4574. Final current-shape throughput root is /home/lucca/evidence-final/orb-1sd-throughput.GxmO8h. Preflight load was 0.94 and compositor CPU 0 percent. All three detached and three attached invocations completed at 58x93, with six raw DAT and six pidstat files retained. Summary SHA-256 is 1f2e719ffc712a96e6175e24117e1d6f761b114bf0fa532fbf70a6ba8af3f02b. No benchmark exceeded both accepted baseline p50 and p95 by more than 25 percent. title: Expose semantic command regions without replacing the terminal grid
description:
Contract routing:
- Requires a new user-approved semantic-region contract before implementation; this planning Bead reserves no permanent ORB-C* ID.
- Preserves ORB-C1 through ORB-C9 and every accepted predecessor contract and extends the client-neutral presentation boundary.
- Requires a separately owned Venus consumer contract. Planning this Bead changes no contract index or runtime behavior.

## Why

libghostty already interprets shell integration markers into prompt, input, and output semantics, but ORBF v1 discards that structure. Venus therefore cannot offer reliable jump-to-prompt, select/copy-command-output, command-scoped search, or semantic accessibility without guessing from rendered text.

## Evidence

- `docs/REFERENCES.md:62-70` identifies libghostty-vt 0.2.1 as the semantic-state owner whose public presentation surface must be studied.
- `docs/RATIONALE.md:93-100` assigns presentation/history state to Orbit and semantic actions to the client boundary.
- `src/presentation.rs:100-150` extracts cells and frame metadata but no prompt/input/output regions.
- `docs/CONTRACTS.md:27` requires rich state or explicit unsupported capability under ORB-C6.

## Scope

In scope:
- Authoritative prompt, input, and output regions derived from libghostty state.
- A separately approved and proved identity mechanism if semantic regions require identity beyond the current complete-frame revision; ORB-C8 and ORB-C9 do not promise epochs, stable anchors, or a page cache.
- Venus actions for previous/next prompt, select/copy last command output, and bounded command-aware navigation.
- Graceful absence for shells, SSH hops, subshells, and full-screen applications that provide no trustworthy markers.

Out of scope:
- Replacing the terminal grid with Warp-style blocks, parsing shell text, recording command history, rerunning commands, inventing exit status or duration not exposed authoritatively, requiring shell integration, or moving shell policy into Orbit.
design:
## Implementation Notes

1. Add the user-approved semantic-region contract before code and classify compatibility for the exact Venus consumer.
2. Complete the Execution baseline and Reference gate. Required before code: exact libghostty-vt 0.2.1 source for CellSemanticContent, RowSemanticPrompt, selection command-output behavior, and shell-marker handling; current Ghostty shell-integration documentation; and exact Kitty, WezTerm semantic-zone, iTerm2 command-selection, and Warp block-model references as comparisons.
3. Accept only the smallest source evidence: prompt/input/output marks and navigation mechanisms. Reject client-side terminal emulation and block-list replacement.
4. Do not assume a history epoch or stable row anchor. First prove the smallest identity mechanism semantic regions actually require, then state exactly what resize, reflow, pruning, alternate screen, missing markers, malformed marker order, and reconnect do.
5. Transfer compact region metadata rather than duplicating cell contents. Venus decorates and navigates materialized rows but never infers missing regions.
6. Add output selection/copy as semantic actions resolved by Orbit against authoritative state.
7. Land Orbit proof first and then a separate Venus consumer proof.

Dependency decision: no new crate is expected. Existing libghostty and protocol code should own the behavior; any parser or shell-integration dependency requires the Crate gate and user approval.

Portability disposition: neutral terminal semantics and protocol.

## Stop Conditions

- Stop if the published libghostty version does not expose trustworthy semantic marks.
- Stop if trustworthy region identity needs an unapproved stable-history surface or cannot survive the accepted viewport, history, and reflow behavior without ambiguity.
- Stop for user choice if supporting exit status, timing, remote shell integration, or command rerun requires a new owner or public surface.
- Stop if a proposed UI would replace the canonical grid or behave incorrectly without shell integration.
acceptance_criteria:
1. The semantic-region contract is approved and indexed before implementation, maps to exact accepted ORB-C8 and ORB-C9 proofs and the known Venus consumer, and does not assume a stable-history identity that those contracts do not provide.
2. Orbit emits only authoritative prompt, input, and output regions; absent or malformed markers degrade to ordinary terminal behavior without guessed structure.
3. Regions remain coherent across wrapping, resize/reflow, history pruning, alternate screen, partial marker input, detach/reattach, and strictly ordered revisions.
4. Venus can jump between regions and request selection/copy of command output without owning terminal content or a second command-history model.
5. The underlying grid remains the complete presentation authority; full-screen TUIs and unintegrated shells render and interact normally.
6. Exit status, duration, command text, and other metadata are omitted unless the exact authoritative API proves them.
7. Focused checks cover valid, missing, malformed, nested/subshell, history, alternate-screen, and reconnect cases.
8. A separate Venus proof consumes the exact Orbit revision and demonstrates keyboard-accessible navigation and command-output actions.
9. Locked canonical checks pass; closure records references, compatibility, dependency footprint, portability, LOC, proof revisions, and degradation limits.
notes:
Priority P2: high product leverage, but activation waits for the user to select semantic regions as a new single frontier after the final integration-audit chain. Correct region identity may require a separate approved contract because ORB-C8 and ORB-C9 deliberately provide no epoch or stable row-anchor surface.

Rejected alternatives: Warp-style block replacement, prompt-text heuristics, shell-specific parsers in Venus, persistent command recording, automatic rerun, or claiming semantic coverage when markers are absent.

Planning estimate: effort M; implementation risk MED (marker quality and history/reflow identity); confidence HIGH that libghostty's exposed semantics support a useful degrading slice.

## Activation boundary

Do not implement this epic directly. After the user selects this frontier, split it into an Orbit-owned semantic-region contract and metadata proof and a separate Venus-owned navigation, selection, and accessibility consumer proof. If that design requires stable history identity beyond ORB-C8 and ORB-C9, stop for a separate user-approved owner contract before either implementation. Cross-repository acceptance records exact revisions and degradation when authoritative markers are absent.

Readiness reconciliation (2026-08-21): this semantic-regions epic remains a deferred planning container with no active child; activate only after the final integration-audit chain and explicit user selection.

title: Add cost-bounded Linux CI for Orbit
description: Orbit is private and currently has no .github directory, workflow files, or GitHub Actions runs. Add the smallest automatic CI guard for the current Rust verification surface while preventing unexpected paid runner usage and unnecessary depletion of the private-repository minute allowance. This is repository tooling and changes no ORB-C product contract.
design:
Create one GitHub Actions workflow for the existing private repository. Run it automatically only for pushes to edge that touch Rust, Cargo, toolchain, test, or workflow surfaces, plus workflow_dispatch for deliberate reruns. Use one standard Ubuntu job and run the canonical Rust checks sequentially so compilation work is reused within the job:

- cargo fmt --check
- cargo check --locked
- cargo test --locked
- cargo clippy --locked --all-targets -- -D warnings

Set explicit read-only GITHUB_TOKEN permissions, pin every referenced action to a verified full commit SHA, cap the job at 10 minutes, and cancel superseded edge runs with a concurrency group. Log rustc and cargo versions. Do not add a matrix, macOS or Windows runner, larger runner, schedule, nightly build, artifact upload, cache, coverage service, release step, secret, self-hosted runner, or third-party setup action. Do not make the repository public as part of this bead.

Before enabling the workflow, confirm an Actions budget of $0 with stop-usage enabled and billing alerts for the repository or owning account. If repository-scoped budget control is unavailable to the implementing agent, stop and ask the user to configure or confirm it; do not silently enable paid overage. A workflow cannot enforce the account budget itself.

No crate or manifest change is expected. If CI requires a new direct dependency, Cargo feature, toolchain policy, cache, service, or non-GitHub action, stop for the applicable crate or scope decision. The portability disposition is neutral: Linux CI verifies the authorized Linux-first slice and creates no macOS support promise.
acceptance_criteria:
1. Before editing workflow or documentation files, the bead has an Execution baseline and a pre-implementation Reference gate. It explicitly routes no product contract and records the portability disposition as neutral.
2. Exactly one repository workflow is added. It runs on workflow_dispatch and on pushes to edge only when Cargo.toml, Cargo.lock, Rust source, tests, build.rs, Rust toolchain files, or the workflow itself changes. Documentation-only and Beads-only pushes do not consume a run.
3. The workflow contains one standard Ubuntu job. It has a 10-minute timeout and concurrency cancellation for superseded edge revisions.
4. GITHUB_TOKEN permissions are explicitly read-only at the narrowest useful level. Every external action is GitHub-owned, source-reviewed for the used behavior, and pinned to a verified full commit SHA.
5. The job logs toolchain versions and runs cargo fmt --check, cargo check --locked, cargo test --locked, and cargo clippy --locked --all-targets -- -D warnings. All commands exit 0 on the accepted edge revision.
6. The workflow has no OS, Rust-version, feature, or target matrix; no macOS, Windows, larger, or self-hosted runner; no schedule; no cache; no uploaded artifact; no coverage or release service; and no secret or write permission.
7. Before the first hosted run, a $0 GitHub Actions budget with stop-usage enabled and billing alerts is confirmed for the applicable repository or account. If this cannot be verified or requires user billing access, implementation stops before enabling automatic runs and gives the user exact confirmation steps.
8. One cold hosted run succeeds within the timeout. Closure records its URL, elapsed time, billable minutes reported by GitHub, runner type, and the resulting expected monthly-minute envelope for the observed push cadence.
9. README documentation states what triggers CI, what it checks, how to dispatch it manually, and the cost ceiling. README LOC accounting changes only if required by its actual scorecard rules. CHANGELOG.md is not changed because this bead changes no runtime or consumer contract.
10. No Cargo dependency, feature, product behavior, ORB-C entry, public visibility, branch topology, or macOS support commitment changes.
11. The closure notes tell orb-9o6 to extend this established workflow with its governance command after that command exists; this bead does not pull the deferred governance checker forward.
notes: Completed as repository tooling with no ORB-C product-contract change and neutral portability disposition. Ownership is one .github/workflows/ci.yml workflow: path-filtered edge pushes and workflow_dispatch feed one standard ubuntu-24.04 job with workflow/ref concurrency cancellation, a 10-minute timeout, explicit contents:read permission, immutable GitHub-owned actions/checkout v7.0.1 commit 3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1, credential persistence disabled, checksum-verified official Zig 0.15.2 setup, toolchain logging, and the four canonical Cargo commands in order. README.md documents triggers, manual dispatch, checks, and the $0 budget boundary. CHANGELOG.md, docs/CONTRACTS.md, manifests, lockfile, Rust source, tests, public visibility, branch topology, and macOS commitments are unchanged. Dependency footprint: no Cargo or repository-tool dependency; the existing ten-package Rust graph is unchanged; runtime CI inputs are one pinned GitHub action and the official Zig x86_64-linux archive verified with SHA-256 02aa270f183da276e5b5920b1dac44a63f1a49e55050ebde3aecc9eb82f93239. Owned surface is 59 workflow lines plus 14 README lines and zero Rust LOC. title: Accept the Eon ANSI palette at Orbit startup
description:
## Outcome and contract

Consumer: Eon launching a new Orbit-owned terminal session.

Trigger: `yazelix-orbit serve` receives the optional versioned `--ansi-palette-v1` launch value containing exactly sixteen comma-separated six-digit sRGB entries.

Result: Orbit validates the complete value before socket or PTY creation, starts from the existing libghostty 256-color default, replaces only indices 0 through 15, installs it through `set_default_color_palette`, and emits the effective values unchanged in the existing ORBS frame. Omission preserves standalone Orbit defaults. OSC 4 overrides stay program-owned and OSC 104 resets to the supplied default. Direct RGB, foreground/background, and indices 16 through 255 stay unchanged.

Important failures: missing, duplicate, partial, non-hex, or trailing component input fails as one bounded startup error before the child starts.

Contract routing: harden ORB-C2 and ORB-C6; preserve ORB-C1 and ORB-C3 through ORB-C5 plus ORB-C7 through ORB-C11. The user activated eon-kxj on 2026-08-12, approving this compatible producer-first launch boundary and the exact Eon table below. No ORBS revision or new product contract ID.

## Exact Eon table

`000000,cd0000,00cd00,cdcd00,1093f5,cd00cd,00cdcd,faebd7,404040,ff0000,00ff00,ffff00,11b5f6,ff00ff,00ffff,ffffff`

This is the ANSI 0-15 table from the users configured Ghostty Abernathy theme. Foreground `eeeeec`, background `111416`, cursor color, opacity, and all non-ANSI theme settings are comparison evidence only and are not transferred.

## Evidence and shape

- Orbit `e60554623d2ad1e238fac84d0f8f49be0e81e522` parses serve argv before `run_server`, spawns the PTY in `run_server`, and currently constructs libghostty from size and scrollback only.
- Pinned `libghostty-vt` 0.2.1, Ghostty `a887df42c56f6de86c0fe6da9c4eeca37931e083`, exposes the existing `Palette` and `Terminal::set_default_color_palette`; its documented default/current split preserves OSC overrides and reset semantics. No dependency or schema change is needed.
- Orbit presentation already emits the complete effective palette. Eon owns the fixed product table and launch policy; Orbit remains the sole terminal owner; Venus remains an unchanged ORBS consumer.
- Nova direct colors such as `00ff88`, `ffff00`, and `00ccff` are comparisons and must remain exact. YZX Anima uses named indexed colors, which exposed the muted defaults.

Minimum shape: one parser, one optional `[RgbColor; 16]` value passed into the existing server owner, one replacement of the first sixteen entries in the existing libghostty palette, and focused parser plus real-terminal presentation checks. No config system, environment-per-color input, theme registry, shell escape injection, synthetic OSC, dependency, compatibility layer, or public ORBS change.

Platform: neutral above the existing isolated Linux process seam; no new macOS blocker.

## Acceptance

1. Valid exact input appears in the first ORBS frame and survives detach/reattach.
2. Malformed, partial, duplicate, missing-value, and trailing launch input exits before socket and PTY creation.
3. OSC 4 overrides one index; indexed and full OSC 104 reset to the supplied table.
4. Direct RGB and indices 16 through 255 remain exact; omission preserves current standalone defaults.
5. Locked Rust, governance, Clippy, and diff checks pass. Publish the proof revision before Eon consumes it.

## Required references

Required before code: this complete Bead and comments; current CLI, terminal owner, extraction, lifecycle checks, ORB-C1/C2/C6; `docs/REFERENCES.md`; pinned libghostty-vt 0.2.1 palette API and Ghostty commit above. Comparison only: configured Ghostty/Abernathy, Nova Bar `d659fdf5ae0b4013aacaf31399e2bab064654320`, packaged Anima `d22d091d427af0be307056c65e475802b602d386`. Rejected: all broader theme/configuration/rendering scope.

Stop if the setter does not preserve overrides/reset, if ORBS must change, if a dependency or fork is required, or if another active issue owns the CLI or terminal path.

title: Establish the Orbit terminal conformance corpus
description:
Create the smallest durable Orbit-owned conformance corpus for the terminal semantics Eon actually relies on. Its primary purpose is to protect Orbit's observable contracts while libghostty is upgraded, packaged, ported, or refactored. Qualifying a separately authorized alternative engine is a secondary use, not this Bead's implementation scope.

Observable contract for this verification surface:
- Consumer: Orbit maintainers and coding agents.
- Trigger: a material terminal-engine, binding, build, platform, or Orbit-adapter change, or a separately approved candidate-engine spike.
- Result: one deterministic local check exercises a bounded named set of terminal byte streams and semantic inputs and reports whether canonical Orbit-owned observations still satisfy accepted contracts.
- Important failures: a mismatch is classified as an Orbit regression, upstream engine behavior change or defect, unsupported candidate capability, or corpus expectation error. The corpus never silently broadens product compatibility.

Contract routing:
- Planning and implementation add no user-visible behavior, product contract, compatibility promise, or public format.
- The implementation classifies ORB-C2, ORB-C4, ORB-C5, ORB-C6, ORB-C8, and ORB-C9 as hardened; their accepted behavior remains unchanged. Reconfirm their exact accepted proof revisions at activation.
- Other ORB-C contracts remain outside unless a concrete existing case cannot be separated and its routing is recorded before edits.

In scope:
- Inventory and reuse the strongest deterministic cases already present in src/presentation.rs, src/main.rs, tests/lifecycle.rs, and orbit-protocol tests; treat the retired Formatter-reconstruction suite as historical negative evidence rather than restoring it.
- Organize a small contract-oriented set covering partial parser input, primary and alternate screens, pending wrap, Unicode width and combining behavior, styles and colors, hyperlinks, cursor, title and working directory, terminal replies, semantic input encoding, resize and reflow, viewport and retained-history behavior, selection and copy, and canonical presentation extraction where those behaviors are already accepted.
- Record for each case its stimulus, Orbit-visible observation, semantic invariant or required exact value, and owning contract or regression.
- Use exact byte or frame equality only where the accepted contract requires it; otherwise assert the narrow semantic invariant.
- Run the current pinned libghostty path through existing public APIs with one local command.

Out of scope:
- Adding, selecting, or shipping rio-vt, another terminal engine, or a second production backend.
- A runtime engine trait, feature flag, dual-engine build, compatibility layer, fork, binding extension, new repository, new binary, public replay or trace format, or new dependency.
- Copying or vendoring upstream suites, exhaustive DEC or xterm certification, Venus visual quality, performance benchmarking, hosted CI, or general PTY lifecycle duplication.
design:
Implementation plan:

1. Reread the accepted contracts and inventory every relevant existing test before choosing a shape. Reuse or move one owner for each case; do not copy expectations into a new parallel suite.
2. Complete the Execution baseline and Reference gate before test or manifest edits. Required before code: exact accepted Orbit contracts and tests; pinned libghostty-vt and Ghostty source identities and their applicable public/test surfaces; and the exact FrankenTUI reference routed for deterministic proof architecture. Upstream tests inform coverage ownership but are not imported.
