title: Qualify the Venus stack on Apple Silicon macOS
description:
## Why

The Venus semantic model, scene, renderer, and application loop are intended to remain shared for VEN-C16, but the locked dependency surface is Linux-specific and includes a patched winit revision. Qualify that exact stack on Apple Silicon macOS before selecting dependencies or splitting the native implementation epic. This is research evidence, not a support claim or production change.

## Evidence

- `Cargo.toml:8-20`: AccessKit selects `accesskit_unix`, wgpu selects Vulkan, winit selects Wayland, clipboard ownership is `wl-clipboard-rs`, and winit is replaced by exact fork revision `fb45fbf901fbe70cc9a877b5d651d0b60c206b08`.
- `src/main.rs:3-4`: the binary deliberately rejects every non-Linux target.
- `src/application.rs:26-35`: the shared application owner imports a Wayland window extension beside otherwise cross-platform winit types.
- `src/application.rs:1688-1690,1940+`: native clipboard effects currently call `wl-clipboard-rs` directly.
- `src/render.rs:649+`: one wgpu/glyphon renderer owns the native surface; its native proof is currently Wayland/Vulkan-only.
- `ven-prove-venus-apple-silicon-macos-nm7`: the deferred VEN-C16 epic requires this dependency/tool gate before native code.

## Decision contract

- Consumer: the later VEN-C16 implementation planner.
- Trigger: inspect and, on a temporary Apple Silicon macOS checkout, minimally exercise the exact locked Venus dependency graph.
- Result: a recorded Go, conditional-Go, or no-Go decision names the smallest target-specific Cargo features and native host seams that preserve one shared model/scene/renderer/application path.
- Important failures: an unhealthy patched fork, unavailable Metal/AccessKit path, required renderer duplication, new native-library ownership, entitlement, or unbounded dependency expansion stops the decision and returns to the user.

## Scope

In scope:
- Inspect exact current source and release evidence for winit plus its pinned fork, wgpu, glyphon, AccessKit/accesskit_winit, raw-window-handle, Rust Apple targets, and credible clipboard mechanisms including no new dependency.
- Compare the pinned winit fork with its upstream macOS backend for material divergence.
- On a standard GitHub Actions `macos-15` M1 runner, use a disposable checkout to establish the smallest feature and compile-gate patch needed to check the shared library/application/renderer owners. Retain the proposed diff and command output as decision evidence; do not merge it.
- Add only the bounded qualification workflow needed to reach that runner: manual dispatch, one job, read-only contents permission, concurrency cancellation, a 20-minute timeout, two temporary read-only deploy-key secrets for the exact Eon and Eon Sessions revisions, and no paid or larger runner.
- Delete both deploy keys and Actions secrets and restore the organization deploy-key policy after the final qualification run.
- Name the exact later owners for target-specific dependencies, native clipboard, accessibility adapter, application lifecycle/window attributes, Metal surface/transparency, and their cheapest behavioral proofs.

Out of scope:
- Production source, Cargo, lockfile, Nix, contract-status, or documentation changes other than the mechanically required README LOC scorecard; push, pull-request, or scheduled macOS automation; larger runners; paid overage; broad personal tokens, GitHub Apps, or lasting credentials; and caching before a measured repeated-build need.
- Orbit integration, native UI behavior, transparency/blur acceptance, clipboard delivery, accessibility dogfood, Eon composition, signing, notarization, packaging, Intel macOS, or a VEN-C16 proof claim.
- Selecting a generic platform framework, host trait hierarchy, second event loop, second renderer/model, or shared cross-repository platform crate.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. Record exact inspected versions/revisions, primary sources, macOS environment, commands, temporary diff, results, and limitations in this bead.
2. On real Apple Silicon macOS, capture the current locked failure first, then show whether one minimal disposable feature/compile-gate patch can check the shared Venus owners with winit AppKit, wgpu Metal, glyphon, and AccessKit macOS.
3. State whether the pinned winit fork preserves an acceptable macOS backend or must be replaced/expanded; any fork or dependency decision remains unapproved until the user accepts its gate.
4. Compare native-owned code, standard/platform APIs, already-present crates, and maintained clipboard candidates for correctness, accessibility, transitive cost, licensing, API stability, and removal cost. Select nothing unless the evidence makes one option strictly sufficient.
5. Produce a concise owner map and recommended child-bead split for `ven-prove-venus-apple-silicon-macos-nm7`, with one failure domain and cheapest proof per child.
6. Explicitly state that compilation is feasibility evidence only and does not change VEN-C16 support or proof status.

## Verification

- `cargo metadata --locked --format-version 1` identifies the exact dependency graph without mutation.
- `cargo tree --locked --target aarch64-apple-darwin` identifies the candidate target graph.
- A bounded disposable `cargo check --locked --all-targets` on `aarch64-darwin` records either success or the exact blockers after the minimum temporary patch.
- The normal Eon Desktop working tree remains unchanged except for Beads state, the bounded manual qualification workflow, its disposable patch artifact, and the mechanically required README LOC scorecard.

## Stop Conditions

- Stop if the cited dependency pins or VEN-C16 ownership have materially changed.
- Stop before committing any production source/configuration change or adding any dependency, fork revision, native library, entitlement, or support promise; only the bounded workflow, its disposable patch artifact, Beads evidence, and required README LOC scorecard may persist.
- Stop when the included private Actions allowance is exhausted; evaluate public repository visibility only through a separate user decision and full-history security/license review.
- Stop if qualification would require a duplicate renderer/model/event loop, a paid or larger runner, or more than the bounded Apple Silicon allowance.

## Maintenance Notes

With Orbit `ORB-C14` accepted, this decision is the active Venus research frontier. It does not consume `ORB-C14` because it neither attaches to Orbit nor implements native Venus behavior. The VEN-C16 epic remains deferred until this decision closes and the user activates implementation work.
notes: Rejected up front: generic platform abstraction, second renderer or event loop, documentation-only support inference, selecting a clipboard crate before comparison, and treating compilation as VEN-C16 proof. Use a disposable checkout so the decision leaves no production diff.

title: Record accepted VEN-C13 native clipboard dogfood
description:
## Contract Routing

This is a documentation and proof-record reconciliation. It changes no VEN product contract, runtime behavior, source proof, dependency, protocol, compatibility promise, or consumer code.

Consumer: maintainers and downstream repositories determining the accepted VEN-C13 native-delivery evidence and remaining platform gaps.

Trigger: inspect VEN-C13 after exact Venus source `2d3498258920736eb1bdae2b8869b6547b9735d4` was packaged by accepted Eon `0e25ebc2311d7e41edf90c940f8211dd5839bb83` and dogfooded through Eonova `4fda9b67b0faa33561624633229135e5e2d579ea`.

Result: Venus's canonical contract record cites that exact external acceptance evidence, closes only the native Linux primary-selection dogfood gap it exercised, retains `Partially proved` and the existing Venus source proof, and states the remaining Wayland-without-data-control, macOS, and broader-compositor gaps precisely.

Important failures: do not reprove Venus from a documentation edit, widen one primary-selection observation to every destination/compositor, rewrite history, claim macOS, or make Eon/Eonova a second VEN-C13 owner.

Impact: LOW-MED. Effort: S. Implementation risk: LOW. Confidence: HIGH.

## Why

The current VEN-C13 row still says native delivery dogfood is open. Exact accepted downstream evidence already packaged the VEN-C13 source and observed a terminal-emitted UTF-8 primary write through the native Wayland primary selection, while also proving detached-write denial and preserving live processes. Leaving that evidence only in Eon's tracker makes Venus's canonical owner record and Orbit's consumer-gap prose stale.

## Evidence

- `docs/CONTRACTS.md:16`: VEN-C13 is `Partially proved` at Venus `2d349825...` but lists all native delivery dogfood as open.
- `Cargo.toml:13`: current Venus retains canonical orbit-protocol/ORBS v3 at Orbit `3ee7c80005f3d2bbe81e539799327803716f6174`.
- Eon closed Bead `eon-refresh-clipboard-runtimes-0pt`, acceptance comment 369: published Eon `0e25ebc...` selected Venus `2d349825...`, published Eonova `4fda9b67...`, and observed exact UTF-8 `eon-primary-proof-0e25ebc` through `wl-paste`; the pre-attachment attempt made no clipboard change and live Eonova processes retained identity.
- Eon `docs/CONTRACTS.md:280-322` at `3ee61a1b985fb1f44fc6ee0967c0c331b589a4b2` retains the same package, NAR, rollout, and dogfood evidence.
- Closed Orbit audit `orb-audit-orbit-integration-ur9`, finding 3, independently verified the exact Eon/Eonova proof chain and routed the stale owner record here.
- Orbit's open `orb-reconcile-venus-orbs-v3-docs-4ts` should consume this corrected owner record rather than independently reinterpret the downstream evidence.

## Reference Classification

Required before editing:

- Current `AGENTS.md`, this complete Bead, `docs/CONTRACTS.md`, README, CHANGELOG, and exact VEN-C13 source/proof history.
- Exact Eon `eon-refresh-clipboard-runtimes-0pt` description and acceptance evidence, Eon `docs/CONTRACTS.md:280-322`, and published sources `0e25ebc...` and `4fda9b67...`.
- Exact Eon component graph at `0e25ebc...`, proving it selected Venus `2d349825...`, Orbit/ORB-C11 `3ee7c800...`, and ORBS v3.

Comparison only:

- Current Orbit ORB-C11 row and open docs reconciliation, solely to align ownership and wording.

Rejected scope:

- Re-running native dogfood, changing VEN-C13 behavior/status/source proof, editing Eon/Eonova/Orbit, changing clipboard policy, or claiming unexercised standard-destination, compositor, or platform behavior.

No crate or dependency decision is involved.

## Scope

In scope:

- `docs/CONTRACTS.md` VEN-C13 evidence and gap text.
- A directly stale present-tense proof statement in README only if exact inspection finds one.
- Preserve historical source proof and chronological changelog entries.

Out of scope:

- Product code, tests, manifests, lockfiles, proof-bearing commits, dependencies, protocols, Eon/Eonova/Orbit files, general documentation cleanup, or new native testing.

## Implementation Notes

1. Reverify the exact Eon graph, published sources, package identity, and acceptance comment.
2. Keep VEN-C13 `Partially proved` and its Venus source proof unchanged.
3. Add the downstream native primary-selection dogfood as separately owned acceptance evidence, naming exact Eon/Eonova sources and exercised surface.
4. Narrow the remaining gap to native Wayland without data-control, macOS destination policy, broader compositor coverage, and any unexercised native destination.
5. Do not add a changelog entry because this reconciliation changes no accepted behavior.

Portability disposition: neutral documentation; the recorded proof remains x86_64 Linux.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. VEN-C13 cites the exact accepted Eon `0e25ebc...`, Eonova `4fda9b67...`, and Venus `2d349825...` evidence chain.
2. The row states exactly that native Wayland primary-selection delivery and detached-write denial were observed.
3. VEN-C13 remains `Partially proved` at its existing source proof; no docs commit is represented as runtime proof.
4. Remaining Wayland-without-data-control, macOS, broader-compositor, and unexercised-destination gaps remain explicit.
5. Eon/Eonova remain acceptance consumers, not owners of Venus clipboard behavior.
6. Historical proof identities and accurate changelog entries remain unchanged.
7. No code, test, manifest, lockfile, dependency, protocol, or consumer repository changes.
8. Venus planning lint and diff checks pass.

## Verification

- Inspect exact Eon `eon-refresh-clipboard-runtimes-0pt` and `docs/CONTRACTS.md:280-322`.
- `rg -n 'VEN-C13|2d349825|0e25ebc|4fda9b67|native delivery|primary' docs/CONTRACTS.md README.md CHANGELOG.md` should show one coherent current record.
- `git diff --check` should exit 0.
- `br lint <this-id>` should report no issue.
- `br sync --flush-only` should persist planning state.

## Stop Conditions

- Stop if the exact Eon graph did not package Venus `2d349825...` or the recorded observation cannot be tied to that artifact.
- Stop if reconciliation would require changing VEN-C13 behavior, status, proof revision, or adding a contract.
- Stop if another active issue owns the same documentation surface.
- Stop before editing Eon, Eonova, or Orbit.

## Maintenance Notes

External dogfood may close a gap without moving the source proof. Keep source implementation proof, downstream composition proof, and platform observation distinct.

title: Release supervised Venus after Eon owner loss
description:
## Outcome and contract routing

Harden the existing supervised-presentation boundary in VEN-C14; add no public protocol or standalone lifecycle promise.

Consumer: Venus launched by Eon with the existing private presentation-control opt-in.

Trigger: the supervising Eon process disappears or closes its control stream, including abrupt supervisor loss, while Orbit and PTY work remain live.

Result: Venus treats control-stream EOF or terminal read failure as loss of its Eon owner and exits its native event loop without stopping Orbit. If an immediate replacement managed Venus briefly receives ORBS Busy from the departing client, it uses the existing bounded retry owner until the old attachment is released. Direct standalone Venus retains terminal Busy behavior.

Important failures: malformed or partial control input never presents a window; owner loss never sends a signal, stops a Session, scans processes, invents terminal state, or changes EONW/ORBS. A control worker that cannot notify the event loop terminates without creating another owner.

Exact starting point: accepted Venus source 8e2d22a36ae6f6cab74d3556204a2a537265bff7, accepted by metadata 2212b95142d96c97181313c45480212d4de920d5, with VEN-C3, VEN-C4, and VEN-C14 proved. Eon consumer work remains in eon-consume-orbit-same-boot-management-2y7 against exact Orbit 86aa130629c09dce61d0f232150298656fa5cef4.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Launch the current accepted Eon workspace until Venus is attached to Orbit; record the supervisor, Venus, Orbit, and PTY identities.
2. SIGKILL only the Eon supervisor.
3. Observe that Orbit and PTY work correctly survive, but Venus also remains alive after its private control peer is gone, repeatedly finds EONW unavailable, and retains the sole ORBS presentation attachment; a second Venus receives Busy.
4. The focused mechanism reproducer uses a connected UnixDatagram pair: close the peer and observe that the reader remains blocked instead of receiving EOF.

## Scope boundary

In scope: the existing stdin presentation-control worker, one typed native exit event, managed-only Busy retry selection through the existing retry machinery, focused deterministic regressions, current VEN-C3/VEN-C4/VEN-C14 text, README, changelog, LOC, and an isolated managed-client lifecycle observation.

Out of scope: public control protocol, EONW or ORBS vocabulary, Orbit/Eon source changes, Session shutdown, durable Venus identity, process discovery, pidfiles, signals, a helper/service, new dependency, global Busy retry, window adoption, reboot/logout recovery, macOS proof, or compatibility adapter.

## Acceptance Criteria

The canonical completion criteria are stored in this Bead's acceptance_criteria field.
design:
## Reference and dependency gate

Before code, reread VEN-C3, VEN-C4, VEN-C14, the accepted VEN-C14 presentation reference route, current Application/UserEvent and transport completion owners, exact Eon PresentationProcess construction, and exact Unix stream/descriptor semantics on the proof platforms. Record the accepted Eon and Orbit producer identities at the implementation gate.

Decision: keep Venus transient and make the existing opt-in control channel the sole managed-client lifetime signal. Eon must replace its current UnixDatagram pair with a stream because closing a connected Unix datagram peer does not produce readable EOF on the accepted Linux host. Venus owns translating stream completion into native exit and owns managed-only retry classification. Reuse UserEvent and the existing retry scheduler; add no protocol value, dependency, thread, process identity, or second state machine.

Reject parent-death signals because Linux prctl would create a macOS blocker; reject PID/start-time records, process scans, raw signals, stable adoption sockets, EONW commands, and Orbit presentation introspection because they add authority or vocabulary merely to terminate a transient client.

## Minimum vertical slice

1. Represent supervised launch explicitly from the existing environment opt-in; standalone launch remains unchanged.
2. Keep exact present-command decoding. When the control reader ends for EOF or read failure, send one typed exit event. The application exits through winit's existing event-loop owner; normal Rust drop releases EONW and ORBS transports and never stops Orbit.
3. Under supervised launch only, classify an ORBS Busy received during startup/replacement as retryable through the existing bounded backoff. Do not change standalone Busy or any incompatible, exited, malformed, resource, queue, input, or worker-start terminal failure.
4. Add one deterministic reader/event regression and one managed-versus-standalone Busy policy regression. Reuse existing transport checks; do not create a harness framework.
5. In isolated native or headless-composed proof, close the stream, observe prompt Venus exit with Orbit and PTY identities unchanged, then launch a replacement immediately and observe canonical attachment without terminal Busy.
6. Update the exact contract proof and hand the accepted Venus source/metadata identities to the blocked Eon consumer.
acceptance_criteria:
1. Existing supervised present input still preserves the same Venus process and ORBS attachment and requests presentation exactly once.
2. Closing or failing the supervised control stream causes Venus to exit promptly through its native event-loop owner; Orbit, its PTY child, terminal state, and Eon workspace state remain live and unchanged.
3. An immediate replacement supervised Venus may absorb only the transient Busy race through the existing bounded retry cadence and then attaches to the same authoritative Orbit state. Standalone Busy remains terminal and visible.
4. Each complete present frame requests presentation once; malformed or partial frames do not present or stop anything, and stream termination still has one bounded exit result.
5. No EONW/ORBS change, new dependency, signal, pidfile, process scan, helper, public control surface, compatibility path, or macOS runtime claim is added.
6. Focused red/green checks plus cargo fmt --check, cargo check --locked, cargo test --locked, cargo clippy --locked --all-targets -- -D warnings, docs/contract IDs, LOC, and git diff --check pass on one unchanged candidate.
7. Source proof is committed before proof metadata. VEN-C3/VEN-C4/VEN-C14 and this Bead name the exact accepted source and metadata commits and preserve explicit platform/proof limits.
notes: Planning-only fresh-eyes correction authorized by the user on 2026-08-20. Current Eon uses UnixDatagram::pair for the control fd; a disposable Linux socketpair observation confirmed that peer close leaves recv blocked rather than yielding EOF, while Venus also currently ends only the reader thread on read completion. This ready, unclaimed Venus owner issue is the exact prerequisite for Eon same-boot recovery; no implementation or contract file changed in this planning run.
close_reason: Corrected canonical proof attribution: a768e9a1 remains the accepted mechanical source, while native owner-loss evidence is explicitly scoped to predecessor 754eb057; no runtime or LOC change.

title: Render Anima half-block graphics without repeated text shaping
description:
## Outcome and contract

A user viewing dense Anima graphics in Venus gets exact, correctly colored half-block cells without repeated font shaping for those cells. For an authoritative narrow cell containing exactly U+2580 (▀) or U+2584 (▄), cover the upper or lower half of its cell using its resolved foreground; retain the existing background and style semantics. Preserve ordinary text shaping, U+2588 full blocks, accessibility/text diagnostics, selection, cursor, decorations, clipping and retained-history previews. Wide cells, combined text and other Block Elements are outside this classification.

Harden existing VEN-C1; preserve VEN-C2/C7/C8/C11/C18/C19. No new contract or universal FPS guarantee. Venus owns the scene-to-draw correction; Orbit retains terminal state and Anima retains generation. Current VEN-C1 consumes ORB-C4/ORB-C6 through canonical ORBF v2 / ORBS v13 at Orbit 6bc269c40b18f08b95778939518f77556ba91c67, retaining proof ea9fd28ce0908f218cf65d4e6df368f0a4e565f5. Reconfirm accepted identities before implementation. Platform classification: neutral presentation invariant; native proof target is x86_64 Linux Wayland, with no macOS proof claim.

## Evidence and prerequisites

Completed Eon investigation eon-investigate-anima-performance-vs-nova-g92d measured the same Anima b3133f057fa0029b3e06c85301161168c48bb799 binary at 160×48 plasma cells. Installed Venus a27aad23822d3bd0b0e467ffc32c578bbde8b00d produced 5.08–5.23 visible changes/s and 217–233 ms p95 gaps versus installed Nova 20.15–23.08 changes/s and 67 ms p95. Venus used 90–92% of one core. Its plasma profile attributed 70.31% of CPU-core samples to cosmic-text font fallback through build_scene_text/push_text; aquarium showed the same stack. Sparse matrix was an unaffected discovery control. Current Venus only bypasses shaping for full-block █. A named-font control improved cadence, but is diagnostic rather than a product default.

Raw identities, recordings, profiles, commands and limits: /home/lucca/.local/state/eon/proofs/anima-performance-2026-10-08/report.txt and clean-results.json. Private Sway/GLES2 used Intel/i915 hardware; the original live COSMIC launch surface remains unverified. Preserve Nova's 500 ms stall and 1041 ms dismissal outlier. Earlier discovery runs had sampling gaps and cannot supply final absolute cadence/latency evidence.

ven-render-full-block-cells-without-seams-l9d is accepted precedent, not an open duplicate or blocker. No runtime prerequisite is unresolved for this local correction. Claim only when the sequential frontier and the scene/render owners are free; preserve concurrent work. The user selected implementation on 2026-10-08; the accepted source and proof are recorded below.

## Reference gate before code

Required: current AGENTS.md; docs/CONTRACTS.md VEN-C1/C11/C19; docs/REFERENCES.md selected rendering/typography routes; complete src/scene.rs and src/render.rs cell/run, foreground visibility, rectangle, preview and clipping owners; l9d's complete gate/proof comments; exact Anima b3133f057fa0029b3e06c85301161168c48bb799 HalfBlockField::render_lines and the three reported styles; locked glyphon 0.12.0/cosmic-text 0.19.0 shaping/fallback; Ghostty 45db2c2551ecc016f9746e8e2855f4f8a3871e7b exact-cell Block Elements geometry as a comparable implementation. Record exact inspected identities and applicable licenses before edits; inspection selects no source reuse or dependency.

Comparison only: installed Nova 5bd9c8e54fbd4a719401d22ec531a0408f8c055b / Rio 2ad2987d0580855393667651ce1d22f094901a23 as measured performance baseline, and Kinestra d1589705677dc001304584150557e67cef67f580 as isolated capture pattern. Their renderer/PTY/configuration mechanisms are not selected.

Chosen implementation: extend the existing exact-cell rectangle owner and omit only the classified cells from text shaping, including adjacent same-style cells and history previews. Current glyph runs retain one authoritative cell per run. Keep classification owned once at the boundary that retains authoritative cell identity; do not reconstruct terminal state or overlay retained glyphs, which can double-compose alpha. The reference gate below confirms this shape.

## Acceptance

- A focused failing-then-passing renderer regression proves top/bottom coverage, shared edges, resolved foreground/background and no bleed at scales 1/1.25/1.5/2, including adjacent repeated same-style half blocks. Preserve faint/hidden/blink/inverse, default-background opacity, selection/cursor/decorations and pane/row/preview clipping. Reject combined/wide/non-target cells from the shortcut; ordinary text/full blocks remain correct.
- Repeat fixed 160×48 dense plasma baseline/candidate samples on the same native GPU, recording visible interval distributions, renderer/Orbit/Anima CPU, exact revisions and raw evidence. Show repeatable cadence/tail improvement and removal of the measured half-block shaping bottleneck; a cheaper CPU profile alone is insufficient. If the visible gap remains, reprofile rather than declaring the defect fixed.
- Focused aquarium and physarum observations preserve appearance/responsiveness; matrix remains unaffected. Include a sufficiently dense physarum state rather than extrapolating its sparse startup. Preserve Escape dismissal and terminal-mode cleanup. Do not add a broad benchmark matrix.
- Run the affected locked Rust checks and native rendering observation; distinguish deterministic fractional geometry from actual native fractional-scale proof. Record immutable source/proof identity and remaining compositor/platform gaps before acceptance. Update owned contract proof metadata, changelog and LOC only for accepted implementation.

## Scope boundary and handoff

No Anima logger/FPS feature, lowered producer cadence, font-default change, generic glyph/cache framework, renderer replacement, new module/dependency/protocol, CI matrix, Nova change or new platform. Stop for ownership/contract/dependency expansion or if style fidelity cannot be preserved. Complete at an accepted Venus source revision; Eon pin/package/profile delivery is a separate dependent bead. Preserve live terminals and desktop focus throughout.

title: Render animated Braille progress glyphs faithfully
description:
## Why

Eonova shows an animated Braille progress glyph while Codex is working, but the producer is not yet proved: it may be Codex terminal content, Zellij pane-title content, or native title metadata. In the installed Eonova path the glyph is missing or malformed, while the comparison Zellij presentation is recognizable. This is a visible terminal-fidelity defect, but the owner must be proved before code changes.

Smallest observable contract:
- Consumer: a local user viewing terminal content materialized by Venus.
- Trigger: an accepted canonical Orbit frame contains a narrow Braille-pattern cell from U+2800 through U+28FF, including successive spinner revisions adjacent to ordinary or box-drawing cells.
- Result: Venus presents the exact authored glyph in its authoritative cell on every accepted revision, without disappearance, clipping, substitution, overlap, or stale pixels in adjacent cells.
- Important failure: if Orbit does not author the expected scalar/cell width, return the gap to Orbit. If only the native window title or compositor is wrong, do not compensate in the terminal renderer.

Contract routing:
- Hardens proved VEN-C1 frame-to-draw fidelity; no new Venus contract is proposed.
- Preserves VEN-C2, VEN-C3, VEN-C4, VEN-C7, VEN-C8, and candidate VEN-C9; preserves canonical ORBS v2, EONW v1, input, geometry, lifecycle, and workspace behavior.
- Consumes unchanged Orbit ORBS v2 at accepted proof `9d6d2bb37f20ab4ad9e186c7bc715eabef43e757`.
- Changes no Orbit or Eon contract unless owner-first reproduction proves a boundary gap, in which case stop and report it rather than adding a Venus workaround.

## Evidence

- User observation on 2026-08-10: active Eonova profile `91a31a8772d74d89f8a9399df1338c592ef0c1e6` at `/nix/store/3xnb1pd547mw6rf9gppwvn9ndm3b20z6-eonova-0.1.0` pins Eon `ec0fa0fd0bb6d78a0d37281b069899d1bd13b95e` and Nova `6c7174b4efca5f139a461d204186c5001d6457bd`; that Eon consumes Orbit `64db581445bafca1a08a6530f8e44f9c1edbc169` and Venus `690b038e2b58a0e7761023ac7e004e92327ac901`. Codex CLI is 0.147.0 and comparison Zellij is 0.44.3.
- The malformed Eonova crop is SHA-256 `095a9db2fea47c1c67d42015d05a4e6198f7e157b4771cd5c241b578826ad220`; the recognizable Zellij crop is SHA-256 `1b10f18fbe3c126451d9c6ebbb684bca4b4cfe10efd387c32491ac4fac4dee5d`. The screenshots are discovery evidence, not a deterministic oracle.
- `src/scene.rs:437-508` copies canonical Orbit cell text and width into glyph runs without interpreting terminal bytes.
- `src/render.rs:717-743` projects each glyph run onto the authoritative cell grid; `src/render.rs:825-898` shapes terminal cells with the selected monospace family and exact grid width.
- `src/render.rs:929-973` uses advanced shaping for non-ASCII content, including Braille patterns.
- `src/render.rs:1490-1623` proves ASCII, styled Unicode box-drawing, emitted cell advances, and preedit width, but has no Braille fallback/raster or animated-revision case.
- Closed `ven-ogd` corrected accumulated cell advances and table borders. Its proof does not establish that a fallback glyph exists, remains inside clipping bounds, or redraws cleanly for Braille spinner revisions.
- `src/main.rs:518-523` separately applies Orbit frame title metadata to the native window title. This must be distinguished from terminal-cell rendering during reproduction.
- Eonova runs `Eon terminal host -> Nova yzx enter -> Zellij workspace`; Eon workspace mode and Venus EONW pane headers are inactive. The visible border/title may therefore be Zellij-authored terminal content rather than a Venus workspace header.

Impact: MED for perceived terminal quality and Codex dogfooding.
Effort: S if the existing font/shaping owner is sufficient; M if exact evidence identifies a font-package boundary.
Implementation risk: MED because fallback, clipping, raster cache, cell geometry, and packaging can interact.
Confidence: HIGH that the visual defect exists; MED on the owning layer until the canonical frame is inspected.

## Scope

In scope:
- Owner-first reproduction in the exact Eonova profile, followed by isolated plain `eon terminal -- COMMAND` with the same Eon/Venus generation and a controlled Braille corpus.
- The existing scene/text-layout/raster path in `src/scene.rs` and `src/render.rs`, only where the reproduced defect resides.
- One focused failing-then-passing regression using the exact authored Braille spinner sequence and adjacent border/text cells.
- Native COSMIC Wayland dogfood using the distribution-equivalent Nix candidate.
- VEN-C1 proof/check metadata, user-visible changelog only if behavior changes, and README LOC accounting.

Out of scope:
- Parsing Codex output, inventing spinner state, changing ORBF/ORBS/EONW, pane-title features, Eon pane-label policy, terminal-title heuristics, renderer replacement, font settings UI, a general fallback system, unrelated typography, or another dependency.
- Editing Orbit or Eon in this Bead. Route a confirmed owner gap to that repository for separate user-approved work.
- Treating the screenshots, Zellij internals, or native window-title behavior as the terminal-cell oracle.

## References Before Code

Required:
- Current `AGENTS.md`, VEN-C1 and preserved contracts, `docs/CRATES.md`, `docs/REFERENCES.md`, and the complete scene/render/font owners and focused tests.
- Exact accepted Orbit proof `9d6d2bb37f20ab4ad9e186c7bc715eabef43e757`, current Orbit producer `64db581445bafca1a08a6530f8e44f9c1edbc169`, and the canonical frame/cell-width path.
- Exact locked glyphon 0.12.0 and cosmic-text 0.19.0 shaping, fallback, monospace-width, clipping, and raster-cache behavior.
- Eonova `91a31a8772d74d89f8a9399df1338c592ef0c1e6`, pinned Eon `ec0fa0fd0bb6d78a0d37281b069899d1bd13b95e`, its generated Fontconfig, and pinned Nova `6c7174b4efca5f139a461d204186c5001d6457bd` to establish the exact composition and fonts available to the candidate.

Comparison only:
- The supplied recognizable Zellij 0.44.3 presentation and crop are visual comparison evidence, not an implementation template or correctness owner. Inspect producer source only under the conditional rule below.

Conditional:
- Exact Codex 0.147.0 and Zellij/Nova source only if captured Eonova and isolated-Eon output cannot identify the producer or emitted sequence.
- A separate Eonova or Eon packaging decision only if the same Venus generation differs between Eonova and isolated plain Eon or fails only with the exact Eon `FONTCONFIG_FILE`. Stop before cross-repository edits.
- A dependency or renderer gate only if the selected glyphon/cosmic-text stack cannot render the canonical cell correctly with an available font.

Rejected:
- Hard-coded Codex glyph substitution, special-casing U+280B, ASCII replacement, per-application rules, clipping relaxation that can paint neighboring cells, changing cell widths, bundling a font without owner evidence, or copying Zellij.

Platform classification: neutral presentation invariant inside the existing isolated font/GPU stack. Prove native Linux first; macOS and other compositors remain unproved, with no new blocker inferred.

## Implementation Notes

1. Claim the Bead and record the required Execution baseline and Reference gate before production or test edits.
2. Reproduce first in the exact Eonova profile, then with isolated plain Eon. Capture the exact canonical frame revisions for the malformed Codex state and a controlled sequence such as `⠋⠙⠹⠸⠼⠴⠦⠧⠇⠏` next to the same border/text. Prove scalar values, CellWidth, style, title metadata, and revision order before selecting an owner.
3. Add the cheapest deterministic regression at the existing scene/render seam. It must fail on the actual violated invariant: missing glyph, clipped bounds, wrong fallback, or stale rastered revision. Do not add a screenshot harness if production shaping/raster state provides a stronger smaller oracle.
4. Fix the highest confirmed owner only. Preserve the one authoritative cell grid and existing fallback/shaping stack when sufficient.
5. Rerun exact locked checks, package through the existing Eon Venus recipe, and dogfood the actual Codex working/idle transition plus the controlled corpus. Repeat the complete revised-state review after any correction.

## Verification

- The canonical capture shows whether Orbit authored each expected Braille scalar as one narrow cell and distinguishes terminal content from frame title metadata.
- One focused regression fails before the correction and passes after it for every spinner frame, adjacent box-drawing/text cells, the exact selected style, and redraw replacement.
- Existing ASCII, combining, wide-cell, box-table, preedit, cursor, selection, resize, and accessibility tests remain green.
- `cargo fmt --check`
- `cargo check --locked`
- `cargo test --locked`
- `cargo clippy --locked --all-targets -- -D warnings`
- `git diff --check`
- Native COSMIC Wayland dogfood in exact Eonova and isolated plain Eon with Codex CLI 0.147.0 and the controlled corpus shows recognizable animated Braille cells with no clipping, substitution, overlap, or stale pixels. Record exact revisions, package, font configuration, scale, and remaining platform gaps.
- Advance VEN-C1 only against the immutable proof-bearing Venus commit; retain the exact Orbit proof unless Orbit owns the defect.

## Stop Conditions

- Eonova-only reproduction is not owner proof. Stop Venus work only when canonical text, width, style, revision, title metadata, or configuration evidence identifies Codex, Nova/Zellij, Eonova, Eon, or Orbit as the owner.
- Stop and report a native compositor/title issue if terminal cells render correctly and only `Window::set_title` presentation is malformed.
- Stop for separate Eon planning if the defect is solely the Eon font package or wrapper configuration.
- Stop for the Crate gate and user approval before any dependency, font bundle, glyphon/cosmic-text upgrade, renderer change, or manifest edit.
- Stop rather than weaken cell clipping, fallback, shaping, accessibility, or geometry to satisfy one application screenshot.
- Stop if the active window-bar implementation materially changes the reproduction surface; rebaseline after its accepted commit.

## Maintenance Notes

This Bead is a concrete rendering regression, not a request for pane-name parity with Zellij. The enduring invariant is exact canonical Unicode-cell presentation across revisions. The pending scene/renderer audit should run after this known defect is resolved so it reviews the corrected owner path.

title: Render trustworthy Codex quota in the Eon Bar
description:
## Outcome and contract

Correct `VEN-C22 — Codex quota fact chip` in the existing Venus-owned presentation path.

Consumer: one person using a Venus surface controlled by a full Eon workspace.

Trigger: the current complete EONW v6 snapshot supplies, changes, stales, blocks, or removes its optional normalized Codex quota observation.

Result: one noninteractive Eon Bar chip shows `Codex` plus each available elapsed/total window position and remaining percentage, for example `Codex 3h/5h 74% · 6d4h/7d 42%`. Under width pressure it keeps the complete lowest-remaining window, for example `Codex 6d4h/7d 42%`, then hides before required tabs, controls, or drag space lose their accepted geometry. Hover and the one static AccessKit label express the same observations in human time without raw epoch seconds. Stale retains `old`; blocked and unknown remain explicit.

## Evidence and reference gate

- EONW v6 at exact Eon source `3103a00a904c347472899549ce611da765a71650` is the sole fact, refresh, freshness, permission, and normalization owner.
- Accepted VEN-C21 source `2ce3594b9ca0f62a2723d5ce5a005ed3560aea64` owns the one-row responsive geometry and accessibility path.
- Published Venus `425d4a6afdfdb9304ffb9a2a5daf8251ee1298d5` proves the prior VEN-C22 shape but not this presentation correction.
- User screenshots supply the exact regression vector: observation `1789745261`, weekly reset `1789814936`, duration 7d, and 42% remaining must render `Codex 6d4h/7d 42%` rather than `Codex 7d 42%` with Unix timestamps.
- Nova Bar exact source `bfbf8a7be28b69f9d822c0843bf2dd5066dd49e3` (Apache-2.0) is comparison-only evidence for deriving elapsed/total position from duration, reset, and observation. Its source text, separator style, provider process, cache, polling, configuration, and widget model are rejected.

## Prerequisites and ownership

VEN-C21 and EON-C22/EONW v6 remain accepted prerequisites. Venus Scene owns only deterministic text and existing responsive geometry; the existing renderer, hover path, and AccessKit tree own presentation. Eon owns provider behavior. Orbit is unchanged.

## Scope boundary

In scope: the existing quota formatter; wide, compact, stale, blocked, unknown, absent, missing-reset, unusual-duration, narrow, and hidden presentation; VEN-C22/docs/changelog/LOC alignment; focused and complete current-platform proof.

Out of scope: provider parsing or processes, account identity, network/filesystem access, local clock, timer, cache, action, focus target, alert, threshold color, chart, configuration, generic widget system, second row, another provider, protocol change, dependency, Orbit change, macOS proof, or downstream full-Eon composition.

## Acceptance

- The exact screenshot vector renders `Codex 6d4h/7d 42%` and its hover/AccessKit description says 42% remaining and observed 6d4h into 7d, with no Unix timestamp.
- Wide mode shows every elapsed/total window and remaining percentage. Compact mode selects the lowest remaining window by fact value, not array order, and retains its provider, position, total, and percentage.
- Missing reset data falls back to duration plus remaining percentage and explicitly says reset time unavailable. Unusual minute durations remain exact.
- Stale, blocked, unknown, absent, and width-hidden behavior stays truthful. The chip remains static and yields before VEN-C21 required identity, controls, hit targets, or accessibility order.
- Quota-only refresh and Eon loss retain their accepted workspace, terminal, attachment, and expiry behavior. Venus performs no provider-state inference.
- The existing table boundary fails on the published baseline and passes on the correction. Locked fmt/check/test/clippy, diff, exact LOC, current-platform Nix/native proof are recorded before VEN-C22 returns to Proven.

## Stop conditions

Stop if normalized EONW facts are insufficient, if truthful text cannot yield before required header interaction, or if the correction would require any out-of-scope owner. Keep the issue in progress until exact source and native proof exist.
notes: Platform classification: neutral shared scene and EONW presentation behavior with no platform API. This bead accepts only native x86_64 Linux Wayland because that is the current proved product surface; macOS remains unproved and out of scope.
close_reason: VEN-C22 corrected labels are published and natively proven on x86_64 Linux Wayland; downstream Eon activation remains in eon-deliver-codex-quota-eon-bar-yg0.

title: Render full-block cells without seams
description:
## Contract

Consumer: a local user viewing an Orbit-authored terminal frame in Venus.

Trigger: one or more narrow cells contain the single scalar U+2588 FULL BLOCK, including adjacent rows or columns with distinct foreground colors.

Result: each visible full block covers its exact authoritative cell rectangle. Adjacent full-block cells meet at the cell edge without black or antialiased seams. Existing blink, faint, concealed, inverse, selection, cursor, pane clipping, and row clipping semantics remain intact.

Important failures: do not compensate for producer-inserted spaces, wrong cell widths, or a scalar other than U+2588. Route those failures to the producer.

Contract routing:
- Harden proved VEN-C1. Preserve VEN-C2, VEN-C3, VEN-C4, VEN-C7, VEN-C8, VEN-C9, and VEN-C13.
- Consume canonical ORBS v3 at Orbit proof `3ee7c80005f3d2bbe81e539799327803716f6174`. Frame and cell-width semantics remain those proved by `c905bf9610581747f1b07565814b501ca66cfaa6` and `9d6d2bb37f20ab4ad9e186c7bc715eabef43e757`.
- Change no Orbit, Eon, Anima, or Venus contract.

## Evidence

- User capture `/tmp/codex-clipboard-OWK00s.png`, SHA-256 `cdc8973bbe9ebd02b7f62bf1a8a6555c839c372c77f2de8b0e6a9f3ceaa4be34`, shows Nova running YZX Anima Game of Life. Painted rows occupy 17 pixels followed by one fully black pixel in each observed 18-pixel terminal row.
- Anima `deb5c8babf295caaaaccaba2e6b5d75c1a9c1f49`, Apache-2.0, emits adjacent literal U+2588 glyphs for `GameOfLifeCellStyle::FullBlock`. Its test `game_of_life_screen_lines_preserve_life_rows_without_inserted_gaps` proves the producer inserts no spaces.
- Venus `src/render.rs:66-81` owns the 9 by 18 cell metrics at 1x.
- `src/render.rs:730-756` sends every visible glyph run through text rasterization.
- `src/render.rs:1042-1051` shrinks ordinary text by one fitted pixel after descender correction `038cc2129d7cb4047350a37bb4aa6e4c3b93ccee`.
- `src/render.rs:1057-1071` gives special metrics only to Box Drawing U+2500 through U+257F and Braille U+2800 through U+28FF. U+2588 remains ordinary text.
- `src/render.rs:1223-1264` already owns exact cell-aligned colored rectangles.
- Braille proof `3e27bb7e377da9d9eb7e5cbdbfcfa5add3de0cad` only selected a Braille face and route for U+2800 through U+28FF. It did not cause this defect.
- Ghostty `45db2c2551ecc016f9746e8e2855f4f8a3871e7b`, MIT, treats U+2588 as a covering block and draws it from exact cell geometry. This supports the narrow geometry rule; it does not justify copying Ghostty's renderer or general custom-glyph system.

Impact: medium. The defect is continuously visible in full-block terminal graphics but does not corrupt terminal state.

Effort: small, about 90 minutes.

Implementation risk: low to medium because style visibility and clipping must match the text path exactly.

Confidence: high.

## Scope

In scope:
- The shared Venus scene-to-draw path for an exact single U+2588 cell.
- One focused failing-then-passing geometry regression for horizontal and vertical adjacency at 1x, 1.25x, 1.5x, and 2x.
- Native Eonova/Nova/YZX Anima Game of Life dogfood.
- VEN-C1 proof metadata, current-state changelog, and README LOC accounting after accepted source proof.

Out of scope:
- A general synthetic renderer for U+2580 through U+259F.
- Braille changes, font replacement, shaders, renderer replacement, new modules, new dependencies, manifest changes, Anima changes, Orbit changes, or Eon changes.
- Hiding gaps by expanding rectangles beyond authoritative cell bounds.
- Color-space or vivid-color work owned by `ven-render-vivid-terminal-colors-2ap`.

## References Before Code

Required:
- Current `AGENTS.md`, `docs/CONTRACTS.md`, `docs/REFERENCES.md`, and the complete scene text and rectangle owners in `src/render.rs`.
- Anima `deb5c8babf295caaaaccaba2e6b5d75c1a9c1f49`, especially `src/game_of_life.rs` and its Apache-2.0 license.
- Ghostty `45db2c2551ecc016f9746e8e2855f4f8a3871e7b`, especially its U+2588 covering-character classification and exact full-block sprite, under MIT.
- Current locked glyphon 0.12.0 and cosmic-text 0.19.0 only to confirm that the existing text raster cannot guarantee exact cell coverage.

Comparison only:
- Ghostty's wider U+2580 through U+259F graphics machinery.

Rejected:
- Importing or adapting Ghostty's renderer, adding a custom-glyph framework, growing the box-metrics workaround to another text class, or changing Anima's gap-free output.

No source reuse or dependency is selected.

Platform classification: neutral presentation invariant implemented through the existing GPU rectangle owner. Linux Wayland is the native proof target. macOS remains unproved but gains no new blocker.

## Implementation

1. Claim the issue only when no active implementation owns `src/render.rs`. Record the exact accepted Orbit proof and current dirty paths.
2. Add one deterministic regression that proves exact cell-edge coverage for single, horizontal, vertical, and differently colored adjacent U+2588 cells at all four accepted scales. It must fail on the current text path.
3. Reuse the existing cell rectangle batch for an exact single U+2588 glyph and omit that glyph from text rasterization. Keep one shared predicate so text and rectangle paths cannot disagree.
4. Apply resolved foreground color and existing visibility, faint-alpha, inverse, clipping, selection, and cursor rules. Do not draw outside the authoritative cell rectangle.
5. Run the locked checks and native Game of Life dogfood. Repeat the fresh-eyes and simplification pass after any correction.

## Acceptance

- U+2588 covers the exact cell rectangle at 1x, 1.25x, 1.5x, and 2x.
- Horizontal and vertical neighbors share exact edges with no uncovered pixel or overlap. Differing colors expose any seam or bleed.
- Hidden, blink-hidden, and concealed blocks remain absent; faint and inverse use the existing resolved style policy.
- Selection, cursor, row, pane, and window clipping remain exact.
- Ordinary text, descenders, Box Drawing, Braille, wide cells, combining cells, preedit, and geometry checks remain green.
- Native Eonova/Nova/YZX Anima Game of Life shows continuous full-block cells.
- `cargo fmt --check`
- `cargo check --locked`
- `cargo test --locked`
- `cargo clippy --locked --all-targets -- -D warnings`
- `git diff --check`
- Advance VEN-C1 only against an immutable proof-bearing Venus commit.

## Stop Conditions

- Stop and route upstream if the canonical frame does not contain exact narrow U+2588 cells at the observed positions.
- Stop for user approval before changing a contract, adding a dependency or module, editing a manifest, replacing the renderer, or expanding scope to other Block Elements.
- Stop if exact rectangle drawing cannot preserve the existing style and clipping rules.
- Stop and rebaseline if another active issue changes `src/render.rs` or its scene/color inputs.

## Maintenance

This is a separate correction because the descender proof is already published. The renderer audit `ven-audit-venus-scene-renderer-2db` must review the corrected path.

title: Render glyph descenders without clipping
description:
## Why

Terminal glyphs with descenders are visibly cut short in Eonova. In the supplied `judgment,` crop, the tails of `j` and `g` end on a hard horizontal edge rather than completing naturally. Venus owns native glyph placement and clipping, but the observation came from Eonova; treat it as a candidate VEN-C1 defect until the same Eon/Venus generation is compared outside Nova and Zellij.

Smallest observable contract:
- Consumer: a local user reading ordinary terminal text through Venus.
- Trigger: an accepted Orbit frame contains narrow glyphs with descenders, including `g`, `j`, `p`, `q`, or `y`.
- Result: the selected font's complete glyph ink remains visible in its terminal row with a consistent baseline, without bleeding into an adjacent row or pane.
- Important failures: preserve one authoritative cell-metric owner, coherent cursor/input/resize geometry, box-border continuity, combining marks, and terminal/pane clipping. Do not merely enlarge global bounds until glyphs overlap neighboring content.

Contract routing:
- Hardens proved VEN-C1 frame-to-draw fidelity; no new contract is proposed.
- Preserves VEN-C2, VEN-C3, VEN-C4, VEN-C7, VEN-C8, and candidate VEN-C9.
- Consumes unchanged canonical ORBS v2 at accepted Orbit proof `9d6d2bb37f20ab4ad9e186c7bc715eabef43e757`.
- Changes no Orbit or Eon contract unless owner-first reproduction proves a packaging boundary defect.

## Evidence

- User-provided Eonova crop on 2026-08-10: PNG 93×34, SHA-256 `979627603fd2a1d5a241314c5e9e2dd37fc7c77460ba40e5ead78acb03f9ea5c`. Thresholded ink occupies y=11 through y=24; both `j` and `g` still have multiple lit pixels on y=24 and none below it, despite the crop continuing through y=33. The abrupt shared lower edge is consistent with clipping, but the screenshot is discovery evidence rather than the correctness oracle.
- Observed environment: active Eonova profile `91a31a8772d74d89f8a9399df1338c592ef0c1e6` at `/nix/store/3xnb1pd547mw6rf9gppwvn9ndm3b20z6-eonova-0.1.0`; it pins Eon `ec0fa0fd0bb6d78a0d37281b069899d1bd13b95e` and Nova `6c7174b4efca5f139a461d204186c5001d6457bd`. That Eon revision consumes Orbit `64db581445bafca1a08a6530f8e44f9c1edbc169` and Venus `690b038e2b58a0e7761023ac7e004e92327ac901`.
- `src/render.rs:70-82` defines one 9×18 px cell with nominal 14 px font size at scale 1.
- `src/render.rs:723-741` positions each terminal row at `row * cell_height` and passes exactly one cell height to the text path.
- `src/render.rs:781-813` intersects each text area with that exact rectangle and writes its bottom into glyphon's `TextBounds`.
- `src/render.rs:825-898` creates a cosmic-text buffer whose line height and layout height are exactly the cell height.
- `src/render.rs:946-965` calibrates terminal font size only from horizontal space advance; it does not prove the selected face's vertical raster extent fits the row.

title: Render live terminal title and CWD in every pane header
description:
## Outcome

Render Orbit-authored live title and working directory in every visible Eon pane header, including inactive panes, while keeping Eon topology and Orbit terminal state in their existing owners.

Smallest observable contract:
- Consumer: a person using the native Eon workspace and its accessibility tree.
- Trigger: Eon supplies the active tab's pane identities/endpoints and Orbit supplies accepted read-only metadata for those live Sessions.
- Result: each pane header shows a compact title/CWD label; rapid Codex title animations remain live after another pane is selected. Visual rendering, hit testing, scrolling, and accessibility use one Venus-owned label projection.
- Failures: unavailable or incompatible metadata falls back to pane identity plus honest offline/unavailable state without blocking the selected terminal or inventing activity.

This requires an exact accepted Orbit metadata proof from orb-stream-live-pane-metadata-dz3 and a user-approved expansion or successor to VEN-C8 before code.

Impact: HIGH. Effort: M. Implementation risk: MED/HIGH because it adds bounded multi-Session observation to the native client. Confidence: HIGH.

## Evidence

- Current Venus source at 9f3eea271c804ffb9d52bb374319712da361e790 materializes WorkspacePane with only id/live/selected in src/scene.rs; WorkspacePane::label returns only pane identity and offline state.
- The selected Orbit frame is already converted into Scene.title and Scene.working_directory. src/application.rs sends only Scene.title to Window::set_title.
- VEN-C8 proves the existing tab strip, accordion pane headers, geometry, input routing, and accessibility. It explicitly limits pane labels to identity/offline state.
- EONW v1 already supplies each pane's exact Orbit endpoint and lifecycle, so Venus need not ask Eon to duplicate terminal title/CWD.
- A local last-seen cache alone is insufficient: it freezes Codex's animated title when focus leaves the pane.
- Accepted VEN-C9 already supports --no-decorations; the Eon default change is a separate orchestrator bead after this in-pane replacement is proved.

## Scope

In scope:
- Observe title/CWD metadata only for the visible active tab's panes through the exact accepted Orbit contract.
- One bounded per-endpoint metadata model keyed by Eon-authored pane mapping, retired immediately when topology, endpoint identity, liveness, or active tab changes.
- A compact deterministic label and truncation/fallback policy for nonempty title and working-directory values.
- Existing pane-header drawing, hit testing, scrolling, focus, and AccessKit semantics.
- Keep Window::set_title for the selected terminal title and renderer-failure notice so compositor/task-switcher diagnostics do not regress.
- Focused deterministic scene/model/transport tests and isolated native Wayland dogfood.

Out of scope:
- Eon topology/state mutation, Orbit terminal parsing, terminal-content observation, provider-state interpretation, tab-directory inheritance, Yazi, custom title bars, window controls, manual pane rename, persisted labels, themes, new layout modes, popups, sidebars, or user configuration.
- Observing hidden tabs; begin/retire observers when a tab becomes visible instead of maintaining an unbounded whole-workspace fanout.

## Reference gate before code

Required:
- Exact accepted Orbit contract and proof from orb-stream-live-pane-metadata-dz3.
- Current VEN-C4, VEN-C8, VEN-C9 owners, renderer, scene, accessibility, application model, transport pressure, workspace refresh, retry, and endpoint-replacement paths.
- EON-C10/EONW v1 exact producer proof and current endpoint/liveness semantics.
- Exact Zellij pane-frame label behavior as comparison evidence, including title, CWD, truncation, offline state, and accessibility where available.

Adopt the existing scene/header pipeline and existing transport queue patterns. Reject polling terminal text, parsing provider meaning from titles, putting metadata in EONW, retaining observers for hidden tabs, or adding a UI framework. If a URI/path formatter would require a dependency, show the exact user value and compare the bounded literal/fallback display first.

## Acceptance

- Every visible live pane header displays its own current Orbit-authored title and working directory; empty fields fall back deterministically to pane identity without blank or ambiguous headers.
- A deterministic Codex-style rapid OSC title sequence continues updating in an inactive pane header while input and full presentation remain attached only to the selected pane.
- A CWD change in any visible pane updates that pane only. Venus never uses one pane's active Scene metadata for another.
- Tab selection starts only the new visible pane observers and retires the old tab's observers. Pane removal, endpoint replacement, offline transition, Orbit exit, and workspace loss retire obsolete state and show honest fallback.
- Header labels are bounded, clipped within existing geometry, remain selectable/clickable/scrollable, and visual and AccessKit names match exactly.
- The selected terminal still controls the native window title; first renderer failure retains its existing higher-priority diagnostic.
- Observer pressure or incompatibility cannot block terminal presentation, workspace refresh, input, resize, selection, clipboard, or shutdown.
- No Eon, EONW, Orbit-authority, dependency, custom titlebar, rename, or hidden-tab observer surface is added.
- Focused tests pass, followed once by cargo fmt --check, cargo check --locked, cargo test --locked, cargo clippy --locked --all-targets -- -D warnings, and git diff --check.
- Native x86_64 Linux Wayland dogfood proves multiple panes, live inactive title animation, CWD updates, focus changes, clipping, scale/resize, offline state, accessibility, and no Session interruption.

## Stop conditions

- Stop before code until exact orb-stream-live-pane-metadata-dz3 proof and the Venus contract identity/update order are approved.
- Stop if Orbit metadata is stale, lacks exact endpoint identity, or requires Venus to reconstruct terminal state.
- Stop before manual rename, a custom bar/window-control system, EONW metadata duplication, a dependency, or hidden-tab observation.
- Stop if title/CWD cannot fit the existing pane header accessibly; obtain a product-layout choice rather than silently adding a second bar.

## Maintenance notes

Manual rename remains deliberately unplanned because the user said maybe. If chosen later, Eon must own the rename action/state and an explicit precedence rule over Orbit title; Venus would only render it.

title: Render packaged Nerd Font glyphs without clipping or weight drift
description:
## Outcome and contract

Consumer: a user running managed Yazi, Zellij, or another terminal tool through packaged Eon/Venus.

Trigger: an authoritative Orbit cell contains a supported Nerd Font private-use glyph, in either regular or bold terminal presentation.

Result: Venus renders the complete intended icon at the exact Orbit-authored cell start without cutting its right edge; changing terminal weight may change stroke weight but must not select an ambient face with a different apparent size or geometry. Every later cell retains its exact authoritative start.

Important failures: a missing packaged face, unsupported private-use code point, or unusable glyph must remain bounded and must not crash or prevent attachment. The correction must not infer new Orbit widths, move later cells, hide delimiters, or make behavior depend on an unrelated host font.

Contract routing: hardens existing VEN-C1 without changing a product contract. Preserve VEN-C2, VEN-C3, VEN-C4, VEN-C7, VEN-C8, VEN-C11, VEN-C13, VEN-C14, and VEN-C15. Consume canonical ORBS v4 and orbit-protocol proof 7f067b30e97d0b4787a7c6c0bbe3dd8a80a61c2c unchanged. Preserve authoritative-cell-placement proof 99539163ae901413c56388ae8959c49c608dd46e. Eon remains the packaged-font owner through closed eon-pxn.6 proof fb95671d855fa944c3717103cb13bd0135f8aec8; Venus owns discovery, selection, shaping, and rendering.

## Why

Current packaged Eonova native dogfood on 2026-08-19 shows every ordinary Yazi Nerd Font icon cut on its right edge. Zellij uses the same U+F015 house for active and inactive tabs, but the active house becomes much smaller while the inactive house remains larger and right-clipped. This is a visible renderer defect across applications, not a Yazi or Zellij bug.

Impact: HIGH user-visible product polish across managed tools. Effort: M. Implementation risk: MED because the correction must retain the earlier Unicode cell-placement proof. Confidence: HIGH.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Launch the current packaged Eon/Eonova generation with its wrapped Venus and open managed Yazi in the default sidebar.
2. Observe that ordinary directory, media, and other Nerd Font icons lose their right edge while adjacent labels remain on the expected cell grid.
3. Keep the same Zellij tab name U+F015 and switch that tab between inactive and active presentation. The inactive regular house is larger and right-clipped; the active bold house becomes markedly smaller.
4. Confirm that the same applications render their icons normally in the accepted Mars comparison, separating the defect from Yazi and Zellij content.

## Evidence

- `src/scene.rs:487-521`: `Scene::build_glyph_runs` intentionally emits one complete visible Orbit cell per `GlyphRun`, preserving the fix from ven-preserve-terminal-cell-placement-q9l.
- `src/render.rs:1088-1113`: each cell is placed at its authoritative column and passed to text layout with a width of exactly one or two 10 px cells.
- `src/render.rs:1154-1190`: `push_text_clipped` intersects the text area with that per-cell layout rectangle and writes the result into glyphon `TextBounds`; exact glyphon 0.12.0 clips raster ink outside those bounds.
- `src/render.rs:1289-1296`: terminal bold changes the cosmic-text weight while retaining generic `Family::Monospace` fallback.
- Current installed Zellij layout `/home/lucca/.local/share/yazelix/zellij/layout.kdl:122-127,232`: inactive tabs are regular, active tabs add `bold`, and both display U+F015.
- Eon `flake.nix:188-191`: the installed Venus wrapper supplies DejaVu plus `nerd-fonts.symbols-only` through `FONTCONFIG_FILE`; Symbols Nerd Font Mono has only a Regular face.
- A disposable exact cosmic-text 0.19.0 probe under the live Venus `FONTCONFIG_FILE` shaped regular U+F015 from packaged Symbols Nerd Font Mono at 16.25 px but bold U+F015 from ambient FiraCode Nerd Font Mono Bold at 10 px. Venus then clips both to a 10 px cell. This explains both the right cut and active/inactive size change.
- Closed eon-pxn.6 explicitly says that a discoverable packaged face which still renders incorrectly must be routed to Venus rather than compensated in Eon. Closed ven-preserve-terminal-cell-placement-q9l requires later cell and delimiter starts to remain exact.

## Reference gate before code

1. Reread this complete Bead and all comments, VEN-C1, `docs/REFERENCES.md`, closed ven-preserve-terminal-cell-placement-q9l, and closed eon-pxn.6 including their exact proof identities.
2. Inspect exact locked glyphon 0.12.0 `TextBounds` clipping and cosmic-text 0.19.0 family/weight fallback, face selection, glyph advances, and raster placement.
3. Inspect COSMIC Terminal at pinned commit 7daf10e3b540f612cbc48973469656ecd1635dfc for its terminal-wide clip boundary and measured monospace behavior. It is GPL-3.0-only comparison evidence; copy or adaptation is not authorized.
4. Inspect Nova revision 6c7174b4efca5f139a461d204186c5001d6457bd and its Mars configuration only for the explicit BMP/supplementary PUA mapping to Symbols Nerd Font Mono. Reuse no Mars renderer, font schema, or configuration.
5. Compare the minimum complete shapes: preserve cell-local shaping but separate layout width from visible ink bounds; select a deterministic packaged symbol face for supported PUA ranges; fit or otherwise materialize that face without losing intended icon size; or use an accepted patched primary mono face. Record why the chosen shape preserves q9l and why rejected shapes fail.

## Scope

In scope:
- Existing Venus scene-to-text-render path, expected primarily `src/render.rs` and only the minimum adjacent scene data if the chosen correct boundary needs it.
- One focused deterministic regression covering representative packaged Yazi PUA glyphs and U+F015 in regular and bold styles next to blank and nonblank cells.
- Exact current locked dependency source inspection; no dependency change is expected.
- VEN-C1 proof metadata, changelog, README LOC, and Bead evidence after accepted source behavior.
- Distribution-equivalent Linux proof using the accepted Eon packaged font environment, followed by a downstream Eon pin handoff.

Out of scope:
- Changes to Orbit frames, cell widths, ORBF/ORBS, Yazi, Zellij, Nova, Mars, Eonova configuration, or user font configuration.
- A font picker, symbol-map configuration API, emoji stack, general typography redesign, compatibility path, renderer replacement, or new module.
- Eon `flake.nix`, component pins, profile refresh, or Eonova rollout. If a different packaged font or Eon packaging edit is necessary, stop and return that independently owned change for explicit user authorization and a separate Eon Bead.
- Broad glyph overhang that can obscure a nonblank later authoritative cell or invalidate the existing delimiter proof.

## Implementation notes

1. Start with one deterministic red check at the existing renderer boundary. It must demonstrate clipped supported PUA ink and regular/bold face or geometry drift while asserting unchanged later-cell origins.
2. Keep `Scene::build_glyph_runs` authoritative per-cell placement. Correct the shared font/materialization or visible-ink owner once; do not special-case Yazi or the Zellij house.
3. Use the already selected cosmic-text/glyphon stack and packaged face when sufficient. A direct crate, font package, manifest change, new module, or public configuration surface is a decision gate and stops this Bead.
4. Preserve the existing q9l Unicode corpus and delimiter pixel oracle. The fix is incomplete if icons become complete by covering later nonblank cells.
5. Prove ordinary and bold U+F015 plus representative BMP and supplementary Yazi PUA glyphs in a distribution-equivalent package. Native acceptance must exercise both the Zellij tab transition and populated Yazi sidebar.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. The focused old-source check fails for the diagnosed clipping/weight drift and passes after the correction. It proves complete supported PUA ink, stable regular/bold family and apparent geometry, exact cell origins, and a nonblank following-cell guard.
2. Existing `glyph_runs_preserve_authoritative_cell_starts` and the q9l wide, grapheme, ZWJ, RTL/bidi, fallback, combining, and delimiter surfaces remain green.
3. `cargo fmt --check`, `cargo check --locked`, `cargo test --locked`, and `cargo clippy --locked --all-targets -- -D warnings` exit 0; `git diff --check`, Beads lint/state, and exact README LOC assertions pass.
4. A distribution-equivalent Nix artifact using the accepted Eon font environment proves the packaged Symbols face identity and representative PUA coverage without treating ambient fonts as authoritative.
5. Isolated native COSMIC Wayland dogfood shows complete Yazi icons and equal apparent U+F015 geometry when its Zellij tab moves between active and inactive presentation. Existing Sessions are not stopped or reused for proof.
6. The existing machine delimiter oracle remains exact. Unsupported symbols, non-PUA text, box drawing, Braille, full blocks, emoji, IME, cursor, selection, accessibility, opacity, blur, and tail animation retain their owners and behavior.
7. Platform disposition is neutral renderer/font-selection policy with Linux-native proof. Make no macOS claim; stop if the chosen mechanism relies on a Linux-only font API outside the existing platform seam.

## Stop conditions

- Stop if current source or accepted q9l/eon-pxn.6 evidence has materially drifted.
- Stop if the only complete correction requires changing Eon packaging, adding a dependency/font package, changing a public contract, or introducing a module/configuration surface.
- Stop if complete icon ink and exact later-cell/delimiter presentation cannot both be proved with the selected stack.
- Stop after the same proof failure repeats twice following a reasonable correction attempt; retain the exact failing observation in the Bead.

## Maintenance notes

Do not reopen or undo ven-preserve-terminal-cell-placement-q9l: independently shaped authoritative cell starts are required. Do not patch generated Zellij/Yazi configuration. A viewport-wide clip is comparison evidence, not an automatic choice; reject it if it permits symbol or complex-glyph ink to obscure a later nonblank cell. Remove any Venus-specific symbol path if managed tools stop emitting PUA icons or an accepted packaged primary face makes it redundant.

title: Render terminal colors without washed-out blending
description:
## Contract routing

Harden proved `VEN-C1` color fidelity. Preserve `VEN-C2` through `VEN-C4`, `VEN-C7`, `VEN-C8`, `VEN-C9`, and `VEN-C13`. Consume canonical ORBS v3 at Orbit proof `3ee7c80005f3d2bbe81e539799327803716f6174` without changing Orbit values or terminal authority. This issue proposes no new Venus contract.

Consumer: a local user viewing an Orbit-authored terminal through Venus.

Trigger: a terminal cell supplies a palette or direct RGB foreground, background, underline, or cursor color.

Result: Venus presents the authored sRGB color without a washed-out shift. Opaque fills and glyph interiors preserve hue and saturation; antialiased edges use one declared blending model. Rectangle, glyph, clear, decoration, and cursor paths agree at their shared color-space boundary.

Important failures: Venus must not boost saturation, replace terminal palettes, reinterpret Nova or Zellij themes, change faint-text alpha, add a color setting, or treat a screenshot from another renderer as proof of the authored RGB value.

## Why

The user reported on 2026-08-12 that Zellij's bottom bar and the YZX Anima `game_of_life` view look washed out in Venus, while Nova's bar in the same product looks vivid. The supplied native capture shows the affected orange, yellow, magenta, cyan, and green terminal presentation. The difference may come from source palette values, Venus's color transfer, or glyph alpha blending. One controlled comparison can identify the owner before a fix.

Impact: HIGH because the issue affects common terminal color output and product appearance.
Effort: M.
Implementation risk: MED because a wrong gamma change can fix text while breaking opaque rectangles, cursors, clears, or color glyphs.
Confidence: HIGH in the visible difference and MED in the owner until source and presented values are captured.

## Evidence

- `src/scene.rs:289-304` stores resolved Orbit RGB channels as exact `u8` values.
- `src/scene.rs:425-465` copies frame background, foreground, and cursor colors into the immutable scene.
- `src/scene.rs:648-704` resolves default, indexed-palette, direct RGB, inverse, and selected colors before rendering.
- `src/render.rs:192-205` prefers an sRGB surface and uses opaque compositor alpha.
- `src/render.rs:43-63` converts rectangle RGB from sRGB to linear for an sRGB target.
- `src/render.rs:244-281` selects that fragment path and configures glyphon `ColorMode::Accurate` on the same target.
- `src/render.rs:910` and `src/render.rs:971-976` send authored glyph RGB plus normal or faint alpha to glyphon.
- `src/render.rs:1161-1199` sends rectangle RGB as normalized encoded channels.
- `src/render.rs:1404-1421` converts clear colors according to the selected surface format.
- `src/render.rs:1653-1667` checks the clear-color transfer but does not compare rendered rectangle and glyph output or perceived terminal fidelity.
- The deferred `ven-terminal-presentation-settings-5y7` states that terminal-authored colors remain authoritative. It does not own color correction or a theme override.

## Required reference gate

Inspect Ghostty at exact commit `a887df42c56f6de86c0fe6da9c4eeca37931e083` under the MIT license. Treat it as required comparison evidence, not a dependency or renderer replacement.

Useful Ghostty mechanisms:

- `src/config/Config.zig:375-403` distinguishes native, linear, and linear-corrected alpha blending; Linux defaults to linear-corrected.
- `src/config/Config.zig:2162-2172` interprets terminal colors as sRGB by default.
- `src/renderer/shaders/glsl/common.glsl:112-153` performs one explicit sRGB-to-linear conversion and premultiplies alpha.
- `src/renderer/shaders/glsl/cell_text.f.glsl:20-75` corrects glyph-mask alpha for linear blending without changing the authored color.
- `src/renderer/shaders/glsl/bg_color.f.glsl:1-12` routes opaque backgrounds through the same declared color-space rule.

Reject Ghostty's terminal core, renderer architecture, configuration surface, custom shaders, images, Display P3 support, and general blending modes. Copy or adaptation requires license recording; inspection alone authorizes none.

Use Nova at exact commit `976b45a9ed98b2a836d73f79f8b56c7568518711` as an in-product comparison only. First capture its authored ORBS RGB values. A vivid Nova bar proves that the active display path can show vivid colors, but it does not prove that Zellij or YZX authored the same values.

Read exact wgpu 30.0.0 sRGB target semantics and glyphon 0.12.0 `ColorMode::Accurate` and `ColorMode::Web` behavior before changing code. The selected crates already own the surface and glyph paths; add no dependency.

## Scope

In scope:

- `src/scene.rs` only if capture proves an Orbit-to-scene color mismatch.
- `src/render.rs` color transfer, surface format, blending, glyphon color mode, clear color, rectangle, cursor, and decoration paths.
- Focused renderer and canonical-scene tests.
- `docs/REFERENCES.md`, current `VEN-C1` proof state after a source commit, README LOC accounting, and changelog for an accepted visual correction.
- Native Linux comparison on the same compositor, monitor, scale, profile, opacity, font, and capture method.

Out of scope:

- Changing Orbit, Nova, Zellij, YZX, or their themes.
- Palette enhancement, saturation controls, themes, opacity settings, HDR, Display P3, ICC profile management, arbitrary shaders, renderer replacement, or a new module.
- Treating faint text as full-alpha text.
- Claiming macOS or display-wide color-management proof.

Platform classification: isolated platform dependency through the existing wgpu surface and glyphon paths. Linux is the first proof target. Record macOS as unproved unless the fix introduces a blocker.

## Implementation notes

1. Reproduce with one fixed corpus that includes opaque direct-RGB fills, indexed colors, colored text on black and non-black backgrounds, faint text, cursor colors, Zellij's bottom bar, YZX Anima `game_of_life`, and Nova's bar.
2. Capture the accepted ORBS RGB/style values before presentation. Run the same explicit direct-RGB corpus in standalone Ghostty and Venus under the same native environment with opacity 1 and no custom shader.
3. Separate source differences from renderer differences. Compare opaque interior pixels first, then glyph interior and edge coverage. Record surface format, glyphon color mode, GPU/backend, compositor, scale, capture tool, and exact revisions.
4. Fix the first confirmed owner:
   - If explicit source RGB differs before Venus, stop and route the defect to Orbit or the theme owner.
   - If opaque rectangles diverge, correct the single shared transfer boundary.
   - If rectangles match and glyphs look washed out, correct only glyph color or alpha blending. Use Ghostty's linear-corrected approach as comparison evidence when glyphon can express the same result through its existing API.
5. Keep one color-space decision for rectangle, clear, glyph, cursor, and decoration consumers. Delete a duplicate conversion if evidence proves one.
6. Repeat native comparison and a fresh-eyes simplification pass after the final shape.

## Acceptance

1. The proof records authored ORBS values and presented results, so it identifies palette/theme input, transfer, and alpha blending as separate stages.
2. A fixed opaque direct-RGB corpus matches the declared sRGB values and the same Ghostty corpus within a recorded channel tolerance under the same capture environment.
3. Colored glyphs retain their authored hue and saturation through their opaque interiors. Edge blending matches the selected model without dark halos, pale fringes, or weight changes that make light and dark text inconsistent.
4. Rectangle backgrounds, terminal text, workspace decorations, cursor, clear color, underline, strike, overline, preedit, Braille, and color glyphs use compatible color handling.
5. Normal, faint, inverse, selected, blinking, hidden, and password cursor behavior remains exact.
6. Zellij's bottom bar and YZX Anima `game_of_life` receive native user acceptance beside Ghostty. Nova remains vivid and unchanged.
7. No palette rewrite, saturation boost, configuration surface, dependency, shader system, protocol change, or second color owner enters the patch.
8. `cargo fmt --check`, `cargo check --locked`, `cargo test --locked`, `cargo clippy --locked --all-targets -- -D warnings`, and `git diff --check` pass.
9. Update `VEN-C1` only after the proof-bearing source commit and close the Bead against that source revision.

## Stop conditions

- Stop and hand off if the accepted ORBS values already contain the washed-out colors or differ from the controlled Ghostty input.
- Stop for user approval before changing a product contract, dependency, surface format family, compositor alpha mode, public setting, or platform promise.
- Stop if a proposed fix changes terminal-authored RGB values, applies a global saturation curve, or needs a general post-processing pass.
- Stop if another active issue changes `src/render.rs`, `src/scene.rs`, surface selection, glyphon setup, or cursor color rendering.
- Stop if color correctness requires replacing glyphon or wgpu; reopen the existing renderer crate gate with measurements.

## Maintenance notes

Complete this correction before `ven-rio-cursor-animation-u57`, because that feature adds colored cursor geometry to the same renderer boundary. The later `ven-audit-venus-scene-renderer-2db` should audit the accepted color-fidelity revision. This issue does not mutate those Beads.

Estimated owned change: 40-140 production and focused test lines if Venus owns the defect. A source-palette finding should produce no Venus code.
close_reason: Closed at the Venus stop condition: exact Anima/crossterm indexed cells already reach ORBS with bare-libghostty palette values, so Venus is not the owner. VEN-C1 and Venus remain unchanged. Eon owns default product-palette policy; Orbit owns terminal state and currently has no Eon palette input. Generic direct-RGB ORBS transport was verified; running Nova and native-pixel equality were not.
